prs.title: refactor(core,cli): emit tool call groups from the scheduler and drop the UI lookahead
prs.body:
`useGeminiStream` decided on its own which finished tool calls belong together. For sub-agent calls it looked ahead through the live tool list and held a finished call back until every following consecutive agent call had finished too, and it merged consecutive agent calls into one history item by checking the tool kind. A `TODO` in that code asked for `packages/core` to provide those boundaries instead. This change does that: the scheduler marks each run of two or more consecutive sub-agent calls in a batch with a shared `groupId`, and the hook only holds back and merges calls that share a `groupId`. The lookahead and the `Kind.Agent` checks are gone from the hook. For parallel sub-agents the behavior is the same as before.

## Details

- **`ToolCallRequestInfo.groupId` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/types.ts`)**: new optional field. Calls with the same value are presented, and treated as finished, together. The calls of a group are adjacent in their batch. A call that is not part of a group leaves it unset.
- **`Scheduler` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts`)**:
  - `_startBatch` assigns the groups once per batch, after the requests are ordered, with the new `getToolCallGroupIds` helper. A run of two or more adjacent calls to tools of kind `Kind.Agent` shares the call ID of the first call in the run. A lone agent call and every other call get no group. A tool that is not registered counts as not being an agent.
  - A tail call keeps the group of the call it replaces.
  - The ID is part of the call request, so it is included in every `TOOL_CALLS_UPDATE` snapshot and stays with the call through its status changes. No new event type is needed.
- **`useGeminiStream` (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`)**, in the effect that pushes finished tools to history:
  - A finished call that has a `groupId` waits until every call with the same `groupId` has finished (success, error or cancelled). Calls ahead of the group are still pushed in order.
  - Calls with the same `groupId` are pushed as one history item. Calls without a `groupId` are pushed one by one as soon as they finish, as before.
  - The lookahead and its `TODO(#22883)` comment are removed, and the hook no longer imports `Kind`.
- **Unchanged behavior**:
  - `ToolGroupMessage` still derives how it draws consecutive agent calls from the tool kind. That also covers restored sessions, which do not go through the scheduler. Moving it to `groupId` would be a follow-up.
  - Execution is untouched: which calls run in parallel is still decided by `isParallelizable`.
  - Sequential agent calls are still grouped, because a group follows the order of the requests in the batch and not how the calls are executed.
- **Tests**:
  - `packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler_parallel.test.ts`: contiguous agent calls share the ID of the first call; a lone agent call is not grouped; a new group starts after a call that is not an agent; agent calls separated by another call or by an unregistered tool are not grouped; groups are computed after topic updates move to the front.
  - `packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts`: a tail call keeps the group of the call it replaces.
  - `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx`: new `Grouped Tool Calls` tests. A group is held back until all of its calls have finished and is then pushed as one item; failed and cancelled calls count as finished; calls are grouped by `groupId` and not by tool kind; calls without a `groupId` are pushed individually; finished calls ahead of a group that is still running are pushed while the group waits. The old lookahead had no direct test coverage.
  - On the previous code, 4 of the 7 new core tests and 2 of the 5 new hook tests fail. The others pass before and after the change, because they pin behavior that is meant to stay the same.

## Related Issues

Fixes [#28258](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28258)

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/scheduler/scheduler_parallel.test.ts src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run the full preflight:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. Manual check. This is not easy to do by hand: the difference only shows while two or more sub-agents run in the same turn. That needs a real model session, and the model decides what to call and when each agent finishes. The unit tests above cover the logic, so treat this as an optional smoke test:
   1. Build and start the CLI from this branch:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      npm start
      ```
   2. Ask for two sub-agents in one turn. Any two enabled sub-agents work, for example:
      ```
      Run two codebase_investigator tasks in parallel: one on how the scheduler orders tool calls, and one on how finished tool calls are added to the history.
      ```
   3. Expected, and the same as before this change:
      - While the agents run, both stay together in the live tool area.
      - When the last agent finishes, both results move into the history together as one block. An agent that finished earlier is not printed on its own first.
   4. If the model does not call two agents in the same turn, the check does not apply. Try another prompt.

prs.title: fix(cli): prevent right-hand border bleed in scrollable tool containers
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a UI rendering glitch where bordered tool output containers (such as expanded `WriteFile` and `Edit` views in compact mode and scrollable tool results in alternate buffer mode) intermittently break or bleed past the right-hand border when displaying both a nested vertical scrollbar and dynamically wrapped text.

## Details

    - **Root Cause:**
      - In `DenseToolMessage`, the outer bordered `<Box>` (with `borderStyle="round"` and `paddingX={1}`, consuming 4 columns of border/padding chrome) was capped at `PAYLOAD_MAX_WIDTH` (`124`), leaving `120` columns of inner width. However, `ScrollableList` was passed `Math.min(PAYLOAD_MAX_WIDTH, ...)` without subtracting `PAYLOAD_BORDER_CHROME_WIDTH`, allowing the inner list to span `124` columns on wide terminals (`terminalWidth >= 135`), overwriting the right- hand border `│` and pushing the scrollbar outside the container. On narrower terminals, subtracting `PAYLOAD_SCROLL_GUTTER = 4` from `ScrollableList`'s outer width left a 4-column gap before the right border. Additionally, `colorizeCode` and `renderDiffLines` received `terminalWidth - PAYLOAD_MARGIN_LEFT` instead of the safe inner content width.
      - In `ToolResultDisplay`, when `isAlternateBuffer` is enabled, content is wrapped in `<Scrollable width={childWidth}>` (which reserves 1 column via `paddingRight={1}` for the vertical scrollbar), but nested components with explicit width constraints (`MarkdownDisplay`, `DiffRenderer`, `SubagentProgressDisplay`, `AnsiOutputText`) were passed `childWidth` instead of `childWidth - 1`.
 
    - **Fix:**
      - Explicitly calculate `safeContentWidth = Math.max(0, totalContainerWidth - borderSpace - scrollbarBuffer)` in both `DenseToolMessage` and ToolResultDisplay`.
      - Apply `safeContentWidth` to nested `<Box>` and text-wrapping/diff/markdown containers so wrapped text and diff hunk separators never collide with the vertical scrollbar or overwrite the right-hand border.

## Related Issues

Fixes #24768

## How to Validate

   1. Run the unit and regression tests for `DenseToolMessage` and `ToolResultDisplay`:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/components/messages/DenseToolMessage.test.tsx src/ui/components/messages/ToolResultDisplay.test.tsx

  2. Run typecheck and lint:
    npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli
    npm run lint

  3. In the CLI with alternate buffer and compact tool output enabled (useAlternateBuffer: true, compactToolOutput: true), trigger a WriteFile or Edit tool call with >15 lines and long wrapped lines, expand the diff subview, and verify across narrow and wide terminal widths that the vertical scrollbar remains inside the box and the right-hand border (│) is intact on every row.

prs.title: feat(core): make API request headers and body timeouts configurable
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds two settings, `general.requestHeadersTimeoutMs` and `general.requestBodyTimeoutMs`, so users can raise the model API request timeouts under **every auth type**. Today long-thinking turns that stream nothing for more than 5 minutes are aborted with `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` and replayed from scratch (billed again), up to `maxAttempts` times. API-key users have no way to change this.

## Details

**Root cause:** `packages/core/src/utils/fetch.ts` hardcoded `defaultBodyTimeout = 300000` and `defaultHeadersTimeout = 60000`. The only override was `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()`, driven by the `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` experiment flag. API-key auth never receives that flag, and even when it is present it only changed the headers timeout.

**Changes:**

- **`fetch.ts`**
  - `defaultBodyTimeout` is now mutable.
  - `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts(headersTimeoutMs, bodyTimeoutMs?)` accepts an optional body timeout and validates both values. It applies them to the global dispatcher, the proxy dispatcher (`setGlobalProxy`) and the safe agent.
  - Adds a small `getGlobalFetchTimeouts()` getter.
  - Existing callers are unaffected.
- **`Config` (core)**
  - New `requestHeadersTimeoutMs` / `requestBodyTimeoutMs` params. Non-positive or non-finite values are ignored with a `debugLogger.warn`.
  - `getRequestTimeoutMs()` now prefers the user setting over the experiment flag.
  - New `getRequestBodyTimeoutMs()`.
  - `refreshAuth()` applies whichever timeouts are configured. If only the body timeout is set, the current headers timeout is kept.
- **Settings schema (CLI):** two new `general.*` number settings (`requiresRestart: true`, not shown in the dialog), wired through `loadCliConfig`.
- **Small related fix:** a `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` flag value of `0` was accepted by `getRequestTimeoutMs()` and then made `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()` throw a `RangeError` during `refreshAuth()`. It is now ignored.
- **Generated files:** regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json` and `docs/reference/configuration.md` with `npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings`.

Behavior is unchanged when neither setting is configured.

Example `settings.json` (15 min, per the Gemini latest-model migration checklist):

```json
{
  "general": {
    "requestHeadersTimeoutMs": 900000,
    "requestBodyTimeoutMs": 900000
  }
}
```

Since `settings.json` already supports `${VAR}` expansion, containerized and headless users can drive these from environment variables without a separate env var.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29747
Related to #29693 (the headers-timeout half of the same problem)

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm run build --workspace @google/gemini-cli-core
   cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/utils/fetch.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts
   cd ../cli && npx vitest run src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts src/config/settings.test.ts
   ```
   New tests cover:
   - setting precedence over the experiment flag
   - invalid value handling
   - applying timeouts on `refreshAuth` with API-key auth
   - body-only configuration
   - propagation to the proxy dispatcher and safe agent
   - the flag value `0` edge case
2. Manual check: set `general.requestBodyTimeoutMs` to a small value (e.g. `5000`), run `gemini -p` with a prompt that makes the model think for a long time, and confirm the request is aborted after ~5 s instead of 300 s. Then set a large value and confirm a long silent turn is no longer aborted at 5 minutes.
3. `npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings` produce no further diff.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

prs.title: fix(ui): fix debug console height calculation and terminalBuffer flickering
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes Debug Console (`F12`) height/layout calculation bugs and improves rendering stability in `terminalBuffer` mode by enabling incremental rendering and static history item memoization with safe cache invalidation.

## Details

- **Debug Console (`F12`) height calculation ([`Composer.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/components/Composer.tsx))**: Fixed `debugConsoleMaxHeight` calculation to use `terminalHeight` (`rows`) from `useTerminalSize()` instead of `terminalWidth` (`columns`), preventing the Debug Console from expanding to 20% of the terminal column count on wide terminals.
- **Debug Console inner list viewport height ([`DetailedMessagesDisplay.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/components/DetailedMessagesDisplay.tsx))**: Subtracted the outer box border and header height (`headerAndBorderHeight = 4`) when passing `height` and `containerHeight` to the inner `<Box>` and `<ScrollableList>`, preventing the bottom 4 lines of log messages from being clipped and fixing scroll bounds.
- **Prevent unconstrained height / static refresh flash on `OpenDebugConsole` ([`AppContainer.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.tsx))**: Removed `setConstrainHeight(false)` from `openDebugConsole` so auto-opening the Debug Console on error does not uncap UI heights or trigger a `refreshStatic()` (`clearTerminal`) flash on the next keystroke. Also updated `refreshStatic` to increment `historyRemountKey` in `terminalBuffer` mode (without writing `ansiEscapes.clearTerminal`) so theme and markdown toggles invalidate `<StaticRender>` caches cleanly without screen flashing.
- **Enable `incrementalRendering` for `terminalBuffer` mode ([`interactiveCli.tsx`](packages/cli/src/interactiveCli.tsx))**: Allowed `incrementalRendering` when `config.getUseTerminalBuffer()` is active (in addition to `useAlternateBuffer`), avoiding full-frame log-update erasures on each thinking/streaming tick when `useAlternateBuffer: false` and `terminalBuffer: true`.
- **Mark non-interactive history items as static with cache invalidation ([`MainContent.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/components/MainContent.tsx))**: Expanded `isStaticItem` in `MainContent` to return `true` for completed, non-interactive history items (`user`, `gemini`, `gemini_content`, `thinking`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, `hint`, etc.) while keeping interactive/mutable items (`tool_group`, `compression`, `pending`, and `header` while `updateInfo.isUpdating` is active) dynamic, and included header/markdown/remount state in `keyExtractor` so `<StaticRender>` invalidates when those states change.

## Related Issues

Fixes #10673

## How to Validate

1. Run targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/components/Composer.test.tsx src/ui/components/DetailedMessagesDisplay.test.tsx src/ui/components/MainContent.test.tsx src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx src/gemini.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run typecheck and linter:
   ```bash
   npm run typecheck && npm run lint
   ```
3. Manual verification:
   - Start Gemini CLI in a wide terminal (e.g., 200x40) and press `F12` to open the Debug Console; verify its height is constrained to 20% of terminal rows and all log lines scroll cleanly without bottom clipping.
   - Run with `"useAlternateBuffer": false, "incrementalRendering": true, "terminalBuffer": true` and verify smooth streaming updates without full-viewport flicker.

prs.title: fix(cli): handle response and write stream errors in extension downloadFile
prs.body:
## Summary

`downloadFile()` in `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts` now handles failures from the HTTP response stream and from the destination write stream, instead of relying on `finish` alone: the returned promise rejects exactly once, both streams are torn down, and the partially written archive is removed.

Fixes #28645.

## Details

Before this change `downloadFile()` piped the response into `fs.createWriteStream(dest)` and listened only for `finish`, with no `error` listener on either stream. Because of that:

- A response that failed **after** the headers arrived (mid-transfer network failure), or a write failure such as `ENOSPC`/`EACCES`, emitted an `error` event with no listener — an unhandled `EventEmitter` error — instead of rejecting the returned promise, so `downloadFromGitHubRelease()` never reported a failed download and installation could hang.
- The partially written archive stayed at `dest` for a later extraction/install to pick up.

The fix keeps the existing manual `Promise` wrapper (rather than `stream/promises.pipeline()`, the other option suggested in the issue) because it is the smallest diff that produces the same end state:

- `settled`/"once" guards so the first failure (or success) wins and later events on either stream are ignored.
- On failure: `res.unpipe(file)` and `file.destroy()` stop the download and release the file handle.
- The incomplete archive is unlinked from the write stream's `close` handler, so removal happens after the handle is released (avoids `EBUSY`/`EPERM` on Windows).
- `removeIncompleteDownload()` is best-effort: the file may never have been created.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28645

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/config/extensions/github.test.ts
```

Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 37 passed (37)`.

New regression tests in `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts` under `describe('downloadFile')`:

- response stream error after a `200` → rejects with that error, calls `unpipe`/`destroy`, and unlinks the destination once the stream has closed;
- write stream error (`ENOSPC`) → rejects with that error, destroys the stream, and unlinks the destination;
- a failure that arrives after the first one → the promise still rejects with the first error, and no error is thrown as unhandled.

Also run:

- `npx eslint packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts --max-warnings 0` → exit 0, no warnings.
- `npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli` → `tsc --noEmit`, exit 0.

Not run: full `npm run preflight` (clean + install + build + all workspace tests) — the targeted checks above cover the touched package. End-to-end validation of a real interrupted download was not performed; the suite asserts the failure paths against mocked streams.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not needed; no user-facing change beyond correct error propagation and no longer leaving a partial archive.
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none: the success path is unchanged, and callers already treat a rejection as `failureReason: 'failed to download asset'`.

prs.title: fix(ui): implement synchronized output and isolate spinner rendering
prs.body:
## Summary

Implement terminal synchronized output around interactive UI frame writes and isolate spinner rendering state to eliminate screen flickering in terminal multiplexers such as `tmux`.

## Details

- **Synchronized Output Stream Wrapper (`packages/core/src/utils/stdio.ts`, `packages/cli/src/interactiveCli.tsx`):**
  - Added `wrapWithSynchronizedOutput` and `createSynchronizedStdout` (along with the `synchronizedOutput` option in `createWorkingStdio`) to bracket interactive UI frame writes with terminal synchronized output sequences:
    - Standard terminals: DEC Private Mode 2026 (`\x1b[?2026h` / `\x1b[?2026l`), which is buffered atomically by supporting terminals and silently ignored by non-supporting ANSI terminals.
    - `tmux` environments (`process.env.TMUX`): `tmux` DCS synchronized update sequences (`\x1bP=1s\x1b\\` / `\x1bP=2s\x1b\\`).
  - Preserved passthrough behavior for standalone terminal mode sequences and `dumb` terminals.
- **Spinner State Isolation & Tmux Throttling (`CliSpinner.tsx`, `GeminiSpinner.tsx`, `GeminiRespondingSpinner.tsx`, `LoadingIndicator.tsx`, `StatusRow.tsx`):**
  - Localized spinner tick intervals strictly within `CliSpinner` and `GeminiSpinner` and wrapped `CliSpinner`, `GeminiSpinner`, `GeminiRespondingSpinner`, `LoadingIndicator`, `StatusNode`, and `StatusRow` in `React.memo` so frame ticks do not trigger parent or sibling re-renders.
  - Adjusted the spinner frame and color gradient interval to `120ms` (`TMUX_SPINNER_INTERVAL_MS`) when `process.env.TMUX` is present to reduce PTY redraw overhead.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22004

## How to Validate

1. Build all packages and run type checks:
   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm run typecheck
   ```
2. Run unit tests for `stdio` synchronized output and spinner component isolation:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/stdio.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/components/CliSpinner.test.tsx src/ui/components/GeminiRespondingSpinner.test.tsx src/ui/components/LoadingIndicator.test.tsx src/ui/components/StatusRow.test.tsx src/ui/components/Composer.test.tsx
   ```
3. Launch `gemini-cli` inside a `tmux` session and trigger a model response to verify smooth spinner updates without screen flickering.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

    This change was contributed by @​BPJEnnova.

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    This release contains additional minification patterns for reducing switch statements. Here is an example:

    // Original code
switch (x) {
  case 0:
    foo()
    break
  case 1:
  default:
    bar()
}

prs.title: fix(cli): prevent background git operations from hijacking stdin
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR addresses issue #23480 where background extension update checks (`git.listRemote`) or clones (`git.clone`) spawn Git without disabling interactive terminal prompts. If credentials or passphrases are challenged under slow, private, or authenticated remotes, Git blocks waiting on `stdin`, which is invisible under the Ink TUI, causing the terminal CLI to freeze and hijack keyboard input.

## Details

- Implements a `createNonInteractiveGit` helper in `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts` that configures `simple-git` with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'` and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND: 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes'` (preserving user-configured commands).
- Integrates `createNonInteractiveGit` into both `cloneFromGit` and `checkForExtensionUpdate`.
- Wraps `git.listRemote` background checking in `checkForExtensionUpdate` with a `15_000ms` background timeout race to prevent indefinite network hangs.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests in `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts` to verify environment variable injection and graceful handling of prompt suppression failures.

prs.title: fix(core): time out hanging web searches after 30 seconds
prs.body:
## Summary

The `GoogleSearch` and `WebFetch` tools passed only the caller's abort signal to `geminiClient.generateContent`, so a request whose underlying LLM call never settled left the agent loop in a permanent `Thinking...` state (the issue reports 30+ minute hangs) until the user pressed Esc. This PR adds a 30 second execution timeout to both tools, as requested in the issue.

- **`GoogleSearch`**: when the timer fires, the request is aborted and the tool returns a structured `WEB_SEARCH_FAILED` tool error, letting the model recover or inform the user.
- **`WebFetch`**: the primary LLM-mediated fetch aborts on timeout and the existing all-or-nothing fallback takes over — the direct URL fetch path, which keeps its own per-URL timeout. External cancellation still stops the fallback, while a primary-fetch timeout does not.
- Both tools share a new `createTimeoutAbortHandle` utility (`packages/core/src/utils/abort.ts`) that combines the external signal with the timeout and reports which one fired. It handles the case where `ExecuteOptions.abortSignal` is `undefined`.

## Details

- External aborts (user pressing Esc) are forwarded onto the internal controller, so user cancellation keeps its existing result (`Web search was cancelled.` for search) and remains distinguishable from a timeout via `didTimeout()`.
- Timer and listeners are cleaned up in `finally` blocks, including on the success path.
- No new dependencies and no API changes; the timeouts are named constants (30s), inside the 15–30s range suggested in the issue.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29594

## How to Validate

1. `npx vitest run packages/core/src/utils/abort.test.ts packages/core/src/tools/web-search.test.ts packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.test.ts` — 79 tests pass, including 5 new utility tests, 2 new `GoogleSearch` tests (timeout → structured error; external abort before the timeout keeps the unchanged cancelled result), and 1 new `WebFetch` test (timed-out primary fetch falls back to the direct URL path and returns its result).
2. Existing behavior is unchanged for successful searches/fetches and generic failures (all pre-existing tests pass unmodified).

Validation notes (honest scope): Prettier, ESLint, and `tsc --noEmit` pass on the touched files; the full `packages/core` suite and `npm run preflight` were not run locally — CI covers them.

prs.title: fix(core): split custom headers only before a valid RFC 9110 token
prs.body:
## Summary

`parseCustomHeaders` split `GEMINI_CLI_CUSTOM_HEADERS` on any comma followed by `<text>:` where `<text>` only had to exclude `,` and `:`. Header values that legitimately contain `,"name":` (JSON metadata, e.g. `x-portkey-metadata: {"_user":"alice","env":"prod"}`) or `, <url>` (multi-URL `Link` headers) were cut into a second "header" with an invalid name, and Node's `Headers` constructor then rejects the whole map (`TypeError: Headers.append: ""env"" is an invalid header name.`).

The split lookahead now requires an RFC 9110 token before the colon (`/,(?=\s*[\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+\s*:)/`), so commas inside values are preserved while comma-separated header lists still parse exactly as before.

Supersedes #29604 (same change; recreated so the commit author identity matches the CLA registration).

## Details

- All 10 pre-existing `customHeaderUtils` test cases keep their expected results under the new regex (multi-header lists, values containing commas/colons, entries without a colon, whitespace trimming, empty entries).
- The token character class covers exactly the RFC 9110 `tchar` set (ALPHA/DIGIT via `\w`, plus `!#$%&'*+.^_\`|~-`), so names like `Content-Type` still start a new header while `"env"`, `<https` and similar value fragments do not.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29602

## How to Validate

1. `npx vitest run packages/core/src/utils/customHeaderUtils.test.ts` — 14 tests pass (10 existing + 4 new regression tests: JSON metadata value with commas, multi-URL `Link` header, and a mixed case that must still split before a following real header).
2. The repro from the issue now yields a single header with the full value, and `new Headers(...)` no longer throws:
   ```js
   parseCustomHeaders('x-portkey-metadata: {"_user":"alice","env":"prod"}');
   // { 'x-portkey-metadata': '{"_user":"alice","env":"prod"}' }
   ```

Validation notes (honest scope): ran the full `packages/core/src/utils/` suite (1845 tests pass; the 7 suites failing to collect — `bfsFileSearch`, `filesearch/*`, … — fail identically on unmodified `main` with `Cannot find package 'src/config/constants.js'`, verified by stashing this change, so they are environment-related and untouched by this PR). Prettier and ESLint pass on the two touched files. `npm run preflight` was not run locally; CI will cover it.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (4 regression tests)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (none: header lists parse unchanged, only previously-crashing values now work)

prs.title: fix(scripts): fail the nightly eval summary when no reports exist
prs.body:
## Summary

`scripts/aggregate_evals.js` logged "No reports found." and exited 0 when the artifacts directory contained no `report.json` files. Because the nightly workflow's `Run Evals` step is `continue-on-error: true`, a nightly whose matrix legs all failed before writing a report (an expired `GEMINI_API_KEY`, for example) finished green with only that quiet line in the summary.

On the scheduled nightly, zero reports now emit a `::error::` annotation and exit non-zero, so the summary job — and the nightly run — is visibly red. Filtered `workflow_dispatch` runs can legitimately match nothing, so they keep exit 0 and emit a `::warning::` annotation instead; local runs stay quiet. This is the direction suggested in the linked issue (exit non-zero on `schedule`, annotation elsewhere).

## Details

- Detection is `process.env.GITHUB_EVENT_NAME === 'schedule'`, which GitHub Actions sets automatically; the nightly's full-suite run has no filters, so zero reports there always means every leg failed.
- The `::warning::` annotation is emitted only when running under CI (`process.env.CI`), so local invocations keep the previous plain `No reports found.` + exit 0 behavior.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29598

## How to Validate

1. `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts aggregate-evals` — 3 new tests pass:
   - scheduled run + empty artifacts dir → exit 1 with a `::error::` annotation on stderr;
   - `workflow_dispatch` + empty dir → exit 0 with a `::warning::` annotation;
   - outside GitHub Actions → exit 0, no annotations (previous behavior preserved).
2. Manual repro from the issue: `node scripts/aggregate_evals.js <empty dir>` still prints "No reports found." and exits 0 locally, and fails only when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=schedule` is set.

Validation notes (honest scope): the full `scripts/tests` suite reports 73 tests passing; 8 suites fail to collect locally with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@google/gemini-cli-core"` — a pre-existing environment issue in suites that need a full build (`npm run build`), unrelated to this change (none of them touch `aggregate_evals.js`). Prettier and ESLint pass on the two touched files.

prs.title: feat(subagent): Enable incremental output streaming
prs.body:
This PR introduces the capability for sub-agents to stream incremental messages to the main process. This allows for real-time feedback and progress updates from long-running sub-agent tasks.

To facilitate testing and demonstrate this new functionality, this PR also includes the creation of a new `planning_tool`. This tool uses a sub-agent to generate a detailed execution plan from a user's request and streams its thinking process back to the user.

Key changes:
-   Implemented the mechanism for sub-agents to incrementally stream output.
-   Created a new `planning_tool` that leverages this streaming capability.
-   Added a `usePlanningTool` setting to `settings.json` to control its activation (defaults to `false`).
-   Enhanced the planning tool to produce more detailed, structured plans and gave it access to read-only file system tools.

This foundational work on sub-agent streaming will enable more interactive and transparent long-running tools in the future.

prs.title: fix(core): fix detectPowerShellSubstitution quote tracking and false positives
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes false positive command substitution detection in `detectPowerShellSubstitution` on Windows.
When quotes or escaped characters were present within double-quoted strings (such as `\"`, `""`, or nested single quotes), the parser's `inDoubleQuote` state tracking desynchronized, causing legitimate commands with parentheses (like `git log --format="%h \" (%an)"` or `git commit -m "fix(core): \"quoted\" (detail)"`) to be falsely blocked with a command injection warning.

## Details
1. **Quote State Machine Tracking**:
   - Inside single quotes: In PowerShell, `''` escapes a single quote; handle doubled single quotes `''` without exiting single quote mode.
   - Inside double quotes: In PowerShell, `""` escapes a double quote; handle doubled double quotes `""` without exiting double quote mode.
   - Backslash escape handling: Windows executables and wrappers frequently escape quotes as `\"`. In double quotes, consume backslash escape sequences `['$', '`', '"', '\\', '(', ')', "'"]` via `i += 2` so `\"` does not prematurely toggle `inDoubleQuote` to `false`.
   - Outside quotes: Handle general escape sequences (`\` and `` ` ``) so escaped parens like `\(` are not flagged as unquoted subexpressions.
2. **Regression Testing**:
   - Added unit test suite in `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts` testing escaped double quotes with parens, doubled quotes, escaped substitution syntax, and verifying that actual malicious subexpressions (`$()`, `@()`, bare `()`) remain strictly blocked.
   - Added regression test in `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts` verifying end-to-end execution of PowerShell commands with nested/escaped quotes and parentheses.

## Related Issues
Fixes #29738

## How to Validate
1. Run PowerShell with nested quotes and parentheses:
   ```powershell
   git commit -m "fix(core): \"quoted\" (detail)"
   git log --format="%h \" (%an)"
   echo "a \" b (c)"
   ```
   **Expected**: Commands execute cleanly without being blocked by command injection detection.
2. Run command injection attempts:
   ```powershell
   echo (whoami)
   echo $(whoami)
   echo @(whoami)
   ```
   **Expected**: Blocked with command injection warning.
3. Run test suites:
   - `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts`
   - `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts`

issues.title: Copilot CLI unusable after macOS update/reboot because `.mcp-writer.binding` persists stale filesystem device ID

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Immediately after installing the latest macOS security update and rebooting, all Copilot CLI sessions—both newly started sessions and resumed existing sessions—became unable to process prompts.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.90-3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## Environment
- macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1 on Apple Silicon
- GitHub Copilot CLI reports version 1.0.90-3

## What Happened
On startup after installing 27.0.1, I restarted my copilot sessions, and each of them reported:

`Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: The shared writer lock or its directory changed.`

Attempts to send prompts then hung/failed.

Copilot logs repeatedly contained:

`Scheduled queue processing failed; retrying once {"error":"Message(\"The shared writer lock or its directory changed.\")"}`

and:

`Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned {"error":"Message(\"The shared writer lock or its directory changed.\")"}`

## Root cause

`~/.copilot/.mcp-writer.binding` contained persisted Unix filesystem identities:

```json
{"root":{"platform":"unix","device":16777230,"inode":1767102},
 "lock":{"platform":"unix","device":16777230,"inode":45460913}}
```

After the macOS update/reboot, `stat` showed:

~/.copilot:
device=16777232 inode=1767102
~/.copilot/.mcp-writer.lock:
device=16777232 inode=45460913

Thus, the inode numbers remained exactly the same, but macOS had changed the filesystem device ID from 16777230 to 16777232.

Copilot apparently interprets this change in device ID as indicating that the shared-writer lock or its directory has been replaced/changed, even though these are the same filesystem objects.

The stale device ID appeared only in `.mcp-writer.binding`.

## Attempted workaround

Moving `.mcp-writer.binding` aside did not cause Copilot to regenerate it. Instead, a newly launched Copilot reported:

`Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: Shared writer storage I/O failed.`

and attempts to send requests failed with:

`Request session.send failed with message: Shared writer storage I/O failed.`

Restoring the binding file returned behavior to the original "shared writer lock or its directory changed" failure.

## Successful workaround

After backing up `.mcp-writer.binding`, I changed only the two persisted device IDs from:

`16777230`

to the device ID currently reported by stat:

`16777232`

producing:

```json
{"root":{"platform":"unix","device":16777232,"inode":1767102},
 "lock":{"platform":"unix","device":16777232,"inode":45460913}}
```

I then launched a new copilot process. MCP startup succeeded immediately and Copilot processed prompts normally.

At this point, running `\restart` in the existing copilot sessions allowed them to recover as well (prior to fixing the device id, `/restart` had gone right back to the same broken condition).

### Expected behavior

A macOS update/reboot that changes the filesystem device ID should not permanently prevent Copilot from starting its shared-writer storage.

Copilot should either:
1. tolerate a device-ID change when it can otherwise safely establish the identity/integrity of the shared storage, or
2. safely regenerate/rebind .mcp-writer.binding when the stored filesystem identity becomes stale.

In particular, removing a stale binding currently appears to make recovery worse because Copilot fails with Shared writer storage I/O failed rather than rebuilding the binding.

### Additional context

This effectively disables all Copilot CLI sessions after the OS update, including existing/resumable sessions, until the undocumented .mcp-writer.binding file is manually repaired.

issues.title: Bug: Idle CLI sessions pin one CPU core at 100% (`notify-rs debouncer loop` busy-spins)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

**Environment:** Copilot CLI 1.0.98, macOS 26.6.1 (Apple Silicon arm64, 14 cores).

**What happened:** Four concurrent CLI sessions each used about 100% of one core. Three of them stayed pegged from startup: about 52–54 minutes of CPU time over a similar wall-clock time. The sessions were started with `--allow-all`, or with `--allow-all --autopilot --fleet`. Three shared one git worktree (Maven project) as their working directory; the fourth used a sibling worktree.

**Evidence that this is internal to the CLI, not agent work:**

- The main Node thread is idle (parked in `kevent` under `uv_run`).
- Logs only show periodic OTel and telemetry POSTs. The log files didn't grow over a 5-second window.
- Child processes (jdtls, MCP servers, background shells) were at 0% CPU.
- `sample <pid> 3` shows the thread `notify-rs debouncer loop` on-CPU in every sample (2478/2478) and never blocked. The `notify-rs fsevents loop` threads are idle.
- The hot frames are the same in two separate processes: `runtime.node +0x3dd8278` (and nearby offsets), called from `+0x3ddb8b4` under `+0x25c8c0c`, plus `_platform_memcmp`. It appears to be iterating or comparing over debouncer state already in memory rather than handling new filesystem events.

**Expected:** When no filesystem events are arriving, the debouncer thread should block (on a condvar or timeout) and use about 0% CPU.

**Possible trigger (unconfirmed):** Several sessions watched the same high-churn worktree (Maven `target/` output, Docker/acceptance builds). A large event backlog, or a zero or expired debounce timeout, could leave the loop spinning.

**Workaround:** Exit and run `copilot --resume <session-id>`, or kill the process.

**Request:** Please check the debouncer loop for a busy-wait or zero-timeout path. Please also consider excluding ignored or build directories (e.g. `.gitignore`d `target/`) from the watch.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Not sure but the description `what happened` section may provide clues

### Expected behavior

No idle loop 100% cpu

### Additional context

macOS 26.6.1

issues.title: /restart fails when the CLI was launched with --new-session-id
issues.body:
### What happened

Launching the CLI with `--new-session-id <uuid>` and then running `/restart` fails every time:

```
error: the argument '--new-session-id <id>' cannot be used with '--session-id <id>'

Usage: copilot --log-dir <directory> --plugin-dir <directory> --add-dir <directory> --additional-mcp-config <json> --yolo

For more information, try '--help'.
```

By the time this surfaces the foreground session has already been shut down, so the restart is not recoverable.

### Repro

1. `copilot --new-session-id 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555` (any fresh UUID)
2. Run `/restart`

This matters for embedding hosts, which pass `--new-session-id` on every session launch, so `/restart` is permanently unusable there rather than occasionally.

### Cause

`/restart` rebuilds the child argv from `process.argv.slice(2)`, strips the session-selection flags, then appends `--session-id <current session id>`.

In `cli-main.js` (1.0.98) the strip helper removes `-r`, `--resume`, `--resume=`, `--session-id`, `--session-id=`, `--continue`, `--cloud`, `-i`, `--interactive`, `--interactive=`, `--experimental`, `--no-experimental`, `--fleet` and `-C`. `--new-session-id` is absent from that list, so it survives into the restart argv next to the freshly appended `--session-id`, and the parser declares the two mutually exclusive.

The same rebuilt argv is persisted for the supervised restart path, so both the supervised and unsupervised paths fail identically.

### Expected

The strip helper should drop `--new-session-id` and `--new-session-id=<uuid>`, consuming the following value in the bare form, exactly as it already does for `--session-id`. The session exists by restart time, so re-asserting a creation ID is both wrong and rejected.

### Workaround

Patching the strip helper locally to treat `--new-session-id` like `--session-id` resolves it, but the file lives in the extracted package folder and the fix is lost on every CLI update.

### Version

1.0.98 on Windows, win32-x64.

issues.title: 400 `reasoning_text` in thinking mode must be passed back — triggered by runtime-synthesized assistant turn after a background shell exits
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session using a **custom OpenAI-compatible provider with `wireApi: "responses"`** (DeepSeek, model `deepseek-flash`) is killed by an HTTP 400 on the model call that immediately follows a **runtime-synthesized, model-less assistant turn**.

The trigger is the background-shell-completion flow:

1. A command is backgrounded (short `initial_wait`).
2. When it exits, the runtime emits a `<system_notification>` (`kind.type = "shell_completed"`).
3. The runtime then injects a **synthetic `assistant.message`** to read the shell output. That message has `model: undefined`, empty `content`, and — critically — **no `reasoningBlocks`**.
4. The next request to the provider is rejected because thinking mode requires the previous assistant turn's reasoning to be passed back.

Result: `session.error`, the session ends (`was_interrupted: true`, `interruption_reason: "error"`).

The provider and credentials are fine — the same provider/model served 160+ successful model calls in the same session. It is specifically the model-less synthetic turn that breaks the reasoning passback invariant.

### Affected version

- `copilot --version`: **1.0.95-3** (dist: `pkg/win32-arm64/1.0.95-3`)
- Host: Copilot app (`copilot-desktop-gh-2.98.0`)
- OS: Windows, ARM64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a custom provider:
   - `type`: `custom`
   - `baseUrl`: `https://api.deepseek.com`
   - `wireApi`: `responses`
   - `authKind`: `api_key`
   - model `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; **thinking mode is enabled by default**)
2. In a session, start a long-running command so it moves to the background, e.g. a `powershell` call with a short `initial_wait`:
   `dotnet test --project <integration test project> --filter-class "*SelectiveOperationScaleTests"`
3. Continue working while the shell runs. When it exits, observe the injected turn and the failure:
   - `system.notification` → `<system_notification>Shell command "…" (shellId: 68) has exited with exit code 2.</system_notification>`
   - `assistant.message` with `model: undefined`, `content: ""`, one `read_powershell` tool call, **no `reasoningBlocks`**
   - `tool.execution_complete` for `read_powershell`
   - HTTP **400** on the next model call → `session.error`
4. See error: session terminates.

Exact sequence from `events.jsonl`:

```
22:24:02.368Z  assistant.message           "Let me start the heaviest scale test in the background while I update the documentation."
22:24:02.380Z  tool.execution_start        powershell  { initial_wait: 12 }   → backgrounded as shell 68
22:24:45.826Z  system.notification         kind.type="shell_completed", shellId=68, exitCode=2
22:24:45.827Z  assistant.message           messageId=2414e771-…, model=undefined, content="",
                                           toolRequests=[read_powershell {shellId:"68", delay:0}],
                                           reasoningBlocks=<absent>
22:24:45.833Z  tool.execution_complete
22:24:48.944Z  (model call fails)
22:24:48.976Z  session.error               400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

Raw error envelope and error context:

```json
{"type":"hook.start","data":{"hookType":"errorOccurred","input":{
  "error":{"name":"Error","message":"{\"message\":\"The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 3821e7d3-e76b-4688-8be6-4461e1d1e46b)\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",\"param\":null,\"code\":\"invalid_request_error\"}"},
  "errorContext":"model_call",
  "recoverable":true}}}

{"type":"session.error","data":{
  "errorType":"query",
  "message":"400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 3821e7d3-e76b-4688-8be6-4461e1d1e46b)",
  "statusCode":400}}
```

The synthetic assistant turn (note the UUID-style `toolCallId`, versus the model's `call_00_…` style):

```json
{"messageId":"2414e771-73dc-4bb2-be5b-8b1e537e8982","content":"",
 "toolRequests":[{"toolCallId":"0666f48c-0b07-413f-ae92-aaf94b4ca60f","name":"read_powershell",
                  "arguments":{"shellId":"68","delay":0},"toolTitle":"Read shell output"}]}
```

### Expected behavior

The session should continue. Thinking-mode providers require the reasoning payload on assistant turns; the runtime should satisfy that invariant for **every** assistant turn it sends, including turns it synthesizes itself (or must otherwise exclude those turns from the reasoning-required history).

### Additional context

**Provider configuration (valid, working):**

```
type: custom, authKind: api_key, baseUrl: https://api.deepseek.com, wireApi: responses, headers: {}
model: deepseek-flash  (max_prompt_tokens 840000, max_output_tokens 128000)
reasoning efforts: none | low | high | max
```

DeepSeek documents both a Responses API and thinking mode (on by default) for `deepseek-flash`.

**Why this points at the client, not the provider:**

- 142 of 162 `assistant.message` events in the session carried correct reasoning blocks: `reasoningBlocks.provider = "openai-responses"`, block `type: "reasoning"`, content `[{type:"reasoning_text", …}]`, plus `encrypted_content`.
- 20 assistant turns had no reasoning block. 18 were ordinary model turns; **1 was the model-less synthetic turn above** — and the failure landed on the very next model call.
- Same provider/model serviced 160+ other calls in this session and all other sessions without this error.
- Across 44 local sessions with this provider, there is exactly **one** `session.error` of this kind. It was also the session's only `system.notification`. Correlation is 1:1.

- The injected turn is not a model output, so it cannot carry model reasoning; sending it as a plain assistant turn breaks the API contract for thinking mode.

**Impact:** the entire session is terminated mid-task, losing in-flight work. In this case the session was implementing changes across many files.

**Workarounds used:** avoid backgrounding commands (run them in the foreground) in thinking-mode sessions; set the model's reasoning effort to `none` to sidestep the passback requirement.

**Suggested direction:** when the runtime injects a synthetic assistant turn (e.g. `read_powershell` after `shell_completed`), either attach whatever reasoning payload the provider requires, or mark it so it is not presented to thinking-mode providers as a reasoning-bearing assistant turn (e.g. keep it out of the reasoning-required history, or fold the shell output into the following user/tool message).

**Related observation (possibly a separate issue):** the same provider also produced two genuine context-length 400s in an earlier session — `you requested 1049487 tokens (921487 in the messages, 128000 in the completion)` against a 1,048,576-token context — while `max_prompt_tokens` was configured as 840000. That suggests the app-side prompt budget does not reserve enough headroom for its own token estimation error. Happy to file separately if useful.

Subagents constantly and repeatedly request permissions in interactive mode

If your operation generates subagents to do some work, and those subagents require permissions, then the subagents will constantly request permissions at a high rate.

Have the subagents inherit permissions of the main agent.  Then have the main agent figure out what permissions the subagents require, and ask for permissions once. issues.title: CLI: follow-up to an idle background agent is delayed by minutes to hours while its status shows "running"
issues.body:
> _Filed with the help of GitHub Copilot CLI (model: Claude Opus 5.5). Root-cause analysis and any proposed fix were AI-assisted and human-reviewed before filing._

---

### Summary

`write_agent` behaves very differently depending on the background agent's state:

- **Steering a running agent works.** The steer took effect 12 s after `write_agent` returned
  (23 s after the call; the agent was finishing a 15 s sleep).
- **A follow-up to an idle agent** (its turn has finished) is reported as delivered, but the new
  turn starts minutes to hours later: 6.5 and 9.2 min for two trivial repro agents, about 8.5 h
  in a long, busy session. Meanwhile `read_agent` reports `status: running` with no new turn.
- **There is no cancel/stop operation** for background agents; a stalled one stays `running`.

### Impact

- Coordinator workflows that give an idle agent its next step stall for minutes to hours, with no
  error and no timeout.
- A queued agent looks exactly like a busy one: `status: running`, with no tool-call count or a
  stale one from the previous turn. Even a "stop" sent with `write_agent` waits behind the delay.
- Workaround: never send follow-ups to idle agents; start a fresh one-shot agent with full context.

### Root cause (observed/suspected)

`read_agent` shows the idle state and the final answer in real time. Follow-up dispatch instead
appears to follow the session event stream, which trails real time for background agents:

1. **Observed:** an agent's events (messages, tool calls, `subagent.completed`) are recorded
   minutes to hours late: 5-10 min in the repro, 6-9 h in the long session. The lag differs per
   agent: during the repro, the long-session agent in the same session was still hours behind.
2. **Observed:** in all three cases, the queued follow-up's `user.message` was recorded 0.4-3 s
   after the previous turn's late `subagent.completed`.
3. **Observed:** `read_agent`'s `tool_calls_completed` equalled the number of the previous turn's
   tool calls recorded in the lagging stream at that moment (9 of 13).
4. **Suspected:** a queued follow-up is dispatched only once the previous turn's completion drains
   through that stream, not when the agent goes idle. Steering bypasses this path.

### Log signature / evidence

Local times. Event times are as recorded in `events.jsonl`; first actions (file writes, `Get-Date`) are ground truth.

| | Agent A (steered, then follow-up) | Agent B (follow-up only) |
|---|---|---|
| Previous turn | 13 tool calls; last write 04:27:26 | text-only reply, 0 tool calls |
| `read_agent` shows `idle` | 04:30:31 | 04:23:07 |
| Follow-up sent (`write_agent`: "Message delivered") | 04:30:44 | 04:23:30 |
| `read_agent` while waiting | `status: running, ... total_turns: 1, tool_calls_completed: 9` | `status: running, ... total_turns: 1` (timed out at 04:26 and 04:29) |
| Previous turn's `subagent.completed` recorded | 04:36:52.1 | 04:32:33.7 |
| Follow-up `user.message` / `assistant.turn_start` | 04:36:52.5 / 04:36:55.8 | 04:32:35.5 / 04:32:36.9 |
| First follow-up action | 04:37:13 (**+6.5 min**) | 04:32:43 (**+9.2 min**) |

Also from the repro: the steer took effect at 04:23:05, but its `user.message` was recorded at
04:28:30; A's first tool call (it wrote at 04:21:33) was recorded at 04:26:30. B's turn reports
`durationMs: 624022` in `subagent.completed`, yet `read_agent` showed it done within 170 s of launch.

Long, busy session (one general-purpose background agent):

- It finished a 183-tool-call turn (last file change 21:48; `read_agent` showed `idle` at 22:07).
  A follow-up asking for more work was sent at 22:08.
- `read_agent` at 22:13 and 22:15: `status: running, ... total_turns: 1, tool_calls_completed: 22`.
- At 22:37 a second `write_agent` told it to stop and reply with one word; it returned `delivered, task_status=running`.
- At 06:41 the next day the previous turn's `subagent.completed` was recorded. The follow-up
  started 3 s later and the stop message 11 s after that, so the agent replied "stopped" and did
  no work. The follow-up had waited about 8.5 h.

### Steps to reproduce (ISOLATED)

Everything writes only to a throwaway folder, shown as `<scratch>`.

1. In an interactive session, have the main agent start two general-purpose background agents:
   - **A:** "Make 12 separate shell calls. Each runs `Start-Sleep 15`, then appends
     `<HH:mm:ss> step <n>` to `<scratch>\steer.txt`. Then reply `steer done`."
   - **B:** any trivial task that ends with a text-only reply.
2. While A is still looping, steer it with `write_agent`: "Append `<HH:mm:ss> ack` to
   `<scratch>\ack.txt`, then continue." `ack.txt` appears about 12 s after `write_agent` returns.
3. Once `read_agent` shows B `idle`, send it a follow-up: "Make three separate shell calls running
   `Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss'`, then reply `turn1 done` plus the times."
4. Once A is `idle`, send it a follow-up: "Make two separate shell calls, each appending
   `<HH:mm:ss> turn1 call <n>` to `<scratch>\turn1.txt`, then reply `turn1 done`."
5. Poll `read_agent` and note when each follow-up's first action happens.
   - **Expected:** both follow-ups start within seconds, like the steer.
   - **Actual:** both show `running` with no new turn, then start after 9.2 min (B) and 6.5 min
     (A), each right after its previous turn's `subagent.completed` is recorded.

**Conditions:** the tasks were isolated, but the session was not idle. It was long-running, with
28 idle background agents and five others `running`: three actively working, and two that had
shown `running` for hours (one is the long-session agent above). The hooks listed under
Environment were active. Not yet confirmed in a fresh, otherwise idle session.

### Proposed fix (optional)

1. **Deliver a queued follow-up as soon as the agent is idle** (the state `read_agent` already
   reports), and emit `subagent.completed` when the turn actually ends.
2. **Report the real state:** "queued, not started" (with its age) instead of `running`, without
   the previous turn's tool-call count.
3. **Add a cancel/stop operation for background agents** that does not depend on message delivery.

### Related

- github/copilot-cli#3350: background agents stay `running` with no completion notice. The late
  `subagent.completed` described here may be the same mechanism.
- github/copilot-cli#4101: `write_agent` to an idle agent blocks the caller. Here it returns at
  once, but the agent's next turn starts late.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI `1.0.96-2`
- Windows, x64
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5 for the main session; background agents were `general-purpose`, with no
  model override
- `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` hooks configured; they also fire for background-agent tool calls

issues.title: macOS sandbox blocks Gradle daemon connection despite local networking being allowed

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Gradle cannot execute even an offline `help` task inside the Copilot CLI macOS sandbox when outbound and local networking are configured as allowed.

The Gradle daemon starts successfully and listens on localhost, but the Gradle client cannot connect to it:

```text
java.net.SocketException: Operation not permitted
```

The identical command succeeds with the Copilot sandbox disabled. Restarting Copilot with the sandbox enabled does not resolve the failure.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI `1.0.95`; also observed on `1.0.93`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, enable the Copilot CLI sandbox and allow both outbound and local networking. The configured network settings are:

   ```json
   {
     "allowOutbound": true,
     "allowLocalNetwork": true,
     "allowedHosts": [],
     "blockedHosts": []
   }
   ```

   `/sandbox policy` reports outbound and local networking as allowed.

2. In a Gradle 9.1.0 wrapper project with Java 21 selected, ask Copilot to execute:

   ```bash
   ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --console=plain --stacktrace help
   ```

3. Gradle launches a single-use daemon to honor the project's JVM settings. The daemon binds a localhost port, but the client connection fails with `Operation not permitted`, before any task executes.

4. Disable the Copilot sandbox and repeat the identical command. It succeeds, executing only `help`.

### Expected behavior

When local networking is explicitly allowed, Gradle should be able to connect to its localhost daemon.

If that setting intentionally excludes host-loopback connections, the policy display should make this distinction clear and document a supported way to permit the required connection without disabling the entire sandbox.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64; Gradle wrapper `9.1.0`; Java Amazon Corretto `21.0.6.7.1`.

The command uses offline mode, so dependency downloads are not involved. `--no-daemon` still launches a single-use daemon in this project.

**Kernel-confirmed denial**

In one sandbox-enabled run, the daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:53774`. The macOS kernel log recorded:

```text
Sandbox: java(5913) deny(1) network-outbound remote:*:53774
```

**Effective policy from a separate failing run**

Copilot's debug log identified the generated policy used for the command. Its network section was:

```json
{
  "network": {
    "egress": {
      "default": "deny"
    },
    "ingress": {
      "default": "allow",
      "hostLoopback": "deny"
    },
    "runtimeConfig": {
      "networkProxy": "http://127.0.0.1:55437"
    }
  }
}
```

In that run, the Gradle daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:55438`, not the proxy port `55437`.

This appears consistent with the client being denied a direct host-loopback connection despite `allowLocalNetwork: true`. Gradle's daemon protocol uses raw TCP, so the HTTP proxy cannot carry that connection.

Please investigate whether `allowLocalNetwork` is being mapped correctly to the effective macOS policy, or whether a separate supported host-loopback permission is required.

**Related reports**

- [github/copilot-cli#4854](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4854): a Windows `/sandbox policy` display issue. Unlike that report, the display here says networking is allowed, while the generated policy and kernel denial demonstrate an actual blocked connection.
- [github/copilot-cli#4516](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4516): JVM filesystem-grant failures on macOS, with a recent comment also describing remote-repository/proxy problems. This report concerns the local Gradle daemon connection, without dependency downloads.

Only sanitized excerpts are included here; no project source, credentials, or full conversation/debug logs are attached.

labels.name: area:context-memory

type.name: Feature

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

When using GitHub Copilot CLI with the Claude Sonnet model, there is no visible optimization for Anthropic's prompt caching feature. For long system prompts or repeated context (e.g., large codebases, long instruction blocks), each request re-processes the same tokens, leading to higher latency and unnecessary token usage. 

### Proposed solution

Leverage Anthropic's prompt caching API (cache_control breakpoints) for static portions of the prompt — such as system instructions, repo context, and tool definitions. This would:
   - Reduce time-to-first-token for follow-up turns in the same session
   - Lower API costs by reusing cached prefixes (cached tokens are ~90% cheaper)
   - Improve responsiveness for users working in large codebases

### Example prompts or workflows

Leverage Anthropic's prompt caching API (cache_control breakpoints) for static portions of the prompt — such as system instructions, repo context, and tool definitions. Specifically:
1. **Cache TTL configuration**: Allow users to configure the cache TTL via a settings option — choosing between the default 5-minute TTL or an extended 1-hour TTL (supported by Anthropic's API), suitable for long working sessions.
2. **Cache visibility CLI command**: Add a command (e.g., `copilot cache status`) to display per-turn cache hit/miss stats using the usage fields already returned by Anthropic's API (`cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`), helping users understand caching efficiency and debug unexpected misses. 

Benefits: 
- Reduce time-to-first-token for repeated context in long sessions
- Lower API costs (cached tokens are ~90% cheaper)
- Give power users transparency and control over caching behavior

### Additional context

1. A user runs `copilot cache status` after a multi-turn session and sees that 80% of system prompt tokens were served from cache, confirming cost savings.
2. A user sets cache TTL to 1 hour in config (`copilot config set cache-ttl 1h`) to avoid cache expiry during a long debugging session on a large codebase.
3. A developer asks repeated questions about the same large file — cache hits on the file context reduce response latency from ~3s to ~0.5s after the first turn.
4. A user notices cache misses on every turn via `copilot cache status` and realizes their dynamic timestamp in the system prompt is breaking the cache prefix.
5. A team configures 1h TTL in a shared `.copilot/config` to optimize CI/CD pipelines where the same repo context is queried repeatedly within an hour.

issues.title: Sandbox RW path grants not honored by JVM processes spawned from Copilot CLI

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

### Summary

Sandbox path RW grants configured via /sandbox (e.g. ~/.m2/repository) are not honored by JVM/Java processes, even though the same path is fully writable for plain shell commands. Any Java-based tool (Maven, javac-compiled programs, etc.) fails with Operation not permitted on file/directory writes under a granted path, blocking real-world workflows like mvn clean compile.

### Environment

• CLI version: 1.0.80
• OS: macOS (Darwin), aarch64
• Granted sandbox path: ~/.m2/repository (Read/Write)

### Real-world impact

Running mvn clean compile in a multi-module Maven project fails identically — both the cyclonedx-maven-plugin and Maven core's own DefaultTrackingFileManager/DefaultUpdateCheckManager (writing resolver-status.properties for resolved dependency metadata under ~/.m2/repository/...) throw the same FileSystemException: Operation not permitted, even though the parent directories were freshly, successfully created by shell mkdir moments earlier in the same session.

### Suspected root cause

The sandbox's file-access enforcement appears to differ by process/executable type rather than purely by path: shell built-ins (touch, mkdir) inherit the granted RW access, but JVM processes (java, and therefore javac, mvn) invoking sun.nio.fs.UnixFileSystemProvider (NIO FileChannel.open/Files.createDirectory) are denied on the identical path/grant.

### Affected version

1.0.80

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In /sandbox, confirm ~/.m2/repository (or any path) is granted Read/Write.
2. From the CLI's shell tool, confirm plain shell operations succeed on that path:
   mkdir -p ~/.m2/repository/zz-test-dir && echo OK   # succeeds
   touch ~/.m2/repository/zz-test-dir/file.txt && echo OK  # succeeds
3. Compile and run a minimal Java program that writes a file under the same granted path via NIO:
   ```shell
    mkdir -p ~/.m2/repository/zz-test-dir
    ```

   ```java
   import java.nio.channels.FileChannel;
   import java.nio.file.*;
   
   import static java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption.*;
   
   public class WriteTest {
       public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
           Path p = Paths.get(System.getProperty("user.home") + "/.m2/repository/zz-test-dir/javatest.properties");
           try (FileChannel ch = FileChannel.open(p, CREATE, WRITE)) {
               System.out.println("JAVA WRITE OK");
           }
       }
   }
   ```
   
   ```shell
   javac WriteTest.java && java WriteTest
   ```
4.  Actual result:
   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.nio.file.FileSystemException: .../zz-test-dir/javatest.properties: Operation not permitted
      at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixFileSystemProvider.newFileChannel
      at java.base/java.nio.channels.FileChannel.open
      at WriteTest.main(WriteTest.java:7)
   ```

### Expected behavior

"JAVA WRITE OK" printed.

### Additional context

_No response_

### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

When returning to a long-running Copilot CLI session after a break (e.g., coming back to the terminal after a few hours), there's no way to see **when** each message was sent. The conversation reads as a flat transcript with no time context.

This makes it hard to:
- Know when you last interacted with the session
- Understand the pacing of a conversation (was that exchange 5 minutes ago or 5 hours ago?)
- Orient yourself when resuming after a gap

The agent already receives `<current_datetime>` with each user message, so the data exists — it's just not displayed.

### Proposed solution

Show a **timestamp** next to each user and assistant message in the terminal UI. Something like:

```
[07:23] > How does the G502 compare to the G502 X?

[07:23] The G502 X is essentially a modernised rebuild...

[13:42] > I just came back — when was my last message?
```

Options to consider:
- **Relative timestamps** for recent messages ("2m ago"), absolute for older ones ("07:23")
- **Gap indicators** — when there's a long gap between messages (e.g., >30 min), show a separator: `--- 6 hours later ---`
- **Configurable** — a setting in config.json to enable/disable, or choose format (relative / absolute / off)

### Example prompts or workflows

User works in a session in the morning, walks away, comes back in the afternoon. Currently they see a flat wall of text with no temporal context. With this feature they'd immediately see when the last exchange happened and how long they've been away.

### Additional context

The `<current_datetime>` tag is already injected into each user message for the agent's benefit — this is about surfacing that same information in the UI for the human.

issues.title: Headless mode exits 0 mid-task when a model response has `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` but no tool calls
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In non-interactive mode (`-p` / `--prompt-file`, `--no-ask-user`), the CLI ended a long-running agentic session after one model response that came back empty: `finish_reason` was `"tool_calls"` and the API billed 193 completion tokens, but `message.tool_calls` was missing and `content` was `null`. The CLI treated this as a normal end of the task and logged `runHeadlessMode: succeeded=true` and `exiting with code 0`, even though the agent was in the middle of driving an Android emulator and had not finished.

Because the exit was clean, our wrapper's retry logic never ran. The session's final outputs were never produced. In our case this was a GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) run, which ended with no safe outputs. We only found out after the fact.

Turn 63 response (request ID `00000-8dd40ac2-8861-4961-b4dd-12408dad56f5`), quoted from the `--log-level all` log:

```json
{
  "id": "msg_011Cg27ptWDQ938VwzsJAMAn",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "created": 1791980400,
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": null, "refusal": null },
      "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
      "logprobs": null
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 136561,
    "completion_tokens": 193,
    "total_tokens": 136754,
    "completion_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0 }
  }
}
```

The previous 62 turns all had a populated `tool_calls` array and usually `reasoning_text`. Their tool calls were bash commands about the same size as the 193 tokens here. This suggests the tool call was generated but dropped somewhere between the model and the CLI. That part may belong to the Copilot API team, but the CLI is where the silent success happens.

Right after that response, the log shows:

```
executeHeadlessDirectly completing: operation=prompt, hasError=false, taskBlocked=false, blockedExit=false, ... will return true
runHeadlessMode: operation=prompt, succeeded=true
runHeadlessMode: exiting with code 0
```

Related, but not the same: #3239 is about text-only turns ending the session. Here the response has no content at all, and its `finish_reason` contradicts its body.

### Affected version

1.0.90

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

This is not deterministic, since it depends on the API returning the malformed response. It happened once, after about 30 minutes and 62 successful turns:

1. Run `copilot --prompt-file <prompt> --no-ask-user --log-level all --log-dir <dir> --allow-tool ...` with a long multi-step task that uses `bash` and MCP tools heavily. Model: `claude-sonnet-5.5`.
2. Let a model response arrive with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, no `tool_calls` and `content: null`.
3. The CLI exits 0 straight away, with no error and no retry.

### Expected behavior

A response whose `finish_reason` is `"tool_calls"` but which has no tool calls, or an empty response with completion tokens > 0, is malformed. The CLI should treat it as a transient error: retry the request, or at least nudge the model to continue. If retries run out, headless mode should exit non-zero so automation can tell that the task stopped early.

### Additional context

- Linux x86_64 (GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner), non-interactive. No terminal emulator; the CLI was spawned by the gh-aw harness.
- Session ran 30m 23s and 63 turns: 8.9M input tokens (8.7M cached), 31K output tokens.
- Session ID: `1b556a30-bfaa-48f8-a7ab-274d386b0762`
- Request ID of the malformed response: `00000-8dd40ac2-8861-4961-b4dd-12408dad56f5`, at 2026-10-14T12:20:00Z
