### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## Summary

Add an action to copy the file name, path, or relative path directly from the **git diff review** and **file viewer** panels of the new UI.

## Motivation

Right now, when reviewing a diff or browsing a file, there's no quick way to grab the file's path. Users have to manually locate the file in a file explorer or reconstruct the path by hand, which slows down workflows like:

- Referencing a file in a commit message, PR description, or Slack/chat message.
- Pasting a path into a terminal command (`cat`, `code`, `git blame`, etc.).
- Sharing a file location with a teammate or an AI assistant.

## Proposed behavior

Add a **copy** action in both:

1. **Diff review view**: right-click context menu on the file name
2. **File viewer**: right-click context menu on the file tab.

The action should offer at least one of the following formats:

- **File name only** — e.g. `Component.tsx`
- **Relative path** — e.g. `src/components/Component.tsx`
- **Full/absolute path** — e.g. `/home/user/project/src/components/Component.tsx`

## Nice to have

- Keyboard shortcut to copy the relative path of the currently focused file.
- Visual confirmation (toast/tooltip) when the path is copied, e.g. "Copied to clipboard".

## Willingness to contribute

Happy to submit a PR for this if there's consensus on the approach / a maintainer gives the go-ahead on the general direction.

issues.title: tui: sidebar overlaps vertical tabs and auto-hide has no effect
issues.body:
## Summary

With vertical tabs enabled, the sidebar overlaps and covers the chat — the message list is obscured and can't be scrolled. Separately, the "sidebar auto hide" command has no visible effect in the TUI: after "hide sidebar" it never re-shows, and after "show sidebar" it never hides.

## Environment

- opencode version: v0.0.0-next-17292
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color; TERM_PROGRAM/COLORTERM/WT_SESSION unset
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: next
- Active plugins: opencode-mobile-use (TUI plugin `tui.tsx` provides a sidebar widget; server plugin provides `phone_*` tools)

## Reproduction

Vertical tabs + sidebar overlap:

1. Enable vertical tabs (`tabs.enabled: true`, `tabs.layout: "vertical"` / `tabs.vertical: true` in `cli.json`).
2. Open the TUI with the sidebar visible.
3. Observe the chat pane alongside the vertical tab strip.

Sidebar auto-hide command:

1. In the TUI press `Ctrl+P` and run **hide sidebar**.
2. Run **sidebar auto hide**.
3. The sidebar stays hidden — auto-hide never brings it back.
4. Run **show sidebar**, then **sidebar auto hide** again.
5. The sidebar stays on screen permanently — auto-hide never hides it.

## Expected Behavior

- Vertical tabs and the sidebar should lay out without the sidebar covering the chat; the chat should remain scrollable.
- The "sidebar auto hide" command should toggle auto-hide behavior: the sidebar hides when not in use and re-appears as needed, independent of the explicit show/hide toggle.

## Actual Behavior

- The sidebar covers the chat content when vertical tabs are enabled; the chat cannot be scrolled up or down.
- The "sidebar auto hide" command appears to do nothing — sidebar visibility only ever changes via the explicit show/hide sidebar command.

## Additional Context

- Screenshot attached showing the sidebar overlapping the chat with vertical tabs.
- Frequency: reproducible consistently in this setup.
- No workaround found: auto-hide cannot be made to work, and the overlap persists while vertical tabs are on.

prs.body:
## Summary

`opencode plugin list` reads the plugin registry without waiting for plugin activation, so on a cold location the first call can return an empty list ("No plugins found") while the configured plugins are still registering (issue #54654). Same cold-location race already fixed for `mcp.list`, `skill.list`, `agent.list`, and `model.list`.

## Change

- **`packages/server/src/handlers/plugin.ts`** — `plugin.list` now `yield* awaitPlugins` before reading the inventory, matching `model.list`.
- **`packages/protocol/src/groups/plugin.ts`** — declare `ServiceUnavailableError` on the `plugin.list` endpoint (the await can fail if activation times out).
- **`packages/client`** — regenerated so the endpoint contract carries the new error type.

## Verification

- Regression test `packages/server/test/plugin-endpoint.test.ts` registers a local plugin that only becomes available after its async setup completes. Without the await, `plugin.list` returns `[]` and the test fails; with it, the plugin is listed. `1/1` pass.

prs.title: fix(core): inherit Vercel AI Gateway virtual model metadata from a base model
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54732

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A Vercel AI Gateway virtual model (`vmc/*`) only gets `low`, `medium` and `high`. OpenCode does not know which real model the alias stands for, so it can't offer that model's levels, like `none` or `xhigh`.

This adds an optional `base` to a configured model. It works in the v1 config (`provider.*.models.*.base`) and the current one (`providers.*.models.*.base`). When the base model is in the provider's catalog, the alias starts from that model's capabilities, limits, cost and variants. The alias keeps its own `id` and `modelID`, so requests still go to the alias. Fields set in the same config entry (name, limit, cost, variants) still win.

`modelID` already reuses a catalog model, but it also changes the id that goes on the wire. An alias must keep calling its own id, so it needs its own field.

A model without `base` works as before. I did not change API routing. `vmc/*` still goes to `/v1/messages`. Multi-turn tool use on a GPT-based alias worked in my tests, so I left it.

One limit: if the catalog lists a level that the real model rejects, that level now shows for the alias too.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/config test/variant.test.ts test/v1` and `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core`. Two new tests in `test/config/provider.test.ts`: an alias keeps its id and inherits variants and limit, and a v1 config keeps its own name and limit.
- Live against the Vercel AI Gateway, with a source build and only `base` set in the config. Each request went to the alias id with native effort:

| Alias | Level | Request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vmc/daily-intelligence` (Opus) | `#xhigh` | `output_config.effort: xhigh` | 944 thinking tokens |

prs.title: fix(core): bound skill discovery and watches
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55367
Closes #45961
Closes #51080

Supersedes #55479 and #55234. Both authors are credited as co-authors on the commit.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Skill discovery globbed `{*.md,**/SKILL.md}` with symlinks followed, no depth limit and no exclusions. When a found `SKILL.md` resolved outside the watched sources, the plugin recursively watched the file's parent directory. home-manager links `SKILL.md` files straight into `/nix/store`, so that parent was the whole store: about 1.4M directories, enough to exhaust `max_user_watches`. The same glob also descends into `node_modules` and crashes on symlink cycles.

The skill and compatibility plugins now share `SkillScan.scan`, a breadth-first walk:

- A directory containing `SKILL.md` is one skill. The walk does not search inside it, so a skill's scripts, references and dependencies are never scanned and nested template `SKILL.md` files no longer load as skills.
- Directories without `SKILL.md` are grouping directories and are walked, so `skills/teams/release/SKILL.md` still loads as `release`.
- Hidden entries and `node_modules` below the source root are skipped. The root itself may be hidden, e.g. `.opencode/skills`.
- Grouping directories are visited once per canonical path, which ends symlink cycles. Several names linked to the same skill directory still load.
- The walk stops at six levels or 2000 directories and logs `skill scan truncated`.

Watches are derived from the walk:

- Source roots keep their recursive watch, now ignoring hidden entries and `node_modules`.
- A skill file whose canonical path is outside the watched roots gets a file watch on that path. For a store file, that is one non-recursive watch on the store directory, filtered by name.
- A symlinked grouping directory gets a recursive watch on its canonical path, so new skills behind it are discovered. This is skipped when the walk was truncated, because the watch would cover a tree the walk did not finish.
- The compatibility plugin now also watches content behind symlinked skills in `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`.

Behavior changes: `SKILL.md` files nested inside another skill directory, skills under hidden directories, root-level hidden `.md` files, and other root `.md` files beside a root `SKILL.md` no longer load. The skills docs describe the new rules.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core`: `bun typecheck` and `bun run test test/config` (248 pass), plus the skill, skill-discovery, tool-skill and session-skill suites (31 pass). Root `bun run check` passes.
- New tests cover: leaf skills, hidden and `node_modules` skipping, symlink cycles, a symlinked `SKILL.md` into a store (file watch only, replacement and retargeting reload), symlinked grouping directories, aliases, downloaded roots and the depth limit. Every new test fails on `dev`; the cycle test hangs until it times out.
- Ran `serve` from source on macOS with a store-style tree, a symlinked `SKILL.md`, hidden, `node_modules` and nested skills, and a symlink cycle. The only watch touching the store was the file watch on the skill target, the expected skills loaded, and the server stayed responsive.
- Confirmed against the native watcher that the ignore globs match relative to a canonical watch root, including roots under hidden directories. Recursive skill watches are always subscribed on canonical paths.
- Not measured on Linux: inotify watch counts.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(cli): shut the service down when Windows ends the session
prs.body:
On Windows, a restart or sign-out kills the background service without warning, so its registration file (`service.json`) is left behind. The next desktop launch then waits out the 5 s `spawnDelay` that `Service.ensure()` gives a registered service that hasn't answered yet, before it starts a new one.

This PR gives the service a hidden window that receives Windows' shutdown and close messages, and has the service shut down through its normal path when one arrives.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as Windows
  participant H as Hidden service window
  participant R as ServiceRegistration
  participant S as Service
  W->>H: WM_QUERYENDSESSION
  H-->>W: 1 (no action; another app can still cancel)
  W->>H: WM_ENDSESSION (wParam = TRUE)
  H->>R: delete service.json if this service owns it (synchronous)
  H->>S: open the shutdown latch
  H-->>W: 0, after which Windows may terminate the process
  Note over W,H: taskkill without /F sends WM_CLOSE, which opens the shutdown latch
```

- **Why a window:** `serve --service` is spawned detached, so it has no console. Windows sends these messages only to top-level windows, and sends nothing to a process without one.
- **Why the delete is synchronous:** Windows can terminate the process as soon as `WM_ENDSESSION` returns, so the delete can't wait for the async shutdown. It only deletes the file if the file still names this service.
- **`WM_QUERYENDSESSION`:** agreeing doesn't stop the service, so if another app cancels the shutdown the service keeps running.
- **Message pump:** Bun FFI drives the window from an unref'd 500 ms interval (`PeekMessageW` / `DispatchMessageW`), well inside Windows' 5 s hung-window limit.
- **Runtimes:** the new `#windows-shutdown` import loads the FFI version under Bun and a no-op elsewhere (Node SEA builds), the same way `@opencode/core` handles `#pty`.

```ts
// packages/cli/src/services/service-registration.ts
yield* WindowsShutdown.watch({
  close: () => runFork(options.shutdown),
  end: () => {
    Option.liftThrowable(() => readFileSync(options.file, "utf8"))().pipe(
      Option.flatMap(decodeInfoOption),
      Option.filter(owns),
      Option.flatMap(Option.liftThrowable(() => rmSync(options.file, { force: true }))),
    )
    runFork(options.shutdown)
  },
})
```

### Impact: first desktop launch after a Windows restart

Desktop 2.0.29, local service already stopped, warm disk cache, median of 3–4 launches (`bench:startup`).

| State at launch | Server spawn starts | App shell visible |
|---|---|---|
| Stale `service.json` (today, after every restart) | 5.6 s | 6.1 s |
| No `service.json` (with this PR) | 0.6 s | 1.3 s |

On one Windows machine, the desktop logs show this case on 8 of the last 16 launches: every first launch after a boot waited 5.2–7.3 s before it spawned the server.

### Not covered

- `TerminateProcess` (`taskkill /F`, `Stop-Process`), power loss and crashes still leave the file behind. A client-side check that skips the spawn delay when the registered PID no longer exists would cover those.

prs.title: fix(cli): poll install download progress instead of tracing bytes
prs.body:
The curl installer's progress bar made downloads several times slower, and much slower on machines where starting a process is slow (VMs, WSL, small cloud servers). Users noticed that `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash 2>&1 | cat` was faster, because that skips the custom bar.

**Cause:** the bar tracked progress with `curl --trace-ascii` writing into a named pipe:
- For the 85 MB darwin-arm64 package, that pipe carried a 95 MB text dump (1.35M lines), all filtered by `sed`.
- A bash loop then ran once per received chunk (about 15.8k times), starting two extra processes each time to draw the bar.
- curl had to wait on the pipe, so the download could never go faster than the shell reading it.

**Fix:** run curl in the background with `-D <headers file>`. Every 0.1s, read `content-length` from that file, get the downloaded size with `ls -ln` (busybox `wc -c` reads the whole file), and redraw the same bar. If `sleep 0.1` isn't supported, the loop falls back to `sleep 1`. The cost now depends on elapsed time, not on bytes received. This also removes the named pipe and the `sed` buffering workarounds.

| darwin-arm64, 85 MB | Wall time | CPU time |
|---|---|---|
| plain curl | 1.6s | – |
| before | 11.7s | 14.1s |
| after | 1.67s | 0.48s |

Verified under a pseudo-TTY with macOS's default bash 3.2:
- the bar output looks the same as before
- the downloaded file is byte-identical
- the temporary headers file is removed
- a failing URL still falls back to the existing `curl -#` path
- a full install into a temporary HOME runs and the binary reports `opencode v2.0.29`

The website now serves the install script from `dev` (#55587), so this reaches `opencode.ai/v2/install` after the next dev -> prod promotion.

A manual run in a real terminal (3 full installs each, alternating) averaged 4.98s with the bar and 4.98s with a no-bar variant.

prs.title: fix(core): accept snake_case oauth keys in flat MCP entries
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55335

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Flat (V1-style) `mcp.<name>` entries are decoded with the V1 config schema, which only knows camelCase OAuth keys (`clientId`, `callbackPort`, …). The V2 snake_case names the docs teach (`client_id`, `callback_port`, …) were silently dropped, so OAuth fell back to dynamic client registration and login failed against servers without a registration endpoint. The normalizer now copies recognized snake_case keys onto their camelCase counterparts before the V1 decode. When both spellings are present with different values, camelCase wins and a conflict diagnostic names the path. Keys the flat form cannot express (V2-only `auth_server_metadata_url`, or typos) now get an unsupported diagnostic instead of a silent drop.

prs.title: feat(tui): responsive diff viewer layouts
prs.body:
## Summary
The diff viewer now picks its layout from the terminal width. This replaces the old fixed 80-column panel cutoff and the tree-less middle state in full screen.

| Width | Layout |
|---|---|
| 108+ | Docked side panel (with the **Diff side panel** experiment on) |
| 88–107 | Full screen with the file tree and inset cards |
| < 88 | Full screen in the compact panel layout: no file tree, flush cards, and an `escape close` · `? see all` footer |

- **Panel → full screen:** `SESSION_PANEL_SPLIT_MIN_WIDTH = 108` is the session's preferred width (64) plus a panel at the session's minimum (44). The old cutoff of 80 left each side 40 columns, which is narrower than the session's own minimum. The viewer stays mounted across the switch, so scroll position, review count and source are kept.
- **Full → compact:** `FULL_LAYOUT_MIN_WIDTH = 88` is the tree's minimum (30) plus the insets (4) plus half of 108. Below that, the full layout's patches would be narrower than the narrowest docked panel.
- **`compact()` vs `docked()`:** `compact()` controls how the viewer renders (tree, cards, header, footer, gutter padding). `docked()` still decides where it's mounted: the background and the footer's focus hint.
- **Card gap fix:** with a zero inset, `CardGap`'s spacer still took one cell. That left a dark notch at each card's top-left corner on full screen's base background. It was there in the docked panel too, but invisible on its raised background.

## Behavior changes to note
- Docked panels switch to full screen sooner than before (below 108 columns instead of 80).
- With the experiment off, terminals narrower than 88 columns (including 80) get the compact layout. Before, they got inset cards without a tree.
- `f` (full screen toggle) stays listed in help while the host forces full screen.

## Validation
- `bun typecheck` passes. Full TUI suite: 1485 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.
- New tests:
  - A panel resize from 160 → 107 → 80 → 108 that keeps the same viewer, and keys go only to the focused pane.
  - The 88/87 full-screen boundary, including the card-gap notch. That test fails without the fix.
- Checked in OpenCode Drive at 160, 107, 88, 80 and 60 columns, with the experiment on and off.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

`opencode run` drops every event from child sessions, so what a sub-agent does is missing from a headless run's output. The loop in `run.ts` already tracked child sessions in a `Set`, but all the handlers still compared against the root `sessionID`.

This changes the set to a map of session ID to nesting depth and lets the handlers accept any session in it. Output from a child session is indented with `↳ ` (two spaces more per level), so you can tell whose output is whose. `session.error` from a child is printed, but only the root session's error sets the run's failure state, since a parent can recover from a sub-agent failure. prs.body:
## Why

`unit (windows)` failed on dev ([run 38652333300](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38652333300)) because `adds, disconnects, and reconnects MCP servers at runtime` hit Bun's 5s default timeout. Windows process startup is slow and varies (one spawn in the failing log took ~2.6s), so three sequential spawns sometimes don't fit in 5s. `manages live MCP servers entirely through scoped transforms` failed on Windows the same way in a recent PR run.

## Change

Three lifecycle tests now use the existing in-process `resourceServer({ modern: true, resources: false })` instead of spawning subprocesses:

- `adds, disconnects, and reconnects MCP servers at runtime`
- `manages live MCP servers entirely through scoped transforms`
- `serializes concurrent MCP lifecycle operations` (same 3–4 spawn pattern; hadn't failed yet)

The modern (`2026-07-28`) server is stateless, so repeated reconnects work. The default legacy server supports only one session and returns `Session not found` on reconnect. No timeouts were raised.

The stdio/subprocess behavior is still covered by its dedicated single-spawn tests (location environment spawning, close races, descendants, output schemas, prompts, timeouts).

## Verification

- `bun test test/mcp.test.ts` (78 pass)
- The three changed tests: `--rerun-each 20` gave 60/60 passes in ~0.8s total

prs.title: fix(core): disable Node fetch timeouts for provider requests
prs.body:
Fixes #26602 On Node, a provider that sends nothing for 5 minutes is disconnected with `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`, even with `headerTimeout: false`. Node's built-in fetch applies undici's default 300s `headersTimeout` and `bodyTimeout`. Bun has the same deadline, and Core already turns it off with `timeout: false`. This PR turns off the Node deadline in the same way. - **Who is affected:** the Node CLI (`opencode2-node`) and Core embedded in a Node process. Desktop 2.0.x starts the bundled Bun CLI (`opencode-cli serve --service`), the same service the TUI uses, so it already behaves correctly. - **What still limits a request:** the provider settings `headerTimeout` (default 300s), `chunkTimeout` (default 900s), and `timeout` (no default), on every runtime. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as opencode service (Node) participant P as Provider (Ollama, router, ...) S->>P: POST /v1/chat/completions Note over P: reads a long prompt, sends no bytes Note over S: 300s: undici headersTimeout fires S--xP: socket closed: UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT S->>P: retry about 2s later, same result (up to 10 retries) ``` ## Change Both provider request paths (native routes through `RequestExecutor`, AI SDK routes through `aisdk.ts`) now get their fetch from a runtime-conditioned import, like `#sqlite` and `#pty`: ```mermaid flowchart LR N[Native routes
RequestExecutor] --> R{"#runtime-fetch"} A[AI SDK routes
aisdk.ts] --> R R -->|bun| B["ambient fetch + timeout: false
(unchanged behavior)"] R -->|node| U["undici fetch + EnvHttpProxyAgent
headersTimeout: 0, bodyTimeout: 0"] R -->|workerd| W[platform fetch] ``` ```ts // packages/core/src/effect/runtime-fetch.node.ts const dispatcher = new EnvHttpProxyAgent({ headersTimeout: 0, bodyTimeout: 0 }) export function withoutRuntimeTimeouts(runtime: Fetch): Fetch { if (runtime !== globalThis.fetch) return runtime return Object.assign( (input: Parameters[0], init?: RequestInit) => input instanceof Request || init?.body instanceof FormData ? runtime(input, init) : (fetch(input, { ...init, dispatcher } as Parameters[1]) as unknown as Promise), { preconnect: runtime.preconnect }, ) } ``` - **Undici's fetch, not the built-in one:** Node 24's built-in fetch rejects an agent from undici 8 (`UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG`), so the agent is paired with undici's own fetch. - **`FormData` and `Request` keep the built-in fetch:** undici's fetch does not recognize the built-in classes. For example, it sends a built-in `FormData` as the text `[object FormData]`, which would break image and transcription uploads. - **Proxy variables:** `EnvHttpProxyAgent` honors `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY`, like Bun's fetch and Core's WebSocket transport on Node. - **Injected fetch stays in charge:** a fetch from provider settings, a host, or the test network guard is never replaced on Node. On Bun it still receives `timeout: false`. - **Bundles:** Bun and workerd do not load undici. The Node CLI bundles it through a Vite alias. Without the alias, Vite (which runs under Bun, where `undici` is a builtin) leaves it external and the executable fails at startup with `Cannot find package 'undici'`. ## Before and after A real V2 server and an OpenAI-compatible provider that waits 330s before it sends response headers, with `headerTimeout: false`: | Service runtime | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Bun (Desktop 2.0.29, TUI) | Answered after 330s | Answered after 330s | | Node 26.4 (`opencode2-node`) | Disconnected after 305s: `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT: Headers Timeout Error`, then retried | Answered after 330s | With `headerTimeout: 20000` and a 60s provider delay, patched Node still ends the request after 20s with `Timed out waiting for response headers`. ## Relation to #54793 #54793 by @Yedigaryan found the same cause. This PR differs in three places: - Undici is loaded only under the `node` condition, so it stays out of the Bun and workerd graphs (the review note on #54793). - `FormData` and `Request` inputs keep the built-in fetch. - The Node CLI bundle includes undici; otherwise the executable cannot start. --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Public API: On Node, provider requests now honour HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY, matching Bun (behaviour change, no API surface change)

prs.title: fix(app): keep project settings open when the project folder is missing
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Crash:** a deleted project folder replaced the whole window with `LocationNotFoundError` when you opened project Settings → Extensions.
- **Restart loop:** the desktop app reopens the last settings URL, so Restart showed the same error.
- **Cause:** `projectPluginList` fetched `plugin.list({ location })` without a catch. Solid's `resource.latest` rethrows a failed fetch, and no `ErrorBoundary` sat between settings and the app root.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Settings → project → Extensions"] --> B["plugin.list({ location })"]
  B -->|folder deleted| C["404 LocationNotFoundError"]
  C --> D["projectPluginList.latest rethrows"]
  D --> E["root ErrorBoundary: full-window error page"]
  E -->|"Restart reopens /settings?…&tab=extensions"| A
```

## Changes

- **Missing-folder notice:** `ProjectFolderMissing` reads `useWorkspaceLocation().missing` and shows the folder path on the project General and Extensions pages.
- **Settings lists:** `projectPluginList`, `globalPluginList`, `mcpList` and `pluginList` fall back to an empty list when the request fails.
- **Scoped error boundaries:**
  - Settings content (`SettingsNavigation`): a failed page keeps the settings navigation, and choosing another page renders it again.
  - New-session route: a failed draft shows the error page inside its panel, as the session route already does.
- **Regression test:** `settings.spec.ts` opens a project's saved Extensions URL while every request for its folder returns `LocationNotFoundError`. The new `mockMissingLocation` helper sets up that response.

```tsx
const [projectPluginList] = createResource(
  () => (serverSDK.connection.status() === "connected" ? directorySDK().directory : undefined),
  (directory) =>
    serverSDK.api.plugin
      .list({ location: { directory } })
      .then((result) => result.data)
      .catch(() => []),
  { initialValue: [] },
)
```

## Screenshots

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Whole window replaced by LocationNotFoundError](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab0e03f6-1925-4c7f-9090-9692bf12277f) | ![Extensions page with a Project folder not found notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b83da791-ee72-46dd-ad70-d6b7c93c517e) |

Containment: a settings page that still throws (catch removed for this demo):

- The scoped boundaries render `ErrorPage`, which has a Report button, as the session route does. Unlike the root boundary, they do not send the error to Sentry automatically.

prs.title: fix(core): filter denied providers from the integration registry
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54145

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`enabled_providers` (and the `provider.use` deny statements it normalizes to) trims the provider catalog, but `/connect` reads a different registry: the integrations behind `integration.list`. So a machine locked to one custom provider still offered OpenCode Console, openai, github-copilot, amazon-bedrock, azure, Cloudflare, digitalocean and gitlab in the connect dialog.

A provider and the integration it connects through are the same identity. The catalog that defines a provider now records that identity on the integration it registers (`Integration.markProvider`, called from `plugin/models-dev.ts` and `config/plugin/provider.ts`), and the terminal policy transform removes an integration whose marker a `provider.use` statement denies. The filter reads the policy statements itself rather than a set another catalog produced, because the two catalogs fold independently: under `State.batch` each folds lazily on its own read, so a denied provider is already gone from the provider catalog by the time the integration catalog is folded.

Integrations registered under their own ID, such as the OAuth integration a remote MCP server registers (`mcp_<hash>`), carry no marker and stay governed by `integration.use`, so a provider allowlist does not hide MCP servers from the dialog.

`specs/v2/provider-policy.md` gains the same statement in the "Applying Provider Policy" section. The spec also lists a `hosted:<integration ID>` resource of `integration.use` that no code consumes yet; this change keys off `provider.use`, because that is what the legacy lists migrate to. Say the word if the `integration.use` spelling is the intended surface and I will switch.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/core/test/config/policy.test.ts` activates the models.dev and policy plugins inside a single `State.batch` — the shape real plugin activation uses — and asserts on `Integration.Service.list()`, the call `/api/integration` serves to `/connect`: a wildcard deny with one allow leaves only the allowed provider's integration, an `mcp_*` integration stays, lifting the deny restores the integration, and a config change reaches the registry without a manual reload. Deleting the `markProvider` call from `plugin/models-dev.ts` makes the batch case fail, so it exercises the mechanism instead of passing vacuously. `packages/core/test/fixture/policy.ts` needed an `integration` stub, because the shared host fake `die`s on services a plugin does not declare.

I ran `bun test` under bun 1.4.2 over `test/config`, `test/plugin` and `test/integration.test.ts`. The failing set is identical to a baseline run taken with this change stashed (21 pre-existing environment and directory-watch failures), so nothing here regresses them. `tsgo -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json` exits 0, and oxlint reports nothing on the changed files.

I verified this at the registry the dialog reads rather than by driving the TUI, so the drive script in #54145 is still the end-to-end check if you want the dialog itself on camera.

### Screenshots / recordings

_No UI change in this repository; the dialog renders whatever the registry lists._

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

issues.title: powershell tool falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh 7 is the Microsoft Store build

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store (7.6.7, no MSI), the built-in `powershell` tool runs Windows PowerShell 5.1.

`getPowerShellConfig` in `utils/shell.js` finds pwsh with `where pwsh.exe` and checks the first hit with `fs.existsSync`. The Store build puts an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that alias `existsSync` is false and `statSync` throws EACCES, while `lstatSync`, `accessSync`, and spawning it all work. So the check rejects a working pwsh and silently falls back to `powershell.exe`.

Windows 11 Pro 26300, Node 26.8.1, managed install. The resolver is identical in 1.0.0 and 1.2.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Only the Store PowerShell 7 installed (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell`), no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`.
2. `pi -ne -p -t +powershell,-bash "Use the powershell tool to run: $PSVersionTable.PSEdition"` → `Desktop`.
3. Resolver directly:
   ```
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/shell.js').then(m=>console.log(m.getPowerShellConfig().shell))"
   ```
   → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
4. `where pwsh.exe` → the WindowsApps alias. On that path: `fs.existsSync` → `false`, `fs.statSync` → EACCES, `fs.lstatSync` → 85-byte reparse point, `spawnSync` → prints `Core`.

### Expected behavior

pwsh 7 is used, as `docs/windows.md` says ("runs commands through pwsh.exe when available"). Microsoft is steering users to the Store/MSIX build and retiring the MSI, so more Windows users will hit this.

Fix is small: in the Windows branch of `findExecutableOnPath`, verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` or `fs.accessSync` instead of `existsSync`, or trust `where` the way the Unix branch trusts `which`. Workaround I use today: `$env:Path = "$PSHOME;$env:Path"` before starting pi, so the real package folder comes first (a user-PATH entry alone is not enough from pwsh, because the Store build prepends its alias folder to PATH at startup). Happy to send a PR if you want one.

Related: #8582 has the same symptom from a different cause (a `where` timeout under load); this one is deterministic on an idle machine.

### Version

1.2.0

### What happened?

When calling newer Gemini reasoning models via Google Vertex AI (such as `gemini-4-argon`), the request immediately fails with HTTP 400:

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "Thinking budget is not supported for this model. Use thinking level instead. See https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking for details.",
  "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
}
Google Vertex AI disallows the legacy numeric thinkingBudget parameter for newer generation models, requiring discrete thinkingLevel (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) instead, or omitting thinkingConfig completely when thinking is disabled.

In Pi (v1.2.0), two issues cause this failure:

usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model) in google-shared.ts uses regex /gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-(?:pro|flash)/ which misses gemini-4 models (and custom models defining thinkingLevelMap). This causes the adapter to fall back to getGoogleBudget() and inject a numeric thinkingBudget.
getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model) returns { thinkingBudget: 0 } when fallback === "off", which also triggers the 400 rejection even when thinking is turned off.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a GCP project with Vertex AI access and set the location to `global`:
   export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="<your-gcp-project-id>"
   export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION="global"
2. Run Pi with gemini-4-argon and any thinking level (or default):
    pi --provider google-vertex --model gemini-4-argon --thinking low -p "Say hi"
3. Actual behavior: Request fails with HTTP 400: Thinking budget is not supported for this model. Use thinking level instead.

### Expected behavior

Request should succeed by passing thinkingLevel: "LOW" (or omitting thinkingConfig when thinking is off) instead of thinkingBudget.

1.2.0

issues.title: Feature request: video input support (mirrors the image pipeline)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Feature request: video input support

### What

Add end-to-end **video input** to Pi, mirroring the existing image pipeline.

Pi already reads images end-to-end: `@path` attaches them, the `read` tool
returns them, they flow through the agent / session / both OpenAI-compatible
wire formats, and models that can't see images get a graceful text placeholder.
This request adds the same path for video, so a user can do:

```
pi @clip.mp4 "What number is on the card?"
```

and a video-capable local model answers from the clip.

### Why

Pi is used heavily with **self-hosted** models (llama.cpp, Strata, vLLM).
Several of those endpoints can read video, but there is no way to get a video
into Pi's context today — no `@path` sniffing, no `read`-tool path, no
serializer support, no input-modality flag. The image path was added with the
exact shape this would need; video is the natural next modality.

### OpenAI's official API has no video input item

To be clear about scope: the stable `openai` SDK exposes exactly two media
input types — `input_image` and `input_file` (the latter for documents/audio) —
and **zero** `input_video` / `video_url`. So there is no official OpenAI video
wire format to diverge from. This feature targets the **self-hosted endpoints
that actually read video** (llama.cpp, Strata, vLLM).

### Proposed design (mirrors images, gated two ways)

- **Types**: `VideoContent`, `MediaContent = ImageContent | VideoContent`, a
  `"video"` input modality, and a per-endpoint `compat.videoPartFormat`
  (`input_video` | `video_url`, default `input_video`).
- **Wire formats**: `openai-completions` and `openai-responses` serialize video
  to the correct part (user content and tool-result content).
- **File input**: `@path` sniffs video extensions; the `read` tool returns
  videos up to 50 MB as base64.
- **Plumbing**: videos flow through the agent, `AgentSession`, the extension
  runner, compaction token estimation, and the RPC client/mode.
- **Downgrade**: `transform-messages` drops video to a text placeholder for
  models without video input, exactly like images today.
- **Surfaces**: `list-models` gains a `videos` column; render utils and the
  anthropic/bedrock serializers handle the new content type.

### The `videoPartFormat` split (why the flag exists)

Self-hosted servers disagree on the part, and neither is a superset of the
other:

- **llama.cpp** (and Strata) take llama.cpp's `input_video` part:
  `{ "type": "input_video", "input_video": { "data": "<base64>" } }`.
- **vLLM** (and forks) reject `input_video` outright with
  `400 {"error":"Unexpected item type in content."}` and instead take
  `video_url` with a `data:` URL, when launched with
  `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":64,"video":64}'`.

`videoPartFormat` selects the spelling per endpoint. Default is `input_video`
because llama.cpp's own server is the most common self-hosted video endpoint;
vLLM is the outlier that opts in with the flag.

### Code is ready

I have a working implementation, tested and documented, on a clean base of
`main`. It's a focused, additive change that touches only the image-path
surfaces plus a new `video` modality. It is currently held at
[#10961](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10961) (auto-closed pending
approval), which I'm happy to reopen or resubmit once this is approved.

Summary of the diff: ~50 files, +1013/-204.

- 11 new test cases (completions + responses wire, read tool, list-models), all
  passing.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; full `ai` / `coding-agent` suites green (remaining
  failures are pre-existing on base, unrelated to video).
- Docs: `cli.md`, `llama-cpp.md` (new "Video input" section), `models.md`
  (new "Send video to a vLLM-style endpoint" section), and regenerated
  `models.schema.json`.

### One open question

Is `input_video` the right **default**, or should the default be `video_url`?
I defaulted to `input_video` (llama.cpp/Strata convention); vLLM needs the
opt-in flag. Happy to flip it if you'd prefer the other default.

issues.title: add AgentSession.continue() method to run the post-run loop

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add `AgentSession.continue()` method to continue the current transcript and go through the same post-run loop as `prompt()`: auto-retry, overflow compaction and queued messages.

### Why?

We run pi as steps in Vercel Workflows, so an agent can run longer than one function call (vercel times out at 800s). Each step runs a time slice of the turn, when a slice ends we abort, save the session and the next step continues in a fresh function.

To continue we call `session.agent.continue()` but retry and compaction only run in `_runAgentPrompt` loop. A context overflow in any step after the first would not compact. `prompt("")` works around it but adds an empty user message.

### How?

`_runAgentPrompt` already handles the loop, so continuing is one line plus a public method:

```
  await (messages === undefined ? this.agent.continue() :
  this.agent.prompt(messages));

  async continue() {
      await this._runAgentPrompt(undefined);
  }
```

Happy to put a PR together for this, already running this as a patch locally.

issues.title:
parseStreamingJson silently prefix-salvages final tool-call
arguments, corrupting tool calls without any diagnostic
issues.body:
**Package:** `@earendil-works/pi-ai` (observed on 1.0.4; code lives in `packages/ai`)
**API path:** `openai-responses` (`processResponsesStream`)

## What happened

In a live agent session, the model emitted a `cad_ui` tool call whose full argument string failed strict JSON parsing at `response.output_item.done`. `parseStreamingJson` (`dist/utils/json-parse.js:90-109`) fell back to `repairJson`, then to `partial-json`, whose object parser returns **the keys parsed so far** when any later value throws. The final tool call therefore arrived as:

```json
{"action":"apply"}
```

— the first key of what the model actually sent (an `actions` array was constructed and intended, per the model's visible reasoning). `processResponsesStream` (`dist/api/openai-responses-shared.js:611-619`) then assigns the salvaged fragment as the call's final arguments and emits `toolcall_end` with **no decode-failure diagnostic**.

## Reproduction (verified against 1.0.4)

```js
import { parseStreamingJson } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/json-parse.js';

// Stream cut after the first value — what output_item.done hands the decoder:
parseStreamingJson('{"kind":"viewport.seekAnimation",');
// => { kind: 'viewport.seekAnimation' }        // silent prefix salvage

// Stream cut mid-string-value — partial-json CLOSES the truncated string:
parseStreamingJson('{"kind":"viewport.seekAnimation","clipId":"clip-fl');
// => { kind: 'viewport.seekAnimation', clipId: 'clip-fl' }  // fabricated value
```

No error, no warning, no flag: the decoder manufactures arguments the model never sent, and downstream validation passes because the fragment is a valid subset of the intended schema.

## Live-session evidence: an 18-call blind retry loop

A transcript export from the affected session (downstream app: PartMode, a browser CAD agent using `@flue/runtime` over `pi-agent-core`/`pi-ai`, OpenAI-compatible `openai-responses` streaming) shows the same signature at scale:

- **18 consecutive `cad_ui` apply calls** each carried animation actions shaped `{"kind":"viewport.seekAnimation"}` (or `playAnimation`/`pauseAnimation`) — the kind key parsed before the cut, everything after silently dropped.
- **16 of them** received the consuming app's "That animation clip no longer exists" — a semantically misleading error, because the real problem was that `clipId`/`time` never arrived.
- The model's visible reasoning repeatedly states it constructed the full argument object and hypothesizes harness serialization bugs — from its side it sent complete arguments, so it retried **the identical call** for ~13 minutes (2026-10-13, timestamps 16:24–16:37), never converging.

A consumer cannot self-correct: the salvage is invisible at every later layer, and the resulting validation error contradicts the model's own output.

## Why silent salvage is wrong for *final* arguments

Prefix salvage is exactly right **during** streaming (partial `toolcall_delta` events are genuinely incomplete). But at `output_item.done` the buffer is final: if strict parsing fails there, the model's emission was malformed, and salvaging a prefix manufactures arguments the model never chose to send.

Note the mid-string case is arguably worse than the between-keys case: `partial-json` **closes the truncated string value**, fabricating a complete value (e.g. `clipId: "clip-fl"`) that passes downstream existence checks as a plausible-but-wrong id.

## Suggested fix (either or both)

1. At `output_item.done`, if strict `JSON.parse` fails, **fail loudly**: surface a stream error or an `isError` tool call rather than assigning the salvage.
2. Or attach a diagnostic to the tool call — e.g. `decodeTruncated: true` (plus the failure reason and, ideally, whether a string value was closed by the parser) — so consumers can distinguish "model sent this" from "decoder salvaged this prefix".

## Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-ai@1.0.4` (bundled for browser via Bun.build)
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible `openai-responses` streaming
- The trigger requires the model to emit invalid JSON as its complete final argument string — rare, but when it happens the corruption is silent, the agent-visible error is misleading, and the loop is non-converging.

## Downstream evidence artifacts

The consuming app has since shipped two downstream guards against this signature (a required-field echo naming the received keys, and batch recipe validation) — both exist only because the salvage is silent. Transcript excerpt and repro available on request.

issues.title: cacheWarming "idle" stops silently once an extension handles turn_end and the context holds a custom or compaction message

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What happened?**
With `cacheWarming: "idle"`, the idle warm never fires in our sessions: 507 `cache_warming_decision` events since September, all at `continuationProbability: 1`, none at 0.15. `/session` shows `Inactive (conversation context changed)` right after the run settles.

Cause: `cacheContextIsCurrent` (`core/sdk.js:214-222`) checks each captured message by object identity. When any extension has a `turn_end` handler, `_dispatchTurnEndBoundary` goes on to `_commitBoundaryDrafts`, which calls `_refreshFinalizedContext()` even with no drafts (`core/agent-session.js:492`, `:636`). `sessionEntryToContextMessages` (`core/session-manager.js:179-188`) builds new objects for `custom_message`, `branch_summary` and `compaction` entries on every projection. So `validateRun()` stops the warmer before any decision is emitted. Without a `turn_end` handler, idle warming works.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. `note.ts`: `pi.registerCommand("note", { handler: async () => pi.sendMessage({ customType: "n", content: "x", display: true }) })` plus `pi.on("turn_end", () => {})`.
2. `pi -ne -e note.ts` on an Anthropic model, `cacheWarming: "idle"`. Run `/note`, send one prompt, wait for it to settle.
3. `/session` → `Cache Warming … Inactive (conversation context changed)`.
4. Remove the `turn_end` line → `Decision in 4m …`, and the idle decision fires.

**Expected behavior**
The idle phase compares the prefix the provider saw: compare entry ids, or memoise the projected message per entry (entries don't change after append).

**Version**
1.2.0, Linux. Same symptom as https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10700; related to https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10515.

issues.title: Report session cwd to the terminal via OSC 7

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
> 🤖 **AI-assisted:** drafted with an LLM and reviewed by me.

### What do you want to change?

Report the session cwd to the terminal via OSC 7 (`ESC ] 7 ; file://<host><cwd> BEL`) whenever Pi sets the terminal title for a session, and report the launch directory again when Pi exits.

### Why?

When the session cwd changes (`/resume` into another project, or `switchSession()` from an extension), Pi's tools use the new directory, but the terminal still holds the parent shell's. Manually opened tabs and splits in terminals that track OSC 7 (Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2) then start in the wrong place.

Pi already reflects the cwd in the window title; this is the same job. Extensions doing it individually would be patchy. pi-worktrunk ships a workaround (mavam/pi-worktrunk#27, reported in mavam/pi-worktrunk#26) that I'd remove once core does it.

### How? (optional)

- `packages/tui/src/terminal.ts`: add `setWorkingDirectory(cwd)` to `ProcessTerminal`, encoding the path with `pathToFileURL()` and `os.hostname()`.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`: call it from `updateTerminalTitle()`, which already runs at startup and after `rebindCurrentSession()`.

Happy to implement it.

issues.title: openai-responses: legacy response.reasoning.delta events are dropped, no thinking_delta streamed
issues.body:
### What happened?

`openai-responses` drops `response.reasoning.delta` events, so reasoning from some OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints is not streamed.

Example: Vercel AI Gateway (`https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses`) with `moonshotai/kimi-k3` and `reasoning: { effort: "high", summary: "auto" }` streams:

```
event: response.reasoning.delta
data: {"type":"response.reasoning.delta","item_id":"rs_...","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"delta":"We"}
... (35 deltas)
event: response.reasoning.done
event: response.output_item.done
data: {..."item":{"type":"reasoning","summary":[],"content":[{"type":"reasoning_text","text":"..."}]}}
```

pi emits `thinking_start`, no `thinking_delta`, then `thinking_end` with the full text (backfilled from `output_item.done`). Streaming UIs show an empty thinking block until the item ends; delta-only consumers get nothing.

`processResponsesStream` in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` handles `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` and `response.reasoning_text.delta`, but not `response.reasoning.delta`. That was the official OpenAI event name between openai-node v4.101.0 (2025-05) and its removal in v5.10.2 (2025-07); `response.reasoning_text.delta` replaced it. Bedrock and Vercel AI Gateway still emit the old name.

Same issue elsewhere:
- TanStack/ai#1207, fixed by TanStack/ai#1211 (treat `response.reasoning.delta` as an alias of `response.reasoning_text.delta`)
- strands-agents/harness-sdk#4598 (Kimi K3 on Bedrock)

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -sN https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"moonshotai/kimi-k3","stream":true,"input":"Hi","reasoning":{"effort":"high","summary":"auto"}}'
```

The stream contains `response.reasoning.delta` and no `response.reasoning_text.delta`. Using the same model through pi with `openai-responses` yields no `thinking_delta` events.

### Expected behavior

Treat `response.reasoning.delta` the same as `response.reasoning_text.delta` (string `delta` appended to the current thinking block). This is a small change in the stream loop plus a unit test. I would like to implement it and can open a PR if this gets an `lgtm`.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-ai 1.2.0 (also current main)

---

This issue was drafted by an AI agent (Claude Code) on behalf of @LiyanChen-X; the repro and stream trace were captured against the live endpoint.

issues.title: Sessions wedge permanently at the context ceiling on reasoning models
issues.body:
### What happened?

Sessions on reasoning models wedge permanently at the context ceiling. Every request comes back `stopReason: "length"` with `usage.output: 16`, and auto-compaction reports `Truncated response recovery failed after one compact-and-retry attempt.` In the session I hit this on (gpt-6-astra, 272k window) the last 9 turns spanning 44 minutes and 2 prompts all stopped on `length`, and not one compaction entry was written.

Three things compound:

**1. `estimateTokens()` cannot see reasoning.** In `packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts` a thinking block is scored as `block.thinking.length`. Reasoning models return an empty `thinking` and carry the reasoning in `thinkingSignature`, which is replayed to the provider and billed as input. Over the failing span, 1,524,314 chars of signature and 148,316 tokens of assistant `usage.output` scored at roughly zero: 268,261 real tokens estimated at 24,445, a 0.091 ratio. `findCutPoint()` walks that estimate backwards until it hits `keepRecentTokens`, so it keeps nearly the whole context and compaction cannot get the session under threshold.

**2. `isContextOverflow()` misclassifies it.** `clampMaxTokensToContext` collapses the output budget to free window space and `openai-responses` floors it at `OPENAI_RESPONSES_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (16). The model is asked for 16 tokens and answers `length` having emitted nothing. Case 3 needs `output === 0` (it is 16) and ratio >= 0.99 (268,535/272,000 = 0.987), so real exhaustion is treated as recoverable truncation.

**3. `_overflowRecoveryAttempted` dead-ends the turn.** It clears only on a user message or an assistant stop that is not error/length — impossible once wedged, so each new prompt buys one doomed attempt. The overflow branch also returns before the ordinary threshold-compaction path, so that never runs either.

### Steps to reproduce

Needs a genuinely large reasoning session, so the practical repro is the observable state rather than a script:

1. Run a long tool-heavy session on a reasoning model (gpt-6-astra, 272k window) until context is ~98% full.
2. Send any prompt. The response stops on `length` with `usage.output: 16` and `input + cacheRead` ~= 0.987 of the window.
3. The session emits `Truncated response recovery failed after one compact-and-retry attempt.` and never compacts again, on that prompt or any later one.

I pinned it deterministically instead: a regression test drives that exact usage shape through `_checkCompaction` and reproduces the dead end without a real 268k session.

### Expected behavior

Compaction accounts for reasoning tokens and actually shrinks the session, and a starved 16-token `length` stop is recognised as context overflow rather than recoverable truncation.

### Version

0.85.1

---

I have a fix with regression tests and would like to submit it: https://github.com/Sager611/pi/tree/fix/auto-compaction-wedged-at-context-ceiling — `npm run check` and `./test.sh` both pass. Happy to wait for approval per CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR.

issues.title: OSC 52 copy in fullscreen TUI is swallowed by tmux (no passthrough wrap)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Copy-on-select in the fullscreen TUI writes a raw OSC 52 (`\x1b]52;c;...`). When pi runs inside tmux, tmux consumes the incoming OSC 52 into its paste buffer and does not relay it to its client. pi flashes "Copied!" either way.

On a headless Linux host over SSH (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND), OSC 52 is the only clipboard route, so copying from the TUI silently does nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. tmux on a headless Linux host, SSH'd from another machine (`set-clipboard on`)
2. Run pi, drag-select text in the transcript, release
3. "Copied!" flashes but the client machine's clipboard is unchanged
4. `tmux show-buffer` on the pi host shows the selection: tmux ate it

Traced to core, not an extension. Both OSC 52 emit sites write the raw sequence: `copyToClipboard` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts` and the TUI fallback in `packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts`.

### Expected behavior

The client terminal's clipboard updates. Wrapping the write in the tmux DCS passthrough (`\x1bPtmux;\x1b<seq>\x1b\\`) when `$TMUX` is set fixes it: tmux forwards the unwrapped sequence to its client, where a plain terminal sets the clipboard and an outer tmux picks it up. I have the change with tests ready and can send a PR.

### Version

1.0.0 (also present on current main)

---

Drafted with AI assistance (traced and verified with an agent; I did the diagnosis and reviewed the writeup).

issues.title: bash temp-file stream errors still crash the whole process on 1.0.4 (ENOSPC on a full /tmp, EACCES)
issues.body:
## What happened?

pi 1.0.4 died mid-run with an uncaught `ENOSPC: no space left on device, write` (`~/.pi/agent/crashes.json`: `kind: "uncaught_exception"`, `2026-10-07T02:46:22.281Z`, Linux aarch64). The session log stops at the previous event — the in-flight run was lost, with no tool error and no truncated result.

Context: `/tmp` is a 16 GiB / 1 M-inode tmpfs on this machine; concurrent agent runs had filled it with scratch while the root filesystem had 130 GiB free. Output past `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` opens a temp file in `tmpdir()`, so any temp-write failure (full disk, inode exhaustion, permissions) takes down the whole process instead of failing the tool.

Same bug as #9827 (auto-closed, labeled `no-action`; tc3oliver's EACCES repro is in the comments); same class: #2512/#2513, #5667, #7237 (all closed). Still present on main as of `eb326d2`: `ensureTempFile` opens the stream with no `error` listener at [bash-executor.ts#L62-L70](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf/packages/coding-agent/src/core/bash-executor.ts#L62-L70) and [output-accumulator.ts#L245-L256](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/output-accumulator.ts#L245-L256); [output-files.ts#L31-L34](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf/packages/coding-agent/src/utils/output-files.ts#L31-L34) adds none. Filing again because it still reproduces on the current release and no released version has the fix; close it if the `no-action` call on #9827 stands.

## Steps to reproduce

1.0.4, no extensions, no model call (core API only, so no extension can be involved):

```sh
mkdir ro && chmod 500 ro
TMPDIR=$PWD/ro node --input-type=module -e '
import { createBashTool } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
await createBashTool(process.cwd()).execute("t", { command: "seq 1 300000" }, undefined, () => {});'
```

Result: `throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event` — `EACCES: permission denied, open '…/pi-bash-<hex>.log'`, exit 1. A full disk (ENOSPC) hits the same path — consistent with the real-world crash above (the crash record carries no stack, so that link is inference from the code, not proof).

## Expected behavior

The temp-file failure should degrade gracefully: drop `fullOutputPath` and return the truncated in-memory output (or at worst fail the tool) instead of killing the process.

## Version

1.0.4 (latest release), main @ `eb326d2`. Linux aarch64 (Asahi M1 Pro). PR #9800 has a fix with regression tests for this path (auto-closed, unapproved).

issues.title: 1.2.0: keyboard input stops after an unterminated terminal reply (StdinBuffer waits forever)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

Since 1.2.0, pi sometimes stops accepting keyboard input right after startup. Typed text and Enter are silently ignored. Pressing an arrow key makes input work again, but everything typed before that is lost.

It happens when the reply to the startup color query arrives without its terminator. `StdinBuffer` recognises the reply header and waits for the terminator with no timeout, so every later keystroke is appended to the pending reply and never emitted.

This comes from edb2eb96 ("keep delayed terminal replies out of keyboard input"), and it is still on `main`. In 1.1.0 the same input times out after 50 ms and typing continues.

### Steps to reproduce

Save as `repro.mjs` in the repo root and run `node repro.mjs`:

```js
import { StdinBuffer } from "./packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts";
const sb = new StdinBuffer();
const got = [];
sb.on("data", (d) => got.push(d));
sb.process("\x1b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e"); // OSC 11 reply that never gets its BEL/ST
setTimeout(() => sb.process("hello\r"), 300); // user types afterwards
setTimeout(() => { console.log(JSON.stringify(got)); process.exit(0); }, 1000);
```

- v1.2.0: `[]`
- v1.1.0: `["\u001b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e","h","e","l","l","o","\r"]`

Removing only the `if (TERMINAL_REPLY_HEADER_PATTERN.test(this.buffer)) return;` line in `process()` brings input back.

### Expected behavior

An unterminated reply should not block keyboard input forever. Some upper bound on the wait (well above the 50 ms key timeout) would keep the fix for slow replies and still let typing through.

### Version

1.2.0 (also current `main`)

---

## Motivation

There are gazzilion developers on windows. Some use pi. Many could use pi. There are however too many ways pi can be run on windows and as such it is hard to know where to focus energy (fixing bugs, having best docs, having out of box) vs what ways can be delegated out of core to extensions. 

## Ways to run pi on WIndows:

- Pi runs on windows, uses git bash (default)
- Pi runs on windows, uses wsl bash (?semi-automatic fallback)
- Pi runs fully on windows with pwsh.exe/powershell.exe bash replacement (only plugins?)
- Pi runs fully in wsl2

## Issues seen:

All of these have some papercuts. Windows/wsl bash suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7064, Windows/*  suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7427, Windows/git-bash suffers from git bash being iffy and e.g. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6817 (among some closed). As such, I'd like to ask: how do you use pi on windows? Why this particular way and not any of other of the abovementioned ones? If you use some plugins, why and which ones? What's missing? What's challenging? What UX gaps are you seeing?

issues.title: coding-agent: final-settlement hook receives no cancellation signal
issues.body:
### What happened?

My verification extension runs before a completed turn settles. In Pi 1.2.0, `ctx.signal` exists in `agent_end` but is undefined in `agent_before_settle`. A hook that passes this signal to a cancellable wait cannot respond to `session.abort()`: abort waits for the entire hook. This prevents cancelling long verification commands at the final boundary.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the standalone SDK fixture in the next comment with no discovered extensions, skills, context files, themes, tools or live provider. Its only extension returns a synthetic final answer, then awaits `setTimeout(5000, undefined, { signal: ctx.signal })` in `agent_before_settle`. Call `session.abort()` as soon as the hook starts.

Observed on Windows, Node 24.15.0: signal present in `agent_end`, absent in `agent_before_settle`; abort took 5007 ms. No Tesota code is loaded. Related #6234 concerns a hook that ignores cancellation; this hook attempts to respect it but receives no signal.

### Expected behavior

The final boundary exposes a signal that `session.abort()` aborts, so a cooperative verification hook can stop its work before settling.

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.2.0 (npm latest checked 2026-10-14).

issues.title: durable: per-model compaction settings
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add per-model compaction settings to pi-durable, like pi's `compaction.modelOverrides` (#8133), so one harness can serve both small-window models and large ones without changing how the large ones compact.

### Why?

`settings.compaction` applies to every conversation in a harness. `reserveTokens`, `keepRecentTokens` and `backgroundTokens` are fixed token counts, so they can't suit a large-window model and a small-window model in the same harness.

(I ran into this when testing Apple's Private Cloud Compute model which has 32k context window, and cannot compact with the default settings + small system prompt)

Lowering the settings for the whole harness fixes the small model but changes compaction for every large model too.

A host can't work around this per model:
- `settings.compaction` is read the same way for every conversation, and a getter isn't told which conversation or model is asking.
- `beforeCompact` can decline or supply a summary, but not change how much is kept.
- `beforeRequest` runs after the threshold decision.

### How? (optional)

Port pi's `compaction.modelOverrides` (#8133) to pi-durable. Overrides are keyed by `"provider/modelId"` and resolved wherever `settings.compaction` is read: the threshold check in generation preparation, overflow recovery, and the compaction task. The model is already known at all three. The change is small, and I have a working patch with tests if useful.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): reuse unchanged codemode highlighting
prs.body:
Previously, codemode highlighted the entire script every time its tool row updated—including result progress, timer ticks, and expand/collapse toggles.

Now each row keeps its last highlighted script in `context.state`. It reuses that text when these match:
- Exact script string
- Active syntax palette and color mode
- Number of registered syntax grammars

This results in ~85% lower rendering time for unchanged scripts. Changed scripts still get fully highlighted. Theme changes and newly loaded HTML/CSS grammars invalidate the cache, and so do empty or invalid arguments.

prs.title: fix(ai,coding-agent): prevent one-token provider requests and recover truncated turns
prs.body:
A tool result that pushes the next request past the configured context window left Pi's clamped output budget at 1, so the provider returned an empty `length` stop that compaction could not recover as a truncated turn.

`packages/ai` now resolves the estimated context and unfloored response budget, and every built-in `streamSimple` provider returns a recognizable context-overflow assistant error before network I/O when the window cannot reserve `min(desired cap, 1024)` output tokens. Healthy requests keep their output caps and thinking configuration, and context-overflow errors are no longer retried by the summarization retry loop.

`packages/coding-agent` resolves the response model for compaction through a new optional `Model.responseModelAliases` list (declarable in models.json, model overrides, and provider definitions), so a provider or gateway that renames the requested model can still recover a truncated turn while a genuine fallback, another provider, or a mid-run model switch stays ineligible.

Verified with `npm run check` and the `ai`, `agent`, and `coding-agent` package suites (isolated environment, local LLM tests disabled). New tests cover the incident shape through the real agent loop with a scripted Anthropic transport: the over-window follow-up never reaches HTTP, the tool runs once, exactly one compact-and-retry, and the same turn resumes without duplicating the user prompt.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): bounded clock-mock-immune trust lock retry, reclaim orphaned locks
prs.body:
Fixes #10962.

## Problem

`acquireTrustLockSync` retried an `ELOCKED` trust lock in a synchronous busy-wait on the wall clock:

```ts
const start = Date.now();
while (Date.now() - start < delayMs) { /* spin */ }
```

When a test freezes the clock (vitest fake timers), the loop can never terminate: the worker spins at 100% CPU forever, the designed ~200ms give-up-then-throw is never reached, and the worker ignores SIGINT while spinning. Reproduced and CDP-sampled in #10962 — the sampled worker's stack sat in `acquireTrustLockSync` with `Date.now()` returning the identical value across seconds.

Note the frozen clock makes this worse than ordinary contention: the spin never re-checks the lock, so the worker hangs **even after the peer releases it**. It also wedges harder than a normal slow test — vitest's own test timeout cannot fire because the worker's single thread is spinning, so the run hangs until an external kill.

## Changes

1. **`stale: 5000` on `lockfile.lockSync`** — reclaims an orphaned lock left by a killed process instead of failing on it forever. `lock()` already defaults to `stale: 10000`, so orphaned locks were previously reclaimed only when the reader's clock was ≥10s past the lock's mtime; the explicit value keeps that behavior deliberate and tighter for a lock held for microseconds at a time. (Related: #4919 added `stale` to the other sync locks.)
2. **`sleepSync` via `Atomics.wait`** for the retry backoff — blocks on the futex in real time and cannot be intercepted by `Date` mocks, so a frozen clock now yields the designed 10 × 20ms bounded retry instead of an infinite spin. (`Atomics.wait` is allowed on the main thread in Node.)

No call sites change; the function keeps its synchronous contract and its throw-on-failure behavior.

## Testing

`packages/coding-agent/test/trust-manager.test.ts` gains two tests:

- **reclaims an orphaned trust lock older than the stale window under frozen fake timers** — orphaned lock with a backdated mtime, `vi.useFakeTimers()`, `get()` succeeds.
- **gives up instead of spinning when a held trust lock blocks a frozen fake-timer read** — live lock, frozen clock, `get()` throws the `ELOCKED` error after the bounded backoff.

Mutation check: reverting `trust-manager.ts` (test kept) makes the run hang before vitest can even fire its own test timeout — `RUN v4.1.11` printed, then nothing until an external `timeout 90` kill (exit 124). With the fix: 4/4 pass in ~450ms. Full monorepo `npm run check` (the pre-commit gate: biome, pinned/runtime deps, ts-imports, entry graphs, install-lock, `tsc --noEmit`, browser smoke) passes.

models). This PR adds the same path for video, so a user can do:

```
pi @clip.mp4 "What number is on the card?"
```

and a video-capable local model answers from the clip.

## Why this is safe and focused

**OpenAI's own API has no video input item.** The stable `openai` SDK exposes
exactly two media input types — `input_image` and `input_file` (used for
documents/audio) — and zero `input_video` / `video_url`. So there is no
official OpenAI video wire format to diverge from. This targets the
**self-hosted endpoints that actually read video** (llama.cpp, Strata, vLLM),
and it is **gated two ways** so it only activates where video is real:

1. the model opts in via `input: ["text", "image", "video"]`, and
2. the part spelling is a per-endpoint `compat.videoPartFormat`
   (`input_video` | `video_url`), default `input_video`.

Models that don't accept video get a graceful text placeholder instead of a
400 or a silent drop — the transform downgrades them exactly like it does for
images today.

### The `videoPartFormat` split

Different self-hosted servers expect different parts, and none of them is the
other's:

- **llama.cpp** (and Strata) take llama.cpp's `input_video` part:
  `{ "type": "input_video", "input_video": { "data": "<base64>" } }`.
- **vLLM** (and forks) reject `input_video` outright with
  `400 {"error":"Unexpected item type in content."}` and instead take
  `video_url` with a `data:` URL, when launched with
  `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":64,"video":64}'`.

`videoPartFormat` selects the spelling per endpoint. Default is `input_video`
because it's the llama.cpp/Strata convention; set `"video_url"` for vLLM.

## What changed

- **Types** (`packages/ai`): `VideoContent`, `MediaContent = ImageContent |
  VideoContent`, a `"video"` input modality, and `compat.videoPartFormat`.
- **Wire formats**: `openai-completions` and `openai-responses` both serialize
  video to the correct part (user content and tool-result content).
- **File input**: `@path` sniffs video extensions; the `read` tool returns
  videos up to 50 MB as base64.
- **Plumbing**: videos flow through the agent, `AgentSession`, the extension
  runner, compaction token estimation, and the RPC client/mode.
- **Downgrade**: `transform-messages` drops video to a text placeholder for
  models without video input, like images.
- **Surfaces**: `list-models` gains a `videos` column; render utils and the
  anthropic/bedrock serializers handle the new content type.
- **Docs**: `cli.md`, `llama-cpp.md` (new "Video input" section), and
  `models.md` (new "Send video to a vLLM-style endpoint" section).
- **Schema**: `models.schema.json` regenerated.

## Testing

11 new cases, all passing:

- `openai-completions-video` — `input_video` by default, `video_url` when
  `videoPartFormat` is set, user and tool-result videos.
- `openai-responses-video` — same four cases for the Responses wire.
- `read-tool-video` — local MP4 returns a base64 video tool result; oversized
  videos are rejected before reading.
- `list-models-video` — the `videos` column reports capability.

`tsc --noEmit` is clean and the full ai / coding-agent suites pass (the only
failures are pre-existing, unrelated to video — verified against the base
commit).

## Open question for maintainers

Is `input_video` the right default, or should the default be `video_url`?
I defaulted to `input_video` because llama.cpp's own server (the most common
self-hosted video endpoint) uses that spelling and vLLM is the outlier that
needs the opt-in flag. Happy to flip it if you'd prefer.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): resolve model references through one provider selection policy
prs.body:
Fixes #10160

## Problem

When the named provider lacks a model but several gateways expose `provider/id` as a raw id, `--model provider/id` picked the first gateway in catalog order, ignoring credentials:

```text
pi --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5   # only vercel-ai-gateway has a key
-> openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 (listed first)
```

Provider selection was spread across branches that discarded ambiguity, so results also depended on input shape: `shared` picked the authenticated provider, `shared:high` picked by catalog order.

## Change

`resolveModelReference` in `core/model-resolver.ts` resolves every model reference (`--model`, `--models`/`enabledModels`, `/model`, `pi auth print-*`) in one pipeline. It collects all candidates, then applies one rule: the named provider's match if usable, else the sole usable raw match, else the named provider's match, else ambiguous. Fuzzy matching runs only when no reference candidate exists and prefers usable providers.

## Behavior changes

- No unique authenticated provider among exact matches is now an error, not catalog order.
- Fuzzy matches prefer authenticated providers; an identical best id on several providers is ambiguous.
- With `--api-key`, stored credentials no longer pick the provider.
- `--models`/`enabledModels` patterns add every provider offering the same id and warn about the ambiguity.

`provider/id` still prefers the named provider's exact or fuzzy match.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep leading / root-anchored in skill ignore patterns
prs.body:
## Summary
Skill discovery (and the duplicated package-resource scanner) always stripped a leading `/` from ignore patterns. At the scan root that turns git root-anchored whitelist rules such as:

```gitignore
/*
!/commit-summarizer/
```

into unanchored `*` / `!commit-summarizer/`, so `loadSkillsFromDir` returns no skills while `git check-ignore` still keeps them.

This keeps the leading `/` when there is no directory prefix, and only strips it when prefixing a nested ignore file — the same rule described in #10877.

Fixes #10877

- [x] `npx vitest --run test/skills.test.ts` (29 passed, including new root-anchored whitelist case)
- [x] Temp dir with `/*` + `!/commit-summarizer/` loads only `commit-summarizer`
- [x] Existing nested ignore behavior unchanged for the skills suite

Happy to mirror the same regression under `package-manager.test.ts` if you want both call sites covered explicitly.
