prs.title: fix(core): widen the agent workspace lock retry budget (#14028)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Raises the cross-process workspace lock's acquisition retry budget from 10 retries (5–100ms randomized exponential backoff, ~0.65–1.3s worst case) to 30 retries (~5s worst case), matching the budget the Agent Board lock already uses for the same two-tier locking pattern. Everything else about the lock is unchanged: the in-process mutex still serializes same-process writers, and stale-lock breaking (`stale: 10_000`) still recovers a dead holder's lock after 10 seconds.

## Why it's needed

`main` CI failed on `agent workspace lock > loses no roster update when two processes write at once` (#14028). The test spawns two child processes that each perform 8 read-modify-write roster updates under the store's file lock. On an oversubscribed CI host, one holder's critical section — an fsync-bound atomic JSON write — can outlast the ~1s retry budget, so the competing process exhausted its retries, exited with `ELOCKED: Lock file is already being held`, and failed the test. CI's `--retry=2` does not help because every attempt on a badly placed host hits the same contention. I reproduced this locally: pinned to 2 CPUs with CPU and fsync competitors, the pre-fix code failed 6 of 30 rounds with ELOCKED; with this change, 30 of 30 rounds passed. A longer wait is strictly safer here: the lock guards a low-frequency roster/registry store, so waiting a few seconds for a slow live holder is always preferable to erroring.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm the change is confined to the workspace store's lock options and that the concurrency test passes: run `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/agents/workspace-agents/workspace-lock.test.ts` and expect 1 passed test. To observe the original failure mode, revert the one-line change (`retries: 30` back to `10`) and run the same test on a heavily loaded machine (or pinned to few CPUs with competing load): the worker processes intermittently exit 1 with `ELOCKED: Lock file is already being held`. With the fix, the waiters simply wait out the slow holder instead of erroring.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (no user-visible behavior change; the observable difference is CI stability under host contention: before, 6/30 contended probe rounds failed with ELOCKED; after, 0/30 failed).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests under `packages/core` (vitest), plus a local contention harness pinning the test scenario to 2 CPUs with busy CPU/fsync competitors.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a waiter now holds on for up to ~5s (was ~1s) before failing lock acquisition when a live holder is slow; a dead holder's lock is still broken after 10s via the unchanged stale detection, so crash recovery latency is unaffected.
- Not validated / out-of-scope: macOS and Windows lanes (left to CI; the change is a platform-independent timing budget). A deeper hardening — aborting a transaction whose lock is compromised mid-flight instead of only warning — is deliberately out of scope for this flake fix.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14028

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

将跨进程 workspace 锁的获取重试预算从 10 次(5–100ms 随机指数退避,最坏约 0.65–1.3 秒)提高到 30 次(最坏约 5 秒),与 Agent Board 锁在相同双层锁模式下已有的预算一致。锁的其他行为完全不变:进程内互斥锁仍然串行化同进程写入者,过期锁打破机制(`stale: 10_000`)仍然会在 10 秒后回收已崩溃持锁者留下的锁。

## 为什么需要

`main` 分支 CI 在 `agent workspace lock > loses no roster update when two processes write at once` 上失败(#14028)。该测试派生两个子进程,各自在存储的文件锁下执行 8 次 roster 读-改-写更新。在超额订阅的 CI 主机上,持锁者的一次临界区——带 fsync 的原子 JSON 写入——可能超过约 1 秒的重试预算,导致竞争进程重试耗尽后以 `ELOCKED: Lock file is already being held` 退出,测试失败。CI 的 `--retry=2` 帮不上忙,因为在被调度到繁忙主机时,每次尝试都会遇到同样的争用。我已在本地复现:固定到 2 个 CPU 并加入 CPU 与 fsync 竞争负载时,修复前的代码在 30 轮中有 6 轮以 ELOCKED 失败;应用本改动后,30 轮全部通过。此处更长的等待严格更安全:该锁守护的是低频的 roster/注册表存储,为一个缓慢的活跃持锁者多等几秒永远优于直接报错。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

确认改动仅限于 workspace 存储的锁参数,且并发测试通过:运行 `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/agents/workspace-agents/workspace-lock.test.ts`,预期 1 个测试通过。若要观察原始失败模式,可将这一行改动回退(`retries: 30` 改回 `10`),并在负载较重的机器上(或绑定到少量 CPU 并施加竞争负载)运行同一测试:worker 进程会间歇性地以退出码 1 失败,报 `ELOCKED: Lock file is already being held`。应用修复后,等待者会等待缓慢的持锁者完成,而不是报错。

### 前后对照证据

N/A(无用户可见的行为变化;可观察的差异是主机争用下的 CI 稳定性:修复前,30 轮带载探测有 6 轮以 ELOCKED 失败;修复后,30 轮无一失败)。

### 已测试平台

|     系统    |  状态  |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境(可选)

`packages/core` 下的单元测试(vitest),以及一个将测试场景固定到 2 个 CPU 并施加 CPU/fsync 竞争负载的本地争用 harness。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍:当活跃持锁者较慢时,等待者现在最多坚持约 5 秒(原来约 1 秒)才会放弃锁获取;已崩溃持锁者的锁仍会通过未改动的过期检测在 10 秒后被打破,因此崩溃恢复延迟不受影响。
- 未验证 / 超出范围:macOS 与 Windows 通道(交由 CI 覆盖;本改动是平台无关的计时预算)。更深一层的加固——在锁中途被夺时中止事务而不是仅告警——刻意不纳入本次抖动修复的范围。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明:无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #14028

</details>

issues.title: Turn snapshots fail with "git commit-tree failed: fatal: <sha> is not a valid object" since 2026-10-12 (0.10.0 after rollback from 0.10.1); old user turns are re-delivered

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
Hello,

I would like to report a defect in CodeWhale 0.10.0. We run it on Windows 11 in daily work, and the instance
in question holds a long-running session (about 99 MB) that we would very much like to keep. The problem has
been with us since 12 October 2026.

**Environment**

- CodeWhale **0.10.0** (npm package installed globally). Binary: `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\codewhale\bin\downloads\codewhale.exe`,
  100 331 520 bytes, last written **2026-10-12 15:48**.
- Current version in npm: **0.10.1**.
- Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 10.0.26100, git 2.55.0.windows.5.
- Data dir `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale`; workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale`.
- Session journal `sessions\fd452c83-….json`: **98 989 231 bytes** (it was ~72 MB on 2026-10-12 and grows).

**Symptom 1 — every turn snapshot fails**

```
WARN snapshot: snapshot 'pre-turn:2: <first words of a user message>' failed:
     git commit-tree failed: fatal: 6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9 is not a valid object
```

**Symptom 2 — old user turns are re-delivered as new input**

Because snapshots never complete, past turns are never marked done and are fed back. The order is stable and
reproducible: in the most recent run the app re-delivered turns 2, 3 and 4 — the same three messages, in the
same order, as in every previous run (logs `tui-2026-10-14-20628`, `-14004`, `-23528`). The user sees his own
old messages answered again.

**Symptom 3 — shell operations frequently fail**

```
WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: shell work-graph registration skipped;
     running without a bound operation shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=To-do state is busy; operation was not registered

WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: failed to reconcile shell lifecycle shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=operation binding shell:shell_<hex> is not registered
```

273 such lines in the logs; on the user's side roughly every 3rd–4th shell call fails. Possibly the same root
cause as the snapshot failure.

**Symptom 4 — at startup the store looks empty**

```
WARN snapshot: boot prune failed: git log failed: fatal: bad object HEAD
```

**When it started**

- first occurrence: **2026-10-12T16:00:16Z** — `snapshot prune failed: commit-tree failed: fatal: c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c is not a valid object`;
- 458 lines containing “is not a valid object” in total, over four runs;
- only two lost objects in total: `6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9` and `c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c`.

**What correlates with the date**

On the same day the user updated to **0.10.1** and then **rolled back to 0.10.0**. The package directory is
stamped **2026-10-12 15:48** (the rollback), and the first snapshot failure is at **19:00** local time.
Hypothesis: a snapshot store was begun by 0.10.1, and after the rollback 0.10.0 cannot complete that chain.

**What we tried**

- Reinstalled the same version (`npm install -g codewhale@0.10.0`) — **no effect**. The store is not part of
  the program files; `boot prune failed: bad object HEAD` still appears and snapshots still fail with the same SHA.

**Where we looked for the store (found nothing)**

Workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale` (not a git repo; only `.codewhale\state` with subagent state);
`%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` (no `work-graph`, `objects`, `refs`, `.git` — only `sessions\.work-graph-import-archive`);
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` (depth 4); `%TEMP%`; the app package dir (only `bin`, `scripts`, `test`,
`package.json`, `README.md`); the app's `state.db` is empty and stale (2026-10-04).

**Questions**

1. Where are the snapshot store and the work-graph kept, and how can a corrupted chain be repaired on the
   user's side?
2. How can the **turn queue / parent-commit pointer** be reset so that snapshots work again and old turns stop
   being re-delivered **without discarding the session**? The session is 99 MB and losing it would be costly.
3. Is the `To-do state is busy` shell failure the same root cause as the snapshot failure? Both began in the
   same period.

**Related: cannot move to 0.10.1 with a long session**

On 2026-10-12 we also tried 0.10.1: it installs cleanly, but resuming our session fails:

```
error: selected saved history could not be captured
caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The session file was ~72 MB then and is **98 989 231 bytes** now, so this bound will trigger even more readily.
We cannot test 0.10.1 — and therefore cannot check whether it fixes the snapshot store — while it stands.
Is there a way to raise or bypass it?

**Materials available on request**

Full log excerpts (458 snapshot lines, 273 work-graph lines), the environment dump, and our extended Russian
report. Happy to attach or translate anything you need.

Thank you for the tool, and for taking the time to look at this. I will gladly provide any further logs,
dumps or reproductions you need.

Best regards,
Sergej Malevich

issues.title: Android (Termux): every confined file operation fails with EACCES — `open_confined` opens `/` with `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`, which SELinux denies to apps

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary

Since v0.10.1, on Android/Termux every engine feature that goes through the confined file opener (`WorkspaceFile::open_confined` in `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`) fails with `Permission denied (os error 13)`:

- `workflow journal unreadable (~/.codewhale/workflow-runs.jsonl): Permission denied` on every session start
- `context compaction failed ... error=Permission denied (os error 13)` — and the turn is then settled as **Failed**, which is the most visible symptom
- `spillover: could not save full tool output before cutting it for model context err=... PermissionDenied`
- skill loading via `fs_confined::read_to_string` fails (`read cannot expose...` style errors aside, direct SKILL.md loads return EACCES)

Everything that does *not* go through `open_confined` (plain `std::fs` paths such as `save_checkpoint`, shell tool output, bash subprocesses) works fine, which makes the failure look random.

Logs from v0.9.x sessions on the same device show **zero** occurrences of these warnings; they start exactly at the 0.10.1 install and now appear in every session.

## Root cause

`open_confined` anchors its `openat` walk at the filesystem root:

```rust
let fd = unsafe {
    libc::open(
        c"/".as_ptr(),
        libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_CLOEXEC,
    )
};
```

On Android, app processes run in the `untrusted_app` SELinux domain. That domain has **search** (traverse) permission on `/` and on mount-point directories such as `/data` and `/data/data`, but **not read**, so `open("/", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY)` returns `EACCES` even though the DAC bits are `drwxr-xr-x`. Every `WorkspaceFile` operation therefore fails before it even reaches the workspace, and `com.termux` (uid `u0_a435`) is affected as `untrusted_app` (domain confirmed via `/proc/self/attr/current` = `u:r:untrusted_app_27:s0:c179,c257,c512,c768`).

Verified with strace on a live session — the only non-environment `EACCES` calls in the entire process lifetime are:

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES (Permission denied)
```

(52 occurrences in one session, interleaved with the failing journal/compaction/spillover warnings.)

DAC permissions, ownership, fcntl record locks (EAGAIN, not EACCES, when contended), disk/inode headroom, `TMPDIR`, and multi-process concurrent appends were all checked and are not factors. `realpath`/`opendir` on the same paths succeed — the failure is specific to opening `/` as a readable directory.

## Minimal reproducer

Run inside Termux (`python3 android-repro.py`, attached):

```
workspace: /data/data/com.termux/files/home
open('/', O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY)  [current open_confined anchor]: FAIL errno=13 (Permission denied)
open('/', O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY)    [proposed fix anchor]:        OK
confined walk (fix):             OK
confined write/read through fix: OK
```

## Proposed fix (patch attached, against main as of 2026-10-14)

Open the anchor and every intermediate component with `O_PATH` instead of `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`, and re-materialize the file's immediate parent as a real directory fd after the walk:

- `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY` still fails with `ENOTDIR` on non-directories, so the per-component type check and the symlink refusal are unchanged.
- `O_PATH` requires no read permission, so SELinux `search`-only domains (Android apps, hardened sandboxes) work.
- The final parent is reopened with real flags (`openat(pinned_parent, ".")`) because O_PATH fds cannot be `fsync`ed (`EBADF`) or read, and `WorkspaceFile` uses the directory fd for `sync_all`, `renameat`, `unlinkat` afterwards. This reopen cannot escape the walk: it resolves `.` inside the pinned parent.
- Final file opens (`open_with_flags`, `atomic_write`, `mkdirat`) are untouched.

Verified on-device that with the fix the full `WorkspaceFile` semantics work end-to-end: journal read, `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` leaf creation, `mkdirat` branch, atomic tmp+rename, `fsync` on the materialized parent, `fstat`/`dup` on the directory fd.

## Environment

- codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f), GitHub Releases aarch64 build
- Android 16 (Termux app, `untrusted_app_27` SELinux domain, targetSdk profile c179/c257/c512/c768)
- Workload: multiple parallel TUI sessions; failure rate 100% for compaction once context passes the auto-compact threshold

Happy to test a patched build on the device.

issues.title: 0.10.2: file_search default-active change must move the public tool-surface rows in the same slice

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tools
labels.description: Tool execution, tool schemas, tool UX, and built-in tool behavior

issues.body:
## Observed

`web/`'s public tool-surface contract fails against the current working tree:

```
$ cd web && npm test
FAIL  lib/public-surface-contract.test.ts > public surface contracts > keeps public tool facts aligned with the native core and discovery boundaries
AssertionError: expected [ 'read', 'write', 'edit', …(8) ] to deeply equal [ 'read', 'write', 'edit', …(9) ]
- "file_search"      ← in DEFAULT_ACTIVE_NATIVE_TOOLS, missing from docs/public-surface-facts.json
Test Files  1 failed | 73 passed (74)
Tests       1 failed | 771 passed (772)
```

`web/lib/public-surface-contract.test.ts:432` pins `docs/public-surface-facts.json` → `toolSurface.defaultActive` to the names parsed from `DEFAULT_ACTIVE_NATIVE_TOOLS` in `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_catalog.rs`. The guard is behaving exactly as designed.

## Cause

The in-flight promotion of `file_search` to default-active (`crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_catalog.rs:54`, between `edit` and `bash`) has not moved the public rows with it. Committed `main` (643b724d9; Web Frontend green at that SHA) is consistent at eleven names on both sides, so this is not a broken main: it is the landing checklist for that promotion.

## Rows that must move in the same slice

- `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tests/test_cases_10.rs:3` — `EXPECTED_NATIVE: [&str; 11]` is still the eleven-name literal; the Rust guard fails by construction against the same change
- `docs/public-surface-facts.json` — `toolSurface.defaultActive` (compared exactly, order included)
- `docs/TOOL_SURFACE.md` — "eleven eager native names" (lines 22, 37), the numbered list, and the receipt line (353)
- `docs/zh_hans/TOOL_SURFACE.md` — 十一个 (lines 23, 38, 302) and the numbered list
- `web/lib/content/tools.ts` — the docs/tools page must render `file_search`; the contract test asserts every `defaultActive` name appears there
- Runtime-contract receipt `scripts/measure-runtime-contract.py` if the eager catalog bytes moved — precedent: PR #6399 re-pinned the budget for the eager `load_skill` surface

## Why it matters for 0.10.2

`.github/workflows/web.yml` runs `npm test` and `npm run check` on every push. Landing the native-side promotion without the rows above turns the Web Frontend gate red.

## Reproduce

```
cd web && npm test
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked core::engine::tests::default_active_contract_keeps_discovery_and_core_tools_eager -- --exact
```

Captured 2026-10-09 from working-tree state; committed main was consistent when filed.

prs.title: refactor(commands): adopt portable config shapes for the complete config group (FEAT-028)
prs.body:
## Summary

Refs #5316

This is a large, behavior-preserving refactor: remove the `config` Slash Command Group's concrete `App`/TUI dependencies and replace them with **Shapes** connections. The PR is large because the existing Slash Command Group is large—that is how it was designed. No product-behavior change is intended.

The migration covers all 19 current registrations, including upstream's `/connect` and `/disconnect`. The physical crate move remains separate work.

## What changed

- Portable command contracts, narrow facets, capability declarations and shared actions replace direct App/TUI dependencies.
- Parsing and command rendering live in the portable group; adapters retain concrete observation, persistence and host effects.
- Typed settings/audit/subagent reports and import outcomes cross the boundary.
- Prepared templates validate message contracts; malformed replies fail without a successful action. Host-contract violations remain explicitly outside the prepared-message guarantee.
- The proof compiles the actual group root as an independent library; the migration frontier becomes `["core"]`.
- Upstream behavior retained includes plugin-provider connect/disconnect, pet style/language, localized Work/Full Access receipts and legacy sandbox-token cleanup.

## Historical contributor status and verification (`599119aa5`)

The original contributor verification below belongs to `599119aa5`; the current draft/head status is recorded in the maintainer update below.

Head `599119aa5` fixes the five failures reported on `593d7d717` by both the [macOS job](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38441020291/job/115447780813) and the [Linux job](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38441020291/job/115447780694):

- `/mode` metadata now shares the handler's Work-mode usage, restoring help filtering.
- `/login` again directs plugin-provider sign-in to `/connect`.
- The migrated-command test inventory includes `/connect` and `/disconnect`.
- The moved YOLO test expects upstream's Full Access (Work) receipt, retaining all permission/state assertions.

These were real reconciliation defects, not unrelated upstream failures. Earlier broad local verification did not establish that those fixes were present in the pushed tree; this follow-up records the committed repair explicitly.

## Verification for `599119aa5`

| Five CI regressions reproduced before editing | 5 run, 0 passed, 5 failed |
| Same five after repair | 5 run, 5 passed |

Local execution was on Linux. A passing macOS/Windows run, full hosted CI approval, merge and release are not yet claimed.

Paulo Aboim Pinto

Current head [`b323af876b`](https://github.com/aboimpinto/CodeWhale/commit/b323af876be8cd0ba58fa927d26ff2da1879ad65) preserves Paulo's original commits and all19 command registrations. The existing bridge runs import copying off Tokio workers and the protected no-replace writer keeps concurrently created standing instructions intact. Current main's215 dead-code budget and the contributor's portable proof workflow remain.

prs.title: test(tui): six terminal tests no longer follow the developer's terminal
prs.body:
## What and why

Six tui tests read the terminal environment the suite runs in and fail in setups CI never has:

- Inside tmux or GNU screen, or in Tilix or Terminator (`TMUX`, `STY`, `TILIX_ID` or `TERMINATOR_UUID` set), `apply_env_overrides` caps the redraw rate. The two Ghostty tests in `settings` and `config_fancy_animations_keeps_ghostty_full_motion` assert it is not capped. They already remove the SSH markers for the same reason, and the sibling `no_animations_*` / `other_terminals_*` tests already remove these four.
- Over SSH (`SSH_CLIENT`, `SSH_CONNECTION` or `SSH_TTY` set) the clipboard export goes to the terminal client and says so, while `command_clipboard_export_preserves_structure_and_redacts_secrets` expects "local clipboard". The clipboard target is picked when `App` is built, so the export harness removes the three variables before it builds the app, not inside the test.
- With `NO_ANIMATIONS=1` exported, the two Ghostty tests, `non_vscode_term_program_does_not_force_low_motion` and `tilix_and_terminator_cap_redraws_without_disabling_motion` fail because motion is already off.

Each test now removes those variables for its own duration with `EnvVarGuard`, under the env lock it already holds. Production code is unchanged.

#6973 moves `config_fancy_animations_keeps_ghostty_full_motion` into `config_main_host.rs`. Whichever of the two lands second needs the four `EnvVarGuard::remove` lines carried over to the test's new place.

## Issue

No-Issue: local test failures only, no issue filed for them

## How I tested it

- Ran the six tests with each variable above set on its own. Before: `TMUX`, `STY`, `TILIX_ID` or `TERMINATOR_UUID` fails the three Ghostty tests, any one of the SSH variables fails the export test, `NO_ANIMATIONS=1` fails four. After: all six pass in every case, and also with tmux, iTerm, SSH and `NO_COLOR` set together.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15289 passed, none failed.

No new tests; this changes six existing ones and the export test harness.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 947f670fe; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: test(extension-host): kill the host under a command with the default deadline
prs.body:
## What and why

`extension_host::tests::a_slow_command_is_cancelled_and_a_killed_host_fails_it_as_down` has failed twice on windows-latest since 10-10, once on main:

- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38021394688/job/114123124425 (the run for a dependabot bump, f50bc9ea1)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38123604545/job/114423296927 (main, 25cc4f7a4)

```
timed out after 0s and was cancelled
```

The test runs both of its halves on one manager whose `command_run_deadline` is 300 ms. The first half needs that: it checks the deadline cancels a slow command. The second half starts a slow command, sleeps 100 ms, kills the host with `taskkill` and expects `extension host is down: exited:`. That leaves the kill 200 ms to land. When it takes longer, the command ends on its own deadline first, which is the message above.

The kill half now runs on a second manager from `supervised_manager`, which keeps the default 30 s command deadline, so the only thing that ends the command there is the host going away. The tool-side tests are already split this way (`a_call_past_its_method_deadline_is_cancelled_and_the_host_stays_usable` and `killed_host_fails_calls_once_and_replays_with_fresh_owners`). The first half is unchanged.

The comment about the kill landing inside the 300 ms deadline no longer describes anything, so it is removed.

## Issue

No-Issue: Windows CI flake, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- To make the kill slow on purpose I made one scratch build that keeps the old test next to the new one and reads the sleep before the kill from an environment variable. At the normal 100 ms both pass 5 of 5. At 400 ms and at 2 s the old test fails 5 of 5 with the message above and the new one passes 5 of 5. None of that scratch code is in the diff.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15286 passed, none failed.

No new tests; this changes one existing test.

- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior

prs.title: feat(api): read and write a workspace's project trust over the Runtime API
prs.body:
## What and why

Everything the engine skips for an untrusted workspace is silent, and the only
way to settle it was a terminal and `/trust on --save`. A client that is not the
TUI — the VS Code extension I am building against this API — had no way to see
the verdict or record it, so a user could sit in front of a project whose
trust-sensitive skills, commands, hooks and MCP configuration were quietly not
loading, with nothing in the UI to act on.

- `GET /v1/workspace/status` now reports `workspace_trusted` next to the git
  facts it already carried.
- `POST /v1/workspace/trust` with `{"trusted": true|false}` records the
  decision.

The route is deliberately the only writer a client gets. It calls
`config::set_workspace_trust`, the same function behind `/trust on --save`, so
both front ends write the one `[projects."<workspace>"] trust_level` record that
`is_workspace_trusted` — the gate the engine actually consults — reads back. A
client never edits `config.toml`: the file is the user's, and a second writer
would be a second source of truth for a security decision.

Three details worth a reviewer's attention:

- The workspace is the server's own (`state.workspace`). The route accepts no
  path, so a client can trust the project it is attached to and nothing else.
- The response's `workspace_trusted` is read back through the gate *after* the
  write rather than echoing the request. If a write ever landed somewhere
  `is_workspace_trusted` does not look, the response reports `false` instead of
  claiming success, and `config_path` names the document that now holds it.
- The effect is not retroactive, and the `message` says so instead of implying
  otherwise: skills and commands consult the persisted decision at their
  existing boundaries; project hooks also need exact-file digest approval,
  and project MCP connections are rebuilt at the next engine start. Project
  instructions and existing MCP connections are not removed by this POST.

`/trust add <path>` (the external-path list in `workspace_trust.rs`) is a
different mechanism and is untouched, as is a thread's `trust_mode` / Full
Access — the docs now spell out which is which.

## Issue

No-Issue: no tracking issue; this is the engine half of a client-side gap found while building the VS Code extension against the Runtime API.

## Contributor-reported original local verification

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features --locked -- \
  -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments \
  -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or -A clippy::collapsible_if -A clippy::assertions_on_constants
RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- runtime_api::   # 456 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry                        # 2 passed
```

Three new tests in `runtime_api::tests`, against the real router (they run the
product stack like their neighbours):

- `workspace_trust_is_reported_and_written_through_the_api` — the round trip in
  both directions, that the response names the server's own workspace, and that
  the named document really carries
  `projects."<workspace>".trust_level = "trusted"` / `"untrusted"`.
- `workspace_trust_route_refuses_malformed_bodies` — a missing field and an
  unknown field are both 422, and the document is byte-identical afterwards.
  `deny_unknown_fields` is load-bearing here: a permissive parse would default
  `trusted` to `false` and silently revoke the workspace.
- `workspace_bootstrap_status_reports_the_trust_gate` — sealed, on one thread:
  the status projection follows the gate, up and back down.

**The first version of the HTTP tests was wrong, and CI caught what a laptop
could not.** They asserted the write through a *second* request and failed on
`Test (ubuntu-latest)` while passing locally. The cause is in the test harness,
not the route, and it is worth writing down because it is easy to rediscover the
hard way:

- `unsealed_test_state_root()` returns a root keyed by the *resolving thread's*
  id (`env-holder-ThreadId(N)/config.toml`), and `with_test_state_path` counts as
  a holder while it resolves — so any thread that resolves the user config gets
  its own test config document. Two requests served by different blocking workers
  therefore legitimately read and write two different files. On my machine both
  `spawn_blocking` calls landed on one pooled worker; on CI they did not. I
  confirmed the mechanism with a throwaway probe before changing anything.
- Sealing the home instead deadlocks: the route resolves its config on a
  `spawn_blocking` worker, which is not a member of the test's env scope, so it
  blocks on `lock_test_env` while the sealing test waits on the server. libtest
  has no per-test timeout, so the binary hangs rather than failing.

So the HTTP tests now assert only what one request can prove on its own — and
that is the stronger half anyway, since the read-back happens inside that
request — and the cross-request property moved to the sealed, single-threaded
test where it is deterministic. Re-ran the three 25× plus 12× under
`--test-threads=8` with no failures.

Running these locally needs `RUST_MIN_STACK` (CI sets 8 MiB), otherwise an
unrelated debug-build stack overflow aborts the suite before they run.

## Known limitation (not addressed here)

The route resolves the config path through `config::set_workspace_trust` /
`is_workspace_trusted`, which use the default discovery path — not the
`--config` a runtime may have been launched with. A server started with
`--config /custom/config.toml` therefore records trust in the default document.
That is exactly what the TUI's `/trust on --save` does, so read, write and gate
all agree; making the gate honour a per-runtime override would mean threading a
path through its ~15 call sites, which is a separate change. Flagging it rather
than fixing it half-way, which would be worse: a writer honouring `--config`
with a gate reading the default path is precisely the disagreement the response's
read-back exists to refuse. The consuming extension launches the engine without
`--config`, so it is not affected today.

## Current maintainer correction and gate

The original contribution and its three tests remain. Current main was merged into the original branch without rewriting history. [10d047c1](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/10d047c19246982aa8af4a6b98870d1d05d8d290) corrected both API messages and owning English/Chinese docs to actual trust/context/hook/config boundaries. Default-config discovery remains explicit; project trust does not alter Full Access or external-path grants.

Two maintainer integration errors were then corrected: [3a1eae9f](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/3a1eae9fc9e01c37566849e1930c9d1fa3f43712) keeps the existing feature summary within its120-character contract; [97aac3e](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/97aac3e9694dcd14c80324f0b4572dddb9739801) regenerates its documentation and feature projections with the existing generator. The earlier Ubuntu registry failure and stale-generated-doc web failure remain recorded.

Current exact-head [Web38496306483](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38496306483) passed772Vitest tests, facts/docs validation and build. Native [CI38496306482](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38496306482) completed: macOS19,038/0failed/33skipped, Ubuntu19,035/0/34, Windows18,304passed(oneleaky)/0/27 and Lint. All three trust cases and owner recovery passed on every platform; unique full-suite ordinals and exact source were independently checked. Web772Vitest/facts/docs/build passed. No live authorization or final packaged acceptance is claimed. The source branch/original authored commits and tests remain. This PR merged as itself at [947f670fee](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/947f670fee1aca8ec0cefff329bf36cadf4b9576). Original author commits, three tests and branch are preserved. It is now on main, but not yet folded into the ECD release branch. No release publication or issue closure.

prs.body:
## What and why

`session_control_acceptance::tests::tui_and_api_listings_agree` fails now and then on my Mac:

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: ["charlie", "bravo", "alpha"]
 right: ["bravo"]
```

The test saves its sessions with a workspace under `TempDir`, searches for `brav` and expects only `bravo`. The matcher looks at `title id workspace` and falls back to a subsequence match, so the random `.tmpXXXXXX` part of the path can supply the missing letters. When it does, every session in that workspace matches.

How often depends on the machine's temp path. On my Mac the per-user part of the path already contains `b…r`, so the random part only needs `a…v`: about 1 run in 70 by simulation. Under `/tmp` it is about 1 in 57,000, which is why CI doesn't show it. With `TMPDIR` pointing at a directory named `brav` it fails every time.

`search_sort_and_preview_are_one_projection` in the same file already avoids this, and its comment says why: it pins all three haystack fields. This test now records `/repo` and `/other` as the workspaces, the same way. The session store stays in the private temp directory and the assertions are unchanged.

#5929 put this test's failures down to the redirected `CODEWHALE_HOME` and gave it a private store. It has still failed since then with the output above, which a session written into the store by another test would not produce.

## Issue

Refs #5929

## How I tested it

- With `TMPDIR` set to a directory named `brav`, the test fails on main with the output above and passes with this change. With my normal `TMPDIR` it passes on both.
- The whole `session_control_acceptance` module: 24 passed.
- The 1-in-70 and 1-in-57,000 figures come from a small script that applies the matcher's rule (substring, else subsequence, over the lowercased `title id workspace`) to `.tmp` plus six random alphanumeric characters, 400,000 draws per path.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15247 passed, 46 failed. The same 46 fail on main (2e8bc7bc7) on my machine. Two of them are the command-count checks that 7be1f48a1 has since updated; most of the rest need an extension-host Node version I don't have.

No new tests; this changes the fixture of an existing one.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

issues.body:
### Summary

Upgrading 2026.8.2 → 2026.9.6 silently breaks legitimate `hooks.internal.entries.bootstrap-extra-files` configurations. Two gates in the workspace bootstrap loader (`dist/workspace-*.mjs`, `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) now drop configured paths with only a debug-level diagnostic — no config-time validation, no startup warning, no runtime error:

1. **NEW in 9.6 — basename allowlist:** `VALID_BOOTSTRAP_NAMES = new Set(WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILENAMES)` rejects any configured extra file whose basename is not one of the six standard bootstrap names (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md`), even when the file is inside the agent workspace. Diagnostic: `reason: "invalid-bootstrap-filename", detail: "unsupported bootstrap basename: <name>"`.
2. **Workspace-root guard:** absolute paths outside the agent workspace root (e.g. a shared sibling directory used by several agents) are rejected: `reason: "security", detail: "pattern resolves outside the workspace"`.

Result: configs that loaded fine on 2026.8.2 lose most of their injected bootstrap context after the upgrade, with nothing user-visible. Agents keep running with silently reduced context — this failure mode is very hard to notice from the outside.

### Repro

1. On 2026.9.6, configure:
```json
"hooks": { "internal": { "entries": { "bootstrap-extra-files": { "paths": [
  "memory/PICKUP-BRIEF.md",
  "/abs/path/shared/STATE.md",
  "memory/MEMORY.md"
] } } } }
```
   with all three files existing and readable (`memory/` inside the agent workspace, `/abs/path/shared/` outside it).
2. Start an agent session and inspect injected bootstrap context (or call the loader directly and inspect `{files, diagnostics}`).
3. Observed: only `memory/MEMORY.md` loads. `PICKUP-BRIEF.md` → `invalid-bootstrap-filename`; `/abs/path/shared/STATE.md` → `security`. On 2026.8.2 (with extra-files configured the same way) these loaded.

### Expected

Either of:
- Explicitly configured, non-glob extra paths are honored regardless of basename (the allowlist makes sense for glob expansion, much less for paths the operator wrote out by hand); ideally with an opt-in allowlisted-roots mechanism for shared directories outside the workspace root; **or**
- Config validation rejects/warns on such entries loudly at startup (doctor check + boot-time log at warn level), instead of silently dropping the files per-session at debug level.

### Notes

- `docs/automation/hooks/bundled-hooks.md` documents the basename restriction, so this may be intentional hardening from the recent bootstrap/cron origin work — but there is no migration note, no doctor rule, and no config escape hatch, so existing 8.2 configs degrade silently on upgrade.
- The `.js` → `.mjs` dist rename in 9.6 is incidental but worth noting for anyone tracing the loader.

Version: 2026.9.6 (upgraded from 2026.8.2), macOS arm64, node 24.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A message sent from the Control UI composer while a reply is running is accepted by the Gateway, but within about two seconds the Control UI's stored outbox row flips from `sending` to `waiting-reconnect` on a socket that never closed, so the message shows "Waiting for reconnect" and messages queued behind it can sit in `waiting-idle` without being attempted.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI in a plain browser (reproduced in headless Chromium driven by playwright-core, no extension or injected script).
2. Send a prompt that produces a long reply.
3. While it is replying, send a second message, then a third.
4. Read `sessionStorage["openclaw.control.chatComposer.v4:<gateway>"]`, or look at the queued rows.

Minimal reproduction without a Gateway: the two regression tests in the linked PR write the outbox twice from the same page instance, as the live page does on its next draft or send. On current `main` (dfb6474c538):

```
× chat composer persistence > keeps a sending row in flight when the same page rewrites the outbox
  expected ["in-flight","sending"], received ["in-flight","waiting-reconnect"]
× chat composer persistence > keeps a submitting row in flight when the same page rewrites the outbox
  received ["in-flight","waiting-idle"]
Tests  2 failed | 60 passed (62)
```

### Expected behavior

The second message stays `sending` until the Gateway's receipt retires it, and no reconnect state appears without a reconnect. The Control UI's own disconnect handling (`markQueuedChatSendsWaitingForReconnect`) is the path meant to move an in-flight row to `waiting-reconnect`.

### Actual behavior

The row is stored as `waiting-reconnect` with `sendAttempts: 1` about two seconds after the `chat.send` ack, with zero WebSocket closes. The row then shows "Waiting for reconnect" / "Reconnected before delivery was confirmed. Check the conversation, retry only if your message didn't arrive." for a message the Gateway already has. In the browser run the third message was stored `waiting-idle`, `sendAttempts: 0`, while the second sat in `waiting-reconnect`.

Cause: `normalizeStoredQueueItem` in `ui/src/lib/chat/outbox-store-codec.ts` maps `sending` to `waiting-reconnect` and `submitting` to `waiting-idle`. That is the right replay rule after a reload, but the codec runs on every write (`serializeQueueItem` in `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-queue-serialization.ts`) and every read (`readStoredOutboxStore`), so a live page downgrades its own in-flight send the next time the outbox is written. The existing test "normalizes sending before durable replay" encodes the downgrade within a single page instance, which is why no test tripped.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (eb377ac); still present on `main` at dfb6474c538

### Operating system

Gateway on Linux (containerized); browser client on macOS

### Install method

Docker

### Model

Not model-dependent (Control UI outbox state); observed with an Anthropic model

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> anthropic (direct provider)

### Logs

WebSocket frames from the browser page (credentials redacted), for the second message:

- `chat.send` acked `status: "started"` in 36 ms.
- The next `chat.history` listed it in `pendingInputs` with `state: "queued"` and `runId` equal to the send id.
- The stored row read `waiting-reconnect` at the next sample.
- The transcript later carried it once, with `idempotencyKey: "<send id>:user"`.
- No `close` event on the page socket at any point.

### Impact and severity

Any user who types while a reply is running can see a false reconnect warning on a delivered message and have later queued messages held until something else triggers a drain. Also reproduced in a desktop shell that embeds the same Control UI.

The plugin is enabled without its runtime; the observer logs the "not found … Reinstall or update OpenClaw" line once; the turns themselves run on the embedded runtime's `openai-chatgpt-responses` route without error.

`2026.9.1` (commit `ad6fe23`), the official Docker image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.9.1-browser`

the image's Debian, in Docker on an Ubuntu 24.04 host

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the ChatGPT-subscription sign-in.

`codex agent runtime configured, enabled automatically` at sign-in; `Managed Codex app-server binary was not found for @openai/codex. Reinstall or update OpenClaw…` from the session observer at the first turn.

_No response_

Observed on `2026.9.1`, official `-browser` image, Docker Compose on Ubuntu 24.04.

issues.body:
# Draft — iOS Dashboard after Cloudflare Access sign-in

Based on OpenClaw iOS PR #147244 at `fd060882ebd76d0fdf9597fe046b2ce39db73b2f`.

**Title:** `[Feature]: Open the iOS embedded Dashboard after Cloudflare Access sign-in`

## Summary

Let a paired iOS app open its embedded Dashboard and Settings after a successful Cloudflare Access sign-in, with the same operator authorization and lifecycle controls as native chat.

## Problem to solve

The iOS Cloudflare Access draft resumes native node, operator, chat, and media connections after browser sign-in. However, its own documentation says embedded Dashboard pages and widgets remain unavailable because browser-session support is separate. An operator can connect and chat but cannot use the in-app Dashboard and administrative Settings that are available with an ordinary Gateway connection. This requires switching to an external browser for those tasks.

## Proposed solution

Extend the existing iOS Access ingress/session owner to admit the embedded Control UI after sign-in, without treating a successful native WebSocket connection as proof that the web view is authenticated. Reuse the existing Gateway operator identity, scopes, and device pairing checks; do not introduce a new role model or relax the existing `operator.admin` gate. Bind the web view to the selected Gateway origin and current Access revision. On sign-out, expiry, revocation, account change, or Gateway switch, retire the embedded session and show a clear sign-in/reconnection state. Keep ordinary Gateway routes unchanged.

The precise iOS browser-session handoff and credential lifetime need review before landing. This is not a request to change Gateway roles or create a second authentication policy. Do not solve it by only removing the `ingressAuthorization` UI guard or injecting a long-lived Access token into page JavaScript.

## Alternatives considered

- Leave the native fallback and open the Dashboard in an external authenticated browser: avoids webview session work but does not restore the existing in-app Settings workflow.
- Reuse Safari/IdP cookies implicitly: not a reliable or explicit session contract for an ephemeral WKWebView.
- Pass the native Access credential directly to page scripts: broadens credential exposure and does not establish lifecycle/revocation semantics.

## Impact

Affected: iOS users of Cloudflare Access-protected Gateways who need Dashboard/Settings in the app. Frequency: every such connection after sign-in. Consequence: native chat works while in-app administration and Dashboard pages remain unavailable; operators must switch surfaces.

## Evidence/examples

- Related partial implementation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147244 (draft). Its `docs/platforms/ios.md` explicitly leaves embedded Dashboard browser-session support separate.
- Current UI gates: `apps/ios/Sources/Settings/SettingsHubScreen.swift` and `DashboardPageScreen.swift` at that PR head bypass/replace the Dashboard whenever `ingressAuthorization` is present.
- Existing embedded WebView uses a nonpersistent website data store in `apps/ios/Sources/Web/AuthenticatedControlUIWebView.swift`.
- Live physical-device observation is available privately; sanitized before/after captures should be provided with the implementation. Do not attach private endpoints, identities, session content, or credentials.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, as a dependent PR based on #147244 once the browser-session contract is agreed. Preserve Vincent Koc's existing commits and authorship; add only the new work in the dependent PR.

## Additional information

The foundation #146996 is merged; #147238 and #147244 are still drafts. The dependent PR should base on #147244's branch, not copy its code into a competing PR against `main`. Acceptance proof should include successful Access login, embedded Dashboard/Settings loading with `operator.admin`, correct denial without that scope, origin/account isolation, expiry/revocation/sign-out, unchanged ordinary routes, and inspected sanitized before/after iPhone screenshots.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A native one-shot Codex run completes its work and final response, but OpenClaw returns an error because client cleanup cannot be confirmed. The same cleanup failure later occurred after a real-work run had already saved its completed deliverables.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.6 using the existing Codex integration.  
2. Start a one-shot agent run using the native OpenAI/Codex route.  
3. Allow the run to execute a harmless native command and complete its final response.  
4. Observe that the command and model work complete, but the outer run terminates with the cleanup error shown below.  
5. A later real-work run independently saved its completed deliverables before producing the same cleanup error.

### Expected behavior

After the work and native processes belonging to the one-shot run are verifiably settled, OpenClaw should preserve the completed result and terminate successfully. If cleanup genuinely cannot be confirmed, it should preserve that uncertainty without losing or misrepresenting the completed work.

### Actual behavior

The work completes, but the outer command returns an error:  
Agent exec cleanup failed: Agent runtime cleanup did not settle; state ownership retained until this process exits  
The associated cleanup diagnostic reports:  
Codex one-shot client cleanup could not be confirmed  
The same cleanup failure was subsequently observed after another run had already saved its completed deliverables.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6

### Operating system

macOS

### Install method

npm

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> Codex integration -> OpenAI via existing subscription OAuth

### Additional provider/model setup details

Requested model: openai/gpt-6-astra, High effort. The preserved investigated installation used @openclaw/codex 2026.9.6 with bridge-managed @openai/codex 0.155.1. No API/PAYG fallback was used for the investigated route.

### Logs

```shell
Agent exec cleanup failed: Agent runtime cleanup did not settle; state ownership retained until this process exits

[agent/embedded] agent cleanup failed:
step=codex-shared-client-release
error=Codex one-shot client cleanup could not be confirmed
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

A preserved minimal reproduction and a later real-work occurrence both exhibit the same cleanup failure. Private evidence contains the original command, source excerpts, hashes, and run identities. These are intentionally not attached because they contain private project/environment information. Sanitized excerpts can be supplied if maintainers identify specific evidence needed.

### Impact and severity

Affected: native one-shot OpenClaw runs through the Codex integration.
Severity: Moderate operational/reliability defect; completed work can be reported as an overall failed run because cleanup cannot be confirmed.
Frequency: observed in the preserved minimal reproduction and again in a later real-work run; broader frequency is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.
Consequence: callers cannot reliably distinguish completed work with unresolved cleanup from a genuinely failed task, complicating automation and potentially causing unnecessary retries.

### Additional information

This is not being reported as a confirmed regression; last-known-good version is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. Prior investigation found that the obvious sandbox process-owner path does not establish coverage of the observed ordinary native route, so no local behavioral patch was applied.  
Upstream PR #159841 addresses unsandboxed terminal cleanup on cancellation/activation failure, but inspection did not establish that it fixes successful one-shot closure. Current upstream source also retains an explicit uncertain-cleanup result after native execution.  
Requested direction: identify the smallest supported existing native settlement mechanism that the one-shot close path should await, or the owning upstream correction if no such mechanism currently covers this route. We are not requesting that cleanup uncertainty simply be suppressed.

issues.body:
# sessions.reset leaves the conversation permanently undeliverable: route ownership reports "unavailable" forever, restart does not clear it

**Version** — 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows, npm global install, gateway as a Windows Scheduled Task. Channel: Feishu (websocket).
This is a follow-up in kind to #157142: the same wedged session, but this one is about what the *repair* did.

## What happened

A session was stuck in `state=processing` (see #157142: swarm group with 5 `failed` children, `sessions.abort` → `no-active-run`, `sessions.recover` refused). The only call that cleared the stall was:

```
sessions.reset {"key": "<agent>:feishu:direct:<peer>"}   →  {"ok": true, "entry": {"sessionId": "...", "lifecycleRevision": "..."}}
```

The stall logging stopped immediately, and `/healthz` went back to 3–9 ms. **But every inbound message to that conversation has been undeliverable ever since** (ongoing for ~1 h at time of writing):

```
feishu[<agent>]: received message from <peer> in <chat> (p2p)
feishu[<agent>]: dispatching to agent (session=<agent>:feishu:direct:<peer>)
feishu[<agent>]: failed to dispatch message: SessionWorkStartChangedError: Conversation binding owner changed while preparing the reply. Retry the message.
feishu[<agent>]: inbound debounce flush failed: SessionWorkStartChangedError: ...
```

The error says "Retry the message"; the user retried 5 times over 5 minutes — every attempt fails identically. So this is a durable state, not a race.

## What I traced

`sessions.reset` is out as a cure (it is the cause). The other two paths are refused:
- `sessions.recover` → `Session recovery requires a restart-tombstoned session.`
- `sessions.assignOwner` → requires an `owner` value that we could not derive from anything documented (`{"key": "..."}` alone is rejected: `must have required property 'owner'`).

The refusal itself comes from the route-ownership eligibility check, and it is agent-scoped — the control group is clean:

```
conversations.list {agentId: <affected agent>}   → error: Conversation route ownership is temporarily unavailable   (errorCode=UNAVAILABLE)
conversations.list {agentId: <other agent A>}     → ok
conversations.list {agentId: <other agent B>}     → ok
conversations.list {agentId: <other agent C>}     → ok
```

In `conversation-route-ownership-*.mjs`:

```js
const pluginOwner = resolvePluginRouteOwner(params.config, params.conversation);
if (pluginOwner) {
  if (pluginOwner.kind === "unavailable") return "unavailable";   // ← we land here
  ...
```

and `resolvePluginRouteOwner` calls the channel plugin's `getLoadedChannelPlugin(channelId)?.messaging?.resolveConversationRouteOwner({cfg, accountId, conversation})` — i.e. **our channel plugin is the one answering `{kind: "unavailable"}` for this one conversation**, while answering fine for other conversations on the same channel/host.

A full cold restart of the gateway (2026.9.6, scheduled task, `/healthz=200` after 15 min, 9/9 channels `running+connected`) did **not** clear it: the first `conversations.list` after startup returns the same `UNAVAILABLE`, and the bindings are unchanged.

## Data observations (read-only, on a copy)

- The affected agent's `session_conversations` table holds **10+ rows with `role='primary'` for the same `conversation_id`**, accumulated across resets/`/new`s, most recent pointing at the session id that was reset.
- The same DM peer also has **two `conversations` rows under different `account_id` values** (`account_id='default'` and `account_id='<agent>'`).
- The shared-state `current_conversation_bindings` table is **empty (0 rows)** host-wide.
- The agent's `conversation_deliveries` table is empty after the restart (the queued reply from before the restart is gone), so nothing is silently "in flight".

## What I would like to know

1. Should `sessions.reset` clear or re-point the conversation's route ownership / binding owner? Right now the documented repair for a wedged session moves the conversation into a state where **no** inbound can be dispatched, and none of `abort`/`recover`/`reset`/restart escapes it.
2. Is there a supported repair for `route ownership: unavailable` — an RPC that takes the *conversation* (channel + accountId + peer/thread) rather than a caller-supplied `owner` we have to guess? If `sessions.assignOwner` is the intended door, what is a valid `owner` value (or a read RPC that returns it)?
3. Minor: should `conversations.list` distinguish "this agent has no binding for that conversation" from "ownership is temporarily unavailable"? The second wording sent us chasing a race for an hour.

Happy to run any probe you suggest on the affected host, and to attach whatever log lines you want — the agent/conversation in question is not needed for the report, so I have kept it anonymous.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Usage → **Started by** reports substantial identifiable scheduled usage as **Unattributed**, while **System** shows zero tokens. Existing cron sessions lack creator metadata, and the usage projection has no attribution for those sessions despite surviving metadata identifying their cron origin.

This is an observed attribution/legacy-data compatibility gap, not a claim that newly created cron sessions always lose attribution. The lifecycle stage responsible for missing metadata has not been established.

## Exact observed reconciliation

Date range: **2026-08-26 through 2026-09-24 inclusive**, Australia/Sydney. Read-only inspection of stored usage rollups reproduces every displayed session count, token total and rounded cost:

| Started by | Sessions | Tokens | Cost shown |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared owner | 9 | 31,091,998 | $49.80 |
| Unattributed | 80 | 21,958,218 | $37.48 |
| main (agent) | 2 | 2,561,343 | $2.01 |
| System | 2 | 0 | $0.00 |

The **21,958,218 unattributed tokens** break down as:

| Identified workload | Tokens |
|---|---:|
| Daily memory-maintenance cron | 7,202,105 |
| Weekly memory-review cron | 2,874,879 |
| Release-check cron | 3,118,272 |
| Two recovery cron jobs | 529,218 |
| One deleted dashboard session | 8,054,776 |
| Other sessions | 178,968 |

**62 cron instances account for 13,724,474 tokens and $14.94448776**—62.5% of the Unattributed bucket. Those are identifiable scheduled sessions, not unexplained model requests. Two newer sessions with explicit `createdActor.type = "system"` are recognized as System, but have zero cached tokens.

## Evidence and mechanism

- The existing daily/weekly memory and release-check session nodes have no `createdActor` or `createdVia` in their stored entries.
- `session_windows` / `session_transcript_archives` metadata still identifies cron-origin session keys, including historical instances.
- The deployed usage projection reads `session.storeEntry ?? session.creatorEntry`, then `entry?.createdActor`. If the actor is missing it immediately returns the unknown creator bucket: [projectUsageCreator in v2026.9.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts#L118).
- Historical attribution depends on available current/family creator metadata. Identifiable historical usage can consequently remain unattributed.
- The deleted dashboard session contributes another 8,054,776 tokens / $22.295539. Its session key survives in archive metadata, but its creator was not recoverable from the records inspected. This is a related historical-attribution preservation concern, **not evidence that it should automatically be assigned to the owner**.

Inspection used cached `session-cost-usage-rollup-v3` records, session-node/window/archive metadata, and filename-based archive-cache mapping. No transcript message bodies were read, no cache rebuild was triggered, and no production state was changed. This reconciles the displayed cache snapshot; it does not certify completeness against provider billing.

## Observed reproduction path

1. On an upgraded installation with existing scheduled-session history, open Usage for a range containing cron runs.
2. Observe Started by → Unattributed despite identifiable cron activity; System may show zero.
3. Inspect the corresponding session entries: `createdActor` is absent, while persisted session metadata identifies their cron origin.
4. Sum their cached usage in the same date range and compare with the Unattributed bucket.

This was reproduced/reconciled on an existing installation. A fresh-install synthetic reproduction and a precise first-affected release have **not** been established.

## Expected behaviour / suggested investigation

- Preserve explicit session-creation attribution for scheduled work, including across reset, archival and deletion where usage history is retained.
- Establish whether this case requires a legacy-data migration/backfill, a current writer/lifecycle repair, or both.
- Where trustworthy persisted scheduler provenance exists, resolve scheduled work consistently with the explicit System attribution path. Do not blindly infer human ownership, or turn arbitrary user-controlled session-key text into trusted identity.
- Keep genuinely unknown historical creators unknown; ideally explain missing legacy attribution in the UI.

Useful regression coverage: creatorless legacy cron history; new cron creation/execution/reset; archival/deletion with retained usage; genuinely unknown history; and unchanged aggregate token/cost totals after attribution repair.

## Separate from usage ingestion failures

Related deployment also has usage-refresh worker heap-exhaustion report #156898. This issue is intentionally narrower: the usage above is **already present in stored rollups**, but its creator projection is unknown. A failed refresh is not required to explain that projection. We have not proven a shared cause or causal independence of their histories, and missing main-session usage is not part of this issue's reproduction claim.

issues.body:
## Problem

The whole point of using Agents is automation. After upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.9.5, **everything related to credential/secret entry still requires the user to do manual work** — defeating the Agent's purpose.

We hit this in a single 30-minute session trying to install Fusion 360 on a remote Windows host:

- Agent SSHes, downloads, installs, reports back: not possible
- Agent asks user to run PowerShell commands on the remote box
- Agent asks user to fill a masked UI popup to give a credential
- Agent asks user to save a key in Mac Keychain via GUI
- Agent asks user to submit a GitHub issue manually

**The Agent keeps pushing work back to the user. What's the point of having an Agent?**

## Two real complaints

### 1. Manual operation problem

What I expect from an Agent:
- I say "install Fusion 360 on 算力-2"
- Agent auto-SSHes, downloads installer, silently installs, reports back

What actually happens after 9.5:
- Agent asks me to run PowerShell commands
- Agent asks me to fill things in via masked UI popup
- Agent asks me to save things in Mac Keychain (manual GUI)
- Agent asks me to submit GitHub issue manually

**The Agent keeps pushing work back to me. What's the point of having an Agent?**

### 2. Black box problem

When I try to give the Agent a password/token via the recommended channels:
- I type into the masked UI popup — but I can't see what I typed, so I don't know if I got it right. Three of these prompts in a row failed (same value, same prompt) and the secret store seemed to accept them all but produce wrong values downstream
- The secret store is write-only from the Agent side — I have no way to verify what's stored, no list view, no fingerprint
- WebChat auto-masks credential-shaped content — I don't even know what I sent, the agent sometimes never receives the value
- When the Agent uses a stored credential and it fails, I can't tell if it's because the typed value was wrong, because the store mangled it, or because the server rejected it

**Three layers of opacity stacked on top of each other. I have no end-to-end visibility.**

## Steps to reproduce (representative)

1. Set up an Agent that needs an SSH credential to a remote Windows host (算力-2 / 192.168.3.101)
2. Try to provide the credential via masked UI popup, `secrets action=request`
3. The popup hides the typed value; submit and confirm
4. Have the Agent run an automation that uses the stored credential to SSH
5. Observe: authentication fails server-side with `Permission denied`
6. Try to diagnose: openclaw secrets store is write-only — no way to read what was saved
7. Try the masked UI again three more times with what user is certain is the same value
8. Each time `Stored` is reported, but the actual stored value appears to differ (or the value used in diagnostic is mangled)
9. Try to switch to a public-key approach to bypass the masked UI — Agent asks user to run PowerShell commands, edit NTFS ACLs, uncomment sshd_config lines, restart services
10. Try to send the new PAT via WebChat so the Agent can submit this GitHub issue — auto-masked, agent never sees it

## Expected behavior

A user providing a credential to an Agent via the masked UI should be able to:
- See what they typed (character count at minimum, ideally masked-echo like `••••••`)
- Verify after submit what was actually stored (fingerprint / length / last-4-chars)
- Have the Agent actually automate the workflow that uses the credential

A user messaging an Agent via WebChat should be able to:
- Tell when content was auto-masked and why
- Disable auto-mask for explicitly-flagged credential payloads (e.g. in a code block, or with a `/no-mask` prefix)
- Have the Agent see the original value without round-tripping through a popup

## Actual behavior

- Masked UI: zero feedback on input. Three sequential prompts with what user is certain is the same value produced three different downstream outcomes.
- Secret store: write-only from the Agent side. No `list`, no `get`, no `verify` against `allowedHosts`. After upgrade, overrides are reported successful but actual stored value appears stale or mangled.
- WebChat: `password/token/secret` shaped content is auto-masked before the Agent sees it. User has no visibility into whether masking was applied or not. Confirmed by sending the same content via webchat vs direct shell — webchat version never reaches the Agent.
- Agent workflow: must include explicit user actions in every step (run X, fill Y, save Z, submit W). Agent cannot run end-to-end on its own.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)** — fresh upgrade from 9.4
- macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)
- Node v26.8.1
- Channels affected: WebChat, feishu (xiaofeng bot), secret store
- Single user / single host scenario, but reproducible in any setup that requires credential handoff to an Agent

## Impact

- **Single-user productivity**: blocked for hours on what should be a 30-second operation. Direct quote from user: "OpenCloud 9.5 密码机制真的烦死了，真的逼得我想自己去做自己的 Agent 系统了"
- **Multi-user teams**: Worse — every team member faces the same friction, no admin can debug their issues
- **Production**: makes secret rotation, cross-host automation, and self-service deployment nearly impossible

## Suggested improvements (any of these would help)

1. **Masked UI**: show character count, show last-typed-value-with-confirmation pattern (like 1Password / Bitwarden), show a fingerprint after submit so the user can verify
2. **Secret store**: add `openclaw secrets list` showing what's stored (fingerprint only, not value); add `openclaw secrets verify <name>` that runs a sanity check against `allowedHosts`; add a `last-overridden-at` timestamp
3. **WebChat / messaging**: add a `/no-mask` prefix or fenced-code-block opt-out for explicit credential payloads; show a small indicator when content was auto-masked
4. **Agent automation**: provide a documented, programmatic API for Agents to handle credentials without going through interactive masked UI popups (e.g. read from OS keychain, read from a SecretRefs config field, write to a temp file with explicit user consent)
5. **Diagnostic surface**: when a stored credential fails at use site, return actionable detail ("stored value starts with 'ghp_***AB' but server expects format X" instead of just "Permission denied")

## Type

Bug + Feature Request

## Related

- #155347 (9.5 monitor heartbeats wedged into 'running' state) — suggests 9.5 upgrade landed with multiple rough edges
- #155371 (9.4 → 9.5 candidate doctor crashes with `import.meta` error) — same theme
- Search results: 24414 issues mention `password|credential|masked|mask|secret` in title/body, but **none describe this specific 3-layer black box from an Agent-autonomy perspective** — this appears to be the first such report

---

Filed by: 小蜂 🐝 (xiaofeng agent) on behalf of human operator
Operator note: "现在敲的密码对不对我都不知道，存了多少密码我也不知道，密码是什么我也不知道。这是啥狗屁黑箱啊，两眼一抹黑！"

issues.body: ### Bug type Regression (worked before, now fails) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary On 2026.9.1 (Windows 11, Norton 360 at defaults, Behavioral Protection on) every start of the gateway through the "OpenClaw Gateway" scheduled task that we made died or hung; each failure coincided with Norton terminating a powershell.exe child under "IDP.HELU.PSE90 - Command line detection"; the only PowerShell + csc.exe spawn in the package is the Windows private-directory / plan-file ACL step that runs `powershell -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand …` with `Add-Type -TypeDefinition -Language CSharp` inside; one start made during a 10-minute Behavioral Protection pause came up healthy; 2026.7.1-2 on the same machine runs with no detection. 2026.9.2 ships the same three call sites at the same lines. ### Steps to reproduce Machine: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node v24.20.0, Norton 360 (AV module 26.8.11125 build .993, installer 26.8.11504.0, definitions 260905-6), Behavioral Protection ON (default). Gateway registered by `openclaw gateway install` (Scheduled Task "OpenClaw Gateway" + Startup .vbs). 1. Start state: 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), npm -g, gateway task running; it had run beside Norton at defaults since June with no Behavioral Protection card noticed (Norton History not reviewed for earlier dates). 2. `openclaw update` (elevated PowerShell) -> 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23). Doctor ran twice and passed; the updater's own restart step reported the gateway did not become healthy ("restart-unhealthy") and the updater still ended with `Result: OK` (303.9 s). During that restart step (18:17) Norton showed the first card ("Last Used 05/09/2026 18:17"). 3. `openclaw gateway restart` at 19:03 and 19:11: task exits within seconds, nothing listening on the gateway port; no card seen for these two. 4. Pause Behavioral Protection for 10 minutes; `openclaw gateway restart` at 19:15:54 -> the task-launched gateway CAME UP: node process created 19:16:04, port listening, `gateway status --deep` at 19:18:44 = `Runtime: running`, probe ok. 5. Pause expires; card at 19:26 while that gateway was still up (powershell.exe, conhost.exe, csc.exe Terminated, temp file Deleted). `openclaw gateway restart` 19:44 -> task dies, card. 6. Add Norton Antivirus > Exclusions for the npm package folder and %USERPROFILE%\.openclaw; `openclaw gateway restart` 20:22 -> task dies; card: powershell.exe Terminated, conhost.exe Terminated, csc.exe (…\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe) Terminated, a temp file Deleted; "Last Used 20:22". 7. Add a process exclusion for C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe with "Behavioral Protection detections" and "Apply to Auto-Protect" checked; `openclaw gateway restart` 21:14 -> failure mode changes: 9 x powershell.exe Terminated in that one start, `__PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1` in %TEMP% Deleted, no csc.exe row; the task now STAYS RUNNING — `status --deep`: `Runtime: running (last run 267009)`, port never opens, probe ECONNREFUSED, two node.exe alive. 8. `npm install -g openclaw@2026.7.1-2` (21:30): one more card during the install (the 9.1 service stop/register hook). Restore pre-update `openclaw.json`, `state\openclaw.sqlite` (schema 1) and `agents\main\agent\openclaw-agent.sqlite` (schema 1); `gateway install --force`; `restart` -> 22:17:50 `Runtime: running`, probe ok; no card since. Not tested separately: a logon-triggered start. `openclaw gateway run --force` in a visible shell reached ready at 18:26:57; that path does not pass `--task-supervisor`, so whether the ACL step runs in it was not checked. ### Expected behavior The gateway starts from the scheduled task with Norton at defaults, as 2026.7.1-2 does on the same machine. 2026.7.1-2's dist contains no `Add-Type` (grep: 0 files). Its Windows ACL code is icacls-based: read-only `icacls.exe /sid` inspection (dist/permissions-*.js) and a reset `icacls "" /inheritance:r /grant:r :F` — `(OI)(CI)F` for directories (permissions-*.js:380) — executed from `openclaw security audit --fix` (dist/security-cli-*.js). Whether any ACL step runs at gateway start on 7.1-2 was not checked. 7.1-2 depends on @openclaw/fs-safe 0.4.1. ### Actual behavior Two failure modes, both only with Norton Behavioral Protection active: (a) Before the powershell.exe exclusion (18:20, 18:59, 19:03, 19:11, 19:44, 20:22): the task-launched process exits 0 within seconds; nothing listening; for the 18:59:25 launch it was measured that the gateway's file log contains no line from the task-launched process (it dies before the file logger initialises). Norton History, filtered to "Behavioral Protection", shows dozens of entries titled powershell (IDP.HELU.PSE90%s_cmd) detected by Behavioral Protection — Status "Repaired" in two clusters (the 18:17 update window; 20:22–21:14) — one entry per killed PowerShell spawn. The 18:17 entry verbatim: Details: Threat name IDP.HELU.PSE90 - Command line detection · Threat type Miscellaneous · Status Repaired · Detected by Behavioral Protection · On PC from 14/07/2026, 18:53 · Last Used 05/09/2026, 18:17 · Startup Item Yes · reputation "Many users", "Mature — released 2 months ago", "High — the file risk is high" Activity: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe | Process | Infected <32-hex hash> | File | Infected The reputation fields describe powershell.exe itself (its CreationTime on this machine is 14/07/2026 18:53:26, file version 10.0.26100.8972 — the Windows binary as replaced by a July update). Quarantine stays empty. (b) With the powershell.exe process exclusion in place (21:14): the task-launched process no longer exits — `status --deep` reports `Runtime: running`, the port never opens, two node.exe stay alive; Norton shows 9 powershell.exe terminations for that single start and deletes PowerShell's own `__PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1` probe files, i.e. PowerShell is killed at its own launch before any script runs. Control: the one start made while Behavioral Protection was paused (19:15:54) reached ready and stayed up until the next restart. ### OpenClaw version 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), npm -g, reached via `openclaw update` from 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f). 2026.9.2 tarball inspected (not run): identical Add-Type call sites at identical lines; @openclaw/fs-safe 0.8.1. ### Operating system Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200; Node v24.20.0; Norton 360 AV module 26.8.11125 (build 26.8.11125.993), installer 26.8.11504.0, virus definitions 260905-6, Behavioral Protection ON ### Install method npm install -g openclaw / openclaw update; gateway via openclaw gateway install (Scheduled Task + Startup .vbs) ### Model a local Ollama model. Not relevant: the process dies before any model is loaded. ### Provider / routing chain ollama (local) only; one messaging channel; gateway bound to loopback on the default port ### Additional provider/model setup details _No response_ ### Logs ```shell %USERPROFILE%\.openclaw\logs\gateway-restart.log, verbatim (first 10 lines: the updater's restarts, stamped local +01:00; the rest: CLI restarts stamped Z = local-1h): [2026-09-05T18:20:35.4424752+01:00] openclaw restart log initialized [2026-09-05T18:20:35.4767948+01:00] openclaw restart attempt source=update target=OpenClaw Gateway [2026-09-05T18:20:36.6986634+01:00] openclaw restart skipped schtasks end source=update state=Ready [2026-09-05T18:20:37.5874868+01:00] SUCCESS: Attempted to run the scheduled task "OpenClaw Gateway". start (Behavioral Protection paused) [2026-09-05T18:44:16.351Z] openclaw gateway lifecycle source=cli action=restart mode=schtasks-end interactive=1 [2026-09-05T18:44:18.418Z] openclaw gateway lifecycle source=cli action=restart mode=schtasks-restart interactive=1 [2026-09-05T19:22:45.129Z] openclaw gateway lifecycle source=cli action=restart mode=schtasks-end interactive=1
