mode=schtasks-end interactive=1 [2026-09-05T20:14:12.430Z] openclaw gateway lifecycle source=cli action=restart mode=schtasks-restart interactive=1 <- the hang Add-Type call sites — identical in the 2026.9.1 package (measured on the installed copy before the rollback) and the 2026.9.2 tarball (npm pack, measured): dist/sqlite-readonly-location-*.js:155 "Add-Type -TypeDefinition $nativeSource -Language CSharp" region src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.ts dist/secret-ref-runtime-*.js:467 "Add-Type -TypeDefinition $payload.nativeSource -Language CSharp" (private plan file) dist/update-command-service-*.js:438 Add-Type -TypeDefinition $nativeSource -Language CSharp -ErrorAction Stop (restart script; wrapped in try/catch, logs "native ownership helper unavailable") dist/worker/worker.mjs bundled copy of the first How the first one is invoked (sqlite-private-directory, 2026.9.2): args = ["-NoLogo", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-EncodedCommand", ] script = $ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; $path=; $nativeSource=; Add-Type -TypeDefinition $nativeSource -Language CSharp; build a DirectorySecurity (protected, owner = current user, ACEs for current user, S-1-5-18, S-1-5-32-544, OI/CI); $sddl = …GetSecurityDescriptorSddlForm; [OpenClawPrivateDirectory]::Create($path, $sddl) on any error: throw new Error("Unable to create private Windows SQLite directory: …", { cause: "PowerShell failed (status=…)" }) — no fallback, no opt-out env flag found. Non-Windows path: fs.mkdirSync(dir, { mode: 0o700 }). The update-command-service restart script additionally runs `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "... Invoke-Expression ..."` (line 228), which is the same class of command line. `openclaw gateway status --deep` outputs for 9.1 exist only as notes (paraphrased under Actual behavior); a verbatim capture and an OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1 log of a task-launched start can be supplied on request (needs a 9.x reinstall run inside a Behavioral Protection pause window). ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence Attached: Norton History filtered to "Behavioral Protection" (two shots, the two clusters); the 18:17 entry, Details tab and Activity tab; the "Add exclusion" dialog for powershell.exe with both checkboxes checked. The 21:14 entry is transcribed above (9 rows "powershell.exe | Process | Terminated", plus "__PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1 | File | Deleted"); no image kept. ### Impact and severity On a consumer Windows machine with Norton at defaults, 2026.9.1 cannot run as a service: every task start we made was killed or hung, and `openclaw update` left the machine in that state with `Result: OK`. Workarounds are a version rollback (losing SecretRefs, exact-operation permissions, durable Allow-Always, the 9.x update flow) or turning Behavioral Protection off system-wide. Norton's exclusions (folder; process with "Behavioral Protection detections") did not stop the detection; the process exclusion changed the failure from exit to hang. ### Additional information Measured vs inferred - Measured: the three Add-Type call sites (9.1 installed copy, 9.2 tarball); the Norton cards at 18:17, 19:26, 19:44, 20:22, 21:14 and one during the 7.1-2 npm install; the healthy start at 19:15:54 under a Behavioral Protection pause; exit-0 with no log line (18:59:25 launch); the hang with 9 terminations after the powershell.exe exclusion (21:14); 7.1-2 dist with 0 Add-Type and icacls-based ACL code; 7.1-2 running since 22:17:50 on the same machine with no card. - Inferred: that the terminated PowerShell child is what makes the task-launched node process exit or hang (the sqlite-private-directory path throws on any PowerShell failure, but no stack trace was captured). That the task's logon trigger fails the same way (only CLI/updater restarts were observed). That a running 9.1 gateway re-runs the step later (the 19:26 card came while the 19:15 gateway was up). That "Command line detection" keys on the command line, so path exclusions have nothing to match. - Not measured: 2026.8.x (SecretRef runtime introduced in 8.1); running 2026.9.2; whether `gateway run --force` executes the ACL step. Why the icacls path was probably left - #89223 "SecretRef file provider broken on Windows 11 26200": `icacls /sid` fails (exit 87) on this OS build; closed as not planned. #120211 "fix(secrets): preserve Windows ACL diagnostics" (merged 8 Aug 2026) moves inspection to @openclaw/fs-safe "native inspection". The Add-Type step looks like the replacement for that broken read; but the write side never needed `/sid`: `icacls "" /inheritance:r /grant:r ":(OI)(CI)F" "*S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F" "*S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F"` expresses the same DACL the C# helper builds, without PowerShell or a compiler. Not one vendor's heuristic - openai/codex#25425 and openai/codex#32331: Norton kills PowerShell spawned by the Codex Windows app, same detection family, open since May 2026. - Norton Community 525211 (Android Studio, Microsoft tooling; IDP.HELU.PSE79–81, Jun–Jul 2026) and 528250 (IDP.HELU.PSE90, 1 Sep 2026): file/process exclusions ineffective; nothing but Behavioral Protection off reported to work. - `-EncodedCommand` + `Add-Type` compiling C# through csc.exe into %TEMP% is the pattern behavioural AV is built to stop; a legitimate app doing it at every start will keep hitting it. Ask - No runtime C# compilation and no `-EncodedCommand` PowerShell at gateway start on Windows: icacls for the DACL write (7.x already ships the helper), a prebuilt signed helper or N-API binding, or a config/env opt-out for the native ACL hardening. - The private-directory step should fail soft (log + fall back to `mkdir` + icacls) instead of throwing and taking the gateway down; the restart script already does this ("native ownership helper unavailable"). - Separate issue, not this one: `openclaw update` treating "gateway not healthy after restart" as a failed update (the 9.1 note's rollback triggers on Doctor failure, and Doctor passed here). Related: #120211, #89223, #41804 (Windows scheduled-task launcher). Other Windows/Norton users: please add your Norton AV-module version, OpenClaw version, the "Threat name" / "Detected by" lines from Norton History (filter: Behavioral Protection), whether an exclusion with "Behavioral Protection detections" checked changed anything, and whether the task exits or hangs.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An empty legacy `auth_profile_store` table in the per-agent SQLite makes every agent request fail with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED, while dropping that same table makes startup migrations fail and the gateway refuse to become ready, so no database state satisfies both checks.

### Steps to reproduce

Starting state (observed on our install): `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` has table `auth_profile_store` with one row `('primary', '{"version":1,"profiles":{}}')` — an empty profile set. `state/openclaw.sqlite` has four `auth-profile-v2:*` rows in `migration_runs` marked `completed`, whose `report_json.targetTable` is `auth_profile_stores`, but that table does not exist in the database.
1. Send any message to the agent. Every request fails with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, and separately `openclaw doctor --fix --force` (offline, container stopped). Both report `Failed relocating the shared auth store: shared auth credential rows conflict with the relocation target` and only archive the legacy JSON again. Requests still fail.
3. Delete the single row from `auth_profile_store`, leaving the table. Requests still fail with the same error, so the block is triggered by the table existing, not by its content.
4. Drop the `auth_profile_store` table. `openclaw models auth list` now works for the first time, but the gateway refuses to start: `OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.` / `Skipped historical transcript directive migration ... SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical ... missing table auth_profile_store` / `OpenClaw exited with code 1`.
5. Recreate `auth_profile_store` empty and create `auth_profile_stores` in the state DB with one row `('shared', '{"version":1,"profiles":{}}')`. The gateway boots and reports ready, but requests fail again with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
6. Delete the four `auth-profile-v2:*` rows from `migration_runs`, plus the orphaned `migration_sources` rows. `doctor --fix` now performs a real migration (`Migrated auth profile JSON for ...`) but ends with `Failed relocating the shared auth store: shared auth state rows conflict with the relocation target`. Requests still fail.

### Expected behavior

A legacy store holding an empty profile set (`"profiles":{}`) should be treated as having nothing to migrate and retired, letting requests proceed. When a `migration_runs` receipt is marked `completed` but its `targetTable` does not exist, `doctor --fix` should be able to reconcile that state rather than reporting a relocation conflict on every run. Before the legacy store entered this state, this same install answered Telegram messages normally on the same config and credentials.

### Actual behavior

100% of agent requests fail. The gateway reports ready and Telegram polling runs normally, but each inbound message produces, in the gateway log: `lane task error: lane=main ... error="Couldn't sign in to deepseek. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. ... (Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.) | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED"`, then `Embedded agent failed before reply`, and the user receives only the generic fallback "Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session." The fallback model is attempted and fails identically, so the failure is independent of the provider. `openclaw models auth list --agent main` fails with the same error, so there is no CLI path to inspect or repair the profiles. Docker reports the container as `healthy` throughout. This has been ongoing for over two weeks; each `doctor --fix` run buys a shorter working window than the last (from ~30-90 minutes down to a single message) and leaves another `auth-profiles.json.migrated-*` archive behind (14 accumulated so far).

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2 (0965053)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (container), host Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on a KVM VPS

### Install method

docker (image ghcr.io/hostinger/hvps-openclaw:latest, docker compose)

### Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, fallback openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek (direct), fallback openclaw -> openrouter

### Additional provider/model setup details

Four agents are configured (main, claude, gpt, gemini); the failing one is main. Both providers are custom OpenAI-completions-compatible entries under `models.providers` in openclaw.json with inline API keys, so the working credentials never lived in the auth profile store that is blocking them — the store being migrated is empty. The `migration_runs` receipts reference archive paths such as `/data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-<timestamp>-<uuid>`. The `auth_profile_state` table in the same per-agent DB holds only provider usage stats (a DeepSeek billing cooldown), and it is that table which produces the "shared auth state rows conflict" in step 6.

### Logs

```shell
Per-message failure (gateway log, timestamps local -04:00):
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=32 error="Couldn't sign in to deepseek. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. Run `openclaw models auth login --provider deepseek` or `openclaw configure`. (Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.) | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED"
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash candidate=openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free reason=auth next=none detail=Couldn't sign in to openrouter ... | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
Embedded agent failed before reply: Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.
[diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=telegram ... outcome=error

doctor --fix / --fix --force (steps 2 and 5):
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Failed relocating the shared auth store: Error: shared auth credential rows conflict with the relocation target
Doctor changes: Archived a previously migrated legacy auth source without replaying credentials (~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-...).

Gateway refusing to start with the table dropped (step 4):
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Skipped historical transcript directive migration for /data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: Error: SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for /data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: missing table auth_profile_store
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the same state/config, then restart the gateway.
WARN: OpenClaw exited with code 1

doctor --fix after clearing the receipts (step 6):
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Failed relocating the shared auth store: Error: shared auth state rows conflict with the relocation target
Migrated auth profile JSON for ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-2026-09-08T02-36-43...

Foreign key breakage when receipts are deleted without their sources:
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: SQLite foreign_key_check failed for /data/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite: migration_sources row 1 references migration_runs (foreign key 0); ... row 4 ...
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: all Telegram users of this deployment; the main agent on a self-hosted Docker install.
Severity: High — the agent cannot answer any message, and no supported CLI path can repair it (the auth commands are gated behind the same error).
Frequency: Always, on every inbound message, for over two weeks.
Consequence: The assistant is unusable in production. Docker still reports the container as healthy, so the outage is invisible without reading gateway logs, and the end user only ever sees "Something went wrong while processing your request."

### Additional information

Copies of both SQLite databases were taken before any modification, so the original broken state can be reproduced or shared on request. Steps 3 to 6 were manual database edits made only after the supported paths (`doctor --fix`, `doctor --fix --force`, `gateway stop --force` followed by `doctor --fix`, and plain container restarts) had all been exhausted; they are reported here as diagnostic evidence of the contradiction, not as a recommended workaround. Related but distinct: #41634 (legacy auth profiles accumulate and cannot be cleaned up) describes the same accumulation of archived profile files that we see (14 and counting), though it does not cover the migration deadlock above.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let one task own a set of independent repository worktrees, with a combined Review view, recovery of the repository set, and linked pull requests. A developer should be able to ask for one coordinated frontend/backend/SDK change and review it as one task while retaining each repository's own Git history and publication state.

This is a follow-up design proposal for the managed recovery and publication explicitly excluded from #142521's initial ephemeral-workspace scope. If maintainers prefer to track both contracts there, this proposal can be consolidated into that discussion.

### Problem to solve

Consider adding an API field that requires changes in three repositories:

- `backend`: implement the field and its tests;
- `sdk`: update the client types;
- `frontend`: consume the field and run the application against the changed backend.

The repositories must be available together for integration testing, but the developer also needs separate branches, diffs, and PRs. A single task should keep track of that relationship through review and restart.

Agents can already use ordinary tools to work in multiple directories where authorized. The missing capability is OpenClaw managing those repositories together: selecting them when creating a task, isolating their changes, recovering the task's accepted workspace state, and showing which changes have been reviewed and published in each repository.

Using separate sessions requires manually coordinating task context, validation, and review. Cloning sibling repositories into one managed checkout does not give them independent managed ownership or recovery guarantees.

### Proposed solution

Add a repository-set choice when creating a development task. The first version could use existing registered repositories on one Gateway host, without requiring a new cloud placement mode or a separate project-management product.

**Example user flow**

1. Select `backend`, `sdk`, and `frontend`, with a base branch for each, and start one task.
2. OpenClaw creates an isolated worktree and task branch for every selected repository. The agent sees stable repository names and paths and can run cross-repository validation in the task environment.
3. Open **Review** to see one task summary and diffs grouped by repository. Each group retains its own base, changed files, and branch; cross-repository validation results remain attached to the task.
4. Resume after a Gateway restart with the same repository membership and worktree bindings. Recovery from a completed checkpoint restores the corresponding state of every member, including supported uncommitted changes.
5. Explicitly publish the reviewed changes as separate PRs. The task shows each PR and its publication status, and the PR descriptions link the related changes.

For example:

```text
Task: Add delivery-window support
  backend    4 changed files    tests passed    PR #123
  sdk        2 changed files    tests passed    PR #45
  frontend   3 changed files    E2E passed      publication failed — retry
```

**Lifecycle requirements**

- Repository membership is explicit and fixed for the first version. Do not implicitly adopt arbitrary nested repositories or grant access to unrelated host paths.
- Each repository retains its own identity, base revision, worktree, and publication receipt. A failure preparing one member must not leave the task reporting successful preparation of the whole set.
- A checkpoint is complete only when all members have been captured. Partial capture or recovery must be visible and must not silently replace a previous complete checkpoint.
- PR publication is per repository, not an atomic operation across GitHub repositories. Preserve successful receipts, expose partial failure, and allow retry without creating duplicate PRs. Do not automatically merge the PRs.
- Existing single-repository tasks keep their current behavior and permissions. Deletion and retention behavior for the set needs agreement before implementation.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Create one task from at least two independently registered repositories, with isolated worktrees and separate base revisions.
- [ ] Make a coordinated change and run validation that uses both repositories.
- [ ] Review both sets of changes in one view without mixing their Git baselines.
- [ ] Restart the Gateway and resume the same task with the same repository bindings and edits.
- [ ] Restore all members from a completed checkpoint; show a recoverable failure if a member cannot be restored.
- [ ] Publish linked PRs and correctly represent/retry a partial publication failure.

### Alternatives considered

- **Ordinary tools in a multi-directory workspace:** already useful, but the user or agent must manually maintain the repository set, review context, recovery, and publication bookkeeping.
- **One session per repository:** preserves today's ownership model, but splits the coordinated change and its integration/review context.
- **An ephemeral cloud workspace:** a useful separate contract where agents commit and push their own work, but it does not provide the managed recovery and publication requested here.
- **A monorepo, synthetic parent repository, or symlink directory:** changes the user's repository structure or filesystem layout without defining independent ownership and recovery of each member.
- **An existing multi-repository plugin:** [openclaw-linear-plugin](https://github.com/calltelemetry/openclaw-linear-plugin#multi-repo) documents one issue dispatching one agent session with separate worktrees and branches for multiple repositories. It is a concrete alternative for Linear-based workflows. Its README also says PR creation is not wired into the pipeline and must be performed manually. This implementation should inform the core/plugin decision; the repository-set recovery contract and the need for any generic core extensions still require validation before implementation.

### Impact

- **Affected users:** developers making coordinated changes across independently versioned application, SDK, or infrastructure repositories.
- **Severity:** a missing managed workflow; existing manual cross-repository tool use remains possible.
- **Frequency:** whenever a task spans repositories; no usage frequency or time-saving measurement is claimed.
- **Consequence:** the reports below describe blocked multi-repository cloud build/test workflows and manual coordination of separate sessions, branches, and related changes. These reports support the underlying workflow need; they do not establish that the proposed same-host managed workflow has the same severity, or quantify the benefit of managed recovery.

### Evidence/examples

#### Reported user needs and existing alternatives

1. **OpenClaw: a reported cloud workflow blocker.** On September 8, 2026, `danhayman` reported in [#142521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142521) that the single-root requirement prevented building, running, and testing a real application spanning frontend, backend, and infrastructure repositories in one cloud-worker session. The requested initial solution explicitly excludes managed recovery and publication. Merged #147773 subsequently addressed repository-free startup while leaving broader multi-repository support separate.
2. **Coordinated change sets and linked PRs: an explicit user request.** In the February 6, 2026 report [anthropics/claude-code#23627](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/23627), `malnor` describes changes spanning API contracts, backend, frontend, and infrastructure. The reported workaround is separate remote sessions with manual branch and merge-order coordination. The request explicitly asks for a combined change-set view and linked PRs.
3. **An existing ecosystem alternative.** The [openclaw-linear-plugin documentation](https://github.com/calltelemetry/openclaw-linear-plugin#multi-repo) describes one agent session with isolated worktrees for API and frontend repositories. This demonstrates developer investment in part of the workflow. I have reviewed its documentation, not run the plugin or verified its recovery behavior.

**Evidence boundary:** These reports support cross-repository execution and coordinated changes, without establishing OpenClaw demand volume or validating managed checkpoint recovery. Recovery remains a proposed design goal: we need concrete cases where manual commits/pushes or existing worktree workflows are insufficient, and agreement on which state should survive interruptions. The initial scope remains same-host with fixed repository membership.

#### Source-level capability boundaries

Source inspection at `3c34fe88c1aceb1bac937d48dcb0e54f5423d589` shows the current single-repository boundaries:

- [Managed worktree ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3c34fe88c1aceb1bac937d48dcb0e54f5423d589/src/agents/worktrees/service.ts#L479) rejects binding an existing owner to another repository.
- [Session repository workspace storage](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3c34fe88c1aceb1bac937d48dcb0e54f5423d589/src/state/session-repository-workspaces.ts#L184) rejects a different repository workspace for the same session.
- [The session diff response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3c34fe88c1aceb1bac937d48dcb0e54f5423d589/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts#L385) represents one checkout, branch, and baseline.
- [Snapshot inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3c34fe88c1aceb1bac937d48dcb0e54f5423d589/src/agents/worktrees/snapshot-inventory.ts#L181) explicitly rejects nested Git repositories that cannot be snapshotted losslessly.

These are design observations from source inspection, not a claim of a runtime regression or completed implementation.

Related work:

- #142521 requests an empty, explicitly ephemeral multi-repository cloud workspace and explicitly excludes managed recovery and publication from its initial scope. This proposal covers that separate managed lifecycle.
- Merged #147773 enables starting remote sessions without a source repository, using an isolated backing repository and the existing durability model. Its description explicitly leaves broader multi-repository support and ephemeral modes as separate work.
- Closed, unmerged #48681 explored composite symlink workspaces. That filesystem layout proposal did not provide per-task repository-set review, recovery, and publication.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on the product scope and ownership/durability contract.

### Additional information

The first version would target repositories on the same Gateway host. Cloud migration of a complete repository set, dynamic repository membership, and automated cross-repository merge ordering can be discussed separately.

Before implementation, I would like maintainer feedback on whether this managed repository-set workflow fits OpenClaw, and which generic lifecycle capabilities should live in core versus plugin UI.

issues.body:
## Summary

The agent-facing `dashboard` tool uses one flat schema for every action. In an empty dashboard tab, the model repeatedly emitted `after` for `widget_put` (usually equal to the widget's own name), making it impossible to add the first widget through the typed tool.

This also makes recovery difficult: `after` is optional in the implementation, but the model-facing call repeatedly included unrelated optional fields for the selected action.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.3 (`1391f7c`), current npm stable as of 2026-09-09
- Model: `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`
- Surface: WebChat / Control UI
- Gateway: local loopback, reachable
- OS: Linux x64, Node 24.18.0

## Reproduction

1. Start with a session board containing no tabs or widgets.
2. Call `dashboard` with `action: "tab_create"`, `tabId: "finance"`, and a title. This succeeds.
3. Ask the agent to add the first trusted plugin widget:

```json
{
  "action": "widget_put",
  "tabId": "finance",
  "name": "finance.monthly",
  "size": "full",
  "pluginKind": "session:report",
  "props": {
    "blocks": [{"type": "text", "text": "test"}]
  }
}
```

4. The generated tool call repeatedly includes the flat schema's unrelated optional parameters, including:

```json
"after": "finance.monthly"
```

5. The server rejects the operation with:

```text
widget cannot be placed after itself
```

Using another placeholder value produces:

```text
board widget anchor not found on tab finance: <placeholder>
```

Because the tab is empty, no valid anchor exists. In this run, repeated retries continued to populate `after`; the final `dashboard read` remained at one tab and zero widgets.

## Expected

The first `widget_put` call should omit `after` and append the widget at position 0. The tool schema should make it difficult for a model to include parameters that do not apply to the selected action.

## Actual

The model-facing flat schema encourages/permits argument contamination across actions. The first widget cannot be created when the generated call self-anchors or references a nonexistent anchor.

A similar contamination happened with the `sessions` tool in the same run: a current-session `patch` repeatedly included `targets`, and the server rejected it because `targets` cannot be combined with `sessionKey`/`expectedSessionId`.

## Relevant implementation

`DashboardToolSchema` correctly marks `after` optional, but exposes every action's fields in one `Type.Object`. `insertBoardWidget()` calls `moveWidget()` when placement contains `after`, and `moveWidget()` correctly rejects a self-anchor.

## Suggested fix

Use action-discriminated schemas (`Type.Union` of per-action objects) for `dashboard` and similarly overloaded tools, so `widget_put` can clearly express placement as one of:

- no placement anchor (append/default),
- `position`, or
- `after`.

Alternatively, normalize `after === name` to omitted only when creating a new widget, though an action-specific schema would prevent more classes of invalid mixed arguments.

## Impact

Agent-authored dashboards can get stuck on an empty tab despite valid report data and a healthy board. The failure is especially confusing because tab creation, focus, presentation, and `dashboard read` all continue to work.

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow a verified owner to create, inspect, edit and manually run explicitly authorized project automations from their Telegram forum topic, including existing jobs created outside that conversation, with scoped authorization and Telegram-native confirmation rather than blanket administrator access.

## Problem to solve

I use a Telegram forum group with a separate topic for each project. One project has several recurring research automations. I want to discuss and manage those jobs in the same topic: change a prompt or schedule, run an existing job now, or create another project job.

Creating new conversational automations is not the whole problem. Existing jobs can fall outside the topic's creator-session authority even when their results are delivered there. The documented cross-scope management path requires an authenticated Control UI administrator turn. Being the same human in Telegram, or receiving the job's output in that topic, does not establish that grant.

The current workaround is to prepare instructions in Telegram, open the Control UI, and repeat/authorize the operation there. That defeats the Telegram-first workflow, especially on mobile. I am willing to confirm sensitive operations; I want that confirmation to happen in the project conversation, not require a separate administrative conversation for every change.

## Proposed solution

Please consider an opt-in, maintainer-designed authorization flow:

1. A Gateway administrator explicitly authorizes a verified Telegram owner identity, a specific bot/account + group + topic, and a bounded set of project jobs and allowed operations. A one-time secure setup in Control UI is acceptable; routine management should then work from Telegram.
2. From that topic, the authorized owner can list/get the permitted jobs, create jobs within the approved scope, update them, and request a manual run. Existing jobs should be explicitly enrollable without deleting/recreating them or silently changing creator attribution.
3. Before a mutation or run, show a native confirmation naming the exact job and proposed change/run. Show schedule timezone and destination when relevant. Bind approval to the verified actor, topic, exact operation and job revision; expire it and prevent replay or stale approval.
4. Recheck authorization at execution, audit the actor/operation/result, and support revocation. Return management results to the originating topic, while preserving each job's configured scheduled-output route unless an authorized change explicitly modifies it.
5. Keep ordinary group members, other topics, other jobs and untrusted content outside this authority. Delivery routing alone must never confer management permission.

These are desired security properties, not a claim that a particular configuration key or implementation already exists. Identity binding and capability design need maintainer/security review. Broad operator.admin, raw command/script payload creation, credential access and Gateway updates need not be included in this feature; existing execution/sandbox/approval restrictions should remain in force.

## Alternatives considered

- Control UI for every operation: functional but requires repeated context switching and copying instructions.
- Creating all future jobs in the topic: does not resolve management of existing jobs outside its authority.
- Recreating jobs to change their scope: risks duplicates and lost continuity; not a verified authorization solution.
- Unrestricted Telegram admin access or approval bypass: not requested.

## Impact

- Affected: Telegram-first owners organizing project work in forum topics, particularly remote/mobile operators.
- Severity: blocks the desired end-to-end topic workflow, not the scheduler itself.
- Frequency: whenever a project job outside the conversation's management scope needs inspection, editing or a manual run.
- Consequence: repeated web-UI handoffs, split project context and extra manual work. No measured time-loss claim.

## Evidence/examples

Environment discussed: OpenClaw 2026.9.2, Telegram forum topics.

Example: In a research project's topic, ask “Change the Wednesday research job to 11:00 Europe/Sarajevo” or “Run the existing Friday review now,” approve the exact action there, and receive confirmation in that topic without switching to the Control UI.

- Official automation management boundary: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs#conversational-management
- Related #138567 concerns Telegram-first updates/protected input. Its automated review distinguishes already-supported updates from the remaining protected-input capability. This request is specifically about scoped project automation management, not a report that Telegram updates are unavailable.
- Related #137751 concerns cross-scope management from authenticated Control UI chat, rather than Telegram topic authority.

This is a feature request based on the documented authorization boundary and my desired workflow. No new live denial reproduction or source-level implementation test is claimed here.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

The key requirement is: after explicit secure setup, let the verified owner manage the selected project's automations from its Telegram topic with confirmation, without granting the topic or agent general administrator privileges. Please clarify whether this scoped direction is acceptable and what identity/authorization prerequisites would be required.

issues.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe?

Yes — three real incidents on one machine within 24h (OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2, deepseek-v4-flash / deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp via openai-completions):

| Incident | Model | Symptom | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-03 pseudo-invoke | deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp | Tool call written as plain text: `card\n<invoke name="browser">...` — no `tool_calls`, `stopReason: stop` | Session just ends, tool never runs ("agent stops mid-task"), 15 in a row |
| 2026-09-04 repetition explosion | same | Single assistant message generated **44,207 chars**, the phrase repeated **7,217 times** before a valid tool call finally appeared (`stopReason: toolUse`, tool did execute) | Spam floods the chat channel, garbage lands in session history |
| 2026-09-04 verbal-tic pseudo-calls | deepseek-v4-flash (non-exp) | Operation announcements written as body-text lines (`count: <cmd>`, `call exec <cmd>`) — 190 consecutive | Same, 128 messages polluted |

**The key finding (not covered by existing issues): once garbage text lands in the session transcript, the model starts imitating its own malformed output in later turns.** We verified: switching models does NOT stop the recurrence — only manually scrubbing the session jsonl does. So a guard that only halts generation is not enough; **polluted output must also be sanitized before it is persisted to the transcript**, otherwise the pollution chain continues.

Related existing issues (companion + extension, not a duplicate):
- #44965 — stream repetition safeguard: matches guard 2; we add the transcript-sanitization requirement
- #90288 (closed) — models emitting tool calls as plain text: matches guard 1; still happening with openai-completions + DeepSeek
- #113346 — context poisoning via transcript reinjection: same self-imitation mechanism we observed

## Describe the solution you'd like

Two guards at the gateway model-response processing layer (provider-agnostic, agent-invisible).

### Guard 1: pseudo tool-call detection

Detect tool-call intent emitted as plain text in assistant content:
- Tag forms: `<invoke name="...">...</invoke>`, `<function_call>`, `<tool_call>`, etc.
- Line forms (open-ended; ours originated from a legit `count:20` API field in an old tool result that the model adopted as a "verbal tic" a week later): `count: <cmd>`, `call exec <cmd>` → cover tag forms + configurable regex patterns

Behavior, in priority order:
1. **Parse & execute** if well-formed → run it as a real call, persist the structured call (not the raw text).
2. Else **intercept & retry**: don't deliver to user, don't persist; auto-retry (max 2) with a nudge like "your tool call was emitted as plain text, retry using the native tool-calling channel".
3. Fallback **strip & persist**: replace with `[malformed tool call stripped]` before writing to the transcript — this breaks the imitation chain — plus a warn log.

### Guard 2: repetition & length guard (streaming)

- n-gram repetition: same phrase (≥2 tokens) repeated N+ times in a small sliding window (default N≥8, configurable). The 44k-char incident was already determinable within the first ~2k chars.
- Per-message text length cap (default ~32k chars, configurable).

Behavior:
1. On trigger, **abort the completion** (stop burning tokens).
2. Auto-retry (max 2); still pathological → raise an error instead of persisting.
3. If anything still lands in the transcript, compress the repeated span to `[repetitive output truncated]` — **never persist full repetition into context**.

### Configuration sketch

```yaml
agents.defaults.outputGuards:
  enabled: true
  repetitionThreshold: 8
  maxTextLength: 32000
  pseudoInvokePatterns: [...]   # tag forms + custom regex
  action: parse | retry | strip
```

## Additional context

Repro material available on request: incident session/trajectory files (44k repetition, 190x `count:` run, 15x pseudo-invoke) and our scrubbing methodology notes.

issues.body:
## Summary

On stable `2026.8.2`, a controlled restart can leave the gateway listener present but effectively unavailable for about two minutes while startup sidecars run. During the reproduced window, local HTTP timed out, WebSocket upgrades closed with code `1006`, and the built-in liveness heartbeat reported a 110.7-second delay.

The gateway eventually recovered without another restart, and a real Telegram agent execution plus delivery then succeeded. This is therefore an availability/stability regression during startup, not a permanent channel configuration failure.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.8.2` (`0965053`), package build `2026.8.2-0965053fe6b9-2026-09-01T09-44-31.342Z`
- Node: `22.23.2`
- Linux x64, systemd user service, native npm global install
- Gateway: loopback `127.0.0.1:18789`, reverse-proxied by Traefik
- 16 runtime plugins reported by the gateway
- 11 Telegram accounts configured
- Largest agent SQLite DB: about 102 MiB; Cleo DB has 10 session rows and 1,681 transcript events
- `gateway.reload.mode=off`

## Reproduction

1. Start from a running gateway.
2. Run `systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway.service`.
3. Probe local HTTP/RPC/WebSocket readiness during startup.
4. Observe that the TCP listener appears early, but the gateway does not become usable until roughly two minutes later.

This host has reproduced similar 95-136 second heartbeat delays across several boots on the same stable build, not only the restart below.

## Timeline from one controlled restart (UTC)

```text
06:06:28 systemd: Started openclaw-gateway.service (new PID)
06:06:34 [gateway] loading configuration
06:06:39 [gateway] starting HTTP server
06:06:41 [gateway] http server listening (...; 6.6s)
06:08:29 [gateway] ready
06:08:30 [diagnostic] liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=80674ms elapsed=110674ms
06:08:30 [ws] closed before connect ... code=1006 ... phase=ws_upgrade_started
06:08:31 [ws] closed before connect ... code=1006 ... phase=ws_upgrade_started
06:09:00 [diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_growth rss=1.46 GiB heap=426.6 MiB rssGrowth=957 MiB
```

During the interval after the listener appeared and before `gateway ready`, `curl --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:18789/` timed out with zero bytes. After recovery, local and public HTTP returned 200, `openclaw gateway status --deep --json` reported RPC healthy, Telegram polling probes were healthy, and an end-to-end Cleo agent turn delivered successfully in 6.7 seconds.

## Repeated evidence on the same stable build

The same log contains additional heartbeat stalls of approximately 121.8 s, 131.4 s, 166.2 s, and 125.4 s around recent gateway startup/runtime windows. This makes the observed outage consistent with a recurring stability problem rather than a single slow network request.

## Expected behavior

- Startup work should not block the main event loop for tens of seconds.
- A bound TCP/HTTP listener should either remain responsive with an explicit retryable startup response or not advertise readiness yet.
- WebSocket handshakes and Telegram polling should not be starved while startup sidecars perform model/session/plugin discovery.

## Related issues

- #82398 covered startup WebSocket `1006` under event-loop starvation, but was closed after a channel-start trace fix.
- #124788 covered 100-120 second event-loop freezes on beta.2 and was closed as implemented on main after worker-placement session-evidence changes.
- #117411 covered provider-auth rewarm CPU/RSS growth after hot reload, rather than this cold-start path.

This stable `2026.8.2` reproduction suggests either a remaining startup path or a regression. The available logs establish the user-visible stall but do not identify the exact synchronous stack. A CPU profile or startup-trace breakdown around the 108-second gap between `http server listening` and `gateway ready` would be the next useful diagnostic.

## Safety / privacy

All hostnames, public addresses, tokens, chat IDs, usernames, message contents, and provider credentials are omitted. No `doctor --fix` or package update was run during reproduction.

issues.body:
## What problem does this solve?

Nextcloud Talk 21+ can send an optional `object.inReplyTo` object in bot webhooks. It identifies the message that the user quoted/replied to, including the parent message id and content.

OpenClaw currently accepts the webhook and routes the new message, but drops that parent context. An agent therefore cannot tell whether the user is replying to an earlier message or inspect the quoted text. This is especially noticeable in busy rooms where the current message is short (for example, “please fix this”).

This is a feature request / documented capability gap, not a bug or regression: the current behavior matches the plugin's declared `threads: false` capability.

## Evidence

- The official Nextcloud Talk Bot API documents `object.inReplyTo` as an optional field added in Talk 21: <https://nextcloud-talk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/bots/#sample-chat-message>.
- The same API documents the outbound `replyTo` field for posting a reply to a message in the conversation: <https://nextcloud-talk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/bots/#sending-a-chat-message>.
- The current webhook schema in [`extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/webhook-spool.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/webhook-spool.ts) models only `type`, `id`, `name`, `content`, and `mediaType` under `object`.
- `parseClaimedMessage` in that file maps the webhook to `NextcloudTalkInboundMessage` without any parent/reply fields.
- [`extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/types.ts) has no optional parent-message field on `NextcloudTalkInboundMessage`.
- The outbound path already accepts `replyToId` in [`extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/inbound.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/inbound.ts) and sends it through [`extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/send.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/send.ts).

## Proposed scope

1. Extend the webhook payload type/schema with the optional Talk 21+ `object.inReplyTo` shape.
2. Preserve the parent message id and bounded parent text in `NextcloudTalkInboundMessage`.
3. Populate the standard inbound context fields (`ReplyToId`, `ReplyToBody`, and `ReplyToIsQuote`) so agents and plugins receive the same reply metadata exposed by other channels.
4. Keep the field optional and preserve the current behavior for Talk versions/webhooks that do not send `inReplyTo`.
5. Add focused tests for a Talk 21+ reply payload and for an ordinary message without `inReplyTo`.

## Non-goals

- Implementing message-history synchronization or a new thread model.
- Changing media support or authentication.
- Requiring Talk 21+: older Talk webhook payloads must continue to work unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- A signed webhook containing `object.inReplyTo.object.id` is accepted by the durable ingress path.
- The resulting inbound context exposes the parent id and quoted text without changing the current message id.
- Outbound replies continue to target the current inbound message by default; existing explicit `replyToId` behavior remains intact.
- Payloads without `inReplyTo` produce the same context as today.
- Tests cover both payload shapes and bounded/absent parent content.

I can prepare a focused implementation once the maintainers confirm whether Talk's quote-reply semantics should map to `ReplyToIsQuote` only or also to the channel `threads` capability.

## Summary

Support Microsoft Graph-backed Teams operations for `channels.msteams.cloud: "China"` (Teams operated by 21Vianet) by routing Graph requests and token scopes to the Azure China Graph endpoint.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw supports configuring the Microsoft Teams China cloud for Bot Framework authentication and message delivery, but Graph-backed operations are entirely disabled for that cloud. This prevents China/21Vianet deployments from using the same directory, team/channel, message, membership, reaction, and attachment capabilities available in other Teams clouds.

The limitation is especially significant for configurations that rely on Graph resolution for team/channel or user allowlists: names cannot be resolved, and operators must use pre-resolved stable IDs or give up those workflows. Graph-backed message reads/search and attachment retrieval also fail before any request is made.

## Proposed solution

Add cloud-aware Graph routing throughout the Teams plugin:

- use `https://microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn/v1.0` (and the supported beta endpoint where required) for China Graph requests;
- acquire tokens with the Azure China Graph audience/scope;
- carry the selected Graph root through pagination, absolute `@odata.nextLink` handling, attachment/share downloads, directory lookup, message operations, and allowlist resolution;
- preserve the existing public, GCC, and DoD endpoints and fail-closed host validation;
- add focused China-cloud tests for token audience, request roots, pagination, directory/allowlist resolution, message operations, and attachment paths.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep requiring manually pre-resolved IDs: this avoids Graph calls but removes name resolution and does not restore message, directory, membership, or attachment operations.
- Ask operators to use the global Graph endpoint: China tenants require the Azure China Graph service and token audience; using the global endpoint is not a supported or reliable workaround.
- Implement a separate China-only plugin: this would duplicate the existing Teams authorization, routing, and message lifecycle instead of extending the cloud abstraction already present in the plugin.

## Impact

- **Affected users/systems/channels:** Microsoft Teams China/21Vianet tenants using OpenClaw.
- **Severity:** High for affected China deployments; Bot Framework send/receive remains available, but all Graph-backed capabilities are unavailable.
- **Frequency:** Deterministic for every China-cloud Graph operation.
- **Consequence:** Team/channel and user allowlist names cannot be resolved; Graph message search/read, membership management, reactions, and Graph-backed attachment retrieval fail immediately.

## Evidence/examples

- `extensions/msteams/src/graph.ts` explicitly rejects `cloud: "China"` in `resolveGraphToken` before any Graph request: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/msteams/src/graph.ts#L228-L241
- The token provider also rejects the China Graph scope: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/msteams/src/sdk.ts#L394-L405
- Graph request construction defaults to the global `GRAPH_ROOT`, so the request root is not cloud-aware: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/msteams/src/graph.ts#L49-L58
- The Teams documentation confirms that Graph helpers are disabled for China until Azure China Graph routing is implemented: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/msteams.md#L714
- Repository search found no existing open or closed issue specifically tracking Microsoft Teams China Graph routing.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

## Additional information

This is a feature request for a documented regional capability gap, not a regression report. The implementation should retain the current fail-closed behavior for unsupported or mismatched service hosts and must not broaden authorization or bypass existing Bot Connector boundaries.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add optional time-range filters to `sessions_search` so agents can search visible transcript messages within a bounded period.

## Problem to solve

`sessions_search` supports an exact text query, an optional session target, and a result limit. Each hit already includes a timestamp, but the caller cannot constrain the search by time before ranking and limiting are applied.

This makes requests such as "find the deployment decision we discussed last week" unreliable. The agent can search for `deployment decision` and discard out-of-range hits afterward, but the Gateway returns at most 25 ranked matches across the entire searchable history. Relevant messages inside the requested period may never reach the agent if newer or higher-ranked matches fill that bounded result set first.

This is a missing retrieval capability rather than a defect in the current full-text search contract. The existing search behaves as documented, but it cannot express a common time-bounded recall request.

## Proposed solution

Add optional `minTimestampMs` and `beforeTimestampMs` parameters to the agent-facing `sessions_search` tool and the Gateway `sessions.search` contract:

- `minTimestampMs`: inclusive lower bound (`timestamp >= minTimestampMs`)
- `beforeTimestampMs`: exclusive upper bound (`timestamp < beforeTimestampMs`)

Both values should be non-negative safe integers in Unix epoch milliseconds. When both are present, reject an empty or reversed range where `minTimestampMs >= beforeTimestampMs`.

Apply the predicates inside the SQLite FTS query before `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`, then preserve the existing relevance ordering within the selected window. Visibility filtering, incognito exclusion, session targeting, redaction, indexing warnings, query tokenization, and all output limits should remain unchanged.

Omitting both parameters must preserve current behavior. The transcript search table already stores each hit's timestamp, so this should not require a new index corpus, persistent data format, or migration. Documentation and focused tests should cover either bound alone, both bounds, exact boundary behavior, invalid ranges, multi-session visibility, and limit-before-filter regressions.

## Alternatives considered

1. Include words such as `last week` or a date in the text query. Session search is full-text search over message content; a message does not necessarily contain the date on which it was sent, so this changes the query instead of filtering its timestamp.
2. Fetch results repeatedly and filter them in the agent. The public search is capped at 25 hits and has no result pagination, so the desired in-window match can remain unreachable. Increasing or removing the cap would also increase token and synchronous-query costs without expressing the actual constraint.
3. Search one session at a time after using `sessions_list`. This requires the agent to discover and query many candidate sessions, still cannot constrain matches within each transcript by time, and adds avoidable tool calls.
4. Add a third-party transcript-search plugin. A plugin would need to duplicate the core FTS index, Gateway session visibility rules, incognito handling, and redaction boundary. The built-in query owner can apply a narrowing predicate without creating a parallel access path.

## Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Users and agents recalling exact text or decisions from a known time period across visible session transcripts; this is independent of messaging channel.
- Severity: Workflow friction with a risk of incomplete recall; ordinary transcript search remains available.
- Frequency: Whenever a recall request includes a time boundary; no usage-rate data is available.
- Consequence: Agents may return older or newer matches, incorrectly report that nothing was found, or spend additional tool calls narrowing sessions manually.

## Evidence/examples

- At main commit [`9d10dcb5`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9d10dcb5d39d09be94f48a1bfce1dbfd7a256903), the agent-facing schema accepts only `query`, `sessionKey`, and `limit`, while every result already exposes `timestamp`: [`src/agents/tools/sessions-search-tool.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d10dcb5d39d09be94f48a1bfce1dbfd7a256903/src/agents/tools/sessions-search-tool.ts#L44-L70).
- The public Gateway contract likewise has no time-bound input but requires a timestamp on every search hit: [`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d10dcb5d39d09be94f48a1bfce1dbfd7a256903/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts#L401-L418).
- The SQLite FTS query selects `timestamp`, orders matches by rank and timestamp, and applies a maximum result limit without a timestamp predicate: [`src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d10dcb5d39d09be94f48a1bfce1dbfd7a256903/src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.ts#L43-L101).
- Existing transcript-reading code already uses the proposed inclusive `minTimestampMs` and exclusive `beforeTimestampMs` semantics: [`src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-window.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d10dcb5d39d09be94f48a1bfce1dbfd7a256903/src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-window.ts#L1-L17).
- The session-search documentation describes exact-text search, timestamp-bearing results, visibility filtering, and bounded output, but no time-range input: [`docs/concepts/session-search.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d10dcb5d39d09be94f48a1bfce1dbfd7a256903/docs/concepts/session-search.md#L9-L44).
- Repository searches on 2026-09-01 for `sessions_search date filter`, `sessions_search role filter`, `session transcript search time range`, `session search before after`, `search past conversations date`, `session history date range`, and `time-bounded transcript` found no matching open or closed Feature Issue or implementation PR. Nearby search/filter results concern session-list UI filtering or older QMD visibility behavior rather than pre-limit timestamp filtering in `sessions_search`.

No external user logs or usage measurements are available yet; the source evidence demonstrates the current contract and the bounded-result limitation.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

Non-goals for the initial feature: natural-language date parsing, timezone inference, Control UI filters, semantic `memory_search` changes, role/content-type filtering, search pagination, or broader session visibility. The caller should convert a user-facing date range to epoch milliseconds using the session's existing time context. Because the proposed bounds only narrow the already-authorized transcript set, they must not bypass or alter current access-control decisions.

issues.body:
### Summary

The rate limit retry counter is not reset after a tool call completes, causing the retry budget to be exhausted prematurely within a single run when multiple tool calls occur.

### Problem

In the embedded agent runner, the rate limit retry counter (\consecutiveSameModelRateLimitRetries\) persists across tool call boundaries within a single run. When a user message triggers multiple tool calls:

1. First model call hits rate limit -> retry (counter=1)
2. Second model call hits rate limit -> retry (counter=2)
3. ...
4. Fifth model call hits rate limit -> retry (counter=5)
5. Tool call completes successfully
6. Next model call hits rate limit -> **NO retries available** (counter already at 5)

The 5-retry budget (\MAX_SAME_MODEL_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES\) is consumed during the first model call, leaving no retries for subsequent model calls after tool completions.

### Expected behavior

The rate limit retry counter should reset after each tool call completes, allowing fresh retries for subsequent model calls within the same run.

### Current behavior

The retry counter persists across tool call boundaries, exhausting the budget prematurely when multiple tool calls occur within a single run.

### Proposed solution

Add \ ailoverRetryController.resetSameModelRateLimitRetries()\ at the top of the \while (true)\ loop in \src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-loop.ts\, ensuring the counter resets after each tool call completion.

### Impact

This change affects users who:
- Use providers with rate limits (especially daily quotas like SenseNova)
- Send messages that trigger multiple tool calls
- Encounter rate limits during model calls

Without this fix, sessions are suspended prematurely when the retry budget is exhausted during the first model call, even though subsequent model calls after tool completions should have fresh retries.

### Evidence

- Code path: \src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-loop.ts\ (while loop at line 315)
- Retry controller: \src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.ts\
- Current behavior: counter persists across tool call boundaries
- Fix location: \un-loop.ts:315\ - reset at loop start

### Related

This addresses the concern raised in the discussion about rate limit retry behavior in the embedded agent runner.

issues.body:
## Summary

In the Mattermost channel plugin (verified on 2026.6.11 and published 2026.7.1), an inbound reply inside a channel/group thread is routed to a thread-scoped session keyed `...:group:<channelId>:thread:<rootPostId>`. There is no configuration to make thread replies share the parent channel session. `replyToMode` only controls where the bot's own replies go.

## User story

A user accidentally taps a bot message in the Mattermost mobile app (tapping a message opens the thread view), types a follow-up there, and the reply lands in a brand-new, empty session. The bot answers with no memory of the conversation that happened seconds earlier in the same channel. To the user this reads as sudden amnesia. Thread replies are extremely easy to trigger accidentally on mobile, and Mattermost has no way to disable threads (replies always carry `root_id`; `CollapsedThreads` only changes presentation).

## Proposal

Add a per-chat-type setting, mirroring the existing `replyToModeByChatType` shape:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    mattermost: {
      threadSessions: "scoped",            // default, current behavior
      threadSessionsByChatType: {
        channel: "inherit",                // thread replies join the parent channel session
        group: "inherit"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- `scoped` (default): current behavior, thread root post id keys its own session. Useful for one-topic-per-thread workflows in busy channels.
- `inherit`: inbound thread replies route to the parent channel/group session key. The bot still replies inside the thread (posting placement unchanged); only session routing changes.

Backwards compatible: default stays `scoped`.

## Notes

- DMs appear unaffected in ≤2026.7.1: direct-message thread replies do not produce thread-scoped session keys (verified in live session stores; the runtime does not thread-key `kind === "direct"`). The proposal therefore targets channel/group chats.
- We are happy to contribute the implementation as a PR (config plumbing + routing change + docs + tests) if maintainers are open to the design.

## Related

- #108975 (open) asks for the Slack-side equivalent (configurable per-thread session scope). This proposal is the Mattermost side of the same configurability, in the opposite direction: letting channel/group thread replies inherit the parent channel session.
- #93203 (closed, completed) covered DM threading modes (`dmReplyToMode`); channel/group thread session inheritance was not part of that track. #65729 (umbrella) did not cover it either.

issues.body:
### Summary

When the primary agent model is a **slow local model** (LM Studio via OpenAI-compatible endpoint), a long agent turn gets interrupted with:

> This turn was interrupted because it stopped making progress. Please try again.

...even though both documented timeout knobs are already set very high. The interrupt is **not** caused by `timeoutSeconds` — it is caused by the **tool-loop detector** (`dist/tool-loop-detection-*.js`) classifying slow-but-legitimate tool sequences as "no progress", and its thresholds are **not configurable**.

### Environment / Repro

- OpenClaw 2026.8.1-beta.1, gateway `mode: local`
- Primary model: LM Studio local model (OpenAI-compatible, `http://localhost:1234/v1`) — slow (minutes per turn)
- Config:
  - `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` = 3600
  - `models.providers.lmstudio.timeoutSeconds` = 3600
- Task: a long multi-step task in Code Mode that legitimately repeats the same tool (e.g. repeatedly `read` large files at decreasing offsets, or repeatedly `exec` the same command then `read` the same session output)

Observed: turn is interrupted mid-run with the message above, typically after several repeated tool calls. Switching the primary back to a fast hosted model (DeepSeek) makes the error disappear for the same task.

### Root cause (from source)

- The message text lives in `dist/dispatch-*.js`.
- "making progress" text and the actual logic live in `dist/tool-loop-detection-*.js` (`tool-loop-detection`):
  - `ping_pong` detector: alternating two tools N consecutive times reaches threshold → hard block.
  - `generic_repeat` detector: same tool + same args hash called N times, **or same outcome hash (no-progress streak) reaches `criticalThreshold`** → hard block "Session execution blocked to prevent runaway loops".
  - `warningThreshold` / `criticalThreshold` / `historySize` / `noProgressStreak` are internal; I found **no public config key** under `agents.defaults` (or anywhere in `docs/`) to tune or disable this detector.
  - `docs/gateway/local-models.md` only documents `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds` and `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` for slow local servers. Neither governs this detector.

A real "no-progress" detector is valuable, but for slow local models a legitimate long-running sequence (large-file reads, repeated diagnostics with the same reference file) can look like "no progress" purely because each step is slow, not because the agent is stuck.

### Request

Please expose the tool-loop-detection thresholds under `agents.defaults` (or per model/provider), e.g.:

- `agents.defaults.loopDetection.warningThreshold`
- `agents.defaults.loopDetection.criticalThreshold`
- `agents.defaults.loopDetection.noProgressStreak`
- `agents.defaults.loopDetection.historySize`
- `agents.defaults.loopDetection.enabled` (to disable entirely)

...so users with slow local models can raise (or disable) these to avoid false-positive interrupts on legitimate long tool sequences.

### Workaround (current)

Avoid repeatedly calling the same tool with identical arguments/results in a short window (e.g. read large files once into memory, use `grep`/targeted reads instead of paginated re-reads). This reduces false triggers but is fragile for long autonomous tasks.

## Summary

`openclaw nodes screen record --duration 0` and `openclaw nodes camera clip --duration 0` are accepted by the CLI. The value is parsed by `parseDurationMs` (which only rejects non-finite and negative durations) and then forwarded verbatim to the node as `durationMs: 0` via `node.invoke`, producing a zero-length recording/clip (or a confusing node-side failure) instead of a clean CLI validation error.

## Reproduction

```
openclaw nodes camera clip --node <node> --duration 0
openclaw nodes screen record --node <node> --duration 0
```

Both commands pass `--duration` validation and proceed to node dispatch; a `0` (or any value that resolves to `<= 0` ms, e.g. `0s`, `0ms`, or a sub-millisecond value that rounds to 0) is sent to the node as the recording duration.

## Expected behavior

A zero or non-positive duration is invalid for a recording/clip and should be rejected before node dispatch with a clear error, matching the sibling validation in the same commands:

- `nodes screen record --fps 0` is rejected (`--fps must be greater than 0`).
- `nodes camera snap --quality` / `--delay-ms` / `--max-width` are bounded.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an agent-session view to MCP diagnostics: `openclaw mcp probe <name> --agent <agentId>` (and the `mcp doctor` equivalent) that reports the tool catalog the agent's runtime actually exposes, so probe results answer "what can this agent use right now?" instead of only "is the server reachable from the gateway?".

## Problem to solve

`openclaw mcp probe` and `openclaw mcp doctor` validate the gateway↔server leg: `probeMcpServerIssues` in `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` connects through `buildMcpProbeConfig` and reports `runtime.getCatalog()` tool counts. Nothing in the first-party diagnostics materializes an agent session's effective tool catalog — the projection that survives harness routing, policy, and runtime materialization. When those layers diverge, every probe stays green while the agent cannot use the tools.

This exact blind spot forced operators in the #114154 thread into forensic workarounds:

- kayloehmann (after controlling for server-side confounds): "`openclaw mcp probe`/`mcp doctor` both report the server healthy with the correct tool count at the same time." alongside session runs where "The raw session JSONL shows the assistant's only message for the turn is a single `{"type":"text", ...}` content block... **no `tool_use` block at all**" — with `systemPromptReport.tools.entries` still listing all of the server's tools.
- rhclaw: "The tools are never enumerated — they are not being stripped... directly observable rather than inferred" — operators had to reconstruct this from `[agents/tool-policy]` logs, `--json` run output, and raw `curl tools/list` calls timed against failing turns.

Whatever fixes land for the underlying loss, the diagnostic gap remains: there is no supported command that shows an operator the tool list a given agent's runtime will actually see, nor a diff against the server catalog with per-tool removal reasons (policy vs harness vs materialization).

## Proposed solution

1. Add `--agent <agentId>` to `openclaw mcp probe <name>`: materialize the tool catalog through the same projection the agent runtime uses (the layer that produces the session's effective tool set, distinct from both the gateway client catalog and the informational `systemPromptReport.tools.entries`), and print it with counts.
2. In that mode, also diff against the server catalog and attribute each missing tool to a stage: tool policy (with the rule that removed it), harness/runtime availability, or materialization — the stages operators currently reconstruct by hand from logs.
3. Mirror the flag in `openclaw mcp doctor` so health checks can fail when the agent view loses tools the gateway view still shows.
4. Tests: fixture MCP server + agent config where policy removes a tool and the harness drops another; assert the report names both with reasons (CLI-level, deterministic, no live server).

## Alternatives considered

- Relying on `systemPromptReport.tools.entries`: #114154 shows it can list tools the runtime never actually offers the model, so it is not ground truth for this question.
- Manual JSONL/log forensics: what operators do today; slow, error-prone, and repeats the differential-diagnosis confusion documented in the thread.
- A generic "agent dry-run" command: strictly larger scope; the probe/doctor surface already owns MCP diagnostics and is where operators look first.

## Impact

Affected: operators debugging "MCP tools missing in agent sessions" — a recurring report class (#114154, #122712, #116053, #98193) where every existing diagnostic reports green.
Severity: Medium — diagnosability gap, not data loss; today it turns a minutes-long check into hours of log forensics.
Frequency: Every incident of agent-side tool loss; also useful as a post-setup sanity check.
Consequence: Operators cannot distinguish server faults from session-projection faults, mis-file bugs, and apply server-side workarounds that cannot help.

## Evidence/examples

- kayloehmann's controlled reproduction and standing evidence: [#114154 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/114154#issuecomment-5227819272) — probe/doctor green while sessions emit no `tool_use` at all.
- rhclaw's directly-observable narrowing ("never enumerated — not stripped"): [#114154 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/114154#issuecomment-5204981739).
- Current code: `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` (`probeMcpServerIssues`, `buildMcpProbeConfig`, `runtime.getCatalog()` — gateway-client view only, no agent flag); `systemPromptReport` schema in `packages/gateway-protocol`.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes

## Additional information

Overlap check: no open or closed issue tracks an agent-session view for MCP probe/doctor; #114154 is the underlying loss bug (this issue is the diagnosability primitive that survives its fix); #112761 is a different escape hatch (invoking one tool from the CLI). Kept to the probe/doctor surface — no changes to tool routing itself.

issues.body:
## Summary

Implement the planned Swarm `agents.session()` API: stateful multi-turn worker agents that Code Mode scripts can open, send turns to, and close — the next item in the accepted Swarm build order.

## Problem to solve

Swarm v1 collector children are one-shot. `agents.run()` accepts a single prompt, resolves with the child's final result (text or structured), and the child session is done. There is no way to send a follow-up turn to the same child.

That blocks a whole class of orchestration patterns that the one-shot design otherwise enables:

1. **Iterative refinement** — "improve this draft" loops where the same worker holds the full editing context across turns.
2. **Multi-turn verification dialogs** — a reviewer asks a question, the worker answers from its session state, the reviewer follows up. Today every follow-up must re-serialize all prior context into a fresh prompt.
3. **Stateful pipelines** — a worker that accumulates knowledge (e.g., a summarizer reading a document in chunks) and is queried repeatedly.

The current workaround is spawning a fresh one-shot child per turn and re-sending full context. That wastes tokens, loses the child's native session state, and multiplies child sessions in the registry.

This API is already part of the accepted Swarm direction:

- The original design issue #110325 sequenced the build order as: core → Labs page → QuickJS surface → dots → Codex projection → **`agents.session`** → placement → user docs. Everything before `agents.session` has shipped (`agents.run`, `phase`, `log`, the progress dots, Codex projection).
- The frozen spec `docs/plan/swarms.md` §7 defines the v1.1 surface.
- The user-facing docs already promise it: `docs/tools/swarm.md` ("Limits and roadmap") says "the planned `agents.session()` API will add stateful multi-turn workers".

There is no open issue tracking this slice, so the last committed phase of the accepted plan currently has no tracking item.

## Proposed solution

Implement the v1.1 surface from `docs/plan/swarms.md` §7 as the Code Mode guest API (gated on `tools.swarm` + `tools.codeMode`, same as `agents.run`):

```typescript
agents.session(system: string, opts?: AgentRunOptions): Promise<SessionHandle>;

interface SessionHandle {
  send(input: string, opts?: AgentRunOptions): Promise<string>; // one turn
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Implementation shape, per the frozen spec:

- Use `mode: "session"` spawns plus **per-turn collector completion records** in the existing subagent registry — additive columns only, no new store, no schema-version bump (per the spec's SQLite constraint).
- Keep the v1 semantics that already work: fail-closed approvals (no operator prompts from children), group caps (`maxConcurrent`, `maxChildrenPerGroup`, `maxTotalPerGroup`), ownership rules (only the spawning session or its parent chain), and leaf children (`maxSpawnDepth`).
- Await transport stays snapshot-safe: parked bridge calls idempotency-keyed on `(codeModeRunId, bridgeId)`, so an in-flight `handle.send()` survives gateway restarts and never double-sends — the same property `agents.run()` already provides.
- Pending session handles extend the run's snapshot TTL, consistent with pending `agentWait` behavior.

Suggested scope for the first PR: QuickJS guest surface + registry per-turn records + unit/integration tests, following the lane slicing in `docs/plan/swarms.md` §14. Docs update to `docs/tools/swarm.md` (including the `agents.d.ts` virtual file surface) lands with it.

## Alternatives considered

- **Spawn a fresh one-shot child per turn and re-send context.** The status quo. Wasteful (full context per turn), loses child session state, and inflates the session registry.
- **Use interactive/announce subagents with steering.** Those bind to channels and human-visible conversations; they are not deterministic script-driven workers and do not fit Code Mode orchestration.
- **Saved/named workflows or a graph DSL.** Explicit non-goals of the Swarm design; control flow in code is the orchestration.
- **Do cloud placement first.** Placement is the following phase in the build order and is orthogonal — session handles are equally useful with local children.

## Impact

- **Affected users:** anyone writing Swarm/Code Mode orchestration scripts that need multi-turn workers.
- **Severity:** blocks a class of orchestration patterns (medium; the one-shot API remains functional for fan-out/synthesis).
- **Frequency:** every swarm script with iterative or dialog-style child interaction.
- **Consequence:** token waste from context re-sending, loss of worker session state, and child-session multiplication per logical worker.

## Evidence/examples

- `docs/tools/swarm.md`, "Limits and roadmap": "Swarm v1 runs one-shot collector children; the planned `agents.session()` API will add stateful multi-turn workers."
- `docs/plan/swarms.md` §7 (frozen spec): `agents.session()` / `handle.send()` / `handle.close()` via `mode:"session"` + per-turn collector records; §9 registry constraints; §14 build phases listing `agents.session` as a follow-up PR after the QuickJS surface.
- #110325 (closed, implemented v1): build order names `agents.session` after Codex projection, which has shipped.
- Duplicate check on 2026-08-26 against open and closed issues in `openclaw/openclaw` with queries "swarm session", "agents.session", "multi-turn swarm", "stateful subagent worker", "swarm cloud placement": no existing tracking issue. The only `agents.session` body match is #110325 itself, which is closed and tracks v1.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. I can implement the first accepted slice (guest API + per-turn registry records + focused tests) if maintainers confirm the v1.1 shape from the frozen spec is still the intended direction.

## Additional information

- Repo policy note from the spec: any change requiring a SQLite schema-version bump needs explicit maintainer sign-off first; the spec's stated intent is additive columns only, which would avoid that gate.
- This issue deliberately does not bundle cloud placement (`placement: "cloud:<profile>"`), which is the separate following phase in the build order.
