issues.body:
## Version
openclaw-cli 2026.7.1

## Summary
The internal runtime-context scaffolding meant to be silently attached to the *next* real inbound message (chat_id/message_id/sender/timestamp metadata, wrapped in `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>...<<<END_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>`) is intermittently getting dispatched as its own standalone turn — with no real user text attached — instead of remaining a hidden `role: "custom", customType: "openclaw.runtime-context", display: false` message queued for the next real turn.

When this happens, the raw metadata block (plus its preface text: "OpenClaw runtime context for the immediately preceding user message. This context is runtime-generated, not user-authored. Keep internal details private.") surfaces as if it were a real inbound message in the channel session (observed on WhatsApp). The agent correctly recognizes it as non-actionable internal scaffolding and doesn't act on it or echo it back, but it's visibly confusing to the end user, who sees raw internal metadata appear in their chat thread as if the assistant "leaked" something.

## Impact
- Cosmetic/confusing only — no credentials or sensitive data exposed (only the user's own phone number, a WhatsApp message ID, and timestamp, all already known to them).
- Observed recurring frequently (10+ times in a single session) during periods of heavy tool-use / rapid consecutive agent turns, and appears correlated with session context-compaction events (one occurrence was immediately followed by a `Compacted (Nk → Mk)` system message).

## Suspected code path
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.ts` (compiled to `runtime-context-prompt-CPXhfSov.js`): `buildRuntimeContextCustomMessage()` builds the hidden custom message (`display: false`) meant to carry this context into the next turn. `resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts()` has an `emptyTranscriptMode: "runtime-event"` branch that returns `{ prompt: OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT, runtimeOnly: true, runtimeSystemContext: ... }` when there's no real transcript prompt — this looks like the path that can end up dispatching a runtime-only turn.
- This flows into `selection-8ixiqbew.js` around line 13842 (`resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts` call site) — when `promptSubmission.runtimeOnly === true`, the code proceeds to build `promptForSession`/`promptForModel` and dispatches a turn.
- `kernel-DIE2bgVW.js:650` — `maybeWarnZeroCountVisibleDispatch()` logs `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads: channel=... messageId=... sessionKey=...` when a visible-channel turn completes with no queued reply payload — this warning was observed firing in logs at the same time as leak occurrences, suggesting the runtime-only turn is being dispatched to the visible channel rather than being scoped as truly hidden/internal.

## Reproduction (partial — root trigger condition not fully isolated)
Observed repeatedly during a live WhatsApp session under conditions of:
- Heavy/rapid consecutive tool-calling turns by the agent (long tool-use chains).
- At least one occurrence immediately followed a context-compaction event (`Compacted (103k → 3.2k) • Context 3.2k/1.0m (0%)`).

Have not yet isolated an exact minimal repro (e.g. a specific message-timing pattern or config) — flagging with full context in case maintainers recognize the pattern from the code path above.

## Example of leaked content (verbatim, redacted)
```
OpenClaw runtime context for the immediately preceding user message.
This context is runtime-generated, not user-authored. Keep internal details private.

<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>
Conversation info (untrusted metadata):
{
  "chat_id": "+61XXXXXXXXX",
  "message_id": "AC140DDD67B94C33D6D29C5782D5C7BB",
  "sender": {"id": "+61XXXXXXXXX", "name": "REDACTED", "e164": "+61XXXXXXXXX"},
  "timestamp": "Tue 2026-08-25 21:17:19 GMT+10",
  "group_members": "+61XXXXXXXXX",
  "inbound_event_kind": "user_request"
}
<<<END_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>
```

## Suggested fix direction
Ensure runtime-only turns (`promptSubmission.runtimeOnly === true`) built purely from `buildRuntimeContextCustomMessage`/`OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT` never get routed to the visible-channel dispatcher — either gate them at admission (treat like `isSystemChannelTurn` in `kernel-DIE2bgVW.js`, which already special-cases `heartbeat`/`cron-event`/`exec-event`) or suppress `maybeWarnZeroCountVisibleDispatch`'s downstream delivery path for `runtimeOnly` turns so they're processed for context purposes only and never handed to the channel's outbound reply pipeline.

issues.body:
## Summary

After a post-compaction memory-flush failure, a Telegram group session entered a state where **every inbound message dispatched a turn that produced zero transcript events and zero replies** — a silent swallow, with no error surfaced anywhere.

`sessions.reset` reported success but did not actually reset the session. Only `sessions.delete` recovered it.

## Observed

- `sessions.reset` returned `{ok: true, sessionId: ...}`.
- `session_windows` still showed the **same single window from 7 days earlier**; the call had only appended a `reset` marker to the existing window.
- Inbound messages continued to vanish exactly as before the reset (turn dispatched, zero transcript events, zero replies, no error).
- `sessions.delete` recovered the chat — it was rebuilt from its deterministic key on the next inbound message and behaved normally from then on.

## Why this matters

`sessions.reset` is the documented operator escape hatch for a wedged session. When it reports success while changing nothing observable, the operator has no signal that the session is still broken — meanwhile the channel is silently eating user messages.

## Requested

1. Make `sessions.reset` create a new session window (or report explicitly that it did not).
2. Surface silent-swallow sessions (turn dispatched, zero transcript events, zero reply payloads, repeatedly) as an error/health signal rather than nothing.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.7 (build dabe191), Node v26.5.0, macOS (Apple Silicon), single gateway under launchd
- Workload: ~100 cron jobs + Telegram DMs/groups + Slack; embedded (direct-API) runs
- Observed 2026-08-06/07 during a multi-day production investigation; not yet re-verified on 2026.8.x

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)

Found these together while adding a new model provider (Chutes) and a second Claude CLI identity (`claude-cli-2`) to `agents.defaults.models`. Filing as one issue since they share a root cause: CLI-backend (`agentRuntime`) models are treated inconsistently compared to plain API-provider models.

## 1. `openclaw models list` crashes on any config entry with an empty model override

```
$ openclaw models list
[openclaw] Reason: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'input')
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'input')
    at applyAnthropicSonnet5Cost (register.runtime-*.js:366:24)
    at normalizeAnthropicResolvedModel (register.runtime-*.js:413:87)
    at normalizeProviderResolvedModelWithPlugin (provider-runtime-*.js:124:30)
    at normalizeListRowWithProviderPlugin (list.row-sources-*.js:116:21)
    at appendConfiguredRows (list.row-sources-*.js:388:33)
    at modelsListCommand (list.list-command-*.js:436:9)
```

Reproduces with a minimal config entry like:
```json
"agents": { "defaults": { "models": {
  "claude-cli-2/claude-sonnet-5": {}
}}}
```
`applyAnthropicSonnet5Cost` assumes `params.model.cost` is always populated, but for CLI-backend (`agentRuntime`) model entries, no cost object is ever synthesized upstream (these aren't API-billed, so there's nothing to put there). The function should guard for `model.cost` being undefined before reading `.input`/`.output`/etc. off it. This takes down the *entire* `models list` command — nothing prints, not just the offending row.

Workaround: `openclaw models list --provider <id>` avoids the crash (it apparently skips this normalizer for filtered queries).

## 2. Secondary CLI-backend ids (e.g. `claude-cli-2`) aren't recognized as authenticated

We run two parallel Claude CLI identities via `cliBackends.claude-cli` and `cliBackends.claude-cli-2` (same `command`, different `env.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` source). `openclaw models auth list` / `models status` has a special-cased "Claude CLI native auth" detection that recognizes the provider id `claude-cli` and synthesizes a valid profile from the CLI's own login state — but it's hardcoded to that exact id string. `claude-cli-2` (a legitimate, working second identity, confirmed via successful auto-fallback and a valid injected token) shows up as `Auth: no` in `models list --provider claude-cli-2`, even though it works fine at runtime.

This should generalize to any `cliBackends` entry that shares the same `command`/native-auth mechanism, not just the literal id `claude-cli`.

## 3. Manually switching to a CLI-backend model (Control UI) doesn't work, even though automatic fallback and `openclaw models set` do

- Automatic fallback through `claude-cli`/`claude-cli-2` works fine (confirmed).
- `openclaw models set claude-cli/claude-opus-4-8` at the CLI succeeds cleanly, no error.
- But using the Control UI's chat-model picker to manually swap to any `agentRuntime`-tagged model (all our Anthropic-tab and Claude-Cli-tab entries qualify, since they all carry `agentRuntime.id: claude-cli`) does not take effect as expected.

Best guess: the live "swap active model mid-session" path assumes a plain API-completions runtime and doesn't handle switching to a subprocess-based (`agentRuntime`) engine, unlike full session/agent restarts or fallback resolution, which do handle it. Would appreciate either support for this, or a clear error/explanation in the UI when it's not supported, rather than a silent no-op.

## 4. Built-in model aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`) can't be removed, only shadowed

```
$ openclaw models aliases remove sonnet
Error: Cannot remove "sonnet": it is a built-in alias for "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"
provided automatically by OpenClaw and is not stored in your config file.
```
These built-in aliases add extra rows to the model picker that duplicate the fully-named entries. Not a bug, but a feature request: allow removing/hiding built-in aliases via `openclaw models aliases remove`, rather than only allowing them to be redirected to a different target model.

Happy to provide the full (redacted) config or more repro details if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary
When an agent's `exec` tool call (in this case a BigQuery query run via a wrapper script) fails, the delivery layer's "Exec failed" warning banner is rendered in a way that's easy to overlook/disconnected from the assistant's main answer text. This allowed a real incident where the agent asserted confident, specific numeric figures to the user in a Slack channel while the underlying data-fetch had actually failed — with the only signal of the failure being a barely-visible warning banner tacked onto the same message.

## Observed incident
- Channel: Slack (via the `sheepomatic` OpenClaw Slack integration)
- The agent was asked for a sales figure (units/order-lines for a specific SKU category) from a BigQuery-backed skill.
- The delivered message stated confident, specific numbers (36,110 units / 30,093 order lines) as if they were a valid query result.
- The correct answer (verified afterward) was materially different: 13,837 units / 11,736 lines (Amazon-only, filtered correctly).
- The message *did* include a `⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed: bq.sh ...` warning banner, but it was easy to miss/read as unrelated noise sitting next to otherwise fully-formed, confident prose — nothing in the presentation made clear "the numbers above are NOT valid, the query that would produce them failed."

## Root cause
Two contributing factors:
1. **Agent-side**: the query underlying the failed exec call referenced invented/incorrect table or column names (e.g. `raw_amazon.orders` instead of the real `orders_all`, `purchase_date` instead of `purchase_date_pt`), which correctly caused BigQuery to return a 400/404 at the API level, and the `exec` call surfaced that as a non-zero exit. This part is a skill/agent-instruction issue (invented names) and not itself an OpenClaw bug.
2. **Platform-side (this is the reportable OpenClaw issue)**: despite the exec call failing, the model still emitted specific figures as if a query had succeeded, and OpenClaw's delivery layer only weakly surfaces that failure — a small, easily-glossed-over banner appended near/after confident answer text — rather than making it visually or structurally unmistakable that any adjacent numeric claims are unsupported by a successful tool result. There's nothing distinguishing "this exec failure is informational/side-channel" from "this exec failure means the primary answer has no valid data behind it."

## Why this matters
This is a hallucination/trust problem, not just cosmetics: an operator skimming a Slack message sees fluent, specific, confident numbers and has no strong visual/structural cue that the numbers are unsupported because the tool call that would have produced them actually failed. The warning is present but effectively hidden by the strength/fluency of the surrounding prose.

## Suggested improvements
- When a turn's final assistant message contains a numeric/factual claim that was supposed to be derived from a tool call that returned `isError: true` / non-zero exit, either:
  - Block/replace the response with an explicit "I couldn't get this — the query failed" message rather than allowing the model to freely narrate numbers in the same breath, or
  - Make the failed-exec banner much more prominent (e.g. leading the message, not trailing; distinguishing "the exec that supported this specific answer failed" from "an unrelated informational exec failed"), or
  - Provide the model/system prompt a strong structural signal (not just relying on skill-level instructions) that ties a failed data-fetch tool call to suppression of any confident claims in the same response.
- This class of problem is generic — it isn't specific to BigQuery or Slack; it's about how OpenClaw's delivery/composition layer handles "exec failed but assistant answered anyway" across any channel.

## Workaround applied locally
We added explicit, skill-level hard rules (`FAILED QUERY = NO DATA — NEVER FABRICATE RESULTS`) to force the model to treat any non-zero-exit/`ERROR:` result from our query-execution wrapper as "zero data available," and re-inject that rule after every skill sync so it survives upstream skill updates. This mitigates the specific case for our skill, but doesn't address the general platform gap where a fluently-composed answer can still slip past a de-emphasized failure banner.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)
- macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- Channel: Slack integration

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an explicit, trusted-user-click **Open in default app** action for fs-safe local workspace files in Control UI, backed by a typed operation such as `sessions.files.open`.

## Problem to solve

Control UI currently has to preview or download each file format itself. The workspace viewer now handles text and common images much better, but formats whose best viewer is a native application still require format-specific browser behavior or a download round trip. Examples include PDFs, presentations, office documents, CAD files, and other locally associated formats.

For a local desktop Gateway, clicking a file link should be able to hand the file to the operating system's registered application. The existing alternatives are inconsistent by format and make Control UI grow its own partial file viewer.

This request is intentionally narrower than serving arbitrary host paths. Existing containment and authorization boundaries should remain intact.

## Proposed solution

Add a sibling to the existing guarded `sessions.files.reveal` operation, for example:

```text
sessions.files.open
```

Suggested constraints:

- Operates initially only on a file resolved through the existing fs-safe session-workspace path machinery. Supporting additional explicitly configured roots can remain a separate policy decision.
- Requires an authenticated, explicit user gesture and an appropriate operator capability such as `operator.admin`; rendered Markdown must never auto-open a target.
- Reuses the same local-placement restrictions as `sessions.files.reveal`; refuse remote/exec-node placements where the browser action would unexpectedly launch an application on another host.
- Canonicalizes and validates containment, rejects missing targets/directories and unsafe symlink, hardlink, traversal, or TOCTOU cases, and requires a regular file.
- Invokes the existing cross-platform `open-path.ts` abstraction (`open`, `xdg-open`, or the Windows equivalent) with the path as data, never through a shell or generic exec route.
- Applies an explicit dangerous-file-type policy or administrator allowlist rather than assuming every registered handler is harmless.
- Returns a structured success/rejection result. If the capability is unavailable, Control UI keeps the existing preview/download behavior.

The UI could expose this in the file sidebar and as an action on eligible local-file links.

## Alternatives considered

- **Continue adding browser previews per MIME type:** useful for common formats, but it remains an incomplete reimplementation of native viewers.
- **Download every unsupported file:** adds an unnecessary copy and loses the natural local-file workflow.
- **Reveal in Finder/Explorer first:** safe and already close to available, but requires an extra user action every time.
- **Editor URL schemes:** suitable only for configured editors and not general file associations.
- **Generic Gateway exec:** rejected; this should be a narrow typed operation using the existing opener and file-safety boundary.

## Impact

- **Affected:** operators running Control UI against a local desktop Gateway and working with agent-produced workspace artifacts.
- **Severity:** medium UX friction rather than data loss.
- **Frequency:** occurs whenever an artifact's correct viewer is outside Control UI.
- **Consequence:** users download files unnecessarily or encounter inconsistent behavior between text, images, PDFs, presentations, and other formats.

## Evidence/examples

- #100615 / #100679 added the guarded workspace file viewer and explicitly left native reveal/open behavior outside that scope.
- #109422 already added typed `sessions.files.reveal`, local-placement checks, and the shared cross-platform path opener, so this can be a sibling capability instead of a new generic execution surface.
- #102691 / #102899 provide precedent for trusted-user-action native handoff for external HTTP(S) links.
- #84467 / #86620 correctly made arbitrary host-local Markdown paths inert rather than exposing them through Gateway routes.
- #95685 / #105015 intentionally avoid exposing outside-workspace metadata; this proposal preserves that boundary by default.

Observed locally on OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2` on macOS 26.5.2 arm64: a proof-of-concept authenticated user-click route handed canonical absolute and workspace-relative files to `/usr/bin/open` as a single non-shell argument. The browser produced no new tab, sidebar, or download, including a path containing spaces and shell metacharacters. This validates the UX, but the local patch is not proposed as upstream implementation because the existing typed file APIs provide a safer integration point.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

The Gateway host and the user's desktop are not always the same machine. The action therefore needs to be capability- and placement-aware and must not silently launch applications on a remote server. Arbitrary outside-workspace roots should not be bundled into the initial feature.

issues.body:
## Feature Request: Automatic Model Discovery for Configured Providers

### Problem
Currently, when a user configures a new provider (e.g., Novita AI, OpenRouter, etc.), they must manually add each model to the catalog before they can use it. This creates friction:

1. User adds provider config (baseUrl, apiKey)
2. User must *also* manually register each model they want to use
3. To switch models via Telegram `/model` command, each model must be pre-registered
4. New models released by the provider require manual updates

### Proposed Solution
**When a provider is configured, automatically fetch and register all available models from that provider's `/models` endpoint (OpenAI-compatible).**

- Provider config → auto-discover models → populate catalog
- Users can immediately switch between any model the provider offers
- New models appear automatically (periodic refresh or on-demand)
- No manual model registration needed

### Why This Matters
**Hermes Agent already does this and it's significantly better UX.**

In Hermes, you configure a provider once, and *all* its models become instantly available for switching. No config edits, no restarts, no manual model entries. This is the expected behavior for any modern AI agent framework.

### Benefits
- **Zero-config model switching**: Configure provider → use any model immediately
- **Future-proof**: New provider models auto-appear
- **Telegram/Discord friendly**: `/model` command works with full provider catalog
- **Reduces support burden**: No more "model not found" issues for valid provider models

### Implementation Sketch
```typescript
// When provider config is saved
async function onProviderConfigured(providerId: string, config: ProviderConfig) {
  const models = await fetch(`${config.baseUrl}/models`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}` }
  });
  await registerModels(providerId, models.data);
  schedulePeriodicRefresh(providerId); // optional
}
```

### Current Workaround (Painful)
Users must:
1. Edit config to add provider
2. Manually add each model to `models.providers.<id>.models`
3. Restart/hot-reload
4. Repeat when provider adds new models

### Request
Please implement automatic model discovery for OpenAI-compatible providers. This aligns OpenClaw with Hermes Agent's superior UX and eliminates a major friction point for multi-model workflows.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Sessions under an agent with `runtime.type: "acp"` execute tasks normally and
the reply eventually completes, but the Control UI webchat shows **no
incremental output during the turn** — content only appears after turn
completion. Native OpenClaw runtime sessions in the same webchat stream
token-by-token as expected.

Streaming appears to be enabled at every lower layer:

- `claude` CLI is spawned with `--include-partial-messages --output-format stream-json --verbose` (verified via `ps`)
- Model provider returns `text/event-stream` (verified in gateway's own provider-transport logs)
- `acp.stream.deliveryMode: "live"` was active before session creation (hot-reloaded, then gateway restarted; session created afterwards)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an ACP runtime agent as above with `deliveryMode: "live"`.
2. Open its chat in Control UI (`/chat/claude/<label>`), send a prompt that produces multi-step output over ~1-2 min, e.g. "count from 1 to 10, one line at a time".
3. Turn runs (reply-timing shows `reason=acp_dispatch`, `outcome=completed`, e.g. `totalMs=102557`) with many intermediate blocks (`thinking`/`text`/`tool_use`), but nothing renders incrementally.
4. On **every** ACP turn completion, journalctl shows:

```
[gateway] terminal session persistence failed
  session=agent:claude:acp:<uuid>
  run=<runId>
  error=Error: Terminal write owner changed before commit
```

This error fires for every completed ACP turn across two different ACP
sessions (interactive webchat-bound). It does not fire for native runtime
turns.

### Expected behavior

With `acp.stream.deliveryMode: "live"`, an interactive webchat-bound ACP
session should project harness output incrementally into the Control UI
transcript while the turn runs: assistant text/thinking blocks and tool
activity appearing progressively as the harness emits them — matching the
live streaming behavior of native OpenClaw runtime sessions on the same
webchat surface.

### Actual behavior

The turn executes normally in the harness (multi-block agentic output over
~100 s with `--include-partial-messages` active), but the webchat transcript
shows nothing during the run. The full reply only appears once the turn
completes, as if `final_only` were in effect. On every ACP turn completion
the gateway logs `terminal session persistence failed ... Terminal write
owner changed before commit`; native runtime sessions in the same webchat
stream token-by-token without any such error.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7

### Operating system

ubuntu 24.04

### Install method

npm global

### Model

deepseek-v41-flash

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek

### Additional provider/model setup details

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.7 (c074824) — current npm latest
- OS: Linux x64, Node v24.21.0, gateway mode `local`, webchat via Control UI
- ACP backend: bundled acpx plugin, agent `claude` (Claude Code via `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` wrapper)
- Harness model: routed through an OpenAI-compatible proxy endpoint (SSE-capable, verified)

## Config

```json
"acp": {
  "enabled": true,
  "backend": "acpx",
  "defaultAgent": "claude",
  "allowedAgents": ["claude"],
  "stream": { "deliveryMode": "live" }
}
```

Agent entry:

```json
"claude": {
  "name": "claude",
  "runtime": { "type": "acp", "acp": { "agent": "claude" } }
}
```



### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

## Suspected area

ACP session transcript persistence write-owner race in the turn-terminal
commit path — projected output never reaches the webchat transcript
incrementally. Dist code contains a sibling error pattern
(`Subagent abort-marker owner changed before commit`), suggesting a shared
commit-race guard.

## Impact

Cosmetic for delivery (task execution, results, multi-turn context all work),
but makes long ACP turns appear hung in the UI and defeats
`acp.stream.deliveryMode: "live"`.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add bounded native batch operations to the bundled Memory Wiki CLI so durable-reference automation can ingest related sources/syntheses and verify exact retrieval targets without launching OpenClaw or rebuilding/loading the wiki once per item.

### Problem

Today, automation has to call `openclaw wiki ingest`, `openclaw wiki apply`, and `openclaw wiki search` repeatedly. Each process pays CLI/plugin startup cost, each changed write compiles the vault, and each search independently prepares the digest/page candidates. A durable-reference ingestor that writes and verifies several related artifacts can therefore occupy the Gateway and memory subsystem for much longer than the underlying wiki work requires.

On an existing production-sized vault, three separate exact-target wiki searches took 60.138 seconds wall clock in total (19.773s, 20.568s, and 19.796s). The equivalent bounded batch took 4.120 seconds wall clock and reported 155ms inside the batch operation, with all three exact targets matched. That is a 14.6x wall-clock reduction for this workflow.

### Proposed solution

Add two machine-oriented, versioned JSON commands while leaving the existing single-operation commands unchanged:

- `openclaw wiki apply-batch`: preflight the complete bounded input, apply ordered source/synthesis operations under one vault mutation lease, preserve semantic no-ops, and compile at most once.
- `openclaw wiki search-batch`: run up to six wiki-only exact-target verifications from one digest and bounded page snapshot, returning bounded JSON evidence and failing only required misses.

The proposed limits are 16 write operations, 6 verification queries, 256 KiB input manifests, 8 MiB per source (32 MiB across a batch), and 1 MiB per synthesis. Agent-scoped vault resolution remains intact. Regular search remains the correct path when imported-source synchronization or shared-memory lookup is required.

### Alternatives considered

- Wrapper-side subprocess loops cannot share plugin startup, mutation coordination, compilation, or query snapshots.
- A third-party extension cannot safely reach the Memory Wiki's private mutation and query internals.
- Long-lived caches would add invalidation/lifecycle risk; a bounded per-command snapshot provides the speedup without persistent cache state.

### User impact

Durable-reference and migration automations finish faster, perform substantially less duplicate Memory Wiki work, and produce smaller bounded verification reports. Interactive and existing callers continue using the same commands and behavior.

### Validation performed on the candidate implementation

- Memory Wiki extension suite: 37 files, 312 tests passed.
- OpenClaw changed-file gate: formatting, TypeScript LOC ratchet, dependency policy, production/test typechecks, extension lint, API baseline, database-first guard, runtime loader guard, and zero runtime import cycles passed.
- Independent Codex review: no remaining actionable findings after fixes for complete source preflight and provenance consistency.

The implementation was developed with AI assistance and will be submitted as a linked pull request.

issues.body:
### What problem does this solve?

Workboard cards can currently appear complete without strong execution evidence. Examples include:

- Cards marked `done` without structured proof.
- Parent cards completed while required children or dependencies remain active.
- Planning/decomposition treated as implementation completion.
- Cards linked to open pull requests marked complete before review or merge.

This can make automation report work as finished when it is not.

### Proposed scope

Introduce fail-closed completion gates that:

- Require passed proof containing an exact command, URL, or artifact path plus a result note.
- Reject completion when required children, dependencies, or blockers remain unresolved.
- Keep planning/decomposition states distinct from execution completion.
- Require appropriate review/merge evidence for pull-request-linked work.
- Record explicit, reviewable waivers when follow-up child work intentionally remains open.
- Add diagnostics for legacy inconsistent cards without deleting or overwriting history.
- Preserve the existing authority split: Workboard records execution evidence; higher-level GitHub/Speculoos workflows remain authoritative for review and integration.

### Compatibility questions

- Should this enforcement live in core Workboard or remain a plugin-level policy?
- What legacy/import path should exist for cards created without proof?
- Should decomposition leave the parent open by default?
- What exact evidence is required for pull-request-linked cards?
- Should proof URLs, paths, or notes receive additional redaction or validation?

### Scope exclusions

This proposal intentionally excludes canonical task identity, source-reference metadata, tenant redesign, production configuration, credentials, and scheduler changes.

### Validation evidence

A local implementation prototype passes:

- Workboard extension tests: 185
- Contract tests: 1,428
- TypeScript extension check
- Oxlint with zero warnings/errors

No repository code, configuration, or credentials were changed; this issue is a proposal for maintainer discussion.

issues.body:
## Problem: Hardcoded 300s per-chat sequential queue timeout with no configuration or lifecycle hooks

### Description

The per-chat sequential queue in the Feishu channel has a hardcoded 300-second timeout (`DEFAULT_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 * 1e3`) defined in `monitor.account-*.js`. When an agent task exceeds this timeout, it is **evicted** from the queue (not aborted), allowing subsequent messages to proceed. However:

1. **No user feedback**: During the 300s window, the user sees nothing — no "processing" indicator, no acknowledgment.
2. **No configuration option**: `createSequentialQueue()` accepts a `taskTimeoutMs` parameter, but the call site never passes it, using the hardcoded default.
3. **No dispatch lifecycle hooks**: There's no way to execute code before a task enters the queue or when it starts processing.
4. **Reply ordering issues**: Evicted tasks continue running in the background and eventually send replies, but these may arrive out of order relative to newer messages.

### Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.11
- Channel: Feishu
- Agent: ACP (Claude Code via `claude-agent-acp`)

### Relevant Code

In the bundled dist file (e.g., `monitor.account-BmjJdZph.js`):

```javascript
// Line ~4809
const DEFAULT_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 * 1e3;

// Line ~4975 — taskTimeoutMs is accepted but never passed
const enqueue = createSequentialQueue({ onTaskTimeout: (key, timeoutMs) => {
    log(`feishu[${accountId}]: per-chat task exceeded ${timeoutMs}ms cap (key=${key}); evicting from queue...`);
} });
```

### Use Case

Long-running agent tasks (e.g., large file processing, multi-tool research, code review) regularly exceed 300s. When this happens:

1. User sends a message
2. Agent starts processing (>300s)
3. Task is evicted after 300s — queue is freed, user can send more messages
4. User has no idea their request is still being processed
5. If user sends another message, the reply order may be confused

### Suggested Solutions

1. **Make `taskTimeoutMs` configurable** via `openclaw.json` (e.g., `channels.feishu.taskTimeoutMs`)

2. **Add dispatch lifecycle hooks** — `onBeforeDispatch` / `onAfterDispatch` callbacks that allow sending acknowledgment messages before the task starts processing

3. **Support async dispatch mode** — allow the agent to immediately return an acknowledgment, then process in the background and deliver the result later via a separate channel (e.g., direct API call)

4. **Expose `createSequentialQueue` options** — the function already accepts `taskTimeoutMs` and `onTaskTimeout`; just pass them through from configuration

### Workaround

Currently the only workaround is to edit the dist file directly (changing `300 * 1e3` to a larger value), which gets overwritten on every `npm update`.

### Impact

This affects any integration where agent processing can exceed 5 minutes. The lack of feedback and configuration makes it difficult to use OpenClaw for complex, long-running tasks.

**Problem.** Every resolved exec approval produces an additional "Exec approval: Allowed/Denied" outcome event in the room, 1:1 with the prompt. On Matrix the native path emits it as an edit of the prompt, but the m.replace event still lands in the timeline (and same-chat `/approve` adds a confirmation reply), so busy rooms see each approval twice. Measured on a production Matrix deployment (2026.6.11): in our main room 100 of 493 bot messages (20%) were approval traffic; in a 3-person editorial room with non-technical teammates, 80% of bot messages were approval prompts — the 1:1 outcome echo doubles that load. The ✅/❌ reaction plus the updated prompt already convey the decision.

**Proposal.** Add an `outcome` knob to the existing approval config families, e.g. `approvals.exec.outcome: "update" | "message" | "none"` (default `"update"` = today's behavior) and/or `channels.<channel>.execApprovals.outcome`, consistent with the current `{enabled, approvers, target}` shape. `"none"` skips the outcome delivery entirely; decision state stays queryable via `/approve` / CLI.

**Workaround status.** None — the strings and delivery are hardcoded; no config key exists.

issues.body:
### Summary

Three readability refinements for the plain-text/`ranges` Markdown projection (iMessage and any `plain`-mechanism channel), on top of the #112985 migration: (1) collapse a link whose label is just its URL, (2) keep headings visually distinct when attributed styling can't render, and (3) attach a list to its intro line and put the blank line *after* the list instead of before it.

### Problem to solve

After #112985 the plain-text projection is much cleaner (no more raw `#`/`-`/`[]()`). But on channels where attributed styling is unavailable — e.g. iMessage over the AppleScript transport with SIP enabled, where the `ranges` (bold/italic) can't be applied and the recipient sees pure text — three things still read worse than they should. All examples below are the **actual** output of the current `main` iMessage projection (`extractMarkdownFormatRuns`) on compact input, captured by running the projection directly.

**1. Redundant link label.** Input `[example.com](https://example.com)` →

```
Link: example.com (https://example.com)
```

The label is the URL minus its scheme, so the parenthesized URL just duplicates it. `collectLinkFallbacks` (`packages/markdown-core/src/construct-fallbacks.ts:72-82`) only skips the suffix on a byte-exact `label === href`; `comparableHref` (`:77`) strips only `mailto:`. So `"example.com"` ≠ `"https://example.com"` and the suffix is appended.

**2. Headings lose all distinction in plain-text-only rendering.** Input `# Heading One` / `## Heading Two` →

```
Heading One
Heading Two
```

The `heading: "fallback"` construct with `headingStyle: "rich"` drops the `#` and emits a **bold range** instead. On a client that can't render the range (SIP-enabled iMessage), the heading is plain text — indistinguishable from body copy — and two adjacent headings also collide (no blank line between them). The reader can no longer tell "this is a heading."

**3. List spacing is inverted relative to how the intro reads.** Input `Steps:` + a bullet list, then `In order:` + a numbered list →

```
Steps:

• Item A
• Item B
In order:

1. First
2. Second
```

The blank line lands *between the intro line and its own list* (splitting "Steps:" from the bullets it introduces), while the list runs straight into the next paragraph (`• Item B` → `In order:` with no separation). The intro and its list read as one unit; the separation belongs *after* the list, not before it.

### Proposed solution

**1. Collapse redundant link labels.** In `collectLinkFallbacks` (`construct-fallbacks.ts:72-82`) and its mirror in `render-plain.ts:31-34`, normalize both label and href before comparison (strip `https?://`, a leading `www.`, and a trailing `/`); on match, drop the ` (href)` suffix and show the bare URL as the visible text: `Link: https://example.com`.

**2. Keep headings distinguishable when styling can't render.** Give the plain-text projection a heading affordance that survives without attributed ranges. The exact form is open for maintainer preference — reasonable options: keep the `#`/`##` prefix in the `fallback` path; or add an underline/dashes line; or upper-case a level-1 heading; or a leading marker. Also guarantee a blank line before a heading so adjacent headings don't collide. The goal, not the mechanism: a heading must remain visually a heading in pure text.

**3. Attach a list to its intro; separate after, not before.** When a top-level list immediately follows a paragraph (its intro), do not insert a blank line before the list; insert the blank line *after* the list instead. Spacing points involved: the before-list gap comes from the paragraph separator (`ir.ts` `appendParagraphSeparator`), the after-list gap from `appendTopLevelListSeparator` (`ir.ts:460-465`).

### Alternatives considered

- **Leave as-is (markdown-standard spacing).** CommonMark treats an intro paragraph and a following list as separate blocks, so a blank between them is "correct." But in a chat message the intro reads as the list's header; splitting them and then merging the list into the next paragraph reads worse for a non-technical recipient. The standard optimizes for document rendering, not chat plain text.
- **Rely on bold headings only (current `main`).** Fine on clients that render attributed ranges; on SIP-enabled iMessage (and any pure-text sink) it silently loses the heading. A text-visible affordance degrades gracefully in both.
- **Collapse links only on exact match (current).** Misses the extremely common "label is the bare domain" case; normalization is a small, safe superset.

### Impact

- Affected: plain-text/`ranges` channels — iMessage in particular (AppleScript transport, SIP enabled, a common security-conscious setup where the private-API bridge is off), and by the shared code path any `plain`-mechanism channel.
- Severity: readability/polish — no data loss, but messages to non-technical recipients look noisier and lose heading structure.
- Frequency: every message containing a bare-domain link, a heading, or an intro-plus-list.

### Evidence / examples

Before → after (iMessage, pure text):

```
Link: example.com (https://example.com)  →   Link: https://example.com

Heading One                              →   (some text-visible heading affordance,
Heading Two                                   distinct + separated — form open)

Steps:                                   →   Steps:
                                              • Item A
• Item A                                      • Item B
• Item B
In order:                                     In order:
                                              1. First
1. First                                      2. Second
2. Second
```

Source: current `main` (`bd48b7b26`), projection run via `extensions/imessage/src/markdown-format.ts` `extractMarkdownFormatRuns`. These refine, not undo, #112985.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Open to it — seeking maintainer preference on the heading affordance (item 2) first, since that one is a design choice; items 1 and 3 are self-contained.

### Additional information

Related: #97568 (open) — headings/lists lacking paragraph spacing, but on the Telegram rich-HTML path rather than markdown-core `ranges`/`plain`. No prior issue found for link-label collapse.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw runs well on Android inside proot-Debian under Termux (gateway, agents, and CLI all functional on `2026.7.1-2` / `0790d9f`, Node v22.23.1, ARM64), but there is no documented Android target, and shared storage (`/storage/emulated/0`, sdcardfs/FUSE) has behaviors that break workflows touching it.

1. **No symlinks on shared storage** — `ln -s` returns `EPERM` (`Permission denied`). Consequence: `npm install` is structurally impossible under `/storage/emulated/0`; `node_modules` must live on ext4 under `$HOME`.
2. **No exec on shared storage** — scripts/binaries under `/storage/emulated/0` cannot execute (`Permission denied`).
3. **Stale `st_size` after bulk file creation** — immediately after creating multiple files on shared storage, `stat` reported `st_size=0` for a file whose data blocks held the full content (`cat | wc -c` = 1861, `stat -c %s` = 0; `sync` did not clear it). git sizes blobs by `st_size`, so a `git add` in that window committed a 0-byte blob of a fully-present file. A fresh rewrite of the file refreshed the metadata.

Items 1-2 are platform design; item 3 is a data-integrity trap for any workspace/agent workflow that does bulk writes on shared storage and then runs git.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2` (build `0790d9f`), npm install
- proot-Debian under Termux, Android, ARM64 (`Linux aarch64`), Node v22.23.1

## Ask

- A short platform note for Android/Termux/proot: supported-in-practice status, "keep node_modules and workspaces on ext4 (`$HOME`)", and the stale-stat hazard with its mitigation (verify committed blob sizes after bulk creation; rewrite to refresh `st_size`).
- Optionally: a doctor/health check that flags a workspace living under `/storage/emulated/0`.

## Evidence

- Full field notes (reproductions, hex dumps, shas): https://github.com/musicman12091/obsidian-vault-mcp/blob/main/docs/android-sdcardfs-field-notes.md
- Symlink and exec `EPERM` re-confirmed live on-device this run.

## Summary
When using the OpenClaw iOS app through CarPlay, assistant voice replies are consistently truncated after approximately 3–7 seconds. The same replies play fully on the iPhone directly. This suggests the generated audio is complete and the truncation happens during CarPlay/Telegram playback.

## Environment
- iOS app: OpenClaw (latest TestFlight/App Store build as of 2026-07-22)
- iOS version: current stable
- CarPlay: wired/wireless (both observed)
- Audio routing: iPhone → CarPlay head unit

## Observed behavior
- Voice replies from assistant cut off mid-sentence on CarPlay.
- Reported cut-off points: 2.0s, 2.2s, 2.4s, 3.7s, 4.1s, 6.5s, 8.9s (varies).
- The same voice note plays fully when opened directly in Telegram on the iPhone.
- Very short replies (<~5 s) usually play through successfully.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Connect iPhone to CarPlay.
2. Open OpenClaw iOS app or receive a Telegram voice note generated by the assistant.
3. Trigger a voice reply longer than ~5 seconds.
4. Observe that playback stops before the audio ends.

## Expected behavior
Voice replies should play in full over CarPlay, matching direct iPhone playback.

## Additional context
- The assistant-generated OGG/Opus voice files are complete (verified by file size and direct playback).
- This affects both live Talk-mode replies and pre-generated briefing/digest voice notes sent via Telegram.

## Possible causes to investigate
- iOS audio session configuration for CarPlay (playback category, mixing, interruption handling).
- Telegram voice-player integration with CarPlay audio buffers.
- OpenClaw app not resuming/continuing TTS playback after CarPlay navigation or Siri ducking events.
- `AVAudioSession` route change handling when CarPlay becomes active.

## Request
Please investigate and adjust the iOS audio session / CarPlay playback path so voice replies are not truncated. If helpful, I can capture device logs or test specific builds.

issues.body:
## Bug summary

When spawning a subagent via `sessions_spawn` with a task that requires tool use (e.g. `exec`, `write`, `read`), the subagent's tool-call arguments are not transmitted to the model. Subagent runs spin for ~7 minutes and exit with 0 output tokens, claiming success in their completion message but producing no file artifacts on the host.

Models affected: confirmed on `anthropic-via-perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k2.7-code` and `anthropic-via-perplexity/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`. Likely affects all subagent models since both fail identically.

## Versions tested

- OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (e085fa1) — **fails**
- OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f) — **still fails** despite 2026.7.1 release notes claiming a fix for "incompatible tool definitions" during subagent delegated work.

## Reproduction

Minimal task:

```javascript
sessions_spawn({
  task: '1. Run: echo "test-2026-07-22" > /tmp/subagent_test.txt\n2. Run: cat /tmp/subagent_test.txt\n3. Report both outputs.',
  taskName: 'kimi_subagent_tool_test',
  runtime: 'subagent',
  model: 'anthropic-via-perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k2.7-code',
  lightContext: true,
})
```

## Expected

Subagent invokes `exec` twice, writes the test file to /tmp, reads it back, returns the output. File exists on host.

## Actual

- Subagent runtime: 7m2s (Kimi), 9m15s (Sonnet)
- Token usage: 0 input / 0 output
- Status: agent run aborted (OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT)
- No file produced at `/tmp/subagent_test.txt`
- Model's final completion message claims it performed the work but explicitly admits: *"the test commands could not be executed due to this tooling issue rather than a problem with the task logic itself"*
- Sonnet's completion message: *"Every invocation of exec returned: Validation failed for tool 'exec': command: must have required properties command — my parameter payload was empty on every call"*

## Smoke test (works)

A subagent task that does NOT need tools completes successfully:

```javascript
sessions_spawn({
  task: 'Reply with exactly: KIMI_OK',
  model: 'anthropic-via-perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k2.7-code',
  lightContext: true,
})
```

Returns `KIMI_OK` in ~2s with normal token output. So the subagent runtime and model integration are fine; only tool-call argument transmission is broken.

## Workaround

Do code/scripts work in the main session (not via `sessions_spawn`). For code-specialized models like Kimi, invoke via CLI: `openclaw infer model run --model "..." --prompt "..." --json` to get the model's reasoning, then execute tools in main session.

## Likely root cause

Tool-call argument serialization layer in the subagent runtime is dropping the `command`/`path`/`content` properties before the model sees them. Sandbox boundary may be involved — subagent exec appears to run in a sandboxed context that doesn't share /tmp with the host.

Filed by: bcstar-atl on 2026-07-22. Two subagent models confirmed affected, persists across 2 minor versions.

issues.body:
## Summary

Support owner-bound managed TaskFlow cancellation mutations that atomically persist controller `stateJson` together with native cancellation state under `expectedRevision`.

## Problem to solve

Managed TaskFlow controllers can revision-check normal state transitions, but cancellation currently has a gap:

- `requestCancel(...)` accepts `expectedRevision` but cannot persist controller `stateJson` in the same mutation.
- the terminal cancellation helper does not expose caller-supplied `expectedRevision` or `stateJson`.

A durable controller therefore has to choose between a split write, a second ledger, or losing the native `cancelled` projection. Split writes can leave native status and controller protocol state at different revisions after a crash or conflict.

## Proposed solution

Extend the owner-bound managed runtime so:

- `requestCancel(...)` accepts optional `stateJson` and persists it with `cancelRequestedAt` in one exact-revision mutation;
- a terminal `finalizeCancel(...)` mutation accepts `expectedRevision`, optional `stateJson`, and cancellation timestamps, then persists native `status: "cancelled"` and controller state in one mutation;
- stale revisions and wrong owners remain no-write failures;
- the existing async `cancel({ flowId, cfg })` helper remains available for cancellation dispatch and backward compatibility;
- no schema migration or additional persistence ledger is introduced.

## Alternatives considered

- **Two sequential TaskFlow writes:** rejected because a crash or revision race can expose torn controller/native state.
- **Project cancellation as `failed` or `blocked`:** technically possible but gives operators the wrong native status.
- **Store protocol state outside TaskFlow:** creates a second authoritative ledger and complicates recovery.

## Impact

Affected: plugin authors building durable managed TaskFlow controllers.

Severity: blocks workflows that require crash-safe, native cancellation semantics.

Frequency: every cancellation transition for such controllers.

Consequence: without this API, controllers cannot preserve both exact CAS semantics and an accurate native `cancelled` projection.

## Evidence/examples

The current managed TaskFlow API already supports `stateJson` plus `expectedRevision` for waiting, resume, success, and failure transitions. Cancellation is the remaining asymmetric transition. A focused implementation and tests are ready in a fork and will be linked from the PR.

## Implementation intent

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The change is designed to preserve current owner binding, child-settlement behavior, revision increments, SQLite persistence, and existing callers. It is AI-assisted; I reviewed the implementation and validation evidence.

issues.body:
## Motivation

WhatsApp is the only major chat channel in OpenClaw with no outbound message-edit surface: `streaming.mode: "progress"` (progress drafts) is available for Telegram, Discord, Slack, Mattermost and MS Teams, but not WhatsApp, and the WhatsApp channel exposes no `editMessage` action either.

For bots that run slow tools (in our case: live modbus parameter reads on solar inverters taking 30–90 s per call, driven from a WhatsApp support bot), the user currently gets no in-place status. Typing indicators + lifecycle status reactions help (thanks for those!), but an editable progress draft — one message updated as the agent reads/plans/calls tools, finalized in place — is a much better UX and already exists for the other channels.

## What the protocol allows

WhatsApp supports message edits within a ~15-minute window, and Baileys exposes this (`sock.sendMessage(jid, { text, edit: <key> })`). That window is more than enough for a progress draft whose lifetime is one agent turn.

## Proposal

- Wire an outbound edit capability into the WhatsApp channel adapter (Baileys edit send).
- Let `channels.whatsapp.streaming.mode: "progress"` opt into the same progress-draft renderer used by Telegram/Discord (compact tool-progress lines, finalize-in-place, fallback to normal delivery if the final edit fails).
- Fallback behavior when the edit window expires or an edit fails: send the final answer as a normal message and stop editing (same as the documented Telegram fallback).

## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.6.11, WhatsApp channel via Baileys, Linux gateway.

Happy to help test against a production WhatsApp bot.

issues.body:
## Summary

Please make the `voice-call` realtime barge-in detector configurable instead of relying on hardcoded speech-start sensitivity in the phone realtime path.

This is a request for the phone `voice-call` realtime path, not Google Meet/Talk mode. The practical issue is that the default local speech detector is too sensitive for some telephony/realtime deployments, so assistant playback can be cleared while the realtime voice model is still speaking.

## Current behavior

On current `main`, the phone realtime path has fixed barge-in sensitivity in these places:

- `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-audio-pacer.ts`
  - `DEFAULT_SPEECH_RMS_THRESHOLD = 0.035`
  - `DEFAULT_REQUIRED_LOUD_CHUNKS = 4`
- `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/realtime-handler.ts`
  - `BARGE_IN_REQUIRED_LOUD_CHUNKS = 2`
  - the handler constructs `RealtimeMulawSpeechStartDetector({ requiredLoudChunks: BARGE_IN_REQUIRED_LOUD_CHUNKS })`

Because the audio stream is paced in 20 ms telephony chunks, `requiredLoudChunks = 2` can treat roughly 40 ms of above-threshold audio as a barge-in. In practice, short noise bursts, echo/leakage from assistant playback, or normal phone audio artifacts can be enough to trigger `clearAudio()`.

## Observed impact

In a real phone/realtime deployment, the old values were too sensitive. The assistant voice model output was repeatedly interrupted: queued assistant audio was cleared while the model was still producing the reply, and the caller experienced the assistant output as cut off or silent for about 12-13 seconds before the conversation recovered.

This was especially painful because it looked like a model latency or generation problem from the caller side, but the root cause was local barge-in detection clearing outbound audio prematurely.

## Local workaround that fixed it

A local runtime override changed the barge-in detector to require a stronger, more sustained speech signal:

- `DEFAULT_SPEECH_RMS_THRESHOLD`: `0.035` -> `0.055`
- `BARGE_IN_REQUIRED_LOUD_CHUNKS`: `2` -> `8`

With 20 ms chunks, `requiredLoudChunks = 8` requires about 160 ms of sustained above-threshold audio before clearing assistant playback. That preserved intentional caller interruption while stopping the false-positive clears that caused the 12-13 second assistant-output gaps.

The current local deployment keeps this as a temporary `NODE_OPTIONS --import` overlay and reapplies it during the daily 03:45 update check. That is intentionally a downstream workaround, not a good long-term fix.

## Request

Please expose voice-call realtime barge-in detection settings in config, for example under `plugins.entries["voice-call"].config.realtime.bargeIn`:

```json
{
  "bargeIn": {
    "enabled": true,
    "speechRmsThreshold": 0.055,
    "requiredLoudChunks": 8,
    "requiredQuietChunks": 12
  }
}
```

Exact field names are not important, but the important knobs are:

- RMS threshold for local speech-start detection.
- Required consecutive loud chunks before treating input as barge-in.
- Required quiet chunks before resetting speaking state.
- Optionally a clear enable/disable switch for deployments that want provider-side turn detection only.

## Acceptance criteria

- The phone `voice-call` realtime handler reads barge-in detector values from plugin config.
- Existing defaults remain backward compatible unless maintainers choose to tune them.
- The handler passes configured values into `RealtimeMulawSpeechStartDetector` instead of hardcoding `BARGE_IN_REQUIRED_LOUD_CHUNKS = 2`.
- Tests cover default behavior and custom config values.
- Documentation mentions the tradeoff: lower values improve interruption responsiveness, higher values reduce false barge-in from noise/echo/telephony artifacts.

Related prior issues for context: #10949 and #9635 addressed earlier barge-in/TTS interruption behavior, but this request is specifically about making the realtime phone detector sensitivity configurable so deployments do not need to patch compiled output.

issues.body:
# [Bug]: Stalled direct chat model call surfaces "LLM request failed" instead of auto-resetting/retrying the wedged session

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Summary

A Telegram direct chat session with a large/previously compacted transcript wedged during the assistant/model stage; OpenClaw detected `active_work_without_progress`, aborted the embedded run after ~383s, and delivered a generic user-visible `LLM request failed.` instead of automatically resetting the hot session state and retrying from preserved durable memory.

This appears related to, but not fully covered by, closed issue #20910 ("Auto-reset session when all models time out (session bloat death spiral)"). In this incident the provider request did not behave like a normal timeout/fallback case: the Responses stream ended after ~383s with zero events/content blocks and `Request was aborted`, OpenClaw classified the failure as `unclassified`, no fallback was configured/used, and the direct chat required a manual `sessions.reset` to recover.

## Impact and severity

- Affected surface: Telegram direct bot account routed to an OpenClaw agent.
- Severity: high for chat use. The bot is reachable and receives user messages, but the user sees repeated `LLM request failed.` instead of the tutoring/assistant reply.
- Frequency in this session: occurred repeatedly for the same direct chat until manual session reset.
- Practical consequence: the human user kept messaging the bot, saw generic failures, and missed the intended response until an operator manually diagnosed and reset the exact session key.
- Risk: any long-lived channel session with substantial transcript/compaction history can enter this "gateway and channel are healthy, hot session is wedged" state. The current recovery path correctly detects and aborts, but does not perform the user-preserving automatic recovery step.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.1 (2e08f0f)`
- Update status: stable channel, no registry/git update available at time of incident.
- Install method: npm/Homebrew-managed package, LaunchAgent service.
- Package root: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`
- CLI entrypoint: `/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw`
- Service: LaunchAgent `ai.openclaw.gateway`
- Service command:
  - `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node`
  - `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`
  - `gateway`
  - `--port`
  - `18789`
- OS: macOS 26.3, build `25D125`
- Kernel: Darwin 25.3.0 arm64
- Gateway bind: `0.0.0.0:18789`
- Effective agent provider/model: `codex-lb/gpt-5.5`
- API path logged by OpenClaw: `openai-responses`
- Channel: Telegram, polling mode

## Steps to reproduce

This is not yet a minimal synthetic repro, but this is the end-to-end incident path observed on a real installed Gateway:

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.6.1` as the installed LaunchAgent gateway.
2. Configure a Telegram account and route a direct chat to an agent using `codex-lb/gpt-5.5`.
3. Let that direct session accumulate a large transcript and multiple compaction checkpoints.
   - The affected entry had `compactionCount: 23` after reset.
   - The reset output showed a prior compaction checkpoint preserving a long Russian review session summary.
4. Receive a normal Telegram direct user message in that session.
5. Observe that OpenClaw routes it correctly and starts an embedded agent/model run.
6. The model call produces no useful content for several minutes.
7. OpenClaw's stalled-session recovery aborts the embedded run.
8. OpenClaw delivers generic text `LLM request failed.` to the Telegram user.
9. Further messages in the same direct chat continue failing/stalling until an operator manually resets the exact session key:

```shell
openclaw gateway call sessions.reset \
  --params '{"key":"agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id>","reason":"reset"}' \
  --json \
  --timeout 60000
```

10. After reset, a non-delivered probe against the exact same session key succeeds in ~2.3s, and a delivered Telegram reply succeeds in ~3.3s.

## Expected behavior

When a long-lived channel session is classified as stalled due to `active_work_without_progress` and recovery aborts the embedded run:

1. OpenClaw should recognize the failure as a wedged hot session / compaction or transcript state problem when the gateway, channel, routing, and provider are otherwise reachable.
2. It should preserve durable agent memory/checkpoints, reset the active session file/key to a fresh safe state, and retry the user's turn once.
3. It should only surface a user-visible failure after the reset+retry also fails.
4. The user-facing message should avoid a raw/generic `LLM request failed.` when OpenClaw has enough context to perform a known recovery.
5. Operator diagnostics should clearly say something like `session reset/retry attempted after stalled model call` and include whether the retry succeeded.

## Actual behavior

OpenClaw did detect the session stall and abort the embedded run, but then surfaced the failure directly to the user. No automatic reset/retry was attempted.

The manual recovery that made the session healthy again was exactly:

```shell
openclaw gateway call sessions.reset \
  --params '{"key":"agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id>","reason":"reset"}' \
  --json \
  --timeout 60000
```

After that, the same direct session key responded normally and delivery succeeded.

## Evidence

### Gateway and channel were healthy

At diagnosis time the Gateway was up, the installed service was running, RPC worked, and the port listener existed:

```shell
openclaw --version
# OpenClaw 2026.6.1 (2e08f0f)

openclaw update status --json
# stable channel, latestVersion 2026.6.1, no update available

openclaw gateway status --require-rpc --json
# cli.version: 2026.6.1
# service.loaded: true
# service.runtime.status: running
# service.runtime.state: active
# gateway.bindHost: 0.0.0.0
# gateway.port: 18789
# rpc.ok: true
# rpc.capability: admin_capable

lsof -nP -iTCP:18789 -sTCP:LISTEN
# node ... TCP *:18789 (LISTEN)

curl -fsS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:18789/health
# {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
```

Telegram was connected and polling. The affected account showed `running:true`, `connected:true`, `lastError:null`, and recent inbound/outbound activity.

### Stalled-session detection occurred

OpenClaw diagnostic events showed an active model call making no progress:

```text
session.stalled
outcome=processing
reason=active_work_without_progress
queueDepth=1
activeWorkKind=model_call
```

The log line for the affected direct session:

```text
stalled session:
sessionKey=agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id>
state=processing
age=353s
queueDepth=1
reason=active_work_without_progress
classification=stalled_agent_run
activeWorkKind=model_call
lastProgress=model_call:stream_progress
lastProgressAge=353s
recovery=none
```

Then:

```text
stalled session:
state=processing
age=383s
reason=active_work_without_progress
classification=stalled_agent_run
activeWorkKind=model_call
lastProgress=model_call:stream_progress
lastProgressAge=383s
recovery=checking
```

### Provider stream ended with no usable content, then abort was surfaced

```text
[responses] stream_done
provider=codex-lb
api=openai-responses
model=gpt-5.5
elapsedMs=382908
events=0
types=
stopReason=stop
contentBlocks=0
```

Immediately after:

```text
[responses] error
provider=codex-lb
api=openai-responses
model=gpt-5.5
name=Error
status=undefined
code=undefined
type=undefined
message=Request was aborted
```

Then:

```text
stuck session recovery:
sessionKey=agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id>
age=383s
action=abort_embedded_run
aborted=true
drained=true
released=0
```

Failover decision:

```text
embedded_run_failover_decision
stage=assistant
decision=surface_error
provider=codex-lb
model=gpt-5.5
sourceProvider=codex-lb
sourceModel=gpt-5.5
fallbackConfigured=false
timedOut=false
aborted=true
rawErrorPreview="Request was aborted"
providerRuntimeFailureKind=unclassified
```

OpenClaw then delivered the failure text successfully over Telegram:

```text
telegram outbound send ok
accountId=<telegram-account>
chatId=<redacted-chat-id>
operation=sendMessage
deliveryKind=text
chunkCount=1

message dispatch completed
outcome=completed
duration=385848ms
```

The Telegram user-visible message was:

```text
LLM request failed.
```

### Manual reset fixed the exact session

Manual reset result:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "key": "agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id>",
  "entry": {
    "sessionId": "975ec9f4-b6fd-44a7-8171-4308c2a91005",
    "sessionFile": "/Users/<user>/.openclaw/agents/<agent-id>/sessions/2026-06-03T14-34-47-669Z_975ec9f4-b6fd-44a7-8171-4308c2a91005.jsonl",
    "systemSent": false,
    "abortedLastRun": false,
    "chatType": "direct",
    "model": "gpt-5.5",
    "modelProvider": "codex-lb",
    "compactionCount": 23,
    "origin": {
      "provider": "telegram",
      "surface": "telegram",
      "chatType": "direct",
      "accountId": "<telegram-account>"
    },
    "deliveryContext": {
      "channel": "telegram",
      "accountId": "<telegram-account>"
    }
  }
}
```

After reset, a non-delivered probe against the exact direct session key succeeded:

```shell
openclaw agent \
  --agent <agent-id> \
  --session-key agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id> \
  --message 'Diagnostic only after reset. Reply exactly: TINA_SESSION_OK' \
  --json \
  --timeout 60
```

Result:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "TINA_SESSION_OK"
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "durationMs": 2329,
      "agentMeta": {
        "provider": "codex-lb",
        "model": "gpt-5.5",
        "usage": {
          "input": 7239,
          "output": 8,
          "total": 7247
        }
      },
      "executionTrace": {
        "winnerProvider": "codex-lb",
        "winnerModel": "gpt-5.5",
        "attempts": [
          {
            "provider": "codex-lb",
            "model": "gpt-5.5",
            "result": "success",
            "stage": "assistant"
          }
        ],
        "fallbackUsed": false,
        "runner": "embedded"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A delivered reply then succeeded:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "deliverySucceeded": true,
    "deliveryStatus": {
      "requested": true,
      "attempted": true,
      "status": "sent",
      "succeeded": true,
      "resultCount": 1
    }
  }
}
```

## Why this looks like an OpenClaw bug

This was not a Telegram availability failure:

- Telegram channel/account was running and connected.
- Inbound messages were received.
- Routing matched the intended agent.
- Outbound Telegram delivery worked, including the bad `LLM request failed.` message and the later successful reply.

This was not a Gateway-down failure:

- Gateway health returned live.
- LaunchAgent service was running.
- RPC was OK.
- Port `18789` was listening.

This was not a permanent provider outage:

- A fresh diagnostic session using the same agent/provider/model returned `OPENCLAW_OK` in ~1.9s.
- The exact affected direct session returned `TINA_SESSION_OK` in ~2.3s after `sessions.reset`.
- A delivered reply using the exact affected direct session succeeded in ~3.3s after reset.

The defect is the recovery policy between:

1. Detecting a stalled direct session,
2. Aborting the embedded run,
3. Classifying the runtime failure,
4. Choosing `surface_error`,
5. Sending `LLM request failed.` to the human,
6. Not performing the same `sessions.reset` recovery that immediately fixed the session when run manually.

## Proposed fix

Add an automatic safe recovery path for channel-backed direct sessions when all of the following are true:

- session is `processing`;
- reason/classification is `active_work_without_progress` / `stalled_agent_run`;
- active work is `model_call` or embedded assistant run;
- recovery aborts the run successfully;
- provider result is aborted/unclassified/no-content, not a user/tool validation error;
- the channel account is healthy enough to deliver;
- the session has compaction history or active transcript size triggers indicating a likely hot-session/transcript wedge.

Suggested behavior:

1. Mark the failed run as aborted.
2. Preserve durable memory/checkpoints.
3. Reset the hot session entry using the same supported mechanism as `sessions.reset`.
4. Retry the user's original turn exactly once.
5. If retry succeeds, deliver the real reply and log `auto_session_reset_retry_succeeded`.
6. If retry fails, surface a clearer message and log `auto_session_reset_retry_failed` with the failed reason.

Guardrails:

- Do not reset indefinitely. One auto-reset retry per incoming message/session failure is enough.
- Do not reset on tool permission/validation errors or explicit provider auth errors.
- Keep the original inbound message id/trace linked to the retry for operator audit.
- Make the diagnostic/event stream show that an auto reset was attempted.

## Temporary workaround

Manual operator reset of the affected direct session:

```shell
openclaw gateway call sessions.reset \
  --params '{"key":"agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id>","reason":"reset"}' \
  --json \
  --timeout 60000
```

Then verify without delivering:

```shell
openclaw agent \
  --agent <agent-id> \
  --session-key agent:<agent-id>:telegram:direct:<redacted-chat-id> \
  --message 'Diagnostic only after reset. Reply exactly: OK' \
  --json \
  --timeout 60
```

## Additional notes

- The first attempted `sessions.reset` with a descriptive reason failed schema validation because `reason` appears to require a strict constant. That is probably fine, but a clearer CLI error or accepted enum in help would make operator recovery easier.
- The installed recovery runbook expected this exact manual reset shape for "large transcript failures can show up as preflight compaction stuck near maxActiveTranscriptBytes"; this incident confirms the runbook but suggests Gateway should perform the safe path automatically for channel sessions.
- Public issue is redacted: chat id, account names, local username, and human names have been omitted or generalized.

issues.body:
# Feature Request: Support physical model mapping / custom model aliases (to leverage GCP's Priority & Flex PayGo tiers)

## 🎯 Context: The 429 Problem on Vertex AI
When building advanced multi-agent workflows or processing massive context windows (such as long-running session summaries) on Google Cloud Vertex AI, applications are highly susceptible to `429 Resource Exhausted` rate-limits. This is caused by rigid local project quotas (Tokens Per Minute / Requests Per Minute) or transient global regional capacity spikes.

## ⚡ Google's Three Pay-As-You-Go (PayGo) Tiers
To solve this, Google Cloud has introduced distinct service tiers for Vertex AI Gemini models, controlled via headers (like `X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Shared-Request-Type`):
1. **Standard (1.0x Cost):** Default shared queue capacity.
2. **Priority (`priority` - ~1.8x Cost):** Premium queue, consistent low-latency SLAs, and bypasses standard project rate-limits. Highly effective for 429 immunity during critical workloads.
3. **Flex (`flex` - 0.5x Cost):** Latency-tolerant/background queue with a **50% discount** per token. Perfect for offline tasks, sub-agents, or cron jobs that run in the background.

## 🧩 The Gap in OpenClaw
OpenClaw's unified `Model` schema beautifully supports a custom `"headers"` property per model, which is merged and passed directly to the `@google/genai` client:
```json
{
  "id": "gemini-3.5-flash-flex",
  "name": "Gemini 3.5 Flash (Flex)",
  "headers": {
    "X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type": "shared",
    "X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Shared-Request-Type": "flex"
  }
}
```

However, if we define a virtual model ID like `"gemini-3.5-flash-flex"` to attach the custom headers, Vertex AI rejects the request with a **`404 Model Not Found`** because the `@google/genai` client passes the `model.id` verbatim to the underlying Google API endpoint (e.g. `.../models/gemini-3.5-flash-flex` doesn't exist).

Currently, there is no way to decouple the **User/Catalog Model ID** (used for routing/pricing/headers) from the **Physical Model ID** sent to the provider's API.

---

## 🚀 Suggested Solution

### Option A: Generic `physicalModelId` Override (Cleanest)
Add an optional `physicalModelId` (or `apiModelId`) property to the core `Model` interface in `packages/llm-core`. If present, the provider uses this physical string for the raw API request, while keeping the virtual `id` for OpenClaw's internal session matching, config routing, and custom headers.

In `google-shared.ts` (and other providers):
```typescript
return {
  model: model.physicalModelId ?? model.id,
  contents,
  config,
};
```

### Option B: Suffix stripping in `google-shared.ts` (Quick Hack)
Alternatively, the Google shared provider can automatically detect and strip custom trailing suffixes (like `-flex` or `-priority`) on-the-fly before passing the string to the Google client:
```typescript
return {
  model: model.id.endsWith("-flex") ? model.id.slice(0, -5) : model.id,
  contents,
  config,
};
```

*(Note: We applied Option B as a temporary hot-patch to our local runtime, and it immediately allowed us to route our background sub-agents and cron jobs to `gemini-3.5-flash-flex` with 50% billing savings, while keeping our main chat session on high-speed standard `gemini-3.5-flash`!)*

---

Let us know what you think is the best architectural path forward for OpenClaw to support these complex multi-tier setups natively!

## Summary

The `web_search` tool's JSON schema (in `dist/openclaw-tools-*.js` → `WebSearchSchema`) accepts: `query`, `count`, `country`, `language`, `freshness`, `date_after`, `date_before`, `search_lang`, `ui_lang`, `domain_filter`, `max_tokens`, `max_tokens_per_page`.

It does **not** expose Perplexity's `search_context_size` parameter (added by Perplexity in 2026) — the content-budget knob that controls how deeply Sonar searches: `low`, `medium`, `high`. When the active provider is Perplexity (e.g. `sonar` / `sonar-pro` / `sonar-deep-research`), agents have no way to ask for a deeper search via the tool surface.

## Effect we're seeing

In `three-cubes/tc-agent-zone`, agents doing research that requires depth (TAM analysis, competitor cards, regulatory review) end up issuing many shallow shotgun queries because they can't ask Sonar for a `high` content budget. Workarounds we use today: switch the agent's model mid-session to `perplexity-proxy/sonar-deep-research`, or fall back to manual Kairix + `web_fetch` against primary sources. Both work but neither is the right shape.

## Proposed change

Add `search_context_size` to `WebSearchSchema`:

```js
search_context_size: {
  type: "string",
  enum: ["low", "medium", "high"],
  description: "Provider-specific content budget hint. For Perplexity (sonar/*) this maps to web_search_options.search_context_size. Other providers may ignore."
}
```

Plumb it through to the Perplexity provider call as `web_search_options.search_context_size`. For non-Perplexity providers, the schema field can be silently ignored at the adapter level (or rejected with an actionable `fix:` per `agent-actionable-feedback.md`).

## Reference

- Perplexity API doc: https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/chat-completions-post — see `web_search_options.search_context_size`
- Our local workaround issue: filing as we go through the third-party-research review

Happy to PR the schema + adapter plumbing if helpful.

issues.body:
Today, all model-override surfaces (`/model`, `session_status(model=...)`, `sessions.patch`, the chat-header picker) write persistent session overrides. There is no atomic single-turn override.

For cost-discipline at scale on a multi-tier model routing scheme, agents need to escalate to a higher-tier model for a single turn and auto-revert without explicit cleanup. The sticky-switch workaround works but adds overhead (every phase boundary needs two `sessions.patch` calls and live discipline to revert) and creates a recurring failure mode: the session drifts up-tier when the revert is forgotten, burning higher-cost capacity on turns that do not need it.

## Proposed API additions (one of)

1. **`sessions.patch` with `scope: "next-turn"`** — patch applies to the next single agent turn and auto-reverts to the prior model on completion.
2. **Per-message `model` field in the chat-send payload** — overrides the session model for that send only; resolved model is reported in the response envelope.

Either form would replace the sticky-switch protocol with a single atomic operation and eliminate the drift failure mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- Per-turn override does not change persistent session state.
- Resolved model for the turn is reported in the response envelope (so agents can populate a visible per-turn signal in their reply).
- Works with a new `modelOverrideSource: "agent"` source kind so it does not collide with `user` overrides.
- Logged as an `override` event in any tooling that already consumes `sessions.patch`.

## Frame

Required infrastructure for cost-discipline at scale on multi-tier model routing. Sticky-switch works but burdens the agent with discipline drift; atomic per-turn override is the structural fix. Pairs naturally with a visible per-turn model signal in agent replies, which is otherwise hard to populate accurately from a sticky-switch implementation.
