issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior / configuration gap

### Summary

For Microsoft Teams channel-bound agents, OpenClaw currently forces channel thread replies into per-thread sessions after the #58615 fix. That is correct for many use cases, but it breaks agents that are intentionally bound to a whole Teams channel and expected to maintain a single continuous channel memory.

Concrete local example:

```text
agent:pm:msteams:channel:19:388fab7656954f8fb1af3839bac5127e@thread.skype
```

After the Teams thread isolation changes, inbound channel replies are routed into fragmented sessions such as:

```text
agent:pm:msteams:channel:19:388fab7656954f8fb1af3839bac5127e@thread.skype:thread:1778514795196
agent:pm:msteams:channel:19:388fab7656954f8fb1af3839bac5127e@thread.skype:thread:1778514795196:thread:1778515055246
```

The nested `:thread:OLD:thread:NEW` shape is related to #66771, but even after that is fixed, the remaining problem is that some Teams channel agents should not be split per thread at all.

### Expected behavior

There should be a supported configuration option to keep a Teams channel-bound agent on the canonical channel session key for all messages in that channel, including replies inside Teams threads.

For example, a channel-bound PM agent should keep using:

```text
agent:pm:msteams:channel:19:...@thread.skype
```

instead of automatically forking into:

```text
agent:pm:msteams:channel:19:...@thread.skype:thread:<messageId>
```

### Actual behavior

OpenClaw currently applies Teams channel thread session isolation globally. This can fragment channel-bound agents across many thread sessions, causing the agent to appear to forget prior channel context.

In one production channel, recent inspection found:

- 72 total PM sessions
- 57 matching the PM Teams channel base
- 56 thread sessions
- 52 nested thread sessions

This makes a channel-level PM agent behave like many separate thread-local agents.

### Why this is not just #58615 or #66771

- #58615 fixed cross-thread context bleed by introducing per-thread isolation. That is useful and should remain available.
- #66771 addresses malformed nested keys like `...:thread:OLD:thread:NEW`.
- This issue is about a missing policy/config choice: some channel-bound agents need canonical channel memory, not thread-isolated memory.

So the desired behavior is not “remove thread isolation”. It is “make Teams channel thread isolation configurable per channel/agent/session-binding policy”.

### Proposed solution

Add an explicit policy/config option for MSTeams channel session routing, for example one of:

```jsonc
{
  "channels": {
    "msteams": {
      "threadSessionPolicy": "thread" // current default
    }
  }
}
```

with supported values like:

- `thread` — current behavior: Teams channel thread replies use per-thread sessions
- `channel` — channel replies stay on the canonical channel session

Or, if this belongs in the existing session/thread binding config, expose it there with enough granularity to apply to channel-bound agents only.

A local hotfix that restored the desired behavior was:

```ts
function resolveMSTeamsRouteSessionKey(params) {
  if (params.isChannel) return params.baseSessionKey;
  return resolveThreadSessionKeys({
    baseSessionKey: params.baseSessionKey,
    threadId: undefined,
    parentSessionKey: undefined,
  }).sessionKey;
}
```

That is not proposed as the global default, only as the behavior needed behind an opt-in config/policy.

### Impact

For Teams channels where OpenClaw acts as a project-management or operations agent, fragmenting by Teams thread loses the intended shared channel memory. Users experience this as the agent “forgetting” instructions, project context, and prior channel decisions.

This is especially painful for long-lived channel agents used for project coordination.

### Version / environment

Observed locally after update to:

```text
OpenClaw 2026.5.7
msteams bundled/external plugin at @openclaw/msteams
```

The behavior was initially expected to be fixed around `2026.4.9`, but that fix addressed #58615 by adding thread isolation. This issue asks for a supported way to opt out of that isolation for channel-level agents.

### Related issues / PRs

- #58615 — msteams channel threads share the same session key / cross-thread context bleed
- #66771 — malformed mixed thread session key from old-session reselection
- #59294 — fix(msteams): isolate thread sessions, outbound targeting, and attachment resolution
- #78850 — normalize pre-suffixed thread session keys

issues.body:
## Summary

Long assistant messages in `openclaw tui` appear briefly, then disappear from the screen entirely (including from terminal scrollback) once the conversation continues. Shorter messages render normally. Only reproduced via the TUI so far.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.5.4 (325df3e)`
- Interface: `openclaw tui`
- pi-tui: bundled at `node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-tui/dist/tui.js`
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0, arm64)

## Symptom

- Send/receive a long assistant message that overflows the visible viewport.
- The full message is briefly visible while/just after streaming.
- After the next render (subsequent message, status/footer change, focus event, etc.), the message vanishes — and is also gone from terminal scrollback (cannot scroll up to recover it).
- Short messages are unaffected.

## Likely root cause

`pi-tui` uses normal-screen rendering plus a differential-redraw path that *occasionally* falls back to `fullRender(true)`. `fullRender(true)` issues:

```
\x1b[?2026h          (begin sync)
\x1b[2J\x1b[H\x1b[3J (clear screen + home + clear scrollback)
... rewrites only current `newLines` ...
\x1b[?2026l
```

The third escape (`\x1b[3J`) wipes the terminal’s scrollback buffer. After that, only the bottom `terminal_height` lines of `newLines` remain visible — anything that scrolled into scrollback during prior renders is gone.

There are three triggers for `fullRender(true)` in `pi-tui/dist/tui.js`:

1. `widthChanged` — line ~743
2. `heightChanged` (non-Termux) — line ~751
3. **`firstChanged < prevViewportTop`** — line ~842

(3) is the suspected culprit for this report. While a long assistant message streams, `AssistantMessageComponent` → `HyperlinkMarkdown` → `Markdown.setText()` invalidates and re-renders the entire markdown body on each chunk. As the body grows past the viewport, any changed line in the early portion of the rendered buffer (e.g., a line that re-flows due to a paragraph boundary shift, a blockquote close, or a code-fence open) sets `firstChanged` to a position above `prevViewportTop`. That triggers `fullRender(true)`, clearing scrollback and leaving only the last `height` lines visible.

Code references (paths within bundled openclaw install):

- `node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-tui/dist/tui.js`
  - `\x1b[2J\x1b[H\x1b[3J` in `fullRender` (within `doRender`)
  - `if (firstChanged < prevViewportTop) { fullRender(true); return; }`
- `dist/tui-CD7AaN2H.js`
  - `AssistantMessageComponent.setText` → `HyperlinkMarkdown.setText` → `Markdown.setText` → `invalidate()`

## Why it’s surprising

`pi-tui` deliberately uses normal-screen + scrollback (not alt-screen) so that conversation history remains scrollable in the user’s terminal. `\x1b[3J` in the `fullRender` path defeats that goal whenever a non-resize trigger fires — the user permanently loses the rendered content above the viewport.

## Suggested fixes

Pick one or combine:

1. **Drop `\x1b[3J` from the `firstChanged < prevViewportTop` path.** Width/height changes plausibly justify clearing scrollback (wrapping changes), but a content-change full-redraw doesn’t. For path (3), a redraw of just the visible viewport is sufficient.
2. **Stabilize early lines during streaming.** When only the trailing portion of a streaming markdown changes, ensure earlier lines are byte-identical to the previous render so `firstChanged` lands inside the viewport.
3. **Treat scroll-pinned content above viewport as immutable.** If `firstChanged < prevViewportTop`, accept that scrollback is authoritative for those lines and only redraw from `prevViewportTop` downward.

## Repro

1. Start `openclaw tui` in any terminal that supports `\x1b[3J` (iTerm2, Terminal.app, kitty, alacritty, Ghostty all do).
2. Ask a question that produces an assistant reply longer than the visible terminal height (e.g., “explain X in detail with examples and a code block”).
3. Wait for the reply to finish streaming, then send any follow-up — or trigger any event that re-renders (resize back-and-forth, focus change, status update).
4. Try to scroll up in the terminal. The long message is gone.

## Diagnostic capture

For maintainers reproducing locally:

```
PI_DEBUG_REDRAW=1 openclaw tui
# tail -f ~/.pi/agent/pi-debug.log
```

Each `fullRender` logs its reason (`first render`, `terminal width changed`, `terminal height changed`, `firstChanged < viewportTop`, `clearOnShrink`, `extraLines > height`, `deleted lines moved viewport up`). The expected log line for this bug is:

```
fullRender: firstChanged < viewportTop (<n> < <m>) (prev=<X>, new=<Y>, height=<H>)
```

## Related

- #44130 — TUI scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior (related auto-scroll family)
- #11269 (closed) — original auto-scroll-to-top regression

## Impact

UX bug — content the user already saw cannot be recovered, including via the terminal’s native scrollback. Long-form responses (explanations, code review output, plan documents) are the most affected.

Hi Peter 👋

First off – thank you for OpenClaw. We've been running it as a family and business assistant (Telegram integration, automations, cron jobs, Home Assistant control) and it has genuinely become part of our daily workflow. Really appreciate the work you and the team put into this.

**The problem:**

When a new release drops, it is currently unclear whether it is safe to update a production setup. For example:

- **v2026.4.24** had a postinstall pruning bug (#72042) that broke gateway startup – 1617 dist files missing
- **v2026.4.25** introduced the Active-Memory plugin, which caused 25-30s timeouts per message on Ollama setups (the plugin ran a blocking memory search before every reply)
- The MyClaw newsletter warned "do not upgrade to 4.24" – but this critical info was not in the release notes themselves

We run OpenClaw in production and cannot afford to install every update just to find out it breaks our setup. Right now we have no reliable way to know which versions are safe.

**Proposal:**

Add a simple stability indicator to each release, for example:

- ✅ **Production-ready** – tested and safe for daily-use / production setups
- ⚠️ **Early adopter** – new features, may have edge cases or plugin compatibility changes
- 🔴 **Known issues** – wait for next patch before updating

This could be:
- A line at the top of the release notes body
- A GitHub release label or tag
- A `stability` field in release metadata

For users who rely on OpenClaw for real work (not just experimentation), this single piece of information would save hours of troubleshooting and downtime. We would only update when a release is clearly marked as production-ready.

Thanks for considering! 🦞

*Context: Running OpenClaw as a production family/business assistant with Telegram, Ollama, Whisper, Home Assistant, cron automations.*

issues.body:
The cron tool (used by agents to create/update cron jobs) does not pass through several important payload fields:

- `payload.model` - which model to use for agentTurn jobs
- `payload.timeoutSeconds` - execution timeout
- `payload.contextTokens` - context window limit  
- `maxSpendUsd` - cost cap per run

These fields are supported by the gateway cron engine and stored in `~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json`, but the tool schema rejects them as unexpected properties.

**Impact:** Any cron job created or updated via the tool gets these fields silently stripped. The only workaround is direct file editing + gateway restart, which defeats the purpose of having a cron management tool.

**Expected:** The cron tool add/update schemas should accept these fields and pass them through to the gateway.

**Workaround:** Edit `~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json` directly and restart the gateway.

issues.body:
### Problem

When `PiEmbeddedRunner` assembles the system prompt, all injected content (SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, memory search results, skill metadata) enters the context window as flat text. The agent cannot distinguish:
- Content injected at session start vs. content freshly read in the current turn
- Volatile files (frequently changing) vs. stable configuration
- Stale memory search results vs. authoritative tool outputs

This leads to the agent treating potentially outdated information as current, causing incorrect decisions — especially in long-running sessions where injected project docs may have changed on disk.

### Prior Art

This is a recognized problem in the LLM agent space, but no framework has implemented an in-context solution:
- **MemOS (MemCubes)** — metadata-rich memory containers with provenance/versioning, but metadata stays external to the context window ([arXiv:2507.03724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03724))
- **OpenAI Agents SDK** — memory notes carry `last_update_date` + recency-wins conflict resolution, but limited to memory, not general context
- **"Architectures for Building Agentic AI"** — prescribes TTL policies, content hashes, typed slots per source ([arXiv:2512.09458](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.09458v1))
- **Chroma's "Context Rot" research** — demonstrates universal accuracy degradation with growing context across 18 frontier models

None of these implement **inline provenance metadata within the token stream** that the agent can reason over.

### Proposed Solution

Add structured metadata tags to each context segment during prompt assembly in `PiEmbeddedRunner`:

```
[source: SOUL.md, injected_at: session_start, volatile: true]
## Knowledge Principles
...

[source: memory_search, query: "auth flow", retrieved_at: turn_3, volatile: false]
The auth flow uses JWT tokens stored in...

[source: read("retriever.py"), turn: 12, volatile: false]
def retrieve(...): ...
```

**Agent-side behavior:** System prompt includes a rule: if `volatile=true` and `injected_at=session_start`, auto-trigger a re-read before relying on that content.

### Implementation Scope (incremental)

1. **Phase 1 — Prompt assembly tagging**: `PiEmbeddedRunner` annotates each injected segment with `source`, `injected_at`, `volatile`
2. **Phase 2 — Memory module**: `memory_search` / `memory_get` results carry `last_modified` timestamps
3. **Phase 3 — Agent instruction**: Add provenance-aware reasoning rules to the base system prompt
4. **Phase 4 — Orchestration-level auto-refresh**: Framework detects stale volatile segments and refreshes before inference (no longer relying on model compliance)

### Why OpenClaw is the right place for this

- `PiEmbeddedRunner` already separates context sources (SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, skills, memory) — the injection points are clear
- Metadata-only skill injection shows the team already thinks about context efficiency
- Context compaction + isolation mechanisms exist — provenance tagging is a natural extension
- No existing framework has done this — OpenClaw could set the standard

### Open Questions

- Should volatility be configured per-file (in `openclaw.json`) or inferred from file type/change frequency?
- How should this interact with context compaction — preserve tags through compaction, or re-tag after?
- Token overhead of metadata tags — worth measuring impact on context budget

Happy to contribute a PR for Phase 1 if the approach looks reasonable.

issues.body:
# Feature Request: Add Gateway Received Timestamp to Inbound Metadata

## Problem
Currently, the inbound metadata only includes the message timestamp from the source channel (e.g., WeChat message timestamp). This makes it impossible to calculate accurate **end-to-end processing latency**.

For channels using **long-polling** (e.g., openclaw-weixin with 35s timeout), the current calculation `current_time - source_timestamp` includes the long-poll wait time, which is not the actual processing time.

### Example Flow:
```
Message sent (source_timestamp) → [35s long-poll wait] → Gateway receives → Agent processes → Response sent
```

Current calculation measures: `Response time - Message sent time` = **Includes long-poll wait**

## Desired Behavior
Add a new field to inbound metadata:
- `receivedAt` (or `gatewayReceivedAt`): Timestamp when Gateway actually receives the message

### Expected Inbound Metadata:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "Tue 2026-03-24 20:41 GMT+8",  // Source channel timestamp
  "receivedAt": "Tue 2026-03-24 20:41:37.123 GMT+8"  // Gateway received timestamp
}
```

### Then agents can calculate accurate latency:
- **Processing latency**: `response_time - receivedAt` (actual agent processing time)
- **Channel latency**: `receivedAt - timestamp` (channel delivery time, including long-poll wait)

## Use Cases
1. **Performance monitoring**: Track actual agent processing time
2. **Debugging**: Identify bottlenecks (channel vs. agent)
3. **Channel comparison**: Compare long-poll vs. WebSocket latency characteristics

## Alternative Solutions
1. Add `processingStartedAt` timestamp (when agent starts processing)
2. Add both `gatewayReceivedAt` and `agentProcessingStartedAt`

## Priority
**Medium** - Improves observability and user experience, especially for long-poll channels.

## Additional Notes
- This is particularly important for channels with long-poll timeouts (WeChat, etc.)
- The timestamp format should be consistent (ISO 8601 with timezone)
- Should work across all channel types (WebSocket, HTTP webhook, long-poll)

issues.body:
## Feature Request

**Submitted by:** Kat Arbiz (kat@scalewithsystem.com)

## Summary

Add support for Discord `messageUpdate` and `messageDelete` gateway events so that:

1. **Edited messages** re-trigger agent processing (if the edited message contains a bot mention)
2. **Deleted messages** halt/abort the in-progress agent session that was triggered by that message

## Use Case

Running a multi-agent AI operating system via Discord as the primary chat interface. When I send a command to my bot and realize I made a mistake:

- **Current behavior:** I have to send a new "cancel" message and then re-send the corrected command. The original (wrong) command continues executing.
- **Desired behavior:** I edit the original message → the agent picks up the updated content. Or I delete the message → the running agent session is aborted.

## Proposed Behavior

### Message Edit (`messageUpdate`)
- If the edited message contains a bot mention and is mapped to an active or recent session:
  - If the session is still running: abort the current run and re-dispatch with the new content
  - If the session has completed: start a new session with the updated content
- If the edited message does NOT contain a bot mention: ignore (same as current)

### Message Delete (`messageDelete`)
- If the deleted message is mapped to an active session:
  - Send an abort signal to the running agent session
  - Optionally post a status message: "Command cancelled (message deleted)"
- If the session has already completed: no action needed

## Technical Notes

- The Discord extension uses `@buape/carbon` — event listeners would need to be added for `messageUpdate` and `messageDelete`
- Requires a mapping from Discord message IDs to OpenClaw session IDs (may already exist in session key normalization)
- The abort mechanism exists (`abortSignal` is already used in `channel.ts:626`)
- Relevant files: `extensions/discord/src/channel.ts`, `extensions/discord/src/monitor.ts`, session management layer

## Impact

This would make Discord a more natural and responsive interface for agent-driven workflows, especially for operators who use Discord as their primary command center.

## Environment
- OpenClaw version: 2026.3.23
- Discord extension: bundled
- Node.js: 25.1.0
- macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

Currently, Discord voice conversations are processed with `deliver: false`, meaning STT transcripts and AI responses are only played back as audio — no text appears in any channel. There is no way to route voice session messages to a companion text channel.

## Use Case

A common scenario: voice channel for real-time spoken conversation, with a paired text channel for a readable transcript. For example:
- Voice channel: `#영어-공부하기` (spoken English practice)
- Text channel: `#20-영어-스터디` (transcript + feedback visible to everyone)

## Proposed Change

Add an optional `sessionChannelId` field to `autoJoin` entries:

```jsonc
"voice": {
  "enabled": true,
  "autoJoin": [
    {
      "guildId": "1466079187864391861",
      "channelId": "1485599403099164743",       // voice channel (audio in/out)
      "sessionChannelId": "1485475228883750985"  // text channel to mirror transcript
    }
  ]
}
```

When `sessionChannelId` is set, the voice session route should use that channel instead of the voice channel ID. This routes the agent session (STT transcript + AI reply) to the specified text channel, making the conversation visible as text while audio playback continues in the voice channel.

## Current Behavior

`processSegment` builds the session route from the voice channel ID:
```ts
const sessionChannelId = channelInfo?.id ?? channelId; // always the voice channel
const route = resolveAgentRoute({ ..., peer: { kind: "channel", id: sessionChannelId } });
```

And calls `agentCommand` with `deliver: false`, so nothing is posted anywhere.

## Proposed Behavior

If `entry.sessionChannelId` is configured:
- Build `route` using the text channel ID instead of the voice channel ID
- Change `deliver: false` → `deliver: true` for the paired session
- Audio playback in the voice channel continues unchanged

## Alternatives Considered

- Hardcoding a mirror via the agent's system prompt (fragile, not configurable)
- Using a separate cron/session to relay messages (too indirect)

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.3.x
- Discord voice: working with `@snazzah/davey` installed (see #40669)

issues.body:
## Problem

Synology Chat's outgoing webhook integration sends a **HEAD request** to verify the endpoint before each POST. OpenClaw currently returns `405 Method Not Allowed` for HEAD requests, causing Synology to mark the webhook as broken and **stop delivering subsequent messages**.

Additionally, when OpenClaw successfully processes an incoming message, it responds with `204 No Content`. Synology Chat expects `200 OK` with `{"success":true}` in the body — receiving a 204 causes it to log _"Failed to send a request to the bot server"_ and suppress follow-up messages.

## Behavior

- After successfully processing a message, the bot shows:
  `(Only visible to you) Failed to send a request to the bot server. Please contact the bot owner.`
- Subsequent messages stop being delivered to OpenClaw

## Root Cause

In `extensions/synology-chat/src/webhook-handler.ts`:

1. `createWebhookHandler` returns 405 for any non-POST method, including HEAD
2. `respondNoContent()` sends `204` with no body instead of `200 + {"success":true}`

## Fix

- Handle HEAD requests by returning `200 OK`
- Change `respondNoContent` to return `200 OK` with `{"success":true}` body

## Testing

Verified end-to-end with a Synology NAS bot integration — Synology Chat successfully delivers messages and receives replies after this fix.

issues.body:
## Problem

Currently there is no dedicated Gateway RPC method to change the default agent. The only way is through `config.patch`, which requires:

1. Reading the full config to locate the target agent's index in `agents.list`
2. Constructing a merge-patch to set `default: true` on the target entry
3. Handling `baseHash` conflict resolution

This is unnecessarily complex for a common operation, especially for desktop/web clients that need a simple "set default agent" action in their UI.

## Current behavior

- `agents.list` returns `defaultId` (read-only)
- `agents.create` / `agents.update` / `agents.delete` exist for CRUD
- `agents.update` does **not** accept a `default` field
- Changing the default requires `config.patch` (ADMIN scope), which manipulates the raw config

## Proposed solution

Add an `agents.setDefault` RPC method:

```
Method: agents.setDefault
Scope: ADMIN
Params: { agentId: string }
Response: { ok: true, defaultId: string }
```

Behavior:
- Sets `default: true` on the specified agent entry in `agents.list`
- Clears `default` on all other entries
- Returns the new `defaultId`
- Rejects if `agentId` is not a configured agent

This would be consistent with how `agents.update` handles other per-agent mutations, and keeps the `config.patch` escape hatch for advanced bulk operations.

## Context

Building a desktop client (ClawWork) with an Agents management UI in Settings. We have full CRUD wired through `agents.create/update/delete`, but cannot offer a "set as default" button without either:
- Wiring the generic `config.patch` RPC (heavy, error-prone for this use case)
- Or having a dedicated `agents.setDefault` method

issues.body:
## Summary

In Feishu direct messages, a single user message can sometimes result in **two final assistant replies** when the primary model fails with rate limiting and OpenClaw falls back to a secondary model.

This appears to be **more than a Feishu rendering problem**. Based on logs, the likely issue is in the **failover + final reply delivery coordination** path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: `2026.3.13`
- Channel: `feishu`
- Connection mode: `websocket`
- Feishu channel config tested with:
  - `renderMode: "card"`
  - `streaming: false`
  - `blockStreaming: false`
- Primary model in observed runs: `openai-codex/gpt-5.4`
- Fallback model in observed runs: `cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4`

## What happens

Observed behavior pattern:

1. User sends a single Feishu DM.
2. OpenClaw dispatches the request once.
3. Primary model (`openai-codex/gpt-5.4`) fails with rate limit.
4. OpenClaw falls back to `cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4`.
5. In some runs, Feishu logs show:
   - `dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=2)`

This suggests that one inbound message / one dispatch can produce **two final replies**.

## Important finding

Disabling Feishu streaming did **not** fully solve the issue:

- `streaming: false`
- `blockStreaming: false`

After disabling both, duplicate final replies could still occur.

That makes this look less like a card streaming problem and more like a **final reply dedupe / failover delivery coordination** issue.

## Sanitized log excerpts

### Duplicate final reply after fallback success

```text
[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: ... isError=true model=gpt-5.4 provider=openai-codex error=⚠️ API rate limit reached. Please try again later.
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 candidate=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 reason=rate_limit next=cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_succeeded requested=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 candidate=cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4 reason=unknown next=none
[feishu] feishu[main]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=2)
```

### Another run where only one reply was sent

```text
[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: ... isError=true model=gpt-5.4 provider=openai-codex error=⚠️ API rate limit reached. Please try again later.
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 candidate=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 reason=rate_limit next=cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_succeeded requested=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 candidate=cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4 reason=unknown next=none
[feishu] feishu[main]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
```

### Cooldown probe behavior also observed

```text
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=probe_cooldown_candidate requested=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 candidate=openai-codex/gpt-5.4 reason=rate_limit next=cliproxyapi/gpt-5.4
[agent/embedded] probing cooldowned auth profile for openai-codex/gpt-5.4 due to rate_limit unavailability
```

## Why this matters

This has two user-visible / operational effects:

1. **Duplicate user-facing replies** in Feishu
2. **Extra model invocations / higher cost**, because the system frequently attempts the rate-limited primary model first and then falls back

## What I checked already

- Upgraded from `2026.3.8` to `2026.3.13`
- Disabled Feishu streaming
- Disabled Feishu block streaming
- Confirmed Feishu is running in websocket mode
- Confirmed only one gateway process is active
- Confirmed duplicate replies can still happen even with streaming disabled

## Likely root cause

My current hypothesis:

- The issue is in **reply finalization after failover**, not only in Feishu channel rendering.
- A single dispatch may pass through multiple final-delivery paths after fallback succeeds.
- Existing `queuedFinal` / final reply coordination appears insufficient for this Feishu + failover scenario.

## Possible improvements

A few ideas that might help:

1. **Stronger single-final-reply guard per dispatch**
   - Ensure one inbound dispatch can only emit one final reply regardless of failover path.

2. **Optional model-level cooldown / temporary bypass**
   - Today auth-profile cooldown exists, but the system still probes the primary model path aggressively.
   - A model-level temporary bypass after repeated `rate_limit` failures could reduce both duplicate-reply risk and wasted attempts.

3. **Configurable disable for transient cooldown probing**
   - Something like an opt-out for `probe_cooldown_candidate` behavior might help environments where repeated probing is undesirable.

## Question

Is this a known issue in the Feishu + failover path?

If needed, I can provide more sanitized logs / reproduction notes, but I intentionally removed all private chat identifiers and user identifiers here.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On one Windows installation running OpenClaw 2026.9.5, `plugins inspect discord --runtime --json` takes tens of seconds before producing successful output; tracing places the delay inside runtime inspection, not process shutdown.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On the affected Windows global npm installation with Discord configured, run `openclaw plugins inspect discord --runtime --json`.
2. Measure time to JSON output and process exit.

Observed in two instrumented diagnostic runs on this installation (approximately 33.5 s and 55.689 s overall). A clean-install deterministic reproduction and latest-version reproduction have not been established.

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

Both observed runs exited 0. The detailed run produced valid JSON with Discord status `loaded` and empty stderr. It spent approximately 44.818 seconds inside `withPluginDiagnosticsReportForInspection` (registry acquisition, formatting, and release), then exited naturally about 15 ms after JSON output.

A retained shared-state SQLite worker was idle and unreferenced at exit, as were its three MessagePorts and the 30-minute coordinator timer. These resources did not block shutdown. No worker cleanup attempt or failed termination was observed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5; Node.js v24.19.0

### Operating system

Windows (exact OS build not collected)

### Install method

Global npm installation

### Model

Not applicable: CLI plugin inspection; no model inference tested

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: local CLI plugin inspection; no inference routing tested

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized event summary; seconds relative to the inspection child preload:
6.290  shared-state worker open requested
7.557  worker open resolved
8.468  last worker.unref
9.306  inspection.scope entered
54.125 inspection.scope resolved
54.125 first JSON output
54.140 final CLI finalizer resolved
54.140 natural beforeExit, then exit 0

Overall launcher elapsed: 55.689 seconds. All eight observed CLI finalizers resolved, including agent-databases and plugin-registration-resources; none threw/rejected.

At beforeExit: one shared-state actor, references=1, stores=1, initialized=true, backendClosed=false; requests=0, operations=0, pendingOpens=0, queue=[]; no closing/retirement. Worker, three MessagePorts, and 1,800,000 ms timer: hasRef=false. No calls recorded to store.close, broker.close, closeActor, retire, or worker.terminate.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Timing was collected with a process-local Node loading hook wrapping the inspection scope, broker/store lifecycle methods, worker ref/unref/terminate, and CLI finalizers. Async resources were observed through weak references. Instrumentation and machine load may affect timing; these measurements are not an uninstrumented benchmark.

An unreferenced periodic diagnostic timer did not execute between approximately 5.010 and 53.726 seconds, consistent with substantial event-loop blocking. The responsible operation has not been CPU-profiled.

### Impact and severity

Observed on one Windows installation during Discord runtime inspection. Practical impact: tens of seconds waiting for diagnostic output. Both instrumented runs were slow, but general frequency is unknown. No data loss, failed Discord inspection, or shutdown hang was demonstrated.

### Additional information

The retained worker is included as diagnostic context, not a separate claimed cause or a proven defect. Its opening stack originates in configuration snapshot reading before inspection:
`io.snapshot-B7ifVteM.mjs:409,1059,2220` -> `openclaw-state-worker-store-Dt8l0iTE.mjs:136,70` -> `openSharedStateSqliteWorkerStore`.

Relevant installed source locations:
- `status-DFrqDNjy.mjs:315-333`: measured inspection scope, which awaits inspection.release.
- `openclaw-state-worker-store-Dt8l0iTE.mjs:65-82`: cached shared-state store; lines 27,36-41,116: owner cleanup registration.
- `one-shot-exit-H_TmFTWI.mjs:80-84`: agent-database CLI finalizer.
- `sqlite-worker-store-CpUHa3pA.mjs:449-461,638-648,853-918`: store/actor close and awaited termination; lines 754/802 unref and 810 ref.
- `sqlite-coordinator-CU9e2wyW.mjs:139-165,178-205`: idle timer cleanup and unref.

No installed source edits, gateway restart, forced broker drain, or configuration changes were performed. Before/after hashes matched for four inspected/instrumented modules. Local paths and configuration are omitted. Last-known-good version is unknown. The next useful diagnostic appears to be separate phase timing/CPU profiling of runtime registry acquisition, report formatting, and inspection release.

## Summary

Add an option to display timestamps on each message (user and assistant) in the TUI chat interface.

## Problem

The TUI currently shows messages without any time indication. When reviewing a conversation, there's no way to tell when a question was asked or when the response arrived. This makes it hard to:

- Track how long a response took
- Know when a conversation happened during scrollback
- Debug timing issues with agents/tools

Add a configurable timestamp display for each message in the TUI, similar to how chat apps show message times.

### Display format examples:
```
[11:32] User: my question here
[11:33] Assistant: the response here
```

### Suggested config:
```json
{
  "tui": {
    "showTimestamps": true,
    "timeFormat": "24"
  }
}
```

### Implementation notes:

- The gateway already tracks `updatedAt` on sessions
- Chat events (`evt.state === "delta" / "final"`) could include a server timestamp
- For history replay, transcript records likely already have timestamps
- `UserMessageComponent` and `AssistantMessageComponent` in the TUI would need a small label prepended

## Context

- Related: #2592 (envelopeDateFormat for agent-facing timestamps)
- Related: #25334 (channel messages lack timestamp for agents)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On the sideloaded Android node (ai.openclaw.app), sms.send fails for any single SMS longer than 160 GSM-7 characters, returning errorCode=UNAVAILABLE / SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1; messages ≤160 chars send fine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair a Samsung Android node (Galaxy Z Fold8, Android 17 / One UI 9) on Optus (AU), with SMS + Call Log permissions granted normally.
2. Trigger sms.send with a message ≤160 GSM-7 chars → succeeds.
3. Trigger sms.send with a message >160 chars (forces multipart) → fails; host returns SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1.

### Expected behavior

The long message is split and sent as a multipart SMS, the same way ≤160-char messages send successfully on the same device/app.

### Actual behavior

No SMS is sent. The host gateway log shows:
⇄ res ✗ node.invoke errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1
[openclaw] Reason: SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1
The inbound message that triggered this was 651 chars (well over the 160-char single-part limit).

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5

### Operating system

Host: macOS 26.5.2 (OpenClaw core on Mac mini). Node device: Android 17 / One UI 9 (Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8).

### Install method

Host: OpenClaw core on macOS. Node: sideloaded APK (package ai.openclaw.app), auto-built from the upstream repo by bighamx/openclaw-android-node-apk (builds upstream unmodified).

### Model

Gemini 3.5 flash lite

### Provider / routing chain

Openclaw Tailscale node

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

```shell
Host gateway (redacted):
Inbound message ... (direct, 651 chars)
⇄ res ✗ node.invoke errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1
[openclaw] Reason: SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1
[openclaw] Debug: set OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1 to include the stack trace.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Observation: on the Android node's Settings and permission manager, the app lists SMS and Call Log permissions but no "Phone" (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission entry, so it cannot be granted (pm grant also fails). SIM registers correctly as Optus (mNetworkRegistrationInfo shows mMcc=505 mMnc=02, rRplmn=50502).

### Impact and severity

Affected: any Samsung node user on a carrier whose config triggers the EMS-support check (reproduced on Optus AU); short single-part SMS unaffected.
Severity: High — blocks all long/multipart SMS from the node.
Frequency: Always, for any message >160 GSM-7 chars.
Consequence: Long messages to recipients silently fail (only surfaces as a permission error to the host), breaking automated SMS workflows; short messages still work.

### Additional information

Root cause (grounded in Android framework behavior): the multipart path (SmsManager.divideMessage() → fragmentText() → SmsMessage.hasEmsSupport()) calls TelephonyManager.getGroupIdLevel1(), which is guarded by READ_PHONE_STATE. On Samsung firmware shipping a NoEmsSupport carrier-config list, this reads GID1 whenever a message is fragmented; ≤160-char messages never hit it. The app declares SMS + Call Log but not READ_PHONE_STATE, so the permission never appears in Settings and cannot be granted.

Suggested remediation:
1. Declare android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE in the Android node manifest and request it at runtime alongside SEND_SMS; or
2. Catch the SecurityException in the split path and fall back to sending single-part chunks, so the feature degrades gracefully without the extra permission.

Note: reproduced on the auto-built APK from bighamx/openclaw-android-node-apk (which repackages upstream unmodified); filing here per the README's issue guidance. Prior tracking note: bighamx/openclaw-android-node-apk#1. The device recently switched carrier from Telstra (no failures) to Optus (failures begin) with no other change, which is consistent with the carrier-config-conditional EMS check.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After updating to 2026.9.2 OpenClaw running in a Docker container refuses instructions to "update itself", which is a custom skill that does a single operation - dropping a sentinel file that is a signal to the hosting environment to execute a script automating the official docker update procedure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start 2026.9.X and tell it to write a sentinel file, say "workspace/.ops/.update-requested" that will kick off OpenClaw update through your custom docker automation
2. This instruction will be rejected, because it violates the system instructions, or it will attempt to perform the docker update command, which is not actually intended for Docker

### Expected behavior

The agent should just oblige to execute this command because the strict instructions are only applicable to standalone install and not for Docker (which the instructions from the prompt-builder don't mention).

### Actual behavior

The agent refuses do to anything else than running the official update path when an update is somehow requested. No matter it does not apply in this context (docker install). The assistant acknowledged that Docker requires image replacement, yet remained stuck on the instruction wording.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2

### Operating system

ADM

### Install method

docker

### Model

github-copilot/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> github-copilot

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

github-copilot🤖gpt-6-astra📌🌗🐌 | 📚[⣿⡆⠐⠐⠐]872k 💰0.0000

### Impact and severity

Super frustrating, it completely broke by unattended upgrades that I could initiate from Telegram. They are scripted and can roll back, very stable, super convenient. Now I need to physically on the network and perform upgrade manually again. I wasted over 30 mins on two occasions already trying to convince the agent to simple drop a single file. It is just stubborn and keeps repeating it is not allowed.

### Additional information

The shipped prompt contains these two sentences:

> Update OpenClaw: gateway action update.run, only on explicit user request; restart and completion notice are automatic.

> Never run openclaw update, npm install -g openclaw, or stop/restart the gateway service via exec.

Astra 6 interprets these as a binding, blanket prohibition on initiating Docker image updates, including an explicitly owner-authorized external workflow - not just the commands listed.

These instructions are generated by the prompt builder, which should have a tailored version for docker installs.

My deployment uses an existing host-side updater: the agent creates a sentinel; the host stops the container, backs up state, pulls the image, recreates the container, and rolls back on failure. The agent neither runs an in-container package update nor controls Docker directly.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A valid, funded OpenRouter API key — confirmed working via direct curl against https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions — is consistently rejected by OpenClaw with 401/403 "authentication failed" errors, both via the desktop app's onboarding wizard and via CLI (models auth login + models status --probe). This persists across two full version updates (2026.9.4 → 2026.9.6) and multiple freshly-generated API keys.

Related and possibly overlapping root causes:

#145016 (staged route mismatch in onboarding wizard verify step)
#145929 / 
#148557 / 
#149993 / 
#151103 (auth store "lock may be busy" — false lock contention from a stale-snapshot comparison bug)
#59205 (same class of bug — valid key via curl, 401 via OpenClaw — previously seen with Ollama Cloud after an update)

Environment
OpenClaw version: 2026.9.4 → updated to 2026.9.6 (eb377ac) during troubleshooting, issue persists on both
OS: macOS GoldenGate(Apple Silicon, arm64)
Node version: v26.8.2
Install method: Homebrew npm global install + macOS desktop app 
Provider: OpenRouter, API key auth
Model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 (also reproduced with openrouter/auto)

### Steps to reproduce

Install OpenClaw desktop app on macOS, fresh workspace
Enter a valid OpenRouter API key either via the app's onboarding "Connect with an API key" screen, or via CLI:
   openclaw models auth login --provider openrouter --method api-key --agent main
Set the model explicitly:
   openclaw models set openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
Probe the connection:
   openclaw gateway stop
   openclaw models status --probe
   openclaw gateway start

### Expected behavior

The request should succeed (200), matching direct API behavior with the identical key and model.

### Actual behavior

[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 status=403 elapsedMs=1924
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 status=401 elapsedMs=99
⚠️ openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 request failed (authentication failed, HTTP 401). Re-authenticate the provider and try again.

Note the inconsistent status code across immediate retries of the same request (403 then 401) — this alone suggests non-deterministic request construction rather than a stable, correct rejection.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6

### Operating system

GoldenGate 27.0

### Install method

Npm global 

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5

### Provider / routing chain

open claw / Openrouter

### Additional provider/model setup details

Proof the key and model are valid (isolates this to OpenClaw)

Direct curl with the exact same key used in the failing OpenClaw probe:

bash
curl https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-...-066c14f5" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'

Result: 200, valid completion returned, real cost billed to the account (confirmed in OpenRouter dashboard usage).

Additional observed issues along the way (may be related or separate bugs)
Doubled model prefix: openclaw models set openrouter/auto silently saves the model as openrouter/openrouter/auto instead of openrouter/auto. Setting an explicit model (openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5) avoids this specific duplication.
Auth store / models.json desync: Across this session, openclaw models status repeatedly showed different key suffixes in the sqlite auth store (effective=profiles:...sqlite) versus models.json, even after using models auth login to set the key explicitly. The models.json value appears stale/unused once a sqlite profile exists, but is never cleaned up or reconciled, making models status output confusing/misleading.
The 2026.9.6 update's own migration duplicated the OpenRouter profile: post-update, models status --probe showed two profiles — openrouter:default and a new, previously-nonexistent openrouter:models-json — both independently failing with 401. It appears the update's doctor migration ([update] Doctor migration: openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 model configured, enabled automatically.) created a second profile from the stale models.json value rather than reconciling it with the existing sqlite profile.
models auth logout false "lock may be busy": Attempting to clean up the duplicate/stale profile via openclaw models auth logout openrouter:default --yes fails with Failed to remove auth profile "openrouter:default"; the auth store lock may be busy, reproduced with:
Gateway fully stopped (launchctl unload confirmed no process on port 18789)
PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); returning clean (busy: 0)
agent_database_leases table containing only a lease matching a confirmed-dead PID (removed manually, did not resolve the logout failure)
This matches the exact pattern described in 
#145929/
#148557/
#149980 (stale-snapshot comparison misreported as lock contention).
Desktop app appears to silently rewrite the OpenRouter key on launch/quit, independent of CLI-set values — observed the effective key change across multiple app relaunches without manual intervention, contributing to the desync in point 2.
Suggested starting points for maintainers
Given #59205 describes the identical class of symptom (valid key confirmed via curl, 401 via OpenClaw) for a different provider (Ollama Cloud) after an update, and diagnosed it as an Authorization-header construction issue — worth checking whether OpenRouter's provider adapter shares that same request-building code path.
The inconsistent 403→401 status codes across immediate retries of the identical request point at either non-deterministic header construction or a race between two now-duplicated auth profiles both being tried per request.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

[openclaw-openrouter-auth-bug-report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32836748/openclaw-openrouter-auth-bug-report.md)

### Impact and severity

Severity: High — complete, unrecoverable loss of function for an entire provider integration, with no user-side workaround.

Scope: Blocks 100% of OpenRouter usage through OpenClaw. OpenRouter is one of the primary "bring your own model routing" backends OpenClaw advertises, and this affects both onboarding paths into it (desktop app wizard and CLI), not an edge case within it.
Not user-fixable: This isn't a misconfiguration. It was reproduced with multiple independently-generated API keys, across a fresh workspace, across two full version updates, with the Gateway stopped, with stale state manually cleaned (dead leases removed, WAL checkpointed), and with the key's validity independently confirmed via direct curl. There is no sequence of user-side steps found that resolves it.
Silent data corruption risk: Beyond the auth failure itself, the bug actively damages user config during normal operation — the update process's own migration logic duplicated a working single auth profile into two conflicting ones (openrouter:default / openrouter:models-json), and the desktop app appears to silently rewrite the stored key on its own launch/quit cycle. A user who hasn't gone as deep into CLI/sqlite inspection as this report would have no way to detect that their config is being altered out from under them — they'd just see intermittent, unexplained auth failures.
Misleading diagnostics compound the problem: The "auth store lock may be busy" message actively misdirects troubleshooting effort toward lock contention (the natural read of that message) when the actual cause, per 
#149980, is a stale-snapshot comparison bug. This cost significant investigation time here chasing leases, WAL locks, and process ownership — all red herrings — before finding the real pattern.
No safe recovery path: The one built-in recovery mechanism attempted (openclaw update, hoping a newer release would fix it) instead made state worse by duplicating the auth profile. Version rollback was considered but not attempted, since none of the related open issues indicate a known-good prior version to roll back to.
User-facing consequence: A new user following the documented/expected setup flow (app onboarding → paste key → done) hits a hard, unexplained wall on their very first setup attempt, with the UI's own error message ("Review model runtime policy and retry") giving no actionable path forward. This is a first-run blocker, not a power-user edge case.

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw now has a narrow fix for one specific state mismatch: compaction can succeed after the runner stops waiting, and `sessions.json.compactionCount` needs to be reconciled afterward.

That solves a real bug, but it likely points to a broader design gap:

- compaction completion can become known **after** run-finalization logic has already moved on
- multiple user-visible surfaces depend on run-finalization snapshots instead of post-compaction truth
- timeout handling and state convergence are still only loosely coupled

This follow-up issue is about making that completion/reconciliation model more general.

## Motivation

Current state propagation is fragmented:

- transcript/session history persistence has one source of truth
- session-store counters and cached token snapshots are updated elsewhere
- channel/session recovery logic has its own timeout and abort semantics

That means timeout-late-success cases can leave different parts of the system disagreeing about what actually happened.

## What This Is Not

This is **not** a duplicate of narrower or adjacent issues such as:

- timeout/channel races
- session freeze / lane stall bugs
- `/compact` UX failures
- subagent-specific stats aggregation bugs

Those are related, but this follow-up is specifically about a more unified model for **post-timeout compaction completion semantics** and **state convergence**.

## Proposed Direction

Consider introducing a more explicit compaction completion reconciliation path that becomes the authoritative place to converge state after compaction finishes, even if the enclosing run already timed out or stopped waiting.

Potential scope:

- session-store counters (`compactionCount`)
- token/context snapshots used by `/status` and UI surfaces
- optional internal lifecycle/completion event for downstream consumers
- best-effort state repair after timeout-late-success outcomes

## Desirable Properties

Any generalized solution should preserve:

- current timeout bounds
- non-blocking conversation flow
- low resource usage
- monotonic/idempotent updates

## Possible Shape

A possible design direction:

1. Make compaction success/completion a first-class reconciliation event.
2. Route all post-compaction state convergence through that event.
3. Use monotonic updates (`max(...)` / compare-and-set style semantics) so late or duplicated signals do not corrupt counters.
4. Keep transcript scans off the hot path except as targeted fallback/recovery.

## Why A Separate Follow-Up

The current merged fix should stay narrow and low-risk.

A broader design would touch:

- runner completion semantics
- session-store persistence strategy
- `/status` and related state readers
- potentially channel/session recovery behavior

That deserves separate discussion and review.

## Related

- #45492
- #45493
- #11551
- #25272
- #38233
- #30116

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

### Summary

Agent runs complete successfully, but Telegram replies can remain in
`send_attempt_started` without any visible outbound platform call or receipt.
After a gateway restart, recovery refuses blind replay because the Telegram
adapter does not advertise `reconcileUnknownSend`, and the entry is marked
`failed`. The reply is not delivered and is marked failed after restart —
the user only sees the Telegram "seen" tick.

### Environment

- Channel: Telegram (bot account, direct DM)
- Gateway mode: local (systemd user service, ws://127.0.0.1:18789)

### Observed failure boundaries

- Agent execution: succeeds (`agent_run succeeded`, 13 tool calls in our case).
- Durable queue admission: succeeds (`send_attempt_started` recorded).
- Platform-send start marker: recorded (`platform_send_started_at` set).
- Telegram outbound call/receipt: not observed in gateway log (no
  `sendRichMessage` / `sendMessage ok` line).
- Restart recovery: refuses blind replay with "refusing blind replay without
  adapter reconciliation".
- User-visible result: no reply ("visto" only).


### What I believe is happening (two distinct failure layers)

1. **Primary — original delivery stalls:** the agent's reply is admitted to the
   durable queue and marked `send_attempt_started`, but no successful Telegram
   outbound call or receipt is visible in the gateway log. The exact point of
   failure is in the queue → adapter hand-off and still needs to be localized.
2. **Secondary — recovery cannot reconcile:** in the inspected build,
   `createTelegramOutboundAdapter` (`dist/outbound-adapter-CF1CXHOf.js`)
   declares `durableFinal` capabilities WITHOUT `reconcileUnknownSend`
   (text/media/payload/silent/replyTo/thread/messageSendingHooks/batch only).
   `reconcileUnknownQueuedDelivery()` (`dist/delivery-queue-Dwxuz2Ms.js`)
   returns null when the adapter lacks that capability, so ambiguous
   `send_attempt_started` entries fall back to `unknown_after_send` and are
   marked failed on restart rather than safely replayed.


### Related (not the same issue)

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43661 — compaction timeout →
  duplicate sends; same delivery-recovery area, different trigger.
- https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/message-lifecycle-refactor — documents the
  dangerous boundary between the platform call and the receipt commit, and the
  requirement for `reconcileUnknownSend` to classify interrupted sends.

### Additional information

- A direct `openclaw message send` to the same Telegram account and chat
succeeded and the message was received.
- The direct CLI send created no new durable delivery-queue entry, so it
  validates the direct Telegram path but does not validate the durable
  agent-to-channel path.
- No `resubmit` was attempted; no queue entries were modified.
- Truncated, redacted gateway logs are available on request.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the gateway, send a message to the bot via Telegram DM.
2. Let the agent finish its run (status `succeeded`).
3. Observe the outbound delivery stuck in `send_attempt_started`; no Telegram
   outbound send line appears in the gateway log.
4. Restart the gateway: recovery logs "refusing blind replay without adapter
   reconciliation"; the entry is marked `failed`.
5. The message never arrives.

### Expected behavior

The durable delivery should either (a) complete the actual platform call and
commit the receipt, or (b) when the outcome is ambiguous, reconcile with the
platform and classify the send as sent/not_sent/unresolved so it can be
recovered or surfaced — not silently dropped.

### Actual behavior

The agent completes its run successfully (openclaw audit shows "agent_run succeeded", 13 tool calls), but the reply never reaches the user on Telegram — the user only sees the "seen" tick.

Observed evidence:
- Durable queue entry recorded with "recovery_state = send_attempt_started" and "platform_send_started_at" set.
- No Telegram outbound send line ("sendRichMessage ok" / "sendMessage ok") appears in the gateway log between enqueue and restart.
- After "openclaw gateway restart", delivery recovery logs: "Delivery entry <id> delivery state is send_attempt_started; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation".
- The entry ends as "status=failed", "retry_count=0", "last_error=NULL".
- This exact signature is present in 163 of 166 historical failed outbound entries in the delivery queue (oldest 156 days old), reported by "openclaw health --verbose" as dead-lettered outbound deliveries.
- Control test: a direct "openclaw message send --channel telegram" to the same account and chat succeeds and the message is received, creating no durable queue entry.


### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), installed via npm (global)

### Operating system

Linux 5.15.0-187-generic (x64) · Node: 22.23.2

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free

### Provider / routing chain

Agent model requests route through a local 9Router instance (http://127.0.0.1:20128), which proxies to the upstream free model backend. The failure described in this issue is independent of the provider/model path: it occurs after the agent run completes, in the durable outbound delivery layer. Evidence: the same failure signature affects a cron-driven session (different session key, same send_attempt_started → failed result) and a direct CLI send bypassing the durable queue succeeds.

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Primary agent model: 9router/oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free (contextWindow 98300, maxTokens 8192).
- Fallback chain begins: 9router/oc/hy3-free, then external providers (minimax, openrouter, etc.).
- Telegram channel: single bot account, direct DM, token configured (no secrets included).
- No per-agent model overrides for the main session; the failing deliveries come from both the main session and scheduled cron sessions.


### Logs

```shell
Redacted key log/state evidence (all from 2026-08-19, Europe/Madrid):

1. Agent run completion (openclaw audit):
   06:54:42 | agent_run | succeeded | agent:main:main

2. Durable queue entry (state DB, redacted ids):
   queue_name=outbound | status=failed | recovery_state=send_attempt_started
   retry_count=0 | last_error=NULL | platform_send_started_at=<epoch ms>
   session_key=agent:main:main

3. Delivery recovery on gateway restart (gateway log):
   "Delivery entry <id> delivery state is send_attempt_started; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"
   "Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 2 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)"

4. Absence evidence: no "telegram sendRichMessage ok" / "sendMessage ok" line appears in the gateway log between the enqueue timestamp and the restart timestamp for either affected delivery.

5. Queue signature (state DB aggregate):
   163 of 166 failed outbound entries share recovery_state=send_attempt_started and last_error=NULL; oldest entry 156 days old (reported by "openclaw health --verbose" as dead-lettered outbound deliveries).

6. Control test (same account/chat, direct path): "openclaw message send --channel telegram ..." returned success and the message was received; no new durable queue entry was created.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- The bot can appear unresponsive ("seen" with no reply) even though the
  model and agent run complete successfully.
- The behavior was observed with both `best_effort` and `required` delivery
  policies.
- In this installation, 163 of 166 historical failed outbound entries share
  `send_attempt_started` with an empty `last_error`; the oldest is 156 days
  old, indicating a systemic issue rather than a one-off failure. `health
  --verbose` reports these as historical dead-lettered outbound deliveries.

### Additional information

- Direct CLI send ("openclaw message send --channel telegram ...") to the same account and chat succeeds and is received, and creates no durable queue entry — validating the direct Telegram path but not the durable agent-to-channel path.
- No resubmit was attempted; no queue entries were modified during diagnosis (read-only inspection only).
- The Telegram adapter in the inspected build (dist/outbound-adapter-CF1CXHOf.js) declares durableFinal capabilities WITHOUT reconcileUnknownSend, and reconcileUnknownQueuedDelivery() (dist/delivery-queue-Dwxuz2Ms.js) returns early when that capability is absent — consistent with the "refusing blind replay" behavior.
- Not filed as a regression: no last-known-good version is available (the 163/166 signature spans 156 days).
- Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43661 (same delivery-recovery area, different trigger — compaction timeout). Official docs describing the ambiguous-send boundary: https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/message-lifecycle-refactor

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Updating my Linux/Pi installation from OpenClaw 2026.9.4 to 2026.9.6 fails with runtime-verification-failed during the candidate gateway canary step.

The later attempt successfully resolved core/plugin metadata and installed the candidate into a private staging directory. The saved failure report then records:
startup: Candidate validation deadline exceeded (298088ms)

The live installation remained on 2026.9.4 with its Gateway running and connectivity probe passing. The upgrade is still unresolved.

### Steps to reproduce

An unpinned openclaw update initially failed with plugin-target-unavailable because the target core version was unknown.
An exact-version attempt failed with target-metadata-preflight / npm view failed, without an underlying npm error in the saved report.
Pi triage retried using:
openclaw update --tag 2026.9.6 --yes --json

Its command output was piped through tail -30.
Remaining npm logs show successful core and plugin metadata lookups, followed by a successful staged installation of 2026.9.6.
Later saved failure artifacts report the candidate canary deadline failure below.
My SSH session disconnected during this work. Its precise relationship to the validation failure is unknown.
Subsequent update attempts reported pending recovery. Explicit repair later reconciled two abandoned runs without maintenance or restart.

This is the observed sequence, not a confirmed minimal reproduction.

### Expected behavior

The candidate should complete validation and activate if healthy. If validation cannot finish, diagnostics should identify the blocking startup operation and how the validation budget was consumed.

### Actual behavior

The npm log records:

issues.body:
## Problem

When a session resets via `/new` or `/reset`, OpenClaw injects a hardcoded startup message into the conversation:

> *"A new session was started via /new or /reset. Execute your Session Startup sequence now - read the required files before responding to the user..."*

This text is great for bare/unconfigured deployments, but for fleets with `SOUL.md`, custom identity files, and established personas, it's jarring — it shows up as a cold system bubble in the Control UI and interrupts conversational flow.

## Request

Add a `session.resetPrompt` config key (global + per-agent) that overrides `BARE_SESSION_RESET_PROMPT_BASE`.

**Suggested shape (global):**
```json
"session": {
  "resetPrompt": "You're back. Pick up where you left off."
}
```

**Per-agent override in `agents.list[]`:**
```json
{
  "id": "omega",
  "session": {
    "resetPrompt": "You're back. Pick up where you left off."
  }
}
```

If `resetPrompt` is not set → falls back to the current default. No breaking change.

## Why it matters

Power users with configured agents and custom boot sequences already handle the startup logic in their soul/identity files. The hardcoded text adds noise and breaks flow — especially in the Control UI where it renders as a visible chat bubble on every `/new` or `/reset`.

A one-line config key would let fleets with real personas keep the session handoff clean without changing any default behavior for standard deployments.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

task_runs.detail_json omits the usage field despite it being explicitly scoped in #106041, so any cron job with sessionTarget: isolated has no recoverable token/cost usage once its session is cleaned up.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a cron job with sessionTarget: isolated that calls a model (e.g. an agentTurn job).
2. Let the job run and complete normally.
3. Query task_runs.detail_json for that job's run (e.g. via the state DB) and observe the field set: kind, status, completionStatus, error, summary, storeKey, delivered, deliveryStatus, delivery, sessionId, runAtMs, durationMs, nextRunAtMs, model, provider.
4. Note that usage is absent, even though model and sessionId were captured synchronously at the same completion write.
5. Separately, check the isolated session's transcript file (~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/sessions/<sessionId>.jsonl) after a few minutes — it will already be deleted by cleanup, so there's no fallback source for the usage data either.

### Expected behavior

task_runs.detail_json should include a usage field (token counts/cost), since #106041's plan explicitly listed "model/usage" as fields the new ledger column would carry, alongside model and sessionId, which did ship.

### Actual behavior

detail_json's field set (confirmed live against a running Gateway's state DB) is: kind, status, completionStatus, error, summary, storeKey, delivered, deliveryStatus, delivery, sessionId, runAtMs, durationMs, nextRunAtMs, model, provider. There is no usage field anywhere in it. Because isolated cron sessions are cleaned up shortly after completion (confirmed: 9 checked sessions were already gone at ages ranging 12.6–134.3 minutes), and a workspace-level daily cost logger scans session files at a fixed time (23:55 local) rather than reading from detail_json, usage for isolated-session jobs is unrecoverable after the fact. Concrete example: the "Memory Dreaming Promotion" cron job (sessionTarget: isolated, running daily on the default Sonnet model) shows sonnet_turns: 0 in the daily cost log on 20/20 consecutive logged days, despite confirmed daily execution via cron_run_receipts.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (3928bad)

### Operating system

masOS 27

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 (affected job normally runs on default/unset model, which resolves to anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 -- but the missing usage field affects isolated-session jobs on any model, not just this one)

### Provider / routing chain

anthropic (direct API, no proxy/router involved)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Planned (per #106041, "PR 1 (phases 1–2): make the ledger authoritative, flip reads"):
"Add a generic detail_json column to task_runs (typed codec per runtime); cron writes full run detail (delivery status/trace, errorReason, triggerFired, nextRunAtMs, model/usage) and real ownerKey/agentId instead of the lobotomized mirror."

Shipped (#106392, confirmed live against a running Gateway's state DB, task_runs.detail_json JSON keys):
kind, status, completionStatus, error, summary, storeKey, delivered, deliveryStatus, delivery, sessionId, runAtMs, durationMs, nextRunAtMs, model, provider

model and sessionId shipped; usage did not, despite the write happening synchronously at job completion, before session cleanup.

Why interval-based polling doesn't fix this: a workaround (a separate job polling session files every 10-15 min, ahead of cleanup) was prototyped and retracted. The affected job's own run durations are 11.5-14.6 seconds end-to-end -- the entire session can exist and be gone well inside a single polling interval. No interval can reliably beat a cleanup process that isn't bounded below by anything longer than the job itself.

Proposed fix: add a usage field to the same completion-time write that already produces detail_json's model and sessionId fields. This closes the race entirely rather than trying to outrun it, since there's no delay or interval to tune.

References: Plan #106041 (merged, closed), Implementation #106392 (merged), Related but distinct #94237 (closed, never merged -- attempted to log cache_read_tokens/estimated_cost_usd into cron_run_logs at run time; predates the ledger unification).
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: Anyone running cron jobs with sessionTarget: isolated (any job that calls a model in a throwaway session, as opposed to the persistent main/heartbeat session)
Severity: High (silent data loss -- no error, no warning, just missing cost/usage data with no way to reconstruct it after the fact)
Frequency: Always -- 20/20 consecutive days for the isolated job checked, 100% miss rate, not intermittent
Consequence: Cost/token tracking is systematically wrong for any workload run in isolated cron sessions. A model regression (e.g. a job silently running on a more expensive model than intended) could go undetected indefinitely, since the very mechanism meant to catch that -- the daily cost log -- structurally can't see it

### Additional information

Not a regression in the traditional sense -- the usage field was never shipped, so there's no "last known good" version where this worked. It was scoped in the plan (#106041) but the field was dropped somewhere before or during implementation (#106392) and never tracked as a follow-up.

issues.body:
## Problem

Agent sessions accumulate context indefinitely. Without a maximum lifetime, sessions grow until they hit provider limits or cause timeouts. We observed sessions running for 6+ days without rotation, accumulating 171k/200k tokens and 71 timeouts.

## Proposed Solution

Add a configurable session TTL:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "sessionMaxAge": "24h",
      "sessionMaxTurns": 50
    }
  }
}
```

When a session exceeds max age or max turns:
1. Auto-save agent memory (trigger a system event asking the agent to persist state)
2. Start a fresh session
3. Log the rotation event

## Workaround

We use cron-based session hygiene: a job runs every 4 hours checking context usage and resetting sessions at ≥85% capacity. This works but is coarse — it catches bloat after it happens rather than preventing it.

## Context

Fleet of 24 agents. `contextTokens: 180000` is set (triggers compaction), but compaction preserves the session — it doesn't rotate. A true TTL would complement compaction by ensuring clean starts before context quality degrades from repeated compaction.

issues.body:
## Problem

The system prompt preamble in `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` (line 423) is hardcoded:

```typescript
"You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw."
```

This line appears at the **very start** of the system prompt, making it the highest-priority identity instruction for the model. When agents have custom identities defined in SOUL.md (e.g., "You are Bob, VP of Engineering at Acme Corp"), the model consistently identifies as "a personal assistant" because:

1. The hardcoded preamble appears first (highest priority position)
2. SOUL.md content is injected much later under `# Project Context` (lower priority)
3. The SOUL.md guidance says "embody its persona and tone... **unless higher-priority instructions override it**" — the model interprets the preamble as that higher-priority instruction

This makes it impossible for agents to have custom roles/identities. Even with aggressive override language in SOUL.md ("CORRECTION: ignore the personal assistant line"), models consistently follow the preamble.

## Proposed Solution

Make the preamble configurable via `openclaw.json`, with fallback to the current default:

```jsonc
// openclaw.json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "preamble": "You are ${name}, ${role} at ${org}."
    },
    "list": [
      {
        "id": "bob",
        "preamble": "You are Bob, VP of Engineering at Integrity Labs."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Or alternatively, when SOUL.md exists, replace the preamble with a neutral line like:

```
"You are an agent running inside OpenClaw. Your identity is defined in SOUL.md below."
```

## Minimal Change

In `buildAgentSystemPrompt()`, the fix could be as simple as:

```typescript
const preamble = params.preamble ?? "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.";
const lines = [preamble, "", "## Tooling", ...];
```

With the config plumbed from `agents.list[].preamble` or `agents.defaults.preamble`.

## Context

- Using SOUL.md with detailed agent personas (name, title, organization, personality)
- Tested with multiple models (Claude, OpenRouter) — all follow the hardcoded preamble over SOUL.md content
- The current workaround of adding "CORRECTION: ignore the personal assistant line" to SOUL.md does not work reliably
- This blocks any serious use of custom agent identities

## Environment

- OpenClaw latest (2026.x)
- macOS
- Multiple LLM providers tested
