issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Exec completions from an isolated cron job with `delivery.mode: "announce"` are still queued on the agent main session (`agent:<id>:main`), not on the cron run that started the exec. Each completion runs a full model turn on the main session.

#170872 was closed as fixed by #167113. That fix only silences the completion when the job's delivery is private (`none`/webhook). The remap to the main session is unchanged on `main` (285cf098c593), so announce jobs still pay for one main-session turn per backgrounded exec.

### Steps to reproduce

Setup in which this was observed:

1. An agent with its default main session (never reset).
2. Isolated cron jobs (`sessionTarget: "isolated"`) with `delivery.mode: "announce"` whose agent runs shell commands that outlive the exec `yieldMs`. The commands print output, and some finish after the run has ended or without being polled to completion.
3. Let the jobs fire over a few days.
4. Inspect `agent:main:main`. There is one new turn per such completion.

For the routing step alone, the deterministic `runExecProcess` queue check described in #170872 still applies on `main`: a cron-run session key is mapped to the agent main key.

### Expected behavior

The completion goes back to the run that started the exec while that run is active. Once that run has ended, the completion is dropped; the output stays available through `process log`. This holds whatever the job's delivery mode is.

The completion should not start a turn on the agent main session, which did not start the exec and does nothing with it.

### Actual behavior

Observed on 2026.10.3 from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-15:

- 72 turns ran on `agent:main:main`, triggered by exec completions from two announce-delivery cron jobs: a daily health-check round and a nightly audit. All 72 replied `NO_REPLY`.
- One night alone had 28 such turns.
- The main session had never been reset and had grown to about 250k tokens of context. Every wake re-read that context on the agent's default model (Opus 5.5), using about 0.24% of the weekly subscription quota in that one night for turns nobody saw.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (observed). The routing was re-checked by source inspection on `main` at 285cf098c593. It has not been run on 2026.10.5-beta.

### Operating system

macOS 26.4.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global install (Node v24.21.0)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (agent default, used by the main-session turns)

### Provider / routing chain

anthropic via the claude-cli agent runtime; the exec tool is the OpenClaw `exec` tool

### Impact and severity

This costs money but does not leak anything. Every backgrounded exec in an announce cron job becomes an extra model turn on the main session. When the main session is long-lived, that turn is expensive (here ~250k context each time), and its output never reaches anyone.

Workaround we use: reset `agent:<id>:main` daily when it holds no human messages.

### Additional information

Code path on `main` (285cf098c593):

1. `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts:95` resolves the event session with `resolveEventSessionKeyForPolicy(sessionKey, eventRouting)`. Line 114 enqueues an ordinary session event there.
2. `src/infra/event-session-routing.ts:234` calls `resolveEventSessionKey` (`src/routing/session-key.ts:76`), which maps every cron-run key to `buildAgentMainSessionKey(...)`.
3. `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts:35` sets `sessionEventDelivery: false` only when `sourceDelivery.normalFinal === "private"`. The #167113 silencing therefore does not cover announce jobs.

The cron-run remap came in with #80214, when completions were drained by the heartbeat. #167113 replaced the heartbeat producer with ordinary session events, so the remap may no longer be needed. Routing the event to the cron run's own session key, or dropping it when that run has ended, would fix this.

Related: #170872, #167113, #80214.

issues.title: [Bug]: Managed Git update passes rehearsal then rejects held deleted-agent schemas, leaves Gateway offline

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A native managed Git update from 2026.10.2 to 2026.10.3 passed candidate rehearsal, then rejected two intentionally held deleted-agent stores at the post-activation schema check and left the Gateway unloaded; migrated finalization additionally ended without its result artifact and the handoff reported an offline-maintenance access refusal.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed once on the affected installation on October 15, 2026, 01:58–02:17 UTC; no destructive production replay was attempted.

1. Start a healthy macOS launchd-managed source installation at `050881cd69ff3a87e1fd1d39a54ff3e0b0c45c22` (2026.10.2), with two deleted agents whose existing databases Doctor classifies as `retained-by-deletion`, at agent schema 26.
2. Trigger the managed update, which hands off to `openclaw --profile <profile> update --yes`; selected candidate: `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6` (2026.10.3, agent schema 27).
3. Candidate Doctor, Doctor lint, config, plugins, recovery capability, and candidate Gateway startup all pass. Previous-Gateway readiness is also verified.
4. Activate the candidate and run its live Doctor. Doctor finishes with exit 0 and warns that the same two agent stores are held by deletion.
5. The post-activation inventory marks both held stores as unfinished migrations (expected 27, found 26). Observe failed finalization and the absent production listener.

This is an affected-host reproduction, not a claimed minimal synthetic reproducer. The fixture requirement is an intentional retained deletion, not a corrupt or active agent store.

### Expected behavior

The [update contract at the affected candidate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6/docs/install/updating.md#update-implementation-contract) says recoverable hiccups become warnings and refusal for named data risk keeps the previous Gateway running.

The retained-store behavior introduced by #154136 explicitly preserves held deleted-agent databases and continues unrelated migration. Post-activation verification should use the same active/held classification rather than requiring preserved stores to equal the active-agent schema. If activation cannot safely complete, the owner should produce a durable terminal/recovery outcome and restore availability where safe. Do not bypass a deletion fence or start an incompatible older reader merely to satisfy availability.

### Actual behavior

- Rehearsal passed; source/runtime activation installed the candidate.
- Live Doctor exited 0 in 127,869 ms and reported both stores as `retained-by-deletion`.
- An additional `openclaw doctor` result step was synthesized with duration 0, exit 1, and two schema-mismatch messages for those same held stores.
- The parent subsequently reported `ENOENT` for `<state>/tmp/openclaw-update-migrated-<id>/result.json`.
- The terminal outer result was `status:error`, `reason:openclaw doctor`, with `recovery.serviceRestartSafe:false` and `recovery.reason:runtime-verification-failed`.
- At 02:16:46 UTC the handoff explicitly logged that service recovery was not attempted because the updater rejected activation, then failed state access with `undergoing offline maintenance`.
- At 02:32 UTC, independent native inspection found the target launchd job not loaded, no listener on its configured port, and HTTP connection refusal. No matching updater process was found. Sibling gateways remained running.

The saved report also displayed an earlier `Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.2)` and explicitly warned that this was historical, not current health. It must not be taken as evidence of recovery.

### OpenClaw version

Installed driver: 2026.10.2, `050881cd69ff3a87e1fd1d39a54ff3e0b0c45c22`.

Activated candidate: 2026.10.3, `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6`; build timestamp `2026-10-15T02:02:23.301Z`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0, arm64; Node v26.7.0.

### Install method

Native source/Git checkout, profile-specific launchd service, managed update handoff. The recorded update mode is `git`; this is not a claim that the separately documented adopted immutable/systemd activation path was in use.

### Model

Not applicable: the failure occurs in native update/migration/finalization, not model inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable to the observed failure boundary.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Omitted; no credential changes are implicated or requested.

### Logs

```text
candidate-doctor: exit 0
candidate-doctor-lint: exit 0
candidate-config: exit 0
candidate-plugins: exit 0
candidate-recovery: exit 0
candidate-gateway-startup: exit 0 (12586 ms)

openclaw doctor: exit 0 (127869 ms)
Held agent <retained-agent-A> database <state>/agents/<retained-agent-A>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite (retained-by-deletion)
Held agent <retained-agent-B> database <state>/agents/<retained-agent-B>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite (retained-by-deletion)
Doctor complete.

openclaw doctor: exit 1 (0 ms)
Agent database migration did not finish: <state>/agents/<retained-agent-A>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite; expected schema 27, found 26.
Agent database migration did not finish: <state>/agents/<retained-agent-B>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite; expected schema 27, found 26.

ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<state>/tmp/openclaw-update-migrated-<id>/result.json'
managed update update command exited code=1 signal=null
managed update recovery not attempted: updater explicitly rejected activation
handoff failed: StateDatabaseAccessError: OpenClaw state at <state>/state/openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance; retry when it finishes.
```

The raw log interleaves stdout JSON and stderr; excerpts above separate those streams semantically rather than claiming they formed one valid JSON document.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source boundaries, pinned to the affected candidate:

- [`inspectActivatedUpdateState`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts#L46-L116) checks every non-shared existing inventory entry against the candidate agent schema, without a held/deleted disposition in that predicate. This directly matches the recorded synthesized failure.
- [`collectStateDatabasePaths`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6/src/infra/update-candidate-state.ts#L151-L267) inventories registered and physical unconfigured stores.
- The [installed driver's continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/050881cd69ff3a87e1fd1d39a54ff3e0b0c45c22/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts#L289-L331) reads the private result file after joining the child, before evaluating the returned finalization contract.
- The [candidate finalizer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6/src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts) publishes its result only after executor settlement and terminal history.

The relevant three candidate modules (`update-command-migrated.ts`, `update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts`, `update-candidate-state.ts`) were byte-identical to upstream main `a4d316dc86846952cc2ddd99df026c771ab38900` inspected during this investigation. This is source comparison, not a full updater retest on that newer head.

Raw logs and recovery snapshots were retained privately; no private configuration, database contents, credentials, or conversation identifiers are attached.

### Impact and severity

One observed native managed update left this Gateway unavailable after all pre-activation checks passed. It required operator recovery rather than more waiting. Frequency beyond this attempt is unknown. No data-loss claim is made. Other gateway processes on the same host remained running.

### Additional information

**Proven:** the post-activation gate rejects the same stores Doctor intentionally holds; the managed handoff ended without restoring service and left an offline-maintenance access refusal.

**Unknown:** the exact internal exception/path that prevented the migrated finalizer from publishing `result.json`, and whether that missing result is caused by the retained-store rejection or is an independent secondary failure. The parent-facing `ENOENT` alone does not establish the child's cause. Regression introduction is not established.

**Related but not duplicate evidence:** #154002 / #154136 concerned retained-store refusal during rehearsal; this occurrence passes rehearsal and fails the later schema-verification gate. #163638 / #163803 concern activation migration recovery. The affected candidate already contains merge `b37936459a68b39081647320093207b038efec10` for #163803. #139485 is an older nonterminal OCM finalizer wait; this incident uses native launchd and terminates with an error, so it is not asserted to be the same mechanism.

### Verified recovery outcome

After preserving the original logs and native update recovery snapshots, an operator made an additional consistent SQLite checkpoint (all copied stores passed `quick_check`), then ran the candidate installation's native commands:

```text
openclaw --profile <profile> update repair --yes --json --no-restart
openclaw --profile <profile> gateway start --json
```

- Repair completed with exit 0 / `status: warning`; its final post-plugin Doctor lint reported no findings and exit 0. No core source patch or newer target update was applied.
- Start re-bootstrapped the existing unloaded launchd service. Configuration, service definition, and protected service environment remained byte-identical to the pre-repair checkpoint.
- The running Gateway serves 2026.10.3. Native RPC health is good; local and stable HTTPS `/healthz` and `/readyz` return HTTP 200 with `ready: true` and no failing checks.
- An actual bounded agent-scoped `sessions.list` read succeeds. All 17 loaded plugins report no errors or unavailable plugins. The two configured Telegram accounts and iMessage pass no-send transport probes. No model-generation or outbound-message test is claimed.
- Both retained deleted-agent stores remain at schema 26. Consistent before/after SQLite backup files are byte-identical (SHA-256 equality). Neither deletion state nor held-store schema was manually changed. The Gateway can serve while those stores remain deliberately held.
- Sibling Gateway PIDs and run counts stayed unchanged throughout repair and startup.

This verifies recovery, not a fix to the updater: the failed update is still a failed update, and this issue remains open. Nonfatal held-store, historical Skill Workshop rollback-target, and operator-managed-plugin warnings remain; no unrelated cleanup was attempted.

### Relationship to the earlier same-host report

The morning rehearsal failure was reported as #172259 and fixed by merged #172295 (`aac3febbe63ded457c83c154c629e00f1ad11b5e`). Git ancestry confirms that this incident's candidate already contains that fix. This later incident passes candidate rehearsal and fails post-activation verification; it is a downstream retained-store inventory gap, not evidence that the earlier legacy-main scan fix was absent.

issues.body:
Observed on Linux with a local package build based on OpenClaw 2026.9.7. This is an incident trace, not yet a minimal reproduction.

### Sequence

1. A native package update published the candidate and started its Gateway. A channel verification step failed because Telegram health collection exceeded 7000 ms. The final update receipt reported `state-migrated-no-rollback` and `runtime-verification-failed`; the final verification snapshot nevertheless reported the expected serving build, channels ready and settled.
2. `package-backup-retention` also failed, retaining the original package and its sealed publication recovery helper.
3. After the original updater exited, `openclaw update repair --no-restart --json` was run. An offline pass completed all phases, with plugin/convergence warnings and no deferred phases.
4. A subsequent native package update refused admission with `update-recovery-pending` and directed the operator to the original external-Node publication recovery helper.
5. The exact original helper's `status` reported `publication-complete`.
6. The original helper's `repair` refused with `Package publication object changed: <retained previous package>`.

### Additional observations

- The installed candidate and launcher inspection passed far enough to reach inspection of the retained previous package.
- Many descendants of the retained previous tree have ctime clustered at the end of the original update, while their mtime remains from the prior installation. This is a correlation only: I have not established which operation changed that metadata or whether file bytes changed.
- A separate archive of the currently retained previous package was created and compared successfully using tar before further recovery attempts.
- The recovery helper's tree fingerprint includes descendant inode identity, mode, ownership, link count, size, mtime, ctime and file content hash. Thus unchanged bytes alone would not establish that the recorded fingerprint still matches.
- Source inspection of `package-update-swap.ts` shows the failed retention step returns before calling retirement when the installation outcome is unverified. Therefore this trace does not show retirement deleting or rewriting the retained package.
- Source inspection shows both repair and retirement require the retained-tree match in this phase. I did not edit the journal, remove the anchor, waive the integrity guard or attempt a code-only rollback after state migration.
- The installed candidate was subsequently started with the normal native Gateway start command. Its 45-second readiness deadline expired during startup; later HTTP liveness and readiness returned 200. This does not resolve the blocked publication recovery or prove all runtime operations healthy.

### Request

Please investigate whether native post-publication/update work can change metadata in the retained previous tree and leave an already published candidate permanently blocking future update admission. A supported recovery should preserve the original evidence and verify the selected live package, with an explicit path for this retained-object mismatch rather than requiring operators to edit the journal.

Related runtime SQLite contention evidence: #118885. I am not asserting that the publication mismatch causes that contention.

### Pinned local artifacts and current recovery boundary

The serving package's build info reports custom commit `16902253e50774632ab93962008b21f765845495`, built on 2026-10-03. The preceding updater package was custom commit `f0de89b5d7af696311e62682eaab22d36bfb2643`. These are local build identities, not claims that their source commits are published upstream.

The original sealed `recovery.mjs` is 66,233,492 bytes; SHA-256 `07e5f42197a87f9a8bb67b2bab11ec8ed8549f45eb959b8976a875757816be59`. This pins the exact retained helper artifact; I have not mapped every bundled module to an upstream revision. Its latest native status still reports `publication-complete`. No update/build/recovery job remains running; the serving Gateway remains on the same PID, readiness is true and its restart count is zero in the current observation.

I checked merged #162365 and #163370. Their documented improvements apply to the installed/new updater driver; both preserve the already published original driver's ownership. They do not establish a supported settlement path for this existing sealed operation. The old helper stores the compact aggregate fingerprint, so I cannot reconstruct original differing-entry observations that it never saved. No replacement helper or journal rewriting has been attempted.

### Latest release admission check

On the same installation, a native dry-run targeting the newly published `2026.9.8` also refuses with `update-recovery-pending` before any install step. The original helper still reports `publication-complete`; the serving custom 2026.9.7 Gateway remains running. This is the same retained-operation blocker, not a new 2026.9.8 installation failure. Preparing a candidate on the exact 2026.9.8 release source does not settle that original recovery operation.

issues.body:
## Summary

When using `google/gemini-2.5-pro` via the `google-generative-ai` API, three issues combine to cause rapid session context bloat, aborted runs, and silent Telegram delivery failures.

## Issue 1: textSignature Session Bloat (High Severity)

Gemini assistant responses include a `textSignature` field containing ~15KB of base64 data per response turn. OpenClaw stores these signatures verbatim in the session JSONL history. After 10+ turns, the accumulated signatures alone consume 150KB+, causing:

1. Context window bloat (observed: 416K tokens in one session)
2. Gemini API timeouts on re-submission of full context
3. Compaction failures (session too large to compact)
4. Silent message delivery failures (run aborts before reply is sent to Telegram)

**Expected:** `textSignature` should either not be stored in session history, be stored separately, or not be re-sent to the model on subsequent turns.

## Issue 2: Embedded `<think>` Tags in Text

Gemini 2.5 Pro embeds `<think>...</think>` tags directly in the `text` content field (not as separate `thinking` type blocks). If OpenClaw treats `<think>`-prefixed text as internal/thinking content, the reply is suppressed and never delivered to Telegram.

**Expected:** OpenClaw should either strip `<think>` tags from the delivered text, or not suppress messages that contain them.

## Issue 3: Mixed Text + ToolCall in Same Response

Gemini 2.5 Pro consistently emits text + toolCall in the same response turn. OpenClaw processes the toolCall, gets the result, then emits an empty `content: []` as the final stop. The original text from the first part of the response is never delivered to the user.

**Expected:** Text content from a mixed text+toolCall response should be delivered to the user, not silently dropped.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an agent with `google/gemini-2.5-pro` as primary model
2. Send 5-10 interactive messages via Telegram group topic
3. Check session JSONL — each assistant message contains `textSignature` (~15KB base64)
4. After ~10 exchanges, session reaches 150K+ tokens
5. Subsequent runs timeout or abort; replies never reach Telegram

## Workaround

Switched affected agent to Claude Sonnet 4.6, which does not exhibit these behaviors.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.3.13 (61d171a)
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)
- Gemini API key auth (google-generative-ai provider)
- Telegram channel with group topics

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A streamed assistant reply that contains a fenced code block is re-sanitized in full on every model delta, so the cost grows with the square of the reply length: on `main` (`923e59a01e`, package `2026.10.3`) the 31,162-character fixture below blocks the reply pipeline for 422.3 s of wall time (402.3 s of CPU) before the message finishes streaming, while the same fixture measured 0 parsed characters before #172470.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `923e59a01e` (package version `2026.10.3`) and run `pnpm install`.
2. Add a focused test that streams a reply fixture through the shipped entry point `createAssistantVisibleStreamText()` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.ts`) in 4-character deltas, counts the characters handed to `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` via `vi.spyOn(toolCallRepair, "stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks")`, and prints wall time plus `process.cpuUsage()`.
3. Run it with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <that file> --maxWorkers=1` and compare the four shapes below.

Fixture 1 - prose plus one fenced block that quotes a tool call (the quoted line is the only line carrying a payload marker):

````text
Here is the block:

```text
[tool:read] {"path": "src/index.ts"}
```

Sentence number 1 carries several ordinary words.
...
````

Fixture 2 - identical shape, fenced JSON instead of a quoted call:

````text
Here is the block:

```json
{ "name": "openclaw", "version": "2026.10.3", "deps": { "left-pad": "1.0.0" } }
```

Sentence number 1 carries several ordinary words.
...
````

Fixtures 3 and 4 replace the fenced block with a real plain-text tool call that the sanitizer does have to strip, and with no code block at all.

### Expected behavior

The sanitizer should only pay for replies that actually contain a strippable line-start tool call. The pre-#172470 activation tokens (`["[", "<function=", "to="]`) parse 0 characters for fixture 2 - the measured same-machine value was 5.2 ms / 0 parsed characters at 15,605 characters - and the fixture-1 class was already quadratic before that merge (53.4 s / 30,287,430 parsed characters at 15,562 characters with those tokens, because the quoted line starts with `[`).

### Actual behavior

`main` re-parses the whole reply on every delta whenever the reply has reached a payload opener anywhere, including one inside a fenced code block. Measured through `createAssistantVisibleStreamText()` on 4-character deltas (Windows 11, Node 26.11.1, same machine, same fixtures):

| fixture | chars | wall | CPU | chars re-parsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prose only | 15,517 | 72.4 ms | 94.0 ms | 0 |
| prose only | 31,117 | 176.1 ms | 202.0 ms | 0 |
| fenced JSON block | 15,605 | 461.3 ms | 485.0 ms | 60,902,020 |
| fenced JSON block | 31,205 | 1,681.8 ms | 1,828.0 ms | 243,484,420 |
| fenced tool-call example | 15,562 | 104,088.3 ms | 103,859.0 ms | 60,574,462 |
| fenced tool-call example | 31,162 | 422,270.7 ms | 402,313.0 ms | 242,829,262 |
| real leaked call to strip | 15,546 | 1,288.0 ms | 1,454.0 ms | 30,225,398 |
| real leaked call to strip | 31,146 | 4,749.0 ms | 4,828.0 ms | 121,290,398 |

Doubling the reply multiplies the parse work by ~4 in every affected row. The same code path in a focused test fails a linear bound with `AssertionError: expected 103463884 to be less than 230096`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (`923e59a01e` on `main`)

### Operating system

Windows 11 (Node 26.11.1, pnpm 9.15.0)

### Install method

Repository checkout of `main` plus `pnpm install`; reproduction exercised in-process through the shipped streaming projector.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO - the cost is inside the shared visible-text sanitizer that runs before any provider-specific code, and the fixtures are generated locally, so no provider or model is involved in the reproduction.

### Logs

Raw output of the pre-fix focused test on `923e59a01e`:

```text
FAIL |shared-core| src/shared/text/plain-tool-call-text.test.ts > plainToolCallTextFilter streamed projection > bounds plain-tool-call parse work when a code block only quotes a call
AssertionError: expected 103463884 to be less than 230096
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 26 passed (27)
[test] failed 1 Vitest shard in 225.23s
```

Raw output of the streaming benchmark on `923e59a01e`:

```text
q9t4bench none                 chars= 15517 wall=     72.4ms cpu=     94.0ms parsedChars=0
q9t4bench none                 chars= 31117 wall=    176.1ms cpu=    202.0ms parsedChars=0
q9t4bench json-fence           chars= 15605 wall=    461.3ms cpu=    485.0ms parsedChars=60902020
q9t4bench json-fence           chars= 31205 wall=   1681.8ms cpu=   1828.0ms parsedChars=243484420
q9t4bench tool-example-fence   chars= 15562 wall= 104088.3ms cpu= 103859.0ms parsedChars=60574462
q9t4bench tool-example-fence   chars= 31162 wall= 422270.7ms cpu= 402313.0ms parsedChars=242829262
q9t4bench leaked-call          chars= 15546 wall=   1288.0ms cpu=   1454.0ms parsedChars=30225398
q9t4bench leaked-call          chars= 31146 wall=   4749.0ms cpu=   4828.0ms parsedChars=121290398
```

Same-harness control run with the pre-#172470 activation tokens (`["[", "<function=", "to="]`) rebuilt in the test file rather than by patching the source:

```text
q9t4legacy json-fence           legacy  chars= 15605 wall=      5.2ms cpu=      0.0ms parsedChars=0
q9t4legacy json-fence           legacy  chars= 31205 wall=      4.4ms cpu=      0.0ms parsedChars=0
q9t4legacy tool-example-fence   legacy  chars= 15562 wall=  53419.1ms cpu=  51890.0ms parsedChars=30287430
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots; the reproduction is terminal output, reproduced above. The failure is inside `plainToolCallTextFilter` in `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts`, reached from every streamed assistant message update (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.update.ts`).

### Impact and severity

Affected: every streamed assistant reply that contains a fenced code block with braces, or that quotes a tool call - on every provider, in both the Gateway and the local delivery paths, because `createAssistantVisibleStreamText` is the shared projection used for streamed assistant message updates.
Severity: High. The work runs on the reply pipeline's event loop, so while it runs it delays every other session in the process. The same latch class was reported by operators as the agent freezing with no visible progress: #171416 measured 47.8 s of Gateway CPU for one 24 KB reply, and #119478 reports the same stall.
Frequency: always, and quadratic with reply length - measured 104 s at 15.6 KB and 422 s at 31.2 KB for a fence that quotes a tool call, and 0.46 s / 1.68 s for a plain fenced JSON block.
Consequence: an ordinary code-bearing answer stalls the reply for seconds to minutes; a single 31 KB reply consumes ~7 minutes of blocked wall time. No user-side workaround is available.

### Additional information

Regression boundary: introduced by #172470 (`2120e734ec`, merged 2026-10-14T21:12Z), which replaced `activationTokens: ["[", "<function=", "to="]` with `activationTokens: ["{", "<parameter=", "<function=", "to="]`. `{` occurs in every brace-bearing code block, so the classic `[` latch moved to `{`: the fenced-JSON fixture above went from 0 parsed characters to 243,484,420 at 31,205 characters. The second affected class - a reply whose fenced block quotes a tool call - was already quadratic before #172470 because its quoted line starts with `[` (53.4 s at 15,562 characters), and it stays quadratic after it. The third row, a real leaked call that the sanitizer must remove, is legitimate work rather than a defect; it is included as a control.

Last known good / first known bad for the brace-bearing shape: good before `2120e734ec`, bad from `2120e734ec` onward. Replies without a payload opener (`{`, `<parameter=`, `<function=`, `to=`) are unaffected (`none` rows: 0 parsed characters at both sizes).

AI disclosure: this report was drafted with AI assistance at the author's request, under their direction and review.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On Discord, a reply that was delivered normally is sometimes followed ~100 ms later by the restart-recovery notice "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat, so I won't resend it automatically. Please ask for any missing remainder." — whenever another inbound message lands in the same session during the 1–2 s the reply is in flight; observed 4 times on 2 agents in 8 days, each time with the reply visibly delivered and no gateway restart.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run a Discord agent on 2026.9.1 (the involved code is unchanged on v2026.9.5 and main @ 47f1d6ad8eb) with default outbound delivery (durable queue).
2. In a channel or thread, send a message that produces a reply.
3. While that reply is being posted, have another message arrive in the same session — e.g. send a second message within ~1 s of the reply appearing, or have a second bot reply in the same second.
4. Observe: the reply is posted, then the notice is posted right after it.

### Expected behavior
No notice when the reply reached the chat. The notice should only be sent once the delivery outcome is actually unknown (ambiguous failure, or restart recovery).

### Actual behavior
The notice is posted ~84 ms after the reply it claims it could not confirm. The transcript records it as `provider=openclaw model=delivery-mirror` with `idempotencyKey=main-session-restart-recovery:pending-final:<intentId>`. No delivery error in the gateway log, no restart.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.1 (source build from tag v2026.9.1 plus unrelated local patches; `src/channels/turn/pending-delivery-notice.ts`, `direct-delivery-custody.ts`, `execution.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-completion.ts` are identical on v2026.9.5 and main 47f1d6ad8eb)

### Operating system
macOS 15.7.9 (x86_64) and macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Install method
Source build (`pnpm build`, npm global link)

### Model
Not model-dependent — the notice is emitted by the gateway delivery layer (`model=delivery-mirror`). The agents were on openai gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-6-astra.

### Provider / routing chain
Discord channel → gateway durable outbound queue. LLM route: openai-codex (irrelevant to this bug).

### Logs
```
# Discord message timestamps (openclaw message read --channel discord, UTC), one occurrence:
07:18:20.983Z  user message arrives in the thread
07:18:21.815Z  agent reply posted (visible in the channel)
07:18:21.899Z  notice posted, 84 ms after the reply it says it could not confirm

# transcript_events row for the notice (ids redacted):
{"type":"message","timestamp":"2026-09-19T07:18:22.042Z","message":{"role":"assistant",
 "content":[{"type":"text","text":"I couldn’t confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat, so I won’t resend it automatically. Please ask for any missing remainder."}],
 "api":"openclaw-transcript","provider":"openclaw","model":"delivery-mirror",
 "idempotencyKey":"main-session-restart-recovery:pending-final:<intentId>"}}

# other occurrences (second agent), notice timestamp vs. preceding reply's transcript timestamp:
2026-09-12T05:22:32.138Z  (reply 05:22:30.563Z)
2026-09-12T17:23:54.615Z  (reply 17:23:52.907Z)
2026-09-19T00:37:20.987Z  (reply 00:37:19.273Z)
# In all 4 cases another inbound message (user or another bot) arrived within ±1.2 s of the reply.
# gateway log at those times: no delivery error; gateway-restart log: no restart.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Code path (same on 2026.9.1, v2026.9.5, main 47f1d6ad8eb):
1. `createDirectPendingFinalCustody().onPlatformSendDispatch` (src/channels/turn/direct-delivery-custody.ts) settles the pending final `unknown` before every platform post.
2. `settlePendingFinalDelivery` (src/infra/outbound/delivery-completion.ts) records `pendingDeliveryNotice.state = "owed"` when that `unknown` settlement moves from `queued` — i.e. for every reply that goes through the durable outbound queue (direct `prepared → unknown` claims do not owe).
3. `deliverPendingDeliveryNotice` (src/channels/turn/pending-delivery-notice.ts) runs after every inbound message is recorded (src/channels/turn/execution.ts) and sends as soon as it sees `owed`, without checking whether that send is still in progress. The `delivered` settlement that clears the notice only lands after the platform round-trip, so any inbound message in that window announces a loss that has not happened.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: Discord agents (any channel whose replies go through the durable outbound queue is likely affected the same way)
- Severity: annoying — users see a "missing reply" notice right after a reply that did arrive; operators are misled into hunting for lost messages or restarts
- Frequency: intermittent — 4 in 8 days across 2 agents, only when another inbound message lands within ~1 s of the reply (busy threads, bot-to-bot replies)
- Consequence: no message loss; misleading extra message

### Additional information
Not a regression as far as observed: first seen on 2026.9.1; the code is unchanged through main. Fix proposed in #154417 — defer the announcement while the durable queue still owns the noticed final, without changing when the debt is recorded.

issues.body:
# Native Codex child: advertised OpenClaw tools have no executor

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (`3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107`)
- `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.4
- bundled Codex CLI 0.153.4
- Web UI parent using the native Codex app-server; child created with native `collaboration.spawn_agent`

## Minimal reproduction

1. In a Web UI native Codex parent, create a fresh native child.
2. In that child, discover the first-class `gateway_exec` tool and invoke it once:

   ```json
   {
     "command": "python3 -I -c 'print(\"NATIVE_GATEWAY_EXEC_CANARY\")'",
     "timeoutSeconds": 15,
     "yieldMs": 1000,
     "title": "Native child gateway execution canary"
   }
   ```

3. Do not substitute native shell, an OpenClaw subagent runtime, a parent call, or tool catalog visibility for this operation.

Observed: `OpenClaw did not register a handler for this app-server tool call.` No command marker returned. The same first-class tool executes successfully in the parent control.

No provider, upload, paid request, credential inspection or media operation is needed to reproduce.

## Host source evidence

- Codex turn router resolves an exact thread route. Native child thread has no request execution owner.
- The parent request controller additionally checks the exact parent thread and active turn. Removing those guards is not a safe repair.
- Native subagent monitor has lifecycle/history/notification ownership, not child dynamic-tool execution admission.
- Existing host tool surfaces carry parent admitted-run identity and lifetime. They cannot simply be retained and invoked by arbitrary tracked children after parent yield.

## Dependency contract gap

Exact Codex 0.153.4 `thread/read` does not return the effective child permission/sandbox/approval configuration. `config/read` is cwd-based, not a live-thread settings read. Initial settings are not emitted as a `thread/settings/updated` notification.

The loaded branch of `thread/resume` can return effective settings, but the method has no atomic loaded-only/expected-turn contract. If the thread stops between the probe and execution, it can take the cold-resume path and reactivate a parent-owned child. It also attaches the connection/updates client metadata. Do not use it as a read-only authority query.

Needed contract: authenticated inspection/admission of the exact already-loaded child and active turn, returning effective permissions, approval settings and workspace constraints, without starting/resuming work or applying overrides; fail if that live identity is no longer current. Reuse an existing supported atomic primitive if one exists. Then create child-scoped host execution and keyed request routing without widening delegated authority.

## Separate completion-delivery reproduction

A native child stops after the tool error and returns a final failure description. Parent previously called `sessions_yield`. The durable task records turn completion but `deliveryStatus=failed` with:

```
In-process gateway dispatch requires a gateway request scope or instance binding (method: agent).
```

This must not count as user-visible notification. The receiving parent needs an actual continuation or a visible persisted delivery blocker.

The local reporting candidate preserves the admitted reply operation's Gateway resolver at the queued auto-reply admission boundary and isolates detached completion from ambient request authority. It is separate from the missing native executor and is not a live repair claim.

## Acceptance

- Fresh native child actually returns the unique gateway_exec marker.
- Child restrictions, cancellation, stale/foreign thread rejection and exact-call duplicate protection hold.
- With parent yielded, a deliberate native-child command failure causes a parent continuation and visible blocker without user polling.
- No paid operations are required for any of these checks.

Reported by Rune, an AI assistant, with the operator’s explicit approval. Reproduction and findings were sanitized for public disclosure.

issues.title: [Bug]: Plugin group allowances are lost during browser session access
issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A browser tool admitted by `tools.allow: ["group:plugins"]` is rejected when session access rechecks the conversation policy. The same rejection occurs when the browser is invoked through `dispatch_action`.

### Steps to reproduce

This was reproduced in an isolated regression fixture using the actual browser plugin registration, plugin tool resolver, coding-tool assembly, admitted caller, and session-access authority:

1. Register the browser plugin and configure `tools.allow: ["group:plugins"]`.
2. Assemble the tools for an admitted caller in its own session. The resulting browser tool retains its registered `browser` plugin ownership.
3. Invoke that browser tool directly, or invoke it through the assembled `dispatch_action` tool.
4. Reach the browser method's registered session-access policy, which requires the `browser` tool.

Browser I/O and persisted profile reads were fixed fixtures. No live browser or model request was made.

### Expected behavior

An admitted plugin tool should retain the same plugin-ID and `group:plugins` policy meaning when its authority is rechecked. Exact tool denials, plugin denials, narrower caller restrictions, and current session policy must continue to apply.

The documented `group:plugins` contract covers loaded plugin-owned tools: [tool policy groups](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/sandbox-vs-tool-policy-vs-elevated#tool-groups-shorthands).

### Actual behavior

Both direct and dispatched calls fail with:

```text
browser is not allowed by this conversation's tool policy
```

The direct stack reaches `prepareGatewaySessionAccessAuthority`, its captured caller assertion, and `agent-tools.caller.ts`. Tool assembly evaluates policy using registered ownership metadata, but the captured assertion projects only the tool name. The later current session-resource policy check also uses the name-only projection, so both checks need consistent ownership facts while preserving fresh policy evaluation.

### OpenClaw version

Source revision `5930f05a68b61520ce4ee7e5057858ff146e1737`.

### Operating system

Linux x64; Node.js 24.19.0.

### Install method

Source checkout with locked dependencies.

### Model

None; the fixture invokes the tool authorization path directly.

### Provider / routing chain

Registered browser tool → coding-tool caller context → browser session-access authority. The dispatched case additionally traverses Tool Search and its nested caller assertions.

### Impact and severity

This blocks browser session operations for a caller whose otherwise valid allowance uses the plugin group. Both tested routes reject before the browser effect. The reproduction establishes the authorization mismatch; it does not establish affected release versions or deployment prevalence.

issues.title: [Bug]: Stop reports command cleanup failure during managed sandbox checkpoint
issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Stopping a sandboxed run with an active command can return a command-cleanup failure after the child and command have already terminated. The remaining managed-workspace checkpoint rejects the canceled run's authority instead of settling the command's accepted output.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a guest session in a required local Docker sandbox with a session-owned managed project.
2. Start a command that remains active while the parent run is working.
3. Use the chat's Stop action while the command is active.
4. Inspect the Stop response and retained process outcome.

A focused owner-level reproduction creates a real managed projection and session/worktree binding, prepares the sandbox command, writes guest output, aborts the run with `createAgentRunDirectAbortError()`, and calls the bound backend's `finalizeExec`. The checkpoint rejects with the same abort error on current source.

### Expected behavior

Stop should terminate the request-owned command and complete its required workspace settlement, then report a confirmed stopped outcome. New execution must remain blocked, and genuine checkpoint failures or a replaced session/worktree owner must still fail visibly.

### Actual behavior

The observed Stop response is `UNAVAILABLE`:

```text
Parent run stopped, but descendant cancellation was incomplete: Request stopped, but command cleanup could not be confirmed. Inspect its retained process output before retrying.
```

The command and child are gone. The retained process outcome is failed with `exitReason: manual-cancel`, and its finalization diagnostic is `agent run aborted | OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT`.

The source path is `bindLocalSandboxWorkspace.finalizeExec` → `projection.checkpoint` → the retained `resolveLocalWorkspaceOwner` assertion. Workspace preparation passed the run's abort assertion into that owner, so finalization checks execution liveness after Stop has deliberately ended it.

### OpenClaw version

Observed in source revision `da65be64a3216fa78420099e41b9182c6ef29515`; the owner-level reproduction also fails on `7e823106a77c63640806c0646c9dc8a21b35871f`.

### Operating system

The real user flow was observed on macOS with Docker. The focused real Git/SQLite projection reproduction fails on Linux.

### Install method

Source checkout.

### Model

The owner-level reproduction requires no model call.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable to the reproduced cleanup path.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The focused regression fails at the bound backend's `finalizeExec` with `AbortError: agent run aborted`, code `OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT`, instead of resolving. The production command/process failure reporting is distinct from the workspace checkpoint failure.

### Impact and severity

Guest users receive an incomplete-cancellation warning despite successful process termination. Accepted workspace output cannot complete its required checkpoint through this stopped command's owner. The real Stop flow and the focused owner reproduction both showed the problem; no broader frequency claim or data-loss claim is established.

### Additional information

This report concerns settlement after Stop. It is separate from command admission while another command checkpoints, and from accepting follow-up chat input during cancellation.

issues.body:
### Summary

Since plugin generation capture landed (#144252, first shipped in 2026.9.6), a Gateway with an external or workspace plugin that has a large package or dependency tree blocks its event loop for minutes. It happens at startup, and again whenever the prepared model runtime republishes. While the loop is blocked the Gateway accepts TCP connections but answers nothing, including `/healthz`, WebSocket RPCs and channel polling.

`capturePluginGenerationArtifact` (`src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts`) copies the plugin package synchronously on the main thread. When no `entryFile` is set, `copyPackage` copies the whole root. It then walks and copies the dependency tree through `capturePluginDependencies` → `linkDependency` → `copyPackage` → `copy`.

### Evidence

**Isolated repro on origin/main `4d4d99d`**, using a synthetic 878 MB context-engine plugin:
- The Gateway stalls for 219 s before it starts listening, then for another 168 s.
- It logs `prepared model runtime startup degraded after 120000ms (workspace plugins; agent main)`.

**Production Gateway on 2026.9.6.** The plugin root is a Bun global install: a 134 MB package whose sibling `node_modules` hold 1.5 GB across 221 packages.
- **Startup:** the process started at T+0 and logged `http server listening` at T+2m20s. `/healthz` timed out until about T+7m.
- **Stacks:** four inspector samples taken during the hang all show the same stack:
  ```
  realpathSync / path.join
  ← pluginNativeNamespaceMemberPath / resolvePreparedSource
  ← copy (recursive)
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← linkDependency ← capturePluginDependencies ← captureDependencies
  ← materialize ← copyPackage ← capturePluginGenerationArtifact
  ← bindPluginInstanceModuleLoader ← loadPluginModule ← loadRuntimePluginCandidate
  ```
- **Earlier, during a prepared-runtime republish:**
  - The event loop was blocked for 124 s (`eventLoopDelayMaxMs=124352`).
  - Telegram polling stalled.
  - `config.patch` took 125 s and returned `UNAVAILABLE`, followed by `prepared model runtime reload failed after config commit: prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out; restarting gateway`.
  - The Gateway then restarted, and startup blocked again.
  - Separately, the Control UI's provider sign-in stayed on a blank tab for the whole outage. That is covered by #160954.

A `thinkingDefault` patch alone hot-applies in 50 ms in the isolated repro. The republish in production was probably already pending. Candidate cause: #160120, a refresh loop triggered by an auth profile that fails to resolve. That link is being verified.

### Impact

- Any install with a large external or workspace plugin.
- The Gateway becomes unreachable for minutes on every startup and on every prepared-runtime republish.
- Config hot reloads can escalate into restarts, which block again.
- 2026.7.35 is not affected; 2026.9.6 (npm `latest`/`beta`) is.

### Expected

Capture should not block the Gateway event loop for more than a bounded time. An unchanged plugin should reuse its existing capture instead of being recopied.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `messages.statusReactions.enabled: true` on WhatsApp, an inbound DM that arrives while the session already has an active run ends its lifecycle with the error reaction (❌), even though the message is processed in the next run, which ends `success` and delivers a visible reply.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `messages: { statusReactions: { enabled: true } }` (ack reaction `👀`, `ackReactionScope: "direct"`, WhatsApp `reactionLevel: "minimal"`; `messages.queue` unset, so runtime default).
2. In a WhatsApp DM, send message A that starts a run lasting a few seconds.
3. While A's run is still active, send message B.
4. Watch the reactions on B and the gateway log.

Observed twice in the same DM within one minute (once with A = a PDF attachment and B = a text sent ~1 s later, once with B sent while a tool-calling run was active).

### Expected behavior

The docs (`channels/whatsapp`, "Lifecycle status reactions") describe the cycle as queued → thinking → tool → compaction → done/error. A message whose processing completes successfully and gets a visible reply should end on `done` (✅), or at least not on `error`. Message A in the same test, with no overlapping run, did end on ✅.

### Actual behavior

Gateway log for message B (timestamps local, ids shortened):

```
22:23:59.384 Sent reaction "👀" -> message …CAE6DE
22:24:00.097 Sent reaction "🧠" -> message …CAE6DE
22:24:02.193 Sent reaction "❌" -> message …CAE6DE
22:24:04.899 Sent reaction "👀" -> message …CAE6DE
```

Trajectory for the same session: the run active when B arrived ended at 22:24:02 with `session.ended status=success`. A new run started at 22:24:02, processed B, ended at 22:24:06 with `status=success`, and sent a visible reply at 22:24:06. No ✅ was ever sent for B.

The likely cause is in the WhatsApp plugin's `finalize` (`@openclaw/whatsapp` 2026.10.3, `dist/.setup/monitor-*.mjs`):

```js
outcome: readAgentRunTerminalOutcome(dispatchResult) === "failed" || !didDeliverVisibleReply ? "error" : "done"
```

A dispatch that is admitted into an active run (steered, or queued as a follow-up) does not deliver a visible reply itself, so `!didDeliverVisibleReply` maps it to `error`. The reply then comes from the following run, which is not linked back to B's reaction controller. I did not check which admission mode (steer or follow-up) B got. The same line is in `@openclaw/whatsapp@2026.10.5-beta.3`.

User impact: the ❌ reads as a failure. In this case the same request was sent again 26 s later.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (59cb447); `@openclaw/whatsapp` 2026.10.3

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai (native codex websocket, OAuth)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not provider-related; the issue is in the channel status-reaction finalize step.

issues.title: [Bug]: `openclaw memory …` CLI commands spend 35–60 s capturing plugin sources on every invocation (even `--help`) on 2026.10.3

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:other
labels.description: This issue has meaningful maintainer-visible impact outside the owned taxonomy.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Performance regression

### Summary
Since upgrading to 2026.10.3 (59cb447), every invocation of a `memory` subcommand takes 35–60 s before doing any work, including `--help`. Other CLI commands stay fast. While the command is starting, the process copies plugin sources into a fresh `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<uuid>/captures/openclaw-plugin-build-*` tree (~114 MB, ~11,500 files per run) and removes it on exit. Scripts that call `openclaw memory search` once per query (e.g. an evaluation harness running 20 queries) went from ~16 s per call (measured on 2026.9.8, before the 2026.10.x updates) to ~48–60 s per call on 2026.10.3, and exceeded their scheduler timeout.

The in-gateway `memory_search` tool is not affected: tool-call latency measured from agent transcripts stayed at a median of ~3–4 s.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447), npm global install, Node v22.22.0
- macOS 26.6 (Apple silicon), APFS
- Gateway running as a LaunchAgent; several npm-installed plugins enabled

### Measurements (same host, same minute, load average 6–8)
| command | wall time |
|---|---|
| `openclaw --version` | 0.96 s |
| `openclaw config get agents.defaults.memorySearch` | 2.3 s |
| `openclaw memory status --help` | 36.9 s |
| `openclaw memory search --help` | 35.7 s – 63.0 s (3 runs) |
| `openclaw memory search --agent <id> "<query>" --json` | 47.7 s |

`/usr/bin/time` for `memory search --help`: real 52.8 s, user 8.7 s, sys 17.0 s — about half of the wall time is spent waiting, consistent with filesystem-bound work.

### Evidence
- `sample` of the running CLI process: main thread and libuv threadpool dominated by `lstat` / `open` / `getattrlist` / `read`.
- `lsof` during start-up: the only open state file is `plugin-captures/<uuid>/owner.sqlite`.
- A new `plugin-captures/<uuid>/captures/openclaw-plugin-build-*` directory appears for each invocation and is removed when the command exits.

### Expected
`memory --help` and `memory status` should not need a full plugin-source capture; argument parsing and help should be near `--version` speed. If a capture is needed for `memory search`, reusing the capture between invocations would avoid repeating the copy every time.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install 2026.10.3 with a few npm-installed plugins enabled.
2. `time openclaw --version`
3. `time openclaw memory search --help`
4. While step 3 runs, `ls ~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/` shows a new capture instance.

### Workaround
We run the per-query CLI calls concurrently (4 at a time) and raised the per-call timeout to 180 s.

issues.body:
### Summary

The gateway's own WAL auto-checkpoint on `state/openclaw.sqlite` is reported as blocked on every attempt since boot, and has **never completed**:

```
openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader
  state=blocked  checkpointedFrames=866  logFrames=17091
  consecutiveBlocked=14  lastCompletedAtMs=null  never_completed=true
```

The WAL therefore keeps growing (unbackfilled 41.5 MB at 15:33 → 65.7 MB at 19:09) instead of being checkpointed.

### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.7 (c074824)**
- Windows 10.0.26200 (x64), Node v24.18.0
- State DB `state/openclaw.sqlite` ≈ 405 MB, `-wal` 47–73 MB

### What was ruled out

A Sysinternals **handle.exe** scan of all processes for `openclaw.sqlite`:

```
node.exe  pid: 33900  .sqlite  x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -wal     x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -shm     x1
```

**No other process holds any handle on the DB** — every handle belongs to the gateway process itself. This is not an external contender; the pin is **in-process**.

The gateway's own telemetry cannot name the holder either:

```json
"candidate_connection": {
  "connectionId": 2, "operation": "sqlite connection", "ownerKind": "worker",
  "threadId": 2, "ageMs": ~25200000, "transactionOpen": false,
  "trackedReaders": 0, "blockingOwner": "unknown",
  "readerCount": 0, "scope": "current-thread", "nativeStatements": "unobserved"
}
```

Note the internal inconsistency: it reports "blocked by a reader" while also reporting `readerCount: 0` and `blockingOwner: unknown`.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Maintenance stops the gateway, checkpoints cleanly, restarts:
   `[checkpoint] PASS | [('openclaw-agent.sqlite',(0,0,0)), ('openclaw.sqlite',(0,0,0))]` (12:00:01)
2. After restart (~12:03) the block immediately re-forms and **never** clears for the rest of the uptime (observed 12:03 → 19:05, 71 blocked records, `never_completed=true`).
3. Only another full gateway restart clears it.

### Correlated (NOT proven) impact

- `Agent run failed: the Gateway state database was busy (SQLite: database is locked)`
- repeated `cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`

Same DB, same subsystem. Timing supports a link; no controlled reproduction was done, so causation is **unproven**.

### Suggested directions (guesses)

- Likely a long-lived connection or unclosed read snapshot inside the worker pool (threadId=2, `ownerKind=worker`) — a single un-reset statement pins the WAL.
- `blockingOwner=unknown` + `readerCount=0` + "blocked by a reader" suggests the reader-tracking path does not cover all connection kinds.

---
*Reported from a self-hosted single-user deployment. Paths sanitized.*

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash)

## Summary

A config hot-reload that **fails and is explicitly reported as rolled back** ("Gateway generation N: replacement not applied") still leaves unrelated, already-running plugins permanently unusable — every subsequent call touching them fails with `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.` This persists until a full Gateway process restart; nothing short of that recovers it.

This looks related to #153572 and #153290 (same error text, same general "reload leaves an unrelated plugin instance retired" shape), but the trigger here is different: those describe a reload that *applies successfully* still bricking one plugin. This one is a reload that *fails* and is reported as *not applied* — yet the teardown of unrelated plugin instances happened anyway and was never rolled back along with the rest of the generation.

## Steps to reproduce

Deterministic minimal repro: not isolated. Observed production sequence on OpenClaw 2026.9.5:

1. Edit `openclaw.json` (in our case, an agent tool-allowlist change unrelated to `codex`, `discord`, or `memory-wiki`).
2. Gateway attempts a live config hot-reload ("generation 2").
3. That reload fails during activation because one specific, unrelated plugin's shutdown hook overruns its budget:
   ```
   config reload failed: PluginRuntimeApplicationError: Plugin operation failed during activate:
   Plugin candidate cleanup failed; automatic recovery could not safely start |
   plugin services failed to start | Unpublished plugin resource cleanup failed |
   plugin host cleanup timed out: unpublished plugin resources |
   plugin service stop failed (plugin=memory-wiki, service=memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup):
   plugin service startup settlement timed out after 5000ms
   Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.
   ```
4. Despite "replacement not applied", every subsequent call that touches `codex` or `discord` (two plugins with no apparent relationship to `memory-wiki` or to the config change made) fails:
   ```
   ⇄ res ✗ sessions.list ... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin codex was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
   refresh failed: Plugin discord was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
   session snapshot publication failed: Plugin codex was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
   ```
   This repeats continuously (~200+ occurrences observed over ~10 minutes) for `sessions.list`, `sessions.describe`, `sessions.catalog.list`, `chat.history`, and session-snapshot publication.
5. New agent turns (`openclaw.chat`) still complete successfully in this state — the breakage is specifically in session-listing/metadata/snapshot RPCs, not the core turn-execution path.
6. A full `systemctl restart` of the Gateway process (not a further hot-reload) is the only thing that clears it. After the restart, zero recurrences.

## Expected behavior

A config reload that fails and reports "replacement not applied" should mean exactly that: the previous generation's plugin instances remain intact and serving, with no partial teardown of any plugin — related or not to the config keys that changed, and regardless of which plugin's shutdown hook caused the activation failure.

## Actual behavior

The rollback claim ("not applied") does not hold for plugins unrelated to the one whose cleanup timed out. `codex` and `discord` were torn down as part of the failed generation-2 attempt and never restored, even though the log says the replacement was not applied.

## OpenClaw version

2026.9.5, npm install

## Operating system

Debian/Linux (Raspberry Pi, aarch64), systemd user unit (`openclaw-gateway.service`)

## Impact and severity

- Affected: any Gateway that hits a hot-reload activation failure for any reason — the triggering plugin (`memory-wiki` here) does not need to be one the operator is actually using or aware of.
- Severity: high while it lasts — Control UI becomes largely unusable (session list/describe/history all fail) even though new turns keep working, which makes the symptom confusing to diagnose from the client side.
- Frequency: presumably occurs on any hot-reload activation failure, not specific to `memory-wiki`'s cleanup timeout — that was just this incident's specific trigger.
- Workaround: full Gateway restart. No config-level or CLI-level recovery found.

## Related

- #153572 (closed) — same error text and general shape, but for a hot-reload that *applies successfully*.
- #153290 (closed) — plugin reload removing the previous build generation while a live adapter still references it; different specific mechanism (ENOENT vs `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`) but same "reload leaves a live consumer holding a dead reference" family.

issues.body:
### Summary

Keep Claude Code's own memory (`CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/rules/`, and auto memory) out of ordinary `claude-cli` agent turns by default, with an Anthropic plugin setting to opt back in and a Doctor-guided path to import existing Claude auto memory into OpenClaw memory.

_Updated 2026-10-07: this originally proposed an opt-in setting. Reworked to a default with an opt-out after confirming the privacy-boundary problem below and the Codex harness precedent._

### Problem to solve

On the `claude-cli` backend, OpenClaw launches Claude Code with `--setting-sources user`. That keeps project-level `CLAUDE.md` files out, but Claude Code still loads its user-level memory into every ordinary turn: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/`, and its auto memory for the workspace (the `MEMORY.md` index under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` plus instructions to keep saving there). Verified on Claude Code 2.1.282 through an OpenClaw Gateway built from current `main`.

These sit next to OpenClaw's system prompt and workspace bootstrap files, so:

- memory and rules exist twice: OpenClaw's workspace instructions and memory, plus Claude Code's own;
- OpenClaw's session privacy rule is bypassed: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` withholds the workspace `MEMORY.md` from group, channel, cron, and subagent sessions, but Claude auto memory is keyed by working directory and reaches every session of the agent;
- the agent saves durable memory under `~/.claude/projects/` instead of the workspace `MEMORY.md` / `memory/`, where `memory_search` does not index it, OpenClaw backups do not include it, and other runtimes cannot see it;
- host-global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` rules apply to every `claude-cli` agent on the Gateway, alongside each agent's own workspace instructions.

Restricted runs already exclude exactly these surfaces through `CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS` in `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts` (`autoMemoryEnabled: false` plus `claudeMdExcludes`). The Codex harness isolates the same way by default: `appServer.homeScope: "agent"` gives each agent its own Codex home, and sharing `~/.codex` is an explicit opt-in. Ordinary claude-cli runs have no switch at all:

- the backend-args override is gone (`agents.defaults.cliBackends` is retired), so an operator cannot add `--settings` themselves;
- a separate `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` breaks session continuity (#145309);
- process-wide Claude Code environment variables in a service drop-in work as a stopgap, but they are not an OpenClaw setting.

### Proposed solution

- Ordinary fresh and resumed `claude-cli` turns pass Claude Code `--settings` with the memory fields of the restricted profile (`autoMemoryEnabled: false` and the same `claudeMdExcludes` patterns), built from one shared field set so the two cannot drift. Restricted runs keep their stricter profile with no duplicate `--settings`; side questions already use `--safe-mode`.
- One Anthropic-owned opt-out restores the previous behavior:

  ```json5
  {
    plugins: {
      entries: {
        anthropic: {
          config: {
            claudeCli: { excludeNativeMemory: false },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  }
  ```

- Reverse migration stays operator-initiated, like Codex memory import. `openclaw doctor` lists each claude-cli agent whose Claude auto memory is no longer loaded and prints a scoped `openclaw migrate claude --agent <id> --from <that workspace's memory dir>` command, which imports only that workspace's memory into `memory/imports/claude-code/`. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is host-wide, so it is not copied automatically; the docs say to move needed rules into the agent's `AGENTS.md` or `USER.md`.
- Paired-node runs, whose node host rejects Gateway `--settings`, keep the node's own Claude Code configuration instead of failing.

### Alternatives considered

- Opt-in only (the first version of this proposal). It leaves every existing installation with duplicated memory and the privacy bypass unless the operator knows to turn it on.
- Default-on without a reachable override (#140487 as reviewed). Its review blocked on the unreachable backend-args escape hatch; the typed plugin setting fixes that.
- Automatic migration on update. `openclaw migrate claude` without `--from` imports every Claude project's auto memory and appends `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` to `USER.md`, which would mix other projects into each agent and spread host-wide rules again.
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: breaks continuity today (#145309) and also separates credentials and transcripts, which is far more than this needs.
- Environment variables on the Gateway service: process-wide, outside OpenClaw config, and invisible to OpenClaw docs and validation.

### Impact

- Affected: operators running `claude-cli` agents on a host where Claude Code is also used directly, so a user `CLAUDE.md` and auto memory exist.
- Severity: Claude auto memory reaches group and channel sessions that OpenClaw keeps `MEMORY.md` out of; agent memory silently diverges from OpenClaw's memory; host-global rules leak into every agent.
- Frequency: every ordinary `claude-cli` turn.
- Consequence: knowledge stranded under `~/.claude/projects/`, manual migration when an agent moves to another runtime, and instructions the operator did not configure for that agent.

### Evidence/examples

- Real-world report on OpenClaw 2026.9.8: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140487#issuecomment-6012070440
- ClawSweeper review of #140487 (Revision 12), whose merge-risk options include approving a new default once a reachable override and installed-Claude upgrade proof exist.
- Claude Code documents both settings (`autoMemoryEnabled`, `claudeMdExcludes`): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Implemented in #166073, which builds on the approach in #140487 by @zijunl.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary Summary — In one webchat session driving a Windows node via exec host=node: (1) the same [OpenClaw exec completion] batch — same ids, output and exit codes — was republished ~15 times over ~40 minutes, each delivery running a turn; (2) the operator's attempts to stop it were silently dropped, with two mid-loop messages recorded as pendingInputs entries in state: "cancelled" that never became turns. Environment — Gateway OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d) Linux x64; node host OpenClaw 2026.9.5, Windows 10; webchat; single main session; no subagents, no cron, no at jobs; tools.exec unset → backgroundMs: 10000, notifyOnExit: true. Finding 1 — The batch grew with slow commands and froze without them (15 → 19 → 20 ids, then no further deliveries once nothing exceeded backgroundMs). Reply length was irrelevant: long digests, single-line replies and silent handling all produced the same rate. Ids: e4b55390, d93557f9, 6e38e4b0, 09bd3c4d, 64b5c3e2, 650bd5bc, 61f61316, 094a3213, 04b38852, 68d958b2, 6f6ded5a, d667d75d, cf2cc13a, 4b26a54d, d606b941, 912ce242, 8bddaf71, f5d80025, 19a9467a, 2a6ed384. Finding 2 — While the loop ran, "you can stop now." and a second correction were cancelled rather than delivered, so there was no way to interrupt from the chat; the loop ended only when a later message happened to be admitted. Requested: surface dropped/cancelled inputs back to the sender, or let a stop instruction preempt pending wake deliveries. Mitigations, all unsatisfactory — tools.loopDetection doesn't apply (it targets repeated tool calls within a run; cf. #34574); heartbeat.every: "0m" doesn't stop targeted completion wakes; tools.exec.notifyOnExit: false removes legitimate completion signals too (cf. #141973); the agent can only self-impose "report once" discipline, which changes chat volume, not wake count. Ask — dedupe/coalesce already-delivered batches (per #150598 rule 3); give cancelled inputs a visible outcome; consider a per-session wake rate limit. ### Steps to reproduce Preconditions Gateway on defaults: openclaw config get tools.exec shows no overrides for backgroundMs (10s) or notifyOnExit (true) One agent session (we used webchat), Node ≥ v22, no subagents, cron or at jobs configured Steps In a single session, issue a burst of exec commands that each run longer than backgroundMs — e.g. ten of sleep 12 && echo step-N Let the agent handle them normally; no special reply handling needed Watch the notices: completions arrive as a batch of command ids, not one notice per command Keep issuing slow commands: the batch's id set grows while earlier ids keep reappearing (we went 15 → 19 → 20 ids) Stop issuing slow commands: the id set freezes and the re-deliveries stop Measure amplification as (deliveries of the same id set) ÷ (distinct completed commands) — we observed ~15 deliveries for 20 ids over ~40 minutes, each delivery running one agent turn Controls, to isolate the trigger A single slow command produces one notice and no repetition Commands under backgroundMs (e.g. sleep 5) produced no notices and no batch growth — so the aggregation appears gated on backgrounding tools.exec.notifyOnExit: false removes the notices entirely (blunt: also removes legitimate completion signals) suppressNotifyOnExit: true per invocation is untested — our probe completed under backgroundMs and so generated no notice regardless, leaving the flag's effect unconfirmed Secondary repro (dropped stop signal) While the loop is active, have the user send a stop message ("stop", "you can stop now."). In our run two such messages never became turns; both appear in the session's pendingInputs with state: "cancelled". The loop ended only when a later message happened to be admitted. Expected vs actual Expected: each backgrounded command yields at most one completion notice, delivered once Actual: one batch of ids re-presented ~15 times, each presentation running a turn, batch content byte-identical Not the trigger (ruled out in our run) Reply length — long digests, single-line replies and silent handling all gave the same rate Subagents/cron — none existed in the session ### Expected behavior one message and stopped ### Actual behavior a loop every few second with no way of stopping it. ### OpenClaw version OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d) ### Operating system Debian 13 ### Install method npm global ### Model Deepseek V4.1 flash ### Provider / routing chain platform.deepseek ### Additional provider/model setup details _No response_ ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence # Evidence log: repeated `[OpenClaw exec completion]` deliveries Session: `agent:main:main` · sessionId `a2da274a-bdd6-4c82-9131-5a8fa75cb375` · channel webchat · agent=main Extraction: `sessions_search` (query `OpenClaw exec completion`, role `user`). on every delivery: the **same batch** — 20 command ids, identical captured output and exit codes. Cadence over 13:08:56 → 13:38:11 (24 intervals): span 29 m 15 s, **median ≈70 s**, mean ≈73 s, min 31 s, max 118 s. issues.body:
## Summary

`/home/<user>/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/` accumulates multi-GB session directories from plugin-build and model-catalog operations. These directories are never cleaned up after the operation completes, so disk usage grows permanently with each gateway restart or periodic model-catalog refresh.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: current (as of 2026-09-25)
- OS: Fedora Linux 43, x86_64
- Node: v26.5.0

## Reproduction

1. Start the gateway — a new UUID session dir is created under `tmp/plugin-captures/`.
2. Restart the gateway (or wait for a model-catalog refresh).
3. Another 2–2.6GB dir is created. The previous one is never deleted.
4. Repeat until disk fills.

## Observed behaviour

```
/home/paul/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/
├── 441ed98f-...  2.6G  ← current (active gateway PID 423172)
├── 9611f0b0-...  2.2G  ← orphaned (empty owner.sqlite, no process handles)
├── ec2004c1-...  2.2G  ← orphaned
└── 9f1ac35d-...  743M  ← orphaned
Total: 7.7GB across 4 restarts
```

Each directory contains:
- `owner.sqlite` — empty (no owner record) in orphaned dirs; locked in the active dir
- `captures/openclaw-plugin-build-*/node_modules` — npm build artifacts (~150–200MB per plugin build)
- `captures/openclaw-model-catalog-*/` — model catalog data

## Impact

- Root filesystem reached **99% full** (4.2GB free on a 215GB partition) within normal usage
- Gateway stability risk — a full disk breaks the gateway, messaging, and the sessions path itself
- At ~2GB per restart, disk returns to critical within 2–3 restarts without manual cleanup

## Expected behaviour

Completed build/catalog session dirs should be deleted (or at minimum their `node_modules` pruned) once the operation finishes and the owning gateway process exits.

## Workaround

Manually delete orphaned dirs where `owner.sqlite` is empty and no process holds a file handle:

```bash
# Check for live handles before deleting
lsof +D ~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<dir> 2>/dev/null | wc -l
# Delete if 0
rm -rf ~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<orphaned-dir>
```

Deleted 3 orphaned dirs (5.1GB) to recover disk. Active dir left in place.
