prs.title: fix(agents): refuse recovery-instruction echoes in settled-turn finalization
prs.body:
Related to #137915

## What Problem This Solves

When a turn ends with tool calls and no answer, OpenClaw re-asks the model for the final reply — but that re-ask never said the reply would be published, so a model could read it as internal state and have its planning, or the re-ask text itself, delivered as the user's answer. The re-asks now state the delivery contract, and a reply that restates one is refused instead of published.

- Problem: the recovery nudges that re-ask a settled tool turn carried no delivery semantics, and the single pre-adoption validation point accepted any non-empty text — including a verbatim restatement of the nudge OpenClaw had just injected.
- Solution: every injected nudge now carries a delivery contract, and the validation point that gates the terminal reply refuses a reply reproducing two separate, non-overlapping runs of the wording the run actually injected, re-entering the existing bounded tool-free recovery.
- What changed: `src/agents/recovery-nudge-text.ts` (new zero-dependency leaf: the contract, the 8 nudge bodies, `withRecoveryDeliveryContract()`, `isRecoveryInstructionEcho()`), `run/incomplete-turn-recovery.ts` and `run/terminal-resolution.ts` (compose their prompts through it), `harness/settled-turn-finalization-result.ts` (refuse an echo), `worker/embedded-agent.runtime.ts` (re-ask once when the worker's own finalization echoes).
- What did NOT change: no new retry channel, budget, config flag, API, or schema. Empty and silent finalization, the runner's bounded retry (2 attempts, tools disabled), and the worker's empty-finalizer failure path behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The invariant is "the text a run delivers must be the model's answer; runner-injected instruction text must never be delivered", and two code paths broke it: the wording side never said the reply is published, and the acceptance side only rejected empty text. Both are fixed at the source, which is also why the earlier candidate (#141206) was not reused — it filtered after publication.

- Best fix: yes. It reuses the existing pre-adoption validation point and its existing bounded tool-free retry instead of adding a second interception layer.
- Alternative: matching the nudge text at delivery time (rejected: filtering after publication is what got #141206 closed) and duplicating the nudge strings inside the validator (rejected: drifting copies, and a value import there drags the runner policy graph into the lightweight plugin-SDK facade).
- Risk / non-goals: a reply quoting only a short fragment of a nudge (for example one truncated sentence) is deliberately not treated as an echo — the matcher requires two non-overlapping 8-word runs drawn only from the instruction actually injected so ordinary prose cannot be discarded by accident, and the delivery contract covers that case at the source. The worker re-ask is echo-only, so an empty finalizer reply keeps its previous behavior.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive the agent's planning notes, or OpenClaw's own recovery text, as the assistant's answer. A turn that would have done so is re-asked once and otherwise falls back to the existing failure/fallback path.

## Evidence

Observed result, production validator, before → after (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs verify-recovery-echo.mjs <repo-root>`, no stubs):

| Input reply | Before fix | After fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. restates the settled-tool nudge | delivered to the user | refused (`EmptySettledTurnFinalizationError`) |
| B. restates the delivery contract | delivered | refused |
| C. genuine answer | delivered | delivered |
| D. planning prose quoting one nudge fragment | delivered | delivered |
| E. answer reusing one generic run of the wording | delivered | delivered |
| E2. answer opening with the nudge's first 9 words, then answering | delivered | delivered (overlapping windows no longer count) |
| F. planning prose, no quote | delivered | delivered |
| G. empty text / H. silent token | refused | refused |

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs verify-recovery-echo.mjs <fixed-worktree>
# settled-tool nudge resolved: true
# settled-tool nudge ends with the delivery contract: true     # was false before the fix
A. reply restating the settled-tool nudge  | <not delivered> | EmptySettledTurnFinalizationError
B. reply restating the delivery contract   | <not delivered> | EmptySettledTurnFinalizationError
C. genuine answer                          | <delivered: {"assistant":{"role":"assistant",...
G. empty text                              | <not delivered> | EmptySettledTurnFinalizationError

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs verify-recovery-echo.mjs <pre-fix-checkout>
# settled-tool nudge ends with the delivery contract: false
A. reply restating the settled-tool nudge  | <delivered: {"assistant":{"role":"assistant",...
```

Regression tests, both captured failing with only the base validator restored:

- `harness/settled-turn-finalization-result.test.ts` › classifies a reply that restates the recovery nudge as an empty answer — FAIL before (echo accepted), PASS after.
- `run/settled-turn-finalization.test.ts` › retries after the finalizer restates the recovery instruction — FAIL before (`runSettledFinalization` called once), PASS after (called twice, delivers the retried answer).
- `worker/worker.runtime.test.ts` › re-asks once when the finalizer restates the recovery nudge (new, PASS), plus `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <7 agent test files>` → 3 shards, 139 tests passed.

Plugin-SDK module load (module hook counting resolved files for facade `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime.ts`): 6124 files before, 6126 after, and the facade's load set contains no `incomplete-turn-recovery` (facade + runner policy graph would be 6136).

What was not tested: no live model provider was exercised (no credentials here), so the wording change is covered by source-level reasoning and the resolver output above rather than a live completion; the two pre-existing `worker.runtime.test.ts` cases `after an empty model response` and `accurate running-process status` fail in this environment identically with and without the change (`exec` tool results come back as `isError`).

## Review round

Rebased onto `main` and folded in the recovery nudge `main` added meanwhile (`TEXT_TOOL_CALL_RETRY_BODY`, now contract-wrapped like the other six), so the rebased branch also carries that wording in the echo catalog.

- **Matcher false positive (addressed).** The detector counted two overlapping sliding windows of the *same* sentence as a restatement, so nine consecutive words shared with a nudge could discard a genuine answer. It now requires two **non-overlapping** runs, and callers pass the exact instruction they injected (the runner, the built-in harness, and the worker all hold it) so only the wording actually sent can match. `settled-turn-finalization-result.test.ts` and `incomplete-turn-recovery.test.ts` cover the corrected cases, including the reported "The previous attempt did not produce a user-visible answer because the provider stopped early. The disk has 12 GB free." reply, which is now kept.
- **Publication boundary (open).** Confirmed with the worker harness: an echoed finalizer turn is committed to an accepted transcript request before `assertSettledTurnFinalizationResult` runs, so the current rejection cannot withdraw those bytes. Moving acceptance to the owning publication/persistence boundary is a larger change and is not part of this revision.
- **Real behavior proof (open).** No shipped entry point (CLI/Gateway/worker/channel) has been exercised end to end.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `rg`, `git log`, `git diff` and `node --import tsx` runs against production modules to trace issue #137915 to the two paths above and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: the runner injects a re-ask whose reply is published verbatim, so the contract is stated in the wording and the pre-adoption validation point refuses a reply reproducing two non-overlapping runs of the injected text. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Twenty-three page and settings components already render through Solid routes but still register custom-element bridges and create nested rendering roots. This removes those redundant registrations and the unused `PageLayout` adapter while preserving the existing host elements, selectors, defaults, focus behavior, cleanup, and lazy loading.

Devices route and Apps search inputs retain equality filtering so unrelated shell updates cannot reset inventory or replay imports. Cloud Worker profiles derive from their owner snapshot; Skill Workshop removes nullable guards excluded by required context. Bridges with actual imperative or legacy callers remain. Coupled fixtures retain their assertions. The catalog fixture adds bounded scalar failure diagnostics and rethrows the original error; it does not alter assertions, waits, or production code.

There is no intended user-visible change and no dependency change. The host elements surround the same content, so this cleanup has no visible markup change requiring new screenshots.

## Evidence

Published head: `f180d34d47cd09084c6bcb64d7dcd14533bc5971`. It normally merges `origin/main` at `6866eac6`, including the independently landed native-consent repair [#172719](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172719). All automatic overlaps were inspected; no manual source changes or conflict resolutions were needed.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI types / whitespace | Passed on current head; `pnpm tsgo:ui` took 179.36s. |
| Production Knip | Passed once on committed current head, no unused files or dependencies; 725.72s wall time. |
| Independent Codex autoreview | Production changes, coupled fixtures, adapter deletion, and diagnostic addition passed through P2 with validated `scoped-clean` results. Reviewed patch reused for conflict-free main integration. |
| Focused tests | Earlier unchanged-patch proof: Connection 25, Apps catalog 11, Devices 37 passed. Investigated MCP import timeout retained below. |
| Full CI | [38675932433](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38675932433), `ci:full`: **45 successful, 4 failed, 23 skipped jobs**. Failures are three test shards and the aggregate gate; all nine failed cases also fail scheduled main, as listed below. |
| Startup | **349,885 B gzip JS / 8 requests; 46,058 B gzip CSS / 1 request.** Original 374,285 B JS budget passes. |
| Same-runner strict performance | Actual CI base `514fe3d1` → merge `838ddf80`: Chat boot **1,690,065 → 1,689,938 B (−127)**; New Session **1,380,823 → 1,380,716 B (−107)**; startup CSS unchanged. Both builds and strict comparison passed in CI. |
| Previously affected cases | Connection's original visible-label case passes **1.751s**. All three catalog cases pass, including the historical error-status case in **11.771s**. Native-consent browser shard 5 passes after the main repair. |

Production LOC across 31 changed production files: **9,294 → 9,125 (−169)**. The complete batch is **40 files**, compared with integrated main `6866eac6`; main's commits are excluded. Much of the whitespace diff unindents the former Meetings and Memory Import bridge bodies.

## Current CI failure accounting

Each name and assertion below was personally compared with the latest completed scheduled-main run [38672095119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672095119), head `a4d316dc`. This records matching failures; no native inherited-failure exception has been admitted.

| Exact failing test | Scheduled-main comparison |
| --- | --- |
| `Control UI progressive Model Providers loading > keeps a Models route selection saved before the initial provider details arrive` | Same picker click/poll timeout; only line offsets differ. |
| `Control UI progressive Model Providers loading > keeps the current Models catalog after late route data and invalidation` | Same picker click/poll timeout; only line offsets differ. |
| `Control UI progressive Model Providers loading > opens the Models route from snapshot catalog publication and refreshes after overlapping reads` | Same picker click/poll timeout; only line offsets differ. |
| `Control UI progressive Model Providers loading > opens the Models route from ordinary catalog publication and refreshes after overlapping reads` | Same picker click/poll timeout; only line offsets differ. |
| `Provider browser login through real HTTPS Gateway > rejects cancelled and stale callbacks, then saves a fresh sign-in and serves an existing session` | Same modal-count assertion at line 211: expected 0, received 1. The separate provider-login fixture lane owns its correction. |
| `Control UI exact stagger with a real Gateway > timeout override: clearing restores the default after save and reload` | Same fixture CLI exit-1 assertion at cliJson:298. |
| `Control UI exact stagger with a real Gateway > failure alert round trip: preserves partial policy through metadata save and clone` | Same fixture CLI exit-1 assertion at cliJson:298. |
| `Control UI exact stagger with a real Gateway > failure alert round trip: clears field overrides through the real picker` | Same fixture CLI exit-1 assertion at cliJson:298. |
| `Control UI exact stagger with a real Gateway > clone payload policy: preserves public options through the real Gateway and CLI readback` | Same fixture CLI exit-1 assertion at cliJson:298. |

## Landing blocker

Fresh native `review-init` completed for this head. `review-checkout-main` then failed to read 13 Git blobs during its journaled checkout. After those blobs became readable, one supported recovery refused the absent tracked file:

> Working-tree entry "apps/ios/README.md" is neither its journaled source nor target entry
>
> Refusing scripts/pr transition for PR #171809: the index or working tree contains unowned transition state.

Both operations drained and released their locks. The checkout and transition journal are preserved without manual restoration or further retries. Preparation and merge submission were not reached; no auto-merge request or merge outcome exists.

## Retained investigation limits

The previous-head Connection `system.info` timeout remains unexplained. Two temporary actual-router unit probes and one unchanged original browser-case replay passed; no speculative Connection fix was added. The current-head pass is positive evidence, not a claimed explanation of the old timeout.

The historical catalog error-status timeout also remains unexplained: two bounded attempts on its actual CI base stopped before the case. Later CI passes are retained as positive evidence; this integration also preserves main's stronger provider-readiness and rejected-reply fixture assertions. There was no third replay.

The earlier local MCP case `mcp-app-view localization > clears successive app updates in the Apps page's embedded conversation` timed out during fixture import while its other 26 cases passed; the exact case subsequently passed CI. That local delay is still recorded as an investigated failure, not a claimed fix.

prs.title: refactor(database): generic family port and backup provider
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Database port, Doctor discovery, and PostgreSQL backup/restore/fingerprinting hard-coded Workboard ownership. They now dispatch through one lazy database-family provider registry. Workboard remains the only production family; its schema, migrations, admission API, and worker dispatch remain in use.

A provider supplies its family id, configured store-root resolver, admitted SQLite table matcher, and lazy descriptor loader. The descriptor combines generated metadata, bundled PostgreSQL DDL, and the expected catalog. Importing the registry no longer pulls in Workboard's descriptor/API or compiled-worker preparation graph.

Descriptors now support canonical triggers recreated after loading, source-admitted optional fragments with dependencies, projection tables omitted from copying and rebuilt by an owner hook, and an owner-supplied source-version migration on a private SQLite copy. Backup records admitted fragments; restore checks them against the captured image. Unknown PostgreSQL families refuse and name supported families. Unreadable metadata preserves the namespace-ownership diagnostic.

The table-scoped capture APIs from #171764 remain intact. Export, restore, fingerprint, and private-copy migration cores are the actual functions used by worker handlers. The synthetic proof calls those cores in-process: one PG fixture, one SQLite→PG→SQLite roundtrip, zero synthetic compiled-worker entries or launches. Workboard's existing tests retain the real-worker dispatch proof.

State (R13), agent (R15), Logbook (R16), Team Reports (R17), and Matrix roots (R18) will plug into this registry. None is enabled here. Search rebuilding remains a follow-up; this adds its projection hook contract only.

**Net production change: +452 lines**, including regenerated metadata. Workboard's bundled DDL is unchanged.

## Evidence

Final head: `c9db1fe7c2d0083702f9a4962d5ddba69db6a569`. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674905385).

| File | Local command wall | Local test execution | Final-head CI execution |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `port-provider.test.ts` | 156.53 s | 0.134 s, 11 passed | 0.070 s, 11 passed |
| `port-provider.postgres.test.ts` | 85.17 s | 3.132 s, 1 passed | 0.699 s, 1 passed |
| `port-provider-imports.test.ts` | 79.72 s | 6.428 s, 1 passed | 0.569 s, 1 passed |

Local measurements use `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on a heavily loaded host; the final unit rerun also waited for a checkout artifact lock. Its initial measurement was 60.93 s wall / about 0.030 s execution. The unit and PG files perform **zero shared worker compilation**. CI seconds above are test-execution seconds; the combined conformance job does not expose independent per-file command wall times. The existing 60-second PG test deadline is unchanged.

The synthetic roundtrip proves private migration with an unchanged original source, canonical triggers on both engines, fragment dependencies, projection rebuild/omission, backup/restore fragment admission, unknown-view/trigger refusal, and fingerprint change detection. It is selected by the existing PG conformance directory alongside Workboard; without the conformance connection its PG case is skipped.

[Final-head PostgreSQL conformance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674905385/job/116226638256) passed **468 tests**, with 38 skipped: 41 unit-fast, 116 infra, and 311 Workboard extension cases. Existing command roundtrip/recovery and all three real-worker backup/restore cases passed.

All production/test types, corrected core-lint jobs, source contracts, architecture, schema-generation verification, wrapper-shadowing, and baseline ratchets passed. The latter includes database-worker, dialect, assertion-safety, max-lines, timeout-race, and mock-export checks. Local line-cap and focused format/lint/type checks passed. The new import guard passed locally and in CI; the local wrapper inventory assertion passed, while an unchanged wrapper fixture timed out in the broader local closure suite.

The implementation delta and subsequent test-only lint correction each received an isolated Codex review with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The first new-head lint run caught a `map`/object-spread rule in the cyclic-fragment fixture; the final head fixes it and both previously failing lint jobs are green. An unchanged subprocess-shutdown fixture also failed on the prior head and passed on the final head without a source change; no fix is claimed.

## CI failure classification

| Check | Classification and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `check-dependencies` | **Inherited.** The same eight untouched exports occur on exact main baseline `a4d316dc86846952cc2ddd99df026c771ab38900`: [main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672095119/job/116217606122). Final-head production/full-tree scans reproduce those symbols; script exports pass. No baselines or ignores changed. |
| UI E2E 5/9 | **Unrelated branch drift.** The old live-preferences test expects speed disabled; current main expects it enabled. The control owners are unchanged. |
| UI E2E 2/9 | **Unrelated branch drift.** The reasoning test counts saved details without expanding their collapsed group. Main contains that test fix and the exact baseline passes the case. |
| UI E2E 4/9 | **Unrelated branch drift.** Global `Copy path` text matches a menu item and hidden tooltip. Main scopes the menu-item selector and the exact baseline passes the case. |
| Real-Gateway UI 2/2 | **Inherited.** All four cron fixture setup failures reproduce on exact main: `automations add` / `cron.add` exits 1 at `cliJson:298` before UI assertions. [Main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672095119/job/116217604473). Underlying CLI stderr is not present in the job log. |
| Real-Gateway UI 1/2 | **Unresolved outside the changed scope; not confirmed inherited.** Five unchanged screenshot-content guards report a fixture marker; the log does not name the matching value. Workboard distribution times out at the gateway-switch button before its mocked Gateway/asset assertions. All six pass on [exact main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672095119/job/116217604739). Main has a modal-action wrapper change, but its connection to the timeout is unproven. The small public diagnostic artifact confirms a connected chat page and successful chat/history RPCs for the captured assertion; it does not expose the marker. |

R12's merge-base-to-head diff contains no UI files. The three mocked-Gateway UI classifications rely on the specific source/test drift above, not a same-name failed job. The real-Gateway 1/2 failures remain explicitly unresolved; no R12-caused path has been established. All jobs in the final-head CI run finished; Android test-wear passed. The aggregate CI gate is red on the dependency and UI jobs classified above. A separate PR-evidence check rejected the earlier nonstandard section headings; this body now uses the required What Problem This Solves and Evidence headings. This stays a draft and will not be merged by this lane.

prs.title: feat: search public GitHub issues and pull requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent can read a known public GitHub item but cannot find relevant issues or pull requests from a repository name through that reader. A sandboxed session otherwise needs an externally supplied URL or separate network and credential access before it can begin that research.

This adds `github_search` for public issues and pull requests in one explicitly chosen repository. It builds on the public item reader in #172692; this contribution contains the search behavior and its directly required invocation adapter.

## User Impact

Permitted agents can supply an `owner/repo` repository, an explicit issue or pull-request kind, optional plain-text keywords, and an open/closed filter. Search each kind separately when both are needed; this supports GitHub App user tokens as well as the existing credential paths. Each response contains up to 20 matches with readable item URLs, sorted by the most recent update. The caller can follow `nextPage` or pass a URL to `github_read` for the discussion and changes.

Results explicitly distinguish an empty search from incomplete GitHub results and the API's 1,000-result limit. The new tool follows the coding profile and default sandbox tool policy; custom allowlists can permit it by name. Tool deny rules shape the available tool surface, and active invocation, operator, plugin, and identity authority is checked through delivery. The Gateway retains credentials, and neither private search nor GitHub writes are added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Search extends the existing GitHub plugin, public API transport, identity selection, and admitted reader handler. The request fixes the chosen repository and public visibility before dispatch. Keyword text cannot supply qualifiers or Boolean operators, and returned references are checked against that repository before delivery. Repository visibility is checked before search and again before returning an authenticated result.

The implementation keeps the existing request lifetime and authority checks rather than selecting credentials or adding network access inside the sandbox. Search has no separate client, cache, service, or persistent state. The plugin documentation describes filters, continuation, limits, and access behavior.

## Evidence

The baseline's real admitted tool assembly exposed only `github_read`: the new discovery expectation failed while all nine existing reader controls passed. Focused integration coverage uses actual plugin registration, sandbox policy, admitted tool execution, Gateway dispatch, and managed identity selection, with only external GitHub I/O stubbed.

The search scenarios cover page continuation followed by reading a result, issues and closed pull requests, empty/incomplete/capped results, retry information, query scope escapes, private and mismatched repositories, request cancellation, and caller closure during search. Existing reader and direct-caller checks remain part of the selected validation.

Read-only probes through the authenticated GitHub CLI confirmed issue/PR response fields, another page, empty results, and literal treatment of a quoted Boolean word. Those probes qualify the upstream response contract; the invocation tests qualify OpenClaw's integration.

The admitted invocation file passed all 17 cases in 71.39 seconds (74.87 seconds including the test helper). The other 25 related files retain 470 passing cases, covering the existing reader, identities, UI adapters and sandbox consumers. Changed-file formatting/lint, affected production and test types, and the descriptor line-budget checks passed on the qualified candidate. The runtime build completed in 80.4 seconds. In a fresh guest session with sandboxing required and container networking disabled, the tools returned 20 items on each of two issue pages and a separate pull-request search, then read returned issue and PR references through `github_read`. The inspected results preserved continuation, 1,000-result and partial-content markers. That live flow used the Gateway path throughout. Independent engineering and adversarial review passed on head 7ac4d0add1d890d8eb0f979d4f196296b5852e8e. Hosted CI still owns the pending broad-suite result and timing.


<details>
<summary>Live guest execution facts</summary>

The native runtime build and restart both exited 0 on `7ac4d0add1d890d8eb0f979d4f196296b5852e8e`. The fresh guest used the OpenClaw harness with sandboxing required; its actual Docker container reported `NetworkMode: none`. These are the inspected tool-result facts from that run:

```json

    "page": 1,
```

prs.title: fix(models): request native runtime consent during provider setup
prs.body:
## Problem

Each host-native runtime handled the "native permissions" consent its own way. Muse Code had a provider-specific prompt inside `extensions/meta/muse-login.ts` plus SDK fields (`ProviderAuthResult.nativeRuntimeConsent`, `ProviderAuthContext.agentId`) to send consent back to core. Every other native runtime would need the same copy, or the user is asked in chat instead of at setup.

## Solution

- New core owner `src/agents/harness/setup-consent.ts`. Provider setup activation (Provider Access and AI Setup, including access-only `selectModel:false`) calls it once the auth result has identified the runtime, before verification and activation.
- Eligibility comes from the selected harness's capability (`executionEnvironment === "host-only"`), not from provider names. Codex and direct Copilot declare exact tool-policy enforcement and are not prompted.
- If the target agent has not already remembered the harness, setup shows one step: "Use <runtime>'s native permissions?". It uses the same boundary text as the chat prompt and says the choice is remembered for this agent. Cancelling activates nothing and remembers nothing.
- Continue stages `rememberNativeRuntimeConsent` in the same setup commit, through the existing activation writer. Pre-commit authority revalidation and the shared harness/registry cache are unchanged.
- Clean cutover: Muse's own prompt, `ProviderAuthResult.nativeRuntimeConsent` and `ProviderAuthContext.agentId` are deleted. These were added in #172610 and never released.
- The chat prompt stays as the fallback for runtimes that never went through setup (for example config-edited routes). Mandatory sandbox and workspace restrictions are still enforced.

Follow-ups, already implemented on a separate branch: enabling an installed ACP agent (OpenCode, Qwen Code, Pi, Kilo Code, ACP Copilot) through one core setup operation, and the CLI/onboarding paths.

## Evidence

Live run on an isolated Gateway (real `muse` 1.3.0, real Meta approval, `tools.deny=["browser"]` so consent is required):
1. Provider Access → Meta → Muse Code: one setup warning ("Use Muse Code's native permissions?") → Continue → "Muse Code is connected".
2. "Start a new chat with Muse Spark 1.3" → reply `NRC_FINAL_OK` with no chat prompt. The primary model is unchanged. The session has `full` / sandbox `off` and no per-chat consent, so the remembered agent consent was used.

![setup consent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7665c0f3-79e4-4be7-a31c-9e0eaf1aea39)
![connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c4158d8-4a0e-4e2c-bd3f-eaeb19f04913)
![chat without prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5fd683f-80b3-4c18-a635-03cfcd6c8f04)

Tests: `setup-consent.test.ts` (host-only prompts once; already remembered skips; non-host-only skips; cancel persists nothing; authority recheck after the answer), activation and credential-lifecycle suites (consent committed with activation; `selectModel:false` keeps the model; failed verification persists no consent), and the Meta login suite without the provider-specific prompt.

### Authority proof for the post-login consent step

Live, same isolated Gateway (real Muse login; Muse binary wrapped to record each invocation):
```text
Real Muse login succeeded; post-login native-permissions consent appeared.
03:38:16.171Z  wizard.next => running, native-permissions select step.
03:38:24.177Z  Browser operator device token revoked while consent waited.
03:38:24.488Z  WebSocket closed: 4001 "device removed"; consent dialog dismissed, Continue unavailable.
Replay of the recorded Continue answer:
  INVALID_REQUEST / WIZARD_NOT_FOUND / "wizard not found"
Final config byte-identical (SHA256 03e07d5c…2240):
  nativeRuntimeConsent absent; plugins.entries.muse absent; agentRuntime absent
Muse invocation recorder: "login" invocations only; zero "serve" (no verification process or model/list).
```
Tests: "rejects consent when authority is revoked while the prompt is open"; and "sets up the Muse route for main (… authority)", which checks rejection after Continue, unchanged config and no verification call.

## Update behavior

No migration. The removed SDK fields shipped in no release. Agents already listed in `nativeRuntimeConsent` are not asked again.

prs.title: fix(update): recover stopped gateways after unverified service activation
prs.body:
Refs #171435. This fixes the stopped-Gateway recovery outcome; the initiating native installer failure in the report remains undetermined.

## What Problem This Solves

An update can leave a runnable Gateway stopped after an installer or service-definition recovery receipt cannot be verified, then tell the operator to keep it stopped without identifying a data risk.

## User Impact

Final recovery now restarts an owned service stopped by the update, preserves its existing definition and retained packages, and verifies readiness using the normal update budget. Verified recovery of an unverified definition/installer receipt succeeds with a warning directing the operator to `openclaw update repair`. Recovery of availability alone preserves unrelated update failures. Failed startup keeps the original update failure and reports the concrete startup error with repair/status commands. Named data risks still prohibit startup and retain the stopped guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Package rollback refusal and runtime recovery were coupled: an unverifiable definition backup prevented rollback, while final recovery only observed the stopped service. Final recovery now reuses the existing managed-service ownership checks and native restart path after package retention settles. It promotes the outcome only after version, service, and readiness verification. Both the installed package and previous package remain retained for repair.

Doctor's named data-risk reason now survives error-to-result conversion and takes priority within the existing five-fact diagnostic bound. Generic unverified recovery no longer produces “keep the Gateway stopped” advice, including in the managed handoff helper log. Native command errors put their concrete cause before the executable path so support-path redaction preserves the actionable failure.

Production +143/-16 (net +127); tests +306/-98 (net +208); docs +10/-0. The additional production code carries data-risk evidence and completes recovery through the existing lifecycle owner. No configuration/CLI options, dependencies, database schemas, or retention policy changes.

## Evidence

- Caller selection collected 176 ordinary test files; 174 executed and two existing Linux-only file gates remained skipped on macOS (`update-command-system-service.test.ts`, `update-managed-service-handoff-settlement.test.ts`). The frozen 20-file infrastructure replay passed 463/463. The 43-file and additional handoff runs found only the diagnosed expectations/fixture failures described below, resolved by passing targeted replays. No source guard, timeout, retry, or platform gate was bypassed. The filename scan also matched unrelated live-only Node-provisioning and E2E lease fixtures; those are not importers of the changed handoff module.
- Negative control on unchanged base `e106d1fa54ec`: both new stopped-service cases fail. The healthy case remains an update error; the refused-start case observes only `install`, with no recovery `restart` attempt.
- The regression uses the real finalizer and native CLI response parsing with a synthetic executable returning an invalid definition-backup receipt. It checks successful recovery, concrete startup refusal, persisted outcome/guidance, and filesystem retention of both package versions. Service/RPC I/O is synthetic; native Linux systemd execution remains a platform proof gap.
- Focused recovery, guidance, Doctor-result, and changed Git-mutation proof: 78 tests pass. The final full recovery suite is 36/36 in 54.25 seconds wall time (47.73 seconds in Vitest, 81% tests). prs.title: fix: cancelling a task or killing a session can still deliver the child's completion
prs.body:
fix: cancelling a task or killing a session can still deliver the child's completion

Closes #139964

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who cancel a task by id (`openclaw tasks` cancel path) or
kill a session through the HTTP admin endpoint could still receive the child subagent's
completion notification afterwards. The cancel appears to succeed, then a completion for
the very run that was just cancelled is delivered anyway.

This only happens when the child's completion races the cancellation. The bulk stop
surfaces (`/stop`, chat abort) are not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancellation intentionally opens a bounded `killReconciliation` window so a run that
genuinely finished while the cancel was in flight is not thrown away. Inside that window a
real success reconciles the killed run back to `subagent-complete`
(`subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts:307-341`). That part is by design.

The mechanism for honouring the operator's intent already exists:
`killReconciliation.suppressTaskDelivery` propagates into `suppressCompletionDelivery`
(`subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts:381-383`). The bulk paths feed it —
`chat-abort-runtime.ts:85` and `auto-reply/reply/abort.ts:178` both pass
`suppressTaskDelivery: true`.

The two precise-cancel entries could not. Both go through `killSubagentRunAdmin`, whose
params type (`task-registry-control.types.ts:39-48`) had no field for suppression, so
`task-registry-cancel.ts` and `session-kill-http.ts` had no way to express it and
`killSubagentRunAdmin` passed nothing down to `killSubagentRoot`. The wiring below that
point already supports it (`killLatestSubagentRun` spreads params into `killSubagentRun`).

## Shipped Solution

Five production lines, no refactor:

- `task-registry-control.types.ts` — add `suppressTaskDelivery?: boolean` to the
  `killSubagentRunAdmin` params type.
- `subagent-control-kill.ts` — forward `params.suppressTaskDelivery` into
  `killSubagentRoot`; the rest of the chain already spreads it.
- `task-registry-cancel.ts`, `session-kill-http.ts` — pass `suppressTaskDelivery: true`,
  matching the bulk stop paths.

Behaviour for callers that do not ask for suppression is unchanged.

## User Impact

An explicit cancel now suppresses the child's completion delivery on the cancel-by-task-id
and HTTP admin kill paths, so operators stop seeing a completion notification for work they
just cancelled. No change to the reconciliation window itself: a run that really finished
still reconciles to `subagent-complete`, it just no longer announces after an explicit
cancel. No API removals; the new field is optional.

## Evidence

New test `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.precise-cancel-suppression.test.ts`
drives the **real** registry/SQLite fixture (`useSubagentControlFixture`) and the real
`killSubagentRunAdmin`, asserting that a suppression request survives as durable
cancellation ownership on `killIntent`/`killReconciliation`, and that a caller which does
not ask for suppression is unchanged.

**Negative control** — with the four production lines reverted and the test unchanged, the
suppression case fails (`expected false to be true`) while the non-suppression case still
passes. The test therefore proves the gap rather than restating the implementation.

Both call sites are covered by updating the existing exact-argument assertions:
`session-kill-http.test.ts` (2 assertions) and `task-executor.test.ts` ("cancels active
subagent child tasks"). These fail without the fix.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/tasks/task-executor.test.ts src/gateway/session-kill-http.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.precise-cancel-suppression.test.ts \
  src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.retirement.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.recovery.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.concurrency.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-errors.test.ts
→ exit 0, 328 passed (2 + 33 + 184 + 109)

pnpm tsgo:core                          → exit 0
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs → exit 0
oxfmt --check (all 7 touched files)     → exit 0
```

Scope note: this closes the wiring gap reported in #139964. The end-to-end delivery of a
late completion notification to a real channel was not reproduced end-to-end there and is
not claimed here either; the fix is justified by the wiring asymmetry against the bulk
paths plus the test-pinned reconciliation behaviour.

prs.title: test(qa-lab): keep stalled repeated-request fallback live past its allowance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the `Gateway repeated-request recovery` e2e (`recovers semantic stagnation and settles the active run before draining one queued followup`) times out on nearly every `main` run, and flakes on `release/2026.10.4`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Gateway E2E is green again for this case, so it stops masking real regressions and blocking release validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #164808, repeated-request recovery can abort a retry or fallback request only after that request's own allowance (`started + 45s`) has expired. The mock's stalled fallback sent no bytes, so the client's idle watchdog ended it at exactly `started + 45s`. That left a window of about 10 ms for the 30 s diagnostic heartbeat to see an expired allowance while the request was still active. The heartbeat almost never lands in that window, so recovery never fires and the test waits out its 250 s budget.

The mock's stalled fallback now accepts the SSE stream and sends `: keepalive` comments, like a live provider that has stopped making progress. Keepalives reset the client idle watchdog but not its 2x progress deadline, so the request stays active from `started + 45s` until `started + 90s`. That 45 s window always contains a 30 s heartbeat, so recovery aborts deterministically. This is the case repeated-request recovery exists to handle.

The test contract is unchanged. It still asserts semantic stagnation recovered, one `session.recovery.requested`/`completed` abort, the active run settled with an error, and exactly one queued followup drained with stall guidance. Only the mock's stalled response shape and the comments changed. No product code changed.

## Evidence

Failing CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38631255539/job/116093414480 (release-ci). The heartbeat observed the stall at `ageMs: 43618`, and the next heartbeat landed after the fallback had already timed out (`durationMs: 45011`, `failureKind: timeout`). `main` jobs on `9ed9c2cd174` and `15fdc5a3d14` fail with the same 250 s stability timeout.

Local before (origin/main `95d09cc0b2d`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-repeated-request-recovery.e2e.test.ts`): **FAIL** with `timed out after 250000ms waiting for stability events`. Timeline: the fallback started at T, the heartbeat at T+21.1s emitted `session.stalled` (`ageMs: 45514`) but the allowance was not yet expired, the fallback timed out at T+45.006s, and the next heartbeat landed at T+51.1s. No recovery.

Local after: see the follow-up comment with repeated runs.

prs.title: fix: keep gateway responsive during external plugin preparation
prs.body:
Related: #160959

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway responsiveness during source capture of large non-bundled plugins.

## User Impact

Selected external plugins prepare their captured source without occupying the gateway's main thread. Plugin selection, admission checks, registration, and synchronous CLI behavior remain intact. Capture no longer has an arbitrary two-minute deadline. Plugin evaluation remains synchronous; this does not eliminate every initialization or cleanup stall.

## Why This Change Was Made

Async loading gives each captured external plugin its own retained preparation worker, so synchronous requests from an active plugin never queue behind another plugin's preparation. Existing plugin-instance caching avoids preparing already-loaded instances again, and recovery retains the original capture and worker. This uses more worker threads than a shared preparation lane to avoid a host/worker deadlock.

The worker inherits capture storage, read-only state, installation roots, and admission facts; loaded native images remain retained through cleanup. Bundled plugins and existing compute-worker loading retain their current paths. Commit `8b42910723963650fcf145b792ef274fe48c0944` removes the capture deadline raised in review; other asynchronous operations retain their 120-second deadline and synchronous operations retain 30 seconds.

## Evidence

### Actual built Gateway: stable versus candidate

Executed on Windows with Node 24.21.0 using the actual `openclaw.mjs` entry points, isolated state and a loopback port. The fixture registers `proof.echo`, carries a persisted configuration marker, and contains 4,000 generated JavaScript payload files (16,384,000 bytes). All 4,000 files were verified in each generation's captured tree.

The stable package was the official npm latest, 2026.10.3 (`59cb447`), with tarball integrity verified. Its exact published AI and Koffi dependencies were installed in the temporary test package; other missing dependencies were linked read-only from the source checkout. This is a qualified package comparison, not a claim of a fresh standalone dependency installation.

During the actual `plugins.reload` RPC, independent HTTP `/healthz` and WebSocket `health` probes ran with a 15-second deadline. Reload was accepted only after the plugin's RPC returned its new revision.

| Measured during reload | Published stable | PR candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Captured payload files | 4,000 | 4,000 |
| Reload duration | 22,951 ms | 21,160 ms |
| HTTP probes / failures | 6 / 1 timeout | 165 / 0 |
| WebSocket probes / failures | 6 / 1 timeout | 154 / 0 |
| Maximum HTTP latency | 15,006.7 ms, timed out | 2,337.1 ms |
| Maximum WebSocket latency | 15,012.1 ms, timed out | 2,382.3 ms |
| Newly registered revision | 2 | 3 |
| Restart required | false | false |

After stable completed its reload, it was stopped and the PR build opened **the same stable-created state**. Plugin registration and health passed. Plugin settings, agent workspace settings, and a synthetic project file were preserved. The candidate then reloaded successfully; its runtime module URL confirmed the preparation-worker capture path. All temporary gateway processes exited. No operator gateway, agents, projects, or models were changed.

This is one synthetic run. Stable latency is censored by the probe deadline. The candidate still showed approximately 2.4-second worst-case health latency, and replacement reported that it waited for retained work. This proves removal of the observed long health timeout in this workload, not zero stalls. It tests package replacement against stable-created state, not execution of the npm updater itself.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal/result output and artifact provenance</summary>

```text
source commit: 8b42910723963650fcf145b792ef274fe48c0944
pnpm build: exit 0, total 5m 16.9s
stable: READY; proof.echo revision=1 marker=preserve-me; health.ok=true
stable reload: capturedFiles=4000 revision=2 restartRequired=false
  durationMs=22951 HTTP=6/1-failed WS=6/1-failed
candidate upgrade: sameState=true settingsPreserved=true projectPreserved=true
candidate reload: capturedFiles=4000 revision=3 restartRequired=false
  durationMs=21160 HTTP=165/0-failed WS=154/0-failed
  HTTP.maxMs=2337.1 WS.maxMs=2382.3 workerCapturePath=true
harness: exit 0; temporary gateway processes stopped
```

The build began with the timeout correction present in the working tree, before that identical source was committed. Consequently its build-info commit is `ad62b25065ef17771e685b969757ffc6bc67c12f`; its compiled source includes the correction committed as `8b429107`, verified in the generated worker client. This is the built PR source, not the separately adapted live hotfix.

Compiled module: `dist/plugin-generation-worker-D3ihD2Ek.mjs`  
SHA256: `8D0B60C803EED92522A2E39E00C8F7E640CFD9E8767BE619FD945FE52EBB3ABE`

</details>

### Timeout regression and focused checks

- The new real-worker regression holds native publication while advancing the host task clock by 120,001 ms. It **fails on the previous implementation** with `WorkerTaskError: worker task timed out`, then passes with this fix and verifies artifact resolution and disposal. This is simulated elapsed time, not a 120-second wall-time capture.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-generation-worker.test.ts src/plugins/loader.async-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **8 passed**, 2 files, 98.61 seconds including wrapper/worker preparation; new regression 872 ms. CI seconds not yet available.
- Core and plugin-test TypeScript checks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed, exit 0, 5m 16.9s.
- Fresh independent source review of the timeout correction found no actionable P0/P1 issues.
- Earlier evidence: 22 existing retained-native/lazy-alias regressions passed before the final transport correction; the current focused worker/loader suite was rerun afterward.

Remaining startup/module-evaluation and session-cleanup delays are outside this change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `src/gateway/gateway-route-model-reuse.test.ts` fails intermittently with `prepared model runtime catalog generation was superseded` (`UNAVAILABLE`, `retryable: true`, `retryAfterMs: 0`) when its first `models.list { refresh: true }` races a startup model publication. Seen in Full Release Validation CI for 2026.10.10-beta.1 (run 38662503008, job 116187245728, `gateway-server-isolated-6`).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Removes a release-gate flake in the Gateway route-model reuse proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

`models.list` documents that a refresh whose catalog owner goes stale is rejected with `UNAVAILABLE`, `retryable: true`, `retryAfterMs: 0` (docs/gateway/protocol/operator-methods.md), and the Control UI retries once (#147926). The test's startup refresh did not follow that contract, so a startup publication that superseded the refresh failed the whole proof before it measured anything. The test now retries that one startup refresh once when the Gateway returns a retryable `UNAVAILABLE` response; every other failure still throws, and the rest of the proof is unchanged.

Checked whether #172632 (364cc6843a0, "recover agent admission after runtime supersession") covers this: it changes startup agent admission only, not the `models.list` refresh path or its retryable rejection, so it does not prevent this failure.

## Evidence

- CI failure: run 38662503008 / job 116187245728, failed after 22.7 s at the first `models.list` call with the retryable supersession error above (the only `models.list` call outside `expect.poll`).
- `pnpm test src/gateway/gateway-route-model-reuse.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this branch: 1 passed; wall time 722 s including the test's required `dist` build (test body ~162 s). The race did not reproduce locally on unmodified release or main (2/3 passes each; the other runs hit local-load Gateway readiness timeouts, unrelated).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-visibility.test.ts` "a hidden-foreign role cannot discover sessions…" fails with `expected [] to deeply equal ['agent:main:own-role-read']` when post-write session maintenance runs before the test lists sessions. Seen in Full Release Validation CI for 2026.10.10-beta.1 (run 38662503008, job 116187245615) and earlier in FRV child run 38643270988 (job 116124329613, before the release cut).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Removes a release-gate flake in the session read-visibility proofs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixtures seeded session rows with `updatedAt: 42` (1970). Post-write age-retention maintenance correctly archives such rows (`archivedAt`, `archiveReason: "age-retention"`), and default `sessions.list` then hides them. Whether that archive lands before the list depends on maintenance scheduling and machine load, so the test flaked. On the release branch the archive fires promptly. On current `main`, #172674 (ebb8d84506c) changed scheduling so it no longer fires during the test, which hides the problem without fixing the fixture. The fixtures in this file now seed current timestamps. No assertion depends on the old value.

## Evidence

- Root cause captured with temporary instrumentation on `release/2026.10.10`: when the test failed, a fresh projection, a no-client list, and an unsearched list all returned `[]`, and the stored entry was `{"updatedAt":42,…,"archivedAt":…,"archiveReason":"age-retention"}`. On `main`, the same probe showed the entry still unarchived 5 s after listing.
- `release/2026.10.10` with the old fixture: `-t "hidden-foreign"` fails 1/1. Full-file runs under parallel load failed 11 of ~30.
- `release/2026.10.10` with this change: full file 2/2 passed (61 s and 57 s wall), `-t "hidden-foreign"` 1/1 passed.
- `main` with this change: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-visibility.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 12/12 under 3-way parallel load (87–229 s wall).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: format, lint, and core test typecheck passed. The remaining failures are already on `main` and unrelated: the `OPENCLAW_*` env-var count budget (455 > 454) and existing Knip unused exports.

prs.title: fix: usage undercounts Claude CLI turns that make several model calls
prs.body:
Related: #148603 (this PR fixes the whole-turn accounting; the issue's final per-call output count is listed under Not in scope below)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session usage, `usage.cost`, and the Usage page count only the last model call (with its stream-start output count) for Claude CLI turns. Turns that make several model calls, such as tool-using turns, are therefore heavily undercounted.

## User Impact

User impact: Claude CLI turns now record the whole turn's tokens in the session transcript, so usage reports and anything built on them (cost estimates, budget alerts) match what Claude Code reports.

- Context-window sizing, preflight compaction, and memory-flush gating keep using the latest model call.
- Chat context displays (Control UI message footer, iOS/macOS chat) keep showing the latest call's context size.
- Turns recorded before this change keep their existing counts.
- No config, schema, or migration change (see compatibility below).

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's terminal `result` event already carries whole-turn usage, and the stream parser keeps it as `diagnosticUsage` (#120100). Both CLI transcript writers still persisted the last call.

- **Both writers:** they now persist the turn total as the usage counters. `contextUsage` is derived from the last call through one shared helper (`resolveCliTranscriptUsage`), so every context reader still sizes the window from the latest call.
- **Reply-path writer:** it adds that context marker only when the backend reports a turn total separately. Other CLI backends keep their unmarked records, which context readers already refuse to treat as a fresh context size (#120497).
- **Memory flush and preflight:** their transcript snapshot now takes the last completion's output from the context marker instead of the turn counters.

- **Chat context displays:** chat history now forwards an available, coherent `contextUsage` marker with assistant usage. The Control UI message footer and the native context control and footer size context from it. Rows without an available marker keep sizing from the counters, as before.
- **Tiered pricing:** summed tokens cannot recover each request's tier. `usage.cost` now leaves a turn unpriced when its counters exceed the marker's prompt and their sum reaches past the lowest tier.
  - A sum inside the lowest tier keeps every call there, so it is still estimated. Flat pricing is unchanged.
  - The rule reads the usage shape, so it also applies to Codex harness rows whose summed prompt crosses a tier boundary.
  - `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION` moves to 8 so cached usage summaries rebuild with the new rule. `main` is at 7 since #169660, which also carries version-6 summaries forward; both were priced under the old rule, so this PR accepts only version 8. The schema cutover still moves version-6 rows, and readers rebuild them.

Live `agentMeta.usage` / `lastCallUsage` and the context-engine hook message are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (after the fix, live OpenClaw)

Setup:
- A production OpenClaw 2026.9.2 gateway with Claude Code 2.1.263 on a Claude subscription.
- This PR's three production edits applied as a local backport, with identical logic, because the host runs the published build.
- Output is redacted to usage counters; the session id is replaced.

Two non-delivering `openclaw agent` turns ran on one dedicated session:
- Turn 1 makes two model calls: a Read tool call, then the reply.
- Turn 2 reuses the existing session.

```text
$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:<proof> --json \
    --message "Use the Read tool to read IDENTITY.md in your workspace, then reply with only the number of lines in that file."

# live run metadata (unchanged by this PR)
turn 1  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 325}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918}
turn 2  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}

# persisted assistant transcript records, read back from the session's SQLite transcript
turn 1  usage {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918, totalTokens 149604,
               contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 74920, totalTokens 74921}}
turn 2  usage {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102, totalTokens 75025,
               contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 75022, totalTokens 75023}}

# Claude Code's own transcript for the bound CLI session (deduplicated by message id)
turn 1  model calls 2  sum input 4 / output 89 / cacheRead 74593 / cacheWrite 74918  last-call prompt 74920
turn 2  model calls 1  sum input 2 / output 3  / cacheRead 74918 / cacheWrite 102    last-call prompt 75022

# usage.cost for the agent's day, read back before and after the two proof turns (rollup refresh)
before  totalTokens 404634  output 13   cacheWrite 45337   totalCost 0.3800  missingCostEntries 0
after   totalTokens 629263  output 105  cacheWrite 120357  totalCost 0.8764  missingCostEntries 0
delta   totalTokens +224629 (= 149604 + 75025)  output +92 (= 89 + 3)  cacheWrite +75020 (= 74918 + 102)
```

What this shows:
- The persisted counters equal Claude Code's per-turn totals exactly.
- The usage report's delta equals the two persisted records. The dollar figure comes from a locally configured `claude-cli` price entry; this PR does not change pricing.
- `contextUsage.promptTokens` equals the last call's prompt.
- Without this change, turn 1 would have been persisted as output 1 / cacheWrite 325.
- A scheduled heartbeat turn on the same gateway also persisted its final output count (9) and not the stream-start value (1): `usage {input 2, output 9, cacheRead 69062, cacheWrite 10885, totalTokens 79958, contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 79949, totalTokens 79950}}`.

### Real behavior proof for the chat display and pricing follow-ups

Setup:
- OpenClaw built from this branch at 4f6d8a833ce, run as an isolated local gateway (own state directory, loopback only, channels off).
- Both turns ran with `openclaw agent` through the real `claude-cli` backend. The `claude` binary on `PATH` was a stand-in that emits the usage of the live turns above as Claude Code stream records: one `assistant` record per model call and the terminal `result`. No model call was made.
  - The first call's record is derived: turn total minus the last call.
  - `qa/scenarios/channels/telegram-claude-cli-compaction-final-priority.yaml` uses the same stand-in technique.
- The runner, transcript writer, chat history, `usage.cost` and the Control UI are the built product with no proof-only changes. The only stand-in is the `claude` binary.
- **Before** is this branch with the source changes of fa8ed7c9688 and db6439b5fd3 reverted and rebuilt. That is the state reviewed at 9366812645d: whole-turn counters stored, displays and pricing not yet following the marker. **After** is the head.
- The turns ran once, on the before build. The after build read the same session from the same state directory. The transcript writer is identical in both builds.
- Proof configuration: a 200,000-token context window, and a `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-5` price entry with a tier boundary at 100,000 prompt tokens (`$3 / $15 / $0.30 / $3.75` per million tokens below it, `$6 / $22.50 / $0.60 / $7.50` above). Each call of turn 1 stays below the boundary (74,595 and 74,920 prompt tokens). Their sum (149,515) crosses it.

```text
$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof --json \
    --message "Use the Read tool to read IDENTITY.md in your workspace, then reply with only the number of lines in that file."
$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof --json --message "Reply with only the word ok."

# run metadata from the stand-in, equal to the live run above
turn 1  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 325}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918}
turn 2  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}

# openclaw gateway call chat.history: assistant usage as the Control UI and the apps receive it
before  turn 1  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918, totalTokens 149604}
        turn 2  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102, totalTokens 75025}
after   turn 1  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918, totalTokens 149604,
                 contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 74920, totalTokens 74921}}
        turn 2  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102, totalTokens 75025,
                 contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 75022, totalTokens 75023}}

# openclaw gateway call usage.cost --params '{"days":1}': totals
before  totalTokens 224629  totalCost 0.6315762  missingCostEntries 0
after   totalTokens 224629  totalCost 0.0229089  missingCostEntries 1
        missingCostByModel {"claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-5": 1}
```

What this shows:
- **`usage.cost`, before:** turn 1 is priced from its summed prompt at the upper tier. That is `$0.6086673` of the total; the rest is turn 2. Both of its calls sit in the lower tier, where the same tokens cost about `$0.3047`.
- **`usage.cost`, after:** turn 1 is left unpriced and counted in `missingCostEntries`. Turn 2 is a single call and keeps its estimate, `$0.0229089`.
- Token totals are the same in both builds (224,629 = 149,604 + 75,025).
- The before build stored its usage rollup under version 6. On the head, the first `usage.cost` read reported it stale and refreshing. The next read, 3 s later, was fresh with the new totals, and the stored rollup carries version 7. No manual step was needed.

**Control UI** (web): the usage details of turn 1's reply in the chat view. They show when the message footer is hovered.

Before: `75% ctx`

![Control UI message footer before: 75% ctx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/web-before.png)

After: `37% ctx`

![Control UI message footer after: 37% ctx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/web-after.png)

**Native** (iOS): the message footer (top) and the context control's menu (bottom).

Before: `75% ctx` with a warning, and "149.6k of 200.0k tokens used"

![iOS chat before: 75% ctx, 149.6k of 200.0k tokens used](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/native-before.png)

After: `37% ctx`, and "74.9k of 200.0k tokens used"

![iOS chat after: 37% ctx, 74.9k of 200.0k tokens used](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/native-after.png)

- The iOS app target is a Debug build of `apps/ios` on an iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.4.1), from a reduced project without the watch app, in the app's screenshot fixture mode (`--openclaw-screenshot-mode`).
- A local, uncommitted patch to the fixture transport seeds the chat history with turn 1's usage row and a 200,000-token window. The chat text and the model label (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) are the fixture's own.
- Both runs receive the same history payload, marker included. Before reverts the Swift changes of fa8ed7c9688, so only the app code differs.
- The macOS app renders the same shared `OpenClawChatUI` views from `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`. It was not captured separately.
- The screenshots hold proof-session and fixture content only: no endpoints, addresses, keys or personal data.

### Tests and checks

Regression tests. Each one fails on `main` and passes with this change:
- `cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` › "persists the terminal Claude turn usage for a multi-call turn"
  - Runs a turn whose parsed output carries the last call and a separate turn total through `runPreparedCliAgent`, then reads the persisted transcript back.
  - Before: input 2 / output 1 / cacheRead 27,376.
  - After: 6 / 77 / 54,631, with `contextUsage` at the last call's 27,378 prompt tokens.
- `transcript-persistence.test.ts` › "persists the terminal CLI turn usage while keeping last-call context"
- `session-transcript-readers.test.ts` › "sizes CLI output from the context marker when counters cover the whole turn"
  - Before: 30,000 output tokens.
  - After: 2,000 output tokens.

- `chat-display-projection.test.ts` › "forwards an available context marker with assistant usage"
- `chat-message-timestamp.test.ts` (new file) › "sizes context from the marker when usage counters cover a whole turn"
  - Before: 75% ctx for a two-call turn in a 200k window.
  - After: 37% ctx.
- `ChatContextUsageTests.swift` › "whole-turn counters report the latest call's context marker" and "usage footer sizes context from the marker and keeps whole-turn counters"
  - Before: 149,000 tokens and "98% ctx".
  - After: 75,000 tokens and "49% ctx".
- `session-cost-usage-pricing.test.ts` (new file) › "leaves a multi-call turn unpriced when its sum crosses a tier" and "prices a multi-call turn whose sum stays in the lowest tier"

Guard test:
- `cli-run-transcript.test.ts` › "keeps CLI usage unmarked when the backend reports no separate turn total"

Suites and checks (branch merged with `main` at 035bf890344):
- Merge history: the merge at efa6458a090 had three conflicts, all code `main` had moved: the transcript accounting reader now lives in `session-transcript-accounting-policy.ts`, and the chat footer's `extractGroupMeta` in the Solid `chat-message-timestamp-view.tsx`; this PR's two edits were re-applied there unchanged. The merge at 432d890350b was clean. The merge at 035bf890344 had one import conflict in `chat-message-timestamp-view.tsx`; both helpers are kept.
- #120008 (usage reports marked unavailable) landed in three files this PR also changes: the chat history projection, the usage pricing estimate and the Control UI footer. Both changes are kept side by side: an unavailable usage report is skipped before this PR's context marker and tier guard are read.
- On the merged head, `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=4` passed 2,239 tests across 171 files:
  - every test file in `src/agents/cli-runner/` and `src/agents/command/` (live and e2e files excluded);
  - the `cli-runner.*`, `cli-output*`, `usage*`, `agent-runner-memory*`, `session-transcript-readers*`, `chat-display-projection*`, `session-cost-usage*` and `usage-format*` suites;
  - the Control UI `chat-message*` suites, including the six chat browser tests;
  - the usage cache suites (`session-cost-usage-cache.*`), `doctor-usage-cost-cache.test.ts` and the schema cutover test `openclaw-agent-db.storage-migration.test.ts`.
- The version 8 move updates two cutover tests from #169660: a migrated version-6 report is still moved (the cache test checks it arrives byte for byte), but no longer decodes as current (`session-cost-usage-cache.sqlite.test.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db.storage-migration.test.ts`). Our earlier fixture change in the cutover test (4f6d8a833ce) is replaced by `main`'s stored version 6.
- CI on the first merge failed two of this PR's new tests and one existing e2e test:
  - `cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` and the guard test in `cli-run-transcript.test.ts` relied on runtime config being loaded on demand, which #169714 removed. Without config the persistence wrapper wrote no row, so both saw an empty transcript. Both now pass `config: {}`, as #169714 did for the neighbouring tests. Both fail on the new merge without that change and pass with it.
  - `cli-runner.fault-sequences.e2e.test.ts` › "dispatches bridge mode through one fresh CLI child and bypasses the native run budget" fails with "Runtime config is not prepared" on this head, and identically with all of this PR's source changes reverted (tests kept). It comes from `main`, not from this PR.
  - Left out of the local run: `session-cost-usage-cache.creation-race.test.ts`, new on `main`, fails on this Mac with "state … is undergoing offline maintenance", identically with this PR's source changes reverted.
- Test cost of the four added tests, from `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on an M-series laptop:
  - `cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` (new file): 2.2 s for the test, 11 s for the file. It runs the real runner and transcript store, because that is the only layer that proves the turn total is wired from the runner into the writer.
  - `transcript-persistence.test.ts`: 63 ms for the added test.
  - `session-transcript-readers.test.ts`: 144 ms for the added test.
  - `cli-run-transcript.test.ts`: 201 ms for the added test.
- Gates re-run on the merged head: `oxfmt --check` and oxlint on the changed files, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:core:test`, and the line-cap, assertion-safety and mock-export ratchets. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Gates last run before the merge of `main`: import cycles (0 runtime, 0 madge), dead-code exports, deprecated API usage, `lint:ui:i18n`, stylelint on the changed UI files, and the max-lines and test-timeout-race ratchets. The SQLite-worker ratchet last ran before the chat-display and pricing commits, which add no database code.
- The three regression tests moved out of `cli-runner.reliability.test.ts`, `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` and `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`, which are over the line cap and may not grow.
- Chat display and pricing follow-up:
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatContextUsageTests` passed 14 tests on the merged head; SwiftFormat and SwiftLint at the pinned versions report nothing on the changed files.
  - The added TypeScript tests take 0 to 2 ms each. Each new regression test fails with its source change reverted.
  - The iOS app target was built (Debug, simulator, reduced project without the watch app) for the screenshots above. Not run locally: the full OpenClawKit suite, the full iOS project and the macOS app build.

Live Claude Code semantics (stream-json, `--include-partial-messages`):
- A tool-using turn's `result` reported 77 output tokens, while its two `assistant` events carried 15 and 1.
- In one warm stdio process, each turn's `result.usage` covered only that turn (78 output tokens each time). Only `total_cost_usd` accumulates, so persisting `result` usage does not double count warm sessions.
  - Rechecked on Claude Code 2.1.293: two turns in one process reported cache writes of 28,094 and then 5,619, while `total_cost_usd` rose from 0.0057 to 0.0072.

## Upgrade and data compatibility

- **No schema, migration, or config change.** The persisted assistant `usage` keeps its existing shape. `contextUsage` is an existing optional field that the agent-command writer has persisted since #120497.
- **Existing records are untouched.** Older unmarked CLI records still hit the existing provenance barrier, so readers treat them exactly as before.
- **Old and new records mix safely in one session.** Accounting sums the counters, and context readers use the newest record's marker (proof turn 2 above ran in an existing session).
- **Upgrade.** Only turns recorded after the update carry turn totals, and nothing needs to run. Rolling back leaves new records readable, because their counters are ordinary usage fields.

## Related

- #148676 targets the same issue. Its current revision uses the same projection for both writers and the same reader change.
  - It also switches live `agentMeta.usage` to the turn total in `cli-run-settlement.ts`.
  - This PR leaves live `agentMeta.usage` on the last call.

Not in scope (possible follow-ups):
- `lastCallUsage` still takes its output count from the stream-start `assistant` event, because `readCliUsage` does not read `message_delta`. This only affects the small output side of the context marker.
- A run with several interim `result` events persists the last segment's total. That undercounts rather than double counts, and the behavior predates this change.
- Live `agentMeta.usage` for CLI runs (reply footer, session store counters, cron run records) still reflects the last call.
- Subscription dollar pricing (#102771).
- Turns whose reply goes out through the message tool, and room-event turns, write no CLI assistant row, so they still add nothing to `usage.cost`.
- Rows whose marker is `unavailable` (for example an aborted Codex turn) keep sizing context and choosing a tier from their counters, as on `main`.

AI-assisted (Claude Code).

prs.title: fix(codex): retain complete answers while previews are pending
prs.body:
Closes #139249

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex replies lose the end of their answer when a channel preview callback stalls. Even when Codex has supplied a complete final answer, terminal settlement could return only the earlier streamed prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep assistant-start, partial-reply, and reasoning presentation callbacks ordered in a projector-owned queue, independently of canonical native notifications. Finalization joins accepted presentation under the existing receipt-anchored settlement deadline and abort grace. Callback failures are isolated, and queued callbacks cannot start after cancellation or projection closure.

Media, transcript checkpoints, native plan persistence, and async-message delivery retain their existing awaited ownership. No new configuration, timeout, protocol, or storage changes.

## User Impact

Complete native answers remain available in the result and transcript projection even if presentation stalls. Settlement timeout and cancellation still release the run and retain their existing failure classification.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing stalled-presentation lifecycle reproduction on main `925fb0c3353ce98f1c8d6d1f2c27bbb8472af095`: before the fix, expected `Done. The complete answer survives pending presentation.` but received only `Done.`; the same regression passes with the repair.
- **106/106 tests passed** across `run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts`, `run-attempt.settlement.test.ts`, `event-projector.assistant.test.ts`, and `event-projector.reasoning.test.ts`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with those paths.
- Added coverage for callback ordering, captured reasoning snapshots, synchronous throws, rejected promises, and queued callbacks fenced after close/abort.
- After rebasing onto main `efa4b5dfbb3`, 8/8 targeted regressions passed, including blocked-delivery timeout and user-stop cases; `git range-diff` confirmed the patch was unchanged.
- Fresh autoreview: scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings. `git diff --check` and changed-file formatting passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 925fb0c3353ce98f1c8d6d1f2c27bbb8472af095` passed the preceding guards, plugin boundaries, and 5 doctor-contract tests, then stopped before typechecking: `Declaration input escapes checkout ... shared installs and external symlinks are unsupported.` The targeted lint wrapper hits the same dependency boundary. Full typecheck/lint and subsequent changed gates are unverified locally; they are not reported as green.
- Personally inspected pinned Codex `rust-v0.153.4` (`3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a`), `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1390-1420`: completion emits `last_agent_message` in the terminal summary.
- Production delta: +27 lines, needed for one ordered presentation owner, failure isolation, closure checks, and the bounded finalization join. Existing blocking presentation awaits removed. Tests counted separately.
- Proof boundary: deterministic app-server/run lifecycle tests; no live Telegram replay. This host has neither an authenticated Convex CLI nor the QA broker credential pair, so the Telegram Test Server lane is unavailable. Testbox/AWS Crabbox were not used.

Follow-up identified during sibling review: the separate `/btw` collector awaits its start callback in a detached delta handler; rejection and delayed-delta behavior without a terminal summary need separate investigation. It does not use this projector.

Maintainer edits are enabled; access through GitHub's maintainer workflow/secrets option is acceptable for this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the release-only Team-scale cold-load E2E (`ui/src/e2e/team-scale-cold-load.e2e.test.ts`) times out on every run because it waits for the Users section's collapse toggle, which #172243 removed.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Full Release Validation's `checks-ui-e2e` shard that carries this test (FRV child run 38662503008, job 116187236429, 2026.10.10-beta.1 candidate) goes green again.

## Why This Change Was Made

#172243 (`4fa4e7e8d6d`, "filter sidebar users by online status") replaced the collapsible `.sidebar-online .sidebar-session-group-toggle` header with an always-open list plus a presence filter, and dropped the matching unit-test selector. This test is in `RELEASE_ONLY_UI_TEST_FILES`, so PR and main CI never ran it, and it kept calling `getAttribute("aria-expanded")` on a toggle that no longer exists. Opening the Users rail now shows the list directly, so the test drops the toggle step. The 120-person assertion stays unchanged and still proves the full roster renders.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Release candidate `ca780561df3` (release/2026.10.10), unmodified | Fails deterministically: `locator.getAttribute: Timeout ... waiting for locator('openclaw-app-sidebar').locator('.sidebar-online .sidebar-session-group-toggle')`, the same signature as CI job 116187236429 |
| This branch (origin/main `95d09cc0b2d` + fix): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/team-scale-cold-load.e2e.test.ts` | 1/1 passed. The test body took 9.6s; the full invocation took 315s wall time locally, almost all of it the bundled preview build and transform |
| `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check` | pass |

The test file and `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-online.tsx` are unchanged between the release cut `459cad76530` and origin/main, so main fails the same way.
