prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid off-page ownership waits in session lists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a session sidebar refresh waiting on runtime ownership preparation for sessions outside the requested page.

## User Impact

A ready sidebar page can return while an unrelated session's native runtime is slow. Selected rows still wait for their current facts. Search and Board filters retain their full-inventory preparation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary list selection needs committed entry, lineage, and membership metadata. Full runtime facts belong to the selected page. Carry that distinction through initial selection and placement re-selection, while preserving initial model-catalog readiness and existing full-preparation callers.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `0b1fe4f10e10901940df9404c627db0ba95dd494`.
- [Baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674747439/job/116225990486) executed the real `sessions.list` regression at `42c96ef59aa`. It reached held off-page ownership before responding: `first: off-page ownership`, 0.698 ms to the gate. This proves an unnecessary dependency, not a measured multi-second production delay.
- [Repaired boundary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38675250852/job/116227955293) at `e5bd84761fa`: off-page response completed in **2.686 ms while ownership remained held**. Selected rows, search, and both Board filters still reached ownership first (0.818, 0.641, 0.306, 0.358 ms to the gate). All seven tests passed.
- Test file cost: baseline 30.90 s, repaired 35.97 s including cold transforms; repaired Vitest wrapper 38.44 s. Local dependency-backed tests were not run: the checkout is code-only and normal PR CI is the approved proof route.
- That run exposed two stale sibling expectations: unconditional off-page display materialization and the old selection options. `7f5acf95fb4` preserves the in-flight freshness and role-revocation assertions under the page-scoped contract.

Since heartbeat instructions migrated from the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` into the database monitor scratch (doctor imports the file, archives it under `backups/heartbeat-migration/`, and removes it — per `docs/gateway/heartbeat.md`), the runtime never reads `HEARTBEAT.md` anymore.

The skip reason is a machine-readable string that appears in run records and logs; anyone grepping for the old value will need to update. Happy to instead keep the old literal and only change display text if maintainers prefer strict log compatibility — but since the docs describe scratch semantics anyway, the clean rename seemed right.

prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline rises from 4031 to 4033 for `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (`outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:662`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:129-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI tested `cf49e1d3c83` merged with main `0858cc64613`. On that head 88 checks passed, none failed, 49 were skipped and CodeQL was neutral. In `checks-node-changed-1`, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` passed 20 tests, and the shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115. Locally at `cf49e1d3c83`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`, four ratchets and five generated-file check scripts passed, and `extension-feishu` passed 1256 tests.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.
- Regression tests for schema acceptance, account selection, off-mode finals, comment delivery, block posts, preview dedupe and presentation cards each failed before the fix and passed after.

prs.title: feat(agents): plugin-declared human-approval tools exempt from harness tool watchdogs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A tool that blocks in a `before_tool_call` hook waiting for a **human approval**
(e.g. a World ID / operator verification) can legitimately take minutes. Under
the **codex** harness, such a dynamic-tool call is killed by the per-call
watchdog (`CODEX_DYNAMIC_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS = 90s`) and the agent then retries the
tool — spawning duplicate approval prompts and a confusing, unusable HITL
experience. codex already exempts `ask_user`/`secrets` by **hardcoded tool
name**, which doesn't work for a pluggable approval system where any plugin can
gate any tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generalize the human-wait exemption from hardcoded names to a **plugin-owned,
contract-driven declaration**, so the host/harnesses never need editing when a
new plugin gates a new tool.

- New generic seam: `api.declareHumanApprovalTools({ tools, timeoutMs })` — a
  plugin declares which of its tools may block on a human approval and the
  longest wait it expects (typically from its own config; the host never reads
  plugin config directly).
- The registry aggregates declarations (longest budget per tool);
  `resolveHumanApprovalToolTimeoutMs(tool)` exposes the rollup to harnesses.
- codex's `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` consults it: a declared tool gets
  the human budget (clamped to the codex max), otherwise the default. An
  explicit per-call `timeoutMs` still wins; undeclared tools are unchanged.

Harness generality: the built-in `openclaw` and `copilot` harnesses impose no
per-tool-call watchdog, so they need no change and already wait up to the core
approval budget; the signal is available for any future watchdog.

## User Impact

- HITL-gated tools under codex are no longer killed mid-scan and retried, so no
  duplicate approval prompts — the human simply completes the approval.
- Fully pluggable: any plugin opts in by declaring its tools; no core/codex/host
  edits. Fully customizable: the budget is the plugin's own configured value.
- Fail-closed preserved: this aligns the watchdog with the approval budget; a
  human who never responds within that budget still times out.

## Evidence

- Verified against `../codex`: the app-server awaits the `DynamicToolCall`
  response with **no per-call execution deadline** (only a 1s cancellation-
  propagation test and unrelated infra timeouts; MCP `tool_timeout_sec` applies
  only to MCP servers), so extending OpenClaw's wrapper budget is sufficient.
- Unit tests: registry aggregation (longest budget wins, blank/non-positive
  ignored) in `registry.runtime-config.test.ts`; codex resolver precedence
  (declared tool → human budget; undeclared → default; explicit arg wins) in
  `dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts`. `pnpm build` green; SDK surface budget
  updated (+1 accessor); `$autoreview` scoped-clean (0.98).

prs.title: feat: let the agent request compaction itself (session_compact tool)
prs.body:
Closes #138083

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running assistant sessions that switch between unrelated topics carry the
finished topic's history until token pressure finally triggers compaction. The
model has no way to say "this discussion is done, archive it now," so context
budget is wasted and the eventual pressure-driven summary mixes unrelated
topics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a `session_compact` built-in tool that lets the model request compaction
of the current session, following the established `sessions_yield` pattern:
the tool records the request, the runtime owns execution.

Key design decisions:

- The tool is only offered when the runtime provides a compaction request
  receiver, so unsupported contexts never see a dead tool. Heartbeat turns do
  not install the receiver at all (they never execute agent compaction).
- Execution runs after the reply's delivery settlement — strictly later than
  the turn's deferred lifecycle completion, which releases the embedded
  active-run handle first (the manual pipeline rejects requests with
  `active_run` while the handle is still registered). Scheduling the work
  behind delivery keeps a non-streamed final reply from waiting on the whole
  summarization request. The run itself goes through the existing manual
  compaction pipeline (`trigger: "manual"`, `force`, focus passed as
  `customInstructions`), reusing lane queueing, checkpoints, hooks, quality
  guards, and provider/model overrides unchanged.
- A committed compaction is recorded through the same accounting owner as
  `/compact` (`incrementCompactionCount` with the committed successor entry as
  the writer fence), so finalization never persists the pre-summarization
  usage as the current context.
- The tool is registered in `CORE_TOOL_DEFINITIONS` under the `sessions`
  section with `coding`/`messaging` profiles and the OpenClaw group, so
  profile allowlists, `group:sessions`, and `group:openclaw` agree with
  runtime eligibility.
- No new config options, no SQLite schema changes, no new file storage: the
  summary lives in the session transcript as today, and full history stays on
  disk.

## User Impact

The agent can now proactively compact on topic shifts instead of only
reacting to context pressure. Behavior is the same contract as `/compact`:
recent turns are preserved, the summary is stored in the session transcript,
and the operator can always inspect the full on-disk history.

## Evidence

- New focused tests (`pnpm test` scope):
  - `src/agents/tools/session-compact-tool.test.ts` (4 tests): error paths
    without session context or runtime receiver, scheduling with and without
    focus, callback payload.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.agent-compaction.test.ts`
    (7 tests): manual-pipeline invocation with focus/force, committed-entry
    writer fence plus `incrementCompactionCount` accounting on success,
    accounting failure logged without throwing, no-op without a request,
    heartbeat skip, skip outcome and failure both non-fatal.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-agent-compaction.test.ts`
    (2 tests): drives a full `executeAgentTurn` with the real
    deferred-lifecycle manager and asserts the turn surfaces the recorded
    request on the settled outcome without running compaction in-turn (the
    finalize side owns execution, after delivery settlement).

    (3 tests): the scheduled compaction runs only after `ownerSettlement`

## What Problem This Solves

Immediate channel introductions and isolated webhook turns reuse the cron executor but are not stored automations. They currently reach the scheduled-job inference-account guard and can stop before inference or delivery. The Telegram join-introduction QA failure in #171524 reports that exact refusal after consuming the join update.

## User Impact

Immediate event turns use the ordinary configured account-resolution path again. Stored automations, including manual runs and event schedules, retain recorded-account enforcement and native-only CLI handling when unbound.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry a private, trusted caller classification through model routing and embedded/CLI admission. Only the immediate channel-join and hook producers select `event`; the Gateway stored-job service explicitly forces `cron`. The executor defaults to `cron` and never infers the classification from the payload, schedule, session key, missing binding or audit ingress.

Recorded inference bindings, runtime authority and currentness checks remain unconditional. Delivery restrictions, untrusted-content wrapping, join-introduction tool denial, unattended bootstrap and optional terminal replies are preserved. This adds no configuration, schema or public RPC selector. Canonical #172717 remains the owner of native CLI account handling; this does not replace its fix.

## Evidence

- Focused local proof: **162 distinct cases in seven files pass** — 42 auth/propagation/routing cases, 109 Gateway producer/lifecycle cases and 11 channel-introduction cases. The final nullable model-routing assertion also passes its three-case replay. Node24.16.0/macOS arm64, not hosted Linux24.19 evidence.
- Credential controls use the real preparation and stored-profile owners: configured direct credentials are refused for an unbound scheduled job and admitted for an immediate event; scheduled CLI profile adoption is refused, ordinary event CLI forwarding selects the exact configured profile, and recorded bindings refuse incompatible CLI routes under both classifications.
- Negative control against unchanged035 production: the event execution, event model-routing and event CLI forwarding cases fail, while all five default/scheduled controls pass (27 unrelated cases filtered). Only production was reverted; exact candidate source is restored. This is local causal proof, not a hosted inheritance classification.
- Strict production and selected-test types, typed lint, formatting and whitespace pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. A subsequent nullable test-access typing correction preserves the same nonempty trigger assertion and has passing current checks; production is unchanged from that review.
- Initial local attempts selected the wrong owner for a database-backed channel test or stopped during cold test startup; corrected maintained routing and prepared compilation pass. New fixture assumptions about model materialization, routing projection location and a missing CLI mock result were corrected before final proof. These are not CI failures or passing baseline claims.
- Local real-Gateway Telegram setup was stopped during a long build before runtime; no local Telegram E2E pass is claimed. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad Linux proof. The prior feature failure table remains `unknown`/no matching main job, not a hosted signature match.

Related #172590 and #171524. No assertion, delivery requirement, account ownership check, retry or case deadline is weakened. The feature PR remains unmerged with auto-merge off.

prs.title: fix(native-session): keep binding lease wait deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `src/agents/harness/native-session/binding-leases.ts`, the `transact()` loop measured its lease-acquisition **wait budget on the wall clock**:

```ts
const deadline = Date.now() + options.lease.waitMs; // seeded once, outside the loop
while (true) {
  ...
  await update(key, ...);        // multiple await ticks
  ...
  if (Date.now() >= deadline) {  // re-read wall clock every iteration
    throw options.errors.leaseTimeout(key);
  }
  await sleep(options.lease.retryIntervalMs); // monotonic setTimeout
}
```

The deadline is seeded with `Date.now()` and then re-read as `Date.now() >= deadline` on every iteration, which crosses several real `await` ticks (the atomic `update` and the `sleep`). Because the budget is measured on the wall clock across asynchronous ticks, an NTP/system clock adjustment distorts it:

- **Clock rollback** → `Date.now()` reads low every iteration, so the loop keeps sleeping and the wait stretches *past* the configured `waitMs` (binding acquisition hangs).
- **Clock jump forward** → `Date.now()` trips the deadline early, throwing `leaseTimeout` and **killing a healthy acquisition** that should have succeeded.

This is the same wall-clock-remaining-budget defect family already fixed elsewhere in the harness (`attempt-deadlines.ts`, `queue-helpers.ts`), and it ships for plugin native-session bindings where `waitMs` is 70s (Codex app-server `CODEX_APP_SERVER_BINDING_LEASE.waitMs = 70_000`, Agents API `agentsapi-bindings.ts`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The relative wait budget `waitMs` is a duration, not an absolute epoch, so it must be measured on a monotonic clock. `performance.now()` is unaffected by wall-clock adjustments, so seeding and consuming the deadline with it keeps the budget accurate no matter how the system clock jumps.

The in-repo harness already uses `performance.now()` as the monotonic accessor for exactly this purpose (`src/agents/harness/attempt-deadlines.ts`, `src/utils/queue-helpers.ts`), so this aligns with the established precedent.

Only the budget deadline was moved to `performance.now()`. The lease-expiry TTL checks inside the loop (`lease.expiresAt <= Date.now()`) were deliberately left on `Date.now()`: those compare cross-process lease epochs written by other workers/processes and must stay on the wall clock.

## User Impact

Users of plugin native-session bindings (Codex app-server sessions, Agents API bindings, conversation/thread-bindings session runtimes) can hit:

- **Hangs**: under a wall-clock rollback, a lease acquisition waits longer than its configured 70s budget before timing out.
- **Spurious failures**: under a wall-clock forward jump, a healthy concurrent binding acquisition is rejected with `leaseTimeout`, failing an operation that should have succeeded.

After the fix, the wait budget behaves deterministically regardless of system clock adjustments.

## Evidence

- The deadline is seeded at `binding-leases.ts:164` (`const deadline = Date.now() + options.lease.waitMs;`) outside the `while (true)` loop and consumed at `:223` (`if (Date.now() >= deadline)`) inside it, with `await update(...)` and `await sleep(options.lease.retryIntervalMs)` (`:226`, which routes to `src/utils/sleep.ts` `setTimeout`) between ticks — a genuine cross-tick wall-clock budget.
- `sleep()` (`src/utils/sleep.ts:19`) uses `setTimeout`, i.e. monotonic timing, so the only wall-clock measurement of the budget is the `Date.now()` seed/consume pair, which is exactly what this PR replaces.
- `performance.now()` is used as the global monotonic accessor in the same harness module tree (`src/agents/harness/attempt-deadlines.ts:40,49`), so no new import or dependency is introduced.
- Typecheck passes (`tsc --noEmit`): no errors reported for `binding-leases.ts`.
- The pre-commit formatter (oxfmt) reports the file as correctly formatted.
- `binding-leases.ts` was introduced by #165044 (2026-10-04); the bug is not covered by any existing tracked fix in the codebase.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare recorded Decision answers offline
prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

## Evidence

prs.title: perf(trajectory): reuse committed runtime window facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trajectory appends reread their retained sequence and byte count even when the same Gateway writer already knows those facts. Empty-conversation token resets also prepare a session snapshot for a patch that does not depend on its contents.

## User Impact

This is an internal storage optimization with no intended user-visible change. Event ordering, byte limits, crash recovery, and destructive-cleanup lease-loss aborts remain intact. No schema migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The trajectory owner retains the last session's next sequence and retained UTF-8 byte count per physical execution owner. The existing append command consumes those facts inside the writer FIFO and returns the committed facts before the FIFO is released. Lifecycle receipts and retention invalidate them. Cold appends and actual overflow keep the SQL-side size projection and bounded suffix scan; this change does not replace that projection with full event payloads.

The token reset uses the existing closed `fields` operation, merging its fixed patch against the current row inside the writer command. Its prepared target and source-authority guard remain in place.

Accepted edges for removed work:

- The ordinary trajectory window reread is skipped when committed facts prove the append is under budget. Switching the recent session, reopening the owner, or invalidation makes the next append cold; exclusive offline repairs remain outside the runtime owner's lifetime.
- Facts are consumed before an append is awaited. A lost or unknown result leaves the next append cold; a retention sweep may also cause a cold read even when it deletes nothing.
- Unsupported unnotified orphan deletion may leave a sequence gap or trigger an extra overflow read; supported lifecycle and offline repair paths publish invalidation or retire the owner.
- The constant token reset no longer prepares a detached snapshot or performs its generic CAS. Unrelated metadata changes merge into the current row instead of rejecting the reset; real source closure still blocks the effect.

## Evidence

Candidate `6575a825f984e412e53f04b13db6d8d3729abaf9`, measurement base `a4d316dc86846952cc2ddd99df026c771ab38900`. Current main was integrated without conflicts. Changed-file formatting, basic oxlint and diff sanity pass. Two isolated Codex review rounds found no accepted P0–P2 issues; the later test-only trigger-admission correction was directly inspected and its formerly failing case passed locally and in final-head CI.

Final-head [PR CI run 38676159695](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38676159695) checks candidate merged into `bf1a8406d59ec04d55be379728817ac4c266f9e5`, merge ref `231ddbe799b282358d62bb55ca79e9ca4ee0731e`. All selected behavior tests, production/test types, typed lint, source contracts/export collisions, boundaries, docs, build and ratchets passed. Madge and Kysely checks passed.

The exact-head [Knip dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38676203783/job/116230683614) reports the same 20 findings as [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672095119/job/116217606122): identical scan/file/symbol tuples, no new or touched-file finding. Both unused-file scans and the script-export scan pass. This uses the authorized inherited-static-failure exception.

Final-head behavior proof: trajectory writer 14 cases, SQLite store 30, SQLite retention 21, retention owner 3, runtime 23, tool definitions 7, and normalization 20 all pass. The new regressions cover committed sequence/byte facts, Unicode budgets, actual overflow, oversized newest-event reset, lifecycle deletion, metadata receipts, and lost-result settlement. Existing cleanup authority and lease-loss aborts remain covered. The bootstrap regression proves the prepared target and source guard; it is not itself SQLite persistence proof.

Two CI defects were repaired: a new test initially passed an object to a callback API, and the existing rollback fixture installed its SQLite trigger outside the writer FIFO. CREATE/open and DROP now use separate writer-admission callbacks; the tested append and assertions remain outside them. No retries, timeouts or weakened assertions were added. One Knip dispatch was rejected before validation because its invocation used a short SHA; the linked replacement uses the full SHA.

Touched-area T1: **0 → 0**. Repository T1 **223 → 223**, deprecated-only **12 → 12**; changed dialect categories **0 → 0**. Madge reports **0 cycles** and Kysely guardrails pass. The SDK surface and update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle paths are unchanged; no SDK API diff or published-driver update cell is required by this scope.

Three alternating base/candidate harness pairs are queued and will be reported after landing under the campaign's measure-after-merge rule. No measured warmed-turn reduction is claimed yet. The source-level expectation is one fewer trajectory window SELECT per resident under-budget append, with unchanged trajectory request count. The token-reset reduction concerns a cold recovery path. No wall-time claim will be made on this loaded host.

| Warmed-turn metric | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All-thread SQL statements | Pending measurement | Pending measurement |
| Worker requests | Pending measurement | Pending measurement |
| MAIN-thread SQL statements | Pending measurement | Pending measurement |

The measured report will also attribute trajectory window reads and requests, exact-entry facts, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshots, row facts and watermark reads, including whole-workload totals.

prs.title: fix(agent): finalize settled turns when harness callback is absent
prs.body:
## Summary

- route a genuinely absent settled-turn finalizer into the existing deterministic host fallback
- preserve the finalizer-available truncated-stream recovery merged in #140367
- preserve deliberate silence, terminal errors, detached isolation, cancellation authority, and no-replay semantics
- prove the persistence/delivery boundary through real SQLite and `dispatchReplyFromConfig`

## What Problem This Solves

Codex can complete a turn after tool side effects without emitting a final assistant message. Current `main` recovers this when a tool-free finalizer is available, including truncated completion streams after commentary. A distinct gap remained when the selected harness exposed no `finalizeSettledTurn` callback: OpenClaw returned `not-attempted` before reaching its existing safe host fallback.

This refresh keeps the merged available-finalizer behavior and removes only that stale availability precondition.

## Why Each Change Exists

- **Request resolution:** removes the precondition so an absent callback reaches the existing host-owned fallback; terminal assistant errors remain excluded.
- **Persistence fencing:** detached sessions never append a transcript; superseded writers and unresolved targets still fail closed.
- **Cancellation boundary:** cancellation before persistence suppresses the outcome; after a successful append, the committed idempotency key remains authoritative so durable state and delivery cannot disagree.
- **Tests:** true callback absence, not merely a throwing callback, proves durable, detached, pre-append, and post-append behavior. The integration matrix crosses real SQLite and the production reply dispatcher.
- **Documentation:** states the optional-callback and pre/post-commit contracts without suggesting tool replay.

## User Impact

A settled tool turn no longer ends silently merely because its harness omits the optional finalizer. OpenClaw emits the deterministic no-model fallback once, while preserving deliberate silence, failure-honest terminal errors, detached non-persistence, and cancellation semantics.

## Evidence

- exact head: `601c46ccf71224c6a5b20c6040009cd4e19fbc35`
- real SQLite → source dispatcher integration: 19/19
- related settled-finalization and terminal-resolution matrix: 85/85
- combined fresh local run: 123/123 across five requested test files
- `pnpm check:changed`: exit 0
- `pnpm build`: exit 0
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: exit 0
- independent Cursor review on exact head: `NO_MATERIAL_FINDINGS`
- Codex protocol inspected directly: `item/completed` applies item-side effects separately; `turn/completed` may contain no loaded assistant items
- current-main relation: #140367 / `04081aa1361d6a4097d0b489126a737481220f53` is preserved and remains an ancestor

## Scope and Risk

- no configuration, migration, provider, or tool-execution change
- no model/tool/attempt replay
- production change remains concentrated in terminal request resolution and fallback persistence
- added test-support module only keeps the real integration harness within repository size limits

prs.title: fix(ui): keep agent switching responsive with self-parented Home
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #172744: the Control UI sidebar can crash and stop agent switching when the canonical Home session points to itself as its parent.

## User Impact

Home navigation, child conversations, and agent switching remain usable with self-parented Home lineage or with no Home session loaded. There is no visual redesign, configuration change, or data migration. The reporter's exact stored lineage has not been replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Home is a navigation root regardless of its persisted ancestry. Marking the scoped Home input with the existing `sidebarRoot` presentation flag prevents the generic tree filter from dropping it, while preserving child discovery and hidden-worker summaries. The ordinary-session candidate producer also excludes Home before both categorization and child promotion, preventing a self-parent edge from adding Home back among roots and hiding its children. Stored lineage and ordinary session placement retain their existing owners. Absent Home rows are already explicitly handled by the consumers; this fixes the producer rather than hiding its broken result with optional chaining.

Original fix by @ericcaiwx-star; maintainer cleanup consolidates the rationale, checks rendered children and shared agent selection in both sidebar modes, adds the absent-Home control, and documents the navigation contract. Contributor history is preserved, with Eric Cai credited in the cleanup commit.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation on `origin/main` at `6866eac64e4b`: the Home input lacks `sidebarRoot`; the generic tree filters its self-parent link and the caller assumes a first result. Related #172684, #172575, and #172618 are merged but do not repair this path. Collision checks before work and before push found no competing fix.
- PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. Exact-head CI is pending; it covers the UI regressions and CI-selected build, lint, type, and test lanes. No local tests, typechecks, negative controls, live Gateway proofs, or Crabbox/Testbox leases were run. Live proof was intentionally skipped per maintainer policy.
- Regression file: `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.home-projection.browser.test.ts`. Cases: `keeps self-parented Home navigable with child discovery in chip mode`, the equivalent `roster mode` case, and `keeps agent switching available without a Home session`. These mount the real sidebar with the existing mocked Gateway fixture and exercise the agent menu. The fixture does not persist agent identity, so this is not reload-persistence proof.
- Changed-file oxfmt passed (3 files, 412 ms). Static core oxlint passed (2 TypeScript files, 231 rules, zero diagnostics, 0.665 s). The wrapper could not load the parent install's missing Solid plugin; the temporary core config omits only the `ui/**/*.tsx` override, which matches neither changed TypeScript file. No applicable rules or repository config were changed. `git diff --check` passed.
- First CI: [run 38675050009, UI job 116227329275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38675050009/job/116227329275) failed only the two new rendered-child assertions; 32 jobs passed. Source tracing identified Home being promoted as its own child. This is repaired in the shared candidate producer; no assertion or timeout was weakened. This failure is change-related, not attributed to main.
- Second CI: [run 38676183538, UI job 116230559692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38676183538/job/116230559692) passed the production repair but failed the final roster-to-chip DOM assertion. The fixture had changed the host mode directly while its preference subscriber still tracked chip mode. Setup now uses the real preference owner; the DOM and shared-selection assertions are unchanged.
- Deslop complete. Fresh isolated Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, no actionable findings. The current-main merge left the reviewed sidebar patch unchanged.
- ClawSweeper currently has only acknowledgment comment `6183398659`; there are no substantive bot or human findings to resolve. Further P0–P2 code findings will be handled; PR CI is the proof per maintainer policy.
- Exact numstat versus merged `origin/main`: production **+4/-4 (net 0)**; tests **+78/-0**; docs **+2/-0**. Three browser cases reuse the existing fixture with no added timers or polling. The first CI run exposed the missing ordinary-root exclusion through both rendered-child assertions; the absent-Home switching case passed (658 ms). Both assertions are retained. The second run passed the complete chip case (1332 ms), the absent-Home case (337 ms), and both rendered-child checks. Its remaining roster assertion exposed a fixture preference mismatch; mode setup now uses `patchSettings` instead of bypassing the preference owner. Final runtime/test wall time awaits the corrected fixture head.
- No detached, background, cleanup, or deferred side effects are added. No screenshots are needed for this crash-only change.

prs.title: feat(state): select the shared-state database engine from config
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`database.engine: "postgres"` currently leaves Gateway shared state on SQLite. Resolve the configured engine before the first shared-state read, so a fresh Gateway uses PostgreSQL consistently from preflight through runtime.

**Two main-latent fixes, independent of engine selection:**

- **Config-reloader readiness:** R1's boot timing exposed startup reconciliation that could finish after Gateway readiness. Readiness now joins initial watcher setup/reconciliation, already-queued file-stability work, and resulting scheduled reloads. The existing scheduler, debounce/retry behavior, and session-event authority checks remain intact.
- **Same-value runtime publication:** A provider-auth refresh could replace the runtime config and metadata identities despite suppressing the corresponding session-change event. That invalidated a pending first `/hooks/wake` and returned HTTP 503 before an intentional reload. The publisher now treats exactly that existing suppression condition as a full no-op: it keeps the config/source/metadata identities, revision, and cache state and emits nothing. Actual content/provenance changes and existing same-object invalidation remain distinct; auth refresh order is unchanged.

## User Impact

SQLite remains the default. Existing installations with an unset or SQLite engine keep their current startup and data behavior; this change does not migrate data during an update or configuration change.

This is an intermediate implementation behind the existing experimental gate: shared state and workboard can use PostgreSQL, but **agent databases, including transcripts and agent memory, remain on SQLite**. Existing SQLite shared state refuses a PostgreSQL selection and names `openclaw database port`; that command currently supports workboard only, so shared-state porting remains a prerequisite for switching an existing installation. Use a fresh state directory for this experimental shared-state path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host resolves an env/file/exec connection SecretRef from the core-only config snapshot before shared-state access. One immutable engine input then follows config preflight, direct server/bootstrap entry points, reader contexts, writer admission/registry, and lease heartbeat workers. Store-backed connection references remain forbidden, and connection/admission failures never fall back to SQLite. PostgreSQL startup inspection uses admitted worker reads instead of treating its SQLite identity anchor as application data.

The existing state owner and synchronous boot-admission exception retain ownership of opens, transactions, and cleanup. Agent database openers are unchanged.

The startup device-identity presence check awaits the existing shared-state identity worker. Persisted identities therefore do not reopen PostgreSQL on the Gateway main thread after restart. Synchronous ownership contracts stay independent of read dispatch; asynchronous ownership preflight lives in its own module, with its callers and test mocks migrated together. Test fixtures accept the engine connection contract without changing their behavior.

The PostgreSQL bridge now constructs its client inside the handled connect request. Malformed connection URLs previously threw before the worker installed its request handler, so the synchronous host received neither a reply nor an Atomics notification and waited for its 120-second deadline. Constructor, connection-refusal, authentication, and connection-setup failures now return a correlated `PostgresConnectionError` with guidance to check `database.postgres.connection`, network, and credentials. The 60-second connection timeout is unchanged. An in-suite regression checks the real host connection and a bound below the bridge deadline.

The readiness barrier remains at the config reloader owner. It waits for watcher reloads through their existing scheduler and does not join plugin lifecycle operations that themselves await readiness. Shutdown wakes the barrier before awaiting it. Recorded file-observation errors retain the existing best-effort retry behavior. Duplicate-dispatch tests now use an explicit runner-entry signal instead of racing a two-second poll against ordinary admission. The regression holds the initial source read, makes a formatting-only source edit, and checks that the first hook after readiness returns 200 and completes.

## Immutable boot selection

The database engine is a process-lifetime fact. Gateway boot, embedded kernels, and CLI state preflight install the host-resolved selection before state admission. Equal installations are idempotent; a conflicting engine, connection, or schema prefix is refused with restart guidance and without exposing the connection value.

This replaces the engine's `AsyncLocalStorage` entirely. The whole-Gateway wrapper and the special close binding are gone, so engine selection cannot replay or propagate unrelated startup contexts through config watchers, hooks, health, or store scheduling. Read workers, the writer broker, and lease-heartbeat workers install the resolved input sent by the host. Generic agent-worker contexts also capture that input for any shared-state access; agent databases remain SQLite. Redundant per-cache engine comparisons are removed.

Interrupted database-port manifests are checked before engine installation. Store-backed SecretRefs remain refused. Tests can reset the selection only through a test-support module after closing their state owners.

## Runtime publication audit

The runtime snapshot revision is an internal cache/authority token, not a public API or SDK contract.

`resolveRuntimeConfigCacheKey` retains `runtime:${revision}:${fingerprint}` across an existing no-op, avoiding unnecessary invalidation in agent/model policy, descriptor, project, web-fetch, MCP-auth, and Gateway metadata/approval caches. Model projections also retain their canonical cache key.

Provider-auth activation still updates credential state and its own secrets revision; only the identical runtime-config publication is skipped. Runtime `*IfCurrent` callers and secrets activation guards compare captured authority with current authority. An unchanged publication can keep the same revision; changed content/provenance still invalidates the old comparison. Config-write completion uses application receipts/applied-revision notifications independently of runtime metadata.

No runtime code or test-only waiter was found that awaits a runtime metadata revision/cache-key increase as a refresh-completion signal. No waiter was changed. Test expectation updates are confined to `runtime-snapshot.test.ts` (identity/revision and source-only cache behavior), `runtime-snapshot-value-fact.test.ts` (canonical fleet/model-cache reuse), and `session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts` (source-only no-ops). `cli-metadata-lifetime.test.ts` now publishes actual runtime plugin-enablement content when proving discovery invalidation.

## Evidence

- Runtime snapshot suites: 61/61 passing. Both deterministic regressions were proven against negative controls: removing the readiness barrier fails the early-ready assertion; restoring the old publisher makes the pending-auth-refresh hook return HTTP 503 (`Session event configuration changed`).
- SQLite capture: all 88 statements match the previous capture byte-for-byte (cold 46, restart 36, write 3, read 3, close 0).
- Format, core typecheck, type-aware lint, Madge (zero cycles), line-cap, database-dialect, timeout-race, assertion-safety and mock-export checks pass. Max-lines suppressions pass at 534; its wrapper reports the inherited environment-count budget failure (455 > 454), with no new environment variables in this delta. The full-tree database-worker scan exceeded 15 minutes locally and was stopped; exact-head CI remains the required evidence for it.
- One final isolated Codex autoreview of the combined delta: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Local limitations are preserved rather than hidden by replay: a full secrets-runtime run passed 311 cases and timed out in the managed-local-embedding case; that case passed a focused recheck without source or timeout changes. An earlier full hooks run passed nine cases and timed out only in the cold initial-reconcile regression; the same regression also passed with diagnostic markers that have been removed. Five RPC-deadline failures in the two broad plugin-lifecycle suites remain unexplained; the readiness-cycle audit found no cycle. Those suites and the remaining broad checks are assigned to exact-head CI. Host load was over 100 on 32 logical CPUs during these runs.

The current focused owner run has passed eight Gateway files (265 tests, including both health/store cases), the worker-context file (3 tests), and config-source observation (10 tests). CLI metadata and two full hooks-admission repeats remain in progress. Exact-head CI results will be recorded after the pushed commit completes its required jobs.

prs.title: fix(daemon): avoid argument-quoting scalar paths in WorkingDirectory and EnvironmentFile (#137747)
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #137747. Renders \`WorkingDirectory=\` and \`EnvironmentFile=\` as literal scalar paths rather than wrapping paths containing whitespace in argument quotes.

## Root Cause
In \`src/daemon/systemd-unit.ts\`, both \`WorkingDirectory\` and \`EnvironmentFile\` entries were processed through \`systemdEscapeArg()\`. While arguments in \`ExecStart=\` and inline assignments in \`Environment=\` use argv/token quoting, \`WorkingDirectory=\` and \`EnvironmentFile=\` are parsed by systemd (\`config_parse_working_directory\` and \`config_parse_unit_env_file\`) as scalar pathnames without stripping surrounding double-quotes.

Consequently, when a working directory path contained spaces (e.g. \`/run/ocqa/cwd/space dir\`), the generated directive \`WorkingDirectory="/run/ocqa/cwd/space dir"\` caused systemd to report \`LoadState=bad-setting\` and fail startup. Similarly, an \`EnvironmentFile\` with spaces was quoted, causing systemd to silently ignore the file.

## Proposed Changes
- In \`src/daemon/systemd-unit.ts\`:
  - Directly render \`WorkingDirectory=${workingDirectory.trim()}\` and assert no CR/LF characters, omitting the \`systemdEscapeArg\` wrapper.
  - Directly render \`EnvironmentFile=-${entry.trim()}\` without \`systemdEscapeArg\`.
- In \`src/daemon/systemd-unit.test.ts\`:
  - Add unit test verifying that paths with spaces are preserved literally without quotes.

## Verification
- Ran \`pnpm vitest run src/daemon/systemd-unit.test.ts\` (26 passed).

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the error message in stack diagnostics under Bun
prs.body:
## Problem

`src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts > default error diagnostics > calls exit(1) via injected exit hook when resolveVersion rejects` failed only in the Bun shard of an extended-stable 2026.9.33 Full Release Validation CI run ([job 116175762356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659000655/job/116175762356), shard `bun:core-unit-fast-isolated`):

```
AssertionError: expected '[openclaw] Failed to resolve version:…' to contain 'version resolution failed'
+ [openclaw] Failed to resolve version: Error
+     at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)
```

The Node shard in the same job passed the same test, and other FRV runs passed it under Bun.

## Root cause

This is a product formatting defect that the test exposed. The version fast-path failure reporter (`src/entry.version-fast-path.ts`) and `formatUncaughtError` (`src/infra/errors.ts`) print `error.stack ?? error.message`, which assumes V8's `Name: message` stack header. Bun can create `stack` during garbage collection, after the code that threw is gone. A stack created that way has a bare `Error` header and no message. `message` itself is still intact.

Standalone proof with Bun 1.4.2:

```js
const errs = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) errs.push(new Function("return new Error('version resolution failed " + i + "')")());
for (let k = 0; k < 5; k++) Bun.gc(true);
// 200/200 stacks start with "Error\n    at anonymous (...)"; errs[0].message === "version resolution failed 0"
```

GC timing decides whether that happens, which is why only some Bun runs failed. When it does, users running under Bun see a version-resolution or uncaught-error diagnostic that never says what failed.

## Solution

- Add `formatErrorStackWithMessage(error)` to `@openclaw/normalization-core/error-coercion`. It returns the stack unchanged when the stack already contains the message. Otherwise it swaps a bare name header for `Name: message`, or puts that header in front of a stack that has none. It falls back to the message or name when there is no stack.
- Route the version fast path and `formatUncaughtError` through it, and register the helper with the coercion-helper declaration guard.

Other `err.stack ?? err.message` call sites (hooks discovery, diagnostic events, main-session restart dispatch, unhandled rejections) have the same assumption. They are left for a follow-up to keep this backport small.

## Evidence

- Regression: the existing fast-path failure cases now throw an error whose `stack` has the shape Bun produces (`"Error\n    at …"`). Before the fix, both the pretty and JSON cases fail on Node with the exact CI output (`Failed to resolve version: Error\n    at resolveCommitHash …`). After the fix, they pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts src/infra/errors.test.ts packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.test.ts test/scripts/check-coercion-helper-declarations.test.ts`: all pass.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts`: passes (local Bun 1.4.2).
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `pnpm check:coercion-helpers`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the touched files.

## Test cost

No new tests. Only the error fixture in two existing cases changed. The file's tests take about 20 ms; `--maxWorkers=1` wall time is dominated by the shared compiled-worker preparation, which is unchanged.

Conditional backport candidate for extended-stable/2026.9.33. The cherry-pick conflicts only in `src/entry.version-fast-path.ts` and its test, because 2026.9.33 still has the injected-deps version of that file. The resolution is a one-line `detail` swap plus the same stack-shaped fixture in the `resolveVersion` rejection case. With that resolution, the tests pass on 2026.9.33.

`check:changed` passes everything except two failures that already exist on `origin/main` (base `17bea1c022a`) and involve no touched file: the `OPENCLAW_*` env-var count budget (455 > 454) and Knip unused exports in unrelated modules (`AuthProfileAuthorizationError`, `rememberNativeRuntimeConsent`, …).

prs.title: fix(feishu): restore responsive streaming feedback for long tasks
prs.body:
Related: #91941
Related: #108265

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Feishu replies stay blank before model output, slow CardKit writes delay the answer, and a five-minute chat watchdog lets later messages overtake explicitly longer tasks.

## User Impact

Streaming users receive a processing receipt and the complete answer on the same card, with agent/model/provider attribution and elapsed feedback. Later previews are paced at five seconds; finalization bypasses that wait. Configured long-task budgets apply at task start, including after config reloads. Denied and message-tool-only delivery create no early card.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** this proposes automatic receipts and elapsed feedback for existing Feishu streaming settings, plus one optional public callback. Pacing and queue-budget repairs can be separated if maintainers prefer that scope first. This PR does not claim to resolve every client-rendering latency report in #91941.

## Why This Change Was Made

The merged snapshot-coalescing fix in #166610 remains intact. The existing streaming session owns CardKit serialization, accepted answer content, finalization and timer cleanup. The optional `onPreviewStart` callback supplies feedback after core run admission under preview/send policy; execution callbacks keep synchronous completion ownership.

Provider omission in the original submission came from a local display preference. Follow-up `bfa747f405cdec5419b83dac50413f59448c78c0` restores the established agent/model/provider attribution for upstream. It also fixes a denial bypass exposed by the combined proof: the old partial-preview path could create a card even when core reported `sendPolicyDenied`. The shared preview/progress owner now checks that denial before any callback is forwarded.

The author's original measured reports are [the latency follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108265#issuecomment-5188113342) and [the CardKit investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108265#issuecomment-5189157959). #108265 was consolidated into #91941.

### Contract and scope

- `onPreviewStart` is optional. It does not grant authority, represent accepted answer content, settle a final receipt, or replace `onPreparedAgentRunStart`. Repeated invocation reuses the active preview. Denied/aborted/message-tool-only delivery cannot use it; channels without it retain existing behavior. Feishu also disables early previews when message hooks can rewrite or suppress delivery, when streaming is off, or with raw rendering.
- Body previews and elapsed updates share the session's serialized CardKit queue. The first answer replaces the receipt. Empty silent replies discard the receipt; feedback/token errors remain best effort and cannot prevent authoritative finalization.
- The watchdog uses `max(300 seconds, configured agent budget + one account HTTP request timeout)` and reads configuration when each task starts. Unconfigured tasks retain 300 seconds; `0` uses the existing safe timer maximum. Expiry releases ordering without cancelling the original task. Multiple HTTP requests, media, token renewal or model fallbacks can exceed that grace; complete final delivery is not guaranteed within it.
- No new config key, stored-state format or migration is introduced. A saved canonical `timeoutSeconds: 600`, partial-streaming/card configuration remains unmodified through candidate admission and delivery. Relevant keys already exist in [v2026.10.3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1); this compatibility proof does not establish a binary updater run.

## CI repair and attachment cleanup

Latest repair commit: `f167f0113189a0f222c78194f4d0ea026c7a4527`.

The completed CI run `38528165522` for `0a713fbf23867924a17befa2b4e1e991ae60e88e` passed its test shards and failed only `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (`115733877738`). The detailed log identifies `src/process/terminal-pty.test.ts:40`, not a Feishu assertion. CI checked merge tree `b3df1bdb63ec6b9d5926aafe726eb20dc1ec1e9c` against main `d07bd8b6ad7bba7832d9edc7b4f9a8dcdca8f683`. That tree incorporates main's `97e2332b` repair, which deliberately isolates the real Node PTY helper from synthetic Bun/platform fixtures but omitted the required isolation annotation. The follow-up preserves that repair and adds a precise `mock-isolation` reason. The scanner correctly rejects the recorded unannotated CI factory and accepts the fixed one. No scanner policy, baseline expansion, skip or retry is used.

The late attachment-only finding is also fixed at the existing streaming close owner: when media is already accepted and no answer text remains, discard the unused receipt. A nonempty accepted preview stays on its card, and the attachment's receipt remains authoritative. Three native SDK/HTTPS cases reproduce the problem for image/file-only replies before the fix, and cover preserving an accepted preview. Post-receipt model selection and real silent cleanup in the same core/TLS suite replace the two redundant mocked-session cases.

Current follow-up validation:

- Core/native HTTPS composition: **9/9 pass** under Node 24.21.0 (117.80 s cold launcher). Before the repair, the image-only and file-only scenarios failed only the missing receipt deletion; attachment sends and receipts had succeeded. Accepted-preview plus attachment was a passing control.
- PTY: **12 pass, 5 existing platform skips**; Feishu dispatcher, delivery traces and feedback siblings: **107/107 pass** (73.22 s combined launcher). No test expectations or final-write error handling were weakened.
- Mock export ratchet on Node 24.21.0: passes with **9616** grandfathered factories; timeout-race ratchet passes. The baseline is unchanged.
- Targeted production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, MDX, extension boundary and packaged Feishu runtime build pass. New-head CI remains pending until this push is checked. Independent source review found no additional P0–P2 issue. The CLI autoreview attempt for this fix again timed out after 300 seconds with no valid report; it is recorded as unavailable.

## Evidence

Latest head `0a713fbf23867924a17befa2b4e1e991ae60e88e` integrates main at `142ec158b52786970f4945c9e9a4ab4e9cac07e0` to resolve the queue conflict. It retains main’s rejected-final static fallback and recovery deduplication, along with the configured watchdog callback. The private queue option is now callback-only; the removed numeric/unbounded compatibility machinery and throwing-logger suppression remain removed, consistent with #171606.

After integration, 153 unaffected Feishu assertions passed; the one old final-429 assertion was updated to require both the preserved preview and main’s complete static final reply. Corrected trace/queue/config coverage is 25/25 (23.92 s launcher); merged core dispatch is 146/146 and the combined HTTPS path is 6/6 (133.46 s across two launch shards). Merged Feishu production/test typechecks, core/Feishu type-aware lint, formatting, MDX, boundary and ratchet checks pass. Feishu runtime and unified core builds pass. New-head CI is pending.

Earlier results and live API captures below apply to `bfa747f405cdec5419b83dac50413f59448c78c0` before main integration; they are supporting prior-head evidence. No new-head live Gateway/client or binary-upgrade capture is claimed.

- **Combined submitted path:** public `dispatchChannelInboundTurn` → core admission/visibility → actual Feishu reply dispatcher → native Lark SDK/CardKit HTTPS. Six cases pass: two delayed-write/backlog controls plus automatic, denied, message-tool-only and silent delivery. Real core records/session admission run in the repository's existing database-worker test project. Only model output and loopback server responses are synthetic. Test body 4.72 s; cold launcher 62.46 s.
- **Regression fixes:** 99/99 pass across `delivery-trace.test.ts`, `monitor.message-handler.timeout.test.ts` and `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` (60.88 s launcher). The original PR CI's six Feishu trace failures were reproduced locally (24.00 s): intentional receipt/cadence/first-element replacement changed four goldens and one old endpoint assertion; the 300 ms rate-limit script hit final delivery under the new cadence, and the fixture missed a finalization observer. Channel-specific pacing, joined settlements, regenerated traces and independent preview/final 429 assertions repair those failures. A rejected final body still reports failure and retains prior accepted content; tests are not weakened to hide it.
- **Core policy:** full `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` 146/146 pass (38.27 s launcher), including receipt plus partial-preview checks for automatic, denied and message-tool-only delivery. The combined denied case failed with physical CardKit writes before the shared-owner repair and passes with zero writes afterward.
- **Configuration/FIFO:** 10 receive-handler cases pass, including saved canonical settings unchanged beyond five minutes, hot updates, account HTTP overrides, default watchdog and bounded `0`. Time is controlled and the model handler is a gated I/O fixture; this is not a real six-minute model run.
- **Build/static:** canonical Feishu packaged runtime, unified core runtime (33.8 s) and public SDK declarations (194.9 s) build. Targeted production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, MDX, extension boundary, mock-factory and timeout-race checks pass. No full `pnpm build` claim; new-head CI is pending. Original-head CI also passed its baseline ratchets, which the local Git 2.34 helper could not run.
- **Review:** independent source review found no remaining P0–P2 issue after these fixes. The required CLI autoreview ran again for this follow-up but timed out after 300 s with model-catalog/network errors and no valid report; status remains `reviewer_unavailable`, not clean.

### Live candidate capture

On October 14, the candidate public core and Feishu source dispatched into a real Feishu DM using isolated local state and a synthetic model resolver. User-identity API reads observed the receipt **before any model text was returned**, idle elapsed updates, and the final marker `FEISHU_PR171189_SOURCE_OK` on the same message. The final read had no residual receipt. Public captures contain no chat/user/message IDs, credentials, IPs, private endpoints or real model routes.

| Observation | Measured value |
|---|---|
| Source dispatch → card send completed | 37.958 s, cold isolated source initialization included |
| Source dispatch → receipt read | 39.394 s |
| Idle receipt footer | `Agent: main \| Model: fixture-model \| Provider: synthetic ⏱ 43.0s` |
| Final request → core final delivery settled | 2.171 s |
| Source dispatch → final read | 52.100 s |

These are **renderings of the actual Feishu user API text**, not native Feishu client screenshots or real-model performance measurements.

![Live API elapsed update](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9fd40ae5-5625-44e3-a2d0-3ffd05450000)

![Live API final reply after closure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e2e5736-8ea3-4bf5-8d65-9e7c61628b60)
