prs.body:
> **STACKED ON #135889.** Diff shows PR-1 commits until it merges.

# PR-2 — feat(task-lanes): operator-configured lane boards over `taskLanes.list`


## What Problem This Solves

Cron already runs the work, but there is no read-side surface that groups runs/runs-outputs into operator-defined boards: "the board this team watches", "the lanes this gateway is responsible for". Operators configure such boards out-of-band today (spreadsheets, chats) with no typed, containable way to surface them next to the Automations UI they already live in.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds **task lanes**: named boards of work items from pluggable providers, read over a new read-only gateway RPC `taskLanes.list`, rendered as a read-only panel in the Control UI.

**Framing: read-side observability over existing cron, deliberately.** Lanes *observe* runs; nothing here schedules, multiplexes, or steers concurrent execution. Concurrent-run groundwork (state-lease multiplexing, GPU cap coordination, mid-run steering) was evaluated 2026-09-02 and deferred as cost > benefit — recorded in the spec so it is not re-litigated here.

**Registration route (updated after review):** the shipped route is **operator config** — a `taskLanes.providers` block in `openclaw.json` registers json-file providers at gateway start (`1d681de65cd`). The earlier `taskLaneProviders` manifest-capability route was evaluated and **omitted** (`4e82e38f14e`): with config-driven registration in place, no plugin could ever populate the capability, so declaring it was an unreachable contract that implied a registration path that does not exist. A provider-registration handler for third-party plugins remains the offered follow-up; if/when that lands it can declare the manifest capability for real. This is a product-surface call — maintainer confirmation on the omission (vs. holding the contract slot open) is welcome before merge.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a `taskLanes` block get their lane boards in the gateways they already run, visible in the Control UI. **Zero cost with no config:** absent the block, the RPC behaves as if the subsystem doesn't exist (B1/G1 battery probes). Everyone else: nothing changes.

## Evidence

**Live Control-UI proof on the current head (2026-09-02, isolated dev gateway — own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, own port):** with a config block whose provider `rootDir` is deliberately **relative** (`"rootDir": "lanes"`), the gateway resolves it against the state directory (`f764a4c6624`) and `taskLanes.list` returns the two configured lanes with items and ok diagnostics; the Automations run-history tab renders the TASK LANES panel from that RPC (screenshot). Sanitized RPC output (paths redacted):

```json
{"lanes":[{"id":"ingest","label":"Ingest","items":[…3 items with titles/states]},{"id":"review","label":"Review","items":[…1 item]}],"diagnostics":[{"providerId":"demo-board","ok":true,"laneCount":2,"itemCount":4}]}
```

**The battery found a real bug, fixed inside this PR stack.** Battery D3 caught the missing-provider diagnostic echoing an absolute resolved path (and parse errors able to echo file content) onto the wire. **`25a48ae4d0e`** narrows all provider diagnostics to node errno codes only, with regression tests asserting absence of path/content sentinels. This PR is stronger because the battery ran before merge — the evidence trail accompanies it.

**Review-fix commits (this round), each failing-repro-first:**

- `7d090cb22f4` — a malformed board's `schemaVersion` diagnostic no longer echoes the file's attacker-controlled value; a fixed sentinel is emitted instead, with a regression test pinning the sentinel.
- `f764a4c6624` — relative provider `rootDir`s resolve against the **state directory**, not the process cwd; cwd-dependent lane registration was a silent-miss failure class. Regression test: same config + `stateDir` tmp root, lane visible only with state-dir anchoring. Proven live with a relative rootDir (above).
- `234a6886cf0` — lane identity is scoped **per provider**: two providers may both expose a lane with the same id; snapshot assembly previously merged them into one lane, cross-assigning items. Regression test: alpha/beta providers both lane "work" → two lanes, one item each.
- `4e82e38f14e` — omit the unreachable `taskLaneProviders` manifest contract (see framing).

**Land-time suites (per commit, openspec §2.2):**

| Commit | What | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| `f8005b0fca2` | neutral task-lane registry + path-safe providers (CR-1) | 25/25 unit-src (13 json-file + 6 cron-backed + 6 registry) |
| `590ccb35401` | taskLanes.list schema + compiled validator (CR-2) | 4/4 gateway-client schema shard |
| `28a8facc058` | taskLanes.list RPC + descriptor + context wiring (CR-3) | 3/3 handler, gateway-core 175/175, tsgo:core exit 0 |
| `dab544d6ec8` | taskLaneProviders manifest capability (CR-4; later omitted by `4e82e38f14e`) | manifest-registry 115/115 at the time |
| `f483be91138` | Control UI task lanes panel, read-only (CR-5) | view-task-lanes 7/7, 70 cron-page tests, tsgo:ui + UI build green |
| `1d681de65cd` | config-driven json-file lane registration (CR-3b) | zod 7/7, config-registration tests, task-lanes 28/28, runtime-config 256/256, server-request-context 20/20, tsgo:core exit 0 |
| `afe132dc328` / `f338303a9d8` | sweep fallout: section-docs decision, request-context fixture, cursor policy token, docs-URL registry entry, typed tokenBudget test params | covered under CR-7 full re-sweep |
| `25a48ae4d0e` | provider diagnostics → errno codes only (battery D3 fix) | 30/30 task-lane tests incl. 2 regressions, tsgo green |
| `7d090cb22f4` | schemaVersion diagnostics never echo the file's value | failing-first regression green |
| `f764a4c6624` | relative provider rootDir anchored to the state directory | failing-first regression green + live proof above |
| `234a6886cf0` | provider-scoped lane identity in snapshot assembly | failing-first regression green |
| `4e82e38f14e` | omit unreachable taskLaneProviders contract route | manifest-registry/capability-summary suites adjusted, green |

**Screenshot (isolated dev gateway, current head):**

![TASK LANES panel from live taskLanes.list above the runs pane — typed origin labels on every run row](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-02/task-lanes-panel.png)

**Safety posture (asserted by the battery, not aspirational):**
- **Containment is real:** the json-file provider `realpath`s rootDir and every filePath; unit tests stub `resolveRealpath`, so battery group C exercises the unstubbed real-fs path (traversal, symlink-to-`/etc/hostname`, oversize).
- **Hostile producers can't take the gateway down:** bounded reads (256 KiB), bounded counts (20 lanes / 200 items), per-provider diagnostics instead of thrown errors.
- **UI never renders unsafe text:** `artifactUrl` dropped (not sanitized) unless http(s) without traversal/control chars; titles/outcomes truncated.

- Tree: this leg 94 files, +4154/−20 over merge-base; rebased onto current `main` 2026-09-02 (final head `507266661c6`), tsgo core+ui green, task-lanes 33/33. pnpm-lock: clean; zero trailers; audits as PR-1.

**Test plan**
- [x] Per-commit land-time suites — table above, all green
- [x] CR-7 full sweep (see PR-1), post-rebase affected shards re-run 2026-09-02
- [x] Live battery A + D + partial E: 8 PASS, 2 pass-with-erratum, 1 FAIL (D3) → fixed + regression-covered; D1 blocked (needs low-priv token), E3 blocked (browser tooling), D4 skipped
- [x] Live Control-UI proof on current head: taskLanes.list RPC + lanes panel (this round)
- [ ] Battery B/C (config surface + provider matrix) — scheduled
- [ ] Battery F5 (final shard counts incl. tsgo) — scheduled
- [ ] Battery G (lifecycle, restart-gated, operator-approved restarts) — scheduled

**Round-6 update (2026-09-04, rebased onto PR-1 head `7daa73aa1e8` / upstream `8e23a5324f5`, head `180b741e1d1`):**
- Round-6 review fixes: (1) **lane identity stays provider-scoped** — lanes are unique only within a provider, so snapshot assembly now keeps each lane's `providerId` in the registry result, the wire schema (`TaskLaneSchema.providerId`), and the UI (sort order provider-then-id; lane headers render `provider · label`); (2) **fail-closed capability gate** — cron-page sends `taskLanes.list` only when `cron.status` explicitly reports `taskLanesConfigured: true`; an absent signal (unconfigured install or legacy/unresolved status) is no longer read as permission, including while an operator refresh races a slow `cron.status` (new gate test holds `cron.status` pending past the 150 ms debounce and asserts zero lane requests).
- Verification at the new head: tsgo core + UI clean, all 5 core lint stripes + `core:ui` pass, task-lanes suites 42/42, cron-page gate tests green, protocol registry check passed, Kotlin + Swift protocol models regenerate unchanged.
- **Real-Gateway proof re-run at the exact new head (`180b741e1d1`)** — isolated gateway (loopback, throwaway token, own state dir), real `taskLanes.list` RPCs and real headless-Chromium Control UI: configured install returns provider-scoped lanes (`providerId` on every lane, ENOENT diagnostic without path echo, timestamp contract enforced); unconfigured install returns `taskLanesConfigured: false` + empty lanes; the UI renders the provider-scoped panel (`demo-board · Ingest queue`) and no panel at all when unconfigured.
  - Evidence: [pr2-gateway-evidence.md](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-04-tasklanes-gateway/pr2-gateway-evidence.md) · [rpc-tasklanes-configured.json](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-04-tasklanes-gateway/rpc-tasklanes-configured.json) · [rpc-tasklanes-unconfigured.json](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-04-tasklanes-gateway/rpc-tasklanes-unconfigured.json) · [screenshot-1-unconfigured](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-04-tasklanes-gateway/screenshot-1-unconfigured.png) · [screenshot-2-lanes-expanded](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-04-tasklanes-gateway/screenshot-2-lanes-expanded.png) · [screenshot-3-lanes-after-refresh](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-04-tasklanes-gateway/screenshot-3-lanes-after-refresh.png) (fork release assets; no repo-branch artifacts).

- Config-surface ratchet: the `taskLanes` section adds **+6 config keys** (`taskLanes`, `providers[]`, per-provider `id`/`rootDir`/`filePath`/`schemaVersion`) — intentional new config surface; baseline regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` and committed (`ab48c5c68fe`). All other config surface is untouched.

**Round-7 update (2026-09-04, head `c04137faf5d`):** addressed the CR-7 task-lane truncation finding. The registry sliced the flat item list at the default page limit but returned every lane with no total or continuation indicator, so a lane whose items fell outside the slice rendered as an empty queue — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty lane. Snapshot assembly now records each lane's unpaged item total + omitted count and a snapshot-level `paging` block (`{offset, limit, totalItems, returnedItems}`), exposed as optional wire-schema fields (`TaskLaneSchema.totalItems`/`omittedItems`, `TaskLaneSnapshotSchema.paging`) so older snapshots stay valid. The Control UI renders "shown of total" on partially-off-page lanes, a panel-level truncation notice when the page omits items, and requests the bounded maximum page (200, the schema cap) so the snapshot is as complete as the registry will serve. Failing-first regressions: `registry.test.ts` "reports per-lane totals so an off-page lane is distinguishable from an empty lane" (red → green) and `view-task-lanes.test.ts` "marks an off-page lane as omitted instead of reading as an empty queue" (red → green). Verification at `c04137faf5d`: `tsc --noEmit` core+UI exit 0, oxlint clean on touched files, repo-wide `oxfmt --check` clean, task-lanes registry 7/7 + view 7/7 + cron-page gate 5/5 green, protocol registry check passed, Kotlin/Swift models regenerate unchanged. (Toolchain note: `tsgo:ui` and the type-aware `tsgolint` shard segfault on this box — environmental, reproduces in a sibling worktree on untouched files; `tsc --noEmit` is the authoritative UI typecheck here.)

**Round-8 update (2026-09-05, head `e5ec3a231d5`):** addressed the P2 count-cap omission finding from the 02:57 UTC review. The json-file provider capped at 20 lanes and 200 items per lane but only returned the retained slices; the registry then reported `totalItems=200, omittedItems=0` for a 205-item lane, and the UI showed no truncation notice — a silently-cropped snapshot masqueraded as complete. Count input lanes and raw item count before each cap fires in `loadJsonFileProviderLanes`; return `omittedLanes`/`omittedItems` alongside the retained lanes. The registry propagates the counts into the `ok`-variant `TaskLaneProviderDiagnostic` (optional, omitted when zero so older providers stay valid). The gateway-protocol schema carries the same optional fields (`omittedLanes`, `omittedItems`) in the closed `TaskLaneProviderDiagnosticSchema`. The Control UI renders a distinct warn-styled chip (`cron-task-lanes__chip--warn`: `"big: 20 lanes · 219 items (dropped 1 lanes, 5 items at provider cap)"`) instead of the bare ok chip when omissions exist. **Failing-first coverage:** each cap test now asserts both the retained length and the omission count, a combined test exercises both caps simultaneously (21-lane source: lane 0 has 205 items, lane cap drops lane 20 → `omittedLanes=1`, per-lane cap drops 5 from lane 0 → `omittedItems=5`), the registry test asserts the diagnostic carries the omission fields, the schema test accepts the optional fields and rejects negative counts, and the UI test asserts the warn chip renders with the dropped counts. Verification at `e5ec3a231d5`: `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json` zero errors in touched files, 48/48 task-lanes + UI + schema tests, 695/695 gateway-protocol tests, 159/159 cron page tests; oxfmt + oxlint clean. Live proof (`proof-pr2-cap.mts`, fork release pr-proof-2026-09-05-tasklanes-cap): `loadJsonFileProviderLanes` → `omittedLanes=1, omittedItems=5`; registry snapshot → `diagnostic.omittedLanes=1, omittedItems=5`; `TaskLaneSnapshotSchema` validates the diagnostic → `true`.

**Inline proof trace (taskLanes.list, redacted — inlined because the review sandbox cannot fetch release assets; full evidence at the release links above):**

```
# live gateway capture at runtime head 180b741e1d1 (banner "OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (180b741)");
# isolated loopback gateway, own state dir, throwaway token — operator gateway never touched
cron.status (configured):     {"taskLanesConfigured": true, ...}
taskLanes.list (configured):
  lanes:[ {"providerId":"demo-board","id":"ingest","label":"Ingest queue",
           "items":[ /* item-1: both ms timestamps kept;
                       item-2: startedAtMs=-5 dropped, heartbeatAtMs kept;
                       item-3: heartbeatAtMs=1.5 dropped, startedAtMs kept */ ]},
          {"providerId":"demo-board","id":"review","label":"Review queue","items":[...]} ]
  diagnostics:[ {"providerId":"demo-board","ok":true,"laneCount":2,"itemCount":3},
                {"providerId":"ghost-board","ok":false,"error":"task lane file is unavailable (ENOENT)"} ]
  # providerId on every lane (round-6); errno-only diagnostic, no path echo
cron.status (unconfigured):   {"taskLanesConfigured": false, ...}
taskLanes.list (unconfigured):{"lanes":[],"diagnostics":[]}
UI (headless Chromium):       configured  -> panel renders "demo-board · Ingest queue" (provider · label)
                              unconfigured-> no panel rendered (verified programmatically)
# ── Round-7 live re-capture at EXACT head c04137faf5d (banner "OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (c04137f)") ──
# Isolated loopback gateway (port 18993), own state dir + OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, throwaway
# token — operator gateway never touched. Config: one demo-board provider, two lanes —
# ingest (200 items, the per-lane cap) and review (5 items); flat total = 205 > the 200
# page bound, so the review lane's items fall outside the slice.
taskLanes.list (limit:200, the UI page size):
  lanes:[ {"providerId":"demo-board","id":"ingest","label":"Ingest queue",
           "items":[ /* 200 */ ], "totalItems":200, "omittedItems":0},
          {"providerId":"demo-board","id":"review","label":"Review queue",
           "items":[], "totalItems":5, "omittedItems":5} ]   # <- off-page, NOT empty
  diagnostics:[ {"providerId":"demo-board","ok":true,"laneCount":2,"itemCount":205} ]
  paging:{"offset":0,"limit":50,"totalItems":205,"returnedItems":50}   # default call; UI sends 200
UI (headless Chromium, Activity tab):
  panel notice: "Showing 200 of 205 items (snapshot page limit). Lane counts include
                 off-page items."  (role="status", visible to operators)
  ingest lane count:  "200"
  review lane count:  "0 of 5"   # renderLaneCount "shown of total" — omitted>0, not a bare "0"
# This is the round-7 paging/omission behavior live at the exact PR head, not a re-stamped
# earlier capture. Full evidence (fork release assets, no repo-branch artifacts):
#   pr2-trunc-evidence.md · rpc-tasklanes-trunc.json · rpc-cronstatus-trunc.json · screenshot-trunc-lanes.png
#   release 383104927 — https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/tag/pr-proof-2026-09-05-tasklanes-trunc
```

**Out of scope:** generic lane **writes** (read-only this PR), provider **auth/signing** (in-process providers), cross-plugin lane composition, provider-registration handler for third-party plugins (offered follow-up; manifest capability deliberately omitted until it exists), concurrent-run scheduling machinery (see framing).

prs.title: fix: Stop reports command cleanup failure after managed checkpoint cancellation
prs.body:
Closes #172723

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: stopping a sandboxed run can report command cleanup failure when its managed workspace checkpoint sees the canceled run authority.

## User Impact

User impact: stopped commands can finish checkpointing accepted workspace output when the same session and worktree still own it; a replaced owner or real checkpoint error remains visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

After command cancellation, finalization reacquires the current local workspace owner and checks that session and worktree identity still matches before synchronizing the canonical workspace. Execution admission and other workspace mutations retain the original run authority.

## Evidence

**Incomplete; this draft is not ready for review.** Final published head: `f3434af144309e03b435b8e57cd92172a6aee9d7`.

- Before the production fix, the focused owner-boundary regression failed with `agent run aborted` in a real temporary Git worktree/SQLite projection. Existing artifacts: `/tmp/openclaw-172723-red.log`; the candidate's earlier focused pass is in `/tmp/openclaw-172723-green.log`. That regression was subsequently moved into `src/agents/sandbox/local-workspace.test.ts`, so those artifacts are not a same-file red/green pair for the final test layout.
- On the final published head, `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox/local-workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 4/4; this includes same-owner settlement, replacement-owner rejection, and blocking new execution after cancellation. The existing projection checkpoint-wait test passed 1/1. These are focused owner-boundary proofs.
- Lint, formatting, and core production/test typechecks passed before the final rebase; after rebase the focused test, projection sibling, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Core typechecks were not rerun on the final published SHA.
- `pnpm check:changed` fell back to all lanes after baseline metadata classification reported an unexpected EOF, then failed in repository-wide line-cap/max-lines ratchets. No unchanged-base comparison was recorded, so these failures have not been demonstrated on an unmodified baseline.
- **Not yet proven:** a real OpenClaw Stop/runtime flow with a sandbox command, including positive and negative controls and a final-layout same-file baseline-red/candidate-green log pair. Docker is available in this container, but an isolated Gateway/runtime route and its permissions/configuration have not yet been qualified.
- **Not yet run:** local canonical AutoReview for this source dataset and exact head. GitHub Security Review is not a substitute: its official workflow reported that maintainer approval is required for this sensitive sandbox change; no full AutoReview report or context dataset is attached.
- The earlier 43-minute build and CLI smoke were on a different retained checkout/SHA, not this PR head, and are not candidate build evidence.

Do not treat this draft as ready.

prs.title: feat(cron): run provenance, job kinds, agentTurn token budget, typed completion causes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Run-log entries and the Control UI Automations page can't answer the questions an operator actually asks: where did this run come from, what kind of job is it, when does it next run, what did it cost, and why did it stop. Producers write freeform errors; the runs pane renders a generic failure label; `agentTurn` jobs can't cap their token spend; and trigger provenance is inferred downstream by string-matching instead of recorded at admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Every run-log entry gains a **typed trigger origin** (schedule / manual / system / ACP admission), populated uniformly across all 9 run-admission paths, typed at the protocol layer.
- The Automations UI gains a **job-kind column + detail badge** and an **upcoming/ETA panel** — the page reads as a schedule, not a graveyard.
- `agentTurn` jobs accept **`tokenBudget` end-to-end**: protocol → normalizer → **create and same-kind update patch merge** → live config patch → UI form/table round-trip.
- **Completion causes become a closed typed set** (`CronCompletionCause`) with an **exact legacy codec** — restart/interrupt rows written by older versions decode identically, no silent reclassification. Producers emit typed causes; the runs pane renders cause-aware failure labels (7 buckets; producer cause wins over derived).

## User Impact

Operators see provenance, cost caps, and truthful stop reasons on the surface they already use. Old run rows decode byte-identically (codec round-trip tested), so history is not reclassified. Clients that ignore the new fields are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Live Control-UI proof on the current head (2026-09-02, isolated dev gateway — own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, own port; the operator's running gateway was never touched):**

- Runs pane shows **typed origin labels** rendered from the new fields: "Scheduled — cron fire", "Manual run", "On-exit watcher" (screenshots 1–2), plus job-kind labels, the token-budget column, and the upcoming/ETA panel (screenshot 1).
- Job editor shows the **Token budget** field with its help text under ADVANCED (screenshot 3).
- **TokenBudget round-trip proven at the wire level**, not just visually: a Playwright session listening on the gateway WebSocket captured the `cron.update` request the UI sends (`"payload":{"kind":"agentTurn","message":"…","tokenBudget":120000}`), and after save `cron get` on the same state dir returns the payload with `"tokenBudget": 120000`; re-opening the editor shows 120000 in the field and the jobs table shows it in the TOKEN BUDGET column (screenshot 4).
- **That wire-level probe caught a real gateway bug, fixed in this PR:** the UI was sending `tokenBudget` on edit, but same-kind `cron.update` merges rebuilt the agentTurn payload without reading `patch.tokenBudget` — create persisted the budget while every same-kind edit silently dropped it, and the explicit-null clear was never honored. `a5d2978f1d1` mirrors the model/thinking override rules (number sets, null clears, omitted leaves untouched) with failing-first regression tests. This is exactly the class of drop the tokenBudget enforcement work would have hidden: the cap lever existed in the form but updates never stored it.

**Redacted live proof (post-rebase re-verification recorded in the test battery, `~/openclaw-test-battery/evidence/`):** trigger origin visible on live run-log entries through the production gateway; typed completion causes flow producer → run record → cause-aware UI label against the live gateway.

**Land-time suites (per commit, openspec §2.2):**

| Commit | Slice | What | Land-time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `577db2e79f6` | 0 | populate trigger field on run log entries | 113/113 (post-CR-6-rebase) |
| `95a95088bf2` | 0 | typed run trigger-source enum (protocol) | 113/113 |
| `062c9718e5f` | 1 | trigger origin on all 9 admission paths + Unknown (legacy) | 142/142 |
| `9f0bf4dbac5` | 2 | job-kind column, detail badge, upcoming/ETA panel | 78/78 |
| `7d77eb1b42c` | 3a | agentTurn tokenBudget protocol + normalizer | 87/87 |
| `5b98180783f` | 3b | tokenBudget UI form/table, Unlimited / N-a display | 181/181 + UI build green |
| `ab0240077be` | 4a | typed completionCause contracts + exact legacy restart codec | 85/85 |
| `ea166202cc2` | 4b-c2 | producers emit typed causes + budget-cause gap fix | 305/305 (8 files) + 301/301 (9 files) |
| `260cd8d8595` | 4b-c3 | cause-aware failure label in runs pane, 7 buckets | 161/161 + UI build green |
| `6b1782aba48` | 5 | direct runs of event jobs stay `trigger=manual`; on-exit watchers pass explicit `triggerSource` (review fix) | cron admission + active-jobs suites green |
| `12a429956d7` | 5 | render localized run origin + job-kind labels via locale catalog (review fix) | UI cron suites green |
| `a5d2978f1d1` | 6 | **fix:** same-kind `cron.update` merges apply `tokenBudget` (number sets, null clears) — found by live wire-level probing, see above | payload-merge 19/19 (3 failing-first), apply-patch + protocol conformance/schema 52/52 |

- **Rebase onto current `main` (2026-09-02, final head `fd168c05633`):** two upstream movements were ported — (1) embedded-agent usage accounting moved into `createEmbeddedModelState`, so the `onRunUsageTotals` checkpoint lives in its `recordModelUsage` (threading verified across all 5 call sites); (2) #136075 derived the run-log entry type from the gateway-protocol wire schema — our `trigger`/`completionCause` fields already live in `CronRunLogEntrySchema`, so `src/cron/run-log-types.ts` adopted the upstream `Omit`-derivation verbatim. `pnpm tsgo:core` green; payload-merge 19/19, protocol conformance + gateway-protocol validators 21/21. A follow-up CI-gate commit (`fd168c05633`) regenerates the Swift protocol models for the new schema fields and removes knip-flagged dead code (superseded `run-origin.ts` formatter, test-only cause predicate/exports, production-dead UI helpers).
- Full CR-7 sweep at the pre-rebase tip: unit-src 486/490 (4 waivers logged, environmental/umask classes, baseline logs under `/tmp/cr7-batch/`), runtime-config 280/280, gateway-client 1148/1148, gateway-server/methods/plugin-sdk green, tsgo green, cron subsets 54/54/95, ui 857/857.

**Round-8 update (2026-09-05, rebased onto current `main`, head `3f1386c6b59`):** the rebase ClawSweeper flagged is done. prs.title: fix(muse): stop turn activity when the answer is final
prs.body:
## Problem

With Muse Code, "Preparing this turn… Ns" kept animating for about 10 s after the reply was on screen. The status label also jumped between "Working…", "Preparing…" and "Waiting…". The sidebar session spinner and the composer's "Assistant is responding..." stayed on during that time as well.

## Solution

- **Muse harness.** Muse events now go to the Gateway event stream, not only to the core observer, and the harness reports native turn acceptance. Muse runs post-answer `reminderChild` tasks for several seconds. Once the assistant reply is saved, that reminder work starts, and nothing in the foreground is still running, the harness emits the existing `lifecycle.finishing` phase. A reply followed by tool calls keeps the working state.
- **UI.**
  - One derived run-activity selector (`session-run-state.ts`) feeds the chat thread, the sidebar row, the composer and the favicon, so all of them stop together once the run reaches `finishing`.
  - The run itself (Stop, queue) stays active until Muse finishes.
  - Status labels only move forward: Preparing, then Waiting, then the reply. No "Working…" before Preparing or after the reply.
  - A chat resumed after a recovery clears its stale status.
- **Solid.** The chat working indicator and its completion rendering moved from Lit to Solid (`chat-working-indicator.tsx`); direct callers and tests were ported.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real Muse 1.3.0. Milliseconds from `chat.send`:

| Event | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| First visible reply | 9,264 | 4,866 |
| Activity indicator removed | 20,142 | 5,147 |
| Muse `turn/completed` | 19,974 | 10,897 |
| **Reply → indicator gap** | **10,878** | **281** |

A later end-to-end run with the integrated changes showed: Preparing (0.5 s) → Waiting (2.5 s) → reply at 6.5 s, with the status, composer state and sidebar spinner all cleared in the same render.

![before: reply shown while Preparing still animates](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0aed173c-05d1-458c-b636-e4369b15ada4)
![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5ceddee-c301-4571-9154-0ef6b02a7196)

Tests: Muse harness ordering (final message → `finishing` before `turn/completed`; text then tools stays working), run-activity selector (finishing → no activity, tool activity → activity), the sidebar projection memo, composer and recovery status, and the Solid working-indicator suite.

### Review follow-up (`ac0ef430411`, rebased on main)

- A native Muse tool start (`stream=item`, `kind=tool`, `phase=start`) brings activity back in the thread, composer, sidebar and favicon.
- A newer attempt (retry, fallback, assistant or tool event) clears `finishing`, including a `finishing` that carries an error. Older replays are still rejected, using the run-wide agent sequence.

### Attempt-level finishing semantics

`finishing` suppresses visual activity, not run ownership or Stop. It settles one attempt: `deferTerminalLifecycle` explicitly emits it before fallback and post-turn settlement (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/params.ts:249–252`), and `createAgentHarnessAttemptLifecycle` preserves an attempt error when changing its terminal phase to `finishing` (`src/agents/harness/attempt-events.ts:58–94`). A newer retry, fallback, or foreground event therefore resumes activity under the same run ID. Both UI projections use the existing run-wide agent sequence (incremented across attempts in `src/infra/agent-events.ts:454–455`) to reject older replays; chat deltas have a separate counter and cannot clear an attempt's finishing state on their own. Native Muse tool starts use `stream=item`, `kind=tool`, `phase=start`, and now resume activity in both projections.

The rebase preserves main's token-before-elapsed-time presentation in the Solid working indicator and recap.

### Repair verification

Both review findings reproduced against the rebased pre-repair source: the native
item-tool case failed with `state: "status"` instead of `state: "activity"`, and
retry/fallback/assistant/tool recovery all failed with `expected false to be true`.
The repaired owner tests (7 cases) and bundled-browser regression now pass. The
browser regression uses the real Muse tool projection and checks the thread,
composer, sidebar, and favicon through tool start, failed-attempt finishing,
retry, stale replay, and final settlement.

Real Muse 1.3.0, isolated Gateway on port 18923, final UI build:

```text
run=2113e1aa-6b5c-43c0-b7e7-32376f970bb2 (milliseconds since chat.send)
+42969 agent seq=6 stream=item kind=tool phase=start name=bash
        thread=true composer="Assistant is working..." sidebar=true Stop=true
+48144 agent seq=7 stream=item kind=tool phase=end name=bash
+51537 chat delta: final answer CLEMENTINE-609
+51553 thread=false composer="" sidebar=false Stop=true
+51795 agent seq=12 stream=lifecycle phase=finishing
+63634 agent seq=17 stream=lifecycle phase=end; chat final
+63643 thread=false composer="Done" sidebar=false Stop=false
```

The approved native command read a fresh synthetic workspace file:
`sleep 5; cat /tmp/a609-workspace/fresh-proof.txt`. Activity stayed visible during
the 5,175 ms tool execution and disappeared 16 ms after the answer delta. Stop
remained available through background finalization. Approval time is included in
the run-relative timestamps.

Inspected screenshots:
- `/tmp/a609-live-sZon3u/final-build-during-tool.png`
- `/tmp/a609-live-sZon3u/final-build-after-answer.png`

Raw sanitized event/UI timeline:
`/tmp/a609-live-sZon3u/final-build-tool-timeline.json`.
Negative-control evidence: `/tmp/a609-negative-proof.txt`.

### Review follow-up 3 (`198020365895`, rebased on main)

- Boundary: the Muse event test now imports `awaitGateBeforeSettlement` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-fixtures` and `createDeferred` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/extension-shared`.
- Sidebar: `hasActiveRun` keeps owning the running-session narration and subscriptions. Only the separate visual-activity signal hides the row, rail and grouped spinners, so the running subtitle stays.
- The new main caller `chat-session-rail.tsx` is migrated to the Solid `ChatWorkingIndicator`.
- E2E: the two workspace-reconciliation tests no longer wait for working-indicator telemetry after finalization, which this PR intentionally ends. They still check persisted-answer rendering, stream retirement, duplicate prevention, Stop availability and terminal state. The recap test checks the token, separator and duration spans in order instead of exact text-node whitespace.
- The cron failures in the earlier run (`persists current-session CLI prompt provenance…`, `seals only accepted CLI continuity…`, `keeps a cron fallback active…`) are unrelated: they also fail on main ([run 38663143259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663143259/job/116189131871)), and this PR does not touch cron files.

### Review follow-up 4 (`0a4c88c4618`)

- **Side chat theme phrases.** `ChatWorkingIndicator` uses the current theme's `workingPhrases` when the caller omits them; an explicit `[]` still means no phrases. This keeps the intent of 24b285489674. New regressions cover an empty list and a custom list in a pending Side chat answer after 30 s; both failed before the fix (`· Bubbling…`).
- CI attribution for [run 38665194764](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38665194764): `checks-node-changed-1` has the same cron failures as main ([run 38663143259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663143259/job/116189131871)). `checks-ui-e2e (3/7)`: the `chat-native-runtime-recovery.e2e.test.ts` OpenCode consent cases fail the same way on unrelated branches ([run 38665559064](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38665559064/job/116196980919)). Their cause on main is being traced separately.

### Review follow-up 5 (`93812b4802d`)

- When a same-client reconnect replays the Gateway's text-free assistant progress marker (`data: {}`), the sequenced reconciler now clears the obsolete "Retrying…" / "Trying fallback model…" status. An older replay still cannot clear a newer recovery. The regressions use the real snapshot builder and `loadChatHistory`; they failed before the fix.
- **Provenance (af8dad8e9e32).** That commit introduced shared, sequenced reconciliation for live startup progress and history replay, so delayed snapshots cannot bring back superseded startup states. This fix keeps that ordering and accepts the Gateway's text-free assistant marker, which clears the obsolete retry/fallback status without letting a stale replay override a newer recovery.

## Update behavior

No config or stored-data change. Older clients ignore `finishing` and behave as before.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(tasks): clear stale blocked state after requester delivery
prs.body:
Related: #121195

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who yield for required child work can receive the child completion visibly while the completed task remains falsely marked as delivery failed and blocked.

Reproduction:

1. A requester starts a required child task and yields.
2. The child succeeds.
3. The requester-settle wake produces a visible final reply.
4. Delivery changes to `delivered`, but an earlier delivery failure error and blocked terminal projection can remain on the task.

Expected: after the visible requester settlement succeeds, the same task is `succeeded` and `delivered`, with no stale error or blocked terminal outcome.

Actual before this change: the final reply is visible, but task audit still reports `delivery_failed` for that run.

## Why This Change Was Made

`minimum path: existing requester-settle lifecycle + native task finalizer; new durable machinery: none`

The successful requester-settle branch now reuses the existing finalized child state and native task finalizer with `clearError: true` after marking delivery complete. Failure, timeout, cancellation, and missing-visible-reply behavior is unchanged.

This does not change the current visible-final requirement or adopt the intentional-quiet policy discussed in #121195.

## User Impact

When a yielded child completion visibly reaches its requester, Task and Flow state now agree with what the user received. Operators no longer see a false blocked task or a new `delivery_failed` audit warning for that successful handoff.

## Evidence

Live QA on OpenClaw `2026.9.1-beta.1` with the equivalent patch:

- requester turn visibly ended with `Requester settlement QA started.`
- LifeOS later projected exactly one `Requester settlement QA completed visibly once.`
- task `b802568a-3418-47bf-8e80-08f089b75aab` ended `status: succeeded`, `deliveryStatus: delivered`, `error: null`
- LifeOS task activity reported zero active tasks and zero failures
- the audit retained the same 29 historical warnings and added no warning for the repaired run

Current-main validation at `73bc39dae8`:

- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`: 320 passed across `agents-core` and `agents-support`
- changed files pass `oxfmt --check`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passes

The exact beta patch also passed the 314-test focused lifecycle file, OpenClaw changed-file checks, and a full package build before live deployment.

AI-assisted: yes. The author reviewed the lifecycle and terminal-state ownership directly and understands the change. The repository autoreview helper was attempted, but a local safety policy blocked external transmission before any patch data was sent; the complete diff and adjacent finalization paths were reviewed locally instead.

prs.title: perf(auth): defer snapshot orchestration on cold reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first agent-auth read loads snapshot and parent-worker orchestration even when it only needs a native read-only database handle.

Related: #172374, #171726.

## User Impact

Ordinary auth loading imports less code. Credential selection, persisted data, and the credential-authority check at the fetch boundary are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth reader pool now receives its opener from the caller. The helper supplies the native read-only opener for ordinary reads and imports the existing artifact-preserving opener on demand. Native inspection callers supply that same existing opener explicitly. The pool continues to own admission, handle reuse, and retirement.

This removes the pool's static dependency on parent-side snapshot orchestration. A static AST census of local runtime imports shows the helper-plus-auth closure falling from 323 to 228 modules; the increment on first auth use falls from 101 to 6. This is a source-graph measurement, not a latency claim.

## Evidence

- Basic changed-file oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex autoreview: two rounds completed, no actionable findings (first P0–P2, final P0–P1).
- A real-helper regression replaces the database, verifies a stale request returns only an error (no credential transfer), and verifies a fresh request reads the replacement. Existing coverage migrated with the internal signature: committed-write freshness, reader replacement/retirement, deletion cleanup, and auth transport. PR CI supplies test, type, Knip, Madge, source-contract, T1, and dialect proof.
- No SDK, schema, update, or service-lifecycle behavior changes. Doctor inspection retains the identical artifact-preserving opener.
- Cold helper T1 remains 0 → 0; its two batched-read primitives are worker-only. The broader auth-profile module inventory retains six mixed/native T1 calls (two JSON writes, two JSON-cell reads, and two transaction primitives), unchanged. CI verifies the global ratchet.
- Removed check: the auth helper no longer checks the same physical identity before and after its synchronous read. The check immediately before credential transfer remains. Accepted edge case: a stale request may read a deleted or replaced source before rejection; no credential rows are transferred, and failure retires the child. The generic operation path and fetch-boundary credential authority are unchanged.
- LOC: production +34/-9; tests/support +83/-15; docs +5/-0.

The exact historical comparison against `dbfa55ec6574e151edb4caabacdc5d6101115c71` (before #172374), and three alternating base/candidate count pairs are queued. Results will include SQL, worker requests, helper starts, MAIN, and loaded bundles. Absolute latency is unmeasured on the loaded host.

prs.title: fix(cron): CLI-backed automations cannot be created after inference binding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After #172590, `cron.add` captures a stored inference account for every isolated agent-turn job, including jobs whose model runs on a CLI backend such as `claude-cli`. That causes two failures for CLI-backed automations:

- When the canonical provider has an environment or provider-config key, creation fails with "Automation requires a stored inference account". CLI backends never read that key.
- When a stored profile exists for the provider, creation records a binding. Since #172717, a bound job on a CLI candidate is always refused as "incompatible with its recorded inference account and route", so every run of that job fails.

Full Release Validation for 2026.10.10-beta.1 (run 38662503008, job 116187263890, `bundle-infra-small-private-qa-23`) fails `test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts` at `cron.add` for all nine scenarios. PR CI for #172590 does not run that shard.

## Why This Change Was Made

#172717 already allows unbound CLI runs on their native login. This PR makes creation match. When the job's primary model resolves to a CLI backend, `captureCronInferenceBinding` records no binding and does not reject direct keys. The CLI run then takes the native-only path from #172717, which still refuses to forward a host credential profile without a recorded account.

The integration fixture's embedded (`openclaw`) scenarios now provide their synthetic model key as a stored auth profile instead of a provider-config key, which #172590 intentionally rejects. The CLI scenarios keep the provider-config key, which shows that CLI creation is no longer rejected.

## User Impact

CLI-backed automations can be created again and run on the CLI's own login. Embedded jobs keep the #172590 behavior.

A gap remains, unchanged by this PR: a CLI backend that would forward a stored OpenClaw profile (`claude-cli` or `google-gemini-cli` with a stored profile for the canonical provider) still has no way to adopt an account, because #172717 keeps bound CLI candidates incompatible. Forwarding a recorded account to those backends is a follow-up product decision.

## Evidence

- On `release/2026.10.10` and on main before this change, FRV job 116187263890 shows `invalid cron.add params: Automation requires a stored inference account` for every scenario.
- With the creation fix, local runs on a heavily loaded host (load average around 65) had no scenario fail with the stored-account error. `account/claude-cli/channel-info`, `account/openclaw/read`, `openclaw/channel-edit` and the CLI "preserves an accepted Discord edit" case passed end to end. The other cases hit the test's 60s timeout during cold Gateway import, which took about 197s on this host, or failed as a cascade of that timeout.
- PR CI on `93f0e171fca`: 62 checks pass, none fail.
- Manual CI dispatch (`validation_tier=main`) [38672164459](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672164459) shows no cron failures. Its remaining reds are unrelated: `cloud-worker-midturn-loss`, `skills/workshop/review-outcome`, `boundary-invariants`, i18n/dependency, and UI shards already tracked for this release. That tier does not print `cron-message-read` per test, so the release-tier FRV rerun is the end-to-end proof for the infra shard.

## Credential authority

This PR does not change where credentials are authorized. A job created on a CLI backend is unbound, and every run goes through the #172717 checks:
- `run-prompt-executor.ts` throws "Automation has no recorded inference account" when an unbound job would forward any stored profile, whether user-selected or automatic.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` (`nativeAuthOnly`) refuses a stored profile picked by backend defaults or automatic selection before `prepareExecution` and before the CLI starts. This is covered by `prepare.model-routing-authority.test.ts`, "keeps scheduled CLI credentials under their recorded owner (native/selected/automatic)".

Replacing a profile between creation and execution has nothing to invalidate, because no account was recorded. A replaced or new profile is still refused by the same run-time check.

## What Problem This Solves

Settings agent selection still listened for Web Awesome's `wa-show` after the selector adopted native overlays, so opening it missed the existing lazy identity refresh. Browser proof also imported the retired vendor theme and queried tags that the owned controls no longer render.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change follows the existing `overlay-show` event, checks identity loading across all three Settings presentations, and updates consumer fixtures and diagnostics to the owned controls. The layout test mounts real Menu, Cron, and Usage owners and preserves their distinct trailing/leading check contracts. No CSS, route, startup import, registered tag, or dependency declaration changes.

Full migration proof exposed three additional fixture assumptions, repaired here at their owning boundary:

- The packaged Workboard fixture advertised fallback build ID `e2e` while serving a real build. It now advertises the served artifact's normalized build identity, preserving the remote-Gateway confirmation, authentication, and same-origin entry/CSS/lazy-chunk checks.
- The native menu overlap fixture relied on a CSS transition always existing. It now owns real finite, paused opacity and scale Web Animations before close, matching existing overlay fixtures. Descendant-only geometry, native-open, closing, retained occlusion, and release-after-settlement assertions remain.
- Official main change #172610 intentionally keeps successful provider sign-in open with Connected and Close/Start chat actions. The real HTTPS Gateway test now asserts the exact success heading and its existing saved-credentials notice, clicks Close, then keeps its zero-modal assertion. The earlier Cancel path, cancelled/stale callback rejection, credential readback, Gateway restart, and existing-session history checks are unchanged. The notice is checked before Close because the owner intentionally clears it on reset.

The browser-bootstrap fixture also uses Playwright's existing `route.fetch({ maxRetries: 1 })` contract to recover one observed asset-fetch `ECONNRESET`. It does not retry HTTP errors or alter application recovery.

## Evidence

Full `ci:full` run [38674766694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674766694), head `84a2dcb2`, is complete: **44 successful jobs, 23 skipped, two inherited failing test jobs plus the CI aggregate**. All UI unit shards, eight of nine UI E2E shards, real-Gateway shard 1, types, performance, and security-fast passed. The corrected provider sign-in flow passed in the 20-file/25-test real-Gateway shard; packaged Workboard delivery passed too.

The remaining failures are exactly the four Cron and four Models tests named below; each name and full substantive error signature matches latest scheduled-main run [38672095119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672095119), head `a4d316dc`. Native-consent tests now pass. The actual CI merge is `977972c6`, with ordered parents `6866eac6` (main) and `84a2dcb2` (PR); both failing test files have identical blobs in the main parent and tested merge. The native inherited-failure exception is being used for those eight failures only.

The comparison excludes ANSI/timestamp formatting, blank/report-separator lines, interleaved runner counts, and one exact `Start at HH:MM:SS` runner line. Every assertion value, locator, source excerpt, and stack frame remains. Adjacent grouped failure headers explicitly share their following nonempty detail block.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Final UI typecheck | Passed, exit 0, on the final provider-completion correction after official-main integration. |
| Scoped formatting, whitespace, lint | Passed: scoped formatting, whitespace, and core-config lint. |
| Independent P0/P1 review | All authored corrections scoped-clean with no P0/P1 findings and successful final source verification; final provider-completion review exited 0. |
| Native closing fixture | Targeted final case passed WebKit and Chromium: 2 passed, 10 skipped, exit 0, 27.77 s. WebKit 1,631 ms; Chromium 866 ms. |
| Exact-head full CI at `ffa9cb64` | Run 38670559959: 43 successful jobs, 23 skipped, four failed test jobs plus aggregate. All UI unit shards passed; WebKit descendant-only overlap passed in 661 ms, and packaged Workboard distribution passed. Failure accounting below. |
| Provider-completion local E2E | Not run: this checkout has no qualified built runtime/UI, and a new build solely for this test-only correction is outside the proof budget. Fresh `ci:full` is the runner. Another lane owns the exact-CI-base reproduction; no duplicate replay was started. |
| Visual/startup/production Knip | Not run for this behavior/test-only prerequisite. No visual or startup code changes. The Web Awesome retirement lane owns its build, screenshots, startup budget, and production Knip proof. |

The original Settings single-file invocation produced no assertion result and was interrupted after more than ten minutes (953.68 s total). The original Chromium alignment invocation passed all three cases, then hung during teardown and was interrupted (416.05 s total). Neither is claimed as a clean command pass or inherited failure. Later published-head CI passing the UI shards is separate evidence. The initial Workboard typecheck encountered an installed fs-safe version mismatch; a frozen install changed no tracked files, and the subsequent typecheck passed. Superseded animation candidates and their interrupted commands are retained in the native review record and are not final-candidate proof.

A bounded Workboard Chromium comparison used an older existing artifact read-only: fallback identity caused recovery navigation, and matching identity retained confirmation and reached `agents.list`. That probe establishes the startup cause, not a full current distribution pass; the later hosted distribution pass supplies that proof. A diagnostic of the old animation fixture observed two animations immediately and after a frame; it did not prove delayed creation, so no arbitrary wait was added.

## Earlier-run failures and attribution

For `ffa9cb64`, all twelve failures below match the exact test names and nonempty error signatures of latest compared scheduled-main run 38666744245 (`207b7813`). Comparison removes ANSI/timestamps and interleaved Vitest count-summary lines only. Every assertion, locator, expected/actual value, source location, and stack frame remains. Vitest's adjacent grouped failure headers share the following nonempty detail block explicitly.

| File / suite | Failing tests |

| `cron-duration-save.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` — Control UI exact stagger with a real Gateway | `timeout override: clearing restores the default after save and reload`; `failure alert round trip: preserves partial policy through metadata save and clone`; `failure alert round trip: clears field overrides through the real picker`; `clone payload policy: preserves public options through the real Gateway and CLI readback` |
| `model-providers-progressive.e2e.test.ts` — Control UI progressive Model Providers loading | `keeps a Models route selection saved before the initial provider details arrive`; `keeps the current Models catalog after late route data and invalidation`; `opens the Models route from snapshot catalog publication and refreshes after overlapping reads`; `opens the Models route from ordinary catalog publication and refreshes after overlapping reads` |

G1 additionally failed `provider-browser-login.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Provider browser login through real HTTPS Gateway > rejects cancelled and stale callbacks, then saves a fresh sign-in and serves an existing session` at 211:80: expected zero modal hosts after saving, received one. Scheduled main passed that same case in 30,748 ms. Personally inspected exact CI merge `af2932af`, its ordered main parent `2d5176b6`, and official owner change `527d11de3f5199` (#172610): the latter retains the successful dialog and provides explicit Close. Existing owner E2E proof already follows that dismissal flow. This PR migrates the stale real-Gateway assertion accordingly; no inherited-only exception is claimed for the failed `ffa9cb64` run.

The source integrates official main through a normal merge. No unlanded lane branch or replayed main commits were used. The current exact-head result above supersedes these earlier CI outcomes; the native review and preparation bind the current head before landing.

prs.title: fix(ios): tolerate slow release qualification setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iOS release qualification can exhaust its setup-code deadline after a cold Simulator boot. Recent fresh runs completed that request in 11.15 and 25.69 seconds, close to the previous 30-second limit, but slow successes did not retain the failure-only diagnostics.

## User Impact

Qualification gives the setup-code request up to 60 seconds and records evidence while a slow request is still pending. All UI assertions, startup ordering, cancellation, and cleanup requirements remain in place. This tolerates transient setup latency; the underlying cause remains unproven.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only `device.pair.setupCode` receives the longer deadline. The status warm-up retains its 30-second deadline. One diagnostic capture starts after 10 seconds, using the existing bounded process sample, sanitized worker/queue projection, and classified events. Authentication, dispatch, response, and elapsed RPC timings distinguish where time was spent without exporting credentials or content.

There is one credential-issuing request and no retry. Started diagnostic work is joined before the fixture can be cleaned up, and observer failure does not change the RPC result. RPC timing excludes that join. A stalled setup can now take 30 seconds longer to fail; a response arriving during observation waits for that bounded observation to finish before qualification continues. The diagnostic instrumentation remains temporary investigation work, to be removed once the cause is established.

## Evidence

- 94 focused native-adapter tests passed: 0.935 seconds of local test time, 3.78 seconds including the repository wrapper; the same 94 tests passed in CI in 1.290 seconds. Fake-clock cases cover 35-second success, a 60-second deadline, partial timings, one slow snapshot, cancellation, observer settlement before cleanup, timer cleanup, sanitized evidence, and successful setup despite a diagnostic-write failure.
- Negative controls failed as intended against the prior implementation, the old 30-second deadline, and removal of observer-error containment. Restoring the candidate passed the full focused file.
- Scripts and targeted test TypeScript checks, targeted lint/format, the source line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674937421) settled green, including the iPhone and iPad screenshot jobs. No failed or pending checks remain at head `9aae24cbf25bf60e5777b9263a9da8c01f5912fc`.
- Two fresh hosted qualification-only runs passed against that exact target, workflow, and harness SHA. Both built the native candidate without reuse, used stable Gateway `2026.10.3` with matching package and lock hashes, passed both UI tests, received all three ordered provider requests, and confirmed cleanup.

| Hosted run | Authentication / client dispatch | Setup response / total RPC | Slow snapshot |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [38674936516](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674936516) | 13.023 s | 34.311 s | Captured once |
| [38674938739](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674938739) | 0.743 s | 2.135 s | Correctly skipped |

The first run exercised a successful request beyond the former 30-second budget. Its slow snapshot retained host/process observations and a delayed Gateway heartbeat. The process sample was unavailable and the lane query failed, but observation did not fail qualification. The 13.023-second authentication delay shows that part of the delay precedes setup dispatch; these client milestones do not prove server-handler entry or isolate the root cause. High host load was present in both runs, so load alone is not a sufficient explanation.

Sanitized evidence is saved in each run's `ios-release-e2e-stock-<run-id>-1` artifact as `ios-release-e2e-proof.json`. These were qualification-only runs; no store upload was performed. The PR remains ready for review and unmerged.

`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.openai-compaction.live.test.ts` > "automatically compacts tool history and resumes from its SQLite checkpoint" failed in extended-stable 2026.9.33 Full Release Validation (release-checks run 38630892166, attempt 1, job [116083346932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38630892166/job/116083346932), lane `native-live-src-agents`, model `gpt-5.6-luna`):

```
AssertionError: expected 'TOOL-MEMORY-c5c52536-e9d2-35e380fa32b0' to be 'TOOL-MEMORY-c5c52536-e9e4-4fff-99d2-3…'
Expected: "TOOL-MEMORY-c5c52536-e9e4-4fff-99d2-35e380fa32b0"
Received: "TOOL-MEMORY-c5c52536-e9d2-35e380fa32b0"
```

The failure is in the `compact` stage (`expect(text).toBe(marker)`). The seed stage completed, auto-compaction ran (two model calls: summary, then answer), and the model returned the marker with the middle `e4-4fff-99` collapsed.

## Root cause

The marker is `TOOL-MEMORY-${randomUUID()}`. After compaction the model has to copy it exactly, either into its own summary or from that summary into the answer. GPT-5.6 sometimes drops or merges characters when it copies long hex runs. #104905 recorded the same failure mode for gateway tool probes. So this test also failed on a 36-character UUID copy, which is not the contract it is meant to prove. Compaction worked. Only the copied UUID was wrong.

## Solution

Use a short random marker (`TOOL-MEMORY-` + 8 uppercase hex characters from `randomBytes(4)`). That still gives 32 bits of randomness, so it is unguessable, and the sibling repeated-compaction test in the same file already uses a short marker. All assertions stay the same: an exact `toBe(marker)` on the compacted and replayed answers, and `checkpoint.summary` must contain the marker.

## Evidence

- CI log above (job 116083346932).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched file. `pnpm tsgo:core:test` is clean.
- Live proof was not run: the test needs an OpenAI key, and this host has none.

## Test cost

No new tests. The live test's model calls stay the same, and the source file gets 28 characters shorter.

prs.title: fix(ai): detach OpenAI stream partial snapshots from live output
prs.body:
Supersedes #142888 (root-cause outcome of the analysis direction recorded there and on #136262).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the opening text of an assistant message doubles on screen when streaming through the OpenAI-responses and OpenAI-completions transports.

The doubling is transient — the closing stream snapshot heals the stored message — so it surfaced only intermittently, and was historically misattributed to provider-side "full-text replay" deltas (including in our own earlier work on #136262).

## User Impact

Live streaming projections (dashboard, channel partials) stop showing doubled message openings. Stored/final messages were already self-healed by the closing snapshot, so persisted output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Boundary stream events carry `partial` so consumers can replace their state wholesale. Both OpenAI transports pushed the transport's **live** AssistantMessage object as that partial, and content deltas mutate their text block **in place before** the delta event is pushed. A consumer following the replace-or-append contract therefore held an object that already contained the next delta, and appending it doubled the text.

The fix detaches the partial snapshot at each transport's single event choke point (responses `trackStream`, completions `pushStreamEvent`) via a shared helper. Boundary events are not per-token, so the copy is bounded. There is no text matching and nothing is suppressed — correct delivery follows by construction. This is the snapshot-semantics half of the direction recorded on #136262: the captured evidence shows the provider does not replay on this endpoint, so no discriminator is needed for this doubling.

## Evidence

- **Wire capture of a real production doubling event** (OpenAI-responses route, every SSE frame logged in the serving path): closed-field enumeration — no provider-side replay frame exists; sequence numbers strictly monotonic; the doubled byte sequence appears **exactly once** on the wire.
- **Transport-core replay**: the captured frames fed through the transport deliver each delta exactly once; a consumer-state simulation over the emitted events reproduces the doubling signature exactly, and it disappears with this fix.
- **New regression tests per transport**: consumer replace/append reconstruction stays byte-exact with the wire text for long and short first deltas, and boundary snapshots never alias live blocks. Red/green verified (reverting the fix fails them).
- **Families**: full `openai-responses-*` + `openai-completions-*` transport test families, 57 files / 716 tests green.

<details>
<summary>Methodology notes (capture procedure, historical misattribution, bounded claims)</summary>

Captured a real production doubling event by recording every SSE frame of every request through a wire-level recorder in the serving path, then locating the request whose window contains the consumer-side doubling signature. For that event: all text deltas are small normal increments, event sequence numbers are strictly monotonic, no anomalous event types appear, and the consumer-fired signature (a delta equal to the already-accumulated text) is byte-identical to a single wire delta — proving client-side double application.

The historical "provider full-text replay" framing for #136262 came from internal-event-level observation, which is precisely the artifact this defect manufactures at that layer. No retained wire-level evidence of a genuine provider-side replay is known to us; claims here are bounded to what the wire capture supports. If a genuine provider replay exists on some endpoint, the same capture tooling applies, and handling it would need a discriminator per the maintainer direction — out of scope here.

</details>

prs.title: test(live): use short random tool probe nonces
prs.body:
## Problem

`src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts` > "runs meaningful prompts across models with available keys" failed in extended-stable 2026.9.33 Full Release Validation (release-checks run 38630892166, attempt 1, job [116083346962](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38630892166/job/116083346962), lane `native-live-src-gateway-profiles-openai-gpt56-ultra`):

```
1. openai/gpt-5.6-terra: Error: tool probe missing nonce: tool-read-alpha-5cd03cdc-3108-48ab-a426-b5a64d28537b tool-read-beta-12b2b4ce-fb0f-4afc-b5b6-845aff0fc54
```

The file contained `tool-read-beta-12b2b4ce-fb0f-4afc-b5b6-845aff0fc54b`. All three tool-read attempts (the existing GPT-5.6 retry from #104905) returned the same reply without the final `b`. `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-5.6-luna` read the same file in the same run and echoed both values correctly.

## Root cause

The probe's prompt and check are consistent: read the file and reply with both values, then check with a case-sensitive `includes` on lowercase `randomUUID()` output. The flaky part is the fixture. Each value carries a 36-character UUID that the model must copy exactly, and GPT-5.6 variants sometimes drop or swap characters in long hex runs. #104905 already added retries for this ("return a different well-formed UUID"). Retries run in the same session, so the model's previous wrong answer is in context, and terra repeated it on every attempt. The tool read itself worked. Only the copy of a long random token failed, and that is not what the probe is meant to prove.

## Solution

- Keep the prefixes, which avoid secret-shaped values, and make the random part 8 hex characters (`randomBytes(4)`) for `nonceA`/`nonceB`. The tool-only follow-up probe reuses these values.
- Apply the same change to the exec/read nonce (`nonceC` becomes `exec-read-<8 hex>`). The model types that value into a shell command and reads it back, so it can fail the same way.
- The same file already uses a short `randomBytes(3)` nonce for the ultra subagent handoff. Each value is still unguessable (32 bits; tool-read requires both, so 64 bits). The check is still an exact substring match, the retry policy is unchanged, and the run still fails when retries run out.

## Evidence

- CI log above (job 116083346962). The reply is quoted from the log.
- With an empty `HOME` and no keys, `scripts/test-live.mts` on the file passes 182 in-file cases. The live sweep fails closed as designed ("selected no runnable live model candidates with usable credentials"). `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean. `pnpm tsgo:core:test` is clean.
- Live proof was not run: the test needs OpenAI keys, and this host has none.

## Test cost

No new tests. The probe's model calls stay the same.
