prs.title: fix(gateway): prepare config restarts outside the restart-signal fence
prs.body:
## Problem

The QA Lab runtime-pair lane (core) failed scenario `config-restart-capability-flip`, codex cell: `restores image_generate after restart and uses it in the same session: timed out after 120000ms` (mock provider).

- 2026.9.33 release-checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38610718735/job/116014305463
- main candidate release-checks run 38572083801 (same scenario)

On the main candidate, the Gateway logged this sequence:

- `config change requires gateway restart (gateway.controlUi.basePath) — preparing`
- `admission closed: restart-signal fence` (13:57:51.524)
- `Waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global held by 71e7070d…` (the lease was taken about 200 ms after the fence closed)
- `restart still deferred … with 1 gateway request(s) active` every 30 s for 3 minutes

Meanwhile `config.get` returned `unavailable during gateway restart`, and no SIGUSR2 was sent until the harness stopped the Gateway. A restart request hung with admission closed.

## Root cause

Lock-order inversion between config restart preparation and config reloads (`src/infra/restart.ts` `emitPreparedGatewayRestart`, `src/gateway/server-reload-restart.ts` `beforeEmit`):

- The deferred config restart ran its preparation (`assertRestartReady` + `prepareRuntimeConfig`) in `beforeEmit`, which runs **after** the deferral closes the restart-signal admission fence.
- `prepareRuntimeConfig` → `withRestartPreparation` (`src/gateway/config-reload.ts`) waits for the plugin lifecycle lease.
- A watcher/config reload takes that lease first and then enters root admission (`runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkAdmission(…, "reload:config")`), which waits while the fence is closed.

The restart held the fence and waited for the lease. The reload held the lease and waited for admission. Both waited until the 300 s deferral deadline. Even after that deadline, the forced attempt closed the fence again synchronously before the waiting reload could run.

## Solution

- `deferGatewayRestartUntilIdle` gets an optional `prepareEmission` hook.
  - The hook runs before each attempt as its own independent root, under the same idle rule the fenced attempt uses, and never under the fence.
  - Each prepared result serves one fenced attempt. Retries prepare again, and new work that appears after preparation discards the prepared result.
  - A stuck preparation is bounded by the same deadline as a stuck attempt.
  - While preparation holds the deferral, it is reported through `onStillPending`.
- The config restart coordinator moves its existing preparation from `beforeEmit` to `prepareEmission`. While preparation is running, the still-deferred warning names it (`restart preparation pending; …`). Emission behavior, failure messages, and supersession checks are unchanged.

Scheduled restarts (`scheduleGatewayRestart`) do not pass the hook, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression `prepares outside the restart-signal fence so lease holders can finish`. Its preparation waits on a "lease" whose holder needs root admission.
  - On the old source it fails: `requestRecoveryRestart` is never called.
  - With the fix it passes.
- New `reports a pending restart preparation instead of waiting silently`. It fails on the old source, which logged nothing.
- `src/gateway/server-reload-restart.test.ts` 7/7 and `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` 127/127 pass. These include the existing deferral, timeout, supersession, and secret-revalidation contracts.
- `src/infra/restart.test.ts`: `cleanStaleGatewayProcessesSync > uses explicit port override` fails locally on both the old and new `restart.ts`. It is unrelated to this change (`restart-stale-pids.ts`, which this PR does not touch).
- Real flow: `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --runtime-pair openclaw,codex --scenario config-restart-capability-flip` passes with the fix. Both cells ran in about 32 s each. Before the fix, the same local run passed in 85–120 s per cell, and the hang did not reproduce locally because it depends on timing.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` are clean.

## Test cost

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-reload-restart.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 62 s wall on a loaded host, most of it Vitest transform and import. The two new tests take about 11 ms and 20 ms and use fake timers only.

Conditional backport candidate for extended-stable/2026.9.33. Source changes cherry-pick cleanly. `server-reload-restart.test.ts` has a trivial import conflict.

## What Problem This Solves

Small, serial Gateway and embedded-agent selections still request 32-class runners even when their complete workload fits 16-class capacity.

## User Impact

Eligible CI jobs request the 16-class while retaining their test inventory, process boundaries, worker limits, and deadlines. No product behavior changes. Realized Blacksmith savings and native latency remain unmeasured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing precise-selection rule to qualified Gateway client/server and embedded-agent configs. Require one or two explicit files per group and a two-worker pin or fallback. Keep parallel work, builds, dist, memory reservations, explicit large-runner requirements, and unqualified configs at their planned capacity. An explicit wider worker pin now prevents downsizing even when a fallback is present. Capacity is checked across the entire packed job; the ownership test continues to check logical shard placement and execution metadata independently of final job sizing.

Correct the CI skill's hosted-offload guidance: the optional rows are security and browser-extension E2E; Control UI unit rows already retain the 8-class.

- Complete current five-file selection replayed through the production shard executor at base `a4d316dc86846952cc2ddd99df026c771ab38900`, using the pinned Bun runtime where selected: 139 tests passed, no skips. The two emitted jobs completed in 292 and 88 seconds.

prs.title: fix(update): reduce snapshot writes on copy-on-write filesystems
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Strict update/Doctor checks and recovery-generation inspection always streamed private SQLite snapshots. This enables copy-on-write cloning when the filesystem and source/destination attributes permit it.

## User Impact

Artifact-preserving snapshots can now share unchanged storage with the source while retaining an independent writable file. Unsupported filesystems or unavailable native copying retain the existing full-copy fallback. Full source comparisons and generation hashes still run; this does not eliminate their read cost.

A source replacement detected during guarded copy admission now stops that snapshot instead of retrying. Those helper errors cannot reliably distinguish source drift from simultaneous destination or cleanup failure, so preserving the original refusal is safer than hiding it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing fs-safe guarded synchronous copier at the canonical snapshot owner, with `clone: "auto"`, exclusive creation, and an owned destination descriptor. Keep the original source pin, resolve admitted aliases to their physical path, and retain destination fsync, source revalidation, private-only checkpointing, WAL coherence checks, and cleanup.

No schema, configuration, protocol, staging-placement, runtime, or dependency changes.

## Evidence

- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0/P1 defects. The implementer and plan reviewer inspected the exact fs-safe 0.26.5 contract directly.
- Regression cases cover synchronous native/fallback copying, independent private writes, sidecar aliases and retargeting, guarded source-admission refusal, and simultaneous source/destination or fsync failures. Existing WAL and replacement tests retain their checks; their copy-completion probe now recognizes native-owned descriptors.
- Focused Testbox execution was stopped after the allocation queued; no tests ran there. [Current-head snapshot CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38675722472/job/116229138783) passed all 81 tests across seven files, including synchronous native/fallback snapshots, quota errors, concurrent writers, worker cleanup, and staging ownership. The initial obsolete `writeSync` quota injection and added type-assertion ratchet violation are corrected; broader CI is still running.
- A real Btrfs synthetic probe with a 32 MiB NOCOW source and a COW destination fell back to `copy-file-range`: auto wrote 33,636,352 bytes versus 33,669,120 for the old streaming path. With matching NOCOW attributes on a fresh private destination, the same guarded API reported `clone` and wrote 49,152 bytes across the same subvolume boundary. A private clone write preserved the source digest; identity checks and cleanup passed.
- The current fs-safe 0.26.5 creates a destination without that attribute parity, so this patch alone still falls back for the mismatched layout. Landing is held pending the dependency-owned repair and its consumption. Idle-WAL preservation, external-writer refusal, and complete lifecycle qualification remain required.

Production delta: +21 lines; test delta: +140 lines. The added production code preserves source-alias admission and error ownership while removing the forced streaming-copy path.

Follow-up outside this PR: make generation evidence owned by snapshot acquisition so repeated full-family reads can be reduced with equivalent change detection. Blindly halving the hash passes is unsafe: committed WAL-prefix snapshots and whole-WAL generation hashes cover different bytes, and normalized backup digests are not interchangeable with committed-content digests.

prs.title: fix(update): Windows updates stop at a refused Reef migration when the state path is deep
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` fails on Windows with `doctor-failed` ("Refused plugin migrations that do not match the immutable action order and authority declared by reef.") when the candidate migration rehearsal runs under a deep state directory.

## User Impact

User impact: Windows updates whose state directory sits at a moderately deep path (for example under `%TEMP%` or a long user profile) can finish the candidate Doctor rehearsal again instead of stopping with a refused Reef migration. This blocks the 2026.10.10-beta.1 Windows packaged-upgrade release checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #168340, candidate Doctor loads plugin migration contracts from a temporary source capture rooted in the rehearsal `TMP`, which is the private update-canary directory. On Windows the nested `captures\openclaw-plugin-build-XXXXXX` template then crosses `CreateDirectoryW`'s 248-character limit. Node namespaces long paths for `mkdir` and file I/O but not for `mkdtemp` (`src/node_file.cc` `Mkdtemp` never calls `ToNamespacedPath`), so only the capture allocation fails with `ENAMETOOLONG`. Reef's doctor contract then fails to load, its declared five migrations no longer match the zero loaded ones, and Doctor refuses.

Plugin source captures now allocate their temporary directories through one helper that passes the `\\?\` extended-length spelling to `mkdtemp` on Windows and returns the ordinary spelling, matching every other capture file operation. POSIX behavior is unchanged.

Update behavior: the fix runs inside the candidate package, so an installed 2026.10.x driver picks it up when it rehearses this candidate; no driver change, migration, or state shape change is involved.

## Evidence

- Release Checks run 38667134742 (candidate d6105820e06), jobs 116203364720 and 116203364839: `upgrade-update.log` shows `failed to load doctor contract for reef from ...\doctor-contract-api.js: ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, mkdtemp '~\openclaw-plugin-captures-<hash>-RLCA7j\captures\openclaw-plugin-build-XXXXXX'` followed by the reef refusal. The rehearsal root is `...\home\.openclaw.update-captures\openclaw-update-canary-<uuid>` (151-154 chars), which puts the template at 254-257 chars.
- Main bisect over scheduled Release Checks: Windows packaged upgrade passed at 23cf1bc3b6d and fails from 3cfb066c022 onward with the same error; #168340 (2cd5dea12c86) is the only capture-placement change in that window. release/2026.10.5 (without #168340) passes the same lane.
- `src/plugins/plugin-source-capture-path.test.ts` allocates a real capture beneath a >240-character root and writes into it; it is added to `test:windows:ci:2`, where `mkdtemp` without the fix fails with `ENAMETOOLONG`. Local `pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-source-capture-path.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 passed, 50ms test time.
- Sibling `pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-source-capture-directory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed (77s wall, unchanged suite). Targeted oxlint/oxfmt clean; `pnpm check:changed` core typecheck and 13 core test graphs passed before my local 15-minute cap; PR CI covers the rest.
- Windows proof: focused `windows/packaged-upgrade` cross-OS dispatch on this head (linked in a comment once complete).
- PR CI `checks-ui-e2e (2/9)` fails in `ui/src/e2e/model-providers-progressive.e2e.test.ts`; the same tests fail on the unrelated PR run 38674766694 at the same base, so it is pre-existing and not touched by this change.

prs.title: fix(browser): initialize configured extension relays on HTTP server startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #112832.

`startBrowserControlServerFromConfig()` bound the HTTP control listener without initializing configured `driver: "extension"` relays, leaving `state.extensionRelays` empty until a browser route later called `ensureExtensionRelayForProfiles()`. After a Gateway restart with `OPENCLAW_EAGER_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1`, the paired Chrome MV3 extension service worker could not reconnect to `ws://127.0.0.1:<relayPort>/extension` until an agent browser request triggered lazy initialization.

## User Impact

Configured Chrome extension relay profiles (`driver: "extension"`) now start listening as soon as the browser HTTP control server starts, allowing the paired Chrome extension service worker to reconnect immediately after a Gateway restart without waiting for a first failing browser tool call. If the relay module or relay auth token fails to initialize during HTTP server startup, the bound HTTP listener closes cleanly and no partial runtime state or bridge auth is published.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Extract `prepareConfiguredExtensionRelays(resolved)` into `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay-bootstrap.ts` and share it between `extensions/browser/src/server.ts` and `extensions/browser/src/control-service.ts`.
- Run `prepareConfiguredExtensionRelays(resolved)` inside the HTTP server startup `try / catch` block before `ensureBrowserControlRuntime` and `setBridgeAuthForPort` so a relay module or token initialization error closes `server` and leaves no half-initialized runtime state.
- Add regression tests in `extensions/browser/src/gateway/browser-request.shared-control-state.test.ts` covering both eager relay initialization on HTTP server startup and live TCP listener rollback when relay module loading fails.

## Real Behavior Proof

Live runtime verification starting `startBrowserControlServerFromConfig()` with `OPENCLAW_EAGER_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1`, a pre-existing paired `credentials/browser-extension-relay.secret`, and profile `chrome: { driver: "extension", cdpPort: 18999 }` before any browser request is issued:

- **Before (`upstream/main`)**: `startBrowserControlServerFromConfig()` binds only control port `18991`; relay port `18999` is not listening (`relayPort (18999) listening: false`, `state.extensionRelays` is `undefined`), and a paired extension WebSocket connection to `ws://127.0.0.1:18999/extension` fails with `ECONNREFUSED`.
- **After (`05570baa44c`)**:

```text
18:54:27 [browser/extension-relay] extension relay for profile "chrome" listening on 127.0.0.1:18999
18:54:27 [browser/server] Browser control listening on http://127.0.0.1:18991/ (auth=token)
18:54:27 [browser/extension-relay] extension authenticated and connected to relay
1. Eager HTTP startup (before any browser request):
   controlPort (18991) listening: true
   relayPort (18999) listening: true
   paired extension WS handshake: {"type":"auth.ok","v":2}
2. After stopBrowserControlServer:
   controlPort (18991) listening: false
   relayPort (18999) listening: false
18:54:27 [browser/extension-relay] extension relay for profile "chrome" listening on 127.0.0.1:18999
18:54:27 [browser/server] Browser control listening on http://127.0.0.1:18991/ (auth=token)
18:54:27 [browser/extension-relay] extension authenticated and connected to relay
3. After restart with existing browser-extension-relay.secret:
   relayPort (18999) listening: true
   paired extension WS reconnect handshake: {"type":"auth.ok","v":2}
```

## Evidence

- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base upstream/main` (passed)
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/browser/src/gateway/browser-request.shared-control-state.test.ts` (9 passed)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` (0 errors)
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/browser/src/server.ts extensions/browser/src/control-service.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay-bootstrap.ts extensions/browser/src/gateway/browser-request.shared-control-state.test.ts` (0 warnings, 0 errors)

prs.title: test(openai): verify Decisions auth across agent harnesses
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Decision credentials and tool results need regression coverage across OpenClaw and Codex when the primary model uses an API key or ChatGPT OAuth.

## User Impact

The documented setup separates primary-model authentication from the Platform API key required by Decisions. It explains both harnesses without implying that a Codex login authorizes Decision requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tests exercise the real OpenAI auth policy and credential selection before the leaf credential resolver: incompatible OAuth and Sign in with ChatGPT profiles are skipped without refresh, while an explicit incompatible binding remains terminal.

Codex bridge tests assemble the real shared Decision tool schema, exercise direct and searchable tool surfaces, preserve typed success/unavailable outcomes, and propagate cancellation. The tool execution boundary is synthetic; these tests do not claim a native model-driven Codex round-trip.

Stack: based on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172748. No production runtime changes.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- One bounded, no-hydration AWS run is preparing the final stack's focused tests. Results will replace this pending status.
- Fresh live Platform API proof returned HTTP 200 from `gpt-6-luna` with predicate, choice, and score answers (396 input tokens, 0 output tokens).
- Personally checked Codex source at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs:53–57,237–254` and `codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses.rs:100–102,140–155`. Native inference uses Responses; Decisions remain an OpenClaw-owned tool capability.
- The native model-driven harness matrix and remote OAuth entitlement are not established by the fresh API probe or mocked bridge tests.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render agent and theme artwork with Solid
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Deterministic agent faces still rendered through Lit, and native consumers could not reuse the existing claw/mark/custom-art selection policy. Pending avatar artwork could also settle through a retired Lit child during palette or sidebar updates.

This ports the face renderer to Solid, adds `ThemeBrandingIcon`, and uses it in command-palette results. Avatar fallback loading stays under its Solid owner. Theme branding still belongs to the existing plain TypeScript owner; the native renderer subscribes to it and explicit branding props remain caller-owned. Agent geometry, host tags, classes and lazy artwork loading are preserved. The two thin legacy entry helpers remain for the still-unported identity renderer; its cutover will retire them.

The reviewed follow-up restores three contracts: custom working/subagent artwork stays at 18px/16px through the legacy display-contents wrapper; changing an artwork URL immediately shows the loading fallback until its replacement is ready; and drawer focus forwards `preventScroll` through the existing tooltip-safe handoff. It does not add another focus owner. Regression tests exercise the actual fetch, sanitization and rasterization path and both plain and tooltip-wrapped focus targets.

Current main `614f559915ff4b6a0b81fd37e1561ba44f5217c8` is integrated by ordinary, conflict-free merge. This includes the canonical reasoning disclosure fixture (`7b9fedd`), clipboard/live-preference fixtures (`459cad7`), and private workspace-path repair (`869029b`), while retaining the prior tooltip owner repair. Main also extends the existing artwork loader to support raster theme backgrounds (`c94f47e`); the artwork SVG regressions pass against that current loader. No test deadline or retry was increased.

## Proof

Candidate: `f4670633621c94b97b8681d0ea4bff1037a08cd7`. The final cleanup makes `renderAgentAvatarFallback` private: its last external caller moved to Solid, while the remaining legacy renderer still calls it internally. The one-keyword correction passed a fresh UI typecheck and isolated Codex review through P2. Replacement-head CI, final production Knip and fresh native admission are pending.

## What Problem This Solves

Global model defaults disappeared while the Models page waited for provider authentication and installed-agent details. This broke the existing progressive-loading behavior even when the saved configuration and model choices were already available.

## User Impact

Users can select and save an already configured default model immediately. Late provider details and catalog refreshes preserve that selection and an open picker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial loading boundary added in #172608 wrapped the whole page. Keep its existing one-shot readiness latch around provider and installed-agent details, while leaving the independent global defaults and setup summary mounted. This changes no domain state or mutation authority and preserves the lazy page boundary.

prs.title: fix(gateway): strip __controlUiReconnectResume from chat.send params before validation
prs.body:
<!--
Closes: #165433
-->

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `chat.send` requests from non-Operator-UI clients (e.g. webchat on a browser reconnect with a preserved `sessionId`) are rejected with `invalid chat.send params: at root: unexpected property '__controlUiReconnectResume'`. `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` only strips the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker when both `value === true` AND `isOperatorUiClient(clientInfo)` returns true; in every other case the `__`-prefixed marker leaks into the AJV-strict `chat.send` schema and the request is dropped before dispatch.

## User Impact
User impact: Webchat and other browser-based reconnect paths that emit the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker now have their messages admitted and dispatched normally on reconnect. No user-visible change for Control UI clients — their behavior is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made
`__controlUiReconnectResume` is an internal `__`-prefixed wire field added by the Control UI to signal "treat this as a reconnect resume, not a fresh run." Such fields should never reach the public `chat.send` schema. The patch decouples "strip the field before validation" from "record that a resume was requested" — the field is now stripped whenever it is present on the input record, and the `resumeRequested` flag is still gated by both the strict-value check and the Operator UI client check, preserving the downstream semantics. The strict-value check is unchanged on purpose so a non-true value (e.g. `false`, `1`, the wrong type) still does not mark a resume even from an Operator UI client.

## Evidence
- Six focused unit tests added in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-server-timing.test.ts` (new file) cover the regression and the surrounding cases: field absent, non-object input, true value with operator UI client, true value with non-operator UI client (the regression), true value with missing `clientInfo`, non-true values with operator UI client, and input-record immutability.
- A local reproduction on the bundled `dist/chat-server-timing-soo795Of.mjs` (the same logic, minified) confirmed the bug and the fix: pre-patch, a `webchat` clientInfo with `__controlUiReconnectResume: true` returned the marker in the result params; post-patch, the marker is stripped and `resumeRequested` is `false`.
- `diff -u` of the patched file vs. upstream main shows changes confined to the `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` function body; no other exports, signatures, or unrelated fields are touched.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Adding a Claw should create ordinary OpenClaw resources and enter the new agent chat without an installed-Claw lifecycle.

## User Impact
Add creates a new numbered agent each time, installs agent-owned files/skills/automations and required shared dependencies, then hands off to chat. Existing plugin and MCP resources remain independently managed. Exceptional trust warnings still require consent.

## Why This Change Was Made
This replaces the earlier plan, review, status, update, and removal lifecycle with a one-way Add operation. Ordinary agent deletion owns agent-scoped cleanup. The foundation in #171622 is merged; the UI follows in #171600.

## Evidence
- The previous hosted run at `3a0e0a590d6` failed two new approval-routing E2E cases because the shared fixture lost its plugin registry between tests. On this head, each case owns a fresh Gateway and the real-Gateway suite passes 4/4; repository test TypeScript shards pass.
- Focused stateless Add and package cleanup tests pass 33/33. Concurrent direct Adds create distinct numbered agents (Gateway Add suite 18/18). Core typecheck passes.
- This stack removes an orphan Windows-shim poll left behind by an earlier private-control hook; the focused Windows process suite passes 16/16. A Claw plugin-batch test fixture now supplies the required agent manifest; its suite passes 16/16 and the Claws test typecheck passes.
- Current head `d6a0835a2ff` includes main at `159e4a53b3c` and a deterministic Gateway timing fixture. The exact Linux merge-ref reproduced the old failure (2/4 red) and passes the full timing file 82/82 after the fix. On the merged core tree, focused stateless Add and plugin-batch tests pass 25/25.
- A staged plugin-batch preparation failure previously left a newly installed plugin behind because rollback reused a closed batch. The new stage/compensation regression failed before the fix and now passes; its focused suite passes 10/10, with core and Claws test typechecks passing.
- Exact-head hosted run [38674113277](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38674113277) completed with one failed test shard, `checks-node-changed-compact-small-18-3`; the required `openclaw/ci-gate` is consequently red. Its nine `test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts` cases reject `cron.add` with `Automation requires a stored inference account`. The same focused file fails 9/9 with that error on isolated clean `main` at `527d11de3f5`; no Claws code owns that test. The standalone main-regression repair is being investigated separately. This is inherited evidence, not a passing CI claim.
- The earlier real Add-to-chat recording and before/after screenshots are linked in #171600. They are prior-head live proof, not a claim of an exact-head live recording. The restacked UI head passes 5/5 bundled browser E2E tests across mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop, including Add-to-chat.
- This PR has no Lobster extension, pnpm lock/workspace, or dependency-patch diff. Hosted CI and current-head review remain required before landing.

prs.title: fix(openrouter): cache prompts for Anthropic latest aliases
prs.body:
Fixes #172642

## What Problem This Solves

OpenRouter Anthropic `~…-latest` aliases miss the stable prompt-cache checkpoint, causing repeated session prompts to lose explicit cache reuse.

## User Impact

Canonical Anthropic refs and `~anthropic/claude-*-latest` aliases, with or without the `openrouter/` qualifier, retain the same stable-prefix cache breakpoint through request building and wrapper application. The final payload marks the stable block and leaves the volatile suffix unmarked. Non-Anthropic models and custom proxy routes keep their existing behavior. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the shared Chat Completions compatibility resolver and OpenRouter's wrapper must classify the model before message conversion removes cache-boundary information. They now use the same `normalizeOpenRouterModelFamilyId` implementation as the other OpenRouter family checks. This covers direct and managed request builders; the upstream API model ID remains unchanged.

Move the existing normalizer unchanged into the model-catalog normalization owner and expose it through the existing lightweight `model-ref-parse` SDK entrypoint so bundled OpenRouter and core share one implementation without a core-to-plugin runtime import. That entrypoint is already inventoried and private-local-only; no public API baseline or new subpath changes are needed. Remove the superseded raw-prefix helper and keep its already-normalized Kilocode caller equivalent. Production delta: +27/-29 (net -2); tests: +68/-36; docs: +3/-1. No background or deferred effects are added.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: the wrapper and builder compatibility resolver checked raw IDs, while the existing normalizer already handled aliases. Normalization history: `d92d68ac7766`; builder marker contract: `b7848ca6b197`.
- Addressed ClawSweeper's P2 “Normalize alias classification before the builder removes cache boundaries.” The resolver now preserves the boundary until the builder creates the marked stable block, preserving retention, transient-carrier, and string-only decisions before wrapper application.
- `src/llm/providers/stream-wrappers/proxy.test.ts`: `preserves the cache breakpoint through request building for OpenRouter model %s` now runs the real request builder plus wrapper with OpenClaw’s production endpoint resolver in a scoped transport host and checks the complete final messages and unchanged wire model ID. Canonical/qualified/tilde refs retain the breakpoint; non-Anthropic and custom proxy controls remain unmarked. This replaces the former synthetic-payload proof.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts`: `preserves the stable cache breakpoint for OpenRouter model %s` captures the direct transport's final payload for canonical and tilde aliases, including the stable-system and user markers, uncached suffix, and absence of internal sentinel text.
- Changed-file syntax lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config --config .oxlintrc.json <changed TS files>`), `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed. Deslop complete. Fresh isolated autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings; complete builder/converter/marker-policy source was included.
- PR CI is the test gate for these regressions, affected core/provider tests, typechecking, and build/package boundaries. Updated exact-head CI: [run 38665568237](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38665568237) passed on `eb84eceaefb43079e70e8e18344722d6b2831494`: 58 jobs passed, 23 skipped, zero failures, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. All selected Node regressions, production/test typechecks, lint, build, docs/boundaries, and UI E2E passed. Run elapsed: 18m24s.
- Exact-head request-build regressions passed in [job 116197453270](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38665568237/job/116197453270): canonical and qualified Anthropic refs, both tilde alias forms, non-Anthropic controls, and custom-route controls. CI case times: bare tilde 107 ms; qualified tilde 76 ms.
- Local tests, local typechecks, production-revert negative controls, and live Gateway/Crabbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases or Gateways were started; no measured live cache-hit or billing result is claimed.

Prior-head CI's clipboard failure was inherited: [PR job 116177021091](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659315496/job/116177021091) and [scheduled-main run 38654297528, job 116160591100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38654297528/job/116160591100) both fail `chat-flow.clipboard.e2e.test.ts:386`, “shows a visible error when the workspace header copy-path clipboard action fails,” because `getByText('Copy path')` matches a menu item and hidden tooltip. No UI files are changed here. The clipboard failure did not recur on the final head. No CI rerun or merge was requested.

CI repair: run `38664782873` passed the new alias/canonical/non-Anthropic payload cases but exposed two custom-route fixture failures. The expanded fixture had used the reusable transport library’s inert host defaults; it now supplies the real endpoint policy through a scoped host. Assertions and production behavior were kept intact. The replacement exact-head CI run passed the corrected fixture and the full selected checks.

prs.title: fix(agents): drop throttled exec update events
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: exec live output throttling capped detailed payloads, but throttled `tool_execution_update` events still emitted generic tool/item updates with no new user-visible payload.
- Solution: make throttled exec updates a true no-op until the next allowed live update or final result.
- What changed: `handleToolExecutionUpdate` now returns before emitting generic exec update traffic when the live exec update throttle suppresses the detailed output, with regression coverage for global agent events and `onAgentEvent` emissions.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): final exec result events, command completion items, non-exec tool updates, and the existing live exec output size cap are unchanged.

## Motivation

- #84850 captured a 60s gateway sample with average CPU at 83.66%, 42/60 samples at or above 100% CPU, and 0.00 kB/s average read I/O during an embedded exec tool run. Dropping redundant throttled update events reduces avoidable gateway projection/broadcast work in that hot path.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #84850
- Related #78645
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Gateway CPU saturation from #84850 during embedded exec tool output. Throttled exec updates should not continue producing generic tool/item event traffic when they carry no new visible output.
- Real environment tested: Local Linux OpenClaw worktree on Node 24, using the repo Vitest wrapper plus the redacted pidstat/gateway log evidence from the affected run.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, and `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Copied terminal capture from the patched worktree:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  76 passed (76)

$ git diff --check
(no output; exit 0)

$ codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted
No discrete correctness issues were found in the current local changes.
```

- Observed result after fix: The regression test proves the first exec live update still emits visible output, while the next update inside the throttle window emits no additional global agent events and no additional `onAgentEvent` traffic. Final result handling remains covered by the existing exec result tests.
- What was not tested: I did not rerun the private 60s live CPU-saturation gateway session because the original setup/session details are local and redacted; the fix was verified at the exec tool update seam that emits the redundant events.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Redacted source evidence from #84850:

```text
pidstat summary:
rows=60
avg_cpu=83.66
avg_usr=79.42
avg_sys=4.25
avg_rd=0.00
cpu_ge_100_count=42
max_cpu=190.0

redacted gateway correlation:
2026-05-21T05:07:47.187+00:00 agent/embedded embedded run tool start: runId=[redacted run id] tool=exec toolCallId=REDACTED
2026-05-21T05:08:04.330+00:00 agent/embedded embedded run tool end: runId=[redacted run id] tool=exec toolCallId=REDACTED
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: the live exec throttle suppressed detailed output but still allowed generic exec update item/tool events to be emitted for every throttled update.
- Missing detection / guardrail: existing coverage checked output truncation/throttling but did not assert that suppressed updates stop all generic event emission.
- Contributing context (if known): #78645 bounded live exec output payloads, but redundant event emission could still keep gateway event projection hot during high-volume exec output.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a second exec update inside `LIVE_EXEC_UPDATE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` emits no global agent events and no `onAgentEvent` traffic.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the redundant CPU work starts at the embedded tool update handler before gateway websocket fanout sees the event.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing exec output throttling tests cover payload capping but not generic event suppression.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Exec tool output updates inside the live update throttle window are dropped completely instead of sending generic no-payload progress events. Start, allowed live update, and final result events are preserved.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[exec update inside throttle] -> [generic tool/item events] -> [gateway projection/broadcast work]

After:
[exec update inside throttle] -> [no emitted event] -> [next allowed update or final result closes state]
```

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No

2. Run `git diff --check`.
3. Run `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.

### Expected

- First exec live update emits visible command output.
- A throttled follow-up exec update emits no generic event traffic.
- Final exec result behavior remains unchanged.

### Actual

- Targeted wrapper passed: 2 files, 76 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed with no output.
- Autoreview found no discrete correctness issues.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [x] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: allowed exec live update still emits output; throttled exec update emits no global or local agent event traffic; final exec output/result tests still pass.
- Edge cases checked: existing large-output truncation and final output redaction coverage still passes in the same target file.
- What you did **not** verify: private live CPU-saturation rerun from the original affected setup.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Suppressing throttled updates could hide command progress between allowed live updates.
  - Mitigation: the first allowed update and final command result remain emitted; only no-payload updates inside the existing throttle window are dropped.

prs.title: feat(provider): add Databricks Unity Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #155633

## Problem and user impact

Organizations routing inference through Databricks Unity Gateway currently hand-author workspace routes, credentials, transport and model metadata. This adds provider-specific onboarding and model resolution through an externally distributed plugin.

Operators install `@openclaw/databricks-provider`, supply `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`, and run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice databricks-token`. Models use `databricks/<catalog>.<schema>.<model-service>`.

Same-workspace onboarding preserves existing routes, APIs, model entries, aliases and primary selections. Fresh setup uses `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1` with `system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`. Non-interactive onboarding refuses reuse of a saved profile when `DATABRICKS_HOST` selects a different workspace, and rejects invalid explicit hosts before persistence. Trusted manual provider-config edits remain operator-controlled routing changes; this does not introduce immutable workspace identity in the credential format.

## Implementation and distribution

- Databricks host validation, auth, onboarding and model resolution stay in `extensions/databricks`.
- Reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible streaming transport and credential store.
- Follows the in-repo-source / external npm and ClawHub package pattern used by official providers such as Cerebras and Radius; excluded from the core npm tarball.
- Adds `DATABRICKS_HOST` to untrusted workspace `.env` filtering, with a regression. Credential environment filtering comes from the manifest.
- No new external runtime dependencies, generic transport, credential owner, schema or migration. The lockfile adds only the workspace importer and existing `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency.

## Current candidate

Head `edda4d7bf4c717a627015024ab7c61ed9ef27a43`, rebased onto main `9828e28906f50d674625bb1474814bd5c4b4681e` on October 13, 2026. Conflicts were confined to generated config baseline artifacts and resolved through their generator. Package version/build compatibility is aligned to `2026.10.2`; minimum host remains `>=2026.9.6`. Plugin inventory was regenerated.

Databricks production code and its tests are byte-identical to previously reviewed head `ad52f68faf19ccdf8ca0315201561927739f7e72`. Prior-head CI is historical evidence, not current-head CI.

## Live installed-package proof — October 13

Executed against a real Databricks workspace using the current candidate. The token existed only in the child process environment; onboarding used `--secret-input-mode ref`. Workspace and token are redacted.

| Boundary | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Core runtime build | Completed successfully, 83.3 seconds |
| Release-pipeline plugin pack | `openclaw-databricks-provider-2026.10.2.tgz`, 8 files, 3 runtime JS modules, manifest, package metadata, README and 2 assets; no runtime dependencies |
| Managed install | `plugins install npm-pack:<tarball> --force --accept-capabilities`, exit 0 |
| Runtime identity | `plugins inspect databricks --runtime --json`: loaded, global origin, installed `node_modules/@openclaw/databricks-provider/dist/index.js`, provider `databricks`, no diagnostics |
| Source exclusion | Both bundled discovery and bundled source overlays disabled throughout install, onboarding and agent turns |
| Onboarding | Exit 0, primary `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`, `openai-completions`, environment SecretRef; token absent from `openclaw.json` |
| Streaming and real tool round trip | `agent exec` exited 0; two HTTP 200 `text/event-stream` responses; exactly one successful `read` call; final reply exactly matched random file nonce `DBX-baf85764f87acf9d` |
| Non-catalog model | `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-6` resolved dynamically; real streamed agent turn exited 0 and replied `DYNAMIC_OK` |
| Invalid explicit workspace | Browser URL containing `?o=1234` rejected with exit 1 before inference; active `openclaw.json` SHA-256 unchanged |

This proves local package installation and real inference through the installed runtime. It does not claim that the package is published or that catalog-linked official publisher trust has been established.

## Installed-runtime authority and stable-upgrade proof

Using the same packed plugin with bundled discovery and source overlays disabled:

- Started with published latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.2` (`b8952d4`), created an existing Databricks Serving route and saved synthetic workspace-A credential through its published SDK, then installed the candidate and ran candidate onboarding. Exit 0; deep comparisons confirmed provider route/API/model metadata, primary selection, aliases/model entries and saved credential including workspace metadata were unchanged.
- Positive control: saved workspace-A credential was reused successfully without a token environment variable.
- Workspace-B selection without a fresh token exited 1 before network access; active configuration hash was unchanged.
- Hostile cwd `.env` supplied an attacker workspace and token. A benign dotenv witness was loaded, proving the actual cwd loader ran, while `DATABRICKS_HOST` stayed absent. Onboarding exited 1 for missing trusted workspace; configuration hash was unchanged.
- A Node preload denied and recorded fetch, HTTP(S) and socket connection attempts. Both negative cases recorded `attempts: []`; it did not modify provider auth/config logic. Synthetic credentials were used for these boundary probes.
- The real-token live run above was separately scanned across 23 isolated state files: zero occurrences of the supplied token.

## Validation

- Focused provider, real-transport loopback and workspace `.env` suites: 28 tests passed across 3 files. Combined wall time 80.44 seconds on a heavily loaded macOS arm64 host, Node 26.5. Provider files: 19 tests, 28.32 seconds wall, individual transport scenario 416 ms. No new tests were added in the rebase.
- Extension package-boundary production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and changed-source formatting passed.
- Config baseline, plugin inventory and version-sync checks passed.
- Full docs checks passed: formatting, Markdown/MDX, glossary, links, config examples and changelog checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Fresh independent review was completed. Findings were checked against owning paths:

- The proposed interactive SecretRef failure did not reproduce through the registered auth method with source overlays disabled and an explicit plugin load path. The reviewer retracted it.
- The proposed dynamic API override failure is prevented by core's `applyConfiguredProviderOverrides`; the final resolution probe retained `anthropic-messages` and the configured route. No duplicate override was added to the plugin.
- The proposed immutable credential/workspace binding would change the trusted manual-config contract and credential semantics. The implemented guard covers onboarding workspace selection, not arbitrary operator edits; that scope is explicit above.

Current-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38397087861) completed with 167 successful jobs, 22 skipped jobs and 6 failed jobs (5 shards plus the aggregate gate). The Databricks shard, production/test types, lint, package boundaries, docs, source contracts and npm-lock checks passed. The failing shards were OpenAI realtime auth fixtures (missing admitted database worker), Codex dynamic-tool host instructions, node-worker launch wire timeout, Telegram emoji gateway timeout, and QA POSIX SIGTERM lifecycle timeout. These are outside the Databricks diff; only the OpenAI failure was independently reproduced and repaired in separate #171064 (18 unchanged tests pass). Other failures are attributed by hosted logs and unchanged source scope, not claimed baseline reproductions. Dependency approval remains separate from the failed CI gate.

## Limits and maintainer decision

This is Unity Gateway support. Existing workspace Serving configuration is preserved, but broader Serving compatibility belongs to dependent #163202, which still requires its own repair, restack and validation. OAuth token minting/refresh, automatic live model discovery and per-workspace pricing are outside this change; unknown model services use fallback metadata.

The remaining product decision is whether Databricks receives official provider catalog sponsorship and in-repository maintenance. Maintainer edits are enabled. If accepted, the final head requires the existing maintainer dependency-change approval path; publishing/release is a separate action.

prs.title: [codex] Expire Telegram message-cache plugin state
prs.body:
## Summary
- gives Telegram prompt-context message-cache plugin-state rows a seven-day TTL
- normalizes existing no-expiry rows in a TTL-enabled namespace on the next write so upgraded `telegram.message-cache` rows can age out too
- preserves sibling namespace budgets and adds focused coverage for the Telegram message-cache persistent store options

Refs openclaw/openclaw#87332 and openclaw/openclaw#87357.

## Notes
Current `main` already contains the generic plugin-state cap fix from `e3395867507` (`fix(plugin-state): evict current namespace on plugin row cap`). This PR addresses the remaining `telegram.message-cache` permanence angle from #87332.

The follow-up commit also addresses the review concern about pre-existing `expires_at = NULL` rows. When a namespace writes with a TTL, plugin state now updates live rows in that same namespace that were previously immortal to expire at the same deadline as the write. That keeps the upgrade path bounded without touching sibling namespaces.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts -t 'plugin-state store|persistent'`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts -t 'default TTL|Telegram sibling|plugin row cap|plugin overflow'`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts`

Behavior addressed: Telegram message-cache plugin-state entries now get a TTL instead of being permanent live rows, and old no-expiry message-cache rows receive a bounded expiry after the namespace writes under the new TTL policy.
Real environment tested: local macOS source worktree at `upstream/main`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: focused Vitest and oxfmt commands above.
Evidence after fix: Telegram message-cache tests passed for persistent/default store coverage; plugin-state tests passed for TTL normalization, sibling namespace budget, and plugin cap behavior.
Observed result after fix: default Telegram message-cache plugin state opens with namespace `telegram.message-cache`, max entries `3000`, and a seven-day default TTL; existing no-expiry rows in that namespace are assigned the new expiry deadline on the next TTL write.
What was not tested: live Telegram traffic or a production SQLite file from a real user profile.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Solid tool-result views still sent built-in controls through a Lit template and directive before returning to Solid. Both consumers now render through native `PluginSurface`. Defaults and companion controls keep their originating Solid owner; the existing `PluginView` continues to own selection, callback revocation, operation lifetime, and recovery. The transparent span required by direct-child CSS selectors is preserved. Hidden retained surfaces park replacement selection until reveal, combining explicit and inherited presentation. Delegated default cleanup removes only its bounded DOM range, preserving the plugin’s own toolbar and status nodes. Existing plugin callback revocation remains with its current owner. Ordinary same-revision refresh and presentation-only hiding preserve the mounted view. Genuine deselection or owner retirement still revokes callbacks immediately and may reset plugin-local state while hidden; that is an accepted authority boundary.

Delete the unused replacement directive and test-only no-provider Lit fallback. The migrated regressions mount actual native owners and preserve raw SDK props, session identity, default delegation, drafts, revocation, and cleanup. The remaining 18-line Lit contribution helper serves `chat-pane-embedded-panels.ts`; legacy default/companion mounting still serves the `solidContent` values supplied by `chat-view.tsx`. These are explicit chat migration boundaries. No startup import, page registration, dependency, host tag, or CSS class is added.

The identity and tool-result fixtures use the real mixed-shell application context boundary. Canonical main now owns the end-follow fixture in full; that file is no longer in this PR’s diff. The mobile System busyness case taps its controls; desktop cases retain clicks, and the real touch drag and all placement/no-page-scroll assertions remain. Canonical main supplies the French Workboard selector correction.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |

The final parking and delegated-DOM repair passed a focused P0–P2 review with complete owner, test, projection, bridge, and SDK context; no actionable findings. The test-only presentation restoration also passed independent P0–P2 review with complete context and final source verification. |

The original defect was established by source review; no baseline rerun under the campaign budget. |

prs.title: fix(telegram): first DM message lands in root chat when the client creates the topic separately
prs.body:
Closes #169443

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Telegram threaded mode (`has_topics_enabled: true`) the user's first DM message is answered in the root chat and the topic the client just created stays empty, when the client sends `forum_topic_created` and the message as two separate updates.

Telegram for Android (observed since 2026-10-09, 12 of 12 attempts, reproducible on demand) creates the topic and then delivers the message **without** `message_thread_id`:

```json
{"message_id": 500, "date": 1760000000, "chat": {"id": 1001, "type": "private"}, "from": {"id": 1001, "is_bot": false},
 "message_thread_id": 500, "is_topic_message": true,
 "forum_topic_created": {"name": "hello", "icon_color": 0, "is_name_implicit": true}}
```

```json
{"message_id": 501, "date": 1760000000, "chat": {"id": 1001, "type": "private"}, "from": {"id": 1001, "is_bot": false},
 "text": "hello"}
```

`resolveTelegramMessageThreadSpec` resolves the second update to `{ scope: "dm" }` without an id, so the turn runs in the root DM session, the reply goes to the main chat, and the user later opens an empty topic and continues without the original message. Clients that deliver the first message inside the topic (with `message_thread_id`) were never affected.

## User Impact

User impact: a new DM conversation started from such a client now runs in the topic the client created. The session key, reply, typing indicator and auto label all target that topic, the same as when the first message arrives inside the topic.

Scope of the adoption is deliberately narrow:

- private chats only; group/forum and channel Direct Messages resolution is unchanged;
- the `forum_topic_created` service message must come from a human user (bot-created topics are ignored);
- the adopted message must come from the same user, have a larger `message_id` than the service message, and arrive within 3 seconds by `date`;
- a message that arrives inside the topic clears the pending adoption (normal clients);
- the decision is made **once per bot account at ingress admission** and persisted with the spooled update, so lane key, authorization, message context, session and delivery all read the same topic fact, before and after a restart;
- a `forum_topic_created` update whose window was already spent never rearms adoption when it is inspected again (drain, retries);
- both per-account maps are bounded (512 entries).

## Why This Change Was Made

The receiving bot account's ingress monitor (`createTelegramIngressMonitor`, one per account in polling and webhook transports) is the only place that knows the account and sees every update exactly once at admission, before the lane key is derived. The adoption state (`pending` by `chat:user`, `consumed` by `chat:createdMessageId`) therefore lives in that monitor's closure (`extensions/telegram/src/dm-topic-adopt.ts`); there is no module-level state shared between accounts, so a topic observed by bot A can never admit a root message sent to bot B (and `requireTopic`/topic allowlists for bot B keep rejecting it exactly as on `main`).

The decision is recorded on the message object (`WeakMap`) and written to the durable spool payload as the optional field `adoptedDmThreadId` (payload version unchanged). `deserialize` and `deriveLaneKey` restore it before lane inspection, so a replay after restart derives the same `telegram:<chat>:topic:<id>` lane as the stored claim and the row is dispatched instead of being rejected as `TelegramIngressPayloadError`. `resolveTelegramMessageThreadSpec` only reads that fact (`getTelegramAdoptedDmThreadId`), so every consumer behind the resolver (session key, authorization, message context, native commands, delivery) sees the topic without any further derivation. `bot/helpers.ts` gains the lookup call only.

## Evidence

- Inbound handler regression (`bot.create-telegram-bot.native-pipeline.test.ts`, "client-created DM topic adoption through the inbound handler"): the real account ingress monitor admits `forum_topic_created` 500, root message 501 and a later root message 502 from a private chat **without** `chat.is_forum` (so `withResolvedTelegramForumFlag` copies the message before `authorizeInboundMessage`); 501 reaches the model with session key `agent:main:main:thread:42001:500` and its reply is sent with `message_thread_id: 500`, while 502 runs in the root DM session and is sent without a thread. With `direct.<chat>.requireTopic: true`, 501 is admitted into topic 500 and 502 is dropped before any outbound call (the adopted topic feeds the same `requireTopic`/topic-config gate as a native `message_thread_id`). Before this revision the adopted fact lived in a `WeakMap` keyed by the admitted message object and was lost on that copy.
- Redelivery after a failed durable append (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "keeps the adopted topic for a redelivery after every durable append attempt failed"): the account monitor admits `forum_topic_created` 500, then every spool append attempt for root message 501 fails (the transport fails closed and Telegram redelivers); the redelivered 501 is a freshly parsed object with no symbol/WeakMap association, and it is still admitted into lane `telegram:1001:topic:500` with `adoptedDmThreadId: 500`, resolves to `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }` and dispatches once, with no failed rows. The decision is recorded per account by `chat:message_id` (bounded map) in addition to the message object. Unit case (`dm-topic-adopt.test.ts`, "adopts a redelivered copy of the decided message after a failed durable append"): the redelivered copy is adopted while the next root message stays root. The helper-level per-account case was removed in favour of the two-account ingress test.
- Durable row compatibility (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "replays legacy spool rows without adoptedDmThreadId unchanged and restores it from new rows"): a spool row written before this change (no `adoptedDmThreadId`) replays in lane `telegram:1001` and resolves to `{ scope: "dm" }` with no failed rows; a row carrying `adoptedDmThreadId: 500` replays in lane `telegram:1001:topic:500` and resolves to `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }`. The payload version is unchanged: the field is optional, old rows are read as before, and an older reader simply ignores it.
- Normalization and serialization (`thread-spec.test.ts`, "keeps the adopted topic on normalized message copies but not in serialized JSON"): the fact survives `withResolvedTelegramForumFlag` (a spread copy) and is absent from `JSON.stringify` and `structuredClone` output, so durable rows carry it only as explicit payload metadata.
- Account isolation (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "scopes client-created DM topic adoption to the receiving bot account"): bot A admits `forum_topic_created` 500 from user 1001; the same user's root message 501 admitted by bot B within the window stays in lane `telegram:1001` and resolves to `{ scope: "dm" }` (no topic fact reaches bot B's authorization), while bot A's copy of 501 lands in `telegram:1001:topic:500`.
- Restart replay regression (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "adopts a client-created DM topic at admission and keeps it through restart replay"): admit 500, admit 501 → claim lane `telegram:1001:topic:500` with payload `adoptedDmThreadId: 500`; abort the owner before dispatch, close the state database (fresh monitor, fresh adoption state, re-parsed update objects) → replay dispatches 501 once in lane `telegram:1001:topic:500`, resolver returns `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }`, no failed rows. With the durable restore removed, this test fails (the replayed row never reaches dispatch), so it demonstrates the failing base and the passing head.
- Idempotency (`dm-topic-adopt.test.ts`, "does not rearm the window when the consumed service message is resolved again"): resolve 500 → adopt 501 → resolve 500 again (fresh object too) → 502 within the window is not adopted.
- Resolver boundary (`thread-spec.test.ts`): adopted root message resolves to `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }` on repeated resolution; the next root message and a never-adopted message stay `{ scope: "dm" }`. The former duplicated unit cases were removed; unit tests keep only the edge cases (message inside the topic, 3 s window, older/lower `message_id`, bot-created topic, other user, group chat, bounded maps, per-account state).
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/dm-topic-adopt.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/thread-spec.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts --reporter=dot` → 3 files, 42 passed; `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.native-pipeline.test.ts -t "client-created DM topic adoption"` → 2 passed. `oxfmt` and `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on the touched files clean.
- Local full `pnpm check:changed` was not completed because the development host hit its memory limit; the full verification is the CI run on this PR.
- Provenance / durable transport admission (f7786a16cfe: polling offsets and webhook acknowledgments follow committed spool writes, with shared replay and retry ownership): this change keeps that contract and intentionally adds one admission-time decision. The receiving account's ingress monitor decides once, during admission inspection and before lane derivation, whether a root DM message belongs to the topic its author just created; the fact is stored in the durable row as the optional `adoptedDmThreadId` field and restored before lane inspection and authorization on replay, so acknowledgment still follows the committed append and replay/retry ownership is unchanged. The reason is the client behaviour in #169443: the topic is created by a separate service update and the first message arrives at the root chat without `message_thread_id`, so the fact cannot be derived from the message alone at replay time. Decisions are also retained per account by `chat:message_id`, so a redelivery after a failed append (transport fails closed) reaches the same topic.
- Live behavior (redacted gateway log, 2026-10-11 23:08 UTC): the same adoption semantics run as a local dist patch on a production gateway (OpenClaw 2026.9.7), **not** a build of this branch; this excerpt shows the two inbound updates, the adoption, and the reply delivered into the adopted topic. Chat/user ids → 1001, message ids → 500/501/502, thread → 500, host and bot names removed. Restart replay has no live stand and is covered by the regression test above. A run on the Telegram Test Server with this branch is not provided and is not planned by the author; the remaining proof items (candidate Test Server evidence, authorization negative controls at delivery, latest-stable state upgrade) are left to the maintainers' judgement.

```text
23:08:30.037 [telegram][diag] isolated polling worker update received updateId=…234 queued=1   # forum_topic_created, message 500, message_thread_id 500
23:08:30.045 [telegram][diag] isolated polling offset queued updateId=…234
23:08:30.123 [telegram][diag] isolated polling worker update received updateId=…235 queued=1   # root message 501, no message_thread_id
23:08:30.124 [dm-topic-adopt] adopted chat=1001 user=1001 message=501 thread=500 topicCreatedBy=500 delaySec=0
23:08:30.229 Inbound message telegram:1001 -> @bot (direct, 4 chars)
23:08:37.824 post-run flush start session=agent:…:telegram:direct:1001:thread:1001:500
23:08:38.023 telegram outbound send ok accountId=default chatId=1001 messageId=502 operation=sendRichMessage deliveryKind=text threadId=500 chunkCount=1
```

- Docs: one paragraph in `docs/channels/telegram/threads-and-sessions.md` (unchanged in this revision).

prs.title: fix(workboard): completing a card with an over-long stored run id fails after committing terminal state
prs.body:
Related: #172203

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `workboard.cards.complete` fails with a run-id normalization error for cards whose stored execution carries a run id longer than the notification bound (e.g. a 164-character id against the 120-character bound), after the terminal proof/DONE state has already been committed — leaving a completed card behind a failed call.

## User Impact

User impact: completing a card with any stored run id now succeeds — the card reaches `done` with its proof, the completion notification replays the **exact** stored identity (so run-id subscriptions and card alerts keep matching), and full provenance stays on the card.

## Why This Change Was Made

`completeDirect` copies `cardRunId(existing)` (card.runId or execution.runId — unbounded by execution normalization) into the completed notification, while `normalizeNotification` bounded notification run ids at 120 characters. Producer and consumer did not share the same admission rule: when the stored identity exceeded the bound, the completed notification failed normalization — on the published 2026.9.9/2026.10.2 builds after the terminal state had committed (#172203).

Revision 2 aligns the rules per the review's P2 direction: notification run ids are identity references matched by exact equality (`workboard.notificationEvents` subscriptions, card alerts) — not display text — so `normalizeNotification` now admits run ids through `normalizeRunId` (the shared 512-character admission helper upstream introduced in the meantime) instead of the old 120-character bound, and the three notification producers keep copying the full stored identity. Truncation was removed: a capped reference would have silently dropped the completed event for subscribers of the real run id (`notificationEvents` matches by exact equality) and broken `card-alerts.ts` matching.

## Evidence

- New regression tests (store level, deterministic):
  - `completes cards whose stored run id exceeds the old notification bound`: a card whose execution carries a 121-character run id (the exact shape the review called out for subscription replay) completes successfully; the completed notification replays the exact id; a subscription for that id receives the completed event, while a distinct same-prefix run id stays isolated (no cross-delivery).
  - `bounds blocked-notification run ids copied from stored execution identity` → renamed semantics: the blocked notification path replays the exact identity too.
  - `loads pre-existing notifications and completes long-run-id cards after upgrade`: data-model compatibility — a store holding a notification written under the old 120-character bound plus a card with a long stored execution run id keeps loading (legacy notification intact) and completes with both run ids present.
- Full workboard suite green on head `5d6312cd8ef` (merged with current main): 30 passed + 1 skipped files, 324 passed + 11 skipped tests, including the review's own oversized-notification heal test. `oxlint` on touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Merge with current main verified: upstream's parallel `normalizeRunId`/`MAX_RUN_ID_LENGTH = 512` helper is adopted verbatim in `normalizeNotification`, and the notification producers keep copying the full stored identity.

## Risk and Compatibility

- Existing stored notifications (all written under the old 120-character bound) load unchanged — covered by the upgrade test.
- Notification run ids may now be up to 512 characters (matching execution admission's practical ceiling); subscription run ids remain bounded at 160 by their own admission rule, so subscribers reference prefixes/subsets as before.
- No behavior change for run ids ≤ 120 characters (the overwhelming majority).

## LOC

production +3 / −4 across 2 files (plus merge); tests +77 / −16 in 1 file. No docs or generated code.

## Not Tested

- No live Gateway qualification against published 2026.9.9/2026.10.2 builds; the store-level regression pins the boundary the report's fixture recipe exercises (create → complete with an over-long stored run id), and the subscription-replay test pins the exact-match consumer behavior the revision feedback identified.

prs.title: fix(gateway): lighten session event row snapshots
prs.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?
- High-frequency session event broadcasts rebuild full gateway session rows, including child-session and transcript-heavy work that event snapshots do not always need.

Why does this matter now?

## What Problem This Solves

Copy and loading adapters still import Lit to wrap existing Solid components in redundant templates. Return their existing Solid directives directly and keep the tooltip template type inside the designated interop module. Hosts, copy behavior, loading states, and lazy boundaries are preserved; no dependencies are added.

The coupled drawer correction uses the existing `focusWithoutTooltip` helper for programmatic navigation focus. Fixture corrections wait for actual readiness while preserving behavioral assertions. Failure-only sidebar and menu diagnostics retain the original snapshots, assertions, and timeouts. Provider facade cleanup follows the test and consumer cutovers in #172358 and #172250 in a separate focused change. This PR keeps the captured main provider implementation and canonical gallery deletion, removing its duplicate wrapper-only provider change.

## Focus correction

Final manual review found that the drawer focus change dropped its previous `preventScroll: true` option. Replacement `1d63adf7da24e8b10f730fb97b5c670d292272f4` forwards native focus options through the existing tooltip suppression owner. Both wrapped and plain targets retain actual focus without opening a tooltip. The same replacement adds a bounded, failure-only trace for the unexplained menu exit failure; it changes no production menu timing. The real-Gateway wait-clock fixture now waits for the persisted resumed parent completion and exactly one reply paragraph, matching its existing update phase while preserving every clock, lifecycle, child-completion, and provider-request assertion.

## Evidence

The two-file delta passed independent P2 review, formatting, and whitespace checks. A repository reference audit found no remaining `renderCopyButton` caller. Current `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed in **240.06 seconds**, with before/after source and dependency hashes unchanged. Current full CI completed with thirteen inherited cases detailed below. Final production Knip and source binding are complete; seven inherited scan findings are recorded below.

The compatible base remains canonical main `614f559915ff4b6a0b81fd37e1561ba44f5217c8`; there is no main-only refresh. Prior published `45bc75741ad74f7f82ea38a6e725bfd2c9523d3c` already incorporates the clipboard/live-preferences, persisted-tool reasoning, and Session Details workspace-label corrections. prs.title: feat: let agents read public GitHub items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GitHub plugin can read public issues, pull requests, and commits in the Control UI, but agents have no corresponding tool. An agent given a known GitHub link cannot use that reader or the Gateway's selected identity when its sandbox has no GitHub credentials or network access.

## User Impact

`github_read` accepts a public GitHub item URL and an optional refresh flag. It returns the existing bounded document: title and body, applicable discussion and review comments, file changes, and PR checks, with partial and truncation markers intact.

The tool joins the coding profile and default sandbox allowlist. Explicit tool policies and plugin disablement still govern access. Credentials stay in the Gateway, which selects the invoking agent's identity and rejects private repositories. Custom sandbox allowlists must permit `github_read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin registers the tool and reuses its existing URL parser and public reader. A narrow host adapter binds requests to the admitted caller, current tool authority, and shared reader identity selection. Caller and plugin lifetime checks cover upstream requests and delivery, including cached results. Model-facing text uses the existing external-content wrapper.

The runtime Gateway request options gain an optional abort signal, composed with the current request lifetime. Agent and UI reads share the existing transport cooldown; invocation cancellation stays outside the cacheable upstream-error path. The existing UI reader keeps its permission contract. Repository search and GitHub writes are outside this change.

## Evidence

- The baseline registration regression failed because no agent reader was registered; the 35 existing plugin tests passed.
- Twelve integration cases pass through the registered plugin, admitted tool surface, Gateway routing and real synthetic managed profiles, with fixed GitHub I/O. They cover coding/plugin/group policies, Tool Search, private cached reads, denial/deactivation, cancellation, caller/plugin retirement, direct-RPC refusal and shared cooldowns. During both a fresh fetch and cached-result validation, publishing a replacement identity causes refusal with no subsequent GitHub requests or document delivery. Cached mode also proves no item refetch. Vitest wall time: 51.64s; helper total: 54.94s.
- The affected GitHub owner/importer batch passed 384 cases across 19 files. Formatting/lint and selected types passed. The final change adds only the two identity cases; prior full compiler, related-test and build results retain their original source attribution and remain applicable to unchanged production.
- A fresh guest in an ordinary workspace read public issue #171140, PR #172678 and commit `40ec02fed59d0d0e1306d787d39e4756af2b5df4` through actual nested `github_read` calls. Role-required sandboxing was active, Docker network mode was `none`, and the guest retained only session read/write scopes. Returned documents accurately marked bounded comments, patches and checks; a private reference returned the opaque unavailable/not-public HTTP 404 and no content. No shell, web-fetch or credential-inspection fallback was used. This acceptance ran on `9a879ff5a96ecfb1c8584b66a15c0faf97c2962c`; final production code is byte-identical. The private-reference test proves refusal without distinguishing which 404 branch ran.
- A fresh runtime build, GitHub cold-entrypoint profile and SDK export checks passed. The canonical SDK API report contains only the new tool/default descriptor and optional request signal, with no added or removed entrypoints. Independent review, including the test-only follow-up, is clean. Exact-head CI passed; automated review found no actionable defects and accepted the authority proof.
