prs.title: fix: native worker turns fail after message delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native OpenClaw worker turns returning HTTP 500 when the message tool records a delivered reply before the worker commits its tool result.

## User Impact

Native worker turns can continue after their own delivery bookkeeping advances the Gateway transcript. Delivery records remain visible. New user messages, ordinary assistant responses, and other runs’ delivery records still invalidate a stale worker cursor. Interrupted commits recover their original entry IDs even after their branch is abandoned, without changing or publishing into the winning branch.

No breaking public API, SDK, wire-protocol, configuration, or database-schema changes; no migration or worker upgrade is required by this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns the canonical transcript. A message-tool delivery mirror advances its head without changing the worker’s model context. The shared commit policy now tolerates only delivery mirrors whose run identity matches both the worker’s server-owned run and its base entry. Active-prefix validation and pending-batch DAG recovery use the same predicate, preserving stale-writer rejection, original commit receipts, and ambiguity rejection.

Contributor: @sallyom — original fix, reproduction, and native integration evidence.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @sallyom](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4d2505f6-cd12-43a2-842e-f24769e00b28)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1cfe1075-2982-48a3-bea1-c60decfe25cb)
- [Compatibility re-review and CI diagnosis](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/bdc39b7d-315d-4a50-a3de-48f53940e793)

## Evidence

### October 15 follow-up

Current head: `80a4a3438526a500a5802bdf979974bbe775f135`. The unrelated CI deadline adjustment has been **removed at the author’s request**. This candidate has exactly the same Git tree as verified product-source head `21798015`; there is no CI workflow change in the PR diff.

- **P2 repaired:** `1c357cb14a2bc6263d2ab57580c71359869a4f01` recovers mirror-backed pending batches across abandoned branches, preserving original entry IDs, ambiguity rejection, and silent winning-branch recovery. The old ClawSweeper finding targets `6b48a17`, before this repair.
- **Compatibility:** the optional internal commit-input `runId` does not change the public worker request/response, wire protocol, SDK, configuration, database schema, stored-row format, or live-authority gates. Missing/null run identity keeps the previous strict behavior. No migration or worker upgrade is required. Fresh complete-candidate independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects; removing the CI-only delta leaves the reviewed product source unchanged.
- **Current-head CI is green:** [run 38666134389](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666134389), attempt 1, passed on `80a4a3438526a500a5802bdf979974bbe775f135`. Required CI, dependency-review, and security-review contexts are successful. GitHub reports the PR clean and mergeable, with no unresolved review threads or outstanding enforced approvals. The prior CI history below is retained for accuracy.
- **Historical CI diagnosis:** [Original run 38608855662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38608855662/job/116010977250) exhausted the 15-minute `check-test-types-core-2` job deadline after six successful compiler graphs, before root-partition completion. A sample of **24 other failed PR runs** (nine recent, fifteen from October 14 evening) did not reproduce that same typecheck timeout; observed nonpassing type jobs in the sample exited with compiler errors after about six minutes instead. This does not establish a widespread timeout regression. CI infrastructure is outside this PR and will be handled separately by the author.
- [Prior-head run 38663637208](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663637208) completed all five hosted core-type stripes successfully. It separately stalled in `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/node-worker-launch-wire.e2e.test.ts`, hitting the 300-second no-output watchdog and reporting unreleased test resource claims. That is a distinct unresolved failure, not the original typecheck deadline or a proven transcript regression. A local reproduction was refused by the managed-Gateway artifact fence before tests ran; isolated Testbox execution did not complete runtime preparation before cancellation, so neither is counted as product proof. That older failure is not evidence that the final candidate is red: current-head run 38666134389 passed. No CI workaround remains in this PR.

### Product-source proof at `21798015`

Verified product-source head: `21798015b293d1decd982fecd61987f5ed78f6d7`, including conflict resolution against main `291e6905cae8abd1286983e0e66434fc3af1d9c5`. The test-routing conflict retains this regression and main’s removal of the retired incognito SQLite-worker test.

- **40/40 focused tests passed on the final composed branch:** 19 shared-policy cases, 6 delivery-mirror integration cases, and 15 existing transcript-commit cases. Commands: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/<file> --maxWorkers=1` for `transcript-commit-policy.test.ts`, `transcript-commit.delivery-mirror.test.ts`, and `transcript-commit.test.ts`. Before current-main integration, all 42 focused cases also passed, including 2 incognito SQLite-actor cases since retired by main; those retired paths were not restored.
- **P2 fail-before/pass-after:** against the original PR policy, durable selection back to the base duplicates committed IDs, while a later-user winning branch returns `stale-base-leaf`. Both regressions now recover the original IDs, leave transcript entries and the winning branch unchanged, and emit no abandoned-branch public/internal updates.
- Additional policy coverage checks interleaved mirrors, missing/null run identity, mismatched base/mirror provenance, ordinary assistant/foreign-provider barriers, and ambiguous complete batches.
- Fixed the original CI error, `TS2554` in the new regression’s `expectDefined` call. Gateway-other test typecheck passed (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json --incremental`, 30.72s on the composed branch); targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the complete candidate found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Final composed-branch timing: policy suite 11.09s wall; real persistence/recovery mirror suite 72.16s wall (~9.66s test bodies, including 38.06s cold worker compilation); existing committer suite 56.24s wall. The integration cases exercise real reply persistence, transcript commits, and interrupted receipt recovery; the cheaper policy cases cover the provenance matrix without database boots. Current-head hosted CI succeeded in run 38666134389; per-file hosted timings are not separately extracted. Full build and full local suite were not rerun; PR CI supplies broad validation.

<details>
<summary>Original native integration evidence (prior head; not rerun for this repair)</summary>

A fresh native oc harness with worker inference on a remote node exposed the original same-run delivery-mirror failure. The original regression failed against unchanged production code and passed with the initial fix.

Full native OpenClaw/OpenShell k3d integration passed: **1 test, 0 failures, 0 skips**, 944.92 seconds total, with OpenClaw commit `6b48a17ac0f4691634bda59282b6a3371d095265`. Command: `OCC_K3D_OPENCLAW_SOURCE=/private/tmp/oce-native-openclaw bash scripts/k3d test --harness openclaw`, using existing authorized credentials.

That live run used the local Enterprise PR #1982 candidate at base `32d0268ca4947782a6bff8df6b80267e8568be08` plus staged native-readiness and test-setup repairs. It verified two Agents’ workspace access and successive worker sessions, cross-Agent enrollment/device-token rejection, real setup expiry with fresh setup admission, and live node revocation while the independent peer continued working. Enterprise main alone was not the tested candidate. The run did not separately expose the mirror-to-tool-result sequence; the focused production-owner regressions provide that boundary proof.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): reload durable OpenAI auth for Codex runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An embedded Codex run could reuse a stale in-memory auth-profile snapshot after Gaia's durable OpenAI OAuth profile changed. OpenAI/Codex runs now read the durable profile for each auth plan while preserving the current provider auth-pin behavior. Non-OpenAI routes retain the existing snapshot-based loader behavior.

This PR does not change model routing, the Codex transport-override compatibility check, Slack recovery, runtime configuration, or live deployment behavior.

## Evidence

- The regression creates an empty runtime snapshot plus a durable OpenAI OAuth profile and verifies the OpenAI path reloads the durable profile.
- The regression calls the production auth-store decision helper with `usesOpenAIAuthRouting: false` against an empty runtime snapshot plus a durable Anthropic profile; it verifies non-OpenAI behavior remains snapshot-based and would fail if durable reload became broad again.
- The existing OpenAI API-key provider-pin test remains green.

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.auth-store.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.auth-pin.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.auth-store.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`

No live runtime, install, restart, activation, or Slack request was performed.
## ClawSweeper after-fix proof

- Existing stale-snapshot regression: 3 test files passed, 6 tests passed.
- Real OpenClaw local-agent CLI proof used a fresh temporary HOME, CODEX_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, config, workspace, and agent directory.
- Provider/Codex token variables were unset; external CLI and keychain overlays were disabled; no API key was configured.
- Before starting the model process, the effective auth store contained exactly one synthetic OpenAI OAuth profile and zero ambient profile IDs. Any other profile would have aborted before a request.
- Loopback-only endpoint: 1 model request, model `proof-model`, Authorization header present, 0 embedding requests, 1 transport probe, deterministic `PROOF_OK` reply, and no startup error.
- Direct Codex contract check: the sibling auth manager caches its snapshot and exposes an explicit reload that rereads storage (read-only source check at `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs`).
- This proof used synthetic OAuth data only; no real credential, token, transcript, or live Gaia runtime was used or included.

## What Problem This Solves

Apple Watch lacks on-Watch Gateway setup, direct conversations, and session-scoped approvals independent of the iPhone relay. Its existing node and voice connection do not provide operator chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add Watch-owned setup and foreground conversations on the parent's paired operator HTTPS transport. One controller owns setup, credential handoff, and node/voice/operator lifecycle coordination.

Reuse existing Watch Keychain configuration, preferences, device identity, and Gateway-scoped credentials. No configuration option, schema/protocol version, or independent-app metadata is added. The companion delivery journal stays separate.

## User Impact

- Enter an existing voice-node setup code using native Watch text input; choose an agent and conversation, read bounded history, and explicitly request chat and approval scopes.
- Send messages, stop replies, and resolve session-scoped approvals using only offered decisions after the scope upgrade is approved. Direct sends never silently fall back to **Chat via iPhone** or replay after an uncertain connection failure.
- A canonical timeout ACK selects `This run ended or was cancelled. Check history before sending again.` without changing run IDs, history, wait handling, ownership checks, or resend behavior.
- Static labels perform localized lookup; agent and conversation names remain verbatim. Approval details use constant localized format keys with unchanged authoritative scope values.
- Replacement operator grants retire active Watch voice before credential replacement. Backgrounding retires direct chat; returning reloads canonical history and subscriptions.

Initial setup retains `operator.read` and `operator.talk`. Chat adds `operator.write` and `operator.approvals`, never administrator or pairing scope.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add paired operator HTTPS connections
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142916

Stack base: `main`, integrated through `fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b`. The shared connection foundation landed via https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145950; the original https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142931 was closed without merging.

**Current qualification: draft, not merge-ready.** Signed candidate `f5f5c1fe4185d687ffbb7d2966b443d7cd96117c` refreshes the HTTPS layer onto audited main `fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b` so its Watch child can resolve the new shared TLS conflict. This parent needed no manual resolution; its complete tree equals the predicted clean merge tree `e17870062aebcf0727e8ab92b9570941d637f9b6`. Earlier runtime validation remains bound to its recorded heads, not this refresh. Required exact-head checks, security-owner disposition, and the held admission qualification remain outstanding. No admission experiment was retried.

## What Problem This Solves

Already-paired watch clients need direct conversation and approval access over HTTPS without duplicating Gateway authentication or requiring an ordinary WebSocket connection.

This is the Gateway transport layer of the phone-optional watch program. The native Watch conversation client remains separate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142967.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add bounded, in-memory operator connections at `<basePath>/api/operator/connections`. Begin returns a challenge; later HTTP requests carry ordinary Gateway frames, ordered submission sequences, and cumulative output acknowledgments through the shared connection and RPC owners.

Admission requires a signed, already-paired device and explicit device-token authentication. The scope ceiling is read, write, approvals, and Talk. Shared secrets, bootstrap credentials, ambient proxy authentication, administrative scopes, and pairing scopes do not replace that contract. Existing method authorization, device invalidation, profile binding, and request lifetime owners remain in the canonical path.

Each request retains its prepared ingress through awaited work. Retired authenticated output is discarded. Poll cancellation does not cancel accepted RPCs; an uncertain submission is retryable only within the same logical connection. Rejected connections retain their per-IP capacity charge until final removal. Expiry, termination, and failed delivery settle outstanding callbacks.

## User Impact

Already-paired clients can carry conversation and approval requests over HTTPS. HTTPS is required except on direct loopback. An IP or forwarding-policy change requires reconnecting; seamless network handoff is not claimed.

This does not provision watch credentials, redeem setup codes, add configuration options, change persistence or protocol versions, or enable independent-app metadata. Connection keys, queues, and sequence state are ephemeral. Native UI, physical-watch, and background qualification remain separate.

## Main Integration

- Current refresh: [f5f5c1fe418](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f5f5c1fe4185d687ffbb7d2966b443d7cd96117c) integrates [fecba819ef2e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b). Complete-tree equality and `git diff --check` passed. The parent and child were published together with exact-head leases; auto-merge remains off. No fresh parent runtime test pass is claimed.
- Previous refresh: [38c10d27592](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/38c10d27592d43b3f33a3f78a0289ecb0e3c3640) merges observed main [32e30e59d9a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/32e30e59d9a7fd1f5b3a9e9659427d45145779dd). Its tree `cb18bbb3d5c4c0bb12a06b1c59ef85cc886cf880` exactly matches the conflict-free merge-tree prediction; signature and whitespace checks passed. This parent refresh is required for the downstream Watch child's real native-i18n v3 conflict, not cosmetic drift. No new transport behavior, security verdict, admission experiment, or current-head runtime pass is claimed. Subsequent bullets describe earlier integration history.
- October 2 drift check: main was audited through `0272aba9cee72fce7456834887519fd9d5e703a5`, 47 commits and 966 changed files after the frozen base. The combined 57-file HTTPS/Direct Watch stack overlaps only the generated native string inventory, with no overlap between changed entry IDs. `git merge-tree --write-tree` for this HTTPS head and that exact main SHA completed without conflicts, producing tree `a8f517381c8461cb266836acdecd0b20c1fd582d`. No branch rebase or merge was performed. This is source/mergeability evidence, not behavior, CI, or held-qualification proof; the outstanding boundaries remain unchanged.
- Replayed only the HTTPS layer onto the audited main revision. Kept the current client registry, preauth queue, request-context, profile/policy, worker-setup, and request-lifetime APIs.
- Preserved main's byte-backed JSON text delivery. Both string and Buffer frames use the same HTTP delivery/ACK path; the WebSocket adapter retains `binary: false` for Buffer-backed text.
- Grouped shared transport startup in `server-startup-connections.ts`. Both handlers attach before listening, and heavy transport imports remain lazy. The retired `server-ws-runtime.ts` adapter is not restored.
- Fixed a reproduced shutdown stall: an unpolled startup rejection retained a tracked delivery callback, while HTTP cleanup was registered after the connection drain. The connection-dependent sidecar now retires HTTP delivery before that drain. No timeout increase or polling workaround was added.

Production: +1,228/-191 (net +1,037); tests: +1,255/-0; docs: +128/-1. Production growth supplies the new bounded HTTP transport and its integration with existing owners. No policy baseline or exemption was weakened.

## Evidence

The focused tests, build and static checks below predate the current main refresh. They are retained as source-bound historical evidence; fresh exact-head qualification remains required.

- Before the shutdown fix, the real-server regression failed because `server.close()` did not settle until fixture cleanup forcibly terminated the pending transport. After the owner-ordering repair it passed.
- At `fa7aaad7fd116e68a993f0aafa1da653a4a0b739`, six focused files passed 46 tests with one host-network skip (`127.0.0.2` is not bindable). Coverage includes real HTTP requests, sequential scope upgrades and chat/approval effects, established-connection revocation, cancellation, replay, Buffer delivery, startup, and shutdown. Reply generation is stubbed; approval fixtures do not execute commands or deliver externally.
- Final `b50449929ea3f04c4de3e23be7ecf99e6440afbb` changes only the regression spy's argument lookup from that run. The exact-head shutdown regression passed again (14.15 seconds including its wrapper), and the Gateway-server test type graph passed. The assertions and production tree are unchanged.
- The selected static checks passed across the initial run and scoped retries: core types, all 27 test-type graphs, graph boundaries, formatting, ratchets, dependency/plugin guards, dead-export scans, changed-file lint, native schema guard, runtime import cycles, sidecar/media guards, and webhook/pairing guards. The initial run stopped at spy-style lint failures; those were repaired, and all nine remaining plan steps passed. The complete pipeline was not restarted from the beginning.
- `pnpm build` passed on exact head `b50449929ea3f04c4de3e23be7ecf99e6440afbb` in 8m 47.2s, including runtime bundles, native protocol generation, declarations, built-module load checks, SDK exports, and the Control UI build.
- One scoped autoreview at `6f80d5712e5543925e62d7aed4e0f49e33f7d491` returned no P0 findings. Only test-observation lint cleanup followed; production is byte-identical. This review does not qualify the held admission experiment or clear the security-owner request.
- The eight local integration commits have valid signatures. Added source was checked for private path and endpoint literals; public evidence excludes local paths and credentials.

The current focused runs do not explain the historical `sessions.create`/`sessions.delete` fixture timeouts recorded on `79ac553afc522863f453308687bfbb446f188c2a`. No assertion of flakiness or retrospective root-cause repair is made.

### Remaining Qualification

- The previously held verification-to-registration admission qualification remains unexecuted. Established-connection revocation and shutdown tests do not prove it. No reproduced defect or passing result is claimed for that gap.
- The latest ClawSweeper review requests security-operations owner disposition of the bounded transport contract and missing admission proof. No completed owner acceptance or waiver is recorded.
- Required hosted `openclaw/ci-gate` must pass on the published head. Local checks are not a substitute.
- Native Watch onboarding, direct conversation, delayed-hello, physical-device, and background proof belong to the downstream client work.

Rank-up disposition: the requested admission evidence and security-owner acceptance remain open, not silently skipped. This body refresh records only the completed main-integration and lifecycle proof. The PR stays draft.

prs.title: refactor(ui): remove Lit dependency from subscriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared subscription owner still depends on Lit lifecycle types although its rendering consumers use Solid.

## User Impact

Subscription refresh, cleanup, immediate domain-state reads, and lazy boundaries retain their existing behavior. No user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the subscription owner and synchronous test host from `ui/src/lit/` to `ui/src/lib/`, adopt the existing Solid lifecycle contract, and update every internal caller together. The old source paths are deleted. The assertion allowance follows the renamed file without increasing its count.

Main’s canonical generated boot manifest is retained unchanged. Six existing shared-boot members statically import the moved owner, and the shared group includes dependencies recursively. The old path is only an inert membership entry; neither path is a dynamic entry. No dependency, state owner, DOM, CSS, tag, route, or lazy entry is added. This is a module/type migration; screenshots are not applicable.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI types | Exact diagnostic candidate `eeb4bc1` passed |
| Direct controller tests | 3 files, 19 cases passed once with one worker; unchanged behavior reuses that proof |
| Scoped lint / formatting | Original 37 TypeScript paths passed; integrated diff and retired-import audit pass |
| Independent review | Original migration review remains valid; the additional nine-line diagnostic passed an independent P2 review with final source verification |
| Production builds / strict performance | Exact `eeb4bc1` CI performance job passed. Original migration base/head also passed on the same machine with zero violations; those paired measurements are historical. |
| Startup | Current `eeb4bc1` CI checkout: 349,926 B gzip, 8 JS / 1 CSS request; CSS 46,058 B. Historical same-machine original pair: 348,707 → 348,739 B (+32 B); raw JS falls 480 B. |
| Route boot | Chat 1,759,463 → 1,652,350 B gzip; New Session 1,349,338 → 1,349,272 B |
| Production Knip | Final exact `eeb4bc1` full production scan, including exports, completed in 977.54 seconds with seven baseline findings and no additions or new ignores; exit 1 is preserved |
| Full CI | Replacement exact `eeb4bc1` [run 38671892424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38671892424) completed with 42 successful jobs, 5 failed jobs including the aggregate, and 24 skipped jobs; 14 test cases failed. All UI units, lint, types, and performance passed. Thirteen cases match scheduled main; the remaining Workboard failure has an assigned canonical fixture repair. No inherited-only exception is claimed. Prior `4eeccd3` [run 38665167173](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38665167173) failed: 42 jobs succeeded, 4 failed, 1 was cancelled, and 24 were skipped. Its 13 observed failures and incomplete Gateway1 coverage remain recorded below; no inherited-only exception is claimed. |

Production LOC: 13,496 → 13,496. Tests: 3,454 → 3,502. Total: 16,950 → 16,998 across 41 logical paths, compared with final merge base `6ff48344f3efeff72420ca7118d770c43640369c`.

Migration parent `4eeccd3becf00c12617328238f5c2bb6ee4de26a` normally merges main `6ff48344f3efeff72420ca7118d770c43640369c` without conflicts. The auto-combined sidebar and new-session files retain only subscription-owner import changes relative to main; the assertion allowance remains one at its moved path. The authored source patch remains identical to the reviewed predecessor (stable patch ID `2fcca2f6a099cf1aabbb84104ccf27719005ff33`). Package, lockfile, and workspace inputs are unchanged; the private frozen install is reused. Paired build base is `eda41b03a1a0dc02abecc8351a3d4da25b05c367`; those historical measurements cover the original functional migration, not the later integrated manifest.

Final head `eeb4bc1007300c6e16220d130edf25870d82910b` adds nine failure-only diagnostic lines to that reviewed migration. When the initial document probe fails, it prints the existing readiness result and safe Gateway readiness receipts with captured raw logs omitted. Request deadlines, retries, assertions, and cleanup remain unchanged. This preserves evidence if a later CI cancellation prevents artifact upload; it does not claim to fix the transport timeout.

## Current full CI failures

Run `38671892424` tested merge `97566b8d74e0a1afaea3f9b5ce7e9480f7dce9dc`, joining main `a4d316dc86846952cc2ddd99df026c771ab38900` and exact head `eeb4bc1007300c6e16220d130edf25870d82910b`. The four Models, four native-consent, and four Cron cases named in the table below fail with the same names, assertion lines, and signatures as the scheduled-main run `38672095119` at that exact main parent. Its first real-Gateway job also reproduces the provider-login failure below, while its Workboard case passes.

The current first real-Gateway job completed with 2 failed and 23 passed tests:

| Additional current failed test | Observed failure and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `provider-browser-login.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Provider browser login through real HTTPS Gateway > rejects cancelled and stale callbacks, then saves a fresh sign-in and serves an existing session` | Profile readback succeeds, then modal count remains 1 instead of 0 at `211:80`. The same case, count mismatch, and assertion/cause frames fail in scheduled main `38672095119`. The assigned canonical fixture repair waits for the completed wizard and explicitly closes it. |
| `pages/workboard/workboard-distribution.e2e.test.ts > Packaged Workboard delivery > loads entry, CSS and lazy Workboard chunks from the UI origin with an authenticated remote Gateway` | The gateway-switch button resolves, detaches, and the click times out at `88:90`. The assigned canonical repair aligns the packaged fixture's build identity. No inheritance claim yet. |

The unmatched Workboard failure prevents inherited-only admission. Their existing repair owner is handling the reviewed fixes separately; this branch will consume only landed main commits. The Command Palette case now passes, which does not establish a cause or fix for its earlier timeout. Current route measurements are Chat 1,689,288 → 1,689,326 B gzip (+38 B) and New Session 1,380,109 → 1,380,090 B (-19 B), with unchanged request counts.

## Prior full CI failures and attribution

The run tested merge `54c77cee07bd9a3359b28f4ea9f9cf0db3a5326a`, joining main `614f559915ff4b6a0b81fd37e1561ba44f5217c8` and exact PR head `4eeccd3becf00c12617328238f5c2bb6ee4de26a`. Each failed job log was fetched once. The newer scheduled-main [run 38666744245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245), at `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209`, reproduces the exact four Models, four native-consent, and four Cron cases with the same failing lines and signatures. Its real-Gateway 1/2 job passes, so the additional Command Palette timeout remains unmatched. The thirteen-case run does not qualify as inherited-only.

| Failing case | Evidence and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `model-providers-progressive.e2e.test.ts`: “keeps a Models route selection saved before the initial provider details arrive” | Picker trigger click times out at `271:21`; canonical owner is correcting the fixture for the intentional initial skeleton. |
| Same file: “keeps the current Models catalog after late route data and invalidation” | Same trigger click timeout at `359:21`; same assigned repair. |
| Same file: “opens the Models route from snapshot catalog publication and refreshes after overlapping reads” | Trigger-enabled poll expires at `624:54`; same assigned repair. |
| Same file: “opens the Models route from ordinary catalog publication and refreshes after overlapping reads” | Same poll at `624:54`; same assigned repair. |
| `chat-native-runtime-recovery.e2e.test.ts`, selection refusal: “recovers native OpenCode only with explicit consent: confirm” | Modal visibility wait times out at `245:25`; the canonical owner is repairing the named-session identity lookup. |
| Same file, selection refusal: “recovers native OpenCode only with explicit consent: cancel” | Same modal wait and assigned repair. |
| Same file, send refusal: “recovers native OpenCode only with explicit consent: confirm” | Same modal wait and assigned repair. |
| Same file, send refusal: “recovers native OpenCode only with explicit consent: cancel” | Same modal wait and assigned repair. |
| `cron-duration-save.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: “timeout override: clearing restores the default after save and reload” | CLI seed exits 1 before UI opens, at `cliJson:298:41`; repair tracked in #172683. |
| Same file: “failure alert round trip: preserves partial policy through metadata save and clone” | Same CLI seed failure. |
| Same file: “failure alert round trip: clears field overrides through the real picker” | Same CLI seed failure. |
| Same file: “clone payload policy: preserves public options through the real Gateway and CLI readback” | Same CLI seed failure. |
| `command-palette-search.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: “finds a grouped spawned conversation beyond the roster and treats a full result page as success” | The initial document readiness HEAD times out after approximately 2 seconds before dashboard handoff or browser/search actions. Relevant source is byte-identical to the tested main parent; scheduled main passes this shard. The timeout cause remains unproven. |

Real-Gateway 1/2 also exceeded its 24-minute job limit. Its partial log reports 17 passed modules and the failed Command Palette module, with no final suite summary. The cancellation does not erase that failed case or prove the remaining shard coverage. The test gives the readiness owner a 60-second overall deadline, but the owner deliberately caps each HTTP request at 2 seconds and returns immediately on transport error; it retries only an explicit preparing response (503 with Retry-After). No timeout or retry policy has been changed, and no search regression or inherited attribution is established for this case. The test, readiness owner and its tests, fetch guard, timeout helper, suite, and Gateway fixture are byte-identical in the tested merge, its main parent, and the inspected PR head. The entire tested `src/` tree also matches its main parent. Existing failure artifacts were not uploaded by the cancelled job; the reviewed failure-only stdout diagnostic is now included in the replacement head, without claiming a fix.

The four cron cases create isolated agent jobs without the model/profile now required by main's stored-inference contract. The separate 11-line fixture repair supplies a synthetic profile before Gateway startup while keeping cron disabled. Its six-test file and 48-test real-Gateway shard passed; its publication is handled separately. This PR has not integrated an unlanded branch. The original CI did not capture precise CLI stderr, so no specific stderr is claimed.

## Canonical repairs already integrated

Prior exact `44f200` [run 38659334261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659334261) failed 12 cases across capture, clipboard, reasoning, live preferences, and cron. The current head includes canonical main repairs `459cad76530457e5c0a32bc21d4982920e9991e7` (clipboard and live preferences), `7b9fedd04ff56585d1ab08b1cfbbb1031b409b3b` (persisted reasoning disclosure), and `869029b986a26950706a805d3bac67105f40ee32` (private workspace paths in Details). Each full patch was inspected; independent owner proof was reused without duplicate test runs. The browser cases above are different failures; their matching scheduled-main signatures and assigned canonical repairs remain recorded.

## Production scan attribution

The full production Knip command reports seven existing exports/types also present in scheduled-main run `38666744245`: `AuthProfileAuthorizationError`, `configuredOrFalseAsync`, `WorkerPreparationArtifactsSchema`, `readPairedDevicePairingRecordsFromDatabase`, `renderCopyButton`, `getChatRunOwnerSessionKey`, and `PostgresSchemaDefinition`. Each file-and-symbol pair was compared against the baseline log. No new finding or ignore was introduced. The scan result remains failed; earlier narrower scans are not represented as full-export proof.

## Investigated proof gaps

Both prior `session-link-reconnect.e2e.test.ts > Session link reconnect > recovers an interrupted session-link open while respecting newer navigation` variants (`false` and `true`) failed the total resolve count at line 103 (expected 2/1, observed 4/3). Main’s canonical repair `8f57414a3ad7c8f576f8393b928b1c3280dda8d8` settles title lookups and uses the subsequent navigation-request cursor while retaining exact retry counts and the route, history, content, and startup assertions. This repair is included through the ordinary main merge.

The prior run also failed `agent-file-lifecycle.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Control UI agent file lifecycle with a real Gateway > reads and saves the selected agent workspace through an isolated Gateway` at the whole-test 120-second deadline (declaration line 405; suite wrapper line 609). Gateway setup reported ready at 98.85 seconds and HTTP listening at 99.9 seconds. The browser connected with about 10 seconds remaining and reached four expected stale-file conflict responses before the deadline; cleanup completed cleanly. The test, helper, suite, actual timeout configuration, and Gateway source tree match the tested main parent. No failing UI assertion or matching scheduled-main failure was established. The setup-budget timeout remains recorded without an inherited or causal-fix claim.

An earlier local scoped lint invocation timed out in plugin-SDK declaration preparation after 300 seconds, before target lint. An earlier HTTPS deep-link reload in `browser-bootstrap.e2e.test.ts` timed out; failure-only diagnostics retain the original transport, assertions, and timeouts. Later passing runs do not establish either root cause. The earlier tooltip correction is superseded by main’s event-based fixture repair verbatim. Historical Workboard-locale failure was reproduced on its exact merge base and resolved by canonical main `efbe8513fc85d8`; that is historical evidence, not replacement-head proof.

The replacement diagnostic passed UI typechecking, formatting, diff checks, and independent P2 review. Its one scoped lint invocation stopped before target lint when plugin-SDK boundary declaration preparation timed out after 300 seconds; the managed process exited 1 naturally. No lock was removed, guard bypassed, or local lint/E2E replay run. Exact-head PR CI will supply target lint proof; the local preparation failure remains unresolved.

## What Problem This Solves

Native session menus and picker navigation still reached Lit-specific modules after their Solid ports.

## Changes

Remove the obsolete DOM application-context relay from the shared menu controller and both menu callers. Menu owners and the now-native sharing/avatar subtree consume Solid context directly. The existing focus/search test mounts through the native Solid application provider to exercise that boundary.

Move the unchanged `revealInScrollRegion` helper into the framework-neutral scroll observer and update all five consumers. The remaining Lit scroll directive keeps its current owner and behavior.

Existing E2E assertions wait for committed width invalidation and the enabled Send control before `/btw`. Main now owns the completed tooltip-reopen lifecycle and session-details readiness repairs; those files are no longer in this authored diff.

## Current proof

Published head: `0dda0f239cb9f1b1789a2add59548c879dc80c0c`. This ordinary two-parent merge integrates actual main `6ff48344f3efeff72420ca7118d770c43640369c` into reviewed `de701e840f2bd271c770c92cbc14c339650aaa68`. No main commits were replayed. prs.title: feat(huggingface): support device-code login and token refresh
prs.body:
Related: #163235

## What Problem This Solves

Hugging Face inference users with a public OAuth app cannot sign in through OpenClaw or refresh the resulting credentials automatically.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw models auth login --provider huggingface --method oauth`, enter your public client ID, and authorize the displayed code from any browser. Only `inference-api` is requested. Existing API-key setup remains available.

An operator-owned public OAuth app without a client secret is required. Access-only grants expire and require re-login; refreshable grants use the existing auth-profile lifecycle. No client registration, hosted metadata, configuration schema, or new dependency is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Device authorization works on remote hosts without an inbound callback. The provider owns the protocol and uses existing auth profiles for expiry, client identity, and refresh-token rotation. Catalog discovery uses the existing OAuth-aware resolver so an OAuth-only account can discover models.

This is the usable base of a two-part stack. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163244 exposes the same method in onboarding and should land second.

## Evidence

- Focused plugin tests: 20 passed (`pnpm test extensions/huggingface/oauth.test.ts extensions/huggingface/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`), 72.13 seconds wall including cold compiler preparation; new device/lifecycle cases use fake timers. CI timing is not yet available.
- Final provider suite: `pnpm test:extension huggingface --maxWorkers=1` passed all 30 tests in four files, 62.03 seconds wall, including existing discovery/proxy behavior.
- Covered public-client request scope, pending/slow-down/transient polling, both HF verification hosts, cancellation, caller revocation, device/token expiry, access-only storage, refresh-token preservation/rotation, redacted errors, and OAuth catalog credentials.
- Provider documentation passed the scoped MDX check. Independent review findings were addressed with regression coverage.
- Scoped type-aware lint, provider package-boundary typecheck, provider test-fixture typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Validation ran in an isolated checkout with independently owned frozen dependencies. Broad repository gates were not run.
- Live proof gap: no operator-owned public OAuth client ID or authenticated grant was available. No real login, refresh, or inference request was performed; mock boundary proof is not production-readiness proof.

Contract references: [HF public-client/device OAuth](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/oauth), [HF device/refresh implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/blob/main/src/huggingface_hub/utils/_oauth_device.py).

prs.title: fix: /tools verbose advertises automations scope the turn cannot execute
prs.body:
Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/tools verbose` shows the full Automations action set (including `add`) during a management-only turn, whose runtime tool only accepts `list`, `get`, `update`, `run`, and `remove`, so discovery and execution disagree about what the turn can do.

## User Impact

User impact: In a restricted management-only turn, `/tools verbose` now describes exactly the actions that turn can execute. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This covers the verified discovery mismatch only. The issue also reports a Telegram `add` rejection; that path is not reproduced or claimed fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron tool chose its description and schema from the bound management grant. Inventory construction (`/tools`, `tools.effective`) has no run id, so it fell back to the unrestricted description. The change splits read-only admission metadata from exact-run execution grants:

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` resolves the admitted management scope (entitlement, liveness, run id) without requiring the execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` keeps its full exact-run authority checks, including the live `approvalAuthority` and operational instance match.
- The description, display summary, and schema all derive from the same resolved mode, so discovery and runtime stay consistent.

A no-run-id inventory outside an admitted turn still reports the configuration surface rather than promising per-turn authority.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts` exercises `handleToolsCommand("/tools verbose", ...)` inside a management-only admitted turn. It fails before the fix (full description with `add job`) and passes after, and asserts the discovered parameters equal the runtime tool's parameters.
- Grant-isolation coverage: `src/agents/cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts` confirms metadata resolves without the execution grant while `bindCronManagementGrant` stays undefined without caller identity, and that a foreign run id resolves nothing.
- Focused tests (418 total, 3 shards): `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts`, `src/agents/cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`.
- `pnpm build` and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <upstream main> -- <changed files>` on the exact commit.
- Independent `autoreview` (pi engine, P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Not covered: the reported Telegram `add` rejection. The supplied arguments there also lack a schedule, so a successful creation is not established by this change.

**Superseded by [#172719](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172719)**, merged to main as `30d32ee541df601b63429173e1c4809642396e56` on October 15, 2026 at 02:53:20 UTC. That landed repair fixes the same agent-qualified native-consent regression, with owning-agent precedence and remembered-consent coverage. Closing this redundant proposal; the evidence below records this PR's unmerged candidate. Its branch and blocked native checkout/journal remain preserved.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary agent-qualified chats stopped offering the explicit native-runtime consent dialog after #172607 added remembered-consent lookup. Its agent lookup used the RPC helper that returns an agent only for global sessions, so recovery returned before opening the dialog.

## User Impact

Native-runtime model selection again offers the existing confirmation flow for agent-qualified chats. Global chats, explicit agent overrides, remembered consent, cancellation, current authority, and mutation routing retain their existing behavior.

Source inspection found that #172610 intentionally retains the completion dialog; a separate focused test correction is being prepared.

### Native landing blocker

Both `review-init` attempts exited and explicitly reported that their operation locks were released after all child processes drained. No merge intent or merge request exists, and the PR head remains pinned to the reviewed SHA above.

The first attempt could not read blob `8d8eb6c17f58ad233dedb5970b712e729727636b` for `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests.swift`. The blob subsequently became readable and its full contents hashed to the expected ID. Native journal recovery then refused the interrupted checkout:

```text
Working-tree entry "apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests.swift" is neither its journaled source nor target entry
Refusing scripts/pr transition for PR #172734: the index or working tree contains unowned transition state.
```

The file is absent from the worktree while the index contains that blob. The journal, index, and worktree are preserved. No manual restoration, journal edit, deletion, namespace replacement, or further native retry has been used to bypass the guard; a supported workflow-owner recovery is required.

Two earlier direct-main push attempts were rejected non-fast-forward as main advanced. This PR is closed as superseded by the independently landed repair; no native recovery or branch deletion was attempted during closeout.

prs.title: fix(memory): prune stale recall when dreaming sources are archived
prs.body:
Related: #172688

## What Problem This Solves

Dreaming artifact repair can archive its session corpus while leaving short-term recall entries pointing to the old paths, especially through the Gateway repair action, until nightly repair runs.

## User Impact

After a successful archive and cleanup, recall immediately excludes missing archived sources and retains daily notes and archived sources that still exist. A failed move preserves recall. Cleanup failures produce a warning while still reporting the completed archive. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

The filesystem rename and SQLite cleanup remain separate: a crash between them can leave dangling entries, and the next nightly repair removes them. Cross-owner crash atomicity remains a follow-up to the linked issue; this PR adds no durable file/state coordination.

## Why This Change Was Made

The archive owner now holds the existing workspace mutation lock through rename, live-source filtering, and pruning, so the Gateway and CLI callers use the same behavior. Recall rows and their phase signals are deleted in one existing SQLite worker transaction. Nightly dangling cleanup uses that operation too, preserving retry convergence while avoiding partially committed recall/phase deletion. The bundled Doctor/Gateway facade binds the worker to its managed plugin instance or its captured standalone bundled module, so these entry points can actually dispatch the operation.

The operation uses existing keyed namespaces and the host's Kysely-backed plugin-state worker. The lock keeps the workspace binding and selected recall keys current across source inspection; action-bound stores revalidate live authority at write admission. Source existence is checked after the rename. The archived destination is a recorded result and is not reused as mutation authority.

## Evidence

- Added `prunes archived corpus recalls and phase signals while preserving existing sources`, `preserves recall and phase signals when the archive rename fails`, and `rolls back interrupted archive pruning and lets nightly repair finish`. These exercise the archive owner, real recall/phase storage, reader, and artifact audit; a SQLite phase-delete failure proves both stores roll back.
- Added `prunes archived and dangling recall through the bundled Doctor facade` using real persisted rows and the actual facade/worker path.
- Retained the nightly retry-convergence regression as `converges on retry when recall and phase cleanup rolls back`.
- Changed-file oxlint with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Deslop removed a redundant async wrapper.
- Codex autoreview: the final prescribed branch review returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Automatic GitHub review found the missing bundled-facade worker binding and ambiguous retry guidance; both are fixed, with a real facade regression added. Main was merged afterward without changes to the reviewed files.
- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38668904647) is the test gate. All tests, production/test types, lint, docs, and guards passed on `7f9adb7e6403c5ba1a31002088b51ca7940c234e`. SDK declaration preparation timed out after 300 seconds without a type diagnostic; one targeted retry passed on the same head without source changes. The same 239-root declaration graph had passed on the prior head with identical production code. The latest scheduled main boundary job also passed, so this timeout is not labeled inherited.
- Final-head regression times: successful archive 953ms; failed rename 30ms; interrupted prune/nightly recovery 95ms; nightly retry 63ms. The real facade regression passed in 15.382s (27.68s Vitest wall; 68.23s CI wrapper including native preparation). Its production facade/plugin load and worker path cover the binding gap that store-only fixtures missed.
- One earlier CI run failed the new facade fixture before product behavior because it was in the thread-only SDK lane (`Shared-state admission requires the host broker`). It now runs successfully in the existing forked database-worker lane, with unchanged assertions.
- Local tests, negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy; no leases were created.


Production LOC grows by 111 lines: the worker operation, dispatch, source-scoped filter, facade source binding, and truthful archive/cleanup failure reporting need new code. The old split phase-cleanup rewrite is removed; unrelated behavior was not deleted to meet a size target.

prs.title: feat(agents): add warn-only usage budgets
prs.body:
## Current-head repair status

Current source head `2283dc79eebccced7ccdb06c4a0a2c5a6b96924a` addresses both actionable P2 review findings:

- Budget warnings now use the canonical successful terminal source-delivery contract. A completed, non-aborted terminal block stream can be followed by one standalone warning; reasoning-only, commentary-only, status/progress-only, message-tool-only progress, and aborted streams do not claim or emit one.
- The documented per-agent override now uses canonical keyed `agents.entries` with an explicit default agent.

An independent static review found no remaining issue in these two repairs. The contributor head was not executed locally because it is untrusted; exact-head secretless GitHub CI is required. The existing runtime proof below is from an earlier head and must not be treated as proof of this repair.

The maintainer product decision on accepting the public `usageBudget` config/default surface remains open. This source-only head also still conflicts with current `main` in generated config baseline count/hash files; those generated files were deliberately not guessed or hand-edited.

Related to #42475.
Closes #113481.

AI-assisted: this change was implemented with Codex assistance. I reviewed the code and understand the implementation. No agent transcript is included.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw exposes estimated session cost, but an unattended agent cannot proactively tell its owner when known daily spend crosses a meaningful amount. The broader #42475 design covers enforcement before provider dispatch; this PR implements only its informational `warn` mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the standalone `modelSpend` implementation with a smaller consumer of existing usage infrastructure:

- `agents.defaults.usageBudget` and per-agent `usageBudget` accept a daily USD interval with `action: "warn"`.
- Per-agent `{ usageBudget: { enabled: false } }` disables an inherited default.
- Existing per-session cost rollups provide the estimated spend total; this PR adds no spend ledger or SQLite table.
- Only the warning watermark is stored in the existing per-agent `cache_entries` table.
- The current session rollup refreshes after primary and queued follow-up runs. A one-time background warm includes the agent's other sessions.

Warnings repeat at each crossed multiple, reset at 00:00 UTC, and are appended only to direct replies for an owner-authorized sender. Delivery and accounting are best-effort. Unpriced calls are excluded from the known total and called out in the warning.

This mode never blocks a model call, pauses an agent, switches models, rotates credentials, or changes retry/fallback behavior. Pre-dispatch reservations and enforcement remain in #42475 / #104060.

## User Impact

Operators can opt an agent into daily spend warnings without changing model execution:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      usageBudget: {
        daily: { usd: 10 },
        action: "warn",
      },
    },
    entries: {
      local: { default: true, usageBudget: { enabled: false } },
    },
  },
}
```

At known UTC-day spend of $23.50 with a $10 interval, the next eligible owner DM receives the $20 threshold warning. Repeated replies do not duplicate that threshold; later spend can trigger $30.

## Evidence

Current exact head: `2283dc79eebccced7ccdb06c4a0a2c5a6b96924a`.

### Prior-head runtime proof

This proof predates the current head and does not cover the streamed-warning repair below. An ignored proof runner started an isolated real Gateway child and the real `qa-channel` inbound dispatch/reply pipeline at the exact head above. Only the model provider was deterministic (`mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna`). The Gateway used this effective policy:

```text
agents.defaults.usageBudget.daily.usd=10
agents.defaults.usageBudget.action=warn
commands.ownerAllowFrom=["qa-channel:qa-owner"]
channels.qa-channel.allowFrom=["qa-owner"]
```

The isolated `qa` agent was seeded with one current-UTC-day assistant usage entry costing `$12.34`. The first owner turn warmed the real SQLite cost rollup. The proof then sent a non-owner direct turn followed by an owner direct turn. Redacted QA bus evidence:

```text
exact head: 2fa01bd6688b44d6fa4720e1f9dabefa27016d77
runtime: isolated real Gateway child + qa-channel inbound dispatch + mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna

inbound  sender=qa-owner chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: OWNER_WARMUP_OK"
cursor=2 kind=outbound-message text="OWNER_WARMUP_OK"

inbound  sender=qa-guest chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: NON_OWNER_OK"
PASS     no outbound reply and no usage warning

inbound  sender=qa-owner chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: OWNER_ALERT_OK"
cursor=5 kind=outbound-message messageId=04616fda... replyToId=c314b44c... text="OWNER_ALERT_OK"
cursor=6 kind=message-edited  messageId=04616fda... replyToId=c314b44c... text="Usage budget warning: Known spend is at least $12.34 UTC today, crossing $10.00. Warn-only mode; model calls continue. 1 unpriced model call is not included."

PASS model reply completed before warning delivery
PASS warning remained scoped to the authorized owner direct route
PASS warn-only mode did not prevent the model call or reply
```

`qa-channel` maps a second final payload onto an edit of its existing preview, so the event timeline is the durable evidence: the model reply and warning have the same message ID and `replyToId`, and the reply event precedes the warning edit. The redacted local artifacts are under `.artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-113548-usage-budget-proof-2fa01bd/`.

The prior Feishu capture targeted the superseded standalone accounting design and is intentionally not claimed as proof for this head.

### Automated proof

- Exact-head CI run [30631148220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30631148220) completed with 71 jobs and no failures.
- Structured Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) returned clean with no accepted/actionable findings and 0.88 correctness confidence.
- Focused Vitest proof passed 119 tests across five focused files:
  - `src/agents/usage-budget-warning.test.ts`: 5/5
  - `src/config/zod-schema.usage-budget.test.ts`: 3/3
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: 59/59
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.sqlite.test.ts`: 5/5
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts`: 47/47
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` emitted successful format, config metadata, API baseline, boundary, dead-code, typecheck, lint, database-first, import-cycle, and guard stages. Blacksmith CLI was unavailable, so this used the repository's trusted-source local fallback; GitHub CI remains the exact-head broad gate.
- Config baseline generation/check passed with the intentional core schema count update.

### Scope reduction

| Version | Files | Additions | Deletions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous standalone implementation | 37 | 1544 | 93 |
| Current warn-only slice | 20 | 615 | 22 |

Removed scope includes provider allowlists, provider-call instrumentation, custom spend tables, timezone configuration, compaction accounting callbacks, cross-channel delivery plumbing, and the standalone nano-USD ledger/tests.

## Relationship to #42475

This is the non-enforcing warning action from #42475, using the same `usageBudget` configuration namespace and UTC daily window direction as draft #104060. It intentionally leaves hard limits, reservations, concurrency control, monthly budgets, provider admission, and status/doctor surfaces to the broader enforcement work.

## What Problem This Solves

This measurement PR compares the combined test-performance series on the same compact pull-request matrix as the 459-second baseline. Manual CI expands to a different full named-shard topology and is not a comparable wall-time measurement.

The PR targets the frozen original base commit `d01f03b91c37ed658483293a5c5ed8aff6f6eced`, so later product growth on `main` does not contaminate the comparison.

- Baseline run 30757987976: 459 seconds.
