prs.title: fix(sessions): reclaim expired cron history placeholders
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Isolated cron runs can leave canonical retained-history placeholders after their live session entry is gone. Those intentionally empty SQLite rows are outside the readable session-entry model, so ordinary pruning cannot enumerate them; one observed production store accumulated 1,733 placeholders anchoring 19,206 transcript events.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch extends `openclaw sessions cleanup` with one narrow eligibility contract:

- only canonical cron retained-history placeholders qualify;
- `cron.sessionRetention` owns the age boundary;
- malformed, unidentified, live, referenced, or admitted sessions are preserved;
- transcript state is archived before deletion;
- cleanup covers exactly the logical agents the caller selected, even when several agents share one SQLite store;
- candidates are revalidated under lifecycle admission and the SQLite write transaction;
- committed transcript archives are published after lifecycle and writer locks are released;
- placeholders are swept before disk-budget eviction, so reachable history is not evicted first.

The implementation reports preview/apply counts through the existing cleanup summary. It does not add a second cleanup policy or an unidentified-row deletion mode.

Owner scoping is recorded where it is produced rather than re-derived downstream. When `--all-agents` collapses several configured agents onto one physical database, `dedupeSessionStoreTargetsBySqliteTarget` now records the collapsed logical owners on the surviving target (`SessionStoreTarget.sharedOwnerAgentIds`), and the tombstone sweep scans that owner set. Single-agent selections never go through that dedupe, so `--agent <id>` and the default selection stay scoped to exactly one owner.

## User Impact

Cron-heavy installations can reclaim otherwise unreachable session-store debris through the existing cleanup command without weakening the canonical-key safety boundary or risking live/referenced sessions. `--all-agents` reclaims every selected agent's expired cron history in a shared store instead of silently reclaiming only the physical store owner's, and a single-agent run still touches only that agent.

## Evidence

Historical validation on head `8c0cccfa70bc3989929df42e6579096539863214` (not the current refreshed head):

- focused cleanup, retention, targets, archive-store, session-accessor, runtime, and serialization suites: **144/144 passing** across 20 files;
- adjacent `--all-agents` target consumers (doctor session SQLite / shared-store / transcripts, maintenance schema preflight, default-agent store, CLI route args, status-health-sessions, gateway session startup migration): **313 passing, 2 skipped, 0 failing** across 9 files;
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: passing;
- focused type-aware Oxlint over every changed core and script file: passing;
- `pnpm check:changed`: every branch-owned lane passes (conflict markers, max-lines ratchet, assertion-safety ratchet, changelog attributions, doctor deprecation registry, wildcard re-export guards, duplicate-scan coverage, coercion helpers, dependency pins, formatting, deprecated API usage, wrapper shadowing, package patch guard, dead-export scan, core tsgo graph boundary, script erasability, typechecks, targeted lint, import cycles, database-first legacy-store guard, and the remaining repo guards). Two lanes fail and both are provably inherited from `main` at this head: `typecheck core tests` reports six errors, all in `src/gateway/server.channels-start-outcomes.test.ts`, whose blob is `9166d13ec73c950184a438b5a49d21adeba7b4dd` on both this head and `origin/main`; and `plugin boundaries` reports the purely date-driven "5 compatibility record(s) are due for removal" from `src/plugins/compat/registry-records.ts`, `src/plugins/compat/registry.ts`, and `scripts/plugin-boundary-report.ts`, all byte-identical to `origin/main`, which `scripts/check-changed.mts` documents in place — "After 2026-07-24, lapsed compatibility windows intentionally fail this gate until their scheduled deletion PRs land."

### Production LOC and stored data model

The owner-set repair adds no second cleanup path: the target-to-owner-set mapping moved into the sweep's own entry point, which left `cleanup-service.ts` 4 net lines smaller than before the repair. Round-local production delta is +10 net, 8 of which are the required invariant comments at the ownership boundary.

The branch's remaining ~+406 production lines are feature growth, not a bug-fix diff: 344 of them are the single new `cleanup-tombstones.ts` module carrying candidate listing, lifecycle-admission revalidation, in-transaction revalidation, archive materialization, post-lock archive publication, and cache invalidation. `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` is net -26. The reducible piece is the double revalidation, which is what makes the delete safe under concurrency; the tradeoff is flagged rather than silently trimmed.

No SQLite schema change is involved: the module issues no DDL, adds no table, column, or index, and does not touch a schema version; its writes are `DELETE`s plus existing archive rows through existing Kysely helpers. `shouldRunSqliteSessionSchemaBaselineCheck` does not select this branch's paths, so `check:changed` never schedules the SQLite schema baseline lane for it.

### Real behavior proof

`scripts/proof-117074-tombstone-shared-owners.ts` drives the real `runSessionsCleanup()` against real on-disk SQLite agent databases in a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, through real target resolution, lifecycle admission, write transactions, and archive publication. Nothing between the entrypoint and the assertions is stubbed.

```text
[1] --all-agents over an exact shared .sqlite locator
  ok   dedupe collapses both agents to one physical target = 1
  ok   selected target owner = "main"
  ok   swept remnants across selected owners = 2
  ok   main placeholder removed = 0
  ok   ops placeholder removed = 0
  ok   main transcript archived = 1
  ok   ops transcript archived = 1
[2] --agent main over the same shared store keeps ops isolated
  ok   swept exactly the requested owner = 1
  ok   ops placeholder preserved = 1
  ok   ops not archived = 0
[3] --all-agents over per-agent stores sweeps each store once
  ok   per-agent stores stay distinct targets = 2
  ok   swept one remnant per store = 2

assertions: 22, failures: 0
All runtime assertions passed.
```

On the previous head the same proof reports `assertions: 22, failures: 4` — `swept remnants across selected owners: expected 2, got 1`, plus the surviving `ops` node, transcript, and missing archive. Scenarios 2 and 3 pass on both heads, so the change is scoped to the multi-owner selection.

Two unit regressions pin the contract at the sweep boundary (`cleanup-tombstones.test.ts`): a full selected owner set sweeps every owner of a shared store, and a subset selection leaves an unselected third agent's placeholder, windows, and transcript untouched.

The focused suite also uses one main-owned explicit shared SQLite store containing canonical `main` and `ops` placeholders. Enforcing cleanup as either logical agent opens the physical database as `main`, removes and archives only the selected agent(s), and leaves unselected agents' node, window, and transcript state intact. The completed-sweep case verifies the archive row has a numeric `published_at` and the archive file exists before the command returns.

Exact-head real-store CLI proof used a temporary SQLite agent store containing one 48-hour-old canonical cron placeholder with one transcript event:

```text
before={"nodes":1,"windows":1,"events":1}
command=openclaw sessions cleanup --agent main --enforce --json --store <redacted-store>
tombstoneRemnants={"candidates":1,"removedNodes":1,"sweptTranscriptStates":1,"olderThanMs":86400000}
wouldMutate=true
after={"nodes":0,"windows":0,"events":0,"archives":1}
```

The temporary store was moved to trash after verification.

**Proof boundary:** the multi-owner path is proven through the real cleanup service, target resolution, lifecycle admission, write transactions, archive publication, and real SQLite stores. This is the owner of the CLI cleanup behavior; a live operator Gateway run is not intrinsically required to prove it. This is not a claim that an operator Gateway or production database was modified.

### Current head and round history

Current signed head: [`9adc742d334`](https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/commit/9adc742d334965245b6126ba363d272b87e35f75). The older test counts and inherited failures above remain historical, not current results; round 25 below carries the current ones.

Eleven rounds landed since the September 8 refresh:

1. **`2882b1b5be0` — bounded reference work across tombstone batches.** Candidate revalidation no longer enumerates the full store twice per candidate: the sweep primes reference analysis once for a batch of up to 32 candidates and answers each later boundary from that pass, while a connection-local token (`PRAGMA data_version` plus a TEMP-trigger generation counter) proves no insert, update, or external commit landed since. Both candidate revalidation boundaries are retained; a token change re-reads the store. The single-candidate `instr` probe became exact `IN` membership over the candidate set.

2. **`e63ac16d66f` — reference-preservation repair.** The `IN` prefilter was narrower than the reference parser it prefilters for, which is the regression ClawSweeper raised as [P1]. `collectSessionStateIdsForEntry` trims every id it collects, and an entry parses only when its `sessionId` equals `current_session_id`, so a row whose current id carries leading or trailing whitespace owns the trimmed id — and equality rejected that row before the parser could see it, in both the batch priming scan and the final deletion check. A `trim(current_session_id, …)` membership branch reproducing exactly the code points `String.prototype.trim` removes restores the conservative semantics; both reads share one query builder, so one branch covers both.

3. **`23f7d41a4bd` — concurrent-write latency measured.** `scripts/proof-117074-concurrent-write-latency.ts` drives the real sweep over a seeded 3,096-row mixed store (3,000 live sessions, a seventh of them carrying optional reference fields, plus 96 expired cron placeholders) while a separate OS process performs Gateway-turn-shaped session work through the real accessor at ~120 operations per second. No production file changed.

```text
    candidate scan over the whole store: 9.82ms
    quiet sweep: 70373.94ms total, 733.06ms per candidate, 3 reference batches
    transcript-archive worker threads: 192 spawned, 70023ms of worker lifetime (99.5% of the sweep, off the main thread)
    before sweep: n=729 rate=121.5/s mean=3.14ms p50=2.31ms p95=4.3ms p99=26.35ms max=28.61ms
    during sweep: n=8186 rate=116.06/s mean=3.42ms p50=2.38ms p95=9.76ms p99=27.59ms max=63.79ms
    sweep: 70530.58ms with a writer vs 70373.94ms quiet (1x), 734.69ms per candidate
    with a writer: 0/192 questions served, 192 fell back to a fresh read
    32 reference questions: unbatched 163.11ms (5.1ms each) vs batched 6.23ms (0.19ms each)
```

A continuously written store invalidates the memo completely — 0 of 192 reference questions served, in every run — so the optimization delivers nothing while writes keep landing. It cannot thrash: invalidation deletes the batch, so a batch primes at most once and every later question in it takes the unbatched read. That bounds the degraded case at the pre-batch cost plus one scan per 32-candidate batch, about 12 ms per candidate against a per-candidate sweep cost of 648–888 ms, because ~99.5% of the sweep's wall clock is transcript-archive worker threads running off the main thread. With `resolveBatchedReferencedSessionIds` forced to decline at source, the harness fails exactly the two assertions that pin the memo, EXIT 1. Caveat: run from source under `tsx`, so archive-worker boot is inflated and the reference share of a built runtime's smaller total would be correspondingly larger, still order 1–2%.

4. **`2770adddc6c` — the store writer is released across archive encoding.** The sweep took store writer admission once per candidate and awaited archive materialization inside that hold. The store writer queue is process-local and FIFO (`runQueuedStoreWrite` drains it with `await task.fn()`), so unrelated session writes in the same process — including the Gateway that invoked `sessions.cleanup` — waited for a transcript being encoded on a worker thread. The reclaim now follows the scheduling `session-history-eviction.ts` and `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle.ts` already use: a short `session.maintenance.tombstone-prepare` section revalidates and plans, the writer is released for materialization under reclamation admission, and a short `session.maintenance.tombstone-commit` section re-reads the placeholder and its references inside the deletion transaction before deleting. Lifecycle admission is held across the release and nothing decided before it is trusted after it, so the delete still requires two independent revalidations.

A same-process writer scenario was added to the harness. It runs the Gateway-shaped writer on the sweep's own event loop and reads the real `openclaw.session.write` diagnostics channel, which reports how long each write held the lane and how long it waited for it. Same host, same store, same scale, with and without the fix:

```text
before the fix (head 23f7d41a4bd)
    during sweep: n=4140 rate=58.09/s mean=11.96ms p50=2.49ms p95=19.92ms p99=361.1ms max=444.5ms
    session.maintenance.tombstone-sweep: n=96 mean=370.98ms p95=436ms max=448ms held
    unrelated same-process writes: n=4140 max queue wait=442ms
    (before sweep: rate=123.33/s p95=4.85ms max=31.51ms)

after the fix (head 2770adddc6c)
    during sweep: n=8060 rate=115.48/s mean=3.29ms p50=2.31ms p95=6.51ms p99=27.37ms max=77.89ms
    session.maintenance.tombstone-prepare: n=96 mean=5.54ms p95=8ms max=12ms held
    session.maintenance.tombstone-commit:  n=96 mean=13.34ms p95=27ms max=34ms held
    unrelated same-process writes: n=8060 max queue wait=0ms
    (before sweep: rate=113.33/s p95=6.6ms max=202.05ms)

assertions: 23, failures: 0
All runtime assertions passed.
```

The unfixed head fails three of those assertions rather than merely reporting worse numbers, so the harness is a regression gate and not only a measurement.

Gates at this head: 13 session, cleanup, cron, reclamation, eviction, and store-writer-queue suites were requested and 13 executed — 215 passed, EXIT 0 (81 / 34 / 31 / 22 / 17 / 8 / 8 / 7 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 1 per file; the 81 is `.each` expansion of 17 literal cases). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:scripts`, the type-aware scripts and core oxlint lanes, `format:check`, `deadcode:unused-files` (0 entries on both scans), `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `check:no-conflict-markers`, and `git diff --check` all exit 0. Both proof harnesses exit 0 (23 assertions and 22 assertions, 0 failures).

5. **`5ba3e0d5b80` — upstream `main` integrated.** A merge of `origin/main` only; no branch production file changed in it. This is the head ClawSweeper reviewed as Revision 44 with no findings.

6. **`525a2013c7f` — second `main` integration, and the reference batch rekeyed to the database path.** Upstream's worker-coordinated transcript-archive publish can release and reopen the cached `DatabaseSync` for a path mid-sweep. The batch was keyed by the connection object in a `WeakMap`, so every such dispatch orphaned it and the next candidate fell back to a full re-scan — confirmed empirically by identical archive-publish dispatch counts on a working and a broken tree, with a connection-cache `MISS (fresh open)` immediately following every dispatch only where the batch was lost. Keying `activeBatches` by path fixes that. It also introduced the defect below.

7. **`e552c861ff0` — the reference batch is bound to its originating connection.** Path keying answered *how a batch is found* but left *whether it may be believed* unanswered. Both halves of the validity token — `PRAGMA data_version` and the TEMP-trigger generation counter — are connection-local in the strict sense: on a replacement handle they restart from that handle's own baseline rather than advancing, so a reading taken after an external commit is indistinguishable from one taken before it. Because the sweep releases its store writer across archive materialization and an unborrowed handle can be evicted in that window, both final reference checks could accept a stale memo and delete a generation a live session still references. The batch now carries the handle its token came from plus the priming closure; a replacement **rebuilds** the memo through the live connection (so the remaining candidates keep their single pass) instead of inheriting a proof that cannot describe it, and falls back to a store read if the rebuild cannot be established. `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-batch.test.ts` covers the close/reopen late-reference case: on the unfixed tree it fails with `- Set { "victim" } / + Set {}`, and passes 4/4 with the fix.

8. **`a2b4a1a6e1d` — the proof harnesses join their database owners before removing fixture roots.** `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesForTest()` only *starts* asynchronous resource closure, so the `rmSync` that followed it took the shared-state database out from under reclamation workers that still needed it to release their durable leases. Both harnesses reported every assertion passing and then looped on ENOENT until a wall clock killed them, which made their exit status useless as a verdict. Each harness now collects its fixture roots and releases them through `cleanupSessionStateForTest`, the existing awaited lifecycle owner, before any root is removed; the concurrent-writer child releases its own leases and its parent joins the child's exit rather than killing it. The drain runs once, after the last scenario, because it is process-wide: draining between scenarios left every later scenario measuring a cold store and blew the latency harness's busy-timeout ceilings (7247 ms and 12395 ms against a 5000 ms bound, versus 1603 ms and 204 ms with a single end-of-run drain). Measured at this head: `proof-117074-tombstone-shared-owners.ts` 22 assertions / 0 failures / **0 ENOENT lines / EXIT 0**, against a pre-fix control on the same tree of 22 assertions / 0 failures / **284419 ENOENT lines / EXIT 124**; `proof-117074-concurrent-write-latency.ts` 23 assertions / 0 failures / 0 ENOENT lines / EXIT 0. The same round cleared four branch-owned CI lanes: an unused exported type (`SessionReferenceOwnerSink`, now module-local) that failed `check-dependencies`, two `node:sqlite` row assertions that needed `// SAFETY:` invariants for `check:assertion-safety`, and an `oxfmt --check` violation in the latency harness that was failing both `check-lint` and `check-docs`.

9. **`2390dc75a78` — the latency harness fails when its writer process exits badly.** Revision 47 found the join added above incomplete: the exit promise resolved regardless of exit code or signal, and the child published its report *before* awaiting its own drain, so a drain exception or the 30-second kill backstop still let the harness print a passing result. That is the original defect's own shape — a verdict outrunning its shutdown. The child now drains first and publishes afterwards, so a readable report is evidence the drain *succeeded*; the parent keeps the exit outcome and throws on a nonzero code, a signal, or the backstop firing, with the child's captured output attached. Negative control: with the child forced to `process.exitCode = 3` the harness throws `writer process did not shut down cleanly: code=3 signal=null`, never prints `All runtime assertions passed`, and exits 1. At this head the harness reports 23 assertions / 0 failures / 0 ENOENT lines / EXIT 0, with busy-timeout ceilings observed at 137.77 ms and 83.17 ms against the 5000 ms bound.

10. **`83b5b6d460f` — the cleanup suite drains its fixture databases, and its scan-budget fixture stops manufacturing an external commit (this round).** Two coupled defects, and fixing only the first moves the failure rather than removing it. (a) `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesForTest()` in `afterEach` only *starts* asynchronous resource retirement, so the registered temp-dir hook could remove the fixture databases while reclamation workers still held their durable leases; the suite's 17 assertions passed and the shard then exited 1 on `AggregateError: Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state` caused by `ENOENT ... /state/openclaw.sqlite`. `afterEach` now awaits `cleanupSessionStateForTest({ stateDir: tempDir })`, the existing awaited lifecycle owner, and Vitest's reverse-order `afterEach` scheduling settles it before the tracker's removal. (b) With drainage correct, `keeps the reference work SQLite performs flat as the backlog grows` then fails at `expected 33 to be less than or equal to 3` in the whole-file run too, not just under a `-t` filter. Instrumented cause: every entry write ends in `kickSessionEntryMaintenanceAfterWrite`, which queues a coalesced `setImmediate` maintenance pass; that pass reclaims with `forceInProcess: false`, so `runSqliteSessionReclamation` dispatches a Worker that opens the store on its own connection and commits. Probing `PRAGMA data_version` across each sweep phase shows the sweeping connection observing `dv 2 → 3` with the TEMP generation unchanged, one candidate after the seeding's maintenance pass lands. From that connection the commit is indistinguishable from an external writer creating a reference, so `revalidateSessionReferenceBatch` correctly drops the batch and the remaining candidates take the unbatched read — one batched pass plus 11 × 3 fallback statements is exactly the 33 observed. The order dependence has the same source: a whole-file run satisfies the maintenance age gate in an earlier test (one dispatch for the entire file) while the scan-budget test alone dispatches 30. The two scaling fixtures now seed through a local helper that passes the existing `skipMaintenance` option, so the fixture's own background maintenance cannot commit inside the window whose database work is being measured; every other test seeds exactly as before. **No production file changed, and reference invalidation is not weakened** — the batch still drops on any real external commit, and `re-reads references for a later candidate when a late owner appears mid-batch` still covers that path at full strength. Negative controls, each reverting one half: reverting only the awaited drainage gives 17 passed then the same `AggregateError` / `ENOENT` at EXIT 1; reverting only `skipMaintenance` gives `1 failed | 16 passed` with `AssertionError: expected 33 to be less than or equal to 3` at EXIT 1, in the full suite as well as under `-t`. At this head: the file passes 17/17 with the shard at EXIT 0 where it previously exited 1 on teardown; each measurement test passes alone under `-t` (`1 passed | 16 skipped`); and the acceptance scope (`cleanup-tombstones`, `cleanup-service.order`, `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-batch`) is 22 passed at EXIT 0.

11. **`9adc742d334` — the reclaim's undo restores the conversation, not just the rows that owned it (this round).** Addresses revision 58's [P1] and three of its four [P2]s, plus three breakages the branch carried that a source-only review could not see because **the branch did not compile at `164d9b405ab`** (`pnpm tsgo:core` reported five errors there; one was the review's own database-path [P2], the rest arrived in the 2026-10-08 `main` merge with no conflict marker — `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` gained a leading operation argument, and `readSqliteDataVersion` moved to `infra/sqlite-schema-facts.js`, which also broke the latency harness).

    [P1]: the post-delete snapshot held only `session_nodes` and `session_windows`, but `transcript_events` cascades off `session_windows` (`openclaw-agent-schema.sql:575`) along with eight other tables, and two more cascade off `transcript_events` — so restoring the metadata put a placeholder back with its conversation permanently gone while the sweep counted the candidate as restored. The new `cleanup-tombstones-snapshot.ts` captures the full cascade by walking `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` outward from `session_windows`, so a table added later is captured without anyone updating that file and a cascade the walk cannot follow by name throws rather than silently restoring less than the delete removed. Restoration now runs through the lifecycle mutation owner, the writer lane and a write transaction instead of bare inserts on a long-lived handle, and each restored generation is marked for the transcript index owner's reconcile (its projection table carries no foreign key and its FTS5 table has a delete-only trigger, so replaying projection rows would desynchronize it). Both directions measured on the existing restore test: with the fix, `transcript_events` = 1 with its seeded text intact and `transcript_event_identities` = 1; without the cascade capture those three assertions fail while every pre-existing assertion in the same test still passes.

    [P2] handle reuse: `batchDatabase` was opened once and reused across awaited archive materialization and publication, either of which can release and reopen the cached connection; every synchronous group now re-acquires the current handle. [P2] proof seeding: both harnesses deleted the readable entry outside an entry transaction, which `writeSessionEntrySnapshots` refuses; both now seed through `runOpenClawAgentWriteTransaction` and run to completion (22 and 23 assertions, 0 failures). [P2] off-thread database work is **not** addressed — it is enforced by `check:database-worker-ratchet` (main-thread SQLite T1 796 -> 804, eight call sites in `cleanup-tombstones.ts`), this round adds none of them, and `runExclusiveSqliteSessionWrite`'s `writer: "worker"` is an admission-queue choice rather than a thread dispatch, so the ask is a module redesign and a maintainer question is open on the PR.

    Also this round: the branch's own *"admits an unrelated same-process write"* test was measuring the wrong thing — run as a control with no sweep and nothing held, a plain `replaceSessionEntry` reports `pending` after 500 `setImmediate` turns, so the probe called an unobstructed write blocked; it is now a wall-clock budget asserting the write completes before the parked sweep is released. `check:line-cap-ratchet` (which the previous environment could never run, because git 2.34 lacks `cat-file --batch -z`) reported a real violation at `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-state.ts` 700 -> 712 counted lines; narrowed reference reads and the batched analysis moved to `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-scan.ts`. The *"keeps the reference work SQLite performs flat"* test was removed at the reviewer's request: its 6.5x per-candidate allowance accepts the per-candidate scanning it was written to forbid, so it could not discriminate, and it shipped a `DBG_SCAN` debug branch; its sibling holds a tight 1.5x ratio and still guards the quadratic-revalidation regression.

    Gates at this head: `pnpm check:changed` 35 / 37 lanes green. The two reds are the worker ratchet above and `lint:core`, whose eight `max-lines` offenders are each byte-identical to `origin/main`. `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `deadcode:unused-files` (Knip production and full-tree, 0 entries each), `git diff --check`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:scripts` all clean — the three tsgo lanes were red at the reviewed head. Focused vitest: 11 files, 99 tests, 0 failures. Both proof harnesses exit 0.

**Status of the merge risks.** The writer-admission defect is fixed and measured above, including a negative control that fails on the unfixed head. Contended latency is measured on both axes: across processes (a second OS process at ~120 ops/s, p95 4.3 → 9.8 ms) and within one process (the axis a separate process structurally cannot observe, p95 6.6 → 6.5 ms, queue wait 0 ms). No representative-scale latency *improvement* is claimed for the contended case; the claim is that the degradation is bounded and off the critical path.

**Integration status, current as of this edit.** `525a2013c7f` merged then-current `origin/main` and resolved the three conflicted files recorded in the round-10 comment (`session-canonical-key.ts`, `targets-dedupe.test.ts`, `combined-store-gateway.test.ts`), and GitHub reported `mergeable: true` at `e552c861ff0`. That is no longer true: the fork's `main` is **1,863 commits behind `upstream/main`** as measured at this edit, GitHub reports `mergeable: false` / `mergeable_state: dirty` for head `9adc742d334`, and because no merge ref is produced the heavy `pull_request` matrix is not dispatched here at all — so the lightweight lanes are the only CI signal on this PR. The branch has only ever been fast-forwarded; the conflict is upstream drift, not a rewrite. Syncing the fork is not ours to do, so re-integrating and validating the resolved tree remains the outstanding merge-risk item.

No green-CI claim is made here: read the live check list on the PR rather than this paragraph, which cannot stay current.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.title: chore(copilot): cover transcript finalization durability
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds missing integration coverage for Copilot attempt finalization when a tool transcript group is still committing or its SQLite transaction fails.

## User Impact

No runtime or user-visible behavior changes. This test protects the existing final-attempt durability contract; it does not require persistence before the SDK tool reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new cases exercise the registered SDK tool handler, simulated SDK completion events, the attempt-owned journal, canonical SQLite group append, and attempt finalization together. A deferred append proves that an attempt cannot finish successfully before persistence settles. The failure case uses a real transactional fault to verify rollback, the preserved transcript prefix, a visible persistence failure, unsafe replay, and no automatic tool re-execution.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135969. That PR remains open: this coverage does not implement or supersede its stronger pre-reply receipt and replay guarantees.

## Evidence

- Initial independent source review and scoped Codex autoreview found no actionable source findings. Separate independent delta review accepted the fixture corrections at `2d28d3e71add2b71dbdc61e40b2cdde6134cbd9e`.
- Formatting and `git diff --check`: pass.
- One test file changed, production LOC unchanged. No changelog entry needed.
- Initial CI at `b3e2968f42251fdec387acafe7da2613ec69e42b` exposed two fixture mistakes: the retired `@sinclair/typebox` import prevented test loading, and the inline parameters rejected the existing Copilot `auth` option. No integration cases ran. Evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660633869/job/116181178004 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660633869/job/116181601147.
- The correction uses the current `typebox` package and validates the parameters against the public attempt contract plus the existing internal auth option. Runtime values, assertions, transaction gates, and cleanup ordering are unchanged.
- Runtime execution and affected types/lint require fresh exact-head CI. The source checkout has no qualified dependencies; its shared dependency refusal was preserved. Initial general lint passed, but it does not establish corrected-head proof.
- Before landing, verify that CI executes all three cases in `extensions/copilot/src/attempt-session.integration.test.ts`, including both new commit/rollback cases.
- No live model-provider, real Code Mode engine, or whole-PR135969 qualification is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the `check-dependencies` CI job (Knip `deadcode:exports`) fails on `main` (scheduled CI run 38663143259) and on the `release/2026.10.10` FRV CI (job 116187243542), blocking 2026.10.10-beta.1, because recent refactors left eight exports with no remaining consumers.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Unblocks red `main` and the 2026.10.10 beta release gate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each flagged symbol lost its last outside consumer in a recent PR. The fix deletes the export (or the symbol) instead of adding Knip exceptions:

| Symbol | Orphaned by | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AuthProfileAuthorizationError` re-export in `src/agents/auth-profiles/authorization.ts` | #172590 (callers import `authorization-contract.ts` directly) | drop the value re-export, keep the type re-export |
| `configuredOrFalseAsync` (`src/gateway/talk/session-config.ts`) | #172556 / #170343 | module-private |
| `WorkerPreparationArtifactsSchema` | #172342 | module-private |
| `PostgresSchemaDefinition` (type) | #172265 | module-private |
| `readPairedDevicePairingRecordsFromDatabase` | #172388 (last outside caller removed; only a test imported it) | module-private; the test reads the same rows through the exported `readDevicePairingStoreStateFromDatabase(...).pairedByDeviceId` |
| `renderCopyButton` (`ui/src/components/copy-button.ts`) | #172383 (Solid migration left only the browser test) | inlined into `renderCopyAsMarkdownButton`; the clipboard browser test now drives that production renderer |

## Evidence

- `pnpm deadcode:exports`: on base reproduces exactly the CI list; with this change production, full-tree and script scans pass with 0 entries. `pnpm deadcode:dependencies`: passes.
- Release branch: the same patch applies cleanly to `origin/release/2026.10.10` (c92d7743aa9c). Unpatched, its `deadcode:exports` list is identical to the list above; patched, all three scans pass with 0 entries.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep persisted reasoning steps visible
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved reasoning and tool steps disappearing when live previews hand off to persisted assistant rows.

## User Impact

With reasoning enabled, saved thoughts and their tool steps remain visible in transcript order. Disabling reasoning still collapses the tool activity. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persisted assistant rows containing tool calls were normalized as tool results, so adjacent reasoning steps collapsed into generic activity even after their matching live previews retired. Pass the existing reasoning preference into grouping and count enabled assistant thinking as visible assistant content. Durable ownership, receipt matching, and completed-work classification stay unchanged.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing receipt regression extended with two metadata-owned saved thoughts/tools and a live third thought | Failed before the fix: only the current thought remained visible |
| Whole changed chat-reasoning test file, one worker | 15/15 passed |
| UI typecheck | Passed |
| Scoped lint and whitespace | Passed |
| Independent Codex review through P2 | No actionable findings |
| Post-merge production/unit patch comparison | Byte-identical to reviewed patch |
| Final-head CI performance (run 38672885176) | Passed: startup JS 349,932 B gzip; CSS 46,058 B gzip in 1 request; chat boot +54 B with unchanged request count |
| Final-head reasoning browser proof | Both reasoning-on and reasoning-stream cases passed on shard 3 (426/426); all six reasoning-visibility cases passed on shard 2 |

The unit test preserves the original receipt assertions and checks that reasoning off hides thoughts and renders one activity summary. The browser regression retains every thought-count, transcript-order, completed-work expansion, and final-answer assertion. With reasoning on, persisted assistant rows render directly under expanded work without a nested Raw details group; stream mode still requires Raw details expansion. Both tool summaries must remain present exactly once. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no local E2E or UI build was run for this behavior correction.

LOC: production 1,511 → 1,525 (+14); test 489 → 545 (+56). Browser test 227 → 240 (+13). Total 2,227 → 2,310 (+83), across four files (+92/-9). The growth is the regression scenario and plumbing the existing preference; no new abstraction or state owner.

CI exposed obsolete midstream and final nested Raw details expectations for reasoning-on mode. The explicit mode-specific assertions keep completed-work expansion, reasoning counts, transcript order, and final-answer proof, and add exact-once presence checks for both tool summaries. All four cron-duration-save real-Gateway failures, four Models loading failures, and four native-consent failures match the latest scheduled main run 38672095119 (a4d316dc) by exact test name and assertion/stack signature. Both reasoning cases now pass on this PR’s final head.

Run 38670066751 also observed one provider-browser-login failure: the dialog remained mounted after an API-key profile was saved. The older scheduled-main run had passed, so this was initially unattributed. The newest scheduled-main run 38672095119 now reproduces the same case and assertion. Source inspection confirms an obsolete test expectation after the login controller intentionally retained the connected completion screen; the focused correction is tracked in #172732. No provider-login behavior is changed here. Final-head Gateway 1 reproduces that exact same case and full assertion/stack signature. In total, all thirteen final-head failed cases match the newest scheduled main run. The native inherited-failure route retains this failed CI state explicitly.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render chat widgets and tool previews with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat widgets, tool previews, source cards, and detail-slot renderers still use Lit around the Solid chat surface.

## User Impact

The layout and existing actions remain intact. Widget actions are positioned in their first attachment frame, and canvas frames retain their document and controls across row replacement. Retained hidden transcripts pause widget activity and placement observation, then resume the same host on reveal.

## Why This Change Was Made

These surfaces now render with Solid, with their superseded Lit implementations removed. Canvas remains a ref-owned DOM island under its existing frame owner; MCP, canvas, and YouTube retain their lazy imports. Remaining Lit callers use thin adapters. Main's native tool cards, syntax folding, media identity, and composer lifecycle fixes are preserved.

The candidate integrates main `c94f47ea885ba1bb8eb80ed9f5434b43678f66f3`. All 19 tracked widget production paths are byte-identical to the previously reviewed `5f11b5391c46` implementation. Main now also contains the same diff-runtime cleanup, leaving 18 production paths in this PR's effective diff. prs.title: improve: keep latest commentary visible in progress draft headers
prs.body:
Related: #132781

## What Problem This Solves

When newer work lines evict model commentary from a bounded progress draft, the latest model-authored status disappears with them. This PR keeps the latest completed preamble available as a headline independently of the rolling history.

## User Impact

Progress drafts retain the current model-authored status above the work history. Where `streaming.progress.commentary` is supported and enabled, a completed preamble is both a headline candidate and a bounded history entry. Compact previews can display both; Slack Block Kit cards keep their existing deduplication of matching narration/history text. No configuration keys or channel narrators are added. Matrix and Mattermost retain their existing configuration surface and do not expose the optional commentary setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared compositor stages headline and commentary changes together before publishing, including keyed retractions. Incomplete preambles do not replace the last completed text. Current-main startup, final-delivery, quiet-mode, and Telegram ownership rules remain intact. Telegram dispatch and adopted action-edit snapshots both retain authored history when the existing commentary option is enabled.

### Narration interaction

- A fresh completed preamble has headline priority for 20 seconds; narration received during that window is retained.
- At expiry, retained narration takes over, otherwise a retained plan explanation can take over. Without either fallback, the preamble remains visible.
- A distinct new preamble can regain priority. Existing identity/deduplication rules remain unchanged.
- Headline selection neither reorders commentary history nor exempts it from `maxLines`.

## Evidence

Current head: [cdfa980c158](https://github.com/MertBasar0/openclaw/commit/cdfa980c158f4eae91454d00f890851b80b29244), incorporating main `553c6bde778c0c55b7418a5908d5fdeef735cf82`. All six local merge conflicts were resolved. The following evidence supersedes the previous-head validation summary.

- The final focused repository-wrapper run passed all four shards with `--maxWorkers=1` in **168.18 seconds**: Telegram dispatch HTTP **29/29** (89.54 s), Telegram action-edit HTTP **9/9** (36.76 s), shared compositor suites **63/63** (4.23 s), and the complete Slack preview-fallback suite. Other affected boundary runs passed: Discord process draft progress **18/18**, Discord REST draft preview **11/11**, Telegram progress lifecycle **14/14**, Matrix visibility **2/2**, and streaming/progress helpers **37/37**. Hosted CI time for this head is not yet measured.
- The two commentary-enabled Telegram action-edit variants failed before forwarding the existing account commentary setting, then passed after the fix. A dispatch negative control also failed the four enabled-commentary reasoning variants when forwarding was omitted. The correct source was restored before final proof.
- All six freshness-order/commentary combinations passed. The independent review's suggested startup/expiry P2 was rejected after inspecting the unchanged startup owner, which already schedules expiry. No speculative scheduling change was introduced. A fresh independent diff review of the final behavioral patch completed `scoped-clean` with no P0–P2 findings; this is not independently executed runtime or live-channel proof.
- Core production, all 27 core-test type graphs, extension production/test types, both full lint lanes, formatting, and the other 35 planned diagnostics passed. **The aggregate changed check remains failed:** the environment-variable budget is 476 while pinned main and this candidate both contain the same 477 names, with no additions or removals. No budget, ignore, suppression, or dependency override was added. The diagnostic continuation is not presented as a green aggregate gate. A full global test run and build were not rerun.
- The previous-head CI task-progress failure belonged to the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime subsequently removed by [#159179](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159179). Its retired test was not restored or described as passing. The gateway teardown race was addressed upstream by [#153302](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153302); the unchanged current-main reset suite passed **20/20** after integration. Obsolete Telegram test copies were removed only after preserving their six reasoning/preamble variants and two atomic-publication cases in the canonical HTTP suite.

## Open Review Work

- Maintainer agreement is still needed on independent headline/history presentation, as noted in the [earlier review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137696#issuecomment-5533988664). Atomic publication and narration/plan handoff are covered locally.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof and inspected before/after screenshots in both chat and this PR remain outstanding. The QA broker/login and required QA credentials were unavailable. Local HTTP mock-transport tests are boundary evidence, not live evidence or a substitute for the screenshot completion/landing gate. Team QA access or validation by an authorized team member is needed.
- Hosted CI must be evaluated on **this exact head**. Earlier failures and local results do not establish new-head CI success. This update publishes only the PR branch and does not merge the PR into main.

prs.title: fix: failed turns lose their "ended before a reply" notice when another session is mid-turn
prs.body:
Related: #150372

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose turn fails before any reply would see the turn
marked failed but get no explanation in the conversation, when the failure is
handled while another session's agent turn is still running.

The affected surface is durable conversation history: the "This turn ended
before a reply: ..." notice that normally explains a failed turn. On an affected
run the session status still becomes `failed`, but the transcript has no notice,
so the conversation simply stops with no visible reason. The Gateway logs
`terminal session persistence failed ... SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`.

Observed on 2026.9.4 on a subagent session whose run failed after provider
context-overflow recovery was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway's definitive lifecycle write now runs detached from any inherited
owned-transcript write context, which is what every comparable detached Gateway
and registry path already does (`update-run-notice.runtime.ts`,
`session-event-wake.ts`, `subagent-registry-run-wait.ts`,
`sessions-send-tool.ts`, and the explicit `else` branch in
`session-prompt-state.ts`).

Cause: agent events dispatch synchronously through `notifyListeners`, so the
Gateway handler executes in the emitter's async context and inherits that
attempt's writer context. Inside `withCurrentTranscript`,
`withOwnedSessionTranscriptWriterFence` spreads the inherited fence last, so it
replaces the `sessionId` and `expectedLifecycleRevision` that
`persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` had just read from its committed status
write, and adds an `expectedWriterRunId` the Gateway never supplied. That last
part is what makes the failure loud: without a writer id a fence mismatch
returns `err(refusal)`, but with one `withCurrentTranscript` throws. The status
write is awaited first and had already committed, which is why the session shows
`failed` with no notice.

Non-goal: this does not change the ownership guard itself. It changes only which
context the Gateway's own write is validated against. `chat-send-dispatch-errors.ts`
still calls `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` directly, outside this owner
seam; that path is guarded by `if (!hasActiveRun)` and is left alone here.

## User Impact

A failed turn keeps its durable explanation even when the failure is processed
while another session's turn is running. Operators reading a session after the
fact see why it stopped instead of a silent gap, and the spurious
`SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` no longer appears for writes whose
owner never actually changed.

## Validation

`src/gateway/session-lifecycle-terminal-write-detach.test.ts` (new, 9 tests),
verified against `main` at `cea9c9cb7695e8817ca72d7fcc2884d031e5ff30`.

With the source change reverted, the 6 inheritance tests fail with the exact
production error, `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer
claim changed before transcript persistence`; the 3 ownership-protection tests
pass both before and after, so they are not vacuous.

Coverage: ordinary failed run; same-session compaction followed by failure under
an unchanged owner; duplicate suppression when the run already has a durable
assistant error; repeated terminal events; a delayed retained callback that
reinstalls a settled context; the non-definitive `persist()` fallback; and three
cases that must stay rejected (cross-session report, replaced session, expired
run authority).

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-terminal-write-detach.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-persistence-owner.test.ts
  -> 43 passed  (6 fail without the source change)

pnpm tsgo:core                      -> exit 0
oxlint --type-aware (changed files) -> exit 0
oxfmt --check       (changed files) -> exit 0
```

The 21 pre-existing tests in `session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts` are
unmodified and still pass. CLI-history behaviour is unchanged: the detach happens
before `writeContext.run`, which still re-establishes the CLI history writer, and
the five existing CLI-history-through-terminal-persistence tests still pass.

The incident that prompted this was observed on the 2026.9.4 release build; the
affected file is byte-identical there and on `main`, and all figures above are
from `main`.

prs.title: fix(test): status concurrent-writer E2E flakes with database is locked after Gateway start
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the status shared-state E2E test (`reads status while the Gateway owns state and another writer is active`) fails intermittently with `database is locked` when the freshly started Gateway is still writing state.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This removes a flaky release Gateway E2E failure. `openclaw status` was not at fault.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure is in the test fixture's own writer, not in the status read path. The fixture opened `new DatabaseSync(databasePath)`, which uses node:sqlite's default busy timeout of 0, and then ran `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The Gateway keeps writing after `/readyz` reports ready, so when that write overlaps, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` fails with `SQLITE_BUSY` before `openclaw status` runs. Product writers wait up to `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) for the write lock. The fixture now uses the same timeout, so it still acts like a normal concurrent writer and the read-only status contract from #124142 stays the same.

## Evidence

- Failing CI: Run 38659003163 attempt 1, [Repo E2E (Gateway 1/4)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659003163/job/116178543430), extended-stable/2026.9.33 candidate `ee321a1587b`. The error was thrown at `test/status-shared-state-readonly.e2e.test.ts:194` (`writer.exec("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")`): `{ code: 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR', errcode: 5, errstr: 'database is locked' }`. Status never ran.
- Deterministic reproduction through the real test, using a local scratch patch that was not committed: right after `startGateway()`, a separate process holds a write transaction on the Gateway's `openclaw.sqlite` for 300 ms, standing in for a post-ready Gateway write.
  - Old fixture: fails with the exact CI error at `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `errcode: 5`.
  - New fixture: passes.
- Status is not blocked by the writer: in a scratch probe against the same live Gateway, `status --json` took 12.6 s / 19.1 s with no writer and 11.7 s / 16.1 s with the writer held. The host load average was 50–140, so the time comes from load, not from lock waits.
- Unmodified test with the fix: passed locally. One loop iteration on this heavily loaded shared host timed out on the existing 15 s `status --json` limit (no lock error). The probe above shows that comes from host load. In CI the whole test takes 4.4 s.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root` passed. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the touched file.
- Test cost: no new test, and this test's runtime does not change (4360 ms in the CI job above). The busy wait only applies when the Gateway is writing at that moment, for at most a few hundred milliseconds.

prs.title: fix(e2e): typed onboarding lane times out on the optional memory setup prompt
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Package Acceptance `release-typed-onboarding` Docker lane times out (`Timeout waiting for log: to search`) for every package that contains optional memory embedding setup (#163693), including the 2026.10.10-beta.1 candidate and every `main` release-check candidate since that feature landed.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Release validation can qualify packages that offer optional memory embedding setup again; the lane no longer blocks 2026.10.10 publication on a harness gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

#163693 intentionally added a `Set up memory embeddings?` confirm (default No, documented in `docs/start/wizard.md`) after first-agent setup and before the web search provider picker. The typed-onboarding driver went straight from the first-agent prompt to waiting for the searchable web search picker (`to search`), so the wizard sat on the new confirm until the 60s wait expired. The driver now accepts the default No when the confirm appears and continues unchanged when it does not (older packages go straight to the picker).

The release harness resolves this scenario from the frozen target, so 2026.10.10 needs this commit cherry-picked onto `release/2026.10.10` (applies cleanly).

Update behavior: none. This only changes the Docker E2E driver script; no product, update, Doctor, or migration code changes.

## Evidence

- Failing candidate run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38667134742 job 116205368769; the artifact onboarding log ends on `Set up memory embeddings? ○ Yes / ● No` before the `to search` timeout. The same lane fails on `main` candidate runs (for example 38652005622, 38529602619) and passes on `release/2026.10.5`, which does not contain #163693.
- Local reproduction with release/2026.10.10 package bytes (b29410f1c44): the prompt order is first agent → `Set up memory embeddings?` → web search picker (`Type: to search`).
- Fixed driver functions run verbatim against the same package bytes in a PTY: wizard exits 0, memory setup is skipped and `ollama` web search is selected in the written config.
- Full lane, local Docker: `bash scripts/e2e/release-typed-onboarding-docker.sh` from `release/2026.10.10` (b29410f1c44) with this commit cherry-picked, using the exact candidate package artifact `package-under-test-38667134742-1` and its prepublish plugin registry (`docker-e2e-prepublish-plugin-registry-38666065157-1`): `Release typed onboarding Docker E2E passed.`
- `bash -n` on the scenario.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): stop posting routine reconnects as system events
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent's main session fills up with "WhatsApp gateway connected" and "WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status N)" system events when WhatsApp reconnects on its own.

The WhatsApp watchdog closes and reopens an app-silent socket on a routine schedule (status 499), and transient closes like 428 or 503 also reconnect by themselves. Each one posted a disconnected event and then a connected event to the agent, so a healthy channel produced a steady stream of events the agent could not act on.

## User Impact

User impact: agents no longer see routine WhatsApp reconnects. They still get a "WhatsApp gateway disconnected" event when monitoring actually stops (logged out, session conflict, or reconnect attempts exhausted), which is the case that needs attention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconnects that the monitor recovers from are already visible in the gateway logs and in channel status. The system event now only fires on a close where the reconnect policy decides to stop. The "connected" event is dropped, since it only ever followed one of these routine closes or the first start.

## Evidence

- New test in `auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts`: a retried close (499) posts no system event, and a following logged-out close (401) posts exactly one "WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status 401)".
- The new test fails on `main` (3 events posted) and passes with the fix. The full file passes (28 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass. oxfmt and oxlint clean on the touched files.
- Seen live on a long-running gateway: the main session got a disconnected/connected pair from every watchdog reconnect.
- Test cost: the touched file runs 28 tests in 1.6 s (37 s wall with transform, single run, `vitest run --config <e2e config> extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts`); the new case takes about 0.1 s.

Runtime output, before and after. This drives the real `monitorWebChannel` loop and the real gateway system-event queue (nothing mocked there); only the Baileys socket is scripted, so it can close with 499 (watchdog reconnect) and then 401 (logged out). After each step it prints the channel status the gateway receives and the system events queued for the agent's main session (`peekSystemEvents("agent:main:main")`). A terminal close on a live link needs logging out the linked phone, so I did not force one on a production account.

`main` (093ccc8a1):

```
[proof] status connected=true reconnectAttempts=0 lastDisconnect=none
[proof] connected (listener 1); system events: ["WhatsApp gateway connected."]
[proof] status connected=false reconnectAttempts=1 lastDisconnect={"status":499,"loggedOut":false}
[proof] status connected=true reconnectAttempts=0 lastDisconnect=none
[proof] closed 499, reconnected (listener 2); system events: ["WhatsApp gateway connected.","WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status 499)","WhatsApp gateway connected."]
[proof] status connected=false reconnectAttempts=1 lastDisconnect={"status":401,"loggedOut":true}
[proof] closed 401 logged out, monitor stopped; system events: ["WhatsApp gateway connected.","WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status 499)","WhatsApp gateway connected.","WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status 401)"]
```

This branch:

```
[proof] status connected=true reconnectAttempts=0 lastDisconnect=none
[proof] connected (listener 1); system events: []
[proof] status connected=false reconnectAttempts=1 lastDisconnect={"status":499,"loggedOut":false}
[proof] status connected=true reconnectAttempts=0 lastDisconnect=none
[proof] closed 499, reconnected (listener 2); system events: []
[proof] status connected=false reconnectAttempts=1 lastDisconnect={"status":401,"loggedOut":true}
[proof] closed 401 logged out, monitor stopped; system events: ["WhatsApp gateway disconnected (status 401)"]
```

The recovered 499 close still shows in channel status (`lastDisconnect` 499, then connected again) but queues nothing for the agent. The 401 close stops the monitor and queues exactly one notification.

prs.title: fix(e2e): align release Docker lanes with store-backed channel setup and talk catalog warming
prs.body:
## Problem

The 2026.10.10-beta.1 Plugin Prerelease candidate run ([38667135653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38667135653)) failed three Docker E2E release lanes on harness drift, not product regressions:

- `npm-onboard-channel-agent`, `npm-onboard-discord-candidate-channel-agent`, `npm-onboard-slack-candidate-channel-agent`: `assert-channel-config` still required plaintext tokens in `openclaw.json`. Since #169732, `channels add` writes new channel credentials to the protected secret store and persists a `{ source: "store", id: "CHANNEL_SETUP_<hex>" }` SecretRef, so the lanes failed with `telegram config did not persist botToken; expected 123456:openclaw-npm-onboard-token, got {"source":"store",...}` (same for Discord `token` and Slack `botToken`).
- `kitchen-sink-rpc`: since #172556, a cold `talk.catalog` read answers `UNAVAILABLE` / `retryable: true` / `retryAfterMs: 250` (`talk-catalog-warming`) while the first snapshot builds; Control UI, Swift and Android retry it. The walk's `retryRpcCall` only retried transport/startup strings, so the first catalog probe failed the lane with `GatewayClientRequestError: Talk catalog is warming; retry shortly`. Nothing warms the catalog before the probe, so this is a consistent failure, not a flake.

## Solution

- npm onboard lane: each channel token field must be a store SecretRef with a `CHANNEL_SETUP_` id; the referenced team secret-store row in `state/openclaw.sqlite` must hold exactly the fixture token (wrong or swapped values fail, without printing values); and the plaintext token must not appear anywhere in `openclaw.json`.
- kitchen-sink walk: `isRetryableGatewayCallError` also retries typed request errors the Gateway marks `retryable: true`, within the existing ready-timeout budget. Both RPC paths carry that flag: the in-process `callGateway` error and the CLI fallback via `parseGatewayCliRequestFailure`.

## Evidence

- Lane logs from artifacts `docker-e2e-npm-onboard-*` and `docker-e2e-kitchen-sink-rpc-plugin-update` of run 38667135653 (errors quoted above).
- Real CLI boundary: with an isolated `HOME`, the built release/2026.10.10 CLI ran `channels add --channel slack --bot-token … --app-token …`. The `origin/main` assertion then failed with the same CI error (`did not persist botToken; expected xoxb-proof-bot, got {"source":"store",...}`). This head's assertion passes, and swapping the bot/app tokens fails with `slack botToken SecretRef CHANNEL_SETUP_… did not store the expected token`.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/npm-onboard-channel-agent-assertions.test.ts test/scripts/kitchen-sink-rpc-walk.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 files, 106 tests passed; 141.9 s wall locally, mostly cold transform (the assertion tests spawn node per case, under 100 ms each). `pnpm tsgo:scripts` and oxfmt are clean.
- Kitchen-sink retry: no predicate-only unit test. `retryRpcCall` drives a built Gateway client against a live Gateway, so the boundary proof is the release Plugin Prerelease `kitchen-sink-rpc` rerun.
- Clean `git cherry-pick` onto `origin/release/2026.10.10`.

When the normal event/message lookup cannot identify the conversation type, resolve it from the existing chat metadata API using the known chat ID. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settings navigation still rendered through Lit inside the Solid shell. This ports the sidebar, embedded Settings header/list, and lazy fallback to Solid while preserving host tags, classes, routes, search ranking, connection recovery, and agent selection.

The shell retains one lazy renderer. Components subscribe to the existing selection, identity, locale, and branding owners, which remain synchronous TypeScript. Unrelated status publications preserve the current search draft and navigation focus. Sidebar controllers use the existing Solid lifecycle contracts; custom-element bridges expose precise JSX props. No dependency or new state owner is added.

The branding region still uses the existing `LitContent` adapter until its separate port lands. The generated boot manifest retains the old `settings-sidebar-lazy.ts` membership string; it is not an entry point, and recursive group dependencies include the emitted TSX implementation. Paired measurements confirm Settings remains lazy. The final sweep owns obsolete manifest membership cleanup; the review thread was answered and resolved.

| Current head | `982de049d4d701948e1124393d03b6cfcbd3fe58`, ordinary integration of canonical main `22e08398513c2b506bab8270aa6bc38901d08957`. The sole conflict preserves main's reserved footer connection line in the Solid replacement; the old Lit file remains deleted. |

prs.body:

Related: [openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#1705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1705), the companion Reactor welcome-screen consumer of this Gateway catalog.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Native clients need the connected Gateway's welcome text and starter prompts without copying the web strings and manually keeping them synchronized.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: native clients can display the same localized welcome hint, recent-chats label, and ordered starter prompts as the installed web dashboard. Existing web copy and layout remain unchanged.

This is an additive, authenticated `operator.read` method. Older Gateways remain unsupported rather than silently receiving copied native strings. Missing or invalid installed assets return actionable `UNAVAILABLE`; restart the Gateway after updating its installation. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

`controlUi.welcome.get({ locale? })` returns a versioned catalog with requested/resolved locale and stable suggestion IDs, display text, and send text. The renderer and build generator share one ordering/key owner, the existing English catalog and translation-memory materializer, and the same locale fallback rules.

Normal runtime postbuild generates and packages the 21-locale artifact. The Gateway lazily reads and validates it once per process, with retry after a failed load. Requests do not fetch GitHub, scrape compiled JavaScript, load UI source, or require the Control UI HTTP server. Agent identity and recent-session data keep their existing owners.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Local validation used Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.7.0 on Windows:

- `pnpm test test\scripts\control-ui-welcome-catalog.test.ts ui\src\i18n\lib\registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed, 14 tests. The integration changes the English source and verifies both the web translator and generated installed-catalog RPC receive it; stale translations fall back to current English. It also covers invalid parameters, missing/corrupt assets, repair/retry, ordering, and locale negotiation.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: passed.
- `node scripts\run-tsgo.mjs -p test\tsconfig\tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental`: passed.
- Type-aware lint passed for every changed production, build-script, and test TypeScript file using the repository's matching core/scripts/root-test configurations.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm ui:welcome:check`, `node scripts\check-docs-mdx.mjs docs\gateway\protocol\operator-methods.md`, targeted Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- All normal `pnpm build` phases completed through guarded recovery after host file-metadata instability; this was not an uninterrupted green invocation or a runtime-only build. Canonical `package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` packaging with `--allow-unreleased-changelog --skip-build --pnpm-pack` passed its required bundled-dependency, extraction, inventory, and import-graph checks. The packaged welcome catalog matches the generated artifact byte-for-byte.

**Known gaps:** a later combined test run passed the catalog integration again but the existing `src\gateway\server-methods-list.test.ts` suite failed before test execution when compiler snapshot preparation reported changed metadata for `extensions\xai\package.json`. Its later UI shard did not run; the earlier 13 browser-locale tests passed. The UI build printed a startup-gzip budget violation: 373,503 bytes against 373,454 bytes (49 bytes over). Full repository checks/tests and installed native-client RPC proof are not claimed. The latest integration test body took 1.587 seconds and its file took 22.21 seconds locally; the earlier combined 14-test run took 173.71 seconds. CI seconds have not been measured. No visual change is intended.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): reject nonregular diagnostic logs without blocking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw voicecall latency --file <path>` and `voicecall tail --file <path>` hang before reading anything when the custom log path is a FIFO with no writer. The diagnostic reader synchronously opens the path before seeking retained JSONL records; it never reaches useful output or an error.

With a writer present, a FIFO's zero size is instead treated as an empty log. This reader tracks file offsets and replacement/truncation identity, so streaming pipes do not satisfy its existing retained-log contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

At the shared `readLogLines` owner, open nonblockingly on POSIX and reject nonregular descriptors before using size/offsets. Close the descriptor through the existing `finally`. Both custom-file commands gain the same behavior. Preserve configured symlinks, retained-record bounds, rotation/copytruncate handling, partial UTF-8 records and stdout backpressure. Windows keeps its current open mode.

Read the full command module, latency/tail callers, CLI registration, command output/number parsing, plugin CLI/service-mode guard, history-store owner and existing tests. The `calls.jsonl` history name is deliberately served by SQLite and remains on that separate canonical path; this patch affects custom diagnostic files only. No real phone call or transport behavior is changed. Native descriptor flags and the existing `fstat` are adequate; a library, timeout or alternate stream backend would add unnecessary policy.

All-state FIFO/symbol searches and open voice-call PR changed-file comparisons found no viable competing implementation. The prior streaming/backpressure work retains file-position semantics; this patch does not replace that reader or create a second path.

## User Impact

Custom log input now produces `Voice-call log must be a regular file.` instead of blocking on an absent pipe writer or silently accepting a pipe as an empty file. Existing regular logs and symlinks retain their actual latency summary. The nonregular-input rejection is intentional; this does not add a CLI option, config/default, schema/protocol, dependency, permission or storage change. Existing logs, SQLite call history and plugin configuration are untouched.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 24.16.0, built OpenClaw 2026.10.3. Identical actual CLI harness on unmodified main base and clean committed head, with separate home/config/state/workspace per case. The voice-call plugin is enabled with its mock provider, but CLI mode does not start calling services, open real channel credentials or place a call.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs voicecall latency --file <fixture>
node openclaw.mjs voicecall tail --file <writerless-FIFO>
```

Proof command: `node voicecall-log-fifo-live-proof.mjs checkout new-output-directory green` (`red` on the base).

Regular and symlink controls contain two JSONL records with turn latencies 120/240 ms and listen waits 30/50 ms. The harness parses actual CLI JSON and checks `recordsScanned=2`, average turn latency 180 ms and average listen wait 40 ms. Negative cases use native `mkfifo` files without writers, check the actual exit/error and retain the FIFO. Every run reads back original config and file bytes/type. A 30 s watchdog diagnoses a stuck owned child; no production timeout is introduced.

| Scenario | Unmodified main base | Committed head |
|---|---|---|
| Regular custom log | Exit 0; two records, averages 180/40 ms; 7.48 s | Same summary; exit 0; 7.79 s |
| Symlink to regular log | Same summary; link retained; 8.17 s | Same summary/link; exit 0; 7.50 s |
| `latency` with writerless FIFO | Blocked beyond 30.08 s | Exit 1, regular-file error; 7.64 s |
| `tail` with writerless FIFO | Blocked beyond 30.09 s | Exit 1, regular-file error; 7.52 s |

Blocked writerless commands: **2/2 → 0/2**. Source/config preservation: **4/4** on each version. Total durations include CLI/plugin initialization, not a command-wide timeout guarantee.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/cli-call-log.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  RED: two new FIFO cases fail for the intended empty-log/wrong-error behavior
  GREEN: 9 passed; 27.46 s wrapper, 21.32 s test file
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/voice-call/src/cli-call-log.ts extensions/voice-call/src/cli-call-log.test.ts
  exit 0; type-aware lint enabled, artifact preparation skipped
oxfmt --check extensions/voice-call/src/cli-call-log.ts extensions/voice-call/src/cli-call-log.test.ts
git diff --check
  clean
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  exact committed-head build passed, 3m 44.1s
```

The regression keeps a writer descriptor present so the test worker cannot hang if blocking `open` regresses; it proves that both commands reject an actual FIFO rather than treating it as empty. The independent built-CLI proof above covers the writerless blocked-open risk. An initial source-import subprocess test exceeded its startup timeout even after the fix and was replaced, not counted as a passed regression. Existing seven cases retain large-file history, rotation, partial UTF-8, record selection, backpressure/descriptor cleanup and SQLite-history deduplication. CI seconds are unavailable.

Two files: production **+7/-1 (net +6)**, tests **+19/-0**; no generated/lock files. The added lines implement and explain one admission invariant at the existing shared reader.

Exact-head receipt: base `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6`, clean tree `166dfdd4ec324b0635aa83a4e5c1d31c96482518`, RED checked `2026-10-15T02:15:28.494Z`. Head **`20481851c9bdd742915c136c4fa28224eee8e3c7`**, clean tree `c35feb48b337c7f24c1df204f0821e006eac8fc6`; matching runtime build commit, built `2026-10-15T02:35:55.187Z`, GREEN checked `2026-10-15T02:41:05.303Z`. Both runs use harness SHA-256 `01059f4039c9ede5c0bdcf94ae8d312f4961e4ee36f6437496786f1b45e769ad`. Receipts/logs remain local; published observations above do not imply hosted artifacts.

Not tested: native Windows/macOS, telephony/provider services, real call delivery, broad suites or a long-running external tail consumer. No call/session transport claim is made. Independent automated autoreview was waived by the contributor; no automated pass, upstream CI result or rating is claimed.

<details>
<summary>AI disclosure</summary>

Implemented with AI assistance for Leon-SK668. Source/caller/sibling inspection, actual native CLI RED/GREEN and filesystem readback, focused regressions, typed lint and a committed-head runtime build were performed. No raw transcript, private configuration or credentials is included.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): join nested lint compiler cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation npm source qualification spent 1,430.50 seconds in lint, timed out, retained artifact ownership, and left an orphaned `tsgolint` process ([failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663305730/job/116189445103)). The shard watchdog could kill its nested cleanup owner before that owner had drained its separately detached compiler group.

## User Impact

Timed-out or cancelled lint now joins nested compiler cleanup before reporting completion and releasing its artifact claim. Unverified cleanup still fails and retains ownership. This prevents orphaned work and stale claims from compounding release failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing managed-command owner for shard launch, cancellation, deadlines, and process drainage. Remove the competing raw-spawn supervisor while preserving timeout exit 124, parent-signal results, diagnostic collection, and the final failure trailer. Runner sizes, shard plans, retries, and deadlines are unchanged.

The initial full-lint stall remains unattributed: the runner exposed 8 CPUs/31 GiB and launched three shards, but the log has no peak-memory or pressure measurement. This change makes no full-run speedup claim.

## Evidence

- Real nested-process regression fails on the original runner because the compiler is still alive at timeout return; the patched case passes in 555 ms.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4yprtdyt066rtgwtzsfp050`, [execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672012707): 51 tests passed across `run-oxlint.test.ts` and `lint-status.test.ts` in 17.48 seconds, covering signals, deadlines, sibling drainage, artifact claims, and final reporting.
- After strengthening the existing rejected-cleanup assertion, `pnpm test test/scripts/run-oxlint.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`: 33 tests passed; measured wall 8.73 seconds. PR CI: all 33 tests passed in 5.389 seconds ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672659779/job/116219498774)).
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, targeted type-aware oxlint for both changed files, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent review and autoreview through P2 completed; the test finding was fixed and independently verified.
