prs.title: fix(migrate-hermes): refuse lossy memory text imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hermes memory migration reports success even when `memories/MEMORY.md` or `memories/USER.md` contains malformed UTF-8. Node's string read silently substitutes replacement characters, and the migrator appends the corrupted text to an existing operator workspace file. The original bytes can no longer be recovered from that appended text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode the source bytes with the built-in fatal UTF-8 decoder before creating or appending the target. Invalid text becomes the existing item-level error with an actionable re-encoding message. Preserve valid BOMs and literal U+FFFD characters; neither is evidence of invalid encoding.

The canonical owner is the Hermes append helper, called by both memory-file items through the provider's apply path. Read the provider, plan/apply dispatch, memory item definitions, source selection, report and real CLI caller. Sibling opaque memory-file copies remain byte copies; config/env parsing has a separate format contract. The installed fs-safe append implementation was inspected; it protects target-file admission but does not validate source encoding. The standard TextDecoder solves this without a dependency, encoding guess, replacement-character heuristic or new migration option.

All-state encoding/Hermes searches and open migration implementation checks found no viable same-fix competitor. The open Windows EBUSY work concerns config-file publication, not this append owner.

## User Impact

Malformed memory input now fails the affected migration item before modifying its target. The CLI reports the error and returns a nonzero status. Operators can re-encode the source and retry. Other provider items retain their existing behavior; this is not an all-items transaction or rollback change.

Valid UTF-8, including a BOM, Chinese text, emoji and a literal replacement character, retains the exact existing import bytes and repeated-import skip behavior. No config/default, schema/protocol, dependency, authorization or OpenClaw version-upgrade migration change. Existing backup and report generation remain enabled. The deliberate compatibility change is rejection of previously lossy invalid-text imports.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 24.16.0, built OpenClaw 2026.10.3. Identical real CLI harness on unmodified main base and clean committed head, with isolated source/home/config/state/workspace directories:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs migrate apply hermes --from <source> --item memory:MEMORY.md --no-auth-credentials --yes --json --backup-output <new-backup-directory>/
```

The second malformed case selects `memory:USER.md` instead.

Proof command: `node hermes-utf8-live-proof.mjs checkout new-output-directory green` (`red` on the base).

The malformed source bytes are `61 c3 28 0a`, with a pre-existing target containing `Existing operator memory.\n`. The valid control includes a BOM, Chinese text, emoji and literal U+FFFD, then repeats the exact same migration. The harness reads the real JSON item report, CLI exit, target bytes, original source/config bytes, backup archive existence and the generated report's `summary.md`. Default verified backup is not bypassed. No source helper call substitutes for CLI dispatch, and no auth credential or running channel is used.

| Scenario | Unmodified main base | Committed head |
|---|---|---|
| Malformed MEMORY.md | Exit 0, item `migrated`; corrupted text appended | Exit 1, item `error`; target byte-identical to its original |
| Malformed USER.md | Exit 0, item `migrated`; corrupted text appended | Exit 1, item `error`; target byte-identical to its original |
| Valid Unicode + BOM + literal U+FFFD | Exit 0, exact expected import bytes | Same exact bytes, exit 0 |
| Repeated valid import | Exit 0, item `skipped`; target unchanged | Same idempotent result |

Lossy imports: **2/2 → 0/2**. Input/config preservation and backup/report existence: **4/4** per version. The two malformed runs took 9.61/9.15 s on the base and 9.89/9.76 s on the head. Valid import/repeat took 8.84/9.16 s on the base and 9.16/9.10 s on the head. These durations include CLI dispatch and verified backup; no performance guarantee is claimed.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/migrate-hermes/files-and-skills.test.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  RED: both malformed cases fail because the baseline marks them migrated
  GREEN: 27 passed across two files; 151.85 s wrapper
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/migrate-hermes/helpers.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/files-and-skills.test.ts
  exit 0, with type-aware lint enabled
oxfmt --check extensions/migrate-hermes/helpers.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/files-and-skills.test.ts
git diff --check
  clean
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  exact committed-head build passed, 4m 2.2s
```

Test time includes compiled subprocess preparation and an existing provider plan/apply path; the two new malformed-data tests use the provider boundary. Existing tests retain copy behavior, source/target safety, planning, secrets exclusion and idempotency. The wrapper's full SDK declaration preparation timed out after 300 s; that run is not a pass. The listed scoped command skipped artifact preparation, not typed rules, and used the actual extensions TS project. No whole-SDK declaration or full typecheck pass is claimed. CI seconds are unavailable.

Two files: production **+11/-1 (net +10)**, tests **+27/-1 (net +26)**; no generated/lock files. The production growth is the explicit decode/error result at the shared append boundary; all existing append paths remain canonical.

Exact-head receipt: base `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6`, clean tree `166dfdd4ec324b0635aa83a4e5c1d31c96482518`, RED checked `2026-10-15T02:10:32.489Z`. Head **`ce48070b8b9e6db5f4540ee27f3d2b00d832a6d1`**, clean tree `ce09dcb4a705a4c576666f072c9915dcf2b039d5`; matching runtime build commit, built `2026-10-15T02:32:36.150Z`, GREEN checked `2026-10-15T02:38:16.851Z`. prs.title: fix(ios): report a screenshot simulator that stops booting
prs.body:
## Problem

`ios-screenshots-ipad-13` failed on `xcode-27-xlarge` in an extended-stable 2026.9.33 Full Release Validation CI run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38582207900/job/115915240483

```
Called from Fastfile at line 245
[!] Screenshot capture requires its task-owned simulator to be the only active simulator.
```

That message suggested that some other simulator was running.

## Root cause

No other simulator was running. The failed run's `screenshot-diagnostics.json` artifact records the Watch `boot` phase as `outcome: failed` with `activeSimulatorCount: 0`. The sequence was:

1. The iPad simulator captured all four screenshots, then shut down and was deleted (`activeSimulatorCount: 0`).
2. The task-owned Apple Watch simulator was created. `xcrun simctl bootstatus <udid> -b` reported "Waiting on System App" up to 40 s, then a terminal `Status=4294967295, isTerminal=YES, Elapsed=00:00`. The reset elapsed time means CoreSimulator ended the boot; in a passing run the same terminal line has `Elapsed=00:41`. `bootstatus` still exited 0. The 1-minute load average was about 150 on the 5-CPU runner.
3. The simulator was left `Shutdown`, so cleanup skipped `shutdown` and only ran `delete`. That leaves an empty active list, and `require_exclusive_screenshot_simulator!` (`apps/ios/fastlane/Fastfile:243`) compared it with `[udid]`, so it raised the "only active simulator" error.

The check could not tell "another simulator is active" apart from "the task-owned simulator is not booted", so it reported a simulator conflict that never existed. It also accepted an owned simulator in `Booting` or `Shutting Down` state as valid.

The simulator dying mid-boot under load is CoreSimulator/runner behavior. This PR does not add a retry for it.

## Solution

`require_exclusive_screenshot_simulator!` now:

- names every other active simulator (name, UDID, state) when exclusivity is actually violated, and
- requires the task-owned simulator to be `Booted`. Otherwise it fails with `Task-owned screenshot simulator <udid> is <state>, not Booted; CoreSimulator ended its session.`

This keeps the exclusivity guarantee and strengthens it, because a simulator that is half-booted or shutting down is no longer accepted. Cleanup is unchanged and still deletes the owned simulator.

## Evidence

- The new regression scenario `boot-ended` in `test/scripts/ios-release-fastlane-gates.test.ts` copies the CI sequence: iPhone and iPad succeed, then the Watch `bootstatus` exits 0 but leaves the simulator `Shutdown`. Against the old Fastfile it fails with exactly the CI message, `Screenshot capture requires its task-owned simulator to be the only active simulator.` With the fix it reports `... is Shutdown, not Booted ...`, keeps the 8 iPhone/iPad PNGs, and deletes the owned Watch simulator.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ios-release-fastlane-gates.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: the changed test passes. Two other cases fail locally with or without this change, because the host's system Ruby 2.6 lacks `Array#filter_map`. That failure comes from the local environment and does not affect CI.
- `ruby -c apps/ios/fastlane/Fastfile`, oxfmt and oxlint are clean.

## Test cost

This adds one scenario to the existing single-Ruby-process ownership test, with no new process boot. That test took 4.6 s; the full file took 35.9 s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reject FIFO TLS material without blocking validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured Gateway TLS certificate, private key or CA path that is a FIFO without a writer blocks startup before TLS validation can report the invalid input. Public certificate inspection has the same admission gap. The existing byte-limited cert/key reader cannot help while `open()` is waiting for a writer.

This is a malformed local material path, not a claim that OpenClaw normally creates FIFO certificates or that an untrusted remote user can configure these paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit configured material nonblockingly on POSIX, check the opened descriptor is a regular file, then use the existing read policy. Both server startup and read-only public certificate inspection use this owner. Keep configured symlinks, current 64 KiB cert/key limits and the existing uncapped CA-bundle contract. Windows retains its current open mode.

Read the full TLS owner, startup preparation/kernel caller, local HTTPS probe, certificate inspection, renewal consumer and adjacent tests. Renewal retains previously accepted material on reload failure. The installed fs-safe bounded descriptor implementation was inspected: its limit applies after opening; the generic regular-file API rejects symlinks, so substituting it would change supported configured paths. No new package, timer, fallback or config option is needed.

All-state semantic/symbol searches and open TLS PR changed-file checks found no active implementation of this fix. Historical #110046 proposed new fixed input caps and was closed for inactivity with unresolved compatibility concerns. This patch does not adopt that policy or replace certificate-generation code: it preserves today's cert/key bounds, uncapped CA reads and staged generation/publication safeguards. #171105 fixes SSH probe endpoint selection in a different owner.

## User Impact

Invalid nonregular material now reaches the normal required-TLS startup failure path and produces an actionable diagnostic instead of blocking inside the reader. Regular material and symlinks still start an actual HTTPS listener with the configured certificate. Invalid TLS never falls back to an unencrypted listener.

Three existing path inputs now explicitly reject nonregular descriptors; this validation change matters for compatibility. FIFOs could not supply the seekable bounded cert/key input or a terminating unattended startup in the reproduced case. No config/default addition, protocol/schema, dependency, trust policy, certificate generation or migration change. CA bundles gain no size cap. Existing valid deployments require no new operator action.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 24.16.0, built OpenClaw 2026.10.3. Identical native Gateway CLI harness on unmodified main base and the clean committed head. Each case uses its own home/config/state/workspace, loopback port, synthetic local auth token and one-day locally generated certificate. No channel, remote provider or model turn is exercised.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <isolated-port> --bind loopback
```

Proof command: `node gateway-tls-fifo-live-proof.mjs checkout new-output-directory green` (`red` on the base).

The harness reads HTTPS `/readyz` through the generated CA and compares the peer certificate fingerprint. Invalid cases check that no TCP listener remains, read the real `gateway.startup_failed` stability JSON and verify source material/config bytes or FIFO/symlink type.

| Scenario | Unmodified main base | Committed head |
|---|---|---|
| Regular cert/key/CA | HTTPS 200, matching peer fingerprint; 25.42 s | Same verified HTTPS; 20.23 s |
| Symlinked cert/key/CA | HTTPS 200, matching fingerprint; links retained; 20.80 s | Same, links retained; 22.07 s |
| Ordinary invalid PEM | Startup failure artifact; no listener; 14.21 s | Same existing failure path; 14.68 s |
| Writerless certificate FIFO | Still waiting at 30.02 s; no failure artifact | Regular-file error in failure JSON; no listener; 14.84 s |
| Writerless private-key FIFO | Still waiting at 30.07 s; no failure artifact | Same explicit rejection; 13.39 s |
| Writerless CA FIFO | Still waiting at 30.00 s; no failure artifact | Same explicit rejection; 13.29 s |

Unresolved TLS input reads: **3/3 → 0/3**. Input/config preservation: **6/6** on each version. These are end-to-end observation times including Gateway bootstrap, not reader performance guarantees. The 30 s watchdog diagnoses the original block; it is not a new production timeout.

The claim is that TLS input validation returns and publishes startup failure, not that the entire Gateway CLI naturally exits within a deadline. Both an ordinary invalid PEM control and rejected FIFO runs remained alive at the observation point; the harness explicitly terminates its owned process groups afterward. An earlier check requiring immediate process exit failed and is not counted as successful proof. A separate command-lifecycle repair is outside this reader change.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts src/gateway/server-tls-renewal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  GREEN: 21 passed across two files; 113.83 s wrapper
  TLS file: 17 passed, 91.21 s dominated by transform; renewal: 4 passed
  RED: new bounded FIFO subprocess times out; 16 existing TLS cases pass
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/tls/gateway.ts src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts
  exit 0
oxfmt --check src/infra/tls/gateway.ts src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts
git diff --check
  clean
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  exact committed-head build passed, 3m 41.6s
```

The regression checks server cert/key/CA admission and public inspection in a killable child, so a blocking-open regression cannot strand the test worker. Existing coverage retains symlink chains, exact leaf byte limits, large CA bundles, safe certificate generation and renewal behavior. CI seconds are unavailable.

Two files: production **+19/-8 (net +11)**, tests **+48/-0**; no generated/lock files. The added owner logic shares descriptor admission across both existing entries and the CA read without growing another reader path.

Exact-head receipt: base `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6`, clean tree `166dfdd4ec324b0635aa83a4e5c1d31c96482518`, RED checked `2026-10-15T02:36:25.590Z`. Head **`ae35fd5cb1862ffcb3f354ebddbd9f95fd9a97b4`**, clean tree `c154433ff616eb713b607e56098bea37952e5109`; matching runtime build commit, built `2026-10-15T02:24:20.926Z`, GREEN checked `2026-10-15T02:34:48.911Z`. Both runs use harness SHA-256 `61a6994c0c35d2c1872680b52c38d359cfc396798a312d760dca19b544ed3a56`. Receipts and logs are retained locally; the observations above are the published evidence, not a claim of hosted artifacts.

Not tested: native Windows/macOS, real external PKI or client/mTLS authentication, automatic live certificate rotation, broad suites, or natural Gateway failure-process exit. No claim about shipped releases beyond the tested main base. Independent automated autoreview was waived by the contributor; no automated pass, upstream CI result or rating is claimed.

prs.title: test(process): compile the native Claude CLI fixture once per suite
prs.body:
## Problem

`src/process/exec.windows.integration.test.ts > ordinary Claude CLI executable launch > completes an ordinary agent turn through native` failed on `checks-windows-node-test-1` (windows-2025) in a Full Release Validation CI run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38630644574/job/116081449035

```
×  process  src/process/exec.windows.integration.test.ts > ... > completes an ordinary agent turn through native 31245ms
   → Native fixture compilation failed: 
```

The `node-leading` and `npm-shim` cases in the same suite passed.

## Root cause

`test/helpers/claude-cli-native-spawn-proof.ts` compiled the `claude.exe` fixture with `csc.exe` inside each native case and gave it a fixed 30 s limit. The case failed after 31.2 s with no compiler output, which matches that 30 s limit firing during a cold `csc.exe` run. The error message checked only `code !== 0` and printed nothing but stdout and stderr, so it hid the fact that the compiler had timed out.

In passing FRV Windows runs, the native case takes 3 to 7 s longer than node-leading (for example 50.4 s vs 47.3 s, 59.8 s vs 52.4 s, and 42.6 s vs 39.8 s), so compilation normally takes a few seconds. On a loaded runner it can take more than 30 s. That compile time is setup, not the launch contract this case tests.

## Solution

- Compile the native launcher once in a suite `beforeAll`, using a suite-owned temp dir (`useAutoCleanupTempDirTracker(afterAll)`). The native case then copies the compiled `claude.exe` into its isolated npm prefix. The exe takes every path from the proof env, so its location does not matter.
- Give compilation a generous setup budget: 120 s inside a 150 s hook. This replaces the 30 s limit, which was nested inside the case budget. The launch assertions, the agent-turn timeouts and the 360 s case budget do not change.
- Make compile failures diagnosable. The error now reports `termination`, `code`, `signal`, `timeoutMs`, stdout and stderr.
- `runClaudeCliNativeSpawnProof` takes a discriminated `{ kind: "native", launcher } | { kind }`. A native run must now have a compiled launcher.
- `csc.exe` now runs with the normal process env instead of the stripped per-case fixture env (which had a synthetic `USERPROFILE`/`APPDATA`/`LOCALAPPDATA`). Only the agent run under test needs that isolation.

## Evidence

- Could not reproduce locally because the native case is Windows-only and the host is macOS. The fix rests on the CI timing above: 31.2 s ≈ the 30 s compile limit plus fixture setup, against a normal compile time of a few seconds.
- `OPENCLAW_CLAUDE_CLI_SPAWN_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/exec.windows.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on macOS exercises the changed helper through the `npm-shim` case: 1 passed, 2 skipped (Windows-only).
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and `pnpm tsgo:test:root` pass, and oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.

## Test cost

No new tests. On Windows, the existing native case now pays compile time once in `beforeAll` instead of inside the case, so total cost is unchanged (a few seconds). On non-Windows hosts the file is skipped unless `OPENCLAW_CLAUDE_CLI_SPAWN_PROOF=1` is set. The macOS opt-in run took 7.5 min wall, almost all of it the existing runtime-preparation `beforeAll` in a fresh worktree; the case itself took 38.5 s.

prs.title: test(gateway): prewarm history worker before composed SDK request budgets
prs.body:
## Problem

FRV normal CI job https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38610437410/job/116012489426 (shard `agentic-control-plane-runtime-state`, project `gateway-server-parallel`) failed:

```
src/gateway/server.app-sdk-composed-resources.test.ts > composed preview App SDK Gateway contracts > proves event, run, artifact, environment, and schema contracts
GatewayClientRequestTimeoutError: gateway request timeout for artifacts.list
Serialized Error: { code: 'CLIENT_TIMEOUT', method: 'artifacts.list', timeoutMs: 2000, requestSent: true }
```

## Root cause

`artifacts.list` is the first request in the real-Gateway part of this test that reads through the session history worker (`readSessionArtifacts` -> `readSessionHistoryPageInWorker` -> `withSessionHistoryWorkerDatabase`). The Gateway already has an owner that boots that worker before the first read, `prewarmGatewaySessionHistory`, but neither of its triggers runs in this fixture:

- The post-ready `session-history-worker` prewarm (`server-startup-handler-prewarm.ts`) is part of the post-attach sidecars. The minimal test Gateway (`minimalTestGateway`) skips those sidecars.
- The connect-time prewarm (`ws-connection/connect-session.ts`) runs only for non-ephemeral operator clients. The App SDK `GatewayClientTransport` connects in the default `backend` mode, which counts as ephemeral.

So the first `artifacts.list` paid for a cold worker boot inside the 2 s client request budget. Timings I recorded locally under load (temporary instrumentation in the handler and history runtime):

| run | first `artifacts.list` (client) | time spent in worker `readPage` | later reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3054 ms | 2798 ms | 5 ms |
| 2 | 1218 ms | 1131 ms | 4 ms |
| 3 | 3173 ms | 3058 ms | 3 ms |

Session resolution, SQLite scope preparation, and acquiring the database owner each took about 2 ms. Nearly all of the time went to the first worker task, meaning the worker boot.

## Solution

After the fixture starts the minimal Gateway, it now awaits the same production prewarm owner (`prewarmGatewaySessionHistory(getRuntimeConfig())`) that a full Gateway runs after it becomes ready. It also asserts `isSessionHistoryWorkerCold()` is false, so the test fails loudly if the fixture ever stops warming the worker it reads through. The 2 s request budgets, the assertions, and the production code are unchanged.

## Evidence

- With the fix and the same instrumentation: the prewarm took 1908 ms before the client connected, and the first `artifacts.list` then took 81 ms (worker read 37 ms). The prewarm targeted the same `openclaw-agent.sqlite` path that the artifact read used.
- The fixed test passed 2/2 times under host load of about 55-90 with the original 2 s request budgets. Note: on this overloaded host the whole test exceeds its 30 s `it` budget before and after the change (the deterministic and startup phases take 40-75 s here), so I raised that budget for these local proof runs only. The committed file keeps 30 s. In CI the whole test took 21.9 s.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched file. `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed.

## Test cost

One extra worker prewarm per run, about 2 s locally under heavy load. This is the same boot the first `artifacts.list` already paid for, moved ahead of the request budget. `pnpm test src/gateway/server.app-sdk-composed-resources.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` wall time on this host is 200-236 s, dominated by host load and transforms; the test body took 49-60 s locally.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): Gateway fails to start under Bun with channel identity admission timeouts
prs.body:
Related: #172244

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway running under Bun fails to start with "Channel identity policy could not obtain database admission after 3 attempts ... SQLite host admission timed out".

## User Impact

Bun-installed Gateways start again. No configuration, schema, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bun starts `process.hrtime` at zero in each thread (Node shares one origin). The worker sent an absolute deadline from its own clock; the host compared it against its clock, which is ahead by however long after process start the worker spawned, so every deadline-bearing admission expired on receipt. #172244 added a 1 s deadline with three attempts to channel-identity writes, which Gateway startup publishes during secrets preparation, so under Bun all three attempts fail instantly (about 0.8 s total in the failing log) and startup aborts.

The worker no longer sends an absolute deadline. The host derives its own deadline from the relative `deadlineMs` when it receives the request, and the worker still enforces its own budget through the shared decision word (CAS to `TIMED_OUT`/`GRANTED`), so a late host grant still cannot be accepted after the worker gives up.

## Evidence

- Root cause probe (Bun 1.4.2 / Node 24, macOS): a worker spawned 1.5 s after start reports `process.hrtime` about 1568 ms behind the host under Bun; under Node the difference is 0.2 ms.
- CI: `install_smoke_release_checks / bun_global_install_smoke` fails with this exact error on every main-lineage Release Checks run since #172244 landed (8e4fbe242ed, 15fdc5a3d14, b5432d5ef7e, and the 2026.10.10-beta.1 candidate d6105820e06), and passed on adef3b3f90e just before it.
- New regression `grants a deadline admission when the host thread clock origin is ahead of the worker's` fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (local, heavily loaded host): `sqlite-worker-operation-admission.timeout.test.ts` 9/9 (23 s wall), `sqlite-worker-operation-admission.test.ts` 27/27 (142 s wall), `src/state/user-channel-identities.worker.test.ts` 6/6 (72 s wall). The added case takes about 6 ms.
- oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass; autoreview (Codex, P2) scoped-clean.
- Gap: the Bun global install smoke was not rerun locally; PR/release CI owns that lane.

Follow-up (not changed here): the SQLite source fence (`sqlite-source-fence*.ts`) also carries a `process.hrtime` deadline across threads. Under Bun it errs toward a longer worker-side window, while the host-side check stays authoritative, so it does not cause failures.

prs.title: fix(ui): resolve native consent recovery for agent sessions
prs.body:
## Problem

#172607 (`8f1a499eb50`) broke native-runtime consent recovery for chats on concrete agent sessions (`agent:<id>:…`). Recovery looked up the owning agent with `scopedAgentIdForSession`, which only returns an agent for global chats. On a concrete agent session the new `!agentId` guard returned early, so the "Use <runtime>'s native permissions?" modal never opened. Main's `ui/src/e2e/chat-native-runtime-recovery.e2e.test.ts` now fails 4/11: selection or send refusal, confirm or cancel.

## Fix

Recovery resolves the owner from the concrete session key first (`parseAgentSessionKey`), then the explicit option, and uses the UI-selected agent only for global chats (`resolveUiSelectedSessionAgentId`). Unconsented concrete-agent chats show the modal again, and remembered consent stays silent for the owning agent.

## Evidence

- Parent of #172607 (`1a8dcc0b488`): E2E 11/11 pass. `8f1a499eb50` and main `e106d1fa54e`: 4 fail at the modal wait (lockfile unchanged across these revisions).
- This branch: the unchanged E2E file passes 11/11. Recovery, model-runtime and send unit tests pass 80/80, with remembered-consent coverage for global keys, concrete agent keys, and a different owning agent. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, the chat test-type graph, oxlint and oxfmt pass.

![modal shown for concrete agent session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91c6863c-ade0-4d7d-b108-f645c0761da1)



### Live proof (`11fef68caef`, real Gateway, real OpenCode via acpx, `tools.profile=full`, `tools.deny=["browser"]`)

```text
(a) agent:main:nre-modal-a
    Native selection displayed consent modal.
    Continue saved nativeRuntimeConsent=acp-opencode, permissionMode=full, sandboxMode=off.
    chat.send started; real OpenCode returned NRE-NATIVE-CONFIRMED.
(b) agent:main:nre-modal-b; UI-selected agent=other
    main remembered consent=[]; other=[acp-opencode].
    Gateway returned AGENT_RUNTIME_RESTRICTED/tool-policy with recovery.
    Consent modal remained visible. Cancel performed no permission recovery.
(c) scopes=[operator.read, operator.write]
    Native selection and send both returned AGENT_RUNTIME_RESTRICTED.
    Native session/prompt count: 1 -> 1; history messages=0.
(d) queued revocation
```

prs.title: fix(discord): keep typing active while owned child work runs
prs.body:
Related: #161732, #160039

## What Problem This Solves

Discord typing can stop after a parent yields even though request-owned child work or a local background process is still executing. This patch keeps the existing indicator associated with attributable work, with one core cadence, exact owner cleanup and fail-closed handling of unowned activity.

## User Impact

Typing persists for real owned work, pauses during a human-input wait, resumes only when execution resumes, and retires on cancellation, terminal work or audience retirement. Ordinary channels that do not opt in retain their existing failure recovery. This is a lifecycle fix, not a new status command, progress-card feature or session-recovery framework.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher becoming idle does not establish that its linked child or local process has finished. Core owns the request-scoped lifetime; Discord forwards the audience identity and failure-owner hook through its actual lazy callback producer.

The latest correction keeps an already observed, exact physical child wait suspended across an answered-but-not-yet-running transition. A fresh unknown execution does not inherit that custody. Current run context and owner-generation fences prevent stale waits from reviving typing; terminal cleanup releases the observer. The SDK reference now documents opt-in cadence, audience identity, paused custody, failure ownership and default-channel compatibility.

## Evidence

### Behavior addressed

Keep typing after parent yield while attributable work runs; pause during a child human wait without dropping ownership; keep it paused after the answer until that execution resumes; retire it at terminal work and reject stale or unattributed successors.

### Real setup tested

The preceding published head `4e54b3332ec45de397d3d50ab4ce6cb25fc00d6c` ran the source Gateway E2E through the real Gateway, embedded runner, subagent registry and core buffered channel pipeline. Only provider/Discord HTTP endpoints were nonce-fenced external fakes. The hosted command selected the default `child-yield` scenario: one case exercising the yielded child after the 120-second expiry, typing posts beyond expiry, terminal successor and quiet retirement. The file defines other scenarios, but they were not selected in this hosted run; overlapping/error/cancellation coverage is not claimed here. It passed in 201.125 seconds of test execution (253.686 seconds including file setup). It is source lifecycle proof, not live Discord admission or installed-release proof, and is not claimed as a rerun of the latest correction.

The runtime correction `d692a4af8602d72b3ea4e6b1d2196ccbdc6d5e2f` additionally ran an integration regression composing the actual `ask_user` tool and cleanup, agent events and tracked execution claims, subagent registry/projection, typing observer and controller. Question RPC/prompt delivery and channel callbacks are test boundaries; the core ownership and projection implementations are not mocked.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts --maxWorkers=1 src/auto-reply/reply/typing-background-work.owner-integration.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts --maxWorkers=1 src/auto-reply/reply/typing-background-work.runtime.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/typing-persistence.test.ts
```

### Evidence after fix

- The real-tool custody regression passed **1/1** in a 27.709-second command run. It observes real initial execution, wait/pause, answered-unknown retention without typing, matching running-event resumption, terminal sealing and a fresh-generation unknown that cannot resurrect the retired controller.
- The affected observer/controller files passed **34/34** in a 37.175-second command run. Those runtime/observer input bytes are unchanged by the latest fixture-only correction. No OOM or timeout occurred; source read-back matched, and test containers were removed.
- The initial new regression failed before reaching `ask_user`: it had passive routing metadata instead of a tracked execution owner/running event. The fixture was corrected to the real producer contract; the original failed attempt is retained, not counted as passing.
- The prior ordinary-channel recovery file passed **28/28**, and the actual Discord producer regression file passed **36/36** on the preceding source. Those unchanged checks are retained, not called new-head full-suite passes.
- Scoped formatting and documentation links passed. Fresh automated source review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in this correction; its unchanged-source coverage was limited and supplemented with direct contract reads and the executed tests. Normal commit hooks ran.

### Observed result after fix

Answering the child question no longer ends the completed parent controller’s custody: typing stays paused through the real projection’s unknown gap, then resumes on the matching execution signal. Terminal completion seals it, and a fresh unknown successor does not reactivate it.

### What was not tested

Full new-head CI, the Gateway E2E rerun of this latest correction, live Discord/provider endpoints, private bound-thread admission and an installed release remain unclaimed. The preceding CI run still failed a Discord draft-preview chunk assertion and a built LINE-doctor 30-second timeout. Their exact test/helper input blobs match the pinned baseline, but the baseline workflow did not select the same cases; causality is therefore unresolved, not dismissed as a baseline flake. No assertions or time budgets were weakened to hide these failures. Broad local dependency-sensitive gates were limited by an older retained dependency installation; hosted CI must validate the frozen-lock dependency closure.

AI-assisted contribution. No human-review claim, maintainer-ready claim or merge request is made.

Latest fixture-only follow-up: `bf841e704be6bce7f40b5cd208c1a32e95fe6db2` resolves the new integration fixture’s actual CI diagnostics: required braces, redundant default `void` arguments and four calls to an optional hook. The test now explicitly requires that hook before exercising it, rather than using optional calls that could hide a missing implementation. All existing pause/resume/terminal/successor assertions and time budgets remain. The corrected real-tool test reran and passed **1/1** with current-source read-back and cleanup; runtime code and the retained 34-test proof are unchanged. Full new-head lint/types/CI and automated review are still pending.

The latest automated review of the runtime correction reported a deferred-start pause race. Commit `31b087227f2e8aab7c3492f6d3dab77559cfb13a` now invalidates the pending start continuation when the audience pauses, preventing it from rearming cadence or TTL. The complete channel-callback file passed **30/30**, including both zero-interval and 3-second-adapter deferred-start variants, and scoped review accepted the two-file change. This cannot retract an already in-flight HTTP request; it fences its continuation. New-head hosted validation is pending. It also correctly distinguishes the direct `ask_user` construction above from supported child tool registration: `ask_user` is restricted to primary bootstrap sessions. The child case is therefore **composition coverage, not supported child ingress proof**. Supported execution/approval wait-resume evidence through the real channel callback producer remains required; no tool allowlist or authority restriction will be relaxed to manufacture it.

Historical proof correction: the earlier body overstated the hosted scenario matrix. That command ran one default `child-yield` case, not all four available scenario definitions. The proof above has been narrowed accordingly.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Windows `installer fresh` cross-OS release check fails at `models-set` on every candidate since `config set` began refusing local writes while a Gateway owns state (#168417).

## User Impact

No product change. Release Checks can qualify Windows installer installs again; 2026.10.10-beta.1 (run 38667134742, job 116203364834) and main (runs 38529602619, 38652005622, 38668627501) are blocked by this lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

On Windows the installer lane onboards with the managed Scheduled Task Gateway and exercises its lifecycle (ready, restart, stop, start), leaving that Gateway running. The lane then ran `openclaw config set models.providers.openai ... --merge`, which is intentionally an offline-only owner operation (`onForeignOwner: "refuse"` in `src/cli/config-cli.ts`), so it fails with "This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership". Linux/macOS never hit this because they do not start a managed Gateway before `models-set`.

The lane already stops the managed Gateway and waits for it to settle before starting its manual Gateway. This moves `models-set` to that window: after the managed stop, before the manual Gateway starts. Product behavior is unchanged and documented in `docs/cli/config.md`.

Update behavior: no change to `openclaw update`, Doctor, service lifecycle, or migrations; harness-only ordering change in `scripts/lib/cross-os-release-checks/lanes.ts`.

## Evidence

- Failure (candidate d6105820e06, artifact `installer-fresh-models-set.log`): `models set` succeeds via the Gateway, then `config set models.providers.openai` returns `Cannot admit config set ... This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership. No local mutation was attempted.` Same error in main runs 38529602619 and 38652005622; release/2026.10.5 (without #168417) passes the lane.
- Focused: `pnpm test test/scripts/openclaw-cross-os-release-checks-upgrade-lane.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed (~180s wall, mostly transform).
- Hosted Windows proof on this head: Cross-OS release checks `suite_filter=windows/installer-fresh` run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38673165956 (result to be recorded below).

prs.title: fix: catalog list fails when Codex thread previews are huge
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the session catalog fails to parse Codex `thread/list` pages when stored previews are huge, then one bad host stalls `sessions.catalog.list`.

Fixes #156831

## User Impact

User impact: large Codex homes keep listing. A hung or unparseable host is fail-soft instead of blocking sibling hosts until the 60s deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog decoding drops the tail of a native `preview` string before JSON.parse, but only once the retained prefix already fixes the displayed text: the selector's 2,048-unit prefix, no terminal controls, and more than 500 units of collapsed, trimmed text. Each whitespace run is kept as one unit while reading, since the projection collapses runs anyway, so text after a long whitespace run survives. Controls before the first ANSI introducer (ESC, CSI, OSC) are deleted in place by the sanitizer, so each run of them is kept as one unit too. Only previews whose ANSI sequences leave the display undetermined are cut at 64 KiB. The displayed preview matches the existing projection and 8–24 MB pages still stay under the 8 MiB incomplete-frame recovery.

Each local catalog host gets one fail-soft deadline that covers page reads and adoption projection, on both the non-progressive path and progressive `finishLocalHost` / publication. It uses the existing 60s default request allowance (`CODEX_CATALOG_LOCAL_HOST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so slow large homes are not marked unavailable earlier than today; paired nodes stay at 8s.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest, all passing at f200f2f87f:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-preview-bound.test.ts` (19 tests): oversized preview parse, escaped quotes while skipping, skipped fragments vs the 1000-line recovery cap, and displayed-preview parity with the canonical selector for whitespace-heavy prefixes, escaped newlines, sparse words, terminal controls and a surrogate at the display boundary, text after whitespace, escaped newlines or removable controls beyond the 64 KiB fallback, removable controls between whitespace runs and before an ANSI sequence, and whitespace-only preview lines vs the recovery cap.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-worker.test.ts` (25 tests): 9 MiB preview recovery, plus worker vs inline projection parity for a whitespace-heavy prefix, a control-laden preview, `" ".repeat(65_536) + "meaningful text"`, and `"\u0007".repeat(15_000) + "meaningful text"` (the last two fail before this change, pass after).
- `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-list-operation.test.ts` (16 tests): progressive and non-progressive host timeouts with sibling fail-soft, and a new case that holds the adoption read after paging completes (fails before this change, passes after).

`oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean.

Not yet attached: an after-fix `sessions.catalog.list` trace from a real large Codex home.

prs.title: feat(autoreview): review sandbox candidates with the configured agent
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/172336

## What Problem This Solves

A sandboxed coding session can have the canonical review skill but no reviewer CLI or credentials, leaving required review blocked before a source handoff.

## User Impact

Operators can enable the optional AutoReview plugin to review the session's full Git candidate through the configured agent's isolated runtime. The tool is discoverable only with an admitted supported sandbox and explicitly selects the native entry point before guest CLI preflight.

**Draft; no installation or rollout.** Enablement requires the exact shared canonical helper version, an operator-trusted Docker/Podman image with immutable system paths and Python 3.10+/Git, and a configured runtime that enforces isolated inference. Unsupported or incomplete execution never returns a clean review. Live agent identity, image/toolchain availability, and one actual captured review must be qualified before deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin retains canonical capture, report validation, attribution, priority filtering, and drift checks. Helper bytes are pinned once from an operator-selected shared installation; no helper implementation is vendored, no guest credential is installed, and guest Git metadata is processed only inside the existing sandbox.

Three owner boundaries make that possible:

- The tool completion closure retains the admitted agent, session, requester restrictions, and lifetime; configured-agent inference cannot substitute an ambient system agent or caller-selected model/profile.
- The prepared runtime must admit the requested restriction on external/repository capabilities before inference. Existing calls that omit the requirement keep their behavior.
- The duplex sandbox capability retains the exact decorated backend, uses daemon-confirmed immutable image facts and sanitized startup environment, and joins communication, guest cleanup, transport extinction, and finalization before returning.

Results include source hashes, threshold, reviewer identities, explanation, and findings within a separate 4,000-byte cap. Omitted findings produce an incomplete result. Evidence covers changed source and explicitly supplied context; missing callers, dependencies, or live behavior remain unproved.

Production delta: **+1,147 net lines** (core +454; plugin +693, including provenance tooling). Tests: **+1,089 net lines**. The growth supplies the three invocation/isolation/cleanup contracts and canonical adapter; the existing command binding is reused, and the generic ambient facade stays unchanged.

Release-note context: optional native AutoReview for sandbox candidates, with configured-agent inference, shared-helper pinning, and explicit image/install enablement. See [operator documentation](docs/tools/autoreview.md).

## Evidence

- Independent source review covered requester/lifetime binding, prepared-owner isolation admission, exact sandbox placement, daemon image/env trust, cancellation cleanup, and bounded outcomes. Reported defects were fixed and re-reviewed.
- Final AutoReview: scoped-clean through P2 on the full candidate integrated with pinned main `73b94171af6a5ec9f56104e268ec67a59245a538`, plus relevant owner/provider context. The checkpoint-aware preparation flow is preserved for both ordinary and raw sandbox programs. The separately reviewed canonical helper was outside that review's supplied dataset.
- Canonical dependency: [agent-skills #322](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/322), head `30fd865b6f79fab3e6f20f465496c3c6f3cd2b13`; **603 helper tests total, 4 skipped**, metadata checks passed, all 14 hosted checks successful. This draft pins the complete helper SHA256 `37c412329c63caa569ac5e9350f91d8fc72feb9f122ade2045d52fbd91f87469`.
- Provenance regeneration check, privacy scrub, `git diff --check`, and targeted **oxfmt 0.71.0** passed.
- Added focused tests for bound V2 completion, runtime isolation refusal, decorators, Docker/Podman raw argv/env, daemon fact refusal, communication cleanup, source pinning, protocol frames, complete native round trip, and incomplete/substituted outcomes.
- **OpenClaw tests, typecheck, lint, SDK surface check, and build are pending.** One [scoped exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38606052355) was requested for `383f1571888c82711359a22b10d0d72d46bd9ab4` using the existing `release_gate` admission path; the PR remains draft. The run is in progress, not passing proof. The task checkout has no qualified dependencies; remote proof stopped before allocation because the shared tooling install has tsx 4.23.13 while the frozen task requires 4.23.15. No shared dependency repair or worktree installation was performed.
- Direct Codex source check: `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs` and `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/plan.rs` at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: internal planning emits plan updates; the promised restriction is external/repository capabilities, not a literal absence of every internal tool.

The draft remains unmerged and undeployed. Hosted source proof does not substitute for the later live identity/image/review qualification gate.

prs.title: fix(system-agent): use configured fallbacks when primary admission fails
prs.body:
Closes #151605.

## Problem

Bound system-agent maintenance admission tried only each agent's primary route. If the primary failed with a retryable error, admission gave up even when the same agent had a usable model in its ordinary configured fallback chain.

## Change

- Admission now also tries the owner's configured fallback chain (agent-local or defaults), in authored order, under the same agent owner. Utility-model verification and empty/strict chains are unchanged.
- The winning candidate is bound exactly (`fallbackModelRef` on the route). Session reuse and persistent-apply revalidation recheck that same candidate; if the chain, credential, runtime, or policy changes, the binding is invalidated.
- A bound session cannot be silently replaced by a nested runtime fallback (`modelFallbacksOverride: []`).
- A successful reply followed by owner drift now reports `unknown` instead of `auth`, so the ladder stops instead of trying another candidate.

## Simplification

Earlier revisions also fenced which operations a fallback-bound session could run and added extra config/SecretRef write checks. That was not required by the issue and has been removed. This revision is rebased on current `main` and touches 5 source files (+154/−24).

## Tests

prs.title: fix(workers): reclaim idle buffers and reduce catalog decoder memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog decoder workers retain unrelated runtime modules, and completed large buffers can remain uncollected when JavaScript heap growth stays below the idle-GC threshold.

## User Impact

Lower catalog-decoder memory overhead and automatic reclamation of dead external buffers while keeping workers warm. No configuration, schema, or supported public SDK changes are required.

This is a bounded improvement, **not a demonstrated fix for the separate multi-GiB Gateway memory report**. Reclaimed buffers do not guarantee that RSS returns to the OS, and the prepared-model worker showed no material improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep catalog routing, terminal text helpers, and admission transport on lightweight imports. Observe heap and external-memory growth independently in the existing idle collector, preserving its threshold, burst debounce, cancellation, and worker reuse.

The terminal helper remains an official-plugin-private runtime surface; it does not expand the supported public SDK.

prs.title: fix(openai): reject oversized Decisions requests before API calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Decision requests with 201–256 questions or more than 255 choice alternatives reach the API even though the provider rejects them.

## User Impact

Oversized requests now return `unsupported-input` before credential resolution or network traffic. The model catalog and tool guidance advertise the actual limits: 200 questions per batch and 255 alternatives per choice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Decision V1 input bounds are broader than the [OpenAI Decisions API contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/decisions/methods/create). The OpenAI plugin now uses its manifest limits for preflight validation, keeping vendor policy with the provider. Split independent questions into separate requests or reduce the alternatives.

This follows the existing implementation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166320. It does not change model defaults, credentials, or the V1 text/JSON contract.

## Evidence

- Regression cases cover 200/201 questions and 255/256 alternatives, including zero credential resolution and zero HTTP calls for rejected input.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review and autoreview found no remaining actionable issues.
- A fresh bounded request to `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions` returned HTTP 200 from `gpt-6-luna`, with predicate, choice, and score answers (396 input tokens, 0 output tokens). This verifies the live API contract, not the modified OpenClaw adapter.
- Deterministic tests, type checks, and build are pending exact-head CI. The task-owned Testbox allocation was stopped when queued; local execution remains unavailable because the native dependency guard rejected the available shared install.

prs.title: fix: in-flight agent runs lose tool output after a plugin reload replaces a middleware plugin
prs.body:
Closes #162328

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every tool call in an agent run that was already in flight returns "Tool output unavailable due to post-processing error." after a plugin reload replaces a plugin that owns tool-result middleware.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can hot-reload a middleware plugin (`openclaw plugins reload <id>`) without breaking running turns and background subagents. In-flight runs keep their tool output and apply the replacement plugin's post-processing, the same as a run started after the reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

#157339 made the runner skip middleware whose plugin was **removed** mid-run, and deliberately left a **replaced** plugin failing closed. Its case 5 reasoned that a replacement is refused while the plugin has retained work, so the path could not be reached from a turn. In production the replacement was applied between two tool calls of a running subagent. The run's resolved middleware list is not retained work, so the stale handler stayed in the list. Every later call hit the retired instance, threw `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`, and failed closed for the rest of the run. That happened even for tools outside the middleware's matcher, because the retired-instance wrapper throws before the registration's matcher check runs.

The runner now asks the handler's own Gateway owner what applies now, before choosing a path and again right before each call:

- **Live instance:** run the handler as before.
- **Retired, plugin gone from the current registry:** drop the handler (unchanged from #157339).
- **Retired, plugin replaced:** run the replacement's middleware for this runtime from the owner's current registry. This is the same list a run started after the reload resolves.
- **Closing or unlinked owner:** keep the stale handler, which fails closed (unchanged).

The retired instance itself never runs. All runtimes (embedded, native hook relay, Codex dynamic tools, agentsapi) share this runner, so there is one owner and no caller changes.

## Evidence

**Production trace (before, OpenClaw 2026.9.7, sanitized):** a subagent in code mode made 20 normal tool calls. An operator ran `openclaw plugins reload <id>` for a plugin whose middleware is scoped to `memory_search`. The Gateway logged `Plugin replacement applied: <id>`, and from the next call on every call logged `[openclaw] tool result middleware failed for exec` (5/5, including `return {ok:true}`). The subagent stopped with no work done. Runs started after the reload were unaffected. Details are in #162328.

**Focused tests** (`--maxWorkers=1`, local, Linux arm64):

| Test | Before (main `1b9d7e70a`) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts`, new case: a stale handler hands over to the replacement (exec unchanged, `memory_search` rewritten by the replacement, stale handler never called) | fails: result is the post-processing error | passes; file 36/36, 28 s wall |
| `src/plugins/loader.test.ts` (real plugin loader), "middleware plugin was replaced" case, now reloading the same plugin into a second real instance | fails: post-processing error instead of `compacted` | passes; all 5 removed/replaced/closing/unlinked cases pass, 22 s wall for the filtered run |

The removed, Gateway-B, closing-owner and unlinked-registry cases from #157339 are unchanged and still pass. The closing and unlinked cases still fail closed.

Also run: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files, and `pnpm tsgo:core` (clean). Typechecked the two test shards that contain the changed test files (`tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json`, `tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`): clean. The full `tsgo:core:test` and `pnpm build` did not finish within this host's 10-minute isolated-task limit, so CI covers those.

**Not tested:** a live Gateway reload against a running channel turn. The production trace above is the before-evidence; I did not rerun the reload against a production Gateway. The loader test is the real-loader composition of the same path.

prs.title: feat: show native child progress after parent yield
prs.body:
Closes #150696.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex-native children can continue working after their parent yields, but channel users lose ongoing progress even when progress streaming is enabled.

This follows #139456 and #147571. **Maintainer decision requested:** whether this bounded post-yield presentation belongs under the existing progress preferences. Native notification defaults and the issue's product-decision gate are unchanged.

## User Impact and Boundaries

With progress streaming and tool progress explicitly enabled, the original conversation receives bounded task labels, observed tool/wait state and last-activity time. Supported channel edits update one message. Unset tool progress stays quiet; registered channel account resolution preserves channel-owned inheritance and opt-outs.

- The bundled Codex caller grants presentation ownership only after successful native yield; the public SDK path still has the host-authority gap described below. Owners are retired on requester resumption, reset or monitor retirement. Queued sends/edits recheck requester, child and destination after asynchronous work.
- Edits keep the original requester origin separate from the observed receipt. Existing account/topic/message-cache checks remain authoritative; a receipt is never promoted to trusted inbound or direct-operator authority. Telegram retries retain the final pre-HTTP authorization check.
- Failed or identityless sends are not blindly repeated. Completion during an in-flight update retains its final snapshot.
- Child prose, reasoning, command arguments and tool results are excluded. Presentation is best effort and process-local; refused edits do not change completion delivery.
- Native mirrors retain their silent lifecycle policy; the existing completion owner still delivers the final reply. No new scheduler, configuration key, SQLite schema or Control UI history API. No production deployment is included.

The retained monitor uses the existing task publisher rather than adding a second delivery mechanism. #87666/#112440 cover broader policy/portable-hook proposals; #149490 owns native completion consumption. Those remain separate.

## Current Change and Review Scope

Current head: `425392fb511159e3ceaddd2c36795c3722666b76`. The description previously identified `18a689fa` as current; that was an older revision. Validation on that revision is retained below as historical evidence, not proof of the current head.

The current ClawSweeper review identifies an author-side authority gap: the plugin-facing progress registration path must require a host-confirmed successful requester yield. Requester session identity and lifecycle revision are necessary checks, but do not by themselves grant permission to publish after yield. This finding remains unresolved in the published head. A successful bundled Codex call site does not establish safety for every SDK caller.

The SDK/product owners still need to decide whether this bounded presentation should use the existing explicit tool-progress opt-in. These decisions are separate from the implementation finding and from real-platform proof.

## Evidence

- Historical head `18a689fa73d61e3bd128fd8a69004ad23cc88c05`: the isolated native-yield channel integration file passed 11/11 composed cases, including session-ID and lifecycle-revision replacement before progress-owner registration with zero Discord HTTP effects. Four-file format, syntax/rule lint, and whitespace checks passed. Local whole-core types and type-aware lint did not complete within their resource deadline. These are historical results, not qualification of `425392fb511159e3ceaddd2c36795c3722666b76`.
- Earlier head `953ef4e`: Telegram retained-message loopback tests passed 3/3 and its hosted CI completed without failures. These are also prior-head results; loopback transport is not Telegram Test Server proof.
- The current review and CI observation below are bound to `425392fb511159e3ceaddd2c36795c3722666b76`. No fresh real Telegram observation, installed-package proof, complete local build, or host-authority integration pass is claimed here.

## Current CI and Remaining Gates

Observed on October 11, 2026; these CI runs completed on September 27, 2026, not as a fresh October 11 run. The current-head check-run refresh retrieved all 222 attempts and selected the newest attempt per check name: 217 distinct checks, with 133 success, 42 skipped, 39 cancelled, 1 neutral, and 2 failure. The failing checks are `checks-node-changed-config-compact-small-10` and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`; the current suite is not green. The aggregate annotation also reports a selected `checks-node-core-test-nondist-shard` failure; its annotation does not establish the cause.

The failed test annotation is `test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts` at line 190: it collected 80 production suppression entries against an allowlist of 77. The three additional entries are in `src/plugins/plugin-instance-owned-values.ts` and `src/plugins/plugin-return-value.ts`. This observation supersedes the old description of a 78-versus-77 gateway snapshot entry. It identifies the diagnostic, not proof of its root cause or an author-side waiver. No unrelated allowlist-only change is included in this PR.

Remaining author work: enforce host-owned successful-yield authority at SDK registration and final channel I/O; verify non-yielded callers and revoked/replaced requester claims through the actual publisher-to-transport path; qualify the resulting exact head and its CI; and obtain redacted real Telegram Test Server behavior proof.

The native Telegram proof and SDK/product-owner decision remain outstanding. This PR is not ready to merge. [The maintainer's scope clarification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150995#issuecomment-5875388037) confirms that merged #160039 supplies top-level continuation typing, not the bounded task/tool/wait updates proposed here, and does not supersede this PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Picker option icons and channel artwork still cross a Lit template boundary even though their callers render with Solid. That leaves a Lit image directive and untyped picker content in the shared rendering path.

## User Impact

Provider icons, channel artwork and owner avatars now render as native Solid content. Pickers keep their existing classes, selection behavior and lazy loading. Channel images retain the monogram fallback after failure until their URL changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrow picker leading and group content to JSX, convert every existing callback, and delete the unused channel template helper and image directive. The channel page retains list, detail and setup artwork, including source replacement and stale-image handling. The model-picker browser fixture now mounts and disposes Solid roots directly while retaining all four existing scenarios and assertions.

Repeated close notifications now preserve an already-empty collapsed-group set. During a config save, a disabled picker could otherwise recreate its native group artwork, trigger the document mutation observer, and retire itself again until the renderer stalled. The repair stops that cycle at the state update while retaining the normal group reset and re-enable behavior.

Provider group artwork is created lazily when the deduplicated group renders. Searching a large catalog no longer constructs and discards one group icon per model.

Wizard changes are limited to its header artwork; wizard controls remain with their migration owner. Domain owners are unchanged.

Replacement head `d1099b25b1176863cf98e4e2b0f0b0b795293210` integrates canonical main `ebb8d845`, including the clipboard, live-preference, reasoning-fixture, and session-details privacy repairs. Main’s channel presentation and account behavior are preserved. prs.title: fix: automations switch accounts when interactive defaults change
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automations could change inference accounts or authentication routes when interactive defaults or credential ordering changed, including when OAuth and API keys were enabled together. A model pin did not preserve account ownership.

## User Impact

New isolated agent-turn automations retain their selected authorized account and compatible route across fresh runs and plain model changes. Same-account token refresh continues to work. Revocation, deletion/reconnection, lost permissions, and incompatible routes fail explicitly instead of switching identity or billing. Automatic ownership stays distinct from an explicit user pin.

An explicit `model@profile` update adopts a different authorized account. Legacy jobs without trustworthy recorded ownership require explicit adoption before using host credentials; this change does not guess their historical account. Existing native runtime authority and configured credentialless inference remain supported. Environment-only and provider-config keys cannot establish durable account ownership, so creation rejects them with instructions to select a stored profile. Moving to a different credential owner also requires explicit adoption.

## Implementation

Store a private, secret-free inference binding in the existing cron SQLite record, then carry it through preparation, retries, and provider dispatch. Reuse the credential authorization owner for shared and personal accounts, preserving refresh continuity while enforcing replacement/revocation. Keep capture authority alive through the durable job commit. Personal account lifetimes persist in their existing private credential records; concurrent fresh captures share the same current lifetime without reviving old grants. Tool/delivery ownership remains separate, and public job responses exclude private binding metadata.

## Verification

- Real Gateway creation/update, authorization, and SQLite reload: **17 passed**. Includes both routes, explicit adoption, owner permissions, aliases, agent moves, native authority, rejection of unowned keys, and credential replacement between capture and commit.
- Real embedded-runner integration: **2 passed / 4 real runs**. Both auth types survive changed defaults, ordering, last-good account, and model selection. HTTP assertions check endpoint, model, bearer credential, and OAuth account header; only provider HTTP I/O is substituted.
- Personal authorization: **9 passed**, including a real native-writer subprocess reconnect and concurrent fresh adoption. Personal account state: **26 passed**. The reconnect/concurrency regression failed before the owner fix.
- The repeated-run regression fails when the original cron preparation/executor is restored and passes with the repair. Separate regressions demonstrate that environment/config-only creation previously succeeded but now fails before persistence.
- Focused core: **98 passed**; auth/state siblings: **40 passed**; orchestration/executor: **10 passed**; personal OAuth worker: **22 passed**.
- CI follow-up verification: recovery/compaction **121 passed**; personal/state/authority/writer **131 passed**; wrapper closure **18 passed** plus all three previously failing source-provisioning cases; gateway validation **132 passed** plus rechecked strengthened cases; cron MCP/tool/thinking **13 passed**; gateway mutations **10 passed**; PR automation **3 passed**; manual/workspace authority **12 passed**, plus the real fallback/transcript case.
- Formatting, focused syntax lint, whitespace checks, and the relevant database-admission/credential-writer/assertion ratchets passed. Full typechecking and type-aware lint are blocked locally by the compiler's physical-checkout guard rejecting the supported shared dependency graph. No guard bypass or duplicate dependency graph; PR CI supplies broad/type verification.

## Test Audit and Review

Audited complete touched test files, including fixtures, imports, cleanup, and negative controls. Replaced forwarding-only proof with real-owner/repeated-run coverage; retained distinct permission, refresh, reconnect/revocation, disposal, and incompatible-route cases. Removed one redundant empty-history call-shape test, simplified an unreachable parameter branch, and moved capability-denial assertions before expiration/removal so they cannot pass for the wrong reason. All credentials are synthetic, with isolated state and no live services.

Fresh independent API-key-only review covered production and full test quality. Actionable findings were fixed and rechecked, including native adoption, agent moves, real-runner proof, unowned credential creation, concurrent adoption, and capture-to-commit authority lifetime.

One remaining review suggestion—adding cross-process credential-write fencing to job creation—is intentionally not implemented. An overlapping external credential replacement can leave a job with an already-retired binding; execution fails closed and requires explicit adoption, without switching identity or billing. The normal owner-published replacement path is checked through commit. This bounded, visible failure is preferable to a new cross-owner transaction/fencing mechanism for job bookkeeping.

The initial CI failures were corrected at their owners: auth-provenance typing, wrapper dependency closure, credential-writer boundaries, and older fixtures without stored inference accounts. A follow-up test-type failure was fixed by using the canonical persisted-store reader for private job fields rather than widening the public CronJob type; all 17 Gateway cases passed again and an independent API-key-only review of that correction was clean. No checks were skipped and production authorization was not weakened.

prs.title: fix(agents): isolated cron-run exec completions no longer wake the agent main session
prs.body:
Fixes #172651

## What Problem This Solves

Background exec completions from isolated cron jobs with `delivery.mode: "announce"` start unrelated, often expensive model turns on the agent main session.

## User Impact

Completions stay on the cron run's originating session while that run is live. Once the run ends, its completion cannot start a new turn or deliver a late reply; retained output remains available through `process poll` and `process log`. Normal session completions and the cron job's normal announcement delivery keep their existing behavior. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat-era cron-to-main remap survived the switch to ordinary session-event admission in #167113. Exec now captures the cron run's own destination and reuses it at completion. The existing event owner checks the originating run's lifetime throughout admission, execution, and delivery.

Maintainer review also found that the original liveness lookup omitted `sessionId`, which excluded real registered cron runs. The fix captures matching run IDs using the actual session identity; later continuation turns cannot make an ended origin appear live. The broad heartbeat/subagent routing policy remains with its existing owner.

Original fix by @LiuwqGit; maintainer cleanup corrects the run-identity lookup, uses the existing event-lifetime assertion, removes duplicate routing and overlapping mock tests, and documents the behavior.

## Evidence

- Source/history: confirmed on main at `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209`. `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` captured and enqueued through the generic cron-to-main routing policy; `run-executor.ts` only made private-delivery runs transport-silent. The earlier notification change is `753a7a57be105d1d64d5205cce0c8486a0662453`.
- Regression: `keeps exec completion bound to its origin: %s` in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts`, with `ordinary`, `live cron`, `ended cron`, and `cron ended during admission` cases. Real exec and session-event admission check the model's destination, no model call after source retirement, and retained process output; only inference is mocked. The live cron fixture uses a real session ID and has no private-delivery suppression, covering the announce-mode defect.
- CI is the test gate: exact-head PR CI passed its selected runtime tests, production/test types, lint, docs, and guard lanes, including the background-followup regression file. Local tests, typechecks, and negative controls were intentionally not run. Live Gateway proof and cloud leases were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy ("relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint").
- Local format: `oxfmt --write` on the three changed files passed. Static lint: parent-installed `oxlint --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the two changed TypeScript files passed, 2 files / 264 rules / no diagnostics. The nested install lacks the UI-only Solid lint plugin, so the temporary core config retained all applicable rules and omitted only the `ui/**/*.tsx` override. No dependency installation or repository configuration change.
- Deslop: removed the one-use liveness helper, repeated destination calculation, comment narration, and the contributor's overlapping runtime mock tests. Production `+24/-4` (net `+20`), tests `+77/-0`, docs `+1/-0` versus the merge base. Production growth is the bounded origin-lifetime predicate and session-specific capture; there is no obsolete implementation of that contract to remove safely.
- Regression results: [exact-head job 116207848229](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38669009718/job/116207848229) passed all 7 tests in the affected file. New cases: ordinary `6831ms`, live cron `617ms`, ended cron `49ms`, ended during admission `46ms`. Vitest duration `24.01s`; wrapper wall time `26.70s`. Four cases share the existing integration fixture; no new timers, sleeps, polling loops, or production test seams. No local runtime measurement was run under the proof policy.
- Autoreview: Codex branch review through P2 returned `scoped-clean`, with no accepted/actionable findings. Review was static; no contributor code was executed. Fresh P2 reviews of both CI fixture corrections also returned `scoped-clean`. Main merges were mechanical and did not change the reviewed files.
- CI correction: [run 38666939018, job 116201328447](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666939018/job/116201328447) exposed a PR-caused fixture error: `test.each` does not supply the test context. Changed it to `test.for`; all four prior failures occurred before exercising production behavior. No rerun was used to hide the failure.
- CI type correction: [run 38667654324, job 116204516493](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38667654324/job/116204516493) found two PR-caused TS2532 diagnostics on fixture array entries after runtime tests passed. Used the existing `expectDefined` helper to preserve those invariants without casts. Production is unchanged.
- Exact-head CI: [run 38669009718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38669009718) **passed** on `d2a0e7e3458e5482b59d18ef7a17ce11b6c3e714`: 47 successful jobs, 29 skipped, no failures. Both `openclaw/ci-gate` checks are green. The previously failing `check-test-types-core-3` passed in [job 116208654740](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38669009718/job/116208654740). Merged `origin/main` at `7e823106a77c` before pushing (no rebase or force-push).

Deferred-path facts: the captured run IDs stay fixed and their execution ownership is rechecked before event effects; the existing target/event owner revalidates lifecycle generation, session binding, agent/config/store identity, permissions, cancellation, and the captured delivery route. Process output limits and TTL remain the process registry's existing contract; this patch adds no path or limit state.

ClawSweeper started reviewing the final head at 2026-10-15 02:16 UTC ([status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172690#issuecomment-6182886829)); no completed review or human code findings were available at closeout. Independent P2 autoreview is clean. PR CI supplies proof under maintainer policy.
