prs.title: fix(claude-cli): stop cache-prefix churn after child completion
prs.body:
Related: #146902

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable Claude CLI cache-prefix changes when a managed session switches between ordinary messages and verified subagent completions.

## User Impact

Managed local Claude turns use the same OpenClaw-mediated tool surface for both entry paths when their effective policy is unchanged. They no longer alternate between native tools/user customizations and the restricted OpenClaw MCP surface merely because a child completed.

This consistently excludes Claude user settings, CLAUDE.md/rules, native auto-memory, user hooks/plugins, Chrome, and additional native MCP servers. OpenClaw remains the owner of instructions, selected skills, and tools. Native-only features are not preserved on this managed path. Explicit native selections, node-only execution, side questions, and isolated utility completions retain their existing contracts.

Actual instruction edits and permission/catalog changes still take effect and may invalidate the cache. Existing native transcript content is not purged. Upgrades across releases use the normal Doctor migration path. The follow-up repairs preserve the captured source conversation context on completion and forward CLI verbosity through the canonical Gateway validation/persistence owner. Fresh-session verbosity and installed cross-turn prefix equality now pass.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary turns previously retained the native surface, while verified completions required an exact policy-filtered MCP projection. That changes the tools-first cache prefix and can change native instruction loading on the same resumed session.

Use the existing exact projection for ordinary local bundled Claude agent turns as well. Preserve all current discovery, execution, requester-lineage, sender, and delegated-policy checks. Bootstrap routing uses the final file capabilities. Exact runs keep selected skills in the host prompt instead of preparing a native skill plugin that the restrictive argument resolver removes.

Keep the existing private per-turn facts flow and refreshed system instructions. Do not revert instruction refresh or move arbitrary system instructions into user context.

**Maintainer direction:** @VACInc requested retaining native isolation on the managed path, with OpenClaw-owned instructions, skills and memory preserved, after the ordinary-turn compatibility tradeoff was discussed. This deliberately extends the isolation previously used on restricted turns; it is not a claim that ordinary native customization was already disabled. The requested follow-up is regression/permission/retained-session proof, green exact-head CI and resolution of review concerns. This product direction is separate from, and does not supply, the required GitHub security approval.

## Evidence

**Installed/native acceptance passed at `9c0003337106e51ce39d41313de1b01bf94aa764`**, tree `b3b46f7cc1a09742db24c372bb34fda0861e632e`. [Isolated proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_093c6984fa3e00942e5e405105905c87).

- **132 affected tests passed across six files**, including schema/CLI wiring, event handoff and permissions, real MCP background-exec completion, and real Gateway verbosity persistence. This includes both adjacent schema tests retained when merging main to resolve the actual conflict.
- The full canonical package build passed, followed by disposable-prefix installation: **OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (9c00033)**. No reduced-plugin build or declaration bypass. Tarball SHA-256: `dda82afd059e08c14f9baa00700b616bfe7a4fb035eb854891d3b505f3a4eae5`.
- **Fresh installation:** installed Gateway startup/health, CLI `agent --verbose on --thinking off`, actual Claude Code **2.1.299**, MCP read and `chat.history` passed. Native binding was created, verbosity/thinking persisted, and settings bytes remained intact.
- **Genuine stable upgrade:** official `openclaw@2026.10.3` (**59cb447**) created the session/history/native binding using `agent --local`. Installed candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` migrated agent schema **24 → 27**. No direct internal migration calls substituted for the CLI.
- **Installed ordinary → actual background-exec completion → ordinary:** the command wrote a sentinel; completion and the final ordinary turn read it through real MCP. Shipped history RPC retained the original history and completion. The OpenClaw session, native binding, native transcript prefix, settings bytes and thinking/verbosity preferences survived. **Doctor legitimately canonicalized config; upgrade config bytes were not unchanged.**
- **All six complete raw serialized `{system, tools}` prefixes were identical**, without normalization, across those three turns. SHA-256: `c6a8ef35e463ff9099a7ad67b3b70a74f287cc70346617d102b3f2bfa25a4e9d`. Stable user-instruction and settings-hook positive controls passed; the candidate excluded newly added native user instructions/hooks while retaining OpenClaw context.

The package, affected-test and installed-runtime phases each exited **0**. The workload ran independently under PID 1 on a secretless AWS runner; native execution used UID 1000, no capabilities, no-new-privileges and loopback-only networking. Provider replies were deterministic localhost fixtures: no provider credentials or paid inference.

### Review and proof scope

The independent whole-candidate P0/P1 review found no findings before the mechanical main merge. Earlier focused format/lint/type/protocol checks remain evidence for their tested inputs; the affected boundary tests and full package/installed proof above ran on the merged head. Required **current-head CI and human security/review gates remain separate**; this evidence does not waive them. ClawSweeper feedback is advisory, not a fresh-comment gate.

The installed proof covers packaging, installation, Doctor and foreground Gateway/native-process continuation, **not** an updater transaction, installed-system-service deployment, live-provider behavior or cache-hit measurement. Denied/revoked/closed/replaced permission cases are exercised by the production-boundary MCP tests, not every installed CLI variant. Historical stable project-instruction loading did not pass its positive control, so project-customization suppression is not claimed from that test. Private raw prompts, provider requests and session transcripts are not published.

<details>
<summary>Earlier failures and their disposition</summary>

- Baseline `315e772a` used different ordinary/completion tool surfaces; the original repaired candidate `4a38ecda` passed 119 focused preparation/MCP/retained-session tests. That was source-bound proof, not installed-entrypoint equivalence.

prs.title: fix(triage): reject FIFO update artifacts without blocking recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw triage --update-result <path>` never finishes when the diagnostic artifact is a FIFO with no writer. The reader already requires a regular file, but its blocking open never reaches that check. This can stall the command intended to help recover an installation.

This is a malformed local artifact path, not a claim that the updater normally creates FIFOs. No remote path replacement or full update/rollback behavior is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use nonblocking admission on POSIX at the existing open, followed by the existing descriptor regular-file check and `finally` close. Keep symlinks to regular diagnostic files supported, the 8 KiB bound, fatal JSON decoding, sanitization and failure schema unchanged. Windows retains its existing open mode.

Read the full `readTriageUpdateFailure` owner, CLI registration, unattended triage caller, support-artifact writer and pending-sentinel sibling. Interactive recovery consumes already-sanitized in-memory diagnostics; explicit artifact input uses this reader. The installed fs-safe bounded descriptor reader was inspected: it bounds bytes after admission and does not own this open. Native flags solve the gap without another library, timer or recovery path. All-state symbol/semantic and overlapping changed-file scans found no active same-fix competitor; #145456 changes update correlation, not this file admission.

## User Impact

Invalid file input now returns the existing regular-file error instead of waiting indefinitely. Valid artifacts still generate a retained sanitized repair prompt. No config/default, protocol/schema, dependency, authorization, migration or updater policy change. The FIFO and existing configuration remain untouched; no new operator action for valid inputs.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 24.16.0, built OpenClaw 2026.10.3. Identical actual CLI harness on clean base and committed head, using separate isolated home/config/state/workspace per case and no running channel or model. It invokes:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs triage --json --non-interactive --no-export --update-result <fixture>
```

The FIFO fixture is a native `mkfifo` path without a writer. Positive controls contain `{"error":"synthetic update failure control"}`. The harness reads the JSON result, exit code, emitted prompt file, input type/content and configuration bytes. It never substitutes a direct helper call for CLI dispatch. A 45 s watchdog kills only a stuck owned process group; no production timeout was introduced.

Recorded proof command: `node triage-update-fifo-live-proof.mjs checkout new-output-directory green` (`red` on the base).

| Scenario | Unmodified current-main base | Committed head |
|---|---|---|
| Regular JSON artifact | Exit 0; saved prompt contains the synthetic failure; 10.16 s | Same artifact readback; exit 0; 14.14 s |
| Symlink to regular JSON | Exit 0; prompt readback succeeds; symlink retained | Same; exit 0; 12.03 s |
| Malformed JSON | Exit 1; `Invalid update failure diagnostics JSON.` | Same structured error; exit 1; 12.23 s |
| Writerless FIFO | Still blocked after 45.08 s; no JSON output | Exit 1 in 10.85 s with `Update failure diagnostics must be a regular file.` |

**Hung FIFO runs: 1/1 → 0/1.** Every scenario preserves config bytes and input bytes/type on both versions. The total CLI duration includes Doctor collection; this is an input-admission repair, not a promise about a command-wide timeout. No repair agent, model request, service restart or production channel was used.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/triage-update.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  RED: new FIFO child times out (ETIMEDOUT); 7 existing cases pass
  GREEN: 8 passed; wrapper 10.27 s, file 5.81 s, FIFO test 1.95 s
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/triage-update.ts src/commands/triage-update.test.ts
  exit 0
oxfmt --write src/commands/triage-update.ts src/commands/triage-update.test.ts
git diff --check
  clean
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  exact committed-head build passed, 4m 3s
```

The regression uses a bounded child process so a blocking-open regression cannot strand the test worker. Existing tests retain bounded/sanitized diagnostics, post-install failure evidence and malformed/successful-result rejection. CI seconds are not yet available.

Proof receipt: base `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6`, clean tree `166dfdd4ec324b0635aa83a4e5c1d31c96482518`, RED checked `2026-10-15T02:07:50.394Z`. Head **`38964e22f3d47c8785ab5ac9e37ebe5e87da2a9b`**, clean tree `41af638e96790ff9ace2b08767e93c25304eb079`; matching runtime build commit, built `2026-10-15T02:16:17.471Z`, GREEN checked `2026-10-15T02:21:48.779Z`. Matched harness SHA-256 `f61d5c0bfe475e4a5ef239bb2c4ece6c8016b1f54c87e69e9fd5f65c01722b82`. Receipts/logs are retained locally; observations above are the published evidence, not a claim that local files are hosted artifacts.

Two files: production **+4/-1 (net +3)**, tests **+35/-0**; no generated/lock files. Added production lines explain and implement admission at the existing owner.

Not tested: native Windows/macOS, full managed update/rollback, interactive repair-agent execution or broad suites. Independent automated autoreview was waived by the contributor; no automated pass, upstream CI result or rating is claimed.

prs.title: feat: let agents create independent persistent sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An explicit request to start a separate task needs to create a normal session that the user can revisit and continue. Agents currently have a suggestion-card tool and supervised child-spawn tools, but neither expresses that independent-session contract. Treating the request as a suggestion adds another acceptance step; treating it as a spawn applies child execution and completion semantics to work the user intends to own separately.

This contribution adds the dedicated `sessions_create` agent tool, backed by the existing Gateway `sessions.create` owner. It does not add creation to the `sessions` management action enum or change how suggestion cards are accepted.

## User Impact

When the tool is available, an agent can create a persistent visible session and optionally submit its opening message. Omitting `message` creates an idle session. Optional `label`, `agentId`, `cwd`, `group`, `model`, and `permissionMode` use the existing creation settings; `user` selects an admitted requester when several people are participating. The requesting agent is the default destination, while other omitted settings follow destination defaults.

The result distinguishes a created session from a successfully started turn. If the initial turn cannot start after creation commits, the receipt still identifies the session and reports `runError`; callers must not assume nothing was created or blindly create another session. The new session is not a supervised child and does not produce a child-completion notification to its creator. Existing Home/sidebar grouping remains separate from execution ancestry.

Guests and other limited operators retain their existing agent, workspace, sandbox, and session-access restrictions. Creation requires live admitted `operator.sessions.write` authority, not merely tool visibility. It does not grant access to another person’s sessions or permission to choose or manage personal accounts. A qualified creation can consume the requester’s existing saved new-chat default. No configuration or persisted-schema migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway owner already validates and provisions ordinary sessions. The tool is a bounded adapter over that owner rather than a parallel creation service or a disguised spawn. Creator identity comes from the live admitted operator; it cannot be supplied through model arguments. The opening message is attributed to the requesting agent with inter-session provenance, rather than presented as newly authored human input or interpreted as a slash command.

The adapter keeps source authority binding until the initial input is durably accepted. After acceptance, ending the source turn does not discard the new session’s accepted work. Operator revocation, destination cancellation or replacement, and Gateway retirement still apply. Completion-time participant changes do not erase an already committed creation receipt.

Native, Codex, and compact-catalog guidance distinguish explicit independent-session requests from supervised helper delegation and proactive suggestions. That guidance follows actual authorized tool availability; it does not advertise creation when policy removes the capability. Existing `sessions` management actions and explicit allow/deny precedence remain unchanged.

## Compatibility

`sessions-create-tool-schema.ts` is the model-facing TypeBox argument schema, not a database schema. It reuses fields from the existing `SessionsCreateParamsSchema`; the Gateway protocol schema, SQLite tables, migrations, and stored record formats are unchanged. Creation and the opening message use the existing session and pending-input owners, with the existing inter-session provenance representation. No migration is needed. The durable creation/custody tests and real continuation-after-reload scenario exercise those existing storage paths; existing external creation and session-management behavior remain covered.

Slow startup must still return the creation outcome. The adapter waits for the creation owner to settle instead of inheriting the generic ten-second response deadline, preserving the session identity even when its opening work fails.

## Evidence

Current head: `527119cb40e4afe260b818edc120d964f41e4414`, rebased onto `11f50d2c3e2ad5469f68300ebe973e8242d5dc73`. The integration preserves the current chat-input owner, composed request authority, and independent accepted-input custody.

The runtime and test execution below were verified on `f525c858fd73fdfc2e3660bfd8c0061e66df8f5b`. The final follow-up changes only three test-mock isolation comments and removes one obsolete exact baseline entry. The native mock-export guard and scoped formatting/lint pass; no executable test, assertion, or runtime behavior changed.

Remote formatting/lint, native localization, and all selected production/test type graphs passed. All 19 related test groups passed: 3,463 tests across 216 files; the existing Windows-only media-file test is skipped on Linux. The Gateway group passed 1,361 tests in 337.97 seconds, including slow successful creation, slow startup failure, source cancellation, accepted-input independence, participant and guest restrictions, destination replacement, and operator revocation. The related-test entrypoint took 2,829.71 seconds including its full runtime/declaration preparation. The supervised-spawn boundary passed 46 tests in 227.81 seconds.

Independent engineering review is clean on the final head, and automated static review is scoped-clean through P2. The final runtime and UI build passed and the refreshed preview preserved existing session identities and transcript bytes. Real-provider inline, suggestion and supervised-helper controls also passed. Additional capture was omitted after maintainer live testing; the recording below retains its original head identity. Current CI results are reported by the PR checks.

## Historical live visual evidence — before this rebase

The following captures were tested and inspected on `95deca7dbf0f4b8915e3c3660be0a7a82c946317`. The recording is retained with its original build identity; the current production-boundary proof is described above.


| Before | After |

| ![Source conversation after a supervised helper; no independent task in the sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efed5103-d532-4f93-ace6-71e61bf1f257) | ![Same source after the explicit request; independently created planning session appears in the sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7079f87-4350-4970-90bf-b905234d733e) |

### Live creation, source continuation, destination continuation and reload

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f276fa1e-abb4-4196-9945-1fc56a8fd5c6

### Visual verification

- Baseline: 3bfa7cd910594dd33ff5827a793ffe48e2157a3f
- Exact head: `95deca7dbf0f4b8915e3c3660be0a7a82c946317`
- Scenario: Ordinary work, suggestion and supervised\-helper controls; explicit composer request creates and starts exactly one independent session; continue both conversations and reload the destination\.
- Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.9\.8 \(95deca7\), tree09a78c358d9d8c9215a7c05d3b718896347cec6c; Node24\.18; native OCM Vite preview; live OpenAI gpt\-5\.4 with built\-in openclaw harness; compiled artifact/build digests retained in assertions\.json\.
- Ordinary work / suggestion: 0 / 0 independent sessions
- Supervised helper: 1 helper; 0 independent sessions
- Explicit creation: 1 independent session; runStarted=true; no runError
- Isolation and durability: No spawn parent; source and destination continue separately; destination survives reload
- Browser errors: 0
- Feature\-absence baseline on the exact candidate, not a pre\-fix timeout reproduction
- Normal native browser pairing and real OpenAI inference; tool discovery defaults preserved
- Durable createdVia=operator, spawnedBy=null, spawnDepth=0, parent is not source
- Slow startup and permission/cancellation cases retain their separate Gateway boundary proof
- Code\-mode history does not establish an exact internal call count; a real receipt and one durable destination corroborate creation

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary connector runtime refreshes during Codex thread startup when OpenClaw has no thread-local app inventory but the native app server already has a snapshot.

## User Impact

Explicit plugin startup can reuse the existing native app snapshot. Missing plugin apps still trigger readiness repair, and account-wide app admission retains its existing cold-start refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor explicit `forceRefetch: false` instead of overriding it on a local cache miss. Preserve automatic cold seeding when refresh intent is unspecified and explicit forced refreshes. Account-wide admission uses that default because it has no plugin readiness repair.

- Direct production-entry verification passed: three refresh-intent cases across two independent cache keys, plus native-ready reuse, cold native readiness repair, warm local readiness repair, and account-wide cold seeding.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: refactor(ui): port chat metadata rendering to Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves chat comment previews, question summaries, pull-request rows, and GitHub publication controls to Solid while keeping admission, cancellation, publication, and dismissal authority in their existing TypeScript owners. Native Solid callers share one pull-request renderer and visibility predicate; obsolete Lit adapters are removed where no caller remains. Active legacy consumers retain thin adapters.

The integration preserves Environment and Context, collapsed background tasks, Changes / All changes navigation, compact pull-request geometry, retained check disclosures, and scoped callbacks. Release-note context: Control UI chat metadata rendering moves to Solid.

Current head: `b6c9364ec1eda9bb33fbd89feaa5a13919982ac8`, including main `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6` and the reviewed capture diagnostics and Workboard readiness correction. The normal merge retains both chat CI JSX declarations and main's modal-actions declaration.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Review | Clean independent P0–P2 migration review reused after all 18 renderer/domain production paths were verified byte-identical; the remaining ambient-type file differs only by main's approved modal-actions declaration. Capture diagnostics, their four explanatory lint comments, and Workboard readiness have separate clean reviews with verified context. The committed diff exactly matches the reviewed candidate. |
| Local proof | UI typecheck passed once on this final integrated tree (395.28s). Prior unchanged-renderer proof: Details 5/5, focused reconnect/attachment proof 3/3, and native disclosure/layout proof 7/7 passed. Two untraced Details reactivity warnings were inspected without establishing a defect. No repeated local suites. |
| Final-head UI unit jobs | All three `checks-ui` shards passed for PR head `b6c9364e` in run `38670218529` (jobs `116211728950`, `116211729008`, `116211728980`). |
| Current-main fixture integration | Keeps main's strengthened live model/reasoning/Fast assertions and workspace-menu clipboard selector. Main also expands persisted Raw details before the `/reasoning on` count/order assertions. This is a fixture adaptation, not a claimed reasoning runtime fix or a new passing test result. |
| Workboard readiness | Reuses the existing settled-confirmation-modal helper before clicking the gateway switch. Original delivery, authentication, revision, origin, socket, lazy-chunk, and error assertions remain intact; no retries or timeout increase. Review passed; replacement CI owns execution. |
| Capture diagnostics | Four real-Gateway capture files report only a fixed category and visible-text-match boolean. Original `textContent` predicates, forbidden values/order, and false assertions remain intact, so hidden private text still blocks capture. Diagnostics identify failures; they are not a claimed fix. |
| Local tooling gaps | The earlier integrated live-preferences attempt ended with SIGKILL/exit 137 after 174.13s, before browser assertions, with no established cause. The shared privacy probe ended 143 without Gateway assertions. No additional local tests or builds were run. |
| Scoped lint | The sole four-file lint run passed on the prior head. Three complete files still match; main subsequently changed managed-media diagnostics outside its unchanged capture guard, so final whole-file lint belongs to CI. The intentional visible-text reads retain narrowly scoped explanations. |

All 419 audited owner/config/helper/manifest blobs and all 607 symbol/quoted-module reference rows match exact base `95d09cc0`, supporting zero introduced findings. prs.title: fix(pr): allow reviewed corrections to refresh their baseline again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A reviewed correction cannot refresh its baseline again when another upstream repair is needed after the first native refresh. This blocks the existing correction workflow even when its source, incoming review and signed provenance remain valid.

## User Impact

Maintainers can refresh a previously refreshed correction onto a descendant baseline through the same native command. Every refresh still requires fresh candidate review and completed gates before publication; interrupted or changed authority refuses safely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preparation owner validates the retained signed binding chain and prior READY reviews, preserves incoming review identity and historical proof, and retains the complete product/fixup review scope even when upstream subsumes a change. The existing transition journal accepts only the exact old or new binding/context during recovery. Gate and publication policies are unchanged.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163259. This follows the landed baseline-refresh repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163955 and preserves the complementary pending-publication work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162704.

## Evidence

- The real preparation-owner regression failed on the old second-refresh guard (6.13 seconds).
- All 39 baseline-refresh cases passed in 136.14 seconds, including chained ancestry/proof retention, stale gate refusal, malformed authority, interrupted installation, foreign ref preservation and subsumed/later-fixup scope.
- All 72 correction preparation/publication/merge cases passed in 168.83 seconds; the eager PR wrapper inventory case passed in 5.15 seconds. Runs used one worker with no retries.
- Selected changed-check coverage is complete: root-test types, structural/dependency/dead-code guards, scripts/root lint and formatting. The initial plan caught one consistent-return lint error; explicit `undefined` fixed it, and the failed/remaining checks passed.
- Fresh independent review found no P0–P2 issues; the subsequent one-line, behavior-preserving lint correction also received independent review.

- The [completed exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165400#issuecomment-5989646105) reports no findings or security issues.
- [Hosted CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37274512080/job/111649085414) failed the gateway-server type graph: `server-lifecycle.catalog-write.test.ts:162` omits the required `resolveGatewayContext` and `loadSubagentRegistryActivation` dependencies. Tested merge `021be16548e3b24639673b650176fd807d9977e5` has baseline `3dc4128bdfef9278e33b0117bdb80fff87f5c99c` and this PR head as parents. The failing file is byte-identical to that baseline; the merge changes only this PR's three tooling files. The [separate Gateway-owner handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165331#issuecomment-5989731212) names the existing sibling fixture and required proof. Native preparation and merging remain held pending a qualified remedy; no CI retry or gate waiver has been used.

These are isolated native-owner fixtures, including signed publication against a fixture remote. The new capability has not been used on the dependent PR or dispatched a live merge. Its existing signed candidates, reviews and build/test proof remain historical and unchanged.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse committed owner facts for warm reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warmed turns still repeat reads of facts already held by their owners. Publish the session actor's transcript watermark with entry-patch snapshots; retain bounded heartbeat absence and committed outcome facts for the existing executor lifetime; read interrupted-input prompt history in one byte-bounded SQL statement without an unused total; and carry ACP committed postimages through the existing write receipt.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Session bookkeeping reuses committed facts and avoids unused history work; no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Writers remain authoritative. Heartbeat facts are replaced by persistence/claim results and invalidated by session removal, lifecycle replacement, uncertain writes, and executor retirement. ACP read fills stay reader-local so they cannot overwrite a later committed postimage. Pinned snapshots keep their direct-read path. SQL still bounds message payload bytes before transfer.

## Measurement

Three alternating pairs completed with the unchanged shared synthetic harness: M1, C1, M2, C2, M3, C3. Base: `a3067578bd0e317f43e721156a329f8fc6c9326b`; candidate: `bf823c74679ab70f0b64bdcea69eaa06eb5603b4`. Each side contains 30 warmed turns. Medians and ranges below pool individual turns, rather than taking a median of run medians. All six successful runs have the pinned head, matching harness hashes, complete warmed SQL/request attribution coverage, and successful fixture process cleanup.

**The causal warmed median is unchanged: 114 statements / 31 requests / 0 MAIN.** Causal counts include turn-attributed work on all threads even when it finishes outside the turn's wall-clock window. Raw-window counts include everything observed during that window, including background work. These scopes are reported separately; a background decrease is not claimed as savings from this PR. No latency claim is made on the loaded host.

| Warmed metric, median [min–max] | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Causal all-thread statements | 114 [114–139] | 114 [114–129] |
| Causal logical requests | 31 [31–38] | 31 [31–39] |
| Causal MAIN statements | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Raw-window all-thread statements | 146.5 [122–182] | 138 [121–179] |
| Raw-window logical requests | 45 [33–55] | 44 [36–53] |
| Raw-window MAIN statements | 0 [0–9] | 0 [0–13] |

Across the 30 warmed turns per side, causal totals are **3522 statements / 961 requests → 3509 / 960** (−13 / −1). Raw-window background MAIN totals are 13 per run on both sides; their placement among turns varies.

| Run | Causal statements | Causal requests | Raw-window statements | Raw-window requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | 114 [114–120] | 31 [31–33] | 142 [132–175] | 45 [37–49] |
| C1 | 114 [114–119] | 31 [31–33] | 139 [124–167] | 44 [36–50] |
| M2 | 117 [114–139] | 31.5 [31–37] | 148 [139–168] | 45 [40–49] |
| C2 | 119 [114–129] | 32 [31–39] | 138 [129–179] | 43.5 [37–52] |
| M3 | 114.5 [114–125] | 31 [31–38] | 148 [122–182] | 46 [33–55] |
| C3 | 114 [114–128] | 31 [31–36] | 139 [121–166] | 42 [37–53] |

The updated baseline's increase from the predecessor’s 82 / 27 follows #172462: compact durable receipts stopped carrying full-history indexes. This restores 17 SQL / 2 requests for cohort hydration, 9 / 1 for anchors, 4 / 1 for durable input preparation, and 2 SQL in existing active-accounting work. The bounded context/anchor-facts follow-up, #172702, is now merged and preserves compact append receipts; its effects are not included in this comparison.

### Whole workload and first use

Whole-workload values below are per-run totals, shown as median [min–max]. The whole workload includes boot, connect, first use, warmed turns, control work, and shutdown.

| Scope | Base statements | Candidate statements | Base requests | Candidate requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Whole workload | 4935 [4893–4954] | 4834 [4789–4859] | 1084 [1078–1095] | 1072 [1047–1073] |
| Causal turns | 2101 [2059–2110] | 2074 [2037–2098] | 558 [546–560] | 553 [549–563] |
| Background | 2834 [2834–2844] | 2761 [2715–2797] | 532 [524–537] | 509 [494–524] |
| Causal first turn | 277 [258–292] | 269 [252–272] | 71 [70–72] | 70 [69–71] |
| Causal second session | 640 [636–645] | 636 [632–639] | 163 [163–164] | 165 [163–167] |
| Raw first-turn window | 1360 [1099–1387] | 1073 [876–1379] | 169 [162–172] | 170 [156–170] |
| Raw second-session window | 766 [764–791] | 762 [726–784] | 220 [219–233] | 217 [203–231] |

Whole-workload MAIN is unchanged at 476 statements per run, entirely outside causal turn work. Across three runs, whole-workload totals are 14782 / 3257 → 14482 / 3192 statements / requests. Causal turn totals are 6270 / 1664 → 6209 / 1665 (−61 statements / +1 request); background totals are 8512 / 1593 → 8273 / 1527 (−239 / −66). The background reduction is observed variation, not claimed PR savings.

Outside warmed turns, source-backed removed classes account for **48 fewer causal statements**: interrupted-input prompt history 33 → 9 (−24), actor transcript watermark 22 → 0 (−22), and ACP selected metadata 3 → 1 (−2). Overall outside-warmed causal requests are +2. Most removed statements were inside existing worker requests, so statement removal does not imply request removal.

### Shared read families

These are SQL statement totals over 30 causal warmed turns or three complete workloads per side. Families can coexist within one request; the rows are not additive request savings.

| Read family | Warmed base → candidate | Whole-workload base → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-entry facts | 7 → 8 | 87 → 84 |
| Actor hydration | 5 → 5 | 32 → 32 |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 0 → 0 | 20 → 21 |
| Row facts | 32 → 31 | 127 → 123 |
| Transcript watermark | 8 → 1 | 47 → 18 |
| Interrupted-input prompt history | 6 → 3 | 51 → 18 |
| ACP selected metadata | 4 → 3 | 23 → 19 |

The extra warmed exact-entry read is disclosed: ordered reads are 3 → 3, standalone retained-facts misses are 2 → 4, and writable-facts reads are 2 → 1. In pair 2, three candidate standalone misses originate at `session-entry-read-facts.ts:383` through `session-entry-read-runtime.ts:508`; ordered reads remain 2 → 2 and writable reads fall 2 → 1. These are causal reads, not background. The read files are unchanged, and baseline M3 independently exercises the standalone path, but per-invalidation evidence is insufficient to explain every candidate miss. Whole-workload exact reads decrease by three. The extra whole-workload entry-cache snapshot load occurs only in background first-turn work: M1 loads three times and every other run four; warmed loads remain zero.

### Operation deltas

All values below are totals across 30 warmed turns per side. These are observed logical operation differences, not blanket attributable savings. Combining both entry-patch caller forms gives 458 / 180 → 456 / 180 statements / requests. Trajectory append is unchanged at 120 / 30 → 120 / 30. ACP metadata requests remain 60 despite fewer SQL reads; prompt-history invocation count rises from two to three while SQL falls from six to three.

| Operation / caller | Statement delta | Request delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordered cohort `session-entry-read-ordered.ts::<anonymous>` | −15 | −3 |
| Entry patch `session-entry-patch.ts::<anonymous>` | −4 | −1 |
| Prompt history `readPendingInputHistory` | −3 | +1 |
| Transcript `readTranscript` | −2 | 0 |
| ACP `readAcpSessionMetaForEntries` | −1 | 0 |
| Actor `acceptInput` | −1 | 0 |
| Writable facts `session-entry-read-writable.ts::<anonymous>` | −1 | −1 |
| Actor `appendTranscriptEvent` | +1 | 0 |
| Transcript `readAnchors` | +1 | 0 |
| Entry patch `patchSessionEntryInWorker` | +2 | +1 |
| Transcript `readExactEntries` | +2 | +2 |
| Read-only session worker `sendMessage` | +2 | −1 |
| Activity summary `readActivitySummarySource` | +6 | +1 |

One earlier C2 attempt failed before any successful turns: `sessions.create` returned `UNAVAILABLE` / `SessionStoreUnavailableError` with a schema-missing diagnostic, and the Gateway database open completed after the rejection. It is excluded from all measurement statistics. The same pinned candidate later completed successfully without a source change; that replay does not establish a fix or explain the availability failure.

Touched-owner T1: **1 → 1**, the unchanged `selectAcpSessionRow` call behind deprecated synchronous `readAcpSessionEntry` (shipped v2026.9.4; compatibility ends 2026-12-31). Bundled Gateway paths use workers. Removing this call requires changing that public SDK contract; this PR adds no MAIN SQLite.

## Removed work and accepted edges

- Heartbeat absence/retry reads: a known absence or committed claim is authoritative until an owner publication or executor retirement. Unsupported out-of-process writes are not freshness-polled.
- Actor watermark reread: entry patches trust the actor's already-reconciled watermark; uncovered residency still hydrates through its owner.
- Interrupted-context total and read transaction: the caller consumes a single bounded page and never uses a total. The public history list retains its total and snapshot contract.
- ACP post-write reread: covered rows/deletions come from committed receipts. Evicted or unknown keys use the ordinary worker reader. An ordinary partial cohort may span a concurrent commit; explicit pinned snapshots retain direct reads.
- Projection admission recheck: published display facts use existing owner invalidation. Replacement during preparation may briefly leave old display metadata; disclosure and execution authority remain checked at real effects.

Generic async-planner CAS remains because its callback releases the writer queue and permits real intervening updates. Live authority at real effects, pending-input custody, and destructive-cleanup lease-loss aborts remain intact.

A forthcoming trajectory receipt proposal will address sequence/retained-byte facts: existing settlement notifications lack complete mutation scope, while per-session invalidation would discard the cache on each transcript write. Correct coverage across retention, window deletion/copy, import, and native writers requires an owner receipt change. No trajectory saving is claimed here.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting and diff checks passed. Codex autoreview completed in two rounds: the production change is clean through P2, and the CI correction is clean through P1. The focused actor-residency suite passed 8/8 tests. Typed lint passed after fixing four local-name shadowing errors. The seven CI-repair cases passed locally across the ACP cache and accepted-facts projection files, preserving returned-value and lifecycle assertions. Final-head CI run 38648616890 completed green (52 passed, 25 skipped), including touched-owner tests, typed lint, production/test types, source contracts, Madge (zero cycles), T1/dialect ratchets, and PostgreSQL conformance. The separate exact-head dependency scan completed in [run 38662199083](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38662199083/job/116186330262). Every reported Knip export/type/file finding also appears under the same rule and file in the completed [main dependency scan at 4612504e2bde](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38654297528/job/116160592188); no candidate-only finding remains. Landing uses the authorized inherited-static-failure exception. Local Knip attempts timed out and are not passing evidence. No schema, SDK surface, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change; the update cell is not applicable.

LOC: 21 files changed, +479 / −124 lines (net +355).

The earlier 79-statement sample omitted the activity-summary commit (BEGIN, session-node upsert, COMMIT: 3 statements / 1 request). Current diagnostics show each summary consumes newly appended messages and advances transcript coverage even when synthetic summary text repeats; the write remains necessary. The older run’s raw logs were discarded, so the reason it omitted that commit is unknown. No extra saving is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(search): engine-owned full-text and vector capabilities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Search callers currently construct SQLite-specific FTS5 and vec0 operations, which prevents the admitted database adapter from owning search primitives.

## User Impact

SQLite search behavior is unchanged. This adds experimental SDK search capabilities through existing entrypoints; it does not enable PostgreSQL search, change a schema/version, or affect LanceDB.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move FTS schema/maintenance, native expressions, sqlite-vec loading, and the killable KNN child into `src/infra/database-engine`. Memory-core retains body/path retrieval, hybrid scoring, and exact fallback; standing intents retain chronology and token verification; transcript search retains branch/role visibility before LIMIT.

The [documented design summary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a5493239a29979e2e157e199be28b94826055fa/docs/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md#database-engine-adapters-experimental) describes the experimental contract. Optional `DatabaseEngineAdapter.search` binds `FullTextCapability`, `VectorCapability`, and `TextIndex`/`VectorIndex` handles at admission. Existing `fullText`/`vector` labels remain diagnostic metadata. Bundled callers migrate together; no SDK subpath is added.

P3-5b will supply PostgreSQL native `simple` + unaccent text search with `ts_rank_cd` normalization 2 and explicitly engine-local ranking, plus exact pgvector cosine. PostgreSQL capabilities remain `null` with an admission diagnostic here. ANN remains deferred; SQLite keeps its L2-candidate/cosine-rerank strategy and missing-vec exact fallback.

## Evidence

Validation base: `617cc0900281f8adc27e189e602b502e851a034c`, the origin/main snapshot used for the final rebase.

- Final-source before/after capture: **972/972 executions identical**, including SQL text, execution order, bindings, outputs, and errors. Covers all four FTS indexes and vec0, queries, writes/triggers/rebuilds, body/path/trigram, intents, transcript relevance/recent/snippets, and missing-vec fallback. The previous 970-execution fixture gained only main's transcript-schema `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT` pair.
- All **44 output phases** and **23 coverage checks** pass. The actual child process returns the same **861,839-byte** dense-NUL response. Source inputs were pinned and verified across 26 process/thread reports.
- Main capture (962 executions) SHA-256: `60152cb5f85963dac672e9a909ae130f1b3edd579c9bc90259012258733f8d59`. Output SHA-256: `136045ed0f5c591d1c0206f543f567d5b0f11c4724ffc37d3497c8762625b54b`.
- Owner suites: **26 files / 323 tests passed, 0 skipped**, all with `--maxWorkers=1`: memory-core body/path/trigram/vector/KNN child/missing-vec, standing intents, transcript search/index, memory-host-sdk schema, and sqlite-vec loader. Supplementary tests passed 40/40, runtime process build graph 10/10, and wrapper inventory/closure 4/4 selected cases (17 intentionally filtered out): **377 tests across 35 files** in total. Format, all three lint scopes, and all three typechecks passed. Worker ratchet passed (live T1 223 → 223; compatibility calls 12 → 12). Assertion safety passed after removing two redundant erased casts and canonically pruning eight obsolete allowances; its baseline shrank 6,310 → 6,302. Max-lines and line-cap passed. The bundled environment-count guard retains an inherited failure: base and head contain the exact same 455 names against the unchanged budget of 454 (zero names added or removed). The stale worker inventory was regenerated canonically (604 files / 2,318 calls) and passed document format/whitespace checks.
- Import boundaries: canonical SDK/packages inventory is empty. The canonical `src` inventory reports two inherited `import.meta.url` edges in untouched `src/infra/database-engine/port-roundtrip.test-support.ts` (lines 18 and 24), with identical base/head blobs and zero new edges. The obsolete wrapper scripts named in CONTRIBUTING are absent, so these checks invoked the existing exported checker API directly; the inherited diagnostic remains exit 1.
- Canonical SDK baseline/diff regenerated against the final rebased source for all three existing entrypoints: 39 → 55 exports, **16 export additions (12 unique symbols)**, and the additive optional `DatabaseEngineAdapter.search` member. No removed exports or new/removed entrypoints. API acknowledgement digest: `2ff03af4`. Added symbols: `admitStoreSearch`, `FullTextCapability`, `SearchSchema`, `SearchStore`, `StoreSearchCapabilities`, `TextIndex`, `TextIndexDefinition`, `TextQuery`, `VectorCapability`, `VectorIndex`, `VectorSearch`, and `matchesVectorRow`.
- Final Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean for P0–P2**, with both review partitions completed and final source verification passed.

The final cast cleanup emits byte-identical JavaScript through the repository loader, and its candidate capture was rerun against the unchanged baseline. Broad PR CI remains pending; the full local `pnpm build` was not completed. The canonical `build:ci-artifacts` profile passed before the final rebase, while the current runtime process build graph and SDK generation passed.

Net production growth is **+348 lines** (1,656 additions / 1,308 deletions), excluding tests, fixtures, docs, and wrapper metadata; moved implementation nets out.

<details>
<summary>Changed files (69, including moved/deleted paths)</summary>

Coordinator file-list clearance is required before landing; this PR remains a draft.

