prs.title: perf(text): bound plain-tool-call parse work for code-bearing streamed replies
prs.body:
Fixes #172663

## What Problem This Solves

A streamed assistant reply that contains a fenced (or indented) code block with a payload marker (`{`, `<parameter=`, `<function=`, `to=`) permanently activated the shared visible-text sanitizer. From that delta onward every later delta re-ran the canonical plain-text tool-call parse over the whole accumulated reply, so the work grew with the square of the reply length and the reply stalled mid-answer with no visible progress.

Measured through the delivery projection on 4-character deltas (17 KB fixtures, same machine, characters counted at the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` boundary):

| fixture | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fenced tool-call example | 59,381 ms / 36,474,073 parsed chars | 63 ms / 0 parsed chars |
| fenced JSON block | 296 ms / 36,576,790 parsed chars | 64 ms / 0 parsed chars |
| prose only (control) | 40 ms / 0 parsed chars | 51 ms / 0 parsed chars |
| real leaked call (unchanged class) | 1,421 ms / 36,354,717 parsed chars | 1,688 ms / 36,354,717 parsed chars |

## Why This Change Was Made

`createActivatedProjector` probes appended text for activation tokens and, once one appears, hands the entire buffer to the canonical transform on every later delta. That latch is what makes code-bearing replies quadratic: the marker inside a code block is protected text, so the canonical parse keeps returning the input unchanged while paying a full Markdown code-region scan plus a tool-call scan each time.

A payload marker quoted inside protected code cannot start a plain-text tool call — the canonical parse already excludes those ranges through the same `findCodeRegions` resolver — so the streaming probe no longer latches on such a marker. The probe checks the matched marker's offset against those protected ranges and remembers the containing region's end, so a closed code block is resolved once instead of once per delta.

Ownership is unchanged: the canonical transform still decides what gets stripped, how Markdown is protected, and how replacements are reported. Only the streaming activation decision is gated, and the citation behavior from #172470 is preserved — brackets still do not activate, payload markers in ordinary prose still do.

## User Impact

Replies that include code — the common shape for a coding agent — stream continuously again instead of consuming CPU quadratically and appearing frozen. Operators who saw multi-minute stalls on code-bearing answers (reported in #172663) get the reply at streaming speed.

## Evidence

Bounded-work regression fails before the fix and passes after it, through the shipped entry point (`assistantVisibleTextFilters("delivery", true)` + `createTextProjection`, 4-character deltas, parse work counted with a spy on `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`):

```text
# source fix temporarily stashed
FAIL  plain-tool-call-text.test.ts > bounds plain-tool-call parse work when a code block only quotes a call
      Tests  1 failed | 15 passed (16)

# with the fix
 ✓  bounds plain-tool-call parse work when a code block only quotes a call 51ms
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Existing streaming-equivalence cases still hold: every sample in `plain-tool-call-text.test.ts` (including fenced calls, a fenced call followed by a real call, and split payloads) still matches the canonical strip at chunk sizes 1, 3 and 7.

Suites run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/text --run --maxWorkers=1` — 13 files, 183 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers --run --maxWorkers=1` — 2 shards passed
- `npx oxfmt --check` on the three touched files — clean

Non-goal (unchanged by this PR): a reply that really does carry a strippable plain-text call still re-parses per delta once that call is admitted. That residual quadratic class is separate from the code-bearing activation fixed here.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used code tracing to locate the activating latch and the existing protected-range owner, then reused that owner for the streaming decision. The implementer understands the code: the probe only decides whether the streaming projector must run, and it answers with the same `findCodeRegions` authority the canonical strip already uses. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): reduce live-event shell redraws
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of an active dashboard deep link receives about 125 Gateway events in 20 seconds. Unrelated presence, session, catalog, and run-state publications repeatedly invalidate the sidebar and chat shell. The campaign evidence measured 143 sidebar, 104 chat-page, and 137 chat-pane renders, with substantial steady-state churn after eight seconds.

## User Impact

Visible unread, attention, presence, run, and identity changes still update. Hidden roster content retains its mounted snapshot with zero renders, then reconciles once to the latest data when shown. Child-owned changes leave the chat page idle. Home indicators remain live outside Sessions; owner-excluded catalog activity stays quiet while visible titles, errors, and pagination update.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session, presence, roster, and chat owners admit presentation changes, and the existing frame owner coalesces them. Superseded frame machinery, upward child forwarding, duplicate controllers, and mirrors are deleted. Probe and fixture growth stays in bench/test files. No configuration option, Gateway schema, durable stored shape, or permission model changes.

A cached-roster feedback loop also rebuilt the collapsed Set for an unchanged Gateway URL; the existing scalar settings scope is now memoized. Plugin replacement identity remains child-owned: its direct subscription replaces A with B without a sidebar-parent render.

## Evidence

**Do not land.** Candidate `dfa988f23d32027cf8de82566b327b490875fbe1`, rebased onto main `95d09cc0b2d3a79ba954e9100de592a54b0e84f6`. Complete-PR review and subsequent fixes are reviewed through P2. Full UI and final raw-census audit are still pending; CI has an unresolved nonstatic failure described below.

### Render census

The final-head matched 125-event benchmark completed on AWS `cbx_8ebd4cea1237`: **chat-page 0, chat-pane 74**, below the requested pane ceiling of 111, with matching final probed DOM. Sidebar totals, contemporary-base comparison, rates, and every-pane-producer accounting will be filled from the retained raw census after collection. No pane-only improvement against contemporary main is claimed yet.

[Active native proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7b8b1ca7e1dd7d3204ca14d67e0191b6): focused tests, controlled old-producer regression checks, matched benchmark, changed checks, clean-base static replays, and full UI e2e on the exact candidate.

### Correctness and validation

- **552 focused tests / 13 files passed.** Native `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times include interactions 76 cases / 15 s, catalogs 82 / 13 s, sessions 104 / 18 s, roster 151 / 28 s, and cached-roster/row rendering 12 / 7 s.
- A controlled one-production-file replay restores the exact old projection while retaining current tests: Home 2 and catalog 1 fail at their owning assertions; plugin replacement 2 passes on both implementations with zero parent renders. Final source restoration and per-phase source receipts pass.
- Keyboard, question/attention, mobile hidden-roster transition, and Team-scale browser fixtures passed. Typechecks, lint, format, and line-cap checks passed.
- Full UI e2e is running with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`. Its complete pass/fail list and wall time remain pending.

Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38668000070) has **67 successful checks**. Its sole substantive failure is [UI e2e 4/5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38668000070/job/116205211831): four confirm/cancel cases in `chat-native-runtime-recovery.e2e.test.ts` wait for a missing prompt. Source tracing finds the same global-only agent resolver in main's recovery helper; ordinary agent-scoped keys provide no agent and return before the dialog. The relevant test and owners are byte-identical on pinned base/head. Native base/head replay is pending, so inheritance is not yet claimed. This nonstatic failure does not meet the lead's CI gate.

### Proven inherited static failures

Clean pinned main and head independently fail the environment-name budget at **455 versus 454**, and the unused-export scan reports the same seven entries:

- `AuthProfileAuthorizationError` — `src/agents/auth-profiles/authorization.ts`
- `configuredOrFalseAsync` — `src/gateway/talk/session-config.ts`
- `WorkerPreparationArtifactsSchema` — `src/gateway/worker-environments/preparation-identity.schema.ts`

- `getChatRunOwnerSessionKey` — `ui/src/pages/chat/history-merge.ts`

No budget or export exception was changed. Clean-base source receipts agree before/after.

### Presentation timeout

The presentation readiness timeout was replayed **10 times on base and 10 times on head, alternating on the same AWS box**: all 20 invocations passed all eight cases (160 test cases), [paired replay](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_95433ed5f1e4094fb2c5f46b1dec46af). Classification: **unreproduced**, not proven inherited or head-only. No assertion or timeout was weakened.

### Production size

Strict runtime TypeScript delta: **+587 LOC**, 1,070 added / 483 deleted across 34 files. The required `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'` reports 47 files, 2,509 additions / 561 deletions; those exclusions also count bench/probe/fixture and TSX-test growth.

This remains above the original +350 LOC. Visible projection (+297), presence scope (+104), and child hydration/descriptor admission (+108 net) preserve visible membership, collapsed summaries, menu identity, plugin inputs, expiry, discovery, and freshness while suppressing unrelated publication. Redundant scheduling and forwarding paths are removed. The remaining runtime growth is a lead-review tradeoff.

### Synthetic visual proof

Final-head inspected screenshots will replace these explicitly historical synthetic captures.

prs.title: fix(mcp): restore requester identity for CLI tool policies
prs.body:
Closes #170576. Reported by @davidcittadini.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes owner-aware `before_tool_call` policies rejecting legitimate CLI harness tool calls because the loopback MCP route omits the host's requester identity.

## User Impact

Policy plugins receive the same host-derived channel, account, sender, and ownership facts available to embedded and native harness calls. Missing identity and attach-only grants remain fail-closed; client-supplied headers cannot assert ownership. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing harness requester projection, capture it with the CLI tool grant, and pass that captured context to the hook. Existing grant authentication, currentness checks, and tool policy remain in place. This restores hook metadata; it does not change the separate requester-origin admission work in #157806.

## Evidence

- Exercised the production CLI grant builder, grant capture, HTTP `tools/call` handler, hook bridge, and tool execution with an owner-aware policy. Before the fix, the owner and guest cases fail; missing-identity and attach-only controls pass. All four pass after the fix, including forged-header rejection.
- 94 related tests pass across CLI grant context, grant storage, and MCP HTTP suites. The final typed hook-fixture correction was replayed separately: four passing cases, already included in that total.
- Production and test type checks, targeted typed lint, formatting, assertion and line-budget checks pass. Runtime build passes (134.2 seconds). Fresh independent review and the scoped fixture follow-up found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The original proof exercised the in-process production HTTP boundary with synthetic state. The fixed head now also passes the separately launched isolated Gateway/CLI proof below. Current-head CI passes; applicable maintainer/security review still governs merging. The CLI executable is a self-authored protocol fixture, so this does not establish vendor CLI/API behavior.


### CI follow-up

[CI run 38517156521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38517156521/job/115698790012) found one stale expectation in the existing CLI preparation test: its exact grant-context comparison omitted the newly restored `requester` field (114 sibling cases passed). The same failure reproduced locally; the expectation now explicitly includes the admitted Telegram channel and canonical sender, preserving the exact matcher and unknown-ownership behavior. The repository `test:ci-failed 171791 --run` replay passes (one selected case, 42.32 seconds wall time), and targeted test types, typed lint, formatting, and independent correction review pass. Production code is unchanged, so the earlier 94-case boundary proof and runtime build remain applicable; the new head's CI has now passed (see current-head CI below).

The review reports no introduced code finding and requested an installed CLI/Gateway policy, final-effect proof, and revocation during an awaited policy. The isolated proof below now covers those requested boundaries at the fixed head; synthetic hook/effect tests alone were not treated as that evidence.


### Current-head CI

CI and `openclaw/ci-gate` pass for `f688d319e94fa18469358d6e93b9ec13c30c22be`: [run 38522318284](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38522318284). This resolves the stale preparation expectation failure. The installed-policy, final-I/O and awaited-revocation proof is recorded below.

### Isolated Gateway/CLI policy proof

At `f688d319e94fa18469358d6e93b9ec13c30c22be`, a separately launched loopback Gateway, native QA transport, and self-authored Claude stream-json protocol executable passed all four cases in 313.28 seconds. A public-SDK `before_tool_call` policy was installed and activated through the public plugin install/reload and capability-consent CLI; reload reported runtime generation 4, and the actual generated configuration validated. State, credentials, senders and message contents were synthetic, with no vendor API or external channel delivery.

- Native QA owner ingress produced the host-derived channel/account/sender/owner facts and exactly one intended QA message through real MCP HTTP and the production message tool.
- An ingress-allowed guest reached the same installed policy. Forged HTTP requester/channel/account headers did not assert ownership; policy denied, with zero marked outbound messages.
- A public attach grant exposed the message tool but carried no requester. Forged identity headers still failed policy; no marked message was sent. Public revoke made a fresh request return HTTP401.
- A real owner tool call waited inside the installed policy. Public `sessions.abort` was started without joining it; the original CLI grant returned HTTP401 while the policy was still held. The fixture policy then returned allow. The original HTTP call settled as a tool error, Stop returned `ok:true/status:aborted` for the exact observed run, and stale list/call requests returned HTTP401. Final marked outbound remained zero.

After confirmed native process-tree shutdown, the complete bus had marked counts owner1/guest0/missing0/cancel0 across all QA destinations/accounts. Both local services stopped and private state/credentials were removed. The first 447.492-second attempt passed the first three cases but rejected the current Stop response because the fixture expected an obsolete `aborted` boolean. The fixture was corrected to the native `ok/status/abortedRunId` contract and independently rereviewed before this passing recovery; no product code or policy semantics changed.

This proves the native QA→Claude CLI MCP route and native run/grant cancellation. It does not prove a distinct caller socket-disconnect case (the hook did not report caller cancellation), attach revocation during an already accepted call, provider role propagation, Codex/embedded-provider paths, vendor behavior, warm-process transfer, or crash/restart durability.

The chat pane is owned by Solid, but its remaining transcript renderers and controller interfaces still depended on Lit. This ports that rendering chain while preserving transcript row identity, scrolling, reply navigation, search, and live subagent activity.

## User Impact

Solid renders the compact feed and reply geometry through the existing controller and virtualizer owners. Host tags, classes, selectors, row keys, and cleanup contracts stay intact. prs.title: chore(qa): cover Control UI reconnect continuity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI reconnect coverage needs to prove that a streamed turn survives browser socket loss, Stop retains its partial reply in Gateway history, and the next turn stays independent.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This adds real Gateway and Chromium coverage for reconnect continuity, abort retention, and exactly-once rendering, without live provider credentials or operator state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only inference is synthetic. The test cuts the browser WebSocket while the Gateway keeps streaming, then checks the reconstructed run, Stop, and a clean follow-up, then verifies retained state after reload. A fresh authenticated, cursor-free `chat.history` read after successful abort verifies the retained assistant text and first run identity independently of browser IndexedDB. The long composition is registered in the release-only inventory and remains eligible when directly changed.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway + Chromium scenario passed: one test, 27.610 s scenario / 68.891 s file / 107.29 s Vitest duration. Full runtime and matching Control UI assets were built in the isolated worktree. The file owns a real Gateway and browser, which explains its release-only tier.
- Focused workflow routing passed all seven cases, including prebuilt/frozen selectors and private resource ownership (41.99 s Vitest duration). The frozen non-prebuilt case initially failed because its expected inventory omitted the newly registered file; that registration is now included.
- The modified release-only planner assertions passed in the two-file routing command; unrelated capacity cases were interrupted after their earlier passing output rather than claiming a full-suite pass.
- Full core test typecheck, scripts typecheck, standard focused type-aware lint, formatting, workflow checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Workflow checks used the existing newer Homebrew Python because system Python 3.9 cannot run the required pre-commit version.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects. The accepted ClawSweeper finding is addressed by the post-abort Gateway history assertion.

The first current-main browser run exposed a stale test-only `openclaw-app.runtime` probe. The test now uses the canonical readiness helper and visible reconnect status, and the real browser replay passed. This is coverage, not evidence that an underlying Gateway stall is fixed.

Investigated local timing failure: the complete-union native inventory case first exceeded its unchanged 120 s budget (144.662 s), with no reported inventory mismatch. An isolated unchanged main control at `22e08398513c2b506bab8270aa6bc38901d08957` passed the same case in 61.134 s; the final PR head passed in 51.274 s (58.66 s wrapper). Both used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'owns the complete inventory once'`. The original timing trigger remains uncertain; these passing replays are not presented as a repair or proof of an inherited failure. No timeout, assertion, or budget was weakened.

The two prebuilt inventory variants initially rejected the added parallel file because their exact expected count remained 27. Updating that count to the deliberately registered 28 files preserves the ownership assertion; both variants passed (47.64 s Vitest / 60.88 s wrapper).

Final head: `c94fc5c03a104b6b556b5e56cf021afa7fd2b370`, rebased onto main with conflicts resolved. No merge or auto-merge was requested.


## Review and CI disposition

[ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155468#issuecomment-5771837646) cleared this head: platinum overall and proof, diamond patch quality, ready for maintainer review, with the prior finding resolved and no remaining code findings or checklist items.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38669023879) completed with three unrelated failures. Merge is held; this PR is ready for review, not green for merge.

- UI E2E shards 2/9 and 5/9 failed the same eight untouched model-provider/OpenCode tests as [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245) at `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209`. Compared exception signatures, locators, and source call sites match; this is more than a job-name comparison.
- Docker's cron cleanup seed failed because main's stored inference-account requirement from #172590 rejects the old fixture's inline provider key. The tested merge included main `7e823106a77c63640806c0646c9dc8a21b35871f`; this PR changes neither that fixture nor production cron/account code. [Canonical repair #172709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172709) stores a synthetic account and selects it explicitly. Its [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38667536442) passed the affected `cron-mcp-cleanup` selection. Docker attribution is based on the unchanged source and verified repair, not a matching main failure log.

The canonical Docker repair is still open. Rebasing alone cannot include it yet; unrelated fixes have not been copied into this coverage PR. Recheck CI after the upstream failures are repaired.

prs.title: fix: preserve Gateway delegation for channel replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repairs a dropped host-ownership handoff that can send channel-origin delegated OpenClaw requests over WebSocket without their private run authority, producing `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Ordinary and fast reply session setup clone the inbound context without copying its privately bound Gateway resolver. Use the existing scope-checked `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence` helper at both boundaries.
2. A deployment of that first repair still reproduced the error. Further tracing found that Discord's provider supplies the host-bound `buildContext`, but `buildDiscordMessagePreflightContext` dropped it. Message processing then selected the plain fallback builder, so there was no Gateway binding for session initialization to preserve.

**Scope correction (September 17):** that second, Discord-side production correction has since landed upstream independently, in `34f29edb265` — *fix(discord): restore OpenClaw delegation from guild messages* (#143006, September 9). `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-context.ts` is now byte-identical between this branch and `main`, so this PR no longer carries that production change. What it retains on the Discord side is the **regression test** that pins the forwarding behavior, which upstream did not add. The independent convergence is corroborating evidence that the diagnosis was correct.

**Production surface at the current head** (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD`, re-derived this round — the previous four-file list in this section was stale, and named `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.ts`, which is byte-identical to `main`):

- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts` — the two session-preparation call sites that copy the admission evidence.
- `src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.ts` — the fenced resolver stored at preparation.
- `src/plugins/channel-gateway-root-slots.ts` (new), `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts`, `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-context-binding.ts` — the channel Gateway slot lifecycle added by rounds 23 and 24.

It adds no permissions, infers no authority from identifiers, transports no grants over WebSocket, does not weaken the delegation guard, and does not select a global Gateway.

## User Impact

Channel session preparation retains scope-bound Gateway ownership, so calls keep their intended local route. The absent-builder fallback remains unchanged. No configuration or credential changes are required.

## Evidence

### Round 24 — the slot history compacts failed replacements instead of stacking them

Revision 25's finding: rollback retires a staged candidate but leaves it as the slot's `current` claim with the predecessor still linked to it, so the next claim appends *behind the retired candidate*. Repeated failed replacements therefore extend the chain indefinitely, every `ownsLiveRegistrySlot` check crosses all of it, and because each link's value strongly holds the next record together with its whole registry, no failed generation can be collected while the live owner lives.

Measured, not argued. The harm is cost and retention, **not a wrong answer** — `isChannelRecordSuperseded` returns the same boolean before and after, which is why the regression below is a retention probe rather than a behavioral one.

| Six failed replacement generations on one Gateway root, five tracked by `WeakRef` | Reviewed head `e81523edf20` | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Unowned control collected (`--expose-gc` works) | yes | yes |
| Live owner still held | yes | yes |
| `isChannelRecordSuperseded(liveOwner)` | false | false |
| **Failed generations still retained** | **5 of 5** | **0 of 5** |

**Fix.** `claimGatewayRootChannelSlot` now walks back from the slot's current claim through retired candidates — via a new predecessor link recording the claim each generation displaced — and links from the exact *live* predecessor. Overwriting that predecessor's single successor link is what releases every compacted generation: nothing else references them once `current` moves. A retired candidate never owned the slot, so it is removed from the history rather than inserted into it.

**Controls, three, with distinct failure reasons.**

1. Revert only `src/plugins/channel-gateway-root-slots.ts`: the new `registry-runtime.channel-ingress.slot-retention.test.ts` fails with `retainedGenerations: 5` where it expects `0`.
2. Revert the same file and run the rollback regression: **3 passed**. The requested repeated-failed-replacement case is preservation coverage — it pins the restore and committed-rejection semantics the compaction must not break — and it is honestly not the pin for the leak.
3. Keep the fix but drop the retired-guard from the back-walk, so it can step past a *live* predecessor: all three rollback cases fail with `expected {} to be undefined` — a staged candidate then never fences the predecessor's retained binding. The guard is load-bearing.

The regression spawns a `--expose-gc` child that drives the real `createRuntimeBuilder` ingress chain and the repo's existing `collectForRetentionCheck` fixture, matching the pattern already used by `src/process/spawn-broker/proxy-retention.test.ts`.

### Round 23 — staged-rollback slot restore

Supersession is derived from lifecycle rather than a permanent mark: a record counts as superseded only while a successor in its chain belongs to an unretired registry, so rollback hands the slot back to the exact predecessor and commit does not. The slot bookkeeping moved into `src/plugins/channel-gateway-root-slots.ts`, which returned `registry-runtime.ts` to its `origin/main` counted size. Full detail is in the round 23 comment on this PR.

### Delegated-authority expiry before final effect (round 22)

The open security ask was whether an **already-prepared** delegated operation is rejected **before it performs I/O** once its channel is unbound, retired, or replaced — with the Gateway itself still running. Round 22 measures that directly, at the production fence, with a real observable effect.

Where the fence is: `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` captures the retained resolver, and every delegated call then passes through `bindInProcessGatewayContext` (`src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts:113-133`), which resolves the binding *before* `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` and throws `Gateway instance unavailable for <method>` when it yields nothing. For work that has already entered a handler, `resolveInProcessGatewayDispatch`'s `assertContextCurrent` is composed into the `sessionMutationCommitGuard` that `handleGatewayRequest` hands every handler, so a revocation that lands mid-await still fires before the handler's final write.

Both runs below drive the same chain of real production functions — `registerChannelIngressHostOwner` → `resolveStableChannelMessageIngress` → `createHostChannelInboundEventContextBuilder` (which runs `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`) → `finalizeInboundContext` → `initFastReplySessionState` (one of the two call sites this PR adds `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence` to) → `readChannelContextGatewayContextResolver` (exactly what `agent-runner-execution.ts:544` reads) → `withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver` → `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` → `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` → real `handleGatewayRequest` → a registered method handler whose **final effect is a real filesystem write**. Rejection "before I/O" is measured by that file's absence, not by an exception type alone.

In every scenario the channel host's own `resolveGatewayContext` keeps returning the live Gateway — only the **channel** lifetime is revoked — and a control call bound straight to a live root Gateway reaches its final effect, so each row is a channel-authority result rather than a Gateway-availability result.

| Scenario | Binding copied to sessionCtx | Operation accepted | Handler entered | Handler committed | **Final effect** | Successor Gateway redeemed | Gateway still active |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| allowed, channel live | true | true | 1 | 1 | **PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| unbound context | false | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| retired before dispatch | true | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| replaced before dispatch | true | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| retired **during awaited work** | true | false | 1 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| replaced **during awaited work** | true | false | 1 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |

Rejections: `Gateway instance unavailable for sessions.list` for all four retired/replaced rows. The two mid-flight rows are the sharpest result — the handler had already started and was stopped by the production commit guard before its write.

The `unbound` row is honest about a different mechanism: with no retained binding there is no in-process delegated path to enter at all, so the call degrades to an ordinary authenticated external Gateway client (`gateway sessions.list requires credentials before opening a websocket` in an environment with no configured Gateway credentials). No in-process delegated effect occurs, but that row is *not* produced by the lifetime fence.

**Negative control.** Reverting only `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`'s fenced resolver back to `main`'s `state.gatewayResolverByPreparation.set(preparation, params.owner.resolveGatewayContext)` — and nothing else — flips all four retired/replaced rows from **NOT PERFORMED** to **PERFORMED**, with `handler committed` going `0 → 1` in each. The standalone run exits 1 with 16 assertion failures; the committed regression test reports `4 failed | 2 passed (6)` at `expect(fs.existsSync(effectPath)).toBe(effect)` — `expected false, received true`. The fence, not the harness, is what rejects the stale authority.

That round added `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.delegated-effect.test.ts` so the behavior stays pinned in CI. The standalone `pnpm tsx` proof that produced the table is deliberately **not** committed; it is retained with its logs alongside that round's gate output.

#### Round 22b — the real delegated apply owner

Revision 15 accepted the table above but pointed out that its handler substituted for `sessions.list` and guarded its own write, leaving the real delegated approval/application chain — which has its own authority checks — unexercised. That is a fair hit, and the chain is reachable directly.

`prepareDelegatedSystemAgentApproval` (`src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval.ts`) is production code, and its `isAuthorityActive` already consults `callerIdentity.gatewayContextResolver()`. `assertLiveApprovalAuthority` runs at preparation, again inside the proposal resolver, and once more through the `assertCurrent` callback the apply owner invokes immediately before its effect. The repo's existing `system-agent-approval-authority.test.ts` exercises exactly that path — but with a synthetic `() => liveContext` resolver. What was missing was the same path driven by the resolver **this PR copies into the reply session context**.

The new cases build that resolver through the same real production ingress chain, hand it to `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity` with a real claimed run authority (`claimAgentRunDelegatedAuthority`), and drive the real `prepareDelegatedSystemAgentApproval` to its apply. The channel host's own resolver keeps returning the live Gateway throughout, so only the channel lifetime can reject.

| Channel state at apply | Outcome | Apply effect |
|---|---|---|
| live | resolves `{ kind: "completed" }` | performed once |
| retired while the apply owner awaits queued work | rejects `system-agent approval authority is no longer active` | **never performed** |
| replaced while the apply owner awaits queued work | rejects `system-agent approval authority is no longer active` | **never performed** |

**Negative control on the apply owner.** With the same single-line revert, both revoked cases resolve `{ kind: 'completed' }` and the apply effect is performed:

```
× fences the delegated system-agent apply owner when the channel is retired
  → promise resolved "{ kind: 'completed', reply: { …(3) } }" instead of rejecting
× fences the delegated system-agent apply owner when the channel is replaced
  → promise resolved "{ kind: 'completed', reply: { …(3) } }" instead of rejecting
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  6 failed | 3 passed (9)
```

Without the fence, the real apply owner applies a change under expired channel authority. That is the behavior this PR prevents.

The channel-ingress setup shared by both blocks is extracted into a single `prepareChannelBoundResolver` helper rather than duplicated.

### Earlier evidence

- The session regression uses a real host-bound channel context, actual inbound finalization, `getReplyFromConfig`, and real prepared-run admission. Only the embedded runner is stubbed to inspect the admitted resolver. Live, retired, replaced, and deliberately unbound cases retain the existing owner checks.
- The retained Discord regression invokes actual `preflightDiscordMessage` and actual `buildDiscordMessageProcessContext`. Against the pre-fix implementation the injected-builder case lost its callback while the absent-builder case passed; against the current implementation both pass and processing uses exactly the context object returned by the injected builder. Because the production forwarding now comes from `main`, this test guards it against regression rather than proving a change in this diff.
- An additional diagnostic exercises the real Discord DM builder and preflight assembler with private host ownership, retaining the resolver through fast session initialization. The initial simplified session regression did not cover this earlier adapter handoff.
- **Withdrawn, not restated:** earlier revisions of this section carried a "157 focused tests pass" breakdown and a "complete five-file changed-file gate" claim. Both were measured at head `1b2ca891101a45d0ab372231f326526bd4db7006`, three commits and two `origin/main` merges back, and the branch diff is now fourteen files. Neither figure has been re-run, so both are withdrawn rather than repeated. The re-evidenced gate figures are in *Gates* below.

### Gates

Two `origin/main` merges (`5c7e0f141a81`, `671e3911b5dd`) and the round 23 commit (`e81523edf204`) landed after the figures withdrawn above were taken, and this round adds one commit on top. The earlier commands are kept only as a record of what was run then.

Round 24, at this head:

```sh
# the round's own delta (3 files: 1 core production, 2 core tests), staged
pnpm check:changed --staged
# focused suites at the exact staged content
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.rollback.test.ts \
  src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.slot-retention.test.ts
# mergeability surface, with linuxbrew git 2.55
git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only upstream/main HEAD
```

The branch-wide `pnpm check:changed` run exits 1 on the **line-cap growth ratchet** only, with exactly two rows — `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` 1041 → 1043 and `src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts` 1998 → 2178. Both are reproduced byte-identically by running that lane on the clean reviewed-base tree with this round's changes stashed, so neither is introduced here; CI's `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` treats them as advisory and passed at the previous head with the same rows. Clearing them means extracting ~180 lines out of an upstream-owned test file, which would create new conflict surface in a file this branch does not otherwise own. That is left as a separate decision rather than folded into a finding fix. Because `check:changed` stops at the first failing lane, the later lanes are reported above from the `--staged` run over this round's delta.

```sh
# earlier head 1b2ca891101 — record only, not re-run
pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-context.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.test.ts src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.test.ts src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 045524c6f883ca31df7240a107872bd01f2c3378
pnpm build
```

## Related Work and Open Questions

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138596 (previously inspected at `537130294ac2e1360700ab2f094df4b8e9a8b05d`). That PR addresses authenticated CLI/subprocess and worker calls that legitimately cross the Gateway WebSocket boundary, carrying existing host-signed runtime authority. This PR preserves the original local Gateway route at the channel session handoffs. Non-overlapping file sets are not a compatibility proof.

The changes may be complementary, but we have not established that both are required or that either replaces the other. A differential comparison should exercise baseline, this fix, the related fix, and both against the same channel-origin delegation probe. The related PR is not incorporated here.

These production changes are model/runtime-agnostic. Codex enters host tool execution through a native dynamic-tool callback; the bundled Claude CLI MCP handler binds caller identity from its admitted client grant. Those entry paths differ, but no matched successful Claude call has established why the observed behavior differed. No Codex enterprise-policy restriction is demonstrated.

## Post-deployment evidence and remaining validation

On September 8, the operator restarted a real Gateway built from integration `5936dbff50dfbf81c511db450dc1a5be87482e92`, which contains this topic head. A real Discord-origin native Codex turn then invoked the delegated OpenClaw system tool for read-only Gateway status and health. That delegated read completed normally, reported the matching deployed build, and did not fail with the previously observed missing active-run authority error. No configuration, credential, service, or trust changes were made by the probe.

This is successful complete-path **read-only evidence on the combined integration**, not an isolated-topic differential comparison and not evidence of permission to perform mutations. The integration contains other authority fixes, so this observation does not establish which companion fixes are required. Note that the probe ran on September 8, before upstream #143006 landed, so at that time the Discord forwarding under test came from this branch. The probe also predates rounds 23 and 24, so it carries no evidence about the channel Gateway slot lifecycle.

### What is resolved, and what is not

Resolved: rejection before final I/O for retired and replaced channel contexts, including revocation during awaited work, with the Gateway kept active — measured both at the in-process dispatch fence against a real filesystem effect and at the **real delegated system-agent apply owner**, each bound to production by its own negative control. Restoration of the exact predecessor when a staged channel replacement fails (round 23), and compaction of repeated failed generations out of the slot history (round 24, measured 5 of 5 retained → 0 of 5).

Still outstanding:

- **Companion-fix attribution.** The September 8 deployment combined other authority fixes, so it still does not establish which companion changes are required. The differential comparison against #138596 described under *Related Work* has not been run.
- **Unbound is a different mechanism.** An unbound context performs no in-process delegated effect, but because it leaves the in-process path entirely rather than being rejected by the lifetime fence, it is reported separately above rather than folded into the fence result.
- **No booted-gateway probe for the fence rounds.** The Gateway host in rounds 22 and 22b is an in-process object held live for the run, not a booted gateway service, and round 22b's approval engine seam (`resolveOperatorApproval`) is a stub — the *authority chain* around it is production. Every step between channel ingress and the apply fence is production code; the host and that engine seam are not.
- **Merge conflicts, measured.** `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only upstream/main` against the reviewed base reports four conflicted files: `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts`, `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts`, and `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`. Round 24 adds no conflict surface — its only production change is in a file this branch introduced — and the set is unchanged at this head. Resolving them needs a decision about rebasing this branch, which is not taken here.

## Problem and change

prs.title: fix: code examples stall streamed replies with repeated sanitization
prs.body:
Fixes #172663

## What Problem This Solves

Streamed replies containing fenced JSON or quoted tool calls repeatedly sanitize the entire reply on every later delta, delaying delivery and consuming Gateway CPU.

## User Impact

Code examples stay visible while the rest of the answer streams without repeatedly parsing an earlier protected payload marker. Real leaked tool calls remain filtered; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plain-call filter's payload tokens introduced by #172470 latched even inside code. Its existing incremental activation probe now retires tokens classified inside settled block code, sharing the Markdown-owned predicate already used by #171573. Inline code and unprotected tokens retain canonical filtering, and source replacements reset the carried state. No parser or state owner is added; #138204's XML leak filtering is retained.

This removes the persistent activation caused by an earlier code example. As with #171573, newly encountered markers and mutable inline code can still need canonical parsing; this is not a universal linear-time claim for arbitrary Markdown. Production LOC is +32/-14 (net +18), tests +40/-0, docs +0/-0. The small production increase carries the exclusion in the existing probe and shares the XML rule; unrelated behavior was not removed to meet the nonpositive-LOC target.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate under the maintainer policy for this campaign.

- New `bounds sanitizer work after %s in token-sized deltas` cases cover fenced JSON, a fenced tool-call example, and an unterminated fence. They bound total characters passed to the canonical sanitizer and Markdown resolver across four-character deltas, and assert exact final text without timing thresholds.
- `rechecks retired code markers after a source replacement` verifies resets and a real leaked call after protected code. The prefix-equivalence matrix also covers inline code, tilde fences, unterminated fences, and leaks after closed fences.
- CI covers these regressions, existing citation and XML/GLM/invocation leak regressions from #138204, projection siblings, production/test types, and repository lint. Local test wall times and a negative-control result are not claimed.
- Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt pass; `git diff --check` passes. Deslop shared the existing settled-block rule and found no further cleanup needed.
- Isolated Codex autoreview through P2 on `0004f87b35065bb3ca8625acbc98da5749f77d71`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Main `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209` was merged without rebasing; all five reviewed files are byte-identical after the merge.
- Exact-head [CI run 38666569013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666569013) passed on `04000364d6a1f4d23d4f05f7b5fb84cb0f39f15b`: **41 successful jobs, 27 skipped, zero failures**. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` is green, including production/test types and lint. No CI rerun was requested.
- The [plain-tool-call suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666569013/job/116200196379) passed all **23 tests** (4.16 s wrapper-reported wall; 2.57 s Vitest duration). New work-count cases took 15/8/5 ms for fenced JSON, a quoted call, and an unterminated fence; the replacement case took 5 ms. The existing assistant-visible-text suite passed 47 tests, projection suite 13, and XML/GLM/invocation handler suite 52, preserving #138204 coverage.
- GitHub Codex review completed on the exact head without posted findings. ClawSweeper posted only its maintainer opt-in notice; there are no ClawSweeper code findings to address and no automated re-review request was sent.
- Local tests, typechecks, production-only negative controls, live Gateway proof, and Crabbox/Testbox leases were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No live proof is claimed.

prs.title: fix: Cron repair shows a false empty-response error in WebChat
prs.body:
Related: #169614

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WebChat reports an empty-response error when an internal Cron failure-repair turn follows its instruction to reply `NO_REPLY`.

## User Impact

Automation owners can receive a deliberately silent repair outcome without a false failure row in their conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the optional-reply contract for internal `cron_failure_repair` turns before the non-deliverable-channel rule. Private completions and subagent turns still take their existing required-reply path.

## Evidence

- New regression failed on the unmodified source: expected `optional`, received `required`.
- `pnpm test src/agents/command/attempt-execution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 22 passed; 109.45s command wall time (94.59s Vitest duration; new regression 28ms).
- Existing CLI optional-output tests: 2 passed, including `NO_REPLY`; 175.26s command wall time, including worker compilation.
- `pnpm build`: exit 0.
- Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38214068648) passed for commit `a04d1a96a5ce4010b9b24403213be0f2dc2cfeaa`, including tests, type checks, lint, and the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. Dependency and sensitive-change gates also passed.
- Independent static review: no P0–P2 findings. The prescribed autoreview helper could not produce a report: Codex launch failed; Claude was stopped after 10 minutes without a result.

Validation limits: `pnpm check` did not pass in this Windows checkout, with errors in unchanged changelog attribution and SQLite-worker ratchets. The full local test suite was not run. No authenticated Claude service was exercised. The isolated real-Gateway composition below now covers scheduler dispatch, the registered CLI runner, lifecycle settlement and public WebChat history.





## Updated behavior evidence (2026-10-15)

Reviewed head remains `a04d1a96a5ce4010b9b24403213be0f2dc2cfeaa`; no source change or new claim of CI coverage. `pnpm build:runtime` exited 0 in 3m 6s; its stamp records this exact head and `inputsClean: true`.

**Real Gateway boundary proof with a synthetic CLI backend:** launched the supported `pnpm openclaw gateway run` entry point using an isolated state directory, workspace and loopback listener. A local plugin registered a tool-free Node subprocess through the normal CLI-backend API. Only its model decisions were synthetic: ordinary job turns exited 1 with `synthetic temporary upstream error`, while the scheduler's actual repair brief returned exactly `NO_REPLY` with no tool calls. No Gateway, command-policy, scheduler, CLI-runner or history helper was mocked, and no external model service was called.

Public RPC sequence: `chat.send` seeds a dashboard/WebChat conversation; `sessions.messages.subscribe` subscribes to that owner; `cron.add` creates an enabled recurring agentTurn job with explicit owner pointing to the seeded conversation and `failureAlert.after: 2`; two `cron.run` calls wait for actual failed execution; the scheduler independently dispatches the repair; `chat.history` reads the resulting conversation. The proof asserts that both failures are the intended synthetic upstream errors, the repair lifecycle ends successfully, and history has no empty-response failure notice, failed-request notice or assistant NO_REPLY message. The scratch job was removed afterwards.

<details>
<summary>Captured subprocess, Gateway lifecycle and WebChat history</summary>

The following are projections of captured records; ephemeral IDs are consistently replaced with labels, and addresses, local paths and credentials are omitted.

```json
{"time":"2026-10-15T02:16:41.092Z","repair":false,"failedJob":false,"toolCalls":0,"output":"PROOF_SEEDED"}
{"time":"2026-10-15T02:16:43.302Z","repair":false,"failedJob":true,"toolCalls":0,"output":"synthetic temporary upstream error"}
{"time":"2026-10-15T02:16:46.722Z","repair":false,"failedJob":true,"toolCalls":0,"output":"synthetic temporary upstream error"}
{"time":"2026-10-15T02:16:48.613Z","repair":true,"failedJob":false,"toolCalls":0,"output":"NO_REPLY"}
```

Public cron.run completions:

```json
{"attempt":1,"run":{"status":"error","completionStatus":"failed","error":"synthetic temporary upstream error","errorReason":"timeout","provider":"cron-proof-cli","model":"fixture"}}
{"attempt":2,"run":{"status":"error","completionStatus":"failed","error":"synthetic temporary upstream error","errorReason":"timeout","provider":"cron-proof-cli","model":"fixture"}}
```

The real scheduler's input in public history begins:

```text
Automation repair request from the scheduler, not a user message. Do not relay it; follow the steps below.
An automation (id [job]), created in this conversation, failed 2 consecutive runs. No failure alert was sent.
...
1. Transient (provider outage, network, rate limit, or temporary upstream error): change nothing and reply exactly NO_REPLY.
```

Captured terminal event:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-15T02:16:48.832Z","event":"agent","payload":{"runId":"cron-failure-repair:[repair]","stream":"lifecycle","data":{"phase":"end","aborted":false,"executionSettled":true,"terminalDelivery":{"status":"failed","resultCount":0},"terminalReply":{"disposition":"silent"}},"sessionKey":"agent:main:dashboard:[proof]"}}
```

Corresponding chat event: `state: "final"`. The public session projection reports `status: "done"`, `lastRunError: null`, `hasActiveRun: false` and `lastRunId: "cron-failure-repair:[repair]"`.

Public history before: two messages (seed user + assistant `PROOF_SEEDED`). After: three messages (the same two + the scheduler-authored repair brief); **zero new assistant messages and no failure notice**. The proof driver exited **0** after its assertions.

The fixture deliberately has no external delivery channel: Gateway logs therefore contain an unresolved-channel delivery warning and the terminal event above honestly reports failed delivery with zero results. This is not an external-delivery success claim. The repaired turn itself settles successfully and does not produce the empty-response error or WebChat failure row. Authenticated Claude protocol/service behavior and external channel delivery remain unverified.

The prior red helper regression and CLI boundary tests remain the before-fix evidence; this run supplies the missing after-fix real-Gateway composition.

</details>

### Maintainer direction still requested

Please confirm whether scheduler-authored `cron_failure_repair` turns should honor the repair brief's explicit silence instruction. This update supplies runtime evidence; it does not claim maintainer approval. Private completions, subagent work and ordinary WebChat requests retain the required-reply behavior in this PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Open same-root overlays request animation frames continuously even though CSS anchor positioning already follows their triggers. Only anchors in another root need the sampled spatial proxy.

Stop sampling while the active binding is hidden or local, and resume it when a remote binding becomes active, including after disposing a temporary local binding. Positioning, focus, markup, CSS, and the existing lifecycle owner are preserved.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed on the authored change |
| Anchor browser suite, Chromium + WebKit | 32/32 passed; 8.35 s |
| Scoped lint/format + diff check | Passed |
| Independent review | Scoped-clean P0–P2 |
| Paired production builds | Passed at d25a316fc7c / 5ddc92e16cf on the same Mac |
| Strict paired startup check | 350,109 → 349,628 B gzip (−481 B); CSS 45,993 B and one request unchanged; zero violations |
| Current integrated head | 49462d9c61241e9e93148a6c8dbef0f572cf4516; merges official main a6b34a1350bf; the authored two-file change is byte-identical to the tested/reviewed head |
| Final same-runner CI performance | Passed: 349,972 B startup JS gzip; 46,058 B startup CSS in one request. Chat boot 1,689,235 → 1,689,266 B (+31), New Session boot 1,380,047 → 1,380,098 B (+51); request counts unchanged. |
| Final broad proof | `ci:full` run 38665559064 completed with three failed test jobs: four native-consent, four Models and four inherited cron cases; attribution below. |

Production LOC: 276 → 281 (+5). Test LOC: 273 → 304 (+31). The five production lines enforce the existing local/remote lifecycle distinction and restore sampling during binding handoff; no new owner or abstraction.

The added test covers frame requests and cancellation through local → remote → temporary local → remote → hidden. Existing cases cover geometry, focus, vetoes, and closing transitions. This is scheduling-only: rendered markup and CSS are unchanged, so no new visual screenshots are needed.

The paired build numbers above apply to the named historical pair, not the final integrated head. A further head-only build at 3a6da37d855 passed with 349,562 B startup JS gzip and 45,996 B CSS in one request; this is historical, unpaired evidence. Final same-runner CI performance covers the integrated head. No local suite or build was repeated for unrelated main changes.

## Earlier CI attribution

Earlier CI is not claimed green. Its reasoning-history, live-preference, clipboard, workspace-privacy, and Models-loading failures now have official main fixes included in this head. No fixture weakening is included. The original local real-Gateway cron/catalog diagnostics stopped during worker preparation before assertions and provide no behavioral proof.

The four cron CLI-admission failures in run 38658271926 match scheduled-main run 38663143259 (main a10ae12e01bdcb5f4214bad403edf1512bf96561): timeout override clearing; both failure-alert round trips; clone payload policy. Their test names, error text, and owner frames match, before browser interaction. They are inherited evidence only if the same failures remain in the new run.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop interrupted Tailscale Serve and keep local access when Serve is denied
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on 2026.9.33, an interrupted Gateway start could leave the Tailscale Serve process running. And when the tailnet policy denied Serve, the Gateway lost its local access as well.

## User Impact

User impact: stopping or interrupting Gateway startup now stops the Tailscale Serve process it started, including when it runs under sudo. When a tailnet denies Serve, the Gateway keeps working on loopback and reports the denial, instead of failing local access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backports #167514 and then #171509, adapted to 2026.9.33:

- **Startup timer:** 9.33 keeps its manual startup timer. The `stop-failed` and abort handling are added there.
- **Abort race:** 9.33's `racePromiseWithAbortSignal` can't map abort reasons. The hostname lookup still maps failures to null and rethrows the original interruption.
- **Startup deadline:** `routeClaimError(mode, startupDeadlineExpired)` is wired through the worker's failure handler.
- **Dropped test:** a main-only "stopped-daemon ingress" test depends on handling that 9.33 doesn't ship.

No version, dependency, schema, SDK or config changes.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** `tailscale.claim` (43), `server-tailscale` (15), `server-start.tailscale`, `tailscale-route-owner.sudo`, `server-runtime-state.tailscale` (7), `server-tailscale-upgrade` (8), `tailscale-parent-loss.process`, `tailscale-route-owner.worker` (5), `tailscale.discovery` and `tailscale.test` (41). All pass.
  - New tests use fake timers.
  - `tailscale-route-owner.sudo` needs a short `TMPDIR` on macOS because of the Unix socket path length limit.
- **Checks:** `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` pass, along with oxfmt/oxlint, the line-cap ratchet and the export-name collision guard.

prs.title: improve: avoid repeated SQLite admission after handle closure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closing the final SQLite handle discarded the physical store’s admitted facts. Reopening the same store then repeated quarantine, schema, and other admission reads during connection and first-turn work.

## User Impact

OpenClaw reuses admitted facts across handle closure while preserving quarantine refusal and in-process write invalidation. There is no schema migration, public API change, or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission owner now retains facts for the physical store’s process lifetime, until a write receipt or explicit invalidation/retirement. Remove final-close retirement, its native-open rebind loop, and the seal’s artificial retention reference. No second cache or synchronous fallback is introduced.

Fresh quarantine inspection still selects the decision row. It reuses the physical database’s schema-version fact; DDL continues to invalidate that fact.

Accepted edges for removed checks:
- Final-close/worker-close retirement: an idle store retains its admission payloads until explicit retirement or process exit; closing a handle does not imply a store changed.
- Native-open retirement retry and identity recapture: a pathname renamed after native binding leaves that handle on its original physical file; subsequent opens identify the replacement. The native-open identity bracket remains.
- Fresh quarantine schema bypass: external schema changes while the Gateway owns the store are unsupported; in-process DDL invalidates the schema fact, and fresh decision SELECTs remain.

Explicit retirement, quarantine record/clear receipts, and clean-close seal publication checks remain because they protect real stored data or custody. An exiting worker with open handles invalidates the existing write, schema, and fact revisions: committed DDL can otherwise outlive its interrupted receipt publication. A normally closed worker retains the store facts. The final heartbeat carrier member now uses the existing close request/reply instead of forcibly terminating its worker with an open database; native handles settle before worker exit.

## Evidence

Type-aware lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Codex review identified an interrupted-worker DDL case; the existing worker-exit invalidation now covers it. Final Codex review is scoped-clean through P2 (two rounds total).

[Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666298629) passed on `080397cc893`: all nine changed test files, the gateway-owner lease and heartbeat siblings, the 5,000-message worker stress case, all selected type and lint checks, source contracts/export collisions, Madge (zero cycles), T1/dialect ratchets, PostgreSQL conformance, security checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

CI exposed three admission-lifecycle expectations and a readiness fixture that suppressed the worker's close acknowledgement. These were repaired and passed fresh CI; they are not classified as inherited. Knip reports six unused exports/types, matching the exact findings in [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663143259/job/116189131420) at `a10ae12e01bd`; none is introduced by this change.

T1 in the touched area: 0 before → 0 after (CI T1 ratchet passed; repository live calls 223 → 223). No SDK exports changed. [Published-driver × candidate update proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38664697643/job/116209878342) passed on the production-identical `d8f3412cbda`; the later push changes only the readiness test. The update ran once and verified readiness, running version, durable/incognito sessions, and clean service shutdown. Candidate packaging, integrity, and npm installation also passed.

Three alternating base/candidate pairs of the shared SQL workload are running. The first baseline attempt completed all 13 turns and shutdown but failed cron setup because the fixture lacked a stored inference account; that attempt is excluded. The lane copy now saves its synthetic key through `models.authSetApiKey` immediately before cron creation and selects the returned profile. This prerequisite is counted identically on both sides; ordinary turns and SQL observers are unchanged. The shared harness is unmodified. Counts will include connect, first turn, warmed turns, whole workload, requests, MAIN statements, and admission-operation attribution. No latency claim is made on this loaded host.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect statements / requests | pending | pending |
| First-turn statements / requests | pending | pending |
| Warmed statements / requests / MAIN | pending | pending |
| Whole-workload statements / requests | pending | pending |

Production diff: 77 fewer lines; tests: 26 fewer lines; docs: 8 more lines. Superseded retirement code and tests are removed. Related: #172370, #172373.

## Follow-up

P2 from automated review: prune admission reference cells left by exited read-only task workers without applying writer-crash invalidation. The task-host read-only path skips exit tracking, so retaining store records also retains those cells. Deferred under the two-round review limit; no P0/P1 finding remains.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

Yes. Authored with Cursor/Grok assistance. Human: Stan Shih (stantheman0128). Rebase onto current main, review-finding follow-up, and live proof also Cursor.

prs.title: fix(mcp): accept projected names in tool filters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp probe` prints provider-safe tool names such as `docs__read-page`, but per-server `toolFilter` rules previously matched only raw MCP names. Copying an exact name from probe could therefore hide the intended tool, especially when sanitization, App-only tools, utility tools, or reserved names introduced collision suffixes.

## Summary

- accept exact model-facing names printed by `openclaw mcp probe` in per-server include and exclude filters
- keep simple `*` globs scoped to raw MCP names
- keep model-visible raw exact names ahead of projected aliases; App-only raw names do not shadow model-visible aliases
- allocate the complete projected namespace before filtering, including resource and prompt utility tools
- preserve the planned model-facing IDs after filtered or session-denied tools disappear
- keep external/native reserved names safe without reusing a filtered tool's planned alias
- implement matching in the canonical `mcp-tool-filter.ts` owner and name allocation in `agent-bundle-mcp-names.ts`
- document the raw/projected matching contract

Fixes #98193.

## Evidence

The regressions cover:

- exact projected include and exclude matching
- raw-only wildcard behavior
- listed-tool sanitization collisions
- hidden App-only raw-name collisions
- resource/prompt utility aliases
- listed/utility duplicate raw names
- collision suffixes retained after filtering
- session-denied inventory
- external reserved names skipping every pre-filter planned alias
- a real stdio MCP runtime catalog and materialization path

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-tool-filter.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-names.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` (48 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` (94 passed)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all changed TypeScript files (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- `oxfmt --check` on all changed files
- `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed files>`; all completed gates passed through core typecheck, and its final core-test lane was rerun separately after the combined 600-second orchestration window ended
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (PASS)
- independent fail-closed review of projected-name, utility, session-denied, and external-reserved collision matrices

## Duplicate Check

Checked current `origin/main`, issue #98193, this PR, and open PR search for MCP probe/projected-name filter fixes. Current main centralizes raw matching in `mcp-tool-filter.ts` but does not implement the projected-name contract added here.

## Browser / Playwright

Not applicable. This changes MCP runtime filtering, materialization, CLI/config documentation, and TypeScript tests; it does not change browser or Control UI behavior.

prs.title: fix(telegram): cap rich message media at 20
prs.body:
Closes #129004

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram rich sends can silently lose the media and trailing content after the twentieth attachment. The shared splitter previously allowed 50, and direct edits bypassed the splitter.

## User Impact

Exactly 20 media stay in one rich message; 21 are delivered in ordered pages of 20 and 1. An edit replaces one message, so over-limit rich edits use one complete plain projection when it fits 4096 Unicode characters. Larger replacements fail explicitly before the plain edit request, preserving the existing message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing rich-block planner owns the 20-media budget and keeps galleries, nested lists, and trailing text intact. The direct edit owner checks the same budget for both Markdown and supplied native blocks. Its plain fallback counts Unicode code points: emoji must not consume two characters merely because JavaScript uses UTF-16 strings.

This update integrates main `364f1ddf3b6646a016c06fd29ddce3186a39892f`, uses its maintained block measurement and HTTP transport fixtures, and removes the retired mock test files. No new SDK surface or configuration is added.

## Evidence

Candidate: `c7d640a93d1ff80cc7274a8f0eb901e49a38ab64`.

- 168 unique focused HTTP/planner cases covered. The initial run passed 167 and exposed one overly strict test assertion for an optional receipt; after correcting that assertion, both 20/21-media cases passed (63.15 seconds). No production change followed the initial run.
- Syntax/boundary lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, and whitespace checks passed. Full build and repository-wide typechecks were not run locally; hosted CI passed on this commit.
- Independent autoreview identified the Unicode length issue; a direct check against the configured server bot accepted 4096 emoji and rejected 4097 with `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`. The guard was corrected and the existing HTTP boundary regression now includes both cases.
- Exact-head live verification through the configured server bot: **7/7 passed** in 25.29 seconds. Twenty media used one rich send; 21 used two sends preserving all 21. Complete 4001/4096-character edits succeeded, including emoji; 4097-character ASCII and emoji replacements were rejected locally with zero API calls.
- Exact-head [hosted CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36124480972) passed. Previous-head checks are historical evidence only.

The owner selected the Telegram bot and Bot API already configured in the server's OpenClaw as the live test environment. The checks above use the candidate source sender, isolated state, and the owner's private chat. The working Gateway was not restarted. Packaged Gateway startup and the Convex-leased environment were not exercised; screenshots were explicitly waived. Acceptance of the recorded evidence remains a maintainer decision.

Historical proof retains its original identity: `6caa2b268277e205fd069b5da890492ae5fb1730` had real Telegram/recipient readback for 20-media, 21-media, and full edit fallback; `21332384fb81adc6e366ff6159ce214b5505f9df` had 378 focused tests and a full Linux build. These are not claims about the new commit.
