prs.title: fix(ui): show the pending cron action instead of a generic saving label
prs.body:
Closes #147801

## What Problem This Solves

En la página de Automations, pulsar **Run now** o **Remove** y dejar la operación en vuelo hace que el botón de guardar pase a decir **"Saving…"**, aunque no se esté guardando nada. El usuario no puede distinguir "guardando" de "ejecutando" o "borrando".

El defecto es más amplio que el reportado: también ocurre con Pause/Resume pendiente.

## Root cause

`ui/src/pages/cron/view.ts:1096` hace:

```ts
props.busy ? t("cron.form.saving") : t("cron.form.saveChanges")
```

pero `props.busy` es `state.cronBusy`, un **cerrojo de mutación**, no un anuncio de guardado. `withCronBusy` envuelve **cuatro** operaciones distintas —

| call site | operación |
|---|---|
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:744` | `addCronJob` (guardar) |
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:929` | `toggleCronJob` |
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:953` | `runCronJob` |
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:972` | `removeCronJob` |

— y solo **una de cuatro** anuncia un guardado. La identidad de la acción se pierde en `index.ts:440`, que solo pone `cronBusy = true` sin registrar quién lo tomó. `CronState` (`ui/src/lib/cron/types.ts:146`) no tenía ningún campo para ella.

## The fix

`CronState` gana `cronPendingAction: "save" | "run" | "toggle" | "remove" | null`, que se publica al entrar en `withCronBusy` y se anula en su **mismo** `finally`, junto a `cronBusy = false`. Los cuatro call sites pasan su identidad.

Las **etiquetas** dejan de leer el cerrojo:

- submit → `pendingAction === "save"` → "Saving…"
- Run now → `pendingAction === "run"` → "Starting…"

Los doce `?disabled` y `aria-busy` **siguen** usando `busy`: el cerrojo no se toca, y un Run now en vuelo deja el guardado igual de deshabilitado que antes. Una clave i18n nueva.

## Evidence

**Antes del fix** — con las siete fuentes de producción revertidas a `main` y los tests finales en su sitio, los cuatro escenarios de página fallan con el texto exacto del issue:

```
×  → expected '\n                  Saving...\n      …' to contain 'Save changes'
×  → expected '\n                  Saving...\n      …' to contain 'Save changes'
×  → expected '\n                  Saving...\n      …' to contain 'Save changes'
×  → expected undefined to be 'save' // Object.is equality
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  4 failed (4)
```

Esos 14 tests discriminan en total: 4 de página, 1 en `view.editor.test.ts` y 9 en `action-feedback.test.ts` (que afirman la identidad y su anulación en `run`/`toggle`/`remove`).

**Después del fix:** `4/4`, y las suites del área en `29/29`, `15/15`, `203/203` sin regresión.

Lo que fija el comportamiento: con `cron.run` en vuelo el submit dice **"Save changes"** y Run now dice **"Starting…"**, ambos siguen deshabilitados; al resolver *y* al rechazar ambos vuelven a idle y `cronPendingAction` queda `null`; con `cron.remove` pendiente el submit tampoco dice "Saving…"; y con `cron.update` pendiente el submit **sí** sigue diciendo "Saving…" — ese último caso es el que ancla el fix, porque es el único correcto que ya pasaba.

## Two decisions worth a look

1. **Los tests de página van en un fichero nuevo** (`cron-page.pending-action.test.ts`) porque `cron-page.test.ts` ya está en el tope de la regla `max-lines` del repo (1000, `.oxlintrc.json:390`) y añadir el bloque lo subía a 1113. `cron-page.test.ts` queda idéntico a `main`.
2. **"Starting…"** usa `…` (U+2026) mientras su vecina `cron.form.saving` usa `"..."` ASCII. Es deliberado — convención de la app para "arrancando" — pero un revisor puede pedir simetría local.

`toggle` y `remove` pendientes no anuncian nada: el editor y Run now quedan en etiqueta idle, solo deshabilitados. Es lo que pedía el encargo (una clave i18n, no cuatro) y el andamiaje ya está para añadir "Pausing…"/"Removing…" si se quiere.

## Checks not run

`pnpm tsgo:ui` no es ejecutable en un worktree con `node_modules` compartido: el guard hermético de `scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts:131` lo aborta, y al esquivarlo el compilador nativo agota el techo obligatorio de 6 GB incluso con el `include` reducido. Como sustituto se ejecutó **el mismo binario** con un `tsconfig` restringido a los ficheros tocados: el conjunto de errores es **byte-idéntico antes y después** (`diff` de ambos logs vacío), 7 errores preexistentes todos en `src/**` sobre `WriteTextAtomicOptions`, **cero** en los ficheros tocados, también sobre el shard de tests. **El typecheck oficial queda pendiente de CI.**

Nota: `ui/src/lib/cron` tiene 5 fallos **preexistentes** en `main` (falta `quickjs-wasi` en el store compartido, y contaminación de locale entre ficheros del mismo worker). Verificados idénticos antes y después; no los introduce este cambio.

## Process note

prs.title: fix(openai): enable prompt cache keys for Azure
prs.body:
## Summary
- centralize Azure OpenAI chat-completions prompt-cache-key detection in the shared completions compat defaults
- apply that default in the legacy provider builder, boundary-aware OpenAI transport, and embedded-agent extra-params retention eligibility path
- include traditional Azure hosts, Azure AI Foundry project hosts, and regional `.api.cognitive.microsoft.com` Foundry hosts
- preserve Azure long prompt-cache retention (`prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`) when callers request `cacheRetention: "long"`, and preserve explicit `cacheRetention: "none"`
- add regression coverage for Azure prompt-cache key emission, long/disabled retention, extra-params propagation, and both request paths

## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw already gates OpenAI-compatible prompt cache keys behind `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`, but Azure OpenAI chat-completions endpoints were not auto-detected. Azure users therefore needed explicit per-model compat config before stable session prompt-cache keys were forwarded, which can silently reduce prompt-cache hit opportunities for long stable prefixes.

The change treats Azure OpenAI chat-completions endpoints (`azure-openai`, `.openai.azure.com`, `.cognitiveservices.azure.com`, `.services.ai.azure.com`, and `.api.cognitive.microsoft.com`) as prompt-cache-key capable by default. The default now lives in the shared completions compat path used by both request builders and by embedded-agent extra-param cache-retention eligibility; explicit `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey` / `compat.supportsLongCacheRetention` overrides continue to win.

## Evidence
- Searched existing issues/PRs before filing. Found related prompt-cache work (#78747, #82939, #94518, #83709, #69272, #67427), but no open PR specifically enabling Azure OpenAI chat-completions prompt cache keys by default.
- Verified upstream `main` only enabled chat-completions `prompt_cache_key` for `api.openai.com` or explicit `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`; Azure endpoint detection was absent in both relevant request paths and extra-params retention eligibility.
- Added regression tests that confirm Azure OpenAI chat completions forward `prompt_cache_key`, preserve `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"` for long retention, preserve `cacheRetention: "none"`, cover the regional Azure Foundry host, and propagate embedded-agent `cacheRetention` for detected Azure models.
- Live Azure proof, redacted terminal output from `thomais2026v2-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/chat/completions` using `gpt-5.5`, `prompt_cache_key`, and `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`:

prs.title: fix(ui): bridge tool stream state to composer run status indicator
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the agent is actively running tools, the Activity panel correctly shows "Activity: N tools Exec" with a spinner, but the composer area displays no "In progress" indicator and no Stop button — appearing completely idle. Users cannot tell whether the agent is working or has stalled.

Root cause: the composer's in-progress state is driven exclusively by `chatRunId` and `sessionsResult[].hasActiveRun`, while the Activity panel uses an independent agent event stream (`activityEntries[]`). There is no bridge between these two data paths. When `chatRunId` is cleared by a racing `sessions.changed` event (via `reconcileChatRunFromSessionRow()`) while tools are still streaming, the composer goes idle while Activity correctly shows running tools.

Fixes #98540

## Changes

- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.ts`** — Add `hasActiveToolExecution()` and `resolveActiveToolRunId()` helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`** — Re-export the new helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-chat.ts`** — `hasAbortableSessionRun()` checks activity entries as third signal; `handleAbortChat()` falls back to tool stream runId
- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.test.ts`** — 9 unit tests for new helpers

## Evidence

**Test results (9 new + 26 existing pass without regression):**

✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is undefined ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is empty ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are done ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns true when at least one entry is running ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are error ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when activityEntries is undefined ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when no running entries ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the runId of the running entry ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the most recently updated running entry's runId


Existing `app-tool-stream.node.test.ts` (26 tests) pass without regression.

**Screenshot showing the bug:** See #98540 for screenshot evidence.

prs.title: feat: add session stream mode command
prs.body:
Implements the session-scoped streaming control discussed in #74077 (closed automatically for inactivity).

Related: #80989

> AI-assisted with OpenAI Codex; the resulting code and tests were reviewed and validated locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Preview streaming is configured globally per channel, so users cannot switch one active chat between off, partial, block, and progress behavior without editing config. This adds a session-scoped control that preserves channel configuration as the fallback.

## User-Facing Behavior

Authorized Telegram, Discord, and Slack users can run:

```text
/stream status
/stream off
/stream partial
/stream block
/stream progress
/stream default
```

`/streaming` is an alias. Text commands also accept `final` as a compatibility alias for canonical `off`.

The selected mode is persisted only for the current session. `/stream default` removes the override and reports the inherited channel mode. `off` disables previews without suppressing normal final delivery or an inherited block-delivery fallback.

## Implementation

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.streamingMode` state and preserves it across the same lifecycle boundaries as adjacent session preferences.
- Lets supporting channel plugins declare their inherited streaming mode and resolve account config without core assuming a plugin-specific config shape.
- Applies the session override before Telegram, Discord, and Slack account configuration in both preview selection and block arbitration.
- Capability-gates native command registration. ClickClack and other non-participating plugins do not advertise `/stream`; unsupported text invocation returns a clear response and does not persist state.
- Uses conflict-aware session persistence with `touchedFields: ["streamingMode"]` so a concurrent lifecycle change returns the standard retry response instead of acknowledging a lost write.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

This PR intentionally introduces one optional public channel-plugin contract: `plugin.streaming.sessionModeDefault` plus `resolveSessionMode({ account, sessionMode })`.

The contract keeps defaults and account-shape knowledge inside each channel plugin and makes native registration capability-aware. Please confirm whether this is the preferred long-term opt-in boundary for session-scoped streaming controls. The feature should not merge without that API sponsorship.

## Evidence

Exact candidate head: `7b98d15970f59dd3441bf4de782f67880f9c38da`  
Feature base: `d09401295626bebd53aa84492b91e7909e22487f`

- Production-focused matrix on the immediately preceding, production-identical head `9f8a86c87baf7a1528a85f6ac2638e0ec2b5c4d2`: 16 files / 699 assertions passed, covering command selection/persistence, lifecycle carry-forward, capability gating, stream/block resolution, and Telegram/Discord/Slack preview plus final-delivery behavior. A diff-caused duplicate Slack stream-mode mock was reproduced at 205/207 and repaired to 207/207.
- Exact-head boundary repair: the prior hosted `check-additional-boundaries` correctly found that a new standalone Gateway test root raised `gateway-root` from 720 to 721. That regression assertion now lives in the existing `sessions.recover` production-path test; the standalone root is removed. The exact-head recovery file passes 29/29, the repository boundary guard passes at the 720-root cap, and formatting/type-aware Oxlint/`git diff --check` pass.
- Clean merge simulation against live `openclaw/main` `89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea`: passed (tree `23fbae78977fb69774005b763f246b9b21dcdbdb`), with no paths changed on both sides since the feature base.
- Current repair gates: lower-level exact build, 49-file current-format check, direct type-aware Oxlint, `git diff --check`, and docs format/MDX/internal-link/config-example/glossary checks pass. Full wrapper `check:changed` remains delegated to hosted clean-install CI because local shared dependencies were intentionally not reconciled.
- Conflict-marker, coercion/deprecation, boundary, dead-export, dependency-pin, Plugin SDK export-sync, surface-budget, subpath-export, and wildcard-re-export guards pass.
- Fresh independent `gpt-5.6-sol` Max review found no actionable P0-P2 issue.
- A prior clean-install hosted core type shard passes after the test fixture was typed from the public resolver contract; no production behavior changed. A prior compact declaration-tooling failure also passed on rerun and was not diff-caused.
- Hosted exact-head run `34457781315` is terminal with **171 successes, 39 skips, and five failures** including the derivative `openclaw/ci-gate`. The four primary failures are outside this PR's changed paths: the current-main UI max-lines violation, runner-native tsgo `ETXTBSY`, a database-preflight artifact timeout, and a real-heartbeat cron timeout.

Current-head credentialed Telegram proof is `blocked_external`. The official Test Server doctor cannot load the OpenClaw QA broker because this host has no authenticated Convex broker access; no private credentials or local setup were used. A maintainer-run proof still needs to exercise `status`, `off`, `partial`, `progress`, `default`, and normal final delivery on this exact head.
\n## September 23 Exact-Head Refresh\n\nExact candidate: `b7904d5b97acfdb10c2769c621155e80633685fd`  \nFrozen base: `5e5f9c27559776303d962aa37f8c09f676e640d4`  \nMerge tree: `833e0e75c52bf1d4929761c49ddd3c6f870528b1`\n\n- Full focused Telegram, Discord, Slack, command, session, lifecycle, and Gateway matrix passes on this exact head.\n- Canonical pre-PR receipt passes all selected deterministic gates, including types, dead exports, type-aware lint, dependency/boundary guards, cycle checks, and repository ratchets.\n- Fresh independent `gpt-5.6-sol` review found no actionable P0-P2 defect.\n- Proof Lab records official credentialed Telegram Test Server evidence as `blocked_external` on maintainer broker credentials and route authorization; no local unit test is presented as live transport proof.\n- The optional public channel-plugin streaming contract still requires maintainer sponsorship.\n\n## Scope and Compatibility

- No dependency, lockfile, workflow, permission, secret, or generated bundle changes.
- The optional persisted field is backward-compatible: absent or invalid values fall back to channel config/defaults.
- Only Telegram, Discord, and Slack opt in. ClickClack, Mattermost, Microsoft Teams, Matrix, and other channels remain unchanged.
- The narrower tool-progress toggle discussed in #80989 remains out of scope.

prs.title: fix: chat images intermittently fail to load during replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: assistant images intermittently appear broken when reply completion invalidates cached session metadata during an image request.

## User Impact

Images remain readable through ordinary transcript activity. Permission narrowing, session replacement, cloud placement, and retired database owners still refuse access. No configuration or data migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The media route selected a valid durable session row, then relied on an optional actor cache to revalidate it. A transcript update could invalidate that cache between metadata admission and the image response, producing an incorrect HTTP 404.

Reuse the existing retained session reader, consume its current writer-published metadata at the policy check, and release it with the response. The filesystem, requester, physical source, and current permission checks remain in place. No retry, timer, or browser assertion change is involved.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original browser EncodingError on current main: metadata checks returned 200, then an actual IMG request returned 404 with “Media access changed.” Its cached session row was absent while requester authority remained live; refetch returned the expected PNG. A bounded three-run baseline reproduced once.
- The real-store regression passes all three cases: transcript-only activity, permission narrowing, and owner retirement. All 36 existing media-policy and memory-adapter cases pass with every assertion retained.
- The unchanged native real-Gateway image-ordering test passes 5/5 runs, covering live rendering, persisted history, reload, ordering, and duplicate checks. All 40 captured media responses returned 200.
- Production and Gateway-root test typechecks, typed lint, boundary lint, formatting, and independent P2 review pass. PR CI supplies broad proof.

The screenshots use only the isolated synthetic fixture. Before: the orange image is broken after its request is refused. After: both images render in their authored sections.

![Before: an authorized image request is incorrectly refused during reply completion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33b9b1f8-b191-4901-870d-6e52ca006324)

![After: both synthetic images render in their authored sections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2dfe769a-dbca-4b52-90a3-eae520f285a5)


## CI Repair

The first PR run exposed an unbound cleanup callback and a missing isolation explanation on the placement fixture. The repaired head calls cleanup through its policy object and documents why the core test worker isolates the placement broker. The exact core lint configuration, mock-export ratchet, formatting, and 32 focused route/policy cases pass locally. A fresh independent review of this repair is clean. The five native image-ordering passes remain valid; no image policy semantics or e2e assertions changed in the repair.

prs.title: fix(agents): prioritize skill-creator over direct skill_workshop calls for skill creation
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #104104 The model non-deterministically routes between invoking the `skill-creator` skill and calling the `skill_workshop` tool directly when a user requests skill creation. This happens because the system prompt presents two competing, unprioritized directives at the same level: 1. **Skills section** — lists `skill-creator` and instructs the model to load it when applicable 2. **Skill Workshop section** (`skill-workshop-prompt.ts`) — unconditionally directs: "Route durable skill work through `skill_workshop`" When `skill_workshop` is chosen directly, the `skill-creator` workflow (validation rules, structure conventions, edit workflow) is bypassed entirely. ## Why This Change Was Made The Skill Workshop prompt section now includes explicit routing priority: "When the `skill-creator` skill is available, load it first — it owns the creation workflow and will route to `skill_workshop` when ready." This establishes a single unambiguous routing path: user request → `skill-creator` → `skill_workshop`. The change is a one-line edit to `skill-workshop-prompt.ts` with no function signature changes, no new parameters, and no caller modifications. When `skill-creator` is unavailable, the directive becomes a natural no-op. ## User Impact Users creating skills via chat will consistently get `skill-creator`'s structure and validation guidance before the proposal reaches `skill_workshop`, resulting in higher-quality skill proposals. ## Evidence - `pnpm test src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` — 94/94 pass (including "instructs models to use skill_workshop only when the tool is available") - Change: 1 file, 1 line (`src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts:11`) - After the modification, when creating a skill, it can reliably trigger skill-creator first, and then trigger skill workshop.

## What Problem This Solves

Real-Gateway UI shards exhausted the former 20-minute whole-job limit on 16-class runners while test cases were still passing. Main's interim 24/25-minute allowances still leave less headroom than the approved 30-minute budget.

## User Impact

Normal Blacksmith real-Gateway paths get 30 minutes. Hosted/retry paths retain 40 minutes. Runner size, worker count, shard split, individual test deadlines, and other jobs are unchanged; there is no production UI change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Peter approved this on October 14, 2026: “Gateway shard limit: raise it to 30 minutes -> ok”. After #170607 moved this workload from eight visible CPUs / 31 GiB to four CPUs / 15 GiB, successful jobs reached 17–19 minutes (observed maximum 19:04). Applying the reported 1.39× slower-runner factor puts that maximum near 26:30; this is a headroom estimate, not a measured post-change runtime.

The first attempts of [PR #171744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38558653729/attempts/1) and [PR #172245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38585248708/attempts/1) hit the 20-minute real-Gateway limit without a failed assertion. Their later coordinator-authorized attempts passed both shards.

Main subsequently landed interim 24-minute shard-1 and 25-minute shard-2 limits in `82668049aceea3` and #172143. Both main updates were merged into this branch, preserving their other changes. This PR replaces the interim timeout expression with the approved 30-minute normal-path limit and updates the existing route assertions and detailed CI documentation together.

The job command, canonical/prebuilt Vitest configs, runner watchdog, and desktop-proof script have no inner 20-minute aggregate suite deadline. Their separate per-test, no-output, and desktop deadlines stay unchanged.

After GitHub mergeability remained `UNKNOWN`, merged current `main` into the branch without conflicts and pushed `012642df1a6431d52e2cabeb3484fca9e8c8c0b2` to force recalculation. Fresh CI ran for this head; results and the remaining attribution are below.

The refreshed run passed both real-Gateway shards in **17:31** and **16:17**. Attempt 1 failed the separate mocked-Gateway config-safe-write raw-editor case. prs.title: fix(session): defer flushPendingToolResults by one event-loop tick
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Feishu (and any channel) "missing tool result in session history" race (#84134): when an agent calls a tool whose HTTP response is still in-flight at idle, the runner flushed a synthetic error before the real result landed.

The earlier one-tick `setImmediate` defer (prior PR head `db2e0ab`) only let results already queued in that event-loop phase win; a real HTTP result settling on a later turn was still replaced with a synthetic error. ClawSweeper correctly flagged this as a heuristic, not a settlement guarantee (P1: "Replace the one-turn heuristic with a settlement barrier").

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the fixed event-loop delay with a **runner-owned settlement barrier**:

- The tool-result guard already owns pending tool-call tracking (`trackToolCalls` / `delete(id)`). Each `delete(id)` is the synchronous signal that a real result just landed.
- This change promise-ifies that signal: each pending id now carries a deferred that resolves when its real result is appended (`session-tool-result-state.ts`).
- Before flushing synthetics, `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` awaits the guard-owned settlement (`waitForPendingToolResultSettlement`) or a timeout — not a guessed tick count.

A real in-flight HTTP result that settles after the agent reports idle now wins over the synthetic flush. A result that never settles is still flushed once the timeout elapses (fail-safe preserved).

The settlement is skipped when idle itself timed out (agent stuck) so cleanup does not double-wait before the fail-safe flush. The abort path (`timeoutMs <= 0`) still flushes immediately.

This is prevention at the flush boundary; #84419 (transcript repair) remains a complementary after-the-fact mitigation for already-persisted transcripts.

## User Impact

Feishu users who saw "Something went wrong" after the agent used the message tool should now receive the real tool result. The fix applies to all channels — any tool call with a pending HTTP response benefits from the settlement barrier.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` now awaits the guard-owned tool-result write completion before flushing synthetics, so a real in-flight result that settles after idle wins over the synthetic error.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/feishu-message-tool-result-84134-v2` @ commit `fc66e80ac8d`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.subscription-cleanup.test.ts --run
pnpm tsgo:core
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
     ✓ waits for idle so real tool results can land before flush
     ✓ flushes pending tool call after timeout when idle never resolves
     ✓ flushes pending on cleanup timeout instead of leaving orphaned tool calls
     ✓ clears timeout handle when waitForIdle resolves first
     ✓ clamps oversized idle wait timeouts before scheduling
     ✓ immediately flushes pending tool results without waiting when timeoutMs is 0 or less
     ✓ settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn
     ✓ flushes synthetic when a pending result never settles within the timeout

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.subscription-cleanup.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm tsgo:core
tsgo:core exit=0  (core source typecheck clean)
```

**Discriminating proof — the rejected one-tick `setImmediate` heuristic fails this regression**:

To prove the regression actually locks the multi-turn race (not just microtasks in the current turn), the implementation was temporarily reverted to the prior `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` defer and the same suite re-run. The settlement-barrier regression then fails exactly as the rejected heuristic would in production:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts --run
     × settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn 10ms
 FAIL  src/agents/.../waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts > settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn
AssertionError: expected true not to be true // Object.is equality
    253|     expect((messages[1] as { isError?: boolean }).isError).not.toBe(true)
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
```

Under the one-tick defer, the real result lands in the second check phase (nested `setImmediate`) but the defer's flush runs in the first check phase and injects a synthetic error (`isError: true`) before the result arrives. Under the settlement barrier, the guard awaits its own `delete(id)` signal, so the real result wins. The implementation was restored to the settlement barrier afterward (working tree clean).

**Observed result after fix**:

- The "later event-loop turn" regression (nested `setImmediate`) proves a real result landing in the second check phase is NOT overwritten by a synthetic — and the discriminating run above proves the prior one-tick `setImmediate` heuristic fails this exact scenario, which is the behavior gap ClawSweeper flagged.
- The "never settles" regression proves the fail-safe still flushes a synthetic once the timeout elapses, keeping the transcript structurally valid for provider replay.
- 38 guard tests + 6 cleanup caller tests pass — no regression in `flushPendingToolResults`, `guardedAppend`, or the abort/cleanup paths.
- Core source typecheck passes (`tsgo:core` exit 0).

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu DM end-to-end with real CardKit streaming; production agent-runner trace. A live run requires Feishu channel credentials and a running gateway, which are not available in this contributor environment. The settlement barrier is guard-owned and the discriminating proof above exercises the exact flush boundary (real result arriving after idle via a later event-loop turn) that a live Feishu HTTP response would trigger through the same `pendingState.delete(id)` → deferred resolve path.

## Root Cause

`flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` called `flushPendingToolResults()` immediately after `waitForAgentIdleBestEffort` resolved. When a tool call (e.g. Feishu message tool) had an in-flight HTTP response, the agent could report idle before the response callback fired. The immediate flush saw the still-pending tool call and injected a synthetic error; the real result then arrived but the synthetic was already persisted.

A one-tick `setImmediate` defer only drains callbacks already queued in that event-loop phase — a real HTTP result settling on a later turn was still pending and received a synthetic error. The settlement barrier awaits the guard-owned `delete(id)` signal instead, so any valid result that lands within the timeout wins.

## Regression Test Plan

Target: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.guard.waitforidle-before-flush.test.ts`
Added scenarios:

- `settlement barrier awaits a real result that lands in a later event-loop turn` — real result appended in the second check phase (nested `setImmediate`) still wins (no synthetic). A one-tick `setImmediate` defer fails this regression (proven by the discriminating run above), which is the exact behavior gap ClawSweeper flagged.
- `flushes synthetic when a pending result never settles within the timeout` — fail-safe: real result never lands → timeout → synthetic injected.

Existing scenarios preserved (idle wait race, idle timeout, cleanup timeout, timer clamp, abort `timeoutMs <= 0`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Feishu (and all channel) users who previously saw "Something went wrong" after the agent used a tool with a pending HTTP response should now receive the real tool result. Non-abort cleanup adds up to one settlement-timeout wait when results are genuinely in-flight; the abort path is unchanged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: settlement barrier waits for a multi-turn-delayed real result; fail-safe synthetic on never-settling result; all existing guard + cleanup tests unaffected; core typecheck clean.
- Edge cases checked: abort path (`timeoutMs=0`) skips settlement and flushes immediately; idle-timeout path skips settlement (agent stuck) to avoid double-wait; no-pending path returns immediately.
- What you did NOT verify: Live Feishu DM end-to-end with CardKit streaming.

## Best-fix Verdict

- Best fix: Yes — the settlement barrier is the runner-owned completion boundary ClawSweeper asked for. It awaits the guard's own `delete(id)` signal (the exact point a real result lands) rather than a scheduling guess, with a defined timeout/cancellation path.
- Refactor needed: No
- Alternative considered: keeping the one-tick `setImmediate` defer (rejected — fails any result settling after one event-loop phase, which is the bug); adding a guard in `guardedAppend` (unreachable — toolResult branch returns before the flush check); deferring in the Feishu dispatch layer (channel-specific fix that leaves the race for every other channel).

## AI Assistance 🤖 (required for AI-assisted PRs)

AI-assisted: Yes
AI model: GLM-5.2
Human confirmed understanding of code changes: Yes

## Change Type (select all)

- Bug fix
- Refactor required for the fix

## Scope (select all)

- Gateway / orchestration
- Skills / tool execution
- API / contracts — Session tool result guard

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #84134 — Feishu message tool "missing tool result" regression
- Related: #84419 (transcript repair dedup mitigation), #84708 (replay poison recovery)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Highest-risk area: the settlement barrier adds up to one `timeoutMs` wait to non-abort cleanup when results are genuinely in-flight. For the abort path (`timeoutMs=0`) and the idle-timeout path, settlement is skipped, preserving immediate flush behavior.
- Mitigation: the settlement only awaits already-tracked pending ids; a real result resolves its deferred immediately (microsecond-scale), so the timeout is a ceiling, not the common case. `clear()` resolves all deferreds to avoid dangling promises.
- Compatibility impact: None — the `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` signature is unchanged; `waitForPendingToolResultSettlement` is optional and no-op when absent.

prs.title: fix: preserve plugin allowances through session tool checks
prs.body:
Fixes #172604.

## What Problem This Solves

A registered browser tool could pass assembly under `tools.allow: ["group:plugins"]` and then fail when session access checked it again. Tool Search had the same problem because its outer caller also checked the target without registered ownership. Plugin-ID allowances were affected when the plugin ID and tool name differed.

Both the captured caller check and the current session-resource check lost that ownership, so correcting only one left the operation blocked.

## User Impact

Configured plugin-ID and `group:plugins` allowances now work through both checks, directly and through `dispatch_action`. Exact tool, plugin-ID and group denials retain precedence, including current policy changes and narrower caller restrictions. No configuration migration, additional operator scope or plugin SDK option is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The caller captures minimal ownership facts once from its finalized concrete tools. For current resource checks, the router carries the selected method's owner and registry; session authority resolves the required tool against that factory's declared membership. Registration name hints may be narrower than the concrete tools a factory returns, and ambient plugin scope may differ from the selected method registry.

The existing policy evaluator remains authoritative. Current policy is still checked at the operation boundary; ownership metadata is not a cached allowance. Core and other name-only callers retain their behavior.

## Evidence

The base regression fails for direct and Tool Search calls. The corrected registered-plugin fixture crosses real request authorization and passes 17 cases, including factory-produced names, selected/ambient registry mismatch, mixed-case/padded references, exact/plugin/group denials, spoofed ownership, nested restrictions and current denial before effects. Browser I/O and profile storage are isolated in this focused fixture.

The existing `test/plugins/browser-session-authority.gateway.test.ts` scenario also passes with `group:plugins`: a real authenticated Gateway, registered browser plugin, Chromium and controlled HTTP destination admit the writer's requests. Nonmembers and membership revoked during actual context allocation or navigation preparation produce no extra destination requests. This complements the direct/Tool Search authorization proof; no live model or deployment is claimed.

The four focused policy/authority files passed 77 cases in **49.76 seconds**, and eight direct caller/importer files passed in **95.06 seconds**. The real-browser scenario passed in **63.11 seconds**, including worker preparation. Remote formatting, lint, the mock-isolation ratchet and production/test type checks passed. The prior full private-QA build and unaffected Linux importer proof remain applicable. Three Windows-only cases were not run on Linux; no Windows pass is claimed. Hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38665867135) completed in 810 seconds of observed workflow time, totaling 13,179 job-seconds across 50 executed jobs; these totals include the selected baseline suite. Its sole failing test family is `test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts`: nine automation-creation cases reject the fixture's direct inference credentials. The same nine failures reproduced on unmodified CI base `22e08398513c2b506bab8270aa6bc38901d08957` in 106.97 seconds. This patch does not change cron credential binding or its inputs. All other selected jobs passed; 27 unselected rows were skipped. The cron failure is tracked for a separate repair.

<details>
<summary>Existing real-browser run: output and destination assertions</summary>

The successful run used `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_SNAPSHOT_E2E=1` and the existing `test/plugins/browser-session-authority.gateway.test.ts` scenario. Reproduce it with `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_SNAPSHOT_E2E=1 pnpm test test/plugins/browser-session-authority.gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` after the repository's Chromium preparation.

The runner verified source tree `86b338b56684bd4af694d760c2ce9666775d2371`. The run preceded the commit; the published commit has that identical tree:

```text
$ git show -s --format='%H %T' 4abd93746150ac2ee1669c4cf720af49c3722581
4abd93746150ac2ee1669c4cf720af49c3722581 86b338b56684bd4af694d760c2ce9666775d2371

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 63.11s
[stage-3:coverage] {"partial":true,"passed":["node"],"failed":[],"unrun":[],"retry":null}
```

The destination assertions satisfied by that run were:

| Operation | Cumulative destination request paths |
|---|---|
| [Nonmember request rejected](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4abd93746150ac2ee1669c4cf720af49c3722581/test/plugins/browser-session-authority.gateway.test.ts#L186) | `[]` |

prs.title: fix(agents): forward thinking env to paired-node claude runs
prs.body:
Closes #111807

## What Problem This Solves

Con `/think off` y una ejecución **en nodo par** (paired node), el nivel de razonamiento no se respeta: el nodo vuelve a su propia resolución de effort y el usuario ve thinking aunque lo haya desactivado.

El camino local sí funciona. La asimetría está en el salto de entorno.

## Root cause

`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-logging.ts:62` define `NODE_CLAUDE_FORWARD_ENV_KEYS` con solo dos claves:

```ts
export const NODE_CLAUDE_FORWARD_ENV_KEYS = new Set([
  "CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT",
]);
```

`execute.ts:387-389` filtra `preparedBackend.env` por ese set antes de `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` (`execute-node-claude.ts:221`). Como `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` — el único mecanismo real de `off`, emitido en `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts:94` y `cli-backend.ts:279` — no está en la lista, **se descarta entero**: no llega ni como env ni como clearEnv.

Esto es el hueco de nodo par que mantenedores dejaron abierto explícitamente en este issue. La parte titular ya la arregló #125528 (`1b9d3ac57d1`, `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` + `CLAUDE_CLI_CLEAR_ENV`); el PR previo del mismo autor (#111826) se cerró como `superseded` con la nota de que *el hueco de nodo par sigue tracked en #111807*.

## The fix

Dos literales más en la allowlist. `execute.ts:387` y `:397` ya derivan del mismo set, así que no hace falta tocar nada más.

No se toca `resolveClaudeCliEffortArgAction`: su semántica de `off` ya es correcta y está fijada por `cli-shared.test.ts:391-407` y `:409-420` (verificados en verde).

## Evidence

**Antes del fix** — el test nuevo falla de verdad, con la clave descartada entera (`invocation.env` llega `undefined`, no un objeto con la clave vacía):

```
× forwards MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=<redacted len=22>
  → expected undefined to be '0' // Object.is equality
× forwards the fixed-budget pair for a positive thinking level
  → expected undefined to match object { …(2) }
× keeps non-allowlisted backend env off the paired-node request
  → expected undefined to be '0' // Object.is equality
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  3 failed (3)
```

**Después del fix** (verificado también tras rebase sobre `upstream/main` actual):

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

El tercer test acota que la allowlist no se convierta en un volcado del env del backend.

**Regresión en verde:** `vitest.agents-support` (media-guard), `vitest.agents-core` (cli-runner.spawn, 60 tests), `vitest.auto-reply` (agent-runner-execution-cli-admission, 11), `vitest.gateway` (node-claude-skill-runtime), y `vitest.extension-providers` con los tres ficheros de `cli-shared` (57 tests). `oxfmt --check` y `oxlint` limpios en ambos ficheros.

## What this proves, and what it does not

La prueba es de **cableado**, no de efecto: demuestra que `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` sale de `preparedBackend.env`, atraviesa el filtro de `execute.ts:387` y llega a `env` y `clearEnv` de la petición al nodo. No demuestra que Claude Code en el nodo lo obedezca: eso exige un nodo par real con Claude Code 2.1.215.

Dos indirecciones sostienen la conclusión: la clave hermana `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` ya viaja por ese mismo RPC y está en producción, así que el nodo aplica el env; y el efecto de `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` sobre Claude Code está probado en vivo por el autor de #111826 y documentado en `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md:233`.

## Risk worth a reviewer's attention

`execute.ts:397` deriva `nodeRuntimeClearEnv` del mismo set, así que este diff **también** empieza a borrar `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` y `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING` del entorno heredado del proceso remoto en toda ejecución claude-cli con nodo par. Es lo correcto — ambas están en `CLAUDE_CLI_CLEAR_ENV` precisamente para que gane el valor de OpenClaw — y es lo que hace el nodo simétrico al camino local, pero es un efecto más allá del titular del issue.

## Checks not run

`pnpm tsgo:core` no es ejecutable en un worktree con `node_modules` compartido: el guard hermético de `scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts:131` lo aborta (`Declaration input escapes checkout…`), e invocar el compilador nativo saltándose ese guard agota el techo obligatorio de 6 GB incluso con un `tsconfig` de un solo fichero. **El typecheck queda pendiente de CI.** Sustitutos ejecutados: `oxlint` con el tsconfig del repo (0 warnings, 0 errors) y `oxfmt --check` limpio.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every bundled plugin must ship a 512px `assets/icon.png` and a monochrome `assets/activity.svg`. Advisor (#169564) and MCP Events (#165399) landed without `assets/`. FRV only reported Advisor because the test stops at the first missing file. A scan of every tracked `extensions/*/openclaw.plugin.json` on main and on release/2026.10.10 finds these two plugins as the only gaps.

Both are native OpenClaw plugins, so, following #172299 (mcp-relay), they reuse the shared OpenClaw mascot identity byte-for-byte. Their new activity glyphs join the "Agent or task flow" family: a compass for Advisor's course correction, and a trigger bolt for MCP Events starting automations. Each glyph is one stroked path with the same attribute set as the `mcp-relay` and `acpx` glyphs. Both icon source inventories record the new rows.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(facetime): release validation fails after the release version bump
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the FaceTime package manifest test fails on every release branch after `pnpm release:prepare` bumps the version (Plugin Prerelease run 38662499961 for 2026.10.10-beta.1: expected `minHostVersion` `>=2026.10.10-beta.1`, got `>=2026.10.3`).

## User Impact

User impact: none for users; release validation for 2026.10.10-beta.1 and later releases no longer goes red on this test. The shipped manifest does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

#171633 changed the test to require `openclaw.install.minHostVersion === ">=" + package.version`, with the comment "Release preparation bumps the package version and host contract together." That is not what release preparation does. `scripts/sync-plugin-versions.ts` (the release version alignment step of `release:prepare`) moves `version`, the `openclaw` peer range, `compat.pluginApi`, and `build.openclawVersion`, and deliberately preserves `minHostVersion`:

```ts
// minHostVersion is a compatibility floor, not release alignment metadata.
// Keep it stable unless the owning plugin intentionally raises it.
```

That contract dates to 0e3f9657da9 ("fix(plugins): preserve bundled host compatibility floor") and is pinned by `src/scripts/sync-plugin-versions.test.ts` ("preserves workspace openclaw devDependencies and plugin host floors"), which keeps a `minHostVersion` equal to the previous version untouched. Changing the sync tool to bump floors would reverse that decision for every plugin whose floor happens to equal the previous version, so the fix belongs in the FaceTime test.

The test now asserts the declared floor (`>=2026.10.3`) exactly, and still asserts that `compat.pluginApi` and the peer range equal `>=<package version>`. Install (`src/plugins/install-shared.ts`) rejects hosts below the `pluginApi` range, and release prep keeps that range at the release version, so a published FaceTime package still refuses hosts older than its own release.

## Evidence

- Current main (version 2026.10.3): the test passes before and after, because version and floor are currently equal.
- Release tip `c92d7743aa9` (scratch worktree): fails before with the exact FRV diff. With this test change, `pnpm release:prepare -- --version 2026.10.10-beta.1 --write` reports "release version alignment: passed" and leaves no package changes (`sync-plugin-versions.ts --check`: Updated 0, Changelogged 0). The later "version-owned generated metadata" step fails only because the scratch host has no Control UI translation provider (`pnpm ui:i18n:sync`), which is unrelated. Then `pnpm test extensions/facetime/tests/package-manifest.test.ts src/scripts/sync-plugin-versions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes (2 + 16 tests).
- `pnpm test extensions/facetime/tests/package-manifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this branch: 2 passed, about 13s wall time (most of it is the existing `npm pack` test).

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves
A Slack agent serving several private customer channels needs to recall sibling threads without opening every conversation belonging to the agent.

## User Impact
Operators can opt into `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` to allow verified same-agent, same-channel session access while excluding other channels. Defaults and existing visibility modes are unchanged; thread sessions stay separate and recall is on demand, not automatic prompt injection.

This is **not a complete multi-tenant sandbox**: shared memory files, filesystem access, message-plugin history tools, external integrations and already-mixed transcripts need their own boundaries. Missing route facts deny cross-session access. Archived memory transcript hits are conservatively excluded. No production deployment or live Slack test was performed.

## Why This Change Was Made
The existing visibility decision owner already serves history, list, search, send and status. This extends that owner rather than introducing a second memory system or provider-specific policy in core.

- Compare trusted stored provider, explicit account, opaque destination, chat kind and workspace/space. Thread IDs are not part of the channel comparison; arbitrary peer IDs are not split to infer authority.
- Require the same agent; main aliases, spawned ownership, A2A permission and scoped grants cannot widen the new boundary. DM/main callers remain self-only.
- Prepare requester metadata once for list/search and filter candidates before returning metadata or reading snippets. Direct access uses exact owner-qualified descriptions and propagates the described session incarnation into the existing lifecycle fence.
- Apply the same policy to memory transcript hits, reject conflicting transcript aliases, and keep the default sandbox spawned clamp from widening `channel` to `tree`.
- No new storage, migrations, background jobs or model calls. Channel-only overhead is one requester metadata read for inventory/search, or two exact metadata reads for a direct cross-session access; unchanged modes do not incur these reads.

## Evidence
- Focused shared-policy, history, list, search, access and memory suites: **233 tests passed** (initial 6-file run, 4 shards, 46.09 seconds wall with `--maxWorkers=1`). The list regression was subsequently moved into its own small file to satisfy the repository line-cap guard.
- Final targeted recheck: **58 tests passed** across the policy suite and the extracted list regression (16.23 seconds wall). `pnpm check:changed` passed, including core/extension/test typechecks, SDK exports/surface/boundary checks, changed-file lint, config docs, dead exports and import cycles. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent native Codex review: no actionable P1/P2 findings. The repository `autoreview` helper was also invoked, but its separate CLI account could not access its configured review models; it did not produce a review, so the independent native review was used instead.
- Mock-Gateway tests exercise actual session tool entry points; they verify that another channel's history is never read and its metadata/snippets are not returned. SDK cases cover account/workspace/provider/agent mismatches, main/DM, malformed or missing facts, opaque peer IDs, incognito, scoped grants and sandbox clamps. Memory proof includes conflicting aliases and archived-hit denial.
- No live customer or Slack traffic, production config change, broad benchmark, or production deployment. CI timing is not available at submission; no workflow dispatch or rerun requested.


## 2026-10-10 refresh and after-fix proof

- Refreshed with current `main` by a normal merge at exact head `9b99db182f547aba65f3edfef8e9fd2d376ae932`; no force push. The search path now re-authorizes each channel-scoped candidate immediately before `sessions.search` and uses the exact session incarnation fence when available.
- Focused session visibility/search/history/memory suites: **141 tests passed**. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed all changed-file typechecks, SDK/boundary/config checks, lint, dead-code and cycle checks. Full `pnpm build` passed; its advisory Control UI startup gzip budget message was unchanged outside this backend patch.
- Isolated after-fix behavior proof used the built package at this exact head, an actual child Gateway process, canonical SQLite session storage, the model-facing `sessions_search` tool, and synthetic Slack-shaped routes/transcripts. No production Gateway/config, customer data, live Slack, or model call was used.

prs.title: refactor(cron): reduce catch-up and receipt-binding reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron startup and clock-jump catch-up reread the jobs already loaded by the scheduler command, and execution diagnostic binding checks receipt existence before its conflict-safe insert.

## User Impact

Reduces cron database work without changing schedules, exactly-once claims, persisted future retries, or delivery authorization. No schema change, migration, or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The synchronous worker command owns catch-up from load through mutation. Pass its jobs map into catch-up and persist changed runtime rows directly, removing the ID-only load, second row load, and duplicate runtime-authority read. Queue admission retains execution authority. Diagnostic binding writes directly through the existing first-link-wins owner.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- Catch-up row/authority rereads: reuse command-owned facts without an intervening await; unsupported out-of-owner SQLite writes during that command are not detected. Each new command still loads current jobs, so preceding in-process edits remain visible.
- Receipt existence before diagnostic binding: a callback delayed past pruning may leave an orphan diagnostic link. The link confers no execution or delivery authority.

Claim uniqueness, receipt settlement, finalization's merge with current operator edits, and final external-effect authority checks remain intact. The superseded catch-up mutation path is deleted.

## Evidence

Formatting, changed-file oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. [CI on c78d824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660294807) passed all 30 selected jobs: production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge (0 cycles), and the T1/dialect ratchets. The changed scheduler and queue files passed all 30 tests, including in-process catch-up edits, persisted overflow/restart behavior, and diagnostic binding retries; finalization's concurrent-edit/idempotent-settlement regression also passed. Codex autoreview completed clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Knip production/full-tree export scans completed in [the pinned dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38669076876/job/116207922175). Every finding matches the same file and rule in [the latest scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245/job/116200464795), so the campaign inherited-static-failure exception applies; none concerns a changed cron file. The script export scan and both unused-file scans passed with zero entries. The unrelated tail of the diagnostic CI dispatch was cancelled after the requested scan completed. Two local Knip attempts timed out; a queued Testbox was stopped before proof ran. The separately named Gateway startup-recovery E2E remains pending. An earlier local scheduler/queue run was cancelled during worker-cache startup without assertion results; the completed CI run supplies that proof. No SDK surface, update/Doctor, schema, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change.

Cron T1 call sites remain 0 → 0: both changed production owners already execute in workers. CI's whole-repository T1 ratchet reports live calls 223 → 223 and deprecated-only calls 12 → 12. Net production LOC: -14; tests +34; documentation +4.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed all-thread SQL/turn, median [min–max] | pending | pending |
| Warmed requests/turn, median [min–max] | pending | pending |
| Warmed MAIN SQL/turn | pending | pending |
| Complete cron phase SQL / requests | pending | pending |
| Whole workload SQL / requests | pending | pending |

Three alternating baseline/candidate pairs are pending. The shared workload covers scheduled activation, claim, transcript preparation, execution, terminal settlement, retention and history; delivery is configured as `none`, so it does not prove an external send. Source-level savings are two row SELECTs plus the redundant authority read per nonempty catch-up, and one SELECT per successful diagnostic binding; requests are unchanged. Measured per-operation attribution will replace these pending totals. No latency claim on the loaded host.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve literal download output paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browser download capture silently changes output paths containing surrounding whitespace, writing to the wrong file when a trimmed-name neighbor exists.

## User Impact

User impact: browser downloads write to the exact output path supplied by the caller. Whitespace-only paths still fail with an explicit error, and managed (auto-generated) download paths are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The download path was trimmed at every layer of the CLI → route → Playwright capture → writer pipeline, so whitespace never reached the writer. The route's `toStringOrEmpty`/scoped resolution, `downloadViaPlaywright`'s `opts.path?.trim()`, and the `waitfordownload` CLI's `normalizeOptionalString` all stripped surrounding whitespace before the downstream `writeExternalFileWithinRoot` (fs-safe, which does not trim) ever saw it. Each layer now uses the existing non-trimming helpers (`readNonBlankString` / `readStringValue`) to reject blank input while preserving the literal path. The route keeps the GHSA-XWJM-J929-XQ7C temp-downloads-root gate (`resolveWritableOutputPathOrRespond`) for fail-fast traversal/root rejection without triggering the browser click, and hands the literal resolved path to the downstream capture/writer, which re-confines the path without trimming.

## Evidence

Product head: `73c078429ac5`; RED base: `919fcc263201`.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/output-files.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.files-downloads.test.ts
```

| Layer | Scenario | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| writer | `path: " report.pdf "` | writes `report.pdf` | writes ` report.pdf ` |
| Playwright transport | `downloadViaPlaywright({ path: " report.pdf " })` | saves `report.pdf`, neighbor risk | saves ` report.pdf `, neighbor untouched |
| download route | `POST /download { path: " report.pdf " }` | hands `report.pdf` to capture | hands `<root>/ report.pdf ` to capture |
| download route | `POST /download { path: "." }` | 200, triggers browser click | 400 "Invalid path", no click |
| all layers | `path: "   "` | rejects blank | rejects blank |
| route | `path: "../../pwned.pdf"` | 400 "Invalid path" | 400 "Invalid path" |

Validation: 4 files, 73 passed. Pre-fix the two whitespace cases fail (trimmed path received); post-fix they pass. The new root-rejection guard fails pre-fix (request returns 200 and reaches `downloadViaPlaywright`) and passes post-fix (400 before any playwright call). The route's traversal/absolute-path 400 and the absolute-path contract (`path.resolve(DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_DIR, path)`) are unchanged. The download authority fixtures now use a filename confined beneath `DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_DIR` so the real containment check is exercised instead of the prior mocked resolver.

Scope: 8 files; production +30/-19, tests +111/-0. No config, protocol, schema, permission, dependency or upgrade changes.

Not tested: real CLI binary browser downloads (needs a running Gateway + browser session; not feasible in this worktree — the shipped binary does not contain this patch and the dev state DB schema conflicts with the build), Windows trailing-space filenames, or the complete browser extension suite.

## AI Assistance

Per review, retained the scoped temp-downloads-root gate (`resolveWritableOutputPathOrRespond`) for fail-fast traversal/root rejection (GHSA-XWJM-J929-XQ7C), while still handing the literal resolved path to the downstream capture/writer. Switched the download authority fixtures to a filename beneath `DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_DIR` so the real containment check runs.

prs.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

**Problem:** Replies lose their typed current-turn identity before agent runtimes, so quoted text can be flattened into prompt prose and active steering can miss the fact that a message is a reply.

**Why now:** This is the runtime-handoff portion of #88032. The bug still exists on frozen current `main`; the generalized runtime-context projection it extends is already upstream.

**Value:** Embedded and native Codex agents receive bounded reply facts consistently on ordinary, collected, and actively steered turns without trusting quoted human text.

**Fix:** Carry presence booleans as runtime-owned instructions and bounded opaque identifiers as untrusted conversation data, with explicit empty replacement on later non-reply turns.

**Scope:** 25 files, `1,160` additions / `150` deletions. The diff is larger than the review target because one atomic contract spans the shared producer, queue collection, embedded runtime, native Codex adapter, active steering, and generated prompt fixtures.

**Risk:** Session-state and prompt-boundary regressions. The implementation bounds every identifier, keeps quoted content out of the trusted object, and tests positive reply paths, non-reply clearing, collection, escaping, and both steering runtimes.

**Proof:** The earlier 249-test contract matrix passed, and the final runtime-only repair adds a current-head 51/51 focused pass. The exact frozen-base deterministic gate is green on this head.

**Non-goals:** No persisted schema, configuration, provider-specific ingress, or live Telegram transport change.

**Maintainer ask:** Review and merge the typed current-reply runtime contract.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw can receive a real reply but flatten the reply relationship into prompt text before embedded or native Codex runtimes, including while steering an active turn.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can reliably distinguish a current reply from ordinary text while reply identifiers stay bounded and untrusted; later non-reply turns cannot inherit stale reply state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt owner already projects typed runtime context, but reply presence and identifiers were not carried through every queue/runtime boundary. This change extends that accepted owner instead of restoring the older parser architecture. It keeps presence facts runtime-owned, keeps quoted text out of the trusted object, and projects opaque identifiers only as conversation data.

Related: #88032

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`.
- Exact candidate: `9bad767bf1930c0d86cf8a0090e1f07246e74454`.
- The earlier exact-head matrix passed 249/249 across reply preparation, collection, embedded prompt/runtime context, retained native Responses replay, Codex turn parameters, ordinary and message-tool-only steering, and generated prompt snapshots.
- The latest rolling review found that runtime-only attempts could retain the new reply facts while dropping existing inbound quoted-body/sender fragments. This head restores the combined fragment carrier, updates the direct helper assertion, and passes 51/51 focused prompt-builder/full-runner tests including the unchanged inbound-context contract.
- Existing isolated boundary proof covers the unchanged runtime seams: a real pinned Codex app-server against a loopback provider and an ephemeral Gateway/embedded runtime against a loopback provider. Synthetic identifiers only; no production Gateway, configuration, credentials, private conversation data, or public transport send.
- A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh was explicitly authorized and completed in the isolated worktree; it changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The exact deterministic receipt passes every selected lane at head `9bad767bf193`, including prompt snapshots, all type graphs, dead exports, lint, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`; merge tree `0c4634bea2af` is clean.

<details><summary>Contract and scope details</summary>

- Reply-target, quote, and reply-chain presence are runtime-owned booleans.
- Current message/thread/reply/chain identifiers are opaque provider data, bounded individually and as a serialized object.
- Collected turns keep aggregate context while the newest item owns the singular reply anchor.
- Embedded runtime projection uses typed runtime-context fragments.
- Codex projects reply facts as application context and identifiers as untrusted context, including `turn/steer` batches.
- Every later non-reply turn explicitly replaces prior reply values with false/empty state.
- `$` and `@` are neutralized before pre-inference scanners inspect identifier JSON.
- No persisted schema or configuration migration is introduced.

</details>

AI-assisted; reviewed and validated before submission.

prs.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### 1. Production requestFeishuApi auto-retry on real 99991663 (7/7 passed)

Loads the ACTUAL `comment-shared.ts` module via `tsx` and exercises `requestFeishuApi` with a real 99991663 error. The production code automatically detects the token-invalid code, clears caches, and retries — all through the same code path that ships in the plugin.

```
 PRODUCTION requestFeishuApi AUTO-RETRY PROOF — PR #97295
 Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 Time: 2026-07-08T06:01:43Z
 Commit: 83830f71ec

─── 1. Real Feishu API: get token ───
  ✅ GET TOKEN: code=0
  ✅ BOT INFO:  code=0

─── 2. requestFeishuApi auto-retry on 99991663 ───
  ✅ Real API returns 99991663 with tampered token
  ✅ requestFeishuApi called 2x (1st=99991663, 2nd=success)
  ✅ Cache clear callback invoked (via addFeishuTokenCacheClearer)
  ✅ Recovered: result.code=0

─── 3. Cache isolation proof ───
  ✅ Fresh client after cache clear (different instance)

  RESULTS: 7/7 passed

  Production module exercised:
    extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts
      → requestFeishuApi() — auto-retry on 99991663
      → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() — detects 99991663/99991664
      → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer() — registers cache clearers
    extensions/feishu/src/client.ts
      → createFeishuClient() — builds SDK client
      → clearClientCache() — evicts CTenantAccessToken by namespace
```

### 2. Retry path steps (production code flow)

```
send() → 99991663 thrown
  → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() detects 99991663
  → clearFeishuTokenCaches() → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer callbacks
  → clearClientCache() evicts CTenantAccessToken
  → retriedTokenInvalid = true (prevents infinite retry loop)
  → requestFeishuApi() RETRIES → SDK/fetch gets fresh token
  → send succeeds → code=0
```

### 3. Unit tests (113/113 passed)

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
 Tests       113 passed (113)
```

**Cache storage model**: All token caches are in-memory (Map + Lark.Cache), not persisted. No migration needed.

(Proof scripts run locally and deleted — not committed.)

prs.title: fix(cli): report uncompleted channel probes with a failing exit status
prs.body:
Related: #169942

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels status --probe` exits successfully when the requested probe never runs because the Gateway is unavailable or still starting. A watchdog checking the exit code can mistake config-only output for a completed probe.

## User Impact

An explicit probe now exits 1 after preserving its existing plain or JSON diagnostics when it cannot execute. Ordinary status retains its offline config-only success behavior. Successful Gateway responses retain their existing exit policy, including account-level probe results.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command owns both the explicit probe request and the fallback/startup branches, so it can report incomplete work without changing shared readiness, authentication, or rendering behavior. Preserve the runtime exit exception so a pending-startup exit does not get caught as a connection failure.

## Evidence

The real CLI was built normally from this checkout and run with isolated state, configuration, and claimed ports. No third-party channel or model service was used.

| Actual CLI scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stopped Gateway, ordinary status, plain/JSON | 0 | 0 |
| Stopped Gateway, explicit probe, plain/JSON | 0 | 1 |
| Running isolated Gateway, explicit probe, plain/JSON | — | 0 |

Stopped-Gateway JSON retained `gatewayReachable: false` and `configOnly: true`; plain output retained its config-only diagnostic. The running Gateway control did not fall back.

The focused owner suite failed four new assertions before the fix and passed all 13 tests afterward, covering transport/auth failure, pending startup, ordinary fallback, successful RPCs, and exit-exception propagation. The owner suite took 2.06 seconds locally (1.08 seconds in Vitest); hosted CI seconds are unavailable before submission. Targeted formatting and type-aware lint passed. Real CLI proof exercises stopped/running Gateways; pending-startup and unresolved credential cases are covered at the command owner boundary. No external provider credential-health claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Captured real CLI results</summary>

```text
Stopped Gateway, before:
plain ordinary=0 probe=0; JSON ordinary=0 probe=0
Stopped Gateway, after:
plain ordinary=0 probe=1; JSON ordinary=0 probe=1
Running isolated Gateway, after:
plain probe=0 configOnly=false; JSON probe=0 configOnly=false
Focused owner tests: 13 passed
```

</details>


### Review follow-up

Updated the CLI documentation to distinguish ordinary status from explicit probes: unavailable or still-starting Gateways keep ordinary status non-failing, while `--probe` exits nonzero when its checks did not run. This follow-up changes documentation only; the recorded runtime proof and 13 passing command-flow tests cover the unchanged implementation.

prs.title: fix(doctor): classify protected working directories through a scoped provider
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor and update retention checks cannot safely classify a same-account process when Linux denies its working-directory metadata.

## User Impact

Operators with an invocation-scoped, root-owned metadata provider can supply positive working-directory evidence without running OpenClaw as root. Ordinary launches and deployments without that provider retain the existing conservative refusal. This change does not install a provider or change service permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional provider is discovered through a fixed, authenticated runtime socket. Requests contain only numeric process identities and birth values. Returned paths are accepted only after root-owned endpoint checks, bounded client settlement, and matching process generation, credentials, command arguments, and runtime service-marker observations. The census uses one deadline and never starts provider clients for foreign credential tuples.

Successful native working-directory observations, including deleted paths, keep their existing retention-veto semantics. Missing, denied, truncated, drifted, or invalid provider evidence cannot clear a holder.

## Qualification Status

- Source head: `4ba4b4a26068290db114e59ea5e6fc4dfe225171`. Independent scoped review passed. The deleted-path evidence and same-birth command-drift findings have regression coverage.
- Exact-head local proof passed: 206 focused tests across six files, including provider/CWD/census/ownership, wrapper closure, and the existing forced-descendant regression; scoped format, lint, and core types passed.
- The current returned CI rollup has 138 rows with no failed or pending result. The named CI gate, build, security, and dependency checks passed. Skipped checks are not execution proof, and this projection does not establish API exhaustion.
- Landing remains blocked on a successfully completed package/export and published-driver qualification, followed by genuine non-container Linux Update and Doctor execution with positive provider/census evidence, live-holder retention, nonholder collection, and complete provider/client/unit/socket teardown.
- Hosted qualification attempts were interrupted by runner shutdown before package export. The initiator is unknown; this is not evidence of a product defect. The bounded retry cycle is stopped. No production deployment occurred, and this PR is not ready to land or deploy.

prs.title: feat: provision Crabbox runners for release validation and manual CI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation and regular manual Linux CI share busy hosted/Blacksmith queues; selecting a self-hosted label alone does not supply capacity.

## User Impact

Operators can run the SHA-pinned release dispatcher through `pnpm ci:full-release:crabbox --max-runners 10 -- --sha <candidate> --workflow-sha <tooling>` to provision campaign-specific, one-job AWS Crabbox runners for Linux release workers. The same controller now dispatches supported standalone workflows with `--workflow <file.yml> --ref <trusted-branch-or-tag> -- -f key=value`, or supervises an existing manual run with `--run <id>`. This extension adds routing for 32 Linux job definitions across 12 additional workflows. Native Windows/macOS, credentialed publication, Telegram live execution/attestation, and short coordinators retain existing routes. Linux App stays hosted because its Ubuntu 22.04 image is unsupported by Crabbox. Automatic push, pull-request, and schedule routing stays unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The controller uses existing Crabbox broker authentication and GitHub runner registration, observes queued jobs on the exact release transport, preserves baseline CPU/architecture labels, and caps active leases. It stops completed runners, cancels remaining campaign jobs before failure cleanup, and supports retained-request recovery. Named YAML runner anchors replace 91 repeated expressions across the release workflows; shared CI definitions use multiline scalars for readability. Distinct routing policies remain separate. Standalone dispatch records the exact run ID returned by GitHub API 2026-03-10 before checking source identity. Recovery never guesses an uncertain dispatch. Standalone supervision includes that exact root and positively label-identified same-ref/SHA children; cancellation leaves unrelated runs alone. The original release routing flows through 22 workflows; the parent selector is packed into its existing admission envelope to preserve the 25-input limit, and remains part of exact input/evidence identity.

**Required rollout action:** use a GitHub credential authorized to administer repository Actions runners (repository admin or an appropriately authorized GitHub App). The current authenticated account has maintain access; runner listing/registration returns HTTP 403. Preflight rejects that condition before dispatch. This PR is not an end-to-end successful release run.

## Evidence

A second AWS lease proved corrected Docker preparation, non-root daemon access, Compose, and a real hello-world container; that lease was also released. The initial unconditional Ubuntu Docker package installation conflicted with promoted Docker CE and was corrected to preserve existing installations.
- Actual controller CLI recovery with fixture external services passed for a completed parent, including active and released-with-cleanup-debt leases, plus legacy and retained-flag inventory contracts; cleanup was delegated to Crabbox stop without redispatch.
- Scheduler, envelope, and routing tests: 24 passed; focused wrapper wall time 9.69 seconds, individual Vitest tiers 0.52 and 2.18 seconds. Coordinator follow-up routing proof: four passed, wrapper 8.48 seconds.

- Workflow validation (zizmor and workflow-owner checks), targeted controller lint, syntax, formatting, diff whitespace, and documentation links passed.
- Prior independent Codex autoreview: scoped clean at P0/P1 after correcting Docker preparation and terminal/retained lease recovery. Fresh P0/P1 review of the extension found a child-cancellation race; shutdown now cancels newly identified children on later polling passes, verified through the actual CLI with fixture external services.
- Anchor cleanup: all 17 edited workflow documents parse identically to their pre-cleanup versions; four routing tests pass (3.54-second wrapper), workflow validation and diff checks pass.
- Standalone receipt/adoption and expanded routing suites: 17 passed (4.63 seconds Vitest, 15.55 seconds wrapper). Admission suite: seven passed (10.64 seconds wrapper). CI seconds have not been observed. Workflow validation, focused lint, formatting, line-cap checks, and docs links passed.
