- Actual controller CLI boundary proof: terminal recovery stops released cleanup-debt leases, cancels a labeled child, leaves an unrelated active same-SHA run untouched, and never provisions after completion.
- No new full release campaign dispatched; ARM and full job compatibility still need live rollout proof.

## Capacity and Cost

A prior full-validation campaign reached 402 non-skipped jobs outside CI, including 391 x64 Linux jobs and about 30.8 x64 Linux runner-hours. The current CI graph adds roughly 217 jobs, so plan for about 620 jobs across the complete graph; counts vary with inputs, skips, and retries. The controller limits concurrent leases, not total jobs.

Budget scenario: 620 jobs averaging ten minutes is 103.3 runner-hours. At assumed compute rates of $0.75–$1.50/hour, that is roughly $78–$155, plus boot/idle time, storage, network, hosted coordination, and native-platform costs. These are planning assumptions, not an AWS quote or measured Crabbox billing; the profile mix and actual runtimes determine cost. Existing matrix concurrency limits remain intact.

prs.title: fix(storage): defer WAL timers during owned offline maintenance
prs.body:
Related: #166413, #170022

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recurring shared-state WAL maintenance failures behind an offline-maintenance fence held by the same process, and keeps genuine reader/busy diagnostics bounded.

## User Impact

Optional local timer work records an intentional deferred outcome and waits for owner release instead of repeatedly attempting fenced work. Real storage errors remain visible. Database contents, schemas, permissions, retention and durability settings are unchanged; no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing physical owner supplies its release/loss signal. Periodic admission publishes a typed `deferred` observation with reason/PID, joins cancellation, and resumes the existing cadence after release. Explicit checkpoints retain their authority checks; deferral does not clear prior real warnings. Repeated reader/busy warnings are grouped by cause and summarized without dumping reader inventories or claiming an observed reader is the proven lock holder.

**Current-main reassessment: partially fixed upstream, not fully duplicated.** Main already suspends shared-worker autonomous WAL work during maintenance, quietly refuses known foreign offline/schema maintenance, parks idle checkpoint ticks, and settles worker-owned final checkpoints. This refresh preserves those paths. The remaining PR delta is same-process release-driven typed deferral/queued host revalidation and compact grouped diagnostics—not a replacement cross-thread scheduler or an integrated large-store recovery claim.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh merges pinned main `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209` into the published history. Candidate `a4bce38403dde309a71505817da7c4f604d10791` retains first parent `16cf632c8bb374ab548cb57b210199d0b7485202`. prs.title: perf(sessions): retain bounded transcript facts between turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compact durable append receipts stopped transferring full transcript indexes, keeping receipt size independent of transcript length. Warmed turns consequently lost reusable context and anchor facts and repeatedly hydrated them from SQL. This follow-up restores reuse in the Gateway's existing actor replica without putting those indexes back into receipts.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Ordinary warm turns reuse bounded transcript facts while cold and unsupported reads keep the canonical reader. This continues #172557 and preserves the compact-receipt property of #172462.

## Design

Cold bounded hydration seeds a resident context window. Committed append deltas advance it, with at most the configured context byte/event limits plus 512 KiB / 128 events of append slack. The existing recent-event suffix remains capped at 512 KiB / 128 events; positive anchor facts are capped at 128 KiB estimated / 128 entries. Omitted anchors are unknown, never proof of absence. No full-history index is retained by the Gateway.

Identity-preserving prompt metadata rewrites update covered resident rows and preserve immutable anchors. Unsupported rewrites, resets, complex navigation, and reads outside retained coverage fall back to the canonical bounded reader. SQL-side payload limits remain in SQL. Durable input preparation remains because it supplies actual hook, retry, and pending-input custody facts.

## Removed work and accepted edges

- Repeated context and anchor hydration now consumes covered owner facts. After eviction or an unsupported rewrite, the next read may perform one cold hydration.
- The duplicate prepared-message idempotency reread and deep comparison are removed. If another owned append claims that key while hook preparation runs, the canonical committed message wins; the hook may already have run. Final-effect authority and pending-input custody remain checked by their owners.

## Measurement

Pending three alternating base/candidate pairs with the same synthetic workload. Report warmed all-thread statements and logical requests as median [min–max], MAIN counts, touched-operation deltas, and whole-workload totals. No wall-time claims on the loaded host.

| Warmed metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All-thread SQL statements | pending | pending |
| Logical requests | pending | pending |
| MAIN statements | pending | pending |

Pending separate 256-event and 35,500-event receipt/residency probes plus externally sampled Gateway RSS. Receipt size must remain O(appended events); report actual maxima and resident bounds separately from process RSS, which includes workers and SQLite.

## Evidence

All five edited tests pass on corrected head `bd609c6f757`: transcript replica (16), durable reuse (2), memory transcript (8), receipt bounds (3), and input custody (12). They cover cold seeding, append reuse, metadata rewrite reuse, bounded pre-input context, eviction fallback, canonical idempotent retry, and compact receipts. Changed-file formatting, basic lint, and diff checks passed. Codex autoreview completed in two rounds: production clean through P2; numeric type correction and documentation clean through P1. A later required timestamp was added to the synthetic message fixture. Corrected-head typed lint, source contracts, Madge, production types, aggregate and all five core test-type shards, build, and T1/dialect ratchets pass in [PR CI 38668303119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38668303119). The exact-head [Knip scan](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38668321994/job/116205691368) reports the same 23 rule/file/symbol tuples as [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245/job/116200464795), with zero candidate-only or touched-file findings. Both unused-file scans and script exports pass with zero findings. Knip is an inherited-static exception, not a green scan.

The five cron session-lifecycle failures match [main job 116189131871](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663143259/job/116189131871): the same provenance/continuity/fallback tests fail because their automation lacks a recorded inference account. The failing test and rejection sources are unchanged. The broader dependency-scan workflow also encountered four UI consent-modal timeouts matching [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245/job/116200464190); the UI tree is unchanged. These failures are reported to the main-failure owner.

Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception and head-pinned REST squash fallback after the native workflow rejected this lane’s external-root layout. Per campaign policy, measurements may finish after merge; no performance result is claimed until the runs complete.

No schema, retention, permission, public SDK, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change. No update cell applies. Area T1: **0 → 0**; whole-repository ratchet: 223 → 223 live calls and 12 → 12 deprecated compatibility calls. Changed-file dialect groups: 0 → 0. Current diff: production +278/−55 lines; tests +370/−65 lines; documentation +22/−11 lines. The added production code maintains bounded resident windows; it adds no receipt payload fields.

prs.body:
Fixes #157925

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Skill Workshop groups a proposal from the previous local calendar day as "earlier" instead of "yesterday" when the intervening day spans 23 or 25 hours (DST transitions).

## User Impact

User impact: proposals submitted yesterday stay under the "Yesterday" group in Skill Workshop across spring-forward and fall-back transitions, instead of sinking into "Earlier" where they are easier to overlook. No behavior change on normal 24-hour days.

## Why This Change Was Made

`recencyGroup` in `ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/proposal-records.ts` compared day starts with a fixed `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` duration. The fix compares local calendar-day keys instead, deriving the previous day via calendar subtraction anchored at local noon — noon is never a skipped hour, so zones that skip local midnight entirely (e.g. America/Santiago) stay exact, which a plain `setDate(-1)` from the day start does not.

## Evidence

- New regression test `ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/proposal-records.test.ts` (5 tests): spring-forward 23h day, fall-back 25h day (both America/New_York), skipped-midnight day (America/Santiago), plus same-day/older and month-boundary cases. The host timezone is simulated with a `Date` shim driven by `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, since worker-thread runners ignore `process.env.TZ`.
- Red on the original code: the same test file fails 3/5 against the pre-fix implementation (both New York cases fail exactly as the issue's hardware probe shows).
- Green on the fix: `pnpm vitest run src/pages/skill-workshop/proposal-records.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 5 passed (~8s duration; test time itself ~30ms, rest is vitest startup/transform). Related suites `ui/src/lib/skill-workshop/index.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/proposals.test.ts` also pass (27 tests total across the three files).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.ui.json --noEmit` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on both files.

Posted by Kevin's agent on his behalf — AI-assisted (Muse, Meta's Muse Spark).

prs.title: fix(google): keep runtime context from replacing the user request
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini sometimes answers OpenClaw's turn-scoped runtime context instead of the user's request. Each agent turn appends a runtime-context carrier (current date/time zone plus capability snapshots) after the user prompt. OpenAI Responses projects it as a developer item and Anthropic as a native system block, but Gemini has no mid-conversation developer or system role, so the Google projection sent it as a bare trailing user turn, and the model treated it as the thing to reply to.

Found by the gateway live suite: `google/gemini-2.5-flash` failed the exec+read probe 2/2 on main with replies such as:

```text
I have noted the current date as 2026-10-14 and the time zone as America/Los_Angeles.
```

In a real session that is a user asking for something and getting a date acknowledgement back.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Google projection (`packages/ai/src/providers/google-messages.ts`, used by both the managed Google plugin transport and the SDK path) now wraps runtime-context carriers in fixed, context-only framing parts while keeping them as their own content entry. Keeping the carrier separate (instead of merging it into the user message) means turn-scoped expiry never rewrites user bytes, and the fixed framing keeps retained replay deterministic, so earlier turns stay a stable cached prefix. Only messages with the trusted runtime-context marker are framed; user-authored lookalike text is untouched. `docs/concepts/context.md` documents the Google exception.

## User Impact

Gemini agent turns answer the user's request instead of acknowledging the injected date/time context. Other providers are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Converter regressions in `google-messages.test.ts` cover managed and SDK replay, canonical and legacy markers, transient expiry, retained-prefix byte stability, and user-authored lookalikes; they fail before the fix.
- Live gateway suite with a real Gemini key: main `gemini-2.5-flash` failed 2/2 (runtime-context acknowledgement); this branch passes 3/3 (183/183 each). `gemini-2.5-pro` and `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` also pass on this branch.
- Autoreview (P2 scope): clean.

Follow-ups noted, not changed here: the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions user-role fallback (providers without developer role) and Google Interactions use different carriers; no live failure observed for them in this sweep.

prs.title: fix(android): prepare focused proof before running Gradle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes focused Android proof stopping before tests when a fresh Testbox lacks the pinned Java/SDK or native generation dependencies.

## User Impact

Developers get one selectable focused Android preparation/run operation and a clear prerequisite failure that does not count as executed tests. Ordinary Gradle commands and installed OpenClaw update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android entry uses the existing focused Testbox admission pool, runner, deadline, and source-trust interface. Its concrete `check` job mechanically follows the maintained focused transport rather than assuming the allocator resolves reusable jobs. It omits unrelated Go/provider-credential hydration; the existing shell preparation and Android toolchain actions still own all provisioning and unchanged pins.

Android CI consumes the same frozen native-generation dependency operation instead of duplicating its install step. The Gradle wrapper discovers the action-owned SDK and offers opt-in `--proof` prerequisite checks; actual test execution/results still come from Gradle task reports. The lease freshness owner tracks the transitive Android preparation action so changed pins cannot reuse stale preparation.

## Evidence

- Real empty-worktree proof entry reported missing Java/SDK/generation dependencies together, exited nonzero, and explicitly reported no Gradle/tests executed. This host has no Java/Android SDK.
- New prerequisite/SDK-discovery regressions fail on the original wrapper; the transitive preparation-invalidation regression fails on the original lease owner.
- Gradle wrapper: 12 tests pass, final wrapper wall time 3.73s (384ms tests).
- Testbox admission: 46 tests pass, wrapper wall time 4.91s; includes concrete Android profile admission, expiry, and transport equivalence.
- Lease freshness: 23 tests pass, wrapper wall time 10.86s (6.85s tests).
- Focused main-ref transport: 8 selected cases pass, wrapper wall time 47.49s; unchanged suite-level subprocess preparation accounts for most runtime. The two new profile cases take about 1.1s each. The rest of that file is left to PR CI.
- Three existing Android workflow guards pass (6.73s wrapper).
- Targeted script/test typecheck, lint, format, workflow validation, docs MDX, and diff sanity pass. Workflow validation used the already installed Python3.14 through a task-only PATH shim because system Python3.9 does not meet the pinned pre-commit floor.
- Original candidate: independent P0–P2 review passed. Its exact-head CI run 38660510715 passed all six executed Android lanes (Play, third-party, Wear, ktlint, and both native-access emulator configurations), but failed Docker seed and the aggregate gate.
- Docker attribution: run 38664095375 on b3442f7a061d passed all six Android lanes and ordinary checks; its sole originating failure was cron-mcp-cleanup at cron.add, rejecting an inline-only credential. Main account-ownership change d25a316fc7c (#172590) introduced the stored-account requirement without updating this existing fixture. The classifier called it new because no comparable main scope/signature was available, not because the Android patch changed cron. This branch now includes the minimal independently reviewed fixture repair from [#172709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172709), without merging unrelated main changes.
- ClawSweeper P2 follow-up: explicitly set OPENCLAW_ANDROID_GRADLE_ALLOW_LINUX_ARM=1 only in the prerequisite regression's child environment. This forces the intended diagnostic branch on Linux ARM; the deliberately invalid JAVA_HOME still prevents Gradle from starting. Production behavior is unchanged.
- Follow-up proof: real-wrapper Linux ARM branch replay (platform/architecture simulated on macOS) confirms the original environment exits at the ARM guard and the fixed environment reaches the prerequisite stderr. Native pnpm test test/scripts/run-android-gradle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 passes all 12 cases, 3.65s wrapper / 374ms tests. Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, and git diff --check pass. No real Linux ARM host proof is claimed.
- Fresh follow-up AutoReview: scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- Removed one implementation-coupled whole-job equality assertion. Independent Android admission, shared pool, expiry, runner, idle lifetime, and cleanup contracts remain covered. `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-testbox-budget.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 45 tests pass, 6.17s wrapper / 2.74s Vitest. Targeted lint, format, and diff sanity pass. Independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.
- Fixture repair boundary proof: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron.inference-binding.test.ts test/scripts/cron-mcp-cleanup-docker-client.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21 existing tests pass, 417.19s wrapper (372.49s Gateway suite including cold worker preparation; 3.89s Docker-client suite). Script types/lint/format and independent P0–P2 review pass. No new behavioral tests added.
- Exact head c784bb017f4ec208c7e3a50dcaa2402976e85e1c: [CI run 38667577780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38667577780) passed all six executed Android lanes and the repaired Docker seed tier. CI seconds: Play 701, third-party 533, Wear 487, ktlint 482, native 4-KiB 617, native 16-KiB 523; Docker seed tier 516. The live aggregate/security gates are green with no pending or failed checks, and GitHub reports CLEAN/MERGEABLE. Android screenshots/release smoke were outside the selected CI scope and skipped. Full packaged Docker cleanup success is exact-head CI evidence, not a claim from local owner tests.

**Acceptance gap:** no freshly hydrated Testbox reached a selected real Gradle task in this task. Candidate workflows cannot be allocated through the maintained main-only trust path before landing, and no paid allocation or guard bypass was authorized. Automatic PR Android CI can establish candidate shared preparation/Gradle proof, but is not fresh Testbox rollout proof. No merge, release, deploy, or live Gateway operation was performed.

prs.title: fix: keep the Gateway responsive during reply-tagged streams (2026.9.33 backport of #166782)
prs.body:
Backport of #166782 (main merge `3a2160c77f40`) to `extended-stable/2026.9.33`. Fixes #166781 on this line.

## Problem

Streamed replies that contain a reply directive such as `[[reply_to_current]]` re-parsed the whole Markdown document on every delta. On long replies this is quadratic and blocks the Gateway event loop, which delays delivery and health responses by many seconds.

## Solution

Cherry-pick with `-x`. `resolveStreamingReply` in `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.stream.ts` is identical to main's before the fix, so that part applied cleanly. When the previous directive has a settled visible suffix and the append adds no new `[[` marker, reference definition, or `MEDIA:` line (and no code opener precedes the marker), it reuses the previous cleaned text plus the append delta. Anything uncertain still takes the full parse. The block chunker's `plainAppend` check now also accepts that proven append.

Difference from main: on 2026.9.33 the `plainAppend` block in `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.update.ts` sits inside the `!isPhasePendingAnthropicText && !isPhasePendingCompletionsText` guard, which caused the conflict. I applied the same widened condition inside that guard. Behavior is otherwise unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression test `streams a long reply-tagged answer without a quadratic slowdown` (`embedded-agent-subscribe.directive-delivery.test.ts`): fails on unmodified 2026.9.33 (`expected 10286 to be less than 1000`) and passes with the fix (5 ms).
- CPU check: an 8,000-character `[[reply_to_current]]` reply streamed in 4-character deltas (2,000 deltas) through `createSubscribedSessionHarness`/`subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` took 156,911 ms before the fix and 249 ms after. This was a throwaway local test that was not committed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe`: all 3 shards passed.
- `pnpm tsgo` (core) passed. `oxfmt` is clean on the touched files. `pnpm lint:core` reports no findings in the touched files. Its only failures are 5 `max-lines` errors in untouched files that were already on this branch.
- Test cost: the new test runs in about 5 ms.

## What Problem This Solves

Gemini counts thinking tokens inside `maxOutputTokens`. OpenClaw sent the caller's `maxTokens` straight through as `maxOutputTokens` while separately adding a thinking budget, so on Gemini 2.5 models a capped request could spend the whole allowance on hidden thinking and return an empty answer with `finishReason: MAX_TOKENS`. Gemini 2.5 Pro was hit hardest: it cannot disable thinking, so even thinking-off requests thought dynamically inside a tiny cap.

Found by the direct live model suite: `google/gemini-2.5-pro` failed 3/3 on main (and on an older main) with empty or truncated prompt, file-read, and image probe answers.

Direct probes against the Gemini API (`gemini-2.5-pro`, prompt "Reply with the word ok."):

| generationConfig | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `maxOutputTokens` 64 + `thinkingBudget` 2048 (sent today for thinking low) | MAX_TOKENS, empty text |
| `maxOutputTokens` 64, no thinking config (sent today for thinking off) | MAX_TOKENS, empty text |
| `maxOutputTokens` 64+2048 + `thinkingBudget` 2048 | STOP, "ok" |
| `maxOutputTokens` 64+128 + `thinkingBudget` 128 | STOP, "ok" |

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared Gemini/Vertex wire policy (`buildGoogleGenerationConfig` in `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts`) now serves both the managed Google plugin transport and the SDK path; the plugin's duplicate thinking-config logic is deleted. When a numeric thinking budget is sent, the caller's `maxTokens` stays the visible-answer allowance and the budget is added on top via the existing `adjustMaxTokensForThinking` (clamped to the model output limit), matching the Anthropic and Bedrock paths. Gemini 2.5 Pro with thinking off and an explicit cap reserves its minimum 128-token budget. Thinking-level, automatic, and Interactions requests keep the caller cap unchanged, since those models pass live with small caps and dropping caps would change cost for bounded callers. Omitted caps stay omitted.

The Google plugin reaches the shared policy through two new exports on the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-transport-runtime` entrypoint (documented in the runtime hooks guide).

## User Impact

Capped Gemini 2.5 requests (simple completions, tools with output budgets, short probes) return answers instead of silent empty replies. Uncapped agent turns are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Transport-boundary tests assert serialized `generationConfig` for 2.5 Pro low + 64, 2.5 Pro off + 64, 2.5 Flash off (budget 0, cap unchanged), omitted cap, model-limit clamping, and level models keeping the caller cap; 285 tests across six files pass, plus SDK export/surface checks.
- Live on this branch with a real Gemini key: direct suite passes all 12 Google catalog models including `gemini-2.5-pro`. `gemini-4-argon` hit one transient `{}` provider error under concurrency and passes alone on both branch and main.
- Autoreview (P2 scope): clean.

Separate pre-existing issue found during proof, not changed here: `gemini-2.5-flash` sometimes answers the trailing turn-scoped runtime context instead of the user request in the gateway exec+read probe (reproduces on main); tracked as a follow-up fix.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep the Models page stable while it loads
prs.body:
## Problem

Opening Models (`/settings/model-providers`) showed skeleton rows that kept reappearing, and the page height kept changing. After a provider sign-in finished, the whole page reloaded: skeletons again, plus usage and cost requests restarted.

## Solution

- One initial loading boundary for the Models body. Loaded rows never return to skeletons.
- `loaderPending` changes no longer reapply stale route data that cleared loaded content.
- Background core refreshes no longer cancel and restart the independent usage and cost requests.
- After a login finishes, only the connected provider's credentials refresh (`refresh(providerId)`). Usage, cost, catalog and other cards stay as they are.
- The readiness summary and status regions reserve their space, and the settings shell reserves its header and sidebar-footer space before load.
- While a provider's models are being checked, a small animated status is shown instead of text that toggles on and off.

## Evidence

Measured in a real browser against a real Gateway built from this branch:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Initial CLS, first 8 s | 0.0724 | 0.0041 |
| Settings shell CLS on direct load | 0.0472 | 0 |
| Page RPCs on open | 10 | 8 |
| Page RPCs during a 40 s login | 17 | 4 |
| Usage / cost RPCs during login | 5 / 3 | 0 / 0 |
| Skeleton reappearance after load | yes | 0 |
| Provider rows kept after login | — | 4/4 |

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d54d1bd9-ecd4-45b7-8224-157005438a7a)
![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/924d89fe-b5a3-4ac8-8f91-336783985c78)

Tests: the Models page controller, view and login suites (100 tests), including "after a successful login only provider X refreshes; existing rows do not return to loading" and the settings shell layout traits.

### Review follow-up (`81c614724b`)

- When a login finishes, one shared catalog reconcile runs (`models.authStatus` once, then `models.list` once). Invalidations that arrived during the login are merged into that read, so newly available models appear without a manual Refresh. Usage and cost requests are not restarted.
- If the targeted status refresh fails after the credentials were saved, the existing rows stay and the page shows "Sign-in saved, but refreshing status failed. Retry", with a retry for that provider only.
- Fixed the test-type errors (TS2698 / TS18046) with typed fixtures.

Real Gateway, real Muse Code sign-in:
```
before: default Model picker disabled; no usable chat model
after: default Model picker enabled; Meta row shows 4 models
existing provider rows retained: 1/1 (same DOM node)
skeleton reappearances during login: 0
login completion models.authStatus requests: 1
login completion models.list requests: 1
usage.status / sessions.usage requests during login: 0 / 0
active model unchanged
```

The WebKit `session-hovercard-automations.browser.test.tsx` failure in the earlier run does not reproduce: same macOS runner, origin/main `f8e52977e06` PASS 3/3 and this branch PASS 3/3. This PR does not touch that test or its owners.

### Review follow-up 2 (`92fcef963f6`)

- **Deferred invalidations are applied when the picker closes.** Credential invalidations that arrive while Connect provider is open are kept. Closing, cancelling or completing the login then reconciles credentials, without restarting usage or cost.
- **Refresh by credential owner, not display brand.** A selected choice carries `capability.provider`, so a brand like `example` refreshes its `example-owner` credentials. The existing alias fixture covers this.
- **i18n / lint.** The source copy scanners now classify `.test-support.ts(x)` as test files. The raw-copy baseline was regenerated through the documented flow.

**Linux WebKit `session-hovercard-automations.browser.test.tsx`:** not caused by this PR. The same failure (line 86: expected `<summary>`, got the automation `<a>`) appears on unrelated PRs: [#171301](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38652781026/job/116155820482) (before this PR's failure), [#171625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38654938998/job/116162907110), [#172543](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38656531959/job/116168108835). The test mounts the hovercard directly and does not load the Settings layout this PR changes.

## Update behavior

UI only. No config or protocol change.

prs.title: feat(agents): remember native runtime consent per agent
prs.body:
## Problem

Every new chat that used a host-native runtime such as Muse Code asked again: "Use Muse Code's native permissions?" The owner wants to approve this once and not see it again.

## Solution

- New agent-scoped config `agents.entries.<agentId>.nativeRuntimeConsent: string[]` (harness IDs). Helpers live in `src/config/native-runtime-consent.ts`.
- Core evaluates the list at every turn (`assertAgentHarnessExecutionEnvironment`). The usual gates still apply: current session identity, Full Access, sandbox off, no tool allowlist, no `disableTools`, no swarm collector. Required sandbox or workspace-only restrictions still refuse. Remembered consent is never copied onto the session, so removing a harness from the list revokes it on the next turn.
- When an admin selects a remembered harness (model selection or `sessions.create`), the session is raised to Full Access with sandbox off. Only admins: non-admin callers keep today's refusal.
- In chat, a remembered harness recovers silently. Other harnesses still get the existing two-choice prompt.
- Revoke from Settings → config: "Remembered native runtime permissions".
- Schema, help/labels, docs (`docs/gateway/config-agents/entries-and-multi-agent.md`) and the generated config baseline are updated. The key is new and optional, so no migration.

## Evidence

Live run on an isolated Gateway (real `muse` 1.3.0, real Meta sign-in):
- With `muse` remembered for `main`, a second new chat with Muse Spark 1.3 replied with no permissions prompt (screenshot).
- After removing `muse` from the list in Settings, the next new chat showed the prompt again. `chat.send` over RPC to an unconsented session returned `INVALID_REQUEST`, and `chat.history` stayed empty.

![second chat, no prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c5bb9fb-f6b8-49ed-9508-55ac998b5670)

Tests: `execution-environment.worker.test.ts` (remembered consent admits; removal refuses with no session patch; forbidden states refuse), `sessions-patch-native-recovery.test.ts`, `sessions-create.native-consent.test.ts` (admin, non-admin, and admin without a profile-bound authority), `chat-model-restriction-recovery.test.ts`.

Note: the `check:max-lines-ratchet` env-name budget reports 455 > 454 on this branch. This branch adds no `OPENCLAW_*` names (added and removed sets are empty), so the overage comes from main.

### Review follow-up (`79e67a17ffa`, rebased on main)

- **Implicit promotion uses the permission owners.** A model-only `sessions.patch` or a `sessions.create` that promotes to Full/sandbox-off goes through the same sandbox validator and permission-change preparation/acknowledgement as an explicit `permissionMode` patch, so an active run refuses it the same way.
- **Revocation before native I/O.** Right before native `runAttempt`, core rechecks admission against the live config (`readRuntimeConfig()`), not the prepared snapshot.
- **Provenance (b46c38cfa732).** That commit set up runtime-selection preparation inside the existing session mutation lane, keeping worker-placement validation, commit-time authority checks and the post-commit queued-selection refresh. This change keeps those owners and sends implicit permission promotions through the existing containment and permission lifecycle, instead of treating them as plain model-field assignments.

Live proof: isolated Gateway on this head, real `muse` 1.3.0, `tools.profile=full`, `tools.deny=["browser"]`. `main` remembers `muse`; `other` does not. With no OpenClaw restriction, Muse may run without consent by design; consent is only required when OpenClaw has a restriction Muse cannot enforce.

1. Non-admin caller is refused:
```text
connect granted: role=operator scopes=[operator.read, operator.write]
sessions.create(model=meta/muse-spark-1.3): agentRuntimeOverride=muse; permissionMode/sandboxMode unset (no promotion)
chat.send -> INVALID_REQUEST code=AGENT_RUNTIME_RESTRICTED reason=tool-policy
  "Muse Code uses its own tools and cannot enforce this chat's OpenClaw tool restrictions."
sessions.patch(model=meta/muse-spark-1.3) -> same restriction; chat.send -> same restriction
chat.history: messages=[] ; native turn/start count unchanged (9)
```
2. An agent without the consent entry is refused:
```text
connect granted operator.admin/read/write; agent:other:<id>
sessions.create(model=meta/muse-spark-1.3): no permission promotion
chat.send -> INVALID_REQUEST code=AGENT_RUNTIME_RESTRICTED reason=tool-policy recovery.action=use-native-permissions
chat.history: messages=[] ; native turn/start count unchanged (9)
```
3. Revocation stops already-queued work:
```text
sessions.create: permissionMode=full sandboxMode=off
00:22:01.543Z first native dispatch: turn/start count 8 -> 9
00:22:01.565Z second chat.send accepted; queueDepth=2 sessionState=processing
00:22:02.190Z config.patch nativeRuntimeConsent=[]
00:22:40.343Z first turn completed
00:22:40.427Z queued drain refused: "Muse Code cannot run with this chat's tool restrictions."
00:23:12.193Z native turn/start count still 9 (no second Muse turn)
```
4. Upgrade cell: state written by the previous main build `962375d5ee` loads on this head; `config validate` passes; config SHA-256 is unchanged before and after (`47d3347e…e301`).

## Update behavior

The key is additive and optional. Existing configs load unchanged; with no key, behavior matches today's per-chat prompt.

Production LOC: **487 → 476 (−11)** in `logbook-view.tsx`. The existing UI test gains five lines of net coverage for button identity and focus across a real controller refresh; it retains its capture-toggle assertions.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage chart decoration still carries temporary object lists and redundant SVG fragment wrappers from the renderer migration.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Chart geometry, labels, element order, classes, and range interactions retain their existing contracts.

Render the two fixed time-series axes directly with reactive SVG attributes, avoiding fresh axis object lists on model updates. Remove single-element SVG fragments and their surrounding whitespace from time-series grip lines and heatmap labels. prs.title: fix(ui): isolate media test cleanup and await geometry events
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Unrelated PRs #171660 and #172044 intermittently fail media fetch-count assertions because earlier fixtures can still issue requests through a later test’s global fetch mock.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dispose Lit fixtures and their nested Solid roots before restoring globals. A failed image otherwise remains subscribed and starts another request after a catalog notification. Cancel generic stale-document recovery during stale-chunk teardown as well; removing its stylesheet banner alone leaves an `online` listener that can issue a foreign document HEAD request.

Exact fetch counts remain, expressed as URL-array assertions where useful. The old-auth case now completes its canceled response late and verifies that it creates no blob URL and cannot replace the current image. No production behavior changes.

Two bounded fixture repairs were needed after integrating main: await the existing strict first geometry-event marker, and configure the disabled cron-job fixture with the same synthetic model/account setup as the existing cron CLI tests. The latter follows main’s new inference identity capture; all four failing cron cases also fail in scheduled main run 38663143259, job 116189130280. CLI failures now include already-redacted stderr. No assertion, timeout, retry, or production guard is weakened.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original failures | #171660: run 38602286369 / job 115985456978, expected 2 fetches, got 4. #172044: run 38554654222 / job 115821288779, expected 1 fetch, got 3. Logs fetched once. |
| Root-disposal negative control | Removing fixture disposal makes the failed-image/catalog regression fail: expected 1 fetch, got 2. |
| Recovery negative control | All 54 existing cases passed; a temporary next-fixture `online` probe failed with an unexpected document HEAD request. |
| Focused proof | Recovery, attachments, and lifecycle: 106 passed, including the temporary probe subsequently removed; 105 permanent cases remain. |
| CI-order replay | Ten preceding worker files, one worker: 385 passed. Timing-dependent replay was not used as causal proof. |
| Prior full CI | Run 38631348064 passed all selected full UI unit, nine browser E2E and both real-Gateway shards on the four-file repair. Later runs also passed media units, lint/types, and the repaired geometry shard. |
| Local validation | `pnpm tsgo:ui`, formatting and diff checks pass. Isolated reviews through P2 of the media, geometry and cron changes found no actionable findings. Exact final head `5a2c3f64f2de38103edaa87620f24b7ee93eb82e`: full CI [38666617986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666617986) completed. Media units, lint/types and both real-Gateway shards passed. Only the eight exact-base inherited browser cases below failed. |
| Cron diagnostic limit | One local in-process diagnostic was interrupted after 10m05s without assertions; 390.8s was worker preparation. It is not claimed as behavioral proof. The temporary file was removed. Final PR CI owns browser/persistence proof. |
| Startup / visual proof | Not applicable: test-only changes, no production/CSS/startup/visual delta. |

The original logs omit request URLs, so the exact abandoned request behind each historical extra count cannot be proven retrospectively. Both fixture leaks were independently reproduced. The native fixture conversion in #171652 can retire the temporary Lit helper when its callers migrate.

Main’s reasoning fixture repair (`7b9fedd04ff565`) and workspace-path display repair (`869029b986a269`) are integrated rather than duplicated. No test leases, dependencies, sleeps, or test retries were added.

Six files: **4,173 → 4,238 lines (+65)**; production LOC delta **0**. Clean main integration preserves the five-file reviewed media patch byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `8eb5afcb8976b7acfc9d63c529b7cebbdb5ef25827126eb60d1728cfba843a27`).

## Exact-base inherited CI failures

PR CI tested merge `1ba6ef6984b1439e5c834ae354dfca5bfd7bb9a3`, with ordered parents main `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209` and this PR head. Scheduled main run [38666744245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245) tested that exact base and failed the same cases at the same assertions:

| Cases | PR job | Exact-base main job | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Four `model-providers-progressive` cases: saved initial selection, late catalog/invalidation, snapshot publication, ordinary publication | [116200294133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666617986/job/116200294133) | [116200463985](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245/job/116200463985) | The Models page hides published controls until deferred auth details finish. Both runs: 416 passed, 4 failed. |
| Four `chat-native-runtime-recovery` cases: selection/send × confirm/cancel | [116200294319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666617986/job/116200294319) | [116200464190](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245/job/116200464190) | The consent lookup uses an RPC override helper that returns no agent for explicit conversation keys; all four time out waiting for the modal at line 245. |

The affected source inputs are unchanged by this PR. Native inherited-failure admission is requested with retained checkout, source and exact-test evidence; the run is recorded as failed, not green. All other test jobs passed, including the real-Gateway proof of the cron fixture repair. The interrupted local cron diagnostic is not used as behavioral proof.

prs.title: improve: reduce plugin ownership allocations on large inventories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin ownership checks repeatedly canonicalize the same paths while checking installed packages, creating avoidable startup and status-command allocations on large inventories.

## User Impact

Reduces transient allocations for plugin-heavy startup and status checks. Ownership, update, uninstall, and containment rules are unchanged; no configuration or migration is required. Gateway peak-RSS improvement is not established.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare each root and install record once within the existing synchronous ownership phase. Reject impossible canonical POSIX prefixes cheaply, while leaving actual containment and all Windows path rules with the existing path owner. A new phase still gets a fresh resolver after updates or yields.

## Evidence

- Actual native CLI inventory verified 80 installed plugins before Gateway startup and plain status execution.
- Native cumulative sampled allocations through the ownership owner fell from 288.25 to 10.12 MiB. These include collected objects and are not retained heap or qualification evidence.
- One unprofiled local replay reduced status CLI process-tree peak from 904.2 to 854.0 MiB. Gateway peak increased from 1130.9 to 1151.1 MiB; no overall RSS pass is claimed.
- Release source: 41 existing ownership/update/cohort tests passed. Final independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Complete release and fresh-main changed-file gates passed; fresh-main tests passed all 39 existing cases (119.75 s including compiler preparation; no tests edited). Those earlier measurements and checks apply to their recorded source revisions.
- Linux qualification outcome: [run 37819859658](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37819859658) completed **red** under unchanged budgets. Its mock-provider lane tested `0b82c02587a301a6918856ad44d915122dbe6f77`; the ownership module has the same SHA-256 (`e643a2c7b4ca677f2e788cb227824269c8966cde170d9ac44325b8805a00d134`) as the reviewed PR head `a7320ff5da0b14231ec676d277806533113e8a7b`. The run's workflow SHA is a different identity, `2b988ee83444f08ccaf37aa5e98f370726c75f6e`.
- The retained mock-provider report contains 3 PASS, 1 BLOCKED, and 1 FAIL. `fresh-install/onboarded-user` was blocked because the status CLI CPU confidence interval (116.8–204.2%) straddled its 200% ceiling. `gateway-performance/many-bundled-plugins` failed at 1,202 MiB peak RSS against the unchanged 1,177 MiB budget. The mock agent-turn scenario passed. The source-performance lane passed. No baseline comparison was recorded, so these failures cannot be attributed to this optimization or declared inherited. Linux/RSS qualification is **not** claimed, and no thresholds or baselines were changed.
- Rebased onto current main to preserve the dormant bundled-plugin reload repair from #167647. The current fs-safe 0.26.5 containment implementation was inspected: canonical POSIX descendants still require the rejected prefix, and Windows still bypasses this optimization. On head `2984019b34229c55bc8a2f2fc5b10f01150732b5`, five existing ownership/update/uninstall/service-reload files passed all 45 tests (`pnpm test <five files> --maxWorkers=1`, 168.16 s including 44.69 s compiler preparation; no new test/CI cost). The exact management reload subset, including bundled selection with a dormant install record, also passed 11/11 (`pnpm test src/plugins/management-service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t reload`, 47.69 s; 8 unrelated cases excluded by the filter). Core typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.

No new tests, dependencies, cache lifetime, schema, retention, activation behavior, or public SDK changes.


Exact-head CI on `2984019b34229c55bc8a2f2fc5b10f01150732b5` passed: [run 38666737090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666737090), including the trusted aggregate gate. Fresh ClawSweeper review is platinum, ready for maintainer review, with no findings or remaining checklist items.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): report opening timeouts before reconnecting
prs.body:
Related: #172507

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost Control UI WebSocket opening-timeout errors when a reconnect retires the optional HTTP health probe before it finishes.

## User Impact

The UI receives the known timeout reason before retrying, rather than silently losing it. Unknown upgrade failures retain their existing live-Gateway/busy classification.

The 30-second opening deadline and the underlying Gateway stall remain. This is a partial fix for failure reporting in #172507, not a claim that the outage or pre-authentication socket closures are eliminated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first reconnect waits 800–960 ms, while the health probe can take 1,000 ms. A retry cancels the probe and discards its result, including an already-known opening-timeout reason. Only unexplained closes need that availability inference.

## Evidence

- The new production-client regression fails before the fix: expected one close notification with the opening-timeout reason, received zero. With the fix, the notification arrives before retry, and the retry still creates the next socket.
- Focused tests: 22 passed across the reachability, browser socket, and shared-auth handshake files. Vitest 789 ms; repository wrapper 2.40 seconds. Existing unknown-close classification and stale-probe tests pass.
- Independent Node WebSocket client process against an isolated Gateway with a 35-second block before upgrade: before, the UI callback receives no close notification; after, the timeout notification arrives at 30.006 seconds, before retry scheduling. Authentication succeeds at 35.674 seconds and a subsequent health RPC succeeds at 36.361 seconds.
- The same experiment reproduces the incident's server log shape: `code=1006`, `phase=ws_upgrade_started`, `handshake=pending`, server-side duration 5 ms. That expired socket still closes; this PR preserves its client-side explanation while recovery continues.
- Targeted UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Broad suites belong to PR CI.

The live experiment uses synthetic state and a controlled stall; it does not reproduce the reporter's original agent database workload.

## CI follow-up

Run [38653358487](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38653358487), head `83b57291a3e7c1decb76372a88996285e11b319e`, has one failing test in [checks-ui (1/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38653358487/job/116157737471): the sidebar keyboard-navigation case at 390px RTL expected native surface occlusion `[false, true]` and received `[false, true, false, true]`. The extra surface opens at 398 ms and closes at 568 ms, before the tested picker opens at 578 ms. The fixture uses a synthetic Gateway client; the affected sidebar owners are unchanged here. The remaining 608 files / 6,866 tests in that job passed.

A source-order focused replay of `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-filter.browser.test.ts` passed 14/14 in 13.68 seconds. That passing replay is not a repair or proof of an inherited failure. The classifier labels the job new because the matching main job passed; the incidental surface's precise source remains unresolved. No assertion was weakened, no retry added, and no CI rerun requested.


## Inspectable real-transport evidence

These are sanitized event records from the already reported independent Node WebSocket client and isolated real Gateway experiment. The client used the production browser client; the server paused upgrade handling for 35 seconds, while the client’s clock and retry loop kept running in a separate process. This is controlled failure-reporting proof, not reproduction of the reporter’s database workload.

Before (`30b54f615c3`, no patch):
```json
{"event":"retry","elapsedMs":30022,"detail":{"delay":845}}
{"event":"hello","elapsedMs":35533,"detail":{}}
{"event":"rpc","elapsedMs":36045,"detail":{"ok":true}}
```
`observed-closes 0`: no timeout close callback reached the UI.

After (`83b57291a3e7`, original reviewed patch):
```json
{"event":"close","elapsedMs":30006,"detail":{"code":1006,"reason":"gateway websocket opening timed out after 30000ms","willRetry":true}}
{"event":"retry","elapsedMs":30006,"detail":{"delay":924}}
{"event":"hello","elapsedMs":35674,"detail":{}}
{"event":"rpc","elapsedMs":36361,"detail":{"ok":true}}
```
`observed-closes 1`: the known reason arrived before retry; authentication and RPC recovered. Server diagnostic remained `code=1006`, `phase=ws_upgrade_started`, `durationMs=5`, `handshake=pending`, as expected for the expired socket.

## Cleanup refresh

Rebased onto pinned main `22e08398513c2b506bab8270aa6bc38901d08957` because the prior head’s UI CI failure was outside the patch. `git range-diff` confirms the one patch is unchanged. The CI failure above remains prior-head evidence; its passing focused replay is not presented as a repair. ClawSweeper found no actionable code findings on the original patch.

Current rebased head `be8e2660f0f`: focused production-client suites 22/22 passed, 9.20-second wrapper / 5.61-second Vitest; UI typecheck and format passed. Targeted type-aware lint also passed. Exact-head CI passed: [run 38666637452](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666637452), including all three UI shards; the trusted aggregate CI/security gate published success. No new test time added.

Fresh ClawSweeper review of rebased head `be8e2660f0f922e734225884d0fc9e88228825c6`: no code findings; proof confidence platinum and patch quality diamond. Overall remains gold because this is a partial repair of the linked outage.

prs.title: fix(ios): recover release setup after a Gateway handshake disconnect
prs.body:
Closes #172217

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS release qualification failing when the Gateway closes the setup-code connection before the request is sent, such as after a cold Simulator boot stalls the host.

## User Impact

Release qualification can recover from a transient setup handshake failure without restarting the whole run. This is a release-runner reliability fix with no app UI change. Recovery during an actual cold Simulator boot has not been verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native runner now makes at most three setup-code attempts for a Gateway transport close or timeout, using a fresh connection only when the transport explicitly reports that the request was never dispatched. The existing 30-second timeout per attempt stays unchanged. Sent or uncertain requests, cancellation, failed fixtures, and unjoined work stop recovery.

Failure evidence records the attempt count, transport kind, dispatch state, and close code. Only the fixed `invalid-handshake` close reason is exported; other reason text is withheld to avoid leaking credentials into proof artifacts.

## Evidence

Reproduced through the existing `createNativeDependencies` / `runTrials` native adapter harness, with synthetic transport failures and mocked native commands. Base: `ecd4d32c4b3f93305e80c2ca3902445d3fc4b7a4`, macOS arm64, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.9.0.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-dispatch handshake close, next connection succeeds | One attempt; preparation fails | Two attempts; qualification fixture completes |
| Pre-dispatch transport timeout, next connection succeeds | One attempt; preparation fails | Two attempts; qualification fixture completes |
| Persistent pre-dispatch close | One attempt; preparation fails | Three attempts; preparation fails with transport diagnostics |
| Request already dispatched or dispatch unknown | No replay; close details absent | No replay; sanitized close diagnostics recorded |
| Cancellation | Stops | Stops and confirms cleanup |

Before the production fix, the six new regression cases failed. The recovery cases observed one setup-code attempt where two were required, the exhaustion case observed one instead of three, and the close-diagnostic controls found no transport context.

```text
# Before: new regressions against unchanged production source
pnpm test test/scripts/ios-release-e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'setup-code-(handshake|closed)'
Tests  6 failed | 87 skipped (93)
[test] failed 1 Vitest shard in 4.73s

# After: complete owning test file
pnpm test test/scripts/ios-release-e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Tests  93 passed (93)
test file body: 961 ms
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 6.04s
```

Also passed:

- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental`
- Scoped typed lint for both changed files using the scripts and root-test configurations.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, `check:script-erasability`, and `check:line-cap-ratchet --base origin/main`.
- Required AutoReview returned `scoped-clean` through P2; the earlier independent source review also found no actionable issues.

Limits: the adapter harness mocks `callGateway`, Xcode, and Simulator operations. It proves recovery decisions, bounded attempts, diagnostics, and cleanup, not actual host-stall timing or real cold-boot recovery. Hosted CI duration is not yet available.

prs.title: feat(capability): add private model-run prompt files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private one-shot model evaluation prompts being exposed through process arguments and lets local and Gateway model probes request the same bounded generation settings.

## User Impact

POSIX users can pass a private prompt from a mode-`0600`, current-user-owned regular file instead of argv. Local and Gateway probes can request matching maximum-output-token and temperature overrides, and JSON output reports them explicitly as requested overrides rather than provider-resolved settings. Windows is intentionally unsupported for prompt files because this contract depends on POSIX ownership, mode, and no-follow semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI opens prompt files with no-follow semantics, verifies ownership, exact mode, regular-file identity, and a 1 MiB bound, then reads through the opened descriptor. Unsafe, empty, oversized, replaced, or ambiguous prompt input is rejected before local or Gateway execution.

The additive Gateway fields are accepted only for `modelRun=true` and flow into the existing stream-parameter owner. Requests without a generation override omit the new wire field, preserving compatibility with released Gateways whose closed schema predates it. These fields do not expand tools, sessions, persistence, routing, or delivery authority.

## Evidence

Conflict reconciliation candidate: `3ec979263b711b53d8cf91fda987eafb431ba835`, incorporating upstream `eaa6938874c35698bf5317169320c0c36bcc6a1d`. The approved POSIX-only private-file and requested-overrides contracts are unchanged. The upstream protocol tests and private-file tests are both retained. Source-turn routing/admission assembly was extracted unchanged into its owning sibling module to satisfy the existing line-cap ratchet.

- Focused Node 24 tests passed: Gateway **395**, CLI **97 / 1 Windows-only skip**, and protocol **19**. The previously failing full Gateway chat CI file also passed **77/77** on this candidate; this passing replay does not establish a root-cause fix for the older CI failure.
- Fresh independent feature-scoped P0–P2 autoreview: no actionable findings. The review assessed the supplied patch; focused Gateway tests supply integration proof.
- Formatting, all changed-file lint, line-cap ratchet, core production types, and affected Gateway/protocol/CLI type graphs passed. Broad repository type coverage remains the responsibility of new-head PR CI; this is not a claim that all 28 local graphs ran.
- Remaining canonical guards passed: coercion/deprecation, native schema, database-first storage, media, runtime sidecars/import cycles, webhook-body ordering, and pairing guards.
- The broad changed check is **not fully green**: the existing environment-variable count is **455 / budget 454**, directly reproduced on pinned upstream. The canonical dead-export scans also reproduce the same **19 unique unrelated findings** on this candidate and pinned upstream; every reported source file is unchanged. No budgets, exports, or scan configuration were modified.

prs.title: feat(memory): sub-tokenize code identifiers and add FTS5 substring fallback
prs.body:
Closes #172093

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: keyword and hybrid memory search over `unicode61` SQLite FTS5 tables returns zero lexical matches when querying by partial compound code identifiers (such as `ProviderRuntime` against `resolveProviderRuntimeConfig` or `ChildrenAttribute` against `kAXChildrenAttribute`) or across `CamelCase`, `PascalCase`, `snake_case`, and `kebab-case` identifier conventions.

## User Impact

User impact: developers and agents searching memory by sub-identifiers or cross-convention symbol names (`CamelCase`, `PascalCase`, `snake_case`, `kebab-case`) now recall matching notes without losing exact-identifier ranking priority or trigram CJK behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite FTS5 `unicode61` indexes `resolveProviderRuntimeConfig` and `kAXChildrenAttribute` as single contiguous tokens, while `tokenizeFtsQuery` keeps underscores attached inside `"gateway_session_lifecycle_event"`. As a result, strict `MATCH` queries miss cross-convention equivalents and `planKeywordSearch` previously returned `substringTerms: []` for non-trigram tables even on relaxed `matchAny` fallback.

- Add `splitCodeIdentifierSubtokens(term)` in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.ts` to split `CamelCase`, `PascalCase`, acronym boundaries (`HTTPResponse`), and `snake_case` tokens into constituent sub-tokens.
- Expand `buildMatchQueryFromTerms` (for non-trigram tokenizers) so compound code identifiers emit a disjunction of the exact token, the joined compound form, and the conjunction of constituent sub-tokens (`("resolve_provider_runtime_config" OR "resolveproviderruntimeconfig" OR ("resolve" AND "provider" AND "runtime" AND "config"))`).
- Populate `substringTerms` and constituent sub-tokens in `planKeywordSearch` when `matchAny: true` so `searchKeywordWithFallback`'s relaxed pass (`matches UNION ALL substrings` via `openclaw_memory_normalized_contains`) recalls partial compound identifiers inside longer symbols (`ProviderRuntime` inside `resolveProviderRuntimeConfig`, `ChildrenAttribute` inside `kAXChildrenAttribute`).

## Evidence

### 1. Base-Fails / Head-Passes Vitest Suite

- **Base-Fail (`upstream/main` `9f83c05ea3a` + `keyword-query.test.ts`)**: `1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, `3 failed | 30 passed (33)` (`splitCodeIdentifierSubtokens is not a function`, `expected '"repairDoctorSqliteNoCow"' to be '("repairDoctorSqliteNoCow" OR ("repair" AND "Doctor" AND "Sqlite" AND "No" AND "Cow"))'`, `expected [] to include 'chunk-kebab'`).
- **Head-Pass (`HEAD` `ff972eed44c`)**: `2 passed (2)`, `33 passed (33)` across `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts` (`4/4`) and `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts` (`29/29`).

<details>
<summary>Verbatim Base-Fail and Head-Pass Vitest Output</summary>

```text
# Base-Fail (upstream/main 9f83c05ea3a)
 FAIL  |extension-database-workers| extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts > keyword-query code identifier tokenization and fallback > splits CamelCase, PascalCase, acronym, and snake_case identifiers into sub-tokens
TypeError: splitCodeIdentifierSubtokens is not a function
 ❯ extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts:58:12

 FAIL  |extension-database-workers| extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts > keyword-query code identifier tokenization and fallback > includes compound and sub-token conjunction alternatives in FTS5 match queries
AssertionError: expected '"repairDoctorSqliteNoCow"' to be '("repairDoctorSqliteNoCow" OR ("repai…' // Object.is equality
Expected: "("repairDoctorSqliteNoCow" OR ("repair" AND "Doctor" AND "Sqlite" AND "No" AND "Cow"))"
Received: ""repairDoctorSqliteNoCow""
 ❯ extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts:81:19

 FAIL  |extension-database-workers| extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts > keyword-query code identifier tokenization and fallback > recalls CamelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and partial sub-identifiers across SQLite FTS5
AssertionError: expected [] to include 'chunk-kebab'
 ❯ extensions/memory-core/src/memory/keyword-query.test.ts:129:59

 Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
      Tests  3 failed | 30 passed (33)

# Head-Pass (HEAD ff972eed44c)
 ✓ |extension-database-workers| extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts (29 tests)
```

</details>

### 2. SQLite FTS5 (`unicode61`) Runtime Probe (Before vs After)

Indexed a temporary workspace SQLite FTS5 database (`memory_index_chunks`, `memory_index_fts`, `memory_index_paths_fts`) with three markdown notes containing `resolveProviderRuntimeConfig` (`memory/auth-notes.md`), `gateway_session_lifecycle_event` (`memory/gateway-events.md`), and `kAXChildrenAttribute` (`memory/macos-ax.md`), and queried through `searchKeywordWithFallback`:

prs.title: perf(subagents): reuse maintenance protection facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session maintenance reloads the complete subagent protection projection on every pass, even though the registry owner publishes every committed change.

## User Impact

Maintenance protects the same child transcripts with fewer background database reads. There is no schema, retention, configuration, or SDK change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain a compact maintenance-only snapshot in the existing registry cache primitive. Registry restore supplies a complete snapshot; otherwise one coalesced worker read fills it. Existing write receipts apply postimages, deletions, and replacements before later captures. The SQL projection continues excluding large retained task and reply payloads.

Removed check: the per-pass durable maintenance-protection reread. Accepted edge case: unsupported out-of-process writes while the Gateway owns the database do not refresh resident protection; sanctioned writers publish receipts or operate under exclusive offline custody.

The final cleanup capture still checks current source/maintenance admission and overlays live registry rows. Destructive cleanup must still abort on lease loss. As before, maintenance uses `current: true` to bypass inspection snapshots.

## Evidence

- Registry maintenance T1 calls: **0 → 0**; the cold query already executes in the existing state reader worker.
- Regression coverage checks one bounded cold read followed by reuse, plus committed updates/deletions while an untouched durable-only row remains protected. Existing parser and live-overlay coverage remains.
- Codex autoreview completed (one round). Its P2 private-snapshot concern was declined: `current: true` exits `stateSnapshotReads` and ignores inherited synchronous snapshot sources (`openclaw-state-db-readonly.ts`), so maintenance deliberately consumes current protection rather than private inspection membership.
- Changed-file oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38661879866): passed, including all four maintenance tests, sibling owner tests, changed-file checks, type-aware lint, production/test types, export-name collisions, Madge, and database-worker/dialect ratchets. No failures or retries.
- Separate Knip export scan completed: six inherited findings, no finding in changed files. Every rule/file pair also appears in [scheduled main CI 38663143259, job 116189131420](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663143259/job/116189131420) and [newer main CI 38666744245, job 116200464795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38666744245/job/116200464795). Inherited findings: `AuthProfileAuthorizationError`, `configuredOrFalseAsync`, `WorkerPreparationArtifactsSchema`, `PostgresSchemaDefinition`, `webhookHeaders`, and `getChatRunOwnerSessionKey`. No baseline or export policy was changed.
- No update cell or SDK diff is applicable: this changes neither their owning surfaces nor schemas.

| Shared harness metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warmed all-thread statements, median [min–max] | pending | pending |
| Warmed requests, median [min–max] | pending | pending |
| Warmed MAIN statements | pending | pending |
| Maintenance background statements / requests across ten warm turns | pending | pending |

Three alternating base/candidate pairs will be reported with causal counts, legacy window totals, shared read-family attribution, and background counts. No latency claim is made on the busy host. Measurement is evidence and may follow green-CI landing under the campaign policy.
