prs.title: feat(openshell): run brokered inference on sandboxed nodes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Run native worker inference behind OpenShell's credential broker without requiring OCE or Kubernetes, with optional canonical agent files shared across its sessions.

## User Impact

Opt-in `openclaw openshell worker create/run/configure` commands provision a dedicated broker-attached sandbox through OpenShell, enroll its ordinary OpenClaw node, and configure the existing paired-device worker-inference profile. Docker and Podman use the same OpenShell gateway/CLI contract; neither engine is managed directly by this plugin. Existing sandbox-only behavior stays unchanged.

Optional `worker.agentWorkspace: { agentId, remoteRoot }` now binds one configured agent to an existing private directory on the paired node through File Transfer. Both Gateway and worker sessions use that canonical document owner; ordinary coding tools still use each session's task workspace. Setup never seeds or synchronizes documents, copies private Gateway state, widens node-command approvals, or overrides an existing File Transfer policy. Prepare the directory/files and review the existing grants before applying the binding.

**Scope and important limits:** one configured model, a qualified operator-supplied Node/OpenClaw image, and a foreground node host. OpenShell v0.1.3+ provider profiles, executable/endpoint policy, egress enforcement, and real provider credentials remain operator-owned. `worker run` owns a **dedicated sandbox** and stops the entire sandbox on exit/cancellation; cleanup failures explicitly report that the remote node may remain active. `configure --required --apply` affects all Gateway sessions and blocks turns when its worker is unavailable. No production deployment, real provider credentials, releases, or production configuration were changed during development or qualification.

**Historical standalone Docker E2E passed on October 10**, including broker authorization, revocation, and confirmed remote cancellation. It uses a synthetic OpenAI-compatible HTTPS upstream, not a paid model account. Full Podman, real-provider API, and latest-stable upgrade qualification remain separate gaps.

### Compatibility and operator actions

No breaking change was found in the existing sandbox-only `mirror`/`remote` flow when `worker` is absent: its schema fields/defaults, backend and SSH/mirror paths are preserved; CLI registration launches nothing. This PR adds no core/SDK API, database migration, dependency, or worker-protocol change. **The new worker mode is not a drop-in plugin upgrade for older Gateway/node builds.**

- Released OpenClaw **v2026.10.1** lacks the native-inference stack and `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile`; its strict OpenShell plugin schema also rejects the new `worker` block. Installing this plugin alone does not backport core capabilities. Use matching qualified Gateway/node builds and their supported Node version; generic plugin host/API metadata is not worker-mode qualification.
- For downgrade, finish/stop turns, reconcile pending browser inputs and reclaim native placements on the compatible build first; then remove required/native profiles and `plugins.entries.openshell.config.worker`. Older Gateways do not interpret `settings.inference` as a local-inference requirement. No complete stable upgrade or cross-version data-downgrade qualification is claimed.
- **OpenShell v0.1.3+ applies to the new mode only.** Upgrading an older OpenShell deployment has its own breaking migration away from managed inference routes and requires recreating pre-upgrade sandboxes per upstream. This PR does not automatically upgrade OpenShell or migrate those records.
- The workload needs Linux/OpenShell kernel enforcement (including Landlock), a qualified non-root Node/OpenClaw image with Git and POSIX process tools, and an imported provider profile authorizing the actual Node binary and HTTPS endpoint. Native Windows worker inference is unsupported; Docker/Podman selection alone does not establish host capability.
- Initial support is one model using `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, or `anthropic-messages`, with broker environment placeholders and correct CA trust—not every provider/auth adapter. The runner is foreground and stops the entire dedicated sandbox on exit. `--required --apply` affects all Gateway sessions; unavailable workers block turns. Rotation requires a new node process, and model/state changes are not silently overwritten.

Full Podman E2E, real-provider behavior, and latest-stable upgrade qualification remain gaps, not inferred failures. [Setup and rollback guidance](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/openshell-workers#compatibility-and-rollback) records these boundaries; the source-bound historical Docker evidence below remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing owners instead of adding another provider or inference protocol:

- OpenShell creates/retains the sandbox with named existing providers and `--no-auto-providers`, then owns attachment readiness through `sandbox provider attach --wait`.
- The remote bootstrap refuses missing/raw model credentials, accepts only OpenShell's injected opaque placeholder, and writes canonical node model config containing an environment reference—not a key. It maps OpenShell's CA file to Node's supported trust setting without disabling certificate verification.
- Pairing uses `connect --target-file` with a private stdin handoff; reconnect uses `node run`. The Gateway profile derives the exact device ID from read-only `node identity --json` inside the selected sandbox, optionally checks an expected ID, preserves unrelated config, and refuses conflicting bindings.
- Core remains the owner of live pairing, admission, device availability, worker-local inference selection, recorded placement snapshots, and rejection of Gateway fallback. No core/SDK runtime changes, new credentials store, or OCE API dependency.

Current OpenShell calls the real provider endpoint, not the retired workspace inference route. API/CLI contracts were inspected at released NVIDIA/OpenShell v0.1.3 (`e1f3c82caa3ed3b65de22889ae7ef32a774878ef`). Placeholder-format checks and provider readiness are not cryptographic custody attestation or upstream model probes; the deployment trust contract remains explicit.

The original default-off worker option adds 15 plugin config fields; the optional agent-workspace binding adds 3 more (18 total over the pinned main base). Canonical config-baseline outputs were regenerated; this growth is intentional, not an unrelated baseline waiver.

## Evidence

### Rebase and merge-readiness audit — October 15

**Rebase published; compatibility qualification is not yet complete.** Head `10f275f9aa8dd0947205acc52a7f930fe37cece0`, tree `27246c3751887649c030dc868480de0a819b10d3`, one squashed commit on main `17bea1c022a9bc90a464c7f8c2a01d784d246cb7`. GitHub reports mergeable, OPEN and non-draft. No merge or auto-merge was requested or performed.

Only the canonical configuration baseline outputs conflicted; regenerated them rather than selecting hashes. All 16 nongenerated PR files are byte-identical to prior published head `8b2556a8d1a73f5fcb4c8b0c4b1599c8b84ea834`. The +18 plugin fields, trimmed tests, Sally credit and publication marker remain intact. Later main `e106d1fa54ec11e55cbd23d17334a99e7492c2b7` composed without conflict.

**Source review:** fresh independent full-delta review at `508e3c10fb1fd2ae108e27aabd8aa7c04575a0f0` (the same nongenerated PR blobs) found no P0–P2 findings. Existing sandbox-only defaults and mirror/remote owners remain unchanged by this PR. New SDK consumers match current contracts; File Transfer remains the canonical document/policy owner with no local fallback. Latest stable is now **v2026.10.3**, build source `59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1`; it still lacks the new native-inference/required-profile semantics. Plugin-only installation on that old host is not qualified, and rollback after opt-in still requires the documented cleanup. This is a bounded source verdict, not a guarantee across versions or deployments.

**Fresh final-head checks:** 123/123 tests in eight existing-sandbox and worker files, **42.68s wrapper wall**; extension production/test types, canonical baseline and whitespace checks passed. On the preceding `508e3c10fb1f` refresh, the same 123 tests passed in 64.65s, targeted typed lint passed on 10 plugin files with zero warnings/errors, and formatting passed. Full canonical build plus package-integrity validation completed in **1530.04s** on that precise earlier tree `65519cbcb42ef3102799d4a59d6c9093b090ad77`; it is not relabeled as a final-head full build.

**Genuine installed upgrade attempt — did not pass:**
- Disposable rootless Podman, Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0, private prefix/HOME/state/workspaces, synthetic data only. Host networking was used solely to reach the enforced managed egress proxy; TLS verification remained enabled. No hosting Gateway, production state, provider credentials or model calls were involved.
- Installed registry-integrity-verified OpenClaw 2026.10.3 and the released `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox@2026.10.3` via their normal package/plugin owners. Authored sandbox-only remote settings and unrelated config through the released CLI; created a durable session/transcript through the released Gateway and four synthetic workspace files. Captured a stopped-state backup before updating.
- Built the exact candidate core package with the canonical packer and separately packaged the candidate plugin through the prepublish plugin-artifact owner; the default core package correctly excludes OpenShell. No custom bundled distribution or fake version was substituted. Core SHA-256 `9a7f74575b81e35a1f87eb74f5624fde97cee3b2115afc9fd2cc56ce22dcabec`; plugin SHA-256 `406c03d31215646e9526d86d08baf82dbf65cd4f1d237430743f2162bba03acd`.
- Ran the **installed released updater**, `openclaw update --tag /proof/packages/openclaw-candidate.tgz --yes --no-restart --json`. An interrupted first attempt settled failed with a stale managed-proxy authorization; its durable outcome was reconciled before retry. The retry used fresh authority and took **437.15s**, exiting 1.
- Candidate package installation, snapshot, Doctor, Doctor lint, config, database-schema, runtime and plugin-availability admission passed. **The candidate Gateway startup probe did not pass**: it stalled at `startupz` despite the child logging readiness; the candidate was not activated. The old released core remained installed. The non-default-state/no-service fixture also cannot qualify managed-service recovery. This is an observed qualification failure, not a demonstrated OpenShell data-model defect.
- A cold restart of the retained released installation verified **exact full configuration, all four document bytes, the original session ID and exact transcript messages preserved**. This proves preservation after the refused update—not successful candidate data migration. The candidate plugin was not force-installed after core admission failed.

**Probe-route control:** on the unchanged released installation, the existing readiness helper and authenticated Gateway probe succeeded, while the released public `ensureGlobalUndiciEnvProxyDispatcher()` plus `fetch` failed for both `/startupz` and `/readyz` with `UND_ERR_SOCKET` under the same enforced proxy environment. Original config/data checks still passed afterward. This demonstrates an independent local HTTP/proxy-path failure in this venue; it does not retroactively make the candidate update pass. The inherited canary diagnostic replaces the last transport failure with a generic startup-stall message, so the exact failed canary request was not retained. No proxy, TLS or admission gate was bypassed. A qualified runner/probe route is still needed for the successful update cell.

**Readiness:** no source-review blocker found, but the requested successful installed-release-to-candidate upgrade/preservation cell remains unproven. New-head CI was attached and running at publication; prior-head green CI is not reused as current-head success. Historical broker/authority evidence below remains source-bound, and full external Podman, real-provider and downgrade qualification remain unclaimed.

### Conflict-only refresh — October 13, 15:43 UTC

Rebased the existing single commit from `c89bc66069cd79a14743f1459c8315f0be13c826` onto main `a55dafd57b8155ea31bb7fe97fd163acd7e3d48f`. New head: `8b2556a8d1a73f5fcb4c8b0c4b1599c8b84ea834`; tree: `babcc40fe9cf5a0a13c32246634e6be7c5e4e2bd`. The branch still contains **one commit**, retaining Sally's co-author trailer, publication marker and the previously trimmed tests.

- Conflicts were limited to `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`. Regenerated both through the canonical generator; the intentional plugin-schema delta remains **+18 fields**.
- All implementation and test blobs are unchanged from the prior head. Four PR-path blobs changed: those two generated files and two documentation files that automatically retained main's terminology edits. The base-relative range diff changes only generated metadata. No new behavior or permission changes.
- **Fresh focused proof:** 21/21 tests in four OpenShell files, **56.59s wrapper wall**; extension production and test typechecks passed (**27.06s combined**); targeted typed lint passed for 10 plugin files with zero warnings/errors; changed-file formatting, canonical baseline verification and whitespace checks passed. The private worktree dependency install was normally reconciled to main's pinned fs-safe 0.26.3 with the frozen lockfile; no dependency source files changed.
- Mechanical replay review compared the complete old/new patches and changed blobs. Existing substantive reviews remain source-bound; no new implementation required re-review. A read-only merge against later main `0538c07d971655f1e7cbe66279112f608595ecd6` completed without conflicts, so the tested base was retained.
- The full integration/build suite was **not rerun for this metadata-only resolution**. Earlier integration, real-broker and build evidence below remains historical; the prior build-timeout and external Podman/real-provider/stable-upgrade gaps remain disclosed. Hosted CI is separate from these focused passes. No merge or readiness transition.

### Requested rebase and squash — October 13

Rebased onto main `cf66264e598fd98718cff54a9fa378fbeb80d35a` and squashed the eight PR commits into **one**: [c89bc66069cd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c89bc66069cd79a14743f1459c8315f0be13c826), tree `9f7c83f558a56d8e70259072d0396ad37cbdcfb2`. Sally's co-author credit and the publication marker are preserved. GitHub readback confirms one commit, no merge conflict, OPEN and non-draft; no merge or readiness transition was performed.

Only the generated configuration-baseline hash conflicted. Both canonical baseline outputs were regenerated, preserving the new base plus this PR's intentional 18 plugin fields. All 16 nongenerated PR files—including implementation, documentation and trimmed tests—are byte-identical to the prior published head `225ec22581c3`. Prior independent reviews remain attached to their actual source; this mechanical replay introduces no additional implementation change.

- **Final-base focused proof:** 21/21 tests across OpenShell registration, config, worker CLI and bootstrap passed; **49.38s wrapper wall**. Extension production/test typechecks, canonical config-baseline check and whitespace checks passed.
- **Earlier in this refresh, on main `7f4197068b3d`:** root-test type shards passed (combined production/test/root type run **258.57s**); typed lint passed for all touched plugin production/tests and the E2E, with zero warnings/errors; changed-file formatting passed. These receipts are not relabeled as final-base broad CI.
- Initial build/type attempts exposed stale task-local dependencies after the base update (including fs-safe 0.26.0 instead of pinned 0.26.2). A normal frozen-lockfile install in the private, idle worktree fixed that environment without changing tracked files. The focused tests and applicable typechecks were rerun afterward.
- **Integration rerun remains incomplete:** the isolated Podman E2E reached the normal full-build prerequisite, but the 600-second execution budget expired during the second tsdown invocation, before any integration case ran. Its task container and descendant processes are gone; retained artifact ownership was recovered through the build owner's documented procedure. This is neither a failing workspace assertion nor a fresh integration pass. The earlier source-bound successful integration and live-broker evidence below remain historical.

Broad CI is left to the newly published head. Full external Podman broker, real-provider and stable-upgrade qualification remain unclaimed.

### Requested test trimming — October 12

[225ec22581c3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/225ec22581c330281c563c6b7c65a96e5bdbebdf) is **test-only: 43 net lines removed** relative to `7661c1e7cc77` (11 added, 54 removed across four test files). The workspace E2E shrank **690 → 656 lines**. Compared with the original PR base `3eff8f0e249b`, total added test lines are now **1,264**, rather than 1,307; this is not a claim that the whole PR is net-negative. Production code, schemas, permissions, and behavior are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ios): retry stalled App Store screenshot processing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS Store Release timing out when App Store Connect leaves a screenshot in `UPLOAD_COMPLETE`, as in [run 38653449205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38653449205).

## User Impact

Releases can recover from stalled screenshot processing while preserving completed screenshots. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace only stalled assets in up to two rounds, ten minutes apart, within the existing one-hour processing budget. Preserve file order and verify the final count, checksums, and completion states. Explicit processing failures and API errors still stop the release; uncertain uploads are not retried blindly.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original timeout through the real screenshot upload owner with simulated Apple responses; the new regression failed before the fix and passes afterward.
- All 24 focused release tests pass, covering normal completion, selective replacement, retry exhaustion, API errors, uncertain mutations, and final screenshot verification. The nine new cases take about 0.5 seconds locally.
- Ruby syntax, targeted TypeScript checks, lint, formatting, and changed-test selection pass. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Read-only App Store Connect inspection confirms the same iPad screenshot remains stalled and the failed run never uploaded build 2. Live replacement behavior will be verified by a full release run after landing; no upload was performed during local testing.

prs.title: feat(discord): AI auto-naming for threads via channels.discord.thread.autoName
prs.body:
Related: #160865.
Follow-up draft with the same implementation: #171389.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord threads can retain generic names after their conversation makes the topic clear.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `channels.discord.thread.autoName`: `false`/`0` disables naming by default, `true` uses five admitted messages, and a positive integer sets the threshold. Per-account overrides are supported. A new thread can receive one concise title from a bounded human/agent transcript. Manual renames are preserved.

Title generation uses the agent selected by Discord account/channel/role routing or an active conversation binding, including that agent's model and credentials. An admitted human continues to authorize subsequent agent messages after their text leaves the recent transcript window; their access is rechecked before generation and renaming.

Maintainer product acceptance is still required for the optional setting, model processing, and persisted lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord plugin uses existing admission, isolated conversation-label generation, REST scheduling, and worker-backed SQLite owners.

- Naming authority and shutdown cancellation reach model preparation, credential handoff, dispatch, and utility/primary fallback.
- Existing routing owners select the effective agent. A prepared binding inspection retains owner authority through model work and queued Discord PATCH retries. A configuration change during naming cancels the optional attempt. The existing generic inspection operation is exposed through the existing bundled SDK binding-runtime subpath.
- A single human authorization identity is retained separately from the 20-message text window. It contains no message text and remains subject to current member and policy checks.
- Boolean claims expire after the 24-hour eligibility window. Claim/budget namespaces reject new entries at 10,000 rows. A durable two-attempt account/parent budget spans ten minutes and is reserved before model work. Transcripts are bounded and not persisted.

## Evidence

### Current rebase and conflict repair

Head: `997c50c1e5c8b055da0eb21b9b1272e3d21d9632`; rebased onto main `207b7813aea9aa3c4bd6171407a664f92979c209`. Three generated configuration artifacts conflicted with upstream configuration changes. The bundled channel metadata and configuration count/hash baselines were regenerated with their canonical generators.

All 26 feature source, documentation, and test files outside the generated artifacts and shared test inventory retain their exact pre-rebase blobs. The inventory preserves the new upstream worker test and the three naming tests. Compared with current-main channel metadata, the regenerated output adds only the global/account `thread.autoName` schema entries and its UI hint.

- Channel metadata and configuration-baseline generator checks pass.
- Extension production types and the complete extension-test typecheck pass.
- All 123 focused tests across ten Discord files pass in secretless, network-disabled Node 24.19.0 Docker. They cover naming admission and effects, real label/model preparation and routing, persistence, policy, startup, listeners, interactions, and configuration. Focused wall time: 107.73 seconds; current CI timings remain pending.
- Focused generated-metadata lint, formatting, staged-content guard, and diff checks pass. The committed tree matches the validated candidate (`5db5913f75ff458f4c3db8fc169b1276e6a3c4ac`).

[Current-head CI run 38667278183](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38667278183) is attached to this head; results are pending at publication.

### Previous CI repair

Head: `40c6a070c768e414bc4588a9757b5f644f782337` on the original `feat/discord-thread-auto-name` branch. The CI regression was two existing `DiscordLivePolicy` test fixtures missing the required `isConfigCurrent` callback. Both fixtures now include it. The two displayed CI gate failures reflected that same test-type failure.

The complete tracked tree matches the isolated, validated candidate at `aecbedbb0522f00e6595484cc855155636748ee5` (tree `b71bdc84805e0d8696129e4aaae69fa7e1e86084`):

- The unchanged previous revision reproduced both original TS2741 errors; the full extension-test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, the CI project) passed with the fix.
- All 36 tests in the two changed files passed in secretless, network-disabled Node 24.19.0 Docker. Wall time: 48.92 seconds; test execution: 0.125 seconds for listeners and 0.027 seconds for modal policy deadlines. Current CI timings remain pending.
- Focused lint, formatting, staged-content guard, and diff checks passed. A fresh independent P0-P2 review of this two-line repair returned `scoped-clean`.
- Production behavior and existing assertions are unchanged by this CI repair. The feature evidence below is retained at its actual source revisions.

[Pre-rebase CI run 38653271150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38653271150) completed successfully at `40c6a070c768e414bc4588a9757b5f644f782337`, including production types, test types, and the aggregate CI gate. It is prior-head evidence.

### Previous routing and transcript-window revision

Head: `b3edf25833476c34bbb0e1d0d2eb2a08dbc141d2`; rebased onto main `f7e1bfd33ca67bcd035eb92f0eed1e7906fc4193`. This revision addresses eleqtrizit's [agent-selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160873#discussion_r4275919677) and [transcript-window](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160873#discussion_r4275919707) findings. The conflicting configuration baselines were regenerated with the canonical generator.

- The added regressions reproduced the defects on the previous implementation: four routing cases dispatched to the default agent/provider, and thresholds 21/22 failed to generate a title after human text was evicted.
- All 73 focused tests across seven files passed in secretless, network-disabled Node 24.19.0 Docker. They cover the real conversation-label runtime, isolated completion, credential preparation, plugin loader, admission, state, routing, startup, and serialized Discord REST effects.
- Assigned-provider cases cover parent, account, current guild-role, and explicit thread-binding routing; the recorded model dispatch uses the assigned agent and synthetic credentials, with no default-provider dispatch. Binding/configuration changes during preparation and utility fallback prevent further effects.
- Sequential threshold 21/22 cases produce exactly one rename with only the latest 20 agent messages in the prompt. Human role revocation after eviction blocks generation or final PATCH.
- Focused wall time: 98.21 seconds. Changed-file test execution: 12.21 seconds for admission/effects and 22.46 seconds for the real runtime. Runtime cases retain native model/credential/plugin preparation to prove provider isolation and final dispatch.
- Extension production and targeted regression typechecks, focused lint/format, staged-content guard, assertion/line-cap/timeout-race/mock-export ratchets, SDK export and surface checks, canonical configuration-baseline check, supported JavaScript runtime build, and the isolated Discord plugin startup profile passed. The inherited environment-count subcheck failure is recorded below.
- A fresh independent P0-P2 review of the corrective delta returned `scoped-clean`.

[CI run 38640481573](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38640481573) completed at `b3edf25833476c34bbb0e1d0d2eb2a08dbc141d2`: its test-type job failed with the two missing fixture callbacks repaired above; its other selected checks passed. The prior full CI pass was on `3b52cb706383c709d4e209e6ae49f9be19a6014e` ([run 38482177212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38482177212)); this is historical evidence.

Historical local baseline observation at `b3edf25833476c34bbb0e1d0d2eb2a08dbc141d2` against pinned main `f7e1bfd33ca67bcd035eb92f0eed1e7906fc4193`: both contained the same 455 production environment names against a 454-name budget. Upstream [#170374](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170374) introduced `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_REHEARSAL_COMMAND_STARTED_AT_MS`. The local max-lines suppression check passed, then its environment-count subcheck failed. The completed CI run at that head passed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`.

### Historical live and released-data evidence

The demonstration below ran at `f2b5c61988be2af10c7f6a5880790ba2f6b61c6f`. It proves the ordinary Gateway's live threshold rename on that candidate. The corrective revision above was validated separately through production-path fixtures; no repeat live Discord/model call is claimed.

Actual config and Discord state records created by published `openclaw@2026.10.3` survived that candidate's Doctor and V2 reopening unchanged, including timestamps, with naming disabled. This is stored-data/config compatibility proof; it does not claim a complete installed-updater replacement or live Discord upgrade. That candidate's package metadata was `2026.10.2`; the current branch metadata is `2026.10.3`.

### Live Discord threshold rename

A normal foreground Gateway running the compiled candidate at the reviewed SHA connected to live Discord on October 13, 2026. It used separate state, workspace, and task credentials, with a real configured model service. A new public thread was created after Discord READY with `channels.discord.thread.autoName: 2`. The human participant posted two plain test messages without mentioning or replying to the bot.

The following redacted trace combines actual Gateway status, Discord REST observations and audit records, and the isolated Gateway's SQLite protection records. Timestamps are UTC; credentials, message contents, account/guild/channel identifiers, model identifiers, and provider endpoints are omitted.

```text
source_sha=f2b5c61988be2af10c7f6a5880790ba2f6b61c6f
foreground_cli=node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run
autoName=2
2026-10-13T22:21:06.515Z Discord lifecycle=ready connected=true
2026-10-13T22:22:34.146Z new public thread name="Untitled"
2026-10-13T22:34:18.894Z admitted human message 1 (plain, no mention/reply)

2026-10-13T22:34:51.980Z isolated Gateway claim=true expires_after=24h
2026-10-13T22:34:52.619Z isolated Gateway naming_attempts=1 budget_window=10m
2026-10-13T22:34:55.102Z Discord THREAD_UPDATE audit: actor=bot "Untitled" -> "Test messages for check"
2026-10-13T22:34:59.368Z Discord GET: humans=2 name="Test messages for check"
bot_conversation_replies=0 (Discord also emitted its type-4 name-change system message)
```

The source snapshot had no tracked changes. This used the compiled candidate's ordinary Gateway and label/REST paths; no synthetic model response, event injection, or manual rename was used. The operator Gateway was not restarted or reconfigured. The earlier synthetic regression and released-data compatibility checks remain separate evidence.

## Maintainer Decision Still Required

The setting, model processing, and durable lifecycle need maintainer acceptance in the [feature discussion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160865). Discord owns the feature; existing shared owners provide model execution, REST scheduling, and storage. Claims/budgets are bounded, reconstructible protection; transcripts are not persisted. Rollback disables `autoName`; boolean claims remain readable by the previous implementation. Acceptance is not asserted by this repair.

**Remaining before merge:** maintainer acceptance of the feature/lifecycle. The live Discord threshold-rename demonstration is recorded below. [Follow-up draft PR #171389](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171389) carries the same reviewed implementation and evidence.

Release-note context: Discord can optionally name new threads after an admitted conversation threshold, with bounded persisted protection and restart-safe spending limits. Human credit: @art22s. No release-owned changelog edit.

Title failure diagnostics omit arbitrary provider error strings, which can contain transcript/request text. Model selection and authentication remain with the shared label owner.

prs.title: fix(ui): sidebar stress test fails after approval rows became single-line
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `checks-ui` fails on `main` (and on the 2026.10.10 release candidate) in `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.stress.browser.test.ts` "full sidebar state stress" for three matrix cases (`category/light/220`, `person/dark/220`, `none/dark/280 rtl`), reporting `stress-crowded no title space after viewers join` / `title shifted with presence`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Restores a green `checks-ui` shard on `main` and the release branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bisected to #172618 (approval-waiting sidebar rows stay on one line). The stress fixture's `crowded` row got its second line only from the pending-approval subtitle. After #172618 it renders single-line, and the single-line CSS contract (`layout.css`, "the title absorbs all shrink, so the icon endcap keeps its intrinsic width") lets its very full endcap (PR, outbox, draft, disk, incognito, participants, plus four joining viewers) take all of the title width at 220px, and shift the title in RTL.

The fixture now gives `crowded` agent-declared attention instead of a pending approval, so it stays the two-line "everything at once" row in every matrix case, including previews off. The plain `approval` row still covers pending approvals.

Tradeoff for the #172618 owner: an approval-pending row with an extremely crowded endcap and several viewers can now show little or none of its title at the narrowest sidebar width. Every other single-line row already works this way by design, so this PR doesn't change product layout.

## Evidence

- Before: `pnpm test ui/src/components/app-sidebar.stress.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` fails 3/8 deterministically on `origin/main` d5e4322d493 and on release candidate d6105820e06. Same three cases failed in both the node and bun `checks-ui (2/3)` shards of FRV CI run 38662503008.
- `git bisect` (178545e323f good → 459cad76530 bad): first bad commit 4612504e2bd (#172618).
- After: 8/8 pass, 6.4s wall.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` clean.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): align group silence guidance with silentReplyPolicy
prs.body:
Fixes #168306

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: required group and channel turns fail with `CLI produced no text output (reason=empty_response)` on CLI-backed harnesses (`claude-cli`) when `silentReplyPolicy` is `"disallow"` (the default) because the group system prompt still instructs the model to stay silent (`"mostly lurk"`, `"reply only when directly addressed"`, `"stay silent"`, `"most need no response"`) while omitting the `NO_REPLY` token instruction.

## User Impact

User impact: group and channel conversations with default `silentReplyPolicy: "disallow"` receive brief replies on required turns across both `automatic` and `message_tool_only` (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies = "message_tool"`) delivery modes instead of failing with `empty_response`, while `silentReplyPolicy: "allow"` and ambient `room_event` turns retain full lurk and `NO_REPLY` suppression behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSilentReplySettings` (`src/config/silent-reply.ts`) defaults `silentReplyPolicy` to `"disallow"` for group conversations and omits the `NO_REPLY` instruction when silent replies are disallowed. However, `buildGroupChatContext` and `buildGroupIntro` in `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts` unconditionally emitted silence instructions in both `automatic` and `message_tool_only` modes, and `prepareReplyRunContext` (`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts`) and `prepareCommandConversationContext` (`src/agents/command/conversation-context.ts`) called `buildGroupIntro` without passing `silentReplyPolicy`.

- Gate the lurk/silence lines in `buildGroupChatContext` and `buildGroupIntro` (`src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts`) on `params.silentReplyPolicy === "disallow"` regardless of whether `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` is `"automatic"` or `"message_tool_only"`, replacing them with required-turn participation guidance (`"For required conversational requests, reply briefly even when another participant is addressed; do not speak on their behalf. For optional ambient events and synthetic continuations, follow the current-turn guidance."`).
- Pass the resolved `silentReplyPolicy` into `buildGroupIntro` in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts` and `src/agents/command/conversation-context.ts` so primary group turns and inter-session command continuations assemble identical session-stable system prompts.
- Add regression coverage in `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, and `src/agents/command/session-preparation.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### 1. Base-Fails / Head-Passes Test Verification

Against `upstream/main` (`b3bf2eae12b`), the new regression tests fail in both `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts` (`3 failed | 7 passed`) and `src/agents/command/session-preparation.test.ts` (`1 failed`, `conversation-context.ts` omitting `silentReplyPolicy` on `buildGroupIntro`). On `HEAD` (`3266e8b4801`), all `126/126` tests pass across the three suites (`10/10` in `groups.test.ts`, `91/91` in `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`, `15/15` in `session-preparation.test.ts`), with `0` `tsgo` and `0` `oxlint` diagnostics.

<details>
<summary>Verbatim Base-Fail and Head-Pass Vitest Output</summary>

```text
# Base-Fail (upstream/main b3bf2eae12b + regression tests from 3266e8b4801)
 FAIL  |auto-reply-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts > group runtime loading > keeps prompt helpers off the heavy group runtime
AssertionError: expected 'Activation: always-on (you receive ev…' to contain 'You see every message; answer require…'
Expected: "You see every message; answer required conversational requests briefly, and follow current-turn guidance for optional ambient events or synthetic continuations. When you do reply"
Received: "Activation: always-on (you receive every group message). You see every message; most need no response. When you do reply, address the specific sender noted in the message context."
 ❯ src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts:109:7

 FAIL  |auto-reply-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts > group runtime loading > avoids unconditional silence instructions when silent replies are disallowed
AssertionError: expected 'You are in a Discord group chat. Your…' to contain 'For required conversational requests,…'
 ❯ src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts:132:30

 FAIL  |auto-reply-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts > group runtime loading > keeps message-tool-only required turns free of silence guidance when silent replies are disallowed
AssertionError: expected 'You are in a Discord group chat. Norm…' to contain 'For required conversational requests,…'
 ❯ src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts:158:29

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  3 failed | 7 passed (10)

 FAIL  |agents-support| src/agents/command/session-preparation.test.ts > preserves the slack channel system prompt on completion (private=undefined)
AssertionError: expected 'You are a personal assistant running …' to be 'You are a personal assistant running …' // Object.is equality
- Activation: always-on (you receive every group message). You see every message; answer required conversational requests briefly, and follow current-turn guidance for optional ambient events or synthetic continuations. When you do reply, address the specific sender noted in the message context.
+ Activation: always-on (you receive every group message). You see every message; most need no response. When you do reply, address the specific sender noted in the message context.
 ❯ src/agents/command/session-preparation.test.ts:303:55

# Head-Pass (HEAD 3266e8b4801)
 ✓ |auto-reply-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/groups.test.ts (10 tests) 318ms

```
</details>

### 2. Shipped-Entrypoint Runtime Probe with Local Loopback Telegram Bot API Server

Exercised `prepareReplyRunContext` (`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts`), `prepareCommandConversationContext` (`src/agents/command/conversation-context.ts`), and `deliverReplies` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.replies.ts`) with a Grammy `Bot` connected to a local loopback HTTP Telegram Bot API server (`http://127.0.0.1:50419/bot<REDACTED_TOKEN>`):

1. **Required group turn (`"@openclaw_bot can you see this?"`), default `silentReplyPolicy: "disallow"`, `automatic` delivery mode**:
   - `upstream/main`: `hasMostlyLurk: true`, `hasStaySilent: true`, `hasMostNeedNoResponse: true`, `hasNoReplyToken: false` -> contradicts `terminalReplyExpectation: "required"`.
   - `HEAD` (`3266e8b4801`): `hasRequiredTurnGuidance: true`, `hasRequiredIntroGuidance: true`, `hasMostlyLurk: false`, `hasStaySilent: false`, `hasMostNeedNoResponse: false`; `deliverReplies` posts `POST /bot<REDACTED_TOKEN>/sendMessage` to `chat_id: "-100168306"` (`ok: true, message_id: 101`).
2. **Required group turn, `silentReplyPolicy: "disallow"`, `message_tool_only` mode (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies = "message_tool"`)**:
   - `upstream/main`: `sourceConversationContextByMode.message_tool_only` still contains `"mostly lurk"` and `"stay silent"`.
   - `HEAD` (`3266e8b4801`): `hasRequiredTurnGuidance: true`, `hasMostlyLurk: false`, `hasStaySilent: false`; `message(action=send)` posts `POST /bot<REDACTED_TOKEN>/sendMessage` (`ok: true, message_id: 102`).
3. **Optional/ambient turns (`agents.defaults.silentReply.group = "allow"` and `InboundEventKind: "room_event"`)**:
   - Preserves `hasMostlyLurk: true`, `hasStaySilent: true`, `hasMostNeedNoResponse: true`, `hasNoReplyToken: true`, `roomEventReplyExpectation: "optional"`; `deliverReplies` suppresses `{ text: "NO_REPLY" }` (`delivered: false`) and sends `0` additional HTTP requests to the loopback Telegram server.
4. **Command continuation parity (`prepareCommandConversationContext` on `inter_session` `subagent_settle`)**:
   - Matches `prepareReplyRunContext` (`hasRequiredTurnGuidance: true`, `hasRequiredIntroGuidance: true`, `matchesReplyRunContextIntro: true`).

<details>

prs.body:
Builds on #172607 (merged).

## Problem

Muse Code sign-in from Models had several problems:
- The waiting step had no loader, so it looked stuck.
- The dialog stayed open for many seconds after the browser approval.
- It ended with "Account connected. Choose a model when you want to test a reply." and only a Close button.
- Every new chat then asked about native permissions.

## Solution

- **Ask once, at setup.** Before the device code, Muse Code shows the native-permissions explanation (Continue / Cancel). Continue records `muse` in the agent's `nativeRuntimeConsent` (via #172607's helper), in the same setup commit that enables the runtime and routes the model. Later chats do not ask again. Two optional fields on existing SDK types carry this: `ProviderAuthContext.agentId` and `ProviderAuthResult.nativeRuntimeConsent`.
- **Visible progress.** The existing spinner sits next to "Waiting for approval in your browser…". Once the CLI reports success, the server's own wizard progress label ("Testing your AI connection…") is shown under the same code, using an optional `progressLabel` on the wizard step. No timed or simulated steps.
- **Faster finish.** Setup verification reuses the credential-bound, read-only Muse host for the pre-commit `model/list`, so there is no second Muse process. The finish action no longer waits for config reconciliation and a full catalog refresh; it uses the verified starter model from the completion receipt.
- **Useful completion.** A centered success state: "Muse Code is connected", "Muse Spark 1.3 is ready for your agent.", primary **Start a new chat with Muse Spark 1.3**, secondary Close. The model comes from the hosted recommendation ranking when available, otherwise the provider's verified starter model. The new chat is created with that model for the session only; the agent's default model does not change. This applies to any provider login that has an available model.
- The dialog keeps a stable size between states, focuses the primary action, and respects reduced motion.

## Evidence

Live run on a fresh isolated Gateway built from the integrated branch (default `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, real `muse` 1.3.0, real Meta approval):

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Approval → "Testing your AI connection…" | about 2 s after `muse login` exits |
| Approval → completion with **Start a new chat with Muse Spark 1.3** | about 6 s (before: about 28 s on the reporter's Gateway, about 17 s isolated) |
| Start chat → first reply | 6.5 s, no permissions prompt; default model unchanged |
| Second new chat with Muse Spark 1.3 | reply, no prompt |

About 12 s of the approval-to-finish time is spent inside the opaque `muse login` CLI, which polls Meta; it exposes no polling option.

Before:
![before completion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b88d608e-3e7c-4f94-820f-ff0882f143c0)

After:
![consent once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f238267-fc2f-411e-a7c2-1deaa2475fb5)
![waiting with loader](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc637ee7-95f5-40f1-8a78-d1a21c990dcd)
![completion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0173618e-7a1e-4bff-bc3f-f9fb6767f1eb)
![first chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f67ce5d-c79a-4e47-8eb4-b912a2348260)

Tests: Meta login (consent prompt before spawn, cancel with no effects, one approval), Muse harness verification host reuse, setup credential lifecycle (consent written in the same commit), Models login completion (starter offered before catalog refresh, hosted ranking first, session-only model), and the wizard view/progress label suites.

### Review follow-up (`c07c0dd0a06`, rebased on #172607 `79e67a17ffa`)

- **Cancellation during catalog-host startup** (`0ed298e21fa`). The setup signal now reaches pool acquisition. A cancelled startup closes the initializing Muse host instead of leaving it in the idle pool. Regression: "closes a catalog host cancelled during initialization" uses a real fake-Muse child held at `initialize`. Before the fix the child was still alive; after, it is gone before verification returns.
- Fixed existing sign-in test type errors.

Live, final head, real Muse 1.3.0:
```text
Models → Provider Access → Meta → Muse Code
Consent shown once: "Muse Code runs on the Gateway host under its own permissions." → Continue
Device code with spinner: Waiting for approval in your browser…
Meta approval: APPROVED
00:23:57.499Z Testing your AI connection…
00:23:59.678Z Muse Code is connected / Muse Spark 1.3 is ready for your agent.
Start a new chat with Muse Spark 1.3 → session model=meta/muse-spark-1.3 permissionMode=full sandboxMode=off
User: Reply with exactly S610_SIGNIN_OK. Do not use tools.  Assistant: S610_SIGNIN_OK
status=done hasActiveRun=false; no permission prompt; agent default stayed openai/gpt-5.6-luna
```

Upgrade cell: state written by the previous main build `962375d5ee`, with Muse routing, plugin and credential. After main's own agent-database migration (v26→v27 via `doctor --fix`, not part of this PR), the default model, Muse routing, Muse plugin config and credential bytes were unchanged, and the Muse catalog was available. The consent entry stayed absent until a new sign-in added `["muse"]`.

Non-admin, other-agent and revocation proofs: see #172607.

### Rebase onto main (`34095abf2ed`)

Replayed onto main after #172607 and #172608 landed. Kept #172608's refresh by credential owner and its deferred reconcile. The UI no longer imports the Meta extension manifest: `modelActivation.modelName` now comes from the Gateway's captured provider catalog. Test assertions are updated for the new waiting copy ("Waiting for approval in your browser…") and the explicit success-dialog dismissal.

**Upgrade / stored data:** no schema or stored-row change. The consent entry is written only by a new sign-in through #172607's config helper. The upgrade cell above shows a previous-main state loading with its default model, Muse routing, plugin config and credential bytes unchanged.

## Update behavior

No migration. The new SDK and wizard fields are optional. Existing Muse users keep their routing; the consent is written only by a new sign-in.

prs.title: fix(openai): name the direct image route on 401/403 scope errors
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90074

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenAI image generation fails with a bare `HTTP 401` / `Missing scopes` error that does not say which route or credential OpenClaw used when explicit `models.providers.openai` settings select the direct Images API.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who hit a 401/403 on OpenAI image generation now see the selected route, endpoint, credential class and credential source in the error (or `configured-header` when configured auth headers replaced the resolved credential). When explicit `models.providers.openai` settings pin the direct route, the message also names the `baseUrl`/`api` settings that switch to a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile instead. The original error keeps its class, status and detail; 429 and other statuses are unchanged. Routing precedence is unchanged; no config migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The clawsweeper review on the issue recommends keeping explicit provider settings authoritative and making image failures identify the effective transport and credential class. This PR does only that: on a 401/403 from the direct Images API route, the existing `ProviderHttpError` keeps its class and status (failover classification is unaffected) and gets a short route suffix appended. Query strings are dropped from the shown endpoint, header values are never shown. Credential attribution compares the final request auth header with the resolved credential, so `headers.Authorization` / `request.auth` overrides are reported as `configured-header`. Other status codes and the Codex Responses route are unchanged. The helpers live in a new sibling module `image-generation-diagnostics.ts` (the existing sanitizer moved there unchanged), so the provider file shrinks and the large test file is untouched.

Changed since the review of `33833df6d19`: the suffix is built only from facts resolved before the request (route, resolved credential, explicit direct config), and the OAuth advice depends on the explicit config instead of a profile lookup. Nothing reads the auth store after the request fails, so another provider's pending migration (`AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError`) can no longer replace the HTTP 401/403/429. The annotation runs only for the Images API response itself, not for later image URL downloads. Current `main` is merged in; the conflict in `image-generation-provider.ts` was resolved onto the async auth preparation from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169111 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169714

## Evidence

Real `openclaw infer image generate` runs from built checkouts (`pnpm build`) of the previous head `33833df6d19` and this head `214e40e5f8d`, with real HTTP transport against a loopback Images API stub that answers 401, 403, 429 or 200. Every run uses a fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` whose agent still holds a legacy Anthropic profile awaiting migration (the CLI logs `requires legacy credential migration; affected providers: anthropic`), explicit `models.providers.openai` (`baseUrl` = stub, `apiKey` synthetic), and runs inside a network namespace that only has `lo` (`api.openai.com` does not resolve). Each case made exactly one `POST …/v1/images/generations` with `Bearer synthetic-openai-key`; the auth profile file was unchanged afterwards.

The standalone CLI activates a secrets runtime snapshot for the agent before provider auth (`prepareLocalCapabilityAccountSecrets`). To exercise the reviewed case (no prepared `authStore`, no runtime snapshot), these runs skip that one step in the built output of both heads (one added `return;`; diff, restore and checksum check are in the logs):

| CLI run, no runtime auth snapshot | 401 | 403 | 429 | 200 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| previous head `33833df6d19` | Anthropic migration error replaces the HTTP error | same | same | image written |
| this head `214e40e5f8d` | HTTP 401 error + route suffix | HTTP 403 error + route suffix | HTTP 429 error, unchanged | image written |

With the CLI unchanged (snapshot active), both heads kept the HTTP error for 401/403/429; this head adds the explicit-route advice to the 401/403 suffix.

<details>
<summary>CLI output, 2026-10-15 (UTC)</summary>

```text
# previous head 33833df6d19, no runtime snapshot, stub answers 401 (POST 00:58:01Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: Auth profile store …/state/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; affected providers: anthropic; run openclaw doctor --fix.
# same message for 403 (POST 00:58:08Z) and 429 (POST 00:58:15Z)

# this head 214e40e5f8d, no runtime snapshot, stub answers 401 (POST 00:58:24Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 401): Missing scopes: api.model.images.request [type=stub] (route=images-api url=http://127.0.0.1:35789/s401/v1/images/generations credential=*** source=models.json; explicit models.providers.openai settings select the direct Images API. To use a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile instead, set baseUrl "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex" and api "openai-chatgpt-responses", without apiKey, auth "api-key", or auth headers)
# 403 (POST 00:58:28Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 403): Project does not have access to model gpt-image-2 [type=stub] (route=images-api url=http://127.0.0.1:35789/s403/v1/images/generations credential=*** source=models.json; explicit models.providers.openai settings select the direct Images API. …)
# 429 (POST 00:58:33Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 429): Rate limit reached for images per minute [type=stub]

# CLI unchanged (snapshot active), previous head 33833df6d19, 401 (POST 00:56:03Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 401): Missing scopes: api.model.images.request [type=stub] (route=images-api url=http://127.0.0.1:34331/s401/v1/images/generations credential=*** source=models.json)
```

</details>

Provider-module counter-check with the seven cases from the review (401/403/429 with and without a prepared store, plus 200; real auth-profile owner, real loopback HTTP): previous head 4/7 (the three no-store cases end in `AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError`), `main` 7/7, this head 7/7. Re-adding an eager post-failure store read to this head makes the new no-store tests in `image-generation-provider.direct-errors.test.ts` fail 3/3.

<details>
<summary>Earlier live run against api.openai.com (2026-10-06, previous head; the advice wording has changed since)</summary>

Setup as in the issue: `models.providers.openai = { baseUrl: "https://api.openai.com/v1", api: "openai-completions" }`, an `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment, a ChatGPT OAuth profile in the auth store (synthetic token), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Before (`origin/main`) | `OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 401): Incorrect API key provided: syntheti****cess. … [request_id=req_b37ec54f…]`, no route or credential |
| After, resolved credential | same text plus `(route=images-api url=https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations credential=oauth source=profile:openai:chatgpt; … set baseUrl "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex" and api "openai-chatgpt-responses" …)` |
| After, plus `headers.Authorization` in provider config | OpenAI echoes the header key (`sk-proj-****…roof`), message reports `credential=configured-header source=models.providers.openai` instead of the profile |
| Hint followed (`baseUrl` + `api` as suggested, `OPENAI_API_KEY` still set) | `image auth selected: provider=openai mode=oauth transport=codex-responses …`; request goes to the ChatGPT backend (its 401 comes from the synthetic token) |

The runs also showed what the bare message hid: with the issue's config the OAuth profile token, not `OPENAI_API_KEY`, was sent to the Platform Images API, which is consistent with the `Missing scopes: api.model.images.request` from the original report. Whether that credential choice should change is the open precedence decision on the issue; this PR does not change it.

</details>

Tests (this head):

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/openai --maxWorkers=1` (Linux, 2 shards): 96 files, 1152 passed, 1 skipped, 416 s wall.
- `pnpm test` on `image-generation-provider.direct-errors.test.ts`, `image-generation-diagnostics.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.auth.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.url.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.tls.test.ts` (`--maxWorkers=1`, macOS): 84 passed, 38.6 s wall.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `npx oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean.
- Baseline ratchets: line-cap, assertion-safety, database-dialect, test-timeout-race and test-mock-exports OK locally against the merge base; CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` green on this head. Its `OPENCLAW_* count 455 exceeds budget 454` warning comes from `main`; this diff adds no `OPENCLAW_*` name.
- `codex review` against the merge base: no findings.

Gaps: the stub stands in for the OpenAI service, so no authenticated OpenAI call was made. The no-snapshot runs change one line in the built CLI to reach the reviewed provider path. CLI output masks the credential class (`credential=***`) because the log redactor treats `credential=` as a secret assignment; the error itself carries `credential=api-key` (asserted in the tests) and `source=` stays visible. Not tested through a running Gateway.

prs.title: fix(ui): locale refresh fails for every locale after adding a source-only locale
prs.body:
Related: #62063

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Control UI Locale Refresh run fails since Swedish (`sv`) was registered as a source-only locale, so no locale refresh (and no `sv` translation memory) can land on `main`.

## User Impact

The post-merge locale refresh can bootstrap `sv.tm.jsonl` and publish the ~90 pending translations for every other locale again. `pnpm ui:i18n:check` stays strict: it keeps failing until that generated refresh PR lands, which is the intended parity gate for release validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

#62063 followed the documented source-only flow from #131015: register the locale, omit generated memory, and let the refresh workflow create it. The refresh matrix runs `sync --locale <x> --write` per locale, and each worker then rebuilds the catalog fallback baseline in scoped (`allowCatalogDrift`) mode. That baseline builder still threw when **any** sibling locale's memory file was absent, so every non-`sv` worker failed with `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/sv.tm.jsonl does not contain sv translations`. The `sv` worker itself succeeds (it writes its own memory first), but `finalize` requires all workers, so nothing is published.

The scoped worker's baseline output is not part of its artifact; the finalize job rebuilds it after fan-in. Scoped sync now skips a sibling whose memory file does not exist yet. Absent memory stays fatal for the aggregate `sync --write` and `check`, and empty/malformed memory stays fatal everywhere.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `origin/main` `1a8dcc0b488`: `OPENCLAW_CONTROL_UI_I18N_AUTH_OPTIONAL=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts sync --locale de --write` failed with `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/sv.tm.jsonl does not contain sv translations` (same error as every non-`sv` job in refresh runs 38650341262 / 38632178442 / 38658532861; the `sv` job succeeds after ~90 min).
- With this change the same command exits 0 (`catalog: fallback_keys=113 fallback_pairs=2249`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` still fails on the missing `sv` memory, by design (strict parity; release FRV and generated-memory PRs run it strictly).
- `pnpm test test/scripts/control-ui-i18n-verify.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 passed, 7.4s wall (~2s test time). Test now pins: absent memory tolerated only in scoped sync, fatal for write and check; malformed memory fatal in scoped sync.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/control-ui-i18n.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed (48s wall).
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, `pnpm check:script-erasability`: passed.

Release note: `release/2026.10.10` also needs the generated locale refresh output (including `sv.tm.jsonl` and the pending keys) to pass strict `pnpm ui:i18n:check`; this change only unblocks generating it.

prs.title: feat(approvals): configurable exec approval outcome echo
prs.body:
Related: #113262

Replaces #113357, which was closed as stalled without real-behavior proof. This
rebases the change onto current `main` (upstream refactored `handleResolved`,
so the previous diff no longer applied) and ships the missing proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Every resolved forwarded exec approval posts a second message to the chat target
(`Exec approval: Allowed` / `Exec approval: Denied`). In busy rooms that
follow-up can dominate the bot's traffic, and the strings were hardcoded with no
config key to suppress them.

## User Impact

User impact: operators forwarding exec or plugin approvals can now set
`approvals.exec.outcome` (or `approvals.plugin.outcome`) to `"none"` and resolve
approvals without the extra decision message landing in chat.

- `"message"` is the default and keeps today's behavior exactly.
- `"none"` suppresses only the resolved-decision follow-up. The approval prompt
  and its expiry notification are unaffected, and the decision stays queryable
  through `/approve` and the CLI.
- No migration and no breaking change: the field is optional and defaults to the
  current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The forwarder always published the resolved payload from `handleResolved`. This
adds a single configuration decision between resolution and outbound delivery.
The knob lives on the existing forwarding config next to `mode` and `targets`,
and is shared by exec and plugin forwarding because both use the same pipeline.

Scope is **forwarded approvals only**. Native approval clients — reaction
shortcuts, DM cards, and same-chat `/approve` — publish their own resolved
outcome through their channel adapter, and are intentionally unaffected. The
approval decision is still applied in every case; only the extra chat message is
suppressed. A `"update"` mode that edits the original prompt instead of posting a
new message is not included: it needs per-delivery message-id tracking plus edit
support on every forwarded channel.

## Evidence

Reproducible validation transcript against production code. Neither the forwarder
nor the config schema is mocked; only the outbound `deliver` boundary is.

```
$ pnpm test src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "forwarding outcome"

 ✓ keeps publishing the decision when outcome is unset (default)   23ms
 ✓ keeps publishing the decision when outcome is message            3ms
 ✓ suppresses the decision echo when outcome is none                2ms
 ✓ still releases the pending expiry when outcome is none           2ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 40 skipped (44)
```

`suppresses the decision echo` observes the delivery count at the channel
boundary: 1 delivery (the prompt) with `outcome: "none"` versus 2 (prompt plus
decision) by default and with `"message"`.

**Regression guard.** Reverting only the gate in `exec-approval-forwarder.ts` makes
exactly the two behavior tests fail and no other:

```
 Tests  2 failed | 42 passed (44)
 × suppresses the decision echo when outcome is none
 × still releases the pending expiry when outcome is none
```

The expiry test guards a real leak: `pending.settle()` is what removes the pending
entry **and** clears its expiry timer, so a suppressed outcome still settles with
a no-op terminal. Returning before `settle` would leave the entry in the registry
with its timer armed and fire an "expired" notice for an already-resolved
approval.

**Gates**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 44 passed, 0 failed (22.7s wall) |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | passed |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | all lanes passed |
| `pnpm exec oxlint` (changed files) | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` (changed files) | clean |
| `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` | 1282 config fences validated against the schema |

**Test cost.** The four new tests are 30ms total; the file's measured wall time is
22.7s with 1 worker, dominated by transform, not by the added cases.

**Target boundary.** What the knob does and does not touch:

| Path | Affected |
|------|----------|
| Forwarded approval decision echo (`approvals.exec` / `approvals.plugin`) | Yes — suppressed by `"none"` |
| Forwarded approval prompt delivery | No |
| Forwarded approval expiry notification | No |
| Native reaction shortcut outcome | No — channel adapter owns it |
| Native DM card outcome | No — channel adapter owns it |
| Same-chat `/approve` confirmation | No — channel adapter owns it |
| The approval decision itself | No — still applied |

**Gap.** No live-channel proof: the `deliver` boundary is mocked, which is
isolated channel-boundary evidence rather than a live Matrix/Slack run. The issue
asks for a Matrix deployment, and confirming it there is the natural follow-up
before treating this as resolving the reported room noise.

prs.title: fix(feishu): quick-action and confirmation cards fail to send
prs.body:
Fixes #79824.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Feishu quick actions or a command-confirmation card receive no card because those two producers still emit a V1 action row inside a schema 2.0 card.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the supported V2 column/button row in the current quick-action and approval producers. Button labels, styles, command envelopes, actor/chat/session binding, expiry, and callback policy stay unchanged.

This updates the original fix to current main. Native-card normalization and presentation buttons already avoid legacy action rows, so their current owners and the old outbound implementation are not changed. Approval persistence, inbound forms, and streaming are outside this repair.

## User Impact

Quick-action menus and their confirmation cards no longer contain the legacy row rejected by the V2 schema. Confirm/cancel behavior and existing actor, conversation, expiry, and duplicate-callback safeguards are preserved.

## Evidence

- Current baseline `83c1767446cb101f239cbed430524e2934556ebe`: the candidate regression suite reports **8 failures** against unchanged production code.
- Candidate: **215 focused/adjacent tests pass**, including actual produced-button confirm/cancel, wrong actor/chat, expiry, and duplicate handling.
- Real producers, production JSON serialization, and callback dispatch were exercised through a **local HTTP schema fixture**: launcher, direct approval, and metadata-produced approval reject legacy rows before the fix and accept the V2 rows after it.
- Independent P0–P2 source review is clean. Scoped repository checks and exact-head/native landing receipts are linked in the current proof comment.
- **Limitations:** the HTTP schema validator and transport are controlled fixtures, not the authenticated Feishu service. No current-head visual render or production message was attempted; no Feishu credentials or operator runtime were used.

### Original contributor evidence and credit

Original fix and live reproduction by **@xiabee (Yunjie Xiao)**; original commit ancestry is preserved, including `09ecc9eba006808b5a679454183083daecbfd12e`. The maintainer port changes only the remaining current producers and focused tests.

The contributor reported a May 9, 2026 production hot-patch experiment on OpenClaw 2026.5.7 / Kylin Linux with the Feishu Windows client. Before that rewrite, the service returned `230099 / 200861 / unsupported tag action`; afterward, delivery recovered and a button callback reached the agent:

```text
Before: ErrPath: ROOT -> body -> elements -> [1](tag: action);
        cards of schema V2 no longer support this capability
After:  Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed
        handling structured card action feishu.payload.button
```

That historical report supports the schema diagnosis; it is **not** a current-head live validation or a claim that every old outbound path remains defective.

[Current exact-head proof, raw artifacts and landing status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79832#issuecomment-5681181015).

prs.title: feat: support picking a specific on-device TTS voice for Talk Mode
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves On-device Talk Mode text-to-speech on iOS and macOS always fell back to Apple's low-quality default voice, even when a user had downloaded and selected an Enhanced or Premium voice in Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content. macOS had no on-device voice or speech settings UI at all. ## Why This Change Was Made On-device synthesis only ever resolved a voice via `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language:)`, which returns Apple's undocumented per-language default and ignores any specific voice the user picked. This adds a specific-voice picker (enumerated via `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()`) to both platforms' Talk Mode settings, filtered by the current recognition language, with graceful fallback to the previous language-only behavior if a selected voice is later uninstalled. macOS gains a new "Speech" settings section for this. Investigated and intentionally did not attempt to support selecting Siri voices specifically: Apple does not expose Siri voice identity to any third-party app via `AVSpeechSynthesizer`/`AVSpeechUtterance` on any current iOS version (confirmed via WWDC20 session 10022 and Apple engineer forum responses) — even `prefersAssistiveTechnologySettings` silently substitutes a same-language non-Siri voice. This is a permanent Apple platform restriction, not a gap in this change. A macOS global keyboard shortcut to toggle Talk Mode was developed alongside this but is being split into its own follow-up PR to keep this PR to one topic, per repo policy. ## User Impact Users can now pick a specific downloaded Enhanced/Premium on-device voice for Talk Mode in Settings, on both iOS and macOS, instead of always hearing the default system voice. ## Evidence - Full `OpenClawKit` shared package suite: 1311 tests / 101 suites, all passing. - Focused iOS Swift Testing suites (`TalkSystemVoiceSelectionTests`, `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, `TalkSpeechLocaleTests`) green via `xcodebuild test` on iOS Simulator; one pre-existing, unrelated locale-dependent test failure confirmed present on `main` before this change (`git log -p -S` verified) and unaffected by this diff. - macOS `SettingsViewSmokeTests` and `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests` green via `swift test`. - Manual on-device verification on a physical iPhone (iOS 26.6, Russian system locale) and the macOS app: downloaded Enhanced voices via system Accessibility settings, selected one in the new OpenClaw picker, triggered Talk Mode with no external TTS provider configured, and confirmed the selected voice (not the default) was used for playback on both platforms. ### Screenshots macOS — picker showing installed voices, "Yuri (Enhanced)" selected: iOS — same picker in a Russian-locale device, "Ruslan" selected: ### Fixes from review Two issues found during this review round, both fixed and covered by new regression tests: 1. **Directive-language override bug**: an explicitly-picked voice was applying even when a Talk directive requested a different language mid-conversation (e.g. a French reply could be spoken in a picked English voice). Fixed in `TalkSystemSpeechSynthesizer.resolveVoice` — an explicit voice now only applies when its primary language subtag matches the resolved synthesis language. 2. **Doubled quality suffix**: the macOS screenshot above was captured before this fix and shows the bug it caught — Apple's own `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.name` already includes a localized quality suffix for many modern Enhanced/Premium voices (e.g. "Yuri (Enhanced)", Russian "Милена (улучшенный)"), so appending our own suffix doubled it. Fixed in `TalkSystemVoiceCatalog.label(for:)` to detect an already-decorated name and skip the extra suffix.

prs.title: fix(oauth): report authorization received instead of completion at code capture
prs.body:
Closes #127268

## What Problem This Solves

Six bundled local-browser OAuth flows tell the callback browser that OAuth/authentication is complete as soon as a valid code is captured, before token exchange and credential construction can still fail — so a later exchange failure leaves the operator holding a browser page that already claimed success while the CLI reports no provider-auth result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture-time pages now report only the established fact (`Authorization received` heading in the shared `oauthSuccessHtml`, `authorization received` titles in the Chutes/MSTeams/Meet/OpenRouter capture pages, factual OpenAI message text). Terminal `progress.stop("… OAuth complete")` calls are untouched — those run post-exchange. No signature changes, so no SDK baseline/entrypoint churn; the `oauthSuccessHtml` doc comment now states its capture-time semantics.

## User Impact

Operators watching the callback browser see `Authorization received … while sign-in finishes` instead of a premature completion claim; a subsequent exchange failure no longer contradicts already-rendered success.

## Evidence

- Updated `openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts` callback-body assertion to the new message; `provider-oauth-runtime.test.ts` escaping tests use pass-through titles and are unaffected.
- All touched files pass an esbuild transform check; local vitest lane cannot run in this Windows checkout (rolldown native binding failure at config load), so CI runs the affected suites on the exact head SHA.

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose outbound session key to channel adapters
prs.body:
Related: #117210

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin outbound adapters cannot correlate a send with the canonical agent session even though the delivery pipeline already carries that session context. Plugins currently have to reconstruct or omit that relationship.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an optional `sessionKey` to `ChannelOutboundContext` and forwards `OutboundSessionContext.key` through the existing channel-handler boundary. The field is additive and omitted when no session is present, so existing adapters and callers keep their current behavior.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can make session-aware outbound decisions and correlate sends with the originating session without deriving identity from unrelated fields. Existing channel adapters remain source-compatible.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `forwards the canonical session key to plugin outbound adapters`
- Focused regression test passes under Node 25.9.0.
- `pnpm build` passes under Node 25.9.0.
- Full `deliver.test.ts` result improved from 3 failures before the implementation to 2 pre-existing media-staging failures after it; the new regression changed from red to green.
- Static diff scan found no environment-specific literals or credential values.

AI-assisted: Yes. The contributor reviewed the implementation, test results, and final diff.
