prs.title: fix(gateway): warn and retry raw close on Control-UI media handle failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`handleControlUiAssistantMediaRequest` in `src/gateway/control-ui.ts` served every Control-UI image/audio/video request from a `FileHandle` and closed it through `closeOpenedHandle`, which discarded any failure with `.catch(() => {})`. The read stream is created with `autoClose: false`, so that explicit close is the only thing that releases the descriptor. A rejected close therefore leaked one descriptor per affected media request with nothing in the logs; the same silent swallow sat in the `meta` probe path in `resolveAssistantMediaAvailability`. In a long-running gateway the accumulation ends at the process descriptor limit, where config reads, state writes, and new connections all start failing for every user — with no trace pointing at media serving.

## Why This Change Was Made

A close failure is exactly the kind of outcome that must be recorded where it happens instead of being inferred later from unrelated `EMFILE` errors. Both close sites now go through one helper, `closeAssistantMediaHandle`, which logs a `warn` on the `gateway/control-ui` subsystem logger and then retries the raw descriptor close. The retry needs the numeric descriptor captured *before* `FileHandle.close()` is called, because the promise API clears `fd` before the underlying close settles — reading `handle.fd` after the rejection yields `-1` and no fallback is possible. A single shared helper keeps the two paths from diverging and keeps `handleClosed` semantics untouched: the flag still prevents concurrent close attempts from the stream `end`/`close` and response `close` handlers.

## User Impact

- A failed media handle close is now visible in gateway logs instead of silent.
- The descriptor is retried rather than abandoned, so a rare close failure no longer walks the process toward descriptor exhaustion that takes down the whole gateway.
- No behavior change on the success path: the same handle lifecycle, the same response bytes, no new config or public surface.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/control-ui.ts`: `closeOpenedHandle` sets `handleClosed = true` and then awaited `opened.handle.close().catch(() => {})`; the flag is set even when the close throws, so no later handler retried it. The `finally` block in `resolveAssistantMediaAvailability` had the identical swallow.
- The stream in the same function is created with `autoClose: false`, and its `end`/`close`/`error` handlers plus the response `close` handler all delegate to `closeOpenedHandle` — confirming the explicit close is the sole descriptor release path.
- `FileHandle.close()` resets its internal descriptor before the underlying close resolves, which is why the helper reads `handle.fd` first and guards the fallback on `fd >= 0`; the raw `fs.close` callback logs its own failure rather than swallowing a second error.
- Logging matches the surrounding gateway convention: a module-level `createSubsystemLogger` and `log.warn(\`...: ${String(err)}\`)`, as in `src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts` and `src/gateway/config-reload.ts`.
- Accepted tradeoff, noted for reviewers: the raw retry can target a descriptor the runtime already released for error classes such as `EIO`. The alternative is an unbounded, invisible leak, so the retry is bounded to one attempt and logged.

Fixes #116346

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix: defer aborted delivery recovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- leave an aborted delivery recovery pending instead of recording a failed attempt
- preserve existing failure accounting whenever send evidence exists or the queue row was already finalized
- cover retry budget, queue state, audit events, and recovery logging with a regression test

## Root cause

The recovery catch path invoked `onFailed` and persisted a queue failure for every thrown error. An `AbortError` commonly represents shutdown or cancellation rather than a provider delivery failure, so it consumed retry budget and stored a misleading `lastError`.

## Impact

Cancelled recovery work remains eligible for a later recovery pass without incrementing `retryCount`. Errors with send evidence keep the existing unknown-send safeguards, and ordinary or permanent failures retain their current behavior.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` (59 tests)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the 2026.10.10-beta.1 plugin npm preflight rejects `@openclaw/codex`, `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider`, and `@openclaw/meta-provider` because their packed artifacts contain exec sites missing from the reviewed security-scan inventory ([failing run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38662472813), candidate `d6105820e06`).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Release tooling only: the beta plugin publish preflight can pass for these three plugins again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each new finding is an existing first-party process launch that the bundler moved into a new chunk (or a new plugin entry), all reviewed against source:

- `@openclaw/codex` `dist/.setup/installed-probe-<hash>.mjs` (1): `extensions/codex/src/app-server/installed-probe.ts` spawns the resolved managed Codex binary with fixed `app-server --listen stdio://` args through the same reviewed `resolveCodexAppServerSpawnInvocation` used by `transport-stdio`.
- `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` `dist/.setup/managed-server-<hash>.mjs` (2): bundled `llama-server-vc-runtime.ts` `runExpand` (Windows `expand` with fixed cabinet args) and `llama-server-install.ts` `runServerCommand` (`sw_vers`, managed `llama-server --version`/`--list-devices`), both `execFile` without a shell.
- `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` `dist/.setup/media-catalog-<hash>.mjs` (1): bundled `hardware.ts` `runHardwareProbe` (`/usr/bin/vm_stat`, `/bin/df -P`, `/usr/sbin/diskutil info -plist`), `execFile` without a shell.
- `@openclaw/meta-provider` `dist/muse-login.js` (1): `extensions/meta/muse-login.ts` spawns the operator-configured Muse binary (default `muse`) with fixed `["login"]` args, no shell.

prs.title: refactor(placement): reduce SQLite work for local turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each local turn's placement claim and release already use conditional DML, but each also opens and commits a separate explicit transaction. Those four envelope statements buy no additional atomicity for the single-statement local effect.

## User Impact

Local turns do less database bookkeeping. Claim exclusivity and release behavior stay the same; there is no configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing single-statement writer path for local owners without a remote environment. Admit the caller before the statement and install the returned claim/projection facts from the committed receipt before notifying observers. Lost replies settle from the native receipt or exact persisted claim identity without replaying the write. Remote worker and remote-exec placement retain their transaction, lease, and admission behavior; PostgreSQL retains its adapter-owned transaction custody.

Known SQLite lock failures during local cleanup remain retryable after pre-effect admission. The startup-settlement regression holds a real peer writer lock through the first release attempt, then verifies cleanup and the next turn.

Removed checks and accepted edges:
- Remove the second local admission round-trip: a caller revoked after the effect was admitted can still have that bookkeeping write settle; actual execution retains its own live-authority boundary.
- Remove local precommit publication fencing: local claim authority changes when the committed receipt installs; no extra fence is maintained for the worker-to-host delivery interval.
- Skip the pending workspace-result lookup for local release regardless of returned placement state: local claims have no remote workspace result to publish.

No schema, retention, update, plugin SDK, or persisted-data contract changes. The synchronous path remains worker-only; area T1 calls are **0 → 0**.

## Measurement

Three alternating baseline/candidate pairs of the shared synthetic Gateway workload are pending. Reported counts will include all threads and per-operation attribution; no latency claim is made on the loaded host.

| Warmed per-turn metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All-thread statements, median [min–max] | Pending | Pending |
| Worker requests, median [min–max] | Pending | Pending |
| MAIN statements | Pending | Pending |
| Local claim + release statements | Expected 6 | Expected 2 |
| Local claim + release requests | Expected 2 | Expected 2 |

## Evidence

- The local placement worker test run was interrupted after more than 20 minutes of preparation without a verdict; PR CI owns the test result. Tests cover claim/release publication, competing claim identities, stale release, lost replies, refusal before the local effect, and remote admission and terminal settlement.
- Independent Codex review: initial change clean at P0–P2; contention follow-up clean at P0/P1 (two rounds total). Formatting, core type-aware lint, and diff whitespace checks passed. The obsolete local precommit-fence test was deleted. Both local test attempts were interrupted during worker preparation; neither is counted as passing.
- Final-head [CI run 38663467109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663467109) passed all 50 active jobs at `00315abe8943154ff8266877f041d6f7b7cf332a`: tests, types, source contracts, Knip, Madge, T1 and dialect ratchets. Dependency, security-review, and CI gates all passed.
- Published-driver update cell and SDK API diff are not applicable.

Current diff: 5 files, 120 insertions / 76 deletions (production +65 / −17).

prs.title: qa(subagents): cover deferred completion delivery on a busy requester lane
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A completed child can spend its entire announce budget trying to dispatch onto its requester's already-occupied session lane. In production, idle admission took 0.68 s while busy requesters admitted only after 286.9 s and 310.8 s; the announcer had already given up at about 120.1 s. A child that succeeded was therefore reported as failed because its parent happened to be busy.

The production fix for that landed separately in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136423. **This PR is now QA coverage only** — a scenario that pins the end-to-end behavior on a busy requester lane, which #136423 does not carry and which the merged unit coverage cannot reach.

## Scope Of This PR

Five files, all QA:

- `qa/scenarios/agents/subagent-completion-busy-lane-telegram-live.yaml` — the new scenario.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-session.ts` — one opt-in option on the QA Lab transcript helper (`assistantReplyText` → `assistantReplyStartLine`), added because the scenario cannot otherwise identify a real assistant reply event. Purely additive; every existing caller's result is unchanged.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-session.test.ts` — unit coverage for that option, including the failure mode it exists to remove.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts` — a catalog guard for this scenario's lane and ingress-participant contracts.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-flow-runner.busy-lane-completion.test.ts` — **new this revision.** Drives the scenario's own flow through the production flow interpreter against a simulated requester and child, so the completion oracle itself is tested rather than only inspected. No child processes, no real timers, no polling: the generated `node -e` scripts are evaluated in-process with injected filesystem, clock and timer seams.

There is **no production source change on this branch**. `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` returns exactly those five paths; `src/`, `packages/` and `ui/` are byte-identical to `origin/main`.

## What Changed This Revision

**[P2] The visible completion now requires child-only information.** Revision 27's finding was correct and is the reason this revision exists. The initiating prompt used to mint `childVisible` itself and tell the requester to send that exact string after its own marker. A requester that never consumed the steered payload could therefore satisfy every outbound-marker, tool-count, ordering and duplicate-window assertion by replaying its own instructions. `childTranscript` only proves the child finished, and the production owner reports `delivered` as soon as the wake is **queued** (`subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts`), so `delivery.status` does not close the gap either.

The fix follows the `issue-109025-completion-policy-live` pattern, adapted to this scenario's shape:

- `childResult` and `childVisible` are **no longer minted by the scenario**. The child's own readiness-barrier `exec` mints a fresh UUID the moment it observes the hold, writes it to a workspace file only the scenario reads, and prints the child's whole terminal reply line. The child learns the token by running that command and in no other way.
- The scenario reads the token out of band (`childTokenPath`, shape-checked against a UUID) and *derives* both markers from it. The read resolves inside the window the requester is still blocked in, well before its own reply.
- The initiating prompt carries the two **prefixes** and a literal `<token>` placeholder. It never carries the value. By construction it cannot: the token does not exist until after the prompt has been sent.
- The requester must publish `TELEGRAM_BUSY_CHILD_VISIBLE:<token>` using the same token out of the delivered child result. That text still differs from the child's own `TELEGRAM_BUSY_CHILD_RESULT:<token>`, so the assertion continues to separate a requester-authored send from the direct fallback echoing the child's result — while now being impossible to produce without the completion.
- A run-time assertion (`!requesterInstruction.includes(childMintedToken)`) fires before any later wait, so a future edit that puts the token back fails where the cause is legible instead of silently restoring a vacuous pass.

**[P2] The oracle fixture is now independent of wall-clock scheduling.** Revision 28's finding is one the first commit of this revision introduced, so it is fixed here rather than deferred. That fixture spawned the generated hold and barrier commands as real child processes and let the hold expire on a real 800 ms timer, then recorded `childEndedAt` from whenever the barrier promise resumed — a delayed worker or slow spawn pushes `childEndedAt` past `proofContents.finishedAt` and fails the honest-requester case despite correct token consumption. It also broke `AGENTS.md`'s test cost budget outright, which forbids new real timers, sleeps, polling and per-test process boots.

The generated command is `node -e "<script>"` and the script is the part worth exercising, so it is now evaluated in-process via `node:vm`'s `runInNewContext` with injected seams: a filesystem rooted at the temp workspace, a caller-controlled `Date.now`, and a `setTimeout` that **queues instead of firing**. Nothing is observed from the clock — one `Date.now()` reading seeds every timestamp the scenario orders, the hold's deferred release is drained explicitly *after* the barrier has minted, and the proof file's `mtime` is pinned with `utimes` rather than inherited from the write. The fixture also asserts the barrier queued **zero** timers, which is what proves it took the synchronous path and therefore has no window to be delayed past. The two production pollers are replaced with one-shot evaluations that keep the flow's own predicates and `sinceIndex` slicing and drop only the retry loop.

**The catalog source-expression guard is removed** per the review's Tests note. It pinned internal variable names and exact expressions that the flow tests already exercise behaviorally, so an identifier-only refactor would have broken it without changing behavior. `scenario-catalog.test.ts` is back to its state at `71182e8c336`, retaining the lane and ingress-participant guards.

**What the previous revision changed** is kept below for the review history.

## What The Previous Revision Changed

Both ClawSweeper Revision 25 findings were fixed, with no suppression and no renaming around the problem.

**[P1] Both retired Tasks CLI polls replaced.** The two `waitForCondition` steps invoked `runQaCli(env, ['tasks', 'list', '--json', '--runtime', 'subagent'])`. The Tasks CLI was retired by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159179 without a compatibility facade, so the first poll could never discover the spawned child and the scenario stopped before validating delivery — dead on arrival, not merely imprecise. Both polls now read the isolated Gateway's own `subagent_runs` rows through `readNativeQaSubagentRuns`, and the dependent flat fields migrate to that helper's real shape:

| Retired flat field | Native replacement |
|---|---|
| `task.status === 'succeeded'` | `run.execution.status === 'terminal' && run.execution.outcome?.status === 'ok'` |
| `task.endedAt` | `run.execution.endedAt` |
| `task.deliveryStatus === 'delivered'` | `run.delivery?.status === 'delivered'` |

The three downstream overlap assertions and the step's `detailsExpr` moved with them (`completedChild.endedAt` → `completedChild.execution.endedAt`). The completion poll is deliberately left **unfiltered** rather than filtered by `spawnedChild.requesterSessionKey`, so the existing "requester session key changed between spawn and completion" assertion keeps its meaning instead of becoming trivially true.

**[P2] Ingress now uses the leased primary participant.** `senderId: alice` matched neither a leased alias nor a tester user ID, so `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts` threw `Telegram QA sender requires primary or a named leased participant alias.` before the initiating message was ever sent. The scenario now sends as `primary`, which is the alias the adapter always creates for the leased credential itself and therefore the only ingress identity a healthy multi-participant lease can guarantee.

**One defect the review did not name, fixed alongside.** The scenario declared no `requiredChannelDriver`. `scenario-lane.ts` only excludes a scenario from a lane when that key is present, and the scenario's `channel: telegram` alone is satisfied by the **crabline** mock driver — so the scenario was eligible on a lane where no leased-participant contract exists at all, while its own success criteria claim "a real Telegram inbound turn". `coverage-report.ts` also derives the reproduce command's `--channel-driver` argument from that key, so its absence published a repro command that would run the mock driver. The scenario now declares `requiredChannelDriver: live`, which is the same key the other live Telegram scenarios (`telegram-policy-hot-reload`, `telegram-rich-inline-composition`, `telegram-prepared-delivery-recovery`) use.

**A correction owed on that revision.** The catalog guard originally went into `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog-channels.test.ts`, and that single insertion is what turned this PR from `mergeable_state: clean` into `CONFLICTING`. It was measured rather than assumed: `git merge-tree --write-tree upstream/main d8f24e28d1a` exits 0 with no conflict, while the same probe against that first commit conflicts in that one file and nothing else — `upstream/main` had removed 367 of that file's lines, including the test the guard was inserted after, so the insertion point no longer existed. ClawSweeper's Revision 26 independently asked for the same block to be trimmed. The follow-up commit did both: `scenario-catalog-channels.test.ts` restored byte-identical to `origin/main`, the two meaningful contracts moved to `scenario-catalog.test.ts` (which upstream has not touched), and the helper-name and exact-expression substring assertions dropped.

## Which Admission Path Production Takes, And Why The Scenario No Longer Picks One

Two earlier revisions tried to make the scenario *establish deferred admission*. Both were wrong, and the reviewer was right both times. The corrected reading, verified in source:

| Seam | What it does |
|---|---|
| `subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts` | When the requester is active the completion **wakes it first**, with `steeringMode: "all"`, and returns `path: "steered"` on success. The lane-serialized `agent` call below it is never reached. |
| `subagent-announce-active-wake.ts` | On `source_reply_delivery_mode_mismatch` the helper **deletes `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` and retries** — which is exactly the `message_tool_only` gate a direct-message completion sets. |
| `run/attempt-stream-prepare.ts` | The **openclaw** runtime registers its turn through `setActiveEmbeddedRun` with message injection v2 and `supportsTranscriptCommitWait: true`. |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts` | The **codex** runtime does the same. |

`execution.runtime` accepts only `openclaw` and `codex`, and both register a steerable active run. Every other refusal reason in `prepareEmbeddedAgentQueueMessage` is `no_active_run` / `stale_run` / `not_streaming` / `compacting` / `guarded_injection_unsupported` / `tool_authority_mismatch` — runtime-capability or liveness states, none of them a scenario knob.

**Conclusion: no configuration this suite can select makes a busy requester refuse the completion steer.** Asserting deferred admission would fail healthy delivery, which is precisely the merge risk this PR carried. So the scenario asserts the outcome instead of a path:

- `execution.runtime` and `config.harnessRuntime` are unset.
- **`runtimePairLane: core` stays dropped**, so the scenario cannot contribute a release-validation result before it has been executed once. The branch's catalog-count file remains identical to `origin/main`.
- The observed path is **recorded as evidence**, not asserted: `admissionPath` resolves to `separate-requester-turn` or `steered-active-run`, alongside `postReplyUserMessages` and `postReplyTools`.

## What The Scenario Asserts

A real Telegram inbound turn drives a real Gateway:

1. The requester spawns exactly one native child, then occupies its own lane with a foreground `exec` holding for 60 s (`yieldMs` 90 s, backgrounding and `process` polling explicitly forbidden).
2. The hold command writes a readiness marker the instant it starts. The child blocks on that marker in a bounded `exec` before replying, so the overlap under test is **established by a barrier, not by relative model latency**.
3. **The payload the requester must publish is minted by that same child `exec`, not by the scenario.** The barrier mints a fresh UUID when it observes the hold, records it where only the scenario reads it, and prints the child's terminal reply line. The scenario derives both markers from the recorded token; the initiating prompt carries only the prefixes. A requester that never consumes the delivered completion therefore has no way to produce the awaited text, and a run-time assertion fails the scenario outright if the prompt ever regains the token.
4. The child reaches a terminal/ok execution state while the hold is still in flight — asserted against timestamps the runtime produces: `proofContents.startedAt <= completedChild.execution.endedAt <= proofContents.finishedAt`, and `proofContents.finishedAt <= execEvent.timestamp`, which fails loudly if the `exec` had backgrounded itself at the default 10 s yield.
5. **The cutoff for everything downstream is the requester's actual visible reply event.** `readSessionTranscriptSummary(..., { assistantReplyText: parentMarker })` returns `assistantReplyStartLine`: the index of the last assistant event whose *visible* text is exactly the marker. The scenario waits for that index to exist and then slices from it. It does not use a serialized-substring probe, and it does not use an observation-time event count.
6. **No transcript summary is read before the requester's `message`-tool result is committed.** A dedicated wait re-reads the requester transcript until a successful `message` result is present, and every subsequent summary comes from that read.
7. **From the reply event onward the requester records exactly one `message`-tool send, and zero `sessions_spawn` / `exec`.** This holds on both admission paths. The user-message count in that window distinguishes the two and is reported, not asserted.
8. Across the whole session the requester used exactly one `sessions_spawn`, one `exec`, and one `message`, in that order; the child used exactly one `exec` and finished with exactly the marker its own barrier minted; the requester's own reply reaches Telegram strictly before the completion reply; and the completion appears exactly once across an 8 s duplicate window.

## Why The Cutoff Needed A Helper Option

`probeTextEndLine` is computed as `events.findLastIndex((event) => JSON.stringify(event).includes(probeText)) + 1` over the full event list, so it matches reasoning blocks and tool arguments that merely quote the same string. That matters here and not only in theory: `summarizeSessionTranscriptEvents` counts a successful tool call only when the assistant invocation *and* its result are both inside the selected slice, because `assistantToolNamesByCallId` is built from that slice. A cutoff that lands between the two silently drops a delivery that actually happened.

`assistantReplyText` matches the assistant event's extracted visible text with exact equality, and returns the index of that event rather than the position after it — so a model that emits the reply text and the completion's `message` call in the same assistant message still has its invocation inside the window. The unit test seeds exactly that shape and asserts both halves: from the reply anchor the send counts as 1; from the serialized-probe cutoff it counts as 0.

## Evidence

**Two earlier evidence tables are withdrawn, not restated.** The table pinned to head `2729a7d055b7972d96844ae3b864270d9b1f2538` was withdrawn in the previous revision. The table that replaced it was pinned to head `71182e8c336337ead86ede27c9c1909c4f3b508e` and claimed `exit[check:changed]=0` across 34 lanes; the head has moved twice since, so that number is withdrawn too and re-measured below rather than carried forward. The first commit of this revision also reported 41 lane headers at `2a689053391`; that reading belonged to that commit and is superseded by the one in the table, not restated. Everything in this section was re-run at head `2cf433a582762d3c68cc0de52fd2db7fdc70d930`, in the branch worktree, with `git 2.55` on `PATH` through a git-only shim directory (three ratchet lanes silently bail under the host default `git 2.34`, and prefixing all of linuxbrew's `bin` would swap the pinned Node).

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` | **`exit[check:changed]=0`, 41 `[check:changed]` lane headers** (`check:changed` prints no summary block on success, so the exit line plus the lane set is the whole signal) |
| `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only upstream/main HEAD` | **exit 0, empty conflict set** — unchanged in character from the reviewed base, which is also conflict-free |
| focused Vitest — the two test files this commit touches | **2 files / 12 passed · EXIT 0** (3 flow cases + 9 catalog cases, the predicted count) |
| `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` on the changed files | **clean** |
| Knip unused-file scans (production / full-tree / script) | **0 entries each** |

### The completion oracle, measured

The live scenario needs a Convex + Telegram Test Server lease a fork cannot obtain, so the oracle itself is measured by driving the scenario's **own flow** through the production flow interpreter (`runScenarioFlow`) against a simulated requester and child. The hold and barrier commands are still taken verbatim from the scenario — they are the part worth exercising — but as of this commit they are **evaluated in-process** through `node:vm`'s `runInNewContext` with injected filesystem, `Date.now` and `setTimeout` seams, not spawned. The Gateway-side reads (registry rows, transcript summaries) are simulated. Two requesters are modelled, and the only difference between them is whether the delivered completion is consumed:

| Requester | At this head | At the reviewed base `71182e8c336` |
|---|---|---|
| Publishes the token out of the delivered child result | **PASS** (`verdict: PASS`, `childMintedToken` is a UUID, `deferredCompletionCount: 1`) | **FAIL** — `timed out after 120000ms waiting for outbound marker`. The base scenario awaits a string the requester cannot derive from the child's result at all. |
| Never consumes the steered payload; replays the completed marker its own prompt already carried | **FAIL** — the flow rejects with `timed out after …ms`, which is what the committed case asserts | **PASS** — the whole scenario succeeds. `rejects.toThrow` reports *"promise resolved … instead of rejecting"*. |

(The `120000ms` in those messages is the scenario's own declared timeout being reported by a waiter that evaluates its predicate once; nothing waits for it. Before this commit the fixture clamped the same wait to a real 1500 ms, which is part of what made it scheduling-dependent.)

The second row is the finding, reproduced: **on the reviewed base a requester that ignored the completion entirely passed the scenario, while a requester that actually consumed it failed.** This head inverts both.

Each case fails for its own reason, so one red is not mistaken for proof of three. Reverting **only** the scenario YAML to `71182e8c336` and keeping the committed tests:

```
CONTROL — scenario YAML at 71182e8c336, committed tests unchanged
  honest requester          FAIL  timed out after 120000ms waiting for outbound marker
  non-consuming requester   FAIL  promise resolved instead of rejecting      <-- the defect
  prompt-leak guard         FAIL  "scenario no longer asserts that the prompt
                                   withholds the child-minted token"
```

The third case is the run-time leak assertion, exercised by injecting the leak into a cloned copy of the loaded flow (`rejects a prompt that regains the child-minted token`); on the base scenario the guard action does not exist at all, which is what that message reports. All three pass at this head.

**Test cost**, per `AGENTS.md`'s budget: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-flow-runner.busy-lane-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reported **5.86–6.20 s across five consecutive runs, all green** (Vitest's own `Duration` 3.93–4.34 s); the three cases themselves account for **0.67 s** of that, and the remainder is the wrapper's `dist` staging, which every extension-qa file pays once. Before the determinism fix the same three cases cost **4.9 s** (1741 + 2338 + 836 ms) in real child processes and real polling.

### Per-finding base-fail → head-pass, previous revision

Retained from the previous revision for the review history; these were measured against base blob `d8f24e28d1a44486da6954c292fe5580a56257c2`, not against this head.

```
=== BASE d8f24e28d1a ===
FAIL  [P1] retired Tasks CLI polls replaced
FAIL  [P2] leased Telegram participant used for ingress
FAIL  [extra, not in review] live channel driver is required

=== THAT HEAD ===
PASS  [P1] retired Tasks CLI polls replaced
PASS  [P2] leased Telegram participant used for ingress
PASS  [extra, not in review] live channel driver is required
```

**What these measurements are and are not.** They are validation-level measurements: they prove the scenario no longer calls a CLI that cannot be registered, no longer sends as an identity the live adapter rejects, can no longer be claimed by a mock-driver lane, and — new this revision — can no longer be satisfied by a requester that ignores the child's result. They are **not** an execution of the scenario against a real Gateway and a real Telegram transport, and they are not presented as one.

## Known Gap — the scenario still has not been executed end to end

I want to name this boundary exactly rather than gesture at it, and I am not claiming otherwise anywhere in this PR.

Its live lane is `qa-live-transports-convex.yml` → `run_live_telegram`, which runs `pnpm openclaw qa telegram --provider-mode live-frontier --credential-source convex --credential-role ci` in the `qa-live-shared` environment and hard-requires three maintainer-held secrets: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SITE_URL`, and `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SECRET_CI`. The Convex pair leases the real Telegram bot credential. A fork cannot obtain any of them, which is the correct behavior — so this run is a maintainer action, not a contributor one. With `requiredChannelDriver: live` declared, the previously-suggested `--channel-driver crabline` reduced-fidelity fallback is no longer an eligible lane for this scenario; that was the point of declaring it.

On the merge-risk item — *"eligible Telegram QA executions can reject healthy delivery"* — the completion oracle now requires information only the child can produce, the two defects that made the scenario unexecutable are fixed, the cutoff is a real reply event rather than a serialized substring match, no transcript summary is captured before the requester's message result is committed, the scenario still contains no assertion that discriminates between the two admission paths, and it declares no runtime-pair lane membership, so it cannot reject supported steering or contribute a misleading release-validation result before it has been executed once.

One thing the corrected oracle asks of the live run that the old one did not: the requester must copy a UUID out of the delivered completion into its `message` send. That is the same demand the merged `issue-109025-completion-policy-live` scenario already makes of a requester (it must run an `exec` command carrying the delivered token), so the pattern is established rather than novel — but it is a real behavioral requirement on the model, and the first authorized run is what confirms a frontier requester satisfies it.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes redundant infra and reply/agent bookkeeping, and stops verbose logs from retaining private reply previews and raw bash command text.

## User Impact

User impact: verbose logs retain suppressed-reply metadata and background-session identifiers without recording private reply or command text. Execution inputs and user-facing replies are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This bundles two disjoint wave-4 lanes: x05 simplifies infra migration own-write replay, process-stable OS/plugin caches, asset discovery, suspension timers, and ephemeral presence; x06 consolidates auth/outbox/kill-scope adapters and simplifies reply preparation, catalog retention, context refresh, question delivery, and redundant synchronous checks.

Main's rewritten restart-claim admission owner and its tests are kept unchanged; the overlapping x06 hunks were dropped rather than recreating the old inline implementation. Storage retains its existing SQL transactions, validation, receipts, postcommit/source-retirement checks, schema, durability, and recovery semantics. Web Push cleanup was already withdrawn from x05 and is not included.

Combined delta: **487 net production lines removed** (+207/-694), **716 net lines removed overall** (+380/-1,096), across 71 files. Production excludes tests, fixtures, test harnesses/support, declarations, and generated code. Bundle integration also removes the now-zero commands-config assertion allowance and two obsolete sixth arguments in root catalog-publication tests; production inputs are unchanged from the reviewed candidate.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Presence uses heartbeat wall time: clock corrections may temporarily retain stale rows or expire fresh rows early; updates/reconnects or restart repair the display. Process-stable OS facts require restart after unsupported hot-patching. Same-object plugin metadata changes use the directory cache's existing TTL/reset, and assets appearing after negative canonical root discovery require owner invalidation/restart.

Migration writes trust successful statements inside their synchronous transaction instead of rereading their own writes; broken drivers or out-of-contract triggers no longer get bespoke replay diagnostics. Native timer cancellation replaces synthetic canceled-callback replay fencing. Discovery/context metadata and overlapping plugin reloads may remain stale until the next refresh; configured context-limit publication still checks its current promise. Failed legacy provider discovery keeps the same-account/profile/source last-good provider view, including overlays. Registration-time answers may briefly race prompt delivery; terminal publication still closes it. Security/effect authority, durable write settlement, FIFO ordering, and cancellation remain with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Fresh bundle proof: core plus seven touched test-type graphs pass (infra, messaging, agents-root, agents-other, agents-tools, agents-sessions, gateway-methods); type-aware lint and formatting pass; runtime and Madge cycle checks both report zero; scoped presence MDX, diff-whitespace, and native schema-version checks pass (v22 unchanged). The assertion-safety ratchet passes after removing the stale zero-count commands-config allowance: 2,695 files, 6,302 grandfathered assertions. The conflict-touched restart-claim and catalog-owner suites pass 65 cases, and all three lint-suppression cases pass (505.10s wrapper including preparation and generated-source verification). Both private-text logging regressions pass (224.89s Vitest / 240.48s wrapper, two cases; 302 unrelated cases filtered). These are real owner/dispatch compositions, so cold graph preparation dominates the local timings.

Fresh independent P0–P2 review through the requested command-auth route completed with one P2 finding, declined after direct source verification: it alleges an `await notifySubagentCompletion` after capturing the run row, but that call does not exist in the module. The removed duplicate check follows synchronous `log.warn`; the later mutation rereads and validates the owner, and resume revalidates after its await. No accepted/actionable finding remains. This is a completed findings report with an evidence-backed decline, not a claim that the reviewer returned scoped-clean.

PR CI is the broad proof, including build and remaining lane coverage; no CI reruns are requested to chase green. The local full-build and broad-suite runs are intentionally left to CI on this heavily loaded host.

### First CI failure disposition

Run [38661392653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38661392653), attempt 1, tested `067948b460071c1e31a6bb528f79ac8126ef7d09`. Build, security-fast, and all other selected lanes passed except the two jobs below and their aggregate gate. This is not an all-green run.

| Failed job | Finding | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-test-types-core-5` (116183905001) | Root test calls at lines 643 and 660 still supplied the removed sixth catalog argument (TS2554). Exact root-other graph fails at bundle head and passes on main `b5432d5ef7e17bc2cb52e86cfb73e57a7014c2c6`. | Fixed bundle-owned missed callers: removed those two unused arguments with all assertions retained. The exact failed graph, targeted lint/format, and all three OAuth-retention cases pass (35.85s Vitest / 81.31s wrapper). Fresh follow-up P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. No production code changed. |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11-2` (116183757264) | Fifteen CLI cron cases across five files reach the existing missing-inference-account refusal before their mocked CLI work. Classifier says unknown because no matching compact job exists on scheduled main. | Manually investigated inheritance: the selected terminal-abort case fails identically at bundle head (76.15s Vitest / 86.83s wrapper) and clean main `b5432d5ef7e17bc2cb52e86cfb73e57a7014c2c6` (97.80s / 109.88s), with generated-source verification. The cron fixtures and authorization producer are unchanged. The required account gate is not weakened. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` (116186822780) | Aggregate of the preceding failures. | Do not relabel green; a new head is required for the actual caller fix, then remaining inherited reds require native exception evidence. |

The 455/454 environment-name budget failure reproduces on pinned bundle base `69d500b410f5d2f6ad169b9852f4d2c28cc720e0`. The bundle adds no environment names or budget increases.

The MCP case `retires timed-out shared MCP sessions before later catalog retries` fails identically on that clean main base and reviewed bundle head `4859325ab8e7ecd32457c12c285cf052eeceb44d`: the operation settles before `first initialize pid`, with an empty fixture log. The later commit only removes one stale baseline row; production/test inputs are identical. Main: 218.45s Vitest / 237.29s wrapper; bundle: 218.74s / 237.86s. Both completed generated-source verification. The test, runtime, and manager are unchanged. This fixture uses only configured static servers, so the manager returns its static lease before the x06 combined-runtime adapter. This establishes an inherited local startup failure, not a fix or a passing replay. Connection/test deadlines remain unchanged; 57 unrelated cases were filtered, not skipped in source.

Source-lane proof is retained for unchanged inputs; fresh bundle checks cover the touched type graphs, lint/format, lint suppressions, cycles, the conflict-touched restart-claim owner, catalog publication, and both private-text log regressions. Broad local lane runs were incomplete; they are not presented as all-green proof.

### Current-head CI and inherited-failure qualification

Run [38663116938](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38663116938), attempt 1, completed for `c5bb4cc570d5568a5484c0e73bf9eda5b7019cc1`: 133 terminal jobs, 844 seconds wall from first job start to aggregate completion; summed reported job wall time 27,573 seconds (parallel jobs/setup included). Build, security-fast, repaired root-other types, and every other selected lane passed.

The actual checkout is merge `03b0ed9f2bf1e3db8f2c453f6deca1ea2cc5722b`, with ordered parents main `a10ae12e01bdcb5f4214bad403edf1512bf96561` and the exact PR head. Its tree matches Git's reconstructed merge; its baseline-to-merge delta is exactly 71 files, +380/-1,096. The cron subtree is byte-identical to the inspected main replay and unchanged by that merge.

| Remaining failed job | Attribution and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11-2` (116189346193) | Same 15 CLI cron cases across five unchanged fixtures. The reporter honestly classifies this as unknown because scheduled main has no matching compact job. Manually qualified as inherited by identical head/main account-admission refusal, unchanged owning guard/fixtures, and exact tested-merge source comparison. No authorization check or test expectation is weakened. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` (116192996542) | Aggregate failure caused solely by that cron shard. Security-fast passes independently. Requires the requested native inherited-only exception; this run is not relabeled green. |

No failed job or workflow was rerun for green. The only follow-up push fixes the two concrete root-test caller errors found by the first run. Exact-head review, current-attempt failure accounting, retained artifact hashes, reconstructed checkout, and native authority/security verification govern exception admission.

## Source Lanes

Credited source lanes: **x05**, `deslop/x05-infra-database-20261014` at `d34ab5fc846aedc31e6d2d76f5be4baf19330491`; **x06**, `deslop/x06-reply-agents-20261014` at `8a633333d0d5d204bc2a514838a98b0e9a6d65dd`. Both commits are cherry-picked onto the fresh bundle base, with the rewritten restart-claim overlap omitted.

prs.title: fix: preserve follow-ups after stopping preparation
prs.body:
Fixes #172658

## What Problem This Solves

A chat prompt sent after Stop can be accepted and saved, then silently disappear while the stopped turn is still finishing preparation. The new input never reaches the follow-up queue or model execution, leaving the conversation idle without an answer.

## User Impact

A fresh prompt keeps its own cancellation and waits for the stopped attempt to release the session before running. The stopped attempt remains cancelled, and the new input remains subject to its original caller authority and the existing session lifecycle checks. This changes no permissions, configuration, schemas, timeouts, or execution placement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatch coordinator already recognizes Gateway inputs with their own turn-adoption lifecycle as eligible for queue resolution. Its cancellation selection used only the separate low-level dispatch flag, however, so ordinary Gateway input could borrow the stopped predecessor's abort signal before reaching the queue.

The correction uses that existing Gateway queue-custody decision when selecting the cancellation owner. It extends the same ownership separation already used for low-level channel successors without changing queue policy or clearing the predecessor early. The queue documentation now describes prompts accepted after Stop.

## Evidence

The new case extends the existing native chat preparation harness. It uses real `sessions.create`, `chat.abort`, and `chat.send`, real input recording and queue/settlement owners, and a deferred execution boundary that models preparation before provider work. On unchanged production source acb3f37f71f77557b3154392134ed2416e2c824a, the follow-up ACKs `started` but has no queued-turn registration; the regression fails there. The three existing successful/rejected/unavailable steering controls pass.

The corrected regression passes: the new input retains queue custody without starting a competing execution, then runs once after the original owner settles. The original operation remains aborted, the new user input is recorded once, and the follow-up emits its final response.

Changed-file formatting and lint, all selected compiler groups, and seven related test files passed. The qualified set covers 124 distinct cases, including authenticated caller, role-revocation, session lifecycle, ACP completion, worktree ownership, and the existing steering controls. The changed file ran 4 cases in 77.16 seconds of Vitest wall time (83.51 seconds through the selected-file runner, including worker preparation). CI job seconds are pending publication.

Independent review, hosted CI, and before/after browser captures remain pending. The browser scenario uses a supported preparation hook and a synthetic loopback provider with the real Gateway; it does not require a cold install or establish a cold-setup performance improvement.

prs.title: fix(release): expose Linux builder admission and retain failed bundles
prs.body:
Closes #170291

## What Problem This Solves

Linux release requests do not expose their actual downstream builder/admission in publication status, and failed packaging checks discard completed bundle bytes needed for diagnosis.

## User Impact

Release operators can follow the exact request attempt to its builder and see receiver admission separately from dispatch acknowledgement. Completed failed-build bundles are retained for 14 days as explicitly unqualified diagnostics. Signing and publication eligibility are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Linux workflow now records its request, tooling, builder, selected source, and admission outcome. The existing bounded FRV reader consumes that evidence and reports an absent child as awaiting admission, a stale-main rejection as rejected, and terminal builder results without treating them as publication qualification. Correlation titles select candidates only; authenticated receiver artifacts own admission. Historical dispatches missing an exact attempt remain unknown rather than adopting a newer request attempt.

Failure-only diagnostic uploads contain completed `.deb`/AppImage bytes, source/tooling identity, failed-check outcomes, and checksums. They never expose the artifact IDs used by signing. This reuses existing workflow artifacts and readers, with no durable cache, new recovery dispatch, permission change, or alternate signing path. Production changes implement the previously absent read-only Linux surface and its owner evidence, with focused shell and CLI regression coverage.

## Evidence

- [Observed packaging failure, run 37763337117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37763337117): build, finalization, and staging passed; packaged runtime failed; normal bundle uploads and signing/publication skipped. Its artifacts retain runtime logs but not completed bundles.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'exact Linux request|exact completed Linux bundle'`: 3 passed, 6.68s wall time. Runs production workflow shell bodies, checks exact receiver JSON and retained bundle bytes/checksums, and verifies that signing depends on the failed build and consumes only qualified artifact IDs.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/frv.release.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'correlates the Linux builder'`: 6 passed, 14.52s wall time. Exercises real CLI transport/artifact boundaries for awaiting admission, exact admission, stale-main rejection, wrong source, foreign request, and unknown historical attempt.
- Existing Windows/readback sibling scenarios passed (9 total focused FRV tests, 17.77s wall time before the final historical-attempt case).
- `pnpm test test/scripts/linux-updater-manifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'same-tag request|earlier request|requests Linux|dispatch'`: 9 passed, 11.96s wall time.
- Regression controls against pinned pre-fix main fail: admitted Linux observation is absent; failed-bundle retention has no owner step. Original source bytes were restored afterward.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, targeted script/root-test oxlint, formatting, `git diff --check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, and `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH pnpm check:workflows`: passed. Initial workflow check correctly rejected the system Python 3.9 prerequisite; the installed supported Python runtime was used without changing product code.
- Fresh independent autoreview: scoped clean at P0/P1, no actionable findings.
- Live GitHub GET proof and official contracts: [workflow-run filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs#list-workflow-runs-for-a-workflow), [workflow_run default-branch identity](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run), and [pinned artifact action](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/tree/043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a). Request creation-time filtering returned two current-day builders rather than all eleven historical runs; no head-SHA filter hides stale-main rejection.

No real release build, signing, publication, or recovery was dispatched for this PR. Retained diagnostics support exact-byte inspection/checker reruns but do not implement full requalification without rebuilding. Prior-head CI 38314104129 passed 40 jobs with 26 skipped in 991 seconds wall time. That is historical proof for 513eeb0be8e1eedfb54e70befbea93c0a2c55a11, not the corrected head. Corrected-head [CI 38504601578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38504601578) passed: 40 jobs successful, 26 skipped, 484 seconds wall time, at exact head `83221c6a3d8e4a73a164b198e0e498a069d50ee1`. The companion Linux, macOS, and Windows checks also passed on that prior head. The prior-head CodeQL check failed; the subsequent correction below cleared those annotations.

## Review follow-through

- Corrected the actionable unconfirmed-dispatch finding in `83221c6a3d8e4a73a164b198e0e498a069d50ee1`. Producer failures before any request now remain `dispatch-unconfirmed`, not `awaiting-admission`. The existing CLI table now covers the failed publisher job retaining evidence with no request ID.
- Red control: that exact CLI case failed before the correction (`awaiting-admission` versus expected `dispatch-unconfirmed`), 5.16s wrapper wall time. After correction, 12 selected Linux/Windows/publication cases pass in 28.30s (26.16s Vitest); targeted script/root-tooling lint and typecheck, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Correction delta: production +3/-3, tests +21/-22.
- Hosted request-to-builder release execution and real diagnostic upload remain unrun: they require an actual release operation, outside this review-only handoff. Existing production shell and CLI boundary fixtures establish the changed contracts; no live-after-fix release claim is made.

### CodeQL CI correction

The cache-poisoning query combines the declared `workflow_dispatch` event with selected-tag build execution, even though the existing validation dependency excludes that event. The first correction (`18e989c76fa`) made the restriction explicit on the build job; hosted analysis proved that insufficient, with the same two annotations. That attempt is not claimed as a passing fix.

Commit `03c4e7fa2b62c6d007255e660e6d99812c0750e5` separates the existing entry points: `Linux App Release` is `workflow_run`-only; manual mirror dispatch uses `Linux App Mirror` (`linux-app-mirror.yml`). The mirror job moved byte-for-byte. The shared dispatcher and effect-time authenticated writer-path contract cut over together. Builder request titles, selected-source validation, signing, shared publication concurrency, and permissions are unchanged. Frozen historical tooling keeps its original workflow contract. No scanner suppression or alert dismissal was added.

- Regression control: the existing mirror-boundary test fails before the split because the builder still declares both triggers (4.15s wrapper wall time).
- Seven focused Linux workflow/admission/retention/credential-isolation cases pass, including the real shell dispatch function's exact workflow, pinned ref/SHA, five inputs, and retained acknowledgement: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'serializes Linux manifests|detaches Linux mirror|stale Linux release|exact Linux request|exact completed Linux bundle|isolates release credentials' --reporter=dot`; 8.77s wrapper wall time, 5.93s Vitest. Authorization and dispatch transport are fixed fixtures in that route test; they do not claim live publication authority.
- Full `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`: 58/58 passed, 5.09s wrapper wall time, 3.29s Vitest, including effect-time writer/parent revocation and metadata/publication recovery.
- Script and root-test typechecks, targeted script/root-test lint, shell syntax, formatting, `git diff --check`, docs MDX (1,352 files), and `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH pnpm check:workflows` passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 AutoReview is scoped-clean for the complete split and callers.
- Follow-up delta from `83221c6a3d8`: production/config +136/-117 (net +19, mostly moving the 90-line mirror job); tests +70/-6; docs +3. No durable state or public CLI argument changes.
- `03c4e7fa2b62` encountered a concrete conflict with current main, so PR CI did not attach. Integrated pinned main `30b54f615c32a80547a6c6fd288a0c7780325a61` in `04766b04d421cd7f7ffd5b0209530c617db2a64f`. The only conflict was the workflow-test reader migration: retained main's cached `readWorkflow` and the mirror assertions. Main's source-SHA packaging and signed-input publication recovery fixes remain intact.
- Post-integration proof: 21 selected Linux/mirror cases passed (18.19s wrapper); all 58 channel-owner cases passed (18.13s); nine Linux/Windows real-CLI cases passed (28.88s). The full integrated PR received fresh P0–P2 AutoReview: all three chunks scoped-clean. Workflow checks, script and all four root-test type graphs, targeted lint, and formatting passed. The first type attempt used stale installed native-package declarations; a task-private frozen-lock install brought fs-safe/proc-safe to the versions already pinned by main, after which types passed. No dependency or lockfile changes were introduced. An unrelated blank line in main's changelog remains inherited; the PR delta against pinned main passes `git diff --check`.
- Historical head `04766b04d421cd7f7ffd5b0209530c617db2a64f`: [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38642384644) and [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38642384802) passed; aggregate scan check neutral with **zero annotations**, no suppression/dismissal. [Main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38642385593) completed successfully: 40 passed, 27 skipped. macOS and Windows companion checks passed; Linux companion failed at the source-package build deadline, addressed below. These are prior-head results, not current-head proof.

No real release build, signing, publication, recovery, or merge was dispatched for this correction. Hosted mirror dispatch remains a release-operation acceptance gap, not an executed test.





### Linux companion CI follow-through — current head `92227d1d13a14c7ca675aabf31b5ddfdf68265aa`

The red [Linux companion job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38642385077/job/116121306738) is independent of publication-report PR #170274. Native tests passed; cold canonical source packaging completed its package-declaration phase in 38m38s, then the package builder's 45-minute deadline interrupted the next declaration phase (`parentSignal: SIGTERM`, exit 143). There was no compiler diagnostic or failed native assertion at that boundary.

The same-source desktop staging change in #171117 already gave Windows a 60-minute package build budget inside a 105-minute job. Linux's outer budget increased then, but its inner package builder remained at 45 minutes. This correction applies the same existing, step-scoped budget to Linux. It retains the full canonical build, declarations, tarball integrity, install and native desktop checks. No global/default timeout, release budget, publication eligibility, runner class, dependency, or package contract changed.

prs.title: fix: doctor warns when CLI agents cannot run background review
prs.body:
Related: #163599

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: When autonomous learning is on, agents on a CLI-backed runtime such as `claude-cli` never get a background review, and `openclaw doctor` reports nothing about it.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` warns about each affected agent, so operators can see why those agents learn nothing in the background. Existing sandbox and tool-policy findings stay unchanged, and `off` mode stays quiet.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background review only counts turns on a runtime that reports its resolved model and whether `skill_workshop` was available. The embedded runner and the Codex app-server harness report both; other CLI-backed runtimes do not. Doctor now resolves each agent's runtime the same way runs do, including the auth-profile pin on the configured primary model (for example, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5@anthropic:claude-cli`), and reports agents that land on a CLI runtime. The self-learning page lists this case under "Nothing is learned".

This revision is rebuilt on current `main` after the self-learning rework and fixes the review finding: the runtime check now follows the configured auth-profile pin. Curator status from #163599 is not covered, so this PR does not close the issue.

## Evidence

I ran real `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/skill-workshop-tool-policy` commands with an isolated `HOME`, state directory, and config file. The config has four agents: `cli-pinned` (primary pinned to `anthropic:claude-cli`), `api-pinned` (pinned to `anthropic:api`), `sandboxed` (CLI-pinned, `sandbox.mode: "all"`), and `codex` (Codex app-server runtime). I ran Doctor with each auth order: API profile first, then CLI profile first. The profiles exist only in config; no credentials were used.

| Config | `main` at 64ae50243 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto`, API profile first | Sandbox warning for `sandboxed` only | Runtime warnings for `cli-pinned` and `sandboxed`, plus the same sandbox warning |
| `auto`, CLI profile first | Sandbox warning for `sandboxed` only | Same three findings; `api-pinned` and `codex` stay quiet |
| `off` | No findings | No findings |

The new finding, as Doctor prints it:

```text
agents.entries.cli-pinned.model: background review is unavailable on CLI runtime "claude-cli" because it does not report the resolved model and skill_workshop availability.
fixHint: Background review needs a runtime that reports them, such as the embedded OpenClaw runtime or the Codex app-server harness.
```

- Without the pin, as in the previous revision, the diagnostic flips both cases: no warning for the CLI-pinned agent under API-first order, and a false warning for the API-pinned agent under CLI-first order. I checked this by calling the diagnostic with and without the pin. The new regression test covers both directions, and `doctor-core-skill-workshop-check.test.ts` passes (9 tests).
- `check:changed` on this branch: core, core-test, extension, and extension-test typechecks, lint, formatting, the line-cap ratchet, and the boundary guards pass. I moved the Workshop check into `src/flows/doctor-skill-workshop-check.ts` so that `doctor-core-checks.ts` does not grow. Two gates fail on files this PR does not touch: the `OPENCLAW_*` environment variable budget (455 vs 454) and the Knip unused-export scan (8 exports elsewhere in the tree).

prs.title: fix(mcp): restore recovered tools on the first due retry turn
prs.body:
Fixes #172614

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MCP tools remaining missing for one extra turn after a failed server becomes reachable and its catalog retry is due, including after sign-in.

## User Impact

The first turn after a due retry can use the recovered server's tools. If startup still fails, the catalog remains empty for that server and reports its unavailable reason, next retry time, and reachability guidance. That turn waits within the existing connection/listing budgets; retry backoff still applies. Previously healthy catalogs retain their existing background recovery behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog owner treated a cached startup failure like a previously successful catalog and returned it while recovery ran in the background. It now awaits the existing catalog loader until that server runtime has listed successfully. This keeps recovery, bounds, diagnostics, and disposal with their existing owners; healthy sibling tool calls remain available during the wait.

No new background or deferred effects are introduced. The existing loader retains owner-scoped configuration/requester/path facts and checks runtime retirement after awaited work before publishing.

## Evidence

- Confirmed in current-main source and history: tool materialization consumes the per-server `getCatalog()` result; its due-retry path returned the failed catalog immediately. Background retries originated in `f3d94d23021b`; the last-successful-catalog contract from `1d03e5d2ce45` is preserved.
- Regression: `lists recovered tools on the first turn after a failed startup retry is due` exercises the real runtime, SDK, and startup backoff with fixture HTTP responses and a blocked listing. It checks empty tools plus an unavailable reason after failure, no early retry, and recovered tools on the first due turn.
- Updated `allows only the first failing runtime one early catalog retry before backing off` checks the awaited failed retry and its new cooldown. `retries a failed MCP catalog without stalling healthy siblings` checks first-retry recovery while an existing healthy sibling remains callable, without polling for a later catalog.
- Changed-file core oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed. Deslop: clean. Exact numstat: production +1/-1 (net 0), tests +41/-14, docs +1/-1.
- Codex autoreview (branch scope, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Used the installed shared helper because this checkout contains only the skill entrypoint.
- PR CI is the test gate and covers the regressions, affected test shards, typechecking, lint, and repository checks. Local tests, typechecks, negative controls, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. Local test wall times and lease IDs: not applicable.

Exact-head [CI run 38659449951](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659449951) passed on `4e9f4230fc3d0ac1cb144ff9481a490d1caf23ee`: all 40 executed jobs succeeded, including affected Node tests, production/test typechecks, lint, and repository checks. The final PR rollup has 61 passing checks with no failures or pending checks. No CI rerun was needed. GitHub Codex review completed without posted findings; ClawSweeper posted its maintainer opt-in notice and no code findings.

CI file results: `agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts` passed all 6 tests (Vitest 4.62s; shard wall time 6.40s, job `116177422652`); `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` passed all 58 tests (Vitest 56.11s; shard wall time 59.31s, job `116177422721`). The existing runtime suite includes real stdio/sibling transport integration; this change reuses that fixture and removes recovery polling rather than adding another process fixture.

prs.title: refactor(automations): migrate periodic heartbeats and retire the executor
prs.body:
Related: #134994. Final sequential slice of #164265, following #166889 and #167113; adopts the approved design from #135933 under Peter's October 3 and October 12 decisions.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled monitoring still has a separate heartbeat execution, delivery, and recovery path alongside Automations.

## User Impact

Existing monitors become ordinary editable Automations. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before startup after upgrading. The July-2026+ migration preserves job identity/history, scratch bytes and revisions, disabled state, schedule anchors, pending occurrences, quiet hours, allowed model selections, target routing, and tool authority. It verifies durable conversion before retiring legacy inputs and retains ambiguous input with recovery guidance. Repeated Doctor runs preserve operator edits and deleted jobs.

Migrated jobs use **standard Automations delivery**, with no `delivery.duplicateWindowMs` or `delivery.skipIfNoRoute` options. Doctor emits this notice once when the cutover receipt completes:

> Migrated heartbeats now use standard Automations delivery. Heartbeat-specific duplicate suppression and no-route skipping were removed: repeated updates can be delivered, and a missing route no longer skips the run before execution. Delivery failures follow ordinary automation handling. Review the migrated jobs' delivery settings if you relied on either behavior.

This is a **breaking plugin-SDK change**: heartbeat execution and reply exports are removed outright, without deprecated aliases. Upgrade affected plugins using `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces.md`. The deprecated `reply-runtime` export budget remains **1**. The existing nondeprecated prompt hook and protocol-v4 projections retain their documented contracts.

The approved shared-state compatibility fence now advances **22→23** so older Gateways cannot ignore migrated job policies. Main consumed version 22 for its separately approved portable ACP/cursor identities; this integration preserves that migration and the prior predicate columns. This is the same fence approved in #134994 (originally numbered 16); this cutover adds no tables or columns. Its existing regression checks schema-22 reader refusal while retaining identical stored job and catalog bytes. It preserves main’s separately landed agent schema **27**, without adding a per-agent schema migration. Keep the verified pre-update backup for rollback. Automatic updater admission normalizes supported July fields through the existing Doctor transforms; it preserves main's prior retirement of global `includeReasoning`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor conversion and periodic retirement land together because the old reconciler could otherwise recreate converted or deleted monitors. The ordinary scheduler owns periodic jobs, and the already-landed ordinary session event owner handles immediate follow-ups. The periodic runner, reconciler, dispatcher, response tool, SDK aliases, obsolete callers, and private status wrapper are deleted.

Immediate Slack interactions use ordinary occurrence receipts: failures are reported and settled. The old pre-adoption passive queue could retain a notice through a soft restart or later turn; there is no retained passive mirror or automatic failed-event replay in the new owner.

Durable migration receipts, portable Claw custody, and guarded scheduler admission account for the production growth. Idle deferral preserves unstarted slots and stream buffers; on-exit admission retains its exact receipt and command output while foreground work settles. Main's worker-backed deletion owner, terminal-write drainage, first-session identity, and memory-plugin lifecycle are preserved. Deferred notices stay with their selected scheduled occurrence and are accepted only when the complete batch fits the existing prompt limit.

Phase E's standalone memory backend remains intact, including its factory, registry, expiry, federation, and meaningful coverage. Its heartbeat-specific adapters use ordinary Automations. Protocol-v4 controls and the existing nondeprecated prompt hook delegate to ordinary job receipts; they do not retain a heartbeat executor.

The fresh-main integration preserves main's worker-owned recovery, configured-owner authority, output-accumulator deletion, cron blocker-report wording, empty-mutation worker handling, and speech-only delivery. Main’s separately landed #170716 now owns the original physical-database custody repair. This integration keeps its native-consent implementation unchanged and removes S3’s duplicate repair, without restoring repeated absence queries. Memory tests exercise main's explicit session-maintenance trigger and virtual quiet-window scheduler while retaining their retry and completion assertions.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Peter approved default-model fallback on October 12: when a legacy heartbeat explicitly selected a model outside the agent's model policy, Doctor drops that override and the migrated automation uses the agent's allowed default. Doctor records a visible migration notice naming the agent, job, dropped model, and effective default, with the next step: pick an allowed model or add it to the agent's `modelPolicy.allow`. Allowed explicit models are preserved. This avoids blocking conversion while preserving the ordinary automation permission boundary; no allowlist, grant, or configuration option is added. The original duplicate-suppression/no-route notice above remains unchanged.

Release-note context: heartbeat migration can switch a disallowed legacy model to the agent's allowed default and records the replacement with repair guidance. Ordinary automations still reject disallowed explicit model overrides. The breaking plugin-SDK export removals and standard Automations delivery change described above remain part of this release context.

## Credential-writer guard precision

The proactive receipt key now has the enforced return type `automation-default:${string}:${string}`. The credential-writer guard uses the native TypeScript template-literal API to inspect its fixed head. Only a head that cannot form a prefix of `authProfiles.store` is excluded; empty, matching, credential-prefix, plain-string, and unsafe union variants remain guarded. Trimming remains conservative, so whitespace cannot hide a credential key. This adds no allowlist, cast, indirect dispatch, or owner exception, and preserves the existing persisted keys and atomic job/receipt transaction.

The new safe case failed against the old guard; all 92 existing and added guard cases now pass (12.10s wrapper). The pre-rebase suppression guard passed 3/3 (25.15s wrapper); main's later inventory repair is incorporated; the latest suppression run and independently reproduced main inventory failure are recorded below. Independent P2 review is scoped-clean (0.98). The schema-23 package declaration and Voice Call migration descriptor are aligned; the original idle-WAL admission regression passes (241.88s wrapper), with unchanged assertions. The full failed database-worker ratchet command passes: T1 calls decrease 454→453 and deprecated-only calls stay 9; its resolved merge base is `71692b03a277790e5781705dcdfeb6f4ba0c810f`. Exact-head hosted CI remains required.

## Visual comparison

[Inspected synthetic before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167796#issuecomment-6150693557) show the scheduler diagnostics cutover and the ordinary automation policy controls. The comment names the historical capture revisions and source continuity; it does not claim a new exact-head capture or main's later layout changes. Images are embedded on this PR, and GitHub's rendered HTML plus attachment round-trips are verified.

## Evidence

The schema-cache integration correction includes active-run and pacing policy in the existing key: its regression fails before the fix and the complete file passes 13/13 afterward (schema plus suppression wrapper 94.72s), without adding fields or raising the cache budget. Independent P2 review is scoped-clean (0.98). Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. No broad local check-changed or SDK preparation is repeated. Final exact-head hosted CI remains required.

A distinct ordinary automation still refuses the forbidden override before provider invocation. Migration/profile/notice proof passes three cases (123.51s wrapper); execution proof passes (112.02s wrapper), using synthetic provider adapters.
