prs.title: feat(ui): plugin themes can ship light and dark backgrounds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin themes can recolor the whole Control UI and bring their own icons, hats, and critters, but **Appearance → Background → Theme** always shows the neutral plugin artwork, so a theme can't ship the backdrop it was designed around.

## User Impact

User impact: a plugin theme can declare `backgrounds: { "light": "...", "dark": "..." }` in `openclaw.plugin.json`, and people who pick that theme with **Theme** background artwork see the plugin's image for the current color mode, dimmed the same way a custom uploaded background is. A mode with no declared image keeps the neutral artwork. Built-in, personal, and imported themes are unchanged.

Older Gateways reject the new manifest key, so a theme that uses it needs a Gateway that includes this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backgrounds join the existing theme artwork path instead of adding a new owner:

- **Manifest:** `backgrounds` maps `light` and/or `dark` to a PNG, JPEG, or WebP inside the plugin root, using the same containment and duplicate-key rules as other artwork.
- **Gateway:** it captures each image into the plugin metadata (at most 512 KiB, the authenticated image route's cap) and checks its image signature. An invalid image drops the theme with a plugin warning, like invalid SVG artwork does. Bytes are kept as base64 because runtime metadata snapshots are deep-frozen and a Buffer cannot be frozen. The existing `plugin-theme-art` route serves them with a `background/<mode>` kind.
- **Control UI:** it fetches the image with the same authenticated artwork loader and publishes it through `--app-background-image`, which the shell canvas, session backgrounds, and the Settings preview already read. Placement, visibility, and accessibility fallbacks stay with their existing owners.
- **Dimming:** plugin images are untrusted art, so they get the custom-upload treatment instead of the built-in one. The token carries a theme-colored scrim equal to a default-strength upload's opacity (`readBackgroundOpacityLimit` × default visibility, × 0.65 in light mode), so every surface reading the token is dimmed, including the shell canvas for users who never set a background preference. Full bleed skips the extra bundled-artwork cap so the image isn't dimmed twice.

Accepted edge: the scrim is fixed at default visibility, so raising **Image visibility** above the default doesn't brighten plugin art the way it brightens an upload; lowering it still fades it. On light palettes with low muted-text contrast the image is very faint, which is also what an upload would get.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b9ef4908-ae7e-4224-b975-a3d984feb1b7)

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway built from this branch (`pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated> gateway run`, loopback), Ghost Claw installed with `openclaw plugins install <zip> --force --accept-capabilities`, captured with headless Chromium on the new session page. Background preference left unset (default canvas path).

**Before** (same theme without `backgrounds`: neutral plugin artwork):

![Before: Ghost Claw with neutral plugin artwork, real Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaabbcc4-fed2-46ce-ab21-be2bae182ff8)

**After** (dark mode, `backgrounds.dark` served by the Gateway and dimmed like an upload):

![After: Ghost Claw dark mode with its dimmed firehouse background, real Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f368ca31-6ce9-4195-be71-56e0d6a75cbf)

<details><summary>Light mode</summary>

Light mode uses `backgrounds.light`; on this palette the upload-equivalent dimming leaves it at about 2% strength.

![After: Ghost Claw light mode, real Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b15c80f5-c11f-42e5-8a61-9253d4d107b3)

</details>

Gateway receipts from that run: `GET /__openclaw__/plugin-theme-art/ghost-claw-theme/ghost-claw/background/dark` → 200 (`/light` → 200 in light mode); root token `linear-gradient(color-mix(… var(--bg-content, var(--bg)) 91.3%, transparent) …), url("blob:…")` dark, 98.1% light.

The live install also caught a real bug the unit tests missed: capturing the image as a `Buffer` made `plugins install` fail with `Cannot freeze array buffer views with elements` once the metadata snapshot was finalized. `theme-catalog.test.ts` now runs the background case through `finalizePluginMetadataSnapshot`.

Tests:

- `pnpm test src/plugins/theme-catalog.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-themes.test.ts src/gateway/plugin-theme-art-http.test.ts`: 94 passed.
- `pnpm test ui/src/app/theme-background-artwork.test.ts ui/src/components/session-background.test.ts`: 22 passed (upload-equivalent scrim math, mode switch, superseded loads, Full bleed without double dimming).
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` on all 21 changed TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt --check` on the PR's files: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (all projects) passed. Remaining failures are outside this diff: the `OPENCLAW_*` env-var budget (455/454 on the base), extension oxlint errors in untouched `extensions/agentsapi`, `extensions/anthropic`, `extensions/codex` files, and pre-existing unused exports in untouched files. The one finding in this diff (an exported test-only helper) is fixed in `4deec75`.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) on the dimming commit: scoped-clean.

auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(ui): let plugin themes ship light and dark backgrounds

Plugin themes can declare `backgrounds: { light, dark }` in the manifest with
PNG, JPEG, or WebP images up to 512 KiB. The Gateway captures and sniffs them
with the theme's other artwork, serves them through the authenticated
plugin-theme-art route, and the Control UI paints the image for the active
color mode through the existing --app-background-image token. Modes without a
declared image keep the neutral plugin artwork.

Co-authored-by: Patrick-Erichsen <20157849+Patrick-Erichsen@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ui): dim plugin theme backgrounds like custom uploads

Plugin background images now carry the same palette-derived dimming a
default-strength custom upload gets, as a theme-colored scrim layer in
--app-background-image, so every surface that paints the token (shell canvas,
session background, Settings sample) stays readable. Full bleed no longer
stacks the bundled-artwork cap on top of that.

Captured background bytes are stored as base64: runtime plugin metadata
snapshots are deep-frozen, and freezing a Buffer throws, which broke plugin
install on a real Gateway.

Co-authored-by: Patrick-Erichsen <20157849+Patrick-Erichsen@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(ui): cover plugin background dimming through its owner

Keep the scrim helper private and assert the published token from
syncThemeBackgroundArtwork in both color modes.

Co-authored-by: Patrick-Erichsen <20157849+Patrick-Erichsen@users.noreply.github.com>

prs.title: fix: speed up cold session lists with large inventories
prs.body:
Related: #172507

## What Problem This Solves

Cold session lists become slow with a large active session inventory, even when the sidebar requests only a small page.

## User Impact

Cold lists spend less Gateway CPU preparing the roster. This is a measured performance improvement; it does not establish the cause of the reported pre-auth disconnects or resolve the entire incident. No config, schema, or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preparation reads database facts in 64-row worker batches. Accepted active rows remain dirty until display materialization, so repeatedly starting readiness, acquisition, and batch selection at the beginning rescans an ever-growing prefix. Preserve a live dirty-set cursor across accepted batches, retain pending read joins, and restart traversal when registry, topology, membership, or a joined read changes readiness. Entry lineage acquisition still precedes batch reads.

## Evidence

Measured the real `sessions.list` handler with isolated SQLite state, actual row-fact workers, six concurrent clients, 25,000 active sessions, and a 200-row compact sidebar page. Temporary CPU profiling instrumentation was removed from the patch.

- Pinned main base `8f57414a3ad7`: cold requests approximately 5,353 ms; candidate approximately 3,015 ms (44% lower). Worker read time summed 676 ms before and 824 ms after, so the improvement is in roster preparation rather than faster SQLite reads.
- Main-thread CPU samples dominated by repeated readiness/acquisition scans before; those scans largely disappeared after. Event-loop maximum across initialization and requests was 836 ms before and 928 ms after: no claim that a 30-second stall or disconnect was fixed.
- Reproduced the same actual handler over 25,000 isolated sessions on v2026.10.3: cold approximately 5,417 ms, with repeated readiness/batch scans dominating main-thread CPU. Only the temporary fixture request was adapted to omit main’s unsupported `source` parameter; release production code was unchanged. The repeated scans also exist in v2026.10.1, so this is not attributed to the release upgrade.
- 39 tests passed across worker-read, selection-progress, list-page, runtime-ownership, and prepared-read suites, covering exact/bulk joins, publications during reads, topology, archive metadata, and opaque ownership. Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/session-row-projection.worker-read.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.selection-progress.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.list-page.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.runtime-ownership.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.prepared-read.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; wall time 247.46 seconds on this busy host. No new tests or CI test time added.
- Existing gated cold benchmark passed before and after; candidate wrapper wall time 76.53 seconds including compiler preparation and synthetic setup.
- Core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and format checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(codex): give the context engine a real budget for native-owned models
prs.body:
Closes #171854

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a context engine such as lossless-claw compacts far too early, and the Codex thread is replaced almost every turn, when a Codex chat on the ChatGPT login has no per-model `contextTokens` setting.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex chats without a per-model context setting now give the context engine the window Codex itself reports, for example 380,000 instead of lossless-claw's 128,000 fallback. The engine's own threshold fraction then applies to the real window, the thread-bootstrap projection is no longer cut to 24,000 characters, and threads are not replaced below that threshold. If OpenClaw has resolved a budget, it still wins. If no window has been observed yet, the budget stays unknown, as it is today. No new configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core intentionally resolves no budget for a native-owned model (`setup.ts:175`). The Codex harness already observes the real window, but it passed only the core budget to the context engine. Now:

- **At turn start** (bootstrap, assembly, projection size): the core budget, else the window Codex reported for the bound thread (`startupContextTokens`), else the operator's authored cap. The thread's reported window is used only when the thread's model is the model running this turn (a provider prefix does not count as a different model), bounded by a smaller authored cap, and only when no newer turn in the rollout superseded it without reporting a window. A same-generation model switch keeps the thread, and a failed switch leaves the old window as the last report.
- **At turn end** (the durable completion candidate): the core budget, else the window Codex reported **during this turn** (`contextTokensSource` `runtime` or `runtime-configured`), else the authored cap. A `resolved` value is only the startup estimate and is ignored.

The durable outbox already persists `runtimeContext.tokenBudget` and `modelContextWindow` and forwards them to `commitTurn` across recovery and retry. This change only supplies the producer value.

The open PRs #158740, #171359, #171495 and #171707 cover chats with an authored cap. This PR covers the unconfigured case and touches the same two consumers, so it may need a rebase on whichever of them lands first.

## Evidence

**Tests** (`node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run …` on `56eaa4ca4fc` plus this branch):

- `selection.test.ts`, `run-attempt.context-budget.test.ts` and `startup-binding.test.ts`: 118/118 pass. `tsgo` core, extensions, extensions-test and src-test shards, `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- The new cases fail without their source change:
  - Reported window, operator cap, and startup estimate ignored (`selection.test.ts`): fail on `main`, because `main` passes no budget.
  - Window from a different model on the same thread, a provider-qualified model name, and a newer turn that reported nothing (`run-attempt.context-budget.test.ts`): against the previous commit the qualified-name case got `undefined` instead of 258400 and the newer-turn case got 258400 instead of `undefined`.
  - Authored cap lowered below the thread's reported window (`run-attempt.context-budget.test.ts`): without the bound, `expected 258400 to be 32000`.
  - Unrefreshed startup estimate at turn end: before the source check, the engine got `tokenBudget: 380000` and `modelContextWindow: 380000` from a `resolved` estimate (expected undefined / 200000).
- Controls: a resolved host budget still wins over a reported window. With no observation and no cap, the budget stays undefined.
- Existing durable coverage that carries these values to `commitTurn`: `context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts` (accept → drain → commit, and retry after a failed commit).

**Live A/B** (from #171854): two throwaway Gateways, real `openai/gpt-6-luna` on the ChatGPT login, lossless-claw 1.1.0, threshold 0.05, 6 turns, no per-model config.

```
baseline  commitTurn tokenBudget=128000 modelContextWindow=200000 threshold=6400
          compaction after turn 4; turn 5: NEW THREAD reason=context-engine-binding-mismatch
patched   commitTurn tokenBudget=258400 modelContextWindow=258400 threshold=12920
          no compaction; turns 2-6 on one thread
```

**Production, first commit of this branch, 14 Oct**: a new Codex session (gpt-6-luna, lossless-claw) logged `threshold: selected phase=commitTurn … tokenBudget=380000` on turns 1 and 2, and `assemble: done … tokenBudget=380000` on turn 2. Before the change, the same deployment logged `tokenBudget=128000 modelContextWindow=200000` for every Codex turn. The model check, the newer-turn check and the turn-end source check were added after that run and have not run live.

**Gaps:**
- No `startupContextTokens` with `appServer.homeScope: "user"` (rollouts live outside the agent's Codex home) or on the first turn of a new session. Assembly there has no budget, as on `main`; the turn-end value still arrives.
- No measurement of prompt-cache reuse.

AI-assisted (Claude, with a Codex review pass); I reviewed and ran the changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inconsistent modal completion-button placement when dialogs show validation, status, long content, or narrow-screen layouts.

## User Impact

One plain light-DOM action row uses the existing native modal stylesheet across Solid, retained Lit callers, and the Workboard plugin. prs.title: fix: distinguish workflow approval and exception capabilities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading operator capability reports when a CI-exception policy read is unavailable or a release environment approval read fails.

## User Impact

Operators get route-specific guidance without grant changes: ordinary green-CI landing remains available to MAINTAIN writers, while an unreadable exception policy stays blocking. Release monitoring distinguishes no pending approval, unavailable status, and false/unknown caller approval capability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending environment approvals describe the authenticated caller, so their reads must not use the public-evidence anonymous rate-limit fallback. Failed reads now remain unknown without stopping validation monitoring, and only an explicit `current_user_can_approve: true` produces an approval command. Public release evidence keeps its existing fallback.

The existing classic-protection refusal now explains the supported ordinary green-CI alternative and distinguishes repository writes, organization membership, policy reads, CI bypass, environment approval, and production deployment. No landing admission, permissions, credentials, environment approvals, or deployment rules change; generic 404 and hidden/null policy responses still cannot prove absence.

## Evidence

- Final release checklist suite: 147 passed, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`, 19.79 seconds wall time (17.70 seconds Vitest duration). Existing fixtures account for most runtime; the five added diagnostic cases use fixed external I/O and no real waits.
- Native landing/refusal boundary: 7 passed across the merge outcome, prior-CI, and REST suites; 32.80 seconds wall time. Includes ordinary MAINTAIN green-CI completion without organization/exception-policy reads and preserved REST policy refusals. Remaining native compositions are left to PR CI.
- Regression reproduced before the fix. A negative control removing only the production authenticated-read option fails because the anonymous caller's `canApprove: false` incorrectly replaces unavailable status; the repaired monitoring path passes. An initial fixture assertion expected an explicit GraphQL transport field that the existing receipt omits; that assertion was corrected without changing production admission.
- Scripts typecheck, root-scripts typecheck (15.5 seconds), targeted scripts/root-test lint, formatting, docs MDX, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent AutoReview: no actionable P0/P1 findings; final test-strengthening and style corrections received hands-on review.
- Read-only writer-route GitHub contract probe returned HTTP 200 with an empty pending-deployment list. No live approval or release/deployment mutation was performed; approval/throttle variants use captured fixed response contracts.
- Exact-head hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659876414) succeeded on `7c3d22fcbcc605ecd6a6f14805e02c7a2d8f2962`; the native CI watcher returned GREEN and a fresh GitHub rollup had no pending or failed checks. The [changed-test job 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659876414/job/116178877173) took 228 seconds and [changed-test job 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659876414/job/116178877014) took 322 seconds; these include job setup/teardown, not per-file test durations. Per-file CI seconds were unavailable through the default log-output route. No reruns or gate exceptions were used.
- Listed-owner involvement remains a governance blocker: requesting the CODEOWNERS `openclaw/openclaw-release-managers` team was unavailable (REST 422: team is not a repository collaborator; GraphQL did not resolve the qualified slug). Review requests were reconciled before the explicit REST attempt. No permission or credential changes were made; this PR is not claimed merge-ready.

No merge or release is requested by this PR.

prs.title: fix(pr): accept committed renamed conflict resolutions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native PR review transitions refusing a committed conflict resolution when the conflicted file was renamed, as encountered while preparing #171806.

## User Impact

Maintainers can continue the native review and preparation workflow after a committed rename conflict without removing Git conflict metadata or abandoning the recovery journal. Application behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git retains conflict stages under the resolved destination path, while a stage's exact source blob can still live at the old path. The transition owner now binds each stage to its committed merge or rebase resolution, checks the same path first, and then accepts a unique Git-detected rename only when the source mode and blob match exactly. The committed index check remains intact. Ambiguous or undetected renames continue to refuse without changing the index.

## Evidence

The regression creates a real committed rename conflict and checks acceptance, rejection of foreign conflict stages, and a byte-identical index after validation. Existing merge, rebase, and foreign-state cases remain covered. The single focused run passed all 12 cases (113.28 seconds in Vitest; 273.61 seconds including cold wrapper startup). Targeted typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The current head, `540b4ed1472b3b38bdade5b7465ce13dba61d89e`, integrates main `675e88e8422e7c44468ecbbcb9ad414c8c0fb324` because the canonical PR wrapper, SDK build inputs, schemas, and dependencies have materially changed. The authored fix is patch-identical to the independently reviewed version, so its focused proof and review are reused. A frozen-lockfile install passed in 6 minutes 36.6 seconds without tracked-file changes. Exact-head PR CI [38656028401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38656028401) passed, including the SDK package-boundary job, security, source contracts, lint, types, and aggregate gate. No local SDK compiler or broad local suite was run for this integration.

CI run [38614506795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38614506795), attempt 1, failed on the original head `f2643d8eca0e96c0de2b44b6bcdaca7d06f56988`: the extension package-boundary job exceeded the 300-second SDK declaration timeout, which also failed the aggregate gate. There were no failing Vitest cases. The failure report classifies this as new because the comparable main job passed and selected scopes were not compared. The timeout remains unattributed; the focused proof above does not establish that CI passed or that the failure is inherited.

A baseline command was prepared for the exact tested main parent, `83108fb6d5d674c991e7f83b1fc96614c9aa5c48`, with the original Node/pnpm versions and SDK deadlines. The single Blacksmith Testbox allocation entered the queue and was stopped before the payload ran. The SDK baseline remains unrun; no CI rerun, timeout extension, or provider fallback was used.

prs.title: improve: skip no-op session maintenance after delivery settlement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automatic session maintenance repeatedly recounts a young store and opens an empty write transaction when final delivery settlement releases a recovery claim.

## User Impact

Reduces background database work after ordinary turns. Retention policy, capacity limits, schemas, and destructive maintenance protection are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintenance owner now keeps its published entry count and computes the next retention deadline from the delivery receipt. Releasing protection wakes maintenance only for capacity pressure or an already-due deadline; young stores stay idle. This skips the entire redundant planning request sequence, including its count snapshot, age probes, and empty write transaction.

Removed checks and accepted edge cases:

- Protection release no longer invalidates the whole age/count fact. A conservative deadline can still cause an early pass; the actual planner recounts and checks eligible rows.
- Prepared maintenance no longer recaptures generic/scoped write revisions or uses a host currency flag to discard scheduling facts after unrelated writes. Receipt overlap with snapshot capture may briefly overcount or undercount scheduling state until a real pass or the existing 30-minute refresh. Selected-row, transcript, ancestry, live protection, and lease-loss checks still protect destructive effects.

The superseded revision path and its raw no-op-write regression are deleted. Actor receipt publication is unchanged.

## Evidence

The delivery-settlement regression covers young, over-cap, and expired stores through the actual actor operation. Existing preparation tests retain insertion/protection-release coverage and verify that unrelated writes settle without another pass. Local format, lint, and whitespace checks pass. Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38661926105) passed the changed tests, types, lint, source contracts, Knip/Madge checks, and database worker/dialect ratchets without retries or inherited-failure exceptions. Production code shrinks by 32 lines; overall change is +150/−188 across nine files.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |

| Warmed all-thread SQL statements / turn, median [min–max] | Pending | Pending |

| Warmed MAIN SQL statements / turn | Pending | Pending |
| Warm-background SQL / minute | Pending | Pending |

Merged as `ebb8d84506c2bc50ea209f51ec17423bf0236d9d`. Three alternating base/candidate pairs compare that merge with parent `4821920804c9e79c8f6cfd8537ac591a5d321e96`, using the shared harness with an identical five-minute connected-idle window. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Codex harness live test "steers an active turn from another paired device with equivalent permissions" fails intermittently when the model drops trailing characters while echoing the 16-character hex steer marker (for example, got `CODEX-STEER-86DB3125776F416`, expected `CODEX-STEER-86DB3125776F4165`).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Removes a ~5.5% flake from the Codex harness live lane, including the GPT-5.6 Luna Max Docker release lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test proves that a steer sent from a second paired device lands in the active turn and its content reaches the final answer. The truncation comes from the model, not the product: the persisted transcript, built from Codex's completed item text rather than streamed deltas, is truncated identically, and the completed-tail top-up from #168400 is already present. The marker is now four random NATO-alphabet words (for example `CODEX-STEER-KILO-TANGO-ECHO-ZULU`, 26^4 combinations), which models echo reliably. The exact `toBe(marker)` check and the steer-target history check are unchanged, so the contract is not weakened.

## Evidence

- Failure rate on main: 12 of 217 runs (~5.5%). The GPT-5.6 Luna Max Docker lane failed twice in a row today:
  - https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38645739400/job/116136950003
  - https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38645739400/job/116161023136
- Live test needs provider keys, so it was not run locally. Local checks: `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the file, and the file collects and skips without live env (`vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts src/gateway/gateway-codex-harness.live.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 skipped, ~13s). `pnpm test <file>` excludes `*.live.test.ts`, so it reports no matching file.

## What Problem This Solves

Delegated calls can persist transcripts but cannot currently request or track a provider audio recording. When informed consent has been obtained, callers need an opt-in, auditable recording artifact linked to the OpenClaw call record.

- add an opt-in record flag for Twilio outbound calls

- packed the built voice-call plugin candidate successfully (27 files, 135365-byte tarball)

## Protocol compatibility

Inspected Codex MCP handling before changing the tool schema: structured tool output is serialized generically, so the optional record input and optional recording status object are additive.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve shared windows when previewing tabs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening or resizing the Browser panel resizes a user’s real Chrome window when previewing an existing browser session.

## User Impact

Shared browser sessions keep their existing window and page viewport. The preview scales locally and continues to translate clicks into page coordinates. Isolated, locally managed browsers still auto-fit the panel; intentional resize commands remain available. No new setting or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser owner now advertises whether its viewport can be auto-sized. The panel uses that capability rather than inferring ownership from a profile name. Existing-session Chrome MCP, extension, attach-only, remote CDP, and attach-only engines opt out; an older server that does not advertise the capability also stays untouched.

This changes automatic behavior only, not the preview layout or explicit resize action. It avoids save/restore, which would still disrupt the browser and could overwrite a later human resize.

## Evidence

- Red/green regression through the actual panel controller and browser request client: before the fix a shared preview emitted a remote resize; afterward shared and unadvertised previews emit none, managed auto-fit remains, locally scaled clicks reach the expected CSS coordinates, and explicit resize still dispatches.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser --maxWorkers=2`: 261 UI tests and 5 isolated Chromium browser tests pass, including streaming, native browser exclusion, route ownership, and input behavior.
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 42 pass, covering the ownership capability and real attach-only CDP route.
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'agent contract: form'`: the selected real HTTP resize contract passes (1 selected, 48 excluded by filter), including explicit resize and invalid-size rejection.
- UI and browser-extension targeted typechecks pass. Targeted lint reports zero warnings/errors; changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent API-key-based review: scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings. Reviewed production ownership/transport, all five complete touched test files, and shared coordinate/input helpers.
- Every touched test file was audited in full. Managed fixtures advertise their capability; dead singleton-parameter branches and an unnecessary cast were removed, and the attach-only fixture now restores its stubbed globals. Distinct failure/lifecycle cases were retained.
- No personal browser/window was opened, resized, or controlled; no live Gateway was updated or restarted.

Related, but not replaced: #148187 offers a broader optional viewport-lock UI; this fix preserves shared browser windows by default without adding a setting.


### CI prerequisite repair

The initial run [38659496845](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659496845) exposed a pre-existing fixture ordering bug in the transcript end-follow growth test. The fixture awaited two animation frames after committing a new extent; the native corrective scroll could arrive later, with its receipt intentionally retired in the following frame. A real-Chromium trace deterministically reproduced the original assertion: geometry was correct but the owner was still programmatic at the two-frame continuation.

The growth fixture now awaits the expected native scroll and its retirement frame. The matching trace then observes the same expected geometry with programmatic ownership cleared. All existing assertions remain; no production scroll change, sleeps, retries, timeout increases or skipped tests. All 22 tests in the fully audited file pass, targeted UI types/lint/format pass, and a fresh independent API-direct review returned scoped-clean with no P0–P2 findings.

Current candidate: 34875296d9c442a24ee3a076492c62cb9a8d0c70. Fresh exact-head CI is required; no inherited-failure exception is requested.

prs.title: improve(sessions): reuse retained transcript residency charges
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Replacing a cached transcript walks its previous contents again just to recover a size already charged to the cache.

## User Impact

Reduces CPU spent accounting for transcript replacements, especially in sessions with many transcript entries.

Example user flows:

- Keep chatting in a long conversation: cached transcript replacements avoid counting the previous contents again.
- Run a multi-step tool task: cache replacements after tool results reuse the previous transcript's recorded size.

## Why This Change Was Made

Store the transcript's existing charge on its cache cell, estimate incoming contents once, and reset the charge on discard. This preserves the existing structural heap estimator, cache budgets, eviction behavior, and replica APIs.

## Evidence

Comparing baseline `3628a5f8179` with PR head `6ef87210379` shows small, repeatable CPU savings. Native Linux ARM64, Node 24.21.0; 12 matched ABBA/BAAB blocks per case, with 2,000 warmups and 2,000 calls per measurement mode in each fresh process. The benchmark calls the actual replica API using identical synthetic transcripts within default context/cache limits.

| Transcript | Baseline CPU per replacement | Updated CPU per replacement | CPU saved | Mean paired reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 alternating text messages | 0.0194 ms | 0.0100 ms | 0.0093 ms | 48.1% |
| 100 tool-heavy messages | 0.0836 ms | 0.0424 ms | 0.0412 ms | 49.3% |
| 500 tool-heavy messages | 0.2596 ms | 0.1310 ms | 0.1285 ms | 49.5% |
| 32 messages including 512 KiB text | 0.0190 ms | 0.0098 ms | 0.0092 ms | 48.5% |

Simultaneous 95% confidence intervals for CPU saved are 0.0089–0.0097 ms for the ordinary case, 0.0395–0.0429 ms for 100 tool-heavy messages, 0.1263–0.1308 ms for 500, and 0.0089–0.0095 ms for the large-text case. Intervals use matched block means with Bonferroni correction across four CPU cases; correlated calls are not treated as independent samples, and all blocks are retained.

Replacement p95 also improves: **0.0916 → 0.0499 ms** at 100 tool-heavy messages and **0.2757 → 0.1402 ms** at 500. These are per-replacement improvements.[^qualification]

- Every process passes stable-charge and exact retained-input checks, then finishes with zero charged bytes, snapshots, and cells. The two lightweight fixtures were corrected to alternate user/assistant messages; their original simple-object controls remain preserved, and valid tool-heavy results were reused.
- Full source audits match both pinned revisions before and after. Dependency manifests, native assets, runtime and probe hashes match; benchmark tooling and raw evidence remain outside the production repository.
- All 32 targeted replica/transcript tests pass on macOS ARM64, Node 26.10.0 (29.81 seconds). Coverage includes replacement, growth/shrinkage, invalidation, byte eviction, entry limits, receipts, and rollback. Core typechecking, targeted lint, formatting, and fresh independent review pass.

The identical failures reproduce on unmodified baseline `3628a5f8179` (same three-file selection: 77 passed, two failed, macOS ARM64 / Node 26.10.0). No PR-specific cause was identified; Linux/x64 baseline CI was not run, and the CI gate remains red.

prs.title: feat(telegram): add per-message context control with /ignore
prs.body:
Related: #123937

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw agents in Telegram groups currently ingest every authorized message,
even when two humans are talking only to each other. That side conversation can
later surface in an unrelated reply, waste prompt context, or steer the agent's
future behavior.

The existing mention and activation controls are chat-wide and decide whether a
message triggers the bot; they do not selectively remove one update from rolling
group history. `/ignore <message>` adds that message-level context boundary.

```text
Alex: /ignore Dinner at 7? The reservation is under "banana."
Sam: Summarize the deployment decisions from today.

Without /ignore: the side conversation can enter the agent's rolling context.
With /ignore: that update never enters ambient agent context.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Telegram-native `/ignore` command that drops one authorized inbound
update before reply-chain recording, media processing, history compilation, or
agent dispatch. An authorized `/ignore <message>` is intentionally silent; bare
`/ignore` returns usage help. Exact command matching supports commands addressed
to this bot, leaves foreign-bot and forwarded commands alone, and lets an
account-scoped custom `/ignore` retain ownership when configured.

Media albums are ignored as a unit at the existing flush boundary. Durable,
account/chat-scoped message and album tombstones prevent an ignored update from
returning after an edit, replay, process restart, command-policy change, or bot
rename. Privacy tombstones use their own bounded persistence namespace, separate
from the ordinary message-cache LRU, and override cache hydration regardless of
hydration order.

A deliberate direct reply may reintroduce Telegram's replied-to quote for that
turn. Same-chat cached ancestry is detached from the ignored message and its
descendants; unrelated cross-chat messages with the same numeric message ID are
not affected.

`/btw` remains complementary: it keeps a message in context without requiring a
normal reply, while `/ignore` keeps a message out of context.

## User Impact

- Human participants can have one-off side conversations without distracting or
  unintentionally steering the agent.
- Agents retain useful ambient group context without treating every authorized
  message as relevant memory.
- Operators avoid toggling chat-wide mention or activation behavior for a
  message-level need.
- Ignored text and albums skip media work, prompt tokens, and agent dispatch.

This is context hygiene, not deletion, secrecy, encryption, or message
redaction. Telegram retains the original chat message normally.

## Evidence

Validated on exact head
`836dd8b3540018e1eea670b8f5f62d19e10e3206`, based on frozen `main`
`5e5f9c27559776303d962aa37f8c09f676e640d4`:

- Focused Telegram matrix: 350/350 tests.
- Full Telegram bot owner: 186/186 tests.
- Final album-ordering/cache/privacy corrective matrix: 66/66 tests, including
  deterministic record/remove interleaving across durable tombstones.
- Canonical no-fetch pre-PR wrapper: all selected gates pass, including core and
  extension source/test types, dead exports, format, core/extension/scripts
  lint, boundary and dependency guards, database-first storage, runtime cycles,
  and repository ratchets.
- Independent exact-head Sol review: no actionable P0-P2 finding remains.

Independent review found and fixed three final P2s before publication:

1. Cross-chat external reply IDs could be persisted as local reply identities.
2. A later message could overtake an album before its members entered prompt
   context.
3. A recorder could resume after `/ignore` removal and reinsert an embedded
   ignored reply snapshot.

The final implementation preserves cross-chat payload/media without borrowing a
local reply identity, records album members before delayed flush, and serializes
record/remove mutation per account and chat while installing privacy tombstones
before removal waits.

Exact-head Telegram Test Server proof remains `blocked_external`: it requires
maintainer TDLib/Test Server credentials and the official QA route. No live
Telegram claim is made from deterministic local evidence.

AI-assisted implementation and review; I inspected the final diff and understand
the behavior and scope.

The row tooltip uses the same name. **Copy path** still copies the exact full root, and branch copying and Show session files retain their actions. The unused path-line styling is removed and the Control UI documentation describes the privacy behavior.

Release-note context: session Details keeps private absolute workspace paths out of ordinary page text and tooltips while preserving explicit exact-path copying. Existing configurations and stored data require no migration.

## Evidence

The four real-Gateway privacy guards are unchanged. The component regressions cover unlabelled POSIX and Windows roots; both fail before the fix, then the entire component file passes all seven tests. Local proof on the candidate:

- Both new missing-label regressions fail on unpatched production code; all 7 component tests pass after the fix.

The final stylesheet cleanup combines identical adjacent badge rules; rebuilding produces byte-identical compiled CSS to the captured/tested candidate. PR CI supplies broad and platform proof. `ci:full` is selected for the chat surface as required by the UI testing guide; no live-provider run is requested.

The screenshots below use the same synthetic mocked-Gateway session and 1728 × 1000 viewport. The before image intentionally shows a synthetic workspace path; neither capture contains real fixture tokens or private directories.

![Before: Details renders the synthetic absolute workspace path](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/159f2a1b-0898-4ba8-9b6f-994511bb2235)

![After: Details shows the workspace name and retains Copy path](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea330f88-0063-4fc0-9b36-faaa19b8fca1)

prs.title: fix(openai): drop transient reasoning replay state
prs.body:
Closes #113868

## What Problem This Solves

Native Codex Responses can emit temporary reasoning items whose IDs start with `rs_tmp_`. OpenClaw persisted those items in assistant `thinkingSignature` fields and replayed them on later turns even though the IDs are not durable replay state. A follow-up request could then fail with `invalid_encrypted_content`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This current-main rewrite places the rule at the two canonical owners:

- the stream writer keeps the human-readable reasoning summary but omits replay signature and provenance metadata for temporary native Codex reasoning;
- the consolidated replay converter drops matching signatures already present in older transcripts and clears adjacency state, so a later signed text item cannot inherit pairing from an earlier stable reasoning item.

The check is intentionally limited to the native Codex Responses backend. Stable `rs_*` items and temporary-shaped IDs from compatible proxy endpoints retain the existing behavior.

The old branch changed a duplicate provider conversion path that was later consolidated by #123762. This rewrite removes that obsolete surface instead of rebasing it.

## User Impact

Multi-turn native Codex Responses sessions no longer carry temporary encrypted reasoning state into later requests. Visible reasoning summaries and valid stable reasoning replay remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact head: `d54dd8160fa40ac3d090502891ebf5ef6ac170de`, based on current `upstream/main` `ed6e3aabf0`.

- Pre-fix owner regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts` failed in exactly two places: native `rs_tmp_*` state was persisted, and the same item was replayed after a stable reasoning item. Stable native reasoning and proxy behavior passed.
- Exact-head focused and sibling tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-parity.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-prompt-role.test.ts src/agents/openai-responses.reasoning-replay.test.ts` -> 43/43 passed.
- Both consolidated replay facades are covered by the stable -> temporary -> signed-text ordering regression. The temporary item is absent and the text ID is not replayed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware ...` -> passed for all three changed files.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` -> passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-import-cycles.ts` -> 0 runtime value cycles.
- Scope: two production files, +25/-5 (net +20), plus one focused 161-line test file. The previous implementation was four files with production net +39 and edited an owner removed by #123762.

Direct dependency-contract check:

- OpenAI Codex source at `90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d` models reasoning as a first-class Responses item carrying an optional provider item ID and encrypted content: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L950-L999
- Server item IDs are deliberately read as opaque/permissive values: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/response_item_id.rs#L17-L34
- Codex forwards reasoning items as model request input rather than normalizing their provider lifetime: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/core/src/client_common.rs#L53-L90
- The OpenAI Responses contract documents encrypted reasoning as state to replay for stateless multi-turn use, which is why excluding only observed temporary native items must happen before persistence/replay: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create

Known proof gap: this machine does not yet have a redacted exact-head two-turn native provider trace showing a real `rs_tmp_*` response followed by a request that omits it. No live-provider claim is made. No additional AutoReview was run.

prs.title: fix(doctor): keep updater-retired plugin aliases removed during record reconciliation
prs.body:
Closes #136025

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor restores a retired official plugin alias immediately after the updater successfully replaces it with the canonical plugin: `repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls` counts only `updated`/`unchanged` updater outcome IDs and restores every original missing record absent from that set, so the retired alias (e.g. `qqbot`) comes back alongside the canonical record (e.g. `openclaw-qqbot`), losing the updater's committed install-owner migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair now consumes the committed owner migrations attached to the updater result (`resolvePluginInstallOwnerMigrations`): an alias whose canonical target was repaired in the same run stays retired — its original record is not restored, it is excluded from install candidacy, and a change note records the retirement. Migrations are honored only when the canonical target was repaired in the same result, so a failed canonical update without migration metadata keeps the previous preserve-everything behavior (including no persistence write). Plain `skipped` outcomes are still neither success nor failure, per the issue.

Note: this issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`; opening anyway because the fix shape is marked clear (`fix-shape-clear`), the regression is reproduced with exact steps, no open PR or assignee exists, and the change is confined to the owning repair boundary.

## User Impact

After a successful canonical plugin update, Doctor no longer resurrects the retired alias record or attempts to reinstall it; operators see one canonical record plus an explicit retirement note.

## Evidence

- New `keeps a retired duplicate alias removed when the updater commits an owner migration` regression test following the issue's exact repro shape (mocked updater returning only the canonical 2.0.3 record, `updated` + diagnostic `skipped` outcomes, committed `{qqbot: "openclaw-qqbot"}` migration metadata, real temp package files).
- New `preserves original records when a canonical update fails without an owner migration` negative control asserting unchanged records and no persistence write.
- Both edited files pass an esbuild transform check; existing doctor tests that mock the updater without migration metadata are behaviorally unaffected (the resolver returns `undefined` → no-op). Local vitest lane cannot run in this Windows checkout (rolldown native binding failure at config load), so CI runs the full suite on the exact head SHA.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an outbound iMessage reflection could be treated as fresh user input when Messages assigned it a new row GUID but retained the original outbound GUID in `reply_to_guid`. In affected self-chats this could start a second agent turn and create a reply loop.

Echo detection now accepts the reply-parent GUID only when it is bound to the same normalized text in the same conversation scope. The in-memory cache stores that ID/text association directly, matching the persisted-cache behavior while preserving the existing conflicting-ID guard. A different reply body or the same text in another conversation still dispatches normally.

## User Impact

Affected iMessage users no longer have reflected assistant text reprocessed as a user message. Legitimate inline replies remain deliverable.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can emit more than one `rawResponse/completed` notification during a single turn, especially around tool handoffs.

OpenClaw previously had two related observability gaps:

- `attemptUsage` retained only the final provider response, under-counting multi-response turns.
- Codex diagnostics emitted only one turn-level model-call span. Consumers that reconstructed individual LLM calls from transcript timestamps could place the LLM span after its tool call and make several calls overlap until the final answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Accumulate exact `rawResponse/completed` usage once per `responseId` for attempt-level accounting.
- Keep the final response's usage and `contextUsage` as the assistant/current-context snapshot, so summed billing buckets do not inflate the active context window.
- Emit one request-level `model.call.completed` diagnostic per unique response.
  - Response samples and tool lifecycle boundaries are buffered and paired by order at turn completion.
  - A tool start closes the current LLM interval; completion of the final active tool opens the next LLM interval.
  - This remains correct when Codex delivers `rawResponse/completed` after the tool triggered by that response has already run.
  - Parallel tools form one tool phase. When one provider response emits several sequential tools, the shortest surplus tool-to-tool gap is discarded instead of being reported as an LLM call.
- Add `sourceTimestampMs` to completed model-call diagnostics so the OTel recorder can backdate completed-only request spans to their real completion time.
- Attach exact per-response usage to request spans when present, while still emitting a timing span when Codex omits optional usage.
- Attach accumulated `attemptUsage` to the turn-level model span.
- Hash the upstream response ID before exposing it in diagnostics and deduplicate repeated completion notifications.
- Map `reasoningOutputTokens` into `reasoningTokens`.
- Reuse the same response accumulator in bounded/settled-turn paths.
- Fail closed to thread-last usage when an exact response aggregate becomes incomplete.

Transcript timestamps are intentionally unchanged: an assistant tool-call message records when the model produced the tool call, not when that provider request began. Per-response diagnostics now own the LLM timing boundary.

The assistant-completion idle timeout configuration is not part of this PR: `#97233` already exposed `appServer.turnAssistantCompletionIdleTimeoutMs` on current `main`.

This change was AI-assisted. I reviewed the diff and validated the event contract directly against `openai/codex` app-server source and a real app-server turn.

## User Impact

- Token and cost accounting is accurate for Codex turns containing multiple upstream responses.
- Current-context reporting continues to reflect only the latest provider response.
- OTel consumers can render:

  `LLM request -> tool execution -> LLM request -> tool execution -> final LLM request`

  without deriving LLM starts from assistant-message timestamps.

## Upstream Codex Contract

Checked against immutable `openai/codex@95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74`:

- [`rawResponse/completed` is emitted once per upstream Responses API completion with exact, non-accumulated usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/app-server/README.md#L1450)
- [`response_id` is required and `token_usage` is optional](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs#L1820-L1827)
- [The sampling loop alternates provider responses with tool work](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L137-L149)
- [`RawResponseCompleted` is emitted when the provider response completes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2348-L2360)

## Evidence

### Real App-Server Proof

Ran the local authenticated Codex CLI (`0.146.0-alpha.3.1`) as `codex app-server --listen stdio://` with raw events enabled. The prompt required two separate sequential shell calls followed by `DONE`. The proof script used an ephemeral thread and redacted response/tool IDs.

Observed lifecycle, relative to model-turn start:

```text
LLM response-1   0ms .. 8878ms      total=23030
tool-1                 8913ms
LLM response-2         8913ms .. 11874ms   total=23125
tool-2                           11896ms
LLM response-3                   11896ms .. 13492ms   total=23178
turn terminal                                      13496ms
```

No LLM request span overlaps either tool phase. In this run each shell command completed within the millisecond resolution of the captured events.

Redacted projected output:

```json
{
  "rawResponses": [
    {
      "responseId": "response-1",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 22967,
        "cachedInputTokens": 0,
        "outputTokens": 63,
        "totalTokens": 23030
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-2",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23078,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 47,
        "totalTokens": 23125
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-3",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23173,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 5,
        "totalTokens": 23178
      }
    }
  ],
  "projected": {
    "attemptUsage": {
      "input": 24674,
      "cacheRead": 44544,
      "output": 115,
      "total": 69333
    },
    "latestResponseUsage": {
      "input": 901,
      "cacheRead": 22272,
      "output": 5,
      "total": 23178
    }
  },
  "requestSpanDurationsMs": [8878, 2961, 1596]
}
```

The accounting invariant holds:

```text
23030 + 23125 + 23178 = 69333
```

The latest context remains response 3 (`23178`), while turn accounting reports all three responses (`69333`).

### Additional Verification

- Final affected-surface tests:
  - 5 files passed, 182 tests passed.
  - Covers multi-response accumulation/deduplication, delayed response completion, sequential-tool gap collapse, native/dynamic tool boundaries, and OTel source-time backdating.
- Production and test typechecks passed for core and extensions.
- Targeted core/extension lint and formatting passed for all changed files.
- Repository guards passed:
  - max-lines and environment-variable ratchets
  - plugin SDK API baseline, exports, and surface budget
  - deprecated API usage and plugin boundary report
  - guarded/plugin-SDK wildcard re-exports
  - runtime sidecar baseline/loaders
  - dependency pins/package patches
  - import cycles and conflict markers
- `run-attempt` focused lane:
  - 143 tests passed, 4 tests failed.
  - The same four SQLite settled-turn/context-engine assertions were reproduced unchanged on latest `origin/main` before this timing change, so they are current baseline failures rather than regressions from this PR.

prs.title: fix(gateway): grant busy accounts reconnect grace on a validated typed disconnect
prs.body:
Fixes #146800

## What Problem This Solves

A health sample taken milliseconds after a typed Discord disconnect classified a busy account as `stuck` and restarted the whole provider, aborting the account's in-flight reply operations. The busy branch computed `busyAge` from the oldest active run's start age and returned `stuck` before the typed-disconnect branch could validate `lastDisconnect.at` and apply the 120-second reconnect grace, so a long-running but healthy run turned a transient socket blip into an immediate account-wide restart.

## User Impact

A busy channel sampled during a transient transport disconnect now rides out the transport's own reconnect window instead of being force-restarted: no aborted reply operations and no account-wide downtime for blips the client already schedules its own reconnect for. A disconnect that outlives the 120-second grace still reports `disconnected` and restarts. Stale run heartbeats still report `stuck`, and accounts without a validated disconnect keep the run-start-age proxy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run age is not a disconnect age. `activeRunStartedAt` measures how long a task has been running; only a validated `lastDisconnect.at` measures how long the transport has been down. While the run heartbeat stays fresh, the validated typed disconnect now owns the down clock: reconnect grace applies under `CHANNEL_RECONNECT_GRACE_MS` and `disconnected` is reported at the boundary. The lifecycle-validated disconnect extraction moved into a shared `resolveCurrentDisconnectAt` helper so the busy branch and the disconnect branch keep one owner for that invariant. Accounts without a validated disconnect are unchanged: run start age remains the only down-clock proxy there.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix policy red: with the issue's snapshot (busy, 4 active runs, run started 26 minutes ago, heartbeat 1 second old, `connected=false`, `lastDisconnect` 4ms old), `evaluateChannelHealth()` returned `stuck`; the new tests assert `reconnect-grace` (4ms) and `disconnected` (exactly 120s) and both failed before the fix, while the stale-heartbeat-stuck and patch-merged-disconnect guard tests passed throughout.
- Pre-fix monitor red (production change stashed): the new monitor test observed the monitor calling `stopChannel`/`startChannel` for the busy Discord account on a 4ms-old validated disconnect — the reported incident (`expected stopChannel not to be called, but called 1 times`); with the fix the monitor does not restart. The policy assertions ran through `evaluateChannelHealth()` and the monitor assertion through the real `startChannelHealthMonitor` check loop.
- Real-transport proof inside the grace window (committed test `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.real-transport.test.ts`, real clock, real TCP transport, no fake timers, no spy mocks on the monitor path): the production `startChannelHealthMonitor` check loop drives a fixture manager whose transport is a real TCP socket to a loopback server. A 26-minute-old run keeps a fresh heartbeat while the real socket is destroyed mid-run; every monitor tick evaluates `reconnect-grace`, the transport really reconnects (`transport disconnected` → `transport connected` ~250ms later), and the run completes intact (`run 1 completed`). With the pre-fix policy checked out, the same harness fails: the monitor restarts the account, aborts the run, and the run never completes (`timed out waiting for run completion`).
- Real-transport proof of grace expiry (temporary harness, real clock, 124s run): after the real socket drop the loopback server stops accepting connections, so the fixture's real reconnect attempts fail with `ECONNREFUSED` 479 times across the window while the run heartbeat stays fresh. The monitor issues no restart until 120032ms after the disconnect, then stops the account (`monitor STOP (active run aborted)`), starts it again, and the account reconnects (`transport connected`) once the transport endpoint returns. A disconnect that outlives the 120s grace still restarts a busy account. Full transcript:
  ```
  [t=0ms] start (run 1)
  [t=16ms] transport connected
  [t=67ms] transport disconnected          <- real TCP drop; monitor evaluates reconnect-grace, no restart
  [t=321ms..119.8s] transport error (ECONNREFUSED) x479   <- fixture reconnect attempts fail; run heartbeat stays fresh
  [t=120133ms] monitor STOP (active run aborted)   <- 120s grace expired (first restart 120032ms after disconnect)
  [t=120133ms] start (run 2)
  [t=120335ms] transport connected         <- recovered after restart
  ```
- Post-fix: `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts` 58/58, `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` 56/56, `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.real-transport.test.ts` 1/1, plus sibling consumers `src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts` 27/27, `src/infra/channels-status-issues.test.ts` 11/11, `src/plugin-sdk/status-helpers.test.ts` 25/25, `src/plugin-sdk/channel-lifecycle.queue.test.ts` 6/6 all green.
- `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` report only the pre-existing `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts(416)` TS2741 error on current `main` (unrelated to this change); the changed files introduce no new type errors. oxlint (type-aware, repo shard tsconfig) and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover agent admission after runtime supersession
prs.body:
Fixes #172628.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a freshly started Gateway can leave its main agent unavailable when a newer model-runtime publication supersedes deferred startup admission.

## User Impact

The agent can recover during the same startup without another restart. Persistent supersession or a genuine publication failure remains visible in agent readiness with its reason and repair hint. No configuration, schema, protocol, or credential changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-runtime owner and startup-admission owner use distinct supersession errors. The existing four-attempt admission retry recognized only its own error, so a runtime publication replacement escaped as a terminal failure. On a typed supersession error or a silently superseded queued refresh whose snapshot is blocked by a current replacement, the Gateway adapter now waits once for the current replacement and delegates fresh preparation to that existing bounded retry owner. It rereads current configuration, secrets, and plugin metadata without repeating database opening or migration. Genuine failures from either publication propagate unchanged.

The original successor-joining option could follow an unlimited replacement chain. Maintainer cleanup uses the existing admission budget, removes the option-forwarding-only test, extends behavioral admission regressions, and moves the final snapshot check out of the prepublication guard's captured state.

Original fix by @dlmccoy; maintainer cleanup adds bounded recovery, diagnostic coverage, and readiness documentation.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: current main still lacks runtime-supersession recovery at deferred admission. #171054 introduced the bounded admission retry but recognizes only `AgentDatabaseStartupSupersededError`. #169539 changed configured inventory matching in lease admission; it does not repair startup publication failure classification.
- Regression coverage in `server-agent-database-startup.preparation.test.ts`: `retries a superseded publication after model runtime replacement`; `retries a superseded publication after queued model runtime replacement`; `fails admission after four continuously superseded model runtime publications`; `preserves a genuine initial model publication failure without retrying`; `preserves a genuine successor model publication failure without retrying`. The tests exercise real startup admission and its Gateway adapter with controlled model-runtime boundary outcomes, including waiting for the successor, successful availability, no repeat opening/migration, bounded failure, and actionable diagnostics. They do not boot a Gateway or exercise the full provider runtime.
- Exact-head regression result: [CI job 116181303208](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660652772/job/116181303208) passed all 21 tests in the changed file. Vitest duration: 2.50s; wrapper wall time: 4.27s. The two supersession cases took 2ms each; persistent supersession 3ms; genuine initial/successor failure cases 2ms each.
- Changed-file static lint and formatting pass. The nested checkout's wrapper could not find a local dependency directory; the parent install's `oxlint` was used with the trusted main core rules, omitting only the unrelated `ui/**/*.tsx` Solid override. No dependency installation occurred.
- Autoreview caught and prompted repair of a P2: a queued superseded refresh can resolve without throwing. The fix also handles that outcome, and its regression keeps config/secrets unchanged. Final branch autoreview on `26a3595a1f361b34e02231328d2facef856af35c` is scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. The installed canonical helper was used because the repository entrypoint is absent. Deslop complete.
- Exact-head PR CI is the test gate and covers the selected regression suite, production/test typechecking, and repository checks. Pushed head: `26a3595a1f361b34e02231328d2facef856af35c`. [CI run 38660652772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660652772) passed: 34 successful jobs, 29 scope-skipped jobs, and `openclaw/ci-gate` successful. Selected tests, production/test typechecking, lint, docs, and architecture checks passed; no inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was used.
- Initial CI run [38659514816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659514816), job [116177599066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659514816/job/116177599066), exposed a fixture mismatch: the model refresh mock returned `undefined` instead of the real API’s promise, breaking `.catch`. The fixture now defaults to a resolved promise; this is a PR-attributable repair, not an inherited failure.
- Local tests, local typechecks, negative controls, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy: “relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint.” No lease or Gateway was started. Per-test local wall times are intentionally unmeasured; the added cases use deferred promises and existing fake timers, with no real sleeps or extra Gateway fixture.

## Review Resolution

The full latest ClawSweeper review (comment 6180998322, contributor head `b439ad20e9f0c9c71874a52ab082b13e62f2c215`) reports no code findings. Its option-forwarding test concern is addressed by admission recovery/failure assertions. Its live-proof-only request is superseded by the maintainer's policy: PR CI is the proof. No human review findings were present.

Deferred-path facts: the admission lifetime/abort signal, pending recovery identity, physical database witnesses, and deletion state remain checked by the admission owner before retry and final admission; agent ID/environment/paths remain bound to the original inspected target; the adapter checks that target against current config and captures fresh config/secrets revisions and plugin metadata for each attempt. The runtime owner supplies the current replacement promise; it is awaited once rather than retained as authority. The existing four-attempt limit remains authoritative. No session binding or new external side effect is introduced.

## Scope

Numstat versus main: production +25/-11 (net +14), tests +86/-17 (net +69), docs +6/-0 (net +6). The production-growth exception is the typed supersession handoff and one successor wait; cleanup removes captured snapshot state and a one-use variable without deleting unrelated behavior or weakening guards.

prs.title: fix(ui): retire the live terminal copy once its run clears
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WebChat can render a final assistant reply twice — the stored transcript holds one clean copy (`thinking` + `text`, no `textSignature`), while the screen shows two identical stacked copies that survive until a reload. The live terminal projection and the persisted row are supposed to converge through the authoritative-terminal dedup, but the record that owns that dedup is only armed when the persisted final arrives with `hasActiveRun !== true`. When the final row lands while its run still reads active — long turns with tool calls interleaved make that ordering more likely — no record is armed, and nothing arms it later, so `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory` never retires the live copy and both renders stay.

## Why This Fix

`rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` now keeps such a terminal **pending** instead of dropping it, and the run-clear reconcile (`finishSessionMessageRunReconcile`, right before the history reload it already triggers) promotes the pending record via `armPendingAuthoritativeTerminal`. The existing history reconciliation then removes the live copy for that run, so the turn converges to the single persisted reply. A pending terminal for a different run is left untouched, and a terminal that already armed stays armed.

## User Impact

A completed turn no longer shows the same reply twice, and it recovers automatically at run completion instead of waiting for a page reload — the duplicate disappears as soon as the run clears and history applies.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.test.ts` pins the sequence: a final persisted with `hasActiveRun: true` keeps the live copy (the pre-fix state), the run-clear arming retires it, a pending terminal for another run is preserved for its owning run, and the already-clear path still arms immediately. These fail against the old guard because the record was never kept.
- `ui` typecheck (`tsconfig.ui.json`) clean, boundary-guard lint and formatting clean; the neighboring `chat-gateway` and `stream-reconciliation` suites show no new failures (the six locale-dependent "Retrying…" expectations fail identically before and after this change on a zh-CN host).


## Update (c34c8b750b9) — promotion moved onto the history owner

The previous revision armed the deferred terminal inside the run-clear reconcile, which the review correctly flagged: `chat.final` clears the run first and the reloads it triggers never promoted the record, and an already-cleared run skipped the hook. Promotion now lives in the single history-apply owner (`chat-history-hydration`), so every reload path — `chat.final`, session reconciliation, manual reload — arms the pending terminal and retires the live copy.

## Browser reproduction status (open work)

A deterministic Control UI E2E reproduction (mocked Gateway, not committed) puts the reporter's ordering through the real app: a run goes active, the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun: true`, then `chat.final` completes. Against this branch it still renders two copies, and the instrumented trace pinpoints the second one: an **identity-less live projection** (materialized stream message with no `__openclaw` identity) survives beside the persisted final. The promotion fix works on that trace — the armed terminal retires the live-terminal copy — but retiring the identity-less projection needs a change in the stream-materialization/publish path rather than the dedup helper, so this revision does not yet close the reported duplication. Keeping the PR as work in progress rather than claiming the fix.


## Update (fdfd6791b83) — review findings on eligibility and per-run pendings

- **P1 eligibility:** the deferred record now requires the saved row to own the run's final reply (`ownsFinalReply`): stream-segment-keyed rows and text blocks tagged `phase: "commentary"` no longer arm it, so a commentary-only refresh can't set the run-wide suppression flag and hide the actual final.
- **Per-run pendings:** pending records are keyed by run id (`Map` per host) instead of a single slot, so a second run persisting while active no longer drops the first run's terminal; each run keeps its own retirement path (raises from the reviewer's notes).
- Tests: five cases now cover the happy paths plus the commentary-refusal and two-active-runs sequences.

**Still open:** the reported identity-less duplicate (the app-level reproduction still shows two copies after the fix — the surviving copy is a live projection with no run identity, so retiring it needs a stream-materialization/publish change, not the dedup helper), and the cursor-delta history path (promotion currently runs on page responses only).


## Update (61ffd8e733d) — commentary phase via its canonical owner

The eligibility check now asks `resolveAssistantMessagePhase` (the shared phase owner) instead of parsing `textSignature` itself. The direct read also drifted from the contract — signatures are serialized JSON, so an object-shaped fixture never matched — and the canonical owner is the only place that decides commentary vs answer. The commentary-refusal test now pins the serialized form.

**Still open from Revision 3:** retaining every promoted run until its own live copy reconciles (my armed record is still a single slot), the cursor-delta history path, and the identity-less duplicate from the browser reproduction.

prs.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): preserve GPT token limits for deployment aliases
prs.body:
Closes #114165

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and passed the repository autoreview gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring Microsoft Foundry GPT deployments received the generic 128,000-token context window and 16,384-token output limit even when Foundry identified a GPT-5 model with larger documented limits. This could make OpenClaw compact or truncate prompts earlier than the selected deployment requires and advertise an output ceiling below the provider contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Foundry provider now owns an explicit capability table for GPT-5 models whose limits are documented by Microsoft. Capability resolution continues to use the discovered canonical model name, so custom deployment aliases receive the limits of the model they point to, while unknown models keep the existing conservative fallback.

This deliberately does not guess GPT-4.1 context limits because Microsoft documents different limits by deployment type and the current discovery metadata does not expose enough information to choose safely. The existing fallback already matches the documented `gpt-4o-mini` limits. The Claude Opus 5 half of the linked report was fixed independently on current `main`, so this PR does not duplicate that work.

## User Impact

Microsoft Foundry users selecting documented GPT-5 deployments now get accurate context-window and maximum-output metadata, including when the Azure deployment has a custom name. Unrecognized and deployment-dependent models remain on the conservative fallback instead of being overclaimed.

Thanks to @jaserNo1 for reporting the issue and documenting affected deployments in #114165.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the new deployment-alias regression table failed all 19 documented GPT-5 cases: each resolved to `128000 / 16384`.
- A follow-up catalog audit added six official IDs omitted from the first pass. `gpt-5-pro` reproduced the same incorrect `128000 / 16384` fallback (expected `400000 / 128000`); the five chat variants already matched their documented `128000 / 16384` limits through the fallback and are now explicit table entries instead of accidental matches.
- After the fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts` passes: 121/121 tests.
- The regression cases now explicitly pass the deployment list produced by Azure discovery, with a custom deployment name and separate canonical `modelName` for all 25 currently documented Foundry GPT IDs.
- The emitted configuration path is connected as follows:
  1. `buildFoundryAuthResult(...)` passes discovered deployments to `buildFoundryProviderConfig(...)`.
  2. Its deployment mapper calls `resolveFoundryModelCapabilities(deployment.name, deployment.modelName, ...)`.
  3. Capability resolution calls `resolveFoundryModelTokenLimits(modelName)` using the discovered canonical name.
  4. The builder emits `capabilities.contextWindow` and `capabilities.maxTokens` into each provider model entry.
- Production and test type checks pass:
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo`
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
- Targeted extension oxlint, formatting, import-cycle, plugin-boundary, SDK API, dependency-policy, database-first, runtime-sidecar, and test-temp guards pass.
- `git diff --check` passes on the rebased branch.
- Fresh full-branch Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) reports no findings and rates the patch correct with 0.97 confidence.
- Limits are sourced from [Microsoft's Foundry Models sold by Azure documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure).

Credentialed provider proof is not claimed: the execution environment has neither Azure CLI nor Azure/Foundry credentials, so it cannot safely discover a real subscription deployment. The source-level before/after and emitted-config regression evidence above is reproducible without secrets; a maintainer or reporter with a Foundry deployment can add the remaining redacted live-discovery proof.
