prs.title: fix: delivery queue update no longer resurrects terminalized rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a race where a delivery queue entry that was terminalized (dead-lettered or completed) concurrently could be silently resurrected back to `pending` by an update. The entry was read as pending, then a concurrent writer moved it to `failed`/`completed` — or deleted it when no retention fence was authored — between the read and the write, and the blind overwrite wrote the stale payload back over the terminal state. This re-enqueues already-settled deliveries for retry and can drop terminal outcomes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`updateDeliveryQueueEntryInDatabase` (src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts) previously did a read-modify-write: it loaded the pending row, applied the transform, then issued a blind `upsert` with no `updatePendingOnly` guard. The `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` therefore rewrote every column unconditionally.

The fix now performs an **update-only pending write**: the pending upsert mode mutates only a row that is still `pending` at write time, and fails closed with the existing `ENOENT` contract when the row is no longer pending — whether it was retained as a terminal `failed` row or **deleted outright** when no retention fence was authored. This matches the pattern already used by `reserveDeliveryQueueEntryAttemptInDatabase` and the platform-send transitions, and closes the remaining deletion-to-insertion path that an upsert's `INSERT` fallback previously resurrected.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk dead-lettered or acknowledged deliveries being revived as pending and retried after the terminal state was recorded. Delivery queue state transitions are atomic with respect to concurrent recovery and settlement, for both retained terminal outcomes and deleted (no-retention) terminal rows.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts` cover both independently committed outcomes through a concurrent writer on its own physical connection, interleaved between the update's pending read and its write:
  - `fails closed when a concurrent retained terminalize lands inside the update window`: the row is dead-lettered (retained) on a separate committed connection between the read and the write; the update throws `ENOENT`, the committed `failed` status survives, and pending reads return null.
  - `fails closed when a concurrent deleting terminalize lands inside the update window`: without a retention fence the concurrent settlement deletes the row; the pending-mode write fails instead of `INSERT`ing the stale row, throwing `ENOENT`, and the deleted row is not resurrected as pending.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts`: 2/2 pass.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-sqlite-claim.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-terminal.test.ts`: 59/59 pass.
- `session-delivery-queue.storage.test.ts` + `outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts`: 24/24 pass.
- `outbound/delivery-queue.producer-recovery.test.ts`: 10/10 pass.
- oxfmt, oxlint, and `tsgo` (core) clean on the changed files.

## Review feedback addressed

- **P2 — prevent the update from inserting a deleted terminal row:** resolved. The pending upsert mode is now update-only (a real `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'`, no `INSERT` fallback), so a terminalize that deleted the row cannot be resurrected by a stale insert. Covered by the `deleting terminalize` regression above.
- **Low-value sequential tests consolidated:** per review, the two sequential settlement-before-update cases (which rejected at the pre-existing pending read and passed without this fix) were removed; the independently committed read/write-window regression is retained and extended to the deletion case.
- **Test owner routing:** the real-caller test that required the main-thread host broker was removed with the sequential cases, so the infra-owner routing entry in `vitest.unit-fast-paths.mjs` was reverted; the atomicity file now runs in the unit-fast lane and passes there.

prs.title: fix(doctor): update repair fails when a short-lived OpenClaw command holds state
prs.body:
Related: #172151

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair`, and other update-time Doctor runs that don't get delegated update authority, fail right away with "Doctor could not enter maintenance. GatewayStateOwnerContentionError: OpenClaw state database is busy at …" when a short-lived OpenClaw command (a CLI or plugin command, an embedded agent run, another Doctor) holds state at that moment.

## User Impact

User impact: update-time Doctor now waits up to 11 minutes for a non-Gateway OpenClaw process to release state, then continues. It prints the holder's role, PID, and database path, with progress every 30 seconds. A transient hiccup no longer leaves maintenance pending or the update failed. If the holder is still running when the budget runs out, Doctor fails as before (a deferred refusal, no data at risk), and the message names the holder and the next step.

**Update behavior:** the change lives in the new version's Doctor, so it applies to any update *to* a release containing it, from any installed updater. Nothing changes in config, schema, or the installed updater. Manual `openclaw doctor --fix` keeps failing immediately, because the operator is present and the documented contract says contention fails there. A Gateway holder, or a holder whose role wasn't recorded, keeps today's behavior: a wait only under delegated update authority, capped by any service stop deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner.** Every Doctor maintenance entry goes through `acquireDoctorGatewayMaintenanceOwner` (`src/commands/doctor-maintenance-foreground.ts`), reached through `state.acquire()` for the activation, finalize, repair, and stopped-service paths alike. That function already had a bounded wait in update-repair mode, but only when the caller passed an update-authority callback. It also always described the holder as "the previous foreground Gateway". `openclaw update repair` / finalize-owned maintenance has no such callback, so it refused on the first contention. The wait now lives only in that owner, and the update CLI is untouched.

**Other processes only.** Doctor never waits on a holder recorded with its own PID: an owner held elsewhere in this process (or one of its worker threads) cannot release while Doctor waits, so that still refuses immediately. `doctor-health.migration-refusal` pins this ("preserves the live gateway/schema owner before snapshots"); the first revision of this PR waited on those in-process maintenance-role owners and timed out there.

**Contention only.** The state-owner contention error now carries the recorded holder's `pid` and `role` as diagnostic evidence. This is never authority: the physical lock still decides. Only `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError` with a recorded non-Gateway role gets the new wait. Data-at-risk refusals, schema refusals, retired state, unreadable state, and agent-lease refusals fail immediately, as before.

**No lock held while waiting.** Each attempt either acquires or releases everything it touched (the existing `acquireGatewayLock` contract). The holder can therefore finish its work. The wait uses Doctor's maintenance exit signal, so SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupts it instead of being held for the budget.

**Budget: 660 s.** It reuses the allowance update Doctor already gives a replaced Gateway to release state: installation-check tick 30 s + restart drain 300 s + service stop 330 s. One update-time budget, no new constant to tune. The slowest measured update Doctor ran 258 s (60 agents, 1 CPU, 10 MB/s disk). 660 s + 258 s ≈ 15.3 min, well inside the 30-minute `DEFAULT_UPDATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS` and the matching 30-minute abandoned-run threshold. A transient wait isn't capped by a service stop deadline, because nothing Doctor stopped is waiting on that holder. Each wait kind still ends exactly at its own deadline, which the existing settlement test checks.

**Not changed (follow-ups):**
- Active agent-database leases still refuse immediately (`agent-database-in-use`). Retrying them safely would mean releasing state ownership between attempts in the middle of admission, which I'm leaving for a separate change.
- The installed 2026.10.3 driver's own pre-Doctor capture also contends with such a holder. It degrades to "Automatic database restoration is disabled…" (snapshots kept for manual recovery). That code is driver-owned and can't be patched from the candidate.

## Evidence

**Real entry point, before/after (Docker, `openclaw-published-driver-update-e2e`).** The transient holder is a real process that takes offline state ownership through `runWithLocalStateOwner`, the same path OpenClaw CLI commands and plugin CLI commands use while the Gateway is stopped. It holds that ownership for 60 s. Candidate builds are relabeled `2026.10.16`. Before = `main` at `5930f05`, after = this branch at `3273acd`.

`openclaw update repair --yes` with the managed Gateway stopped and the holder active:

| | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `finalize:doctor` | `skipped` after 0.7 s: "Doctor could not enter maintenance. GatewayStateOwnerContentionError: OpenClaw state database is busy at …" | waits 57 s, then `completed` |
| Exit | 2, "Doctor and plugin maintenance remain pending" | 0, "Update finalization completed with warnings." (pre-existing advisories) |

After excerpt:
```
23:17:24.634 Waiting up to 660 s for the OpenClaw agent-embedded process 846 to release /home/appuser/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite before Doctor maintenance. Let it finish, or stop it to continue sooner.
23:17:55.249 Still waiting for the OpenClaw agent-embedded process 846 to release /home/appuser/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite (31 s of 660 s).
23:18:21.476 State ownership released after 57 s; continuing Doctor maintenance.
23:18:29.988 [update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"completed",...}
```

**Published driver `2026.10.3` × candidate, `openclaw update --tag <candidate> --yes`.** The holder starts when the driver stops the Gateway and holds for 45 s, overlapping the activation Doctor. Both before and after finish: version 2026.10.16 installed, `/readyz` 200, durable session marker still visible. On this path `main` already waited silently, because the 2026.10.3 driver passes delegated authority to the candidate Doctor. This PR keeps that and adds the role-aware wait that doesn't need the callback. Both runs also show the driver-owned capture warning noted above.

**Regression tests:** new `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.contention-wait.test.ts`. These drive real `beginDoctorMaintenance` against a real in-process state owner, with fake timers and an injected `performance.now` (no real sleeps).
- Transient holder: Doctor waits, logs the holder and progress, leaves the state DB byte-identical while waiting, and is admitted once the holder releases.
- Persistent holder: fails at exactly 660 s with a deferred `coordinator-contention` refusal. The message names the PID and says "stop it first", then gives the `openclaw doctor --fix` step.
- Manual `doctor --fix` with a transient holder, update Doctor with a Gateway holder, and update Doctor with its own process's owner: all still fail immediately without waiting.
- With the owner change reverted, the two wait cases fail.
- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-maintenance.contention-wait.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 5/5 passed in 18 s wall (about 2.9 s of test time, the CI cost). Also passes under Bun (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`).

**Related suites passed** (Node; `doctor-health.migration-refusal`, `doctor-maintenance.settlement`, and the new file also individually under Bun): `doctor-health.migration-refusal`, `doctor-maintenance.settlement` (it caught an overshoot of the shared stop budget in an earlier revision, now fixed), `doctor-maintenance.foreground-update`, `doctor-maintenance.serving-owner`, `doctor-maintenance.admission-activation`, `gateway-lock`, `gateway-lock.namespace`, and `gateway-state-owner`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `pnpm format:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` are clean. `docs:check-links:anchors` reports only two existing, unrelated anchors.

**Docs:** `docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md`, `docs/install/updating/rollback-and-recovery.md`, `docs/install/update-troubleshooting.md`, `docs/cli/doctor/recovery.md`.

Locally under Bun, `doctor-maintenance.settlement` co-scheduled in one worker with `doctor-maintenance.foreground-update` intermittently fails 6 "rechecks an initially stopped Gateway" cases. The same happens on unmodified `main` (1 of 3 runs), so it is a pre-existing Bun shared-worker flake, not this change.

Autoreview and Testbox were skipped (release follow-up work, targeted local checks only).

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact candidate head: `f1c66eb055618f0aa79505abd7bfacb1498445c8`; frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree: `de8299f6f3c4776fce1a0e00db9843f8289c8f7a`.
- Focused test command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.watch-subscribe-retry.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.session-patch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts` → 5 files, **43/43 passing** on the merged tree. Core and extension TypeScript gates and touched-file formatting pass under Node 26.7.0.
- Production path exercised by the mock-Gateway proof: `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` → `createIMessageGroupActivationResolver` in `group-activation.ts` → runtime `getSessionEntryInWorker` → SQLite worker-backed read; admission uses `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`. The test calls the production decision function with a routed group and real isolated SQLite store, not Apple's Messages transport.
- The proof harness writes persisted activation entries through `runtime.agent.session.upsertSessionEntry` (simulating the command's persistence), rather than issuing live `/activation` commands. Command owner-gating/persistence is separately covered by `commands-session.activation.test.ts`. This distinction matters: it is not a single end-to-end live Apple/command receipt.
- The exact frozen-base deterministic preflight is green after a lockfile-frozen dependency refresh. It passes extension production/test type graphs, touched-file formatting/lint, dead exports, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. The refresh exposed and the branch repaired a strict session-entry test fixture that lacked required identity/timestamp fields and literal activation typing.
- Earlier sanitized behavior receipt (the production behavior path is unchanged by the frozen-base replay):

```json
{ "verdict": "PASS", "base": "9bb171bf39b98a6965a47ab4f636e35a5701b409", "head": "68a07b52e5881bc9294ec1ddaa548a605ad7a433", "harness": "real SQLite session store + worker-backed read + mock Gateway iMessage admission", "sessionKey": "agent:main:imessage:group:99", "decisions": { "mention": "drop", "always": "dispatch", "restoredMention": "drop" } }
```

- Reviewer follow-ups: no-mention diagnostic now explains `/activation always` precedence, covered by the monitor test; the public asynchronous worker-read API has a narrowed, documented parameter/store-selection contract. The monitor test fixture now provides its required session runtime and locally passes the hosted-red shard.

prs.title: feat: let the memory slot owner report its own dreaming status
prs.body:
Related: #138366

## What Problem This Solves

A memory plugin that owns the memory slot and does its own consolidation cannot
describe its dreaming on the Memory page, so the sleep plan reports dreaming as
disabled or unscheduled while it is in fact running every night.

Two host assumptions cause it. `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` gives all three
phases the same expression (`cron: frequency`, three times), so a plugin whose
REM and deep passes run on separate schedules — or whose light pass is triggered
by a conversation rather than a timer — has no way to say so. And the promotion
counters come from memory-core's own plugin state, which stops advancing once
another plugin takes over consolidation.

The workaround available today is worse than the symptom: setting
`dreaming.enabled: true` on the slot owner makes memory-core create its managed
`Memory Dreaming Promotion` cron at the slot owner's own `frequency`, which means
two consolidation passes over the same workspace at the same minute. The plugin
manifest description correctly tells authors to keep the flag false.

## User Impact

Operators running a third-party memory plugin see their real sleep schedule and
consolidation progress on the Memory page instead of "disabled". Installations
without such a plugin are unaffected: with no provider registered, every value
still comes from memory-core exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MemoryPluginCapability` already solves this shape of problem once, in the same
type. `publicArtifacts` lets a non-`memory-core` slot owner contribute data
through an optional provider, with the host keeping ownership of semantics and
nobody reaching into another plugin's private layout. This change applies the
same pattern to dreaming rather than inventing a second mechanism:

```ts
export type MemoryPluginCapability = {
  runtime?: MemoryPluginRuntime;
  publicArtifacts?: MemoryPluginPublicArtifactsProvider;
  dreaming?: MemoryPluginDreamingProvider;   // added here
  // …
};
```

Every field a provider reports is optional and overlays the host-resolved value,
so a partial report can only add information. `scheduled` maps onto
`managedCronPresent`, which lets an event-driven phase report itself as scheduled
without inventing a cron expression it does not have. Reported counters are the
one exception to the overlay: they arrive as `reportedStats` beside memory-core's
own figures rather than in their place, because those figures count the entry
lists the Advanced tab renders and acts on (Revision 22).

**Reporting is kept apart from control.** The contract is reporting-only, and
the page shows the two separately:

* A provider's `enabled` does not override the payload's `enabled`, which stays
  the memory-core configuration the page's toggle writes. It arrives as
  `reportedEnabled` and only lights the dreaming scene. For a slot owner that
  dreams on its own, the toggle therefore reads **Off** next to **Dreaming
  Active**. That is intended: the toggle shows the host switch, which is off
  and has to stay off (see the double-run above). While the slot owner reports,
  the toggle cannot turn the host sweep **on** (that would dream twice), with a
  hint that the plugin runs its own dreaming and is managed in its settings.
  Turning an already running host sweep **off** stays possible, so an
  installation that adopts the provider while `memory-core`'s sweep is on can
  stop it from the page. The hint says what that does: it unloads
  memory-core's dreaming, while a promotion job memory-core already scheduled
  stays in the cron list and keeps running until it is removed by hand or by
  the orphan-cron cleanup (#156667) (Revisions 19–20). The Off confirmation
  that click opens carries the same owner state and says the same thing, instead
  of the generic promise that the sweep stops (Revision 21). The lock lives in one helper
  (`ownerBlocks(enabled)`) used when the toggle is clicked, when the
  confirmation is submitted and before each write step, so a report that
  arrives mid-flight closes the dialog without writing and without leaving a
  failure message.
* The Dreams scene lights on reported `enabled`; without it, only while a
  reported phase is enabled and scheduled. A counters-only report, or one
  whose phases are all disabled, reads as idle while the toggle stays locked
  on presence (Revision 17).
* Settings > Memory schedules each phase by its own `enabled` and managed-cron
  flags while an owner reports; the reported top-level `enabled` does not gate
  the rows, so a reported `enabled: false` cannot hide a host phase that is
  still scheduled, and unreported host phases are not marked running. Without
  a provider the host switch gates the rows as before. The Dreams scene lights
  on a reported `enabled: true` or on a phase that actually runs, the same
  per-phase truth its next-sweep time comes from.
* A reported phase `cron`, empty or not, replaces the host schedule for that
  phase, including the next run inherited from memory-core's managed sweep. Only
  a `nextRunAtMs` the provider reports itself is shown, so an event-driven phase
  (`cron: ""`) shows its last run instead of the sweep's next one and does not
  feed the page's next-cycle time.

The alternative — having the plugin write into `plugin_state_entries` under
`plugin_id = 'memory-core'` — would fix the display and is exactly what the SDK
documentation rules out ("they must not reach into another plugin's private
layout").

## Evidence

**Tests.** Three cases added to `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts`, covering a
provider that reports a partial status, a capability with no provider, and a
provider that throws or reports malformed phases:

```
✓ reports the slot owner's own dreaming schedule
✓ reports no dreaming status when the slot owner registers no provider
✓ keeps the host resolution when a dreaming provider throws or misreports
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Four more in `src/gateway/server-methods/doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts` cover the Gateway
overlay: a report without a search manager, an unchanged response when no
provider reports, the toggle kept on configuration
while `reportedEnabled` carries the report, and a managed-cron fixture where the
sweep's `nextRunAtMs` is dropped for phases with a reported schedule, replaced
by a reported one, and kept for an unreported phase. The two review-finding
tests fail on the previous head and pass on this one. In
`ui/src/pages/agents/memory/memory-panel.test.ts`, cases check that the toggle
reads Off while the scene reads Dreaming Active, that turning on is locked with
the hint while the owner reports and free when it does not, that turning a
running host sweep off stays possible and writes `enabled: false`, and that a
pending confirmation closes without writing and without an error when the
report arrives before the schema lookup, during it, or while `config.patch`
waits in its queue (each of these fails without its guard).
`ui/src/pages/config/memory-overview.test.ts` covers the Settings schedule with
a reported owner. Across the gateway doctor tests, `memory-state`, the Memory
page folder and `ui/src/pages/config`: `768 passed | 1 skipped` (44 files,
58.8 s wall time in one vitest run).

To stay within the line-cap ratchet, the dreaming status composition lives in
`doctor-dreaming-status.ts` and the phase chip formatting in
`dreaming-phase-run.ts`; `doctor.test.ts` is unchanged from main.

**Typecheck and lint.** `pnpm run tsgo:core` and `pnpm run tsgo:ui` exit 0.
`oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files; the line-cap and
max-lines ratchets, `check:assertion-safety`, `config:docs:check`,
`plugins:inventory:check` and `check:import-cycles` pass locally, i.e. every
step of the `baseline-ratchets` job.

**Focused test wall times** (local, `npx vitest run <file>`, one file per run, cold transform included; measured on 692789733):

| File | Cases | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| `src/gateway/server-methods/doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts` | 4 | 15.3 s |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/doctor.test.ts` | 49 | 11.1 s |
| `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts` | 29 | 6.0 s |
| `ui/src/pages/agents/memory/memory-panel.test.ts` | 19 (+1 skipped) | 15.9 s |
| `ui/src/pages/agents/memory/view.test.ts` | 22 | 11.1 s |
| `ui/src/pages/config/memory-overview.test.ts` | 16 | 9.8 s |

**CI durations** (workflow run 35832569740 on 692789733, 07:36–08:23 UTC, 47 min end to end):
`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` 1 min 42 s, `check-test-types` 6 min 10 s (five core shards
4–5 min each), `control-ui-performance` 1 min 56 s, `control-ui-i18n` 49 s,
`checks-ui-e2e (1/9)` 14 min. The previous run on fb7d8b642 (35815842767) took 33 min with
the same job times within a minute. Two jobs failed in the 692789733 run, neither in files
this PR touches: `checks-ui-e2e (6/9)` (`session-ownership.e2e.test.ts`, `sessions.list`
request count) and `checks-node-compact-large-17`
(`server.sessions.abort-authorization.test.ts`, `server.chat-abort-dispatch-rejection.test.ts`);
the same session/abort cases failed on fb7d8b642 and pass locally on this branch.

**Stored data model: nothing persisted changes.** The flagged files
(`doctor.ts`, `doctor-dreaming-status.ts`, `memory-state.ts`, `memory-panel.ts`, …) only
change what `doctor.memory.status` *returns* and how the Memory page renders it. The whole
non-test, non-docs delta (10 source files) contains no write to any store: no file writes,
no SQLite or `plugin_state_entries` access, no schema, migration, backfill or repair code
(`git diff 2e2a609f7..HEAD -- <source files> | grep -iE 'writeFile|sqlite|migrat|schema|backfill|repair|plugin_state|persist'`
matches only one comment). The one write the page performs, `config.patch` of
`plugins.entries.<slot>.config.dreaming.enabled`, exists on main unchanged; this PR only adds
conditions under which it is *not* sent. The `dreaming` capability field is optional, and
the added response fields (`reportedEnabled`, `lastRunAtMs`) are optional additions to an
RPC payload, absent without a provider. Upgrade and downgrade therefore need no migration:
an older Gateway ignores the capability field, an older Control UI ignores the extra
payload fields.

**Behaviour measured on a live install.** The problem statement above is not
hypothetical; it was measured on OpenClaw 2026.9.5 with a third-party slot owner
(`memory-lancedb-namespaced`) before writing this patch:

* Setting `dreaming.enabled: true` produced, within seconds,
  `[plugins] memory-core: created managed dreaming cron job.` — job
  `Memory Dreaming Promotion`, `declarationKey`
  `memory-core:memory-dreaming-promotion`, scheduled at the slot owner's own
  `frequency`, i.e. concurrent with that plugin's REM pass.
* The reason is visible at startup and reads like full deactivation when it is
  not: `memory plugin not selected for the memory slot; skipping its indexing
  runtime and recall registration (consolidation lifecycle preserved)`.
* With the flag left false, the counters the page shows stopped when the slot
  owner took over: `short-term-phase-signals` and `dreaming-session-ingestion-seen`
  last written 2026-09-04 03:15, `dreaming-daily-ingestion` 03:13.

**Real behavior proof through the patched Gateway.** Full write-up with RPC
output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155860#issuecomment-5789477986.
The Gateway was built from tag `v2026.9.5` with this PR cherry-picked on top (contents
identical to head `fb7d8b642`) and runs live with the third-party slot owner
registering the provider:

* `doctor.memory.status` returns `enabled: false` (the memory-core setting the
  toggle writes) plus `reportedEnabled: true`. REM and deep carry the owner's own
  crons (`15 1 * * *`, `0 4 * * *`) with next and last runs. Light carries `cron: ""`
  and no inherited next run.
* Settings → Memory shows those schedules as Enabled, where npm 2026.9.5 showed
  `0 3 * * *` three times as Disabled. The Dreams tab locks the toggle with the
  hint and lights the scene.
* No-provider fallback: an isolated Gateway from the same build with memory-core as
  slot owner returns the unchanged response (no `reportedEnabled`, `0 3 * * *` per
  phase, memory-core's next run), and the toggle stays usable.
* Existing host-enabled configuration: the same isolated setup with
  `memory-core.config.dreaming = { enabled: true, frequency: "30 2 * * *" }` keeps
  `30 2 * * *` on every phase, memory-core's next run, and a usable "Dreaming On"
  toggle. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155860#issuecomment-5791504422.
* Provider present and host dreaming on, then toggle Off (live): the toggle stays usable
  with the `ownerManagedHostOn` hint, Off writes `dreaming.enabled: false` and re-locks it,
  and the provider's report stays visible. memory-core's managed job survives that
  transition because of a separate host gap (#156666, fix in #156667). Details:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155860#issuecomment-5799390841.

| Before (npm 2026.9.5) | After (provider) | Fallback (no provider) |
|---|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/before-settings-memory-de.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/after-settings-memory-en.png) | ![fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/fallback-settings-memory-en.png) |
| | ![after dreams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/after-dreams-toggle-en.png) | ![fallback dreams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/fallback-dreams-toggle-en.png) |

| Existing host-enabled config (no provider) | |
|---|---|
| ![host-enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/hostenabled-settings-memory-en.png) | ![host-enabled dreams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyb3rb1ade/openclaw/proof/155860/hostenabled-dreams-toggle-en.png) |

**Revision 11 finding (P2) addressed in `fe625c84b`.** `resolveActiveMemoryDreamingStatus` validated only the phases. A provider returning `enabled: "true"`, a non-string `timezone` or non-numeric stats reached the page, and a string `enabled` slipped past the boolean-only owner lock. The top-level fields are now validated like the phases (`enabled` boolean, `timezone` string, `shortTermCount`/`promotedTotal`/`promotedToday` numbers, `lastPromotedAt` string), and a malformed report is dropped as a whole with the same warning, so the host keeps memory-core's resolution. `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts` rejects a string `enabled`, a numeric `timezone`, a string counter (`promotedTotal`), a numeric `lastPromotedAt` and non-object `stats`, and passes a well-typed report through. `09d1a8a86` only moves the validators above the existing JSDoc of `resolveActiveMemoryDreamingStatus`. Checks: memory-state, doctor and Memory page suites 180 passed; `tsgo:core`, type-aware oxlint, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:line-cap-ratchet` clean.

**Revision 13 finding (P2) addressed in `c78eb1d74` and `b766a27de`.** A provider may validly report only phases or counters and omit `enabled`, which left `reportedEnabled` unset and the host switch able to turn memory-core's sweep on. The Gateway now marks every report with `reportedByProvider: true`, and the Memory page locks turning the sweep on whenever that is set. `b766a27de` makes Settings > Memory schedule a phases-only report by each phase's own `enabled` and managed-cron flags instead of the host switch. Tests: a doctor case for a phases-only report (`reportedByProvider` set, no `reportedEnabled`), a panel case that renders the switch locked and declines the write through `confirmToggle`, and an overview case where REM and deep read Enabled while the host switch is off. Against the previous rule, the overview case fails. Checks: doctor, memory-state, Memory page and Settings memory suites 199 passed; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:ui` clean, and type-aware oxlint and `check:line-cap-ratchet` clean.

**Revision 15 findings addressed in `7ae60d10a` (P1) and `7b11a8ffc` (P2).** P1: the capability resolver layered a later registration over the earlier one only when it added `publicArtifacts`, so a plugin that registered its runtime first and `dreaming` in a second call lost the runtime and broke memory search. Any providers-only call (`publicArtifacts` or `dreaming`) now layers over the earlier runtime, prompt builder and flush plan, and `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context.md` says so. A new registration-path test in `src/plugins/registry.dual-kind-memory-gate.test.ts` registers the runtime, then `{ dreaming }` in a second call, and checks that the runtime, the flush plan and the provider all resolve; it fails against the previous rule. P2: the Dreams scene now follows the same rule as Settings > Memory, so a phases-only report (`reportedByProvider`, no `reportedEnabled`) lights the scene while the host switch is off. The new panel test fails against the previous rule. Checks on the rebased head: registration, memory-state, doctor, Memory page and Settings memory suites 212 passed; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, the plugins-platform test typecheck shard, type-aware oxlint and `check:line-cap-ratchet` clean.

**Revision 21 finding (P2) addressed in `efdebfad1`.** Beside a reporting owner the
Off click opened the generic confirmation, which promised that the sweep stops and
nothing new gets promoted. `renderDreamingToggleConfirmation` now takes the owner's
plugin id and, while an owner reports, the Off detail says the owner keeps dreaming,
that the switch unloads memory-core's dreaming, and that an already scheduled promotion
job stays in the cron list until removed by hand or by the orphan-cron cleanup. Without
an owner report the copy is unchanged. Tests: `toggle-confirmation.test.ts` (owner vs.
generic detail) and `memory-panel.test.ts` (the click beside a reporting owner opens
the owner-aware dialog, the same click without a report opens the generic one).

**Revision 22 finding (P2) addressed in `172ef6390`.** Reported `stats` were spread over
memory-core's `shortTermCount`/`promotedToday`/`promotedTotal`/`lastPromotedAt`, so the
Advanced tab showed the owner's waiting count beside memory-core's entry lists and
actions. The counters now arrive as `reportedStats` next to memory-core's figures instead
of replacing them. The Dreams scene and Settings > Memory activity rows show the reported
counters, which describe the dreaming they present as running; the Advanced tab keeps
memory-core's figures with the lists they count and, while an owner reports, its
description says that the figures, lists and actions there belong to memory-core and
that the owner's counters are on the Dreams tab. The SDK `stats` comment and the docs
say the same. Tests: `doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts` (reported stats land in
`reportedStats`, memory-core's count and entries stay its own), `memory-panel.test.ts`
(scene shows the reported count, Advanced shows memory-core's with the owner text, both
absent without a report), `memory-overview.test.ts` (activity rows prefer reported
counters). The live RPC captures linked above predate this field and show the counters
in the old overlaid position; the unit test covers the new shape.

**Revision 24 finding (P2) and a self-review pass, addressed in `013834773`.** The
finding: `[]` and `{ phases: [] }` passed the `typeof "object"` checks and locked the host
switch. Both now go through the record guard. The same pass over the whole diff, with the
same questions the reviews had been asking one revision at a time, turned up and fixed:
counters and timestamps only checked for `typeof "number"` (now finite, counters
non-negative); the provider's own `stats` object passed through by reference (the host now
copies the documented fields of the whole report, so extra keys, getters and a `toJSON`
never reach the response, and a throwing getter is dropped like a throwing call); a
reported `timezone` relabeling host phases the provider never touched (taken only from a
report with all three phases); the reported top-level `enabled` gating every Settings
phase row and the scene showing memory-core's next sweep under "Idle" (both now follow
per-phase truth); the Settings activity rows and the scene count filling a counter the
owner left out from memory-core's store (now n/a, or no count, and the phase-signal rows
are labeled as memory-core's). Tests in `memory-state.test.ts`,
`doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts`, `memory-panel.test.ts` and `memory-overview.test.ts`
cover each case; docs and SDK comments updated to match.

**Revision 25 finding (P2) addressed in `162bbe289`.** The Settings activity rows keyed their
owner mode on `reportedStats`, so a phases-only or enabled-only report (owner present, no
counters) fell back to memory-core's promotion and pending counts on the owner's page. The
three owner rows now follow provider presence, the same rule the schedule rows and the Memory
page's switch use: while an owner reports at all they show its counters and n/a for any it
leaves out, all of them for a report without stats; memory-core's phase-signal rows keep their
figures and stay labeled. Test: `memory-overview.test.ts` (phases-only and enabled-only
reports → n/a on all three owner rows, phase signals unchanged).

**Prior art in the same interface.** `publicArtifacts` was implemented on that
same third-party plugin this week and verified end to end: `wiki bridge import`
went from `0 artifacts across 0 workspaces` to `912 exported artifacts`, with no
access to memory-core's layout. This change is the same shape.

I am happy to test a branch of this against that installation — it is the setup
all of the above was measured on — and to adjust the interface shape if a
different one is preferred. The product question on #138366
(`needs-product-decision`) still applies: this PR proposes the narrower,
reporting-only answer to it.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): phone stops notifying after self-chat replies
prs.body:
Related: #150943

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a WhatsApp account linked to a personal number with `selfChatMode` stops getting phone notifications (no sound, no banner) after the agent sends its first reply, until the next socket reconnect.

## User Impact

User impact: people who run OpenClaw on their own WhatsApp number keep phone notifications for incoming chats after the agent replies. Accounts that are not in self-chat mode (presence `available`) behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Self-chat accounts already send a global `unavailable` presence on connect, so the phone keeps its pushes. That is the only place it is sent. Every send from the linked device then shows it as active again, and the chat is left in `composing`, because nothing sends `paused` or re-asserts `unavailable`. This matches the report: notifications come back after a reconnect and stop after the next reply.

Every outbound message (direct sends, auto-replies, media, reactions, polls) goes through the socket session's tracked send. After each tracked send in self-chat mode, success or failure, the session now sends `paused` for that chat (skipped for newsletters) and then global `unavailable`. Both are best effort: errors are logged at verbose level and never fail or change the send result. No new config; it reuses the existing `selfChatMode` safeguard, as the issue review suggested.

In Baileys 7.0.0-rc14 (`lib/Socket/chats.js`, `sendPresenceUpdate`), `paused` with a JID becomes a `chatstate` node for that chat, and `unavailable` without a JID becomes the global `presence` node, the same call the connect path already makes.

## Evidence

- New tests in `extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts` (fake socket, no real timers):
  - self-chat: `composing` -> send -> `paused` + `unavailable`, on the direct send path and on the inbound reply path
  - self-chat: a failed send still restores presence, a failing presence update does not mask the send error
  - not self-chat: no presence updates after a send
- Red before the fix (2 failed, 23 passed), green after (25 passed): `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, about 66 s on a small box.
- `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp`: 107 files, 1247 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, `run-oxlint` on the touched files, `tsgo -p extensions/whatsapp/tsconfig.json`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, docs format and markdownlint: clean.
- Gap: I have not yet confirmed the phone notification change on a real linked phone with this exact build; the before behavior (silent after a reply, back after reconnect) is what the issue reports.

prs.title: fix(memory): accept limit as the memory_search result cap
prs.body:
Fixes #172603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes memory recall failing argument validation when a model calls `memory_search` with `limit`, including Active Memory deep recall through Tool Search dispatch.

## User Impact

`memory_search({ query, limit: 3 })` uses the existing `maxResults: 3` result cap. Canonical calls and the advertised schema are unchanged. When multiple spellings are present, precedence is `maxResults` > `max_results` > `limit`, regardless of property order. Only the selected value is validated as an integer of at least 1; an invalid higher-priority value is rejected instead of falling back to a valid alias. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Memory Core argument preparer already normalizes snake_case before validation for eager and lazy tools. Adding `limit` there fixes both direct and Tool Search calls without another normalization path. Maintainer cleanup flattens the alias-copy condition, extends the existing regression table, and documents precedence.

Original fix by @wr-web; maintainer cleanup, validation regressions, and documentation by @steipete. The contributor commit is preserved.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: main `69d500b410f5d2f6ad169b9852f4d2c28cc720e0` recognizes only `min_score` and `max_results`; a `limit` input survives preparation and fails `additionalProperties: false`. The original normalizer (`c92648c50a3e`) establishes canonical precedence and strict validation.
- Regression tests in `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.test.ts`: `normalizes supported search argument spellings` covers `limit` and unchanged canonical arguments; `keeps explicit result caps over limit` covers conflicts and reversed property order; `rejects invalid result caps` covers zero, negative, fractional, string, and null values, including invalid higher-priority values with valid aliases.
- Local static checks: changed-file oxfmt passed; oxlint passed using the core TypeScript config and unchanged applicable lint rules. The temporary lint config omits only the nonmatching `ui/**/*.tsx` Solid override because this host lacks its dependency. `git diff --check` passed. No dependency installation.
- Deslop completed: removed a redundant explanatory comment and flattened the alias-copy condition. Production LOC vs main: +11/-11 (net 0); tests: +26/-0; docs: +7/-0. No new test file, timers, sleeps, or polling; 9 added table cases. Exact-head [extension CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659776841/job/116178641108) passed all 28 cases in `tools.test.ts`; the 9 added cases total 44 ms of reported test time. Its six-file shard passed 79 tests in 40.49 seconds wall time. No local test timing was collected.
- Pre-commit Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0-P2 findings. Committed-branch Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- Exact-head PR CI is the test gate and covers the regression suite plus applicable lint, typecheck, and test lanes. [Exact-head CI run 38659776841](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659776841) passed all 24 active jobs on `cd02cd14ac40f2f771a1ce24bf07382f658c64f4`, including production/test types, lint, docs, boundaries, and tests. No CI failures or reruns. Origin/main was merged without conflicts before push; the reviewed change is identical after the merge.
- Live Gateway proof, local tests/typechecks, leases, and negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. ClawSweeper's full review (comment 6180939623) found no code issues; its live-proof-only request is superseded by the policy that PR CI is the proof. Earlier contributor runtime claims are not used as evidence for this revised head.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render the agent emoji picker directly in Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent emoji picker’s only production caller is Solid, but it still mounts through a custom-element bridge and a forwarding module. Render `AgentEmojiPicker` directly from the agents overview and delete the bridge/facade. The host tag, classes, defaults, selection callback, popover behavior, and focus restoration stay unchanged.

The coupled tests mount Solid directly, and the E2E ownership inventory follows the `.tsx` implementation. The agents page keeps its lazy boundary. **UI production LOC: 698 → 674 (−24).** No visible markup, styling, startup imports, or dependency additions.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused emoji unit test | 1 file / 1 test passed with one worker; filtering, callback, and remount reset |
| Browser interaction | Reused unchanged-input pass for selection, search reset, popover layering, trigger focus restoration, and disabling while open: local Chromium 1/1 and CI run `38516007464`, job `115695190887` |
| UI typecheck | Passed on integrated head `1447fdbd29823d71c1ed50f25ba0d72a167d7ea9` |
| Formatting / whitespace | Passed |
| Independent review | Production review reused for byte-identical UI files; both failure-diagnostic changes reviewed clean through P2 |
| Production Knip | Inherited: all six findings match clean exact merge base `dad89cf260fae`; both commands exited 1, with no head-only findings or ignores |
| Strict startup performance | Current head `1447fdbd29823`, job `116082105658`: **349,424 B gzip JS / 8 requests; 45,993 B gzip CSS / 1 request** |
| Full CI | `ci:full`; [38629450434](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38629450434) completed: 53 successful jobs, 23 skipped, three failed test jobs plus aggregate. Both real-Gateway shards passed |

No local build or E2E suite was repeated under the polish-wave proof budget. Existing browser proof covers the unchanged DOM and behavior.

The required emoji import/tag/prop edits in `panels-overview.tsx` are disjoint from the other open lanes' controller imports, avatar rendering, and MultiSelect edits. The authored CI inventory change remains only the emoji implementation path; main's other inventory changes arrive through normal merges.

## CI repairs and remaining uncertainty

The previous head's Chromium RTL sidebar case failed after closing the Owners picker. This integration adopts main's correction `da80fb5d38356e42cee7825a6d4c73be7c4294bf`: await its opening animation and keyboard focus before Escape. The exact full 390 px RTL case passed in that repair's CI run `38589232105`, job `115940098615` (4,445 ms). Main's independently proven worker-type corrections are also incorporated.

The previous real-Gateway failure, **Automation catalog publication with a real Gateway > keeps an open automation draft current through real catalog publication and read recovery**, remains investigated but causally unresolved: the published option was absent after the config write. It passed the compared scheduled main run, so no inherited claim is made. Normal failed CI omits the detailed publication archive. This PR therefore adds a failure-only diagnostic derived from the recorded current publication's events, requests, and replies. It emits only synthetic phase names, counts, and booleans; assertions, timing, artifacts, and the original thrown error are preserved. No production code or timeout changes were added for that failure, and no local E2E reproduction is claimed. Both real-Gateway shards passed on the integrated head. That pass does not establish the previous failure’s cause or turn the diagnostics into a runtime fix.

## Current CI failures

No baseline reproduction establishes these failures as inherited. Bounded comparisons of completed scheduled-main runs `38632684569` and `38640790586` found no matching failing case. Failed-log downloads were unavailable; the latter run’s complete check annotations identify different UI teardown modules and a different managed-image Gateway failure. Green job status alone is not claimed as an individual-case pass.

- **Canvas widget view > shows a bounded script error and wakes only once with a surrogate title boundary**: the iframe remained absent in `frameFor`, before the error and wake assertions. A test-only correction flushes pending Solid work within the existing poll. The exact failed case passed once (1 passed, 32 filtered), and independent P2 review completed clean with final source verification. Local commit `b92b0ed7` retains the assertions and timeout; it is held for a batch push with the owned Config and reconnect repairs. This single pass does not prove the old timing cause or eliminate flakiness.
- **Control UI personal GitHub publication > removes publication mutation controls when the connection becomes read-only**: after reconnect, the Details helper timed out waiting for the pull-request group. Open #171562 and #171625 already add the new subscription receipt wait before emitting branch state. Those corrections have not landed or been incorporated here.
- **Control UI guarded config writes mocked Gateway E2E > edits schema and raw config with guarded set, patch, reload, and apply requests**: the Raw editor kept its prior Form value and Save stayed disabled. The failure trace records the original textarea detaching on an owner publication before any input event was captured. Open #171931 repairs the independently reproduced textarea-identity defect with stable action callbacks and a focus/selection regression. That correction has not landed or been incorporated here.

The current production Knip findings are `WorkerPreparationArtifactsSchema`, `postgresSchemaFingerprint`, `readPairedDevicePairingRecordsFromDatabase`, `readGitMetadataFile`, `SessionSplitDiff`, and `PostgresSchemaDefinition`. Exact-base output matches every path and symbol. The current strict performance comparison reports Chat boot −69 B and New Session boot −18 B; request counts and CSS are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(cron): restore owner app reauthorization on October
prs.body:
Related: #170498, #170298

## What Problem This Solves

On the October branch, replacing an automation's allowed tools can report success while leaving scheduled Codex app authorization missing. This backport restores fresh authority capture when the original owner explicitly replaces `toolsAllow` from the original session/account. Ordinary manager edits retain their existing behavior; foreign owners cannot borrow creator authority.

## User Impact

The original automation owner can restore scheduled app access by explicitly replacing the allowed tools from the original authenticated session. Existing jobs remain disabled until separately enabled; rollout and actual-owner reauthorization are still required for tenant recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backport of upstream `4513fcb30065172807ec21fa9165db838f903e0a` (#170498) to `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed`, based on `6f5f5b45348a8f8e89a00e056f108c9487564973`. The Gateway preserves separate management and creator grants and revalidates them under the locked update precondition. Owner-option selection uses the existing write module to meet the October cron-tool line limit without changing its rule.

The follow-ups add tests only. No runtime pin, service, schema, dependency, or production authentication policy changes are included. Dependency advisory fixes are isolated in draft #172664.

## Evidence

### Production-owner regressions

- Original production candidate: seven focused suites, **322 tests passed**.
- Follow-up: real tool → Gateway → locked `CronService.updateWithPrecondition` → worker-backed SQLite. Independently aborting either creator or management authority after locked validation rejects before persistence and leaves the job unchanged. Other-session/account and borrowed-capture cases cannot store creator authority.
- A persisted disabled legacy job is reopened, reauthorized, and reopened again, preserving ID, owner, schedule, creation time, disabled state, message, delivery, runtime state, and existing history. The store and mutation owners are unchanged by this PR.
- Real scheduled admission with synthetic native RPC proves exact prepared-profile/account rejection before client acquisition and revoked current-policy rejection before turn startup. These tests are admission evidence, not the live-effect evidence below.
- Negative control: the four exact pre-fix production files cause all five selected owner/known-tool/legacy/wildcard/missing-capture regressions to fail for the intended missing-authority or falsely-successful-update reason. Candidate production bytes were restored afterward.
- Follow-up Gateway suite: **14 passed**; Codex authenticated-runtime suite: **6 passed**.

### Actual scheduled app effect

The new opt-in live tests connect **real native capture → owner reauthorization → durable storage → actual scheduled app read** on the unchanged production candidate:

1. A dedicated configured native app-server, pinned to **0.160.0**, authenticates through its normal login API. The existing management policy remains enabled. Production `captureScheduledCodexAppAuthority` records the real configured-endpoint identity and the native managed-requirements fingerprint.
2. `cron.owner-app-persistence.live.test.ts` starts with a disabled, stored original-owner job missing runtime authority. The real Automations tool, Gateway handler, locked service, and worker SQLite store apply the explicit owner update. Reopening reads back the exact captured envelope and tool cap while preserving the original job identity and disabled state.
3. `scheduled-app-read.real-binary.live.test.ts` consumes that reopened envelope unchanged through real `runCodexAppServerAttempt` with `trigger: cron`. The native thread policy enables only `github.fetch_pr` in the selected app, and native inventory confirms only that app is callable before `turn/start`.
4. The successful effect is a native `item/completed` / `mcpToolCall` receipt for server `codex_apps`, tool `github.fetch_pr`, exact arguments `{"repo_full_name":"openclaw/openclaw","pr_number":172527}`, completed status, no tool error, and a real result containing that public repository and PR. Assistant prose is not accepted as success evidence.

Sanitized terminal receipts from the same persisted-envelope execution:

| Scenario | Acquired clients | Started turns | Completed app reads | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Different configured endpoint | 0 | 0 | 0 | Rejected before native client acquisition |
| Current app policy revoked | 1 | 0 | 0 | Rejected before turn/app-tool I/O |
| Authorized scheduled read | 1 | 1 | 1 | Exact public GitHub PR read succeeded |

All three opt-in stages passed. Native capture suite: 22.21s; persistence suite: 19.58s; execution suite: 36.61s (20.73s test body). Node 24.19.0 and repository-native live runner; no retries or sleeps added to the tests. The endpoint ran on a dedicated Linux native process through an existing authenticated transport; private hostnames, addresses, account identifiers, credentials, raw app responses, and model routing are omitted.

**Proof boundaries:** caller identity/transport and host thread bindings are test fixtures; native app inventory, policy evaluation, model execution, app invocation/result, Gateway/service/store, and reopened authority are real. This directly invokes the scheduled runtime consumer; it does not claim a wall-clock scheduler dispatch, installed-updater qualification, or recovery of a real tenant job. The developer-host prepared-profile route correctly rejected incompatible legacy MDM/managed-hooks policy before app I/O; it was not counted as a successful test. The passing live effect uses the existing supported configured-endpoint authority path and preserves its captured managed policy. Prepared-account identity checks remain covered by the separate production-consumer regressions above.

### Validation and landing

Both new live-test typecheck projects and targeted extension lint passed. Formatting and diff checks passed. Independent isolated review of the complete pinned-base candidate found no actionable P0–P2 findings; its stated limits match the proof boundaries above. Core lint also passed. Published proof follow-up: `e7cb1c487e99db3c1e7a0d0494419adf6097f39d`; it adds only the two opt-in tests.

Hosted CI on current head `e7cb1c487e99db3c1e7a0d0494419adf6097f39d` failed the production dependency audit ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660670769/job/116181240935)), matching the previous head failure: base versions of MCP client 2.0.0 and SDK 1.30.1 match GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h, and source-map-js 1.2.1 matches GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q. All dependency manifests, lockfile, workspace configuration, and audit wrapper are byte-identical to the tested October base and the subsequently advanced target `849c1d0cf54698abb2456509f740eee7d9c2a9f5`. That target advancement is the disjoint native-readiness heartbeat fix #172633; it does not change this PR's authority owners, native app consumer, or dependency graph. Fail-fast cancelled other lanes; those lanes are **not passing evidence**. The independent dependency repair is #172664; this PR does not suppress, waive, or alter the audit.

The prior ClawSweeper review on `3bcd000` accepted revocation and stored-data proof but held for the missing final app effect. The live receipts above address that hold; exact-head re-review is requested on `e7cb1c487e99db3c1e7a0d0494419adf6097f39d`. Landing remains subject to actual branch rules and review, with no admin/check bypass.

Deployment, image/runtime pin changes, and real-job activation require separate operator approval. Tenant recovery still requires deployment, reauthorization by the actual owner in the original session, and tenant acceptance. No deployment or claim of tenant recovery is included here.

prs.title: fix(novita): send max_tokens on chat completions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Novita rejects OpenAI-compatible chat completions that combine `max_completion_tokens` with `reasoning_effort`, answering with a bare `400 invalid request error`. OpenClaw sent exactly that shape for Novita reasoning models whenever a request carried both an output cap and a thinking level, because Novita requests fell back to OpenAI defaults (`max_completion_tokens`).

Found by the direct live model suite: `novita/qwen/qwen3.7-max` failed its first prompt (system prompt, reasoning `low`, `maxTokens: 64`) with that 400.

## Root Cause

The Novita plugin manifest already declares `providerEndpoints` with endpoint class `novita-native` for `https://api.novita.ai/openai/v1`, but core's endpoint-class allowlist (`PROVIDER_ENDPOINT_CLASSES` in `plugin-metadata-provider-facts.ts`) did not include it, so the declaration was silently dropped and Novita was treated as an unclassified endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit `novita-native` as a known endpoint class and select `max_tokens` for it in the completions compat defaults. This uses the plugin's existing declaration instead of duplicating compat flags across every catalog row or adding provider-name checks, and it covers catalog, configured, and discovered Novita models. Requests keep the `system` role (Novita also rejects `developer`).

Direct probes against Novita for `qwen/qwen3.7-max`:

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `max_tokens` + `reasoning_effort` | 200 |
| `max_completion_tokens` + `reasoning_effort` | 400 invalid request error |
| `system` message | 200 |
| `developer` message | 400 invalid request error |

## User Impact

Novita reasoning-model requests that set an output cap with a thinking level now succeed instead of failing with an opaque 400. Ordinary agent turns and `infer model run` already worked on main and are unchanged. No config or schema changes.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `src/agents/provider-attribution.novita.test.ts` capture serialized requests through the real completions transport for every Novita catalog model plus configured/discovered ids and aliases; all 11 cases fail before the fix and pass after.
- Live on this branch with a real Novita key:
  - direct suite `novita/qwen/qwen3.7-max,novita/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro,novita/moonshotai/kimi-k3`: 36/36 (qwen3.7-max failed on main with the 400)
  - gateway suite `novita/qwen/qwen3.7-max,novita/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`: 183/183
  - `infer model run --local` thinking off/low/high: 200 each
- Autoreview (P2 scope): clean.

Updates the affected dependencies to their first patched releases while preserving existing MCP authentication configuration and stored credentials. This is an independent dependency repair for the October branch; it contains no scheduler changes or release/deployment actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pin MCP SDK to 1.31.0 in all three direct consumers, MCP client/core to 2.2.0 in the Control UI, and source-map-js to 1.2.2 through the existing workspace override policy. MCP ext-apps remains at 2.0.0 with compatible peer ranges. The native pnpm lock regeneration changes only these four package versions; it also refreshes existing yuku package deprecation metadata.

After a legacy same-issuer refresh, verify both credentials are issuer-bound and an issuer-changing challenge makes zero token requests. The updated SDK rejects the old registration before attempting new registration, so the fixture now expects the corresponding SDK error.

prs.title: fix(agents): describe sessions_spawn agentId allowed targets in the tool description
prs.body:
Fixes #149550

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` never said which `agentId` targets are allowed, so models only learned by being rejected.

## User Impact

User impact: the tool description lists the targets the spawn path accepts, for native subagents and ACP. Text only. Lists are capped at 20 ids, so a large roster cannot bloat every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text is built from the real admission rules: ACP ids go through the ACP resolver and `acp.allowedAgents`, and `requireAgentId` is honored. Callers pass the requester's already-resolved subagent status, so building the tool reads no session store. One helper resolves `allowAgents` and `requireAgentId` for all four callers.

Native and ACP lists share one renderer (`describeTargetIdList`, built on `summarizeStringEntries`). It lists the first 20 sorted ids, then `(+N). Only the first 20 ids are listed.` Agent ids are at most 64 chars, so the count cap also bounds bytes (about 1.4 KB per list). The overflow text does not assume `agents_list` exists.

It lives in the tool description, not the `agentId` schema property. Codex drops every schema description once a tool schema passes 5,000 bytes (first pass of `compact_large_tool_schema`), and `sessions_spawn` is already at 5,045 on `main`. The schema is unchanged; the tool description is kept.

Tests: the metadata-only suite that imported the full spawn runtime is deleted. Policy and cap cases live in the target-policy and ACP target tests. One registration assertion and the prepared-requester regression (never a store read) sit in the existing `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Shipped entry point: `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message hi` against an isolated state dir and a local OpenAI-compatible mock that records the model request. Agents `main` and `planner`, `tools.toolSearch: false`. `sessions_spawn.description` in the captured request:

| Config | `main` (base) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No allowlist | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |
| `agents.entries.main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]` | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |

The schema `agentId` stays `{"type":"string"}` in both.

ACP, through the Gateway with a backend enabled: an isolated `pnpm openclaw gateway run` (own state dir, loopback port) with `acp.enabled`, `acp.backend: "acpx"`, `acp.defaultAgent: "codex"`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["codex","claude"]`, agents `main` and `planner`, and `main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]`. The Gateway logs `embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily`. `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message hi` then sent this `sessions_spawn.description` fragment (head `02c4032`) to the local OpenAI-compatible mock (full text, nothing truncated, no secrets):

```
`agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id from: claude, codex. Omit to use the configured ACP default ("codex").
```

The captured `agentId` schema is still `{"type":"string"}`.

Real output, config with `main`, `planner`, `acp.defaultAgent: codex`:

```
description: `agentId` targets a configured agent; ... `sandbox` inherit|require. `agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id, for exam...
schema agentId: {"type":"string"}
acp agentId=codex:     accepted
acp agentId=main:      rejected: agentId "main" is an OpenClaw config agent, not an ACP harness
acp agentId=(omitted): accepted
requireAgentId=true:   ... agentId is required; the requester agent is "main".
```

Codex fixture, `sessions_spawn`: schema 5,045 bytes on both `main` and this branch (byte-identical); tool description 2,805 to 2,884. Checked against `openai/codex` at `064c6b8c`, `codex-rs/tools/src/json_schema/compaction.rs`. A local Codex checkout was not available, and Codex's own normalized byte count was not measured.

The existing `agents_list` rewrite of `configured agent;` still applies (`agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`).

Cap regressions: exactly 20 ids has no overflow text, 21 ids does, and 5,000 allowed ids render under 1,000 chars (native); 25 ACP ids are capped for both the allowlist and example forms.

Main merged; prompt snapshots regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Focused tests, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsgo:core`, changed `tsgo:core:test` graphs and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass.

Test wall (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, measured on this head):

| File | Wall |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent-target-policy.test.ts` (16 tests) | 3.4s |
| `acp-spawn-target.test.ts` (22 tests) | 20s |
| `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` (74 tests, existing suite) | 31s warm; the 2 added cases take 5ms and 51ms |
| removed `sessions-spawn-tool.agent-target-description.test.ts` | was ~74s cold |

CI on `02c4032` (main at `12a91e0919` when it ran), all in files this PR does not touch:

| Red | Same on base? |
| --- | --- |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (wrapper inventory) | Yes. Fails on pure `main` `12a91e0919` and `08005517c4` locally, and on unrelated PRs in the same window. |
| `src/gateway/server.visible-spawn-fallback.product-proof.test.ts` (session storage) | Yes. Fails 2 cases on pure `main` `12a91e0919` locally (`Session patch failed unexpectedly`). |
| `ui/src/e2e/chat-mention-search.e2e.test.ts` (UI) | Not reproduced locally (no browser here). No UI file is touched; unrelated PRs fail other UI e2e cases in the same window. |

Touched tests, `tsgo:core` and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass on this head.

prs.body:
## Problem
`test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-node-exec-timeout.live.test.ts` fails intermittently in release live suites. It failed in 3 consecutive extended-stable 2026.9.33 FRVs, on product code identical to two earlier passes. The failure is "Matcher did not succeed in time": a parallel case such as `explicit` (`timeoutSeconds: 900`) or `stop` never starts on the node within 3 minutes. The case left running on its own, `process-timeout`, started in all five runs, and so did `default`, the parallel case without a timeout argument.

Two problems:
- **Contradictory prompt:** "Use exactly these arguments: {…, timeoutSeconds}" is followed by "Do not … add timeout arguments", so the model can reasonably skip or alter the call.
- **No diagnostics:** when a case never starts, the test throws without the turn state or history, and the job uploads no artifacts. A model that skipped `node_exec`, a stalled provider stream and a failed dispatch all look the same.

## Solution
- **Prompt:** pass only the listed arguments, without adding, dropping or changing any.
- **Diagnostics:** on a start timeout, report the turn status (or `pending`), the message roles, error flags, the tool names in `chat.history`, and the gateway logs. No prompt or tool payloads are logged, consistent with #172038.

## Evidence
- `tsgo` (test root) and oxfmt pass.
- Live-only test: no per-PR CI cost. The next release live run exercises it, and a failure will now name the mechanism.

prs.title: feat: suggest follow-up drafts in the chat composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting the next message after an assistant reply can interrupt the conversation; users have no optional follow-up draft to edit.

## User Impact

Adds **Composer predictions** in **Settings → Labs**, off by default. When enabled, an empty active composer can show a muted suggestion after a reply. **Tab** or **Use suggestion** inserts an undoable draft; it never sends automatically. Typing or Escape dismisses it.

Utility is the recommended default model, with Conversation and Default model alternatives. Each active client may add one model request per completed reply. Unavailable model choices skip predictions rather than silently switching. Read-only, imported, and incognito conversations do not show predictions. No breaking changes or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prediction uses bounded recent visible dialogue in a tool-free, isolated request with existing session and operator authority. Results are discarded when the draft, session, connection, visibility, or run changes. The handler waits for the existing terminal-persistence owner so a final event arriving before its database update does not permanently lose its prediction.

Thanks to Json for the feature request and design input.

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.
