prs.title: perf(state): reuse retained agent writer admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closing an agent's host compatibility handle currently forces `database.prepareWrite` even when its worker and schema admission remain live. The extra request re-enters writer admission and schema refresh before the next write.

Reuse the retained native owner's preparation. Remove the `readmitSchema` option throughout the internal execution path. The owner consumes its published physical schema facts so tracked in-process DDL still triggers repair; cold admission, replacement-file validation, FIFO ordering, and write settlement retain their existing owners. No schema, durability, shipped SDK, or service lifecycle contract changes.

The motivating trace's 161.6 ms request included 123.7 ms after posting and before worker receipt. That interval does not establish schema execution or broker queueing as the cause. This change removes an unnecessary request where a retained worker is already admitted; the completed ordinary-turn fixture did not exercise that removed path or demonstrate whole-turn savings.

### Removed check and accepted edge case

- Remove unconditional schema readmission after host-handle closure. The retained worker and published schema facts remain authoritative; unsupported out-of-process mutation of a live Gateway-owned database is not polled.
- Keep physical schema receipt comparison for real tracked in-process DDL, including a raw handle that never borrowed an agent validation receipt. This protects real schema changes without a database query or cross-thread handshake.

### Measurement

Completed three alternating pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C), ten warmed turns per run, using base `2120e734ec3cf107d2f1f66ab3526909fee63ecf` and reviewed candidate `0d2a393d5777a0338927dbddcdb7fad17140d71a`. Values below are medians [min–max] of the three run means. All six fixtures passed. The one allowed supplemental pair failed on the baseline before any turns: Gateway readiness exceeded the five-minute startup deadline. Its candidate half did not run, and the failed attempt is excluded from the comparison. No further pair was attempted.

| Metric | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warmed turn-caused all-thread SQL/turn | 117.3 [114.6–118.0] | 117.8 [114.6–117.9] |
| Warmed turn-caused requests/turn | 31.8 [31.2–32.5] | 32.1 [31.2–32.2] |
| Warmed turn-caused MAIN SQL/turn | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Raw warmed-window all-thread SQL/turn | 143.5 [141.6–148.9] | 143.9 [142.7–147.3] |
| Raw warmed-window requests/turn | 41.8 [41.3–45.3] | 43.7 [42.7–44.5] |
| Raw warmed-window MAIN SQL/turn | 1.3 [1.3–1.3] | 0 [0–0.4] |
| Whole-workload SQL | 4,884 [4,781–4,976] | 4,942 [4,869–5,003] |
| Whole-workload requests | 1,057 [1,020–1,099] | 1,086 [1,064–1,106] |
| Warmed `prepareWrite` requests/turn | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warmed `prepareWrite` elapsed/service totals per turn | 0 / 0 ms (no events) | 0 / 0 ms (no events) |

There were no warmed `prepareWrite` calls on either head, so the elapsed/service ratio is **N/A**, not a measured speedup. Each run had two cold preparations; their directly joined SQL totals were 38 on both heads in pairs 1 and 3 and 37 on both heads in pair 2. The measured owner-operation delta is therefore zero requests and zero SQL. The retained-handle regression, rather than the ordinary warmed fixture, proves removal of the redundant request.

Shared-family warmed SQL/turn:

| Family | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-entry facts | 0 [0–0.5] | 0.2 [0–0.2] |
| Actor hydration | 0.3 [0–0.3] | 0.2 [0–0.2] |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Row facts | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Token watermark | 0.4 [0–0.6] | 0.3 [0–0.5] |
| Context watermark | 1 [1–1] | 1 [1–1] |

**Measurement conclusion remains unresolved:** warmed medians increased by 0.5 SQL and 0.3 requests/turn, and exact-entry facts increased by 0.2 SQL/turn. The traces do not contain the receipt invalidations/token transitions needed to prove the specific triggering write; these increases are not claimed as a passed non-regression gate or dismissed as noise. Nearby background backfill/reclamation is observed but does not establish causation. This PR was already merged before measurement closeout; this section records the remaining evidence gap rather than retroactively claiming a pass.

Whole-workload MAIN is exactly 476 on every run. The raw warmed MAIN difference is delayed startup plugin-lease checks moving between startup/first-turn/warmed windows, not eliminated MAIN work. Apparent first-turn causal SQL reduction (277 [277–284] to 258 [258–278]) is also not a proven saving: the second cold preparation is turn-tagged in all baselines but background-tagged in candidate pairs 1 and 3.

Pre-run host load ranged approximately 88–156 on 32 cores (supplemental attempt: 160), so no wall-time or latency improvement is claimed. A private copy of the shared harness removed an arbitrary recursion-depth cutoff in the subagent-receipt parser after one excluded attempt failed to recognize a valid nested receipt. The shared harness was unchanged, and all six accepted runs used the same corrected parser. Raw fixture logs are not published.

T1 in the touched host admission/execution modules: 0 → 0. This change adds no SQL and does not move statements between threads. CI passed the worker and dialect ratchets.

## Evidence

The existing retained-worker test now verifies that handle eviction sends no extra prepare request, that committed state survives the reopen, and that a repaired schema also returns to request-free admission. Existing tracked-DDL, rollback, replacement, ownership, and revoked-receipt coverage remains. Obsolete forced-readmission assertions were removed from the retained creation-witness test.

Codex autoreview round 1 is scoped-clean at P0–P2; round 2 is scoped-clean at P0–P1 for the compatibility prose correction. Changed-file type-aware oxlint, canonical formatting, and git diff --check pass. The focused admission suite passed all 32 tests. Final head `0d2a393d5777` passed [CI run 38648451707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38648451707), Security Review, and the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. CI covered changed/compact tests, production/test types, lint, source/export contracts, Madge, and worker/dialect ratchets.

Knip is nonzero with inherited findings: eight production findings match [completed main job 116084501762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38631647790/job/116084501762) at `e589d87d7b7e`; all 17 full-tree findings match that scan or [scheduled-main job 116121040220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38640790586/job/116121040220) at `eaa6938874c3`. Finding files are unchanged between those main revisions, the integrated base, and this candidate. The nine additional UI exports were exposed by main’s removal of their Lit presentation fixture. The script-export scan passed with zero findings.

The remote check:changed attempt never reached lease allocation and was stopped after local staging made no useful progress; no remote pass is claimed. Its covered gates use successful PR CI, with uncovered checks run serially through the local campaign semaphore. No update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service lifecycle contract changes, so the update cell does not apply.

The removed third prepare argument is reachable through the current sqlite-runtime SDK type but never shipped in stable. The latest stable v2026.10.3 (`59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1`) already declares `prepare(source, signal)` in `openclaw-agent-execution-contract.ts`, with no `readmitSchema` option anywhere under src; this patch retains that shipped signature. The scoped sqlite-runtime SDK API comparison completed: four affected exports, no added or removed exports, and the expected preparation-signature change. It also records an unrelated generated Kysely outbox-column difference: the base render consumed artifacts from the later integrated-main install, while the saved candidate render predates it. The tracked schema is byte-identical within both the original and integrated base/candidate pairs, so that generated-artifact difference is not caused by this patch. This is not a full transitive SDK-surface audit. The stale optional-third-argument description in the compatibility record and migration documentation is corrected; the released compatibility record stays active.

prs.title: refactor(ui): replace session dropdowns with native menus
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat header, sidebar session, and sharing menus still used Web Awesome. This ports their rendering to the existing native Solid menu while preserving tags, classes, permissions, compact navigation, and lazy imports.

## User Impact

Session actions and sharing keep their existing contracts. Escape closes an open menu before the mobile sidebar. Search keeps focus while filtering; View preferences update without dismissing the submenu; advertised shortcuts such as A reach the menu before composer autotype.

## Why This Change Was Made

One native menu owner now handles navigation, focus, and dismissal. The full chat CI run exposed seven coupled migration issues, now repaired: a type-only import cycle; recreated search-prefix nodes; eager closed-menu content; missing native-menu recognition in composer autotype; a pointer corridor that could permanently block a hovered sibling; passive close notification before the native hide completed; and recreated divider nodes that detached open native popovers. Current owner rows also remain visible while a cached directory refreshes, and native row/header sizing retains the prior typography and alignment.

Fixed DOM entries retain identity; the browser closes native popovers when an ancestor moves. First-open content is now materialized by the menu's existing admission lifecycle and retained thereafter. Pointer motion directly over another parent row switches to that row; gap travel into the current child still uses Zag's polygon. Domain controllers continue owning actions and permissions.

The Board header uses the same entry factory as its native menu. The quick-action Web Awesome adapter remains for Layout callers being migrated separately; stateless compact helpers remain for the unported catalog filter. No parallel registered implementation is retained.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| TypeScript | Complete UI typecheck passed, including the repaired type-only cycle. |
| Search | Three 60-entry native browser cases passed; member input identity/focus and cached owner-directory regressions passed. |
| Menu lifecycle | Three lazy admission cases, both LTR/RTL sibling cases, native shortcut vs composer autotype, and three close/Escape cases passed. |
| Header retention | Desktop and compact bubble preference cases passed; real built-page Reasoning toggles preserve native View visibility and update authoritative settings. |
| Built user flows | A opens the batch archive confirmation; touch dismissal admits the pending invitation; sibling hover and paced diagonal travel select the intended owner. No page errors. |
| Independent review | Original port and complete repair diff independently reviewed: scoped clean at P0–P2, no accepted/actionable findings. |
| Full chat CI | `ci:full` selects all UI, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shards. First-run failures were traced and repaired; replacement-head run pending. |
| Builds | Exact base build passed (74.78 s); final candidate build passed (23.39 s), same host. |

prs.title: fix: stabilize Slack authorization, plugin discovery, and run recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack events can amplify `auth.test` traffic, a transient plugin detail failure can omit an app for the current startup, and conversations can remain waiting when acquisition inherits the execution budget or recovery overlooks an idle session that still owns a run.

## User Impact

- Reuse a successful Slack account identity and coalesce concurrent authorization requests; failed requests remain retryable.
- Retry remote plugin detail reads once for HTTP 408/500/502/503/504 inside the existing startup deadline. Healthy manifests stay memoized; authorization failures, rate limits, cancellation, and explicit app denial do not trigger this retry. Exhausted reads remain cached for that manifest snapshot; existing activation invalidation and later builds can read fresh metadata.
- Give client/thread acquisition a separate total budget: the greater of five minutes and three control-request timeouts, capped by a shorter execution budget.
- Include idle sessions with an actual active embedded owner in both heartbeat demand and the existing recovery checks, even without queued backlog or unrelated diagnostic traffic.
- Log bounded plugin exclusion reasons and preparation stages that remain pending.

Native execution budgets, runtime-owned waits, and writer fencing remain intact. No dependency, configuration, permission, schema, or deployment changes.

## Evidence

Fault injection through production owners failed before the fixes and passed afterward:

- Real Bolt `processEvent`: 20 events produced 20 `auth.test` requests before, one afterward; 29 authorization and sibling tests passed.
- Real startup entry: a held client factory under a 48-hour execution budget now times out, abandons acquisition, and cleans up a late client without starting a thread or turn.
- Heartbeat/recovery/lane: with the production 120-second warning and 360-second abort thresholds, a quiet Gateway recovers idle/no-backlog work once after backend/runtime protection ends; following lane work runs once.
- Plugin startup provider with warm cache: one transient remote detail failure now recovers within the same build. Healthy metadata is read once; persistent transient failures stop after two reads per manifest snapshot. Cancellation, the remaining total deadline, and explicit denial are covered.

The quiet-Gateway follow-up retains the existing three integration modes with production defaults and a healthy liveness sample. Against the prior head, queued work passes but both idle modes fail (abort count zero); after the minimal demand-count fix, the integration and diagnostic sibling files pass all 60 tests in 22.31 seconds via the native wrapper with one worker. No new fixture, timer, registry, recovery policy, or configuration is introduced.

The earlier fixture cleanup preserves all 17 plugin cases (15.71 seconds wall time). Those tests reproduced eight failures against the pre-retry owner. Previous owner/sibling validation also covered startup and Slack authorization. The remote error contract was checked against Codex 0.153.4 source.

Core production types, focused changed-test types, native lint/format, the line-cap and other initial guards passed. Independent P0–P2 review of the final recovery follow-up found no actionable issue. The broader `check:changed` then stopped in the Gateway/UI test-type graph on the same missing UI dependencies and identical diagnostics as the previous head (including `@openclaw/uirouter`); that full check is not green.

## Scope And Validation Limits

These are synthetic boundary reproductions, not a full historical incident replay or live acceptance. The historical inner await and original plugin response remain unknown. The patch fixes the identified conditions, not every possible cause of missing tools or stalled work.

Physical cleanup continues to preserve ownership and may outlast the acquisition deadline. Ordinary embedded abort/drain already has a 15-second budget and heartbeat recovery is independent per session. This patch intentionally avoids a new timeout/late-result state machine for unobserved permanently hung physical settlement.

Prior-head CI at `d933185d` failed production dependency auditing (GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h and GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q), triggering fail-fast cancellation and a failed aggregate gate. Base and that head have identical dependency manifests/lockfile; no dependency upgrade is included here. Cancelled checks are not passing evidence, and new-head CI remains separate from local validation. No merge or deployment was performed.

prs.title: chore(test): cover removed jsdom listener retention in the shared runner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `checks-ui (3/3)` could go red again without any shared-runner test catching it. PRs based between #172530 and 5e4a1bed (for example #172546, both CI attempts) failed with one Usage retention assertion plus roughly 25 unrelated UI files that reported only `DOM resources failed` teardown errors.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Maintainers get an owner-level gate in the tooling lane for the half of that breakage that still had no direct regression test.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both failures come from the shared jsdom resource tracker added in #172530 (`test/jsdom-resources.ts`). It had two defects. @steipete fixed both on `main` in 5e4a1bed, and #172487 later added stubbed-`window` coverage to the runner fixture:

- **Teardown cascade (covered by #172487).** The tracker stored the live `window` global. `stale-chunk-reload.test.ts` stubs `window` with a plain object that forwards to the native window. File retirement then called native `removeEventListener` on that stub and threw before clearing its list. Because tracking is per shared document, every later file in the same worker failed teardown. How many files depends on worker packing, which made it look like a flake.
- **Retention failure (covered by this PR).** Explicit `document`/`body` removals were never forgotten by the tracker, so removed callbacks and their closures stayed reachable until file retirement. That is what kept the Usage overview payload alive in `usage-page-retention.test.ts`. The only regression signal for this was that UI test, which doesn't run when only `test/` runner helpers change, and that's how #172530 shipped it.

This PR adds that check at the owning boundary: the existing non-isolated runner fixture child. It removes listeners from `window`, `document` and `body` and asserts, with the UI GC helper, that their closures are collectable before retirement. The check is folded into the existing producer test because the harness pins one test per fixture file. Production code is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Crabbox reproduction and proof of the `checks-ui (3/3)` failure.** Direct AWS Crabbox, N = 6 parallel `c7a.xlarge` sessions (4 vCPU / 7.7 GB, plus 4 GB swap). Each session ran the CI shard command pinned to 2 CPUs like the CI runner, with Node 24.19.0 and the pinned Bun 1.4.3. Lanes alternated the pre-fix helper (`test/jsdom-resources.ts` from `5e4a1bed^`) with this branch's helper, 8 runs per lane, all on this branch's tree.

| Helper | Runs | Retention assertion failed | Teardown cascade (`DOM resources failed`) | Whole shard green |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-fix (`5e4a1bed^`) | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 (1–27 suites per run) | 0/24 |
| Current `main` (this branch) | 24 | 0/24 | 0/24 | 22/24 |

The 2 non-green `main` runs each failed one unrelated test, once: `lazy-shell-action.test.ts > respects the canonical reconnect boundary…` and `app-sidebar.session-promotion.test.ts > drags a nested conversation…`. Neither shows these signatures; I'm recording them as separate follow-ups.

<details><summary>Command, setup, and the earlier batch</summary>

Command: the `checks-ui` "Test Control UI" step from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The group payload was built with `createUiTestShardGroups({ includeReleaseOnlyTests: false, includePrExemptRuntimeTests: true })`, which reproduced #172546's CI include list exactly; the only extra file is one test added on `main` since then.

```sh
CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY=bun-compatible \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_CONFIGS_JSON='["ui/vitest.config.ts"]' \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_GROUPS_GZIP_BASE64="<encoded ui groups>" \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONCURRENCY=1 \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_VITEST_ARGS_JSON='["--maxWorkers","3","--reporter=verbose","--reporter=github-actions","--reporter=./scripts/lib/vitest-resource-reporter.mts","--shard=3/3"]' \
taskset -c 0,1 node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts
```

An earlier batch on the same instance type without swap (6 sessions, `main` at `911726f`, 17 runs completed before an orchestration timeout) agreed: pre-fix 8/8 with both signatures, current helper 0/9. Its non-green runs came only from the kernel OOM-killing `chrome-headless` on the 7.7 GB box, which is why the final batch added swap.

Blacksmith Testbox, the repository default, sat `pending` behind the GitHub-hosted queue (about 650 queued runs). Per the Crabbox skill I stopped that allocation and used direct AWS Crabbox, which Patrick had asked for explicitly.

The matching CI failures are #172546's run 38641500904, both attempts (`checks-ui (3/3)` jobs 116121128463 and 116136475451): 26 and 23 teardown-failed suites plus the retention assertion at `usage-page-retention.test.ts:126`.

</details>

**Regression fixture.** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/non-isolated-runner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes about 40–80 s wall on this host; the fixture adds one GC call to an existing child run.
- Current helper: 2/2 passed.
- Helper with only its `EventTarget.prototype.removeEventListener` wrapper removed: fails on the new assertion, `expected [ undefined, {}, {} ]`. The `window` removal was already handled; `document`/`body` closures were retained.
- Helper reverted to `5e4a1bed^`: fails with both CI signatures. The invalid-receiver `DOM resources failed` cascade runs through `11-dom-a-producer`, `11-dom-b-observer`, `13-a-solid-producer`, …, alongside the same retention assertion.

**Gates.** `pnpm tsgo:test:root` passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig.json` on the touched files reported 0 warnings and 0 errors. oxfmt is clean. `pnpm changed:lanes` selects testRoot + tooling.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/35027d72-f77f-4f5a-af79-c690c204faec)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/527489d0-a33d-4e65-b090-6d919cc9ebb5)

prs.title: fix: chat turn splits around the GitHub publication notice
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent's turn in Control UI chat splits in two when the agent publishes a pull request mid-run with `github_publish`. A group footer ("OpenClaw · 1h ago") appears in the middle of the turn, and the "Published … branch …" notice sits outside the turn.

## User Impact

User impact: the publication notice stays inside the turn that published it, live and after reloading history, so the turn reads as one block with one footer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway saved the notice without a run ID, and chat groups a turn by run ID. The publication coordinator now remembers which run requested a publication that it processes inside that run's tool call, and the transcript reporter writes that run ID on the notice. The UI is unchanged.

Tradeoffs:

- The run association is held in memory. If the Gateway restarts after publishing but before posting the notice, the notice is posted without a run ID, as it is today.
- Publications that finish after the turn (worker and cloud sessions, deferred requests) keep today's standalone notice after the answer.
- The notice is now a run-owned assistant message ending in `stop`, the same shape as an intermediate reply in a steered run. If a run is interrupted after publishing and before any later reply, history shows the notice as that run's last reply instead of "Interrupted".

## Evidence

Screenshots replay a real Claude run from session history in Control UI, with tool calls hidden and the history window starting mid-run. Tool arguments, tool results and thinking were stripped. Before uses the notice as stored today; After uses the same notice with the run ID the Gateway now writes.

Before: the notice splits the turn, and the first half ends with its own "OpenClaw 3h ago" footer (shown on hover).

![Before: notice splits the turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b281dcd-326f-4622-982e-f65ab944379e)

After: one turn, with a single footer under the answer.

![After: one turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43772405-b75b-4bd4-b4ce-e2fe84657e8d)

- New regression in `github-publication.test.ts` ("reports an in-run publication notice into the requesting run") runs a local publication through `requestForSessionV2` and the runtime reporter. It fails on `main` (the notice has no run ID) and passes with the fix.
- `github-publication`, `-transcript`, `-runtime`, `-boundaries` and `github-repository-publication` tests: 121/121 pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files. Autoreview (P0–P2) found nothing actionable.

prs.body:
Related: #112986, specifically the generated inbound-metadata contributor left open in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112986#issuecomment-5963559444.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: changing inbound account/source facts and outbound-format hints rewrites the reusable system prompt even though those facts belong to the current turn.

## User Impact

User impact: fresh metadata and the selected delivery format reach the model without changing the reusable system prefix. Live-provider cache-hit or billing savings have not been measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reply and synthetic command-continuation producers now use existing trusted current-turn carriers. Source/group/exec guidance and caller-authored system instructions retain their placement. The source-account versus outbound-account formatting contract from #167898 is preserved. CLI turns retain these instructions even if optional context preparation fails.

The shared plugin handoff projects command runtime fragments into the existing currentInboundContext carrier used by Codex, ACPX, and AgentsAPI. It consumes the raw fragments once, keeps quoted data quoted, and preserves inline/resumed context without changing admitted input. Both ordinary dispatch and settled finalization use that boundary; built-in dispatch retains its existing fragment handling.

This addresses both findings in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172313#pullrequestreview-5525720141. The five delivery-format tests now assert the intended carriers, and their shared command fixture forwards the field that production already forwarded. Its mock-isolation explanation requires a one-entry shrink of the obsolete mock baseline; no allowance was added.

The scope remains generated metadata and formatting. Broader source-dependent policy stays outside this PR, so Related remains appropriate. No config, schema, dependency, or persisted-data migration is required.

## Real Behavior Proof

Current head: `10323e4aac109aaacbdfb0568dd1dd6253572f87`, based on `34e8c4aa277423bb8257354d7c5a93e40dcf0449`.

Native command proof runs the shipped node openclaw.mjs Gateway, authenticated public agent RPC, production command preparation and plugin selection, and the actual Codex stdio client against a local synthetic app-server. Two command turns use the same session/native thread and synthetic Telegram source/reply account, with distinct authored command bodies. Each completes successfully; source metadata and Delivery Format reach turn/start exactly once, remain absent from thread instructions, and authored command/system content survives. Stable native instructions and retained prior input are checked by the runner. No real account, inference, tool execution, or external delivery is used.

This native probe covers repeated command/resume carrier delivery. Cross-account outbound formatting is covered by the command producer tests; source-account variation is covered by the unchanged reply wire proof below. The public agent RPC puts the resolved delivery account in both its run context and command inputs, so varying replyAccountId changes conversation ownership and cannot isolate those two accounts in this route. That existing owner behavior is preserved.

- Reproduced the previous head's three command and two reply/heartbeat delivery-format failures. All five now pass through the repository wrapper with one worker.

- Production and affected test typechecks, scoped source-aware lint/format, diff checks, and line-cap/mock-export/assertion-safety/timeout-race guards pass. Normal pnpm build completes before the shipped native proof. Final canonical AutoReview uses gpt-6.1-sol, medium reasoning, standard tier, completes source verification, and reports no P0-P2 findings across the complete patch.

Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38658230011 for 10323e4aac109aaacbdfb0568dd1dd6253572f87. Its live result is the source for current CI status.

Previous-head CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38597557540 completed with 48 passing and 28 skipped jobs, but did not select the two delivery-format suites. Those suites are now directly changed and were explicitly run locally. The previous-head green result and ClawSweeper score are historical evidence, not current-head results.

The broader original local gauntlet retains four independently reproduced baseline causes: environment-variable budget 455 versus 454, frozen changelog attribution policy, two unchanged unused exports, and Windows SQLite authority/worker diagnostics. No suppressions or baselines were widened to hide them.

prs.title: fix(macos): restore failed dashboard after reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a temporary HTTP failure, the Mac dashboard can remain on “Dashboard unavailable” even after the native Gateway connection successfully reconnects. When the URL and credentials are unchanged, endpoint reconciliation skips the document reload decision.

## User Impact

A successful reconnect now restores a failed dashboard automatically. A healthy or loading document stays in place, preserving its draft. Existing authentication checks still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconcile authenticated endpoints through the existing `DashboardWindowController.update` path even when the URL is unchanged. That owner already distinguishes a failed document from usable content; no additional retry loop is needed.

## Evidence

Red/green TDD in a disposable Parallels macOS 26.6.1 VM, Swift 6.3.3, starting from `21ba1c87488d210c8d85b8fd30ec34e1b0c46601`:

| Same regression | Before production fix | After production fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP 503 → HTTP 200 at the same URL; authenticated native reconnect | **FAIL**, error page remains (2.722s test time) | **PASS**, recovered HTML renders (2.071s test time) |
| Repeated connected notification after recovery | Unreachable because recovery fails | Loaded document and unsent draft preserved |

```text
RED: Expectation failed: !current.isShowingFailurePage
     Native reconnect succeeded and HTTP is 200, but failure page remains
     Test run with 1 test failed after 2.722 seconds with 1 issue.
GREEN: Test run with 1 test passed after 2.071 seconds.
```

Reproduction command inside the disposable macOS VM after building the tests (the native launcher requires a disposable runner):

```sh
node scripts/test-macos-native.mts default \
  --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --skip-build \
  --disable-xctest --filter DashboardSameEndpointHTTPRecoveryTests
```

The test independently verifies HTTP 200 and the recovered body, requires a new authenticated socket generation, delivers the connected event through the existing manager seam, then checks the rendered WKWebView content. The screenshots below show the document after that reconnect, before and after the fix. Real native owners and WebKit run against loopback HTTP and the existing fake WebSocket transport; this is not a live Gateway/account or a claim about the original incident's upstream cause. The initial red test received formatting/Data-decoding lint cleanup before the green run; the recovery assertions are unchanged.

Validation: 36 neighboring reconnect, window, and HTTP response tests passed in the same VM (3.550s test time, 11.93s wall); native test build; focused SwiftLint/SwiftFormat; launcher regression tests (18 passed, 24.03s); focused launcher lint/format. Native regression wall time including SwiftPM/launcher: red 57.37s (cold planning), green 10.52s. The [main CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38657374703) passed (8m 02s elapsed).

![Before: error page remains after successful reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f13073a6-15d8-4fba-baf6-e5c64bc8c93f)

![After: recovered HTML appears automatically after reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a6cd461-0116-454c-b440-d48d0916f0e2)

prs.title: refactor: deslop gateway, codex, providers and packages (wave-4 bundle)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wave-4 bundle B combines the final reviewed consolidation from lanes x03 and x08 in this existing PR. It removes duplicate request/worker preparation, repeated internal observations, private pass-through layers, and handwritten copies of maintained helpers.

Combined production delta after CI/review corrections: **+375/-1,210 = 835 net lines removed**, excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated files, declarations and baseline inventories. No public protocol/configuration/SDK/persisted shape, dependency, schema, retention or permission change.

## User Impact

Supported Gateway, Codex, provider, Matrix, llama.cpp and Crabbox workflows remain available. Security/effect authority, ordinary write settlement, transcript durability, external validation, caller-specific metadata resource limits and paid-resource ownership remain with their existing owners. Mistral's native schema clone additionally preserves valid own `__proto__` properties that the handwritten clone dropped. No operator migration or new option is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway request diagnostics share one request-local timing owner; private background methods share the existing validated-handler path; internal CI-details reads reuse the established durable/memory lifetime owner, with live missing-client role checks preserved. Worker model preparation consumes prepared parent-model facts rather than maintaining speculative invalidation subscriptions. Progress snapshots retain their exact budgets and projection behavior. SSH validation consolidation was withdrawn after the wrapper extraction gate failed; both original validators and diagnostics remain unchanged. Node-launch snapshot simplification was also withdrawn after inconclusive E2E proof; its original parser and snapshot remain.

Codex shares one first-line rollout metadata reader, trusts native fork and canonical transcript-writer responsibilities, and removes synthetic whole-file mutation fences and redundant internal checks. Provider schema traversal shares keyword vocabulary; Mistral uses native cloning; Google reads its owning manifest; Matrix calls its send owner directly; llama.cpp trusts private pinned manifests and successful exclusive copies; Crabbox returns the accepted allocation from its atomic update.

Coverage credit: **lane x03** supplied Gateway/server-method/worker-environment cleanup from original commits `1493b8d77e91c137215a3cbc7ba229350f10bae2` and `38563fc6228f7b58f0558fda96d6a76bf2ff2843` (435 net production lines). **Lane x08** supplied Codex/providers/packages cleanup at `2fd9d38885cf8f46e7b859779ddf44e8a3a84769` (472 net). Both corrective withdrawals are preserved. Requested provenance/coverage ledgers remain local in the respective lane worktrees.

Gateway protocol shapes, standalone memory Phase E, native subagent Stop/delivery settlement, Matrix crypto durability, paid Crabbox holds, measured caches and in-flight foundations were retained. Explicit SQLite JSON-query columns, node-catalog consolidation and Anthropic transport changes were withdrawn after failed or inconclusive proof; this bundle does not revive them.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Worker parent-model/config/store invalidation subscriptions and disposal fences (#169622): introducing proof is synthetic parent mutation during preparation, not a cited human actual-use report. Durable inherited model facts remain the selected snapshot; a change applies on the next preparation. Live child/config, incognito actor and placement/execution/credential authority remain.
- Repeated Codex display/thread/history snapshots (#134660): introducing proof forces concurrent replacement, with no human report of this interval; a concurrent display/model edit no longer cancels the selected fork. Actual child cut/model/catalog and binding/effect authority remain checked.
- Immediate second source-turn precheck (#134660): native Codex owns boundary lookup after the boundary was resolved; a disappearing boundary fails native fork instead of another full listing.
- Typed internal fork-parameter assertion (#139911): the sole caller accepts `CodexThreadForkParams`; an invalid future internal call reaches native validation instead of a redundant partial validator/cast.
- Whole-rollout inode/size/timestamp/selection fences (#137167): first-line metadata is immutable and race coverage is synthetic; later appends/replacement do not invalidate captured metadata. Root/path/link/identity/resource validation and catalog fingerprints remain. Canonical-source-only compressed/window/deadline limits remain caller-specific.
- Alternate-file retry after a selected rollout is unreadable (#161425/#169673): prior synthetic fallback coverage was already retired; only actual absence selects the alternate representation. Corrupt/unreadable selected evidence reports unavailable; next-request recovery and handle settlement remain.
- Atomic transcript batch readback comparisons (#134660): the canonical writer sanitizes, orders, rejects changed targets and returns committed results; successful writes are trusted, with errors and child rollback unchanged.
- Internal array Proxy catches (#163707): materialized tool factories produce ordinary arrays; a future hostile internal array throws normally. External descriptor/schema getter quarantine remains.
- Recovery-promise replacement check (#149864): singleflight and sole assignment/cleanup sites prevent replacement; settlement clears the owned slot.
- Completion-attempt replacement check (#158286): the private map has one admission/deletion owner; settlement deletes its owned attempt. Delivery authority and settlement remain.
- Private llama.cpp/Microsoft manifest basename/duplicate guards (#129035/#163093): malformed pinned manifests are synthetic, not user input; a future broken manifest fails filesystem/extraction operations. Archive/hash/link/resource checks remain.
- Exclusive-copy readbacks (#129035/#163093): no human report of successful `copyFile` producing a partial/nonregular copy; successful exclusive copies are trusted, with I/O failure and unpublished-tree cleanup retained.
- Manual CAB short-read loop (#163093): concurrent truncation of the verified task-owned download is hypothetical; bounded stream copying and native expansion report malformed/truncated input.
- Crabbox postcommit allocation scan (#149680): introducing proof uses controlled interleavings and mocked providers, not an actual-use report. Out-of-owner immediate changes no longer replace the accepted result. Admission, paid holds, replay, retirement and write settlement remain.
- Matrix finite-cooldown revalidation: the Zod boundary already owns finite input; internal invalid numbers are not normalized again. Negative-to-zero clamping remains.
- Matrix extreme-clock fallback (`0840fea50d1`): its only reproduction injects a date beyond year275760; that value now raises ordinary RangeError through the existing monitor failure path.
- Google ancestor manifest hunt/`0.0` fallback (#149880): the owning manifest is known and bundled; broken packaging fails instead of silently reporting version0.0. Environment override and memo remain.
- Mistral handwritten schema clone (#99059): valid JSON/TypeBox schemas remain detached for hooks; non-cloneable non-JSON values quarantine the tool rather than entering SDK serialization. Own `__proto__` schema keys are preserved.

Other shared-owner changes are structural consolidation, not accepted behavior loss. Timing consolidation preserves overlap, ACK reset, thresholds, output and finish/disposal semantics.

Personally inspected sibling Codex contracts: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` (`ThreadForkParams.before_turn_id`), `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs` (`thread_fork_inner`/legacy cutoff), and `codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/paginated_fork.rs` (`BeforeTurn` lookup/truncation). Native fork handling remains with Codex; no wire shape changes.

## Evidence

Bundle local proof: core production types pass; runtime and Madge cycles both zero; lint-suppressions3/3; mock-export ratchet passes9,603 factories; formatting across23 x03 files and diff-check pass. The two lane patches applied without conflicts, so there are no conflicted-file replay requirements yet. Existing dependency installation is reused without reconciliation. Every runnable proof uses task-owned HOME/OpenClaw/XDG paths; no operator Gateway/state was changed and no remote payload is claimed.

Fresh full-bundle independent review raised one P2 request to restore Crabbox's postcommit allocation reread. Declined after checking the actual owner/effect path: Gateway `provider-lifecycle.ts` binds the current operation/profile/owner and invalidates attempts on stop/cancellation; `createCrabboxProvisionAuthority` composes host/project/abort checks; cold provisioning and checkpoint fork retain those checks immediately before provider commands. Operation-derived lease IDs and replay identity checks remain; maintenance does not delete live allocations, and release follows confirmed stop/absence. A whole-catalog reread of accepted warm bookkeeping is not the paid-effect authority and would only restore the synthetic out-of-owner postcommit fence. No accepted/actionable findings remain; this is an investigated rejection, not a claim that the reviewer emitted a clean verdict.

Retained x08 proof: extension production types; zero runtime/Madge cycles; assertion and mock-export ratchets; formatting/diff checks; lint-suppressions3/3; llama.cpp35; Anthropic81 (transport changes subsequently withdrawn); Mistral/GBNF15; Google18; Matrix78 and final affected actions28; Codex non-DB128 and final upstream fork11; Crabbox30 plus four final selected correction cases. Final x08 correction review was scoped-clean through P2.

Retained x03 proof: core production types and targeted lint; zero runtime/Madge cycles; lint-suppressions3/3; progress snapshots46/46; chat diagnostics9/9; final lifetime/abort/patch diagnostics62/62 runtime cases; CI-details13/13 including missing-client role regressions, private backgrounds5/5, node methods14/14, validation26/26. Some runtime runs ended with source-fingerprint refusal after erased-only type edits, so these are compiled-snapshot case results, not exact-final-command passes. Worker adapter, SSH11, service validation5 and move barrier18 emitted passing cases, but the worker batch did not finish. No blanket worker-suite pass is claimed.

### Known local gaps retained for broad bundle CI

| Lane | Original observation and remaining uncertainty |
| --- | --- |

prs.title: fix(telegram): preserve bot-self reply context under group allowlist
prs.body:
Closes #82002

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users replying to a bot-sent Telegram group message (for example a cron or system notification) would lose the quoted bot text when the group uses `contextVisibility: "allowlist"`. The agent only saw the user's short follow-up (such as "what happened?") and answered from stale session context instead of the notification being replied to.

## Why This Change Was Made

Under allowlist visibility, supplemental quote/reply context and reply-media hydration treated every sender against `effectiveGroupAllow`. The authenticated bot's own account is usually not on that list, so bot-authored reply targets were filtered out even though replying to the bot already counts as an implicit mention in groups.

This change treats the bot's own immediate quote/reply target as visible under allowlist policy in both the session context builder and reply-media hydration. Unlisted human senders and forwarded origins remain gated. Deeper thread ancestors still follow the normal allowlist rules (including `allowlist_quote`, which only overrides `kind: "quote"`).

## User Impact

Operators using Telegram groups with group allowlists and allowlist context visibility can reply to bot notifications and have the quoted bot message included in the agent turn again. Unlisted third-party reply context stays hidden.

## Evidence

Pre-fix regression proof (production owners reverted, new tests kept): bot-self text and media cases failed; unlisted human reply target still correctly dropped.

Post-fix:

```bash
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin:$PATH"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts -t "preserves bot-self reply target|still drops unlisted human|hydrates bot-self reply media|redacts forwarded origin inside reply targets"
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.session.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.message-pipeline.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts
```

- Focused allowlist/reply regressions: 5/5 passed
- oxlint on touched files: clean

prs.body:
Closes #124524

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the stock CLI and Gateway session projections against a real signed deployment, wrote failing parity regressions, and validated the shared owner change.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions list` could disagree with the authoritative Gateway in two operator-visible ways:

- archived sessions had no archive marker in JSON or the default table;
- an unlocked historical `agentHarnessId` was shown as the current runtime, even though the next turn follows current policy unless a compatible explicit override or locked transcript owns it.

This made successful lifecycle cleanup look ineffective and made historical execution provenance look like active routing drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change extracts the Gateway existing effective-session runtime rule into one shared resolver and uses it from both the Gateway and CLI. The CLI also projects `archived`/`archivedAt` from the existing timestamp and adds an `archived` table flag.

No new persistence, schema, migration, background reconciliation, configuration, or compatibility path is introduced. The Gateway loses its duplicate inline runtime-resolution block.

## Evidence

Regression-first proof:

```text

- archived fields absent; unlocked historical OpenClaw harness reported as session runtime
- compatible explicit override reported with source session instead of session-key

After fix:
Test Files: 2 passed
Tests: 9 passed
```

Broader relevant Gateway validation:

Repository validation:

prs.title: fix(media): avoid false delivery warnings while the chat is busy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: finished pictures produce “completion delivery was not confirmed” warnings when the original chat turn keeps running for more than two minutes. The pictures can then appear later, leaving a false warning beside a successful result.

## User Impact

Finished images, music, and videos can wait for their original chat without a premature failure notice. Actual delivery failures still retain the saved media and report the problem.

## Why This Change Was Made

Distinguish confirmed queue ownership from an unconfirmed handoff. The two-minute limit still bounds unconfirmed handoff; accepted work follows the durable queue's delivery or failure result. Scheduled turns release the session once the queue accepts completion, so they cannot prevent that completion from running.

```diff
 image ready → completion handoff
- queued or retryable → two-minute deadline → warning
+ retryable → bounded handoff deadline
+ durably queued → wait for actual delivery/failure
```

Related: [#154064 — avoid false failures for queued generation results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154064). This current-main implementation follows the queue-ownership approach proposed there and adds the incident's real-queue WebChat regression, including permanent failure and replay. Credit to that proposal for separating queue ownership from handoff timeout; this PR supplies additional reproducible incident coverage on current main.

## Evidence

Same held-requester reproduction on base `4612504e2bd` and candidate `779a781dc21`, with generation and model output supplied by fixed external fixtures. Requester admission, SQLite queue, recovery, and managed-image transcript persistence are real.

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At 120,001 ms: pending deliveries | 1 | 1 |
| At 120,001 ms: false warning messages | 1 | 0 |
| At 120,001 ms: generation operation | succeeded / blocked | running |
| After original turn releases: image replies | 1 | 1 |
| After original turn releases: pending deliveries | 0 | 0 |

- **Before:** the exact published regression, `waits for the original WebChat turn before settling: delivered`, fails on base `4612504e2bd` at `expect(beforeRelease).toEqual([])` because the transcript already contains the false warning (1 failed / 14 unselected; 27.35 s including worker preparation). **After:** the same test passes on `779a781dc21`; retrying the completed queue row does not add another image.
- **72 focused tests passed** across the queue binding, media lifecycle, retention, and scheduled-turn waiter suites. Covers late permanent delivery failure, generation failure, unconfirmed handoff timeout, stale requester fences, and image/music/video cron lane release.
- Queue-binding suite: 15 tests, 28.61 s Vitest wall time (including setup); the three new scenarios exercise real persistence. Four focused suites: 110.95 s including worker preparation; the final three-case regression rerun also passed in 20.34 s. [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38655406615) passed on `779a781dc21`; all required checks are green (60 passed, 62 intentionally skipped).
- `check:changed`: core production types and changed-file formatting/lint pass. The broader gate reports failures outside this diff: environment-variable count (455 / 454; reproduced on the unchanged staged base), a readonly assignment in `model-request-body.test.ts:69`, and existing unused exports. The relevant Gateway/media test type-check graphs pass separately. These broader failures are not represented as green.
- Proof limits: no live provider, browser rendering, external channel transport, or production deployment is claimed. The real incident was already verified against server logs and all ten saved files; the PR regression uses synthetic content.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce focused validation</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel.media-binding.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-retention.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.async-tasks.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast radius:** background media completion and its scheduled-turn wait. No configuration, protocol, schema, or dependency change. Queued work remains tracked until the existing queue resolves it.

AI-assisted implementation and validation.

prs.title: fix(memory): prevent duplicate Gemini batch jobs after timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini native embedding-batch creation is non-idempotent. If a create response is lost or times out after the provider accepted it, an immediate retry can create a second paid remote job. The provider assigns the batch name only in the response and does not expose a caller-supplied idempotency key.

- https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/batch-api#best-practices
- https://ai.google.dev/api/batch-api#method:-models.asyncbatchembedcontent

## What Changed

This version treats batch submission as a crash-recoverable ownership protocol:

- Memory Core persists an exclusive reservation in the published memory database before Gemini's non-idempotent create call.
- Acknowledged provider batch names are attached to that reservation as soon as they are returned.
- Each request set has a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint; manifests retain content-independent custom IDs and chunk hashes, not source text, credentials, or vectors.
- Restarted managers adopt an acknowledged job only when its exact request fingerprint matches.
- Completed output is reconciled by stable chunk hash and published idempotently to the shared embedding cache, including when source enumeration has drifted since submission.
- Ambiguous create outcomes remain quarantined. Definitive non-ambiguous 4xx rejections (except 408) release the reservation.
- The reservation is cleared only after local cache/index publication commits.
- Closing a manager aborts local polling without cancelling or duplicating an accepted remote job.
- Gemini's native-batch failure mode remains fail-closed instead of fanning a large migration into synchronous paid requests.
- Status output exposes the submission, provider job, timestamps, and recovery state.
- Deliberate quarantine clearing requires both `--force` and `--clear-batch-quarantine`.

The ownership record lives in the published database while a shadow rebuild remains isolated. Independent managers serialize reservation changes through SQLite immediate transactions.

## User Impact

Interrupted Gemini memory migrations can resume acknowledged work without resubmitting already accepted requests. Operators get an explicit quarantine for genuinely ambiguous remote ownership instead of hidden duplicate spend or an uncontrolled synchronous fallback.

## Evidence

Exact candidate head: `ca2a3d6a9bcb7215a9dfba22f8407b06ab116206`

Candidate base at construction: `044cf2e6e027591e6361dbd2784a8b9c68959e18` (`upstream/main` at the time)

- Focused Google provider/lifecycle tests: **67/67 passed**.
- Memory integration tests: **235/235 passed**.
- Plugin contract suite: **1,117/1,117 passed**.
- Total: **1,419 tests passed**.
- Core and extension production/test TypeScript checks passed.
- Changed-file structural, dependency, formatting, documentation, SDK, and extension-boundary gates passed.
- Documentation validation passed: 1,294 MDX files, 13,239 internal links with 0 broken, and 1,224 config examples.
- Full production build passed, including 91 external plugins, 152 public SDK subpaths, CLI bootstrap, and Control UI performance gates.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- A secrets/logging audit found no credentials, request text, vectors, or authorization values added to logs.

The implementation has also been exercised against a real authenticated Gemini migration outside CI: completed jobs were reconciled, cache entries advanced, and a subsequent quota rejection occurred before a new provider job ID was assigned. Completed fingerprints were not replayed. No provider identifiers or credentials are included here.

## Scope

This PR intentionally adds no quota-size, parallelism, or retry-policy configuration. It does not alter production deployment files. Provider transport remains in the Google extension; Memory Core owns durable publication and recovery state.

## Required Before Ready/Merge

- Upstream CI must pass on this exact head.
- An independent exact-head review must complete; the author-side GCP environment does not currently have an independent Codex reviewer identity, so this is not being bypassed.
- Maintainers must approve the fail-closed ambiguity/quarantine contract and its operator-recovery tradeoff.

This PR is kept as a draft until those gates are satisfied.

## What Problem This Solves

After #172558, session-link title decoration and navigation both call `sessions.resolve`. The reconnect fixture counted both as navigation, so both cases failed even though the URL, history, and destination startup assertions passed. Its request wait could also accept the earlier title request instead of the interrupted navigation request.

Wait for title decoration to stamp the link, then use the cursor returned by `deferNext` to observe the new navigation request. Remove the cross-owner resolver total; retain the exact destination startup count, no-history assertion, final URL and history length, stale-response behavior, and absence of a lazy-view error. No production code changes.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original unchanged test on CI main parent `4e2bcb935c5a369c4b81c412c4a6003dcab46a5b` | Both cases fail: expected 2/1 resolver calls, received 4/3; 130.65 seconds including the canonical UI bundle |

Production LOC: unchanged (0). Test LOC: 110 → 112 (+2). This test-only change has no visual or startup-bundle delta. The existing browser integration is needed to cover reconnect, abandoned navigation, and browser history through the actual router.

The red-main direct-push route was attempted twice. Both writes were definitively rejected as non-fast-forward because other changes reached `main`; this focused PR uses the native landing workflow to handle concurrent writers. prs.title: fix(gateway): report active unmanaged restart startup accurately
prs.body:
Closes #119958

## Summary

Fixes the unmanaged SIGUSR1 restart path that reports a 60-second health timeout even when the same gateway process has accepted the restart and is still progressing through startup.

## Root cause

The CLI sends SIGUSR1 and then polls only listener health. An in-process restart can retain its PID while the listener is intentionally absent, so PID and port state cannot distinguish active startup from a dead restart.

## Fix

The gateway loop owns a short-lived renewable startup-progress lease while awaiting each startup. The unmanaged listener waiter accepts a typed `still-starting` result only when that lease is fresh, belongs to the signaled gateway process, and began after this restart request. The normal 60-second listener window is not extended. Missing, stale, expired, or non-progressing lease evidence still fails the restart.

## User impact

A bounded still-starting result tells operators to run `openclaw gateway status --deep` instead of treating a healthy slow boot as failed and applying destructive recovery.

## Validation

Run the focused lifecycle, listener-health, run-loop, and lease regressions; then `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:changed`.

## Credit

Thanks @islandpreneur007 for the source reproduction in #119958.

prs.title: feat(exec): add allowSymlinkPath config option
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a workspace path contains symlink components (for example
`/mnt/ollama/.openclaw/workspace` where an intermediate directory is a
symlink), the exec tool hard-blocks host execution with
`SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval requires canonical cwd (no symlink path components)`.
Operators whose filesystem layout legitimately uses symlinks have no opt-out,
so `system.run` on those hosts is unusable without relayouting the disk.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts`:
  symlinked cwd accepted when `allowSymlinkPath: true`, and the approval plan
  exposing `requestedCwd` next to the canonical `cwd`; full suite passes
  (25/25) after re-integration onto current `main`.
- Rebased onto `origin/main` (`188fd77d91a`): the symlink check now lives in
  `src/infra/system-run-cwd-binding.ts`; the opt-in flag gates only the
  symlink rejection, while realpath resolution and file-identity (TOCTOU)
  revalidation are preserved on both the approval and launch paths.
- Default behavior unchanged: without the flag the denial message and
  identity checks are byte-identical to `main`.

---

## Summary

This PR adds a new `tools.exec.allowSymlinkPath` boolean config option that allows the exec tool to run commands in directories containing symlinks, or when the cwd itself is a symlink.

### Problem

When a user's workspace path contains symlink components (e.g., `/mnt/ollama/.openclaw/workspace` where an intermediate directory is a symlink), the exec tool hard-blocks execution with:

```
SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval requires canonical cwd (no symlink path components)
```

This is overly restrictive for environments where symlinks are a normal part of the filesystem layout and the user trusts the symlink targets.

### Solution

Add an opt-in config flag `allowSymlinkPath` that relaxes the symlink checks in `resolveCanonicalApprovalCwdSync` while still verifying that the resolved realpath is stable (file identity check against `cwdRealStat`).

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.tools.ts` | Add `allowSymlinkPath?: boolean` to `ExecToolConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add zod validation field |
| `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts` | Thread `allowSymlinkPath` through `resolveCanonicalApprovalCwdSync`, `hardenApprovedExecutionPaths`, and `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan`; skip symlink checks when enabled |
| `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` | Read agent-level or global exec config and pass to hardening |
| `src/node-host/invoke.ts` | Load runtime config in `system.run.prepare` path and pass `allowSymlinkPath` |
| `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts` | Add test: symlinked cwd accepted when `allowSymlinkPath: true` |

### Usage

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "exec": {
      "allowSymlinkPath": true
    }
  }
}
```

Or per-agent:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      {
        "id": "main",
        "tools": {
          "exec": {
            "allowSymlinkPath": true
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Verification

- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts` passes (17/17)
- [x] `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` passes (24/24)
- [x] Config validated successfully on live gateway restart

### Notes for Reviewers

- This change is **opt-in**; default behavior remains unchanged (symlinks are still blocked by default).
- The identity mismatch check is relaxed but not removed: when `allowSymlinkPath` is enabled, we still verify `sameFileIdentity(cwdStat, cwdRealStat)` to ensure the symlink resolves to a stable target.
- The `fix(deps): update fs-safe hash and allow exotic subdeps` commit is included in this branch because `origin/main` currently fails to build without it.

prs.title: fix(tlon): preserve provider-native group message ids
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon group sends returned a fabricated `~ship/<unix-ms>` message ID instead of the provider-native dotted `@ud`. Reusing that delivery receipt for a reply targeted the wrong group post. Direct messages use a separate `~ship/<@ud>` contract and are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tlon send owner now formats timestamps once with `scot("ud", da.fromUnix(sentAt))`. Group sends return that bare provider-native ID, while direct messages continue to prepend the sending ship. This repairs the producer boundary instead of rewriting IDs later in receipt or reply routing.

## User Impact

Agents and operators can reuse a sent Tlon group message receipt as the reply target, preserving native thread routing for both text and media sends. Direct-message IDs and existing numeric reply-ID formatting remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the repair: 3 of 8 focused send-owner tests failed, covering group text/media receipts and root-to-reply target reuse.
- After the repair: focused Tlon send-owner tests pass 8/8; the full Tlon suite previously passed 285/285.
- Fresh publication check: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts` passes 8/8, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Extension type, lint, format, package-boundary, and architecture checks passed during validation.
- Direct dependency proof: `@urbit/aura` 3.0.0 declarations and implementation show `da.fromUnix(number): bigint`; `scot("ud", bigint)` renders decimal digits grouped with dots.
- Scope: exactly `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts` and `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts`. Production `+6/-3` (net +3); tests `+74/-2`.
- Exact-head CI is terminal green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- AI-assisted; the patch was inspected and validated. No agent transcript is included.

**Review required: live Tlon group root-to-reply roundtrip unavailable; do not merge until supplied.** No authorized live Tlon ship and disposable group channel were available. The deterministic poke-boundary test verifies the exact outgoing reply target, but it is not a live external-provider roundtrip.

prs.title: fix(qa): own screenshot and recording artifact freshness
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Mantis desktop-browser QA could report screenshots or recordings left by an earlier run as current evidence when an output directory was reused. Empty or symlinked captures could also be accepted, and a screenshot-only success could subsequently fail the Discord status-reactions evidence workflow.

**Draft: the improved implementation is preserved for review, but mandatory real desktop proof is still outstanding. Do not merge or enable automerge yet.** This body replaces the previous head's proof claims; those older claims are not being carried forward as evidence for this rewrite.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture owner now retires exactly its screenshot, recording, summary, report, and error file before preflight. It settles every cleanup without following symlink targets or recursively removing directories. Failed transfers clean only the two possibly partial visual files. Both captures are inspected as regular nonempty files; the screenshot is required, while the recording remains optional. Inspection and cleanup failures retain both causes, and one result drives summary/report publication.

The status-reactions workflow preserves optional-video behavior through copy, independent preview generation, report links, and the evidence manifest. Required screenshots remain required. Existing SSH selection, non-deleting rsync behavior, lease retention, unrelated output files, and remote diagnostic logs are unchanged. A valid video accompanying an invalid required screenshot remains on disk for diagnosis but is not claimed by the failed result.

This is a source-trusted rewrite on main baseline `8c7de197cd6d535943d10a04312547b134cf00e2`, preserving the original author's credit. The contributor branch was not executed locally.

## User Impact

Internal Mantis QA operators get accurate capture evidence and usable screenshot-only status-reactions runs. This does not change the general browser automation runtime. No configuration, dependency, persistent-store, provider, or security-policy surface is added. The root changelog is intentionally omitted under the internal-only exception.

Runtime: **+97/-72 (net +25)**. Workflow: **+22/-19 (net +3)**. Tests: **+411/-1 (net +410)**. Consolidating the duplicate summaries absorbs most of the owner repair; remaining production growth enforces artifact lifecycle, regular-file validation, error preservation, and independent optional-video handling.

## Evidence

- The trusted baseline reproduced six failures through the actual producer with real local filesystem operations and rsync: stale video reuse, false screenshot success, empty captures, symlinks, partial-copy remnants, and preflight remnants. The fresh-capture control passed.
- Regression tests failed before their respective repairs. Final focused suites pass: **28 owner tests + 8 workflow tests = 36**. These cover sequential directory reuse, invalid capture combinations, copy/inspection/cleanup failures, stale reports and errors, directory/symlink safety, absent optional videos, either lane's preview failure, and required screenshot enforcement.
- The same actual-producer/local-rsync harness passes on the final tree with no findings. It uses synthetic PNG/video fixtures and substitutes cloud transport; it is **not live Chrome, X11, remote Crabbox, or Discord proof**. Its preflight check covers visual names; metadata retirement is exercised by the separate owner filesystem tests.
- Workflow tests execute the actual workflow shell step with controlled external commands and validate artifacts through the actual evidence-manifest loader. They do not publish to GitHub or Discord.
- Targeted formatting, `git diff --check`, and actionlint pass. Two independent code/proof reviewers approved the final tree. Native Codex autoreview and a distinct full-source Codex review are clean after addressing both the double-fault error-loss and stale preflight-report findings.
- Native extension typechecking hit its 90-second watchdog without diagnostics under host load; this was not a pass. Full types, type-aware lint, complete workflow gates, and exact-head hosted CI remain pending. No build/SDK preparation or weaker lint configuration was substituted.

Reproducible focused commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/desktop-browser-smoke.runtime.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/mantis-status-reactions-artifacts.test.ts
actionlint .github/workflows/mantis-discord-status-reactions.yml
git diff --check
```

### Remaining desktop proof

The real Mantis CLI must still run against an approved Linux desktop lease with a visible Chrome/X11 capture and actual SSH/rsync transfer, repeating the same output directory from PNG+MP4 to screenshot-only to failure. Standard Testbox cannot exercise this flow: its provider lacks desktop/browser capabilities and inspect does not supply the SSH endpoint/key/user required by the existing Mantis copy owner. Installing Chrome alone would not resolve that transport mismatch. No paid desktop lease has been acquired, and this PR does not add a provider adapter or alternate transport to work around the gap.

### Latest ClawSweeper findings and rank-up moves

The latest substantive review is August 19 on the original head; the August 26 comment is a review-start placeholder, not a new verdict.

- Optional status-reactions MP4 copy, preview/report paths, and full-video manifest entries: addressed, with both independent lanes covered.
- Refresh the old branch against main and rerun producer/consumer proof: addressed by the trusted-main rewrite and final 36-test plus filesystem/rsync run. Main advancing alone is not claimed as a reason for another rebase.
- Real desktop/workflow publication proof and exact-head CI: still pending; the PR remains draft. Earlier proof-sufficient labels and CLI-help output do not establish this rewritten head's real desktop behavior.
- The previous serialized-state warning concerned QA artifact fixtures, not an OpenClaw runtime store or schema migration; no persistent-store design change is included.

Named follow-up: **Mantis Slack/Telegram desktop artifact freshness**. Their separate producer lifecycles still warrant a dedicated sequential-reuse and cleanup audit with their own real-flow proof; this draft does not claim those owners are repaired or execute their authenticated flows.

prs.title: fix(signal): re-probe managed daemon liveness so hangs surface as disconnected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed signal-cli daemon is only proven alive once, at startup (`waitForSignalDaemonReady`). After that, the daemon's SSE endpoint stays idle between inbound Signal events, so a daemon that hangs (deadlocked, wedged on a syscall, etc.) without exiting its process keeps reporting `connected: true` forever — there is no other liveness signal, so the gateway health monitor has nothing to act on and never restarts it (#116295).

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a periodic (60s) liveness probe that re-checks the daemon's own `/api/v1/check` endpoint via the existing `signalCheck` adapter, started once `autoStart` brings the managed daemon up and stopped in the same `finally` block that already tears down the ingress monitor. A successful probe publishes a connected + transport-activity status patch (`createConnectedChannelStatusPatch`/`createTransportActivityStatusPatch`, the same factories the SSE path already uses); a failed probe marks the account `connected: false` with the probe error in `lastError`, which is what the gateway health monitor reads. Wiring reuses the account's existing `setStatus` sink (`createAccountStatusSink`), the same one `startAccount` already writes an initial snapshot through.

## User Impact

A wedged managed signal-cli daemon now flips to disconnected within ~60s of going unresponsive instead of appearing healthy indefinitely, letting the gateway's existing restart/alerting machinery react to it.

## Evidence

- `autoStart` (and therefore the heartbeat) only ever applies to `managed-native` transport, the exact case this issue is about — container-transport accounts don't spawn a daemon here and are unaffected.
- The probe reuses `signalCheck`, the same function `waitForSignalDaemonReady` uses for startup readiness, applied periodically instead of once.

Fixes #116295

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session Stop leaving a Codex parent blocked for new messages or rewind when its native child had already been interrupted.

## User Impact

Stop can retire that child and release the parent's ownership claim without resetting the session, losing history, or stopping a sibling request.

## Why This Change Was Made

An interrupted native turn is already terminal, but its resumable task still needs cancellation settlement. Reuse the exact recorded interruption and the existing cancellation owner instead of trying to interrupt the finished turn again. Caller custody, current-assignment, and session-generation checks stay intact. The existing deadline wait moves unchanged into a sibling module to keep the oversized monitor from growing.

No configuration, schema, or public SDK changes.

## Evidence

- The new owner-boundary regression fails before the fix with incomplete cancellation and passes afterward. It verifies that selected interrupted children release the real parent claim, while unselected children retain it.
- 35 focused tests pass across cancellation, direct authority/follow-ups, and session retirement: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.cancellation.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.direct-authority.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-retirement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (116.91s wrapper wall time). The final changed-file run passed 10 cases in 152.16s; individual cases took 4–37ms, with cold worker compilation/import startup accounting for the wrapper cost.
- Independent AutoReview through P2: no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (36m 1.8s cold build). Extension production/test types, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap, database-worker/dialect, timeout-race, and import-cycle checks pass. The test-types check caught a timer-cleanup callback returning the Vitest helper; it now returns `void`, and test types plus the changed test pass on recheck.

It reproduces against the untouched base `f36f240ab323` with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --staged --base f36f240ab323` before staging this fix. The production dead-export scan also flags `ui/src/components/web-awesome.ts:26` (`consumeDropdownKeyboardDismissal`), which is byte-identical to the base and has only test consumers there. Neither unrelated finding was hidden with an allowance or repaired in this PR.

prs.title: fix(plugins): reject embedded runs whose sessionId disagrees with the key's persisted identity
prs.body:
Closes #120787

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveRunSessionExecutionOwner()` derives the ownership scan scope (`agentId`, `storePath`) from the plugin-supplied session key. `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned()` then scans only that one scoped store, so a plugin-supplied `sessionId` that actually lives in a *different* agent/store is never observed - the ownership check silently passes. The caller's key then binds to a bogus fresh window in its own store instead of executing the foreign session (downstream binding anchors to the key-derived store), but the identity guarantee is broken and integrity-polluting windows get created.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scoped scan cannot see cross-store ids by design, so absence there must not imply safety when the caller also supplied a concrete id. This adds a fail-closed check after the existing scan in `src/plugins/registry-runtime-session-ownership.ts` (reached from `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts` via `loadSessionOwnership()`):

```ts
if (directSessionId && sessionKey && entry && entry.sessionId !== directSessionId) {
  throw new Error(
    `Plugin "${pluginId}" may execute session "${sessionKey}" only with its exact persisted identity.`,
  );
}
```

Deliberate ordering and scope:
- Placed **after** `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned` so same-store mismatches keep their richer pre-existing ownership error (the scan finds locked foreign rows in the same store).
- Only fires when the plugin supplies both a session key with a resolvable entry *and* a differing explicit id; fresh-session create flows (id absent from stores, no key/entry) are unaffected.
- Locked-session flows return earlier with their own stricter identity rules.

## User Impact

- Embedded runs that pair an owned key with a foreign/differing session id are now rejected up front instead of silently creating a bogus execution window.
- Legitimate flows (matching id/key pairs, create-on-run, incognito scans) behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Focused proof (Windows, Node v24.15.0): `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ``src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.sqlite.test.ts`` src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.test.ts` -> 2 passed + 16 passed.

Update: the production guard landed after review feedback (it was correctly flagged as missing from the initial head) — the check above is now in the diff. New regression test uses real per-agent SQLite stores: victim harness-locked session lives in agent `main`'s store while the caller owns a key in agent `researcher`'s store; `{sessionId: victimId, sessionKey: ownKey}` previously resolved (mock executed), now rejects with the exact-identity error and never reaches `runEmbeddedAgent`. The pre-existing same-store case still asserts its original `'owned by plugin "harness-owner"'` error.
