prs.title: fix(ingress): bound pre-adoption abandonment with the existing retry budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An ingress row can defer its turn to the reply queue and then end without ever being admitted. When that happens, the row is released with `lastError: "turn-abandoned"` and an attempt recorded, but the retry policy is never consulted. Such a row can therefore retry forever:
- `attempts` climbs past `maxAttempts`;
- the row never dead-letters;
- it holds the head of its lane, so the messages behind it never run.

Sending abandonment through the shared retry disposition takes a single hunk, but that is only safe once intentional cancellation stops arriving as abandonment. On main, the reply queue settles every unadmitted turn through `onAbandoned`:
- `TurnAdoptionLifecycle` has no `onCancelled`;
- the ingress binding omits it;
- the inbound debounce flush drops it.

Bounding abandonment on its own would therefore charge these as failures: queue clears, Stop cleanup, drops of aborted followups, collect-group aborts and gateway shutdown. That was the P1 on the earlier head of this PR.

This PR lands both halves:
- **`fix(reply)`** makes `onCancelled` part of the reply terminal contract:
  - every intentional relinquish site uses it;
  - both dedupe owners release on either terminal callback;
  - fan-in always offers `onCancelled`.
- **`fix(ingress)`** settles `onAbandoned` through `applyFailureDisposition`. It records one attempt, respects `maxAttempts` and `deadLetterMinAgeMs`, and dead-letters as `retry-limit-exceeded`.

There is no AsyncLocalStorage compatibility flag. Every lifecycle that reaches a fan-in carries `onCancelled`, so the consumer makes the flag unnecessary.

## Since Revision 17 (head `ee2f6dfdf651a8bd4416edb435335c5393190c5e`)

This revision addresses ClawSweeper's review of `e682f7cc17` (fast-forward; no rebase):
- **`7cab4e61eb`, [P1] cancel LINE's unhanded delivery when shutdown returns ownership.** In `extensions/line/src/webhook-spool.ts`, the stop branch for a delivery that returned without `onAdopted` or `onDeferred` now ends ownership through `fannedIn.cancel()` instead of `fannedIn.abandon()`. A row at the retry ceiling is no longer dead-lettered as `retry-limit-exceeded` on stop. The new test "keeps an aged row at the retry ceiling recoverable when shutdown ends an unhanded delivery" covers the active-delivery-return case. It passes (16/16) and fails with only this fix reverted (15/16).
- **`2b67393ddd`, `5c214fa2a4`, `cd45f79821`, [P3] await owned settlement signals instead of polling.** Every `vi.waitFor` this PR added, across 10 test files, is gone. The tests now await one of three signals:
  - the queue's committed write, through `observeChannelIngressQueueWrite`, or the new `observeChannelIngressQueueWrites`, which wraps each queue method once so several observers can't stack;
  - the drain's own `claimNext` commit;
  - deferreds that the owned turns resolve.
  
  These commits are test-only.
- `ee2f6dfdf6`: two lint fixes in the Slack tests (a bound `claimNext`, an unused import).

**Checks at `ee2f6dfdf6` (Linux arm64):**
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- 35/35 focused test files pass.
- `pnpm check` fails only in its lint step. None of the reported files is in this PR's diff against `042db1e706`; the remaining errors (max-lines, ui) are in files this PR doesn't touch.
- The Telegram cancellation e2e passed 3 of 3 repeated runs.

**Proof.** The boundary harness was rerun at this exact head with the same bytes, against control `042db1e706`. Every verdict and final SQLite row matches the `0cb65da5f2` corpus. The corpus is at https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/615595b9fcc318c8c6d45d4a4f0db2ad9069a7a9/PR-124337/PROOFS/ee2f6dfdf651a8bd4416edb435335c5393190c5e

**Still open:** ClawSweeper's request for shipped-Gateway / real-transport cancellation and restart evidence, plus Telegram Test Server proof for cancelled interactive submissions. That needs a Telegram test bot and account, and is not covered by the harness above.

## Since Revision 16 (head `e682f7cc17fdbc34f299b6703e11aa23d90c120c`)

Revision 16 had no findings; the branch had since gone conflicting with main. This head merges upstream main `042db1e706` into `51631e61a23` (merge `8853b1ae51c`; no rebase) and adds two test-only commits. Upstream had refactored the follow-up queue and Feishu settlement, so the cancellation half is re-applied onto upstream's shapes rather than merged textually:
- `completeFollowupRuns` forwards an optional disposition; stop, clear and aborted collect/summary sources settle as `cancelled` through it.
- `consumeQueueSummaryDelivery` keeps its settlement argument; upstream's boolean `false` calls are `"retained"`.
- `dropAbortedFollowups` stays in `aborted-followups.ts` (re-exported from `drain.ts`) and settles through `completeFollowupRuns(…, "cancelled")`.
- Feishu broadcast: a `cancelled` lane state on upstream's pending/deferred/completed/failed model. Feishu flush and delivery, Slack and Telegram regain `onCancelled`; Telegram's abort-reason mapping now lives in `abortedProcessingResult`.
- `c6cfd25c543`: the ingress-cancellation test follows upstream's dispatch fixture move to `dispatch-from-config.test-support.ts`. `0cb65da5f22`: the Slack cancellation test's mocks spread the real modules (first-party mock export ratchet).

- `e682f7cc17f`: oxfmt only. It folds one `if` condition in `bot-handlers.callback-router-controls.ts` onto one line, so behaviour is byte-equivalent to `0cb65da5f2`, where the checks and proof below ran.

Checks at `0cb65da5f2` (Linux arm64): `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; 35/35 focused test files (this PR's suites plus the queue, drain, Feishu, Slack and Telegram suites the merge touched). `pnpm check` fails three ratchets (line-cap growth, max-lines suppression, assertion SAFETY comment) that fail identically on main `042db1e706` and name no file in this PR. The boundary proof below was rerun at `0cb65da5f2`. CI note: `src/plugin-sdk/channel-inbound.test.ts` › "dispatches a published inbound event before automatic session maintenance" fails on main `b3c7dc2af7` itself (3 of 3 local runs), but passes at this branch's tree (`042db1e706` base). It touches nothing in this PR.

## Since Revision 14 (head `51631e61a238de75ae0207af541b341e6edeac0e`)

The branch is rebased onto main `2983dfcfb3` and merges cleanly into main `f986a7aaf1`. The two original commits change only in rebase-conflict hunks: upstream's new `readLaneBacklog` stays drain-only, the vitest path list keeps both entries, and Telegram uses upstream's participant heartbeat. On top of them:

| commit | addresses | change |
|---|---|---|
| `4dd7877d56a` | [P1] carry cancellation through custom channel lifecycle adapters | Telegram, Twitch, and Feishu's merged and broadcast lifecycles forward `onCancelled`. Feishu's pre-flush cleanup runs on cancellation too. |
| `06cd20afc87` | [P1] preserve Slack replay and migration cleanup on cancellation | Both Slack owners wrap cancellation: `releaseClaims()` and `settleTurn()` run, then cancellation is forwarded budget-free. |
| `6ff545fd490` | [P2] clean up deferred MMS attachments on cancellation | The MMS lifecycle has its own cancellation wrapper that cleans up before forwarding. |
| `784a1f1f437` | same class | LINE ends shutdown-rejected ownership by cancellation, not abandonment, because the core types define shutdown as cancellation. |
| `5f713b6bd7d` | same class | Feishu message and comment paths whose abort already fired cancel instead of abandoning. Real dispatch failures still abandon. |
| `3cd7de6f3d4` | found in review | SMS: a rejected MMS unlink no longer skips settlement. Cleanup failure is logged, and the owner settles once, for both cancel and abandon. |
| `d1c4823226e` | found in review | Core `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` contains a rejected async `onCancelled` or `onAbandoned` (logged via the runtime error log). The callback still starts synchronously, and `onSettled` still runs right after it. |
| `bcbc2837f4e` | found in review | Telegram albums: cancelling a coalesced turn settled every participant as `failed-retryable`, which dead-lettered non-head members at the ceiling. A `{ kind: "cancelled" }` result now routes to each member's own `onCancelled`, and the update tracker treats cancelled like retryable (not completed), so dedupe cannot swallow the redelivery. |
| `53cb34f058` | found in review | The dedupe wrapper `releaseBeforeTurnAdoptionRetry` now returns `onAbandoned`'s result, so core can contain its rejection on the wrapped path. |
| `cb1cd8a1d0f` | Revision 15 [P3] mock isolation | The two new Telegram dispatch mocks spread the real module (`importOriginal`) and override only `buildTelegramMessageContext` and `dispatchTelegramMessage`. |
| `4a6c265fa80` | Revision 15 [P3] `drain.ts` line cap | `dropAbortedFollowups` moved verbatim into the sibling module `queue/aborted-followups.ts`; only the parameter type changed, to a named subset alias. `drain.ts` re-exports it, so existing `drain.js` module mocks still catch the call. The baseline is unchanged. |
| `51631e61a23` | Revision 15 [P3] e2e line cap | `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` is restored to its upstream content. The aged-album cancellation regression moved unchanged into `telegram-ingress-coalescing.cancellation.e2e.test.ts`, which uses the shared fixtures; the bundled-plugin e2e glob includes it. |

**New tests.** Each new test failed before its fix and passes after it.
- The aged-row tests seed a row at 7/8 attempts with `lastError` "prior failure". They cancel the deferred turn, then assert that nothing is dead-lettered and that the row returns with attempts and error intact. These run on the real durable SQLite queue for Telegram (single update and a two-member album), Twitch, Feishu (merged turn and handler-entry abort) and LINE (late deferral at shutdown).
- Slack migration fence: a cancelled deferred turn lets a queued `channel_id_changed` run. Before the fix, `stop()` waited on it indefinitely.
- Rejection tests run the failing callback directly and behind the dedupe wrapper. They assert the order release → callback → `onSettled`, that there is no unhandled rejection, and that the error is logged. They check the error text, not a count of log calls.

## Known boundary

- Reply-queue cap evictions still settle as genuine abandonment, which is one bounded attempt. That is intended.
- IRC forwards `onCancelled`, but it does not update its local handoff state on cancellation. That would only matter for a cancellation before `onDeferred`, which the reply lane does not send.
- Channels that call `onAbandoned` on real dispatch failures (Mattermost, MS Teams, Signal) are unchanged. Those failures are charged attempts, as intended.

## Evidence

**Real behavior** (central fix). I ran a production-module boundary harness at this exact head `0cb65da5f2283965905abe1c55aca505e8139550`, with main `042db1e7064930a08c534c4487864d7bfb8c5287` (the merge's second parent) as the control. The chain is the channel ingress monitor → the durable SQLite ingress queue → the drain → the bound reply/followup queue. There is no vitest and nothing in the chain under test is mocked. Each scenario ends with a projection of the SQLite row. Every verdict matches the earlier run at `b2d5e48e5b`.

| scenario | this PR | main (control) |
|---|---|---|
| queued message, then gateway stop (restart-drain clears the followup queue) | **budget-free**: `attempts=0`, no `lastError` | **charged**: `attempts=1`, `lastError=turn-abandoned` |
| restart in a fresh process | redelivered, adopted, completed | redelivered, completed |
| genuine pre-adoption abandonment (reply queue at cap), `maxAttempts=3` | **dead-lettered** `retry-limit-exceeded` / `turn-abandoned` on the 3rd delivery, and the next row in the lane completes | **not dead-lettered** at `attempts=6` (2× the limit) when observation stopped, and the lane stayed blocked |

- Corpus, README and method: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/a499e4a22b/PR-124337/PROOFS/0cb65da5f2283965905abe1c55aca505e8139550 (earlier corpus at `b2d5e48e5b`: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/a2cf9d60fabd7ddb5ee6a985365d60c16eb99bf1/PR-124337/PROOFS/b2d5e48e5b59da6d1d29b2bfb7b2af51aee58f0a)
- Raw logs: `logs/{head,control}-{A1,A2,B}.log` in that directory.
- What this is not: there is no gateway server and no transport socket. The channel plugin is a minimal stand-in, and the agent turn is a stub that adopts through `admitFollowupRunLifecycle`. `METHOD.md` lists every limit. The adapter fixes in this revision are covered by the real-queue tests above, not by this harness.

**Failing control (unit).** At the earlier head, with the production files reverted to main and the tests kept at head, 11 assertions across 6 files fail. They pass at head.

**Tests** (focused, Linux): at `bcbc2837f4e`, 335/335 across 30 files. The set covers the adapter suites above, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e`, the reply lifecycle, the ingress drain and lifecycle, and the ingress-cancellation dispatch suite. The final commit `53cb34f058` changes only `lifecycle.ts` and its test, which were re-run at that head: lifecycle 14/14, cancellation 4/4.

**Revision 15 policy checks at `51631e61a23`:**
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 2983dfcfb3`: OK.
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 2983dfcfb3`: OK.
- lifecycle + ingress-cancellation: 18/18 (`--maxWorkers=1`, 15 s).
- telegram-ingress-drain + coalescing e2e: 57/57 (`--maxWorkers=1`, 70 s).
- the new cancellation e2e suite on its own: 1/1. Vitest itself took 35 s; the first run's plugin-SDK rebuild is the rest of the wall time.
- queue suites and the gateway tests that mock `drain.js`: 247/247.
- `check:import-cycles`: 0.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.

**Typecheck:** `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` are clean at `bcbc2837f4e`. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean at `53cb34f058`. `oxfmt` is clean.

prs.title: fix: warn when plugin cleanup fails during session reset or deletion
prs.body:
Fixes #172446

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin host cleanup failures during session reset or deletion disappear at the default log level.

## User Impact

Operators now see one warning per failed cleanup, naming the session operation, plugin, and hook, with guidance to inspect the reported cleanup error and retry. Successful cleanup stays quiet; failures still do not block reset or deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Gateway paths had their own verbose-only reporting loop. `runPluginHostCleanup` now reports reset/delete failures through its existing `plugins/cleanup` logger, and both duplicate loops are removed. Error diagnostics preserve the previous `String(error)` representation instead of expanding arbitrary thrown objects. Shared logging retains raw file diagnostics, redacts at egress, and caps plain-text console fields at 2,048 characters. Cleanup ordering, return values, and lifetime checks are unchanged.

The warning describes the completed attempt: its operation and returned plugin/hook/error facts deliberately retain that attempt's identity. It uses current logger settings at emission, carries no new config, session binding/path, authority, or limits, and schedules no deferred work.

## Evidence

- Confirmed by source/history on main `6b13edf810259d6d204f40b1ef5be9170f132645`: both Gateway paths used `logVerbose`, disabled at default levels, while the cleanup owner returned failures without warning.
- Added `src/plugins/host-hook-cleanup.logging.test.ts`: “warns once per failed session reset cleanup and keeps successful cleanup quiet” and the corresponding `delete` case. Real cleanup callbacks and the real console logger cover one warning per failure, plugin/hook/operation, next-step text, secret redaction, console bounds, unchanged results, and quiet success.
- Prior-head CI [38635822127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38635822127) completed on `b97ac3ca180d11df9fd4f60a52843201c4aac9e0`: **63 successful jobs, 26 skipped, one failed test shard plus the aggregate CI gate**. The gate remains red; no PR-caused failure was identified.
- **Inherited failure:** [PR job 116100010184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38635822127/job/116100010184), `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7`, fails `session-catalog-resident-entries.test.ts` → “bounds roster projections while delivering adopted sessions without an implicit owner”: `expected 352 to be less than or equal to 320`. The identical test/assertion fails in the latest scheduled-main run [38632684569, job 116088559048](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632684569/job/116088559048), `checks-node-compact-small-2`. This is outside the changed files; no baseline or expectation was weakened. The earlier PR head also hit this catalog failure.
- Changed-file core oxlint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` with explicit changed files), oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. An initial lint invocation started declaration preparation and was stopped; the core configuration completed successfully. Deslop removed duplicate reporting and the unused import. Production: **+12/-14**; tests: **+63/-0**; docs: **+6/-0**.
- Final independent Codex precommit and prescribed branch autoreviews: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The repository helper path is absent; the installed canonical shared helper ran with the prescribed private temporary directory and isolation. GitHub Codex's final-head review completed with no new findings. [P2 comment 4276078757](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172513#discussion_r4276078757) was fixed and resolved: generic remediation covers both session-store and plugin hook failures. ClawSweeper posted only its maintainer opt-in notice, with no code findings.
- **PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy.** Local tests, negative controls, and typechecks were intentionally skipped; test wall time was not measured locally. Live Gateway proof and Crabbox/Testbox leases were intentionally skipped per the same policy. No live Gateway or lease was started.

## Current-head landing evidence

The reviewed fix is unchanged on `73593b2a9db99e7007344267826efffc726e96f3`. [CI run 38646452972, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38646452972/attempts/2) completed after the authorized infrastructure retry. The SDK boundary job and `security-fast` passed. The only failing test is [job 116141983883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38646452972/job/116141983883): `session-catalog-resident-entries.test.ts` → “bounds roster projections while delivering adopted sessions without an implicit owner,” `expected 352 to be less than or equal to 320`; the aggregate gate fails downstream.

The identical test and assertion fail in the latest completed scheduled-main [run 38640790586, job 116121040772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38640790586/job/116121040772). The test and direct catalog implementation inputs are unchanged in the tested PR merge. The CI report calls this unknown because full-main and changed-scope shard names differ; the test-level match was inspected directly. Landing uses the maintainer-authorized inherited-failure exception and does not claim green CI. No additional local tests or live Gateway proof were run.

prs.title: feat: use selected GitHub identities on workers and approved nodes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cloud workers and approved Codex nodes need stock `gh` and HTTPS `git` to use the same selected GitHub execution identity as Gateway agents, including during long turns.

## User Impact

Workers and supported paired nodes use the effective System GitHub account or explicit agent override through a private execution profile, including sessions without a repository. Personal setup stays in Settings, and personal-publication credentials are not used as an execution fallback.

**Trust and upgrade implications:** this is trusted-host bearer-token delegation, not credential isolation. Node administrators or same-user processes can copy the selected token and use its existing GitHub permissions, potentially beyond the current repository or initiating user's permissions. Closing a turn stops delivery and removes the execution profile; it does not revoke a copied token at GitHub. Refresh-capable nodes are required; older nodes must update and reconnect. Unavailable configured managed credentials refuse the whole turn instead of falling back to native credentials.

**Owner decision remains pending:** SDK/security acceptance of that trust-boundary expansion and the upgrade/refusal behavior has not been recorded. Installed-old-node transition and unavailable-account Settings recovery also remain disclosed proof gaps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing identity selector and OAuth refresh owner, deliver same-account rotations through authenticated worker heartbeats or private node messages, and preserve live authority checks, process shutdown, write settlement, workspace reconciliation, and cleanup. Credential-only sessions receive no checkout metadata or publication authority.

## Evidence

### Current rebase and CI — 2026-10-13

Published head: **8c5e405a4ce78b63d2c131f8e8a20a09fa26d565**, rebased onto main **cc397809fb666caf37f19d0dfa9a8edfec90c87c**. All 53 original feature commits remain ancestors. The authored integration merge is preserved; later fixes were replayed or absorbed by newer main APIs. Main’s placement retry and delivery-recovery fixes remain intact. Retained publication/session ownership and async policy APIs coexist with renewable selected-account grants and credential-only sessions.

**Local proof:** 216 distinct focused cases passed across scoped runs: binding 50, identity 20, publication/actor 27, tool policy 19, and execution/launcher/startup/repository-result 100. Affected fixture cases were corrected and rerun; unchanged passing cases were reused, not represented as one aggregate green run. Final binding-file run with --maxWorkers=1: **50/50, 48.92s wall**; publication/actor pair: **27/27, 31.68s wall**. Production types, scoped typed lint, SDK export sync, formatting and whitespace checks passed within their selected scope. Final scoped reviews had no actionable P0–P2 finding. These checks did not cover all CI type/lint/format scopes; per-file CI cost was not isolated.

**Exact-head CI failed.** [Run 38417922200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38417922200), attempt 1, completed **2026-10-13 15:44:37 UTC**. Independent terminal readback verified **181 unique jobs across 2 pages: 148 success, 15 failure, 18 skipped; none pending**. Every job matched this SHA/run/attempt. That is **14 underlying failed jobs plus the downstream aggregate gate**, not 15 independent defects.

Observed failures:

- [Baseline mock-export policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38417922200/job/115381548710): seven factories in worker-github-binding.test-support.ts fail the export-preservation/isolation rule.
- Docs/changed-file formatting: worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts. Hosted lint: duplicate helper imports in worker-github-binding.test.ts and a floating promise in server-plugins.test.ts.
- [Test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38417922200/job/115382484818): publication and binding fixtures omit required updatedAt; the memory fixture uses activeWriterRunId on Partial<SessionEntry>.
- Plugin test and another type stripe: createSyntheticPluginRuntimeClient is undefined in server-plugins.test.ts:1493.
- OpenAI realtime routing: two tests fail with “Auth profile credential writes require an admitted worker.”
- Four test jobs time out: session compaction read-errors, Telegram message-tool settlement (120s), durable Move-result recovery (120s), and node-worker launch wire (240s).
- Restart handoff: expected a captured seal to be defined, but it was undefined.

Failures are not fully attributed to PR versus main; none are dismissed as flaky. The PR remains **OPEN, MERGEABLE, BLOCKED**, at the same head. The green-CI landing condition is unmet. Automated dependency/security statuses succeeded, but separate SDK/security owner acceptance remains unrecorded. No rerun, repair push, merge, or auto-merge was submitted after this result.

Previous head 54318a70159 failed CI 38200616430 (134 success, 24 failure, 17 skipped); that is historical, not current-head evidence.

### Previous requested rebase and resumed push — 2026-10-10

Previous published head: **5be2347170d569bfb279b587a25f85f17b54b8b7**, rebased onto main **19ac11902cdcdd23e91be0028aae1f2b7b7b13c8** and pushed with the exact predecessor lease **27ada723367f2383617c298ebebae5f06375b6bc**. All 53 original non-merge feature commits remain ancestors; the four subsequent maintenance/incognito/GHE/user-alignment commits replayed patch-identically. The recreated integration merge preserves its original author/date and contributor trailer.

Conflicts were resolved by retaining the PR's GitHub profile setup and renewal alongside main's pinned Codex binary selection (`preferInstalled: false`). SDK package exclusions and declaration aliases were regenerated through their owner, retaining both main's Codex-version entry and the worker GitHub entry. Comparing the final candidate with the original-head/new-main merge oracle leaves only those four reviewed conflict-resolution paths. Latest observed main **01e189266093d01ebe4973229c9a2c5dcc1f42ba** has a clean merge preview (tree **f9fd937c063e514e043ed0f700e34c05e3764a68**); it was not needlessly integrated a second time.

**Current validation:** frozen dependency admission passed; production types passed (14.21s), SDK declaration generation emitted 12,465 files, scoped Codex typed lint passed with zero warnings/errors, SDK registration checks and formatting/whitespace checks passed. Independent integration review reported no P0–P2 findings, with disclosed partial-context limitations. Earlier feature proof remains historical, not new-head test evidence.

**Incomplete validation:** both attempted focused test runs were interrupted by SIGTERM during compiled-subprocess preparation (exit 143), before case results. Neither is reported as a pass. Prior aggregate size/environment-count/test-graph limitations and the SDK/security owner decision remain recorded below. New-head GitHub workflows have started; CI is pending, not green. This push does not merge or enable auto-merge.

### Previous bot and signed-in user alignment — 2026-10-10

Previous published head: **27ada723367f2383617c298ebebae5f06375b6bc**. Compared the complete credential/user path with main **07a870b2eaabc277315583e8a05d9060f175266f**. This is a scoped consolidation, not a new authentication mechanism or an approval of the larger node trust-boundary change.

- Initial checkout and renewable worker/node execution now use **one selected-account projection**: existing shared selector, unchanged bot token from `GH_TOKEN`, verified account login, selected host, branch, and configured author. GHE uses that same path and the existing variables; duplicate projection code is removed. Renewable remote normalization now matches main’s initial-checkout normalization.
- The bot account and signed-in person stay separate, as on main. The person remains in the existing admitted operator/caller context for permissions and attribution; their GitHub login never replaces the bot’s verified execution login. Personal **My GitHub** credentials stay in the explicitly selected publication broker. No new GHE user/token environment variables or personal-token fallback.
- **50 worker-binding tests passed** in **20.33s** using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-github-binding.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The extended existing table proves github.com, ghe.com and self-hosted GHE binding parity, plus public/GHE signed-in-user revocation outside ambient caller context. **41 unchanged harness-authority tests also passed** (initial combined command 48.84s). These are synthetic boundary tests, not live Enterprise sign-in tests; hosted per-file CI seconds remain unavailable.
- Production types passed (13.58s), two-file typed lint passed (zero warnings/errors), formatting/whitespace passed, independent P0–P2 review scoped-clean. Production delta **51 added / 57 removed**; test delta **62 added / 14 removed**. No new SDK exports or credential store.
- Changed-check delta now passes its line-cap gate but still stops at the previously recorded environment-count budget (456 vs 455). Broader prior-head size and test-graph limitations remain recorded below. Main merge preview reports four conflicts outside this three-file alignment; no full rebase is claimed. No current-head CI run or merge has been submitted manually, and no clean exact-head CI is claimed. SDK/security owner acceptance remains outstanding.

### Previous GHE credential parity — 2026-10-10 evening

Previous published head: **7401d3cb37eca58076b4c3e6ee468a086495f005**. Main inspected at **3e44be0fb8a60c7ea98a38aa7cf9f50faf7abbd8** already uses the selected bot token with its existing permissions, not a reduced per-session credential. This update applies that same contract to GHE without adding credential variables or a second identity mechanism.

- The private launcher reads the admitted host from the selected profile, using existing `GH_HOST` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR`. It supplies `GH_TOKEN` and `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` privately, clears both `GITHUB_*` fallback variables, and forwards those same variables to Docker/Podman. Public managed profiles stay pinned to github.com.
- Two Enterprise launch cases reproduced the defect before repair and passed afterward, including exact token rotation and refusal when only a github.com credential remains. No native/wrong-host fallback was introduced; existing freshness/authority checks are preserved.
- **111 distinct passing cases across seven files**, combined from each file's final scoped result: worker binding 16, exec identity 7, private exec 19, credential reader 9, source launch 2, managed identity 20, container backend 38. **Six PowerShell cases skipped** because pwsh is unavailable. Container proof uses a synthetic engine process, not a live daemon; no live GHE service or native Windows claim.
- Production types passed (10.45s), scoped typed lint passed (12 files, zero warnings/errors), and formatting/whitespace checks passed (13 files). Independent P0–P2 delta review was scoped-clean; the subsequent production change only renamed a shadowing local variable.
- Test commands used the repository's `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … --maxWorkers=1` wrapper. Wall times: 22.74s initial batch (existing ambient Git-author fixture failure), 17.14s next batch (old one-key managed-env assertion), 11.91s final two-suite batch (58 passed). Both fixture defects were corrected without weakening production checks. Individual-file command wall times and hosted CI seconds were not measured for this update.
- **Remaining gates:** the actual changed-check aggregate still fails the recorded node-registry/recovery line caps. Changed test-type graph admission stops at ui-e2e 722 roots versus 720; no bypass or new full test-type pass is claimed. GitHub currently reports conflicts with main; no clean CI run is attached to this head at the last observation. Prior-head CI below remains historical. Existing SDK/security owner acceptance remains unrecorded, and this base-branch comparison is not that acceptance. No merge or auto-merge was submitted.

### Previous requested rebase — 2026-10-10 afternoon

Previous published head: **0a3498803d8a9f0eeab75298c6469d80349083ce**. [CI run 38063042988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38063042988), attempt 1, **completed with failure at 15:31:24 UTC**. Full paginated inventory: **176 unique jobs — 153 successful, 17 skipped, 6 failed; none running/cancelled within this CI run**. Five root test jobs failed; the sixth is the aggregate gate.

| Root failure | Observed result |

prs.title: fix(agent-core): preserve accepted handoff in tool settlement catches
prs.body:
Closes #126446

## What Problem This Solves

An accepted `sessions_yield` handoff intentionally aborts its active turn with `turnHandoff: true`. The abort-signal wrapper's pre-abort pre-check (`agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87`) threw `Error("Aborted")` with **no yield-handoff exemption** when the run signal was already aborted at wrapper-entry time, bypassing the non-rejecting race (`raceWithAbortSignal`). The execution catch (`readyExecution.execute` catch) then converted this to an error tool result, erasing the accepted continuation. The embedded run settled as `success` while the channel dispatcher had no queued reply payload — the user received no answer even though the delegated continuation was accepted.

## Root Cause

The non-rejecting exemption for `sessions_yield` handoffs lived **only** inside `raceWithAbortSignal` (`agent-tools.abort.ts:40-47`). The wrapper's pre-abort pre-check (`agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87`) runs **before** the race is set up and threw `createAbortError("Aborted")` unconditionally whenever `combinedSignal.aborted` was true — with no check for the yield-handoff reason. When the run signal was already aborted with `SESSIONS_YIELD_ABORT_REASON` (`{ code: "sessions_yield", turnHandoff: true }`), the pre-check threw `Error("Aborted")`, which the execution catch (`agent-loop.ts:1497-1509`) converted to `createErrorToolResult("Aborted")` — producing exactly the issue's symptom: `sessions_yield tool result: Aborted`.

The test at `agent-tools.runtime.test.ts:216-230` codified this behavior ("does not start sessions_yield when the run was already handed off" → rejects with `AbortError: "Aborted"`).

The delivery path then lost the reply: `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` (`payloads.ts`) suppressed assistant text when `runAborted` was true, `terminal-resolution.ts:125-144` collapsed error-only payloads to `payloadCount = 0`, and `execution.ts:119` logged `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads`.

## Canonical Repair

**Producer fix (root cause)**: Add `isYieldHandoffAbort()` exemption to all three wrapper pre-checks (`execute`, `preparer`, `ready-closure`), matching `raceWithAbortSignal`'s four-part contract: `toolName === "sessions_yield"` AND `abortSignal.aborted` AND `combinedSignal.reason === abortSignal.reason` AND `reason.code === "sessions_yield"` AND `reason.turnHandoff === true`. When the run signal is already aborted with the canonical handoff reason, the pre-check no longer throws — the tool runs, calls `onYield`, and returns `{ yielded: true }` normally.

**Consumer fix (defense-in-depth)**:

- **Execution catch** (`readyExecution.execute` catch, `agent-loop.ts:1497`): preserves the handoff when the signal carries the marker (`isAcceptedYieldToolAbort`) AND the error is an `AbortError`. Returns a non-error result (`isError: false`). A genuine tool failure (non-`AbortError`, e.g. "yield bookkeeping failed") stays an error even when the signal has the marker.
- **`afterToolCall` catch** (`finalizeExecutedToolCall`, `agent-loop.ts:1612`): preserves the tool's already-produced result when both `isAcceptedYieldToolAbort(signal, toolName)` AND `isHandoffAbortError(error, signal)` match — i.e., the hook threw the signal's own reason object (e.g., via `signal.throwIfAborted()`) or an `Error` wrapping it as `cause`.
- **`afterToolOutcome` catch** (`finalizeToolCallOutcome`, `agent-loop.ts:1680`): same dual guard as `afterToolCall`.

A sibling tool's hook error, a different handoff owner setting `turnHandoff: true` on a tool merely named `sessions_yield`, or an unrelated `AbortError` is **not** masked (covered by regression tests).

## Scope of ClawSweeper P1 vs. This Fix

ClawSweeper's P1 finding ("Trace a production post-tool abort producer before preserving results") was raised against the **prior** version of this PR, which modified only the `afterToolCall` and `afterToolOutcome` settlement catches. The reviewer's core objection was that the inspected production `afterToolCall` callback delegates to an error-isolating extension runner (`dispatchHandlers` in `src/agents/sessions/extensions/runner.ts:700-707`), which catches handler errors internally without re-throwing, so **no production path was shown to throw the signal's handoff reason into either of those two catches**. The integration test replaced `session.agent.afterToolCall` wholesale to inject the fault — synthetic injection at a production boundary, not a traced production producer.

This revision changes the P1's premise by locating the **real** producer at a different boundary:

| Boundary | ClawSweeper P1 scope | This fix |
|---|---|---|
| **wrapper pre-check** (`agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87`) | Not inspected (prior PR did not touch the wrapper) | **Root-cause producer** — throws `Error("Aborted")` before `raceWithAbortSignal`, with no yield-handoff exemption. Traced and fixed. |
| **execution catch** (`readyExecution.execute` catch, `agent-loop.ts:1497`) | Not in P1 scope (prior PR explicitly left it unguarded, claiming "the yield tool returns normally") | **Direct consumer of the wrapper pre-check's throw** — guard added as defense-in-depth. The prior PR's premise ("yield tool returns normally, non-rejecting race") was incomplete: the non-rejecting exemption lives only inside `raceWithAbortSignal`, which the pre-check bypasses. |
| **`afterToolCall` catch** (`finalizeExecutedToolCall`, `agent-loop.ts:1612`) | P1 target — no production producer traced | **Still no production producer.** The production callback delegates to `dispatchHandlers`, which catches handler errors internally. Guard retained as defense-in-depth; the AgentSession integration test injects the fault by replacing the callback. |
| **`afterToolOutcome` catch** (`finalizeToolCallOutcome`, `agent-loop.ts:1680`) | P1 target — no production producer traced | **Still no production producer.** Same reasoning as `afterToolCall`. Guard retained as defense-in-depth. |

**What changed**: the issue's reported symptom (`sessions_yield tool result: Aborted`) is now traced to a concrete production code path — the wrapper pre-check throwing `Error("Aborted")` → the execution catch converting it to an error tool result → the delivery path collapsing the error-only payload to zero count. The prior P1 blocker ("no traced production producer") is resolved for the **execution catch** via the wrapper pre-check.

**What did not change**: the `afterToolCall` and `afterToolOutcome` catches still have no traced production producer. Their guards remain defense-in-depth: if a future callback or wrapper ever propagates the signal's reason (e.g., via `signal.throwIfAborted()`), the accepted handoff is preserved rather than erased. The issue itself names `finalizeExecutedToolCall` as a catch that "also rewrites the result to an error without consulting the handoff marker," so the guard is aligned with the issue's stated expectation even though the current production callback does not produce the throw.

## Evidence

### Root cause proof: wrapper pre-check produces `Error("Aborted")`

The wrapper pre-check at `agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87` (before fix):
```ts
if (combinedSignal.aborted) {
  throwAbortError();  // throws Error("Aborted") — NO yield-handoff exemption
}
```

This runs **before** `raceWithAbortSignal` (line 88), which is where the non-rejecting exemption lives (lines 40-47). When the run signal is already aborted with `SESSIONS_YIELD_ABORT_REASON`, the pre-check throws unconditionally.

The thrown error reaches the execution catch (`agent-loop.ts:1497-1509`), which converts it via `createErrorToolResult(coerceErrorMessage(error))` into `{ content: [{ text: "Aborted" }], isError: true }` — exactly the issue's `sessions_yield tool result: Aborted`.

### Focused committed proof (post-fix):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.runtime.test.ts
# 1 file, 31 tests passed (includes yield-handoff exemption tests)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts
# 1 file, 86 tests passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts -t "settlement fault-path"
# 1 file, 1 passed | 17 skipped (18)
```

### Updated wrapper test: yield-handoff exemption

The test at `agent-tools.runtime.test.ts` (formerly "does not start sessions_yield when the run was already handed off") now verifies the exemption:

```
it("lets sessions_yield run when the run was already handed off")
  → result.details: { status: "error" } (tool's own error, not "Aborted")
  → onYield not called (no claimYield)

it("preserves a sessions_yield result when the run was already handed off")
  → result.details: { status: "yielded", message: "Turn yielded." }
  → onYield called once
```

Format/lint/typecheck on touched files:

```
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts src/agents/agent-tools.runtime.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts packages/agent-core/src/turn-interruption.ts   # All matched files use the correct format
node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts src/agents/agent-tools.runtime.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts packages/agent-core/src/turn-interruption.ts           # 0 warnings, 0 errors
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                  # no errors (exit 0)
```

### Boundary-level proof: embedded sessions_yield handoff through delivery

The existing qa-lab e2e suite covers the full accepted-yield lifecycle through external delivery: inbound trigger → `sessions_spawn` → child `sessions_yield` self-pause → requester stays parked (quiet window asserted) → follow-up run adoption (distinct gateway runId) → completion announce with exactly one outbound message. It runs against a real ephemeral gateway child process with a mock OpenAI-compatible provider and a mock channel transport (bus), not a unit mock.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-self-yield-followup.e2e.test.ts

✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-self-yield-followup.e2e.test.ts
  > plugin subagent sessions_yield follow-up
  > announces to the original requester only after the follow-up run ends

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

### Harness verdict JSON

```json

  "proof": "mock-gateway-yield-handoff-delivery",
  "command": "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-self-yield-followup.e2e.test.ts",
  "harness": {
    "kind": "mock-gateway-ephemeral-child",
    "provider": "mock-openai (startQaMockOpenAiServer)",
    "channel": "qa-bus-mock (startQaBusServer + createQaChannelTransport)"
  },
  "flow": "inbound → sessions_spawn → child sessions_yield self-pause → requester parked (15s quiet window asserted) → follow-up run adoption (distinct gateway runId) → completion announce (exactly 1 outbound message)",
  "result": { "testsPassed": 1, "testsFailed": 0, "exitCode": 0 }
}
```

### Production-boundary fault-path proof: AgentSession integration test

A new integration test in `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts` drives the fault through the real `AgentSession` → `Agent.prompt` → `runAgentLoop` → `config.afterToolCall` production call chain. It creates a real `AgentSession` via `createTestSession` (mock `streamSimple` provider), registers a `sessions_yield` tool that aborts with the canonical handoff marker, wraps `session.agent.afterToolCall` to throw `signal.reason` on the yield tool, and asserts the requester-visible delivery outcome.

```

✓ |agents-support| src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts
  > AgentSession settlement fault-path
  > preserves the accepted sessions_yield handoff when afterToolCall throws  1666ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 17 skipped (18)
```

### Fault-path coverage

| Path | Coverage | Pre-fix |
|---|---|---|
| wrapper pre-check — sessions_yield when run already aborted | agent-tools.runtime.test.ts (exemption test) | reject with "Aborted" (bug) |
| execution catch — AbortError after yield-handoff abort | agent-core unit (defense-in-depth guard) | rewrite to error (bug) |
| `afterToolCall` catch — hook throws signal.reason | AgentSession integration + agent-core unit | rewrite to error (bug) |
| `afterToolOutcome` catch — hook throws signal.reason | agent-core unit | rewrite to error (bug) |
| sibling tool hook error | agent-core unit (sibling regression) | pass (error preserved) |
| genuine yield-callback error (non-AbortError) | agent-core unit (genuine-error regression) | pass (error preserved) |
| different-owner handoff | agent-core unit | pass (error preserved) |
| non-handoff abort | agent-core unit (control) | pass (both) |
| happy-path yield→delivery | e2e (mock-gateway) | pass (both) |

### Known proof gaps

- **`afterToolCall` / `afterToolOutcome` catches have no traced production producer.** The production `afterToolCall` callback (`agent-session-base.ts:258`) delegates to `runner.emitToolResult` → `dispatchHandlers` (`runner.ts:700-707`), which catches handler errors internally without re-throwing. No production callback calls `signal.throwIfAborted()` or throws `signal.reason`. The AgentSession integration test replaces `session.agent.afterToolCall` to inject the fault — this is synthetic fault injection at a production boundary, not a traced production producer. These two guards are defense-in-depth, aligned with the issue's stated expectation that `finalizeExecutedToolCall` should consult the handoff marker.
- No live Telegram/Codex end-to-end run was executed; the boundary proof uses a mock-gateway harness with a mock OpenAI-compatible provider (per AGENTS.md the mock-gateway harness satisfies the real-behavior-proof gate for channel-visible changes covering the changed path).

## Diff Shape

- Production: `+132/-12` (net `+120`) — `isYieldHandoffAbort` helper + 3 pre-check exemptions in `agent-tools.abort.ts` (+30/-3), 3 helpers in `turn-interruption.ts` (+63/-6), execution catch guard + 2 settlement guards in `agent-loop.ts` (+39/-2), baseline cleanup (-1).

- No config, protocol, schema-version, public API, or docs surface change.

Production growth is inherent to the fix: the wrapper pre-check exemption is the root-cause producer fix, and the three settlement-catch guards are defense-in-depth at distinct shared boundaries, all reusing the existing wrapper-layer tool-name and handoff-reason contracts.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop showing reply icons on progress lines before tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: progress lines an agent writes before a tool call ("Now checking X…") each get their own reply/copy action row when a run renders outside its turn frame — for example, when the loaded history window starts mid-run and tool calls are hidden. Seen with Claude; any provider that doesn't label progress text as commentary is affected.

## User Impact

User impact: only the turn's answer shows reply/copy actions. Progress lines no longer get stray reply icons, whatever the provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The turn footer already picks its action owner with an eligibility rule: the message must have content, must not be commentary, interrupted, an error, or a `toolUse` stop. Plain message groups only hid actions for messages explicitly labeled `commentary`, which OpenAI Responses/Codex set and Claude/Gemini do not. This shares the footer's rule (`assistantMessageCanOwnTurnActions`) and applies it per message in message groups, so reply and inline actions follow the same decision everywhere.

Messages that can't own the turn (progress, commentary, errors) lose their reply button and inline action row in unframed groups too, matching turn frames. A group's footer keeps copy (for example on a transcript search hit) and only drops reply.

## Evidence

Screenshots replay real transcripts in the Control UI with tool calls hidden, starting the history window mid-run (where the run is split by a gateway publication notice).

**Claude** (real Claude Opus session transcript)

Before: every progress line has its own reply icon.

![Claude before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bb7af84-1528-4172-b1c3-fe0fc9736959)

After: only the answer's footer keeps actions.

![Claude after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24cc5a3a-059a-4373-893d-5c475b29efbd)

**OpenAI: unaffected control.** OpenAI's Responses API labels progress lines as `commentary`, so they never had reply icons and the bug can't appear there. This replay uses a real `gpt-6.1-sol` run, split by the same publication notice, to show the fix doesn't change it.

![OpenAI after (same as before)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de9b846f-409b-434b-91d9-3aec427450ce)

The "OpenClaw 1h ago" line in the middle of the Claude screenshots is the normal footer of a message group. It is already present on `main` (see Before). The publication notice is stored without a run ID, so it cuts the run into two groups, and the first group ends with its own footer. This PR only removes that footer's reply icon.

- New Solid regression (`chat-message-group.solid.test.tsx`, "progress before tool calls…", completed and still-working cases): fails on `main`, passes with the fix.
- `chat-message-group.solid.test.tsx` + `chat-agent-run-grouping.test.ts`: 26/26 pass.
- UI e2e `chat-agent-run-transcript`, `chat-message-actions`, `chat-flow.streaming`: 25/25 pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt clean on touched files. Autoreview scoped-clean.
- Gemini: no live Gemini route was available on the test host. Google's stream adapter sets the same `stopReason: "toolUse"` with no phase (`packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts`), which is the shape the fix keys on.

## Worked on by

- @Patrick-Erichsen

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/7f9c50ac-d2cb-4778-9c35-efb6e465a215)

prs.title: fix(sandbox): admit docker bind targets as exec workdirs like file tools
prs.body:
Closes #149941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `exec` rejects `workdir` under a `sandbox.docker.binds` target with `workdir "<path>" is unavailable or not a directory: command was not executed.` even though file tools read/write/list that same folder.

## User Impact

User impact: agents with an extra bind-mounted folder can run commands with `workdir` set inside it, consistent with the file tools' access to the same directory, instead of falling back to in-command `cd` on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec workdir resolver still validated against a pre-#148893 mount view (workspace + read-only skill mounts) while file tools moved to the authoritative `resolveSandboxMountSelection` (binds included), so the two tool families disagreed about the same configured mount. This adds a `bindMounts` field to the exec sandbox config, populates it in `createCoreCodingTools` from `buildSandboxFsMounts` (the same selection owner the file tools' fallback admission uses), and includes those mounts in the container→host workdir mapping table. Precedence stays deterministic (longest container root wins); binds shadowed by managed/protected targets are already excluded by the selection, and missing host directories still resolve to `unavailable`.

## Evidence

Red-green regression (pre-fix code via `git stash` of the production files):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-workdir.bind-mounts.test.ts` → new tests **fail pre-fix** (`{kind:"unavailable", requestedCwd:"/data"}`), **pass after** the fix (56/56 across both exec-workdir test files).
- Sibling suites green: `core-coding-tools.exec-workdir.test.ts`, `core-coding-tools.sandbox.test.ts` (70/70), `sandbox/workspace-mounts.test.ts` + `sandbox/fs-paths.test.ts` (41 passed, 3 skipped).

Runtime probe composing the exact production chain (`createSandboxTestContext` with `docker.binds: ["/tmp/bind-probe/data:/data"]` → `buildSandboxFsMounts` → exec sandbox config → `resolveExecWorkdir`), verbatim output:

```
selected bind mounts: [{"hostPath":"/tmp/bind-probe/data","containerPath":"/data"}]
=== exec workdir=/data, pre-fix config (no bindMounts) ===
{"kind":"unavailable","requestedCwd":"/data"}
=== exec workdir=/data, fixed config (bindMounts from mount selection) ===
{"kind":"sandbox","hostCwd":"/tmp/bind-probe/data","containerCwd":"/data","scriptPreflightCwd":"/tmp/bind-probe/data"}
```

Gates: `oxfmt` clean, `run-oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `pnpm tsgo` (core) exit 0, `git diff --check` clean.

Not tested: a live Docker-sandbox exec (no Docker daemon on this host); the resolver and mount-selection layers above the engine are covered by the tests and probe, and the container-side `docker exec -w` behavior for an existing bind directory is unchanged. The autoreview helper's codex engine failed with an infra error (`codex engine failed (1)`, also seen on another PR today), so the pre-submit review was manual: additive optional config field, one call-site population, one mapping-table inclusion; no public SDK surface touched (`check-plugin-sdk-api-baseline` scope untouched).



Rebased onto current `main` (`26505c528b5`, head `9929483460b`): main renamed the boolean `includeShellTools` option to the tri-state `shellTools` in `CoreCodingToolsOptions`; the bind-mount admission now gates on `shellTools !== "disabled"` (same predicate main uses for sandbox admission). The `BashSandboxWorkdirMount` export flagged by the dependency scan is module-private again (no production consumer outside `bash-tools.shared.ts`). Gates on the new head: focused suite `bash-tools.exec-workdir.bind-mounts.test.ts` 3/3, `pnpm tsgo` exit 0, `run-oxlint` 0/0 on changed files, `oxfmt` clean, `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(ui): make release updates discoverable from the account menu
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The account menu has no direct route to update settings, and development checkouts receive the same new-update notifications as release users.

## User Impact

Users can open **Settings → Updates** from the account menu. Only the **stable** and **beta** channels show new-update notifications; **dev** remains quiet. Opening settings never starts an update, and manually started dev updates retain their progress and recovery UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an **Updates** menu item with an **Available** badge, and share release-channel eligibility with Inbox. Keep the badge on the dedicated Updates row instead of the About/build link. Dismissing an Inbox notice does not hide release availability in the account menu. No configuration migration or automatic-update policy change is required.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI tests cover stable, beta, dev, live channel changes, up-to-date state, and navigation without an update request.
- Before the patch-identical rebase: 185 focused unit/browser tests and 20 selected E2E checks passed, including manual dev update success/failure and Inbox dismissal/account isolation. UI typecheck, scoped lint/style checks, formatting, i18n verification, and changed-doc MDX checks passed.
- Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. All three task commits remain unchanged by `git range-diff` after the signed rebase onto main `a1a4e04f7cb5e63c264fda3d2954725d6ac37c1a`.
- Refreshed head `17b73b920ec0fc7bb2e20d612140ce05b8dd191d`: **38/38 focused tests passed**, including update eligibility, Inbox behavior, and usage-retention regression. Signatures, contributor trailers, and `git diff --check` verified.
- Current-head [CI run 38656978583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38656978583), attempt 1, finished with one inherited failure: WebKit hovercard automation Tab-focus. All other jobs passed or were unselected/skipped, including update-menu E2E and security-fast. The failed owner/test files match the independently reproduced main baseline and actual CI main parent. Landing uses the repository’s inherited-failure exception, not an all-green CI claim; the separate WebKit repair is not included in this PR.
- CI caught one stale caption assertion in the existing Inbox boot-change test. It now verifies the Updates menu item and its Available badge; the focused regression passes without changing production behavior.

<details>
<summary>Historical inherited CI failures and recovery</summary>

Prior CI run [38638874589](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38638874589) tested merge `590d770ca028ffbe2337367091faff49b738a837` (main `8c3cd75842a8347eb2ea78c72a8863526413a6e7` + PR head `33aec87402809085709c42c1677cfc4b6ac86986`). prs.title: fix(release): retry FRV job listings with smaller pages on 2026.9.33
prs.body:
## Problem
FRV 38624817276 for 2026.9.33 has every child green. Its parent reseal still failed twice in `orchestration_error` with 0 blockers. The release decision collector reads `actions/runs/38630892166/attempts/2/jobs?per_page=100`, and GitHub answers that page size with HTTP 502 every time, while `per_page=50` and `per_page=30` return all 128 jobs. Main fixed this in #171952, which the frozen 9.33 tooling lacks.

## Solution
- **Collector and verifier:** port #171952. Job listings in the decision collector (`full-release-validation-state.mjs`) and the strict verifier (`release-ci-summary.mjs`) retry with 50-job pages, then 30-job pages, after a 5xx. Only the last page size spends the normal transient-retry budget. `frv.mjs` already reads with 25-job pages on this line, so its conflicting hunks are left out.
- **node_exec live test:** carry the clarification from #172596 onto 9.33. It removes the contradictory "do not add timeout arguments" instruction and reports why a case never started. This is the live test that needed its maximum reruns in this FRV.

## Evidence
- Reproduced the persistent 502 at `per_page=100` and success at 50 and 30 against the live API.
- `release-evidence-retry`, `full-release-validation-state`, `full-release-validation-state.qualification` and `frv.release` tests pass (226/226). This includes a new regression where 100-job pages return 502 and the listing completes with 50-job pages, without sleeping. The existing async 502 expectations were updated the same way #171952 updated them on main.
- oxlint and oxfmt are clean.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group messages anchored only by chat_guid are silently dropped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iMessage group messages are silently dropped when the bridge delivers them with a valid `chat_guid` (or `chat_identifier`) but no positive `chat_id`. This is a P2 message-delivery regression: the inbound gate at `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` used `if (isGroup && !chatId) return { kind: "drop", reason: "group without chat_id" }`, where `!chatId` is true for `chat_id === 0`, `undefined`, or `NaN`. Direct messages are unaffected, so the failure mode is "group chats go dark while DMs keep working" — exactly the symptom reported by bridges that only emit a guid-style anchor for group threads.

The contradiction that makes this a real bug rather than a deliberate guard: `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/conversation-repair.ts` treats a non-empty `chat_guid` as a *usable anchor* (`isIMessageAnchorless` returns false), so it never repairs these conversations. But the inbound gate treated the same payload as unanchored and dropped it. Two owners of the "is this group anchored?" question answered it differently, and the dropped messages never surfaced an error to the operator.

A follow-up review finding: conversation selection already rejected non-positive `chat_id` values, but `formatIMessageGroupTarget` delegated to `formatIMessageChatTarget`, which accepts `-1`. For `chat_id: -1` plus a valid GUID, inbound routing selected the GUID conversation while the outbound sender addressed `chat_id:-1`.

## User Impact

- **Who is affected:** Operators running iMessage bridges (e.g. Beeper-style bridges, BlueBubbles, or any sync client) whose group payloads expose `chat_guid`/`chat_identifier` but surface `chat_id` as `0`, a negative sentinel, or omit it.
- **Symptom before the fix:** Group messages from those bridges produce no reply, no error log, and no dispatch decision — they vanish between `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` and the conversation binder. DMs to the same account work normally, which makes the bug hard to diagnose. A negative `chat_id` plus GUID would also admit the group but send the reply to the unusable numeric id.
- **Symptom after the fix:** The same group messages dispatch normally, are routed under a stable `chat_guid`-anchored conversation id, and replies are addressed to `chat_guid:<guid>` so the outbound sender can resolve them back to the real thread. Conversation selection and reply targeting now share one positive-`chat_id` rule. When a group truly has no anchor of any kind, it is still dropped, but the drop reason is now `"group without usable anchor"` (accurate) instead of `"group without chat_id"` (misleading).

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound gate and the conversation-repair owner need to agree on what counts as a usable group anchor. Today they don't, and the inbound gate is the stricter one — so strict that it drops payloads the repair owner considers already-anchored. Rather than loosening the repair owner (which risks double-repairing real anchorless groups), this change makes the inbound gate use the same anchor notion as repair: prefer a **positive** `chat_id`, fall back to `chat_guid`, then `chat_identifier`. Reply formatting now uses that same positive-id rule so the outbound send cannot address a different chat than the selected conversation.

Concretely:

- `hasPositiveIMessageChatId` is the single positive-`chat_id` rule used by both `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId` and `formatIMessageGroupTarget`.
- `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId({ chatId, chatGuid, chatIdentifier })` (in `conversation-id.ts`) centralizes the `positive chat_id > chat_guid > chat_identifier` precedence and mirrors the "usable anchor" semantics already owned by `monitor/conversation-repair.ts`.
- `formatIMessageGroupTarget` formats the reply target from whichever anchor survived. A negative sentinel such as `chat_id: -1` is not treated as a usable numeric target.
- `inbound-processing.ts` resolves `groupIdCandidate` through `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId`, gates on `!groupIdCandidate` (not `!chatId`), and routes peer/session/reply metadata through that same anchor.
- `docs/channels/imessage/access-control.md` documents the GUID/identifier fallback, including negative sentinel ids.

The change is intentionally narrow: it does not alter DM routing, echo detection, reaction handling, or the repair owner's logic.

## Evidence

### Bug reproduction (source-level)

Before this change, the group gate was:

```
if (isGroup && !chatId) {
  return { kind: "drop", reason: "group without chat_id" };
}
```

`!chatId` is `true` for `chat_id === 0` (a common "missing" sentinel from bridges), for `undefined`, and for `NaN`. Meanwhile the repair owner considers the same payload anchored if `chat_guid` or `chat_identifier` is present.

The reply-target mismatch on the previous revision: `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId` rejected `chat_id: -1` and selected the GUID, but `formatIMessageGroupTarget` called `formatIMessageChatTarget(-1)` and returned `chat_id:-1`. `send.ts` then put `chat_id: -1` on the imsg send request.

### Real behavior proof (production modules, after fix)

Ran the **real production modules** (`resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId`, `formatIMessageGroupTarget`, `parseIMessageTarget`) with Node via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`. Identifiers are redacted. This is the same target-selection and send-param construction used by the imsg monitor and outbound sender.

```
=== GUID-only group chat_id=0 ===
input {"chatId":0,"chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349","chatIdentifier":"chat349"}
conversation anchor iMessage;+;chat349
old reply target (formatIMessageChatTarget only) (empty)
new reply target (formatIMessageGroupTarget) chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349
parsed outbound target {"kind":"chat_guid","chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
imsg send params {"chat_guid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
aligned true

=== GUID-only group chat_id=-1 ===
input {"chatId":-1,"chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349","chatIdentifier":"chat349"}
conversation anchor iMessage;+;chat349
old reply target (formatIMessageChatTarget only) chat_id:-1
new reply target (formatIMessageGroupTarget) chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349
parsed outbound target {"kind":"chat_guid","chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
imsg send params {"chat_guid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
aligned true

=== positive chat_id still preferred ===
input {"chatId":42,"chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat42","chatIdentifier":"chat42"}
conversation anchor 42
old reply target (formatIMessageChatTarget only) chat_id:42
new reply target (formatIMessageGroupTarget) chat_id:42
parsed outbound target {"kind":"chat_id","chatId":42}
imsg send params {"chat_id":42}
aligned true
```

The `chat_id: -1` case is the review finding: the old formatter would have sent `chat_id:-1`; the new formatter and the parsed imsg send params both use `chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349`, matching the conversation anchor.

Inbound + outbound production path (Vitest, real modules, mock imsg RPC client — no live Apple Messages account on this host):

- `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` for `chat_id: -1` + GUID → `{ kind: "dispatch", groupId: "iMessage;+;chat349" }`
- `buildIMessageInboundContext` → `imessageTo` / `ctxPayload.To` = `chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349`
- `sendMessageIMessage("chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349", "hello group")` → RPC `send` params `{ chat_guid: "iMessage;+;chat349", text: "hello group" }`, and **not** `{ chat_id: -1 }`

A live signed-in `imsg` receive-and-reply from an Apple Messages account is not available in this environment. The trace above is the production decision, reply-target, parse, and outbound send-request chain that the bridge monitor and sender use.

### Regression tests

- `extensions/imessage/src/targets.test.ts` — `formatIMessageGroupTarget({ chatId: -1, chatGuid })` → `chat_guid:...`
- `extensions/imessage/src/conversation-id.test.ts` — `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId({ chatId: -1, chatGuid })` → GUID
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts` — negative `chat_id` + GUID dispatches; reply context uses `chat_guid:`
- `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` — production sender issues `chat_guid` on the imsg RPC and never `chat_id: -1`

### Local validation

- `extensions/imessage/src/conversation-id.test.ts` + `targets.test.ts` — focused cases passed (imessage shard)
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts` — including the new negative-`chat_id` dispatch and reply-target cases (extension-database-workers shard)
- `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` — `sends group replies to chat_guid when the inbound chat_id is negative` passed

This branch is updated with the latest `openclaw/openclaw` `main`.

prs.body:
Closes #127454

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: IPv6 Gateway hosts produce SSH targets and discovery URLs that OpenSSH and `new URL` reject.

## User Impact

IPv6-only remote Gateways work with inferred SSH routing, `gateway probe --ssh`, and discovery output. DNS names and IPv4 are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseSshTarget` now reads `[IPv6]` and `[IPv6]:port` as the raw host. Discovery and status bracket IPv6 through one `formatUrlHost` helper, which replaces six inline copies.

## Evidence

- New tests fail before the fix and pass after (the direct formatter table is dropped). Touched and sibling suites, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, and oxfmt pass.
- `openclaw gateway probe --ssh 'me@[2001:db8::10]:2222'`, before: `ssh: Could not resolve hostname [2001:db8::10]`. After: the raw address reaches SSH and times out (unreachable documentation address).

  ```
  parseSshTarget('me@[2001:db8::10]:2222') = {"host":"[2001:db8::10]","port":2222}  ->  {"host":"2001:db8::10","port":2222}
  parseSshTarget('me@[2001:db8::10]')      = null                                   ->  {"host":"2001:db8::10","port":22}
  discovery JSON = {"wsUrl":"ws://2001:db8::10:18789","sshTarget":"me@2001:db8::10:2222"}
               -> {"wsUrl":"ws://[2001:db8::10]:18789","sshTarget":"me@[2001:db8::10]:2222"}
  ```
- Not covered: the macOS app's Swift SSH parser.

prs.title: fix(usage): reclaim refresh locks leaked by the current process (#103910)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost` can get stuck with `cacheStatus.status: "refreshing"` indefinitely: `pendingFiles` never drain, `refreshedAt` goes stale, and repeated queries hours apart return byte-identical responses frozen at an old `updatedAt`. Root cause: usage-cost refreshes serialize on a pid-stamped lock file (`.usage-cost-cache.json.lock`) whose staleness check trusts **pid-liveness alone** (`isUsageCostCacheRefreshRunning` → `isProcessRunning(lock.pid)`). A lock leaked by the gateway's **own process** — e.g. an in-process SIGUSR1 restart abandoning a mid-refresh promise before its `finally` releases, exactly the long-lived systemd deployment in the report — holds a pid that stays alive for the process's whole lifetime, so every subsequent `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath` returns `"busy"` forever while the background queue keeps re-scheduling. Fixes #103910.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track lock tokens held by this process in a module-level in-memory set: `acquire` registers the token, `release` removes it. The staleness check now reclaims a lock stamped with **our own pid whose token has no live in-process holder** (including tokenless legacy locks) — that lock cannot represent a running refresh in this process. Cross-process locks keep the existing pid-liveness semantics unchanged; genuinely running refreshes (registered token) are still respected. No new options or public surface.

## User Impact

`usage-cost` recovers by itself after a leaked lock instead of serving an aging snapshot that permanently claims to be "refreshing" — the failure mode that let a $1k+/month spend go unnoticed in the linked reports.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression test — forge a lock with `pid: process.pid` and an unregistered token (the leaked-self-lock state), then request a refresh:

```
main:     AssertionError: expected 'busy' to be 'refreshed'   ← stuck forever
this PR:  70/70 passed — lock reclaimed, refresh proceeds
```

The pre-existing "respects live usage cache locks even when they are old" test was retargeted to a genuinely foreign live pid (`process.ppid`), preserving its original intent under the new same-pid contract. Full suite `session-cost-usage.test.ts` 70/70; `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

prs.title: fix(models): keep recommended picker models after upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat model pickers showing every model when an upgrade is newer than the last hosted catalog publication.

## User Impact

Compatible stored recommendations survive an upgrade. The picker still shows the current/default models and recommended choices first, with the rest behind **All models**. A recommended ID cannot restore an unavailable model. No UI code, configuration, or stored data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The build timestamp is a freshness cutoff for remote model rows and prices, not for the publisher-owned recommendation list. Keep those older rows and prices rejected while retaining recommendations in the same captured catalog generation. Match recommendations against the rows actually served.

This preserves the paired row/pricing adoption and in-flight generation rules from #158000, and the publisher ownership and unserved-ID filtering from #166737, #167370, and #167989. The [catalog publication workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/catalog/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml) runs independently of releases and preserves the previous timestamp when catalog content has not changed. #158000 also records published-driver upgrade proof where the hosted catalog was older than the candidate build.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Focused overlay, pricing, and catalog visibility suites: 56 tests passed, including unchanged stale row/pricing rejection.
- The new regression fails on baseline `da65be64a3216fa78420099e41b9182c6ef29515` because the served row has no recommendation, and passes with this fix.
- The regression uses a valid v2 catalog and proves only currently served recommended rows match; stale rows and both pricing maps stay absent.
- Bounded Codex review found one existing snapshot fixture to migrate; it is fixed and its 12-test consumer suite passes. The simplification pass retained one snapshot owner, no UI changes, and no new stored state.
- Isolated real Gateways, same eight synthetic OpenAI models and the same valid stored v2 catalog dated October 2 (older than both builds): baseline shows all eight; candidate shows Default + the served recommendation, with **All models (6)** collapsed. The retired recommended ID never appears.
- Screenshots below are from those desktop runs, cropped only to omit the private sidebar. No provider call or production profile was used.

### Before

![Before: the model picker lists all eight models](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73fb0ec1-a4db-40cf-b01e-ce1bdddadc77)

### After

![After: the model picker retains the recommendation and collapses six other models](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/190b53c2-8670-4de9-99d4-ed06a8c0ea69)

## Merge risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous read behavior; this change writes no state and needs no migration. The affected consumers are model pickers using hosted recommendations. Remote rows and prices retain their existing freshness cutoff.

## What Problem This Solves

When an operator opts a heartbeat agent into `heartbeat.skipWhenBusy`, queued or active work for that same agent in a canonical `session:` or `nested:` lane should make the wake skip; the previous behavior did not apply that guard to these sibling lanes.

## User Impact

With the opt-in enabled, heartbeats now honor the busy guard for same-agent work across those lanes. `false` or an unset option preserves baseline behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change restores the opt-in guard by reading existing command-lane totals. Doctor migration preserves the option while handling unrelated retired configuration. The implementation adds no queue reservation or atomic queue lock.

## Evidence

- Focused source tests: 587 tests across six shards passed.
- Independent runtime, config, Doctor, and active-queue checks: 48/48 passed.
- Core source typecheck and changed-test typecheck passed; changed-test graphs were `infra`, `config-cli`, `other`, and `commands-doctor`.
- Changed-path type-aware oxlint, targeted oxfmt, repository docs format, and diff checks passed.
- Exact-head PR checks for `055bea03` completed; `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36018152684.

### Supplemental validation (2026-09-24)

- Current-head source-pipeline regression: 8/8 r3 cases passed on `055bea03`. The test exercised the source heartbeat runner with one queued same-agent sibling/nested lane, observed `lanes-busy`, then delivery after the preserved wake retried at 1s or 60s; false/unset controls ran immediately. Reply and Telegram send functions were mocked. This is source-pipeline evidence, not installed-package dispatch, and no OS syscall trace was run.
- Published-updater sample: the published `2026.9.5` CLI updated a temporary isolated prefix to a tarball built from `055bea03` in two sampled configurations (`defaults=true` with entry unset; `defaults=false` with `ops=true`). - The no-channel plain updater invocation refused the first sample as invalid config; explicit `--channel stable` was required. These two configurations do not establish behavior for every config shape. No provider/model credentials or live managed service were used; the candidate package was applied only to the temporary prefix. No maintainer decision is implied.
- Independent Tester review passed for the strict mixed-scope updater preservation check and the current-head 8/8 source-pipeline trace; all scope limits stated above remain.
