prs.title: fix(state): avoid unrelated repairs during schema upgrades
prs.body:
Related: #172046, #171764, #172074, #171881.

## What Problem This Solves

A small schema upgrade also ran unrelated index repair, historical transcript and trajectory normalization, archive publication, planner analysis, and ACP replay accounting across retained data.

## User Impact

Upgrading a recent canonical database preserves unrelated retained content and leaves historical repair to a same-version Doctor pass. Full pre-migration backups remain required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Modern version migrations now limit work to their declared tables and required startup columns. Agent finalization leaves unrelated additive indexes alone; canonical shared-state v20/v21 sources run their declared transforms and indexes. Older or noncanonical sources retain repair. Same-version media repair and ACP accounting record completion transactionally. The Doctor prelude carries repair-eligible targets forward, so later entry/directive repair respects the version-only deferral. Planner maintenance uses the existing 1,000-row analysis limit with SQLite optimization.

Full backups remain mandatory. Later stages of the complete Doctor invocation still exceed the proposed table scopes, so this PR deliberately adds **no table-scoped backup declaration**. It introduces no schema version, retention, or SDK contract change. Main's schema-27 outbox migration and required `session_windows` startup columns are preserved.

## Removed work and accepted edges

- Remove unconditional global index repair after modern agent migration: allowed missing additive indexes wait for same-version admission/repair.
- Remove the transcript/trajectory detection scan before mutation: an absent completion marker selects one repair transaction.
- Remove media `PRAGMA data_version` capture/recheck: maintenance has exclusive custody; unsupported external writes are outside the ownership contract.
- Remove repeated same-version schema ensure after media repair: the owner retains the established schema facts.
- Remove repeated ACP payload/accounting repair after completion: unsupported direct SQL edits do not reopen historical repair; restoring missing accounting columns does.
- Remove unconditional `ANALYZE main`: SQLite selects missing/stale statistics, subject to the supported older-SQLite limitation below.

Lease-loss aborts, corruption handling, archive replacement protection, rollback, and backups remain.

## Evidence

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway ordinary-path T1 sites in touched owners | 0 | 0 |
| Global T1 inventory | 223 | 223 |
| Synthetic v25→v27 migration SQL / worker requests / offline MAIN | 257,053 / 8 / 257,000 | 504 / 5 / 467 |
| Warmed-turn SQL / requests / MAIN | No changed warmed path | No warmed-path claim |

The T2 annotation covers only `backfillAcpReplayEstimatedBytes`: `ensureAdditiveStateColumns` calls it from cold schema admission/migration and Doctor repair, with no Gateway runtime caller. CI at 251691f5666 confirmed T1 223→223 and deprecated compatibility calls 12→12. Dialect groups remain mechanical 0→0, design 29→29, engine-maintenance 34→34.

The matched migration measurement uses a frozen v25 schema, 550.6 MiB of synthetic data, 32,768 transcript rows, 32,768 trajectory rows, and 16 stored/physical archives. Counts come from the shared SQL observer. This measures `migrateLegacyMediaPersistence`, excluding full backup and later Doctor stages. The candidate preserves all five raw payload/archive/statistics witnesses. The comparison removes 256,549 statements and 3 requests; each of the 32,768 transcript rewrites, trajectory rewrites, transcript hydration/projection reads, and related FTS inserts disappears from the version-only path. Observed migration elapsed time was 946.6s on base and 76.3s on candidate; these loaded-host observations cannot establish a latency improvement.

Changed-file oxfmt, type-aware oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. Boundary tests cover migration table scope, unrelated payload/archive/statistics preservation, same-version repair, completion-marker rollback, and restored accounting columns. The scope regression includes `session_windows` because current readers require its startup columns. Codex autoreview completed without actionable findings. Final-head production/test types, all lint stripes, source contracts, architecture/Madge, database ratchets, docs, and PostgreSQL conformance pass in [CI run 38649133596](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38649133596). SDK declaration preparation initially exceeded its 300-second limit; the targeted package-boundary rerun passed (job 116150013811), without source changes.

The required **published-driver × candidate update cell passed** on exact head `e81fd59a376` in [Package Acceptance run 38649137981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38649137981), targeted job 116156467627. It runs the installed published updater first. Candidate packaging, package integrity, npm 12 installer acceptance, and the final workflow verification also passed. Six earlier immediate-only Testbox allocations lacked capacity; the supported custom Package Acceptance lane supplied the completed proof.

CI found a historical board fixture retaining schema 27 outbox definitions. Commit 69d39f90661 restores the empty outbox from the frozen historical schema, preserving its nonempty-table guard; that head’s CI test jobs pass. The duplicate local replay was canceled before acquiring a CPU slot, so it produced no local verdict. A Matrix cleanup case failed during global database retirement after its result assertion passed. A bounded local replay stopped during slow module imports without a case verdict, so that earlier failure is not classified as inherited or fixed; that head’s CI test jobs passed without repeating it. Knip script exports passed. The production scan found two helpers made unused by this PR; commit `e81fd59a376` deletes them and the obsolete freshness-helper test while retaining corruption and session-authority coverage. Its other eight findings match the same rule/file/symbol in [main run 38632684569, job 116088558072](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632684569/job/116088558072). Final-head Knip completed: all 8 production and 17 full-tree findings exactly match that main job by rule/file/symbol, with no new findings or scan errors. Script exports also passed; the inherited findings are recorded with the main-failure owner. The remaining CI failure is `test/gateway-completion-replay.e2e.test.ts`: the explicit followup after restart returns `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`, after the real requester/tool effect and durable suspended-delivery assertions pass. The client-only failure log cannot distinguish the untouched session/recovery guards that emit this error; fresh database creation returns before the changed version-migration paths. A focused main comparison was canceled during E2E declaration preparation after more than 40 minutes, before the test ran; its managed children settled and the lane branch was restored. This failure remains unclassified, with no inherited or fixed claim. The preceding head’s complete CI passed; the final cleanup only removed the two unused helpers and their obsolete test. Landing follows the authorized relaxed policy, which blocks proven product regressions and PR-caused static failures; this unresolved test is recorded as a follow-up. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks pass for the cleanup.

The earlier-head Doctor preview failure is inherited: [scheduled main run 38624335362, job 116059989511](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38624335362/job/116059989511), head c5511470ba9982423524feead601431d68a4bdfc, fails `doctor-auth-flat-profiles.test.ts:1761` / `previews noncanonical SQLite sessions without mutating or requiring canonical migration` with the same expected-throw/received-undefined assertion. Its test/read/admission/cache files are untouched. The failure is recorded with the main-failure owner.

LOC against integrated main: production +266/−140, tests +561/−134, docs +27/−5, owner classifications +13. Production growth records repair completion and declares bounded migration work; test growth exercises the owning runtime/Doctor boundaries.

## Follow-up

Supported WAL-safe SQLite 3.44.6 lacks the newer all-table/missing-statistics `PRAGMA optimize` behavior, so planner refresh can be skipped on that vendor-linked line. Restoring bounded maintenance there remains a P2 follow-up. Query correctness and version-migration deferral are unchanged; this PR does not change the runtime support floor.

prs.title: refactor: simplify Workboard and MCP relay internals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard and the MCP relay carry duplicate internal validation, dispatch, rendering, and rollback paths that make their actual owners harder to follow.

## User Impact

Successful card, board, session, and relay flows keep their existing behavior. A failed multi-card operation now leaves individually committed cards and links visible and reports the original error; inspect and repair partial work before retrying. Workspace-specific compensation, revision conflicts, claim redaction, current caller authority, and normal shutdown settlement remain.

No schema, permissions, retention, public configuration, protocol, SDK, or dependency changes. Browser appearance is unchanged: retained CSS selectors keep their declaration sequences, and native render tags/text/attributes remain the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing worker-operation binder and a total typed worker-handler table replace per-method forwarding paths without casts. Canonical card snapshots, metadata, and input facts are carried forward instead of being reread, cloned, frozen, or revalidated. Card moves use the existing mutation runner, including reservations for displaced cards; equivalent native render paths and CSS declarations are shared.

The relay admits its required typed ingress capability once, and initialization returns the signing identity it already decoded. Persisted-state parsing, consent/grant authority, reconnect handling, and resource limits stay at their owners.

Net production reduction against the branch base: **500 lines** (+430 / -930), excluding tests, fixtures, generated files, declarations, and docs.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Failed create/link/decompose after earlier commits: [#126161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126161) introduced inverse-journal recovery around synthetic paused two-connection tests, not a cited human production incident. Partial committed cards/links now remain visible; the original error propagates. Workspace authority and lossless worktree cleanup retain their separate compensation.
- An internal consumer mutating a cached response object: [#164301](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164301) introduced revision-cache protection during a synthetic performance campaign, with no cited human mutation report. Recursive freezing is removed; trusted consumers serialize or read the projections. Performance caches and writer-receipt invalidation remain.
- An old rejected/completed read evicting a newer cache entry: [#165141](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165141) used synthetic cache/concurrency proof, not a human incident. Identity-matched eviction fences are removed; at worst the next request rebuilds an otherwise reusable entry.
- A private persistence caller supplying a non-version-1 wrapper or mismatched key: the relational serializer, carried into [#146976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146976), has only typed internal producers that use literal version 1 and the entity ID. Repeated wrapper guards are removed; external normalization, row/JSON decoding, revision CAS, and owner capacity remain.
- Corrupt old target children being decoded again during a claim after the caller already read that revision: [#146245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146245) added the extra hydration in a synthetic optimization campaign, with no cited human report. The redundant decode is removed; the claim still checks the current row revision and competing owner slots.
- A private caller changing a submitted object before transport: [#146976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146976) added a defensive clone during the worker migration, without a cited human mutation report. Internal callers await their submissions and do not mutate them; worker transport still serializes inputs. Admission and accepted-operation draining remain.
- Old event history requiring repair during an unrelated edit: [#106306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106306) mechanically retained normalization on append, without a cited human corruption report. Typed event producers and persisted row decoders remain; appending no longer reconstructs/revalidates the entire prior history. The event bound remains.
- A typed internal session pin or captured board spec being malformed: [#163823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163823) introduced the rule-based board writer, not a human invalid-pin report. Its sole production producer supplies an in-scope session, operator/reason literals, a clock timestamp, and a decoded spec. Duplicate shape/spec validation is removed; current authority, spec equality, column membership, placement revision CAS, and monotonic timestamps remain.
- Typed automation needing full validation again merely to supply the parent ID: [#106306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106306) carried this path through the store split; [#107087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107087) established the current authority-aware automation producer, not a human malformed-internal-automation report. The create owner already normalizes automation and resolves parent rows. It now supplies that default directly; external metadata normalization still runs at its boundary.
- An older bundled host lacking the current ingress version, or a typed issued relay authority being malformed: [#168233](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168233) introduced these probes/reparsing alongside synthetic security proof, not a human older-host incident. Bundled host and plugin ship together; service admission checks required ingress once. Persisted/external parsing and live security-effect checks remain.

## Coverage log

The three-day additions were inspected first, then seven-day history and largest owners. Detailed lane ledgers were maintained during implementation. Removed clusters are above; structural consolidations also cover optional-field omission, board-summary projection, scoped subscription filtering, worker dispatch, card-move reservations, native inline editors/PR badges, and identical CSS rules.

Subscription scope keeps the exact JavaScript card-ID comparison: SQLite's UTF-8 binding can make a lone UTF-16 surrogate compare equal to U+FFFD, unlike JavaScript. SQL still narrows candidate card rows and owns board filtering; board IDs are validated ASCII. This is a kept public matching contract, not redundant internal validation.

Kept deliberately: live consent/grant/caller/workspace authority; claim/revocation serialization; FIFO mutations; accepted writes at shutdown; restart reconciliation; dependency and owner-slot checks; persisted/import decoding; measured revision/facts caches; bounded network bodies and fragment assembly; current card lifecycle fixes. No dormant feature foundation was removed. Further browser similarities were small adapters with different authority, lifetime, ordering, or presentation contracts; an abstraction would add indirection rather than simplify them.

## Evidence

Final head `650326121af17f17444fec7864689ce7da984bff` completed [CI run 38654050088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38654050088). All selected jobs passed except the inherited sidebar browser case and its downstream aggregate. The corrected Workboard extension bundle passed (job `116160155323`). No jobs were rerun and no pushes were made merely for green. The earlier statement that final-head CI remained required is superseded by this table.

| Failing job | Attribution and proof |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-ui (1/3)` / `116160154641` | Inherited: `sidebar session filter popover > keeps keyboard navigation, focus and surface inside the viewport at 390 px (rtl)` expected occlusion history `[false,true]`, received `[false,true,false,true]`. The same case and exact assertion failed independently in [unrelated PR run 38594619483, job 115969252930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38594619483/job/115969252930). CI checkout `b8acde50ecd61a81e121fcaaa1d266d54ff9652e` contains unchanged UI/test/config inputs relative to main parent `4612504e2bdedacc9d0492f0b4ff6f62d678b1b9`; the sidebar fixture does not import Workboard CSS. Final-head isolated replay passed 1/1 in 15.64 s (13 cases name-filtered); this is not a causal-fix claim. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` / `116167867039` | Downstream aggregate of the sole UI failure above. Complete exact-head check-run inventory inspected; `security-fast`, types, lint, architecture, package boundaries, UI E2E/performance, PostgreSQL, both extension bundles, and the other UI shards passed. |

Landing uses the authorized native inherited-failure admin exception with exact-head failed-CI attribution retained. The automated selector initially classified this as new because its matching scheduled-main job passed; independent unrelated-PR signature evidence, not the selector, establishes the inherited attribution. The sidebar defect remains unresolved and belongs to its UI owner; no assertion, timeout, retry, or skip was changed.

- MCP relay: 9 files / 167 tests passed. Browser: 31 files / 244 tests passed; final renderer replay 3 files / 63 tests passed (overlap, not additive).
- Workboard server: all 12 focused files / 218 distinct tests passed. Final store suite after the claim preflight correction: 87 tests passed (192.71 s Vitest / 219.82 s wrapper). Earlier cold run also passed 87 tests (526.07 s / 559.94 s), including partial decomposition and capacity/partial-save cases. Gateway card-list: 6 tests passed, 384.05 s Vitest / 423.22 s wrapper (89% transforms). Different timings are not a controlled performance comparison.
- Sessions-board suite: 23 tests passed, 100.25 s Vitest / 134.81 s wrapper, including caller authority, scope, pins, expiry, and projection caching. Store sessions-board: 8 tests passed (145.24 s / 171.19 s), including stale-spec/pin CAS, columns, authority ending before a worker write, and prior-schema reopen.
- Batch-read: 11 tests passed (71.26 s Vitest / 96.70 s wrapper), including grouped-write rollback, capacity, attachment joins, and persisted-error ordering. SQLite lifecycle: 4 tests passed (70.77 s / 95.03 s), including accepted-work draining, cleanup retry, admission failure, and error propagation.
- Completed-card promotion: 9 tests passed (93.42 s Vitest / 118.11 s wrapper). Initial tools run passed 12/13 and exposed a real regression: a denied parent claim could leave a child card after rollback removal. The create owner now checks parent authority before initial insertion while retaining live link-effect checks. The unchanged tools suite then passed all 13 tests (147.41 s Vitest / 177.03 s wrapper); the previously failing security case passed in 3442 ms.
- Dispatcher: 15 tests passed (135.15 s Vitest / 159.77 s wrapper), including workspace sandbox limits, post-preflight authority, and shared-worker capacity.
- Workspace compensation: 2 tests passed (122.63 s Vitest / 146.70 s wrapper), preserving concurrent unrelated notes and workspace edits. Scoped-list: 9 tests passed (75.22 s / 110.88 s), including scope-isolated card/history/notification hydration and parent-card behavior.
- Lifecycle-sync: 31 tests passed (324.45 s Vitest / 370.34 s wrapper), including session ownership, current readers, replacement, incognito, and deferred failures. Across both plugins, the focused pass covers 52 files / 629 distinct tests; overlapping replays are not added.
- First exact-head CI run `38651138490` failed `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2`, job `116150755415`: the unchanged scoped-subscription test caught the SQLite/JavaScript surrogate-equality difference described above. Local replay reproduced the exact failure (120.08 s Vitest / 147.98 s wrapper). Restoring the original one-line exact card-ID filter made that same selected case pass (100.04 s / 140.43 s); no test changes, retries, skips, or timeout increases. The other three cases were excluded by the failure-specific name filter, not changed or marked skipped in source. Fresh source types, syntax lint, formatting, and diff-check also pass for this correction.
- That first CI run completed with no other product failures: `openclaw/ci-gate` failed solely downstream from the extension bundle. All other selected lanes passed, including types, type-aware lint, architecture guards, package boundaries, UI checks, and PostgreSQL conformance. This was PR-caused, not attributed to inherited main reds. The correction passed fresh isolated review and the lint-suppression gate (3 tests, 66.03 s Vitest / 89.56 s wrapper). The final-head result and inherited UI attribution are recorded in the table above.
- Production-source and scoped test typechecks for both plugins passed. After the claim preflight correction, the source typecheck, focused syntax lint, formatting, diff-check, and lint-suppression gate passed again (3 tests; 35.10 s Vitest / 47.33 s wrapper); no new suppressions.
- PostCSS comparison preserved declaration sequences for all 772 retained selector/at-rule pairs. No intended visual output change.
- Runtime import check: zero value cycles; final madge check: zero cycles. Subsequent handler-table, pin, and parent-authority edits add no imports/graph edges, so that unchanged-input proof is reused.
- Fresh independent review passed: scoped-clean, no actionable P0-P2 findings on the full candidate. A fresh delta review also passed for the parent-authority correction, confirming preflight, idempotency, and later live checks.
- Local check-changed found the inherited environment-count mismatch: 455 names vs budget 454. The same owner check on the untouched index at the original branch base reproduces the exact failure; this diff adds no OPENCLAW_* name and does not change the budget. Script dead-export analysis passed with zero findings; production and full-tree scans hit the existing 600 s limit (ETIMEDOUT), so those are missing results, not clean scans.
- The check-changed attempt ran over 75 minutes and was explicitly interrupted (exit 130) during the database-first legacy-store guard after 744 s; owned children drained and exited. Media-helper and runtime-sidecar guards were not reached. Its cycle step was not reached; prior unchanged-input zero-cycle proof above remains valid. These unfinished checks and the timeout gaps require hosted CI; they are not reported passing. Completed steps included full extension source/test types, SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, assertions, timeout/mock ratchets, Doctor contracts, SDK/plugin boundaries, dependency/patch guards, formatting, i18n, coercion declarations, and deprecated API usage. Exact-head hosted CI will be recorded separately.
- Earlier interrupted server attempts are not passing evidence. Two recent attempts were stopped while native compilation was active; final proof was sequential with frozen source and reusable artifacts. Type-aware lint failed before linting because SDK-boundary declaration preparation hit its existing 300000 ms timeout on the saturated host; the mandatory check-changed run reproduced the same preparation timeout. No further local retry, timeout increase, or guard bypass was used. Syntax lint and full extension source/test types pass; type-aware lint/package-boundary declarations remain a hosted-CI proof gap.

prs.title: perf(talk): serve catalog snapshots while refreshing readiness
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Talk catalog reads currently await provider configuration, credential readiness and session projection work on every call. Production observations included 2,769 ms and 1,446 ms replies, with other reads delayed on the same connections; a historical 15-minute window averaged 2,780 ms/call at 7.46 calls/min. These are wait costs that the earlier catalog CPU simplification did not address.

## User Impact

The Gateway now serves its last successful catalog snapshot immediately and refreshes it in the background, with one refresh per agent/provider/model selection. Config, plugin, credential and secret revisions invalidate freshness; otherwise reads refresh after 30 seconds. Session visibility is checked before every disclosure, inside the projection's authorization callback. Catalog readiness remains advisory; session creation retains current credential and policy checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cold reads return a retryable warming error. Control UI, Swift and Android callers retry that specific response within ten seconds. Cold provider readiness failures mark only the affected row unconfigured, preserving healthy providers; broader failed cold discovery retries after one second. Failed or late refreshes preserve the last good snapshot. A first successful cold snapshot may publish after five seconds so a consistently slow hook cannot trap callers in warming. A five-second deadline prevents replacement of an existing snapshot; uncancelable provider hooks retain their single-flight slot until they settle. Speech readiness receives a five-second provider timeout. Slow logs distinguish session resolution from catalog configuration, selection and provider phases without logging credentials or provider payloads.

## Evidence

Validation: focused catalog (12), Talk handler (106), file transcription (23), TTS persona (11) and browser Gateway (54) tests passed; changed TypeScript formatting/lint and diff checks passed. Native test cases were extended and are delegated to PR CI, along with builds, typecheck, closure guards and broad suites. No Testbox lease was allocated. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) is clean after fixing cold retry backoff and native compatibility, plus the PR findings about cold provider failure isolation, first-attempt client deadlines, and late cold snapshot publication.

Measurement: actual WebSocket `talk.catalog` calls for an existing visible session, eight clients, 5,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 retained runs, approvals/cron/projects and a 4.32 GiB agent database. Both revisions used the same synthetic state sequentially on the isolated benchmark host. A synthetic speech readiness hook awaited loopback HTTP; models and voices were static. Response payload: 514 bytes. Startup recovery settled before measurement; this is a controlled provider-wait comparison, not a replica of live provider configuration or load.

| Scenario | Before mean / p95 | After mean / p95 | Provider fetches before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.8 s provider, 60 offered RPCs/min, 12 calls | 1,827.50 / 1,959.38 ms | 2.42 / 6.78 ms | 12 → 1 |
| 1.8 s provider, 16-call burst | 1,834.46 / 1,839.96 ms | 13.34 / 16.77 ms | 16 → 1 |
| 6.5 s provider stall, 16-call burst | 6,540.60 / 6,546.56 ms | 8.24 / 10.32 ms | 16 → 1 |
| HTTP 503, 8-call burst | 1,816.67 ms mean | 6.17 ms mean | 8 → 1 |

The steady offered call rate is unchanged at 60/min; the change removes per-call waits and coalesces refresh work. All eight failed-provider reads retained the configured last-good row, versus zero before. Post-timeout and post-failure reads took 1.43 and 1.68 ms and retained that row. Cold start is intentionally different: the initial fast-provider call returned warming in 60.45 ms, followed by a successful 1.91 ms read; baseline cold success took 55.55 ms.

The slow refresh log attributed 1,808 ms of a 1,810 ms refresh to speech readiness. The deadline logged at 5,000 ms, and the timeout-aware provider fetch settled at 5,002 ms. Baseline: `937213650ab782206eb1436175fa53f4cfa06009`; measured implementation: `d1f8efb7cddca47f5d7d31955497d6cd93ce6fae`. Subsequent fixes capture the same map in a constant for TypeScript closure narrowing and isolate cold provider readiness errors. The first Android and browser catalog attempt now also respects the ten-second overall budget, including shorter caller deadlines and cancellation; three fake-clock no-response cases pass. A controlled-clock handler regression also covers a six-second cold realtime hook: twenty concurrent reads share one refresh, and its first result publishes after settlement. All twelve catalog cases pass, including retention of the last good warm snapshot beyond its deadline. Warm refresh behavior is preserved; the new cold behavior has focused regression coverage across speech, realtime and transcription.

Await audit: the old request awaited session projection, `buildTalkRealtimeConfig` (including default readiness), automatic realtime provider selection, speech readiness, transcription configuration/selection and streaming readiness, and realtime config/capability/readiness hooks. Credential availability can queue worker preparation/reads and cleanup; file transcription model availability can resolve execution auth and refresh OAuth. Built-in voice/model lists are static metadata; plugin hooks can perform network work. These readiness awaits now run in the detached refresh, while session authorization remains on the RPC path and has its own slow phase log.

Production attribution remains bounded by existing logs: 46 successful slow responses in the sampled hour mapped to Control UI connections; other RPCs on the same connections were slow nearby. Existing logs cannot distinguish provider readiness from shared queue delays. The new phase logs provide that distinction. Production before: 2,780 ms/call at 7.46 calls/min in the historical window; production after is unmeasured because this PR does not deploy or load-test production.

PR CI found a nullable cleanup closure and three integration fixtures that assumed synchronous discovery. The cleanup now captures its owned map, and the fixtures await the actual refresh root release while preserving their original credential, visibility, model and camera assertions; all eight cases passed in their three focused files. Typed lint is satisfied by an explicit tuple return with no runtime change. Controlled-clock tests cover warming, readiness failure isolation, cold publication after a slow hook, and client deadlines. All fixes received independent review.

Earlier heads encountered an SDK declaration-build timeout, a Watch simulator runtime startup error and an Android SDK download HTTP/2 failure. Those jobs passed on head `4a63beadb76f`; no CI rerun was requested to chase green. Swift production code compiled through iOS screenshot CI; the separate Swift unit-test lane was not selected. The benchmark Gateway and HTTP server were stopped, their ports verified closed, and their sandbox removed.

CI run [38651585679](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38651585679) has two failing test files, with production/test typechecks, SDK boundary, lint, security, UI e2e, iOS screenshots, Android Play/Wear and both native-access variants passing. The sidebar browser timeout is attributed as an unrelated flake under the standing rule: `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu-scroll.browser.test.ts` passed 5/5 on PR head `4a63beadb76f`, 5/5 on the actual CI main parent `d866ef3baf4b`, and 5/5 on tested merge `a987189b1e22`. Test times were 3.61–4.32 s, 3.03–4.71 s and 3.28–3.79 s, respectively. Each process ran one file and one test with CI's pinned Bun/Chromium. The executed sidebar owners and fixture have identical base/merge blobs; the synthetic client never constructs the changed Gateway client or requests the catalog. No CI reruns were requested. The Android onboarding assertion exposed a missing UI publication wait: runtime and ViewModel refresh completion precede Compose state collection and native dialog rendering, but the fixture advanced exactly one frame before asserting visibility. A four-line test repair now advances the controlled Compose clock until the dialog is displayed, preserving the original visibility and background-dismissal assertions. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): avoid duplicate sends after socket failures
prs.body:
Closes #142398

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate WhatsApp sends when an ambiguous socket failure causes retries to generate different provider message IDs.

## User Impact

One logical in-process send keeps the same Baileys ID across attempts and successor sockets; the next send gets a new ID. No configuration, migration, dependency or public callback change.

This does not guarantee exactly-once delivery, recover lost server acknowledgements, or preserve identity across process restarts. Main's bounded retry budget and terminal-timeout/partial-acceptance safeguards are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already removed the outer retry owner in [#169099](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169099). This refresh drops our now-obsolete retry-window plumbing and preserves that simpler upstream policy. Only the missing stable-ID assignment remains: assign it once in the attached socket owner, preserving a supplied nonempty ID and generating a pinned fallback for an empty ID.

The former `reply`/`sendMedia` reconnect-window API expansion is gone, so that specific public-contract decision no longer applies. Normal delivery-risk review still applies. Historical PR commits are retained; no force-push was used.

## Evidence

- Head: `377b7480795a3771ec111e1898b1fd51b98f83e3`; integrated main: `5930f05a68b61520ce4ee7e5057858ff146e1737`. Six WhatsApp paths: one production file (+7 net lines), one focused dependency regression and four existing test-assertion updates. Proof used frozen main `c2854d810f06290d4137a7990b32ea78beb8aa09`; the final branch refresh left all six files, WhatsApp/dependency inputs and relevant test/SDK instructions unchanged.
- **Before/after:** on unfixed main, the real Baileys relay regression fails for generated IDs, empty IDs and a successor socket; its supplied-ID negative control passes. With the fix, all four pass, including a distinct next-send ID.
- **68 focused tests passed** in the five files below. Targeted WhatsApp production/test types, six-file type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. AutoReview was scoped-clean at P0–P2; only two lint-required test brace changes followed it. No full application build or broad suite.
- **Real WhatsApp transport proof passed on this exact head (2026-10-14 23:51 UTC):** the production attached-socket retry owner used a real authenticated Baileys client, real encrypted WebSocket writes and real WhatsApp server acknowledgements. An injected retryable error after the first completed native write produced a retry with the same ID; the next logical send used a different ID. Two labelled self-chat messages, three native writes; 9.270s total including connection/close. No `sendNode`, WebSocket, auth, encryption or server-response mocks. See the redacted trace below.
- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38644399434) completed successfully; no failed or pending checks at the proof update. The latest review identified no code finding and requested this live trace. No source commit, branch refresh or CI rerun for the proof update.

<details>
<summary>Focused test costs</summary>

Each file ran once after the fix with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Wall times include wrapper/setup; test-body time is separate. These are local focused-test timings; the completed current-head CI is linked above.

| `monitor-inbox.delivery-and-dedupe.test.ts` | 18 | 24.21s | 2.470s |

| `monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts` | 9 | 9.47s | 2.077s |
| `monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts` | 22 | 9.68s | 1.703s |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Redacted real-transport failure/recovery trace</summary>

Executed against `377b7480795a3771ec111e1898b1fd51b98f83e3` with Node 26.8.1 and pinned Baileys 7.0.0-rc14. The normal managed Gateway was stopped before the probe and restored afterward; WhatsApp was then linked, running and connected with no channel error. The probe used the existing session in place through OpenClaw's maintained `createWaDirectorySocket` (ordinary inbox handling disabled), then the unmodified production `createWhatsAppAttachedSocketSession`. No copied or newly paired credentials. Native credential saves drained on close; no logout.

Only the instance's `sendMessage` return boundary was instrumented: await the original real native send, record its returned ID, then throw `operation timed out after real transport write (injected)` once. The production retry loop handled that error. For this bounded probe, two attempts and 250ms backoff were selected. No physical network disconnect or successor socket was injected; the existing focused regression separately covers successor identity.

prs.title: fix(update): allow macOS updates from login shells
prs.body:
Closes #172591. Thanks @giulianoaccorsi for reporting this.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS updates refusing with `service-ancestry-unverified` when a terminal shell descends from a root-owned `login` process that macOS will not let the updater inspect.

## User Impact

An external terminal can update when native launchd containment proves it is outside the Gateway's job, even if its ancestry walk is incomplete. Known Gateway ancestors and native service members still cannot stop their own Gateway. Linux and Windows behavior is unchanged. No new configuration, dependencies, or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update preflight required a complete parent walk even after native membership returned `outside`; launchd maintenance already accepted that evidence. Both now use one decision in the service-membership owner. Missing native containment still requires complete ancestry, and unreadable native containment still refuses.

The installed proc-safe ancestry API stops at an unreadable identity and has no parent-PID-only continuation API. No dependency change is needed: native launchd membership independently proves the external terminal.

## Evidence

- Required cross-lane inventory: all 22 test files returned by the changed production basenames were exercised. The remaining 15-file batch passed all 334 tests; the first batch had 159 passing tests and two failures. One was the obsolete macOS CLI assertion, repaired and replayed successfully; the other is the unchanged already-current failure reproduced on the exact base (details below). This leaves 494 passing cases and one confirmed inherited failure across the required inventory.
- Targeted core typecheck and all 28 selected test type graphs passed; the adjusted CLI file also passed its selected type graph afterward. Changed-file lint, format, import cycles, database guards, and all other changed-check steps passed after the line-cap/mock cleanup. The aggregate check remains red only for the inherited env budget and Knip findings below.
- Regression fails on the original production code with `service-ancestry-unverified`; all five cases pass after the fix. The cases cover `outside`, `absent`, `inside`, `unknown`, and an observed Gateway ancestor, with `complete: false, stoppedBy: "unreadable-parent"`.
- Live macOS proof used a task-owned dev Gateway on an isolated state directory/free port, supervised by a unique launchd job. From `/usr/bin/login -f` → shell → probe, the real preflight returned `{"ancestry":{"complete":false,"stoppedBy":"unreadable-parent"},"deniedParent":{"code":"access-denied"},"membership":"outside","block":null}`. The dev job, listener, and state were removed afterward.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. An initial temporary-directory isolation failure was corrected using macOS's private per-user temporary directory; isolation remained enabled.
- Production LOC: +36/−22 (net +14) to share the existing policy across both callers; tests/fixtures: +79/−13; docs: +2; mock baseline: nine obsolete allowances removed, with no new allowances.

prs.title: fix: keep unavailable native-runtime heartbeats quiet
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated heartbeat failure messages when a native runtime is unavailable and an existing `before_agent_reply` readiness hook would have intentionally handled the turn silently.

## User Impact

The readiness hook can silently finish background heartbeats or return its actionable response to a user request before native capability discovery attempts a connection. Healthy native runs retain their supported thinking levels, including `max`. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native thinking-capability discovery ran during queued-run parameter construction, before the reply hook. Move it into the existing runtime-preparation stage after the hook declines the turn, using the selected runtime/model and preserving current-run checks and auth-route compatibility. Host-runtime preparation stays in place. This October backport changes two production files; the remaining changes protect the behavior in tests.

## Evidence

- Three new readiness regressions fail with the original production logic and pass with this change: unavailable heartbeat stays silent, unavailable user request receives the hook response, and a healthy request reaches the hook before discovery.
- Node 24.19: **28/28 focused cases pass** (3 readiness, 8 runtime-capability, 2 parameter-preparation, 15 runtime-selection cases). These are network-free composition/unit tests, not live Gateway or Slack acceptance.
- Production types, all 27 test type graphs, formatting, lint, unused exports, import cycles, and selected schema/storage/auth guards passed. The changed-check run stopped at a local pnpm-cache permission error; that unchanged check and every remaining planned check were subsequently completed successfully.

prs.title: feat(dev): default local tests and CLI to pinned Bun
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local tests and development still default to Node, and opting into Bun currently trusts whichever `bun` happens to be on PATH. Make the pinned OpenClaw fork the local default while preserving explicit choices and CI's planner-owned runtime.

Land after the 94f8f5ffec repin.

## User Impact

`pnpm test` and `pnpm dev` use the pinned fork automatically on supported local platforms. The existing checksum-verifying stager populates a per-user, tag/platform cache; stamped executables avoid repeated hashing. `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` selects an explicit executable. Unsupported platforms or unavailable staging fall back to Node with one actionable notice; `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` forces Node and silences it. Explicit Bun requests fail if unavailable. CI defaults remain Node unless its planner explicitly selects Bun.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep policy in `resolveTestRuntime` and binary acquisition in one small resolver that reuses the existing pin and stager. Local Bun launchers use an absolute executable and prepend its directory to child PATH. In CI, a shared CI-truthiness check preserves the workflow-provisioned `bun` and PATH without accessing the local cache; `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` still wins. Prepared worker copies resolve checkout resources through the existing root locator. Live tests select and propagate the runtime before adding their noninteractive `CI=1` setting. The pin, stager semantics, installer, runtime planner, and workflows are unchanged. Document the known main-only Node coverage gap.

Test classification:
- New `test-runtime.test.ts` and `pinned-bun.test.ts`: default/cache contract coverage, including explicit selection, CI, unsupported platforms, override, cache reuse, stamp mismatch, corruption repair, and staging failure; filesystem/stager fixtures use no network.
- Bucket 2: `run-vitest.test.ts`, `vitest-worker-artifacts.batch.test.ts`, and `agent-plugin-gateway-e2e.test.ts` assumed the literal command `bun`; assert the selected absolute executable and preserved launch contract instead.
- Bucket 2: `test-live.test.ts` previously supplied fake Bun through PATH; use the explicit executable override, and prove the implicit local choice reaches the child environment.
- Bucket 2: `run-node.test-support.ts` relied on the old implicit Node default; its synthetic CLI fixtures now select Node explicitly. `src/infra/run-node.test.ts` now supplies an explicit executable fixture and proves local/default, Node, and Bun launch ordering without relying on PATH. Cancellation behavior stays covered.
- Bucket 2: `vitest-report-owner.test.ts` required V8-specific JSON parse wording. It now checks `SyntaxError` while retaining exact corrupt-byte, saved-original, failed-merge, and old-output assertions.
- Bucket 1: `eager-import-closure.test.ts` exposed the new resolver missing from the trusted wrapper extraction. Include the resolver and its pin/stager resources in `wrapper-components.txt`.

Production LOC: +207/-15 (net +192); tests: +242/-14 (net +228); docs: +23/-6. This lane explicitly adds new capability, so production growth is expected. No fork bugs or new runtime-only skips.

## Evidence

Pinned fork: `1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715`. Ten focused test files pass on both runtimes across the main run and focused final reruns (330 tests total). The new resolver tests take under 50 ms. The existing batch lifecycle file took 39–52 s and the report-owner file took 192–193 s locally (142 s in the first CI run); they verify real subprocess preparation, cancellation, crash handling, and publication rather than mocked helper behavior.

```sh
tests=(test/scripts/{test-runtime,pinned-bun,run-vitest,test-live,vitest-worker-artifacts.batch,agent-plugin-gateway-e2e,run-node-cancellation}.test.ts)
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test "${tests[@]}" --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin/bun pnpm test "${tests[@]}" --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix: keep speed selectable with configured defaults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes speed choices being locked or silently ignored when a configured service tier or fast-mode default is present, including clicking Standard while inheriting `flex` or `auto`.

## User Impact

Users can explicitly select Standard, Fast, or Ultrafast regardless of their configured default, subject to the model's supported choices and existing write permissions. Speed can be changed during an active reply without altering that in-flight request; later requests use the saved choice. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep inherited defaults distinct from explicit session selections all the way to the provider request. Unspecified speed preserves configured `flex`/`auto`, while explicit choices override the configured tier. Context and compaction limits use the effective request tier. The picker tracks displayed selection separately from persisted provenance so an explicit Standard click is not discarded merely because the inherited display looks the same.

## Evidence

- Rendered picker → real session patch → SDK request regression: inherited `flex`/`auto` remains unchanged until Standard is clicked, then `fastMode:false` produces `service_tier:default`.
- Fallback resolution → embedded execution parameters → SDK payload tests cover inherited and explicit selections.
- Focused UI suite: 62 passed; Chromium picker: 5 passed; core resolution/payload/fallback: 24 passed; OpenAI provider: 23 passed. Final permission-fixture recheck: 20 passed (subset of UI coverage).
- Affected core/core-test, UI, extension/extension-test typechecks and provider lint passed. Final `ui-chat` shard, formatting, docs MDX, full docs lint, and diff checks passed.
- Independent full-file review of the original 36 changed files, the final behavior correction, and the four-file CI repair. Provider requests are captured at the SDK boundary with synthetic credentials; no live provider or live Gateway changes.
- CI repair: the SDK-boundary permission suite is explicitly a Node harness, remains isolated, and executes once. Import-boundary proof and all 20 permission tests passed; routing regression failed before the duplicate-project fix and all 11 routing tests passed after. SQL-asset isolation preserves the real schema bytes; the mock-export ratchet passed.
- Incorporated main’s database-reader type repair (`920ab440dc`) to resolve the old CI build/type failures. SDK declarations, core/UI-chat/root-test types, scoped lint/format and diff checks passed on the repaired source. Broad exact-head PR CI remains a separate required gate.

Before: speed choices disabled during an active reply.

![Before: disabled speed choices](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40398e2e-c41b-4717-a4a8-3fcfd1308066)

After: speed choices remain available for subsequent requests.

![After: enabled speed choices](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/327d58a9-eae1-406f-b2d4-b6259c719b6d)

## Current-head validation

Published head: `e31300ede5bab8fcb0592fc0e0dd1707e94d61c6`. It preserves the reviewed speed and native keyboard fixes above and integrates main `f62dd8e0c29fc8acd3836e604da97a280e4fa053`.

CI run 38636158633 on the previous head failed in shared DOM teardown, usage overview retention, and one WebKit menu-occlusion assertion. The repair captures the actual native window registration owner, releases removed listener callbacks immediately, and preserves the existing usage WeakRef assertion. The menu test now observes the real animation-frame sampling boundary while retaining every geometry notification assertion; no timeout increase, retry, skip, or production occlusion rewrite.

Independent source review approved the DOM repair and found the menu synchronization sound. Focused Node usage tests passed 3/3; pinned-Bun affected tests passed 85/85. The cross-file regression demonstrates callback collection before cleanup. All 40 menu checks passed across Chromium/WebKit; scoped lint and formatting passed.

The broader local check is **not** reported green: 606/608 UI shard files passed, with two local differences (repository-contained temporary-root plugin discovery and ICU narrow German duration formatting). An adjacent browser check passed 182 tests and failed two WebKit outside-focus cases; those exact cases passed the previous Linux CI, and the local cause is not established. These results are retained for audit, not hidden by a rerun. Current-head hosted CI remains required before landing.

Prior worker proof remains valid: the complete workload passed locally in 125,848ms with its original 240,000ms deadline. Earlier timeouts are historical, not retroactively green. No live Gateway, provider, credential, policy, or deployment changes.

### Latest main integration

Resolved the new main conflict by retaining Peter Steinberger's upstream DOM resource cleanup implementation from `5e4a1bed3a86187d42997946f62d5c2518be89d5`, without duplicating it. The additional removed-listener and forwarding-window regression fixtures remain. Independent review approved the exact integrated tree; the shared-runner lifecycle regression and all three usage-retention tests passed after integration. The previous queued CI run had no test results before mergeability changed; it is not claimed as CI success. Current-head CI remains required.

### Sidebar fixture isolation

CI run 38642764175 on `93f28078bcb39f75488c0878f619f51f68194323` passed the DOM/usage shards but failed the Chromium 390px RTL sidebar case with extra native-occlusion transitions. The diagnostic first transition preceded the intended picker admission. The fixture parked the previous case's real pointer only after mounting, allowing hover surfaces during initialization.

The repair parks the pointer before mounting. A regression deliberately leaves the pointer over a disposable sidebar control, removes that sidebar, and verifies that its replacement is not hovered before any caller correction. This fails before the repair and passes after it; the original exact occlusion histories, focus, geometry, RTL and keyboard assertions remain unchanged. Independent source review approved the single-file change. All 15 configured Chromium cases passed; no WebKit result is claimed for this Chromium-owned file. New published-head CI is still required. The first CI surface was not identified, so the diagnostic is not claimed to prove a particular tooltip implementation defect.

Scoped type-aware lint and formatting also passed. The subsequent CI result for `3b3a8db73b87df8f6d505bfa9786f783c448e900` is recorded below; predecessor failures are not relabeled green.

### Follow-up: main conflict and cleanup callback type

CI run 38646175696 on `3b3a8db73b87df8f6d505bfa9786f783c448e900` passed the sidebar UI lane but failed two root jobs: the UI test-type shard found a cleanup callback returning VitestUtils instead of void, and the launch-wire worker test reached its 300,000ms no-output watchdog. The borrower/nested-claim cleanup errors followed watchdog termination; the stalled operation is not established. The worker failure is classified unknown, not inherited.

This follow-up preserves upstream early-window registration in the DOM fixture while retaining the removed-listener and forwarding regressions. It changes the sidebar cleanup callback to a block body, discarding only the synchronous return value. Independent full-file review approved both changes. The shared-runner cleanup case, all 3 usage-retention cases, the UI-components typecheck, all 15 Chromium sidebar cases, scoped lint, formatting and diff checks passed.

A single isolated macOS worker reproduction retained the original test/silence limits but exhausted its 600-second command budget during runtime compilation before entering the test. It is not a passing reproduction or a worker repair. No timeout, receipt check, assertion or cleanup guarantee was weakened. The new signed head `89359b7fad883cfb21ebd98d74b6f56682b67a77` requires its own hosted CI and normal review/security gates before landing.


### Follow-up: bound menu input reads

CI run 38650376890 completed on `89359b7fad883cfb21ebd98d74b6f56682b67a77`: the worker and typecheck lanes passed, but the selected-agent sidebar browser case timed out at its unchanged 60-second limit. The passing worker attempt is not proof that its earlier unexplained timeout was repaired.

A same-order browser reproduction and CPU profile identified a 235-deep chain of accumulated VanillaMachine prop-merge closures; reading those closures consumed about 92% of the recorded CPU time. The menu now reads one current props source and dispatches overlay-owned controlled transitions while retaining the previous keyboard event, submenu/anchor watchers, focus, and cleanup behavior. No dependency patch, timeout increase, skip or assertion weakening is included.

The new behavioral regression uses the real menu/overlay and counts public input evaluation across actual open/close and direction changes. Original code fails with 919 input reads versus 55; the repaired source stays bounded. Independent full-file review approved tree `1919472d0a3c6b2722795ca7ed2f33abf2548ed7`. Focused tests passed 45/45; the original 17-file browser order passed 186/186 with the unmodified sidebar case completing in 716ms. UI-components types, scoped type-aware lint and formatting passed.

Published repair head: `e31300ede5bab8fcb0592fc0e0dd1707e94d61c6`. Its own hosted CI and normal review/security gates remain required. Earlier CI failures and local platform-specific gaps above are not relabeled green.

prs.title: fix(agents): deletion hangs when embedded runs do not stop
prs.body:
Fixes #172416

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: deleting an agent hangs forever when an embedded run cannot stop after cancellation.

## User Impact

Agent deletion uses the existing 15-second drain budget, identifies sessions whose runs are still active, and tells the operator to wait for those runs to end before retrying. Configuration and storage remain intact, and the pending deletion journal continues to refuse new work. Placement-read, identity-change, and other owner failures retain their actionable errors instead of being reported as stuck runs. Slow preparation reports the affected sessions and directs the operator to check placement availability. No configuration, schema, or public protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both unkeyed runs and ordinary session drains could wait without a deadline. Reuse the session lifecycle budget for individual runs and the combined agent drain, release captured run waiters on every exit, and remove the obsolete unbounded session-drain branch. The session lifecycle owner reports when placement preparation finishes, allowing the deadline response to distinguish slow preparation from active-work drainage. Only an actual bounded run wait failure receives stuck-run guidance; existing owner errors take precedence over a deadline, even while other drains remain pending. Accepted worker writes retain their cleanup custody, and storage retirement still requires successful drainage.

Deferred session drains carry deletion authority, agent/session identity, config, store paths, and the fixed budget. They revalidate the deletion owner and the drain's live lifetime before privileged effects; late successful drains release their resources. Captured run handles remain identity-bound, and journal ownership blocks storage relocation and new work, so captured config/paths identify the same deletion target. No detached storage deletion is introduced.

## Evidence

Exact-head [CI run 38650064827](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38650064827) completed with **failure** on `cf3df4f3c8964e35a834a80517229db18f8e873f`: 67 jobs passed; two test jobs and the aggregate CI gate failed. Production types, all test-type lanes, and lint passed. No CI reruns were requested.

| Failure | Evidence and classification |
| --- | --- |
| `server.hooks-admission.test.ts:325`: credential reload/replay returns HTTP 503 instead of 200, `Session event configuration changed` | **Inherited:** [PR job 116147258089](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38650064827/job/116147258089) matches [latest scheduled-main run 38648053570, job 116140128158](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38648053570/job/116140128158), head `f62dd8e0c29fc8acd3836e604da97a280e4fa053`, by exact test, assertion, and error. |
| `server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts:3575`: durable Control UI retry test fails in `finally` cleanup with `Cannot mutate session while competing work is in flight` | **Unclassified:** [PR job 116147257332](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38650064827/job/116147257332). No matching failure was found among the latest scheduled-main node jobs. The test, session-reset fixture, and SQLite deletion owner are unchanged against that main head; the failing chat/fixture path does not call the modified deletion drains. CI remains red; this is not claimed as a verified inherited failure. |

- PR CI is the test gate and covers Gateway handler/session regressions, typechecks, lint, and repository checks.
- New regression `preserves a pre-cancellation placement failure: %s` covers placement-read errors, identity changes, and aggregate errors through the real `agents.delete` handler. It checks the original error identity, no abort, preserved state, and released waiters.
- New fake-timer regression `reports slow placement preparation without canceling the run after timeout` holds placement preparation past the deadline, resumes it, and checks no late abort, reclaim, or storage retirement occurs.
- `agents.delete bounds a never-ending run (key: $sessionKey, abortable: $isAbortable)` covers keyed/unkeyed and non-abortable/no-op abort cases with fake timers. Existing `drains an active %s run before retirement and permits recreation without a deletion retry` covers normal settlement. The inventory-failure regression also retains an active run and verifies no cancellation began.
- Changed-file core oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: pass. Deslop complete. Prescribed isolated branch autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Production +65/-48 (net +17), tests +129/-5, docs +1/-0; the production growth retains original failures and distinguishes unfinished placement preparation from active-work timeouts.
- The error-masking and preparation-timeout P2 review findings are addressed: inventory and pre-cancellation placement failures retain the original errors; multiple failures include their actionable messages; still-pending preparation has its own timeout response.
- Live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof, local tests/typechecks, and negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases or live Gateway processes were created. Local test wall times are unavailable; CI supplies execution results.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the dependency check reporting retired internal exports and an intentionally path-launched developer MCP server as unused.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, rendering, public SDK contract, schema, or configuration changes. Active Lit/Solid renderers and PR-tooling consumers remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make unused internal helpers private, remove retired Lit-only adapters left behind by the Solid migration, and keep the transcript-rewrite test on the existing worker binding without weakening its assertions. The three helpers reached by the PR tooling import closure have only same-module callers; only their export modifiers change. Wrapper inventory, import-closure checks, baselines, and suppressions are unchanged.

The settings design guide now demonstrates the maintained Solid components and names only the two remaining Lit adapters, completing the documentation cutover identified in review.

The preparation schema, database-engine contract, pairing store, and companion pairing-store test are unchanged from the pre-PR main base. The launch-wire comparison was inconclusive (details below), so these cleanup hunks were withdrawn under the coordinator's explicit fallback rather than changing production behavior or a deadline.

The narrow Knip entry for `scripts/mcp-events-test-server.mjs` follows its documented invocation in `docs/automation/mcp-events.md`, `test/fixtures/mcp-events/README.md`, and the live driver. It makes the actual CLI and its imported fixtures reachable rather than suppressing unused-file reports.

The ClawHub unused-source graph was already removed on main by d7629d6f109. Foundation intent and follow-on consumers were checked: #171622 described the foundation, and open #171623 imports the deleted source module. This PR neither deletes more feature files nor restores that already-removed graph; the follow-on needs integration against current main.

## Evidence

- Existing focused proof: ClawHub packages 6/6, preparation identity 21/21, pairing publication 25/25, and four UI files 40/40 passed. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- The documented MCP CLI starts successfully via `node scripts/mcp-events-test-server.mjs --help` (exit 0, isolated state).
- Both unmodified cycle checks passed: zero runtime-value cycles and zero broader import cycles. All four targeted strict type projects (core, UI, changed tests, and Knip config), typed lint on all 14 changed files, and the 14-file format check passed with isolated state and bounded compiler parallelism.
- Local Knip was run once as requested; its result and the resulting orphan removal are recorded below. Full changed-file checks were not completed locally. Ordinary PR CI omits dependency scans, so no hosted Knip pass is claimed; the unmodified wrapper-inventory and import-closure checks must pass on the final head.
- Fresh local lint-suppression proof was 2 passed / 1 failed (83.49 seconds): actual 94 summary entries versus expected 92, with two unlisted entries in untouched `src/agents/mcp-event-request.ts` (`eslint/preserve-caught-error` and `unicorn/prefer-add-event-listener`, introduced by e210870acfe). The same test failed in scheduled main CI [38632684569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632684569). This diff adds no suppressions or baseline/allowlist changes. Exact-head CI attribution will be recorded before landing.

### Local Knip proof and the completed retirement

Ran the repository's `pnpm deadcode:report` once at exact head `1d1552fad01f61b4c8ba7bd784bc689449dbfd16`, with isolated state and a 30-minute command deadline. It completed with exit 1 and one finding: unused `ui/src/app/shell-layout-traits.ts`. This was caused by this PR: its last production consumer was the retired Lit settings adapters. The reporter and its Lit-only tests are now removed; repository source searches confirm no remaining caller. The shared layout owner, Solid reporter, and Solid-to-Lit bridge remain. The active Solid layout suite passed 6/6, and the boot inventory was regenerated through its synthetic cold/warm New Session and Chat capture owner. No ignore or synthetic entry hides the finding. Because the report is fail-fast, later all-export/export-wrapper phases did not run; a globally clean Knip result is not claimed.

Both unmodified closure test files passed locally, 21/21, including wrapper inventory, extracted dependency-context, and trusted-anchor handoff cases. The coordinator approved local Knip instead of a broad main-coverage dispatch; no dispatch or CI rerun was requested.

The orphan fix and the coordinator-directed scope withdrawal are committed in `12c9649371767ff9f71e87856242332e903dc01e`. Targeted UI types and the production UI build passed; startup/route budgets passed without baseline changes. Fresh independent review found no actionable findings. New exact-head CI for that follow-up is required before landing; the preceding run below is not its proof.

### Final-head hosted proof

[Run 38651565871, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38651565871) tested exact head `12c9649371767ff9f71e87856242332e903dc01e` at inspected merge checkout `e6d4a3ed815d6c83b2d87a83a1e8a93129f010e6` (main parent `d866ef3baf4b01eccba582db3547fa0b2843e3c9`) and completed with failure. Both unmodified closure suites passed: 18/18 eager-import-closure cases in job 116151939413, including PR wrapper inventory and old-anchor handoffs, and 3/3 wrapper-source-closure cases in job 116151939326. The touched transcript-rewrite suite passed all 11 cases in job 116151939252, preserving payload/generation read counts and lifecycle-fence assertions. Every other selected job passed, including security-fast, builds, types, lint, UI unit tests, eight other UI E2E shards, PostgreSQL conformance, baselines and guards. No rerun or dispatch was requested.

| Failed job | Cases | Classification and investigation |

| [checks-ui-e2e (2/9)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38651565871/job/116151938694) | `sidebar-settings.e2e.test.ts`: keeps Gateway connection fields editable by their visible labels (`system.info` wait, unchanged 29999 ms deadline); `session-link-reconnect.e2e.test.ts`: both interrupted-open variants (3 versus 1 and 4 versus 2 `sessions.resolve` requests) | Published table job 116158062248 says **new** against scheduled main 38648053570 / job 116140126105; selected scope was not compared. That older main job explicitly passed these same three cases. Independent source qualification: main commit 4f9637d3e58 (#172558), after that scheduled snapshot, added automatic session-link title resolution. Both request-count failures reproduce exactly at the CI main parent d866ef3baf4, with isolated state and one worker (2 failed / 1 passed among the three selected cases). The connection-settings case passes at both that main parent (4794 ms) and the exact tested PR merge (4945 ms). Its connection-page/read/poll owners, test controls, and both failing test files are byte-identical between main and the tested merge; removed Lit helpers have no caller on this flow, and the maintained Solid settings components are unchanged. Qualified as unrelated source-scope failures for the coordinator-authorized native exception, **not** relabeled green or claimed repaired. The one CI connection timeout remains unreproduced and root-cause-unproven; passing A/B replays are not a fix. No deadline, retry, assertion, fixture, suppression or baseline was changed. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38651565871/job/116158184700) | Aggregate | Failed solely because of the UI E2E job above. All selected jobs finished; security-fast passed independently. |

The comparison commands selected only those three failed cases with the repository Vitest wrapper and `--maxWorkers=1`; the head comparison selected only the connection case. Initial setup-only attempts did not reach tests (missing isolated workspace dependencies/browser); a private frozen install completed successfully before the actual comparisons. The three PR-import-closure helpers made private are at `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache.types.ts:257` (export introduced by 6f227907bf7), `database-engine/postgres-schema.ts:74` (e3b8a282764), and `git-root.ts:40` (ac3830b776a). Their same-module implementations/callers stay intact; both exact-head closure suites pass unweakened. The session operation-context constructor lost its last production consumers in e589d87d7b7; its remaining fixture now uses the maintained worker binding and retains all original assertions.

### Prior-head CI and launch-wire scope withdrawal

[Run 38646425608, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38646425608) tested head `1d1552fad01f61b4c8ba7bd784bc689449dbfd16`. ## What Problem This Solves

Toast messages still went through a Lit adapter although production callers provide strings or DOM nodes. Render them directly in Solid and use native icon names for provider feedback, removing the adapter and unused Lit content types.

The renderer memoizes message identity, then snapshots a fragment's actual child nodes for Solid to reconcile. This preserves a consumed fragment's recovery link and focus across unrelated options updates, and removes the old message when a second rich toast replaces it. The real sidebar hide action creates a fresh fragment for each notification; the regression reproduced stale old content before the correction, not a `NotFoundError`.

The PR also adds bounded, failure-only diagnostics around a plugin-help Settings-navigation timeout found in integration CI. It preserves the original actions, searchbox deadline, assertions, and error rethrow; it does not claim to repair that unresolved timeout.

The plain TypeScript controller continues to own dismissal deadlines, callbacks, queues, placement, and modal handoff. Host tags, CSS classes, message formatting, and lazy view loading remain unchanged. prs.title: feat(macos): launch the compiled OpenClaw runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app packages and launches a loose Bun installation, preventing it from using the compiled OpenClaw runtime. This cutover makes the compiled executable and its loose sidecar the sole packaged runtime.

Builds on #172384, now merged; this PR is no longer stacked. Related: #171489, #171755. **Do not land:** signed release proof is blocked by dangling links in the builder sidecar, and the release architecture decision is pending.

## User Impact

The app-hosted Gateway, Doctor, terminal CLI, services, and embedded helpers use the compiled executable. Packaging defaults to JIT; `OPENCLAW_MAC_RUNTIME_MODE=bytecode` selects bytecode. `BUILD_ARCHS=arm64` and `BUILD_ARCHS=x86_64` select a single architecture; universal requests fail early until the release architecture decision is resolved.

Packaging invokes the canonical builder, or accepts `OPENCLAW_MAC_RUNTIME_PREBUILT` only after verifying the exact source commit, mode, architecture, compiler revision/commit/SHA256 against the production pin, and executable/sidecar hashes. The canonical signer derives the executable's exact entitlements from the manifest, signs native sidecar files, refreshes hashes, then seals the app. The old macOS materializer and Bun-only verifier are removed; shared Tauri pruning remains intact.

Until the minimal-sidecar builder owns SQLite provisioning, app staging supplies exactly one signed `runtime/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` inside the sidecar. If the builder supplies it, staging reuses it. The verifier denies Homebrew/MacPorts SQLite access, checks Doctor selected the bundled extension-capable library, and exercises the real memory CLI to confirm sqlite-vec loaded from inside the sidecar. SQLite staging moves to the builder when its minimal-sidecar PR lands.

## Update and Rollback

Sparkle replaces the app bundle. First launch clones its complete payload into a new profile-local build directory, then selects it as current after validation. An existing loose seed remains the previous generation. The app rewrites only its managed terminal wrapper to execute `runtime/current/openclaw`, preserving the selected profile and SQLite path. Operator-managed commands remain untouched. Older unused seeds are collected only after Gateway health succeeds; current, previous, and live-process seeds remain retained.

Service installation recognizes the adjacent standalone manifest, probes `<executable> --version`, and writes `<executable> gateway ...` without a script argument. A fresh implicit install selects the running standalone executable even when host Node is available. Explicit runtime choices and saved pins retain precedence. Reinstalling an app-owned service replaces an old Bun-plus-script pin; reinstalling an older app can restore its Bun-plus-script command. Captured old CLI commands remain available for recovery. Runtime retention does not roll back database migrations or user state.

## Validation

- Independent branch review at `cd7ae2ab93124528cdb73fddfa953e2949644b7f`: clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The service-pin, implicit-selection, complete seed identity, and SQLite capability findings are fixed. Doctor now reports SQLite before its host-service identity guard, so isolated profiles receive the same library diagnostic without gaining host-service access; this owning-flow regression failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Service regressions fail before the fix. Compatibility suite: 108 tests, 48.87 s; layout/update suite: 71 tests, 55.20 s; final implicit-selection and sibling suite: 22 tests, 73.53 s including wrapper/import preparation. Scoped type-check and type-aware lint pass.
- Final packaging/provenance/signing suites: 95/95, 81.94 s; six wrong/missing compiler identity cases fail before the fix and reject afterward. Remaining packaging/portability suite: 109/109, 37.15 s.
- Earlier affected scripts: 191 cases covered, with two stale fixtures corrected and rerun. Final standalone staging/SQLite verification file: 15/15, 10.49 s including wrapper. Three invalid SQLite/vector capability cases were wrongly accepted by the old verifier and now fail. Direct argv, exact signing entitlements, SQLite placement/reuse, and complete seed identity have failing negative controls.
- Native app/test compilation passed at the current head with pinned Xcode/SDK (51.91 s). Previous isolated run passed 33/39 native tests; six seeding tests hit the existing ShellExecutor account-temp capture boundary before their product assertions. A signed-container rerun failed before test loading: macOS rejected the nested App Sandbox/seatbelt boundary in both orders. No isolation was weakened; the exact test container was cleaned after process retirement. The remaining six cases require the disposable macOS CI runner.
- Config docs, plugin inventory, protocol, native localization, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, formatting, and documentation-link checks pass. The unchanged integration base also fails the existing environment-name budget at 455/454; this PR adds no counted core/plugin variable and does not raise the budget.
- Exact-head production-pinned JIT build passed: full source build 24m30.6s, standalone build 593.39s. Release-config arm64 app and MLX builds passed (283.96 s and 106.28 s). Canonical signing completed, but strict app verification failed before publication with `No such file or directory`. Fresh-profile dashboard/setup, one turn, Doctor, restart/quit, upgrade, interleaved timings, and notarization-shaped ZIP remain blocked by the builder sidecar issue below. Big-sidecar timings are informational; performance acceptance applies when a minimal-sidecar artifact is available.

<details>
<summary>Exact-head JIT build command and builder manifest</summary>

Both commands ran under the shared mac build lock, with the same commit and build timestamp used for app packaging:

```sh
export GIT_COMMIT=cd7ae2ab93124528cdb73fddfa953e2949644b7f
export OPENCLAW_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2026-10-14T22:36:13.856Z
pnpm build
/usr/bin/arch -arm64 /private/tmp/oc-zc2-macfat/compiler/bin/bun scripts/build-bun-standalone.mjs /private/tmp/oc-zc2-macfat/builder-jit
```

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "mode": "jit",
  "target": {
    "platform": "darwin",
    "arch": "arm64"
  },
  "bun": {
    "version": "1.4.3",
    "revision": "1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715",
    "commit": "65d94e7156da4b6aca649dac5f19b8294b757570",
    "executableSha256": "0674b8787f56be23ee4dc662994d3b5efd97f1d625803fd1c83dbbca288bfece"
  },
  "openclaw": {
    "version": "2026.10.3",
    "commit": "cd7ae2ab93124528cdb73fddfa953e2949644b7f"
  },
  "executable": {
    "path": "openclaw",
    "sizeBytes": 914796418,
    "sha256": "28501df78e1cd5972e9cb714a7105e6ea11d41717ecd70054858e60f54a963d2"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "path": "runtime",
    "sizeBytes": 2712540492,
    "sha256": "a24375087442f1410b469ddd5f5dc003411907cbe47e86e572a98d33e48e4273",
    "fileCount": 91399,
    "symlinkCount": 5662
  },
  "embedded": {
    "workers": 118,
    "plugins": 167,
    "modules": 17686,
    "inlineWorkers": 6
  },
  "pruning": {
    "patterns": [
      "**/*.map",
      "**/*.d.ts",
      "**/*.d.mts",
      "**/*.d.cts"
    ],
    "removedFiles": 66037,
    "removedBytes": 482296961
  },
  "macos": {
    "hardenedRuntime": true,
    "entitlements": {
      "com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit": true,
      "com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation": true
    }
  }
```
