
</details>

## Builder blocker

The exact-head builder output contains three dangling workspace links:

```text
node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/openclaw-control-ui -> ../../../ui
node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@openclaw/solid-lint -> ../../../../tools/solid-lint
node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@openclaw/example-ai-chat -> ../../../../examples/ai-chat
```

A minimal Developer ID-signed app passes strict verification without these links. Adding the exact three paths and targets reproduces the release-app failure: signing exits 0, then `codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=4 <app>` exits 1 with `No such file or directory`. The canonical packager correctly refused to publish the failed app.

Builder-owner request: remove unused dangling workspace links, or materialize their required targets inside the sidecar, before calculating the manifest; regenerate the tree checksum/counts and cover the resulting payload with strict signed-app verification. No builder code or supplied builder payload was edited by this PR. A corrected same-commit artifact is required before the signed live campaign and notarization ZIP can proceed.

Production changes: +641/−1,318 lines; tests: +885/−1,844; docs: +83/−128, relative to the current integration base.

Release-note context: macOS app runtimes launch the compiled OpenClaw executable with a loose resource sidecar while retaining app-owned updates, profile-local seeding, and service migration.

prs.title: fix(claws): bind security review to artifacts and isolate status reads
prs.body:
## Publication Refresh: October 7

Layer 16/16. Previous: [#166800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166800) | Final layer. Published checkpoint: `9e653a8ed286`.

Full stack tip: [#166801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166801). Earlier local-ClawHub lifecycle evidence remains in [#163307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163307), tied to its recorded revision.

Automated branch repair is intentionally not enabled independently on these dependent branches: the inspected repair executor defaults to rebasing onto `main`, without a coordinated restack. The stack owner must reconcile the base and propagate any repairs before requesting merge readiness.

## What Problem This Solves

A clean component scan could override an aggregate ClawHub warning, security review could refer to different artifact bytes, and concurrent status reads could invalidate each other's plugin records.

## User Impact

Claw and managed-plugin installs honor the full registry verdict and exact selected artifact. Malicious or mismatched content stops before persistence; review-required content needs the appropriate acknowledgement. Concurrent status requests complete independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind security evidence to package identity, version, artifact kind, SHA-256, and npm integrity; require trust for Claw-managed official plugins; and give each status read its own plugin cache.

## Evidence

- Fresh before/after regression: copied the committed status tests into the parent `dc3d05c5aaea`. Two concurrency cases failed with `PLUGIN_CACHE_FACT_INVALIDATED`; the same three tests passed at `9e653a8ed286`.
- At `9e653a8ed286`, 100 focused backend tests passed on October 7 in 64.75 seconds, including aggregate malicious/review verdicts, exact artifact mismatch, managed plugin trust, final grant rechecks, manifest disclosure, and Remove authority.
- Combined-stack browser checks: 13/13 passed in 28.51 seconds. `git diff --check` passed for the full stack.
- The unchanged tip previously passed `pnpm check:changed`; this is not a claim of CI success on the current main merge result.

## Stack

This is the final follow-up layer after the existing draft stack ending at #163307. The publication preserves the 12 existing PRs and adds four layers for 45 previously local commits. None of these PRs is a standalone public launch.

## Publication Scope

Related: #163946. This is a draft layer in the Claws Labs stack. The stack retains its previously tested base and currently conflicts with newer main; this publication does not resolve that drift or authorize a release. Production ClawHub support, the compatible published Lobster artifact, official catalog security review, and RFC acceptance remain release gates. The local-source CLI and official-only launch scope are unchanged.

The curated live model lists still name `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2-chat`. ## Why This Change Was Made

Swap the curated ref for `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, which OpenRouter serves today, in the dynamic candidate list, the gateway explicit-ref unit expectations, and the long-context docs matrix. Unrelated `gpt-5.2-chat-latest` legacy-normalization and catalog fixtures are intentionally untouched.

## User Impact

None at runtime: test helpers, live-test expectations, and one docs row only.

- Before: `infer model run` against `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2-chat` returns the BYOK-only 404 above; a direct OpenRouter probe for `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` returns 200.

prs.body:
## Publication Refresh: October 7

Layer 13/16. Previous: [#163307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163307) | Next: [#166799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166799). Published checkpoint: `e05149e2b6b4`.

Full stack tip: [#166801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166801). Earlier local-ClawHub lifecycle evidence remains in [#163307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163307), tied to its recorded revision.

## What Problem This Solves

A Claw review could omit the exact grouped manifest, and installation could proceed despite host plugin policy or leave workspace ownership difficult to reconcile.

## User Impact

Users can inspect the verified manifest before Add or Update. Host-disabled, denied, or unlisted plugins stop before installation. Re-adding a removed Claw selects a fresh workspace, and verified exports preserve their package license.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind manifest disclosure and reviewed workspace facts to the accepted plan, retain the verified archive for later source checks, and use existing plugin and agent ownership checks before effects. This layer contains the previously local source, export, removal, policy, and manifest-review follow-ups.

## Evidence

- Combined stack at `9e653a8ed286`: 100 focused backend tests passed on October 7 in 64.75 seconds, including exact artifact resolution, manifest projection, host plugin policy, staged capability recheck, Remove authority, and approval request routing.
- Combined stack browser checks: 13/13 passed in 28.51 seconds across mobile through desktop, using the real built Control UI with a mocked Gateway. These are UI boundary checks, not a production registry or chat canary.
- Before screenshot: the prior local stack checkpoint `2ab926ce8c93` exposes action/capability review. After screenshot: the combined stack also exposes the exact grouped manifest. Captures use synthetic package data.
- The prior `pnpm check:changed` result applies to the unchanged combined tip; it was not rerun after a rebase because no new rebase was performed.

## Publication Scope

Related: #163946. This is a draft layer in the Claws Labs stack. The stack retains its previously tested base and currently conflicts with newer main; this publication does not resolve that drift or authorize a release. Production ClawHub support, the compatible published Lobster artifact, official catalog security review, and RFC acceptance remain release gates. The local-source CLI and official-only launch scope are unchanged.

![Before: review at the original stack checkpoint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d10c96de-9de6-40ee-bba3-9d4d7ef44ad8)

![After: exact manifest and artifact review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c60c02d-e417-4617-8c15-9993106a244e)

prs.title: fix: streaming a reply that mentions tool calls no longer stalls the Gateway event loop
prs.body:
Closes #172629

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a streamed reply that only *mentions* a tool call in prose locks the Gateway main thread for seconds, because the assistant trace-line scrub re-ran over the whole accumulated reply on every delta. Measured on `main` @ `d37f4756e4a`, streaming with 4-character deltas: **4.3 s** for an 83 KB reply, **18.9 s** at 166 KB, **85.1 s** at 333 KB (~4x per doubling, 858M-13.9B characters rescanned inside one stream).

## User Impact

Streaming a long technical answer no longer stalls every session and channel served by the same Gateway process. The cost lands on the single thread that also sends messages, maintains WebSockets, and dispatches tools, so the affected reply delayed unrelated sessions too; that was true for any reply whose text contains the substring "tool" or "function", which is most technical answers from this product's agents, and it latched on the first mention for the remainder of the reply. Replies are unchanged: a trace line that starts a line is still stripped, and prose that merely mentions a call is still preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

`assistantTraceTextFilter` used `activationTokens: ["tool", "function", "📊", "🛠", ...]`. `createActivatedProjector` latches permanently once a token appears anywhere in the stream and from then on runs `stripAssistantInternalTraceLines(input.text)` - the entire accumulated reply - for every delta, re-scanning every line plus the Markdown code-region parse each time.

The scrub removes whole lines, and only a line head can begin a trace line, so this filter now probes the shape that can actually begin one (indentation, an optional quote, an optional warning glyph, then a trace marker) and re-probes only the last appended line instead of the whole reply. Once a real trace head appears, the canonical transform still owns the result, matching the projector contract that token absence proves identity.

## Evidence

- New regression tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix. On `main`, the work-bound test reports `AssertionError: expected 1097695248 to be less than 749664` - 1,097,695,248 characters handed to the whole-line scrub for an 86 KB reply streamed in 4-character deltas, against a budget of 8x the reply length. With the fix the scrub is never invoked for that reply, and the 5 chunk-boundary cases (channel, warning, quoted, indented, plus a marker line that is *not* a trace line) match the batch sanitizer at every one of chunk sizes 1, 3, and 7.
- Focused tests: `assistant-visible-text.test.ts` 53 passed, `plain-tool-call-text.test.ts` 15 passed, `text-projection.test.ts` 13 passed (81 total, 0 failed).
- Per-stage measurement, same harness before and after (reply lengths in characters, `totalMs` for the whole 4-char-delta stream, then the trace stage's calls/characters/time):

```
doc                    len      totalMs before -> after    trace stage before -> after
phrase prose (tool/function call sentences)  82857   4570 -> 333    20704 /  858.3M / 4287 ms -> 0
                                          166357  20002 -> 2291   41579 / 3459.5M /18909 ms -> 0
                                          333357  90098 ->10754   83329 /13891.3M /85086 ms -> 0
plain prose (bare "function"/"tool")       67107    610 -> 166    16765 /  563.0M /  510 ms -> 0
fenced 1600-line code answer              107182  10789 ->10317   26787 / 1436.1M / 1233 ms -> 0
Markdown table (no trigger token)           4420    3.8 -> 5.0        0 /     0   /    0 ms -> 0
whole probe suite                         --     234.0 s -> 28.9 s
```

- Checks on this branch: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0; `check:max-lines-ratchet` OK (534 grandfathered suppressions); `oxlint` clean with the project config.
- Gaps: this checkout's partial `node_modules` cannot load the repo Vitest project matrix (`@solidjs/vite-plugin` is absent) or the config's `ui/**/*.tsx`-scoped Solid plugin, so the tests ran under Vitest 5.0.1 (the lockfile version) with a scoped config and oxlint ran with that one UI-scoped override omitted; `tsgo:core:test` was not run. `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` and the chained `OPENCLAW_*` env-var-count budget are red on `main` for unrelated `ui/src/**` files (700-line caps, 455 vs 454 vars) and were not touched here.

Related: same file and class as the landed #172340 / #172470, and consistent with campaign #145679.

Residual, deliberately not touched: `plainToolCallTextFilter` still latches on `{`, so fenced code answers keep a separate per-delta whole-reply parse (the `fenced 1600-line code answer` row above improves only by the trace stage's share). That is a different defect in a file with open work (#172440), so it stays out of this PR.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): recover recorded foreground allocations
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156269

Stack 7/19. Depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165381.

## What Problem This Solves

Crashed foreground allocations leave recorded receipts that startup must reconcile safely; generic deletion or reuse must not mutate allocations still owned by foreground custody.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the recorded-receipt recovery consumer and exact allocation guards before physical mutation, preserving fail-closed cleanup uncertainty.

## User Impact

Eligible crashed receipts can be retired at startup. Uncertain allocations stay quarantined instead of being reused or force-removed.

## Evidence

- Source-reviewed, including independent review; `git diff --check` passed. AI-assisted changes.
- Authored regression coverage: Coverage includes recorded recovery, exact identity, quiescence, and Docker/Podman reuse and removal guards.
- Pending on this head: focused tests, type/lint checks, and required build validation; canonical config hash/count generation for the changed schema. Existing results from earlier stack heads are not claimed as exact-head proof.

Production LOC: +570/-21 (net +549); tests/helpers: +708/-1.

Published for review with validation pending. No merge, auto-merge, or deployment is requested.

Follow-up: exact-authority operator reconciliation for quarantined foreground allocations; this slice does not provide that recovery command.

prs.title: perf: reduce retained cron history index work
prs.body:
## Landing status

**Not landed.** The final scheduled attempt in the October 14, 17:46:25–23:46:25 UTC retry window could not obtain immediately available Testbox capacity. Current pushed head: `e3f8bdcd0f43bd1479422938912e58b5b9f35eb7`. The published-driver × candidate update cell and Knip export scan remain unproven; neither gate is waived. Eleven attempts were made: ten reached queued capacity and were canceled, and one stopped before allocation for a main conflict. No remote build, update, Knip, or diagnostic command ran. All task leases are stopped and campaign tokens released. Recovery claims and the protected first-attempt staging capsule are retained.

## What Problem This Solves

Cron history reads still sort retained task records by creation time using indexes inherited from the retired Tasks subsystem. On a synthetic state database with 70,000 task rows, including 10,000 cron rows and a 2,000-row job, replacing eleven nonunique indexes with three indexes aligned to current Cron and Doctor readers reduced all-cron native process CPU by 39%.

## User Impact

State schema 23 keeps one global runtime/run lookup index and two partial cron indexes for creation-time ordering, with and without a source ID. It preserves table rows, rowids, constraints, triggers, history ordering, retention and durability. Exact-name index retirement belongs to one state schema migration; the agent schema remains unchanged. No runtime read, write, authority check or worker request is removed.

## Evidence

| Query plan | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All Cron history | `idx_task_runs_runtime_status` + temporary ORDER BY B-tree | `idx_task_runs_cron_runtime_order`, no temporary sort |
| Per-job Cron history | `idx_task_runs_runtime_source_ended` + temporary ORDER BY B-tree | `idx_task_runs_cron_source_order`, no temporary sort |
| Doctor runtime/run lookup | `idx_task_runs_run_id` | `idx_task_runs_runtime_run` |

The read-only Team aggregate census found 71,370 retained task rows, 7,312 cron rows across 112 jobs, and 2,059 rows in the largest job; its all-cron plan used the same temporary ORDER BY sort. The synthetic 70,000/10,000/2,000 fixture reflects those cardinalities.

Measured relative local results on a heavily loaded Mac, using matched bounded ANALYZE on both sides and alternating samples. CPU includes native row conversion and process runtime overhead; these are not Gateway latency claims.

| Operation | Baseline CPU p50 / p95 (ms) | Candidate CPU p50 / p95 (ms) | p50 change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All cron history, 10,000 rows | 86.813 / 167.951 | 52.887 / 86.527 | -39.1% |
| Largest job history, 2,000 rows | 3.521 / 6.534 | 3.849 / 6.779 | +9.3% (+0.328 ms) |
| Doctor inspection, 200 results | 3.641 / 6.095 | 3.683 / 5.714 | +1.2% |
| Insert, 100 rows | 5.796 / 14.929 | 5.010 / 8.620 | -13.6% |
| Terminal update, 100 rows | 1.991 / 2.563 | 1.522 / 4.493 | -23.6% |
| Delete, 100 rows | 4.281 / 7.417 | 3.549 / 5.869 | -17.1% |
| Prune delete, 500 IDs | 11.163 / 13.425 | 9.003 / 9.928 | -19.4% |
| Recovery normalization, 100 rows | 3.108 / 10.061 | 2.010 / 8.277 | -35.3% |

All-cron CPU improved in 28/30 alternating pairs; per-job CPU improved in 15/30, so the small per-job tradeoff remains uncertain. Tiny keyed reads were 0.003–0.021 ms slower in median, except the largest-job exact lookup (+0.001 ms). Both cron history plans remove USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY. Doctor keeps indexed runtime/run lookup. Every read digest and post-write result matched; all five measured write classes pass the 5% limit by median CPU. Terminal-update p95 rose by 1.93 ms despite its lower median; this run does not establish lower tail latency. Recovery normalization used the actual owner planner and its nine-column update, including changed creation timestamps, in twelve alternating batches. It preserved 1,200 updated rows per side and 70,001 untouched rows; WAL length fell from 3,312,512 to 2,163,032 bytes.

DDL plus bounded ANALYZE on this database took 674.611 ms median process CPU / 8.958 s diagnostic wall time across three samples, producing 10.64 MB WAL. This excludes backup, admission and post-DDL integrity checks. Three fresh-process migrations through the public state owner on a 171.39 MiB synthetic DB with 70,000 retained task rows took 28.517 s [23.673–33.107] owner-open wall time and 2.537 s [2.484–2.675] process CPU; asynchronous close took 0.830 s [0.723–0.972] wall time. Every sample preserved all task bytes, rowids, table definitions and existing table counts, and verified exact 11→3 index replacement and schema publication. Owner timing includes unsealed admission and selected integrity work but excludes the full startup/Doctor backup pipeline; these are overloaded-local diagnostics, not Team upgrade times.

Team-scale upgrade cost: the coordinator's newer read-only 38 GB snapshot evidence reports 514 s for agent integrity checking plus roughly 36 s for a full copy—about nine minutes for those startup components. This is not an end-to-end candidate upgrade benchmark: the selected backup path can add validation and hash work, and the state migration is measured separately above. The state snapshot's integrity check took 11.982 s. The measured live state and agent sizes imply roughly 44.711 GB retained backup capacity before staging/WAL. A standalone startup backup can include admitted agents even for a state-only bump; verified updater backup coverage may avoid a second group. Full candidate upgrade duration remains unmeasured; durability and backup semantics are unchanged. Main now contains table-scoped backup infrastructure, but its production scope declarations are empty and this version 23 migration retains the full-backup path.

PostgreSQL forward DDL is generated from the same retirement list and translated canonical indexes, preserving ASC NULLS FIRST. Existing PostgreSQL conformance checks the upgraded catalog against fresh schema and verifies retained synthetic payloads and local indexes. This is forward-DDL readiness; shared-state PostgreSQL runtime enablement remains with its owner. No R9 timestamp specification was received, and no measured agent index candidate justifies an agent bump.

On the pre-integration candidate, `pnpm db:postgres:gen` and `pnpm db:postgres:check` passed with no new portability omissions (translated state indexes 296 → 288). No retained `INDEXED BY` / `engineIndexHint` reference names a retired index. Both allowed Codex autoreview rounds completed with no accepted P0–P2 findings. Formatting, basic lint and diff checks passed.

CI integration repairs update schema inventories and migration descriptions, remove a test trigger refused by schema admission, and align Doctor and provider fixtures with their owners. The earlier Cron fixture expectation change was reverted: the original assertions preserve a future persisted retry despite stale finalized history. The separate runtime repair remains with the Cron owner. Workspace tests now use the real prompt-report builder and initialize the mock session's prompt and tool allowlist from constructor options, as the SDK does; provenance and healthy-tool-only assertions remain intact. These repairs change tests and bookkeeping, not runtime policy.

Integrated candidate `b3b7e9ab5114cb79f43be5e682761b905f24b5e9` merges main `cff88c2d21d85ff05d812f893a9038f732f5f739`, retaining both the generated PostgreSQL runtime module and the v22-to-v23 forward DDL, their wrapper inventory entries, and both schema-documentation entries. `pnpm db:postgres:gen` passed and regenerated its runtime catalog. [Integrated CI run 38609403566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38609403566) tested merge `a4099095e3532007a3d4da78c7e9eca417c1d67f` against main `6ee0ae0398fea0605269aa6726606c67d6e276ee`: all 14 changed test files executed successfully (201 passing case lines), including the generator's 19 cases, index migration, missing-table admission, ownership, and Doctor coverage. Types, lint, source contracts, and Madge passed. T1 live calls remained 223 → 223 globally (area 0 → 0); changed-file dialect groups remained mechanical 0 → 0, design 19 → 19, and engine maintenance 16 → 16. `pnpm db:postgres:check` also passed locally on the integrated candidate, including the generator tests and canonical/workboard verification. Knip remains pending: the parallel local scan and a sequential production scan both hit their unchanged 600-second deadlines without findings. The remaining local scans were canceled after the repeated timeout; the same required scan was included on the requested update-cell lease, but no capacity was granted.

Prior follow-up `eafa2da92a648e0318d0af4e7114fbb5f8f783c9` additionally repairs one PostgreSQL conformance fixture: it now injects `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION + 1` instead of hard-coding 23, which this migration makes valid. The refusal assertion is unchanged. Formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks passed; [CI run 38616072699](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38616072699) passed PostgreSQL conformance, including the repaired test (444 passing cases and 38 skipped across its three shards). All 24 selected static jobs passed, including production/test types, core/extension lint, source contracts, Madge, and the unchanged T1/dialect ratchets. All 15 changed test files have passing evidence: this fresh PostgreSQL pass plus 14 reused passes whose file blobs are identical. This follow-up changes only that test.

Prior combined head `234fb5b4ddee1ef47e0fe589143524c60840df51` merges main `64ae5024332` to resolve the schema-metadata conflict after the independent agent-schema migration landed. The only manual conflict resolution keeps state schema 23 and agent schema 27. The frozen install and PostgreSQL regeneration passed; regeneration produced no further changes, and diff checks passed. Migration scope declarations remain empty, so this migration keeps full-backup coverage. Fresh [CI run 38634965580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38634965580) passed the selected types, lint, source-contract, architecture-guard, and baseline-ratchet jobs. PostgreSQL conformance passed on merge `5a8adc23` of this exact candidate and main `64ae5024332`: 450 passed and 38 skipped, including the PostgreSQL test file changed by the main integration. The other 14 changed test-file blobs remain identical to their earlier passing evidence. Eight Node jobs failed: memory startup catch-up, pinned auth profile selection, an agent outbox-schema fixture mismatch, worker-launch cleanup, Doctor memory timeout, Cron read timeout/admission/port failures, a different bounded-continuity assertion, and missing archive-worker replies. The failing test files are unchanged by this PR relative to merged main; that fact alone does not prove inheritance. A comparison with the latest completed scheduled main run `38632684569` at `960eacc5cdf0` proves the board v14 migration failure inherited: [main job 116088558318](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632684569/job/116088558318) has the same `:823:69` assertion and `context_engine_turn_outbox` column/index mismatch. The other seven groups have no matching signature in that main run. The archive deletion-generation test passed in main job `116088558314`; its different idle-worker failure does not establish inheritance. Those seven groups remain unattributed. No changed-file product regression has been established. The published-driver update cell and Knip scan remain pending on this combined head.

Current head `e3f8bdcd0f43bd1479422938912e58b5b9f35eb7` merges main `4f9637d3e581` after another merge conflict. The only manual resolution preserves main's wording updates in the state-schema history table and this migration's schema-23 row. The generator and its test file are unchanged from the prior candidate. PostgreSQL regeneration passed without generated changes; formatting and diff checks passed. The package lockfile is unchanged. Fresh [combined-head CI run 38649886001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38649886001) passed the selected production/test types, lint, source-contract/export-collision, architecture, and T1/dialect-ratchet gates, plus PostgreSQL conformance. The architecture job actually ran Madge and reported zero cycles. The live static/PostgreSQL filter selected 18 successful jobs; this is not a full-CI green claim. Knip was not selected and remains pending with the published-driver update cell. Scope declarations remain empty, and full-backup coverage is retained.

The previous candidate CI run [38556474167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38556474167) passed production/test types, TypeScript lint, source/architecture checks, baseline ratchets, PostgreSQL conformance, and applicable security checks. This is prior-head evidence, not proof for the integrated candidate. Its Android formatting failure matched [scheduled main job 115829705578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38557255626/job/115829705578), at the same file, lines, and rules.

Classification of the eight earlier behavioral failure groups against integrated main:

| Previous failure group | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| Update SIGINT progress/compensation | Main repair `7b8a989efb2` observes worker commands before transfer detaches their buffers. |
| Reef outbound | Same transferred-buffer observer repair. |
| Memory publication generation | Same observer repair, plus subsequent worker typing fixes. |
| Cron startup persisted retry | Main repair `418f32e2468` (#171775) restores future persisted retry precedence over finalized history. |
| Telegram command-menu/emoji Gateway timeouts | Unattributed; no matching failure in the inspected main schedules. |
| Codex side-question lost acknowledgement | Unattributed; no matching main failure evidence. |
| Codex bounded assistant continuity | Unattributed; no matching main failure evidence. |
| MXC backend retirement | Unattributed; no matching main failure evidence. |

The landing pass also addresses the existing missing-table review finding: schema 22 is now registered with the migration-admission assertions before canonical DDL runs. Runtime open and Doctor therefore retain their existing refusal for a missing persistent table instead of silently recreating it empty during the 22-to-23 upgrade. The existing missing-table regression now covers both schema 22 and current schema. No new admission mechanism or runtime query is added. A local pre-fix replay was canceled after worker-artifact preparation did not reach test execution; this supplies no red/green claim. Integrated-head CI passed the extended regression and all affected generator/index-migration tests.

The main search covered 11 failed Node job logs across runs `38590548763`, `38581484814`, and `38572535410`. A negative search does not establish inheritance or passing coverage. The integrated run passed all changed tests but was not fully green; no full-green claim is made.

The native-hook pressure shard passed on prior head `a2889bd406678`, but its earlier coverage gap remains a follow-up: the prior log contained 20 successful synthetic tool outputs and 18 matching policy invocations/callbacks. Missing hook-completion diagnostics leave the cause unknown; later deny-mode assertions were not reached, so this is not proof of denied-command bypass or schema-caused regression. A prior Doctor null-child-status failure reproduced on main. Focused local replays that stalled in source/worker preparation were stopped without claiming a test result.

**Pending gate: published-driver × candidate update cell.** The authorized retry window was 17:46:25–23:46:25 UTC on October 14. Attempt 1 froze candidate `b3b7e9ab` but received queued Testbox capacity and was canceled immediately; no build, package, or update test ran. The provider confirms the allocation stopped and the campaign slot is released. The test-only follow-up can reuse an earlier passing cell under the landing policy. Attempt 2 started at 19:03 UTC on `eafa2da9`, then also received queued provider capacity after source preparation. It was canceled before any build/update command; [its workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38624324151) is completed/canceled, its lease stopped, its token released, and its staging removed by the wrapper. prs.title: feat: restore saved questions before serving question reads
prs.body:
Related: #167266. Parent: #171682. Split from #168399; default tool handoff follows this prerequisite.

## What Problem This Solves

Saved questions and owed answers must be restored before question reads can conclude that custody is absent after a Gateway restart.

## User Impact

Startup restores pending questions and schedules owed continuations with the existing native turn owner. Trusted callers may explicitly request durable RPC custody; default ask_user handoff is enabled by the next slice. Failed source admission remains visible while healthy sibling stores recover.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire durable registration and continuation scheduling together, await recovery for question reads, and preserve delayed sidecar admission without deadlocking initial startup. Current-Gateway lifetimes own discovery and write-only receipt repair; claimed execution is never automatically repeated.

No new database migration or retention policy in this slice. The schema/design acceptance and stopped-writer upgrade contract are owned by #168917. The original 900-second default and 3,600-second ceiling remain unchanged; this does not close the issue's multi-day requirement.

## Evidence

- 22 native recovery, refusal, and read-readiness cases passed with identical recovery source on cleaned full candidate ca3b5dc: 52.61 seconds Vitest, 64.75 seconds native wrapper. Covers unavailable stores, delayed admission/rediscovery, healthy siblings, close, and missing-custody reads.
- Six native Gateway process/adapter flows passed at cleanup checkpoint 5b278128 (766.72 seconds wrapper), including restart/busy-lane continuation and queued linked-principal unlink/reassignment with no forbidden provider/tool/delivery effect. This is checkpoint-bound composition proof, not exact-head CI or authenticated live Telegram.
- Fresh production types, targeted typed lint, and formatting passed. Independent P0–P2 autoreview found zero actionable findings (supplied patch/dependency scope).

prs.title: fix(ios): task list has no refresh, clear or dismiss buttons, unlike the web chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the task list (progress card) in the native iOS and macOS chat can only be collapsed. The web chat's card also has refresh, clear and dismiss, so on a phone a finished or stale task list stays above the composer with no way to remove or update it.

## User Impact

User impact: the native task list now offers the web chat's three actions.

- **Refresh** asks the agent to bring the list up to date. It is offered only when the Gateway advertises `progressCard.refresh`, and the header shows a spinner until a new card arrives.
- **Clear** removes the saved list for every viewer of the session. As on the web, there is no confirmation step.
- **Dismiss** hides the list on this device until the list changes.

Where they are:

- **macOS:** buttons in the header, in the web's order: refresh, clear, dismiss, collapse.
- **iPhone and iPad:** the header keeps only the collapse caret. A long press on the card opens the system context menu with Refresh plan, Dismiss plan and Clear saved plan for everyone. This is the menu message rows already use, so the press timing and the lift are the system's. VoiceOver and Switch Control reach the same three actions as custom actions on the header, without the long press.

## Why This Change Was Made

The web card (`ui/src/components/session-progress-card.ts`) offers "Refresh task progress", "Clear saved progress for everyone" and "Dismiss progress card". The native card (`ChatProgressCard.swift`) had one control: the whole header toggled collapse.

- **Touch presentation.** The header is one line tall. A first version of this PR put the three icons in it on every platform. On a phone they sit close together and take room from the step title, and a variant with larger touch areas made the bin easy to hit by accident. The actions keep their function and move behind a long press, as the app already does for message actions. A pointer can aim at small controls, so macOS keeps them.
- **The menu is on the whole card.** On the header alone, the system lifted the header out of the card and left the body behind.
- **The card follows the keyboard.** The keyboard hides when a context menu opens, and the views above it move down. A message row's lifted copy moves with them, because it sits in the transcript's scroll view. The card had no scroll container of its own, so its copy stayed where the press began, over the transcript. The card now sits in a scroll view that never scrolls (`ChatProgressCardMenuAnchor`), and its copy follows as a message row's does.
- **Clear** sends `progressCard.put` without a card and with the shown card's revision as `expectedRevision`, so it cannot remove a card newer than the one on screen. The card is then read again, because the change event can be lost across a reconnect.
- **Refresh** consumes the Gateway’s existing accepted receipt (run ID and authoritative revision). The intent keeps its retry key until acceptance and a saved card strictly newer than that baseline; a read before the acknowledgement cannot retire it. Uncertain failures retry the same intent and reread saved state; an explicit terminal answer retires the key. No extra polling is added. This prevents a stale displayed revision from mistaking an already-saved card for refresh completion.
- **Dismissal** is view state, kept per card, so dismissing the list in one chat does not bring back a list dismissed in another.
- **macOS: requests stay with the window's Gateway.** The macOS transport's card requests (`get`, clear, refresh) share one helper, `progressCardRequest` in `WebChatSwiftUI.swift`. It now calls the transport's existing `requireCurrentOutboxGateway()` before it captures the socket and again before it sends, as `sendMessage` and `synthesizeSpeech` do. A window pinned to one Gateway no longer sends a clear or a refresh to another Gateway that became current in the meantime; the request fails as not dispatched.
- The iOS and macOS transports gain the two requests through the same route and capability checks as the existing card fetch.

## Evidence

**Current candidate:** 4179ea3f6a57a7319079a222f272e021b99d4c1c, tree1bafe982677f435fc446ccb4f330696a4a25f8e6, signedG. Direct parent022ef721; the provenance correction is a normal fast-forward with no ancestry replacement. Incoming743d24e and integrated-maincc397809 ancestry/credits are preserved.

Full native acceptance remains held: identity admission failed before the cancellation prerequisite, and the new4179 error-provenance correction has not yet run natively.** The completed results below are022 evidence, not new4179 executions or the earlier f9 HOLD bundle. | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/59b4e59063474576f917a394cc881b607f1ceba7/ios-task-list/iphone-card-3.png" width="200" alt="iPhone chat on this branch: the task list above the composer shows its current step, the count 1/3 and a collapse chevron"> | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/59b4e59063474576f917a394cc881b607f1ceba7/ios-task-list/iphone-menu-3.png" width="200" alt="iPhone chat after a long press on the task list: a system menu lists Refresh plan, Dismiss plan and Clear saved plan for everyone"> | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/59b4e59063474576f917a394cc881b607f1ceba7/ios-task-list/iphone-dismissed-3.png" width="200" alt="iPhone chat after Dismiss plan: no task list above the composer"> | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/59b4e59063474576f917a394cc881b607f1ceba7/ios-task-list/ipad-menu-3.png" width="260" alt="iPad chat after a long press on the task list: the same three menu actions"> |

**Red on main, green on this branch.**

- On `main` with only the fixture and the UI test applied, the test finds the card, presses it, and fails: `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift:831: XCTAssertTrue failed - Task list menu has no refresh action`.
- On this branch it passes on iPhone and iPad: the header has none of the three buttons, a long press offers the three actions, and Dismiss plan removes the card.

**macOS production-transport proof** (native Swift tests, synthetic loopback servers, not a live Gateway deployment).

The new tests in [`MacProgressCardTransportTests.swift`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/743d24e11ac0ee76a57bbc47260f9148131fc8a3/apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/MacProgressCardTransportTests.swift) run the real `MacGatewayChatTransport.progressCardRequest → GatewayConnection → GatewayChannelActor → URLSessionWebSocketTask` path. Two Network.framework WebSocket listeners represent Gateways A and B; there is no injected or mocked socket. The pin is read from an isolated temporary config, changed from A to B during the test. A DEBUG-only test flag lets the isolated connection use the same primary-runtime pin check; the shared singleton intentionally refuses networking in test processes. Device identity and TLS are not exercised.

- `allowed clear and refresh reach pinned gateway` checks actual frames at A: `progressCard.put` carries `sessionKey=global, agentId=research, expectedRevision=3` (no card); `progressCard.refresh` carries `sessionKey=global, agentId=research, idempotencyKey=refresh-1`. B receives zero card frames.
- `replaced gateway rejects card before network IO` runs clear and refresh at three boundaries: before capture; after capture while capability validation is suspended; and after the final pin check while the connection owner's lease validation is suspended. The last two use the existing endpoint-provider suspension point and lease owner, not a sleep. Every stale action returns `notDispatched`. The test waits for terminal observations on the original sockets before checking zero card frames on both servers.
- **Red control:** removing both card-request pin checks makes clear and refresh succeed on already-connected B before capture: each sends one card frame to B. Four assertions fail (missing rejection plus nonempty B frames for each action). The after-capture cases remain rejected by the existing captured-lease guard, so this red control does not establish that the second pin check is independently necessary.
- **Green:** all 78 tests in 4 suites pass (14.333 seconds), covering the new file plus `MacGatewayChatTransportMappingTests` and `GatewayConnectionControlTests`. SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint: 0 violations.

Redacted trace from the final tested patch:

```text
RED rc=1; 2 tests / 1 suite failed with 4 expected issues
clear   before-capture rejectedBeforeDispatch=false; A card frames=0; B card frames=1
refresh before-capture rejectedBeforeDispatch=false; A card frames=0; B card frames=1
GREEN rc=0; 78 tests / 4 suites passed
allowed A progressCard.put     sessionKey=global agentId=research expectedRevision=3; B frames=0
allowed A progressCard.refresh sessionKey=global agentId=research idempotencyKey=refresh-1; B frames=0
clear   before-capture / after-capture / after-pin-check: rejected; A/B card frames=0
refresh before-capture / after-capture / after-pin-check: rejected; A/B card frames=0
original sockets closed before zero-frame assertions
```

Attribution: the applied proof patch SHA-256 is `c1d13af94b2611655d6ec5e817be02e6b8137b6a33206268385a425c160b20d0`, byte-identical to the committed macOS proof diff on the previously reviewed `c2e7ed023d4` tree. The full prior PR patch was applied first on `a51a76bda63`; the final published commit has the identical source tree. This run includes the independent review corrections (cancellation forwarding, original-socket closure observations, and traces reporting actual outcomes/counts).

The job printed `TREE_RESTORED 1` because its cleanup removed new untracked files only under `apps/macos`, leaving the prior PR's new shared-kit test `ChatViewModelProgressCardActionTests.swift`. A separate disposable checkout reproduced that exact one-file residue, proved every tracked/index file equal to the baseline, and reached clean status after removing only that fixture file. This was a cleanup-scope issue, not a leftover production source edit; a later inspection also found the shared evidence checkout clean.

The original mapping test is retained as request-shape/early-rejection coverage. The new loopback tests supersede its missing after-capture and allowed primary-runtime pin coverage.

**View-model tests** (file `ChatViewModelProgressCardActionTests.swift`), all passing on this branch:

- `clearing the saved card sends the shown revision and removes the card`
- `a failed clear keeps the card and reports the failure`
- `refresh sends one request while pending and again after the card changes`
- `a refresh retried after a failure repeats its key` (also: the retry reads a newer saved card whose change event never arrived)
- `a refresh the gateway ended is not replayed by the next tap`
- `refresh is offered only when the gateway advertises it`

The tests wait on signals, not on a timer: view-model state through the repository's `waitForObservedState`, and requests through an arrival stream on the test transport. As with other users of that helper, a regression that never produces the awaited state leaves the test waiting until the run is stopped, not failing on an assertion.

These call functions that do not exist on `main`, so their red was shown by breaking the source instead. That was done while the tests still waited with a deadline: with one fault per behavior, each test failed on its own assertion. With the signal waits now in the commit, the same faults make the affected tests wait forever instead; one such run was observed and stopped after 15 minutes. The assertions themselves are unchanged.

An existing request test gained a case for the two request shapes (`clearing and refreshing a progress card send the target and one extra field`).

Shared kit suite: 2295 tests in 195 suites passed. SwiftFormat lint and strict SwiftLint are clean on the changed source files and the changed kit and macOS test files. SwiftFormat reports one long line in the UI test file that is already on `main`. The macOS app target compiles (`swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw`).

**On an iPhone.**

- *Against a real Gateway, with the first version of this PR (buttons in the header).* Refresh: the Gateway started a refresh run for the session and finished it 25 seconds later; the agent's turn wrote a new revision of the card. Clear: the card disappeared on the phone, and the app's next read of the card returned an empty one. Gateway log for that minute (UTC; connection id shortened, session key removed):

  ```
  19:20:25 ⇄ res ✓ progressCard.get 1429ms bytes=1307 conn=1b1b…615a
  19:20:55 session turn created: runId=progress-card-refresh:376ac4db…
  19:21:20 message processed: messageId=progress-card-refresh:376ac4db…
  19:22:17 ⇄ res ✓ progressCard.get 887ms bytes=92 conn=1b1b…615a
  ```

  The log has no result line for the `progressCard.refresh` and `progressCard.put` requests themselves in that window, so by itself it does not name the client that sent them; the two presses were made on the phone. The view-model and transport code behind the actions is the same in this version.
- *The long-press menu*, on device builds that carry this card code together with unmerged changes. The menu opened with the system's timing and lift. With the keyboard up and no scroll container, the lifted card stayed mid-screen while the transcript moved down; with the container, it moved with the screen, as a message row did in the same build. No Gateway log was taken from these builds.

**The macOS app, launched** (first version of this PR; the macOS header is unchanged since). The debug product of the macOS app was started with upstream's DEBUG argument `--swarm-chat-fixture`, which opens the real native chat window on a fixture transport with no Gateway. An evidence-only patch (not in this PR) makes that fixture return the same synthetic three-step card as the iOS fixture. Window-only captures, unedited:

| macOS, main | macOS, this branch |
|---|---|
| <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/8d8e71aeabf846fb1323f2412ba88990dca39cfb/ios-task-list/mac-before.png" width="420" alt="macOS chat window on main: the task list header shows its current step, the count 1/3 and a collapse chevron"> | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/8d8e71aeabf846fb1323f2412ba88990dca39cfb/ios-task-list/mac-after.png" width="420" alt="macOS chat window on this branch: the task list header shows the count 1/3 followed by refresh, bin, X and chevron buttons"> |

The app ran inside an OS sandbox with networking denied, so these captures show the shared card in the macOS window and nothing more: no button was pressed.

A final independent Codex re-review found no actionable defects in the new transport tests or DEBUG seam after the cancellation and socket-observation corrections. Earlier independent review passes found defects that are fixed in the commit: a refresh retry used a new key each time, dismissal was one slot for the whole view, and (first ClawSweeper review) the key was kept after a terminal answer and a retry did not read the saved card.

**Not covered:**

- The UI test does not choose Refresh or Clear from the menu, and neither request ran against a real Gateway from the simulator or from the long-press builds. Their behavior rests on the view-model tests, the request test and the device run with the first version.
- The keyboard case (menu opened while the keyboard is up) has no automated test; it was checked by hand on a phone.
- The VoiceOver custom actions were not exercised with VoiceOver.
- macOS authority proof uses real native client networking against synthetic loopback protocol responses, not a deployed Gateway. It establishes allowed request frames and stale-action rejection before card-request I/O; it does not prove durable card removal or refresh-worker execution on a live macOS Gateway. Replacement is a controlled config/endpoint change, not a same-address physical-socket reconnect. TLS, device authentication, and unpinned transports (for example the quick-chat reply binding) are out of scope.
- A dismissed card returning when its content changes is not tested; the rule is view state.
- macOS UI: no header button was pressed in the launched app against a Gateway. The transport tests send the requests over loopback; the macOS captures remain collapsed, dark appearance only.
- Not tested: the error text when refresh fails at the view level, the 120-second give-up, the spinner.

AI-assisted (Claude and OpenAI).

</details>

prs.title: fix: preserve updater and gateway observation lifetimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime replacement could retire the updater's own code before recovery capture finished, causing a late `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and rollback.

## User Impact

Updates keep recovery code and admitted worker work alive until their owners finish. Gateway shutdown stops passive observers promptly while joining work already admitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backup owners now load before replacement, and the shared worker-pool factory captures worker code before detached work can lose its generation. A matching native owner drains admitted domain work, retires all its pools, then joins its supervisor and broker before releasing code. This includes pools created during the drain and owners without custom pool cleanup; independently owned native siblings retain their behavior.

CI exposed two related lifecycle defects. A credential-only refresh could publish an unchanged configuration epoch and reject an already-admitted hook; the configuration owner now permits reuse only when recorded runtime/source values and detached provenance still match. Generic publication invalidation and the hook's exact publication fence remain intact. Passive observations stop at request-entry closure while accepted work remains joined by its connection owner. Main's scheduler fence is preserved through the same close handler, and execution retirement and approval-listener ordering remain unchanged.

The repair also removes unused internal exports and obsolete diff wrappers, keeps meaningful pairing assertions through the existing state reader, and renames a private snapshot-read constant incorrectly counted as an environment variable. No configuration, schema, migration, storage representation, protocol, or public SDK contract is added. Existing main's Users-label fixture repair from Vincent Koc is preserved. The sidebar keyboard fixture now parks inherited pointer input before mounting hover controls, preventing a separate rail tooltip from polluting the picker occlusion trace.

The session-link reconnect fixture also uses the existing atomic request cursor to separate prior title-decoration reads from navigation. This preserves the eager off-roster title capability added in #172558 (thanks @Patrick-Erichsen), while still requiring exactly one interrupted navigation request or two requests when reconnect retries it.

## Evidence

Original failures were reproduced before edits. The final eight-case real Worker test fails three cases on the original published producer and passes unchanged after the phased native repair. Focused coverage also includes native supervisor/broker custody and pool preparation, nonempty SQLite snapshot/restore and rollback, credential/provenance drift, the original failed CI files in their original order, held-work drainage, internal observation, pairing/preparation, and diff unit/browser layout. Refreshed-main coordinator/scheduler-fence and received-execution shutdown proof passes. Narrow types, lint, formatting, architecture, environment-budget, SDK, and hard-zero dead-export checks pass. Independent complete-candidate review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Hosted CI must qualify the exact published head before landing.

The UI CI failure was reproduced in the original 14-case order at real native tooltip completion boundaries: the retained pointer opened a rail tooltip before late pointer parking, yielding the same extra occlusion cycle. Moving the existing parking step before mounting passes that same probe and all 14 original cases; 29 real-browser tooltip and three geometry siblings also pass. The original CI trace did not identify its first shadow surface, so the independently captured rail-tooltip reproduction is not presented as its exact surface identity. The final test-only move changes no assertions, timing budgets, mocks, tooltip behavior, or geometry policy; all task-private diagnostics were removed. Scoped independent review, lint, and formatting pass.

The exact failing reconnect file reproduced both CI count failures before the change. Ordered caller diagnostics showed two title requests before the click; those could also satisfy the old navigation wait before its deferred request existed. The cursor correction passes both original cases with all route, history, startup and deferred-response assertions unchanged. Fifty existing title, atomic-deferral and route-recovery sibling cases, focused lint/formatting, and independent P0–P2 review pass. A roster-only attempted correction still failed and was discarded.

Against the refreshed main baseline, production changes total +28 lines and tests/support +418, discounting pure owner moves. Remaining growth provides missing code-generation closure ownership, owner-proven publication reuse, accepted-observation drainage, and the private domain→pool→physical retirement phase. The latter replaces competing peer cleanup without requiring a new public callback contract. Duplicate construction, ambient first-registration lifetime binding, unused exports, and retired wrappers were removed.

Limits and follow-ups: the native cancellation reproduction qualifies the generic explicit same-generation source contract; actual snapshot staging constructs its prebound pool in a detached context, so production staging cancellation is not claimed. PostgreSQL bootstrap/control reaches the intended connection refusal, not a successful external backup. The compiled SQLite bootstrap fixture has no databases; nonempty preservation is covered separately. Unmanaged file-descriptor warnings remain a native-lifecycle follow-up. A prior-head diagnostic observed a synchronous cold GitHub source-facade load blocking client receipt; built-distribution impact remains unqualified. Vite's native configuration loader also reports an existing JSON import-attributes warning, retained as a tooling follow-up. Two pre-click title reads were observed, but whether their distinct owner scopes require both remains an unqualified follow-up; this test correction does not change that behavior. No timeout, prewarming workaround, or CI waiver is included.

prs.title: fix(config): warn when logging.redactPatterns entries are silently ignored
prs.body:
Closes #170375

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `logging.redactPatterns` entry that is invalid or has nested repetition passes `openclaw config validate` without a warning, then log redaction drops it at runtime, so the values it was meant to mask stay visible in logs and diagnostics.

## User Impact

User impact: operators get a validation warning naming the ignored pattern and the reason (`invalid-regex` or `unsafe-nested-repetition`), so they can fix it instead of relying on a mask that never applies. Valid patterns and the built-in default strings produce no warning. Config stays valid; nothing is rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime compiles operator patterns through the shared safe-regex compiler (`compileConfigRegex`) and silently skips rejected ones. The schema only checks `string[]`. The new `collectRedactPatternWarnings` runs the same parse and compile step during plugin-aware validation, next to the existing heartbeat-owner warning, and skips built-in sources that resolve to dedicated matchers before regex compilation, matching runtime. Redaction behavior itself is unchanged.

Typical trigger: a phone-number pattern such as `(\+?\d+[ -]?)+` (the PII use case from the issue) is rejected for nested repetition.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI and config-file loader: `pnpm openclaw config validate` (builds `dist`, then runs the real `config validate` command) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. The config sets `logging.redactPatterns` to 3 custom entries (`ACME-\d+`, `(`, `(\+?\d+[ -]?)+`) followed by all 122 built-in default strings.

Before (`main` code, same config):

```text
Config valid: <tmp>\openclaw.json
```

After (this PR):

```text
Config valid: <tmp>\openclaw.json
2 warning(s):
  ! logging.redactPatterns.1: Redaction pattern is ignored (invalid-regex); values it should mask stay visible in logs and diagnostics. Fix the regex syntax, then run openclaw config validate again.
  ! logging.redactPatterns.2: Redaction pattern is ignored (unsafe-nested-repetition); values it should mask stay visible in logs and diagnostics. Rewrite the nested repetition, for example (a+)+ as a+, then run openclaw config validate again.
```

The valid custom pattern and the 122 built-in defaults produce no warning, and the config stays valid (exit 0).

Runtime effect on `main` (why the warning matters): with the nested-repetition phone pattern configured, redaction drops it and the phone number stays visible:

```text
redactSensitiveText("lead ACME-42 callback +34 600 000 001", { patterns: [phonePattern] })
-> lead ACME-42 callback +34 600 000 001
```

- `src/config/validation.policy.test.ts`: the new `logging.redactPatterns` cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix (invalid regex, nested-repetition `/.../` literal, valid pattern, full built-in default string list). File result: 13/13 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean.

prs.title: fix: keep follow-up replies from failing during local turn settlement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After stopping a local turn, a follow-up can fail with `Session <id> placement authority changed` while the cancelled turn finishes its asynchronous cleanup. The destination remains local, but releasing the preceding turn's placement claim invalidates the generic snapshot used by reply admission.

Stop can acknowledge cancellation before a pending preflight operation unwinds. Existing recovery admission then permits the follow-up. Normal reply-to-reply settlement retains its successor barrier.

## User Impact

Follow-up input can complete admission when the stopped turn settles its claim without changing the destination. Destination, session, lifecycle, service, and source changes still reject admission. The execution stage continues to acquire and validate its own turn claim.

Configuration, schema, stored representation, and update procedures are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reply admission selects local recovery or staged worker custody. It now uses the existing retained placement reader, joins pending native claim publication, and rereads session facts after a settlement wait. It compares the destination and identity before accepting input. The correction is confined to this admission owner; generic observations and execution guards retain their contracts.

## Evidence

A compiled Gateway exercised public `agent`, `chat.abort`, `chat.send`, and `agent.wait` calls with a local mock Responses provider. Task-only scheduling checkpoints held the first turn's preflight and the follow-up's actor read, then observed the real placement finalizer. They did not replace guards or write placement records.

| Admission code | Follow-up result | Provider requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original | Public chat error: placement authority changed; `agent.wait` error | 0 |
| Patched | Public chat final; `agent.wait` ok | 1 |

Both runs acknowledged Stop before claim cleanup, reached the follow-up admission checkpoint, and kept the stopped run cancelled with `stopReason: rpc`. Runtime preparation used the ordinary `pnpm openclaw --version` path. This proves a supported cancellation-cleanup trigger; it does not identify the writer in a historical deployment.

The real-store regression also fails against the original controller. Its command was `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/restart-recovery-claim.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "admits a follow-up"` (9.81s Vitest). All 131 related tests passed (41.12s Vitest, 65.00s runner), plus 37 placement-owner cases and three delayed-settlement/revocation cases. Formatting, lint, size limits, and affected type checks passed.

Hosted CI completed in 1,532 wall-clock seconds. Its two wrapper-inventory failures reproduced on the exact baseline; the separately landed inventory repair and this patch passed together in 72 tests with one existing skip. All other selected CI rows passed.

prs.body:
Related: #162939
Related: #161277

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Claude CLI–backed Control UI sessions on 2026.9.7, every sent message appears twice. The second copy starts with the internal line "requester_profile is the verified linked requester…".

## User Impact

User impact: each message shows up once again, and the internal requester guidance stops showing up in chat. This also covers messages sent while the agent is busy (queued sends), which currently duplicate even without the guidance line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat history merges the Claude CLI's own transcript into the local one, and drops an imported user turn when its text (after `stripInboundMetadata`) matches a local row within 5 minutes. Two things break that match:

1. The verified-requester guidance line is pushed after `Conversation info:` without the `⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` marker, so the stripper keeps it. The imported text never equals the local text. The fix strips it by exact line, the same way the message-tool delivery hints are handled. The prompt the model sees doesn't change.
2. A queued send keeps its send time in `timestamp`. The import carries the time the turn actually reached the CLI, which can be well past the 5-minute window. The merge now uses `__openclaw.recordTimestampMs` when present, the same value `chat-display-projection.history.ts` already prefers.

This doesn't decide #161277 (whether the guidance should be sent at all). It only stops it from leaking into history.

## Evidence

**Before:** live Control UI, 2026.9.7, Claude CLI backend. The extra bubble below sits right after each real message:

![Duplicate bubble holding the requester guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d47e80da-1f2a-410d-9e89-ee278c590d6c)

**Real transcripts.** I ran `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages` on user rows exported from two affected sessions on our Gateway:

| Session | Local / imported user rows | Merged rows, stock | Merged rows, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct chat, unqueued sends | 8 / 12 | 20 (all 8 duplicated) | 12 (left over: tool results, an image-only turn, a resume notice) |
| Direct chat, 2 sends queued 13 min behind a busy turn | 3 / 3 | 5 | 3 |

**Tests:**
- New: `strip-inbound-meta.test.ts` (builder output plus a stored guidance-only row) and `cli-session-history.merge-requester.test.ts` (guidance import, queued send). All four fail on `main` and pass here.
- Focused suites: strip-inbound-meta, inbound-meta, and all three cli-session-history suites. 191 + 2 tests pass.
- `check:changed --staged` exits 0 (core + coreTests lanes, typecheck, format, ratchets).

**Gap:** there's no "after" screenshot from a Control UI running this build. Our Gateway runs the published release, so I can't deploy an unreleased build there. The transcript merge table above is the behavioral proof.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): configure outage retries and recover after exhaustion
prs.body:
Related: #146999.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WhatsApp remaining offline after a temporary network outage exhausts its retry budget, and lets operators configure longer retry cycles.

## User Impact

Linked accounts stay eligible for automatic recovery after transient failures. Configure `channels.whatsapp.reconnect.maxAttempts` and `maxMs`, with fieldwise per-account inheritance. Numeric defaults remain 12 attempts and a 30000ms delay cap. For example:

```json
{"channels":{"whatsapp":{"reconnect":{"maxAttempts":60,"maxMs":120000}}}}
```

Attempt limits must be positive safe integers; delay caps must be timer-safe integers of at least 2000ms. Changes apply when the account monitor restarts. Logout/conflict failures remain terminal; disabled and manually stopped accounts stay stopped. No database migration is required.

**Maintainer decision required:** this deliberately changes the terminal-on-exhaustion policy accepted in #118659. A prolonged outage can now cause repeated delayed recovery cycles. Existing supervision backoff, restart limits, and health-monitor limits remain; the supervisor's existing five-minute task-lifetime reset can reset its ladder after a long cycle. Numeric defaults are preserved, but post-exhaustion behavior changes for existing configurations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monitor hands an exhausted transient retry cycle to the Gateway as stopped and nonterminal. The existing exponential inner backoff reads its limits from resolved account configuration. A bounded `nextReconnectAt` deadline lets health policy respect the scheduled wait without inventing transport activity; stale or expired lifecycle deadlines remain recoverable.

The review's operator-status finding is fixed: Gateway supervision now preserves the current task's transport diagnosis through the handoff. A replacement lifecycle clears `lastError`; historical `lastDisconnect` cannot resurrect an old error. Existing terminal, abort, ownership, and manual-stop guards are retained.

## Evidence

- The new Gateway-manager regression failed before the diagnostic fix: expected `getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN`, received `channel exited without an error`. It now proves diagnosis survives scheduled recovery and clears on replacement while disconnect history remains.
- All 151 Gateway lifecycle tests and 15 WhatsApp monitor-state tests pass. Existing crash-loop and recovery-ownership cases were moved into a sibling test-support module, retaining the original fixtures and cleanup.
- The follow-up passes the complete native changed-check workflow: production types, all 27 core test type graphs, lint/format, line-size ratchets, configuration and dependency checks, and repository guards. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defect.
- The earlier retry/configuration/deadline changes passed 361 focused tests, affected core/plugin type checks, and generated configuration/example checks. The local v2026.9.6 backport validates 60 attempts/120000ms and is linked and healthy; this is configuration/startup evidence only.

**Live-proof gap remains:** no controlled real network outage has yet demonstrated WhatsApp inner-budget exhaustion, Gateway account restart, and restored message traffic. Fake-socket and manager tests are supplemental and are not described as live recovery proof. The proposed bounded real-session test requires operator approval before interrupting the account. Maintainer acceptance of the default-policy change remains outstanding. CI was not manually dispatched or rerun for proof.
