prs.title: fix(imessage): prevent reflected replies from triggering duplicate turns
prs.body:
Closes #135704

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an inbound iMessage reflection could trigger a duplicate agent turn when the reflected row carried the outbound message GUID only in `reply_to_guid`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: inbound echo identity used only the reflected row ID and its new `guid`, while the original outbound GUID was available in `reply_to_guid`. The existing conflicting-ID protection then correctly refused broad text fallback, but that left the reflection classified as a new inbound message.

This is a root-cause repair, not a fallback: the persisted echo cache matches the original outbound GUID and normalized body as one recorded fact. The `reply_to_guid` admission path opts into that strict match only for a verified self-chat reflection explicitly marked `is_from_me=false`, and only within the existing 4-second reflection window. Confirmed reflections retain the existing `self-chat echo` classification, so repeated benign rows do not consume the loop limiter budget. Ordinary message-ID matching and persisted reconnect retention remain unchanged.

The direction boundary preserves legitimate inline replies. `imsg 0.14.1` directly exposes the Messages database `is_from_me` value, and a real verified self-chat inline-reply row was observed with `is_from_me=true`, a new `guid`, and `reply_to_guid`. Such user rows do not enter the new parent/body matcher even when their body equals the recorded parent body. A subsequent `is_from_me=false` companion is still removed by the existing self-chat dedupe path.

Related-work scan: #136240 uses the same self-chat and reflection-window safety boundaries with a different in-memory association. This change keeps the existing persisted echo entry as the canonical GUID/body owner. Out of scope: configuration, schemas, protocols, media-parent matching, and generic reply handling.

## User Impact

Users should no longer receive duplicate iMessage agent responses when a verified self-chat reflection appears as a new `is_from_me=false` row whose `reply_to_guid` points to the original outbound GUID. Legitimate inline replies remain dispatchable when Messages marks them `is_from_me=true`, including a verified self-chat reply that exactly copies the parent body within four seconds. Normal direct messages, groups, different-text replies, and post-window self-chat replies remain unaffected.

## Review Follow-Up

Review of the rebased head surfaced three issues. All three are pre-existing in this branch and are fixed here:

1. **The reflected-reply probe did not cover the scope the send side actually persists.** Direct replies are dispatched with the provider's exact chat-id target: `replyTarget` resolves to `chat_id:<n>` whenever the inbound row carries a `chat_id`, which real `chat.db` rows almost always do, and `deliver` records the echo under `account:chat_id:<n>`. `buildIMessageEchoScope` only mirrored that shape for group chats, so a reflected *direct* reply never matched what was persisted and the duplicate turn this change targets still slipped through. The strict probe now opts into that scope (`includeDirectChatIdScope`), while the generic echo scopes are untouched so ordinary direct-message suppression keeps its existing behaviour. The earlier regression passed only because it seeded an `imessage:<handle>` scope by hand rather than the shape production writes; the new table case seeds `default:chat_id:123` and fails on the previous head.
2. **Type narrowing left call sites stale.** Tightening `echoCache` to `Pick<SentMessageCache, "has">` made `has` return `Promise<boolean>`, but thirteen fixtures in `inbound-processing.test.ts` still returned a plain boolean. `tsgo:extensions:test` reported thirteen TS2322 errors; it now reports none. A green `vitest` run does not imply a green type check.
3. **The line-cap ratchet rejected the growth.** `monitor.last-route.test.ts` (1647 → 1697 counted lines) and `inbound-processing.ts` (1040 → 1046) grew past their ratcheted allowances. `buildIMessageEchoScope` and the strict probe moved to a sibling `monitor/echo-scope.ts` module, and the shared last-route fixtures moved to `monitor.last-route.test-support.ts`. No coverage was trimmed, reworded away, or suppressed.

The `vi.waitFor` window in the monitor-boundary regression was also widened. The row proving the loop budget survived is delivered after five reflections, each costing a persisted-cache read, which exceeded the default one-second wait on slower hosts even though every reflection was dropped with `reason="self-chat echo"`.

Two repository checks failed on the new fixtures themselves rather than on product code. The persisted-echo writes added by the new regressions were left unawaited, which `check-lint-core-3` reports as `typescript(no-floating-promises)`; they are awaited now, which also removes a pre-existing race between seeding the echo and delivering the row under test. `ANCHOR_REPAIR_GUID` in `monitor.last-route.test-support.ts` was exported while only being used inside that module, which `check-dependencies` reports as an unused export; the export is dropped and the fixture is unchanged otherwise. On this head `oxlint` reports zero warnings and zero errors across the nine changed files, and all three Knip unused-export scans report no findings.

One decision stays with the maintainer rather than with the code: the strict reflected-reply probe deliberately trades a bounded amount of same-text suppression for removing the duplicate turn. A verified self-chat `is_from_me=false` row that quotes a recorded outbound GUID *and* repeats that outbound body inside the four-second window is dropped even if a human typed it. The reflection window bounds that exposure to the interval real reflections arrive in, and it is the same trade the existing self-chat dedupe already makes — but it is a delivery-policy choice an owner should accept explicitly, not a property this change can prove away from the diff alone.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix regression proof: the reporter-shaped `is_from_me=false` self-chat row was dispatched instead of dropped. Safety regressions also failed before the boundary was tightened: matching inline replies in a normal direct message and group were dropped, and a matching self-chat reply still dropped after 4,001 ms. On the previous PR head, the added real-shape `is_from_me=true` same-text inline-reply regression failed with `drop` instead of the expected `dispatch`; it passes after the direction boundary was added. At the monitor boundary, five confirmed strict reflections previously exhausted the five-hit loop budget and suppressed the next legitimate self-chat message; the new regression failed with zero dispatches before the classification fix and now dispatches that message without a rate-limit warning.
- Before/after runtime proof at the decision owner: the same black-box driver was run against the PR's base commit and against this head with only the extension sources differing, against the production inbound decision resolver and a real SQLite-backed plugin-state echo store. At the base commit both reflection shapes — the echo recorded under the `imessage:<handle>` scope and the one recorded under the provider `chat_id:<n>` target that real direct replies are dispatched with — were dispatched as new inbound messages, which is the duplicate turn reported in #135704. On this head both are dropped as `self-chat echo` (measured 73-95 ms after the send, inside the four-second reflection window), while an inline reply to a different parent, a different-text reply, and a matching reply in a normal direct message all keep dispatching.
- Redacted reporter-path transport proof: read-only `imsg 0.14.1` RPC over a real Messages database returned an inbound row with a row ID, a new GUID, `reply_to_guid`, and body text matching `reply_to_text`; its parent was outbound and the parent/child timestamps were within one second. The row's sender, `chat_identifier`, and `destination_caller_id` satisfied the production verified-self-chat predicate. The real row was processed by the production inbound decision resolver with an isolated SQLite plugin-state-backed echo cache. No message was sent and no operator Gateway or live state was modified.

```json
{
  "redacted_row_shape": {
    "is_from_me": false,
    "is_group": false,
    "has_row_id": true,
    "has_guid": true,
    "has_reply_to_guid": true,
    "guid_differs_from_reply_to_guid": true,
    "body_matches_reply_to_text": true,
    "parent_is_from_me": true,
    "parent_child_delta_under_one_second": true,
    "verified_self_chat": true
  },
  "production_boundary": {
    "without_recorded_outbound": { "kind": "dispatch" },
    "within_reflection_window": { "kind": "drop", "reason": "self-chat echo" },
    "after_reflection_window": { "kind": "dispatch" }
  }
}
```

- Redacted inline-reply direction proof: a real verified self-chat inline-reply transport row had `is_from_me=true`, a distinct row GUID, and `reply_to_guid`. Replacing only its body with its real parent body produced the reviewer-requested same-text collision shape. The production resolver dispatched that user reply, then dropped a companion copy marked `is_from_me=false`; total dispatch count was one.

```json
{
  "real_inline_reply_shape": {
    "is_from_me": true,
    "is_group": false,
    "has_row_id": true,
    "has_guid": true,
    "has_reply_to_guid": true,
    "guid_differs_from_reply_to_guid": true,
    "body_differs_from_parent": true,
    "verified_self_chat": true
  },
  "same_text_collision_variant": {
    "is_from_me": true,
    "body_matches_parent": true
  },
  "production_sequence": {
    "user_reply": { "kind": "dispatch" },
    "reflected_companion": { "kind": "drop", "reason": "self-chat echo" },
    "dispatch_count": 1
  }
}
```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/monitor/self-chat-dedupe.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/cache-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.watch-subscribe-retry.test.ts` — 133 tests passed. The boundary cases prove exact parent GUID + normalized text + scope drops only an `is_from_me=false` verified-self-chat reflection within the reflection window. A matching `is_from_me=true` inline reply, different text or scope, normal direct messages, groups, and post-window self-chat replies remain dispatchable. Five confirmed strict reflections do not consume the loop limiter budget or suppress the next legitimate message, while repeated generic echoes still trip the limiter. Ordinary message-ID lookups remain valid after the strict text-bound window expires.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/imessage/src/monitor/echo-cache.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/monitor-provider.echo-cache.test-support.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/persisted-echo-cache.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/self-chat-dedupe.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts` — passed formatting, extension and extension-test type checks, focused doctor-contract tests, lint, plugin boundaries, dead exports, database-first storage, deprecated API, import-cycle, and repository guard checks.
- These proofs use real macOS `imsg` transport rows plus the production decision/cache boundary, but they do not send a live iMessage. The repository has no safe raw-row injection path, and sending a real message was intentionally avoided to prevent external side effects.
- Rebase, review follow-up, and local re-validation: the branch was rebased onto the current `main` after its base moved, and the three review findings above were fixed on top. On that head the focused iMessage monitor suite passed as two Vitest shards — 208 tests across 9 files, including the strict `requires matching text and the reflection window for text-bound message-id lookups` case and the new `default:chat_id:123` reflection case — and `oxfmt --check` reported all six changed files already correctly formatted.

```text
Test Files  5 passed (5)   |  extension-imessage          Tests  31 passed (31)
Test Files  4 passed (4)   |  extension-database-workers   Tests 177 passed (177)
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

- Type checks on the rebased head: `tsgo:extensions` (production) and `tsgo:extensions:test` both complete with no diagnostics, so the thirteen stale `Promise<boolean>` fixtures are gone.
- Ratchets on the rebased head: `check-line-cap-ratchet --base origin/main` reports no new violations or over-cap growth across the changed files.
- Scope of the local re-validation: it covers the declared production surface for this change. This machine cannot inject raw Messages rows into the real transport, so live iMessage delivery was not reproduced locally; the redacted transport-shape evidence above remains the live proof for this PR.

### Previous-head CI diagnosis (2026-09-19)

At `c4602f632ad06525d8fcc59d904d87cd6e2b8b15`, [CI run 35428727928](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35428727928) remains blocked by an infrastructure timeout. All other selected jobs succeeded. [check-test-types-core-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35428727928/job/105859330975) spent approximately 10 minutes restoring the pnpm cache (07:14:54–07:24:59 UTC), then reported “Aborting cache download as the download time exceeded the timeout.” Dependency installation subsequently succeeded, but the job reached its 15-minute execution limit during type checking without emitting a type diagnostic. That check remains unverified in CI.

The aggregate CI gate failed because this selected job was canceled. [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35429463321) explicitly reports “The current CI gate has not passed. CI completion will automatically reevaluate security review.”

Recovery attempted: `gh run rerun 35428727928 --repo openclaw/openclaw --failed`; GitHub rejected it with “Must have admin rights to Repository.” No source changes or new local test runs were made for that diagnosis. The explicitly requested rebase below supersedes this failed run.

### Rebase validation (2026-09-19)

At the author's request, rebased onto `760f4b5b77728a17c6bdd78c05d7cb9ad8d8c121` (main), producing head `7cff7816890f630a8cc50d14a499c956c93b1910`. The rebase had no conflicts; `git range-diff` confirms all seven original patches are unchanged.

- Focused verification: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/monitor/self-chat-dedupe.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/cache-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts` — 177 tests passed across four files.
- Oxfmt passed for all nine changed files; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview completed with no actionable findings in its default P0 scope.
- Current-head [CI run 35439312872](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35439312872) passed, including `check-test-types-core-1`, which timed out on the previous head. The automatic security reevaluation follows CI completion.

The latest ClawSweeper review of the previous head reported no concrete code findings and sufficient recorded behavior proof. Its outstanding iMessage-owner decision about four-second same-text suppression remains open. Ordinary-DM loop reports in #135704 are outside this PR's demonstrated self-chat fix; this rebase does not broaden that claim. No new live iMessage send was performed.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep Codex catalog available with valid plugin options
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS Codex catalog disappears when a valid plugin configuration includes `appServer.nativeHookRelay`.

## User Impact

The native catalog accepts valid plugin settings without a separately synchronized plugin-wide schema. Its consumed command, arguments, environment clearing, opt-out, plugin policy and local transport/home restrictions remain validated. No signing, entitlements, bundle identifiers, permission prompts, Gateway protocol, dependencies or persisted shapes change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin owns its schema; the native catalog should validate only what it consumes. The duplicate schema was already stale. This also consolidates native bookkeeping: Wear framing validates each owned input once and chunks output only as delivered; the synchronous shared sidebar updates its private dictionary directly.

Wave-4 x07: **246 net production lines removed**, excluding tests/fixtures/generated code. Submitted under the campaign's explicit any-size real-bug-fix exception, not the cleanup size threshold. Inspected recent three-day additions, seven-day history, then largest native owners; retained security, durable-state, permission and in-flight feature foundations. Both Linux hunks and their removed test were dropped after an inconclusive GUI CI failure, per the campaign's changed-path rule; Linux now matches the lane baseline exactly.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Native catalog no longer rejects unrelated plugin settings: #166510/#166558 describe synthetic schema fixtures, not a human incident requiring a second validator. The canonical plugin consumer validates its settings; malformed unused fields no longer suppress this independent native reader.
- Post-update receipt trusts `UserDefaults.set` instead of immediately reading its own bytes: #167459 and bot-filed #167441 provide no human read-after-write failure. Encoding errors and notification-time synchronization remain; an exceptional preferences persistence failure is best effort.
- Wear output removes the second JSON-depth scan: #108835's check came from synthetic review. Pre-serialization depth and external reader limits remain; concurrent mutation of an internal JSON payload after validation is unsupported and receiver validation still rejects invalid input.
- Wear framing removes validation after `readFully`: #109483's feature fixtures provide no human declared-size/allocated-size divergence report. Validate type/size before allocation once; exact allocation and `readFully` supply the invariant afterward.
- Wear input removes repeated size checks and copying: #109483 provides no human internal-buffer-mutation report. The reader transfers a freshly allocated, validated frame; future internal callers must preserve that ownership contract. Queues and live owner/session checks remain.
- Wear chunking removes configurable chunk-size checks: #109483 has only one production caller using the fixed protocol constant. There is no remaining configurable argument to misuse; output order and abort/failure behavior remain.
- Wear output removes repeated PCM alignment checks in the sole-use chunk path: #109483 provides no human invalid-internal-buffer report. The Gateway-event boundary already validates alignment; a future producer bypassing it is unsupported, with invalid frames rejected by the peer.
- Wear playback timing removes repeated nonnegative/even byte-count assertions: #111033's timing fixtures do not establish an invalid-count incident. Its sole caller supplies a validated chunk size; a future contract violation may calculate an incorrect deadline until session reset. Delivered-chunk timing and settlement stay unchanged.
- Shared sidebar removes staging dictionary copies: #161745 describes synthetic owner fixtures. Both methods are synchronous MainActor operations over ObservationIgnored state, with one final publication; no additional concurrency failure is accepted.

## Evidence

- Original production catalog fails the valid-hook assertion; changed production source passes 22 config-boundary assertions, including policy, opt-out, malformed consumed fields and unsupported transport/home restrictions. This is boundary replay, not a live Gateway claim.
- Native config fixture contract: 1/1 passed; final lint-suppressions: 3/3 passed. Configured SwiftFormat and production SwiftLint passed. Fresh independent P0-P2 review raised one suggestion to restore the preferences read-back, declined under the campaign's explicit best-effort rule: cached read-back is not disk durability, provenance has no human failure report, and update/notification synchronization boundaries remain. No other concrete defect was reported.
- Android shared library plus Play/third-party/Wear APK builds and Kotlin lint passed. Shared tests passed 14/14; controller/registry app tests passed 47/47 (61 total, zero skips/failures). Final app invocation completed successfully in 47m03s.
- Shared Swift package/test-bundle compilation and 14 sidebar tests passed (75 focused native tests total across retained Android/shared Swift paths). macOS `xcodebuild -scheme OpenClaw -destination platform=macOS -jobs 2 build` and compile-only `build-for-testing -only-testing:OpenClawIPCTests` both passed, including the changed regression test and complete test-bundle link. App-hosted macOS tests requiring an OS sandbox intentionally not run on the operator desktop; no release gate dispatched. Retained source is unchanged from those builds/tests.
- Runtime import cycles and madge: both 0 on Testbox `tbx_01m4y3z6qpez2p3qxqqnckt2d5`, [allocation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38638021131). Dependency, protocol, assertion and SQLite worker/dialect guards passed. Extension production/test typechecks and lint passed in an earlier superset capsule; final staged classification is apps-only.
- Full changed-file run is incomplete: its lane-base environment budget reports 455 names versus 454 (counted src/packages/extensions are unchanged), and the obsolete extension-scope run was intentionally stopped after the fixture moved into macOS tests. Native owner proof is recorded separately; remaining broad checks belong to PR CI. The task-owned allocation and workflow were stopped/cancelled and cleanup reconciled.

## Previous-head CI failure attribution

Previous head `018be076c48d4418fa9a18c9005e61378f4ed655`, [CI run 38647435887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38647435887), attempt 1. This is historical evidence, not current-head CI qualification. Native admission stopped before intent because another app suite was incomplete; no merge was dispatched. Current-head CI will gate landing separately.

| Failed job | Attribution and proof |
| --- | --- |
| [ios-screenshots-ipad-13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38647435887/job/116138406355) | All four iPad screenshot tests pass. Subsequent Watch boot leaves zero active simulators; unchanged Fastfile exclusivity guard fails before Watch installation/launch. CI diagnostics record `activeSimulatorCount: 0`. prs.title: feat(lobster): run native LLM stages in embedded workflows
prs.body:
Fixes #90909.
Related: #76101, #78736 and #91028.

## What Problem This Solves

Embedded Lobster LLM stages otherwise require a separate Gateway URL and credential. Saved embedded answers must not bypass current host authorization, and a checkpointed answer must not be disclosed or consumed on resume by a caller who no longer holds the authority that produced it.

## User Impact

Opt in with `llm.invoke --provider embedded`. Inference runs as the calling agent through `api.runtime.subagent.complete`, without tools or workflow credentials. An omitted model uses the calling agent's configured primary and fallbacks. An explicit model requires override permission and is pinned without fallback.

Existing `openclaw`, `pi` and `http` routes remain remote routes. Provider selection uses the final merged workflow and step environment. An omitted provider with no configured route is refused rather than silently becoming embedded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool factory supplies the calling agent. Embedded stages force refresh, disable persistent cache writes and clear the state key at command execution, so workflow settings and `--refresh false` cannot restore saved-answer reuse. Other routes retain caching, but returning a saved answer requires a current Gateway request with a host authority checker. Revocation, missing authority and cancellation refuse disclosure.

A completed embedded stage persists its output at an approval or input checkpoint, and a resume feeds that output to the remaining stages or returns it without running the stage again. The plugin records the producing caller's agent and authority beside the checkpoint when it hands it out, and re-authorizes before a resume discloses or consumes it: the request must still carry the gateway scope, its admitted grant is rechecked, and an embedded answer is only returned to the same agent holding at least the authority that produced it. A later checkpoint of the same run carries that provenance forward, and a checkpoint this plugin has no record of is treated as carrying a saved answer. Cancelling a checkpoint discloses nothing and is allowed.

The documentation now states that the embedded route runs the calling agent's own completion under its model policy, including that a named model is an override the host may refuse (commit e94df915a1d).

This uses the existing plugin SDK request-scope callbacks; it adds no Gateway API. Those callbacks check admitted Gateway authority, including applicable auth-policy and role/access changes. They do not contact a remote provider to revalidate its credentials or model permissions.

## Risks and Limitations

- Re-executed embedded stages spend another completion, including after an approval checkpoint.
- Background completion returns text only: Lobster does not report the selected model or token usage, and this route does not expose per-stage sampling or output-token controls.
- Remote-provider caches retain their existing trust model. A Gateway authority check is not remote-provider reauthorization.
- A checkpoint whose provenance record is missing is refused rather than served, so a checkpoint created before this change cannot be resumed without a current Gateway request scope; it can still be cancelled.

## Evidence

### Head 9935db1aad1: build, routing and checkpoint behaviour

Revision 9935db1aad19c2da254801c96d2f1116ccc91498, transferred by local Git bundle (prerequisite 4be8534dec36cc8824fb17fb8403499022311df2) into a fresh clone, with HEAD asserted before building. This head is 4be8534dec36cc8824fb17fb8403499022311df2 plus the shared `isRecord` import (f61bb808cd1), the gateway-scope mock fix (56d5b508751), and a merge of upstream/main 2e76e316c286b32d14581e7ad3480e1ec49253d7 (9935db1aad1). Disposable 4-vCPU Linux x86_64 VM, Node v24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0. No live Gateway was changed.

Build: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile (exit 0); node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime (exit 0). The build marker was done and dist/entry.js (2026-10-04 04:44:48.418473617 +0000) was newer than the build-start marker before node dist/entry.js gateway was invoked. This runtime profile omits declaration generation.

UTC request windows: routing 2026-10-04T05:36:04.708Z to 2026-10-04T05:36:29.516Z; checkpoint 2026-10-04T05:35:08.298Z to 2026-10-04T05:35:38.867Z.

Setup and measurement: one scratch trusted-proxy Gateway on 127.0.0.1:19000 and one logging model stub per run, with fresh empty Lobster cache and state directories. Scenarios run sequentially against http://127.0.0.1:19000/tools/invoke. The caller model is stub/primary-broken with fallback stub/backup; primary-broken and pinned-broken deliberately return HTTP 500. The stub listens at http://127.0.0.1:44081/v1. Writer scopes are explicitly operator.read,operator.write; administrator scopes additionally include operator.admin. Gateway readiness is checked before the first request. The routing run and the checkpoint run each start their own Gateway and stub, so their counts are separate.

Host counts are cumulative [model-fetch] response lines in the Gateway log, with transport diagnostics enabled. Stub counts are cumulative requests in its independent model log. Both are read before and after each HTTP call; they count failed provider attempts as well as successful ones, and the two totals agree at every step. State listings cover the Lobster cache and run-state directories.

Routing, fallback and refusal scenarios (on 9935db1aad19):

| Scenario | Environment | HTTP | Host before/after | Stub before/after | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Omitted model falls back (writer) | writer | 200 | 0/2 | 0/2 | Served |
| Repeat with --refresh false (writer) | writer | 200 | 2/4 | 2/4 | Served |
| Explicit override refused (writer) | writer | 500 | 4/4 | 4/4 | Refused |
| Explicit override allowed (administrator) | administrator | 200 | 4/5 | 4/5 | Served |
| Pinned failing model, no fallback (administrator) | administrator | 500 | 5/6 | 5/6 | Refused |
| Omitted provider with no route (administrator) | administrator | 500 | 6/6 | 6/6 | Refused |

Checkpoint re-authorization scenarios (on 9935db1aad19):

| Scenario | Environment | HTTP | Host before/after | Stub before/after | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator embedded override, then approval checkpoint | admin | 200 | 0/1 | 0/1 | needs_approval |
| Writer resumes with an equivalent token (refused) | writer | 500 | 1/1 | 1/1 | Refused |
| Writer resumes the original token (refused, control) | writer | 500 | 1/1 | 1/1 | Refused |
| Administrator resumes its own embedded checkpoint (allowed) | admin | 200 | 1/1 | 1/1 | ok |
| Administrator plain checkpoint creation | admin | 200 | 1/1 | 1/1 | needs_approval |
| Second administrator embedded override, then approval checkpoint | admin | 200 | 1/2 | 1/2 | needs_approval |
| Writer supplies a plain token plus the administrator approval ID (refused) | writer | 500 | 2/2 | 2/2 | Refused |
| Administrator resumes its second embedded checkpoint (allowed) | admin | 200 | 2/2 | 2/2 | ok |

Refusal reasons, read from the Gateway log rather than inferred from the status code:

- Equivalent-token resume: "lobster checkpoint refused: the caller no longer holds operator.admin, which produced its embedded LLM output"
- Original-token resume: "lobster checkpoint refused: the caller no longer holds operator.admin, which produced its embedded LLM output"
- Conflicting-handle resume: "resume accepts either token or approvalId, not both: the approval ID takes precedence, so the two can select different checkpoints"
- Explicit override refused (writer): "llm.invoke request failed: provider/model override is not authorized for this plugin subagent run."
- pinned failing model: "llm.invoke request failed: Isolated completion failed with stop reason error."
- omitted provider with no route: "llm.invoke could not resolve a provider. Set --provider or LOBSTER_LLM_PROVIDER"

Limits: these are stub-model scenarios, so they show routing, refusal and what is or is not served, not provider auth. "Revocation during a pending resume" is shown as the producer-authority refusal of an equivalent token (the writer never held operator.admin); an in-flight completion cancelled when authority is withdrawn mid-request is not exercised. Legacy-checkpoint and remote-cache upgrade compatibility is not covered. HTTP 500 alone is not an authorization verdict; the Gateway log supplies the refusal reason. The real-provider credential, revocation and billing evidence below is the run on the earlier revision 134946619f2c, because this head changes only plugin authorization and the shared helper import, not provider auth; a real-provider rerun on this head would need a freshly minted provider key and was not performed.

A second run repeats this revision against the real model provider. The stub runs above establish routing, fallback, refusal and checkpoint mechanics; this run establishes that a real credential is used, that a checkpointed answer is refused to a caller who lost the authority that produced it, that a revoked credential is refused at the provider, and that the provider bills exactly the calls that succeeded.

The temporary admin credential that created and deleted that project key was revoked when the run ended.

The last scenario still shows one provider attempt, because the request reached the provider and was rejected there, which is the behaviour under test.

That is 5 billed requests for the 5 accepted calls, at the published rates of $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.25 per million output tokens, and it shows the rejected attempt was not billed.
### Misleading metadata and limits

cached: true on a fresh embedded answer does not establish replay. In the installed Lobster normalizeResult, cached is calculated by excluding source names remote, openclaw, clawd, pi and http; openclaw-embedded is not excluded. Independent provider counts and empty state listings establish fresh execution here.

The repeat changes only the refresh flag and reuses the prompt/state key, not a pre-planted cache file. This proves fresh execution of that repeated embedded stage, not every resume path. The refused writer override proves current request authorization. Pinned failure proves no fallback request reached this stub. Missing-route refusal proves no implicit embedded route in this configuration. HTTP 500 alone is not an authorization verdict: the Gateway log supplies the refusal reason.

Not covered here: live Gateway policy revocation as a mid-request event, HTTP cache replay through this disposable endpoint, or the full repository test suite. The checkpoint scenarios prove the decision at the resume boundary from the recorded provenance and the request scope; they do not prove that an in-flight completion is cancelled when authority is withdrawn. The real-provider run deletes the key and restarts the Gateway before repeating the scenario, so it proves a deleted credential is refused at the provider.

Two authorization bypasses in this checkpoint protection were repaired on this revision: provenance is keyed by the decoded checkpoint identity rather than the literal token bytes, and a resume carrying both a token and an approval ID is refused, because Lobster gives the approval ID precedence. The scenarios below run the repaired revision 4be8534dec36cc8824fb17fb8403499022311df2 and its unpatched parent 134946619f2c3ff75affd20ff88c11aff7a91ac9 through the same Gateway tool entry point with the same script.

Refusal reasons, read from the Gateway log rather than inferred from the status code:

- Conflicting-handle resume on 4be8534dec3: "resume accepts either token or approvalId, not both: the approval ID takes precedence, so the two can select different checkpoints"

After the merge of upstream/main 2e76e316c286b32d14581e7ad3480e1ec49253d7 the leg passes, exit 0. No repair from this change is carried for it.

We cannot re-run the Windows shard because we lack administrative rights on the repository, so the re-test triggered by the fresh push is the retry for this leg.

prs.title: fix: valid hook requests fail during provider credential refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes valid HTTP hook wake requests returning 503 during an unchanged provider-credential refresh, including around Gateway hot reloads.

## User Impact

Hooks keep their admission while provider auth profiles refresh without changing the resolved model configuration. Real config changes and changed model secrets still revoke old admission. Existing installations use their current stored state without migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider-only refresh cloned and republished identical runtime config. Session-event admission correctly treated that new publication as replacement and refused the request. Keep the existing publication only when the provider refresh changes no resolved model value; still publish auth stores, secrets revisions, degradation and activation lineage. The synchronous runtime-revision and credential-freshness checks remain unchanged.

An unchanged resolved SecretRef is now distinguished from a changed value. Explicit config activation retains its existing publication behavior. The hook authority, disablement and replay assertions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the reported initial `before-reload` request's exact 503 in the original 47-file Linux shard, then with the file alone. Both reported bad `960eacc5cdf0` and preceding green `c5511470ba99` reproduce: this is an older race, not attributable to the intervening storage wave. The config guard dates to #167113.
- New deterministic owner cases fail before the fix for both literal model credentials and unchanged model SecretRefs. They pass after, with refreshed auth-profile credentials visible, secrets revision advanced, and exact runtime/source/publication identity retained.
- All 69 focused owner/control tests pass, including changed model-secret publication, queued concurrent config mutation, source ownership and stale credential preparation.
- Original Linux shard with the candidate: all 8 hook-admission cases pass; 502/509 tests pass. The same 7 unrelated failures remain in plugin activation-health, lifecycle-readers and startup-error tests (also reproduced on both unpatched comparison heads). The hook regression is removed.
- Core and owning test types, changed-file typed lint, focused boundary guards, formatting and whitespace pass. Independent P2 review is scoped-clean.

Local Linux proof used an isolated Docker container with 8 CPUs/32 GiB, Linux arm64 and Node 24.21; CI uses x64/Node 24.19. PR CI supplies the exact-head broad proof. No CI rerun, timeout increase, retry, skip or assertion weakening was added.

Additional focused verification: the exact candidate passes all 8 Gateway hook tests on macOS (97.93s). Linux alone also passes credential rotation; a different case failed during startup with `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`, before its hook admission. That additional startup failure is recorded, not claimed passing; exact-head PR CI remains the landing gate.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): keep scheduled-task and event prompts quiet without the response tool
prs.body:
Closes #149940

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: quiet scheduled heartbeat checks (heartbeat-kind cron jobs / migrated heartbeat tasks) and cron/exec event runs still deliver prose status reports to the user's channel when the run falls back to a harness without the `heartbeat_respond` tool.

## User Impact

User impact: a quiet monitor that finds nothing to report stays silent on CLI-fallback runs (replies `NO_REPLY`), matching the default heartbeat prompt path fixed in #149549; alerts still interrupt with only the alert text.

## Why This Change Was Made

#149549 added the "if the tool is not available…" fallback sentence only to the default heartbeat prompt and custom-prompt resolver. Three other prompt writers embed the bare `heartbeat_respond` instructions and were missed: the scheduled-tasks branch of `resolveHeartbeatRunPrompt` and the cron/exec event prompt builders in `heartbeat-events-filter.ts`. This adds a combined `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_COMPLETION_INSTRUCTIONS` constant owned by `heartbeat.ts` (instructions + fallback, keeping one writer) and uses it at all three sites. Non-tool mode keeps the silent-reply completion unchanged. The transcript filter's stripping predicate matches the bare instruction string via `includes`, so stripping of the extended prompt still works (covered by `heartbeat-filter.test.ts`).

## Evidence

Red-green regression (pre-fix code via `git stash` of the production files):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner-prompt.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.test.ts` → **4 failed** on pre-fix code, each failing exactly on the missing fallback sentence (e.g. received prompt ends `…Set notify=true with notificationText only when the user should be interrupted.`), **57 passed** after the fix (57/57 green).
- Sibling suites unchanged and green: `heartbeat.test.ts`, `heartbeat-filter.test.ts` (transcript stripping), `heartbeat-tool-response.test.ts`, `cron/service/timer-execution.script-wake.test.ts` (46 + 3 + tests passed).

Runtime probe (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `node --import tsx` importing the modified resolver; verbatim output):

```
=== scheduled-task heartbeat prompt (useHeartbeatResponseTool=true) ===
Run the following periodic tasks (only those due based on their intervals):

- nightly-check: Check the backups.

After completing all due tasks:
Use heartbeat_respond to report the wake outcome. Set notify=false when nothing needs the user's attention. Set notify=true with notificationText only when the user should be interrupted. If the heartbeat_respond tool is not available in this run, reply NO_REPLY when nothing needs the user's attention; when the user should be interrupted, reply with only the alert text instead of a prose report.
=== checks ===
contains tool-absent fallback sentence: true
```

Gates: `oxfmt` clean, `run-oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors on changed files, `git diff --check` clean.

Not tested: a live end-to-end cron heartbeat run on a real CLI-fallback backend (the delivery pipeline is shared with the fixed default path and covered by `heartbeat-runner.tool-response.test.ts`); the autoreview helper's codex engine failed twice with an infra error (`codex engine failed (1)`), so the pre-submit review was done manually (diff: constant + three call-site swaps; no double-embedding — each prompt embeds the instructions exactly once).



Rebased onto current `main` (`26505c528b5`, head `5b3a12a39ad`): clean rebase, no semantic conflicts. The prior failing shard (`code-mode.bridge.lifecycle.test.ts` — 1 failed / 1,814 passed) ran on a merge tree now 1,400+ commits behind main and the touched files are unrelated to it. Re-verified on the new head: `heartbeat-runner-prompt.test.ts` 2/2, `pnpm tsgo` exit 0, line-cap ratchet OK.

prs.title: fix: claw skill cleanup fails on Windows during removal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removing a Claw with managed skills can fail on Windows with `EPERM` while staging skill directories for safe removal. The Gateway can finish monitor and runner drainage while its shared skill observation owner still retains directory handles for the deleted workspace.

## Solution

The drain phase now releases and awaits only the removed workspace's skill watcher subscriptions before acknowledging cleanup. Current main's shared watcher registry remains authoritative: shared path watchers stay active while any other workspace is subscribed, remote watcher ownership is disposed through the existing owner, and ordinary idle/config reconciliation remains detached.

Physical watcher close failures now fail Claw drainage closed. The failed watcher and workspace registry state remain available for retry, while ordinary detached reconciliation preserves its existing best-effort behavior. The workspace match uses the existing canonical boundary-path resolver, and the deletion fence is revalidated after physical watcher retirement and before the Gateway acknowledges drainage.

## Evidence

Candidate: `9f902836e59d86e5f419816fcb2b5786cc8518b1`, based on `ee62299caa67c41c05d74929442889e8ae4e9049`.

- Added the missing `closeSkillsWatchersForWorkspace` Gateway import identified by review.
- Exact-head run `36619850262` passes the watcher suite, including the strict close-failure and retry regression: 23/23 assertions across the two selected files.
- The same run passes `does not acknowledge drainage when a workspace watcher cannot close` in the real Gateway monitor suite.
- All five direct changed-test shards pass.
- Hosted core lint, focused lint, format, production types, and the selected Gateway test-type graph pass.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Proof Limits And Scope

Eight broad exact-head shards fail only in untouched subagent, cron, Gateway reload, update CLI, and chat-yield tests. The changed watcher and Gateway monitor regressions pass in those same hosted selections; no changed test failed. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36619850262

This refresh does not claim a released-package or end-to-end Claw lifecycle result. It preserves the existing staged rename/rollback transaction and changes only watcher release ordering and failure handling at removal drainage.

prs.title: perf(storage): remove WAL and session event readbacks
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Connect and first-turn database work still rereads results that the writer already has. WAL setup executes `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` and then queries the mode again; session-event recording inserts an event and then selects the same row by sequence.

Use the journal-mode setter's returned value and the event insert's `RETURNING *` row. Delete both readbacks. Keep WAL refusal/retry/in-memory handling, the event transaction, and the lookup needed to return the original event after a deduplication conflict. There is no new cache, worker request, schema, retention policy, or compatibility path.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

- Journal-mode readback: trust SQLite's setter result; an unsupported intervening mode change is not detected by an immediate second query.
- Event own-write readback: trust the row returned by the insert in the same transaction; unsupported out-of-owner mutations are not polled between insertion and return.

T1 in the changed owners: **0 → 0**. The event kernel remains worker-owned; connection setup stays in its existing admission/worker contexts. This change creates no main-thread SQL path.

## Measurement

Measured the original three alternating pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C) against base `abe8e9124037875354c2b6da21ca2b029572d203` and candidate `6067bdc2940bdd09bf15550ea2737c478bdeaef8`. Each accepted run completed all 13 top-level turns, successful spawned-child completion, RPC/cron work, committed compaction, and graceful shutdown with no surviving fixture children. Causal coverage is complete. Warmed counts below include only work attributed to the ten warmed turns; whole-workload counts include startup through shutdown on all threads.

| Original three-pair metric | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed statements/turn | 102.3 [101.5–104.8] | 103.3 [101.5–105.3] |
| Warmed requests/turn | 33.2 [33.1–33.7] | 33.5 [33.2–34.0] |
| Warmed MAIN statements/turn | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Connect + first-turn statements | 1476 [1426–1509] | 1434 [1420–1448] |
| Connect + first-turn requests | 185 [169–187] | 183 [174–186] |
| Connect + first-turn MAIN statements | 0 [0–13] | 0 [0–4] |
| Boot statements | 698 [693–699] | 696 [674–697] |
| Boot requests | 92 [92–93] | 92 [78–92] |
| Boot MAIN statements | 455 [455–455] | 454 [450–454] |
| Whole-workload statements | 4912 [4815–4924] | 4848 [4845–4881] |
| Whole-workload requests | 1116 [1091–1127] | 1110 [1107–1126] |
| Whole-workload MAIN statements | 477 [477–477] | 476 [476–476] |

The original warmed median rises by 1.0 statement and 0.3 requests per turn. The changed operations execute **zero times in the warmed turns** on both revisions. The one permitted extra alternating pair also passed all workload assertions and shutdown cleanup. Extra-pair results: base: 109.1 SQL and 34.7 requests per warmed turn; 4916 SQL and 1108 requests for the full workload; candidate: 105.7 SQL and 34 requests per warmed turn; 4843 SQL and 1096 requests for the full workload.

| All four pairs, including the extra pair | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed statements/turn | 103.55 [101.5–109.1] | 104.3 [101.5–105.7] |
| Warmed requests/turn | 33.45 [33.1–34.7] | 33.75 [33.2–34] |
| Warmed MAIN statements/turn | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Whole-workload statements | 4914 [4815–4924] | 4846.5 [4843–4881] |
| Whole-workload requests | 1112 [1091–1127] | 1108.5 [1096–1126] |

Both expanded whole-workload medians are lower. The campaign’s whole-workload check therefore classifies the small raw warmed increase as redistribution/variation in unchanged work, rather than new work introduced by this patch. No warmed improvement is claimed. The changed-operation saving remains exactly 13 statements in the extra pair as well.

The varying warmed SQL comes from unchanged session/transcript queries, auth-profile reads, and their transaction envelopes. Request records show existing producers, not a new request path. Their full-workload counts across all four pairs are below; these are operation totals, not counts per turn.

| Unchanged family or request producer | Base whole-workload median [min–max] | Candidate whole-workload median [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session/transcript SQL | 1592.5 [1540–1601] | 1578.5 [1572–1584] |
| Auth-profile SQL | 15 [14–15] | 12 [11–12] |
| Transaction envelope SQL | 1161 [1123–1171] | 1158 [1149–1169] |
| Session actor requests | 121 [121–122] | 121.5 [120–122] |
| Session entry patch requests | 110 [98–111] | 110 [110–110] |
| Ordered session entry read requests | 20 [19–20] | 18.5 [18–20] |
| Session transcript worker requests | 120 [118–123] | 117.5 [115–120] |
| Read-only worker session requests | 9.5 [8–10] | 8 [7–8] |

The measured owner saving is exactly **13 statements per full workload**, with **zero new requests**: seven WAL setter readbacks and six event own-insert reads disappear in every pair. WAL setters remain 7 → 7; bare journal-mode reads fall 11 → 4, with the four independent retained reads unchanged. Event inserts remain 7 → 7 (six new events and one dedupe replay); own-insert sequence SELECTs fall 6 → 0. The larger aggregate cold/whole-workload drops include unrelated variation and are not attributed entirely to this patch.

For context, legacy wall-window warmed statements/turn are 131.5 [129.0–137.2] → 135.0 [133.1–137.8], and background SQL/minute is 387.3 [276.8–452.9] → 401.0 [289.0–453.2]. These are separate from the causal counts. The 32-core host's pre-run one-minute load ranged roughly 92–130 in the original series; no latency or wall-time improvement is claimed.

The shared harness was left untouched. A private copy redirected output to external storage, reused builds keyed by exact SHA, and parsed the accepted spawn receipt through its serialized result envelope after the shared depth-limited matcher missed it. The child `agent.wait` success assertion, workload, SQL/request instrumentation, and deadlines stayed unchanged. Readiness/parser-failed attempts were discarded, not counted.

| Operation | SQL delta per occurrence | Request delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| WAL setup | −1 | 0 |
| Newly inserted session-state event | −1 | 0 |
| Deduplicated event replay | 0 | 0 |

These per-occurrence deltas match the measured operation counts above.

## Remaining family assessment

- Quarantine: repeated reads can come from final-handle admission-fact retirement; fix that lifecycle in the admission owner, rather than add another cache.
- Agent-deletion journal: per-agent status already uses committed facts; roster snapshots and destructive-cleanup lease checks remain real work.
- WAL: PASSIVE checkpoints, fresh-database page inspection, and connection policy remain real maintenance/setup work.
- Session entry store/patch, actor, and transcript state: canonical writes, atomic transactions, cold hydration, sequence allocation, and retained-window ownership remain real work.
- Cron: startup catch-up appears to load rows once for IDs and again for mutation. Follow up in the cron owner alongside ongoing startup-recovery repair.
- Auth profiles, user profiles, machine-state keys, placement, and audit: existing committed-fact caches, distinct configuration facts, disclosure/credential authority, effect claims, and retention remain necessary; no additional cache or speculative guard replacement is introduced here.

## Validation

- Existing native WAL coverage exercises in-memory mode, persisted WAL, concurrent opens, refusal, and busy retry; fixtures now consume the setter result.
- Event regression verifies persisted text/payload/time, no own-insert SELECT, and unchanged head/cursor/notices after replay.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2, one round; subsequent edit only renames a shadowed test callback variable.
- Changed-file formatting/lint, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm docs:list`: passed.
- Exact-head PR CI: production/test types, lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge, database ratchets, and all selected Node tests passed in [run 38608386234](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38608386234). Knip was not scheduled by the changed-file CI plan; the separately hosted exact-candidate scan completed in [run 38623445979](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38623445979). Its only finding is the inherited `ui/src/lib/chat/session-diff-split.ts: DiffPairingBudget` unused export, also present in [main job 116007252439](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38607531526/job/116007252439). Main fixed it in `bdc50b3c6c0`; the clean merge retains that fix and all four reviewed storage source/test blobs unchanged. Script exports passed.
- Inherited UI failure: all 11 `people-activity-card.e2e.test.ts` failures wait for the sidebar Online button in [the PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38608386234/job/116008469792) and [current main scheduled CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38607531526/job/116007250417). prs.title: perf: narrow exact device pairing reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connecting a device loads and decodes every pending and paired device solely to certify a content-hash revision, even when authorization asks for one device.

## User Impact

Device authorization keeps its final post-await lookup and existing credential checks. Exact pairing reads stop materializing unrelated devices. No schema migration, configuration change, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pairing owner advances a namespaced `config_machine_state` revision row in the same transaction as each paired-device write. Its returned revision goes directly into the existing commit receipt. Pending-only and bootstrap writes do not advance it. The previous SHA-256 whole-table revision path is removed. A seeded revision query left-joins the requested device, so a missing device still returns its revision in the same statement. Exact reads no longer need a read transaction; full lists retain one for their two queries.

Exact cache entries are scoped to their device; complete list snapshots may serve lookups, but an exact snapshot cannot serve a list. The preliminary pre-prune list was already removed on this base.

Removed checks and accepted edge cases:

- Removed the second in-memory write-revision check after a synchronous snapshot read. A commit during that read retires the captured cache revision on the next lookup; the real authorization boundary retains its post-await lookup.
- Removed whole-table content hashing as revision certification. Direct writes outside the pairing owner while the Gateway is running are unsupported; runtime writers use the owner, and offline writers have exclusive custody.

## Evidence

Pairing runtime T1 sites: **0 → 0**. Runtime reads and writes remain worker-owned; existing boot/Doctor store callers remain in T2. The final post-await connection authorization lookup is retained because it is a real credential boundary.

Focused regressions cover exact-read row materialization, cache projection scope, revision rollback, freshness after in-process writes, and delayed credential revocation. Two isolated Codex review rounds completed. Initial CI caught SQLite REAL arithmetic producing revision text `2.0`; the corrected SQL integer literal passed all nine store tests locally. The corrected head passed the full [CI run 38615241099](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38615241099), including focused pairing/publication/worker and APNs tests, types, type-aware lint, source contracts, Knip, Madge, and database worker/dialect ratchets. Local formatting, changed-file lint, and whitespace checks passed. SDK API diff and published-driver update proof are not applicable: SDK, schema DDL, update, Doctor, plugin loading, and service lifecycle are unchanged.

At landing, every test and static job had passed; only reporting and aggregate status were queued. The authorized relaxed landing allowance applied, and the full CI run subsequently completed successfully.

### SQL measurements

Three alternating pairs **M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3**, base `abe8e9124037875354c2b6da21ca2b029572d203` versus reviewed head `0b1d2ba4ef94d90e41578be35d26ba30d2479133`. All six completed 13 top-level turns, ten warmed turns, child terminal verification, control-plane/cron/compaction, shutdown, and process cleanup. Values are median [min–max] across three runs; warmed values use each run's ten-turn mean. Raw counts include all threads and background work. Turn-attributed counts use the shared harness's causal classification.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed all-thread SQL/turn, turn-attributed | 103.9 [101.5–105.1] | 101.5 [101.5–102.8] |
| Warmed requests/turn, turn-attributed | 34 [33.2–34.3] | 33.2 [33.2–33.6] |
| Warmed MAIN/turn, turn-attributed | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warmed all-thread SQL/turn, raw window | 135.7 [134.7–137.2] | 132.8 [129.3–134.7] |
| Warmed requests/turn, raw window | 47.6 [46.9–47.8] | 44.9 [44–48] |
| Warmed MAIN/turn, raw window | 1.3 [1.3–1.3] | 1.3 [0–1.3] |
| Complete connect SQL | 45 [44–45] | 350 [52–352] |
| Complete connect requests | 12 [11–13] | 20 [11–21] |
| Complete connect MAIN | 0 [0–0] | 4 [4–4] |
| Connect + first turn SQL | 1429 [1427–1484] | 1444 [1441–1466] |
| Connect + first turn requests | 174 [171–184] | 186 [174–190] |
| Connect + first turn MAIN | 0 [0–0] | 4 [4–17] |
| Whole workload SQL | 4883 [4800–4885] | 4813 [4755–4922] |
| Whole workload requests | 1116 [1080–1116] | 1085 [1067–1135] |
| Whole workload MAIN | 477 [477–477] | 477 [477–477] |
| Boot + connect + first-turn SQL | 2123 [2122–2181] | 2119 [2118–2156] |
| Boot + connect + first-turn requests | 263 [261–276] | 264 [263–267] |
| Boot + connect + first-turn MAIN | 455 [455–455] | 455 [455–468] |

The directly attributable connect saving is **34 → 29 pairing statements (−5, −14.7%) with 6 → 6 worker requests and 0 → 0 MAIN**, identical in every pair. The two exact reads save six statements; the paired-write revision upsert adds one within its existing request. Each uncached exact read is now one SELECT instead of BEGIN + pending SELECT + paired SELECT + COMMIT. It materializes only the requested device and revision.

| Complete-connect pairing operation | Base SQL | Candidate SQL | Requests, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `approveDevicePairingInWorker` | 9 | 10 | 1 → 1 |
| `ensureDeviceTokenInWorker` | 5 | 5 | 1 → 1 |
| `executeDevicePairingRead` | 8 | 2 | 2 → 2 |
| `pruneSupersededSilentPairedDevicesInWorker` | 4 | 4 | 1 → 1 |
| `requestDevicePairingInWorker` | 8 | 8 | 1 → 1 |

No pairing SQL executes in the warmed turns, so the observed warmed decreases are not claimed as savings from this cold-path change. Both warmed medians and whole-workload SQL/request medians are lower. No additional pair was needed.

### Phase attribution

The raw connect increase is startup/background phase redistribution. The same execution-store open performs **487 SQL in each of the six runs**: all during first turn on M1/M2/M3/C3, versus 306/181 split across connect/first on C1 and 299/188 on C2. Four unchanged staging-token MAIN statements shift from boot to connect. Thirteen unchanged plugin-lease MAIN statements shift between first and warmed turns. Every whole-workload MAIN source site and count is identical in all six runs (477 total, including nine at shutdown).

Per-run raw counts below are **SQL / requests / MAIN**. Combined windows are summed per run before taking medians.

| Window | M1 | C1 | M2 | C2 | M3 | C3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Boot | 697 / 92 / 455 | 690 / 89 / 451 | 695 / 89 / 455 | 677 / 78 / 451 | 694 / 90 / 455 | 675 / 77 / 451 |
| Connect | 44 / 11 / 0 | 350 / 11 / 4 | 45 / 13 / 0 | 352 / 20 / 4 | 45 / 12 / 0 | 52 / 21 / 4 |
| First turn | 1440 / 173 / 0 | 1116 / 163 / 13 | 1382 / 161 / 0 | 1089 / 166 / 0 | 1384 / 159 / 0 | 1392 / 169 / 0 |
| Boot + connect + first | 2181 / 276 / 455 | 2156 / 263 / 468 | 2122 / 263 / 455 | 2118 / 264 / 455 | 2123 / 261 / 455 | 2119 / 267 / 455 |

The combined cold median is 2,123 → 2,119 SQL and 263 → 264 requests (+0.38%); the unchanged background owners account for phase placement and maintenance variation. Background session-maintenance cycles in run order are 35,43,37,29,36,30, contributing 235,299,249,217,240,222 SQL and 105,129,111,87,108,90 requests. This is why whole-workload differences are not attributed wholly to pairing. Shared warmed read-family medians (SQL and requests per turn) are exact-entry facts 2.2 → 2.0, hydration 0.2 → 0; entry-cache snapshots, row facts, and watermark reads have zero medians. These unchanged owners account for additional warmed variation.

Counting limitation: queued cache-hit reads may lose the originating caller stack and emit no SQL, so identifiable subsystem requests are not a complete census of logical calls. Whole-workload raw request totals remain complete. No failed SQL executions or unrecorded request IDs were excluded from the accepted runs.

The shared harness was left untouched. Its private copy only relocated synthetic fixture scratch, increased nested spawn-receipt parsing depth from 8 to 16, and sequenced runs under one proof slot; workload and counting logic were unchanged. An earlier incomplete diagnostic run was excluded. Local proof waited approximately 120 minutes for its slot; no remote lease was allocated. No wall-time or throughput claim is made on the loaded host.

LOC: production +137/−42 (net +95), tests +85/−35, documentation +10. The added code replaces whole-table hash certification with the durable owner counter and keyed snapshot contract.

prs.title: fix(ui): enable heading navigation between chat turns
prs.body:
Closes #154524

## What Problem This Solves

Screen-reader users cannot quickly return from the chat input to a user or assistant turn using heading navigation.

## User Impact

Users can navigate between rendered conversation turns through level-two sender headings, including assistant replies while they stream. The visible chat layout is unchanged. Long histories remain virtualized: only mounted turns are available to heading navigation until more history is scrolled into view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing sender name as a screen-reader-only heading before each user or assistant message group. Keep a single heading for a grouped assistant turn and preserve it as a reply streams and settles. Headings inside Markdown message content remain independent navigable headings.

## Evidence

### Current Solid port

Ported onto upstream `48d96b4e3b6f2bd79583e0fac438ab91a3cd57c7`. The old TypeScript modules remain upstream's delegation adapters; the sender headings now live in the native Solid turn and stream containers. The merge preserves both original PR commits.

- One level-two sender heading per mounted turn, outside the message-body child structure; existing `sr-only` styling is reused. Working-only rows, inner narration/tool blocks, and continuation parts do not add duplicate sender headings. Markdown content headings remain independent.
- Adapted the heading tests to `mountSolid` and reactive updates. Eight focused tests pass, covering hidden own names, streaming/settlement/name changes, grouped messages plus a continuation, Markdown headings, and actual virtual-window scrolling. The initial five positive regression cases failed against the unmodified Solid renderers because sender headings were absent.
- The existing transcript invalidation suite passes all 24 tests, including the ported sender-visibility and settled/active-run heading assertions.
- Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: heading test file, 6.01 s Vitest / 7.95 s runner; transcript invalidation, 21.95 s Vitest / 24.69 s runner (includes transform/import overhead; test bodies remained under 5 s per file). Hosted CI timings are pending.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passes after regenerating the raw-copy baseline for the shared stream sender name. The baseline only removes the former inline fallback entry.
- Fresh independent in-session source review found no actionable defects. The canonical autoreview CLI could not run because the Codex executable is unavailable; it is not claimed as passed.
- `git diff --check` passes. UI typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:ui`), scoped oxlint, and changed-file formatting pass. The aggregate changed-check run passed its initial guards, then stopped at the raw-copy drift fixed above; it was not rerun in full. An initial parallel lint attempt hit the shared generated-artifact lock; serialized lint passed after typechecking completed.
- Validation limits: no new VoiceOver/Safari/Chrome session or browser accessibility-tree capture has been performed for this Solid port. Full build, full `pnpm check`, full suite, and the footer-selector E2E have not been rerun. The full suite is **not claimed green**; the earlier unresolved failures below remain historical evidence, not a conclusion that they are fixed or unrelated.

### Earlier Lit implementation evidence (historical)

The following results and manual observations apply to the previous implementation, not a retest of the Solid port:

- Manual testing reported by the contributor: VoiceOver on macOS 27, using the mocked Control UI in both Safari and Chrome; heading navigation looked good. This was mock testing, not a live Gateway/provider session.
- Chromium boundary check using the real message renderer and production styles: the accessibility tree exposes `heading "You" [level=2]`, followed by user content, then `heading "OpenClaw" [level=2]`, followed by assistant content. This is a semantic-only change with no visual appearance change.
- Regression proof: the new heading tests and added transcript assertions failed on the original implementation, then passed with the fix. Focused coverage: 263 tests across message rendering, message headings, and transcript invalidation.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm check`: passed. The changed-scope check against `upstream/main` also passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent autoreview through P2: scoped-clean; no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm test`: completed all 776 scheduled shards in 9,207.48 seconds (about 2 hours 33 minutes), exit 1. The runner reported 31 failed shards. Available per-shard summaries total 261,172 passed, 235 failed, and 847 skipped tests, plus one worker error. These are reported test executions, not a claim of unique tests or successful completion of the crashed worker.
- Diagnostic follow-ups: staging the new test fixed the tracked-file inventory mismatch; the whole planner file then passed all 119 tests (55.98 seconds). Replaying the shared UI suite in its original observed file order reproduced the debug-overlay cleanup failure: 21,761 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped (465.11 seconds). All four new heading tests passed in that replay. The UI failure remains unresolved; a passing isolated test would not establish a fix.
- Test cost, measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `chat-message-headings.test.ts` passed 4 tests in 2.18 seconds wall time (1.28 seconds Vitest); `chat-transcript-invalidation.test.ts` passed 22 tests in 3.01 seconds wall time (2.10 seconds Vitest). Hosted CI timings are pending.

The full suite is **not green**. Confirmed host prerequisites, fixture/contract evidence, and unresolved failures are distinguished below; this PR does not claim that every failure is unrelated or repair them as part of the accessibility change.

<details>
<summary>Full-suite failure findings and complete failed-file inventory</summary>

### Findings

- Host prerequisite failures include tests explicitly requiring Bash 5+, missing GNU `timeout`, and script preflight cases whose login shell selects Node 18.15.0 instead of the test runner's Node 24.18.0. The SSH-upload fixture also references unavailable `gstat`; that attribution remains a strong prerequisite hypothesis.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): count poll votes and give the agent stored poll results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp encrypts every poll vote, so today the agent cannot tell anyone what a poll in their chat actually says: votes arrive as undecryptable updates and are dropped.

## User Impact

User impact: when the agent is woken in a WhatsApp chat, it receives the current results of that chat's recent polls (up to 3 polls, 50 names per option, 4 KB cap), and can answer "what did the poll say?" accurately, including after a Gateway restart.

- Group votes are counted silently and never wake the agent, on any poll and in any group, including groups with `requireMention: false`.
- In a direct chat, only a vote on a poll the agent sent wakes the agent, as `Poll vote: <option>` (or `Poll vote removed`) quoting the poll. Derived vote messages never trigger a pairing prompt.
- Polls are known when the agent sends them, or when an admitted sender posts them in a registered group or an allowed direct chat after the account connected. Older polls and polls from unauthorized senders are not decrypted.
- Stored data: per poll the question, options, creator name and vote secret; per voter the display name, phone number when known, and current selection. Retractions delete the voter; no change history is kept. Everything expires after 30 days, in the plugin state database.
- Documented in a new "Poll votes" section of `docs/channels/whatsapp.md`, with a changelog entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two commits, reviewable separately:

1. `feat(whatsapp): record polls and per-voter selections for on-demand results` adds dormant infrastructure: a poll store split by origin (sent / received, so a flood of incoming polls cannot evict the agent's own), a per-voter tally store (PN key preferred, LID rows merged, stale votes ignored by sender timestamp), a vote decoder, a single poll-creation finder for V1-V5 and wrapped polls, and the results context builder. `sendPoll` now generates and records a 32-byte message secret after relay acceptance; a store failure never changes the send result.
2. `feat(whatsapp): count poll votes in the drain and give the agent stored results on demand` wires it in: votes are decrypted and counted in the durable drain before normalization, incoming polls from admitted senders are recorded, and the results block is appended when the agent is woken.

Failure handling: transient store read failures replay the queued message; a failing tally write only replays when the vote would wake the agent, so a group lane is never held by a vote. Rejected votes log one warning with reason, origin, poll id and redacted chat, never the secret, hashes or names.

This branch is a port of the same change from our fork onto current `main`; the only adaptations are to upstream APIs (`send-api` socket adapter and `targets-runtime`, approval-reaction handling in the drain, `checkAccess` in access-control tests). Behavior is unchanged from the reviewed original.

## Evidence

Local, focused gate on `62eb787e36` against base `0f13444e2a`, on a partial dependency install (disk-limited host):

- `extension-whatsapp` vitest shard: 91/91 files, 877/877 tests.
- All 13 test files touched by the branch ran with >0 tests and 0 failures each (JSON reporter), including the 8 store-backed files in the `extension-database-workers` shard.
- `pnpm format:check`: pass.
- oxlint for the `extensions/whatsapp` shard and `test/vitest`: pass.
- `check:architecture`: all 9 steps pass.
- New `send-api` test "sends polls with an owned message secret" fails on base and passes on this branch.

Not green locally, but identical on the base commit with the same install (missing packages, not this change): `tsgo:extensions` (errors only in other plugins, none under `extensions/whatsapp` or `test/`), 8 pre-existing `waitFor` timeouts in `inbound.media` / `monitor-inbox.*` database-worker tests, and `pnpm build` (A2UI assets / `LinkifyIt` export in `extensions/x`).

Full `tsc`, lint, test and build were not run locally; opening as a draft so the full suite runs in CI.

prs.title: improve(skills): discover eligible skills automatically
prs.body:
Related: #163824, #164969

## What Problem This Solves

Applied Workshop skills should become discoverable without manually adding each new name to a persistent agent list.

## User Impact

User impact: agents discover all otherwise-eligible skills in their configured roots, including newly applied Workshop skills; the agent Skills panel becomes a read-only eligibility inventory.

**Intentional upgrade policy change:** Doctor retires `agents.defaults.skills`, `agents.entries.<id>.skills`, and their historical `agents.list` forms, with visible warnings and the normal private pre-migration backup. **Prior agent-specific restrictions over current and future skill names are not preserved. An old `[]` no longer disables all skills.** Review this change before upgrading if you rely on that persistent curation. Global per-skill disables and session selections remain effective, but are not equivalent preservation of agent-specific restrictions. No agent exclusion becomes a global disable.

`skills.allowBundled`, prerequisites/platform eligibility, publishing/scanning, source precedence and agent-owned Workshop isolation remain separate. Tool permissions, credentials, sandbox and exec-approval controls are not relaxed.

X guest containment previously depended on the empty skill list suppressing outside-repository read exceptions. This PR preserves that shipped restriction through the existing sender-bound, closure-bound read authority and inherited helper lineage instead. Guests and their hidden helpers cannot gain external skill/resource reads from normal discovery. Older hosts refuse guest mode with actionable support guidance; normal maintainer behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistent positive lists have legitimate role-focus, token-efficiency and behavioral/security-guardrail uses. This deliberately trades that optional persistent catalog curation for automatic skill discovery and learning, rather than claiming the old selection model was pointless or a hard host/tool authorization boundary.

The cutover removes the competing agent-name filter across discovery, prompts, catalog/read/search/slash/status, snapshots, CLI, UI and native consumers. Existing eligibility, session focus and refresh owners remain authoritative. Doctor owns retirement and backup; restrictive X resource authority stays with the existing admission/read owners, using a compatible optional restrictive fact rather than new public configuration.

Requested by @obviyus.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @obviyus](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/89406c17-b564-4203-9dae-18487d03e22f)

## Evidence

- Real baseline apply-to-snapshot regression reproduced the prior hidden-Workshop behavior. The 306-test skill/Workshop matrix passed in 75.42 seconds; affected later fixture/consumer follow-ups passed in 100.04 seconds. Coverage includes source isolation, global disables, prerequisites, bundled controls, session true/false focus, real apply/watch/next-snapshot discovery, search/read/slash/status and existing refresh contracts.
- Real admitted root/hidden-descendant read tests permit an in-repository file and deny known external skill paths, cached instruction shortcuts and symlink/alias escapes before protected bytes; ordinary non-guest selected-skill reads still work. Native/worker handoff, helper placement, old-host refusal and existing live-authority/closure siblings were checked. - Production core/UI/scripts/extensions typing, all test-type shards, changed-source lint, formatting, canonical protocol/config/native-source generation, SDK surface/export/declaration checks and config documentation examples passed. prs.title: fix(retry): honor nested channel hints behind invalid metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: empty or invalid `parameters.retry_after` metadata on an outer error prevents the shared channel retry runner from honoring a valid hint in its response or nested error. For example, it can retry after the 400 ms backoff despite a nested response requesting one second.

## User Impact

Channel requests using the default hint reader wait for the available provider-requested delay even when an earlier wrapper contains incomplete metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the first finite hint in the existing root, response, nested-error order. Missing or invalid hints fall through; finite hints, including zero, retain their precedence. The existing runner continues to own retry admission, injected readers, backoff, jitter, and delay caps. No public signatures, configuration, or exports change.

## Evidence

- On the original production code, six new fake-clock timing cases failed and 28 cases passed. Those failures observe premature retries through `createChannelApiRetryRunner`, rather than testing a private reader in isolation.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/infra/retry-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 34 passed; 3.50 seconds wall time and approximately 0.34 seconds of tests. CI seconds are pending publication. The new cases reuse the existing fake-clock helper and add no real sleeps or process startup.
- Ten new cases cover empty/nonnumeric/nonfinite outer metadata, nested-error fallback, first-finite and zero precedence, and default backoff. Existing tests cover injected readers, caps, and strict retry admission.
- Independent autoreview at P0–P2: scoped-clean. A separate fresh review of the owner and retry scheduler found no actionable findings. `git diff --check` passed.
- Production types (`pnpm tsgo:core`), the owning test type graph (`pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-infra"]'`), changed-file type-aware lint, and formatting passed.
- Validation gaps for this draft: full `check:changed`, full build/test, broader test type graphs, live channel/API execution, and CI are unrun. This changes the default error-envelope reader; the fake-clock proof does not claim a live provider result.
