prs.title: fix(acp): generated sessions fail without an agent owner
prs.body:
Closes #137247

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IDE users in explicit multi-agent setups could create an ACP session but have its first prompt rejected because the generated session had no agent owner. An explicit shared session key worked around ownership but lost per-editor-thread isolation.

## User Impact

Users can select an OpenClaw agent with `openclaw acp --agent <id>` while retaining a unique session for each editor thread. Local sessions preserve recorded fixed-store ownership; other local sessions use the existing system/sole-agent selection policy. Remote connections selected by `--url`, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL`, or `gateway.mode: "remote"` defer ownership to the remote Gateway: explicit agents are forwarded, and an omitted agent leaves the generated key bare for Gateway resolution. An explicit remote fleet that cannot resolve an owner still requires `--agent` or an existing agent-owned session key/label.

The new bridge-specific `--agent` interface remains subject to maintainer acceptance as requested in the linked issue. This repair does not add another public option or change `acp.defaultAgent`, Gateway ownership policy, schemas, or persisted-session migration behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generated local session keys include their selected owner, except implicit fixed-store sessions retain a bare key for Gateway ownership; explicit session-key and session-label routing keep precedence. The bridge now consumes the shared Gateway bootstrap's resolved URL override provenance, so environment-selected remote targets cannot accidentally use the client's local agent roster. Documentation describes both local defaults and the remote implicit-owner exception.

The repair incorporates main `7bc4491e537` to resolve the actual merge conflict, preserving main's asynchronous state-database shutdown and the PR's agent-ID validation. The original PR branch/history is retained.

## Evidence

Remote repair head: `834ffe3800e30534bb4c9a8bf9cfd8261b2dfa53`. Fixed-store follow-up: `c552a496ec32e151b4dbb1d9401e9c944f7b4095`. Linux, Node v24.16.0.

| Scenario | Before repair | After repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bootstrap selects a remote Gateway through the environment while local mode has an explicit ops/research roster | New regression fails: local owner validation is not bypassed | Remote ownership is selected from resolved bootstrap provenance |
| CLI URL override and configured remote mode | Remote ownership preserved | Both regression cases pass |
| Real ACP client with local ops/research roster; remote Gateway has only remote-only; environment URL; no --agent | Not previously covered by real remote proof | session/new succeeds; bare generated key; prompt ends with end_turn; Gateway persists remote-only ownership |
| Same differing rosters; environment URL; --agent remote-only | Not previously covered by real remote proof | Agent-scoped key; prompt ends with end_turn; Gateway persists remote-only ownership |
| Same differing rosters; CLI URL; implicit and explicit remote owner | Existing remote behavior | Both real prompt cases pass |

The real compatibility proof runs separate ACP CLI and Gateway processes with isolated client/Gateway state and different rosters, real ACP stdio and Gateway WebSocket traffic, and a deterministic loopback HTTP/SSE model provider. All four prompts returned `PR137348_REMOTE_OWNER_OK`, each made one provider request, and Gateway `sessions.list` confirmed the persisted owner.

```json
{"connection":"env","selection":"implicit","newSession":"ok","stopReason":"end_turn","generatedKeyShape":"acp-bridge:<uuid>","persistedOwner":"remote-only","providerRequests":1}
{"connection":"env","selection":"explicit","newSession":"ok","stopReason":"end_turn","generatedKeyShape":"agent:remote-only:acp-bridge:<uuid>","persistedOwner":"remote-only","providerRequests":1}
{"connection":"cli","selection":"implicit","newSession":"ok","stopReason":"end_turn","generatedKeyShape":"acp-bridge:<uuid>","persistedOwner":"remote-only","providerRequests":1}
{"connection":"cli","selection":"explicit","newSession":"ok","stopReason":"end_turn","generatedKeyShape":"agent:remote-only:acp-bridge:<uuid>","persistedOwner":"remote-only","providerRequests":1}
```

Focused checks:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/server.startup.test.ts \
  src/acp/translator.session-setup.test.ts src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/cli/acp-cli.option-collisions.test.ts
```

All 67 tests pass. The environment-target regression demonstrably failed before the production repair (28 other startup tests passed). Changed-file formatting, docs MDX validation, and `git diff --check origin/main` pass. The supported `pnpm openclaw --help` entry prepared the current runtime build before real-process proof. Required autoreview completed with no actionable findings at its default P0 reporting threshold.

The follow-up resolves the fixed-store compatibility finding from Revision 16. Without `--agent`, a recorded fixed-store owner keeps the generated key unqualified. Gateway retains authority over configured and retired owners instead of letting local system-agent selection override the store. Explicit selection remains agent-qualified. No database schema or stored data changes are introduced.

A new table at the ACP `newSession` boundary reproduced three failures before the fix: missing owner, a different system owner overriding the fixed-store owner, and fallback bypassing a retired store owner. After the fix, all 46 targeted tests pass (session setup, session lifecycle, and Gateway session-request ownership); the explicit-selection case also passes. Changed-file formatting, docs MDX, and diff whitespace checks pass. Fresh follow-up autoreview reports no actionable findings at its default P0 threshold.

The follow-up also passes two real local ACP/Gateway process cases with a fixed store owned by `ops`: no system owner, and a different system owner (`research`). Both use local config without a URL override, agent selector, or session metadata. Each keeps the generated bare key, completes a real prompt against the deterministic loopback provider, and persists the session under `ops`.

```json
{"connection":"local-config","systemOwner":"none","fixedStoreOwner":"ops","newSession":"ok","stopReason":"end_turn","generatedKeyShape":"acp-bridge:<uuid>","persistedOwner":"ops","responseMarker":"PR137348_FIXED_STORE_OWNER_OK","providerRequests":1}
{"connection":"local-config","systemOwner":"research","fixedStoreOwner":"ops","newSession":"ok","stopReason":"end_turn","generatedKeyShape":"acp-bridge:<uuid>","persistedOwner":"ops","responseMarker":"PR137348_FIXED_STORE_OWNER_OK","providerRequests":1}
{"proof":"PR137348 real local ACP/Gateway fixed-store ownership","passed":2,"total":2,"providerRequests":2}
```

**CI:** Latest head `c552a496ec32e151b4dbb1d9401e9c944f7b4095` completed green, verified by the exact-head PR rollup watcher (zero pending checks). [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35103679255). Revision 17 reports no actionable code findings, and the PR is labeled `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`. Maintainer acceptance of the CLI selector remains the only review decision before merge.

**Proof limits:** The remote Gateway is a separate isolated process on loopback, not an external host; the model endpoint is deterministic local HTTP/SSE, not an authenticated paid model. The existing local ACP proof remains in the PR history. No full local test/typecheck/lint sweep was run; standalone markdownlint was unavailable locally, so documentation lint is left to CI. Maintainer acceptance of the CLI selector is not claimed.

prs.title: fix: Control UI hides progress messages during tool runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress messages disappearing from Control UI while an agent calls tools, leaving only an increasing output-token counter.

## User Impact

Live progress text stays visible as it becomes saved history, including through a reload during an active run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Interim assistant messages carry their producer's run ID in transcript metadata; the outer event's run ID is reserved for terminal assistant messages. The UI now recognizes that explicit metadata when admitting live saved messages, while preserving conflicting-identity and client-correlation checks.

The regression began in `af210e1f3fbf` ([#167054](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167054)): retiring the streamed copy exposed an older admission mismatch from `bbbd70542b44` ([#126284](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126284)). An identical boundary test passes on the exact parent `4bf68b98ab51` and fails on `af210e1f3fbf`.

## Evidence

- **Before:** real isolated Gateway on main `923e59a01e20`, Chromium, eight Code Mode calls plus eight nested shell executions, and five ordinary progress messages. Progress briefly appears and disappears; none remains during the final live hold. The continuous-visibility assertion fails while the counter reaches 8k tokens.
- **After:** the same scenario displays all five messages during the active run and after a separately tested reload. Tools, thinking, and completed-commentary retention are hidden in both captures. Two uninterrupted candidate runs pass across 1,379 animation-frame samples with no lost messages or navigation; the baseline fails with missing previously visible text in 528 of 692 samples.
- Only the external Anthropic model response stream is scripted. Gateway persistence, Code Mode, shell execution, pasted attachment, WebSocket delivery, browser navigation, and rendering are real.
- Permanent Gateway regression: **8 failing cases before → 9/9 passing after**, using the real terminal-run resolver and message projector instead of a fabricated outer run ID. UI ownership/recovery suites: **150/150 passing**, including metadata-only tool images, conflicting ownership, client-only rejection, and immediate commentary admission followed by terminal/reconnect deduplication. The existing cursor tests now assert live visibility instead of waiting for history catch-up.
- Runtime and UI builds, UI typecheck, affected Gateway/UI test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and the line-count check pass. The broader changed-file check remains red on verified baseline failures: the environment-variable budget (455 names versus 454), plus unused exports. An independent pristine checkout of `923e59a` produces the identical unused-export sets: 9 production, 17 full-tree, 0 scripts; no added or removed findings.

The video shows continuous 1× clips with matching fixture pacing and a real live hold: no internal cuts, retiming, or frozen frames. The deliberate full-page reload is tested afterward, separately from this uninterrupted comparison. The recording and screenshots use synthetic content. Rollback is a normal code revert; the change is confined to live message admission and regression coverage.

prs.title: fix(memory): stabilize system-only cron catch-up test
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an order/timing-dependent failure in the memory startup catch-up test for system-only cron-base sessions.

## User Impact

Test-only change. Production retention, session exclusion, and both existing assertions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture introduced by #161834 inserts `agent:main:cron:synthetic-job` with `updatedAt: 10`. Enforced 30-day session maintenance can delete this synthetic session and its transcript while the test runs. The resulting empty provenance no longer satisfies the all-system exclusion, so startup catch-up unexpectedly queues the session.

Use `Date.now()` for this fixture and explain why it must stay recent. This preserves coverage of both system-only exclusion and later user-content inclusion.

The failure occurs with the automatic maintenance behavior updated by #171211. Diagnostic rechecks found that a nominal bisect boundary's parent both passed and failed; there is no proven first-bad maintenance commit. The fixture's expired timestamp is the defect being corrected.

Scheduled main CI did not cover this case: `EXCLUDED_FULL_SUITE_SHARDS` in `scripts/lib/ci-node-test-plan.mts` excludes `vitest.full-extensions.config.ts`, whose projects include `vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`. Changed-plugin PR shards use the extension batch runner, so they can expose it.

## Evidence

Prior diagnostic evidence recorded a successful append followed by zero transcript events, session windows, and rewrite watermarks in the failing run. Changing only this timestamp to the current time made both original assertions pass.

Three serial full-file runs through the PR-shard `runExtensionBatchPlan` runner, using `test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`, one worker, and verbose reporting, each passed all 11 tests. Both original cron-session assertions remained unchanged.

| Run | Result | Vitest duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 11/11 passed | 893.61 s |
| 2 | 11/11 passed | 706.91 s |
| 3 | 11/11 passed | 593.92 s |

Durations reflect a heavily loaded local host; no performance claim is made. Formatting, focused lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean with no P0/P1 findings. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38651373751) passed at `668106e21d6435cca82583e8ce62aeba472a96b9`, with no retries or CI overrides.

Production LOC delta: zero. The patch only updates the fixture timestamp and adds its one-line retention comment.

## Publication Refresh: October 7

Layer 14/16. Previous: [#166798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166798) | Next: [#166800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166800). Published checkpoint: `5b4b0c2311b0`.

## What Problem This Solves

A reviewed Claw operation could reach a later effect after plugin grants, scheduled work, or skill watcher ownership had changed.

## User Impact

Changed permissions stop installation before the package is committed. Removal waits for managed skill work to retire, checks current scheduled-job revisions, and preserves resources it can no longer safely own. Default Update remains usable for recorded legacy local sources without restoring package control over models or delegates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recheck staged effective plugin grants at the managed installer boundary, delay the external-mutation marker until that review passes, carry live cron revisions, and use the existing watcher retirement and guarded skill-write owners.

## Evidence

- Combined stack at `9e653a8ed286`: 100 focused backend tests passed on October 7 in 64.75 seconds. The real managed-installer integration covers grants revoked during download, rejection before persistence, and preservation of a previously accepted plugin during a denied Update.
- Reviewed Remove cases reject changed cron targets and revoked authority before apply.
- The prior full `pnpm check:changed` passed at the unchanged combined tip. Earlier real local-ClawHub recovery and cron-race runs are historical evidence; this publication does not claim a fresh production lifecycle canary.

## Publication Scope

Related: #163946. This is a draft layer in the Claws Labs stack. The stack retains its previously tested base and currently conflicts with newer main; this publication does not resolve that drift or authorize a release. Production ClawHub support, the compatible published Lobster artifact, official catalog security review, and RFC acceptance remain release gates. The local-source CLI and official-only launch scope are unchanged.

prs.title: improve(memory-wiki): keep the gateway responsive during large wiki searches
prs.body:
<!-- MUST: Keep "Allow edits from maintainers" enabled for this PR. -->

Closes #166304

Design decisions:

- Single-page reads stay on the calling thread. An exact-path `wiki_get`, a digest claim-id read and every other one-path read run `readWikiPagesTask` in the gateway thread, with the same reader the worker runs; only whole-vault scans (`wiki_search` without digest candidates or underfilling them, `wiki_get` id lookups and misses, `wiki_apply update_metadata`) go through the pool. A short read therefore never waits behind a scan, and results stay byte-identical across the two paths (the identity test covers both).
- Scans run on a two-worker shared-compute pool and yield at checkpoints. `maxWorkers: 2` lets a lookup overtake a long search and two searches overlap. A whole-vault scan is one listing task and then one scan task that, every 64 pages, asks the host over the pool's existing request channel whether to go on. The pool aborts the task's `yieldSignal` when another task is waiting for that task's shared compute permit or its worker; the host then answers "yield", the worker returns what it has read so far (with `readPages`), the task settles and returns its permit, the waiting task is admitted, and the host resubmits the unread rest. An uncontended scan stays one task and pays no task boundary per segment. This is the cooperative checkpoint the pool already offers to tasks that exchange with the host (`packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-core.ts`, `requestCheckpoint` and the contender loop in `dispatch()`); the wiki worker now makes those exchanges. Search keeps a running top `maxResults` with a stable sort, in the worker across segments and on the host across resubmissions, which reproduces one whole-vault sort exactly; a lookup collects `{ relativePath, id }` keys, the host resolves the lookup over the complete listing with the existing priority and reads the one matched page on the calling thread, where it must still match. The checkpoint size comes from a sweep (Evidence, "Checkpoint size").
- Deadline ownership is exactly `main`'s: the pool adds no timeout of its own. `wiki_search` keeps #166329's 30 s deadline and turn cancellation (`tool.ts` keeps `main`'s deadline lines verbatim), and the signal it already threads through `searchMemoryWiki` is forwarded to every pool task of the scan. Callers that pass no signal on `main` (the `openclaw wiki` CLI, the `wiki.search` and `wiki.get` RPCs, the `memory_search` and `memory_get` supplements, `wiki_get` id lookups and misses, `wiki_apply update_metadata`) still run their scan to completion, now in a worker instead of on the gateway thread. The pool requires a watchdog on each checkpoint reply; the reply carries `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime`, so no scan gains a deadline. Choosing operator budgets for unsignalled callers is a policy change this PR does not make; the deadline-ownership table under Evidence shows the unsignalled CLI search, the unsignalled CLI lookup and the deadlined tool search completing or timing out exactly as on `main` on a vault whose scan takes about 50 s (captured before #171961, when the CLI lookup there was a basename scan; the id-lookup and miss shape of the same call is measured through the built Gateway at the merge head under Built Gateway).
- Why checkpoints rather than one pool task per fixed batch: both release the permit within 64 pages, and the previous revision of this branch did the second (`832afc5b07d`). Measured in this sitting, the fixed batches cost 16% to 19% more process CPU and 5% more wall time on an uncontended 10,000-page search (a task boundary, a pipeline drain and a merge every 64 pages, and two to four times the worker's mark-compacts), and a waiting task still had to queue for the batch in flight. With checkpoints a scan only splits when something is waiting.
- Why not a non-shared pool: it would escape the isolate-wide compute budget that memory-core's pools honour, and that budget is what lets a waiting memory-core task take the permit at the scan's next checkpoint. Why not more workers: each worker is another V8 isolate (heap peak about 100 MB while scanning the 140 MB vault measured below), the pool has no backpressure beyond its pending limits, and the event loop is already protected by the first worker.
- Merged with #171961 (the reviewed rewrite of #164781, landed 2026-10-14) on 2026-10-14, head `b998e21c797`. `query-page-lookup.ts` stays the lookup owner exactly as merged: `getMemoryWikiPage` hands `resolveQueryableWikiPageForLookup` an exact read and the per-candidate path-tier reads, which run on the calling thread through this branch's one-page reader, a listing that runs on the calling thread, and a full read that is this branch's worker lookup scan over that same listing and returns only the page the lookup resolves to, which the owner's final resolve re-checks. A basename or extensionless-path hit therefore reads one page on this branch exactly as on `main`; only an id lookup or a miss is still a whole-vault read, and that read is what moves off the gateway thread.

## What Problem This Solves

A `wiki_search` or `wiki_get` lookup over a large memory wiki freezes the gateway for every other client until it finishes.

## User Impact

User impact: a whole-vault wiki read no longer saturates the gateway event loop, a short read no longer waits behind one, and on a host with one shared compute permit a long scan hands the permit to a waiting memory-core task within 64 pages. On the capture machine, under the background load recorded in [`evidence/load-during-capture.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/13b39fd0d8cb5cecf54a8e122159f657a87e6ad0/load-during-capture.txt), a 10,000-page scan that holds the loop at utilization 1 on `main` for the whole search (100 ms timers firing up to 17 ms late, an `fs.access` probe taking up to 17.7 ms) leaves the calling thread at 37 ms of CPU and timers within 2.7 ms of schedule, with every result object identical; an exact-path `wiki_get` issued while that scan runs answers in 3 ms (p50) instead of waiting 7,657 ms (p50) for the scan, as it does when single-page reads share the scan worker; and with the isolate pinned to one shared compute permit, a task for memory-core's retrieval pool issued during an unsignalled 20,000-page scan completes in 83 to 99 ms (p50, max 617 ms), where a pool that runs each scan as one task that never yields holds it for 25,108 to 25,198 ms (p50, max 51,242 ms, 22 of 52 in each of two runs past `memory_search`'s 30 s deadline). Nothing changes in the tool, CLI or RPC surfaces, no caller gains or loses a deadline, and there is no new config.

Compatibility: there is no schema, config, stored-data or on-disk format change (the on-disk compatibility check under Evidence hashes every file of a vault compiled by `main` after `main` and this head query it: identical). The only contract changes are in error objects: a vault boundary refusal still arrives as `FsSafeError` with its original `name`, `code` and `message` (rebuilt on the host from the worker's `{ select: "refused", code, message }`; the test "rebuilds a worker boundary refusal as the same error on the host" proves the rebuild), and other errors from inside a scan arrive as `WorkerTaskError` with code `failed` carrying the original message.

Differences an operator can observe:

- Whole-vault scans run on two worker threads. Scan starters that pass no signal run to completion as on `main`: the `wiki.search` RPC (`gateway.ts`), `memory_search`'s wiki corpus supplement (`corpus-supplement.ts`) and the `openclaw wiki search` CLI (`cli.ts`) call `searchMemoryWiki` with no signal; every `wiki_get` id lookup or miss is a whole-vault lookup task (a basename or extensionless-path hit reads one page since #171961) whose callers pass no caller signal (the `wiki_get` tool forwards only the plugin lifecycle signal, `tool.ts:286`; the `wiki.get` RPC at `gateway.ts:330`, `openclaw wiki get` at `cli.ts:646` and the `memory_get` supplement at `corpus-supplement.ts:29` pass none); a `wiki_apply update_metadata` runs a whole-vault scan under the vault mutation lock from the tool (lifecycle signal only), the `wiki.apply` RPC (`gateway.ts:315`, request signal) and the CLI (`cli.ts:683` and `:707`, none). Each such scan holds one worker and one of the `max(1, cores - 1)` shared compute permits until another task waits for either, and then hands it over at its next 64-page checkpoint; on `main` it occupies the gateway thread for the whole scan. On a host with two cores or fewer that is the only shared permit, so a memory-core task issued during a scan waits for the segment in flight: 83 to 99 ms p50 and 617 ms at most during the 20,000-page scans measured below, against 12 ms p50 (max 34 ms) on `main`, where the scan takes no permit (see Gaps).
- A third concurrent scan takes a worker at the next checkpoint of a running one instead of waiting for a scan to finish, and concurrent scans then alternate per segment; with fewer permits than running scans they also alternate on the permit. On `main` concurrent scans interleave on the gateway thread itself (16-wide async page reads and a `setImmediate` every 16 pages while scoring). See Gaps for what this means for two scans racing one 30 s deadline.
- Exact-path and claim-id `wiki_get` reads run on the calling thread as they did on `main` and are unaffected by the pool's state; they are the common path for an agent that already knows the page.
- A new failure mode reaches scan callers: when the pool's pending limits or the shared admission limits are exceeded, `wiki_search`, `wiki_get` lookups and `wiki_apply` reject with `WorkerTaskError("worker task capacity reached", "overloaded")` instead of running the scan on the main thread (see the "Pool capacity" row).
- `wiki_get` lookups become cancellable: the tool already spreads the plugin lifecycle signal into `getMemoryWikiPage`, and this PR forwards it to the pool, so a plugin stop during a lookup rejects the read instead of letting the scan finish.

## Why This Change Was Made

A whole-vault read (`wiki_search` without digest candidates or with body-only matches, a `wiki_get` id lookup or miss, a basename lookup too until #171961, a `wiki_apply` metadata update) parses and scores every page on the gateway main thread. In the outage behind #166304 (8,928 pages, one `wiki_search` call) the event loop sat at utilization 1 for at least 311 s with p99 delay 359.7 to 453.8 ms, `sessions.catalog.list` took 11.2 s to 46.6 s, three websocket handshakes timed out, and the agent turn stayed blocked for 584 s. Three merged changes narrowed the problem without moving the scan:

- #152487 passed `includeLinks: false` for query reads, removing the link-extraction share of each page parse; #158517 was closed when it merged.
- #166355 (closes #166302) admits digest candidates on distributed token matches, so a multi-term query whose terms all appear in page metadata no longer falls back to the whole vault. Queries that match only in page bodies, vaults without a compiled digest, and digest reads that underfill `maxResults` still read every page.
- #166329 (closes #166303) gives `wiki_search` a 30 s deadline plus turn cancellation, threads the signal through the reader, and yields to the event loop (`setImmediate`) once every 16 pages during scoring. A stall is now bounded at 30 s and other callbacks get a turn every 16 parses, but the parse and scoring CPU still runs on the gateway main thread for the whole budget, `raw` and `parsed` are still retained for every page until the scan ends, and a search that needs longer than 30 s returns a timeout error instead of results.

What remains is the placement: `scanWikiPageSummary`, `parseWikiMarkdown` and `toWikiSearchResult` still execute on the main thread for every page of a whole-vault read. That is the half #158517 described ("there is no worker offload anywhere in `extensions/memory-wiki/src`") and the part #166304 asks for. This PR is not a reopen of #158517; it moves the scan to a plugin-owned worker pool on top of the three fixes above and keeps their behaviour (deadline, cancellation, token prefilter).

Two alternatives were built and measured against this design. A single-worker variant that sends every page read through the pool, single-page reads included (`a5af25c3924`, fork branch `variants/166304-single-worker`), has head-of-line blocking: an exact `wiki_get` waits behind whatever scan holds the worker, and a queued `wiki_search` spends its 30 s deadline before starting (the concurrent-read table under Evidence). A pool-timeout variant that puts a 30 s `timeoutMs` on every scan task (`492827c8100`, fork branch `variants/166304-pool-timeout`) bounds worker occupancy but makes scans that complete on `main` fail on a large vault: measured for the CLI search and the CLI lookup (the deadline-ownership table; a basename on the trees of that capture, where it was a whole-vault read), and by the same unsignalled call shape for the RPC, supplement and `update_metadata` scans. The design above takes neither: short reads never enter the pool, scans get two workers, and every caller keeps `main`'s deadline.

AGENTS.md "Small core, capable plugins": "New capability takes the first fitting step of the capability ladder: existing owner, existing plugin contract, narrow generic core/SDK capability, then universal core surface." The owner exists (memory-wiki owns page reads and scoring) and the contract exists (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` for the host pool and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/worker-task-server` for the worker, the shape memory-core already runs in `manager-cpu-worker-runtime.ts` and `manager-search.worker.ts`), so the first two rungs fit and no core or SDK edit is needed. The placement follows the rule AGENTS.md states for the one CPU-bound workload it names: "Database access runs in worker threads (read-only worker scope, SQLite writer broker), never on the Gateway main thread, which only awaits results and installs published facts." A page scan is not database access, so that line does not govern it; it is the same reasoning applied to the plugin's own CPU-bound read, with the main thread awaiting a result and merging it.

The alternative considered in the issue, yielding between pages, is partly in `main` already (#166329 yields every 16 pages while scoring). It bounds each stall but leaves the scan's CPU on the main thread for the whole budget and every page's `raw` and `parsed` on the main heap until the scan ends; a per-page yield would change neither. The worker does both: the scoring runs on another thread, and only the top `maxResults` `WikiSearchResult` objects (or `{ relativePath, id }` keys for lookups) of each scan task cross the thread boundary. Each page is projected as it is read: a search keeps only results with a score above zero and folds each 64-page segment into a running top `maxResults`, which the host merges across resubmissions; a lookup returns one key per visible page, and the host resolves the lookup over all keys and reads the one matched page again on the calling thread. Reads run 16 at a time within a 64-page segment, so at most 16 raw pages plus one segment's projections and the running top are live in a worker at once (Evidence, "Where the scan runs", for what the sampled heap shows).

Overlapping open work, with merge order:

- #145732 (another author, P1, waiting on author) threads a caller `AbortSignal` into `walkMemoryWikiDirectory` and the supplement paths and adds a raw-text prefilter to `readQueryableWikiPagesByPaths`. Both now run inside the worker, where cancellation arrives as `control.throwIfCancelled()`, so whichever lands second moves the signal to `WorkerTaskOptions.signal` and the prefilter into `readWikiPagesTask`. Overlap: `query.ts`, `corpus-supplement.ts` and the reader.
- #104719 ([Bug]: memory-wiki supplement exhaustive fallback ignores tool deadline; P1, open, #145732 is its linked fix) is the issue behind the unsignalled supplement scan listed in User Impact. This PR does not fix it and does not change it: the supplement still passes no deadline, and its scan now runs in a worker instead of on the gateway thread.
- #129191 (P3) makes bridge-ownership visibility configurable in `createWikiPageVisibilityFilter`. This PR serializes the filter as `{ scopedAgentId } | null`; whichever lands second carries the ownership mode and delegation set through the same `WikiPageVisibility` seam in `query-pages.ts`.
- #135290 (another author, draft) overlaps textually in the `query.ts` read paths and the `tool.ts` imports; resolved on whichever lands second.

Open questions from the issue, answered here:

- Visibility filter serializability: the sandbox filter closed over `appConfig` and a session key only to derive one lowercase agent id. The host now resolves that id (`resolveWikiPageVisibility`) and sends `{ scopedAgentId }` or `null`; the worker applies the same predicate before scoring, so no larger candidate set is needed and nothing non-serializable crosses the boundary.
- Deadline and cancellation: the signal `main` threads through `searchMemoryWiki` (#166329: the tool's 30 s deadline, the caller signal and the lifecycle signal joined with `AbortSignal.any`) is forwarded as `WorkerTaskOptions.signal`, so a timeout or turn cancellation rejects a queued task with the abort reason or cancels a running one and retires its worker. Inside the worker the reader polls the pool's `control.throwIfCancelled()` between pages, the same checkpoint shape `main`'s reader uses for the signal, so a cancelled scan also stops early on its own. The pool task carries no `timeoutMs`: a caller without a signal waits for its scan, as on `main` (the scheduling test "leaves an unsignalled scan unbounded, as on main, and passes a caller signal through" pins this at the pool seam). `wiki_apply` and `wiki_get` forward the plugin lifecycle signal their tools already receive from `WikiToolMemoryContext` (`wiki_apply` destructures it, `wiki_get` spreads the whole context), so a plugin stop cancels those scans too (see User Impact).
- Error contract: the pool transports only an error message, so the worker returns vault boundary refusals as `{ select: "refused", code, message }` and the host rebuilds `new FsSafeError(code, message)`; `name`, `code` and `message` match the original, `cause` and `details` do not cross. Other errors (walk limits from `bounded-walk.ts`, unexpected read failures) arrive as `WorkerTaskError` carrying the original message with code `failed`.
- Direct hit resolution: unchanged from `main` since the merge. `resolveQueryableWikiPageForLookup` (#171961) still resolves the exact page through `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup([exactPage], lookup)`; this branch supplies only its reads.

## The change in one sentence

Move the scorer out of `query.ts` into `query-scoring.ts`, extend `main`'s `query-pages.ts` reader into a self-contained list and read-and-score task that can stop at 64-page checkpoints, run single-page reads through it on the calling thread, and serve whole-vault scans from one lazily created `WorkerTaskPool` (`maxWorkers: 2`, `sharedCompute: true`, no timeout of its own) as a listing task plus a scan task that yields its permit and worker to a waiting task at the next checkpoint and is resubmitted for the unread rest; the pool is owned by the plugin and closed in its service `stop()`.

Diff shape (`git diff --numstat ebc4e6de603..94dd0a0e7f0`): 22 files, +2,158 / -864 in total; production files +1,216 / -784, tests +929 / -79, docs, README and the baseline +13 / -1. Mechanical: the scorer moved from `query.ts` into `query-scoring.ts` (667 lines, of which 15 differ from the base `query.ts` text: the header comment, the import lines and `export` keywords on declarations that were module-private; #166355's token prefilter among the unchanged lines), its removal from `query.ts`, and the three importers of `WIKI_SEARCH_MODES` (`tool.ts`, `cli.ts`, `gateway.ts`) pointed at `query-scoring.ts` so `query.ts` carries no re-export. Behavioural, production: the visibility scope, task union (`list`, and `search` / `keys` / `page` over an explicit path list), per-page projection, segmented task runner and checkpoint in `query-pages.ts`, the pool, checkpoint answer, resubmission and merge in `query-reader.ts`, the worker entry, the dispatching host paths in `query.ts`, and the `apply.ts`, `index.ts` and `package.json` lines. At `2c54327b1ad`, rebased onto `main` `072f977edd46`, `git diff --numstat 072f977edd46..2c54327b1ad` gives 22 files, +2,156 / -857: `git range-diff` shows commits two to five unchanged and the first differing only in `package.json`, which now carries `main`'s `2026.9.9` version line next to the same `workerEntries` key, and in `query.reads.test.ts` (+38 / -68 against the new base), because #169218 deleted on `main` two tests this branch had rewritten ("searches and reads without extracting unused links" and "reads %s without enumerating unrelated pages"; the link-extraction assertion of the first lives on in `query-reader.test.ts` as "reads query pages without extracting the link graph"). The pushed head `79fffcac1e7` gives 22 files, +2,197 / -857: its one further commit rewrites the service-stop test in `index.test.ts` (+50 against the base) and the queued-read test in `query-reader.test.ts` (+489), and makes that file's fresh-worker recovery test start from a closed reader. The merge of `main` `12fe41e2219` (2026-10-14, head `b998e21c797`, tree `f569bc30e306`): `git diff --numstat origin/main..HEAD` ([`evidence/merge-2026-10-14/numstat.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/7d5f93c7f80520a14c43f343dee241abc01bcd9c/merge-2026-10-14/numstat.txt), whole diff [`evidence/merge-2026-10-14/main-12fe-to-head.diff`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/7d5f93c7f80520a14c43f343dee241abc01bcd9c/merge-2026-10-14/main-12fe-to-head.diff)) gives 22 files, +2,250 / -853 (`query.ts` +118 / -730, `query-pages.ts` +177 / -22, `query-reader.ts` +215, `query-reader.test.ts` +498, `index.test.ts` +50, `query.path-lookup.test.ts` +28 / -15, `query.reads.test.ts` +41 / -75, `apply.ts` +6 / -4, `package.json` +4 / -1). Relative to `79fffcac1e7` the merge changes under `extensions/memory-wiki` only what `main` changed plus the resolution ([`evidence/merge-2026-10-14/head-79ff-to-head.memory-wiki.diff`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/7d5f93c7f80520a14c43f343dee241abc01bcd9c/merge-2026-10-14/head-79ff-to-head.memory-wiki.diff)): `query-page-lookup.ts` and `query-shared-memory.ts` are `main`'s files untouched; `query.ts` feeds the owner its reads and keeps `readMemoryWikiPageByLookup` for `apply.ts`, now scoped to an explicit page list when the owner passes one; `query-pages.ts` drops this branch's copy of `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup`, no longer moves `normalizeLookupKey` and exports `isWikiPageVisible`; `query-reader.ts` imports the owner's resolver; `package.json` carries `main`'s `2026.10.3` next to `workerEntries`; `index.test.ts` keeps only the stop test `main` did not remove; `query.path-lookup.test.ts` (#171961's) changes in the two tests that watched the full read through the thread-local fs-safe open hook, and `query-reader.test.ts` in the test that asserted basename reads dispatch as lookups (Tests below). The per-file table keeps the numbers against the old base.

## Contract table

| Input case | Expected outcome |
|---|---|
| `wiki_search`, compiled digest with candidates, enough scoring hits | The candidate paths are read by one scan task (resubmitted for the rest if it yields), scoring each page as it is read and returning its top `maxResults`; the host's running top `maxResults` is returned, every result object identical to `main`'s |
| `wiki_search`, candidates underfill `maxResults` | A listing task (the whole vault minus the candidate paths) and its scan task follow; host concatenates and merges exactly as before (each read returns at most `maxResults`, and the merge never consumes more than that from the wiki corpus) |
| `wiki_search`, no digest or no candidates | One listing task, then one scan task over the listing, resubmitted for the unread rest each time it yields; each page scored as it is read, a running top `maxResults` kept across segments in the worker and across tasks on the host. The stable sort keeps ties in listing order, so the result equals one whole-vault sort (tested with every page tied on title across segment boundaries, and with a yield in the middle) |
| `wiki_get`, digest claim id | One-path read on the calling thread with the visibility scope applied; never enters the pool |
| `wiki_get`, exact path | One-path read on the calling thread; an invisible or missing page falls through to the path tiers and then to the whole-vault lookup task, in #171961's order |
| `wiki_get`, basename, extensionless path or id | `main`'s `resolveQueryableWikiPageForLookup` (#171961) runs unchanged: the exact read, then the path-tier candidates from the listing one at a time, each a one-page read on the calling thread with the visibility scope applied; when no path tier hits (an id lookup, or a miss) its full read is this branch's lookup scan over that listing: a key task (resubmitted if it yields) projects each visible page to `{ relativePath, id }` in the worker, the host resolves the lookup over all keys with the owner's priority and reads only the matched page again on the calling thread, re-checked against the lookup, and the owner's final resolve checks it once more (summary, `raw`, `parsed`). A page that disappears, or whose id changes, between the two reads yields `null` |
| `wiki_apply update_metadata` | The whole-vault lookup scan (listing task, then key task) without a visibility scope, where `main` reads the whole vault, under the vault mutation lock as before; the page's `parsed.frontmatter` and `parsed.body` feed the write, and the plugin lifecycle signal the tool passes is forwarded |
| Sandboxed caller | Host resolves `{ scopedAgentId }`; every scan task and the in-thread read of a lookup's match admit non-bridge pages and bridge pages owned by that id; unresolved id admits only non-bridge pages (fail closed, as before) |
| Page missing or replaced by a directory | Reader returns `null` for that page (absence falls through to discovery, as before) |
| Page replaced by a symlink outside the vault | In-thread read throws `FsSafeError` directly; a scan task catches it in the worker, returns `{ select: "refused", code, message }`, and the host throws `new FsSafeError(code, message)`, discarding the partial results |

Scheduling:

| Input case | Expected outcome |
|---|---|
| Exact-path or claim-id `wiki_get` while a scan runs | Completes on the calling thread without touching the pool (the test holds the search scan at the dispatch seam, so it cannot settle first, and asserts that the read resolves and that the only dispatched task is the search) |
| Uncontended scan | One listing task and one scan task; every checkpoint is answered "continue" (the test asserts the task sequence and that every reply is `null` with the timer-maximum watchdog) |
| Another pool waits for the scan's shared compute permit | At the scan's next checkpoint the pool has aborted its `yieldSignal` (the capacity calls every holder's `requestCheckpoint` when a pool starts waiting and again whenever a checkpoint opens), the host answers "yield", the task returns and releases the permit, the waiting pool is admitted, then the host resubmits the rest. The shared-compute test pins one permit and asserts that order |
| A third scan waits for a worker | The pool aborts the `yieldSignal` of one host-waiting running task per queued contender, so the queued scan gets a worker at the next checkpoint and the yielding scan is queued behind it; the running scans then alternate per segment |
| Two scans at once | Both run, one per worker when shared compute grants two permits; results identical to a serial run. On a one-permit host the second waits for the permit, and the two alternate at checkpoints |
| Three scans at once | Admission is bounded by `maxWorkers: 2`: immediately after the third submission the pool reports three admitted tasks (each scan's listing task) with one or two running (two whenever shared compute has two permits free, as on any host with three or more cores) and the rest queued; at most two workers are ever created (the test reads `getSnapshot()` rather than completion order) |
| Scan started without a signal (CLI, `wiki.search` / `wiki.get` RPC, supplements, id lookups and misses, `update_metadata`) | Runs to completion in a worker, as it ran to completion on the gateway thread on `main`; no task timeout (the test asserts every listing and scan task carries `timeoutMs: undefined`; the checkpoint reply's watchdog is the timer maximum; the deadline-ownership table under Evidence drives it through a 48 to 53 s scan) |
| `wiki_search` tool deadline (30 s, from #166329) | Unchanged, `tool.ts` deadline lines identical to `main`: the tool aborts the joined signal with `wiki_search timed out after 30s`, the pool cancels the task, and `tool.deadline.test.ts` still asserts that message |
| Caller aborts the signal before dispatch | Rejects with the abort reason; nothing is dispatched (the test starts from a closed pool and asserts that no worker thread is created) |
| Caller aborts the signal while the task is queued behind running scans | The queued task rejects with the abort reason; the running scans complete normally |
| Caller aborts the signal between a yield and the resubmission | The signal travels with every task, so the resubmitted task rejects with the abort reason at submission (the pool behaviour the already-aborted test pins) |
| Caller aborts the signal while the task is running | The task rejects with the abort reason, the pool retires that worker, and the next scan starts a fresh one (the test counts the process's `worker` events: exactly one new worker is created for the recovery read) |
| Shared compute (`sharedCompute: true`) | Every listing and scan task takes one isolate-wide shared compute permit at dispatch and returns it when it settles (`packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-capacity.ts`, built by `src/infra/worker-task-capacity.ts` with `max(1, availableParallelism() - 1)` permits). A scan that yields is resubmitted only after its task settles, and the capacity admits waiting pools first come, first served and never lets a newly submitting pool overtake a waiting one, so a pool already waiting (memory-core retrieval) is admitted before the resubmitted scan |
| Checkpoint size | 64 pages per segment (`WIKI_SCAN_CHECKPOINT_PAGES`), bounded in pages, not bytes. A waiting task from another pool waits for the segment in flight, and when a segment takes longer than the gap between that pool's tasks they queue behind each other; the sweep under Evidence shows both (1,024 pages: p50 17,497 to 17,987 ms), and 64 keeps the wait at 85 to 95 ms p50 for 37 to 38 ms of calling-thread CPU per 10,000-page scan |
| Pool capacity | Per-pool defaults `maxPendingTasks: 128` and `maxPendingBytes: 256 MiB` (`packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-core.ts`), plus the isolate-wide shared admission of every `sharedCompute` pool, memory-core's included (`packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-capacity.ts:50-57`). Exceeding either rejects with `WorkerTaskError("worker task capacity reached", "overloaded")` (`worker-task-pool-core.ts:241-248`), deliberately unhandled, the same bound memory-core's search pool carries; it reaches scan callers (see User Impact) |
| Worker heap | No `resourceLimits` are set (same as memory-core's pools); a worker inherits the process V8 flags. Measured below: worker heap peak 99 to 119 MB on the 10,000-page vault (283.9 MB on the previously published head) and 915.6 MB on the 20,000-page, 558.7 MB vault (1,388 MB on the previously published head), an upper bound that includes uncollected garbage |
| Plugin service `stop()` | `closeMemoryWikiQueryReader` awaits the pool's close while keeping it referenced, so a scan issued during the stop rejects with the pool's closed error instead of opening an orphan pool; a scan after the close settles recreates the pool lazily |
| Idle worker | The pool `unref`s a worker as soon as it is idle (`packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-core.ts:735` at the merge head: `idle()` calls `slot.worker.unref()` unless a resource closure is pending) and retires it after 60 s idle. The harness holds a ref'd timer through its sampling window because of that `unref`; neither the `unref` nor the 60 s retirement was observed directly |
| Build | `openclaw.build.workerEntries` emits `dist/extensions/memory-wiki/src/query-reader.worker.js` from both the standalone plugin build and the root bundled build (Build below) |

### Behaviour, case by case

The harness ([`evidence/harness.mts`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/13b39fd0d8cb5cecf54a8e122159f657a87e6ad0/harness.mts)) generates deterministic vaults (four page groups, seeded PRNG), initializes them without compiling (no digest, so every search reads the whole vault) and drives the plugin's real entrypoints. `search` runs `searchMemoryWiki` while sampling `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay` (10 ms resolution), a 100 ms timer-chain probe (timer lateness plus `fs.access` latency), `process.threadCpuUsage()` of the calling thread, `process.memoryUsage()` and `Worker.getHeapStatistics()` for every worker announced on `process.on("worker")`, and stores every result object whole; it passes a never-aborted signal, as the `wiki_search` tool does, so `main` takes its signal-gated yield path. `concurrent` starts one whole-vault search and issues 20 exact-path `getMemoryWikiPage` reads, one every 500 ms without waiting for the previous one. `budget` runs one caller shape: `cli-search`, `cli-get` and `cli-apply` call `searchMemoryWiki`, `getMemoryWikiPage` and `applyMemoryWikiMutation` (`update_metadata`) with no signal, the call shapes of `openclaw wiki search`, `wiki get` and `wiki apply metadata` (`cli.ts:615`, `:646` and `:707`), and `tool` executes the real `wiki_search` tool returned by `createWikiSearchTool`, whose 30 s deadline applies. `contention` is described with its table.

**Shared compute on a one-permit host.** `contention` runs with a `--require` preload ([`evidence/single-permit.cjs`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/13b39fd0d8cb5cecf54a8e122159f657a87e6ad0/single-permit.cjs)) that sets `os.availableParallelism()` to 2 before the capacity exists, so `getWorkerComputeCapacity()` grants one permit, as on a one- or two-core host; every file records `limit: 1` from the capacity's own snapshot. It starts an unsignalled whole-vault `searchMemoryWiki` (the call shape of the `wiki.search` RPC and the `memory_search` supplement) and, once a second while the scan runs, submits a task to memory-core's real retrieval pool (`runMemoryPresenceInspection` from `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-cpu-worker-runtime.ts`: the pool memory-core keyword search runs in, `maxWorkers: 1`, `sharedCompute: true`), timing each task from submission to result. Idle, that task takes 1 to 2 ms. Other cases are covered by the tests below: candidate-only dispatch for distributed tokens (#166355's case, asserted on the task the host dispatches), underfill (candidate read followed by a whole-vault read excluding the candidates), exact paths and basename hits read in-thread and id lookups dispatched as whole-vault scans, sandbox scope applied in the worker, boundary refusal rebuilt as `FsSafeError` on the host, listing-then-swap refusal on the reader, mid-scan cancellation on the reader (#166329's test, kept at the reader seam), a whole-vault search whose dispatched task is cancelled through the pool, a read rejected when its signal is already aborted, a read queued behind two running scans rejected while the scans complete, a running read cancelled and the next read served by a fresh worker, a lookup whose match changed before the in-thread re-read, segment shape and identity across segment boundaries, a yield to another shared-compute pool at the next checkpoint, the admission bound, plugin `stop()` terminating every worker the reader started, and a closed reader recreated by the next read.

None asserts a wall time, a latency ratio or a completion order between independent tasks, and none polls. The shared-compute test pins one permit by mocking `os.availableParallelism()` (the file owns the process-wide capacity singleton) and records events at the pool's `run` seam and at the checkpoint reply: admission and dispatch are synchronous, so when the scan task is submitted it holds the only permit, and a task submitted to a second shared-compute pool at that moment can only be admitted when the scan yields. At the pushed head `query.reads.test.ts` holds 8 tests (the lane log lists each; the cost row above was measured when it held 15), after #169218's deletions on `main`.

## Gaps, stated plainly

`pnpm changed:lanes --json --base upstream/main` for this diff, the `lanes` block quoted from [`evidence/changed-lanes.json`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/13b39fd0d8cb5cecf54a8e122159f657a87e6ad0/changed-lanes.json):

```text
  "lanes": {
    "core": false,
    "coreTests": false,
    "ui": false,
    "extensions": true,
    "extensionTests": true,
    "scripts": false,
    "testRoot": false,
    "apps": false,
    "docs": true,
    "tooling": true,
    "liveDockerTooling": false,
    "bundledChannelConfigMetadata": true,
    "releaseMetadata": false,
    "all": false
  },
  "extensionImpactFromCore": false,
  "docsOnly": false,
```

Lanes that are `true`: `extensions`, `extensionTests`, `docs`, `tooling` (the one-line shrink of `config/max-lines-baseline.txt` counts as a tooling surface) and `bundledChannelConfigMetadata`. Everything else (`core`, `coreTests`, `ui`, `scripts`, `testRoot`, `apps`, `liveDockerTooling`, `releaseMetadata`, `all`) is `false`, and AGENTS.md does not mandate unrelated suites, so only the memory-wiki lane and `check:changed` (which runs the tooling guards itself) ran.

- `Closes` rather than `Related`: the issue asks for exactly this placement change and nothing else in it stays open once this lands; #166304 is a feature request, so if maintainers want the product decision recorded on the issue first, the first line becomes `Related: #166304`.
- Shared compute on small hosts is bounded, not free. On a host with one shared permit, a memory-core task issued during a wiki scan waits for the segment in flight: 83 to 99 ms p50 and 617 ms at most during the 20,000-page scans above, where `main` answers it in 12 ms p50 (34 ms at most) because on `main` the scan takes no permit. Segments are bounded in pages, not bytes, so a vault of very large pages makes each segment, and the wait, longer. A pool that submits tasks faster than one per segment gets one task admitted per yield; the 1,024-page row of the sweep shows that queueing, and 64 pages keeps a segment at about 175 ms on this machine (20,000 pages in about 55 s), so on a host several times slower the same queueing starts at a task or two a second.
- Concurrent scans alternate instead of finishing in submission order. When a scan waits for a worker or a permit held by another wiki scan, the running scan yields at its next checkpoint and goes back into the queue, so the two alternate per segment, as concurrent scans interleave on the gateway thread on `main`. With a permit per scan (any host with three or more cores, up to two scans) they run in parallel instead. Where they alternate, two `wiki_search` calls that each need most of their 30 s alone can both time out, where serving them in order would have finished the first; on `main` the same two searches interleave on one thread with the same result. Preferring a resumed scan over a new one, or yielding only to tasks from other pools, would need either a scheduling hook in the shared pool or plugin-side admission; neither is in this PR. A related pool-level effect: when one task waits, every permit holder that reaches a checkpoint before the waiter is admitted is asked to yield (`requestCheckpoints` counts waiters, not pending yields), so with two scans on two permits both can yield for one waiter; results are unaffected, it costs one extra resubmission.
- Each yield resubmits the unread part of the listing (the paths cross the thread boundary again), so a scan that yields at every checkpoint copies O(n²/64) path strings in total; for a 20,000-page vault that is up to about 3 million path copies spread over the scan, and none at all when nothing is waiting.
- Unsignalled scan starters: the `wiki.search` RPC, the `memory_search` and `memory_get` supplements, the CLI, every `wiki_get` id lookup or miss and every `wiki_apply update_metadata` start a scan with no deadline of their own (User Impact lists each call site), exactly as on `main`, and this PR keeps it that way. Each such scan holds a worker until it finishes or something else waits for it; it then alternates with the waiting scan at checkpoints instead of blocking it, and on a one-permit host it alternates with every other shared-compute task. On `main` the same scans hold the gateway thread itself, so every request waits, not only wiki scans. Giving those callers a budget of their own (#145732's territory for the supplement, a follow-up for the RPC and CLI) is a policy change left to maintainers.
- The contention test models memory-core's retrieval pool with a second pool of the same shape (one worker, `sharedCompute: true`) because extension tests cannot import another extension; the real memory-core pool is exercised by the `contention` harness above, which runs `runMemoryPresenceInspection` (a cheap task in the pool keyword search uses), not a full `memory_search` tool call. The admission wait is independent of the task kind; the task's own run time is not. No test drives two wiki scans on one permit or a caller abort while a checkpoint reply is outstanding; the pool's own suites cover cancellation during a host exchange.
- The shared-compute test's event order relies on the waiting pool's task being admitted (its input prepared synchronously inside the capacity's `drain()`) before the host's `await` chain resubmits the scan. That is how the pool works today; a change that defers input preparation would reorder the events without changing the guarantee.
- Admission test on small runners: with one shared permit the admission test sees one running and two queued tasks, so the two-worker bound is asserted through `maxWorkers: 2` and `workersCreated <= 2` rather than through two concurrent tasks.
- The lookup owner's `readPages` callback is overloaded. `resolveQueryableWikiPageForLookup` (#171961) declares `readPages(relativePaths)` as "read these pages" and calls it with one candidate at a time for the path tiers and once with the whole listing for the full read. This branch's callback reads one path on the calling thread and, for more than one, runs the worker lookup scan over exactly those paths and returns only the page the lookup resolves to (or nothing). That satisfies the owner because its final step runs the same `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup` over whatever `readPages` returned, so the result equals the page a read of every listed page would pick, and the count-based split is right for every call the owner makes today (an empty listing returns nothing without a task; a one-file vault reads its page in-thread and resolves it the same way). The invariant is stated in the code comment; an owner change that read the full listing in pieces, or resolved before `readPages` returned, would need this seam revisited. Making the owner take a `readLookup(relativePaths, lookup)` step instead is a one-line owner change left to maintainers.
- Pool ownership: `query-reader.ts` keeps one module-level pool, created by the first scan and closed by the plugin service's `stop()`, not tied to a service generation as `extensions/AGENTS.md` asks for work that outlives its caller. The CLI is why: `openclaw wiki search`, `get` and `apply` run with no service, so the pool must exist without one. Consequences: a scan after `stop()` recreates a pool no service will close (bounded by the idle `unref` and 60 s retirement), and if a plugin reload shares the module instance, the old service's `stop()` can close the pool under the new service's scans (they reject with the pool's closed error; the next scan recreates it). Tying the pool to a service generation with an explicit CLI close is a small follow-up if maintainers want it.
- Worker spawn cost recurs: the first scan after process start spawns a worker, and the pool retires an idle worker after 60 s, so any scan after a minute of inactivity pays the spawn again. The spawn was not timed in isolation (the harness warms the pool before measuring), the `dist/` spawn path was not measured, and the 60 s retirement itself was not observed (no run waited 60 s).
- `wiki_search` tool calls longer than its 30 s deadline still fail, as on `main` (the deadline-ownership table shows it on all three trees); this PR changes where the 30 s is spent, not the budget.
- Errors other than vault boundary refusals lose their class and `code` across the pool boundary (message preserved, `WorkerTaskError` with code `failed`); `FsSafeError` loses `cause` and `details`. No caller inspected those fields.
- The worker-side cancellation checkpoint is a poll between pages; a single very large page is parsed to completion before the cancellation is observed, the same granularity `main`'s reader has.
- Narrowed public-entrypoint race coverage: `main`'s `query.reads.test.ts` swapped a page for an outside symlink from a thread-local fs-safe `beforeOpen` hook, which never fires in a worker. The branch keeps the exact-read and compiled-candidate refusals through the public entrypoints by placing the symlink before the read, covers the listing-then-swap race on `readWikiPagesTask`, and covers the pool's refusal rebuild on a scoped lookup; the basename route through `getMemoryWikiPage` is no longer exercised with a mid-read swap; since the merge that route is a one-page read on the calling thread again, where #171961's own cases cover it, and the id route through `getMemoryWikiPage` is the one not exercised with a mid-read swap. #171961's `query.path-lookup.test.ts` counted the full read through the same hook; since the merge its id-lookup-and-miss case asserts the one worker scan through the reader seam and the calling thread's opens, and its refused-page case swaps the page after the listing from that seam (Tests), so neither observes the worker's own opens.
- Identity: the suite's pool-versus-in-thread tests use the branch's own reader as the reference, so they prove the thread boundary, the segment merge and the resubmission merge are lossless, not identity with `main`; identity with `main` is shown by the 10,000-page, 20,000-page and on-disk compatibility comparisons above (every result object compared) and by the verbatim move of the scorer. No golden fixture captured from `main` lives in the test suite.
- Diagnostics label the new workers `other` (`src/infra/worker-diagnostic-script.ts` and `worker-request-kind.ts` keep a core allowlist of script names). Adding `query-reader.worker.js` there is a core edit left out of this plugin-local PR.
- Out of scope, follow-up: `compile.ts` still reads and parses the whole vault on the main thread, with link extraction and its own per-page `yieldToEventLoop`, after every `wiki_apply` and in the CLI process before a search. This PR moves query scans only.
- The built-Gateway runs call the tools through `POST /tools/invoke`, which runs the real `wiki_search` and `wiki_get` tools in the Gateway without a model turn; no agent turn or channel was involved. They used `ingest.autoCompile: false` to keep the vault without a digest, one query, HTTP `/healthz` as the concurrent client request, and a machine under heavy unrelated load; the 10,000-page searches hit the 30 s deadline on both trees for that reason.
- Not verified: Bun runtime behaviour of the worker entry and Windows path handling in the worker (the reader code is `main`'s, unchanged).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a sidebar session waiting on an exec or plugin approval grows to two lines because "Waiting for approval" is repeated under its title.

## User Impact

User impact: approval-waiting sessions stay on one line like question-waiting and failed sessions. The leading shield icon, its tooltip ("Waiting for approval" plus the request preview), the trailing attention marker, the hovercard, and section/parent attention bubbling are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Question attention and run failures (#156918) already skip the row subtitle because the leading icon tooltip or hovercard carries that detail. Approvals were the remaining attention kind that still wrote a subtitle. The subtitle resolver now treats approvals the same way, so lower-priority activity text does not appear either. The projection still treats approvals as operator-critical, so any held subtitle is cleared immediately.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI (dark theme), same session with a pending exec approval.

**Before** (row height 44px, subtitle present)

![Before: approval-waiting session shows a second "Waiting for approval" line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3826c433-c6cd-425d-b0d9-d332b642062d)

**After** (row height 30px, no subtitle)

![After: approval-waiting session stays on one line with the shield icon](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7817eb42-9c16-4a16-a148-9557a73df23a)

- `session-row-subtitle.test.ts`, `app-sidebar.people.test.ts` (attention cases now assert the single-line class and no subtitle for exec and plugin approvals, plus the existing aria-label tooltip), `app-sidebar-session-row-render.test.tsx`, `app-sidebar-session-projection.test.ts`: 175 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxfmt, oxlint on touched files: clean.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar approval rows and approval countdowns still created separate custom-element bridge roots even though every production caller renders with Solid.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Existing host tags, selectors, timer accessibility attributes, expiry behavior, modal-description updates, and lazy loading remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Render the sidebar row and countdown directly under their Solid callers, remove the nested props wrapper, and let the existing Solid owner dispose their clocks. Preserve the main approval-card bridge and the outer dialog's imperative `show()`/`dialogOpen` API.

The chat-footer fixture installs its clock mock before rendering. Direct Solid rendering samples time synchronously; the retired custom-element countdown waited for a microtask. This preserves the existing expiry assertion without depending on that retired scheduling behavior.

Production LOC across the three production files: **1,174 → 1,163 (−11)**. Test LOC across the three coupled files: **830 → 826 (−4)**.

## Evidence

Signed head `c6c563407f362a75e56e026c36c172a2ffe411dd` merges pinned main `7367b5b07f109fd56f7bf070688e40b5c295e354` to incorporate the shared jsdom tracker repair `5e4a1bed3a86187d42997946f62d5c2518be89d5`. There was no active merge request to cancel. The source change remains exactly six files, with every reviewed file and the full authored patch byte-identical to independently reviewed `f7610dc`. Production LOC remains **1,174 → 1,163 (−11)** and test LOC **830 → 826 (−4)**.

The direct approval owners/imports, rendering and mounting helpers, projections, translations, Solid compiler/configuration, and dependency inputs are unchanged. The separately inspected gateway-page-controller update changes only its host/controller types. The existing owned frozen install and source-only review are reusable; broad runtime proof remains tied to the new head.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current full CI | [Run 38646016884](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38646016884) completed for exact head `c6c5634` with `ci:full`. All three UI unit shards, all nine browser shards, Gateway shard 2, type/lint and strict performance passed. Gateway shard 1 failed the managed-image ordering case, so the aggregate gate is failed. The sole case and decode signature match newest scheduled main run `38648053570`. Native inherited-failure admission is being prepared; failed CI is not relabeled green. |
| Clean-checkout UI typecheck | **Passed once on prior clean head `8499012`** in 107 seconds; reused after inspection of unchanged authored and determining UI/compiler inputs. |
| Production Knip | **Passed once on final head `c6c5634`**, tree `93662a34e22043f4480b0b7047da9e88e3898c06`: exit 0 in **15m22s**. All 10 captured scan/wrapper PIDs are absent; head/tree remained unchanged and the checkout is clean. Heavy slot released. Existing frozen dependencies were reused; no repeated install or new lease. |
| Independent Codex review | Corrected-candidate source review was `scoped-clean` through P2, with no findings. Current six-file/full-patch equivalence was verified before the signed merge commit. Full-index binary patch SHA-256: `416f36987e01fb3be1ac6acb5b7398d86ca68a2b518f90a9cbf068bcba5bf80a`. |
| Formatting and whitespace | Authored file bytes remain identical to the formatted reviewed source; scoped `git diff --check` passed. |
| Approval card, dialog, and chat footer | **Passed on current head**: 8 approval-card, 15 approval-dialog, and 2 chat-footer cases (25 total), with each module recorded as passed. The repaired UI shard 3 passed all **608 files / 7,185 tests** (2 skipped), including the previously failing usage-retention assertion; no teardown failure. The earlier local approval-card attempt was inconclusive under filesystem contention and remains recorded as such. |
| Build and strict performance | **Current-head check passed**, job `116134073571` in run `38646016884`. The same runner built tested merge `ddc255c3fa06790b95c76528cd2f02dc0285207d` and base `b00ea8bab3529ccc7120795d06637bec64e21bbb`: startup JS **349,476 B gzip / 8 requests**; CSS **45,993 B gzip / 1 request**. Chat boot **1,763,357 → 1,763,409 B (+52 B)**; new-session boot **1,349,668 → 1,349,709 B (+41 B)**. Request counts and CSS bytes are unchanged; no new eager import or lazy-boundary change. No separate base startup-JS total is printed. No extra local build. |
| Visual contract | Existing host DOM and styles are preserved. No visible markup change or extra local build/capture battery under the polish wave's lighter proof rule. Existing synthetic CI failure captures were inspected locally. |
| Native landing | Prior mergeability timeout stopped before intent or dispatch. The failed head had no active merge request. Final-head Knip and source verification passed; fresh native review/preparation is running, followed by the authorized inherited-only admin route with exact-checkout and source evidence. |

### Current Gateway Failure

`Managed image ordering through real chat.send and history > keeps headings, managed images and trailing prose ordered live and after reload without duplicates` is the only failing case in real-Gateway shard 1 (`116134073524`). The supported classifier initially marked the job pre-existing by job name only; the exact-test comparison is now complete.

Newest scheduled main [run 38648053570](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38648053570), job `116140126251`, at `f62dd8e0c29fc8acd3836e604da97a280e4fa053` fails that same sole case with `locator.evaluateAll: EncodingError: The source image cannot be decoded`, at `assertDecoded:325:64` and the initial live decode at `348:15`, before ordering assertions. Both jobs report 1 failed / 19 passed files and 1 failed / 24 passed tests. Earlier scheduled main `38640790586` has the same failure.

The current failed job's retained log records checkout `ddc255c3fa06790b95c76528cd2f02dc0285207d`, whose ordered parents are baseline `b00ea8bab3529ccc7120795d06637bec64e21bbb` and exact PR head `c6c5634`. The new head includes the repair through an ordinary main merge, without a duplicate fix, rebase, or rerun-for-green.

### Earlier Uncertainty

The earlier widget-sandbox failure on `65e5652` remains unattributed: collapse timed out in the trusted-pointer helper after expansion. Subsequent complete browser passes do not establish a causal repair; the integrated widget change supplied diagnostics only. The exact-base diagnostic attempt reached its allocation limit without running a test. The local approval-card attempt likewise produced no assertion result before its authorized drain. prs.title: fix: preserve operator tasks across repeated restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: authenticated non-browser operator tasks can stop recovering after a restart when an inter-session steering message becomes the latest input.

## User Impact

CLI/API operator work can continue through repeated restarts without being mistaken for a new delegated request. The original operator identity and current access policy are still revalidated before execution; revoked authority cannot resume. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Non-browser authenticated operators legitimately use internal ingress. Recovery previously recognized retained human custody only for Control UI and channel ingress, so it could tombstone valid operator work with `delegated_authority_unavailable`. The source-policy helper now recognizes the retained operator claim and leaves exact claim matching and live authorization to the existing Gateway restoration owner.

This addresses a reproduced failure path; it does not establish the exact cause of the original historical incident. No cleanup, durability, or authorization policy was relaxed.

## Evidence

- Production-boundary regression fails before the fix with `delegated_authority_unavailable` and passes afterward.
- Two successive recoveries retain the original source; revoking the operator role before the second recovery prevents execution.
- 193 focused tests passed across the recovery store, operator runtime, and operator source suites; the two final-form regressions passed again.
- Core and affected-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review and AutoReview found no P0/P1 issues. The test uses real source capture, durable recovery, dispatch, and authorization restoration; provider execution is mocked. No live Gateway was restarted.

prs.title: fix(spawn-broker): keep target input that arrives before resource ownership
prs.body:
Closes #163509

## What Problem This Solves

The worker-side native resource attachment forwarded target input only after the factory admitted ownership:

```ts
// Keep the target's original port queue until the factory has installed its real receiver.
void initialized.promise.then(() => {
  target.on("message", (value: unknown) => { /* transmit resource-target */ });
});
```

A `MessagePort` delivers queued messages to whichever `message` listener attaches **first**, and `port.start()` drains the queue outright. Both are observable in plain Node:

```text
start() before handler -> late handler sees: []
untouched port      -> late handler sees: ["untouched"]
C listener1 (attached first):   ["C-early"]
C listener2 (attached 30ms later): []            # same queue, only the first listener wins
```

So input that arrives after the port exists but before ownership is admitted is received by the target port and never forwarded. Measured against the real client with a real broker socket, with the input posted before `resource-created`:

```text
observed on target port: [ 'early-input' ]      <- input reached the port
received by broker:      [ 'resource-attach' ]  <- never forwarded as resource-target
control (input posted after resource-created): [ 'resource-attach', 'resource-target' ]
```

The attachment had **no test coverage at all**: `attachBrokerNativeResource` appears in no `*.test.ts` / `*.test-support.ts`, and the 1,623-line lifecycle support layers replace the socket wholesale (`worker-native-lifecycle.runtime.test-support.ts:182` `connect: () => ({...})`). That is why the window went unnoticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collect target input from the first tick and forward it when ownership is admitted, instead of relying on the port still holding its queue:

- The listener is installed synchronously in `attachBrokerNativeResource`, so nothing can drain the queue first.
- Input arriving before `resource-created` is buffered locally and forwarded in order once admission lands, preserving the existing "factory admits ownership first" ordering.
- `dispose()`/`lose()` still tear the port down; no new lifespan.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

- Native worker input that arrives during broker startup is no longer silently dropped.
- No change to the ordering contract: nothing is transmitted as `resource-target` before the factory admits ownership.
- No schema, config, state, or protocol change. `MessagePort` is not a public API surface.

## Evidence

### Baseline RED (current main `0614328f729`, production file at base)

The new case where another consumer starts the port fails, and it fails on the missing forward:

```text
 × spawn broker native resource client > forwards input that arrived before another consumer started the port
   → expected [ { type: 'resource-attach', …(1) } ] to deep equally contain { Object (type, id, ...) }
   Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```

### Candidate GREEN (head `e14bbede1ef`)

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/process/spawn-broker/resource-client.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text
 ✓ attaches, forwards factory-admitted target input, and closes through the broker
 ✓ forwards input that arrived before another consumer started the port
 ✓ rejects a response identity that belongs to another attachment
 ✓ fails the attachment when the startup deadline passes without readiness
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Neighboring suites (unchanged behavior):

