prs.title: fix: decision_evaluate rejects choice and score questions on DeepSeek models
prs.body:
Related: #166486, #143819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: On a DeepSeek route, `decision_evaluate` rejects `choice` and `score` questions and any object `state` during local argument validation, so the decision provider is never called.

## User Impact

Agents on DeepSeek models can call `decision_evaluate` with all three question types and structured state, the same as on other providers. Before this change, only a `boolean` question with string or null `state` got through.

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek does not accept `anyOf`/`oneOf`, so OpenClaw flattens union schemas for that route. OpenClaw's local argument validation uses the flattened schema. Two flattening rules dropped valid input:

- A union that mixed object or array branches with other types kept only its first branch. The decision tool's `state` (string, object, array, or null) became `string | null`.
- When object branches defined the same property differently, the first definition won. The question's `criteria` kept the boolean branch's `{ true, false }` object, which rejected the choice map and the score array.

Both cases now drop the conflicting type constraint and keep the property's annotations. Branches that differ only in annotations still keep the first annotation. String-literal unions and primitive-only unions such as `string | integer` keep their current behavior. DeepSeek still receives no union keywords.

Tradeoff: On DeepSeek, these properties no longer carry a type hint. The owning tool still validates its own contract. `decision_evaluate` still rejects a `score` question whose `criteria` is an object, and the regression test covers that rejection.

## Evidence

I ran real `openclaw agent exec` turns on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with an isolated `HOME` and state directory, twice per build: with the tool exposed directly (`tools.toolSearch: false`) and through the default Tool Search `dispatch_action` path. A loopback OpenAI-compatible server registered as the `deepseek` provider asked for one `decision_evaluate` call with object `state` and three questions (`boolean`, `choice`, `score`). A loopback TypeSafe local server (`plugins.entries.typesafe.config.baseUrl`, `decisionModel: "typesafe/kev-latest"`) answered. TypeSafe calls a boolean question `noul`.

| Build | Direct tool | Tool Search (`dispatch_action`) | TypeSafe server |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` at 64ae50243 | `Validation failed for tool "decision_evaluate"`: `state: must be string`, `questions.area.criteria: must not have additional properties`, `questions.urgency.criteria: must be either object or null` | `Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:decision_evaluate": state: must be string; ... Expected input: { questions: { ... }; state: string \| null }` | never contacted |
| This PR | `status: "ok"` with answers for all three questions | `status: "ok"` with answers for all three questions | received `{ failed: noul, area: choice, urgency: score }` |

On both builds, the fake DeepSeek server confirmed that the `decision_evaluate` schema it received contained no `anyOf` or `oneOf`.

- The new regression test in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-tools.test.ts` uses the real `DecisionEvaluateInput` contract. It fails on `main` with `state: must be string` and passes with this change. `provider-tools.test.ts` and `provider-tools.nullable.test.ts` pass (34 tests).
- `check:changed` on this diff: core, core-test, extension and extension-test typechecks, lint, formatting and the boundary guards pass. Two gates fail on files this PR does not touch: the `OPENCLAW_*` environment variable budget (455 vs 454) and the Knip unused-export scan (8 exports elsewhere in the tree).

prs.title: fix: renew expired Sign in with ChatGPT credentials before fallback
prs.body:
Fixes #172563
Fixes #172562

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable model fallback when a Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC) access token expires, and prevents delayed OAuth responses from overstating that token's lifetime.

## User Impact

OpenClaw retries the selected SIWC model after one successful credential refresh; failed refreshes and unauthorized retries retain normal fallback. No configuration change or credential migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

SIWC uses the auth-profile OAuth manager without provider-exchange runtime state. Recovery now reaches that existing manager, forces renewal even when stored expiry is still in the future, and locks the recovery to the selected profile. The existing immediate-retry flag prevents repeated refresh retries. API keys, other providers/flows, and unrelated authentication errors keep their current behavior.

The shared SIWC login/refresh parser caps the relative expiry at a valid access JWT `exp`. These unverified claims can only shorten scheduling lifetime; identity verification, account binding, opaque-token support, and the existing five-minute pre-expiry margin remain intact. Native Codex login remains separately owned; credentials are not transferred between processes or profiles.

The model resolver now forwards its auth options together instead of duplicating each property. Production delta is +43/-24 (net +19): the remaining growth implements the bounded recovery branch and JWT validation. No new SDK export, configuration, schema, or detached/background effect is introduced.

## Evidence

- Confirmed both defects in main source and history: the recovery guard required runtime exchange state, and the SIWC parser used only response-time `expires_in` arithmetic. The affected owners were unchanged between task base `c3e8224adc895bbccc2b7d3dfe269d86c5f81a23` and inspected main `b9948b13604a`.
- PR CI is the test gate. Regressions cover `recovers expired SIWC auth without runtime exchange state (refresh fails: %s)`, `does not force-refresh unrelated auth`, `persists a forced model-auth plugin refresh before returning`, and `bounds refreshed credential expiry: $name`. The persistence test exercises the model resolver through the real OAuth manager; expiry cases use fixed synthetic tokens and no sleeps.
- Changed-file lint using the root oxlint configuration, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed. An initial core-tsconfig lint invocation could not resolve extension SDK types; the scoped syntax lint passed.
- Deslop: simplified duplicate model-auth option forwarding; no speculative compatibility or new refresh owner.
- Autoreview: Codex branch review against the task merge base returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The installed shared helper reviewed an isolated candidate snapshot before the task-branch commit; no tests ran during review.
- Local test execution, negative controls, local typechecks, and live proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No Gateway or Crabbox/Testbox lease was started. Local test wall times are therefore not measured; CI owns test results and timing.
- Merged current `origin/main` (`911726f8ed3c`) without rebasing before push. Exact-head [CI run 38647544247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38647544247) passed for `cc5c0f0267951c45e45e1e09d3abba35c53f33c2`: 43 successful jobs, 25 conditional skips, and no failures. All planned Node test shards, production/test typechecks, lint, build, and documentation checks passed; no CI retries were needed.

- Hosted Codex review completed without reported findings. ClawSweeper posted its maintainer opt-in notice only; no ClawSweeper P0–P2 findings were present.

prs.title: fix(gateway): omit media-store URIs from the workspace file projection
prs.body:
Fixes #150322.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI file panel offered an inbound chat attachment as an openable workspace file, and every click failed. `sessions.files.list` projected the assistant's `read` of `media://inbound/<id>` as a workspace entry with `missing: true`, and `sessions.files.get` answered `INVALID_REQUEST session_file_not_found` for that path. The attachment itself was healthy — the same bytes preview in the chat bubble — so the panel was advertising an action that could never succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The touched-file projection in `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:85-108` resolves every tool-argument path against the session root. `expandPath` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/path-utils.ts:33-47`) understands `file://` URLs, so an absolute `file://` path lands outside an out-of-tree root and is already excluded. A media-store identity had no such handling: `path.resolve(root, "media://inbound/x.png")` collapses the double slash and lands at `<root>/media:/inbound/x.png`, which is lexically inside the root. The entry survived the workspace filter, failed `stat`, and was reported as a missing workspace file.

Repair classification: **behavior-completing**. The projection already excludes `file://`, parent-relative, home and out-of-root shapes — `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:446` encodes exactly that contract — and the media-store URI was the one non-workspace shape that slipped through it.

The exclusion belongs at this projection boundary rather than inside the shared `resolveToCwd` (the `read` tool resolves `media://` URIs through it), and rather than granting the workspace file RPCs media-store access: the media store owns those bytes and already serves them through the authenticated `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` route (`src/gateway/control-ui-resource-routes.ts:7`). The predicate reuses the existing non-throwing scheme classifier `classifyMediaReferenceSource(...).isMediaStoreUrl` (`src/media/media-reference.ts:54`) instead of adding another URI guard.

## User Impact

The file panel no longer offers a dead attachment entry. Genuinely missing in-workspace files are still listed as missing, and the chat attachment preview is unchanged. `sessions.files.get` on a media URI still answers the same not-found error, so no wire contract changes: the URI was never an openable workspace path. Write paths are unaffected because `setSessionWorkspaceFile` only accepts a candidate that already exists as a file (`src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:555-570`), which the phantom path never does.

## Evidence

### Inherited required-check failure: `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` (2026-10-11)

The only red required lane on this head is a Control UI end-to-end timeout, and it is **not caused by this diff**:

- Failing case: `ui/src/e2e/chat-panel-layout.e2e.test.ts` › `Control UI chat panel layout` › `preserves live content and saved geometry across main, dock, focus, and narrow layouts` — `TimeoutError: locator.waitFor: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`, waiting for `[data-panel-slot="terminal"] openclaw-terminal-panel .tp-host canvas` (60× resolved to a hidden `<canvas>`).
- This PR's diff touches only `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts` and its two tests — no `ui/**` file.
- Independent witness on a different, unrelated PR: #169173 (`refactor(storage): reduce SQLite bookkeeping per turn`, no UI files) fails the **same** case with the **same** locator and the **same** 30 s timeout at 2026-10-11T15:21:00Z (job `114503482331`). Two unrelated diffs failing one canvas-visibility case in the same hour is an inherited lane failure, not a diff-caused regression.
- Per the review's own instruction ("repair only a demonstrated diff-caused failure"), no repair is attempted here.

### ### Rebase note (2026-10-11)

This revision's head is `2b57a7808702016484afcd8dbb031e78fd1621dc`, rebased onto `main` @ `3529142cc84` because the previous base (`9f049a640d5f0c22628747a926b8ebd29377a4a5`) predated a material amount of merged work. The rebase replayed the same commits with no conflicts and the patch is unchanged: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` still reports +57/-3 across 3 files. The proof receipts below were captured on the pre-rebase head and were not re-run on this base; CI re-runs on this head.


Handler-level: the real `sessions.files.list` and `sessions.files.get` handlers over the real touched-file projection chain (`collectTouchedFilesFromMessage` → `resolveTouchedFilePath` → `toSessionFileEntry`), with the suite's standard mocks for the session entry and the transcript reader (`sessions-files.test-support.ts`). The mocked reader returns the real reader's message-event shape, and nothing in the projection under test is mocked. The transcript read itself is not part of this defect — a `read` tool call carrying a media URI is the input, and the projection is what mishandles it. Before and after use the same input: an assistant `read` of `media://inbound/image---15547f7e.png` plus ordinary workspace paths. The projection code is byte-identical between the revision the before-state was captured on and `main` (`git diff --stat origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts` is empty; current `main` is `79121743a16`).

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.files.list` media entry | `{"path":"media://inbound/image---15547f7e.png","name":"image---15547f7e.png","kind":"read","missing":true}` | absent |
| In-workspace missing file | `{"path":"missing.txt","missing":true}` | unchanged |
| In-workspace real file | `{"path":"src/readme.md","missing":false,"workspacePath":"src/readme.md"}` | unchanged |
| `sessions.files.get` on the media URI | `INVALID_REQUEST session_file_not_found` | unchanged (still not a workspace path) |

The existing contract case "omits transcript paths outside the workspace without hiding missing workspace files" (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:446`) now carries the media-store URI in its input list.

- Red on unpatched `main`: `expected [ …(2) ] toHaveLength(3)` → received 4, failing at `sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:473`.
- Green with this change: 10 passed in `sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts`.
- Baseline on this host: the same suite without the change fails only the `git init -b` case at `:107` (local git 2.27 has no `--initial-branch`), so the failure list is identical with and without the change.
- Siblings (`sessions-files.preview`, `sessions-files.repository`, `sessions-files`, `agents-files`): 16 failed | 60 passed both with and without the change. The 16 are `fatal: not a git repository` fixture failures on this host — zero new failures.
- `oxlint` on both changed files: exit 0. `check-tsgo-core-boundary`: exit 0. Import-cycle check: 0 runtime value cycles.
- `tsgo:core` reports one error in the untouched `src/wizard/clack-prompter.ts` (`TS2305 ... CANCEL_SYMBOL`, dependency drift in this checkout); the changed files produce none.

Not covered: this change excludes only the `media://` store scheme. Other unhandled URI schemes can still project phantom entries; they are a separate follow-up, not claimed here.

### Test cost (`sessions-files` suite — this PR's only test touch)

Measured on this host (Node v24.18.0, `vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test.ts`, isolated worktree, shared dependency install; before = parent `4144ede2113`, after = head `6dbc9a3ad56`):

| Run | Before vitest duration | Before wall | After vitest duration | After wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 36.00s | 60.7s | 55.62s (cold transform cache) | 85.3s |
| 2 | 47.11s | 86.8s | 21.01s | 45.5s |
| 3 | — | — | 44.23s | 68.4s |

Both sides report `41 passed (41)` — the change adds one input entry to an existing case and no new test. Run-to-run variance on this host exceeds any before/after delta, and test execution is ≤10% of the suite duration (transform dominates at 56–78%), so the added guard has no measurable suite-cost impact.

CI on head `6dbc9a3ad56` (run `36964744772`): the changed-file shard `checks-node-changed-compact-large-10` finished in **1m37s** total; within it, shard `agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-7` ran this file alone with `41 passed`, vitest duration **4.71s** (tests 5%).

## Evidence: real Gateway + real Control UI, before/after

The handler-level evidence above isolates the defect. This section shows the same correction in the running product: a real Gateway process serving the real Control UI in Chromium, on one seeded session, with identical state and interactions in both runs — the only difference is this PR's guard.

| Frame | Files panel |
| --- | --- |
| Before | `3 read`: `media://inbound/proof-attachment---e29d1ac8-02e…` marked **Missing**, next to `missing-notes.md` and `notes.md` |
| After | `2 read`: the media-store entry is gone; the genuinely missing in-workspace file is still listed |

Before — ![Control UI Files panel listing the dead media-store entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof/150446/proof/150446/before-files-panel-media-entry.png)

After — ![Control UI Files panel with the media-store entry omitted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof/150446/proof/150446/after-files-panel-media-entry-omitted.png)

Both frames also show the chat attachment preview rendering unchanged, so the authenticated assistant-media route is untouched. The same real Gateway answered `sessions.files.list` over the wire:

```text
before (guard removed)  -> files[0] = {"path":"media://inbound/proof-attachment---e29d1ac8-….png","kind":"read","missing":true}
after  (this PR)        -> the media-store entry is absent; "missing-notes.md" (missing) and "notes.md" (present) remain
```

How the captures were produced:

- Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; real Gateway (`openclaw gateway --port 34567 --auth token --allow-unconfigured --bind loopback`) from an isolated `dist` build, serving the real built Control UI; Chromium driven by Playwright.
- State seeded only with production writers: `saveMediaBuffer` (real inbound media bytes in the media store), `upsertSessionEntry`, and `appendSessionTranscriptMessageByIdentity` (a user message carrying the media reference, plus assistant `read` calls for the media URI, an existing workspace file, and a genuinely missing in-workspace path).
- Build disclosure: this host's dependency set predates current `main` by 182 commits and `tsdown` fails on that drift, so both runs build from commit `50c6072e470`, whose `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts` and `sessions-files.ts` are byte-identical to `main` (`79121743a16`). AFTER is `bdab8e88449` (that base + this PR's guard); BEFORE is the same base with only the guard removed, everything else unchanged.
- Sanitization: the frames show isolated local paths only — no keys, tokens, IP addresses, or personal data.

## Impact Surface

| File | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:94-100` | Exclude media-store identities in `resolveTouchedFilePath` | All four call sites are read projections (list filter, relevance map, entry projection, get/set candidate list); `set` additionally requires an existing file, so no write target moves. |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:460-462` | Add the media-store URI to the existing exclusion contract case | None; strengthens an existing assertion rather than adding a parallel test. |

## Ownership

`.github/CODEOWNERS` does not route `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts` or `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts` to a restricted owner: the `src/gateway` secops entries cover `*auth*`, `*secret*`, `secrets*.ts`, `security-path*` and `resolve-configured-secret-input-string*` only.

## Compatibility

No configuration, schema, protocol or retention change. Only the `media://` store identity is excluded, and `sessions.files.get` keeps its existing not-found response for such a path.

## Unrelated CI failures on this head

None of the failing checks touches this diff; `openclaw/ci-gate` only aggregates them. Every failing job names a file this PR does not change:

| Check | Failing point |
| --- | --- |
| `check-lint-core-5` | `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts:623` (`typescript(unbound-method)`) |
| `checks-node-compact-large-2` | `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list.freshness.integration.test.ts` |

| `checks-node-compact-small-15` | `test/scripts/worktree-setup.test.ts` (`Cannot find module '…/scripts/lib/bundled-plugin-source-utils.mts'`) |
| `checks-node-compact-small-24` | `test/scripts/pr-operation-lock.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-small-26` | `test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts` |

prs.title: fix(line): retire promoted default-account credentials on setup rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #144545

LINE credential rotation after doctor's single-account promotion is a **silent no-op on current main**: setup reports success, but the promoted stale credential keeps being used.

The chain, all on shipped code:

1. LINE declares `singleAccountKeysToMove` with its credential keys (`extensions/line/src/setup-core.ts`), so doctor's single-account migration moves them into `accounts.default` and deletes them from the channel root.
2. A later default-account rotation goes through `patchScopedAccountConfig`'s default branch, which applies `clearFields` at the **channel root only** (`src/channels/plugins/setup-helpers.ts`) — the promoted stale credential in `accounts.default` is never touched.
3. LINE's resolver reads `accounts.default` ahead of the channel root for the default account (`extensions/line/src/accounts.ts`, candidates `[accountConfig, baseConfig]`), so the promoted pre-rotation credential keeps winning.
4. LINE's setup retires only the *complementary* form of each credential family (#132150), so a same-form stale value in `accounts.default` (e.g. a promoted inline token under a fresh inline write) survives even root-only clearing.

Net effect: an operator rotating a LINE channel access token — because it leaked, or to move it into a file or the environment — gets a successful-looking setup that keeps the old token active.

## Why This Change Was Made

Single-layer fix at the LINE setup owner (`extensions/line/src/setup-core.ts`):

- Retirement covers **both forms of each written credential family** at the channel root (not only the complementary form); the patch re-adds the written form after the clear.
- `patchLineAccountConfig` additionally retires the rotated fields from an existing promoted `accounts.default` record, constrained two ways (round-4 review):
  - **Credential fields only** — the helper also serves the DM-policy writer (`clearFields: ["allowFrom"]`), and clearing account policy fields could invalidate a saved record (`dmPolicy: "open"` losing its allowlist), which the previous root-only clear preserved.
  - **Resolver-exact record selection** — record selection now **reuses the shared account-lookup owner** (`resolveAccountKey` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/account-resolution`), which is exactly what LINE's resolver reaches through `resolveAccountEntry`. Reimplementing the comparison locally drifts from that contract and can clear a record the resolver never reads while the active stale credential survives.

The shared setup writer keeps its existing single-layer clearing contract: `src/channels/plugins/setup-helpers.ts` is **byte-identical to `main`** — no SDK caller outside LINE sees any behavior change.

Salvaged from the closed #132254: its Google Chat credential-selection work carried the unresolved review findings, but the review rounds there produced the red/green evidence that this LINE defect is live on main. This PR is the smallest slice that fixes LINE: no shared-helper change, no `credentialSourceFields` factory option, no resolver changes, no other channels touched.

## Fresh base — rebase rework

The prior head was 4593 commits behind `main` and `CONFLICTING`. `main` had since replaced the local `resolveExistingAccountKey` writer helper with the `resolveChannelAccountKey` / `resolveAccountKey` owner (`src/routing/account-lookup.ts`), and the old helper compared with `normalizeAccountId` (which sanitizes punctuation: `-default-` → `default`). The LINE-local comparison was therefore rewritten to **call the shared owner directly** instead of duplicating it, so the writer and the resolver can no longer diverge. The shared writer (`setup-helpers.ts`) and its suite are untouched and reverted to `main`.

This branch is a fresh base on current `main` with the same net production change (plus the LINE-only regression tests); `MERGEABLE` is restored.

## User Impact

- Before: rotating a promoted LINE credential (inline→file, inline→inline, file→file, →`--use-env`) silently kept the old token; the exposure the operator tried to close stayed open.
- After: the rotation retires the promoted stale value at both config layers, and the resolver selects the credential the operator just configured. Named accounts are untouched.

## Evidence

### Red/green — regression tests fail on pre-fix code, pass at head

Same test file, production file swapped between pre-fix `main` and this head (Docker `lexiflow-all`, Node v24.18.0, Debian 12):

```text
Pre-fix (setup-core.ts without the retirement; same file at this base):
  extensions/line/src/setup-core.test.ts     7 failed | 10 passed (17)
    # all seven promoted-rotation cases red for the intended reason
    # (stale promoted credential still resolver-selected); both controls green

At head (10dd989a943):
  extensions/line/src/setup-core.test.ts     17 passed (17)   # 7 existing + 10 new
```

The new LINE cases assert the **resolver-selected** credential (`resolveLineAccount`), not just config shape — e.g. pre-fix, rotating a promoted inline token to `--use-env` left `accounts.default.channelAccessToken` stale and the resolver kept selecting it. Record-selection coverage: a `Default` + `default` case-colliding map (exact record cleared, variant preserved), a variant-only map (cleared under its authored key), and a `-default-` + `Default` misleading-key map (only the record the resolver actually reads is cleared). A policy-preservation case proves a DM-policy write (`clearFields: ["allowFrom"]`) leaves the promoted record's saved policy untouched.

### Round-trip at head — promotion, rotation, reload

Real adapter (`lineSetupAdapter.applyAccountConfig`) + real resolver (`resolveLineAccount`) over a persisted config, Docker `lexiflow-all`, Node v24.18.0:

```text
STEP 1  fresh default setup (inline)             → root token PROOF_TOKEN_A
STEP 2  promoted shape: accounts.default = { name: "Main", channelAccessToken: PROOF_TOKEN_A, ... }
                                                 → resolver(default): PROOF_TOKEN_A
STEP 3  rotate default inline → PROOF_TOKEN_B
        accounts.default = { name: "Main" }      (promoted stale credential retired, name kept)
                                                 → resolver(default): PROOF_TOKEN_B ✓
STEP 4  rotate default to files
        accounts.default = { name: "Main" }
                                                 → resolver(default): PROOF_TOKEN_C (source: file) ✓
        persisted accounts.default on disk = { "name": "Main" }
```

Control — the same sequence against pre-fix production files:

```text
pre-fix: resolver selects PROOF_TOKEN_A   after inline rotation (STALE)
pre-fix: resolver selects PROOF_TOKEN_A   after file rotation   (STALE)
         accounts.default keeps { name, channelAccessToken: PROOF_TOKEN_A, channelSecret: ... }
```

The silent no-op from #144545 is reproduced end to end on pre-fix code and cleared at this head.

### CLI end-to-end at head — `channels add` → rotation → reload (2026-10-09, admission checks intact)

Full round-trip through the shipped `channels add` CLI entry (`src/entry.ts`) at head `10dd989a` (`extensions/line/src/setup-core.ts` sha256 `c2f4180dafdadfad…`), Node v24.18.0, Linux kernel 4.19, state + config on ext4. **The shared-state DB generation admission check (`src/state/openclaw-state-db-open.ts`) runs fully intact — zero source modifications anywhere in the tree** (file sha256 `dda5887212554922…`, pristine). Isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the resolver probe reloads the persisted config from disk after every step and resolves through the real `resolveLineAccount`.

Two environment notes, both shipped behavior, no code touched: the installed-service state-dir guard degrades to its designed warn path ("could not be verified") because this minimal environment exposes no user bus — the same degradation any CI container gets; and `OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off` selects the official JS fallback because kernel 4.19 predates `openat2`. (The earlier Docker attempt ran on a kernel 3.10 host, which predates `statx` entirely, so Node cannot observe a real birth time there and the generation check cannot pass on any filesystem — the proof moved to an environment where the intact check passes.)

```text
$ openclaw channels add --channel line --token PROOF_TOKEN_A --channel-secret PROOF_SECRET_A --name Main
Added LINE account "default".
$ openclaw channels add --channel line --account work --token PROOF_TOKEN_WORK --channel-secret PROOF_SECRET_WORK --name Work
Added LINE account "work".
persisted: accounts.default = { channelAccessToken: PROOF_TOKEN_A, channelSecret: PROOF_SECRET_A }
           accounts.work    = { enabled: true, channelAccessToken: PROOF_TOKEN_WORK, ... }
resolver(default) = PROOF_TOKEN_A (tokenSource=config)

$ openclaw doctor --yes        # doctor single-account promotion pass; account already in promoted shape
→ resolver(default) = PROOF_TOKEN_A (unchanged)

$ openclaw channels add --channel line --token PROOF_TOKEN_B --channel-secret PROOF_SECRET_B   # inline rotation
Added LINE account "default".
persisted: accounts.default = {}          ← promoted stale credential retired
           root = { channelAccessToken: PROOF_TOKEN_B, channelSecret: PROOF_SECRET_B }
resolver(default) = PROOF_TOKEN_B (tokenSource=config) ✓

$ openclaw channels add --channel line --token-file files/token.txt --secret-file files/secret.txt   # file rotation
persisted: accounts.default = {}, root = { tokenFile, secretFile }
resolver(default) = PROOF_TOKEN_C (tokenSource=file) ✓   (file contents: PROOF_TOKEN_C)

accounts.work = { PROOF_TOKEN_WORK, ... } untouched throughout.
```

Pre-fix control — the identical CLI flow in the same intact-check environment with only `setup-core.ts` swapped to its merge-base version reproduces the #144545 silent no-op end to end through the CLI:

```text
after inline rotation:  root = { PROOF_TOKEN_B, ... } but accounts.default keeps { PROOF_TOKEN_A, ... }
                        resolver(default) = PROOF_TOKEN_A   (STALE)
after file rotation:    root = { tokenFile, secretFile }, accounts.default keeps PROOF_TOKEN_A
                        resolver(default) = PROOF_TOKEN_A   (STALE)
```

### Blast radius — shared writer untouched

`src/channels/plugins/setup-helpers.ts` and its suite are byte-identical to `main`; sibling `clearFields` callers (clickclack, buzz, nextcloud-talk, slack, zalo, matrix, nostr) see zero behavior change by construction. The LINE-local retirement only activates for a default-account write that passes credential `clearFields` while an `accounts.default` record exists.

### Lint / types

```text
oxfmt --check (2 changed files)         clean
tsgo tsconfig.json (prod lane)          exit 0
tsgo tsconfig.extensions.json           exit 0
```

### Test cost

Per `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md` (cost budget), measured at head `10dd989a` on 2026-10-09 (UTC), single worker (`--maxWorkers=1`, vitest v5, Docker `lexiflow-all`, Node v24.18.0):

```text
extensions/line/src/setup-core.test.ts — 17 tests
  cold run   Duration 4.04s (wall 4.9s)    tests 8%
  warm run   Duration 2.12s (wall 2.9s)    tests 11%
```

Within the <5s per-file target; no contract here needs more.

CI seconds (run `36593929774`, this head, 2026-09-29): the file runs in shard `changed-extensions-config-1` of job `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` — shard total 13 files / 188 tests in 42.92s; job wall 149s.

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: a default-scope LINE credential rotation now retires the promoted `accounts.default` credential, so `resolveLineAccount` selects the rotated credential instead of the stale promoted one.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker `lexiflow-all` (Debian 12), Node v24.18.0, over the real adapter + resolver with real token files on disk.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/setup-core.test.ts
  # CLI round-trip at head (see "CLI end-to-end at head" above):
  openclaw channels add --channel line --token PROOF_TOKEN_A --channel-secret PROOF_SECRET_A
  openclaw doctor --yes
  openclaw channels add --channel line --token PROOF_TOKEN_B --channel-secret PROOF_SECRET_B
  openclaw channels add --channel line --token-file files/token.txt --secret-file files/secret.txt
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: inline rotation resolves `PROOF_TOKEN_B`; file rotation resolves `PROOF_TOKEN_C` (source: `file`); `accounts.default` keeps only its non-credential fields; pre-fix control keeps resolving `PROOF_TOKEN_A` after both rotations; `Tests 17 passed (17)` vs pre-fix `7 failed | 10 passed`. The same outcomes hold through the shipped `channels add` CLI entry at head (GREEN), and the pre-fix CLI control keeps resolving the stale `PROOF_TOKEN_A` after both rotations (RED).
- **Observed result after fix**: rotated credentials win at both config layers; promoted non-credential fields, saved account policy (`dmPolicy`/`allowFrom`), and named accounts are preserved; misleading-key maps clear only the record the resolver reads.
- **What was not tested**: the live LINE Messaging API (the defect is entirely in config write/read ordering, before any network call). The CLI write path is covered end to end with the shared-state DB generation admission check fully intact and zero source modifications — environment notes are disclosed in the CLI section above.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? Yes — rotations of promoted LINE credentials now actually take effect (previously a silent no-op). No change when no `accounts.default` record exists; no change for named accounts.
- Config/env/migration change? No — config shape unchanged; only stale duplicate values are retired at write time.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-execution change? Secrets-adjacent by intent: a superseded credential is now removed instead of silently remaining active.
- Highest-risk area: none beyond the LINE setup path — the shared setup writer is untouched; the LINE-local clearing is credential-fields-only (a DM-policy write cannot invalidate a saved account policy record) and delegates record selection to the same account-lookup owner the resolver uses (covered by resolver-level tests: case collision, authored-key variant, misleading normalized key).

prs.title: fix(config): align dry-run preview with the commit's roster guard
prs.body:
Fixes #133895 ## What Problem This Solves `openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json --dry-run` reports `Dry run successful` (exit 0) while the equivalent committing write is rejected with `Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: main.` (exit 1). A preview that claims a write will succeed, when the same write is refused, misleads scripts and operators into trusting a change that cannot be persisted. Maintainer-flagged follow-up: #133895 was explicitly left open by #133920 (merged) — "Two named follow-ups remain. #133895 tracks an empty-roster preview that accepts a request the root writer rejects." ## Why This Change Was Made The dry-run branch (`src/cli/config-cli-runner.ts`) ran only the write-topology projection (`prepareConfigWriteTopology`) before validation, so the committing writer's roster-retention guard (`assertCanonicalAgentRosterRetainsEntries` inside `resolvePersistCandidateForWrite`) was never armed for previews. This change adds a preview-only persistence probe that mirrors the commit exactly: 1. **Same routing order** — the probe consults the commit owner's include-write decision (`resolveConfigIncludeWriteBoundary`, the same candidacy the committing `tryWriteIncludeOwnedConfigMutation` uses) on the **pre-topology** candidate with the same normalized explicit paths the committing write receives, because the commit selects the include writer before root topology preparation. An edit owned by an authored `$include` skips the root writer's projection, exactly like the commit. 2. **Same routing inputs** — the probe passes the committing write's `persistCanonicalAgentRoster` write option to the routing decision, not the topology-derived flag. Topology preparation derives `persistCanonicalAgentRoster` from roster shape (e.g. an `ownership: "explicit"` agents include gaining a second entry), but the committing CLI never supplies that derived value when it selects the include writer — feeding it into routing made preview refuse an agents-include roster expansion that commit accepts. 3. **Same guard, root-owned writes only** — root-owned previews run the shared persistence projection (`resolvePersistCandidateForWrite`), arming the roster-retention guard — reusing the existing owner's guard instead of adding an empty-roster special case or weakening commit protection (the direction #133895's body specifies). 4. **Same invocation order** — the probe runs after `validateConfigMutation`, matching the commit (validation errors surface before persistence checks). This also keeps pathological inputs on the schema-error path: validation rejects them before any persistence projection runs. 5. **Same no-op short circuit** — the committing command reports `No change` before persistence, so no-op previews skip the probe instead of rejecting an include-owned explicit set. Classification: `behavior-completing` — preview now reports the same refusal the commit already enforced, without refusing edits the commit accepts. ## User Impact - `--dry-run` on a guarded roster removal now fails with the same `Config write would drop agent roster entries...` error and exit 1 as the committing write, instead of falsely reporting success. - `--dry-run` on an edit owned by an authored `$include` previews successfully — including edits that topology preparation reshapes at the root (e.g. `session.store` beside `agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId`), roster expansion into an explicit-ownership `agents` include, and no-op assignments — exactly matching the committing write. - Genuinely allowed root mutations still preview successfully; the existing preview assertions still pass. ## Evidence ### Real CLI proof (packaged `dist` binaries, exact head `6091c72e1cc` vs base `9658ea8d8af`) Refreshed 2026-10-08 with the admission-valid fixture. Current main rejects legacy `agents.entries.*.default` markers at config admission (`Legacy agents.entries default markers need explicit surface owners`), so the 2026-09-22 transcript's `default:true` fixture no longer reaches the changed owner. Every scenario below uses `{"agents":{"entries":{"main":{}}}}` (or no root roster), which passes admission on both builds. Environment: Node v24.18.0 on the remote docker runner (`lexiflow-all`), `dist` built from each tree with `build-all.mts` on 2026-10-08 (both report `OpenClaw 2026.9.8`; the in-container `.buildstamp` records `head: null` because the build host has no git — the trees were synced from the exact SHAs above). Each scenario uses an isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, one real CLI process per invocation (`node dist/index.js config ...`), no mocks or output/exit interception. `OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off` because the host kernel (3.10) predates `openat2` — fs-safe's documented JavaScript fallback, as in earlier rounds. (The `ui:build` phase fails on this host over a stale `ui/node_modules` missing `jsonc-parser`; the CLI dist is complete, and the failing phase is unrelated to the config CLI.) **A. Empty-roster replace on the admission-valid `main:{}` fixture — RED on base, GREEN on this head** config: `{"agents":{"entries":{"main":{}}}}`, root config sha256 `a2dbb0aa4ecc…f8134` before every run ```text base (9658ea8d8af): $ openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json --dry-run Dry run successful: 1 update(s) validated against …/openclaw.json. exit=0 <- preview claims the write is fine $ openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json --dry-run --json { "ok": true, "operations": 1, "inputModes": ["json"], "checks": { "schema": true, "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true }, "refsChecked": 0, "skippedExecRefs": 0 } exit=0 <- JSON preview also reports success $ openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: main. exit=1 <- commit refuses: preview/commit mismatch BYTES-UNCHANGED: yes this head (6091c72e1cc): $ openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json --dry-run Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: main. exit=1 <- preview refuses with the guard's own diagnostic $ openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json --dry-run --json { "ok": false, "operations": 1, "inputModes": ["json"], "checks": { "schema": true, "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true }, "refsChecked": 0, "skippedExecRefs": 0, "errors": [ { "kind": "schema", "message": "Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: main." } ] } exit=1 <- completed validation summary preserved (operations 1, schema check true); the retention refusal is appended classified "schema" (not "conflict") $ openclaw config set agents.entries '{}' --replace --strict-json Config write would drop agent roster entries without an explicit deletion: main. exit=1 BYTES-UNCHANGED: yes (root config sha256 identical before/after every run) ``` **G. Agents-include roster expansion under explicit ownership — accepted on both, no false refusal** root config `{"agents":{"$include":"agents.json"}}`, include `{"ownership":"explicit","entries":{"main":{"name":"before"}}}` — identical on base and this head: ```text $ openclaw config set agents.entries.work '{"name":"worker"}' --strict-json --dry-run Dry run successful: 1 update(s) validated against …/openclaw.json. exit=0 root unchanged: YES include unchanged: YES $ openclaw config set agents.entries.work '{"name":"worker"}' --strict-json Updated agents.entries.work. Change will apply without restarting the gateway. exit=0 root unchanged: YES include now holds both "main" and "work" ``` **I1. Include-owned scalar edit — identical on both builds** root `{"agents":{"entries":{"main":{}}},"logging":{"$include":"logging.json"}}`, include `{"level":"info"}`: ```text $ openclaw config set logging.level '"debug"' --strict-json --dry-run Dry run successful: 1 update(s) validated against …/openclaw.json. exit=0 root unchanged: YES include unchanged: YES $ openclaw config set logging.level '"debug"' --strict-json Updated logging.level. No gateway restart needed. exit=0 root unchanged: YES include now { "level": "debug" } ``` **N. No-op include-owned assignment — identical on both builds** ```text $ openclaw config set logging.level '"info"' --strict-json --dry-run # include already says "info" Dry run successful: 1 update(s) validated against …/openclaw.json. exit=0 include unchanged: YES $ openclaw config set logging.level '"info"' --strict-json No change exit=0 include unchanged: YES ``` Environmental noise, identical in both dists: a best-effort `Config health-state write failed: ENOENT … openclaw-state.worker.mjs` warning (the health-state sidecar resolves its directory from the process cwd rather than `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; both builds behave identically), and — only in the base dist's include scenario — a whatsapp `persistedAuthState` module warning caused by the renamed `dist-r6-main` directory confusing a `dist-runtime` fallback path. Neither touches config write routing.
Historical transcript (2026-09-22, head 094424f8aa vs main 43247c9b2, legacy default:true fixture — superseded by the run above because current admission rejects that fixture before the changed owner runs) The 2026-09-22 run demonstrated the same preview/commit parity with `{"agents":{"entries":{"main":{"default":true}}}}` on the September trees: preview RED on main (`Dry run successful`, exit 0, `ok: true`), GREEN on the PR head (refusal with the guard's diagnostic, `ok: false` + appended `kind: "schema"` error), bytes unchanged, and the same G/I1/N controls. The scenario logic is unchanged; only the fixture's admission validity moved with main.
### Regression tests (exact head, remote docker runner) `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on Node v24.18.0, `lexiflow-all:latest`, `OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off` (same kernel reason): ```text src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts + config-cli.roster-preview.integration.test.ts 61 passed (2 files) — the five preview/commit parity tests moved verbatim into the sibling file (the roster file sat exactly at the 1000 counted-line cap): ✓ rejects emptying the roster in preview just like the commit (#133895) ✓ previews an include-owned edit without tripping the root persistence guard ✓ previews an include-owned edit that topology preparation reshapes at the root ✓ previews a no-op include-owned assignment without persistence rejection ✓ previews an agents-include roster expansion under explicit ownership src/cli/config-cli.test.ts + config-cli.integration.test.ts 245 passed (245), including: ✓ reports schema errors for deeply nested replacement values without an engine failure ``` Rebased head `6091c72e1cc` (2026-10-08): the four preview fixtures moved from the legacy `{ main: { default: true } }` form to the admission-valid `{ main: {} }`, because current main rejects legacy `default` markers at config admission and the old fixtures never reached the roster guard. Scenario intent is unchanged; the strengthened empty-roster regression also asserts the appended error category `{ kind: "schema" }`. Re-verified on the rebased head (bare vitest, `vitest.cli.config.ts`, `--maxWorkers=1`, remote docker runner, 2026-10-08): **27 passed (2 files)** in 64.9 s. Full CI on `6091c72e1cc` is green (all `checks-node-*`, `checks-ui-e2e`, and security lanes SUCCESS). RED check: the new parity tests fail on the previous heads and pass on this head — the agents-include expansion test fails on `fa9351daeda` (routing fed the topology-derived flag) with a preview-only `Config write would flatten $include-owned config at agents...` refusal while the commit accepts; the deeply nested schema test fails with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` on every earlier revision of this branch (projection ran pre-validation). - tsgo core lane: no errors in the changed files. - `git diff --check` — clean. ### Test cost After the line-cap split, the changed test surface is two files (`config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` restored to its grandfathered base content, plus the new `config-cli.roster-preview.integration.test.ts` holding the five preview tests). Measured with the policy command on one worker, exact head `094424f8aa`: | Where | Command / environment | Wall | Vitest | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Remote docker runner (`lexiflow-all`, Node v24.18.0, `OPENCLAW_FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off`) | `run-vitest run src/cli/config-cli.roster-preview.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | **139.2 s** | 129.40 s (shard 136.70 s) | Result: **61 passed (2 files)**, exit 0 (2026-09-22). Test content is identical to the pre-split single file, so the per-file cost shape is unchanged; CI seconds for the new head will be recorded from its run (previous head: `agentic-cli` shard, 386 files in 728.59 s, this file's span 54.2 s, [job 106342251486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35602512957/job/106342251486)). ### Scope and risk - Production: `src/cli/config-cli-runner.ts` — dry-run branch only; committing behavior untouched. - Tests: `src/cli/config-cli.roster-preview.integration.test.ts` (new sibling holding the preview/commit parity tests) — `config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` is byte-identical to main. - Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the commit owner's `resolveConfigIncludeWriteBoundary` routing decision and the existing `resolvePersistCandidateForWrite` projection — no new validator, option, config key, or persistence policy. - Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Preview only.

prs.title: feat(discord): auto-name threads after a conversation threshold
prs.body:
Continued in #160873. This duplicate is closed; the validated fixture repair is now on the original PR at `40c6a070c768e414bc4588a9757b5f644f782337`.

Related: #160865. Historical follow-up to #160873 and #171389.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord threads can retain generic names after their conversation makes the topic clear.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `channels.discord.thread.autoName`: `false`/`0` disables naming by default, `true` uses five admitted messages, and a positive integer sets the threshold. Per-account overrides are supported. Eligible new threads receive one concise title using their routed agent and current access policy; manual renames are preserved.

A bounded human/agent transcript is sent to the selected model and is not persisted. Worker-backed claims expire after 24 hours, with a durable two-attempt account/parent budget per ten minutes. Maintainer product acceptance of the optional setting, model processing, and persisted lifecycle remains outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord plugin reuses existing admission, conversation routing and bindings, isolated conversation-label generation, REST scheduling, and SQLite workers. Human authorization survives eviction of their text from the recent transcript window and remains subject to fresh access checks.

This replacement includes the previous routing and threshold fixes and repairs their CI regression: two existing `DiscordLivePolicy` test fixtures omitted the newly required `isConfigCurrent` callback. Both now explicitly describe their fixed configuration. Production behavior and existing test assertions are unchanged by this corrective commit.

## Evidence

- The [failed exact-head CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38640481573/job/116122234118) reports precisely two TS2741 errors for the missing fixture callback. Its CI failure table classifies this as **new**. Both displayed `openclaw/ci-gate` failures reflect that same typecheck failure; the security workflow explicitly reports that the CI gate did not pass.
- At `aecbedbb0522f00e6595484cc855155636748ee5`, the full extension-test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, the CI project) passes after the unchanged baseline reproduced both original TS2741 errors. All 36 tests in both changed files pass in secretless, network-disabled Node 24.19.0 Docker; wall time 48.92 seconds, with 0.125 seconds of listener tests and 0.027 seconds of modal policy-deadline tests. Focused lint, formatting, staged-content guard, and diff checks pass. New-head CI timings remain pending.
- A fresh independent P0-P2 review of the fixture repair returned `scoped-clean`.
- Historical feature validation at `b3edf25833476c34bbb0e1d0d2eb2a08dbc141d2`: all 73 focused tests across seven files, production and targeted regression typechecks, lint/format, SDK checks, supported JavaScript runtime build, and isolated Discord plugin startup passed. The completed [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38640481573) passed its other selected checks; test types caused its failure.
- Prior live Discord threshold-rename and released-data compatibility observations at `f2b5c61988be2af10c7f6a5880790ba2f6b61c6f` are documented in the earlier PR. Those observations are historical; this CI fixture repair makes no new live-service claim.
- [Current-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38650469792) is running at publication. No CI rerun, assertion weakening, type suppression, or baseline change is used for this repair.

prs.title: fix(mcp): release event request callbacks after completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed MCP Events requests retaining their transport callbacks, and removes the four suppression entries that broke main’s lint inventory after #165399.

## User Impact

Completed requests release their callback captures. Errors retain a sanitized diagnostic cause without exposing credential-bearing URLs or remote response bodies. Authorization, MCP 2 request metadata, HTTP/SSE behavior, deadlines, and updates are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK Transport contract uses callback properties. Bind them as one typed set and retire them after transport closure and send settlement. The request owner also normalizes transport failures at the existing redaction boundary; retaining the raw caught error as cause would expose fields that boundary deliberately removes.

The labeler and typed-hook inventories are repaired separately. The intentional live-fixture Knip entry is covered by #172574. The unrelated provider-owner sort suppression is addressed separately by #172599.

## Evidence

- Before the production change: both JSON/SSE callback-retirement checks and the sanitized-cause regression fail (3 failures, 6 passes).
- After: 99 request/transport/native authority/subscription lifecycle cases pass across four shards with `--maxWorkers=1`; every original case and assertion remains.
- Core production types, targeted types, strict lint, boundary lint, formatting, and P2 review pass.
- The unchanged suppression inventory removes all MCP request entries; its remaining failure is solely the provider-owner sort finding addressed by #172599.

This is local boundary proof with synthetic HTTP responses, not live signed-callback qualification. PR CI supplies broad exact-head proof. No new suppression, allowlist, dependency, schema, or public SDK export.

prs.title: docs: add Pethost one-click deploy guide
prs.body: Closes #171391 ## What Problem This Solves Readers who deploy OpenClaw from Pethost's one-click template have no page that says where its gateway token is kept and where to run the device approval for the first browser. ## User Impact User impact: readers who deploy OpenClaw from Pethost's template can follow one guide from the template to a connected Control UI, including the gateway token and the first browser's approval. ## Why This Change Was Made The guide follows the shape of the Northflank and Railway pages. Its navigation entry and its card on `/vps` are each added at their alphabetical place, `docs/.i18n/glossary.zh-CN.json` has the page title, and `docs/docs_map.md` is untouched. Docs-only: no code, config, schema or runtime changes. The template pins the official image at 2026.10.3 (the current release today), generates `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, keeps `/home/node/.openclaw` and `/home/node/.config/openclaw` on named volumes, and on the first start writes `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` for the project's HTTPS address and `gateway.trustedProxies` for Pethost's proxy network. Inside the container the Gateway listens with `--bind lan`, as a Docker setup must; the port is not published, so it is reached only through the HTTPS proxy, with token auth and device pairing on. ## Evidence I work on Pethost. The path as it runs today, on a Pethost test machine on 2026-10-13 with OpenClaw 2026.10.3: 1. The project created from the template deployed, and its health check (`/healthz`) passed. 2. The Control UI at the project's address asks for the gateway token. 3. After `openclaw devices list` and `openclaw devices approve ` in the service's terminal, the Control UI connects. The screens above are from an automated pass in headless Chrome. I then went through the guide by hand in a browser, end to end, on Pethost: it works as written. Docs checks: `markdownlint-cli2` with `config/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc` reports 0 issues on the changed pages, `scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` passes against the base (and fails without the glossary entry), and `git diff --check` is clean. The link and anchor check (`pnpm docs:check-links:anchors`) was not run locally (no full install); CI is left to run it.

prs.title: fix: avoid redundant PR head fetching during preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant PR-head fetching during final preparation verification, which can trigger another expensive Git connectivity scan even when the exact authenticated commit is already retained locally.

## User Impact

Maintainers avoid one unnecessary canonical fetch in the preparation workflow. There is no change to the product, public API, or required operator configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Final publication verification now uses the retained PR ref already owned by head acquisition. The existing acquisition owner still authenticates the live PR identity before and after acquisition, preserves checked-out-branch refusal, and fetches canonically when the retained ref cannot be reused. Prepared-tree comparison and publication receipts retain their existing authority.

## Evidence

Exact-head [CI run 38639883274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38639883274) passed for `3ae03ab8fb05f28184e6be2a8566fb825d8b6eed`, including the SDK boundary, test, lint, and type checks. The original local deadline failures below remain preserved.

The full supervised-preparation regression failed on the original implementation because it fetched the immutable PR head twice. With this change it passes with exactly one fetch, all three fresh main checkpoints, and exact preparation stamps. This proves the fetch reduction; the local runs do not establish a timing speedup.

The focused run finished with 20 passing tests and seven unchanged 120-second deadline failures (56 tests outside the selection). Passing cases cover canonical fallback, missing/failed/dangling head acquisition, checked-out and rebasing branch refusal, stale pull refs, PR identity drift, and the complete supervised preparation. Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, shell syntax, whitespace checks, and an independent review passed.

The seven local timeouts remain unresolved and are recorded for native review. A host sample during the run showed 0% idle and load averages above 128 on 32 CPUs, but contention has not been established as the sole cause. No timeout was raised and no test was rerun for a passing result; exact-head PR CI remains required.

<details>
<summary>Original local deadline failures</summary>

Each case reported the existing 120000 ms test deadline, without an assertion mismatch. Reported case duration includes surrounding work:

- `reuses the exact local PR commit without fetching or changing checkpoints` — 179866 ms.
- `review-init acquires the authenticated head despite a stale pull ref` — 148537 ms.
- `review-checkout-pr acquires the authenticated head despite a stale pull ref` — 140081 ms.
- `prepare-run acquires the authenticated head despite a stale pull ref` — 158751 ms.
- `rejects PR oid drift during prepare-init acquisition without changing preparation stamps` — 144254 ms.
- `retains the publication receipt and releases the drained lock on mismatched receipt ownership` — 169967 ms.
- `retires prior publication evidence only after a fresh reviewed preparation` — 375041 ms.

The single final run used `pnpm test test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the focused case-name selection covering retained-head reuse, canonical fetching, branch refusal, supervised preparation, publication receipts, prior-evidence retirement, identity drift, and authenticated-head acquisition. The test process exited 1 after 3140.77 seconds; every original failure remains preserved.

</details>

prs.body:
Closes #172429

## What Problem This Solves

The chat Details inspector spreads useful session context across separate controls, while its dark floating surface and redundant desktop header take attention away from the conversation.

## User Impact

Users can inspect the workspace, branch, model, context usage, changes, helpers, automations, and task progress together in a lighter panel with subtle section dividers. The desktop Details toggle opens and closes it without a duplicate title or close button; mobile retains an explicit close control. No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing session data and actions in collapsible Environment, Context, Changes, and background-task sections. Preserve the adaptive dock/popover behavior, move the popover closer to the header, and keep progress actions independent. Hiding progress also closes the floating inspector so its Undo toast remains reachable.

## Evidence

- 13 focused component tests cover environment/context data, disclosure retention, desktop toggling, keyboard dismissal, mobile close and focus return, and distinct progress actions.
- Production-renderer mocked-Gateway E2E covers the complete docked, floating, dark, narrow, side-panel, and independently scrolling flows.
- UI typecheck, focused lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, and English copy baseline validation.
- Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings, including a fresh review of the CI correction.
- Corrected stale desktop-close E2E callers to use the visible Details toggle. The seven initially failing CI files now pass locally (47 tests).
- Reproduced and fixed a desktop-to-mobile resize regression: an already-open inspector no longer covers the persistent Panels header. The production-renderer regression failed before the fix and passes after it.
- The narrow pre-PR publication row now uses the same wrapping limit as published PR rows. The existing 900px/300px browser test failed before the fix and all seven cases pass after it; no assertion was weakened. [Before/after evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172436#issuecomment-6180105777).
- Integrated current `main` after CI exposed the already-fixed missing activation-hint file in the PR tooling inventory (`51afdbea12bb4bd`); no duplicate tooling repair.
- [Mobile resize before/after evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172436#issuecomment-6175679828).
- Exact-head CI run `38650157809` is failed on three independently reproduced baseline assertions: WebKit automation-hovercard Tab focus and both session-link reconnect request-count cases. All reproduce on the CI checkout’s protected-main parent `6dc4f1b5cf5` without this PR, with unchanged owning source. Landing uses the documented inherited-only exception; these checks are not claimed green. The Details Chromium/browser and production-renderer checks pass.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop sidebar refresh loops with legacy session participants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes continuous sidebar reloads on personal gateways when legacy sessions contain other participants. The loop can make sidebar controls unusable and flood the gateway with identical session-list requests.

## User Impact

Chat and sidebar filtering settle normally, and legacy conversations stay visible. Explicit owner selections still apply, including owners with no matching sessions. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar used participant visibility in filtered rows to decide whether to apply the owner filter. Applying the filter could remove those rows and reverse that decision. Query selection now uses the gateway's complete owner inventory; participant information continues to control attribution display.

The model-picker browser fixtures also unmount their Lit renderer before removing their container. Removing only the DOM left a 300-option picker reacting to later tests and caused the agent-menu CI timeout. All four model-picker behavior cases and their assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

Current head `8466519217a6dcb82e7288ba20131aea8c512844` passed [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38650937293): all 28 jobs, including all three UI shards, browser E2E, performance, lint, types, and security. The additional CI repair changes only test fixture ownership. Original product proof below is reused because all three owner-query fix files are unchanged.

- Synthetic browser reproduction on canonical main: 283 `sessions.list` requests in two seconds, without gateway events. The same fixture with the fix settles at two total requests across six seconds, including one Chat-pane request.
- Base controls settle when selecting All or removing only the legacy row's participant information. A two-owner inventory also settles.
- Regression tests fail on the base for visible and truncated legacy participants and a same-ID human/agent owner. All 122 focused sidebar tests pass with the fix.
- Independent code review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Independent browser validation passed all five clauses: stable idle requests; preserved draft and selection; All/My filter changes; an explicit empty owner; and one refresh after a real list invalidation. Five unrelated presence updates and menu toggles caused no further requests.

Changed-file lint, formatting, UI and affected test type checks pass. The broader changed-check command remains red for the existing environment-variable budget and unused exports in 12 unchanged files. No failing check is represented as passing.

Attached before/after screenshots and raw browser recordings use synthetic data only. Request counts above are measured by the mock Gateway, not inferred from video. This proves the sidebar feedback bug; it does not establish the cause of every native WebKit freeze.

<details>
<summary>Test scope and audit</summary>

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.owner-query.test.ts ui/src/components/session-owner-filter-controller.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.personal-agent-scope.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.sessions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

Four files, 122 passing tests, 10.15 seconds wall time. The final four-regression run passes in 2.92 seconds wall time. The first exact-head CI run failed two browser cases. The agent-menu timeout was traced to an abandoned model-picker renderer. A minimal ordered replay on unchanged base took 31.63 seconds for the menu test; explicit renderer teardown reduced it to 0.815 seconds. The repaired candidate passes the original 23-file worker sequence, 226 tests in 41.82 seconds; the agent-menu case fell from 48.38 seconds to 0.654 seconds. Targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent P0-P2 review is clean.

The separate RTL390 occlusion failure is inherited: [PR #172081 CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38594619483/job/115969252930) reported the identical `[false,true,false,true]` sequence before this owner-query fix. A bounded pointer experiment was inconclusive; no causal repair is claimed and its assertions are unchanged. Both failing files passed in a Linux Chromium replay, 15 tests in 17.45 seconds. The Testbox payload passed; a cleanup-settlement timeout was reconciled through native stop.

The entire `model-picker.browser.test.ts` was audited. Its four distinct cases cover a large catalog, provider details and unknown models, free-form entry, and hover/selection behavior. The broad body-removal hook and duplicate host removal are replaced by per-fixture renderer disposal and container removal. Tooltip disposal is preserved. No tests or assertions were removed.

The entire new `app-sidebar.owner-query.test.ts` file was audited. It exercises the mounted sidebar with the real session capability, observes requests and rendered rows, covers explicit empty-owner selection, and disposes its own fixture. A bounded response budget lets the failing test report the loop without starving the runner. No existing coverage was removed.

The repository-wide environment-variable budget check fails on untouched base as well: 455 names versus a budget of 454. The changed files introduce no environment variables.

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid rescanning every agent during catalog delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary full-agent roster work when the Gateway delivers an adopted session through its catalog.

## User Impact

Session catalog delivery reuses the roster already prepared by its topology owner. This restores the existing projection budget without changing session visibility, owner assignment, or ACP admission. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

#172474 (`9cd8aafc011c`) made each temporary catalog selection traverse all configured agents again, adding 32 projections in the regression. The topology scope already captures that roster. Carry its roster-only IDs into selection while keeping them distinct from the broader ACP-inclusive store-admission IDs, as that PR intended. Existing topology invalidation continues to retire stale scopes; there is no new cache or lifecycle owner.

A separate test-only commit follows #172370 (`de66915152ce`): its WAL setter now returns the journal mode directly through a prepared statement. The published SDK retry test still injected BUSY through the retired `exec` path. Move that injection to the real statement `get` path; retain the exact retry count, persisted WAL, and maintenance-close assertions. The production monotonic retry deadline remains unchanged.

Release-note context: avoid redundant agent-roster projection during session catalog delivery. Public APIs, authority, schema, durability, and retention are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact parent/culprit comparisons: the catalog case passes on `47680810e0a8` and fails on `9cd8aafc011c` (352 versus unchanged bound 320). The SDK suite passes on `f0b93c9dd9ce` and its retry case fails on `de66915152ce` (zero intercepted attempts).
- Catalog, selection, and projection retention: 18/18 passed. Selection, filters, and identity benchmark after completing synthetic scopes: 28/28 passed, including roster refresh and ACP distinction.
- SDK and native WAL tests: 43 passed, with seven existing platform-specific skips. Negative control replacing the monotonic deadline with wall time fails on the injected clock jump; production source restored byte-for-byte afterward.
- Production core, Gateway root/method tests, and SDK test types passed; targeted lint and format passed.
- Independent P2 reviews of both commits: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. PR CI supplies broad exact-head proof.

Inject the same failure at the real prepared statement execution and
preserve native bindings. Keep the two-attempt, persisted-WAL and clean
maintenance-close assertions. Production retry behavior is unchanged.

The unchanged file passes the culprit parent and fails after it. The
repaired SDK and native WAL suites pass 43 cases (seven existing platform
skips). Replacing the monotonic deadline with wall time makes the repaired
case fail. Targeted types, lint, formatting and P2 review passed.

Refs: #172370, #135019

* fix(sessions): reuse the topology roster during catalog delivery

Reuse the roster already captured by session topology instead of traversing every configured agent for temporary catalog selections. Keep roster ownership distinct from ACP-inclusive store admission.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep messages queued after handler timeouts
prs.body:
Related: #127229 (the pending-update retry variant)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram messages disappearing when a slow ingress handler times out and its retry is mistaken for an already completed duplicate.

## User Impact

Timed-out messages remain retryable and are processed once before their queued followers. Completed duplicates remain suppressed. No configuration, schema, retention, retry-budget, permission, or protocol changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing tracker distinguishes pending from completed duplicates, and middleware records the corresponding retryable or skipped outcome. The shared drain still owns retries and FIFO ordering.

This retains @diregoblin's fix and regression while removing the broader missing-outcome fallback change and its separate test. The regression uses the existing `withinTest` cancellation helper, as in #170943, so a cancelled test releases its held turn before cleanup joins it.

Production delta against the merge base: +21/-4. Tests and support: +97/-5. Total: 127 changed lines, down from 186. The production growth represents the missing pending outcome, not new state or a second retry owner.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Community evidence: Discord records `1552978751803883622` and `1552978923665621144` describe prolonged typing without a reply. The canonical issue also contains historical variants outside this focused repair.

## Evidence

Real Telegram Test Server, Convex-leased TDLib user, built Gateway; baseline `923e59a01e20549965381a1e72a471762981db9d`, final candidate `4d38a28bd39c6836388c2f8f28af6643ca0da93b`.

Both refs received a real voice note followed four seconds later by uniquely marked text. The local OpenAI-compatible transcription fixture delayed its first request 45 seconds and returned subsequent requests immediately. Both used the existing `OPENCLAW_TELEGRAM_SPOOLED_HANDLER_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`, implemented in the Telegram drain and documented in `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md`.

| Run | Observed native Telegram replies |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline, slow transcription | Only `OPENCLAW_E2E_FOLLOWER_169202` at 51.45s; no voice reply during the 100s recording |
| Final candidate, same slow transcription | `OPENCLAW_E2E_VOICE_169202` at 52.58s, then `OPENCLAW_E2E_FOLLOWER_169202` at 53.60s; each once |
| Fast transcription control, earlier production-identical candidate | Voice at 7.31s, follower at 8.44s; each once, no ingress timeout |
| Final candidate, real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` plus fast transcription | Voice at 15.15s, follower at 16.14s; real HTTPS provider requests and native replies observed |

The model fixture acknowledges each new user marker in order; it does not invent a voice acknowledgment when the voice input is absent. Baseline model input contained only the follower; candidate inputs contained the voice and follower once each, in order.

Sanitized shipped diagnostic evidence:

```text
BASE
claim→adoption stalled for event <voice> after 30001ms; applying retry policy
spooled update <voice> failed; keeping for retry
telegram dedupe: skipped update <voice>
telegram ingress: update <voice> completed without a recorded processing outcome

HEAD
telegram dedupe: skipped update <voice>
spooled update <voice> failed; keeping for retry: Telegram update processing is still pending
[voice subsequently processed, followed by the queued text]
```

The worker-backed regression fails on baseline because the expected pending voice and follower rows are already gone. Final candidate: 30 focused tests passed across tracker and ingress-coalescing suites in 30.79s; the new regression body took 2.96s. Formatting, focused lint and the runtime build passed.

Cancellation proof held the regression's downstream gate, then let the actual Vitest 10-second timeout abort its test signal. The held-gate and completed-cleanup receipts were both observed; the runner exited with only the intended test timeout and no hook timeout. The transient fault injection was removed before normal tests and the build.

The previous production-identical head's hosted CI passed; final-head CI and review are requested after this cancellation-only follow-up. All live leases were released and temporary credential files removed.

Merge danger: two-way door for future processing; reverting restores the old dedupe behavior. Neither this fix nor a revert can recover payloads already scrubbed by the old behavior. Blast radius is Telegram ingress duplicate classification and retry ordering only.

prs.title: improve(sessions): omit storage-only data before cloning model context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing model context deep-copies storage-only submitted text and tool evidence immediately before discarding it.

## User Impact

Reduces context-preparation CPU and copying when conversations contain storage-only metadata.

Example user flows:

- Analyze a large pasted log with its original input retained: model-context preparation skips copying that extra stored text.
- Ask follow-up questions after tools return detailed results: the next model request avoids copying diagnostic metadata excluded from model context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing model-context projection before the final deep clone. The final clone preserves mutation isolation, and durable transcript contents remain unchanged.

## Evidence

67 matched fresh-process benchmark blocks on Linux ARM64, Node 24.21.0:

| Serialized input / metric | Baseline | Updated | Mean paired reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.79 MiB / CPU per call | 0.1298 ms | 0.0771 ms | 40.54% |
| 0.79 MiB / p95 | 0.2127 ms | 0.0994 ms | 51.17% |
| 10.01 MiB / CPU per call | 2.5075 ms | 0.0890 ms | 96.45% |
| 10.01 MiB / p95 | 4.2466 ms | 0.1057 ms | 97.51% |

Both fixtures produce identical 9,831-byte model context. The larger fixture exceeds default context limits and measures the operation under stress; these are context-copying savings.

- Baseline and candidate pass all 23 codec and 32 cohort cases on Linux and native Windows ARM. Windows ARM uses identical fixture-cleanup corrections on both revisions.
- Checks preserve provider context, durable transcript bytes, and nested mutation isolation across tested Node 24/26 and Bun runtimes. Removing the final clone triggers the isolation regression.
- Builds, strict package installation, Linux restart/continuation, types, lint/format, and [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501869492) pass.
- Eight matched Gateway pairs per workload estimate CPU changes of −3.15 ms/turn (−0.83%) for ordinary turns and +3.14 ms/turn (+0.60%) for fast-tool turns.[^qualification]

[^qualification]: Tight Gateway bounds and Windows full-flow/x64 coverage remain unresolved; small observed changes, passing contract/lifecycle checks, and baseline-reproduced Windows blockers justify deferring further qualification.

An allowed current-checkout or saved worktree choice remains usable; project changes and preference restoration preserve the prompt, model, and effort. No configuration or migration is required. The Gateway continues to check authorization and workspace isolation at creation, including requests that bypass the picker or become stale after discovery. ## Why This Change Was Made The picker previously had repository-discovery information but no effective checkout decision for the selected agent and project.
