prs.title: feat(plugins): support turn-local thinking override
prs.body:
Related: #88508

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled for this fork PR.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Model-routing plugins can select a provider/model for one response turn, but cannot select its thinking level through the same hook. For example, a session using model A at `medium` can be routed to model B that should use `xhigh`, while the already-resolved `medium` effort remains in effect.

The plugin-owned `api.runtime.llm.complete({ reasoning })` API discussed in #88508 addresses separate completion calls. This change covers the host response turn routed by `before_model_resolve`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add optional `thinkingOverride?: ThinkLevel` to the public hook result and merge it with the same first-defined/highest-priority semantics as provider/model overrides. Apply it after the effective model/runtime is known, using the existing thinking validation and effort pipeline rather than provider parameters or a second reasoning mechanism.

Precedence is explicit current-message `/think` (or explicit agent-command thinking), then the hook override, then stored/session/default thinking. Existing model-selection locks still bypass the entire routing hook. The native Codex harness, app-server protocol, authentication, and provider catalogs are unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugins can choose a supported reasoning effort alongside a per-turn model route without changing persistent session thinking. The override is turn-local and never writes session `/think` or agent defaults. Hooks that omit it retain their existing behavior, including hook-failure handling and model pins.

## Evidence

- Before the implementation, the new regressions failed on missing hook-result propagation and the model-A/xhigh → model-B/medium → model-A/xhigh sequence receiving the old effort.
- Focused suite: 201 tests passed across six files. Coverage includes independent provider/model/thinking overrides, hook priority, explicit-message authority, omitted overrides, final-model unsupported-level handling, unchanged request thinking, and consecutive-turn isolation.
- Native Codex boundary: deterministic `turn/start` assertions verify both `effort` and `collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort` receive `xhigh`, `medium`, then `xhigh` through the existing mapping. No live provider calls were used.
- Plugin contracts: 1,111 tests passed. Public SDK surface check and docs MDX validation passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed on the rebased commit.
- `pnpm check`: passed on the rebased commit (production/test types, full lint/format, and policy guards).
- `pnpm test`: **not green / incomplete**. Stopped after 97 of 622 scheduled shards had started, with four failing assertions and a worker exit; no unrelated repairs are included:
  - Three failures in unchanged `test/helpers/qa-gateway-cleanup.test.ts` import E2E fixtures and report “Calling the suite function inside test function is not allowed.” The test and imported fixture sources are identical to base `ae22204e7a`. A clean-base targeted reproduction stalled rather than establishing the same assertion failures, so these are not claimed as independently reproduced on main.
  - Unchanged `test/scripts/check-runtime-sidecar-loaders.test.ts` passes `URL.pathname` to filesystem reads; the checkout's spaces become `%20`, producing `ENOENT`. The failing source is byte-identical to base.
  - A `unit-src` worker exited unexpectedly without identifying a failing assertion; its cause remains unresolved.
- Autoreview: final candidate scoped-clean at P0–P2; implementation reviewed and understood. An initial suggestion to run hooks for model-locked sessions was rejected because that would change the existing model-lock/privacy boundary; documentation explicitly preserves it.
- Review follow-up: the Hook catalog now includes turn-local thinking (`6c0ddaee08`). The one-line docs fix passes formatting, MDX validation, SDK-surface validation, and `git diff --check`.
- Real plugin-enabled runtime proof: **passed** on the earlier feature head recorded below. The current-main port preserves the same hook-to-native-Codex effort path; focused regressions were rerun. Maintainer confirmation of the public API direction remains pending.
- Prior current-main integration followed jb510's port (`487e05a865`, `29a3822b1587`) while retaining this PR's API, docs, and expanded tests. On the refreshed head: plugin contracts 1,157 passed; focused hook/setup/runtime/reply/command/Codex tests, `pnpm tsgo:all`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, MDX/link checks, boundaries, import cycles, and size ratchets passed. No new provider calls were made.

### 2026-10-14 current-main refresh

Merged upstream `e7619a2d3f1` while preserving the existing API, explicit-current-turn precedence, and native Codex effort mapping. Adapted reply/command parameter construction and carried thinking through main's new hook-owned fallback selection. The new run-entry regression failed before that propagation and passed afterward. Historical real-provider evidence above remains historical; no provider calls were repeated.

- Passed: 100 focused tests across nine files, production typecheck, four affected test-type graphs, targeted lint/format, plugin boundaries, import cycles, MDX, conflict markers, line-cap ratchet, and diff checks. The new fallback-boundary coverage reuses main's six-case fixture (0.7 seconds of test time; 5.8 seconds file wall time). New-head CI supplies broader validation.
- Full build: interrupted after about 14 minutes of active declaration generation; **not claimed passed**. No compiler error had been reported.
- Full-check limitations: max-lines itself passes, but the combined environment guard reports 455 names against budget 454. An independent count found the same 455 on upstream with no PR additions. `deadcode:full` reports eight unused exports and one unused type in untouched storage/Gateway/UI files; this PR changes none of those files or symbol references. No baseline or unrelated fixes were made. Full repository checks are **not claimed green**.

Validation runs only in dedicated source checkouts. The deterministic tests above do not replace the real plugin-enabled proof requested by review. No installed OpenClaw package, running gateway, live plugin, configuration, session state, or router logs were changed.


## REAL BEHAVIOR PROOF

Completed 2026-09-02 on `6c0ddaee082abba12f101c7cc1da81c5f94b1a71`, using the PR build, an installed deterministic proof plugin, and the **real native Codex app-server**. This was a dedicated loopback Gateway with isolated configuration, state, sessions, workspace, logs, agent-scoped Codex storage, and OAuth profile—not the production installation or router. The three completed turns shared one OpenClaw session.

| Marker | Hook-selected model / thinking | Native turn/start model | effort | Collaboration model / reasoning_effort | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROOF_LUNA_1 | openai/gpt-5.6-luna / xhigh | gpt-5.6-luna | xhigh | gpt-5.6-luna / xhigh | OK; completed |
| PROOF_SOL | openai/gpt-5.6-sol / medium | gpt-5.6-sol | medium | gpt-5.6-sol / medium | OK; completed |
| PROOF_LUNA_2 | openai/gpt-5.6-luna / xhigh | gpt-5.6-luna | xhigh | gpt-5.6-luna / xhigh | OK; completed |

The existing native lifecycle events and response `requestShaping.thinking` agreed. No stub or mocked response was used for this run. The tap and proof plugin are temporary external evidence tooling; no implementation files were changed.

Stored session `thinkingLevel` was absent before and after all three completed turns; `thinkingDefault` remained `medium`. The isolated configuration hash stayed identical throughout the response sequence. Each response had one successful attempt and returned exactly `OK`; native transcripts contained **zero tool calls**. Total: **3 provider response turns, 0 classifier calls, 0 tools**. prs.title: fix: retain Codex context after first-turn startup failures
prs.body:
Related: #169431, #168347, #171707.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes earlier context disappearing when a fresh Codex thread fails before its first input is accepted and the user retries the request.

## User Impact

For context engines using `thread_bootstrap`, the retry receives the history that never reached native Codex. Successful follow-ups continue using the accepted native history without resending the bootstrap. This applies to fresh startup; previously persisted false receipts are not migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh thread creation saves the bootstrap projection before `turn/start` accepts its input. A later startup or dispatch failure can leave a matching epoch that incorrectly suppresses history on retry.

Keep the engine/policy binding at thread creation and record the projection after validated native turn acceptance, only when the complete bootstrap block survived final input fitting. Guard the receipt update by the exact thread/client owner. If the receipt write fails or loses ownership, preserve the already-accepted turn and its result. Existing resume markers, transient ownership and warm/cancellation cleanup remain unchanged.

This is a narrow acceptance-ordering fix. It adds no retry machinery or context-retention policy. It does not provide crash-atomic delivery: an interruption or storage failure after acceptance can still leave conservative replay uncertainty.

Related PR #171707 proposes `thread/inject_items` for authored-cap history, with an earlier seed acknowledgment. This candidate fixes main's rendered `turn/start` carrier. The changes have not been composed or tested together; if that carrier lands first, reconcile the receipt boundary with its acknowledged seeding path.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311`.

**Hosted CI:** [successful run 38632947933](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38632947933), 52 successful jobs and 29 skipped. All four previously failing leaf lanes and the required gate passed. Observed again on October 14 at 21:23 UTC.

**New compatibility evidence:** a supported native-session route now completes the stable 10.3 → current candidate upgrade, preserves the same stored session/native thread, and completes two real local-model continuations with the original facts. The additional archive below contains actual seed/import, migration, native/provider/terminal captures and durable-history checks. This is a bounded native-session result; the earlier legacy-provider-route comparison remains blocked and is disclosed separately.

### Inspectable sanitized artifacts

1. [Original Gateway/native/provider comparison and reproduction archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33455012/codex-bootstrap-acceptance-ce5296cf-evidence.zip)

   File: `codex-bootstrap-acceptance-ce5296cf-evidence.zip`.
   SHA-256: `caaed5e4d49d2e1f9211cd28252304f4fca9b4f12096eeead44faef9ffe23ba6`.

2. [Earlier stable-state preservation, route-barrier comparison and CI follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33459171/codex-bootstrap-18654634-upgrade-followup.zip)

   SHA-256: `758480e533c1342d166e732baddf035491911e7fcc7a84f24a1791506ce2c989`.

3. [codex-bootstrap-18654634-native-upgrade-proof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33463900/codex-bootstrap-18654634-native-upgrade-proof.zip)

   SHA-256: `a21af0ab8f7fb655b2ec21e772e4c85123b40e0b0297893077443b9e508a716f`.

The original archive includes actual rejection/acceptance inputs, actual provider user input and output, Gateway terminal receipts, the complete comparison matrix, check logs, runnable helpers and an offline correlation verifier. The earlier supplement adds retained stable-state reopening captures, Doctor receipts, pristine-main comparison and CI repair evidence. The new supplement adds successful native-session upgrade continuations. Each has source/artifact hashes, a reproduction recipe, offline verifier and redaction disclosure. Raw operator configuration, credentials, private endpoint/model inventory and real user sessions are excluded.

### Fresh startup: main versus candidate

Built and exercised main `24567afc232dfbcd8da3f1eb4e1b1466925d1352` and original candidate `06daa04093a9eab782ac72893b7c45c95318cbcd` with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.9.0. The shipped Gateway used real native Codex 0.160.0 and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. Four isolated synthetic cases, three successful turns each: **12/12 inference requests completed with HTTP 200 and `response.completed`.**

| Case | Bootstrap blocks in actual provider user input: first success / continuation 1 / continuation 2 | Actual model response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main, ordinary control | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on all three turns |
| Candidate, ordinary control | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on all three turns |
| Main, first dispatch rejected before acceptance | 0 / 0 / 0 | `MISSING` on retry and both continuations |
| Candidate, same preaccept rejection | 1 / 1 / 1 | Saved goal and checksum on retry and both continuations |

The fault cases reject exactly one first `turn/start` with JSON-RPC `-32602` before forwarding it to native; those two rejected dispatches make zero provider calls. This is controlled fault injection. Other native messages and provider payloads pass through byte-for-byte, with no response substitution or provider adapter.

The rejected request contains 634 characters including the synthetic history. Main's retry sends only the new 234-character request; the candidate retry sends 877 characters including the history and failed request. The accepted turn ID matches the Gateway terminal receipt. Both later turns retain the same native thread/client and send only their new 245-character request. At the provider boundary, successful history appears once in user messages; assistant echoes are excluded. Nonces are generated independently for each case.

The external fixture uses public context-engine registration, current-turn fencing and a real atomic idempotent SQLite worker commit. No legacy fallback occurs in the qualified matrix; every case commits three accepted turns. The engine supplies controlled history, while native binding/projection, Gateway dispatch and inference are real. It is not a benchmark of an external production context engine.

### Existing native-session upgrade: completed on the current head

Fresh isolated case `upgrade-i-native` ran the built stable `v2026.10.3` and exact current candidate with native Codex 0.160.0 and an already-loaded local LM Studio model. **Exit 0, 48.370 seconds, four HTTP 200 / `response.completed` results:** one native CLI seed, one stable Gateway follow-up, then two candidate Gateway continuations.

The real native CLI created a synthetic conversation. Stable adopted it using the public `sessions.catalog.list` / `sessions.catalog.continue` flow, saved settings, and performed an ordinary `agent` RPC. After all owned processes stopped, candidate Doctor migrated that same state with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and external service ownership. Candidate reopened the existing session and performed two ordinary `agent` RPCs. This uses native-owned model/provider configuration without a `models.providers` overlay, fabricated credential/model, direct database seed, admission bypass or payload translation.

| Check | Before upgrade | After upgrade and both continuations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent / global SQLite schema | 24 / 20 | 26 / 22; integrity checks pass |
| OpenClaw session ID and native thread | Saved by stable | Same IDs; genuine `thread/resume`, no replacement |
| Label, pin, verbosity, usage setting | Saved through public session API | Identical on reopening and after continuation |
| Historical messages | Four user/assistant messages | Exactly equal on reopening; content, IDs, sequence and other metadata retained after both continuations |
| Stored transcript events | 5 | 9; original five equal on all seven common stored fields |
| Original native rollout files | Two retained snapshots | Both preserved byte-for-byte as prefixes |
| Authored configuration | Retained bytes | Byte-identical; Doctor made zero model requests |
| Original goal, checksum and history fact | Present in native seed and stable reply | Present in actual provider history and both actual candidate replies |

Follow-up prompts do not repeat the original nonces. Imported user/assistant seed history is checked before the stable follow-up. Each of the three Gateway turns matches a genuine native acceptance, exact provider last-user input and Gateway terminal turn ID. Both candidate turns reuse the same candidate client and the native thread stored by stable. The binding is exact across Doctor; after continuation, runtime fields such as the client ID and covered-history watermark may advance. Whole final binding byte equality is not claimed.

Post-continuation display comparison excludes only `__openclaw.transcriptPosition.source`, a reader-generation coordinate; `rawSeq` and all other message fields remain exact. Separately, stopped SQLite snapshots prove byte equality of all seven original stored event fields. The source-generation change is not presented as ordinary append behavior; its exact runtime caller was not established. A prior attempt failed its overly broad display comparison and remains excluded. Only the fresh corrected case qualifies.

Inspect the new archive's `native-seed/`, `stable/`, `migration/`, `candidate/`, actual native/provider input-output files, `stored-transcript-preservation.json`, and `upgrade-summary.json`. The result was independently checked against raw synthetic SQLite/rollout snapshots and captured responses. No production Gateway participated.

**Scope:** both builds use default legacy mode with native context ownership. This establishes the tested existing native-session migration/continuation boundary. It does not establish custom-engine activation during upgrade or repair the legacy configured-provider route below. The original fresh-startup matrix independently proves the PR's custom-engine acceptance fix; the earlier supplement independently covers preservation of old custom projection/ledger data up to its route barrier.

### Earlier legacy-provider upgrade comparison: candidate versus pristine main

The latest stable release observed for this test was `v2026.10.3`, commit `59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1` (tag object `3a8c04b0832eabc4410ba7c7a30c9c27e4b5fc81`). Each case first created settings, a real user/assistant exchange and one committed fixture-ledger row through a stable Gateway. After stopping that Gateway, it retained the same synthetic state and native home, ran the supported Doctor migration, and reopened using the target build.

| Observation | Candidate `18654634e2a3` | Pristine main `24567afc232d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent / global schema | 24 to 26 / 20 to 22 | Same |
| Stable real provider completions | 1 | 1 |
| Exact old history reopened | Preserved | Preserved |
| Session ID, label, pin, verbosity and usage setting | Preserved | Preserved |
| Active native binding/projection, native history prefix and one-row accepted ledger | Preserved | Preserved |
| Post-upgrade native turn starts / provider calls | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Successful post-upgrade continuations | 0 | 0 |
| Full compatibility | NOT PROVEN | NOT PROVEN |

Both failed with:

```text
Requested agent harness "codex" does not support openai/lmstudio/<local-model> (Codex cannot reproduce the prepared provider route).
```

Doctor canonicalized the explicit local `codex` provider to `openai`. The canonical custom-endpoint route does not declare Codex compatibility, so admission stops before dispatch. The five inspected Doctor/routing owners are byte-identical between pristine main and this candidate; their hashes are included. The repeated main failure separates this barrier from the PR's acceptance-ordering change, without proving that every old stored binding works.

Doctor ran only in the new synthetic cases, with explicit operator approval and `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`. It exited zero, made no model request, and retained valid pre-migration snapshots/database backups. It also emitted an original-state JSON inspection warning; these were not warning-free runs. Configuration normalization was reviewed, not undone. No admission bypass, fabricated credential, configuration restoration or seeded database row was used.

The supplement's `candidate/` and `pristine-main/` directories contain the actual observations, not only integrity claims. Its verifier reports consistent exported evidence while retaining `fullCompatibility: NOT PROVEN`. The two stable setup completions are separate from the original 12-call matrix and must not be counted as upgraded continuations. All owned test processes stopped; the operator Gateway was untouched.

### Tests and CI follow-up

```text
Original baseline publication-failure regression: 1 control passed, 1 expected failure
Original candidate affected selection:             134/134 passed, 7 complete files
Original final formatted regression suite:          12/12 passed
Published-head provider-review shard:                8 failed / 25 passed
Same shard after two-line CI follow-up:              33/33 passed
Bootstrap regression follow-up:                      12/12 passed
Assertion ratchet, targeted lint/types/format:       passed
Stable and repaired-candidate QA builds:             passed
git diff --check:                                    passed
Hosted CI at current head:                           passed
```

The original 134-test selection covers the new bootstrap boundary plus neighboring active-engine, overflow, binding, warm cleanup and cancellation behavior. It took 143.892 seconds. Three test-only lint repairs and formatting followed it with unchanged runtime implementation; the final 12-test rerun took 50.322 seconds. Coverage includes post-start preparation and dispatch rejection, accepted provider failure/cancellation, indeterminate cancelled dispatch, replacement-owner preservation, receipt-write throw/conflict, fitted-away bootstrap and empty history. Existing expectations were not weakened.

Follow-up commit `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311` adds only the missing `promptState` slot to the provider-review fixture and the required rationale for a mutable bootstrap prompt type assertion. There is no runtime behavior change. The exact previously failing shard now passes; no assertion-ratchet baseline was expanded. Two inherited CI failures came from a wrapper inventory omission fixed upstream by `51afdbea12bb4bd733e5e3594828140194048195`. The successful CI merge includes that repair through its main parent; this branch does not copy it.

Independent Sol 6.1 High source reviews of the original patch and the scoped follow-up found no actionable P0-P2 findings. A separate evidence review checked artifact/source hashes, actual native/provider/Gateway correlations, retained raw synthetic database/prefix preservation and redaction. Source review alone is not counted as execution evidence. Local check receipts retain their actual precommit identities and source hashes rather than relabeling old runs as current-head runs.

### Reproduction and limits

Use each archive's `repro/README.md`: the original for the four-case fresh-startup matrix, the earlier supplement for the expected legacy-route failure, and the new supplement for successful existing native-session upgrade/continuation. Build pinned checkouts with `qaRuntime`; the live entry point is `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`, driven by ordinary `agent` RPCs through public `GatewayClient`. Runners create isolated state and require an explicitly selected already-loaded local model. The new archive's `repro/verify-upgrade-evidence.py` checks its complete file inventory, hashes and exported correlations without service access.

One original preliminary control used an incomplete fixture contract and fell back to legacy; it is excluded from the 12-call matrix. Upgrade setup attempts with missing session permissions, a response-field assumption and an unavailable stable SQLite SDK helper were retained and excluded; the supplement's attempt audit explains each. The earlier custom-engine preservation cases e/f use the common public transaction API and require a committed stable fixture-ledger row before migration. The new native-only case i has no synthetic engine ledger. No failed attempt was discarded or reclassified as success.

Original candidate patch SHA-256: `ce5296cf50997171390a897b9cfddc8311d4e9e3706f1dc46a1b203c35690812`. The immutable original archive remains tied to head `06daa04093a9eab782ac72893b7c45c95318cbcd`; the supplement records head `18654634e2a3c8470447fe0a942d17785d60f311` separately.

The new setup audit also retains an invalid stable config attempt and the display-generation comparison failure; neither counts as a passing case. The corrected test does not ignore stored history changes: it checks all original raw event fields after shutdown. Test processes are stopped; retained fixtures are separate from the production Gateway.

The combined proof establishes local fresh-startup recovery under controlled preaccept failure and successful existing native-session upgrade with preserved history/settings/native thread. It does not establish every provider/engine upgrade combination, repair the separately reproduced legacy route barrier, migrate historical false bootstrap receipts, test remote OpenAI behavior, or prove production incidence, model-quality improvement, latency/cache/billing gains, live store-error/cancellation behavior or crash-atomic delivery. The new supplement has not yet been assessed by the upstream reviewer; acceptance of this bounded compatibility proof remains their decision.

prs.title: fix(agents): custom GLM providers' session titles fail with thinking-off 400
prs.body:
Closes #171068

## What Problem This Solves

Session auto-titles stopped working for custom OpenAI-compatible providers pointed at Zhipu/Z.AI GLM endpoints, and the failure was silent, so new sessions stayed unnamed. Live, through OpenClaw's real title path (`completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel`) with a custom `zhipu` provider at `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` and `glm-5.3-flash`:

```text
400 This model always engages in thinking and cannot be disabled; please use low, high, or max
```

## Why This Change Was Made

`380c115e392` made title calls run with thinking off. For a custom endpoint, the completions compat layer inferred the Z.AI dialect from the base URL and translated off into `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`, which always-thinking GLM-5.x rejects. The bundled Z.AI plugin was fixed separately in #164407; custom providers never reach that hook.

A resolved compat flag (`thinkingOffControlUndeclared`) now marks the one case where the off control is unknown: an inferred `zai` format on a custom endpoint, with no configured `thinkingFormat` and no declared off effort or off mapping. Only then is the off control omitted, so the provider default applies. Everything else keeps today's behavior: explicitly configured `zai` (direct and managed), inferred `deepseek` and `together`, OpenAI-compatible proxies, and declared `none`/`off` efforts or mappings. Older GLM-4.x models behind an inferred custom Z.AI endpoint now think on titles instead of being forced off. That is slower but works, while forcing off breaks GLM-5.x outright.

Failed conversation-label generation now logs a warning (once per provider/model per minute) that names the model and the next step, without prompts, raw provider errors, or auth profile details.

## Evidence

- Live on main: the title path returns the 400 above.
- Live on this branch: the same call completes (`stop=stop`) at the production 4096-token label budget.
- Regressions: zhipu and bigmodel title calls through the real transport; controls proving explicit Z.AI (direct and managed), inferred DeepSeek and Together, and declared off efforts or mappings still send their off controls. 70 focused tests pass.
- Codex autoreview: three earlier passes each found a narrower over-broad case (all inferred formats, explicit Z.AI in managed mode, declared off on inferred Z.AI), and each was fixed with a regression test. The final pass is scoped-clean.

prs.title: fix(ios): choose another account for Cloudflare Access sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #172594

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: adding a Gateway that requires another Cloudflare Access account can reopen the first account’s browser session without a way to switch.

## User Impact

Choose **Use another account** in the initial website sign-in prompt, then sign in with the intended identity. **Continue** keeps existing browser sign-ins.

**The deliberate switch clears website sign-ins, cookies, and cached website data for all Gateways in OpenClaw’s internal Safari browser.** Saved native Gateway connections and standalone Safari are unaffected. No Cloudflare cross-application logout is called.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native Access grants already belong to their Gateway origin in Keychain; the stuck account belongs to Safari’s shared app website store. Use Apple’s supported `SFSafariViewController.DataStore.default.clearWebsiteData()` before opening the website, only after an explicit choice. Preserve the existing website → Done → Continue → encrypted transfer flow, including its identity-provider return-address workaround. Do not clear the selected website login between those steps.

Cancellation and replacement wait for an in-flight reset before another browser opens. No authentication protocol, pairing, native grant policy, or default sign-in behavior changes.

This is a deliberate app-browser reset, not a claim of per-Gateway/private Safari sessions. `SFSafariViewController` does not expose a per-instance ephemeral store; separate private `ASWebAuthenticationSession` instances would not preserve this two-step website login.

## Evidence

- The same hosted UIKit test renders the production alert on baseline and candidate: baseline fails at the missing account-switch action; candidate passes (0.53 seconds).
- 144 named focused cases passed across browser presenter, origin-scoped session/Keychain persistence, encrypted transfer, ingress/cancellation, and typography. The additional real Apple reset/Keychain test passes in 8.94 seconds with callback-driven completion. Its first run correctly exposed a fixture-only three-second mock polling deadline, now removed.
- The real Apple API test verifies unchanged saved grant bytes, original revision, cold Keychain restore, and no transport retirement. This does not claim that a real identity provider displayed an account picker.
- Pinned SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint (486 production files), native localization verification, and scoped P0 code review pass.
- A signed private development composition builds with the existing TLS/Health fixes and embedded Watch companion. Physical two-account login remains operator validation; the operator is offline. No personal account, endpoint, or token appears in these captures.

### Before and after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Original sign-in prompt without account switching](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61877323-8a76-4efd-8741-9f7909f8c13f) | ![Sign-in prompt with explicit account-switch scope disclosure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d09a28d-04c7-44f3-af81-cfb40a2cd36f) |

## Dependency contracts

- [Apple Safari app website data store](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safariservices/sfsafariviewcontroller/datastore): the installed SDK documents clearing local storage, cached resources, and cookies accrued within the app.
- [Cloudflare session management](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/access-settings/session-management/): server logout revokes the user’s session across applications, so it is intentionally not used.

Related, not duplicates: #134467 (post-auth Google profiles), #157874 / #158051 (Dashboard embedding), #161373 (server-side logout).

prs.title: fix(cron): consume resume drain failures instead of crashing the gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resumeScheduling()` (`src/cron/service/ops-lifecycle.ts:73`) fired `drainCronRunQueue(state)` as a floating promise with no rejection handler. When that drain fails **non-transiently** (for example a damaged shared-state database), the rejection escapes to the process-level `unhandledRejection` handler, which treats it as fatal and exits the Gateway.

Scope note: transient store failures such as `SQLITE_BUSY`/`SQLITE_CANTOPEN` are already classified non-fatal by `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts:288-309` (`isTransientUnhandledRejectionError`). The crash path this PR closes is the non-transient one; the reproducer below uses exactly such a failure.

The same call is already guarded on the wake path (`src/cron/service/run-queue-wake.ts:42-45`), which catches the identical rejection and logs `cron: queue drain delayed`. The resume path was missing that guard.

## User Impact

- A Gateway suspend/resume cycle no longer risks a process exit when the cron store fails non-transiently during resume.
- The failure is logged and retried on the next scheduler tick; the Gateway keeps serving requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

One line: attach the same `.catch` the wake path already uses. No behavior change on the success path, no new config, no API surface.

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry | `src/gateway/server-methods/suspend.ts` | 109 | `resumeScheduling: () => context.cron.resumeScheduling()` |
| Coordinator | `src/infra/gateway-suspend-coordinator.ts` | 133 | `entry.resumeScheduling()` after a held suspension |
| Facade | `src/cron/service.ts` | 99 | `CronService.resumeScheduling()` |
| Defect site | `src/cron/service/ops-lifecycle.ts` | 73 | `void drainCronRunQueue(state)` — no `.catch` |
| Drain | `src/cron/service/run-queue.ts` | 301 | rejects via the worker operation / `locked` |
| Precedent guard | `src/cron/service/run-queue-wake.ts` | 42-45 | `void drain().catch(… "cron: queue drain delayed")` |

### Gateway suspend/resume proof (new test)

`src/gateway/server-cron-suspend-drain.test.ts` drives the **real Gateway suspension handlers** (`gateway.suspend.prepare` → `gateway.suspend.resume`) through the real coordinator with a **real `CronService`** and its state worker: 8 concurrency-blocking runs occupy the queue, a 9th request stays queued, the shared-state database is latched as damaged, then the suspension resumes. It asserts the Gateway logs `cron: queue drain delayed`, records **no** `unhandledRejection`, and still answers `gateway.suspend.status` afterwards.

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-cron-suspend-drain.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Control-red (guard reverted on the same tree): the test fails — the warning is never logged and the rejection escapes instead of being observed.

### Cron regression test

`src/cron/service.run-queue.test.ts` → "consumes a resume-scheduling drain failure instead of tripping the fatal unhandled-rejection path" (no fixed sleeps; it waits on the observed drain completion).

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/service.run-queue.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Control-red: reverting the one-line guard makes this test fail with `[ Error { "message": "cron state database is damaged" } ]` where `[]` is expected.

### Lint / format

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/cron/service/ops-lifecycle.ts src/cron/service.run-queue.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-suspend-drain.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <same files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

Related precedent: #169525 fixed the sibling unhandled-rejection path for recovered cron jobs.

octopool: pr_view served from shared cache (hit), refreshes in 1m26s; set OCTOPOOL_FRESH=1 for a live read
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Chat activity row ("1 update from Automation ›") changes its text, icon, color and width when expanded ("From 🕒 Automation ⌄"), and its source link is unavailable until the row is expanded.

## User Impact

User impact: activity rows keep the same "N update(s) from <source>" summary in both states and only the chevron rotates. prs.title: feat(googlechat): edit previously sent text messages
prs.body:
Closes #149091

## What Problem This Solves

Google Chat users cannot correct an app's previously sent message through OpenClaw's message tool or CLI, even though the plugin already updates its own typing placeholders.

## User Impact

Users can explicitly replace the text of a message created by the selected Google Chat app. Supply the full `spaces/<spaceId>/messages/<messageId>` resource name, replacement text, and a target resolving to the same case-sensitive space. Existing shared action and conversation authorization still apply.

No new configuration or OAuth scope is required. Cards and attachments are preserved. Permission and missing-message errors are returned without posting a replacement message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose `edit` consistently in discovery and both action adapters, then reuse the existing text-only PATCH transport. Validate the message resource and its space before updating it. Automatic typing-placeholder behavior remains separate.

The issue's automated review recommends this narrow enhancement but marks product acceptance for maintainer review; this PR supplies the concrete implementation for that decision.

## Evidence

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared message tool, registered Google Chat plugin | `Message action edit not supported for channel googlechat.` | A host-admitted edit reaches the lazy adapter and sends a single text-only PATCH. |
| Mixed-case space resource | Edit unavailable | Preserve canonical space casing; reject a different or folded message space before PATCH. |
| HTTP 403 / 404 | Edit unavailable | Propagate the provider error; no replacement POST. |
| Selected account and malformed resources | Edit unavailable | Preserve selected-account routing and replacement whitespace; reject disabled/unavailable accounts and malformed resource paths. |

- Google Chat plugin coverage: 372 tests passed across the plugin-wide and focused runs; the two auth loopback cases required proxy environment variables to be unset.
- `test/googlechat-message-edit.integration.test.ts`: passed through the real shared message tool, registered lazy plugin, host-issued turn capability, and loopback HTTP server. The fixture keeps the real Google Chat authentication code, generates an ephemeral RSA key, and serves a local OAuth token response. It preserves the previous session-derived send regression while adding explicit edit coverage.
- `pnpm build`: passed, including bundled plugin generation, declaration checks, and native plugin loading checks.
- `test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts`: 10 checks passed alongside the final edit integration scenario.
- Built Google Chat import profile: passed (104.8 MiB peak RSS).
- Claude autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings at its default P0 threshold.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed formatting, Doctor contract tests, boundary checks, all selected typechecks, and unused-export scans. Its repository-wide extension lint exhausted host resources and was terminated (exit 143), so the full local command did not finish.
- Recovery: type-aware lint of all changed Google Chat files and the integration test passed; remaining database-first, media helper, runtime sidecar, and import-cycle guards passed. The full [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34994438834) subsequently passed on `87a2d629875115b718bd53099b1e10ba50624a5a`, including build-artifact checks and all lint jobs.

What was not tested: authenticated execution against a real Google Chat tenant. The transport proof uses the actual shared message tool, plugin, and guarded HTTP client against a local HTTP fixture serving synthetic OAuth and Chat API responses. It does not prove Google-side permissions or ownership checks. The [Google PATCH contract](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/api/reference/rest/v1/spaces.messages/patch) documents `chat.bot` support and the app-authored-message restriction.

prs.title: fix(sessions): unify SQLite row parsers between snapshot and revalidate reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: any session with a non-owner session_participants row (e.g. a multi-participant Matrix room, or any multi-party channel) failed whole-entry equality checks in two read paths that skipped the participant projection the exact-row/revalidation read applies. Concretely: (1) unfiltered bulk replacements (e.g. a group category rename) failed permanently on any session with a non-owner participant, and (2) startup-orphaned session recovery for multi-participant sessions got stuck at status: "running" forever after a gateway restart, since the revalidation comparison never matched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the same shared participant-projection helper (projectSqliteSessionParticipantsBatch) that the exact-row read already uses, to the whole-store snapshot read and the status-filtered snapshot read, so all three reads agree on row shape for sessions with non-owner participants.

## User Impact

Multi-participant sessions (e.g. group Matrix rooms) no longer get stuck at status: "running" after a gateway restart, and bulk entry replacements no longer silently fail on any session with a non-owner participant. No configuration or migration required.

## Evidence

- Two new regression tests: one proves bulk replacement now succeeds on a session with a non-owner participant (previously failed permanently); one proves startup-orphan recovery now correctly marks and recovers a multi-participant session (previously stuck at running).
- Local run today, both directly affected test files: 240/240 passing (src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-participants.test.ts, src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts).
- Note: the fix was originally applied at session-accessor.sqlite-entry-store.ts, but readSessionEntryStore/readSessionEntryCount had already been relocated upstream to session-accessor.sqlite-entry-inventory.ts before this PR'''s target commit; this PR applies the fix at its correct, current location.
- Note: I do not have access to this repo'''s trusted CI (Testbox) from my fork; the above is local test evidence only. Maintainer/CI verification is still needed before merge.

issues.title: Idle compaction can archive a session whose turn is still running through the direct entry point
issues.body:
I think the idle-compaction guard misses turns that arrive through process_direct, and I reproduced it on Linux with Python 3.12 against main at cdb6210.

_check_expired_sessions_if_due passes active_session_keys=self._pending_queues.keys() and check_expired skips those keys, but the only writer of _pending_queues is _enqueue_session_message, the bus path. process_direct never registers there; that is what the API server, the SDK and single-shot CLI use.

The scan reads updated_at from the session jsonl metadata line, and during a direct turn it stays frozen at turn start, because runtime checkpoints go to the sidecar via save_runtime_checkpoint and the main jsonl is not rewritten until the turn ends. The freeze held with and without tool calls.

So a direct turn outliving the idle threshold looks idle. With sessionTtlMinutes at its default of 15, a longer turn gets archival scheduled while still running, and I then watched compact_idle_session commit a summary checkpoint (last_archived 0 to 3) that the live turn's final save overwrites (back to 0, summary gone). No messages are lost, but the compaction is wasted.

Repro: an AgentLoop whose chat_stream_with_retry blocks, process_direct, then while it blocks confirm loop._pending_queues is empty and the metadata updated_at is unchanged seconds later, shrink auto_compact._ttl, and call check_expired with active_session_keys=loop._pending_queues.keys() (one archive scheduled).

Uncertainty boundary: I did not run the documented two-service setup end to end, so how the gateway and API service share a sessions directory is unverified. I compressed the TTL to seconds instead of 15 minutes, so only wall clock is simulated, and in the archive-discarded step I stubbed the summarizer while the reload, the checkpoint commit and both saves are real. Whether the fix belongs in the active set or elsewhere is only a suggestion.

If this is known, or a second guard exists that I missed, point me at it.

prs.title: fix(agent): build the skills summary when the workspace path is a symlink
prs.body:
## Problem

`SkillsLoader.build_skills_summary` prints each plugin skill path relative to `<workspace>/plugins`. The plugin loader hands over skill paths that are already resolved (`_contained` uses `Path.resolve(strict=True)`), but the summary compared them with the unresolved root. When the workspace path goes through a symlink, `relative_to()` raises:

```
ValueError: '/private/tmp/.../real/plugins/demo/skills/hello/SKILL.md' is not in the subpath of '/private/tmp/.../link/plugins'
```

The summary is part of the system prompt (`ContextBuilder.build_system_prompt`, and `SubagentManager` for subagents), so no prompt can be built while an enabled plugin ships a skill. `list_skills`, `load_skill` and `/skill` keep working, which hides the cause. Common triggers on macOS are a workspace under `/tmp` or `/var` (both symlinks into `/private`), a symlinked home or data disk, or a synced folder.

## Fix

Resolve the plugin group's root too. The function already resolves it for the display root; the workspace and built-in groups are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `test_plugin_skill_summary_supports_symlinked_workspace` (workspace at `tmp_path/link -> tmp_path/real`, one enabled plugin skill). On main it fails with the `ValueError` above; it passes with the fix.
- `tests/agent/`: 1847 passed.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `skills.py`.

prs.body:
Prompt file reads, transcript shaping, and local token estimation currently run on the gateway event loop. A slow read or large replay can delay status handling and cancellation before the next model request.

Capture read-only replay inputs from the live JSONL Session on the event loop, and apply prepared request/accepted-history state there. A cancelled caller can return while its physical worker retains the slot until completion. Preserve detached lifecycle hook snapshots, including nonempty cancellation snapshots, and protect the shared tool token cache across worker threads.

prs.title: fix(session): serialize compaction with active turns
prs.body:
An active turn can hold a live Session while SDK or idle compaction invalidates the cache and reloads a second Session. If the turn saves its reply before the delayed summary returns, the compaction save replaces the JSONL transcript and loses that reply.

Share AgentLoop's existing per-session lock with AutoCompact._archive and both async SDK compaction methods. Compaction waits for an active turn before loading and summarizing the transcript; a turn arriving during compaction waits for the saved summary. Other session keys continue independently. Keep the synchronous session APIs, save parameters, JSONL format, and existing command locking. Document the same-session wait restriction for observational persisted-turn callbacks.

This complements #6215's scan-time active-session filtering: an idle archive queued before a new turn and SDK compaction calls still need serialization. #6063 discards stale summaries after reset/deletion by checking Session identity after generation; this change serializes turns and compaction before the cache reload and summary save.

prs.title: fix(skills): bind plugin snapshots to approved content
prs.body:
Fixes a snapshot regression introduced by [#6217](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6217).

Replacing an enabled plugin's `SKILL.md` after discovery could make a prompt snapshot load replacement instructions from its cached path, even though the changed package would be disabled on the next activation check.

Capture plugin documents from the exact bytes used to compute the approved package fingerprint, then pass those documents and validated metadata into the per-prompt skill snapshot. The prompt finishes with approved content; the next prompt excludes the changed package until the user enables it again. Keep the existing plugin listing/tuple API, skill precedence, disabled behavior, and next-prompt refresh.

Validation:
- 68 passed: skills loader, context prompt cache, Agent Plugin lifecycle/containment/activation, and the migrated CLI App alias test. The new Event-controlled `AgentLoop.process_direct` regression covers replacement after discovery and during fingerprinting, approved content, next-prompt revocation, and re-enabling.
- Reused public runtime race probe: original base excludes the unapproved replacement; #6217 head and main reproduce the regression; this fix excludes it.
- Public prompt/runtime probe passes per-build scan/read/parse/CLI reuse, next-build document/new-skill/dependency refresh, precedence, disabled skills, project context, and session persistence. Full explicit turns retain their existing two snapshot scopes.
- Ruff on the three changed files; BasedPyright strict on the two changed production modules; Python import boundaries (10 rules, 158 files); `git diff --check`.

prs.title: perf(providers): estimate missing usage outside the event loop
prs.body:
When a provider returns a successful response without token usage, retry-managed chat calls estimate tokens synchronously on the event loop. Slow estimation delays other gateway work and is included in the measured request duration.

Keep reported usage, physical retry records, and fail-open observer behavior. Protect the shared tool-token cache when estimates run concurrently.

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain tasks for staged signal shutdown
prs.body:
Gateway shutdown handlers capture the empty task list during setup. Rebinding that list after startup leaves a repeated Ctrl+C unable to cancel the running gateway tasks when shutdown is waiting for a channel runner to finish.

Populate the captured list in place. Register SIGBREAK when the platform provides it, using the same first-signal shutdown request, repeated-signal cancellation, and handler restoration as SIGINT. Preserve the existing session flush and JSONL shutdown path.

Validation:
- Python 3.12.10: `COLUMNS=200 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest tests/cli tests/session/test_session_fsync.py tests/session/test_session_cache.py -q` — 693 passed, 3 skipped. The CLI regression uses real SIGINT registration and two signals against a cancellation-resistant channel runner, then checks resource cleanup, session flushing, and handler restoration. Its native SIGBREAK variant runs in the existing Windows CI job.
- Final regression tests against the original snapshot runtime fail on repeated SIGINT cancellation and missing SIGBREAK registration; the patched runtime passes those cases.
- Native Windows Python 3.11.4 smoke, using the exact current handler functions and a ProactorEventLoop: SIGINT and SIGBREAK both request shutdown first, cancel a task added after handler setup on the second signal, and restore previous handlers. This smoke covers the handlers; the full Windows CLI case is left to CI.
- `ruff check nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py tests/cli/test_commands.py`, strict BasedPyright for `nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py`, and `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` pass.

The default-width local CLI run has 10 nested-session path-output assertion failures. The shortest failing case also fails on a clean source archive of upstream snapshot `3a28b9e6ce5e514d4dee9d964056d876a69a6cdc` and passes there with `COLUMNS=200`: line wrapping removes a space from the path when the test joins output lines. The passing CLI/session run above uses that width; this PR does not change path diagnostics.

prs.title: feat(providers): add IO Intelligence (io.net) provider
prs.body:
> **Official io.net contribution.** This pull request is submitted on behalf of io.net, the team behind [IO Intelligence](https://io.net). We would like nanobot (HKUDS) users to be able to run inference on IO Intelligence out of the box. Happy to adjust anything to match the project's conventions, and we will keep the integration up to date.

## Summary

Adds IO Intelligence (by io.net) as a built-in provider, following the same registry pattern as SiliconFlow / Novita AI (OpenAI-compatible gateways whose model ids keep their `org/name` prefix).

IO Intelligence serves an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API at `https://api.intelligence.io.solutions/api/v1` (Bearer auth; `GET /models` is public). Model ids are `org/name` style, e.g. `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`. Users configure `apiKey` (env var `IONET_API_KEY`) and everything else derives from the registry entry.

## Changes

- `nanobot/providers/registry.py` — `ProviderSpec(name="ionet", ...)`: `backend="openai_compat"`, `is_gateway=True`, `env_key="IONET_API_KEY"`, `display_name="IO Intelligence"`, `detect_by_base_keyword="intelligence.io.solutions"`, `default_api_base="https://api.intelligence.io.solutions/api/v1"`, `strip_model_prefixes=("ionet",)` (an explicit `ionet/org/model` id is sent as `org/model`; opencode precedent). Placed in the gateway cluster after Novita AI.
- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — `ionet: ProviderConfig` field (the registry's documented step 2).
- `docs/providers.md` — "IO Intelligence Gateway" section in the same format as the Eden AI Gateway section (config example + notes), including the multi-gateway routing note.
- `docs/configuration.md` — `ionet` row in the provider directory table.
- `tests/providers/test_ionet_provider.py` — mirrors `test_edenai_provider.py`: config field exists, registry contract, forced-provider default base URL, gateway routes unprefixed models when configured (novita-parity), model-id preservation and top-level `reasoning_effort` passthrough through `_build_kwargs`.
- `tests/webui/test_settings_api.py` — `test_settings_payload_exposes_ionet_provider` (precedent parity with the Eden AI / OrcaRouter rows).
- `webui/src/lib/provider-brand.ts` + `webui/src/components/settings/shared/ModelControls.tsx` — WebUI brand entry, deferred model list, and provider icon, matching the OrcaRouter precedent (the WebUI loads the catalog after the API key is saved).
- `webui/src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx` — "defers the IO Intelligence catalog until the user searches" (OrcaRouter-parity coverage for the deferred list).

## Testing

- `pytest tests/providers/test_ionet_provider.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py tests/config` — 209 passed (7 ionet provider tests, including the prefix-strip and unprefixed-routing cases).
- Full python suite — 6102 passed / 9 skipped / 0 failures; serial CLI subset 157 passed. Two timing-sensitive gateway tests flake only under full-CPU parallel runs and reproduce identically on the base commit (environmental).
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py` (full CI scope) — clean; `basedpyright` (strict, full project) — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
- WebUI (bun, as CI runs it): `bun install --frozen-lockfile` clean, `bun run lint` (eslint --max-warnings 0) clean, `bun run test` — 96 files / 1554 tests passed; `tsc --noEmit` zero new errors vs the base commit (verified in a scratch worktree).
- Routing: 14 probe scenarios — ionet-only config routes everything; with other providers configured, colliding families (`deepseek-ai/*`, `qwen/*`, `google/*`, `mistralai/*`, …) route away (hence the docs pinning note); forced `provider: "ionet"` always wins; `ionet/org/model` is sent as `org/model` (prefix stripped).
- Live endpoint (unauthenticated): `GET /api/v1/models` → 200, 35 models, both example ids present, and the response parses through nanobot's catalog parser 35/35; `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` → 401 (base URL + Bearer model correct). `nanobot status` with an io.net config renders "IO Intelligence: ✓".
- `ruff format --check` not applied: the existing tree predates `ruff format` (it flags unrelated pre-existing lines); formatting churn is kept out of this PR. The new code follows the surrounding style.
- Live chat generation not tested (no API key available to the contributor); io.net-side acceptance of `reasoning_effort` on reasoning models remains the one key-gated unknown.

## Notes

- Chat Completions only: the spec sets no `responses_models`, so the OpenAI Responses path is never selected for io.net models (verified against the provider-level Responses restriction and the config-level `api_type` gate).
- `keywords=("ionet",)` keeps model-name matching conservative — io.net ids (`meta-llama/...`, `deepseek-ai/...`) are ambiguous across gateways, so users select the provider explicitly (same behaviour as SiliconFlow/Novita). With io.net as the only configured provider, plain model IDs route to it.
- `detect_by_base_keyword` is kept for registry-schema parity with the other gateway entries; it is only consulted in the local-endpoint fallback loop and has no runtime effect for a cloud gateway like this one.

prs.title: feat(update): integrate managed installs and recoverable in-app updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Connect managed installation, exact-version updates, recovery and the WebUI into one flow. This continues chengyongru's updater work in #5817 and the prepare-only candidate pipeline from #6154; their commits and attribution remain intact. #5817 was closed by its maintainer as a duplicate of this PR. Coordinate #6154 before merging.

- Fresh official installs use a dedicated environment and an explicit package-selection receipt, regardless of uv/pipx on PATH. Interrupted first installs retain their owner for retry. Existing installations retain their owner, extras and constraints.
- Installer-managed WebUI starts a persistent gateway. Other installations retain their prior lifetime; `webui --detach` remains explicit.
- The gateway reviews one exact version, stages a durable job, obtains stop/install/restart confirmation and verifies the restarted runtime. Duplicate/lost requests do not repeat installation.
- Frozen workers and a standard-library recovery launcher remain usable when application dependencies break. Explicit repair reuses saved bytes and the original backup. Restart-only repair does not reinstall packages.
- Unsupported installation owners receive owner-specific instructions. The browser never chooses executable URLs or shell commands.
- Linux and Windows CI exercise native platform-wheel installation, bundled WebUI/TUI and real gateway startup. Routine checks retain small reports, not installable candidates.

## Stable / Preview behavior

Settings → About keeps one check/update flow. A collapsed **Update settings → Receive preview updates** switch is off by default, with all ten locales. Preview is an optional preference rather than a second product mode. Waiting/withdrawal/errors remain visible outside the disclosure; installing a Preview target carries a warning. Switching the preference is separate from installation consent.

| Scenario | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Stable → newer Preview | Save subscription, offer exact verified candidate; no install/restart until confirmation. |
| Preview → next Preview or final release | Offer only a newer compatible version. Installing a final release does not unsubscribe from Preview. |
| Preview → Stable while stable is older | Save Stable, keep running the preview, wait for a newer final. No automatic downgrade. |
| Preview → Stable while Preview index is unavailable | A complete, compatible, verified newer final on PyPI remains available. An older/partial final never becomes a recovery offer or false success. |
| Current Preview withdrawn | Show a warning even if the only replacement is older, missing or incompatible. |
| Offline/partial/unpublished/incompatible feed | Report unavailable/publishing/unsupported, never false green success. |
| Stale tab or lost save response | Compare persisted revision; reject stale writes and reread actual state. |
| Channel changed after review | Invalidate the old review, including Stable → Preview → Stable. |
| Already staged, inactive update | Settle it through worker/stop/admission checks and retain diagnostic files. |
| Preparing, stopping, admitted or failed mutation | Require completion/settlement/recovery before changing channels. |

Preferences live outside replaceable package files, scoped to the OS account and canonical Python environment. Profiles sharing that installation share its subscription. Existing dev builds are not implicitly opted into Preview. The checker and planner use the same validated release feed; stable requires the complete PyPI wheel/sdist set. Preview uses the protected official catalogue and immutable GitHub manifests. An observed catalogue cannot rewind candidates, rewrite an existing version's commit/hash or reinstate a withdrawn version. Published pointers cannot be cleared to erase this history; retain the pointer and withdraw its version instead.

## Compatibility and authority

- The intentional new-install default remains a managed, persistent installation. Existing venv, uv, pipx, source, Docker, service and Desktop installations are not adopted, moved or wiped. Unknown extras are not guessed.
- Inline installation remains limited to supported managed environments and verified POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry transactions. Other owners/platforms retain their manager/distributor workflow; selecting a channel does not broaden authority.
- Channel mutation requires the existing authenticated local package-install permission. Remote callers can inspect but cannot change it. Native distributions retain their distributor's updater.
- Additive `webui.update-channels.v1` and an opt-in status query do not raise the core client protocol floor. Legacy clients keep their original response shape; unsupported states return an actionable failure instead of false success.
- New channel state is separate from configuration/chats. Old plan records without a channel revision remain readable and byte-identical; changing the preference invalidates their execution consent. No automatic chat/config migration, restore or package downgrade is introduced.
- CLI `--plan` follows the saved subscription; explicit `--plan --channel` is inspection only. Legacy `update`/`--check` remain stable-PyPI operations, `--dev` remains editable source, and external managers retain explicit version/channel selection. The release guide spells out these differences.
- Main's exact-text atomic writer is retained in the updater's stdlib atomic module, including Windows replacement semantics and directory durability.

## Verification

Final review and repair, head **`3f2ae0517`**, including main **`152abe794`**:

- Fixed two reproduced failures: leaving Preview was unnecessarily blocked by an unavailable Preview index despite a verified newer final; clearing an observed pointer could bypass catalogue history checks. Regression tests fail before each fix and pass after it.
- Replaced the prominent channel selector with the existing disclosure/toggle controls. Added a Preview-target consent warning, retained all saved/error feedback when collapsed, and updated both user and maintainer documentation.
- **208 focused backend checks** passed before the final catalogue guard; **62 release/feed/version tests** passed with the guard. **71 main-integration/packaging tests** passed after merging the MCP-preset change, retaining both `update_contract.json` and `mcp_presets.json` in package includes.
- **98 frontend checks** passed across update flow, channels, settings, disclosure, locales and gallery; **55 affected frontend checks** passed after the main merge. Counts overlap between runs and are not summed. Ruff, strict BasedPyright, WebUI lint, import boundaries and production TypeScript/Vite build pass.
- Real production UI + isolated gateway: default collapsed setting, persisted preference across refresh, saving/error feedback after collapsing, keyboard toggle, narrow viewport, Chinese/light and English/dark. Browser console was clear. No installation was triggered; no daily configuration/chats were touched. The temporary gateway and tab were closed.
- The first run at `15977924e` passed 8/9 jobs but exposed two Windows test timing failures. A controlled latency probe reproduced those and the matching exit-acknowledgement case: 3 failures before repair, 3 passes after. The exit tests now advance their test clock only after preparation commits and a live PID is observed. The real default-runtime Slack routing test keeps all route/persistence assertions with a bounded integration wait. All **61 relevant routing/stop tests passed**. No production timeout, shutdown guard or recovery authority was relaxed; the other production evidence above is unchanged by this test-only follow-up.
- Current head **`3f2ae0517` passed all nine CI checks**: [run 38598722451](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38598722451). This includes the full Windows Python 3.14 suite after the timing repair. Both native package reports identify test merge `a363f5eed`, whose parents are exactly main `152abe794` and this head. Both served 377 bundled WebUI assets, started a ready gateway and ran native TUI without frontend build tools or fallback downloads. Windows process cleanup used termination, not a claim of graceful shutdown. No remaining blocking defect was found in this scoped review. Maintainer approval and public release acceptance are still required; no approval, merge or publication was performed.

Earlier channel implementation evidence at **`581708535`** (unchanged lifecycle contracts reused, not newly executed counts):

- **314 backend tests passed** for subscription persistence/isolation, authorization, stale requests, discovery races, exact feeds, withdrawal/incomplete metadata, immutable catalogues, old saved plans and worker/stop/restart/recovery contracts. **61 CLI/legacy updater tests passed** after default plan inspection was bound to the saved channel.
- Disposable offline package tests actually install Stable → Preview, Preview → next Preview and Preview → final. Forced dependency-loss failures in Stable → Preview and Preview → final are repaired by the standalone launcher, preserving the original backup and user data. These use controlled release metadata and synthetic wheels, not public release downloads.
- Actual-gateway restart tests exercise protected activation separately from package installation; they are not claimed as public download-to-reconnect E2E.
- All 41 focused update UI tests pass: channel saving/denial/failure feedback, stale tabs, late old-host responses, missing status, no implicit install consent, update dialog and recovery re-entry. After merging `main` at `a48228109`, **310 frontend tests** pass across update and affected main-branch surfaces.
- Real browser verification uses the production build and an isolated real gateway, with controlled upstream metadata. Saved channel, unavailable feedback and refresh persistence were verified. No daily config/chat files or running daily instance were changed; the test gateway was stopped.
- After merging `main` at `a48228109`, **402 backend/packaging tests** pass across candidate/source correspondence, installation guide, packaged probe, provider/file-diff/settings changes and update routes. Python/client import boundaries, Ruff, strict BasedPyright, WebUI lint and production TypeScript/Vite build pass. Counts overlap and are not summed.
- Earlier head **`581708535` passed all nine CI checks**: [run 38559343124](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38559343124). Both Linux Python versions, Windows Python 3.14, Windows process/installer compatibility, WebUI, Linux/Windows native installation, Docker and change classification passed. The native reports identify test merge `0083df755`, whose parents are exactly main `a48228109` and this head. Both installed packages served 377 WebUI assets, started a ready gateway and ran the bundled TUI without frontend build tools or fallback downloads. Linux shutdown was graceful; Windows cleanup used termination, not a claim of graceful exit. Maintainer review is still required; no approval, merge or publication was performed.

Earlier macOS arm64 acceptance used the public installer for a private `0.3.5 → 0.3.6` update, backup, restart and reconnect, plus explicit restart-failure repair. Those labels were not public releases. Earlier Windows/Linux native package/startup checks are historical evidence, not a claim that all channel transitions have interactive native E2E on every platform.

## Release gates — not performed by this PR

- [ ] Maintainer review/approval and merge; coordinate overlapping #6154.
- [ ] Choose actual stable/preview versions. Existing users must install the first updater-enabled version with their existing installation method.
- [ ] Confirm the distributor can honor the three-year corresponding-source/relinking offer in `tui/SOURCE_OFFER.md`; review pinned notices and sources.
- [ ] Build final candidates from the exact reviewed source: five platform wheels, one sdist, matching native archives, checksums and provenance. Verify packaged upgrade/recovery; distinguish native execution from cross-builds.
- [ ] Approve GitHub/PyPI publication and protected release-index ownership. Advance the catalogue only after referenced assets are verified; index final releases for Preview subscribers too. Verify clean public installation and update before announcing availability.

prs.title: refactor(session): centralize state ownership in SQLite
prs.body:
Session persistence currently shares mutable cached sessions across turn execution, metadata updates, and shutdown. This replaces JSONL as the authoritative store with SQLite transactions and routes runtime state operations through a bounded worker pool, keeping storage I/O off the event loop.

A title or goal update can commit while a turn is running without being overwritten by that turn. Reset and deletion revoke old drafts so late results cannot restore replaced state. Accepted writes settle before cancellation or shutdown returns.

## Changes

- Store messages, metadata, provider continuation state, checkpoints, and pending inputs in SQLite with WAL, foreign keys, and `synchronous=FULL`. Metadata and checkpoint updates do not rewrite message history.
- Return detached session views and use explicit operations for turn commits, recovery, imports, forks, delivery, and Dream cleanup. Query sidebar metadata directly instead of scanning JSONL files.
- Admit WebUI messages against the resolved execution session and its generation in separate and shared-session modes. Preserve temporary-session guards and roll back newly created admission sessions when dispatch fails.
- Check revisions before reusing owner-held history; submit changed message suffixes and keep metadata, checkpoint, and follow-up updates off the message table. Queue mutations through one FIFO writer; readers retain their own connections. Drain accepted operations and stop workers before closing their connections.
- Read detached headers for controls and task lists, and project a committed sidebar snapshot without waiting for every active turn. Discover display files once per query and reuse the metadata snapshot for visibility and workspace scope.
- Check idle-archive eligibility through the indexed message suffix before loading a transcript. Skip command and summary checkpoint messages; scanning already archived sessions does not load or copy their history.
- Serialize idle and explicit SDK compaction with turns through the same session lock. Preserve the admitted draft and its delivery route while resolving summaries.
- Bound prompt filesystem work, history snapshots, and local token estimation in background jobs. Reuse skill discovery within one prompt, preserve next-prompt updates, and skip unused run-hook history snapshots. User hooks and runtime state changes remain on the owner loop.
- Drain the session worker on Windows Ctrl+Break and verify normal gateway exit before reopening its database in restart tests.
- When child-session admission is cancelled before its run starts, drain creation and remove the committed child before returning cancellation.
- Make SDK session operations asynchronous and remove deferred-save/flush behavior. Public interfaces intentionally change without compatibility wrappers; update SDK and CLI documentation accordingly.
- Import legacy JSONL once in a single transaction, reject malformed/conflicting sources, and commit completion with any pending workspace isolation. After commit, move workspace JSONL and checkpoints into private backups outside the workspace; external canonical originals and failed-import sources stay unchanged. Resume interrupted isolation before admitting conversations, without reimporting deleted sessions.
- Add ordered, transactional schema upgrades and explicit INSERT column lists. Preserve the v1 schema and reject newer databases before changing persistent settings.
- Keep JSONL support at the one-time import boundary and use SQLite backups for recovery. Remove the former `nanobot sessions restore-workspace` command; session-file export is deferred to a separate UI feature.

## Migration window

JSONL migration is introduced in **0.3.6**, supported through **0.4.x**, and removed in **0.5.0**. A version test requires removing the importer and startup hook at that boundary. Older installations must upgrade through the migration window.

This supersedes the persistence approach in #5580 and includes its event-loop fixes.

## Validation

Current head (`0b29f6243c1f6f7c31813b96c1f54f2f0808cd69`, based on `e8798ba6f`): autocompact and SDK coverage: 184 passed; combined session, WebUI admission, and subagent persistence selection: 189 passed. Ruff passed; BasedPyright over the 10 changed production modules reported 0 errors and 0 warnings. Import boundaries passed (10 rules, 158 files). Focused frontend tests: 99 passed; production build passed. Current-head CI: [run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38573993636).

Built gateway + Chromium verified ordinary message delivery in separate and shared-session modes against a localhost SSE provider stub, authenticated thread reads after refresh (HTTP 200), and shared history across two topics. All isolated gateway, browser, and provider-stub processes were cleaned up.

Previous head (`e8798ba6f`) is based on `4497f7ef2`. Idle scans check only messages at or beyond the persisted archive boundary using the existing `(session_key, position)` index, without adding fields or migrations. Regression coverage verifies that archived sessions and command/summary-only tails avoid full history reads, while subsequent ordinary messages still schedule archival. Focused session/autocompact/consolidator selection: 313 passed, 2 skipped; Ruff, BasedPyright (0 errors/0 warnings), import boundaries, and diff checks passed. All nine checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38537452357).

Retain real AgentLoop, warmed token counting, provider retry/safety, SQLite usage recording, and 200 ms deterministic model waiting.
