prs.title: fix(webui): reconcile turns after reconnect
prs.body:
A connection drop during a running turn could remove its spinner and show an update dot. When the turn finished while another topic was selected, returning could retain a partial answer until a browser reload. Persistent topics now retain their last confirmed execution state during reconnect, and recovery checks every unresolved topic, including inactive ones.

Completed history replaces the corresponding cached turn even when the message count is unchanged. A supplied completion list is authoritative for lifecycle turns: an empty list and idle metadata cannot close a newly queued turn. Hosts that omit the list retain their existing fallback, and supplemental input retains its separate acknowledgement behavior. Completed-turn replacement prefers exact identities and bounds anonymous matches so repeated text in older paginated history cannot move the current turn or its guidance ahead of that history. Newer live turns remain intact. Invalid completion identities admitted by the history parser are filtered so they cannot abort history adoption or discard valid rows.

A terminal wire event or thread update invalidates older shared latest-page reads. Surviving consumers join a fresh read, including when completion and the history update arrive separately. A delayed pre-terminal page cannot reopen the spinner; fresh HTTP failures still surface without undoing confirmed completion. Consumers cancel independently, and reads remain isolated by client, credentials, and cached baseline. Reads started before or during an outage cannot be reused by recovery.

Completed-turn replacement uses indexed anchors and a backward pass with linear time and temporary linear index memory. Initial activity detection is memoized between streamed updates, and recovery drains at most four jobs concurrently. Temporary chats retain their connection-owned lifetime. The WebUI protocol is unchanged; this does not add retransmission of an unfinished stream segment.

Validation:

- Fresh WebUI suite: 2,739 tests across 159 files passed with `bun run test -- --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`.
- Fresh `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports` (362 files), and 38 import-checker tests passed.
- Fresh built Chromium WebUI with an isolated real gateway, a local streaming provider configured through Settings, and a byte-preserving connection relay: normal streaming; disconnect before first output; inactive completion during an outage and return without refresh; two running topics switched back and forth; a new message queued while offline, followed by switching topics and reconnecting. All passed, including refresh parity and no uncaught browser errors.
- Regressions cover malformed completion identities through the actual history parser, the queued-send/HTTP snapshot race, later running and delta delivery, terminal notifications arriving separately from history updates, a failed fresh read after completion, scoped shared-read invalidation, and identified or anonymous guidance following repeated text in a retained pagination prefix. Existing cached-304, incomplete-transcript, compatibility, concurrency, cancellation, and newer-turn proofs pass in the full suite.
- Actual merge-helper benchmark at `9f653216a`, retained because the completion-identity validation follow-up does not change the merge helper, against `389fe741d` on this computer (Node 24.6, warmed synthetic inputs, median): 8,000 rows took 4.241 ms with all rows completed, 4.653 ms with mixed retained anchors, and 6.863 ms with only the latest 40 replaced. These measurements exclude React rendering, HTTP, projection, cache serialization, and device differences. The earlier optimization benchmark at `24cf94e63` reduced the latest-40 case from 156.924 to 11.154 ms; the review fixes retain linear processing.

User documentation describes connection and recovery behavior without implementation details.

prs.title: feat(tools): add read-only Google Drive tool
prs.body: Closes #6187 This adds a `google_drive` tool that reads files from Drive folders shared with a service account. The agent can list a folder, search, read file metadata and download a file into the workspace. Google Docs, Sheets and Slides are exported as text, CSV and PDF on download. Access is limited in three ways: the scope is `drive.readonly`, only files under the configured folder IDs are reachable (the client walks each file's parents to check), and downloads go through the workspace path resolver into a subfolder with a size cap (50 MB by default). Setup is config only for now: ```json "tools": { "drive": { "enabled": true, "credentialsPath": "secrets/drive-service-account.json", "rootFolderIds": [""] } } ``` The tool stays off until it has a readable service-account key and at least one folder ID. The Google libraries come from a new `drive` extra. I have a WebUI settings screen for this as well, but left it out to keep the PR small. It can follow separately if it's wanted. Key loading and API client setup live in `_google.py`, which the Sheets PR reuses. The config models are in `drive_config.py` and `google_config.py` per the config boundary rules, and both are on the import-boundary allowlist. Docs are in `configuration.md`. To try it: create a service account with the Drive API enabled, share a folder with its `client_email`, add the config above, restart, then ask the agent to list or download something from that folder. Checks run locally: ruff, basedpyright on the new files, the import-boundary script, and pytest on `tests/tools tests/agent tests/webui tests/config tests/architecture`. Tested in conversations.

prs.title: fix(agent): skip idle compaction during direct turns
prs.body:
## Summary

Idle compaction excludes sessions in `_pending_queues`, but `process_direct` does not use that queue. A direct turn exceeding the idle TTL can therefore be compacted while still running, and its final save can overwrite the summary checkpoint.

Include sessions with a held dispatch lock in the idle scanner's active set, alongside queued sessions. Direct and bus turns already share those locks, so this requires no separate activity registry or lifecycle bookkeeping.

Related: #6214

## Verification

- Added four regression cases covering direct turns with and without a real `read_file` call, followed by normal completion or cancellation.
- All four cases fail against unmodified main at `a48228109218bce17775014612c7aac2c2ffdce3` and pass with this patch.
- The tests advance only the idle scanner's clock, assert that a running direct turn is not archived, and verify that idle compaction persists a summary after the turn completes or is cancelled. Provider responses and summary generation are stubbed; tool execution, session reloads, checkpoint commits, and saves are real.
- Auto-compaction suites: **99 passed**.
- Adjacent concurrency, direct status, turn-save, recovery, and session-policy suites: **105 passed**.
- Ruff on both changed files, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Scope

This is a same-process activity guard. It does not coordinate separate gateway/API processes sharing session storage, or change arbitration for compaction that was already scheduled before a new turn began.

prs.title: fix(providers): preserve supported Kimi K3 reasoning efforts
prs.body:
## Summary

Update Kimi K3 reasoning-effort handling to preserve `low`, `high`, and `max`, and synchronize the settings suggestions with the [current official documentation](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-reasoning-effort).

## Root cause

The original normalization had a compatibility purpose: assuming K3 accepted only `max`, it converted enabled reasoning values inherited from K2.x presets to `max` to avoid sending unsupported parameters.

The current official documentation explicitly supports `low`, `high`, and `max`, with `max` as the default. K3 still always reasons, but its reasoning effort is configurable. The existing normalization therefore overrides valid `low` and `high` settings unnecessarily.

The settings metadata retained the same outdated restriction.

## Changes

- Preserve supported K3 reasoning levels. In `OpenAICompatProvider._build_kwargs()`, retain normalized `low`, `high`, and `max` values in `wire_effort`, while continuing to map other enabled legacy values to `max` and omit the field for `none` or `minimal`.
- Synchronize settings suggestions. In `reasoning_effort_values_for()`, expose Default, `low`, `high`, and `max` for K3.
- Update existing regression tests. Parameterize supported and disabled effort cases, retain the legacy-value compatibility check, and update the settings assertion.

## Result

Configured `low` and `high` values now reach K3 unchanged in both streaming and non-streaming requests. The original compatibility handling remains in place for other legacy values, and settings suggestions match the documented supported levels.

## Test

- Affected provider and settings test modules: 299 passed.
- Additional OpenAI SDK transport checks: 8 passed, covering `low`, `high`, `max`, and omitted effort in both request modes.
- Ruff checks passed for all four changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: feat(agent): add opt-in completion review for goals and child tasks
prs.body:
A normal model stop currently ends a child task, and `update_goal(action="complete")` closes a sustained goal based on the executor's own claim. For tasks with concrete deliverables, callers need a separate check before treating that result as accepted. Non-empty refusals, content-filter responses, and unrecovered truncation also need to retain their actual stop reasons.

This adds opt-in `acceptance_criteria` to goal creation/replacement and child-task creation. Criteria are fixed at creation. A bounded reviewer uses a separate context with the same configured model, the proposed result, and tool calls/results observed during the current run. It receives no executor reasoning and has no tools. Verdicts require strict JSON and valid evidence references; an evidence fingerprint binds the judgment to its inputs.

- Permit at most two review attempts, each with a 30-second deadline and at most 1,024 output tokens. Include review usage in both run totals and per-round accounting.
- Continue only after `needs_revision`, within the existing execution budget. Invalid/unavailable reviews and exhausted budgets cannot grant completion.
- Prevent same-turn goal criteria downgrades. A verified goal returns its accepted recap immediately, so no later tool call in that run can invalidate the proof.
- Persist child verdicts and carry them through inline results, status checks, and background notifications. Preserve existing execution states and ungated inline behavior; ungated notifications say “finished” rather than claiming success.
- Preserve refusal, content-filter, and unrecovered length stop reasons. Ordinary chat and tasks without criteria make no additional review requests.

The guide documents activation, budgets, delivery receipts, and limitations. This is a semantic review of observed evidence, not direct inspection of external state or a guarantee of model correctness.

Validation on commit `92b287df1774f7823154f94ddbc9d25e441744d5`:

- **All applicable GitHub CI jobs passed on this exact commit:** [run 37942097871](https://github.com/xcosmosbox/nanobot/actions/runs/37942097871). Linux Python 3.11 and 3.14 each passed 9,069 tests plus 160 serial CLI tests. Python 3.14 coverage reached 85.44%. Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, and Docker checks also passed. WebUI/TUI jobs were correctly skipped because their sources were unchanged.
- Ruff, strict BasedPyright, dependency consistency, and diff checks passed.
- Added 32 tests. The focused completion/goal/runner group passed 91 tests; the child lifecycle/context group passed 129; serial CLI tests passed 160.
- Broader agent/session regression: 1,979 passed. The final timeout-hardening change was additionally exercised by the focused group.
- Full Linux/Python 3.12 attempt: 9,056 passed, 48 skipped, 16 failed. Two failures were test doubles missing the new optional argument; these were fixed and covered by the 129-test rerun. All remaining 14 failures reproduced on unchanged upstream `a95e4dd`: 12 require public DNS, two require Unix sockets prohibited by this environment. One additional SSH multiplexing test was deselected after reproducing the same socket failure and teardown hang on upstream. No production or test code was changed to bypass these environment restrictions.

The reproducible experiment runs real file tools with a scripted executor and an independent receipt-based oracle. Both arms have the same per-case total call ceiling, including review calls. Across 9 scenarios per surface:

| Surface | False accepts, disabled → enabled | Total calls, disabled → enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Runner | 3 → 0 | 19 → 30 |
| Sustained goal | 3 → 0 | 34 → 43 |
| Child task | 3 → 0 | 19 → 30 |

All 54 cases passed their assertions. Enabled review accepts the normal success and repaired-success cases, and deliberately leaves one correct artifact unaccepted when the reviewer is unavailable. These are fault-injection results, not measured live-model accuracy, latency, or cost improvements. No live-model experiment was run because this environment has no provider credentials.

Reproduce the experiment with:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.experiment_completion_verification --output /tmp/completion-experiment.json
```

The output records the commit, dirty-tree status, source fingerprint, per-case outcomes, calls, and synthetic usage. Raw verification output is kept outside tracked source files.

issues.title: [Bug]: kanban_attach has no local-path option — large inline base64 risks silent mid-generation truncation

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`kanban_attach` only accepts file content as an inline `content_base64` string — there is no way to point it at a file already on disk. For anything beyond a trivial size, this requires the calling model to reproduce the *entire file* as one continuous base64 string within a single tool-call argument. That string has to survive uninterrupted generation for the whole turn; if the model's response gets cut short (context/output-length limits, a retry, a truncated stream), the resulting base64 *looks* superficially plausible but decodes to corrupt/incomplete data — and the failure mode (a padding/length error deep in `base64.b64decode`) gives the calling agent no clean signal that this is what happened.

`kanban_attach_url` already solves the equivalent problem for remote files — it downloads server-side instead of asking the model to relay bytes through its own output. `kanban_attach` has no analogous "read it directly" path for a *local* file, even though that's the far more common case (an agent that just wrote a report or took a screenshot has the file sitting right there on disk).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Produce a file large enough that its base64 encoding is a non-trivial fraction of the model's typical output budget (observed with a 140 KB PNG → ~187,000 base64 characters)
2. Have an agent call `kanban_attach` with `content_base64` containing that full encoded string
3. Under output-length pressure (verbose/reasoning-heavy models are more prone to this), the emitted string is truncated mid-generation

### Expected Behavior

Attaching a file that already exists on disk should not require passing its entire content through the model's own output — analogous to how `kanban_attach_url` avoids doing that for a URL.

### Actual Behavior

Observed directly in production: a Bridge kanban worker (model: `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`) attempted to attach a real 140,341-byte screenshot. The resulting `content_base64` argument was 16,489 characters — cut off partway through the expected ~187,120 — and failed with:

```
content_base64 is not valid base64: Invalid base64-encoded string: number of data characters (16489) cannot be 1 more than a multiple of 4
```

The file itself was completely intact on disk the whole time; only the model's in-band reproduction of it was corrupted.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Operating System

Ubuntu (Linux 6.8.0, x86_64)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream d0b87dad — confirmed still present on current `origin/main` (3781 commits ahead of this install); `_handle_attach` there still only supports `content_base64`, no local-path option.

### Root Cause Analysis

`tools/kanban_tools.py`'s `KANBAN_ATTACH_SCHEMA`/`_handle_attach` expose only `content_base64`. Any file bigger than "trivial" has to be losslessly reproduced by the model in one shot, which is inherently fragile — this is a design gap, not a decoding bug (see #77215 for the separate decoding-strictness bug in the same function).

### Proposed Fix

Add an optional `path` parameter as an alternative to `content_base64` (mutually exclusive, exactly one required) that reads bytes directly off disk server-side, reusing the existing `kb.KANBAN_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` cap:

```python
content_b64 = args.get("content_base64")
path_arg = args.get("path")
if content_b64 and path_arg:
    return tool_error("pass exactly one of content_base64 or path, not both")
if not content_b64 and not path_arg:
    return tool_error("one of content_base64 or path is required")

if path_arg:
    import os as _os
    src_path = _os.path.expanduser(str(path_arg).strip())
    if not filename or not str(filename).strip():
        filename = _os.path.basename(src_path) or "attachment"
    if not _os.path.isfile(src_path):
        return tool_error(f"path does not exist or is not a regular file: {src_path}")
    size = _os.path.getsize(src_path)
    if size > kb.KANBAN_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES:
        return tool_error(
            f"file at {src_path} is {size} bytes, exceeds the "
            f"{kb.KANBAN_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES}-byte attachment limit"
        )
    with open(src_path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
else:
    # existing content_base64 branch
    ...
```

Also update `KANBAN_ATTACH_SCHEMA`'s description to steer models toward `path` whenever the file already exists on disk, mirroring the existing "prefer `kanban_attach_url` when you only have a URL" guidance.

Verified locally end-to-end (live kanban worker, real file): attaching via `path` produced an attachment byte-for-byte identical (MD5-verified) to the source file, with correct dimensions/content on independent re-decode. No truncation risk, since the file is never round-tripped through the model's output.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Not right now, but the fix above is a working, tested implementation if a maintainer wants to land it directly (happy to share the full patched function on request).

issues.title: Add a strict release mode that reports or refuses unproven client and state teardown
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `AIAgent.release_clients` (`run_agent.py:925`) and `close_all_under` (`hermes_state_registry.py:362`) are best-effort. Each step's failure is swallowed, and the caller gets no signal on whether clients, child processes or SessionDB handles were actually released.

Callers that delete or move a profile, or recycle an agent cache slot, then carry on from an unproven state. Several open reports look like this (#137451, #137304, #127811).

Proposed fix: a keyword-only `strict=False` parameter on both. With `strict=True` they wait on the existing teardown barriers and check each handle closed, and if anything is still live they raise (or return a failure) instead of reporting success. The gateway agent cache and profile delete can opt in and keep the resource registered until teardown is proven.

issues.title: Option to stop replaying reasoning from finished turns
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `build_api_messages` (`agent/turn_context.py:1310`) replays stored reasoning (`reasoning_content`, `reasoning_details`, `reasoning`) on every earlier assistant row whenever the route accepts it. On long sessions, reasoning from turns that already finished can be a big share of the prompt. It costs tokens and context on every request, and the preflight estimate (`:70`) charges for it too.

Proposed fix: an opt-in setting that strips reasoning from assistant rows before the last user message. Routes that require the field keep a minimal pad, thinking-only assistant rows stay as they are, and the current turn goes in full. The token estimate should use the same trimmed view so compression triggers match what's sent. Related: #94211.

issues.title: TUI gateway starts a second notification poller on agent rebuild and orphans the first
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `_start_session_services` (`tui_gateway/session_registry.py:136-140`) always assigns `rec["_notif_stop"] = _start_notification_poller(...)`. It runs on session creation and again from `_announce_built_agent` (`:183`) when the agent is rebuilt for the same session.

The earlier poller's stop event is overwritten without being set. The old thread keeps draining the shared completion queue, and session close (`session_lifecycle.py:407`) can only stop the newest one. Leaked pollers compete for completions, which may explain some of the starvation reports around #120286.

Proposed fix: start a poller only when the record has none or its stop event is already set, or stop the old one before replacing it.

issues.title: Skills hub install: per-request quarantine, cross-process install lock, and per-profile dashboard actions
issues.body:
On main 379cf122:

1. `quarantine_bundle` (`tools/skills_hub_install.py:67`) writes to a fixed `<quarantine>/<skill_name>`, deletes any existing copy first, and never checks whether the quarantine root is a symlink. Two concurrent installs or scans of the same skill (CLI and dashboard, say) can delete each other's scanned files between scan and install.
2. `do_install` (`hermes_cli/skills_hub.py:791`) does an unserialized read-modify-write of the hub lock.json (`:879`), so two processes can lose each other's provenance rows. Atomic writes (#29699) fix torn files, not lost updates.
3. The dashboard install endpoint (`hermes_cli/web_routers/skills.py:102`) names its background action `_hub_action_name("install", identifier)` without the profile, so two profiles installing the same skill share one action and log slot. The scan endpoint (around `:272`) resolves the bundle under the requested profile, then quarantines and scans outside that scope.

Proposed fix: `tempfile.mkdtemp` per quarantine under a root checked not to be a symlink, an exclusive file lock under `skills/.hub` for the length of an install (fail fast with a clear message when it's held), the profile in the action name, and the whole scan body inside `_profile_scope(profile)`.

issues.title: Let managed scope force shared-metrics sending off
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, shared-metrics consent is profile-owned on purpose (`hermes_cli/observability/relay_shared_metrics.py:1316`), and `resolve_send_config` (`shared_metrics_send_config.py:47`) reads only the profile's own config.yaml. A managed scope can't pin `telemetry.shared_metrics.send` off.

Stopping IT config from opting a profile in makes sense. Stopping it from opting out doesn't, because some deployments must guarantee nothing leaves the machine, whatever a profile or the dashboard writes.

Proposed fix: treat a managed `telemetry.shared_metrics.send: false` as a one-way ceiling in `resolve_send_config`, and keep ignoring a managed `true`. The consent offer and dashboard toggle should show the locked state instead of writing a value that does nothing.

issues.title: Add a provider lock that forbids every fallback provider and credential swap
issues.body:
`fallback_providers: []` stops the model fallback chain (`try_activate_fallback`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:2086`), but on main 379cf122 other paths can still move a turn to a different provider or credential:

- credential pool rotation and Codex credential refresh (`agent/client_lifecycle.py:973`, `:570`)
- 401 recovery and the Codex app-server fallback (`agent/turn_recovery.py:401`, `:1712`)
- auxiliary and vision routing, and the background review runtime (`agent/background_review.py:253`)

An operator who must guarantee that one provider and one credential serve a profile has no single switch for it.

Proposed fix: a config key such as `model.provider_lock: true` that each of those seams checks before switching. When it's set they refuse and surface the original error instead of rerouting, and auxiliary tasks stay on the main runtime or fail closed. A managed scope should be able to pin it.

issues.title: Provider plugins with their own client can't start without an API key and base_url
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, CLI startup in `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py` requires a non-empty api_key (`:280`) and base_url (`:296`). The only exemption is `_keyless_custom_base` (`:97`), which covers local OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

A provider plugin that builds its own native client, or authenticates through a local session or SDK, has neither value, so startup fails with "no API key" or "empty base_url". The plugin has to invent a placeholder key and URL to get past the check.

Proposed fix: a `ProviderProfile` flag such as `requires_api_key: bool = True` (or a `keyless` auth_type) in `providers/base.py`. When the resolved runtime's profile sets it, startup skips both checks and leaves client construction to the plugin. Tests: a keyless plugin starts cleanly, and a normal provider still fails without a key.

issues.title: Expose max_result_size_chars and dynamic_schema_overrides on ctx.register_tool
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `registry.register` takes `max_result_size_chars` and `dynamic_schema_overrides` (`tools/registry.py:712-713`), but the plugin-facing `PluginContext.register_tool` (`hermes_cli/plugins.py:454`) doesn't accept or forward them.

Plugins that need a larger result cap, or a schema that changes at runtime, end up editing the registry entry after registration. That depends on private structure and can break on any refactor.

Proposed fix: add both as optional keyword arguments to `ctx.register_tool` and pass them through to `registry.register` unchanged. The existing guard against a `dynamic_schema_overrides` that renames the tool (#84690) still applies.

issues.title: Single-query (-q) turns get a new random task_id on every call
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, interactive chat runs `run_conversation(..., task_id=self.session_id)` (`hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py:326-329`). The single-query paths in `hermes_cli/cli_single_query.py` (`:84`, `:204`, `:227`, `:256`) leave `task_id` out, so `agent/turn_context.py:584` makes a new UUID for the first turn, each recovery retry and each follow-up.

Anything keyed by task id (terminal environments, browser sessions, background processes, approval scope) doesn't carry across turns of the same quiet session, and per-task cleanup can't find the earlier resources.

Proposed fix: pass `task_id=cli.session_id` at all four call sites, the same as interactive chat.

issues.title: execute_code tool calls and their connector batch entries have no distinct tool_call_id
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `_default_dispatch` in `tools/code_execution_rpc.py:30` calls `handle_function_call(tool_name, tool_args, task_id=task_id)` with no `tool_call_id`. Every tool call a script makes reaches `pre_tool_call`, middleware and observers with an empty call id. `tools/connectors/dispatch.py:46` only adds `#<position>` when a parent id exists, so entries in a batch made from `execute_code` share one id too.

Hooks that key approvals, budgets or dedup on the call id end up merging unrelated calls.

Proposed fix: give each RPC request its own id (the parent `execute_code` call id plus a sequence number, or a random hex) and pass it as `tool_call_id`. In `dispatch.py`, always add the position suffix, with a fallback prefix when there's no parent id. This complements #51931, which forwards `session_id` to the same nested calls.

issues.title: browser_tool_session: redact daemon output, and let a provider opt out of the local Chromium fallback
issues.body:
Two small gaps in `tools/browser_tool_session.py` on main 379cf122.

**Redaction.** #56162 routed CDP URLs through `_sanitize_url_for_logs` (`tools/browser_tool.py:185`) at the supervisor and session-creation log sites. Raw agent-browser stdout, stderr and exception text still reach logs and tool results here: the timeout message at `:111`, the stderr log at `:612`, the output read at `:773`, and the exception handler at `:884` (which also logs with `exc_info`). A provider CDP URL with a token in its query string can end up in logs and in the model's context. Fix: pass stdout, stderr and `str(e)` through the sanitizer right after they're read or caught, and drop `exc_info` on that warning.

**Local fallback.** `_create_cloud_session_or_fallback` (`:325-347`) launches local Chromium whenever the cloud provider's `create_session` raises. That's a good default on a desktop. Some deployments pick a cloud provider so pages never load on the host (network isolation, egress policy), and for them a silent local session is worse than a failed call. Fix: an `allow_local_fallback` attribute on `BrowserProvider` (`agent/browser_provider.py:29`), default True, maybe with a `browser.allow_local_fallback` config key. When it's False, raise a clean error that names the provider without the raw exception text.

issues.title: Browser idle cleanup can close a session that became active after it was picked
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `_cleanup_inactive_browser_sessions` (`tools/browser_tool_lifecycle.py:158-160`) builds the list of stale task ids under `_cleanup_lock` and then releases the lock. The teardown at `:168-172` runs later without checking again.

If a browser command calls `_update_session_activity` (`:469-477`) in that window, the janitor still closes the session the agent is using, and the next command fails or starts a fresh browser.

Proposed fix: before tearing a task down, re-read its last activity under the lock and skip it if it's no longer past the timeout. Also mark the picked session as reserved for cleanup, so a concurrent command opens a new session instead of reusing the one being closed, and clear the reservation in a `finally`. A test can pause the janitor between selection and teardown, touch activity, and assert the session survives.

issues.title: kanban: a max_retries=0 card is respawned after a rate-limited run
issues.body:
On main 379cf122, `check_respawn_guard` (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py:1588-1601`) treats a latest `rate_limited` run as neutral. Once the cooldown passes it returns None, and the card is claimed and spawned again.

That's right for ordinary cards. A card created with `max_retries=0` is meant to run once, though, and a worker can hit the quota wall after it has already done external work (sent a message, pushed a branch, called an API). Respawning it repeats those effects. The guard's SELECT (`:1588`) doesn't read `max_retries`, so the per-task limit never reaches this branch.

Proposed fix: select `max_retries` too, and when it's 0 and the latest run is `rate_limited`, return a guard reason such as `zero_retry_rate_limit` instead of None. `describe_suppression` would then show it, and an operator can requeue the card on purpose. Cards with `max_retries` unset or above 0 keep today's behavior. The same rule should apply to the auto-recovery work in #102770: it shouldn't revive a `max_retries=0` card on its own.

issues.title: [Bug]: TUI session list never loads (TypeError in session_authority._handle) after `hermes sessions delete` removes a live-registered session - every `session.list` crashes until gateway restart
issues.body:
### Build
- `hermes --version`: v0.22.1 (gateway `code_sha` `297552a9`)
- OS: Windows 11, native (git-bash); single profile `default`

### Surface and topology
Ink TUI -> shared gateway (`hermes gateway run --quiet --idle-exit`). The CLI reads the same store fine - only the gateway-served `session.list` path is broken.

### Steps
1. Gateway running; several sessions registered in its live registry (normal TUI/CLI use).
2. From another surface, delete one of those sessions while the gateway is up: `hermes sessions delete <id> --yes` (e.g. the current session of *another* open conversation - `sessions delete` allows this).
3. Open the TUI session switcher.

### Expected
List renders; the deleted session is skipped.

### Actual
Every `session.list` returns an error - the switcher never loads. The TUI polls the list (~1.5 s interval), so the crash loops until the gateway is restarted: **517 identical crashes in errors.log in one day**. `hermes gateway restart` fully heals it (the registry is in-memory only).

First reported as finding #5 ("Minor: `session.active_list` crash") in comment https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6181158031 - same signature, Desktop/API entry point. Filing separately because the TUI impact is a hard user-facing failure and the trigger above is deterministic.

### Evidence
```
ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws dispatch crash ... method=session.list
  File "...\gateway\session_controls.py", line 394, in list_sessions
    handle = await self.authority.resolve(self.actor, candidate)
  File "...\gateway\session_authority.py", line 209, in resolve
    return self._handle(ref)
  File "...\gateway\session_authority.py", line 204, in _handle
    return SessionHandle(ref, self.instance_id, self.epoch, row['runtime_revision'], ...
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

### Cause
- `session_authority._handle()` (line 204) assumes `db.get_session()` always returns a row. After `sessions delete` removes the row, the gateway's in-memory `authority.sessions` entry stays (delete does not evict live entries), so `row` is `None` -> `TypeError`.
- `list_sessions()` only skips `RuntimeStoreError` reasons `{permission_denied, profile_mismatch, not_found}` - one stale entry poisons the whole list response.
- Self-healing exists only on the register path (`_reserve_route` re-creates a missing row on the next inbound for that chat), never on the listing path.

### Suggested fix
Raise `RuntimeStoreError('not_found')` from `_handle()` when `row is None` (`list_sessions` already skips it), and/or evict `authority.sessions` entries on delete.

issues.title: Telegram: messages held across a disconnect are replayed out of order
issues.body:
### Bug

When Telegram delivery is fenced (disconnect, or a retryable fatal error), an update that arrives
behind the fence is held at once, while text / photo-burst / album batches that were still buffered
from before the fence are held later — by their own flush or by teardown salvage in
`_cancel_pending_delivery_tasks()`. `_hold_inbound_event` appends, so the reconnect drain replays the
newer update before the older one.

The same happens when a replay is interrupted: `_rehold_from` re-holds the rest of the replay behind any
update that arrived during the interruption.

### Reproduction (no network; `main` @ ca069e12)

```python
adapter = TelegramAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, token="t"))
adapter._text_batch_delay_seconds = 60
adapter._enqueue_text_event(event("earlier"))   # buffered, timer pending
adapter._mark_disconnected()                     # fence
adapter._enqueue_text_event(event("later"))     # held immediately
await adapter._cancel_pending_delivery_tasks()  # teardown salvages "earlier"
[e.text for e in adapter._held_inbound_events]   # ['later', 'earlier']
```

Same result for any mix of text, photo burst and album. Teardown salvage also walks the buffers by
kind (text, then photos, then albums), not by arrival.

### Expected

After reconnect, held updates are handed to the agent in the order Telegram delivered them.

### Impact

Telegram has already acknowledged these updates, so the hold queue is the only copy. Users see their
messages answered out of order after a network blip or a gateway restart. In a group, the agent can
reply to a later message before the question it depends on.

### Related, not addressed here

When the hold queue is full (`HELD_INBOUND_MAX`, default 64), the eviction is not strictly
oldest-arrival-first either: it drops the oldest *held* event before inserting the new one, so an older
update that is held late can survive while a newer one is dropped. This also happens on `main`;
noting it separately so the ordering fix stays focused.

issues.title: httpx2==2.12.0's 1 MiB per-SSE-event cap silently breaks MCP servers with a large tools/list (reported as "SSE stream ended without a response")

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/mcp
labels.description: MCP client and OAuth

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading to an environment that has `httpx2==2.12.0` (the pin Hermes carries for the `mcp` extra since `bc8545bd1a`, "bump httpx2/httpcore2 2.7.0 -> 2.12.0 for the audit advisories"), any HTTP MCP server whose `tools/list` response arrives as a **single SSE event larger than 1 MiB** becomes unconnectable.

The failure is deterministic, but the reported error is a red herring:

```
$ hermes mcp test <server>
  ✗ Connection failed (12.3s): SSE stream ended without a response
```

The real cause, swallowed by the MCP SDK, is:

```
httpx2.SSEError: Server-sent event exceeded the 1048576 byte limit.
```

Hermes then parks the server (`MCP server '<x>' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested`), and the desktop Catalog shows "The server refused the connection." Nothing about the token, the URL, or the network is wrong.

## Root cause

1. `httpx2/_config.py` (2.12.0):

   ```python
   DEFAULT_MAX_EVENT_SIZE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
   ```

   enforced in `httpx2/_sse.py::_SSEEventDecoder._check_size()`:

   ```python
   raise SSEError(f"Server-sent event exceeded the {self._max_event_size} byte limit.")
   ```

   `httpx2 2.9.1` (the last release below 2.12) has no `max_event_size` in `httpx2/_sse.py` at all, so this is a new hard cap, not a pre-existing one. It is still present in `httpx2 2.13.1`. No env var or config knob is documented for it, and `EventSource.__init__` just defaults to the constant.

2. `mcp 2.0.0` builds the SSE reader with the default limit and never passes one:

   `mcp/client/streamable_http.py` -> `event_source = EventSource(response)`

3. `mcp/client/streamable_http.py::_handle_sse_response` wraps the iteration in a bare `except Exception:` that only logs `SSE stream ended` at DEBUG, then synthesizes `MCPError(CONNECTION_CLOSED, "SSE stream ended without a response")`. So the `SSEError` never reaches Hermes, and at default log levels the user sees a generic "no response".

Net effect: with `httpx2==2.12.0` pinned, `max_event_size` is not reachable from Hermes or the SDK, and every MCP server with a >1 MiB single-event `tools/list` (large OpenAPI-backed servers, e.g. Cloudflare's `https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp?codemode=false`, which returns ~3,700 tools in one ~3.6 MB event) is dead on arrival.

## Why it shows up as a sudden break

It only manifests once the dependency environment is rebuilt. If the runtime already has an older `httpx2` (e.g. 2.7.0), the same MCP server connects fine; after an update that produces a fresh environment with 2.12.0, that server stops connecting with no config change on the Hermes or server side. Same tree, same `mcp==2.0.0`, different `httpx2` -> different outcome.

## Reproduction

1. Configure any HTTP MCP server whose `tools/list` is one >1 MiB SSE event. Public example:

   ```yaml
   mcp_servers:
     cf:
       url: https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp?codemode=false
   ```

2. `hermes mcp test cf` -> `Connection failed: SSE stream ended without a response` (deterministic).

3. Server side is provably healthy. The POST to the MCP endpoint for `initialize` returns 200, and the POST for `tools/list` returns `HTTP 200`, `content-type: text/event-stream`, with a complete single `event: message` frame of ~3.64 MB and no `nextCursor`. Other MCP servers on the same host (small `tools/list`, and the same CF server with `?codemode=true` which returns 4 tools) connect fine, so it is purely the event size.

4. To see the swallowed error, run the SDK directly against the endpoint with DEBUG on `mcp.client.streamable_http`:

   ```
   httpx2.SSEError: Server-sent event exceeded the 1048576 byte limit.
     File ".../httpx2/_sse.py", line 223, in __aiter__
     File ".../httpx2/_sse.py", line 184, in decode
     File ".../httpx2/_sse.py", line 124, in _check_size
   ```

   Note that `initialize()` succeeds; only `list_tools()` blows up, which is why a naive "can I reach the server" probe misses it.

## Impact

- Any MCP server that returns a large `tools/list` in a single SSE event is unusable while `httpx2==2.12.0` is pinned. Large API-backed servers are exactly the interesting ones.
- The failure is silent and misattributed: the surfaced error points at connectivity, so it reads as a server outage / bad token, and there is no diagnostic hint that a client-side size cap is responsible.
- Hermes parks the server, and re-running the test reappears to succeed for `initialize` only, which makes triage harder.
- Any user-facing workaround requires changing the server's tool surface (e.g. switching CF to `codemode=true`), i.e. losing functionality to work around a client cap.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Do not let the SDK's default cap decide whether a server is reachable.** The clean fix is upstream in `mcp`: expose `max_event_size` (or a sse-limit option) on the streamable HTTP client so callers can raise it / disable it for tool listing. Hermes already owns its own `httpx` client object for this transport, so it is well placed to pass a limit.
2. **Stop swallowing the cause.** At minimum, catch `SSEError` (or log the full exception at WARNING) in the transport and surface it, e.g. `Connection failed: server-sent event exceeded the 1048576 byte limit`. Today the single most actionable string in the whole failure is invisible at default log level.
3. **Consider the pin.** The 2.12.0 bump was needed for audit advisories, but it also changed transport behavior. If 1/2 can't land quickly, a bump-blocking note or an env/config escape hatch for the SSE cap would help until `mcp` exposes it.
4. For reference, the server side could also paginate its `tools/list` (the response has no `nextCursor`), but that is out of Hermes' hands and shouldn't be required for correctness.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.0+119.g0e427d7 (2026.9.24), git install, Linux x86_64
- runtime venv: Python 3.14, `mcp==2.0.0`, `httpx2==2.12.0`, `httpcore2==2.12.0`
- control: an older runtime environment with `httpx2==2.7.0` + the same `mcp==2.0.0` connects to the same server and discovers all tools

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop boot fails with `Gateway starting (deadline)` when the sticky active_profile is a parked profile — regression after update
issues.body:
## Bug Description

After `hermes update` (2026-10-15, build `297552a9`, report version `0.22.0`), **Hermes Desktop fails to boot whenever the sticky active profile is a profile the supervised gateway cannot serve** — it burns the full `gateway ensure` deadline (~60s), shows *"Hermes couldn't start"*, and retries in a loop. The desktop never gets a definitive verdict such as `inaccessible` / `profile_parked`; it only ever sees `state: starting, reason_code: deadline`.

This is a regression introduced by the update: the **same** `active-profile.json` (a named profile, unchanged since 2026-09-01) booted fine for weeks before the update.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (arm64, headless host), Hermes Desktop `apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app`
- Hermes `0.22.0`, `code_sha 297552a9d646119871391d202509822cd86330df`
- Gateway: **standalone / supervised (launchd)**, `gateway_state.json` → `served_profiles: []`, `multiplex_standalone_reason` populated
- Profiles: `default` + named profiles (`coding-agent`, `youtube-faceless-agent`) that carry **the same `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` value** as `default`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a named profile whose `.env` holds the same `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` as the `default` profile, so the gateway parks it (`multiplex_standalone_reason`, `served_profiles: []`).
2. Set the desktop's sticky profile to that parked profile: `~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/active-profile.json` → `{"profile": "coding-agent"}`.
3. Quit and relaunch `Hermes.app` (or boot after `hermes update`).
4. Desktop calls `gateway ensure` for the sticky profile and waits for the deadline.

## Actual Behavior

Desktop log (first `deadline` line ever recorded in a log that starts 2026-10-01, i.e. ~2 weeks clean):

```
2026-10-15 09:51:09 [hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Gateway starting (deadline). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.
2026-10-15 09:58:23 [hermes] [renderer error:main] Hermes couldn't start: Error: Error invoking remote method 'hermes:connection': Error: Gateway starting (deadline)...
```

174 `deadline` lines on that day, retrying on the same ~60s cadence as the deadline; the user sees a permanent "connection" loop.

CLI equivalent of exactly what the desktop asks for:

```
$ hermes --profile coding-agent gateway ensure --json
{"state":"starting","reason_code":"deadline","endpoint":null}        # ~8s, timeout 6s

$ hermes --profile default gateway ensure --json
{"state":"ready","endpoint":{"api_origin":"http://127.0.0.1:58610", ...}}   # ready in ~1.7s
```

`gateway_state.json` explains *why*, but the desktop never surfaces it:

```
"served_profiles": [],
"multiplex_standalone_reason": "Profiles 'default' and 'coding-agent' both hold the same telegram
credential (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN): one platform token can serve only one gateway ... then run
hermes gateway migrate --multiplex.",
"parked_profiles": {}
```

Note `parked_profiles` is `{}` — the client gets no per-profile verdict to branch on, and `_multiplexer_starting(home)` keeps returning `True` while the running gateway holds the root lock, so the client waits for a multiplexer reservation that will never arrive → `TimeoutError` → `starting/deadline`.

Additional noise after the boot failure: the renderer keeps restoring a session of the parked profile and logs `Invalid gateway ticket response` for `GET /api/sessions/<id>?profile=<parked>` (bounded to ~3 retries on this build).

## Expected Behavior

Any of:

1. `gateway ensure` for a profile that the running gateway **cannot** serve (credential parked / not in `served_profiles`) returns a **definitive, actionable verdict** (`inaccessible` / `profile_parked` / `multiplex_unavailable`) immediately, instead of `starting` + `deadline`.
2. The desktop boot surfaces that verdict in the "Hermes couldn't start" dialog (which profile, why parked, and the documented recovery: give the profile its own token, or remove the duplicate `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, or route it with `gateway.profile_routes`, then `hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`) instead of a bare "Gateway starting (deadline)".
3. If an autostart profile cannot be served, fall back to booting the desktop on a profile the gateway *does* serve (e.g. `default`) rather than failing the whole app boot.

## Regression Detail (why the update caused it)

Same host, same `active-profile.json` (`coding-agent`, set 2026-09-01), ~6 minutes apart across the update:

**Before the update (old build, 2026-10-15 09:43:37)** — desktop spawned its own backend and booted the sticky profile fine in ~4s, each profile getting its own backend:

```
[backend] `serve` supported for Hermes at /Users/mac/.hermes/hermes-agent
[boot] Starting Hermes backend via Hermes at /Users/mac/.hermes/hermes-agent
HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=58297
[boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
[gateway-route win=main] active key=coding-agent via=primary conn=local profile=coding-agent
[gateway-route win=main] conn:local::coding-agent via=primary primary=local/coding-agent
```

**After the update (`[updates] launched posix hand-off` 09:44:40 → `detached update finished OK` 09:49:55)** — no spawn line at all; desktop attaches to the supervised standalone gateway via `gateway ensure`, and the parked profile now fails the boot outright:

```
[updates] detached update finished OK (branch main)
[boot] Using Hermes at /Users/mac/.hermes/hermes-agent
[boot] Desktop boot failed: Gateway starting (deadline). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.
```

So the update changed the desktop boot path from *spawn-own-backend* to *attach-to-supervised-gateway*. A pre-existing, previously harmless configuration (a named sticky profile sharing the default profile's Telegram token) becomes a hard boot failure. `active-profile.json` lives in Electron userData and is **not** rewritten by `hermes update` — it is the boot path, not the file, that changed behavior.

## Impact

- Desktop is unusable (no chat, no settings) until the user manually learns to edit `active-profile.json` — the failure mode gives no clue that the profile is parked.
- Any multi-profile fleet where a named profile duplicates another's platform token and is set as the desktop's active profile hits this on every launch, with a ~60s retry loop.

## Workaround

Set `active-profile.json` to a profile the gateway serves (`default`) and relaunch — verified recovery here: `[boot] Hermes gateway is ready` in ~2.3s. Note the sticky profile stays unusable from the desktop until it gets its own bot token + `hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`.

## Possible Duplicates

#132645 (Windows: `hermes update` leaves the host gateway down when a named profile is the sticky active_profile), #135990 (`active-profile.json` never updated across restarts), #138778 (multiplexed gateway stop marks a profile parked). None of them cover the desktop boot path returning `starting/deadline` for a parked sticky profile.

issues.title: desktop: composer model switch silently fails (session_busy / revision_conflict) until a session-level operation
issues.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.1** (commit `297552a9d6`), desktop app (local build via `hermes update`), Windows 11, local gateway

### What happens

Picking a different model in the desktop composer frequently does nothing — the model doesn't change and there is no visible effect. Switching to another session and back (or similar session-level operations) and re-picking then works.

Renderer log from one day of v0.22.1 use shows repeated failures:

```
Model switch failed: JsonRpcGatewayError: session_busy
Model switch failed: JsonRpcGatewayError: revision_conflict
Model switch failed: JsonRpcGatewayError: revision_conflict
模型切换失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: session_busy
```

At least two of these fired while the session was visibly **idle** — no turn was running.

### Notes

- The desktop switch path is `config.set` with `key: 'model'` (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts`). On the owner the gateway requires `session.mutate operation=model` (revision-fenced; `gateway/session_busy_controls.py::busy_config` raises `use_session_mutation_model` for the legacy verb).
- `session_busy` maps `MUTATION_GUARD_REFUSALS` (a live turn lease / compression lock) — but it fires right after turns end, when no turn is visibly running, so the lease/execution stamp seems to linger past turn end.
- On `revision_conflict` (`hermes_state_runtime.py` mutation revision fence) the desktop neither retries with a fresh revision nor keeps any visible pending state — the composer just keeps the old model until some other operation re-syncs it.

### Expected

- A post-turn model switch succeeds (the lease is released by then).
- `revision_conflict` is retried once with the current revision, or the failed state is surfaced in a way that makes clear the switch did not land.

issues.title: desktop: a fresh session's first submit answers with a busy-style reply until the model is re-picked
issues.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.1** (commit `297552a9d6`), desktop app (local build via `hermes update`), Windows 11, local gateway

### What happens

Open a new chat in the desktop app and send the first message immediately: the turn runs (1 API call lands on the provider) but the reply is a ~66-char fixed busy/apology-style text instead of a real answer, delivered non-streamed. Resending the exact same text right after succeeds normally (streamed, real answer).

The user-visible workaround matches: re-picking the model in the composer (even the same model) makes subsequent submits work, even though the composer already showed that model as current.

Observed pattern in the gateway log (several fresh sessions on v0.22.1, first day of use):

```
# first submit of a fresh local session
... Normal final-send NOT suppressed despite active stream consumer ... streamed=False previewed=False
    content_delivered=False transformed=False final_len=66 — possible duplicate send (see wecom ack-timeout RCA).
... response ready: platform=local ... time=35.6s api_calls=1 response=66 chars

# immediate retry of the same text
... Suppressing normal final send ...: final delivery already confirmed (streamed=True ...)
... response ready: platform=local ... time=12.4s api_calls=1 response=31 chars
```

The `streamed=False` + fixed-length reply on the first submit is the anomaly — the same session's retry streams fine.

### Suspected area

The fresh session's first turn appears to fall into the "active session busy message" family (`gateway/run_busy.py::_handle_active_session_busy_message`) or races the session's initial attach/lease state, producing the fixed busy-style reply instead of a normal streamed turn. A model re-pick (`session.mutate`) seems to re-sync the binding so later submits run normally.

### Expected

The first submit of a brand-new session runs a normal streamed turn; no model re-pick needed.

issues.title: desktop: statusbar cache-hit-rate / tokens-per-second never populate — canonical session.usage ticks carry top-level fields, desktop only reads nested usage
issues.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.1** (commit `297552a9d6`), desktop app (local build via `hermes update`), Windows 11, local gateway

### What happens

Since v0.22.1, the desktop statusbar items **cache-hit-rate** and **tokens-per-second** never populate — they stay at the `—` placeholder during the turn and (user-observed) do not recover afterwards either. The same session's agent log shows healthy per-call cache numbers (`cache=NNN/NNN (99%)`), so the underlying counters exist.

### Root cause

The canonical `session.usage` event carries the session-cumulative counters as **top-level payload fields** — `tui_gateway/contracts/events.py::SessionUsagePayload` documents this explicitly ("a canonical local viewer's session-cumulative counters ... **at the top level**"): `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `tokens_per_s`, `cache_read_tokens`, `avg_latency_s`, etc.

The desktop handler (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/session-info.ts`) only merges **`payload?.usage`** — the nested shape the old TUI usage ticker emitted:

```ts
if (event.type === 'session.usage') {
  if (payload?.usage && sessionId) {   // ← never true for canonical ticks
    ...
    setCurrentUsage(current => ({ ...current, ...payload.usage }))
  }
}
```

With canonical ticks `payload.usage` is undefined, so the merge never runs and `currentUsage` is never updated mid-turn. The desktop's own test (`usage.test.tsx`) also builds the nested shape, so only the legacy shape is covered.

The statusbar labels (`apps/desktop/src/lib/statusbar.tsx`) read `usage.cache_hit_pct` / `usage.avg_tps`, which only the `tui_usage()` projection (`message.complete.usage`) provides — the canonical tick names are `cache_read_tokens` / `tokens_per_s`.

### Expected

Desktop normalizes the canonical top-level shape into the usage store (or the gateway nests canonical ticks under `usage` like the TUI ticker did). Either way a field mapping is needed: `tokens_per_s` → `avg_tps`, `cache_read_tokens`/`prompt_tokens` → `cache_hit_pct`.

issues.title: desktop: live reasoning stream never appears mid-turn — desktop never sets the session's show_reasoning flag (v0.22.1 regression)
issues.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.1** (commit `297552a9d6`), desktop app (local build via `hermes update`), Windows 11, local gateway
- Model: any reasoning-capable model over an OpenAI-compatible provider

### What happens

Since the v0.22.1 update (unified gateway runtime), the desktop app shows **no live reasoning stream while a turn is running**. The reasoning content only appears once the turn completes, rendered from the persisted message.

### Root cause

On the session authority, `reasoning.delta` is only published when the live session's `show_reasoning` flag is on — `gateway/local_viewer_events.py::wire()` installs the reasoning sink only when `show_reasoning(turn)` is true, and that reads the live session attribute: *"off until a viewer sets it"*.

The classic CLI syncs this automatically: `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`'s `reasoning_callback` setter sends `config.set key=show_reasoning value=1/0` on every change (including at attach). The desktop app has **no equivalent sync** — every `show_reasoning` reference in `apps/desktop` (9 occurrences) is renderer-local UI mirroring (`store/reasoning-disclosure.ts`, settings pages, types); none of them pushes the session-scoped flag to the gateway.

Pre-0.21.7 behavior differed: the old emit-side gate fell back to the config default (*"Missing means the config default, not hidden"*, `tui_gateway/server.py::_session_show_reasoning`), so a user with `display.show_reasoning: true` got the stream. The v0.22.1 canonical gate has no config fallback, and desktop never sets the flag → always off.

### Repro

1. v0.22.1 desktop, send any message on a reasoning-capable model → no live reasoning mid-turn.
2. Type `/reasoning show` in the composer → the current session's live reasoning appears (the command sets the session flag; the response echoes `reasoning: show`).
3. Open a new session (or let the session's live state be evicted) → silent again, because the flag is session-scoped and nothing re-sets it.

### Expected

Desktop syncs `display.show_reasoning` to the session on activate (like the classic CLI does), or the canonical gate falls back to the config default the way the pre-0.22 TUI gateway gate did.

issues.title: Anthropic 'credentials are rate-limited for <model>' AuthError has no code, so a kanban worker exits 1 (not 75) at startup and charges the failure breaker
issues.body:
## Summary

When the Anthropic credential is benched for the requested model, `_anthropic_token_or_raise()` (`hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`) raises

`AuthError("Anthropic credentials are rate-limited for <model>; other Claude models remain available (see `hermes auth list`).")`

**without** `code=CODEX_RATE_LIMITED_CODE`. `_ensure_runtime_credentials()` sets `_credentials_rate_limited = is_rate_limited_auth_error(exc)`, and that predicate requires `exc.code == CODEX_RATE_LIMITED_CODE`, so it is `False`. `_single_query_exit_code()` therefore returns `1`, not `KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE` (75). The kanban dispatcher books the run as `crashed` (a plain non-zero exit) and charges the failure breaker, instead of booking `rate_limited` and requeueing without counting a failure.

#112500 (closing #101800) made `chat -q` workers exit 75 on a rate-limit wall, and the credential-resolution path already maps `is_rate_limited_auth_error` to 75. The plumbing exists; only the code on this raise is missing.

Observed on a 0.21.x install; `_anthropic_token_or_raise` is byte-identical on current `main` (compared 2026-10-14).

## Impact (one board, anonymised)

A roughly 2 h model quota window killed 5 running workers with exit 75 (correct handling). The dispatcher then respawned 4-5 workers in a single pass. Each died at startup in under a second with the message above (exit 1, zero tokens, no session) and was booked `crashed`. The failure breaker tripped (with several identical same-pass failures the systemic same-error rule trips it at the first failure, otherwise at the default limit of 2; which rule fired on our board was not checked), and the cards sat blocked for about 1.5 days until a human unblocked them.

## Reproduce (offline, no credentials)

A small script stubs the credential lookup so a token exists but is benched for the model, calls the real `_anthropic_token_or_raise`, then:

- `is_rate_limited_auth_error(exc)` -> `False`
- `_single_query_exit_code(None, credentials_rate_limited=False)` with `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` set -> `1` (not 75)

On a scratch copy of `runtime_provider.py` with `code=CODEX_RATE_LIMITED_CODE` added, the predicate is `True` and the exit code is `75`. Without `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` the exit stays `1`. Not exercised: the `_ensure_runtime_credentials` -> `_credentials_rate_limited` hop (the predicate result is passed in by hand).

## Suggested fix

```diff
-    ACTUAL_LOCAL_NOAUTH_PLACEHOLDER, AuthError, DEFAULT_CODEX_BASE_URL, ...
+    ACTUAL_LOCAL_NOAUTH_PLACEHOLDER, AuthError, CODEX_RATE_LIMITED_CODE, DEFAULT_CODEX_BASE_URL, ...
...
             raise AuthError(f"Anthropic credentials are rate-limited for {model}; "
-                            "other Claude models remain available (see `hermes auth list`).")
+                            "other Claude models remain available (see `hermes auth list`).",
+                            code=CODEX_RATE_LIMITED_CODE)
```

plus a regression test asserting exit 75 for a kanban worker on this error.

Optional hardening: the existing per-task `rate_limit_cooldown` (default 300 s) could be extended to the same credential/model, so a still-limited credential is probed by one worker rather than N.

Related but distinct: #81437 (exit-75 reachability and the `blocker_auth` guard), #101800 (closed), #77881 (cold retries, no continuation).

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I want to start a fresh Telegram conversation inside an existing Hermes Desktop Project without first opening Desktop, editing gateway configuration, changing the profile-wide active project, or permanently binding a Telegram topic to one project.

The model picker already provides the interaction pattern I want: a command followed by Telegram inline buttons. For projects, the equivalent should be `/new -project`, then selecting an existing project.

## Proposed Solution

Add a Telegram inline project picker to `/new -project` (supporting `--project` as an alias is welcome, but preserve the requested `-project` form).

1. `/new -project` opens an inline picker listing non-archived projects from the current routed Hermes profile's existing Desktop project registry.
2. Selecting a project with one workspace starts a fresh session in that workspace. For projects with multiple registered workspace folders, present a second folder picker with Back and Cancel before creating the session.
3. The selected project/workspace becomes the new session's actual working directory and persisted project association, using the same mechanisms Desktop uses. The session must appear under that project in Desktop, not merely receive a prompt mentioning it.
4. Confirm the selected project after successful creation. Subsequent messages in this Telegram chat/topic go to the new session.

Reuse the existing inline model-picker interaction and session-creation machinery where practical. Do not introduce a separate project registry or change the process-global working directory.

### Acceptance criteria / definition of success

- **Non-destructive opening:** opening, paging through, going Back, cancelling, or abandoning the picker does not reset, replace, or alter the current conversation.
- **Real fresh session:** a valid final selection creates exactly one new session ID, preserves the previous transcript, switches only the invoking chat/topic, and carries no prior conversation messages into the new session.
- **Real project context:** persisted session metadata and effective tool working directory agree with the selected registered workspace. Applicable project instructions follow the same rules as Desktop; Desktop groups the session under the selected project. This remains true on subsequent turns and after a normal gateway restart/resume.
- **Profile and conversation isolation:** list/resolve projects from the routed profile. Do not change the profile-wide active-project pointer, another chat/topic's session, or another session's cwd.
- **Complete selection:** all eligible projects are reachable through pagination when needed. Duplicate display names are distinguishable and selections use stable identifiers. Multiple registered workspace folders receive the second picker; no arbitrary path entry is required.
- **Safe callbacks:** enforce existing gateway authorization and bind picker state to the initiating user, chat/topic, profile, and expected current session. Reject forged, wrong-user, wrong-chat, expired, superseded, or replayed callbacks without a session switch. Repeated taps must not create multiple sessions.
- **Safe errors:** an empty registry, deleted/archived project, removed workspace, missing/inaccessible directory, or creation/persistence error produces a useful message, not a fallback to the default cwd. Validate again at selection time. On failure, the previous conversation remains usable and no partial replacement becomes active.
- **Busy-session safety:** follow existing `/new` concurrency policy; do not race an active turn or redirect its output into the new session. Test and document the chosen behavior.
- **Compatibility:** ordinary `/new`, existing session naming, the model picker, and unrelated platforms remain unchanged. Unknown flags must not silently turn this request into an ordinary reset or session title.
- **Evidence:** automated command, callback, session-persistence, and isolation tests cover these paths, with a Telegram-to-Desktop smoke-test procedure and honest results. Document the command and its scope.

### Definition of failure

A picker that only changes a prompt/global cwd, creates a session before selection, loses the old transcript, fails Desktop grouping, lists another profile's projects, changes unrelated conversations, silently falls back on error, or permits replay/unauthorized selection does not satisfy this request. A UI-only scaffold or untested helper not wired into the production gateway path is not an implementation.

## Alternatives Considered

- #128618 and PR #128624 propose config-based channel/topic-to-project bindings. Related infrastructure, but not an interactive choice made when starting a session.
- #61136 proposes persistent topic context and a `/topic workdir` command. This request selects registered Desktop Projects, rather than entering paths or permanently binding topics.
- #37277 proposes session-scoped workspace commands. Related, but the requested UX is a discoverable picker of existing projects.
- PR #104213 addresses project/worktree selection in Desktop, not this Telegram flow.
- Profiles are separate agents/configurations, not a substitute for choosing projects inside one profile.

## Non-goals

No cross-platform transcript merging, automatic migration of existing conversations, project creation/deletion, new worktrees, persistent topic bindings, or gateway restarts. This request does not change the semantics of a later plain `/new` beyond its existing behavior.

## Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

## Scope

Cross-cutting command/callback/session integration; reuse existing components and avoid an unrelated architecture refactor. Exact size depends on current upstream implementation.

## Contribution

Implementation and a focused PR are planned; this issue defines the requested behavior and acceptance tests.

issues.body:
## Problem

`hermes -p <name> gateway stop` on a multiplexed profile writes `gateway.parked` before it asks the host to unserve the profile (`hermes_cli/gateway_profile_lifecycle.py:73-76` on main 379cf122). If the host answers that the unserve failed, the profile is still served but recorded as parked. The CLI prints "parked, but immediate stop was not confirmed", and every rescan retries the same failing teardown while the bots and cron keep running.

## Steps

1. Run a multiplexed gateway that serves a named profile.
2. Make `_unserve_profile` (`gateway/run_profile_reconcile.py:324`) raise, for example by holding a resource its teardown needs.
3. Run `hermes -p <name> gateway stop`.

Expected: the profile isn't marked parked until the host confirms it stopped serving it. Actual: the marker is written first, so state on disk says parked while the profile is live.

## Fix

Branch with a fix and tests: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/main...enckequity:hermes-agent:fix/profile-park-after-confirmed-stop

The unserve-profile verb takes an optional park flag, and the host writes the marker under its reconcile lock once teardown returns. Error answers carry `served_profiles` like pending ones, and the CLI writes the marker itself only when the stop is confirmed, no host answered, or the host no longer serves the profile. I can't open more PRs on this repo right now (open-PR limit), so a maintainer is welcome to pull the commit.

issues.body:
## Problem

The scale-to-zero background-work check treats a probe error as idle. In `gateway/run_shutdown.py:340-344` (main 379cf122) the async-delegation and process-registry probes run inside `_log_suppressed(...)`, so if either one raises, the loop moves on and the check returns `False`. A transient failure reading either source can then let the gateway suspend or idle-exit while a delegation or background process is still running.

The idle-exit busy check already fails closed through `_read_or_awake`, but `has_live_background_work` at `:483` calls the probe directly.

## Expected

An unreadable source counts as busy, the same way the other inputs to that decision do.

## Fix

Branch with a fix and a test: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/main...enckequity:hermes-agent:fix/scale-to-zero-probe-fail-closed

The probes are allowed to raise, and `has_live_background_work` is read through the existing `_read_or_awake(..., True)` helper. Related: #121048 is the same fail-open pattern for the async-delivery probe. I can't open more PRs on this repo right now (open-PR limit), so a maintainer is welcome to pull the commit.

`build_context_files_prompt` resolves `os.getcwd()` with no guard (`agent/prompt_builder.py:1874` on main 379cf122). If a long-running process's launch directory is deleted, for example a removed worktree or temp dir, building the system prompt raises `FileNotFoundError` and the turn fails.

1. Start `hermes` (or a gateway) from a temporary directory with no `terminal.cwd` set.
2. Delete that directory.
3. Start a new session or send a message that rebuilds the system prompt.

## Fix

Branch with a fix and tests: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/main...enckequity:hermes-agent:fix/prompt-context-deleted-cwd

It catches `OSError` around the resolve, logs the same "set terminal.cwd" hint the install-tree fallback uses, and skips project discovery. Related but separate call sites: #45423 (coding_context), #134229 (SubdirectoryHintTracker), #138015 (background review). I can't open more PRs on this repo right now (open-PR limit), so a maintainer is welcome to pull the commit.

prs.title: fix(migration): resolve SecretRef channel tokens instead of dropping them (#131863)
prs.body:
Addresses part of #131863 (the SecretRef half; the cron-archive half is untouched).

## Problem

The OpenClaw→Hermes migration accepts channel credentials as either a plain
string or a `SecretRef` (`{"source": "env", "id": "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"}`) — the
*normal* shape for any install using OpenClaw's secret store. Three channel
migration steps only kept a value when `isinstance(value, str)`:

- `migrate_secret_settings` (telegram `botToken`)
- `migrate_discord_settings` (`token`)
- `migrate_slack_settings` (`botToken`, `appToken`)

A `SecretRef` therefore failed the `isinstance(..., str)` check and was silently
dropped. With `--migrate-secrets` the run still records the `secret-settings`
step as `skipped: "No allowlisted Hermes-compatible secrets found"` and the
`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` / `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` / `SLACK_*_TOKEN` keys never reach the
target `.env` — a non-crashing migration that quietly loses the bot tokens.

## Fix

The resolver for exactly this case already existed — `_resolve_channel_secret`
(it calls `resolve_secret_input`, the same helper the provider-key path uses at
`openclaw_to_hermes.py:1678`) — but it had **no caller** anywhere in the script.
Wire it into the three channel-secret migrations so an env-backed `SecretRef`
(or a `"${VAR}"` template) is resolved to its plain value before the string
check. `resolve_secret_input` only resolves `source: "env"` (and templates);
`file`/`exec`-backed refs still return `None`, so those remain un-auto-migratable
exactly as documented — the change does not invent a value for them and is
otherwise behaviour-preserving (a plain string token still migrates verbatim).

## Validation

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py` → **22 passed**.

Two tests added to `tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py`:

- `test_secretref_channel_tokens_are_resolved_not_silently_dropped` drives the
  real migration (`execute=True`, real `.env` write, no mocks) with env-backed
  `SecretRef`s for telegram/discord/slack and asserts each token lands in the
  target `.env`. It **fails on `main`** (the `SecretRef` is dropped, so no `.env`
  is written: `FileNotFoundError: .../.hermes/.env`) and passes with the fix.
- `test_unresolvable_secretref_stays_skipped_and_plain_tokens_still_migrate`
  pins the invariant: a `file`-backed ref is not invented, and a plain string
  token still migrates verbatim.

Sibling migration suites unchanged: `scripts/run_tests.sh
tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration_hardening.py
tests/hermes_cli/test_setup_openclaw_migration.py` → **20 passed**.
---
