prs.title: fix(approval): route plugin-escalated approvals through the selected transport
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A plugin `pre_tool_call` hook returning `{"action": "approve"}` escalates the tool call to the human-approval gate via `request_tool_approval` → `_run_approval_gate` → `_ACTION_GATE`. That gate was defined with `transport=False` ("parity with the historical gate"), so these escalations always rendered on the built-in gateway/CLI surface — even when the operator had selected an approval transport via `security.approval.transport`. Dangerous terminal commands (`_COMMAND_GATE`) and `execute_code` (`_EXECUTE_CODE_GATE`) already honor the selected transport, so an operator routing approvals to a push device or a different chat silently missed **every** plugin-required approval.

This flips `_ACTION_GATE` to `transport=True` and gives the spec a real `transport_denied` message (it was an empty string). The two other gate specs are unchanged.

Behavior notes:

- With no transport selected (default `builtin`), `_present_with_selected_transport` returns `{"selected": False}` and the gate falls through to the exact same built-in surfaces as before — zero behavior change for default configurations.
- A selected transport replaces every built-in surface for these escalations, same as for command gates.
- Because `computer_use` actions (`tools/computer_use/tool.py`), SSH-config writes (`tools/file_tools_write_guards.py`) and `check_dangerous_command` all reach the same `_ACTION_GATE` through `_run_approval_gate`, the flip routes their approvals through the selected transport too — on `main` each of them still paints the built-in prompt when a transport is selected. The protected instruction-file gate in `file_tools_write_guards.py` is separate: it bypasses `_run_approval_gate` entirely (that half is #120865).
- With `transport=True`, a transport `deny` on this gate now also runs `_record_denial(session_key)`, so it counts toward the denial breaker exactly like transport denials on the command and `execute_code` gates (the gate itself still never prints breaker addendum text).
- A failed/unavailable transport still fails closed unless the operator explicitly set `transport_fallback: builtin` (host-owned fail-closed semantics are unchanged).

## Related Issue

Fixes #133946

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/approval.py`: `_ACTION_GATE` — `transport=False` → `transport=True`; replaced the empty `transport_denied=""` with wording aligned to `_COMMAND_GATE` (no breaker addendum, matching this gate's other messages); updated the stale "no transport" comment.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_approval_transport.py`: added `test_plugin_escalation_uses_selected_transport` (a gateway-context `request_tool_approval` escalation reaches the selected transport with `plugin_rule:<rule_key>`, builtin prompt never materializes) and `test_plugin_escalation_transport_deny_denies_with_action_wording` (a transport deny denies the action with the new wording), plus the shared `_plugin_escalation_gateway` presence helper.
- `tests/tools/test_approval_action_gate_transport.py`: end-to-end coverage contributed by @saftall (the #133946 reporter, cherry-picked from `dc95ac60af` keeping both authors): real plugin discovery + `config.yaml` + `pre_tool_call` dispatch against a temp `HERMES_HOME` — a plugin `approve` escalation reaches the selected transport on both the CLI and gateway surfaces (never the built-in prompt), a transport deny returns the refusal to the model, and the three other `_run_approval_gate` callers (`computer_use`, SSH-config writes, `check_dangerous_command`) are asserted the same way.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_approval_transport.py -q` — Observed result: `25 passed` (23 pre-existing + 2 new).
1. `python -m pytest tests/tools/test_approval_action_gate_transport.py -q` (contributed e2e file) — Observed result: `4 passed` on this PR's head; red-checked by checking out `f925b01791`'s `tools/approval.py` — Observed result: `4 failed` (the built-in prompt materializes despite `security.approval.transport`), so the tests lock the fixed behavior.
2. Red check: stashing the `tools/approval.py` change makes both new tests fail (`test_plugin_escalation_uses_selected_transport` gets a pending builtin card instead of a transport decision; the deny test sees the builtin wording), confirming they lock the fixed behavior.
3. `python -m pytest tests/tools/test_approval.py tests/tools/test_request_tool_approval.py tests/tools/test_write_approval.py tests/tools/test_file_write_safety.py tests/hermes_cli/test_approval_transport.py -q` — Observed result: `304 passed, 7 skipped`, plus one `test_file_write_safety` failure reproduced identically on a pristine `upstream/main` checkout (pre-existing `home_io_guard` environment artifact, unrelated to this diff).
4. `python scripts/check --base upstream/main` — Observed result: `11 checks, ok` (0 blocking, 0 advisory).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(approval):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#121872 was closed unmerged; #120865 covers only the protected-write half in `tools/file_tools_write_guards.py`, which deliberately bypasses `_run_approval_gate` — no overlap)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (approval-related suites listed above; repo-wide unrelated flakes reproduced on clean main are documented in How to Test)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15.4 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A (gate comment updated in-code)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A (no config change)

prs.title: feat(plugins): contribute_worker_env — plugins extend the kanban worker environment
prs.body:
## What

Fires a new `contribute_worker_env` plugin hook at the end of the dispatcher's `_default_spawn`, after the worker environment is fully composed. Each callback may return a dict of env vars; contributions are merged with `env.setdefault`, so every key the dispatcher pinned (kanban paths, profile, timeouts) always wins. Non-dict results are ignored; hook failures are swallowed with a debug log — the same defensive policy as the kanban lifecycle hooks.

## Why

`_default_spawn` is the single choke point where every kanban worker session gets its environment, and that env is inherited by nested coding-agent subprocesses (ACP claude-code / codex children). That inheritance makes it the only place a plugin can wire **per-session observability**: e.g. handing the worker an OTLP exporter endpoint + trace credentials so the coding agent streams per-turn telemetry (model requests, tool calls) natively to a self-hosted Langfuse/OTel backend, tagged with the task binding.

The hook receives the full binding for exactly that purpose: `task_id`, `board`, `workspace`, `branch`, `run_id`, `profile`.

## Safety

- Contributions can only fill gaps, never override dispatcher-pinned keys (tested: a hook returning `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` cannot hijack it).
- No plugins registered → `invoke_hook` returns an empty list, zero behavior change.
- Any exception inside the hook path is caught and logged at debug level; the spawn proceeds untouched.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py::TestKanbanPaths::test_dispatcher_spawn_merges_plugin_contributed_env` — asserts contributed vars land in the worker env, pinned keys win over a hijack attempt, non-dict results are ignored, and the hook receives the task binding kwargs.

prs.title: fix(kanban): don't flag a saturated concurrency cap as dispatcher-stuck
prs.body:
DRE-223: the embedded gateway dispatcher's health telemetry (gateway/kanban_watchers.py) incremented bad_ticks whenever the ready queue was non-empty and 0 workers spawned, without checking whether the concurrency cap (max_spawn / max_in_progress) was already saturated by running tasks. A board running at its configured limit is healthy, fully-loaded steady state, not a stall — it should not trip the same dispatcher-stuck warning as a genuinely broken profile/venv/credential.

Changes:
- hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py: DispatchResult gains capacity_full, set in _tick_spawn_budget at both early-return points (max_spawn and max_in_progress saturation). New any_capacity_full() helper; describe_suppression() surfaces capacity_full=1.
- gateway/kanban_watchers.py: _kanban_dispatcher_watcher no longer increments bad_ticks when the only reason nothing spawned this tick was a full concurrency cap.

No change to max_in_progress (still fixed), no weakening of respawn guards, no gateway restart performed while landing this.

prs.title: fix(agent): re-fold the active /goal and its contract at the compaction boundary
prs.body:
## Problem

`/goal` state lives in `state_meta`, not in the transcript. The model sees it only as a user message — the kickoff, and the `[Continuing toward your standing goal]` prompt queued between turns. The todo list, by contrast, is re-folded into the transcript at **every** compaction boundary (`_fold_todo_snapshot`).

So whether the goal and its completion contract survive a compaction depends on where the goal text happens to sit when the cut lands:

- **Active turn opened by a goal prompt:** survives (the active request is kept in the tail).
- **Active turn opened by something else** (a real user interjection, a busy-steer, a `/heartbeat` tick, a `/loop` tick while the goal is parked): after a mid-turn compaction the goal and contract exist only inside the summary's **lossy free-text `## Goal` section**. `agent/context_compressor.py` writes that slot as model-authored prose ("What the user is trying to accomplish overall"), so **Verification, Constraints and Stop condition are routinely paraphrased or dropped** for the rest of the turn — exactly the fields the judge later enforces. Losing them lets the agent drift from the contract that decides continuation.
- **Gateway hygiene compaction** (in place, between turns, before the next message is appended): if that next message is not a goal continuation, the turn starts from a summary where the goal is free text only.
- **Third-party context engines:** any engine that does not reproduce the built-in active-request anchor drops the goal.

Reported as #133643.

## Fix

Give `/goal` the todo list's own machinery.

- `hermes_cli/goals.py`: factor the goal+contract body out of `GoalManager.next_continuation_prompt` into a shared `_goal_body_block()`, so the continuation prompt and the preserved block render the same contract fields from one place. Add `render_preserved_goal_block()` (active + not parked only) under a distinct, non-imperative header `[Your standing /goal was preserved across context compression]`, and `goal_is_parked()`.
- `agent/conversation_compression_goal_fold.py` (new topical sibling, kept out of the `conversation_compression` facade to respect its line cap): `fold_goal_snapshot()` mirrors `_fold_todo_snapshot` — strips any earlier preserved goal block (refresh, never stack), folds the live active-goal block into the trailing user row the todo fold already produced (so two synthetic user rows never sit adjacent), and appends a flagged row only when the tail is not a user row.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: the compaction commit boundary now calls `fold_state_snapshots()` (todo fold + goal fold) instead of the bare todo fold; the goal row is registered as synthetic (`_goal_snapshot_synthetic` flag + header prefix) so provenance/scaffolding classification (#69292) is unchanged and the row is never treated as human intent.
- Folds **nothing** for a goal the judge marked done, a paused/cleared goal, or a parked (waiting) goal — no resurrection (#34197). Skipped on a continuation-opened turn, where the goal is already verbatim in the request.

Carve-out respected: `next_continuation_prompt` output is byte-for-byte unchanged (only refactored through `_goal_body_block`).

## Why not a whole new mechanism

The todo list already solves exactly this ("state that lives outside the transcript but must survive compaction"); the goal is the one remaining such state. Reusing the fold keeps one code path and one set of provenance flags.

## Validation

- `tests/agent/test_goal_snapshot_fold.py` (new, 11 tests): contract carried verbatim; refresh-not-stack across two boundaries; merge into a trailing real user row (provenance stays real); done/paused/cleared/parked fold nothing; no duplicate on a continuation turn; an unavailable store preserves the pending snapshot; header literal stays in sync; and an **end-to-end** run through `compress_context` asserting the active goal + contract survives a compaction exactly once.
- Regression: `tests/hermes_cli/test_goals.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_goal_command.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_status_notice.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_resume_restart.py`, `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py`, `tests/agent/test_skill_todo_retention_parity.py`, `tests/agent/test_in_place_compaction.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_boundary.py`, `tests/agent/test_salvage_grown_transcript.py` — **all pass** (≈230 tests).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` (per-file isolation, CI parity); `python scripts/check` → 11 checks, ok (ruff + code-health ratchet clean; the new module keeps `conversation_compression.py` at its line cap).

fixes #133643

prs.title: fix(telegram): replay held inbound in arrival order
prs.body:
Fixes #138793

## What

Updates held across a Telegram disconnect are now replayed in the order they arrived.

Before, the hold queue appended in hold order. An update that arrived behind the delivery fence was
held at once, while batches buffered before the fence were held later (own flush, cancelled flush or
teardown salvage), so the reconnect drain replayed the newer update first. An interrupted replay had
the same problem with its re-held remainder.

## How

- Each update gets a process-wide arrival position on first contact in the three enqueue paths
  (text, photo burst, album). A batch keeps its first update's position.
- `_hold_inbound_event` inserts by that position instead of appending; unstamped events keep append
  order. The counter is process-wide so positions stay comparable when a replacement adapter adopts
  its predecessor's queue (#132829).
- The teardown salvage loop moves into the held-inbound mixin, so `adapter.py` does not grow
  (7318 → 7317 lines).

## Tests

New `tests/gateway/test_telegram_held_inbound_order.py`: 11 cases, all failing on `main` @ ca069e12
and passing here.
- all 9 pairs of (buffered-before-fence kind × arrived-after-fence kind) for text / photo burst / album;
- teardown salvage across kinds keeps arrival order;
- an interrupted replay keeps its remaining updates ahead of one that arrived during the interruption.

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/ tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py`: same 13 failures
as `main` on this macOS host (local system proxy / DNS, plus one load-sensitive timing test), no new
failures. `scripts/check --base main`: 12
checks ok, code health 0 findings.

Tested on macOS 26 (Apple silicon), Python 3.14. Not tested against a live Telegram bot;
python-telegram-bot is not installed in this environment (the admission tests skip, as in CI).

---

prs.title: docs(cli): list the five missing top-level commands and document `hermes verify`
prs.body:
## Problem

The CLI reference's **Top-level commands** table is the index readers use to discover
commands, but five commands that `hermes --help` lists are missing from it:
`worktree`, `browser`, `verify`, `monitoring` and `vault`. Of those, `hermes verify`
had **no documentation anywhere** in `website/docs`, so its phases, flags and exit
codes were undiscoverable.

Reproduction:

```bash
$ hermes --help | grep -E 'browser|monitoring|vault|verify|worktree'
    browser             Real-profile browsing helpers (close a browser locking ...
    monitoring          Inspect gateway monitoring (health & diagnostics export)
    vault               Manage the local encrypted autofill vault (add/list/rm ...
    verify              Detect a project's run recipe and smoke-test it
    worktree            Audit and reclaim accumulated git worktrees and merged branches

$ grep -n 'hermes verify' website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md
(no match)
```

The same table also carried one garbled row: the `pause` / `resume` entry read
"no new cron fires (…), kanban dispatch or gateway turns start until resumed",
which says the opposite of what the command does.

## The fix

- Add the five missing rows to the Top-level commands table. Four have topical pages
  (`cli.md#worktree-cleanup`, `features/browser.md`, `developer-guide/gateway-monitoring.md`,
  `features/credential-vault.md`), so the rows link to them rather than duplicating them.
- Add a full `## hermes verify` section: what it detects, the phase order
  (bootstrap → build → test → start → readiness → teardown), every flag, the exit
  codes, and examples.
- Repair the `pause` / `resume` row (`neither kanban dispatch nor new gateway turns
  start until resumed`) and note `hermes pause --reason <text>`.

## Why not another approach

No new page was needed: the four non-`verify` commands already have authoritative
topical pages, and the reference page's job is the command index. `verify` is the
only one with no page anywhere, so it gets the section.

## Validation

```bash
$ hermes verify --help        # every flag row matches the parser
$ hermes verify /tmp/verifydemo --detect-only   # -> {"source":"detected","recipe":{...}}, exit 0
$ hermes verify /tmp/emptyproj                  # -> "No recognizable project found", exit 1
$ hermes verify /tmp/does-not-exist-xyz         # -> "error: not a directory", exit 2
$ python3 website/scripts/check_doc_links.py    # -> OK: no route-style links ... (CI docs-site check)
```

Exit codes `0` / `1` / `2` documented in the new section were reproduced with the
three commands above. `check_doc_links.py` is the same script the `Docs Site Checks`
workflow runs.

prs.title: docs(cli): document the missing `hermes cron` subcommands
prs.body:
## Problem

The `hermes cron` section of the CLI reference contradicts itself and omits three
shipped subcommands. Its usage line already advertises `runs` and `incidents`:

```
hermes cron <list|create|edit|pause|resume|run|remove|status|runs|incidents|doctor|tick>
```

…but the subcommand table below documents neither, and `notepad` appears in neither
place even though `hermes cron notepad` is a real, shipped command.

Reproduction:

usage: hermes cron runs [-h] [--limit LIMIT] [job_id]

prs.title: fix(plugins): disk-cleanup never deletes protected or out-of-scope tracked paths
prs.body:
Fixes #135891.

## Problem

`plugins/disk-cleanup/disk_cleanup.py` `quick()` re-validates the stored category only for the `test` and `cron-output` cases, then falls through to `_delete_item`. Two gaps let a stored `tracked.json` entry delete something it must not:

- `_is_protected_dir()` guards **directories** only. A durable top-level HERMES_HOME **file** — `config.yaml`, `.env`, `auth.json`, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `SOUL.md` — is not covered by it, and `_is_protected_cron_path()` covers only the cron control plane. `track()` accepts such a file (`is_safe_path()` allows anything under HERMES_HOME), so a `track ~/.hermes/config.yaml temp` (or any pre-fix entry) is unlinked by `quick()` after the 7-day temp window.
- `quick()` never re-checks scope. An entry whose path is now a symlink, or no longer resolves inside HERMES_HOME / `/tmp/hermes-*`, is deleted regardless.

Reproduction (failing on `main`, `dce1e9b`): `track(config.yaml, "temp")` returns `True`, and a stored `{"path": "…/.hermes/config.yaml", "category": "temp"}` entry made 30 days ago is unlinked by `quick()`. Same for symlinked and out-of-scope entries.

## Fix

Add one predicate, `_is_protected_scope(p)`, used consistently at every point that reads stored metadata:

- `quick()` / `dry_run()` — an entry that is now a symlink, resolves outside scope, or is a durable top-level HERMES_HOME file is **dropped from tracking, not deleted** (same disposition as the existing stale-entry/protected-dir paths).
- `track()` — refuses the same set up front, so a protected file never enters `tracked.json`.

The protected-file check reuses `_NEVER_TRACK_TOP_LEVEL` (which `guess_category()` already honours) matched at `len(rel.parts) == 1`, i.e. HERMES_HOME-root files only. It deliberately does **not** widen to files nested under durable trees, because `test_stale_cache_dir_entry_is_skipped_but_its_old_files_still_age_out` establishes that only a protected **directory** survives while ordinary `temp` files under it still age out — that behaviour is preserved (see the control test).

Why not refuse via `guess_category() != category` in `quick()`: that would drop every manually tracked `temp` entry outside `cache/` (`guess_category` returns `None` for them), breaking the manual `track` API. The explicit scope predicate targets only the unsafe class.

## Validation

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_disk_cleanup_plugin.py` — **51 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (was 36; +15 new cases in `TestProtectedPathsNeverDeleted`).
- New tests fail on unmodified `main` (14 failures: protected-file `track` refusal, protected-file stale entry, symlink entry, out-of-scope entry) and pass after the fix; the control (`temp` file under `cache/` still pruned) passes in both.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_multiplex_plugin_cache_scope.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_list.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_category_discovery.py` — 22 passed, 0 failed.

prs.title: fix(mcp): a shutdown-race scheduling error is teardown, not a server failure
prs.body:
## Problem

A gateway restart parks every managed MCP server:

```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'virlo' failed after 5 reconnection attempts, parking; will self-probe
every 300s until it recovers (state: degraded → parked): RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown
```

Production observation (long-lived gateway, 7 remote MCP servers, 48h window of `errors.log`):

- 77 identical park WARNINGs, one per server per restart, all clustered inside gateway restarts (e.g. a restart at 13:06 produced the seven `virlo`/`cloudflare`/`x-docs`/`aixbt`/`blockscout`/`crypto-com`/`vfat` parks between 13:07 and 13:11).
- Each park cost 5 reconnect attempts plus backoff for a process that is already going away.
- The WARNING text says `degraded → parked`, so the error log reads as a real MCP outage on a machine whose servers were healthy.

## Reproduction

The error is a scheduling failure, so it needs no network: the code under test reaches the park on its own.

```python
from tools.mcp_tool import MCPServerTask
from tools.mcp_tool_server_run import _RetryBudget

task = MCPServerTask("t")
task._ever_connected = True
task._reconnect_retries = 0
await task._on_transport_error(
    RuntimeError("cannot schedule new futures after shutdown"), _RetryBudget())
```

Before this change: retries are charged and, with the budget exhausted, the server parks with the WARNING above (the first two tests in the new file fail on `main`, the third — the park with an exhausted budget — reproduces the exact production line).

## Fix

`tools/mcp_tool_server_run.py`:

- New `_is_shutdown_scheduling_error()` delegating to `tools.interpreter_shutdown.interpreter_shutting_down` — the shared predicate for this class (both CPython message variants: `cannot schedule new futures after shutdown` / `... after interpreter shutdown`, plus `sys.is_finalizing()`), already used by cron delivery, tool submission and the conversation retry (#55924/#58720).
- `_on_transport_error` checks it right after unwrapping the exception group, before classification: log DEBUG and `return False` (end the run loop), mirroring the existing `self._shutdown_event.is_set()` branch two lines below. Guarding the single entry point covers both the initial-connect and reconnect ladders and the park path.

Whole-bug-class, not one site: the MCP ladder is the sibling call path of the sites that already had this guard; the initial-connect ladder, the reinstated-stdio branch and both park sites all sit behind the same check.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_shutdown_scheduling_error.py` — 4 passed (2 parametrized shutdown variants, the exhausted-budget park case, plus a control asserting a genuine `ConnectionError` still charges the ladder).
- Regression: `pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_reconnect_log_hygiene.py tests/tools/test_mcp_rapid_drop_budget.py tests/tools/test_mcp_parked_self_probe.py tests/tools/test_mcp_park_log_dedupe.py tests/tools/test_mcp_cancelled_error_propagation.py tests/tools/test_mcp_shutdown_scheduling_error.py` — 18 passed.

fixes #136957

prs.title: fix(tui): recognize CRLF fused in one read as Enter (Android mobile TUI input)
prs.body:
Fixes Android/mobile TUI input: on Android terminals, Enter arrives as CRLF fused in a single read. The tokenizer deliberately does NOT split CR/LF (they are paste/newline content inside larger text tokens), so the fused CRLF falls through all branches of parseKeypress and returned name:'' instead of 'return'.

This adds '\r\n' to the lone-Enter branch so a CRLF token that IS the entire read is recognized as Enter, consistent with how lone \r and \n already work. CR/LF embedded in a larger text token remains whole (composer not prematurely submitted).

Includes 2 regression tests (lone CRLF -> return; embedded CRLF in larger token stays paste/newline content). All 209 tests in hermes-ink pass, tsc clean.

prs.title: fix(feishu): drain accepted text batches on disconnect
prs.body:
# fix(feishu): drain accepted text batches on disconnect

## What does this PR do?

Prevents the Feishu/Lark adapter from silently dropping accepted debounced text when disconnect overlaps timer cancellation, downstream dispatch, or concurrent batch ingress.

The shared batch flush now keeps a strong reference to the shielded dispatch child instead of retaining only its cancellable debounce carrier. Feishu teardown closes batch admission before its first await, transfers every still-buffered key exactly once into tracked dispatches, settles all keys concurrently with isolated failures, and bounds the drain below the gateway's five-second per-adapter teardown policy. Batch reset and transport cleanup run from `finally`.

## Proposed Severity

P2 / Medium

## Related Issue

Closes #127768

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/base.py`
  - strongly tracks shield-created text-batch dispatch tasks after the pop boundary.
- `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py`
  - quiesces text/media batch admission before snapshotting teardown state;
  - drains remaining keys concurrently and awaits already-popped dispatches;
  - isolates per-key handler failures and bounds slow dispatch cancellation;
  - always resets batch state and runs transport cleanup in `finally`;
  - re-opens batch admission on the connection path only after stale dispatch ownership is clear.
- `tests/gateway/test_feishu_buffer_drain.py`
  - uses event barriers for cancellation after pop while dispatch is blocked;
  - covers multiple keys, one failing handler, and one slow handler;
  - covers ingress during teardown and fresh post-disconnect admission;
  - asserts exact-once starts, empty batch state, completed handler tasks, and transport cleanup.

No configuration, schema, outbound delivery, or normal debounce cadence changes.

## How to Test

1. Prove the strengthened regressions fail before the production change:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_feishu_buffer_drain.py -q
   ```

   Result before fix: **2 failed** — the healthy key was not reached after a sibling failure, and a slow drain exceeded the bound.

2. Run the focused regression after the change:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_feishu_buffer_drain.py -q
   ```

   Result: **2 passed**.

3. Run the focused Feishu, shared batching, and adapter-lifecycle suites:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_feishu*.py \
     tests/gateway/test_text_batch_flush_invariants.py \
     tests/gateway/test_bounded_adapter_teardown.py -q
   ```

   Result: **170 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** across 19 files.

4. Run lint and whitespace checks:

   ```bash
   ruff check gateway/platforms/base.py \
     plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py \
     tests/gateway/test_feishu_buffer_drain.py
   git diff --check
   ```

   Result: both passed.

## Risk and Compatibility

- The shared base change only adds ownership for the dispatch task that `asyncio.shield()` already created.
- Batch ingress closes synchronously at disconnect, so work accepted before the boundary is stable while teardown snapshots it.
- Remaining keys start concurrently; one exception is logged and cannot suppress siblings.
- Slow dispatches are cancelled inside the adapter budget, leaving transport cleanup in the `finally` path.
- No stale debounce task remains to redispatch the batch after disconnect.
- Feishu media batches retain their existing cancellation semantics; only admission is quiesced with text batching.

## Duplicate Check

No exact duplicate was found. Open PR #99845 addresses a Feishu WebSocket shutdown hang and has a broader lifecycle diff; closed PR #35782 addresses a separate session-gap interrupt loss.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched existing issues and PRs for duplicates
- [x] The change contains only the lifecycle fix and its regression tests
- [ ] I've run the complete repository test suite
- [x] I've run the affected Feishu, shared batching, and lifecycle suites
- [x] I've added deterministic regression tests that failed before the fix
- [x] Tested on macOS 27.2 with Python 3.14.7

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation update — N/A; no user-facing behavior or configuration changed
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update — N/A; no config key changed
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` update — N/A; no workflow or architecture changed
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered — asyncio task ownership/cancellation and dict state only
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas update — N/A; no tool surface changed

prs.title: fix(deps): bump dompurify 3.4.13 -> 3.4.16 (GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2, GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
prs.body:
## Problem

`dompurify` is pinned at `3.4.13` in **three** places, and that version is
vulnerable to two published advisories:

- [GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2)
  (2026-10-05) — `IN_PLACE` returns a force-removed rawtext root whose text can
  be re-parsed (XSS).
- [GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
  (2026-09-30) — `IN_PLACE`: a node-removing `afterSanitize` hook leaves a
  detached subtree that is still returned.

Both are fixed in `3.4.16`.

`dompurify` is a **production** dependency of the desktop app
(`apps/desktop/package.json` → `src/` sanitizes assistant-rendered HTML), so
this is a runtime XSS surface, not just a build-time one.

Reproduction (root lockfile):

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities.dompurify'
{ "severity": "low", "range": "<3.4.16", ... }
```

The pin is duplicated so a single-location bump silently leaves the other
sites vulnerable:

| Site | File |
| --- | --- |
| direct dependency | `apps/desktop/package.json` |
| root override | `package.json` (`overrides.dompurify`) |
| website override | `website/package.json` (`overrides.dompurify`) |

The three copies are also why `npm audit fix --force` aborts with `EOVERRIDE`
today (npm refuses an override that does not textually match the direct
dependency it replaces — see #136475).

## Fix

Bump all three sites to `3.4.16` and refresh the resolved entries in the two
committed lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `website/package-lock.json`). The
override and the direct dependency stay identical, so the `EOVERRIDE`
condition cannot be reintroduced.

Only the `dompurify` entries move; `3.4.16` has the same dependency metadata as
`3.4.13` (no `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies: {"@types/trusted-types": "^2.0.7"}`),
so no other node in either tree changes.

## Why not just bump the desktop dependency

Because the root/website overrides would keep resolving the vulnerable version
for the `^3.3.3` range (mermaid and friends pull it in transitively) — the same
bug class this repo has hit before with `js-yaml`/`aiohttp` (a fix that covers
one site only is rejected or lands half-applied).

## Validation

- Tarball integrity matches the registry:
  `sha512-sqo+pNp3qRhCIpbgRi1y8Tgk27Bo2Ry7w0dC1NBeNTdZChWjz9Xb/KOoZbRP/R6pQZ80Qw8YhXw13hWWBbMRnQ==`.
- Root tree: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` → exit 0 (`added 1422 packages`).
- Website tree: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` with the repo's required
  npm (`>=11.17.0`) → exit 0 (`added 1390 packages`).
- `npm audit --json` at the root no longer reports a `dompurify` entry.
- `grep -rn '3\.4\.13' package.json apps/desktop/package.json website/package.json package-lock.json website/package-lock.json` → no matches.

prs.title: fix(deps): bump concurrently 10.0.4 -> 10.0.6, clearing shell-quote 1.9.0 (GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv)
prs.body:
## Problem

The root lockfile resolves `shell-quote@1.9.0` (via the desktop dev toolchain),
which is vulnerable to a **critical** advisory:

- [GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv) —
  `quote()` command injection via a line terminator (fixed in `1.11.0`).

`npm audit` also flags the carrier itself as critical, because `concurrently`
pins `shell-quote` **exactly** (`"shell-quote": "1.9.0"`), so no consumer range
can float it forward:

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities["shell-quote"]'
{ "severity": "critical",
  "range": "1.8.4 - 1.10.0",
  "fixAvailable": { "name": "concurrently", "version": "10.0.6", "isSemVerMajor": false },
  "effects": ["concurrently"] }
```

Adding an override would paper over a pin that upstream `concurrently` has
already fixed; the correct fix is to move the carrier.

## Fix

`supports-color 10.2.2`, `tree-kill 1.2.2`, `yargs 18.0.0` are all unchanged).

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes an intermittent failure in two browser-control broker tests. Both check the "command timed out while its
controller was offline" path, but they raced a 10–20 ms command timeout against their own `disconnect_owner()` call.
When the timeout won, the broker cancelled on the still-connected controller (correct for that order), nothing was
deferred, and the deferred-cancel assertions failed:

- `test_timeout_while_disconnected_flushes_cancel_before_new_dispatch`
- `test_failed_deferred_cancel_flush_keeps_controller_offline`

Broker code is unchanged; only the tests' ordering is fixed.

## Related Issue

None filed — test-only fix; reproduction below.

Relation to #109935: that PR raises the *second* dispatch's deadline in the first test, which is the same as the
second bullet below. It does not change the asserted timeout racing `disconnect_owner()`: with only its hunk applied
to `main`, the forced-order reproduction below still fails both tests. The two changes apply on top of each other
without conflict.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tests/gateway/test_browser_control_broker_hardening.py`: a small stand-in for the pending command's event reports
  the timeout only after the test has disconnected, so the order no longer depends on the clock. The production
  timeout branch still runs (the stand-in only replaces the wait result).
- The first test's broker now uses a 5 s limit, because with 20 ms its second command could also time out before the
  test completed it (the same race a second time).

## How to Test

1. Force the losing order on `main`: delay `disconnect_owner` by 200 ms (a temporary conftest shim) and run
   `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_browser_control_broker_hardening.py -k "timeout_while_disconnected or failed_deferred_cancel_flush"`.

prs.body:
## Problem

The root lockfile resolves `joi@18.2.3` (transitively, via the desktop dev tool
`wait-on@9.0.10`, which requires `joi@^18.2.1`). That version is affected by
four published advisories, the newest of which is the reason the whole 18.0.0 –
18.2.8 band is flagged:

| Advisory | Severity | Fixed in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [GHSA-6h2x-m376-mqjq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6h2x-m376-mqjq) — quadratic regex backtracking in `Joi.string().isoDate()` | high (CVSS 7.5) | 18.2.6 / 17.13.7 |
| [GHSA-wr44-6hxh-3jwq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wr44-6hxh-3jwq) — prototype replacement via `__proto__` error codes | moderate | 18.2.9 / 17.13.8 |
| [GHSA-6w3j-5fw6-r9vr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6w3j-5fw6-r9vr) — prototype pollution via a `__proto__` language key | moderate | 18.2.5 / 17.13.6 |
| [GHSA-gg4h-3hg2-grpc](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gg4h-3hg2-grpc) — `rename()` with a template target can set the object's prototype | moderate | 18.2.4 / 17.13.5 |

All four are cleared by `18.2.9`, which is the newest release on the 18 line.

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities.joi.range'
"18.0.0 - 18.2.8"
```

## Fix

- Add a root override `"joi": "^18.2.9"` — the same shape the repo already uses
  for other transitively-pinned security fixes (`lodash`, `tar`, `nanoid`,
  `yauzl`, `ip-address`).
- Refresh the resolved `node_modules/joi` entry in `package-lock.json`.

`joi@18.2.9` has byte-identical dependency metadata to `18.2.3`
(`@hapi/address`, `@hapi/formula`, `@hapi/hoek`, `@hapi/pinpoint`, `@hapi/tlds`,
`@hapi/topo`, `@standard-schema/spec` — all unchanged ranges, `engines.node >= 20`),
so no other node in the tree moves. Nothing in the root lock requires `joi@^17`,
so the override cannot force a major across a major boundary.

## Validation

- Tarball integrity verified against the registry:
  `sha512-2mD929bUVKUhOLQQEVhlf6EZ0Mlo0DeRb5MO7cViR9AXLtBauuccEtB1py9Ocxpo/P7ucnh442iY/iOwrh3IQw==`

  reported `high` count drops 19 → 18 with nothing new introduced.

## What does this PR do?

Brings opencode-go's model handling in line with how opencode itself does it. opencode never probes `/v1/models`. It reads the models.dev catalog (`models.opencode.ai/api.json`, byte-identical to `models.dev/api.json`), hides `status: deprecated` rows, and picks each model's wire from its `provider.npm`. Hermes already has the same shape (live list → models.dev → static floor), so this PR changes data, not structure. One commit per fix (the Go `claude-*` routing fix landed separately in #134848):

1. **Hide deprecated models.dev rows** (`list_agentic_models`). opencode hides them from its picker. Hermes merged them in, so a keyless opencode-go picker offered `grok-4.5`, which the relay no longer serves.
2. **Go aux default `glm-5` → `glm-5.3-flash`**, on the profile and in the legacy fallback dict. `glm-5` is gone from both `/zen/go/v1/models` and models.dev and returns 400 `Model is unavailable`.
3. **Sync the curated Go list** with opencode's catalog: models.dev `opencode-go` minus deprecated rows, 31 models. This adds 14 current models and drops 7 the relay no longer serves (`kimi-k2.5`, `grok-4.5`, `glm-5`, `mimo-v2-pro`, `mimo-v2-omni`, `qwen3.5-plus`, `hy3-preview`).

## Related Issue

Refs #133181. This fixes its Go half only. The Zen default (`gemini-3-flash`) is untouched because I couldn't verify a replacement on Zen with the key I had.

The Go Claude-routing half of this PR merged as #134848 (fixes #134844); this branch is rebased on it. A cross-check of `opencode_model_api_mode` against every non-deprecated opencode-go row in models.dev found no other routing mismatch.

**Out of scope:** with a key, the live-first picker still shows `kimi-k2.6`, `qwen3.6-plus` and `qwen3.7-max`. The relay still lists and serves them, while models.dev marks them deprecated. Filtering them out is a picker-policy question, so it's left for a follow-up.

prs.title: fix(acp): stop the 'Install GitHub Copilot CLI?' prompt on Windows startup
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On native Windows, every Hermes startup prints `Install GitHub Copilot CLI? (y/N):` in the user's terminal when all three of these hold:

- VS Code's GitHub Copilot Chat extension has put its `copilot` wrapper on PATH (`%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\github.copilot-chat\copilotCli\copilot.bat`, which runs a PowerShell script). VS Code does this in its integrated terminals.
- The real Copilot CLI (`@github/copilot`) is not installed, so the wrapper offers to install it.
- `copilot-acp` counts as authenticated (here because `~/.copilot/config.json` holds `copilotTokens`), so the model-picker warm-up asks it for live models.

Call path, traced with a `sys.addaudithook` on `subprocess.Popen` during a real startup:

```
model_switch_providers._warm -> list_authenticated_providers -> _lap_overlay_rows
 -> models._copilot_catalog -> plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp fetch_models
 -> CopilotACPClient.list_models -> _session -> _spawn -> _acp_supported
 -> subprocess.run([...\copilotCli\copilot.BAT, "--help"])
```

**Where the bug shows up:** `agent/copilot_acp_client.py::_acp_supported` calls `subprocess.run` without `creationflags`, so the PowerShell child attaches to the user's console. PowerShell's `Read-Host` writes the prompt straight to that console, even though stdout is captured and stdin is `DEVNULL`. The `Popen` in `_spawn()` right next to it already passes `windows_hide_flags()` (#56747). The docstring of `windows_hide_flags()` covers exactly this case ("short-lived synchronous helpers (... version probes)"). This PR passes the same flag to the check.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged. Output is still captured, and the result is the same: `False` for this wrapper, whose `--help` output has no `--acp`. On non-Windows hosts `windows_hide_flags()` is `0`.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. I searched PRs and issues for `_acp_supported`, `copilot.bat`, `copilotCli`, `copilot --help`, "Install GitHub Copilot CLI" and "copilot acp console".

Related:
- #87308 introduced the `--acp` check.
- #133605 (open) also edits `agent/copilot_acp_client.py`, but changes how `copilot.cmd` is resolved and how multi-turn prompts are built. It doesn't touch the check's `subprocess.run` call, so the two PRs don't overlap.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/copilot_acp_client.py`: `_acp_supported()` passes `creationflags=windows_hide_flags()` to the `--help` check, matching `_spawn()`.
- `tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_client.py`: `test_probe_runs_without_a_console` checks the contract that the check runs with the hide flags and `stdin=DEVNULL`. It fails on `main` (`KeyError: 'creationflags'`) and passes with the fix. It needs no host marker: it compares against `windows_hide_flags()` on whatever host runs it, without faking `sys.platform`.

**Not changed, on purpose:** other `--version` checks of external CLIs also run without hide flags, for example `agent/anthropic_adapter.py::_detect_claude_code_version` and `agent/transports/codex_app_server.py::check_codex_binary`. I could not reproduce a prompt or other user-visible effect from them, so I left them out to keep this PR to the verified bug. Happy to follow up if maintainers want the whole set hidden.

## How to Test

Windows 11, VS Code + GitHub Copilot Chat installed, `@github/copilot` **not** installed, from an interactive console:

1. Reproduce the leak on its own:
   ```python
   subprocess.run([r"%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\github.copilot-chat\copilotCli\copilot.BAT", "--help"],
                  capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=8)
   ```
   `Install GitHub Copilot CLI? (y/N):` prints to the console, while `stdout` captures `Cannot find GitHub Copilot CLI (...)`.
2. Run the same call with `creationflags=windows_hide_flags()`. Nothing prints to the console, and the captured stdout is identical.
3. Run `_acp_supported(<wrapper>, ["--acp", "--stdio"])` on this branch in a real console. No prompt appears, and it returns `False`.
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_client.py tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_deprecation.py`: 35 passed, 0 failed. On `main` the new test fails.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. I ran `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/` (the affected directory) in a PM-built test env on Windows 11, not the full suite. Some files fail on this host on both `main` and this branch (same 26 files, none of which import `copilot_acp_client`). See Screenshots / Logs.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A. `windows_hide_flags()` is `0` off Windows. `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py`: no findings.
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Isolated reproduction (flags `0x0` = current `main`, `0x8000000` = this PR):

```
--- probe flags=0x0 start
Install GitHub Copilot CLI? (y/N):
--- rc=0 captured_stdout='Cannot find GitHub Copilot CLI (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/set-up/install-copilot-cli)\n'
--- probe end
--- probe flags=0x8000000 start
--- rc=0 captured_stdout='Cannot find GitHub Copilot CLI (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/set-up/install-copilot-cli)\n'
--- probe end
```

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/` on Windows 11:

```
main:   1007 files, 11150 passed, 62 failed, 97 skipped
branch: 1007 files, 11147 passed, 66 failed, 97 skipped
```

The same 26 files fail on both, and none of them touch Copilot ACP. The 4 tests that failed only on the branch run are in `tests/agent/lsp/test_client_e2e.py` and `tests/agent/test_inline_edit_persistence.py`, both already failing on `main`. They are flaky on this host: two reruns of those files on the branch failed a different set of tests each time.

prs.title: fix(desktop): continue failed rate-limited turns without rewinding
prs.body:
Closes #137277.

A provider 429 after a completed tool must not send Desktop's error-card Retry through Regenerate's rewind. Retry now resumes the proven durable model context, including completed tool results, without inserting another user row or replaying inbound commands. Explicit Regenerate intentionally still rewinds and repeats the work.

## Behavior and runtime compatibility

- Error-card Retry and the existing user-armed reset timer carry explicit Retry intent. Primary chat and tiles share the planner. Missing or refused checkpoints never fall back to a truncating submit.
- Tool-result provenance is committed in existing display metadata. A checkpoint requires an unchanged durable transcript and paired, received tool outcomes; unknown or repaired outcomes are not evidence.
- Standalone TUI/serve uses `prompt.retry` under turn admission, profile scope and a retirement work lease.
- The unified `hermes-gateway-v1` owner also implements `prompt.retry` for Desktop (`source: gui`). It authorizes the actor and subscription, admits a private continuation through the durable FIFO, and rechecks owner epoch, physical transcript, original agent and full history before model execution. Operator provenance is preserved.
- Continuation passes the complete DB history with row IDs to the original user anchor. It preserves API sidecars and context injections, skips inbound command/plugin dispatch, and adds no synthetic continuation prompt.
- Reconnect projects the retained `user` and `retry_token`. New input hides obsolete checkpoints; input queued behind an already-admitted Retry preserves its spent checkpoint until that Retry executes. Duplicate clicks never enqueue another Retry.
- Checkpoint preparation runs outside the event-stream lock. Unreadable checkpoint storage fails closed without suppressing an already-committed terminal completion.

## Integration and exact candidate

The branch was updated by an ordinary two-parent merge commit, preserving the original PR head and merging upstream through `379cf1220fe289b5ecfe8bcf61cd4d5126e140cd`, including the unified gateway runtime and subsequent ACP/MCP admission updates.

Runtime merge commit: `48c40618f467a2dbc8f7800755688d4f6a9e3977`
Parents: `122460b68b65133f6cbde84f6aa4ae099e100ee6`, `379cf1220fe289b5ecfe8bcf61cd4d5126e140cd`
Tested/uploaded runtime tree: `41b6d2d6fbb274077d6709e813f29a384ae35f0a`
Final head: `626f7e61af680ebfc016e4fce76981110dd4d815` (one documentation-only correction of the canonical busy refusal code; parent is the runtime merge above).
Final tree: `b1bead9fc6288fdfe8846e40d1949d4409db91b3`. Production and test sources are identical to the validated runtime tree.

The downloaded remote commit's tree and parents were verified against the local candidate. The ref update used the original head as an expected SHA with force disabled. No upstream main write, PR merge, or duplicate PR.

## Validation from this cloud session

Linux, PM-prepared Python 3.14.7, Node 24.19.0; fake loopback provider and real temporary SessionDB; no paid model or live account.

- Broad integrated Python run after the runtime merge: **770 passed across 21 files**, file retries disabled.
- After upstream advanced to `3068d1c1`: **56 passed across 6 files**, including the new CLI toolset checks and both Retry paths.
- Final candidate after upstream advanced to `379cf122`: **43 passed across 11 files**, including canonical Retry, legacy Retry/E2E, authority, mutation repair, MCP refreeze, hosted member binding and wire contracts. These focused reruns overlap the broad run; their counts are not additive.
- Canonical Retry has 8 real-runtime cases: tool effect count=1 with provider messages equal to the failed request; Regenerate count=2; no duplicate user row; operator; changed history; restart; unavailable checkpoint storage still publishes completion; newer queued input; and a follower admitted while Retry waits at the claim gate. The mode matrix combines related assertions.
- The canonical regression is red on untouched main `3068d1c1` (missing continuation token), green on the candidate.
- Final relevant Desktop Vitest suite: **414 passed across 23 files**. Renderer `tsc -p . --noEmit` passed.
- `python scripts/check --base upstream/main`: all **12 checks passed** against final upstream `379cf122`. `git diff upstream/main --check` passed.
- Targeted Desktop ESLint: zero errors; two existing hook-dependency warnings remain outside this fix.
- Independent read-only Codex reviewer: final **21 passed** (8 canonical + 13 legacy), no remaining blockers. The reviewer also inspected the later upstream ACP/MCP delta and retained the approval.

The old PR description's 762 Python / 349 Vitest results are superseded by the explicit runs above. Final-head GitHub CI is **not passed**: CI run 38676979784, Docker run 38676979716 and Nix run 38676979875 each report `action_required`. Their jobs endpoints were checked and each returned an empty list (zero actual jobs). Maintainer workflow approval is still required; local tests are not a substitute for that CI.

## How to test

```bash
HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/pm-test-env/bin/python scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_session_retry.py tests/tui_gateway/test_prompt_retry.py tests/tui_gateway/test_prompt_retry_e2e.py --file-retries 0 -q
npm exec --workspace apps/desktop -- vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions src/app/chat/session-tile-actions.test.ts src/components/assistant-ui/thread/assistant-message.test.tsx src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/terminal-error-frame.test.tsx src/app/session/hooks/resume-occurrences.test.tsx
npm exec --workspace apps/desktop -- tsc -p . --noEmit
python scripts/check --base upstream/main
```

## Scope and limitations

Eligibility is limited to provider rate_limit, a retained matching agent/context, and proven persisted tool outcomes. Backend restart, agent replacement, transcript changes/compaction, unproven outcomes and unsupported managed/Codex routes fail closed. Tokens are process-local; a lost admission acknowledgement never authorizes a fresh replay.

The effect-before-result-commit window remains unknowable. This is not arbitrary exactly-once execution and cannot prevent a model from deliberately issuing a new tool call after seeing a prior result. Full repository Python/JS suites, native Windows/Electron GUI and packaging were not run.

Read CONTRIBUTING.md and applicable root/area AGENTS.md. No dependency, config key, tool schema or DB migration change. Gateway contracts and integration documentation were regenerated/updated. Implementation, tests and this description used Codex assistance; independent review was by a separate Codex agent, not a human review.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add git-autosave plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `git-autosave` to the plugin catalog: a lightweight, local alternative to directory checkpoints for people
who mostly work in Git repositories.

Directory checkpoints keep a separate snapshot store per working directory. On large or busy projects that store
is costly to maintain (#135009, #122551, #136935), and #125623 asks for a way to exclude directories from it. This
plugin reuses each project's own Git object database instead:

- Before a mutating tool call (`write_file`, `patch`, common mutating terminal commands), it saves the affected
  repository's working state to `refs/hermes-autosave/<branch>` with a reflog, through a private index. HEAD,
  branches, the real index and the working tree are never touched, and nothing is pushed.
- Outside Git it copies only the existing file about to change.
- `hermes autosave find <file>` lists pre-edit versions; `hermes autosave restore <file>` writes only that path.
- Dependency directories are always skipped, and credential stores are never read or copied.

It does not cover non-Git directories the way checkpoints do; the README says when to keep checkpoints on.

**How it differs from `git-hook`:** `git-hook` commits and pushes real branches every turn. `git-autosave` writes a
private local ref, never commits to a branch and never pushes. It is recovery history, not sync.

The repository owner submits this entry (rule 5). It is pinned to the `v0.3.0` release commit
`b4b12d6bf79318c6708ab468327d52e7671d63f9`.

## Related Issue

None for the entry itself. The checkpoint issues above are the motivation.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/git-autosave.yaml` (new; the only file changed).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Runs local `git` subprocesses in repositories the agent touches, with hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor,
  split-index and lazy fetch disabled.
- Writes shadow refs and reflogs into those repositories' `.git`, and file copies into its plugin-data directory.
  Both are local and unencrypted.
- Skips credential stores (`.env`, `auth.json`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.docker`, `.kube`, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and
  dependency directories, including through symlinks. Repositories with mirror remotes or `refs/*` push refspecs
  are skipped.
- `hermes autosave sweep` reads the Hermes session database read-only. The plugin schedules nothing; the README
  shows how to schedule the sweep yourself.
- No network calls, no background processes, no credentials. It only observes: it never blocks, rewrites or
  approves a tool call.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate <checkout at the pinned sha> --install-deps` (Hermes v0.22.1): all 14 checks pass,
   no warnings.
2. In an empty `HERMES_HOME`: `hermes plugins install xiaoyaner0201/hermes-git-autosave`, then
   `hermes plugins enable git-autosave`.
3. In a scratch Git repository, change a tracked file, let the agent overwrite it, then run
   `hermes autosave find <file>` and `hermes autosave restore <file>`: the pre-edit content comes back and the
   branch is unchanged.

The plugin's own suite (465 tests in Hermes v0.22.0 and v0.22.1 environments, including tests through the real
`PluginHost` and `file_tools.patch_tool`) runs in its CI on Ubuntu and macOS with Python 3.11 and 3.13.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the catalog admission rules
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` — N/A, no Hermes code changed
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — N/A, no Hermes code changed
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (plus Ubuntu in the plugin's CI)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation lives in the plugin README at the pinned commit
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: `platforms: [linux, macos]`; Windows is not supported yet and is
  listed under known limitations

## Known limitations

- Windows is not supported yet: terminal-command path parsing assumes a POSIX shell.
- A single V4A patch that moves a symlink and then updates the moved path can miss the edited file on
  case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems (also in `known_issues`).

prs.title: fix(api): make run task registration atomic
prs.body:
## Summary

- make the durable idempotency reservation and live task ownership one admission transaction
- defer live Bot Chat routing until the registered task can run, with truthful terminalization if pre-launch routing fails
- cover a deterministic `asyncio.create_task` registration fault and prove the same idempotency key starts normally on retry

## Problem

`POST /v1/runs` committed its durable `queued` idempotency row before `asyncio.create_task` installed the run in `_active_run_tasks`. If task registration raised while the gateway process stayed alive, retries replayed the original `queued` row forever because its recorded owner PID was still healthy, even though no task could advance it.

## Approach

`RunIdempotencyStore.reserve` now accepts a live-owner registration callback and invokes it after the SQLite insert but before commit. A callback failure rolls the transaction back. The launcher registers the task and its ownership mirrors through that callback; the task yields before any live-owner side effect, so eager task factories cannot cross the commit boundary. Non-idempotent runs use the same registration path.

## Verification receipts

- RED on base `12e4d3e2dd5281adf289f70e5d6c7f33427d6982`: focused regression failed because retry returned `replayed: true` and never ran the agent.
- GREEN: `PUBLIC_SECURITY=false scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_api_server_runs.py tests/gateway/test_peer_dm_into_open_bot_chat.py tests/gateway/test_api_server_active_work_drain.py -q` — **112 passed**.
- `ruff check gateway/platforms/api_server_run_idempotency.py gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py tests/gateway/test_api_server_runs.py` — passed.
- `python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` — no Windows footguns in the staged diff.
- Added-line security scan — clean. `PUBLIC_SECURITY=false`; this is a reliability fix, not a public security report.

## Risk and compatibility

Risk is limited to `/v1/runs` admission timing. Live Bot Chat owner selection now starts inside the already-owned background task rather than immediately before task creation; the peer-run receipt and shutdown/drain tests cover that path. The store callback is optional, the SQLite schema is unchanged, and existing idempotency databases remain compatible. The full repository suite was not run; verification is scoped to the API run launcher, live-owner handoff, and drain accounting.

## Base

- branch parent: `12e4d3e2dd5281adf289f70e5d6c7f33427d6982`
- head: `dd85626c130d940617bd63016fc2f03cbf70f490`
- target: `NousResearch/hermes-agent:main`

prs.title: feat(webapp): serve Desktop renderer in browsers
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `hermes webapp`, an authenticated browser-hosted mode for the **actual Hermes Desktop renderer**. This is not the Web Dashboard: it serves the chat-first Desktop workspace and installs a browser implementation of `window.hermesDesktop` backed by the host running Hermes.

The implementation keeps the existing authority boundaries instead of cloning Desktop UI or adding a parallel backend:

- the renderer is built separately to `apps/desktop/dist-webapp` from the pinned repository workspace;
- the existing FastAPI authentication/session-token and one-time WebSocket-ticket controls gate the surface;
- host files, Git, previews, uploads, profiles, terminal, gateway, and Bot routing reuse existing profile-scoped APIs;
- native-only Electron capabilities are absent or fail explicitly rather than being falsely emulated;
- non-loopback binds remain fail-closed behind configured authentication.

### Lineage and overlap

- Browser bridge/build lineage is carried forward from @adybag14-cyber's #85604; the arbitrary-shell design that originally blocked that PR is not reused.
- The explicit `hermes webapp` product boundary is carried forward from @seagpt's #61171.
- Related browser/Desktop UX work was reviewed in #60829.
- Current main's connection-owner Bot routing (#92731, salvaging #90006) remains authoritative; this PR does not add a second connection resolver.

- Rebased onto main's whole-codebase decomposition (#102117, `d3630f853239e8c41ce7201e09fbdf39bcbc5431`). Webapp behavior follows the topical modules introduced by main, with host-terminal and profile-lifecycle policy in focused owners. All 28 original commits retain their author metadata and full messages, including contributor trailers. The earlier #78628/#78630 proposals and cited shards were reviewed before that main update; no code from unmerged PRs was copied.

Both source contributors are preserved with `Co-authored-by` trailers.

## Related Issue

No single issue. Related work: #85604, #61171, and #60829. This PR does not close those threads.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/webapp.py`, CLI parser/lifecycle code, and docs: add `hermes webapp`, isolated renderer builds, process identity, `--status`/`--stop`, and loopback-by-default launch behavior.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-desktop-bridge*.ts`: implement the browser preload contract for authenticated REST/gateway calls, uploads, files, Git, previews, clipboard, microphone, profiles, and Bot registry routes.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py`, `hermes_cli/web_host_terminal.py`, and the `chat_ws`, `files`, and `uploads` routers: add authenticated Webapp routing, profile-scoped upload staging, and host-terminal setup through the topical owners. The shared `/api/pty` transport remains in the chat router.
- Desktop preview/files/layout/terminal surfaces: website links open in a separate browser tab by default in Webapp; Electron retains its embedded browser with local or remote gateways. Explicit URL previews retain the sandboxed iframe and **Open in browser** recovery action. Other browser adaptations include deliberate native-only degradation, configured-layout persistence, and refresh-safe terminal history.
- Webapp downloads and media: implement the browser save bridge using authenticated download URLs and a HEAD check before handing off to the browser. Audio/video use authenticated HTTP streams with Range support. URLs retain the active profile and proxy base path; Electron keeps its native save dialog and media protocol. Existing managed-file access rules and size limits still apply.
- Profile lifecycle: persist a fresh incarnation per create/import, preserve it across rename, carry it through sessions/workers, and use the same cross-process lifecycle lease for legacy marker backfill, `SessionDB` pathname binding/schema initialization, and attachment writes so delete/recreate cannot cross a checked generation boundary. Partial-delete retries durably recover the token. Publication and retirement coordination lives in `hermes_cli/profile_lifecycle.py`; gateway retirement/fence policy lives in `tui_gateway/profile_lifecycle.py`.
- Upload and attachment handling: reuse the incoming upload spool, check its actual length, and carry captured installation/profile/incarnation ownership through browser picks, drops, edits, drafts, and retries. Already-staged files attach through the owning backend and retain the copy into the container-visible attachment cache.
- Clipboard publication: extract native clipboard images outside lifecycle/session locks, then validate the captured session and profile generation before publishing the image.
- Session display and recovery: derive human/runtime provenance from the backend's canonical classifier and carry it through REST/RPC hydration and reconciliation. Runtime journal boundaries preserve partial replies, tool/reasoning structure, human corrections, and stream ownership across reloads and reused stream IDs; completed replies retire the journal tail. Older gateways retain the existing fallback, with durable row IDs compared before text normalization.
- Detached turn continuity: a brief browser disconnect retains the running session and worker for a bounded reconnect grace period. Resume, activation, and prompt submission check profile generation and disconnect ownership before reattaching.
- Shared policy: use one typed Git REST mapping, the existing upload-generation resolver and desktop control-plane process classifier, an explicit staging destination for private profile initialization, and shared attachment response/error helpers. Profile checks access their lifecycle owner directly.
- Tests and smoke coverage: add browser bridge, uploads, Webapp command/lifecycle, same-name recreation ABA, deterministic barriers at attachment write/DB connect/legacy backfill, fail-closed lease-timeout behavior, concurrent cross-process marker publication, named-launch profiles, partial-delete retry, generation-scoped resume, fallback enumeration, real Chromium host-terminal/layout checks, concurrent clipboard extraction, staged-file ownership, canonical display provenance, and runtime journal recovery.

### Recent browser UX and reliability hardening

- Mobile controls: 44px touch targets for message actions, **Copy**/**More** access, native text selection, and a compact tab picker. Tapping outside the sidebar dismisses it without incidentally focusing the composer.
- Keyboard and media focus: keep the composer visible with visual-viewport fallback and a resize hint; preserve native video/audio controls and prevent queued focus retries from stealing focus after media interaction.
- Ticket and file ownership: carry profile incarnation through tickets and retain the checked ownership boundary through leased, pinned file opens. Profile asset/configuration writes and named-profile mirrors preserve the captured incarnation.
- Private launch containment: on macOS, private auto-open falls back to the operator's manual link instead of putting a bearer in process arguments. Launch-ticket redemption fails closed there; authenticated child-window tickets remain separate.
- Session and platform reliability: harden PTY worker/viewer ownership and reconnect/dead-shell cleanup, roll appearance back to confirmed state without overriding newer peer/profile changes, and correct SQLite lock tracking/read-only inspection and Docker runtime fingerprinting.

## How to Test

1. Build the browser renderer:
   ```bash
   hermes webapp --build-only --force-build
   ```
2. Start locally:
   ```bash
   hermes webapp --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119
   ```
3. Verify Desktop sessions/files/Git/previews/terminal, create and delete a profile, refresh, and confirm the deleted profile remains absent from `/api/profiles`, Bot roster/routes, and the profile filesystem.
4. Click a website link in Webapp: it should open in a separate browser tab without creating a preview pane. In Electron, a normal click should still open its embedded browser, including when connected to a remote gateway.
5. Explicitly choose **Open in app** from a link context menu to use an embedded preview. Sites that reject embedding should retain the **Open in browser** recovery action.
6. Download a file from a chat attachment, play and seek an inline video/audio attachment, and try **Open video file** for an unsupported format. Missing files should show a download error while keeping the chat open.
7. For remote use, configure dashboard authentication first, then launch with an explicit non-loopback bind.
8. At a narrow/mobile viewport, select message text, use **Copy**/**More**, switch tabs, and dismiss the sidebar by tapping outside it. Sidebar dismissal and video/audio controls should not unexpectedly focus the composer. Open and close the software keyboard and check composer visibility; repeat media interaction while a focus retry is pending.
9. Disconnect/reconnect a running session and terminal, switch profiles, and retry after same-name profile recreation. Stale profile/ticket ownership must fail closed. For private macOS launch, follow the manual-link fallback.

### Verification

#### Current head: `043389d0839d3b33e970d4b52dac9c0fdd1c6e73`

prs.title: fix(dingtalk): send plain-text messages as text type instead of markdown card
prs.body:
## Summary

When Hermes replies to a DingTalk chat with a plain-text message (no markdown formatting), the adapter currently wraps it in a markdown card with a generic `Hermes` title. For simple text replies this looks noisy and clunky.

This PR detects whether the normalized content actually contains markdown formatting. If it does, it sends a markdown message as before; if not, it falls back to `msgtype='text'` so plain replies arrive as clean text — mirroring the approach already used by the Feishu adapter.

Additionally, when markdown IS used, the card title is now derived from the first line of the content (truncated to 30 chars) instead of a hardcoded `Hermes` label.

## Changes

- Add `_DINGTALK_MARKDOWN_RE` regex to detect markdown constructs (headings, lists, code blocks, bold/italic, links, blockquotes, etc.)
- In `send_message`, branch on whether the normalized content matches:
  - Markdown present → `msgtype: markdown` with a first-line-derived title
  - No markdown → `msgtype: text` with plain content

## Motivation

- Plain replies get a cleaner presentation in DingTalk (no forced card title)
- Card titles reflect actual content instead of a hardcoded `Hermes`
- Consistent behavior with the Feishu adapter's plain-text handling

## Testing

- Verified locally: plain-text replies arrive as `msgtype='text'`, markdown replies keep `msgtype='markdown'` with a content-derived title
- Syntax/import checks pass

prs.title: fix(telegram): normalize slug case in _build_provider_keyboard (active plugin path)
prs.body:
## Problem

Fixes #35932. Custom providers with mixed-case slugs (e.g. `MyGateway`, `BitFun`, any provider whose key in `providers:` contains uppercase letters) are silently dropped from the Telegram `/model` inline keyboard. All-lowercase providers are unaffected.

### Root cause

`group_providers()` lowercases every slug before returning it (`models_catalog_static.py:479`):
```python
s = str(slug or "").strip().lower()
```

But `_build_provider_keyboard` built `by_slug` with the original mixed-case slug as the key (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:4410` before this fix):
```python
by_slug = {p.get("slug"): p for p in providers}  # key = original case
```

Then looked up using the lowercased slug from `group_providers()`:
```python
p = by_slug.get(row["slug"])  # key = lowercased — never matches
```

The lookup always returns `None` for mixed-case slugs, so the button is silently dropped.

### Why previous PRs (#35933, #35953, #37282) did not fix this

All three targeted `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, which is the **retired** gateway adapter. The active code path is `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`. The triage comment on #35932 identifies this: _"All three diffs currently target the retired gateway adapter rather than the active Telegram plugin path."_

This PR targets the correct file.

## Fix

Normalize the `by_slug` key to lowercase so it matches what `group_providers()` returns:

```python
# Before
by_slug = {p.get("slug"): p for p in providers}

# After  
by_slug = {(p.get("slug") or "").lower(): p for p in providers}
```

The original slug is still stored on the provider dict and appears in callback data (`mp:<slug>`), so the round-trip selection path is unaffected.

## Verification

Simulation of the exact keyboard-build loop before and after the fix, using the real `group_providers()` function, confirmed the bug and the fix:

**Before fix (simulated):**
```
picker slugs:              ['pipioClaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']
group_providers() returns: ['pipioclaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']  ← lowercased
by_slug keys:              ['pipioClaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']  ← original case
BUTTONS SHOWN:             ['pipio', 'deepseek']
DROPPED:                   ['pipioclaude']  ← pipioClaude silently dropped
```

**After fix:**
```
BUTTONS SHOWN: ['pipioclaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']
DROPPED:       []
```

The regression test in `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_model_picker_case_mismatch.py` covers:
- All-lowercase slugs (baseline)
- The specific `pipioClaude` case from #35932
- Parametrized cases: `MyGateway`, `BitFun`, `UPPER`, `CamelCase`, `mixed_AND_UPPER`
- A mixed list where none should be dropped

## Risk

Low. The change is a one-line normalization to the dict key used for internal lookup only. The slug value stored in each provider dict is unchanged, so callback data, model selection, and downstream routing are all unaffected. Built-in providers have all-lowercase slugs and are not impacted.

prs.title: fix(desktop): probe the SSH remote version from the Hermes stdout line only
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Desktop SSH remote bootstrap probes the remote Hermes version with `hermes --version` and reported the **first line** of the merged output as the version. Because the probe appended `2>&1`, any remote stderr warning printed while the CLI started became the "version": in the linked issue, a plugin warning about a missing CLI dependency on the non-interactive SSH PATH was logged as `remote hermes version:` 5,070 times over two weeks, and the real version string never appeared.

Two changes in `probeHermesVersion` (`apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts`):

1. **Drop the `2>&1` merge.** `SshConnection.exec()` returns `result.stdout` only (`runSsh` collects stdout and stderr in separate buffers), so remote stderr now stays out of the probe result instead of being spliced ahead of the version line.
2. **Pick the version line, not the first line.** As a second line of defense against stdout noise (shell banners, login echoes), the probe now returns the first line starting with `Hermes Agent v` and only falls back to the first line when no such line exists — preserving the old behavior for unexpected/unrecognized version strings.

All consumers of the probe result (`remote hermes version:` log line, lockfile `hermesVersion`, the `${version} at ${path}` connection summary) are display-only, so the narrower extraction cannot break any version comparison logic.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138772

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts` — `probeHermesVersion` no longer appends `2>&1` to the remote `--version` command (stderr stays on the ssh stderr channel), and returns the first line matching `Hermes Agent v` instead of blindly taking the first output line.
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts` — regression test: a noisy probe output (a leading non-version warning line followed by the real version line) resolves to the version line, and the probe command itself no longer contains `--version 2>&1`. The watchdog sleeper's own `2>&1` redirection (part of `withRemoteTimeout`, unchanged) is unaffected.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project electron electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts` — Observed result: 98 passed, 1 skipped; the pre-existing `pidIsOurDashboard recognizes an installer wrapper` failure reproduces identically on a clean `upstream/main` checkout (no diff), i.e. it is unrelated to this change.
2. `npx vitest run --project electron electron/ssh-connection.test.ts` — Observed result: 89 passed (includes the `withRemoteTimeout` tests, confirming the watchdog wrapper still behaves).
3. Manual equivalent of the issue scenario: the new test's fixture replays the exact warning line from the issue followed by the real version line; before the fix the probe returned the warning (first line of merged output), with the fix it returns `Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (e06df9c2eae6)`.
