prs.title: fix(build): retry directory renames through transient Windows EPERM
prs.body:
## Problem

`publishDirectory` in `scripts/build/frontend-common.mjs` publishes freshly compiled frontend products (TUI, web UI) with a single `renameSync`. On Windows, antivirus software and the search indexer briefly hold handles inside files the compiler just wrote, so the rename fails with `EPERM`/`EACCES` and the entire install/update aborts after an otherwise successful compile.

Observed on a Windows 11 machine with a resident AV: **5 consecutive installer failures at the exact same rename**, each retry rebuild clean, while manual standalone builds of the same script never failed — the failure correlates with processes that scan newly created files, not with the build itself. This is the classic Windows AV/indexer race on freshly written directories.

## Fix

`renameSyncRetry`: retry `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`ENOTEMPTY` only, linear backoff (6 attempts, 250ms steps). Every other error code propagates immediately; a genuinely locked path still throws after the budget. Applied to all three renames in `publishDirectory` (out→backup, staged→out, and the backup→out rollback), so a mid-publish lock can't strand the product directory.

`rename` is injectable (`{ rename }` option) following the repo's extraction-over-source-regex pattern (`hiddenWindowsChildOptions`), so tests exercise real tempdir renames with synthetic transient failures instead of monkey-patching the read-only ESM binding of `node:fs`.

## Tests

New `scripts/build/frontend-common.test.mjs` (node:test, colocated like `apps/desktop/electron/*.test.mjs`), 5 tests, all green on Windows:
- transient EPERM (2 failures) then success publishes the product
- budget exhaustion throws the last EPERM
- non-retryable ENOENT propagates on first attempt, no retries
- replace path: new product lands, backup cleared
- failure path: previous product restored from backup, original error re-thrown

Also verified end-to-end: `node scripts/build/tui.mjs` builds clean with the patch applied.

## Notes

- No behavior change on non-Windows (retry only triggers on the three codes).
- Failure mode unchanged for permanently locked paths: throws after ~4s budget.
- Tests take ~6.5s wall time dominated by the budget-exhaustion backoff (250ms steps), acceptable for this file's placement.

prs.title: fix(desktop): Artifacts page lists files linked with spaced paths (port block/buzz#8168)
prs.body:
The Desktop Artifacts page now lists files the agent links with CommonMark angle-bracket destinations (paths with spaces) and labels Windows paths by their file name.

Port of [block/buzz#8168](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/8168) ("preserve Markdown attachment destinations": angle-bracketed URLs, spaces, parentheses, optional titles), adapted from their Flutter link normalizer to our Artifacts scraper.

## Changes
- `apps/desktop/src/app/artifacts/artifact-utils.ts`: Markdown image/link scraping parses the destination like CommonMark: `<...>` (spaces allowed) or a bare run with one level of balanced parens, then an optional `"title"` / `'title'`. It was `\(([^)\s]+)\)`, so `![chart](</home/u/My Pictures/q3 chart.png>)` never matched, and the prose path fallback cannot see a path that starts after `<`.
- `artifactLabel`: Windows paths take their basename before URL parsing. `new URL('C:\\x\\y.png')` accepts `c:` as a scheme and keeps the backslashes, so every Windows artifact was labelled `\x\y.png`.
- 2 invariant tests (`markdown-destinations.test.ts`), both red on `origin/main`.

Root cause: chat rendering got angle-bracket destinations in #130020 (#102782), but the Artifacts page has its own regex scraper and was left behind. This PR fixes that second surface.

## Validation

**Live repro (real Electron app + real `hermes serve`, scripted provider via the `e2e/core` harness):** one assistant turn replying with `![chart](</home/u/My Pictures/q3 chart.png>)`, `[report](<~/Reports/Q3 (final).pdf>)`, `![render](<C:\Users\me\My Renders\frame 01.webp>)`, `![logo](/srv/out/logo.png "Company logo")`, then open Artifacts and read the DOM:

| Tree | Artifacts page tabs | Listed |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | All 1 · Images 1 · Files 0 | `logo.png` only |
| this PR | All 4 · Images 3 · Files 1 | `q3 chart.png`, `frame 01.webp`, `logo.png`, `Q3 (final).pdf` |

- `vitest run src/app/artifacts/`: 33/33 (3 files). New tests: 2/2 red on base, green on head.
- `tsc -p . --noEmit`, eslint on touched files, `scripts/check --only health`: clean.

## Ours vs theirs
| | Buzz #8168 | Hermes before | Hermes after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chat render of `<...>` destinations | fixed (mobile) | already handled (#130020) | unchanged |
| Secondary index of attachments | gallery/video/file routing | Artifacts page dropped them | parsed per CommonMark |
| Titles / balanced parens | handled | handled by fallback path scan | handled by the primary parser |

Not ported: Buzz's image-codec decode fixtures and authenticated file-link routing (Flutter- and relay-specific).

## Infographic
![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aae6d42/e4OjG4ai629e28C1d8A_G_ZXVQGhJO.png)

## Korean Desktop support and profile persistence

Adds Korean Desktop support while preserving the original expanded descriptions and Dante's supplementary work. A Korean choice stays with its profile after switching profiles and restarting; routine values/time, focused settings/Bot/permission copy, narrow-window drafts and Korean search follow the selected locale.

### Reviewed integration snapshot
- Candidate: `aecb37062a58b9914df1a23b1250c767b7c394f9`.
- Pinned upstream main: `f42f579cf8bac4918ac9599bece71618afadd846`.
- Original commits and both @dalgme / @dandacompany credits retained; all 201 original description-map strings unchanged.
- Resolved current locale-pack/config-origin/primary-profile integration. Existing upstream en/ja/zh/zh-Hant values unchanged, no deleted paths against the pinned base. Related PRs #40718/#40849/#40872 have not been independently merged.

### Included behavior
- Korean catalog and Korean language detection/selection; language writes patch only the selected profile's display.language.
- Routine `forever` / `local` labels, completed/error state and selected-locale time rendering.
- Bot/Group drafts survive collapsed/zoomed sidebar boundaries; settings inputs expose Korean accessible names/descriptions.
- Korean NFC/NFD search and profile display-name search; restored built-in theme and capability descriptions on current routes.
- Focused Bot, billing/permission/update, Kanban/Radio and voice-stop copy corrections. Custom/community descriptions and model-facing prompts are preserved.
- Regression fixtures cover the current upstream foreground 401 re-login before manual recovery, without changing that authentication policy.

prs.title: fix(auth): tombstone removed pool rows so stale processes cannot write them back
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A credential removed with `hermes auth remove` comes back when any long-running Hermes process that loaded the pool *before* the removal writes the pool again (rotation, cooldown, status change). The root cause is that `write_credential_pool`'s `removed_ids` parameter only filters that single write's disk merge-back — nothing records that a row was deliberately removed, so a process whose in-memory snapshot still holds the row writes it back verbatim.

This PR makes removals durable: `write_credential_pool` records rows passed via `removed_ids` as id → timestamp tombstones in a new `credential_pool_removals` section of auth.json, and every subsequent write drops rows whose id is tombstoned. Tombstones expire after 7 days (a stale process is expected to flush well within that window; expiry keeps the section from growing unboundedly). Re-adding a credential mints a fresh uuid id, so `auth add` is unaffected by an old tombstone.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138756

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/auth.py` — `write_credential_pool` now registers `removed_ids` as removal tombstones (id → epoch) in the store, filters tombstoned ids out of every write's final row list (both caller entries and the merge-back branch), and garbage-collects tombstones older than the 7-day TTL.
- `hermes_cli/auth_pool_merge.py` — verbatim move of the pool-row merge helpers (`_POOL_STATUS_FIELDS`, `_POOL_TOKEN_GENERATION_FIELDS`, `_credential_token_pair`, `_token_pairs_by_id`, `_merge_pool_row_generation`, `_merge_disk_cooldown_state`, `_entry_ids`) out of `hermes_cli/auth.py`, re-exported from their old home so every caller and monkeypatch path keeps working. This keeps `auth.py` under its FILE_LINES cap alongside the fix (code health ratchet: 0 blocking).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_pool_removal_tombstone.py` — new regression tests: stale-process resurrection, concurrently-added row kept, re-added credential with a fresh id survives, expired tombstone stops filtering and is dropped, plain write creates no tombstone section.

## How to Test

1. Run the self-contained reproduction from the issue against this branch (throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, calls `write_credential_pool` directly):
   ```python
   write_credential_pool("openrouter", [row("keep"), row("revoked")])
   write_credential_pool("openrouter", [row("keep")], removed_ids=["revoked"])  # hermes auth remove
   write_credential_pool("openrouter", [row("keep"), row("revoked")])           # stale process flush
   ```
   Observed result on `main`: ids are `['keep']` after the remove and `['keep', 'revoked']` after the stale flush. Observed result with this PR: `['keep']` after both writes — the removed row stays gone.
2. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_pool_removal_tombstone.py -q` → 5 passed.
3. Existing pool surfaces stay green: `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_pool_operations.py tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_profile_fallback.py tests/agent/test_credential_pool.py tests/agent/test_credential_pool_operations.py tests/agent/test_credential_pool_profile_oauth_fork.py -q` → all passed (the merge helpers moved verbatim and are re-exported).

prs.title: fix(agent): nudge a stall line that follows a tool round (#122119)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops a turn ending on a visible line that announces the next step after the agent has already run tools.

Once a turn has a tool result in its history, `looks_like_codex_intermediate_ack()` returns `False`. That leaves `trailing_continue_intent()` as the only catch, and it only knows `let me now` / `I'll now` / `next, I` and gives up past 400 chars. Lines like "I can proceed with the first fix using the terminal tool." or "Let me write the parse script to a file first, then run it." after a tool round ended the turn as if they were the answer.

Two changes. Both feed the existing stall branch in `finish_text_response`, under the shared two-nudge cap.

1. `trailing_continue_intent()` also matches an unconditional `I can proceed ...` tail. Conditions either side ("if you confirm", "once you approve", "pending your approval", "with your go-ahead", "you decide") still end the turn. The length cap goes from 400 to 600 chars so a short progress summary before the announcement still counts. Applies to every model.
2. `visible_reply_announces_action()` runs the existing promoted-reasoning plan-tail check on visible text, for models opted in to intent-ack continuation (`agent.intent_ack_continuation: true` or a list entry matching the model). It screens the last sentence for sign-offs ("let me know", "I'll wait", "I'll be here"), offers ("if you want") and conditions first. Works with or without prior tool results.

Against the examples in #122119:

| Visible reply | `trailing_continue_intent` | `visible_reply_announces_action` (opted-in models) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `I will continue the inventory and fix the defect.` | False | True |
| `I'll fix the defect now.` | False | True |
| `Let me check the remaining files.` | False | True |
| `Next I will run the tests.` | False | True |
| 458-char progress report ending `I will now fix the defect.` | True (was False) | True |
| German / French continuations | False | False |

The stall detectors (`trailing_continue_intent`, `promoted_reasoning_announces_action` and the new code) move to `agent/agent_runtime_helpers_stall_intent.py` to keep `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` under its size cap. `finish_text_response` calls one helper, `announces_unfinished_action()`, to stay under its line cap. No behaviour change from the move. Callers and tests import from the new module, no re-export shim (per AGENTS.md).

### Related work

- #78113 (open) adds `agent/false_stop.py` with two post-tool signatures (a short colon-ended preamble and a CJK-punctuated continuation) behind a new `agent.false_stop_detection` key. This PR adds no module or config key - it widens the existing guard and reuses `agent.intent_ack_continuation` as the opt-in. They catch different shapes. Both touch `agent/turn_final_response.py`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #105163 and #121772 cover other languages. This PR doesn't.

## Related Issue

Part of #122119. Covers the post-tool gap, the English paraphrases and the length cap for opted-in models, and the `I can proceed` tail for all models. Doesn't cover non-English continuations, and default-config models (intent-ack continuation off) still only get the narrow tail plus `I can proceed`. The issue should stay open.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)

## Changes Made

- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers_stall_intent.py` (new): `trailing_continue_intent` and `promoted_reasoning_announces_action` moved here. Adds the `I can proceed` tail with condition screens either side, the 600-char cap, `visible_reply_announces_action` and `announces_unfinished_action`.
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`: moved detectors removed.
- `agent/turn_final_response.py`: the stall check calls `announces_unfinished_action(text, promoted=..., ack_mode=...)`.

prs.title: fix(tools): reject empty and no-op terminal/execute_code payloads
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Rejects `terminal` and `execute_code` calls with an empty or bare no-op payload before dispatch, with an error telling the model to send the real call.

A stalling model (mostly local models over chat_completions) sometimes sends `{"command": ":"}`, `{"command": ""}` or `{"code": "pass"}` instead of the command it meant to run. Dispatch ran it, it "succeeded" with no output, and the model had no signal nothing happened. It either repeated the same empty call or ended the turn thinking the work ran.

`handle_function_call` now checks the payload argument for these two tools only:

- `terminal.command`: missing, blank, or exactly `:`, `true`, `/bin/true`, `/usr/bin/true`, `exit 0`
- `execute_code.code`: missing, blank, or exactly `pass`, `...`, `None`

On a match it returns a tool error naming the tool and argument ("terminal was called with the bare no-op ':' as `command`, so nothing ran. Re-emit the complete terminal call with the actual command you intend to run in the `command` argument.") and fires `post_tool_call` with `status="blocked"`, `error_type="noop_tool_args"`. Everything else dispatches as before, including commands starting with `:` (`: > file`) and `true` inside a pipeline. Both arguments are already `required` in the tool schemas, so a valid call never has them empty.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found. Happy to file one if preferred.

Related, not a duplicate: #43259 guards a `None` command inside `tools/terminal_tool.py`. This PR works at dispatch, covers `execute_code` too, and catches no-op payloads, not just missing ones.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)

- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `model_tools.py`: `_NOOP_PAYLOAD_ARGS` and `_noop_payload_error()`. `handle_function_call` returns the error before the pre-dispatch guards.
- `tests/tools/test_model_tools.py`: `TestNoopPayloadRejection`. Nine rejected payloads (`_execute_tool` never called, error text checked) and five real payloads that still dispatch, including `: > file`, `true && echo ok` and an empty `web_search` query (other tools aren't screened).

prs.title: fix(agent): retry a reasoning-channel runaway once with a wrap-up nudge
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives a turn one retry when the streaming guard cuts a runaway loop in the reasoning channel, instead of ending on "Repetition Detected".

`main` already cuts a live repetition loop mid-stream (`RunawayStreamWatch` in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`) and marks the response `_runaway_repetition = True`. `recover_from_truncation` then ends the turn whichever channel looped. That's right for the visible content channel - a continuation walks straight back into the loop. For the reasoning channel it throws the turn away before the model has answered. It's deliberating in circles, and a fresh request telling it to stop usually gets an answer or a tool call.

- The runaway mark now carries the cut channel (`"content"` or `"reasoning"`) instead of `True`, on both the chat_completions and anthropic stream paths. Still truthy, so the existing check is unchanged.
- On a reasoning-channel cut, `recover_from_truncation` drops the partial, appends a one-line wrap-up nudge ("Your reasoning started repeating itself and was cut off. Stop deliberating; act now with a tool call or give your answer.") and restarts the request. One retry per turn (`_reasoning_runaway_retries`, reset per turn). A second reasoning loop, or any content loop, ends the turn as before, and the looped text never reaches the stored messages.

### Related work

- #78807 (open issue): DeepSeek V4 Flash reasoning loops that run until the user steps in. `main` already cuts them. This PR turns the first cut into one recovery attempt instead of a failed turn.
- #125650 (open): cuts a looping visible stream at 8k-char thresholds via `interrupt()` in `agent/stream_delivery.py`. Different channel, different files, no overlap.
- #117756 (open): cuts degenerate thinking-stream runs inside `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` and keeps the turn alive by trimming the reasoning. Not tested together. They should compose - a #117756 trim keeps the stream going, and this retry only fires after the runaway watch has cut it. Both edit `chat_completion_helpers.py`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Related Issue

Refs #78807. Reduces the impact of a cut reasoning loop, doesn't stop models looping.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`: `_runaway_repetition` set to the cut channel on both stream paths. No line growth - the file is over its size cap.
- `agent/turn_truncation.py`: `_REASONING_RUNAWAY_NUDGE` and the single retry branch in `recover_from_truncation`.
- `agent/turn_context.py`: `_reasoning_runaway_retries` added to the per-turn reset list.
- `tests/agent/test_stream_runaway_repetition.py`: the fake endpoint records request bodies and can serve a plain answer from the second request on. The existing cut test now expects one request for content loops and two for reasoning loops (one retry, then the turn ends). New `test_reasoning_loop_retries_once_with_wrap_up_nudge_and_recovers` checks the retry carries the nudge, the turn completes with the recovered answer, and the looped text isn't in the stored messages.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_stream_runaway_repetition.py`
2. Regression check: with `main`'s source and this branch's test file, the two reasoning-channel cut cases and the new recovery test fail (`assert 1 == 2`, one request, no retry). With the change all 8 pass.
3. Also green, run per file: `test_repetition_guard.py`, `test_continuation_repetition_guard.py`, `test_stall_guards.py`, `test_intent_ack_continuation.py`, `test_degenerate_final_recovery.py`, `test_turn_end_stall_diagnostics.py`, the guardrail tests, `test_codex_incomplete_budget_escalation.py`, `test_content_policy_refusal_stop_details.py`, `test_overflow_partial_terminal.py`, `test_truncated_tool_call_boost.py`, `transports/test_provider_wire_snapshot.py`.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump hermes-dreaming to 2.8.0 (confirmations for holographic 0.15.0; fixes from three reviews)
prs.body:
Bumps the pinned `sha`, `version` and the pinned doc/image URLs of
`plugin-catalog/hermes-dreaming.yaml` to
[2.8.0](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/releases/tag/v2.8.0).
No change to the manifest shape, the tier, the maintainer or capabilities (still
no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars).

**Disclosure updated**, because the release reads two more of the memory
provider's settings: it now says `db_path/scope/cron_writes/min_trust_threshold`
plus `embeddings/mirror_memory_writes` (read only to report them in
`install.py --check`). The scripts still make no network or LLM calls and still
open `state.db` and every fact store read-only.

**Why 2.7.1 → 2.7.2.** A check of the pass against holographic 0.14.3 — the provider the
catalog installs in place of the copy that left the Hermes core — found two
mistakes of the pass's own:

- **The recall floor was a constant of ours, not the provider's.** holographic
  recalls nothing below its `min_trust_threshold` (words, structure and meaning
  alike), and that threshold is configurable while its default is 0.3. The pass
  and its nightly prompt named a hard-coded 0.3, so on a store tuned to 0.5 the
  `trust_feedback` section offered facts retrieval already ignored, and the
  nightly report named the wrong number. The floor is now the explicit
  `gates.feedback_trust_floor`, else the provider's value, else 0.3; a provider
  config that cannot be parsed falls back to 0.3 rather than "offer everything".
- **`install.py --check` was silent about the 0.14 settings.** `embeddings: on`
  now gets a line saying the pass itself still reads words only (vectors are the
  provider's business, and keywords remain the offline path when the endpoint is
  unreachable); `mirror_memory_writes: true` gets a warning, because then the
  pass's own promotions come back as new facts and recall injects what the system
  prompt already holds in full.

Everything else about 0.14 needed no adaptation, which the release notes state:
the `facts` table is unchanged, history and tombstones were already supported,
per-fact vectors never reach the pass's JSON, and the provider's search by
meaning applies the same trust floor to recall.

**Update — now pinned to 2.7.2** (`41f6970`). A Codex CLI review of 2.7.1 found eight defects in the floor change itself, all fixed with a test that fails on 2.7.1: the floor now travels in each `trust_feedback` item (the agent's payload never carried `gates`); a parsed `config.yaml` is the final word, so a nested `hermes-memory-store.diagnostics.min_trust_threshold` is no longer taken for the setting; the PyYAML-less scanner reads a last line without a newline and the one-line flow form; no process-wide cache of the floor; a bad `feedback_cap` no longer resets an explicit floor; `--check` names an override; a non-UTF-8 `config.yaml` no longer crashes `--check`. The disclosure is unchanged: the same provider keys are read.

**Update — 2.7.3** (`907060a`). A full Codex CLI review of the whole 2.7.2 skill found fourteen defects; each was confirmed by a reproduction and has a test that fails on 2.7.2 (24 failures against 2.7.2, none against 2.7.3). Five were quarantine bypasses: a password after "changed"/"forgot" was not treated as a secret; a rejected secret came back in clear text through `trust_feedback`; a memory entry holding a secret reached the prompt as `nearest_entry` / a conflict's entry; the gate dropped the `previously_rejected` and `store` rule fields; and `subagent` / `tool` sessions counted as people because the shipped example listed `cron` only (all three are now always untrusted). The rest: "does not" was taken for a duplicate of "does" by dedupe and the reject list (now offered as a conflict); the forget sweep missed verbatim copies without their own id and extraction logs, and took an unreadable store for a clean sweep; `dream-reject.py` now writes under the shared state lock and atomically; ride-along sections no longer rest on nights the gate kept shut; the approval-queue alert no longer wakes the agent every night; a vanished memory file with one to three big entries now raises an alert. Full list in the [changelog](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/blob/ba27e6c45e1ebdb0bc1fdeaed88a7bef0adfacdb/CHANGELOG.md).

**Disclosure updated once more**: extraction messages now carry their chat type and sender id (so the extraction prompt can attribute a first-person statement to its speaker), and the entry says so. No new provider keys are read; still no network or LLM calls from the scripts.

Tests: 477 (was 447), core `old_text` / `matched_entry` / batch rules checked against Hermes v0.22.0.

**Update — 2.7.4** (`ba27e6c`). Right after deploying 2.7.3 on my own install (before its first nightly run) I ran it next to 2.7.2 on the live store, memory and reject list: its negation check was too coarse (it gathered the "not"s of unrelated sentences of a long profile and invented three conflicts). 2.7.4 compares what each side negates, only words both texts contain; with it the decisions on the install's 58 facts and the secret screening of a month of messages match 2.7.2. Disclosure unchanged from 2.7.3.

**Update — 2.7.5** (`75d3ee6`). A second review of the 2.7.2 → 2.7.4 diff (Antigravity CLI, Gemini 3.8 Flash, running the suite and its own reproductions) found eight issues; six were confirmed and fixed with regression tests: comparatives ("more") counted as negations; a shared negation masked another flip; a spaced hyphen was no password separator, an all-letter password after "changed … :" passed and a number after a dash in a story about the change was quarantined; a candidate whose own text is a forgotten fact stayed as a placeholder; `keywords_needed` keyed its cooldown on the first 300 characters; `dream-reject.py` wrote when the lock could not be taken. The decisions on my install's 58 facts and the secret screening of a month of messages still match 2.7.2. Disclosure unchanged.

**Update — now pinned to 2.7.6** (`93d7326`). A narrow Codex CLI review of the 2.7.2 → 2.7.5 diff (gpt-6.1-sol) found six issues, each confirmed by a reproduction and fixed with a regression test: a conflict with a memory entry holding a secret still carried that entry's numbers (a PIN) and negated words; a Cyrillic password after a dash passed; a fact standing whole inside an entry that says "not" skipped the negation check; "likes X but not Y" equalled the reverse; the forget sweep removed a kept fact sharing its first 85 characters with a forgotten one (items now match by the full-text fingerprint); `dream-reject.py` gained `--hermes-home` so it takes the dream's own lock. The decisions on my install's 58 facts and the secret screening of a month of messages still match 2.7.2. Disclosure unchanged.

**Update — now pinned to 2.8.0** (`cbb7f6d`). New ride-along section `confirm` for holographic 0.15.0, which records who stands behind a fact and counts confirmations: facts people in trusted chats said again on two different days, by messages holding 60 % of the fact's stems and not negating it, are offered to `fact_feedback(confirmed)` — at most 10 a night, never waking the agent; without the provider's confirmations table the section is empty. Measured on a live store: the loose corroboration rule would have offered 26 of 58 facts (topic mentions), the shipped one none. No new data is read or written: disclosure unchanged.

prs.title: fix: show account limits in desktop and TUI /usage
prs.body:
## Summary
- Show provider subscription/account limits and available rate-limit lines in Desktop bare `/usage` and the legacy Ink TUI `session.usage` report, alongside existing session totals and the Nous balance view.
- Resolve the route from the live agent, compute-host metadata, or the selected profile's configuration. Keep home, secret, and terminal scopes bound to the owning profile across worker threads.
- Bound cosmetic quota retrieval with a two-worker admission limit and fail open on timeout or provider failure, without blocking the RPC reader or retaining an unbounded queue of credential-bearing work.
- Preserve invalid-subcommand and no-live-agent reset fallthrough. When a live agent exists, `/usage reset [--force]` uses that agent's exact route rather than independently selecting a different pooled account in the slash worker.
- Declare the on-demand fields in the Pydantic gateway contract and regenerate shared TypeScript/OpenRPC artifacts. Keep the oversized protocol test file unchanged from main by placing usage regressions in topical test files.

## CI refresh
The old head emitted `All required checks pass`, while current branch protection requires `All required checks pass (v2)`. This refresh takes upstream's current workflow definitions unchanged; no CI gate or trust policy is bypassed. Fork-workflow approvals, if requested by GitHub, still require an upstream maintainer.

## Verification
- Full gateway/account regression run: **2,706 passed across 317 files**, with retries disabled. This ran before the last five-commit upstream refresh; the reviewed feature patch and all touched source bytes were verified identical after that rebase.
- Post-rebase gateway/account and generated-contract checks: **131 passed across 8 files**.
- Ink TUI complete check: **1,795 passed, 2 skipped**; typecheck, i18n-key check, lint and build passed. Existing unrelated lint warnings remain.
- `python scripts/check --base upstream/main`: **all 12 checks passed**.
- Behavioral red/green: quota integration cases fail on unfixed main; live-account reset routing cases fail before the correction and pass afterward. UI quota and independent rate-limit rendering also have base-red coverage.
- Independent native Codex review: initial account-reset routing finding fixed; follow-up review found no actionable regressions. Test execution was performed separately in a prepared PM Python 3.14 environment.
- Integration tests use temporary profile config/auth stores and a loopback HTTP quota endpoint, not a real provider account. No real reset credits were consumed and no live Hermes deployment was changed.

Closes #45713

prs.title: fix(plugins): evict sys.modules through an atomic snapshot
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a race that randomly dropped ~5 platform plugins from every boot on multi-home hosts, each logged as:

```
WARNING hermes_cli.plugins: Failed to load plugin 'slack-platform': dictionary changed size during iteration
```

Root cause: `_evict_modules` walked `sys.modules` with a comprehension — `[n for n in sys.modules if ...]`. A comprehension is **not** a snapshot: it iterates the live dict key by key, and each step can release the GIL. On a host serving multiple profile homes, one loader thread per profile imports plugin modules concurrently (background discovery for the default home + per-profile hydration for secondaries), so a peer insert into `sys.modules` mid-walk raised `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` *inside the plugin's own import*, failing the whole load. Which plugins lost the race differed every boot — exactly the random 5-of-21 set reported in the issue, with each failure logged twice (discovery + deferred materialization both attempt the load).

`list(sys.modules)` builds the key snapshot in a single C-level call (atomic under the GIL), and `sys.modules.pop(name, None)` tolerates a peer deleting an entry between snapshot and delete, where `del` would raise `KeyError`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #132259
Fixes #131817
Fixes #123926

(Same `_evict_modules` live-`sys.modules` walk reported independently; #131817 supersedes the earlier fix attempt in #131840.)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/plugins_loader.py` — `_evict_modules` now snapshots with `list(sys.modules)` (one C call) instead of a comprehension (lazy walk of the live dict), and uses `pop(name, None)` so a concurrent removal between snapshot and delete cannot raise.

## How to Test

1. New regression test `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_loader.py::test_evict_modules_tolerates_concurrent_imports`: a peer thread churns `sys.modules` (insert+delete pairs) while the test loops `_evict_modules` with the switch interval tightened to 20 µs. Observed result: passes in ~0.3 s with the fix; against the pre-fix comprehension it reliably fails within a second with `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` (the exact message from the issue).
2. Full-chain reproduction (2 temp HERMES_HOMEs discovering + materializing deferred platforms concurrently, 10 rounds, 20 µs switch interval, `HERMES_PLUGINS_DEBUG=1`): 20 captured "Failed to load plugin" tracebacks ending in `_evict_modules` before the fix; **0** after the fix.
3. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_loader.py tests/plugins/test_plugin_loader.py -q` — 89 passed on this branch.

prs.title: fix(acp): gateway owns each session's editor MCP servers and hermes acp flags
prs.body:
![Gateway owns editor servers](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aae6a61/yDJTkK6K3oLStZ_yYEbHB_XZfIkcnH.png) ## What does this PR do? Under the unified gateway (#106742) the gateway owns every session, but editors' MCP servers and `hermes acp` launch flags were still treated as client-side state the gateway either ignored or pinned and refused to change. This PR makes the editor's `mcpServers` list a **request** that the gateway turns into session state through its single writer, and forwards the ACP launch flags. | Editor action | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `hermes acp --yolo` / `--safe-mode` / `--ignore-user-config` / `--accept-hooks` / `--ignore-rules` | ignored on the gateway path | frozen into the session's policy at `session/new` | | MCP tool names | `editor__` | `editor__<8-char tag>`; existing sessions keep their old names | | One editor MCP server fails discovery at `session/new` | the whole session fails | that server is logged and left out | | Load / resume from a different folder | `cwd_policy_conflict` | the owner's `workspace` mutation moves the session, then attaches | | Load / resume with changed MCP config (e.g. a rotated token) | `acp_mcp_policy_conflict` | `session.mutate operation=editor_mcp` applies it | | Fork with `mcpServers` | `cwd_policy_conflict` | the child gets its own MCP scope | | Editor MCP servers between turns | spawned and shut down every turn | kept connected while the session has a viewer | | A server's tool schema changes | every later turn fails with `acp_mcp_schema_changed` | the manifest is re-frozen at the next admission's start, inside the drain | ## Related Issue **Fixes tracker items ACP-8, ACP-9, ACP-10, ACP-12 and ACP-13 in #134889.** This PR uses `Refs` instead of `Fixes` because #134889 tracks every finding from the #106742 testing, and `Fixes` would close the whole tracker on merge. Refs #134889 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made Two commits: **1. `fix(acp): forward hermes acp flags, keep editor MCP names, rebind moved sessions`** - **ACP-13** (`acp_adapter/gateway_server.py`, `hermes_cli/main_agent_cmds.py`): `new_session` sends `env_launch_flags()`, and `cmd_acp` exports `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS` / `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES`. - **ACP-9** (`gateway/session_local_mcp.py`): names keep the server name. The per-session tag stays, so two sessions borrowing same-named servers never adopt one connection. - **ACP-8 (creation)**: a server that fails discovery at creation is left out of the frozen selection, so later turns never respawn it. - **ACP-12 (load/resume)**: a different folder runs the existing `workspace` mutation (Desktop's "Move to project"), which needs control access and an idle session. Fork from another folder branches, then moves the child. **2. `fix(acp): gateway owns each session's editor MCP servers`** - **`session.mutate operation=editor_mcp`** (`gateway/session_mutations.py`, `hermes_state_mutations.py`, `hermes_state_mutation_prepared.py`): joins the policy-mutation path, so it gets the control-capability and profile checks, the revision/generation fence, idle-only and the writer. Discovery reruns; credentials stay in owner memory and the store gets only a fingerprint. Identical schemas leave the manifest byte-identical. - **ACP-10**: load/resume that gets `acp_mcp_policy_conflict` runs that mutation and retries. A caller without control is still refused. - **ACP-12 (fork)** (`hermes_state_mutation_branch.py`): `session.mutate branch` accepts `mcp_servers`; the child gets its own scope from the fork's list or a copy of the parent's servers. This also stops a plain branch from sharing the parent's scope, credentials and connection, which it did before. - **ACP-8 (lifetime and drift)**: a per-scope reference count keeps a session's connection while it has a viewer and closes it on the last detach or on retire. `refreeze_editor_mcp` runs in `_claim_next` under the claim and mutation locks, so the manifest only changes at a turn boundary (the prompt-caching rationale is kept in comments). - **Event**: `session.tools_changed` (server names and generation only) is published when the manifest changes; the ACP adapter shows it as an agent message. **For reviewers:** - Loading or resuming from another folder now moves the session for every viewer, Desktop's sidebar included (maintainer decision). It fails with `session_busy` / `stale_generation` if a turn is running. - `test_native_cold_editor_rebind_refuses_changed_secret` is renamed `…_applies_changed_secret`: a changed config is rebound. Refusal without control capability or from another profile is still tested. - Servers stay up while *any* viewer is attached, not only editors; the gateway can't tell an ACP subscription apart. With no viewer, a turn starts each server twice (drift check, then turn). - A failed re-freeze is logged and doesn't pause the queue; that turn then fails with `acp_mcp_schema_changed` as before. A server that is down at check time never shrinks the manifest. - `hermes --safe-mode acp` / `--ignore-user-config acp` need `-m` and `--provider`, since neither reads the profile route. A missing one is refused at `session/new` with a message naming it. This is stricter than chat and the TUI, which require only `-m`. - **Open:** retrying a fork exactly after a gateway restart, before the editor resupplies the parent's servers, fails with `launch_credentials_unavailable`. Retiring a session closes its held connection synchronously on the event loop. - **Merge order:** this PR and the session-lifecycle PR from the same batch both edit the last-viewer detach path in `gateway/session_authority.py`. Whichever lands second gets a small rebase. The `release_editor_mcp` call must stay first inside `if not live.subscribers:`, ahead of #138720's `end_reason` split, so an ACP editor that detaches without a reason still releases its servers. ## Review follow-ups Fixes for the independent review and Greptile comments, each with a regression test that fails before the fix: - **CI fix:** `refreeze_editor_mcp` returns early when no session of the owner borrows editor servers, and reads the committed policy from the store instead of `runner.adapters`. - **Workspace move:** a held connection's identity includes the cwd, so a committed move respawns stdio servers in the new folder. - **Live schema drift:** the admission-start check re-lists tools from each held server (5 s bound) instead of reading cached schemas, then re-freezes through `session.mutate`'s own writer (`write_mutation`; the separate copy is gone). - **Removing servers:** an `editor_mcp` change to `[]` closes the held connections. That mutation is the only way to remove servers: an empty or omitted `mcpServers` on ACP load, resume or fork keeps them, so a second client without MCP config never strips the first editor's tools. - **Branch fences first:** a branch runs its prepare-only fences (receipt, revision, generation, idle) before discovering the child's servers, so stale, busy and exact-retry branches start nothing. - **ACP-13:** `hermes -m --provider

--safe-mode acp` (or `--ignore-user-config`) sends that route. Without `-m` or `--provider` it refuses at `session/new` with a message naming the missing flag; the gateway's explicit-model check is unchanged. - **Drift check (maintainer review):** the whole admission-start re-check is best-effort: any failure is logged and the turn proceeds, so it never pauses the FIFO or kills the drain. Held servers are re-listed concurrently under one 5 s bound, and the check runs only after the head passes its admission checks, so a refused head starts no server and commits no change. ## How to Test ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/acp_adapter \ tests/gateway/test_session_mutation_branch.py tests/gateway/test_session_operator_scope.py \ tests/gateway/test_local_session_recovery.py tests/gateway/test_launch_secret_retirement.py ``` 1. **Fail first:** against the commit before each change, the new and updated tests fail for the intended reasons: no flags forwarded, `acp_mcp_discovery_failed`, hex-only names, `cwd_policy_conflict` on load and fork, `acp_mcp_policy_conflict` on cold load, `invalid_params` for `editor_mcp`, and `admitted_turn_failed` on drift. Three tests pass on both by design (refusal without control, from another profile, and an unviewed session releasing its connection). 2. **Security invariants, tested:** scopes differ per session, fork and profile; `state.db` and event frames carry no secrets after a rebind or fork; missing generation, stale revision, a running turn and missing control capability are each refused; an exact retry returns the same receipt. 3. **On this branch** (on `main` at `ca069e12`): `tests/acp_adapter` plus 15 gateway mutation/branch/recovery files give 363 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. `ruff` is clean; the code-health gate reports 0 blocking, 0 advisory. 4. **Not tested here:** a live editor (Zed or VS Code) against a real gateway. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — not ticked: I ran the related suites above, not the whole tree; CI is the full run - [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — not ticked: `ruff check` and the code-health gate pass; the full `scripts/check` was not run - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu Linux (kernel 6.8) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

prs.title: fix(terminal): run foreground local commands in their own systemd scope
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Runs **foreground** local commands in their own transient systemd scope, so a memory-heavy `terminal` command can no longer take the gateway's cgroup — and with it the messaging control plane — down with it.

#70716/#97739 isolated *background* executors this way; the foreground path stayed in the gateway's cgroup, where one big build or pytest can make systemd-oomd kill the process holding your sessions mid-turn. It used to report:

```
$ cat /proc/self/cgroup
0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/hermes-gateway.service
```

This reuses the same foreground spawn point the background path already calls. Rebased onto `main` (`71574220`); head `98fd7a1135`.

## Related Issue

Refs #97739 — the isolation half for foreground commands (the queueing/resource-pressure half is untouched) and #70716.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor
- [ ] 🎯 New skill

## Changes Made

- `tools/environments/local.py`: `_foreground_scope_argv` wraps the `_run_bash` argv when the Linux host is a systemd-supervised gateway (`INVOCATION_ID` checked first), the user-scope probe succeeds and the user bus is alive. An inherited bus address cannot pass for a live bus; a private Bot Desktop bus is preserved; every fallback after those gates logs one warning per process.
- `tools/environments/local.py`: `_run_bash` records the unit; `_kill_process` stops the scope **after** the parent is signalled, in `finally`, so an unexpected group-kill failure re-raises instead of leaking the unit; `_force_kill_process` fires a non-blocking `SIGKILL`; `stop_foreground_scopes()` stops this gateway's own scope glob at host exit, enqueued. `_scope_pid_is_alive()` fails closed: an import or liveness failure skips the scope, with the traceback logged.
- `tools/process_registry_systemd.py` (new, 94 lines): `_stop_systemd_unit()` and `list_systemd_user_scope_units()` moved here by the follow-up below, so `tools/process_registry.py` stays under its size cap. The `memory_max=`/`prefix=` keywords keep background, probe and cron callers unchanged, and `adopt_local` carries the foreground unit into `session.systemd_unit`.
- `tools/terminal_tool_lifecycle.py`: `cleanup_all_environments` calls `stop_foreground_scopes()` after `kill_live_foreground_processes()`.
- `gateway/cgroup_cleanup.py` (`ExecStopPost`): after a permitted cgroup reap it stops each loaded `hermes-fg-*` scope whose PID is gone — the backstop for a SIGKILLed gateway. It uses neither `$MAINPID` (unset by then) nor the PID file (a stale record can name either process); a refused reap means a live gateway owns the cgroup.
- Tests: `tests/tools/test_local_foreground_scope.py` (new, 13 items: 7 parametrized contract rows, 2 over the choke point's flag/`memory_max` decision, kill/adopt, 3 real-systemd rows) + 6 sweep rows in `test_cgroup_cleanup.py`, plus the fresh-read `cgroup.procs` pin restored from `main`. Two allowlist rows; a **Foreground command isolation (systemd gateways)** docs section.

## Credit

- **@oppih** (author): the foreground scope, the user-bus env at the spawn point, the scope stop in `_kill_process`, the unit carried through `adopt_local`, the `ExecStopPost` crash sweep with its docs, and the real-systemd rows.
- **@kshitijk4poor**: 19 commits cherry-picked with `-x` (authorship preserved), including the `process_registry_systemd.py` size-cap split and the `_kill_process` re-raise fix that clears the `BLE001` finding. Two of that head's commits are deliberately left out: the test trim and the sweep-guard removal.
- **@KumarG23**: same idea earlier in #93333 (prior art; no code taken).

## Verification

All numbers on this head `98fd7a1135`, on a Linux host with a real user manager (`running`, `Linger=yes`):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `test_local_foreground_scope` + `test_cgroup_cleanup` | **24 passed, 0 skipped** — all three real-systemd rows ran |
| wider set (5 files, incl. `test_process_registry`) | **147 passed, 5 skipped** |
| code-health ratchet vs `71574220` | **0 blocking, 0 advisory** (2 blocking before the logging fix) |
| `ruff 0.15.10` (the CI pin) over every touched `.py` | **All checks passed!** |
| sizes | `process_registry.py` **2885** (cap 2909), `local.py` 1307 |
| leaked units | none |

Earlier-head counters and the mutation/red-on-base runs are in the **evidence log comment** below.

**CI:** the three workflow runs on this head are `action_required` — a fork PR's first run needs a maintainer's approval.

## Maintainer notes

- **No `MemoryMax` on foreground scopes** (accounting only): the shared background cap would be 4 GiB on most hosts, OOM-killing a working `cargo build` with rc 137.
- **When it applies.** Only under a systemd-supervised gateway on Linux; CLI/TUI and s6/Docker gateways are unaffected, and without `systemd-run` or the user bus the command runs unwrapped.
- **Cleanup is best-effort.** Both stops only enqueue, so a scope may still be stopping when `Restart=` brings up the next gateway.
- **Overlap.** #117598 (@teknium1) and #87549 (`preexec_fn` on the same Popen) are still open; whichever lands first, the others need a rebase.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add Render skills and MCP catalog entry
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds Render to the plugin catalog. The separately maintained [Render for Hermes package](https://github.com/ojusave/render-hermes-plugin) bundles 20 existing skills from [render-oss/skills](https://github.com/render-oss/skills) and connects Hermes to Render's hosted MCP server. Users can inspect their workspace and use the existing deployment, debugging and service-management instructions without configuring the remote connection by hand.

This is a community package maintained by me. The Render Sandboxes terminal plugin is separate and is not included.

## Related Issue

No issue. Related skills-only submission: #138673. That PR now proposes all 21 upstream skill catalog entries for individual installation. This PR packages 20 of those original skills together with the Render MCP connection; the Docker exclusion is explained below.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature: plugin catalog entry

## Changes Made

Only `plugin-catalog/render-platform.yaml`. It pins version `0.1.0` to `1d343332142c27e1b97281ff03e2811f8a083750` in `ojusave/render-hermes-plugin`.

The package uses portable Agent Plugins v1 `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` and skills. It has no native Python entrypoint, hooks, middleware, Desktop code, core overrides or self-updater. The original 127 skill/reference/template files match Render source commit `8675173fe30232384d51c8763d1eea4db0350419` byte for byte. The source record, checksums and MIT license are included.

The JSON-only manifest is intentional: the current loader and catalog CI accept portable packages directly. Adding a native `plugin.yaml` would change manifest precedence.

## Disclosures and scanner findings

- MCP requests go to `https://mcp.render.com/mcp`. Hermes resolves `RENDER_API_KEY` from the active profile when connecting. The package has no code that reads credential stores or refreshes credentials.
- Render tools can inspect and change resources within the key's account permissions; resource changes can incur charges. The server is declared `trust: untrusted`. Calls without `readOnlyHint=true` need approval, including Render's current `list_workspaces` tool. An unattended attempt was denied; the interactive test used Allow once for that specific tool. No approval bypass or permanent allowlist was used.
- Skills guide local file edits and shell/Render CLI commands. Those run on the Hermes host, with the CLI's own authentication. This package adds no telemetry or background process. Existing native `mcp_servers.render` settings override the portable connection and its trust setting, as documented.
- Hermes validation returns CAUTION. The high findings are `bind_all_interfaces`, `python_os_environ` and `sudo_usage` in the original instructional examples. The normal GitHub installer reported 45 findings across all severities; I reviewed its prompt before installing. No scanner rules or files were rewritten to suppress findings.
- `render-docker` is omitted because its Dockerfile cleanup example triggers a critical scanner rule. The included skills remain unchanged. This omission and the warnings are documented rather than presenting all 21 skills as admitted.

## How to Test

1. Clone `ojusave/render-hermes-plugin` and check out the pinned SHA above.
2. Run `python3 scripts/verify_package.py`, then `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps`.
3. Follow the README to prepare MCP support, install, add the Render key and enable `render-platform`. Start a new chat, ask for accessible workspaces and approve only `list_workspaces` once. No deployment is needed.
4. Disable the plugin and restart Hermes. Its skills and portable connection should no longer be registered.

Verified on macOS arm64, Python 3.14.3 and Hermes upstream base `5575a0859d6278bfcef79c28189a24594952efd3`:

- Catalog schema and all 12 `scripts/check --staged --base upstream/main` checks pass.
- Exact pinned package validation passes all four checks, with CAUTION disclosed above. Executable-payload scan passes.
- Fresh ordinary GitHub installation at `81b605532c8f0b2ae9d4e97dca277a52c2b5abff` passed. All 127 files matched, 20 skills registered, and a real interactive Hermes task loaded the packaged skill and returned 16 Render workspaces. The persisted MCP response was checked independently. The final pin changes only README instructions and the test receipt, not manifests or skills.
- Disable/removal checks pass. Temporary test credentials were removed and the test gateway stopped.
- Relevant upstream tests: 139 pass, one fails. All 20 MCP approval tests pass. The failing unmodified upstream test is `test_portable_validation_fails_orphan_and_reports_availability`: it expects an exact availability string, while this macOS result also includes a candidate path. The Render package has no application-presence requirement.

Follow-up audit against Hermes upstream `ca069e12239a2c8d13887ac9f983557d00bdcfd2`: the exact published package again passed `hermes plugins validate --install-deps --json` with CAUTION. All 20 skills loaded without parser diagnostics, and all 127 files still matched Render's source. All 76 portable-loader and MCP-approval tests passed. Two placeholder profile keys resolved independently, and a missing key was rejected before making a request. This audit did not repeat the earlier live Render call.

[Sanitized results and tested revisions](https://github.com/ojusave/render-hermes-plugin/blob/1d343332142c27e1b97281ff03e2811f8a083750/validation/results.json). Linux/Windows live runs, first-time account authentication and production readiness are not established.

## Live deployment follow-up

Tested the published package at `3269568e922bed12ca42d7bbbcbbf682730e0939` in real Hermes `4e1e373c809d` (upstream `ca069e12239a2`) on macOS with Render CLI 2.28.0. Normal GitHub installation registered 20 skills and the packaged MCP connection, with no native Render override. The agent loaded render-mcp, render-deploy, render-env-vars, render-debug and render-cli, created one paid Starter Node service, verified its health and initial page, retrieved real logs, changed WELCOME_MESSAGE through MCP, verified the updated deployment and page, and deleted the service through the CLI. Separate HTTP requests verified both versions; a separate MCP request confirmed deletion with 404. The skills-only distribution completed the same lifecycle on its own service. Both services were removed, the original CLI workspace restored, temporary credentials removed and test gateways stopped.

The run required intervention: Hermes lost its session-turn lease and withdrew pending approvals during longer turns. The failed attempts were preserved, and shorter follow-up turns completed using fresh normal approvals. The root cause remains unresolved. CLI cleanup also initially refused a workspace mismatch; the README now explains that CLI and MCP selections are separate. The reused disposable app reported 3 moderate and 1 critical npm dependency findings; these are fixture findings, not a clean production-app audit. This tests a representative web-service workflow, not every skill or unattended production operation. The updated pin changes only the README and sanitized results; manifests and skills are unchanged. Final package validation passed all four checks with CAUTION, all 127 skill files still matched Render's source, and all 12 repository checks passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution and catalog admission guides.
- [x] Searched existing catalog entries and PRs.
- [x] Only the catalog entry is changed in this PR.
- [x] Conventional commit; required local repository checks pass.
- [x] README setup, approval behavior, source ownership and limits documented.
- [x] Tested on macOS arm64; other operating systems not exercised.
- [ ] Full test suite is green. Not claimed: targeted results and the upstream failure are disclosed above.
- [ ] Upstream catalog CI has passed. Awaiting the PR workflow.

prs.title: fix(windows): stop sandboxed Hermes homes from writing the real User PATH
prs.body:
## Summary
Only the Hermes home that new consoles use can now add itself to the Windows User PATH. Before this change, a process with a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` (a review preview, a lab run, a Windows test run) prepended that home's `bin` to the real `HKCU\Environment\Path` during dependency sync or update. Overriding environment variables does not isolate the registry, so every console opened afterwards ran the sandbox's launcher. On one machine this left 15 stale entries, and `hermes` crashed with `No module named 'ruamel'` from a review tree. One run of the Windows test suite on `main` added 7 more.

Root cause: `_expose_windows_user_bin` and `migrate_windows_bin_path` registered `get_default_hermes_root()\bin`, and that root follows the current process's environment.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py`: `_new_console_environment()` reads the environment a new console receives, via `CreateEnvironmentBlock(token, FALSE)`. `owns_user_path(root)` allows a PATH write only when that environment resolves the same root, and refuses when Windows cannot say. `_expose_windows_user_bin` still publishes launchers into the home's own `bin`, then reports `skipped` instead of writing the PATH.
- `hermes_cli/_install_repair.py`: the update-tail PATH migration runs the same check before writing. The check is wrapped so the function still never raises.
- `hermes_constants.py`: `hermes_root_for_environment(environ)` applies `get_default_hermes_root`'s root rules to another environment. `%NAME%` and a leading `~` expand from that environment only. A relative or unresolvable `HERMES_HOME` returns None.
- `scripts/install.ps1`: corrects a stale comment about PATH ownership.
- `tests/conftest.py` (separate commit): on Windows, both PATH writers raise inside tests unless the test stubs them.

Behaviour changes:
- A custom home owns the User PATH only when `HERMES_HOME` is stored as a user variable.
- `HERMES_DATA_DIR_SUFFIX` channel installs no longer put their `bin` ahead of the stable `hermes`.

Not fixed here (follow-ups):
- A sandbox whose `HERMES_HOME` sits inside the real home, or a review tree run against the real home, still resolves the real root. It can republish the real `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin` launchers bound to its own checkout. Windows has no launcher-ownership check like POSIX `_owns_launcher`.
- `install.ps1` still writes the User PATH when a harness runs it against a sandbox.
- `hermes uninstall` deletes the stored `HERMES_HOME` regardless of which home it is uninstalling.

## Validation
| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `expose_cli()` in a sandbox environment, with the real registry writer and the real Win32 call | `<box>\hermes\bin` added to the User PATH | PATH unchanged, `skipped` |
| `owns_user_path(<real home>)` called from inside that sandbox | — | `True` |
| `test_update_launch_completion.py`, `test_hermes_home_shared_launchers.py` | 7 tests write the real User PATH (with the new guard: 7 `TEST BUG` failures) | 35 pass, PATH unchanged |
| New tests: sandbox, profile and default homes; inherited `%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `~` values; fail-closed migration; real `CreateEnvironmentBlock` | — | pass. Removing the gates fails 3; reverting to process-side expansion fails 2 |
| 84 related test files, run on Windows with the 3.11 dev venv | baseline failure set | same failure set, none new, User PATH unchanged by the run |

The failures in that 84-file baseline also occur on `main` in this environment (for example 9 in `test_old_updater_takeover.py` and 17 in `test_web_server.py`). They come from the dev venv, not from this change. ruff (pre-commit config) is clean. The Windows footgun check finds nothing new.

## What does this PR do?

Stop `hermes whatsapp` re-pairing when the old session directory cannot be removed or recreated. Previously, `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` could leave locked credentials behind, print “Session cleared”, and launch pairing against that same uncleared directory.

The wizard now reports the filesystem failure, asks the operator to stop the gateway using that profile before retrying, and exits nonzero before spawning the pairing process. It does not kill any process or guess ownership from a port.

- [x] Bug fix

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_whatsapp_repair_cleanup.py`: exercise the real wizard and filesystem with native Windows locked credentials, then retry after releasing the handle. Also retain successful unlocked re-pairing coverage. Only prompts, configuration access and the external pairing subprocess are test doubles; deletion is real.

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_whatsapp_repair_cleanup.py --file-retries 0 -q
```

prs.title: fix(local-runtime): account for Windows AMD iGPU memory reservations
prs.body:
# fix(local-runtime): account for Windows AMD iGPU memory reservations

## What does this PR do?

Fixes managed local-model admission on Windows AMD APUs with a large BIOS-reserved GPU memory pool, such as Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S systems configured with 128 GiB physical RAM and 96 GiB reserved for the GPU.

### Problem

Windows exposes only the remaining approximately 32 GiB as OS physical RAM.
Hermes currently caps every integrated GPU's pool at that OS-visible total:

```python
pool = min(ram_total, _windows_igpu_bytes(device) or ram_total)
```

This is appropriate for an ordinary shared-memory iGPU, but discards the separate GPU reservation on these machines. After headroom, Hermes budgets approximately 25.4 GiB instead of recognizing the reserved memory. A model
that loads successfully with the same llama.cpp Vulkan engine is rejected by the planner and omitted from the router's generated presets. Selecting it then produces HTTP 400, `model '...' not found`, even though its GGUF shards are present.

The affected Windows host also returns two identical Radeon adapter records from DXGI. The existing single-candidate check treats those records as ambiguous and cannot use the adapter's memory figures.

### Solution

- Reuse the existing DXGI adapter probe and deduplicate identical adapter records before selection; do not add another registry/WMI probe.
- Add a Windows-only reservation path when the engine positively identifies an integrated GPU, its name matches the selected AMD adapter, and dedicated memory is at least 75% of OS-visible RAM. Reuse the existing large-pool threshold rather than special-casing a product name or a 96-GiB capacity.
- Account for DXGI dedicated memory plus the shared allowance capped at OS-visible RAM. Apply the existing dedicated-memory margin and UMA headroom to their respective portions.
- Preserve `uma=True`, `ram_available_bytes=0`, and `lazy_reads=False`. Shared RAM is not added again as spill space, and AMD integrated-GPU tensor-loading behavior remains unchanged.
- Use a fresh engine memory reading for live/launch budgets. Subtract aggregate heap occupancy, allowing credit for the outgoing server's `own_bytes`, cap shared availability at currently available OS RAM, retain launch headroom, and never exceed the capacity grant.
- Keep the existing budgeting paths for ordinary small-reservation iGPUs, CPU inference, NVIDIA, discrete GPUs, and supported or ambiguous reservation probes.

The Vulkan heap total is used to estimate occupancy, not added to physical capacity. This is not a blanket `min`-to-`max` change or a memory override.

## Related issue

Addresses the native-Windows reproduction of [NousResearch/hermes-agent#102593](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/102593).

[PR #131782](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131782) fixed AMD/Intel backend selection and discrete GPU budgets but intentionally left integrated devices on the OS-RAM path.
[PR #102562](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/102562) addresses the Linux sysfs reservation case; this change does not implement that Linux probe or claim to resolve every platform covered by the issue.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Regression tests

## Changes made

- `hermes_cli/local_runtime/hardware.py`: factor adapter selection, recognize the reserved pool, and wire capacity, live, and launch budgeting.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_windows_reserved_igpu_budget.py`: native-Windows cases covering duplicate adapters, reservation capacity, shared-memory accounting, live occupancy, outgoing-server credit, host-memory pressure, exhausted memory, ordinary/unknown devices, and unavailable live readings.

No configuration keys, dependencies, model files, or llama.cpp changes.

### Automated checks on native Windows

Before applying the runtime change, the new test file reproduced the defect:
**2 failed, 5 passed**. After applying it, the targeted suites produced
**74 passed, 2 platform-specific skips**, with no failures:

```powershell
bash .\scripts\run_tests.sh `
  .\tests\hermes_cli\test_windows_reserved_igpu_budget.py `
  .\tests\hermes_cli\test_local_windows_igpu_pool.py `
  .\tests\hermes_cli\test_local_launch_budget.py `
  .\tests\hermes_cli\test_unified_pool_quirk.py `
  .\tests\hermes_cli\test_local_preset_admission.py `
  .\tests\hermes_cli\test_local_growth.py `
  .\tests\hermes_platform\test_import_hygiene.py `
  .\tests\hermes_platform\test_gpu_adapters.py `
  -j 2 --file-retries 0

python .\scripts\check
```

### Real hardware: capacity

Hardware: Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, 128 GiB physical RAM, nominal 96-GiB GPU reservation. DXGI reported approximately 95.8 GiB dedicated and 15.9 GiB shared, while Windows exposed approximately 31.8 GiB of OS RAM.

Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q3_K_XL`, three GGUF shards totaling approximately 83.81 GiB.

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Budgeted device pool | 31.8 GiB | 111.7 GiB |
| Usable capacity after headroom | 25.4 GiB | 99.9 GiB |
| Model admission | Refused: needs approximately 93.9 GiB at 64K | Admitted |
| Generated context | None | 98,304 tokens |

## Scope and limitations

- The large dedicated-memory gate and exact adapter-name match are intentionally conservative. Before an engine can identify the device, the existing fallback remains in effect.
- DXGI matching uses the existing description/capacity records, not adapter LUIDs. Identical records are deduplicated rather than summed.
- Live occupancy uses llama.cpp's aggregate heap reading, not per-heap DXGI residency. Missing/invalid fresh readings are logged and preserve the existing `launch_budget` fallback contract; they are not interpreted as zero usage.
- Real load evidence covers this Windows AMD machine and driver `32.0.31041.1004`. Other drivers, smaller reservation settings, multi-GPU configurations, and sustained full-context workloads need additional hardware coverage.
- No Linux/macOS reservation behavior, context-window policy, or memory allocation settings are changed.

prs.title: chore(catalog): holographic 0.15.0 — who stands behind a fact; optional search by meaning; disclosure updated
prs.body:
Bumps the pinned `sha`, `version` and `docs_url` of `plugin-catalog/holographic.yaml` to
[0.15.0](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic/tree/v0.15.0). No change to the manifest
shape, capabilities, tier, maintainer or `requires_env`.

**The disclosure changes**, because 0.14.x adds an optional online feature: search by meaning through an
OpenAI-compatible embeddings API the user names. It is **off by default**; off, the plugin makes no network call and
behaves as 0.13.0 did (search scores and recall pinned by a golden test). The description now says "no API key,
network or model calls unless the optional search by meaning is switched on", and the disclosure spells out what
leaves the machine when it is on:

- the text of facts, and of messages and `fact_store search` queries that are not greetings, to the `embedding_url`
  the user configures (https; plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address or a local host name),
  with the key read from the environment variable the user names (`embedding_key_env`; never stored in config), no
  redirects followed;
- never sent: facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by
  pattern, best effort);
- the vectors stay in the same SQLite file (table `fact_embeddings`), deleted with their fact by `forget` / `end` /
  `remove`, and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the embeddings provider
  keeps what it received under its own terms.

`known_issues`: the line on synonyms now says "unless the optional online search by meaning is on".

**What 0.14.0 does** ([changelog](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic/blob/v0.14.1/CHANGELOG.md),
[README section](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic/blob/v0.14.1/README.md#search-by-meaning-optional-online)):
words keep the recall; meaning reorders the facts that share words with the message and may add one fact per turn
that stands far out from the rest of the store and mentions whoever the message names, marked `(by meaning)`. Fact
vectors are made after the turn on the memory manager's background worker, never inside a write; every failure falls
back to words. A separate module (`embeddings.py`), no new dependency (stdlib HTTP client; numpy as for HRR). On a
synthetic set of 100 facts in five languages, paraphrases recalled before the turn went from 22 of 67 to 54
(text-embedding-3-small) and 59 (gemini-embedding-001); chit-chat recalled nothing. Design after
itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic#3; three independent reviews (Codex CLI) before release, every finding fixed.

0.14.1 fixes one thing found while turning it on for a real store: fact vectors were held to the per-message
timeout (3 s) and a batch of 32 facts could miss it; they now share the 8-second after-turn budget. It also records
numbers measured on that store (58 facts with keywords: meaning added one recall in the hardest questions, nothing
wrong or noisy).

0.14.2 fixes two things a user hit moving a live Chinese store (hosted bge-m3) onto 0.14.1 (issue #3): a foreign
binary column left in `facts` by an earlier hand-rolled deployment rode `SELECT *` into tool results and broke every
`fact_store search` on JSON serialization — rows are now read without foreign binary values; and a 400 to
`embedding_dimensions` from a model that cannot shorten its vectors now names the setting. On that store: 5/10
paraphrases recalled (2/10 with the user's own patch), one fact in on meaning alone in 12 turns — the right one —
and no wrong fact by meaning. No disclosure change.

0.14.3 is the result of three full reviews of the plugin (Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI and a Claude agent), each
finding reproduced and covered by a test (28 new tests fail on 0.14.2; 833 pass). Data: a resumed fact's corrected
start could make two versions hold at once; forget could leave a vector, and the vector index kept forgotten text in
memory; a semantic score could stick to text another writer changed meanwhile; an alias set before any fact was
wiped by unrelated rewrites. Security: quoted instructions, Unicode tag/format/control characters and an unscreened
display name (`recall_source: short`) could reach the prompt; a JSON-quoted credential name and a PEM private key
passed the secret screen; the screen itself was quadratic under the provider lock (now linear, and only what is sent
is screened); an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal counted as local on Python ≤ 3.12; a key pasted into `embedding_key_env`
was echoed. Stalled embedding requests no longer pile up threads. No disclosure change: what is sent and when is the
same, with less of it.

0.14.4 changes one rule, from numbers the same user measured on their store (issue #3): an explicit
`fact_store search` used meaning only to fill free places, so when the word matches filled `limit` the fact asked
for was never offered — in three of his five misses it was the store's closest fact in meaning. Now, of the 3 facts
closest in meaning, those closer than the best word match by more than 0.06 of cosine, at least 1 standard
deviation above the mean and mentioning whoever the query names follow the word matches, marked
`"match": "meaning"`. Recall before a turn is unchanged. Measured on a family store: questions sharing no word with
their fact but a name 13 → 18 of 27, none at all 3 → 6 of 12, with the same 1 of 30 on questions that must find
nothing (taking the top 3 by rank alone answered 20 of those 30). No disclosure change: nothing new is sent — the
query's vector is the one search already made.

0.14.5: a token whose shape alone says what it is — an API key prefix, a Telegram bot token, a JWT, a private
key — is now refused as a fact, left out of recall and never sent (before, only search by meaning screened most of
them, and bot tokens and JWTs not at all); 56 borrowed words meet across Latin and Cyrillic (`бэкап` / `backup`) by
exact form. No disclosure change: less leaves the machine, nothing new does.

0.14.6 applies a full review of 0.14.5 (Antigravity CLI): a bot token inside a Bot API address and a temporary
AWS key (`ASIA…`) are screened too; a token count ("max tokens is 8192") is no longer taken for a credential;
borrowed words no longer meet look-alikes in other languages (French `chat`, German `über`). No disclosure
change.

0.15.0 records who stands behind a fact: `said` (the person said it), `confirmed` (the agent's conclusion, the
person agreed) or `inferred` (the agent's own conclusion), with a starting trust by origin and an `(inferred)`
mark in recall; `fact_feedback confirmed` records a person's confirmation (once per fact per session, trust
+0.05 once per person). Measured on 40 conflicting pairs: the fact the person said came first in 40 of 40, against
17 without origins. **Disclosure change:** each version also keeps its origin, and each confirmation its time,
session id and the confirming person's id (no text); `forget` deletes them. Reviewed before release by
Antigravity CLI (4 bugs, 5 risks fixed).

Also in 0.14.0: the system-prompt block no longer carries a live fact count ("Active: N facts"), which changed with
every stored fact and broke longest-prefix prompt caching at each new session.

Tests: 916 pass (Linux, macOS, Windows CI against hermes-agent `main`; also run against v0.22.0).

prs.title: feat(skills): add Meshy 3D generation and printing as upstream-maintained optional skills
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds [Meshy](https://www.meshy.ai) to the optional-skills catalog as two **upstream-maintained catalog stubs**, following the archify / impeccable / brag pattern:

- **`meshy-3d-generation`**: text or image to 3D, retexturing, remeshing and LODs, conversion and resizing, UV unwrapping, rigging, animation (Meshy's preset library or a generated motion) and reference images.
- **`meshy-3d-printing`**: print files at the intended size, printability analysis and repair, multicolour 3MF, splitting a model into printable parts, Creative Lab products and slicer handoff. Preparing an existing OBJ or opening an STL/3MF runs locally with no account.

Each stub's `metadata.hermes.upstream` points at the skill directory in [meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent](https://github.com/meshy-dev/meshy-3d-agent) (`skills/meshy-3d-generation`, `skills/meshy-3d-printing`), so `hermes skills install official/creative/<name>` pulls the live tree through `OptionalSkillSource`, quarantined and scanned like any hub install. Nothing executable is vendored.

Both skills drive the official `meshy` CLI ([`meshy-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/meshy-cli) on npm, Node 22.12+) through the terminal and make no HTTP calls of their own. Sign-in is the CLI's browser device flow; an existing `MESHY_API_KEY` is honoured. They sit in `optional-skills/` because they integrate a paid service (Meshy credits), which the Contributing Guide places there. I'm on the Meshy team and maintain the upstream skills.

**Why stubs instead of the vendored skill this PR first proposed:** the upstream skills pin an exact CLI version and are released with it, so a vendored copy would need a PR here for every CLI release. The stubs track upstream instead.

None. This is a new skill.
