prs.title: feat(slack): stream outbound replies while they are generated
prs.body:
# feat(slack): stream outbound replies while they are generated

**Branch:** `feat/slack-outbound-streaming`
**Commit subject:** `feat(slack): stream outbound replies while they are generated`
**Commits:** 2. First: 12 files changed, 2044 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-). Second: 4 files changed, 264 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-).
**Risk tier:** high per `AGENTS.md` section 5 (config schema). The behavior itself is opt-in and default-off. The vtable slots implemented here already existed, so no interface changes.

## What changed

Slack was the only streaming-capable channel without an outbound stream sink. `Channel.VTable.sendEvent` with its `.chunk` / `.final` `OutboundStage`, and `supportsStreamingOutbound`, already existed in `src/channels/root.zig`, and Telegram already implemented both, but the Slack vtable registered neither. A Slack reply therefore appeared only once the model had finished, and an operator watching a long turn had no way to tell "still generating" from "stuck".

This change adds a per-account `streaming` key, implements the two vtable hooks on `SlackChannel`, and puts the turn-level state machine in a new transport-free module so it can be tested without HTTP.

### Files changed

| File | Change | +/- |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/slack_stream_presenter.zig` | New. Transport-free logic for one streaming turn: transport selection, target parsing, the coalescing window, the late-chunk grace window, the four request bodies, failure classification, and length splitting. 28 tests. | +767 / -0 |
| `src/channels/slack.zig` | `streaming_enabled`, `native_stream_disabled`, `stream_states` and the mutex that guards them; `sendEvent` / `supportsStreamingOutbound`; the native and fallback transports; `streamFinal` reconciliation; `callSlackApi`; `appendPostMessageBody` takes `thread_ts` explicitly. 17 tests. | +733 / -3 |
| `src/config_types.zig` | `streaming: bool = false` on `SlackConfig`, with a doc comment naming the feature gate and the fallback. | +5 / -0 |
| `src/config.zig` | Four tests: the key defaults to false when absent, parses true when present, and appears in the saved config for both values. | +68 / -0 |
| `docs/en/configuration.md` | New `### Slack` section (the page had none) with the parameter list, `#### Slack streaming replies`, `#### Live reasoning in drafts`, the required Slack app settings, verification commands, and common issues. | +107 / -0 |
| `docs/zh/configuration.md` | The same section in Chinese, kept in sync with the English page. | +83 / -0 |
| `src/daemon.zig` | `channelShowsLiveReasoning`; `makeStreamingSinkForChannel` gains a `stream_reasoning` argument and builds the tag filter with the matching think mode; `processInboundMessage` decides it from the outbound channel and the session. 3 tests. | +59 / -5 |
| `src/streaming.zig` | `ThinkMode` (`strip` / `passthrough`), `TagFilter.initWithThinkMode`, and the `inside_think` filter state that forwards a reasoning body verbatim while still stripping tool-call markup. 5 tests. | +103 / -2 |
| `src/providers/helpers.zig` | `quoteThinkBlocks` renders `<think>` blocks as `>`-quoted lines for live drafts; the delivered reply still goes through `stripThinkBlocks`. 4 tests. | +77 / -0 |
| `src/channels/telegram_draft_presenter.zig` | `snapshotDraftText` uses `quoteThinkBlocks` instead of `stripThinkBlocks`. 2 tests. | +30 / -4 |
| `src/session.zig` | `SessionManager.streamsReasoning(session_key)`, a read-only query used to decide whether a draft may render reasoning. | +11 / -0 |
| `src/providers/root.zig` | Re-export `quoteThinkBlocks`. | +1 / -0 |

Two consequences of wiring that sink are worth calling out:

- The draft-side reasoning plumbing: `ThinkMode` in `src/streaming.zig`, `quoteThinkBlocks` in `src/providers/helpers.zig`, the daemon's channel gate, the `streamsReasoning` query, and the Telegram draft presenter. When a session streams reasoning (`/reasoning stream`) and the outbound channel renders it, the thinking is forwarded to the draft and rendered as a quote above the in-progress answer. The delivered reply is unchanged, because the provider still strips think blocks from the final content and `.off` / `.on` previews stay stripped as before. The Notes section below records two gaps in this half.
- A Slack turn that streamed reasoning rewrites the stopped message in place instead of posting the reply a second time, because that turn's draft contains text the final reply omits.

## Why it changed

The outbound staging the daemon needs already existed; only the channel side was missing. Filling it in for Slack is the smallest change that removes the last channel where a reply is delivered in one lump, and it reuses the interface every other streaming channel already goes through instead of adding a Slack-specific path in the agent loop.

Slack's own constraints are why one transport is not enough, and why the implementation carries an account-level degradation flag rather than a single happy path:

- `chat.startStream` is only accepted inside a thread, so a top-level reply can never use the native methods.
- The native methods are gated behind the app's Agents & AI Apps feature, which requires a paid plan, and behind the assistant scope Slack adds when an app is declared as an agent. An app without them cannot stream at all.
- The streaming methods are tiered per minute, so a naive implementation that forwards every model token as one API call would hit the rate limit and break replies that used to work.

## The two outbound paths

`vtableSendEvent` receives `.chunk` events while the model generates and one `.final` event with the authoritative reply. The transport is chosen once per turn and stored on the turn's `StreamState`:

| Reply target | Transport |
| --- | --- |
| Threaded target: `reply_to_mode = all`, an inbound thread reply, or an assistant thread | `chat.startStream` with the first snapshot, throttled `chat.appendStream` deltas, then `chat.stopStream` |
| Top-level target | `chat.postMessage` with the first snapshot, then throttled `chat.update` edits of that same message |
| Any target, once the account has hit a permanent native error | `chat.postMessage` plus `chat.update` |
| Any target, when a native call fails mid-turn | The turn stays on the native transport so the stream can still be closed with `chat.stopStream`; live updates stop and the final reply reconciles the message |

**Native path.** The first flush splits at the `markdown_text` cap and sends it through `chat.startStream`, which returns the streaming message `ts`. Later flushes send only the unsent suffix through `chat.appendStream`, computed from the last snapshot handed to the transport. On `.final`, `pendingFinalSuffix` checks whether the streamed snapshot is a prefix of the final reply. When it is, the remainder is appended and `chat.stopStream` closes the message, so the user sees one message and no duplicate. When it is not, the stream is closed and the reply is delivered separately, because the streamed message holds an intermediate prefix the model later abandoned (text emitted before a tool call, or a reply rewritten by redaction rehydration after the last delta). The one exception is a turn that rendered reasoning: that snapshot can never be a prefix of the final reply, so the stopped message is rewritten in place with `chat.update` instead of leaving the thinking behind and posting the reply a second time.

**Fallback path.** One `chat.postMessage` carries the first snapshot and returns its `ts`; every later flush edits that message with `chat.update`. On `.final`, the reply is split at the `chat.update` cap, the first slice replaces the message, and up to eight overflow slices are posted as follow-ups in the same thread with a warning logged if more are dropped.

`chat.stopStream` is sent with the channel and `ts` only. The content was already delivered through start and append, so passing `markdown_text` there would append it twice.

## Throttling

Slack's streaming Web API methods are tiered per minute, so a token stream must be coalesced before it becomes HTTP calls. The tier table is recorded next to the constants: `chat.startStream` and `chat.stopStream` at Tier 2 (20+ per minute), `chat.appendStream` at Tier 4 (100+ per minute), `chat.update` at Tier 3 (50+ per minute), and `chat.postMessage` at roughly one message per second per channel.

`appendStreamChunk` accumulates deltas in the turn buffer and emits a flush when either condition holds:

- the unsent buffer has reached `STREAM_FLUSH_MIN_DELTA_BYTES` (128 bytes), or
- `STREAM_FLUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (one second) has elapsed since the previous flush.

For a normal token stream every delta is far below 128 bytes, so the interval is the pace that applies and a turn costs about one API call per second, which keeps `chat.appendStream` and `chat.update` inside their tiers. The byte threshold exists so a burst that arrives between two ticks is not held back for the rest of the second. The window opens on the first delta rather than on the first flush, so a short reply that completes inside one second never opens a stream at all and never pays the Tier 2 start/stop pair. Whitespace-only snapshots are not sent.

Two further guards keep the call count bounded in a long-running bot. A finalized target keeps ignoring `.chunk` events for `STREAM_LATE_CHUNK_GRACE_MS` (five seconds), because the daemon publishes the final reply on the durable outbox worker while the outbound dispatcher may still be draining deltas of the same turn; without it those leftovers would open a second stream for a turn that already ended. Above `STREAM_MAX_TRACKED_TARGETS` (64) tracked targets, the channel sweeps finalized entries that are past the grace window, so a bot does not accumulate one entry per thread it has ever answered in.

`stream_mu` covers both the state map and the API calls made from it, since chunks arrive on the outbound dispatcher thread while the final reply may arrive on the outbox worker.

## Permanent errors degrade the account

`classifyStreamFailure` maps the Slack `error` string to a retry policy:

- **Permanent** (`disable_native`): `channel_type_not_supported`, `method_not_supported_for_channel_type`, `unknown_method`, `not_allowed`, `invalid_thread_ts`, `restricted_action_thread_only_channel`, `restricted_action_non_threadable_channel`, `restricted_action_thread_locked`, `missing_scope`, `not_allowed_token_type`, `no_permission`, `restricted_action`, `invalid_arguments`, `missing_recipient_user_id`, `missing_recipient_team_id`. These mean this app, workspace, or channel can never stream natively, so the account sets `native_stream_disabled` once and every later turn selects the fallback transport directly through `chooseTurnTransport`. The warning is logged once per account, not once per turn.
- **Transient** (everything else, including `ratelimited`, `internal_error`, `service_unavailable`, and `message_not_in_streaming_state`): the current turn abandons the native path and the API is retried on a later turn. Unknown codes are treated as transient, so a Slack error that did not exist when this was written can never permanently disable streaming for an account.

A rejection of the start call switches the current turn to the fallback transport. A failure of a later append or update sets `send_failed` for that turn, which stops live updates and leaves the final reply to reconcile the message. If the first `chat.postMessage` of a fallback turn fails, the same flag applies and the reply is sent complete through the existing `vtableSend` path. In every failure case the user still receives the reply; the only difference is whether it arrives progressively.

## Configuration

New key, `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.streaming`, default `false`:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "slack": {
      "accounts": {
        "<alias>": {
          "bot_token": "YOUR_BOT_TOKEN",
          "app_token": "YOUR_APP_TOKEN",
          "reply_to_mode": "all",
          "streaming": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The key is documented in `docs/en/configuration.md` and in `docs/zh/configuration.md`. Both pages state the app-side requirements for the native path: enable **Agents & AI Apps** under *Features* (the gate for `chat.startStream`, and a paid-plan feature), keep `chat:write` for outbound replies and `assistant:write` for the assistant scope, reinstall the app after changing scopes, and set `reply_to_mode` to `all` if replies in channels should stream, since Slack only streams inside a thread.

## Backward compatibility

- The key defaults to `false`. A configuration that does not mention it parses to `false`, and the saved configuration writes the effective value.
- With streaming off, `supportsStreamingOutbound` returns `false`, so the daemon never routes Slack through the outbound staging, and `sendEvent` forwards `.final` to the existing `vtableSend` while ignoring `.chunk`. Delivery is byte-for-byte what it is today.
- `appendPostMessageBody` now takes `thread_ts` as an argument instead of reading the mutable `self.thread_ts` field that `parseTarget` rewrites. The existing call site passes the same value the function read before, so the payload is unchanged.
- No state is persisted. Stream state lives in the channel instance, is released per turn by `finishTurn`, and is freed on `stop`.
- No new command, flag, or migration, and no change to the config file layout.

## Rollback

Set `streaming` to `false` (or remove the key) and restart the channel; replies go back to being delivered complete. `git revert <this-commit-sha>` also works, and no data migration or cleanup is needed because nothing is persisted.

## Security

- No new credentials. The streaming methods authenticate with the bot token the account already has, through the existing `Authorization: Bearer` header built in a fixed stack buffer.
- No new scope is required for the fallback path: `chat.postMessage` and `chat.update` are covered by `chat:write`, which outbound replies already need. The native methods are the same scope but are additionally gated on the app's Agents & AI Apps feature and the assistant scope, as both doc pages state. Enabling `streaming` without that entitlement cannot break replies, because the first `chat.startStream` is rejected and the account degrades to edited messages.
- No new endpoints. Requests go through the existing `root.http_util.curlPost` to the existing Slack Web API base over HTTPS.
- No new inbound surface. The change adds no webhook, listener, or event parser.
- No new file, filesystem, or subprocess access.
- No secrets in logs. Failure paths log the Slack error code, the endpoint name, and the Zig error name only; message bodies and tokens are not logged. The token never leaves the auth header.
- Under `builtin.is_test`, `sendMessage` returns before building a request and `callSlackApi` returns a canned `ts`, so the suite opens no sockets. Both guards carry a comment, per the `builtin.is_test` side-effect rule in `AGENTS.md` section 3.4.
- Tests and docs use synthetic values (`xoxb-test`, `xoxb-YOUR_BOT_TOKEN`, and example channel and user ids), not real credentials or workspace identifiers.

## Validation

Required checks for a code change, both run in CI on the pinned Zig 0.16.0 toolchain:

- `zig build test --summary all` (the `pre-push` hook in `.githooks`; must report 0 failures and 0 leaks)
- `zig fmt --check src/` (the `pre-commit` hook in `.githooks`)

No Zig toolchain was available in the environment where this description was written, so neither command was run here and no pass counts are claimed. Both must be confirmed by CI before merge. The commit message records an author-side container run; that result is not reproduced here.

Test coverage added by this change (63 test blocks):

| File | Tests | What they exercise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/slack_stream_presenter.zig` | 28 | Transport selection across the four target/state combinations; target parsing for a threaded, bare, empty-thread, and DM-style target; the coalescing window (buffered inside it, interval flush, byte-threshold flush, unsent-suffix delta); the late-chunk grace window and the fresh turn after it; prefix versus divergent finals; all four request bodies including JSON escaping and the stop body carrying no text; permanent versus transient classification; length splitting at newline boundaries and without cutting a multibyte character |
| `src/channels/slack.zig` | 17 | The vtable hooks and the full state machine, driven with `callSlackApi` stubbed: native start for a thread target, native kept across chunks, fallback for a top-level target, fallback after the account is degraded, prefix final, divergent final, in-place rewrite after streamed reasoning, late deltas dropped, streaming disabled, empty chunk, short reply inside the window, overflow splitting, and `stop` releasing buffers |
| `src/streaming.zig` | 5 | Strips think blocks by default, forwards them in passthrough mode, survives a tag split across chunks, keeps angle brackets inside reasoning, and still strips tool-call markup in passthrough mode |
| `src/providers/helpers.zig` | 4 | Quote rendering that keeps the answer, plain text untouched, an unterminated block, and a stray close tag |
| `src/config.zig` | 4 | The key defaults to false when absent, parses true when present, and appears in the saved configuration for both values |
| `src/daemon.zig` | 3 | The sink keeps reasoning only when the session streams it, strips it by default, and the channel gate enables only Telegram and Slack |
| `src/channels/telegram_draft_presenter.zig` | 2 | Streamed reasoning renders as a quote, and a draft without reasoning is unchanged |

The new Slack section in both doc pages also carries manual verification steps (`nullclaw channel start slack`, `nullclaw channel status`). Those require a live Slack app and were not run in the environment where this description was written.

## Notes

- Two commits. The first adds the Slack outbound stream and the shared draft-side plumbing for streamed reasoning, which belong together because both are served by the one outbound sink this PR adds: the same `.chunk` events feed the Slack stream and the draft renderers. The second fixes that plumbing on the channels with their own message loop and is a hard dependency of the first. Happy to narrow the scope however maintainers prefer.
- The second commit fixes the channels that are served by their own message loop. Telegram is served by `channel_loop.processTelegramMessage` rather than `daemon.processInboundMessage`, so the passthrough selection the daemon performs never ran for it and its drafts were always stripped; the draft think mode is now resolved from the outbound channel and the session, the same way the daemon already does it. That commit also teaches `TagFilter` the provider's text tool markup, which otherwise reaches drafts and delivered replies verbatim. It is in this branch rather than a PR of its own because it cannot compile without the first commit: the `ThinkMode` and `initWithThinkMode` symbols it consumes, and the daemon-side channel gate, are introduced here.
- Reasoning in a draft is presentation-only. The finalized message is still produced by `stripThinkBlocks`, so thinking never reaches a delivered reply in any mode.
- The native path needs the app's Agents & AI Apps feature, which requires a paid plan. On a workspace without it, `streaming = true` is harmless: the first start call is rejected, the warning is logged once per account, and replies use edited messages.
- Behavior worth knowing when reviewing the native path: a final reply that diverges from the streamed text is posted as its own message, so that turn produces two messages. This is deliberate, because the streamed message holds an intermediate prefix that the model abandoned, and the reply has to be complete. The one exception is a turn that rendered reasoning, which is rewritten in place.

prs.title: feat(providers): support native tool calls while streaming
prs.body:
# feat(providers): support native tool calls while streaming

**Branch:** `feat/streaming-native-tool-calls`
**Commit subject:** `feat(providers): support native tool calls while streaming`
**Diffstat:** 6 files changed, 790 insertions(+), 92 deletions(-)
**Risk tier:** high per `AGENTS.md` section 5 (vtable interface change). The runtime effect is opt-in and default-off.

## Summary

### What changed

OpenAI-compatible streaming requests now carry `tools` / `tool_choice` when the provider serving the turn can emit native tool calls, and the SSE parser reassembles `delta.tool_calls` fragments per index into complete tool calls. Streaming results expose them in `StreamChatResult.tool_calls`, so the agent loop executes them exactly like the non-streaming path: history receives the assistant `tool_calls` message plus the tool results, instead of the provider markup being rendered as plain text.

| File | Change | +/− |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/providers/root.zig` | `StreamChatResult.tool_calls`; new `supports_streaming_native_tools` vtable slot defaulting to false; `emitChatResponseAsStream` hands tool calls to the caller | +34 / -1 |
| `src/providers/sse.zig` | `DeltaToolCall`, `ToolCallAccumulator`, `extractDeltaToolCalls`; `SseLineResult` becomes a struct | +385 / -85 |
| `src/providers/compatible.zig` | advertise the capability when `native_tools` is on and streaming is not disabled | +50 / -0 |
| `src/providers/reliable.zig` | forward the capability through a failover chain to the provider that actually serves the request | +121 / -0 |
| `src/providers/router.zig` | forward the capability through a router to the resolved provider | +41 / -0 |
| `src/agent/root.zig` | keep native tools enabled on streaming turns for capable providers and forward accumulated tool calls into the turn loop | +159 / -6 |

### File by file

**`src/providers/root.zig`**

- `StreamChatResult` gains `tool_calls: []const ToolCall = &.{}`, owned by the caller and freed the same way as `ChatResponse.tool_calls`. Empty when the provider did not stream tool calls.
- New optional vtable slot `supports_streaming_native_tools: ?*const fn (ptr: *anyopaque, model: []const u8) bool = null` plus the accessor `Provider.supportsStreamingNativeTools(model)`. The default is `false`, so every provider that does not opt in keeps the text tool protocol on streaming turns. The query takes the model because the answer can differ per model behind a wrapper.
- `emitChatResponseAsStream` now detaches `response.tool_calls` into the returned result instead of freeing them. Providers that fall back to a blocking `chat` mid-stream (large prompt, curl failure, responses API) must still surface native tool calls to the agent loop, so the calls are handed to the caller rather than dropped. The existing ownership test is extended to cover the transfer and asserts the result carries the call.

**`src/providers/sse.zig`**

- `DeltaToolCall` models one streaming fragment: a required `index` and optional `id` / `name` / `arguments`, because providers split those fields across chunks and some repeat `id` and `name` on every fragment. `freeDeltaToolCalls` frees a fragment slice.
- `ToolCallAccumulator` merges fragments keyed by `index`, so parallel tool calls and argument strings split anywhere in the stream both reassemble. `id` and `name` are recorded on first sight and later repeats are ignored; `arguments` fragments are always concatenated. `toOwnedSlice` transfers ownership of the finished calls field-by-field and leaves the accumulator empty but still deinitializable.
- `extractDeltaToolCalls` walks `choices[0].delta.tool_calls`. It guards on a `"tool_calls"` substring before paying for a JSON parse, falls back to the array position when a gateway omits `index`, and returns an empty slice rather than an error when the payload does not parse or does not have the expected shape.
- `SseLineResult` changes from a `union(enum)` (`delta` / `done` / `usage` / `skip`) to a struct with optional fields, a `deinit`, and an `isSkip` helper. A single chunk can carry content and tool-call fragments and usage together, which a union cannot express; some gateways do interleave a text delta with the first tool-call fragment.
- `curlStream` accumulates fragments into a `ToolCallAccumulator` and passes `tool_acc.toOwnedSlice(allocator)` into every `finalizeStreamResult` return path, including the partial-stream recovery paths that return accumulated output after a curl failure. `finalizeStreamResult` takes the tool calls as a parameter.
- `curlStreamAnthropic` passes an empty slice. Anthropic streaming is deliberately untouched and keeps the text tool protocol.

**`src/providers/compatible.zig`**

- `supportsStreamingNativeToolsImpl` returns `self.native_tools and supportsStreamingImpl(ptr)`: true when native tools are on and streaming is neither disabled nor routed to the responses API. Registered in the vtable.
- Note that `buildStreamingChatRequestBody` already serialized `tools` and `tool_choice` when `req.tools` was non-null. The missing piece was upstream: the agent passed `.tools = null` on streaming turns. The added request-body tests pin both directions of that plumbing.

**`src/providers/reliable.zig`**

- `supportsStreamingNativeToolsImpl` mirrors `supportsVisionForModelImpl`: an explicit `provider/model` ref is answered by the provider that will actually serve it. Without an explicit ref it returns true when the inner provider or any extra is capable. Wrapping a capable provider in a failover chain no longer hides the capability.

**`src/providers/router.zig`**

- The router resolves the model the same way `streamChatImpl` does and reports the capability of the provider that will serve the stream, so an alias routed to a capable provider is not reported as incapable.

**`src/agent/root.zig`**

- Both capability call sites now branch: on a streaming turn the agent asks `supportsStreamingNativeTools(turn_model_name)`, otherwise it keeps `supportsNativeTools()`. The same change is applied to the system-prompt path that decides whether tool specs are described in text.
- The streaming request sets `.tools = if (native_tools_enabled) turn_tool_specs else null`, on both the primary request and the retry request.
- The streaming branch builds its `ChatResponse` with `.tool_calls = stream_result.tool_calls` instead of `&.{}`. That single line is what makes the turn loop execute the calls and record the assistant `tool_calls` message plus the tool results in history.

### Why it changed

**User-visible bug.** With a streaming channel or alias, a model that supports native tools silently fell back to a text tool protocol, so tool-call markup could leak into the reply as literal text.

The cause was two-sided. The agent computed `native_tools_enabled = !is_streaming and self.provider.supportsNativeTools()` and passed `.tools = null` on every streaming request, so the streaming request never carried tool specs. There was also no way for a provider to say "I can emit native tool calls while streaming", so the agent had no correct condition to use even if it had wanted to send them. The result was that a provider which streams OpenAI-style `delta.tool_calls` had those calls displayed to the user as text and never executed, while the identical turn on the blocking path worked correctly.

This patch adds the missing capability query, asks the provider that will actually serve the model, sends the specs when it answers yes, reassembles the streamed fragments, and feeds the result into the same execution path the blocking case already uses.

## Validation

**I did not run the build or the test suite.** The environment where this patch was prepared has no Zig toolchain, so there is no local result to report and none is claimed. The validation signal for this change is CI plus the maintainer's own run, not the author's.

Checks to run, in the order the repository's own hooks run them:

```sh
zig version                          # must print 0.16.0 (upstream pin)
zig fmt --check src/                 # .githooks/pre-commit
zig build test --summary all         # .githooks/pre-push; expect 0 failures, 0 leaks
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall    # size check, see below
```

The `ReleaseSmall` build is worth running because `AGENTS.md` treats binary size as a hard product constraint (target under 1 MB). This patch adds a JSON walk plus an accumulator to the streaming path, so confirming the target still holds is part of validating the change rather than an optional extra.

Tests added by the patch (12 new test blocks plus one extended), all deterministic and network-free:

- `src/providers/sse.zig`: content-only chunks yield no fragments; a single fragment is extracted with `id`, `name`, and partial `arguments`; content and tool calls in the same chunk both survive; two parallel calls with argument strings split across chunks reassemble to the exact expected JSON; argument-only fragments stay keyed by index and produce empty `id` / `name`.
- `src/providers/compatible.zig`: the streaming body carries `"tools":` and `"tool_choice":"auto"` alongside `"stream":true`; the body omits both keys when no specs are supplied; the capability follows `native_tools` and `disable_streaming`.
- `src/providers/reliable.zig`: delegation to a capable inner, and resolution through an explicit prefix where the prefix wins over a capable primary.
- `src/providers/router.zig`: the capability follows the resolved provider, so an explicit ref to a capable provider reports true and a bare model resolving to an incapable default reports false.
- `src/agent/root.zig`: an end-to-end streaming turn. A two-turn streaming provider asserts that tools were advertised on both streaming requests, that the returned tool call was executed, that the final response text is correct, that the streamed text order is preserved, and that the observer recorded at least one tool call.

## Notes

### Review focus: memory ownership

The main correctness risk is ownership of tool calls, which now move `ChatResponse` -> `StreamChatResult` -> `ChatResponse`. The patch transfers rather than copies and clears the source in both places (`response.tool_calls = &.{}` in `emitChatResponseAsStream`, and `entry.id` / `entry.name` nulled in `ToolCallAccumulator.toOwnedSlice`), with callers freeing field-by-field. `AGENTS.md` requires zero leaks under the leak-detecting test allocator, so a leak or double free introduced here would surface in `zig build test`, but the transfer is the part of the diff worth reading closely.

### Scope

The commit subject says `providers`, and the patch also changes `src/agent/root.zig`. The agent change is the consumer side: without it the capability would be advertised and never used, and the bug would remain. Happy to split it into a providers-only PR plus an agent follow-up if you prefer a narrower first step.

### Naming

The vtable field is `supports_streaming_native_tools` (snake_case) to match the adjacent `supports_streaming` and `supports_vision` fields in the same vtable, while the accessor and implementations use camelCase (`supportsStreamingNativeTools`). `AGENTS.md` prefers camelCase for new vtable fields and notes the existing snake_case family, so this follows the local family. Flagging it so a reviewer can ask for the camelCase variant if that is preferred.

### Source-level API change

`SseLineResult` in `src/providers/sse.zig` is no longer a `union(enum)`. All in-tree call sites are updated in this patch. Any out-of-tree code that switches on `.delta` / `.done` / `.usage` / `.skip` needs the struct-field form plus `deinit`. The reason for the change is that one SSE chunk can carry content, tool-call fragments, and usage together, which the union could not represent.

### Config surface

No new config keys, CLI flags, or environment variables. The existing per-provider `native_tools` field now also gates the streaming path, which is a behavior change for users rather than a new surface:

- With `native_tools` on (the compatible-provider default) and streaming enabled, a streaming reply can now execute tool calls instead of showing markup as text. That is the point of the patch, and it is visible to anyone using a streaming channel or alias.
- Providers that do not implement the new vtable slot are unaffected and keep the text tool protocol while streaming.

### Rollback

`git revert <sha>` reverts the whole change. Two operational escape hatches avoid a revert entirely: set `native_tools = false` on the provider entry to force the previous text tool protocol, or set `disable_streaming = true` to force the blocking path, which already used native tools before this patch.

### Security impact

- **New permissions or capabilities:** No new permission surface. The streaming path now advertises the same tool specs the blocking path already advertises for the same turn, and tool execution still goes through the existing dispatcher and policy layer. The capability is default-off for every provider that does not opt in.
- **New external network calls:** No.
- **Secrets and credentials:** No change. The new parse path does not log payloads.
- **Untrusted input:** `extractDeltaToolCalls` parses provider-controlled JSON from the stream. It is defensive: a substring guard skips the parse on the common non-tool path, a parse failure returns an empty slice instead of propagating an error, and unexpected JSON shapes return empty. Tool arguments are model-controlled and remain untrusted; they reach the same dispatcher and validation as the blocking path, which is not weakened by this change.
- **Prompt injection:** No new model-visible text is introduced. The tool specs sent on streaming turns are the same specs already sent on blocking turns.
- **PII in the diff:** None. Test fixtures use neutral placeholders and generic provider aliases.

### Docs

`CONTRIBUTING.md` requires docs updated in the same PR for user-facing behavior changes, so this is called out explicitly rather than left implicit.

I checked the docs tree against `main`: no page documents the OpenAI-compatible fallback to a text tool protocol (`native_tools`, `text tool`, and `<tool_call>` produce no hits under `docs/en/` or `docs/zh/`), so no existing sentence is contradicted by this change and none is left stale. The one nearby sentence in `docs/en/configuration.md` and its `docs/zh/configuration.md` counterpart that mentions native tool calls on non-streaming requests is scoped to the native Anthropic provider, and Anthropic streaming is deliberately untouched here, so it stays accurate.

No docs change is included. If you want the new behavior documented, the natural home is the provider section of `docs/en/configuration.md` plus the `docs/zh` mirror, and I can add it to this PR.

### Formatting

Two hunks introduce consecutive blank lines (`src/agent/root.zig` before `test "slash /new clears history"`, and `src/providers/reliable.zig` before `test "multi-provider fallback: primary fails, extra succeeds"`). If `zig fmt` normalizes runs of blank lines, the `pre-commit` hook (`zig fmt --check src/`) will fail. I could not check this without a Zig toolchain, so run `zig fmt src/` before pushing.

## PR checklist

- [x] Scope is focused and does not mix unrelated refactors
- [x] Commands, config keys, and examples match the current codebase
- [ ] Docs are updated for any user-facing behavior change (see the Docs note: no contradicting page found, no docs change included, offer to add one)
- [ ] Validation was run and results are included in the PR description (not run locally, no Zig toolchain; CI runs `zig build test --summary all` on this head)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or personal data were added
- [x] New code follows existing naming and module boundaries

prs.title: Preset spawn.allow: allowlist for spawn_agent targets
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds optional `agents.presets.<id>.spawn.allow` so a caller can only `spawn_agent` into listed presets (org-chart / coordinator graphs). Enforcement is in `resolve_preset` before provider work; the tool schema / description lists only allowed targets for the calling agent.

**Depends on:** [#1301](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1301) (chat ↔ sub-agent parity / patch `0002`) — **required**. This branch is stacked on that PR. Also [#1280](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1280) if that is still unmerged on the target base.

**Base pin:** `1f6d28ea750d6654d52d5899b8be67727ebf7a19` **with #1301 already applied**. Do not review against bare pin without parity — the hunks expect parity helpers and related `spawn_agent` / chat context changes.

**Compatibility (important):**

| `spawn.allow` value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Absent / `None`** | **Unrestricted** (legacy default — existing configs unchanged) |
| `Some([])` / empty list | Deny all spawn targets |
| Non-empty `Some([…])` | Allowlist only those preset ids |

RPC: `agents.preset.update` accepts `spawn_allow` (`null` clears to unrestricted); `preset.get` exposes `fields.spawn_allow`. Markdown agent defs: YAML frontmatter `spawn_allow` (CSV; empty string = deny all). Docs: `docs/src/session-tools.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-tools` — `test_resolve_preset_rejects_target_outside_spawn_allow`, `test_resolve_preset_empty_spawn_allow_rejects_all`, `test_resolve_preset_absent_spawn_allow_unrestricted`, `test_spawn_allow_bound_schema_*`, `test_execute_rejects_disallowed_preset_before_provider`
- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-config` — schema / agent_defs round-trip for `spawn_allow` (incl. empty list vs absent)
- [ ] Manual: caller with `spawn.allow = ["writer"]` → spawn `writer` ok, other preset → visible `spawn_agent denied`
- [ ] Manual: field absent → any known preset still spawnable (unrestricted)

prs.title: Chat ↔ sub-agent parity: persona, system_prompt_suffix, delegate_only, preset model
prs.body:
## Summary

Today several preset fields only affect `spawn_agent` sub-runs, not direct chat with the same agent. This makes coordinator/worker setups and “talk to the agent as itself” diverge.

This PR aligns the two paths:

1. **Sub-agent persona** — `build_sub_agent_prompt` loads the target workspace `IDENTITY.md` / `SOUL.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GUIDELINES.md` so a spawned agent gets the same written persona as direct chat.
2. **`system_prompt_suffix`** — appended in live chat turns, `raw_prompt`, and `full_context` (same Role / composite suffix content as spawn).
3. **`delegate_only`** — direct chat uses the same shared delegate toolset as spawn (`DELEGATE_ONLY_TOOLS`).
4. **Model resolve** — chat model order becomes explicit → session → **preset** → default / history, so a preset `model` is a real default when the session has none.

Docs comments on the preset schema note that suffix / `delegate_only` apply to chat and sub-agents.

**Base pin:** `1f6d28ea750d6654d52d5899b8be67727ebf7a19` (rebase onto latest `main` before merge). May also need [#1280](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1280) if that change is not already in the base (touches `spawn_agent` tool wiring). Independent of the follow-up `spawn.allow` PR.

**Compatibility:** additive for existing configs. No new required fields. Presets without suffix / `delegate_only` / `model` behave as before.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-tools` — workspace persona injection in spawn (`test_workspace_persona_injected_*`)
- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-chat` — `append_preset_system_prompt_suffix_*`, `resolve_chat_model_id_*`, `delegate_only_keeps_shared_delegate_toolset`
- [ ] Manual: agent with non-empty `system_prompt_suffix` → `chat.raw_prompt` / reply reflects it
- [ ] Manual: `delegate_only = true` → tool list matches spawn delegate set
- [ ] Manual: session without model, preset with model → chat uses preset model

issues.title: A message sent on one device is invisible on the other until the whole turn finishes

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
# A message sent on one device is invisible on the other until the whole turn finishes

## Problem

When a user message is sent — from the web console, or from a mobile app — it is only persisted to the chat history at **run end**. While the run is in flight:

- `GET /api/chats` (history) does not contain the user's own message;
- the run's SSE stream does not contain it either — the stream starts with the assistant's output.

## Reproduction

1. Have QwenPaw running with at least one agent.
2. Open the web console on device A and the mobile app on device B, logged into the same workspace (or open the console on two devices).
3. On device A, send a message that starts a long run (e.g. a coding task that takes minutes).
4. Watch device B:
   - the chat view shows no user message at all — the assistant appears to "start a turn from nowhere";
   - the message only appears on device B **after the run finishes** and device B refetches history.

Same failure mode in reverse: a message sent from the mobile app is invisible on the console until the turn completes.

## Expected

The user's own message should be visible to all connected clients **as soon as the run starts**, not after it ends — the turn should read as "user asked → assistant answering" on every screen from the first second.

## Root cause (server-side)

The console run stream only forwards provider/assistant output; the user message that triggered the run is written to the chat store when the run completes. There is no channel that carries the user message to live observers mid-run. The web console currently papers over this with a **local optimistic echo** — which only fixes the one screen that sent the message, not every other observer of the same run.

## Impact

- Multi-device setups (console + mobile app, or two consoles) experience "I sent a message and it doesn't exist on the other screen" for the full duration of the turn.
- Any API consumer of the run stream (integrations, automation, dashboards) cannot correlate a run with the request that started it until the run ends.

## Proposed direction

Emit the user's message as an out-of-band frame at the **start of each new run's stream** (shape-compatible with the existing `turn_usage` / `replay_end` out-of-band frames, which unknown-frame-tolerant clients already ignore), so that:

- the frame is produced once per run and enters the run buffer like any other frame;
- reconnect/replay of a live run includes it (a late joiner sees the user turn without waiting for run end);
- clients that render history-only are unaffected (unknown frames are ignored).

Design details, per-client handler contracts and compatibility analysis: see the companion design doc (`方案.md`) in this folder, and the in-flight server patch on `feat/harmony-app` (commit `781e7378`).

[Feature] Model pool has no delete/remove action — only enable/disable, so deprecated models can't be purged

Question or topic
The model pool / model-management UI only offers an enable/disable toggle. There is no way to permanently delete a model entry from a provider, so deprecated or broken models stay in the list forever (they can only be greyed out). Please either add a delete action, or document how to remove entries via API.

Context
QwenPaw version: 2.2.2b4
Channel: Console (web UI, default port 8088)
Skill / use case: Custom OpenAI-compatible provider backed by a local relay (base_url: http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1), with model auto-discovery enabled (discovery_strategy: openai_models, model_sync_mode: startup).
Impact: The provider returned several upstream models that were later deprecated upstream. They now fail at call time (e.g. HTTP 410 ModelDeprecated: Model mimo-v2.5-free has been deprecated). Because the UI can only disable them, they stay in the pool and there is no discoverable way to clean them up without hand-editing provider JSON.
Expected
A way to delete a model entry from a provider (a trash/remove action in the model pool or the model-management modal), so deprecated models can be permanently removed and won't be re-added by the next discovery sync.

Actual
The pool list only exposes a selection toggle (enabled/disabled). The only icon that looks like "remove" is in the model selector dropdown and actually calls updateModelPool(..., {selected: false}) — i.e. it deselects, not deletes. It is also hidden behind a "manage" button (its useState(false) flag starts as false), so most users never see it.

What I found in the source (may save maintainers time)
A real delete endpoint already exists and works: DELETE /api/models/{provider_id}/models/{model_id:path} → providers.py, remove_model_endpoint, which calls ProviderManager.delete_model_from_provider → Provider.delete_model (provider.py), adding the id to removed_model_ids and dropping it from extra_models / discovered_models.
There is simply no UI wired to it. In the console bundles (RemoteModelManageModal-*.js, index-*.js) the only model-pool mutations are updateModelPool (enable/disable) and addModel. No deleteModel call exists.
So this looks like a missing-UI gap rather than a backend limitation.

Tried so far
Read the frontend console bundles: searched for removeModel / deleteModel / updateModelPool — the "remove" control is a deselect, not a delete.
Confirmed the backend DELETE /api/models/{provider}/models/{model} route exists (providers.py, remove_model_endpoint).
Verified the running service responds normally (GET /api/models/{provider_id}/pool → 200).
Workaround: calling the DELETE API by hand, or editing working.secret/providers/custom/<id>.json — neither is discoverable from the UI.

issues.title: [Bug] qwenpaw-creator startup hook aborts: os.kill(pid, 0) raises SystemError (not caught by except OSError) when runtime-owner.json holds a stale pid
issues.body:
### Summary

QwenPaw Desktop **fails to start** when `creator-runtime/runtime-owner.json` contains a **stale pid**.
The `qwenpaw-creator` plugin's startup hook calls `os.kill(pid, 0)` as a liveness probe; on Windows this can raise
`SystemError: <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set` (underlying `OSError: [WinError 6] 句柄无效 / invalid handle`),
which is **not** caught by the existing `except OSError:` handler. The exception escapes, the whole startup hook fails,
and the Creator runtime never becomes ready. The app is unusable until the file is manually deleted.

### Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop **2.2.2-beta.4** (Windows 10 AMD64)
- Plugin `qwenpaw-creator` **2.0.1**
- Python **3.12.10** (bundled backend)

### Steps to reproduce (in the field)

1. Let the Creator runtime start successfully once — it writes `creator-runtime/runtime-owner.json`, e.g.
   `{"pid": 2924, "startedAtEpoch": 1791374773.9167662}`.
2. Shut QwenPaw down **without deleting that file** (it is never removed on shutdown).
3. Kill/exit the process whose pid is recorded (normal case after a restart).
4. Start QwenPaw again.

### Expected

QwenPaw starts; stale pid is treated as "no live peer".

### Actual

Startup hook fails, Creator runtime never reaches "ready":

```
2026-10-12 19:08:43 | ERROR | qwenpaw\app\_app.py:627 | ✗ Failed to execute startup hook
    'pawapp_qwenpaw-creator_1744292470816' from plugin 'qwenpaw-creator':
    <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set
OSError: [WinError 6] 句柄无效。

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "qwenpaw\app\_app.py", line 620, in _background_startup
  File "...\plugins\qwenpaw-creator\backend\main.py", line 175, in _startup
    services = creator_file_services(data_root)
  File "...\backend\services\project_files\facade.py", line 849, in creator_file_services
    services = CreatorFileServices.create(resolved)
  File "...\backend\services\project_files\facade.py", line 240, in create
    if _warn_on_second_backend(projects.root):
  File "...\backend\services\project_files\facade.py", line 199, in _warn_on_second_backend
    os.kill(pid, 0)
SystemError: <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set
```

The same error was observed on **2026-10-10 20:05** and twice on **2026-10-12 (19:08, 19:10)**.

### Root cause

`plugins/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/project_files/facade.py` (~line 180-215):

```python
def _warn_on_second_backend(root: Path) -> bool:
    marker = root / "runtime-owner.json"
    try:
        previous = json.loads(marker.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        pid = int(previous.get("pid") or 0)
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
        pid = 0
    peer_alive = False
    if pid and pid != os.getpid():
        try:
            os.kill(pid, 0)          # <-- raises SystemError on Windows here
        except OSError:              # <-- does NOT catch SystemError
            pass
        else:
            peer_alive = True
            logger.error("another QwenPaw Creator backend ...")
    ...
    # marker is written back only AFTER the probe
```

Two problems compound:

1. **Wrong exception type is caught.** On Windows, a failed `os.kill(pid, 0)` did not surface as a plain `OSError`
   here but as `SystemError: <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set`
   (underlying `OSError: [WinError 6] 句柄无效`). `SystemError` is not a subclass of `OSError`, so it escapes.
2. **The marker write-back sits after the probe**, so once the probe raises, the stale pid is **never refreshed** —
   the file stays frozen at the old pid and **every subsequent restart hits the same failure**.
   (In our logs the marker was frozen at a pid written 5 days earlier.)

Note on reproducibility: we could **not** deterministically reproduce it with an arbitrary nonexistent pid —
on the same machine `os.kill(999999, 0)` and `os.kill(<the stale pid>, 0)` currently return a **catchable**
`OSError(winerror=87, ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER)`. The `WinError 6` (ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE) in the field suggests the
failing call took a different path (handle/pid state at that moment). Regardless, the traceback above is the raw evidence.

### Suggested fix

```python
    peer_alive = False
    if pid and pid != os.getpid():
        try:
            os.kill(pid, 0)
        except OSError:
            pass
        except Exception:            # Windows may raise SystemError instead
            logger.debug("liveness probe for pid=%s failed", pid, exc_info=True)
        else:
            peer_alive = True
            logger.error(...)
```

Additionally recommended:

- Prefer a Windows-safe liveness check instead of `os.kill(pid, 0)`
  (e.g. `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` + `GetExitCodeProcess`, or `WaitForSingleObject`),
  because on Windows `os.kill` is not documented as a "signal 0 = probe" operation.
- Move the marker write-back so it always runs (e.g. `try/finally`), so a probe failure cannot freeze a stale pid forever.
- Do not let this *advisory* probe abort the entire plugin startup hook — it is explicitly documented as
  "Advisory (zero-lock) detection ... warns loudly instead of blocking".

### Workaround

Delete (or clear) the marker before starting; it is recreated automatically on the next successful start:

```
%USERPROFILE%\.copaw\creator-runtime\runtime-owner.json
```

### Additional notes

- The trace in `creator-runtime/observability/traces/creator-trace-*.jsonl` shows
  `creator.runtime.starting` with **no matching `creator.runtime.started`** for the failed attempts,
  and a successful `creator.runtime.started` immediately after the marker was removed.
- Happy to provide full logs.

issues.title: [Bug][Desktop] desktop.log never rotates on Windows - sidecar tee handle defeats _SafeRotatingFileHandler
issues.body:
### QwenPaw Version
2.2.2b4 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 10 AMD64, bundled Python 3.11)

### Component(s) Affected
- [x] Core / Backend
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

### Description

`<WORKING_DIR>\desktop.log` grows without bound and no `.1/.2/.3` backups are ever produced, although
`add_project_file_handler()` attaches `_SafeRotatingFileHandler` to exactly that path (defaults 5 MiB / 3 backups,
overridable via `QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_SIZE` / `QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_BACKUPS`).

Measured on one machine (16 sidecar starts between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-11):

```
<WORKING_DIR>\desktop.log   26,445,770 bytes  (102,341 lines)  <-- no rotation, no backups
<WORKING_DIR>\qwenpaw.log    1,606,648 bytes  (  8,496 lines)  <-- under 5 MiB, never triggered
files matching *.log* under WORKING_DIR: exactly those two (no desktop.log.1)
QWENPAW_LOG_LEVEL=info is injected by the app; QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_SIZE is unset -> defaults in effect
```

### Root cause (verified by minimal repro)

`src/qwenpaw/tauri/sidecar_logging.py::install_sidecar_logging()` keeps a raw file handle open for the whole process
lifetime and mirrors stdout/stderr into it:

```python
_LOG_FILE = log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", buffering=1)
sys.stdout = _TeeStream(sys.stdout, _LOG_FILE)
sys.stderr = _TeeStream(sys.stderr, _LOG_FILE)
...
_add_project_file_handler(log_path)      # -> qwenpaw/utils/logging.py
```

On Windows, `os.rename()` inside `RotatingFileHandler.doRollover()` requires DELETE access on the source file; the
long-lived tee handle does not share it, so the rename raises `PermissionError: [WinError 32]`.
`_SafeRotatingFileHandler.doRollover()` catches exactly that and reopens the stream, *deferring rotation to the next
size-exceeding emit* — i.e. it fails again and again, forever, and **silently**.

Minimal reproduction (Windows, any Python 3.11+):

```python
import logging, logging.handlers, tempfile, pathlib

d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); p = d / "x.log"; p.write_text("seed\n", encoding="utf-8")
tee = open(p, "a", encoding="utf-8", buffering=1)      # sidecar _TeeStream equivalent
h = logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler(p, maxBytes=10, backupCount=3, encoding="utf-8")
h.emit(logging.LogRecord("t", logging.INFO, __file__, 1, "x" * 60, None, None))
try:
    h.doRollover()
    print("rollover OK")
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e)
tee.close()
```

Observed:

```
[A] no extra handle (control)      -> rollover OK      files=['x.log', 'x.log.1', 'x.log.2']
[B] with persistent append handle  -> PermissionError: [WinError 32] ... 'x.log' -> 'x.log.1'
                                      files=['x.log']                      <-- NO backup created
```

### Impact

1. Unbounded disk growth in `WORKING_DIR` (26 MB in 18 days for a single-user desktop; growth scales with UI polling —
   27,000+ access-log lines in that period).
2. `desktop.log` mirrors the whole console, i.e. **full conversation content including assistant reasoning and tool
   output**. Users are routinely asked to attach this file to bug reports, so silent unbounded retention is also a
   privacy/retention concern, not just a disk one.
3. `QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_SIZE` / `QWENPAW_LOG_MAX_BACKUPS` (added in #6178 / #6183) are effectively no-ops on Windows for
   this file, and nothing warns the user that they are.

### Suggested fixes

- Rotate by **copy-and-truncate** while the file is held open (copy contents to `desktop.log.1`, then truncate in place
  with `FileShare.ReadWrite`) instead of relying on `os.rename`; or
- Don't keep a raw handle for the tee — write through the rotating handler (single writer); or
- At minimum, log a **one-time WARNING** when a rollover is deferred so the situation is not silent.

issues.title: [Bug] Agent 间调用会话被静默取消（CancelledError）：同秒成对、产物归零，且取消不记录发起方与原因
issues.body:
## 环境
| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 客户端 | QwenPaw Desktop（Windows 10 AMD64） |
| 版本 | **2.2.1**（`qwenpaw --version`） |
| 场景 | 多 agent 舰队（Orchestrator / Reasoner / Executor / Reviewer / Defender）+ 一个飞书通道入口；agent 之间通过 `ChatWithAgent` 互相调用 |
| 涉及代码位置 | `qwenpaw/hooks/error/error_hook.py:90`、`qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py:297,379`、`qwenpaw/app/routers/tool_calls.py:91`、`qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:589` |

## 现象（Actual）
1. **跨 agent 调用会话被静默取消**：日志落 `cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<A>:to:<B>:<epoch>:<hash>): CancelledError`，并伴随 `cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn` 与 `cancel-save: ... closed 1 dangling tool call(s)`。被取消的会话**没有 result、没有产物**。
2. **成对出现**：多为**同一秒**两条一起被取消（形如 `f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:*` + `f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:*`）。
3. **系统性**：本地主日志 3 天内共 **19 次**（10-12: 6 次、10-13: 7 次、10-14: 6 次）；**全部**为 `A:to:B` 跨 agent 会话，未见到单机/用户直连会话被同样取消。
4. **不可溯源**：日志**只**记录 `CancelledError`，**不记录取消的发起方与原因** ⇒ 使用者无法判断属于"框架回收 / 超时 / 上游断开 / 路由错配"中的哪一种。

### 单个实例（逐条可复核的原文形态）
| 时刻 | 日志原文（截断） |
|---|---|
| 11:52:23 | 本地派发台账行：`task_id=<任务号>, agent=f-executor` |
| 11:52:29 | `legion-guard: cb pass task=<任务号> agent=f-executor attempt=1`（本地插件，仅登记、无取消能力） |
| 11:52:29 / 11:52:30 | `Auto-registered new chat` → `builder: built agent for session=...85c3f2e3 agent=f-executor` |
| 11:52:32–35 | 一连串 `Read` / `Bash` 放行（**只读巡检，无写无删**） |
| **11:55:56** | **`cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:...85c3f2e3): CancelledError`** |
| 11:55:56 | `cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn` + `cancel-save: ... closed 1 dangling tool call(s)` |
| 11:55:56 | **同一秒**另一条：`cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:...ccd46635): CancelledError` |
| 之后 | **零 result、零产物**；该会话上下文仅 2 条（末条为 Executor 自述"我先读权威状态机"）⇒ **刚开工即被掐** |

## 已逐项排除的原因（本地只读取证）
1. **审批（approval）** — 取消时刻**无任何** `app/approvals` 行；对照：另一次取消伴随 `Cancelled 1 pending approval(s) for root session ...`，与本例形态不同。
2. **本地插件 / 自定义守卫** — 本地守卫插件源码中无 `cancel` / `interrupt` / `terminate` / `stop_session` 任何关键词（不具备取消能力）；取消时刻亦无任何插件日志行。
3. **危险命令触发** — 被取消的会话上无删除类或命令行写文件类命令（被取消的 Executor 会话刚进入只读阶段）。
4. **保存配置触发的"零停机热重载"**（即 #8225 所述机制）— 四次取消时刻（10-13 11:20:07 / 10-13 14:28:31 / 10-14 09:37:27 / 10-14 11:55:56）**均无** `config.json` 或任一 `agent.json` 的写入（mtime 逐一核对）；日志亦无 reload / restart / `feishu channel started` 标记。⇒ **与 #8225 不是同一机制**。

## 与 `session_id mismatch` 的时间相关（因果假设，未闭合）
- 10-13 `22:24:43` 落 `qwenpaw/app/routers/tool_calls.py:91` 的 `session_id mismatch`（`url=<调用方会话>` vs `backend=1791895062459-d82gki8`）；
- **10-13 `22:29:16`**：该 `backend` 会话被 `cancel_cleanup: cancelled`。
- 另见 `qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:589 Message ignored (task already running)`（框架对"同一会话重复投递"的护栏）⇒ 佐证该**投递 / 回执通道确有重复与错配**。
- **保留**：因框架不记录取消发起方，因果链**未 100% 闭合**；本条的重点不只在错配，更在于**取消本身不可溯源**。

## 影响
单次取消 = 该子任务**会话死亡、零产物、需人工决策重派**；对多 agent 舰队属**可用性级**损失。并且，由于 `CancelledError` 与"agent 自身失败/超时"在日志上无法区分，本地只能靠人工逐条复核（本例即花了一轮人工取证才定性）。

## 期望
1. **让取消可溯源**：取消时至少落一条含 **发起方 / 原因 / 目标会话** 的日志（以区分：框架回收 / 超时 / 上游断开 / 路由错配）。
2. 确认上文「mismatch + 高频重投」路径**是否会导致会话级联取消**。
3. 若"同一秒成对取消"属**既定回收语义**（例如父会话结束回收子会话、收尾回收），请在文档或日志中明示。
4. 提供**可观测手段**（日志字段 / 接口 / 指标），以便本地自动区分"被取消"与"agent 失败"，无需人工复核。

## 最小复现建议
短时间内成批发起跨 agent 调用（同一调用方 → 多个被调方），观察数分钟后是否出现**同秒成对**的 `cancel_cleanup`；本地侧只读日志即可复核。可复跑聚合：以工具调用 id（`tc`）为主键，统计同一 `tc` 在 ≤120 秒窗口内的重复条数与 `session_id mismatch` 计数（正常段为 1，收尾段显著大于 1）。

## 相关 issue（可串联）
- **#8225**（保存 agent 配置触发的"零停机热重载"会取消正在运行的 cron 任务）— 机制不同，本条已显式排除配置保存。
- **#6608**（长命令绕过 `shell_command_timeout`、取消时留孤儿子进程、飞书会话被无限阻塞）
- **#7011**（Console 停止请求可取消活跃飞书会话；已 closed）
- **#8088**（图片路由卡死后被静默取消、用户无回复；已 closed）

---
*本报告按"不依赖私有环境、只读日志取证"整理；不含任何凭据、密钥或业务数据。*

issues.body:
# [Bug] 保存 agent 配置（如心跳设置）触发的「零停机热重载」会取消正在运行的 cron 任务，任务被记为 `cancelled` 且无任何提示（2.2.1）

## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1（`pip show qwenpaw` → Version: 2.2.1；`qwenpaw --version` → QwenPaw, version 2.2.1）

## Description

在 Console 里**保存一次心跳设置**（`PUT /api/config/heartbeat`），会把**当时正在运行的 cron 任务一起取消掉**，任务在运行历史里被记为 `status=cancelled / error="Job was cancelled"`；前端没有任何"这次保存将中断正在运行的任务"的提示，用户第一反应是"我并没有点取消，为什么显示 cancelled"。

**完整链路（实测，2.2.1 安装态）：**

```
PUT /api/config/heartbeat
  └─ app/routers/config.py:711   agent.config.heartbeat = hb
  └─ app/routers/config.py:712   save_agent_config(agent.agent_id, agent.config)   # 改写 agent.json
  └─ app/routers/config.py:718   await agent.cron_manager.reschedule_heartbeat()   # 异步

AgentConfigWatcher（poll=2.0s，监控 agent.json）
  └─ 指纹变化 → 重新加载并比对 _channels_hash / _heartbeat_hash（app/agent_config_watcher.py:35-63, 174+）
  └─ 判定 changed → app/agent_config_watcher.py:231  "config changed, triggering graceful reload"

MultiAgentManager.reload_agent()
  └─ :592  "Reloading agent (zero-downtime): <agent>"
  └─ :611  "Creating new workspace instance: <agent>"
  └─ :140  "New workspace instance started: <agent>"
  └─ :671  "Workspace instance replaced: <agent>"
  └─ :473  "Old workspace instance stopped: <agent>. Zero-downtime reload completed."

旧实例内正在执行的 agent 回合被硬切断
  └─ hooks/error/error_hook.py:90   cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<session>): CancelledError
  └─ runtime/runtime.py:297         cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn (session=<session>)
  └─ app/crons/executor.py:269-270  捕获 asyncio.CancelledError → "cron execute: job_id=… cancelled"
  └─ app/crons/manager.py:785-788   st.last_status = "cancelled"; st.last_error = "Job was cancelled"
```

**实际影响：** 本例被取消的是一天只跑一次、当天唯一的选股任务（19:15:56 启动，19:43:19 被杀，**已跑 27 分钟**）。由于 `cancel-save` 会把中断回合落盘、调度器随后在 19:43:47 自动重投递（`app/crons/manager.py:405`），最终 19:54:06 仍以 `success` 收尾，**业务结果没丢**；但：

1. 整个过程用户**完全无感**，只会在运行历史里看到一个 `cancelled`，无从判断原因（既不是自己点的取消，也不是任务报错）。
2. 重投递是**续做**而非回滚：中断前已执行的写操作（建监控/建分析/发消息等）不会被撤销，续做若重复执行会造成**重复实体**，需要调用方自己做"写入指纹核查"来兜底 —— 这个成本不该由上层业务承担。

**Related PR(s):** 无（reporter 未找到相关 PR）

**Security considerations:** 无。本例只涉及配置下发与运行时任务取消，未涉及凭据、鉴权、越权或数据泄露。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
  - `app/routers/config.py`（`PUT /heartbeat`：写 config + 触发 reschedule）
  - `app/agent_config_watcher.py`（`AgentConfigWatcher._check`：文件变更判定 + 触发 reload）
  - `app/multi_agent_manager.py`（`reload_agent` 零停机替换实例，`:473` 停旧实例）
  - `app/crons/executor.py:269-270` ＋ `app/crons/manager.py:405,785-788`（`CancelledError` → 记 `cancelled` → 重投递）
- [x] Console (frontend web UI) —— 保存设置时未提示"将中断正在运行的任务"，也未在运行历史里区分 `cancelled` 的成因
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) —— 仅间接：被取消的 cron 任务是投递到 console channel 的 agent 任务；若投递目标换成 IM channel，任务半途被切断同样会向该 channel 暴露不完整输出。**未验证**其他 channel 下是否有额外影响。
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website) —— 建议补充"修改 agent 配置会影响在跑任务"的说明
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1（pip 安装态，`site-packages` 无 git 提交信息）
- **OS:** Linux (WSL2)，kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`；userland `Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS`；host timezone `Asia/Shanghai`
- **Install method:** pip（venv `/home/pavino/.qwenvenv`）
- **Python version:** 3.12.3

补充环境：单机、单进程 `qwenpaw app`（PID 在故障前后未变，**排除了进程重启导致的取消**）；多 agent 工作区，本次受影响的 agent 有 1 条 `agent` 型每日 cron 任务。

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 给某个 agent 配置一条**运行时间较长**的 cron 任务（本例：每日 `19:15` 触发的全市场选股，实测典型耗时 25–40 分钟），并让它开始运行。
2. 任务运行期间，在 Console 打开该 agent 的**心跳设置**页（`GET /api/config/heartbeat`）。
3. 点击**保存**（`PUT /api/config/heartbeat`，返回 `200 OK`）。
4. 观察日志（**同一秒起**）：

```
19:43:14 | heartbeat rescheduled: every=1h                                              (crons/manager.py:298)
19:43:14 | AgentConfigWatcher (<agent>): config changed, triggering graceful reload
           (channels: <hash> -> <hash>, heartbeat: <hash> -> <hash>)                    (agent_config_watcher.py:229)
19:43:14 | Reloading agent (zero-downtime): <agent>                                     (multi_agent_manager.py:592)
19:43:14 | Creating new workspace instance: <agent>                                     (multi_agent_manager.py:611)
19:43:19 | New workspace instance started: <agent>                                      (multi_agent_manager.py:140)
19:43:19 | Workspace instance replaced: <agent>                                         (multi_agent_manager.py:671)
19:43:19 | Old workspace instance stopped: <agent>. Zero-downtime reload completed.      (multi_agent_manager.py:473)
19:43:19 | cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<session>): CancelledError                (hooks/error/error_hook.py:90)
19:43:19 | cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn (session=<session>)                  (runtime/runtime.py:297)
19:43:19 | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> cancelled                                      (crons/executor.py:270)
19:43:19 | cron _execute_once: job_id=<job-id> status=cancelled                          (crons/manager.py:787)
```

5. 任务运行历史（`jobs_history`）出现：`{"status": "cancelled", "error": "Job was cancelled"}`。

**可复现性：稳定复现**——本例的取消时间点（19:43:14）恰好落在任务运行窗口（19:15:56 启动、被杀时已跑 27 分钟）内，两者重叠即触发。因此只要"保存 agent 级配置"与"长任务在跑"两个条件同时满足，该问题即出现。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:**
  1. 保存与任务无关的设置（心跳）会**取消正在运行的 cron 任务**，且是"硬切断"——被切在 27 分钟处，回合内的工具副作用已落盘不回滚。
  2. 用户侧无提示：Console 不告警，运行历史只留一个 `cancelled`；`cancelled`（被外部打断）与 `timeout`（跑超时，`crons/executor.py:251/266` → `status=timeout`）在 UI 上不易区分，导致需要翻日志才能定性。
  3. **触发条件是"写文件"这个动作，而不是"值发生变化"**：`save_agent_config()` **无条件重写** `agent.json`，`AgentConfigWatcher` 只比对文件指纹与 `channels`/`heartbeat` 哈希。本例保存前后心跳**间隔相同**（均为 `every=1h`，保存前日志中已有 `Heartbeat job scheduled for agent <agent>: every=1h`），而 watcher 打印的 heartbeat 哈希 `-5931758269779770202 -> 1725766300364508814` **确实变了** ⇒ 这次保存改动的是心跳的**其它**字段。至于"把完全相同的值再存一次"，我们未单独实测，但按上述代码路径应当同样触发 reload —— 请 dev 确认。
- **Expected:** 修改 agent 配置（心跳 / 渠道 / driver 等）不应以牺牲在跑回合为代价。希望至少做到其中一项：
  1. **延迟切换**：`save_agent_config` 后由 watcher 触发 reload 时，若该 agent 有**正在执行的 agent/cron 回合**，则等待其结束（或等到下一个安全点）再做实例替换；或
  2. **重新排队而非取消**：把被中断的回合显式标记为 `interrupted/requeued` 并**从头或从中断点安全续做**，而不是让在跑回合收到裸 `CancelledError`；或
  3. **前置提示**：Console 在保存前检查该 agent 是否有在跑任务，弹窗告知"保存将中断 N 个正在运行的任务（任务名/已运行时长）"，由用户选择"等任务结束"或"立即保存"。
  4. 附带：`cancelled` 的成因（配置重载 / 用户取消 / 进程退出）建议结构化落库，便于 UI 展示与检索。

## Logs / Screenshots

触发请求与取消（`journalctl -u qwenpaw`，已脱敏：主机名、客户端 IP、会话 ID、job ID 掩码）：

```
19:15:56 | INFO crons/executor.py:48    | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> channel=console task_type=agent
                                          target_user_id=default target_session_id=<session>
19:43:09 | INFO (uvicorn)               | 192.168.0.x - "GET /api/config/heartbeat HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
19:43:14 | INFO (uvicorn)               | 192.168.0.x - "PUT /api/config/heartbeat HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
19:43:14 | INFO crons/manager.py:298    | heartbeat rescheduled: every=1h
19:43:14 | INFO agent_config_watcher.py:229 | AgentConfigWatcher (<agent>): config changed, triggering
                                          graceful reload (channels: 2766186957541623328 -> 2766186957541623328,
                                          heartbeat: -5931758269779770202 -> 1725766300364508814)
19:43:14 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:592  | Reloading agent (zero-downtime): <agent>
19:43:14 | INFO agent_config_watcher.py:114 | AgentConfigWatcher already disabled for agent <agent>, skipping cancel
19:43:14 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:611  | Creating new workspace instance: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO workspace/workspace.py:725  | Workspace started successfully: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO agent_config_watcher.py:106 | AgentConfigWatcher started for agent <agent>
                                          (poll=2.0s, path=/home/pavino/.qwenpaw/workspaces/<agent>/agent.json)
19:43:19 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:140  | New workspace instance started: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:671  | Workspace instance replaced: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO hooks/error/error_hook.py:90 | cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<session>): CancelledError
19:43:19 | INFO runtime/runtime.py:297      | cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn (session=<session>)
19:43:19 | INFO crons/executor.py:270       | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> cancelled
19:43:19 | INFO crons/manager.py:787        | cron _execute_once: job_id=<job-id> status=cancelled
19:43:19 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:473  | Old workspace instance stopped: <agent>. Zero-downtime reload
                                          completed.
19:43:47 | INFO crons/manager.py:405       | cron run_job (async): job_id=<job-id> channel=console
                                          task_type=agent target_session_id=<session>     ← 自动重投递
19:43:47 | INFO crons/executor.py:48       | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> channel=console …      ← 续做
```

运行历史落库（该任务当日两条记录）：

```json
{"run_at": "2026-10-13T19:43:19", "status": "cancelled", "error": "Job was cancelled", "trigger": "scheduled"}
{"run_at": "2026-10-13T19:54:06", "status": "success",   "trigger": "manual"}
```

关键旁证（排除其它成因）：

- 进程 PID **前后未变**（同日 `qwenpaw[1362054]`，服务自 10-12 21:29 起持续运行）⇒ 不是进程重启/关机导致的取消。
- 当日**仅此一次**配置变更事件（全天 `journalctl` 中 `AgentConfigWatcher … config changed` 只出现 1 次）⇒ 与本次取消一一对应。
- 该 agent 的 watcher 在 19:43:14 之前**没有**任何 reload 记录。

## Additional Notes

**Workaround（目前采用）：** 不要在长任务运行窗口内保存 agent 级配置。本例的安全窗口是"避开每日 19:15 起的 25–40 分钟"，即 20:30 之后或次日盘前再改。

**同族风险（未逐一验证）：** `AgentConfigWatcher._check` 同时比对 `_channels_hash`，并对**任何** `agent.json` 变化触发同一 reload 路径；另外还存在独立的 `DriverConfigWatcher`（`app/driver_config_watcher.py:49`，poll=2.0s，监控 `<workspace>/drivers`）。因此"渠道设置""driver 配置"的保存**很可能有同样效果**，建议一并纳入修复范围与回归测试。注意：直接编辑 `agent.json`（绕过 API）同样会触发（watcher 是按文件指纹轮询的），所以只在前端加提示并不能覆盖全部入口。

**区分 `cancelled` 与 `timeout` 的提示（对使用者很重要）：**

- `cancelled` = `app/crons/executor.py:269-270` 捕获 `asyncio.CancelledError` → `app/crons/manager.py:785-788` 落库 → **"被外部打断"**。
- `timeout`  = `app/crons/executor.py:251/266` → `status=timeout`、`error="timed out after <N>s"` → **"跑超时"**。

两者是完全不同的成因，但在运行历史里都表现为"没跑完"。本例排查耗时主要花在这里：`cancelled` 必须回日志里找同一秒的 `AgentConfigWatcher … config changed` / `Reloading agent` / `Old workspace instance stopped` 才能定位。若能在 UI 上直接给出成因标签，可显著降低排查成本。

**期望的回归用例（供参考）：**

1. 启动一个长时 agent cron 任务，期间保存心跳设置 → 断言该任务**不被取消**（或按预期被安全延迟/重新排队，而不是落 `cancelled`）。
2. 保存前后心跳配置完全相同 → 断言**不触发**全量 reload（当前是触发的）。
3. 保存 `drivers/` 或 channels 配置 → 断言不与在跑回合冲突。

issues.title: Settings Center ignores public menu visibility overrides for built-in entries
issues.body:
The public menu API can hide a built-in shortcut with a reversible `menu.replace(..., { ...item, visible: () => false })` override. The primary sidebar honors it, but the corresponding built-in entry remains visible inside Settings Center.

Reproduction on v2.2.1:
1. Register a frontend plugin that hides the menu item routing to `core.channels`.
2. Confirm the main sidebar no longer offers that shortcut.
3. Open More settings. Channels is still listed, searchable, and selectable at `/settings/channels`.

Settings Center builds its built-in groups from a static definition and registered routes without consulting the menu visibility callbacks. The same filter remains in current main (4e7b37a92241ddc043e7057f7e392dd7499e93a7), although the settings layout has evolved.

Proposed fix: reuse the existing menu snapshots/flattening when resolving built-in settings navigation. Preserve settings pages without a corresponding menu registration, react to plugin overrides/disposal, and keep visible alternate entries for a shared route. This is display consistency, not an authorization boundary; direct APIs retain their own access rules.

A minimal fix and regression tests are being prepared. No new distribution policy, branding, backend, or business logic is required.

issues.title: [Bug][Console] Message-navigation directory cannot locate accurately: positions are apportioned by item count, only the active anchor is measured

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2b4 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 10 AMD64) - tested against the 2.2.2-beta.5 desktop bundle

## Description

Related to #8186 (message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling). PR #8214 fixed the "user cannot interrupt the auto-positioning" half, but the navigation directory itself still cannot locate accurately - and the two share the same cached state, so this looks like the other half of one mechanism.

### Repro (long session, 40+ messages)

1. Open a long conversation and open the **"导航 (N)" / "Navigation (N)"** panel on the right (`messageAnchors.title`).
2. Click any entry, or click the "scroll directory to active user message" button in the panel header.
3. Expected: the transcript scrolls to that user message, and the active item is scrolled into view inside the panel.
4. Actual: the jump lands at a **wrong position**, and/or the locate button appears **disabled / does nothing**. The mismatch grows with session length.

After using the panel once, a subsequent wheel gesture keeps snapping the transcript back to the list head - the same symptom as #8186. Without touching the panel, plain wheel scrolling is unaffected, so the trigger is the navigation action itself.

## Code evidence

From the installed console bundle `console/assets/chat-vendor-*.js` (2.2.2-beta.5 build):

**1. Anchor vertical positions are apportioned by item count, not by real height**

```js
// orderPercent = (index + 0.5) / total * 100
// when a real rect is unavailable, the estimate is used as-is as a coordinate:
var Ze = V.get(xe.id); if (!Ze) return Se[xe.id] = xe.orderPercent, Se;
```

One long answer and one short "ok" are treated as equal height, so the directory's coordinate system does not match the transcript's real scroll geometry.

**2. Only the active anchor gets a real element ref**

```js
ref: C ? l : void 0     // C = (g.id === n)  -> only the active item is measured
```

Everything else falls back to the estimate above.

**3. The locate button's availability depends solely on the active anchor**

```js
disabled={!n}           // n = activeAnchorId
```

Measurement is throttled behind `requestAnimationFrame` + `ResizeObserver` + `MutationObserver`; while a measurement pass has not produced an active id yet, the button is unusable.

**4. Shared cached-state path with #8186**

The directory caches the current anchor in a mutable ref (`C.current`) and re-runs its measurement on scroll / resize / mutation of the transcript. This is the same state that the jump-and-pin loop maintains (`Ue / RA / NA`, the ~1.6 s re-anchor described in #8186). Hence "positioning is inaccurate" and "wheel gets dragged back" are two faces of one mechanism rather than two independent defects.

## Suggested direction

1. Use the real DOM geometry for anchor positions - the rect map is already collected in the same pass, so the fallback to `orderPercent` should not be used as a coordinate (or should be recomputed on demand).
2. Do not gate the locate action on the active anchor only.
3. Clear the navigation's anchor/reset cache once a navigation completes, so later scroll interaction is not influenced by residual navigation state.

---
*Read-only inspection of the installed console bundle on QwenPaw Desktop 2.2.2-beta.5 (Windows 10 x64).*

issues.title: [Question] Claude Code as a third-party agent harness — status and roadmap?
issues.body:
Hi team,

The third-party agent harness shipped in the 2.2.0 betas is a great addition — Codex and Qoder are already supported in the console, while Claude Code is still marked "Coming soon".

issues.title: [Feature]: web_search built-in tavily provider has no API-key config surface — paid quota unusable (内置 tavily provider 无法配置自有 API key)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

The built-in `web_search` tool's tavily provider always uses keyless anonymous REST (request header `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`), and **there is no configuration surface to supply a user's own Tavily API key**. Users with a paid Tavily subscription can neither consume their own quota nor avoid the anonymous channel's rate limits.

中文：内置 `web_search` 的 tavily provider 固定走 keyless 匿名 REST（请求头 `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`），没有任何配置入口填入用户自己的 Tavily API key。持有订阅的用户既无法消耗自有额度，还随时受匿名通道限流。理解 keyless 是"开箱即用"的产品决策，本单无意要求改变默认；诉求只是**给有 key 的用户一扇门**。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (agents/tools — `websearch` providers & factory)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI — provider dropdown has no key field)
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI (`qwenpaw` config surfaces for `web_search.config`)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **OS:** macOS 15 (arm64), Python 3.12, pip install
- Tavily account: Researcher plan (1000 credits/month)

## Problem Details / Reproduction

1. Inspect outbound requests from `web_search`: every call carries `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`; the account's own quota consumption stays at zero.
2. Look for a place to configure a key: `web_search.config` schema exposes only the provider choice (`tavily` / `anysearch`); the Console dropdown likewise. Neither has an `api_key`/credential field anywhere.
3. Result: a user holding a valid Tavily key has no supported way to make the built-in provider use it.
4. Keyless is not a theoretical risk: our logs contain a real **HTTP 432** (quota-class error) failure from the anonymous path.

This is a feature gap rather than a crash — the symptom is "I have a key but nowhere to put it", with no warning anywhere. It belongs to the same natural evolution as #8139 and #7711 (adding new web_search providers).

## Current Workaround & Its Cost

We patched venv site-packages directly (with the operator's explicit authorization): added an authed provider that reads the key reference from QwenPaw's **existing credential store**, POSTs to `api.tavily.com/search` authenticated, and on any 432/429/401/network error **automatically falls back to keyless** — plus wiring changes in `factory.py` default and the Console dropdown options. End-to-end verified: authed path genuinely used; fallback path PASS.

Costs we are paying, which upstream fixes would eliminate:

1. `qwenpaw update` overwrites the patch — explicit technical debt we must re-apply after every upgrade.
2. During rollout we hit a related papercut: AgentConfigWatcher hot-reloads JSON configs only; Python code changes do not take effect, and the running process kept reporting `Unknown web_search provider` with **no hint that a restart was required**.

## Suggested Implementation

1. Add an `api_key_ref` field to `web_search.config` pointing into the framework's existing credential store (we verified tool-layer code can read it; implementation cost is low and it avoids plaintext keys in `agent.json`); expose a key input in the Console form accordingly.
2. Implement **authed→keyless automatic fallback** officially: degrade with a log line when quota is exhausted/rate-limited. This is the most valuable part of our hand-rolled solution and we suggest adopting it as-is.
3. (Bonus) At startup or config change, if tool-layer module mtime is newer than process start time, emit `WARN: restart required` — prevents the "changed it but nothing happened and nobody knows why" class of confusion.

Severity: **feature-gap level**. All implementation details from our prototype are available on request. Thanks!

---

### 中文版全文

**问题**：内置 tavily provider 无 API key 配置入口，付费额度用不上，只能吃匿名通道的限流与低质量结果（日志有真实 HTTP 432 记录）。**复现**：任何位置尝试配置 key → 无处可填 → 出站请求仍为 keyless。**临时解决及代价**：直改 site-packages 实现 authed + keyless 自动回退（已端到端验证），但升级即被覆盖，属技术债；且暴露"改代码不重启不生效、框架无任何提示"的关联问题。**建议**：① `web_search.config.api_key_ref` 指向既有 credentials 库 + Console 表单露出密钥输入；② 官方吸收 authed→keyless 自动降级；③ 工具层模块 mtime 晚于进程启动时打 WARN "restart required"。原型实现细节可提供，欢迎评论区索取。谢谢！
