issues.title: [Feature]: Email channel: trust an extra CA for IMAP and SMTP (tls_ca_cert_path)
issues.body:
### Summary

Add `tls_ca_cert_path` to `[channels.email.<alias>]` so the email channel and the email tools can reach an IMAP/SMTP server signed by a private CA, with the same file rules as the existing MCP and provider option.

### Problem statement

The email channel trusts a fixed set of roots:

- IMAP (`EmailChannel::connect_imap` and `zeroclaw_tools::email_imap::imap_connect`, used by the read-only email tools) builds a `RootCertStore` from `webpki_roots::TLS_SERVER_ROOTS` only.
- SMTP with `smtp_tls = true` uses `SmtpTransport::relay`, i.e. lettre's default roots.

A mail server whose certificate chains to an internal or corporate CA (common for on-premises Exchange, self-hosted Postfix/Dovecot, or a TLS-inspecting egress proxy) fails the handshake with an unknown-issuer error, and there is no way to fix it from config. The only workaround is disabling TLS for SMTP, and IMAP has no non-TLS path at all.

Other surfaces already solved this: model providers have `tls_ca_cert_path` (#5797) and MCP servers have a per-server `tls_ca_cert_path` (#9405), whose loader (`crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/mcp_transport.rs`) requires an absolute path, a regular file of at most 1 MiB, opens with `O_NONBLOCK` so a FIFO cannot block, and fails hard instead of falling back.

### Proposed solution

- Add `tls_ca_cert_path: Option<String>` to `EmailConfig`, documented like the MCP field.
- Reuse the MCP loader rather than copy it: make `load_tls_ca_pem` take an error-prefix string instead of an `McpServerConfig` (MCP messages stay byte-for-byte the same) and call it from `email_imap`.
- Parse the PEM bundle with `rustls-pki-types`, add the certificates to the IMAP root store (on top of the web PKI roots) and to lettre's `TlsParameters` for SMTP. Chain and hostname verification stay on.
- An invalid file fails the connection with a clear error; no silent fallback to the default roots.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Client certificates (mTLS).
- Disabling verification or pinning.
- Using the OS trust store. Providers moved to it in #6528; the email channel can follow separately.
- Plain-text SMTP (`smtp_tls = false`) does not use the CA. STARTTLS support is proposed separately in #11747; whichever lands second wires the CA into that path too.

### Alternatives considered

- **Copy the reference implementation with `~` expansion and a new name (`tls_ca_file`).** Diverges from the existing option name and file rules for no reason.
- **A global CA setting.** The other surfaces are per-provider / per-server; a per-channel field keeps the same shape.

### Acceptance criteria

- With the private CA configured, `connect_imap` and SMTP over implicit TLS complete the handshake against a server signed by that CA; without it, the handshake fails (so the test is meaningful).
- A relative or `~` path, a missing file, a directory, a file over 1 MiB, or a file without certificates is an error naming the problem.
- The MCP loader's existing tests pass unchanged apart from the call signature.
- Existing configs without the key behave as today.

### Architecture impact

`EmailConfig` gains one optional field. `zeroclaw-tools` exposes `tls_ca_certs` / `imap_root_store` next to `imap_connect`; the MCP loader becomes a crate-shared helper. `zeroclaw-channels` gains `rcgen` as a dev-dependency (already in the lockfile, used by `zeroclaw-tools` tests) for a private-CA test server.

### Risk and rollback

Low to medium: only configs that set the key change behavior, and the change is additive to the trust store. Rollback is reverting the commit or unsetting the key.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage

### Next decision surface

Maintainer triage on this issue. I will open a PR against it with the change and its tests.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [X] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [X] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.title: [Bug]: Email channel answers automatic mail (auto-replies, bounces, lists), risking mail loops
issues.body:
### Affected component

channel

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

`EmailChannel::dispatch_email` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/email_channel.rs`) turns every new message from an allowed sender into an agent turn, and the agent's answer is mailed back to the sender (or `Reply-To`). Nothing looks at the headers that mark mail as machine-generated:

- `Auto-Submitted: auto-replied` / `auto-generated` (RFC 3834): out-of-office replies, vacation responders, delivery status notifications, ticketing systems.
- `Precedence: bulk` / `list` / `junk`: the older de-facto marker for the same thing.
- `List-Id` / `List-Unsubscribe`: mailing lists and newsletters.

So when the agent emails someone who has an out-of-office set, their autoresponder answers, that answer starts a new turn, the agent replies to it, and the autoresponder may answer again. With two automated parties this can become a mail loop; many autoresponders answer a sender only once per period, but not all do, and every bounce, newsletter or notification still costs a turn and an outbound email. RFC 3834 section 2 says an automatic responder should not respond to messages carrying these markers; the agent is an automatic responder in that sense.

A related observability gap: when a sender is not in the allowlist, the record is `Action::Note` with outcome `Unknown` and only the text `Blocked email from <addr>`. An operator watching `/api/events` cannot filter rejections or see which channel alias and subject were involved without parsing the message string.

### Expected behavior

- A message with `Auto-Submitted` other than `no`, `Precedence: bulk|list|junk`, or a `List-Id` / `List-Unsubscribe` header is dropped before it reaches the agent (before the allowlist check, so it never starts a turn even from an allowed sender), and the drop is logged with the reason.
- Both inbound drop paths log structured records: the automatic-mail drop as `Action::Skip` and the allowlist rejection as `Action::Reject`, each with `channel`, `alias`, `sender`, `subject` and `reason` attributes.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Configure [channels.email.<alias>] with "*" (or a domain) in the peer group.
2. From an allowed address, send the mailbox a message carrying
   "Auto-Submitted: auto-replied" (what most out-of-office responders send).
3. Observed: the message starts an agent turn and the agent mails a reply,
   which the sender's autoresponder can answer again.
4. Expected: the message is dropped and logged with reason "auto_submitted".
```

### Impact

Each loop iteration costs a model call and an outbound email, and the agent's sending reputation suffers if it answers newsletters and bounces. #5528 (a runaway 700+ email send through the email channel, from a different trigger) shows how quickly unattended email volume becomes a real problem. Operators cannot see these drops in structured logs either.

### Logs / stack traces

_None: the messages are processed normally, which is the problem._

### ZeroClaw version

`master` at `329e66f76`; also v0.8.5.

### Rust version

1.99.0

### Operating system

Not platform-specific; found by reading the source and confirmed with a test on the dispatch path.

### Regression?

No. The channel has never checked these headers.

### Pre-flight checks

- [X] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

---

I will open a PR against this issue: compute the automatic-mail reason when the message is parsed, drop it at the top of `dispatch_email` with an `Action::Skip` record, and switch the blocked-sender record to `Action::Reject` with the same attributes. Related: #5528 (runaway outbound email, different cause).

issues.title: [Feature]: Email channel: send over SMTP with STARTTLS (Office 365, port 587)
issues.body:
### Summary

Let the email channel send over SMTP with STARTTLS, so it works with servers that only take submissions on port 587, such as Office 365 (`smtp.office365.com:587`).

### Problem statement

`EmailChannel::create_smtp_transport` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/email_channel.rs`) has two modes: `smtp_tls = true` uses `SmtpTransport::relay` (implicit TLS, SMTPS, usually port 465), and `smtp_tls = false` uses `SmtpTransport::builder_dangerous` with no TLS at all. There is no STARTTLS.

Office 365 accepts SMTP client submission only on `smtp.office365.com:587` with STARTTLS. With `smtp_tls = true` the client starts a TLS handshake against a server that speaks plain SMTP first, and the send fails. With `smtp_tls = false` the client would authenticate over an unencrypted connection, which the server refuses and which nobody should configure anyway. So an Office 365 mailbox can receive through the channel (IMAP on 993) but cannot reply. Many self-hosted relays are set up the same way (587 + STARTTLS only).

The "Outlook / Office 365" section of `docs/book/src/channels/email.md` currently has no SMTP guidance at all.

### Proposed solution

- Add `smtp_starttls: bool` (default `false`) to `EmailConfig`. When `true`, `create_smtp_transport` connects in plain text and upgrades with `Tls::Required`, the same setup as lettre's `SmtpTransport::starttls_relay`: if the server does not offer STARTTLS or the upgrade fails, the send fails before any credentials are sent. It takes precedence over `smtp_tls`.
- Document the field (schema doc comment, which feeds the generated config reference) and add an Office 365 example to the email page.

A separate bool keeps the change additive: existing configs deserialize unchanged, and no migration is needed.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- XOAUTH2 for SMTP. `oauth2` covers IMAP only today; SMTP keeps password auth. A tenant that disabled SMTP AUTH still cannot send, and that is a separate change.
- Opportunistic STARTTLS (`Tls::Opportunistic`). Silently falling back to plain text when the upgrade fails is not something a credentialed client should do.
- Changing the default port or `smtp_tls` default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Replace `smtp_tls` with an enum (`implicit` / `starttls` / `none`).** Cleaner on paper, but it is a breaking schema change that needs a migration for every existing config, for no behavior gain over an additive bool.
- **Infer STARTTLS from port 587.** Implicit and surprising; some servers run implicit TLS on non-standard ports.

### Acceptance criteria

- With `smtp_starttls = true`, the client sends `EHLO`, then `STARTTLS`, and never sends `AUTH` or mail before the upgrade succeeds; a refused upgrade fails the send.
- With both flags `false`, no `STARTTLS` is sent (plain-text behavior unchanged); with only `smtp_tls = true`, implicit TLS as today.
- Existing configs without the key keep their behavior.
- Tests drive `Channel::send` against a local fake SMTP server and assert the command sequence.

### Architecture impact

`EmailConfig` gains one optional field (additive, default `false`); `create_smtp_transport` picks `Tls::Required` / `Tls::Wrapper` / `Tls::None` on one builder. No new dependency (lettre already has `rustls-tls` and `smtp-transport`). The config reference is generated from the schema doc comment.

### Risk and rollback

Low. Only configs that set the new key change behavior. Rollback is reverting the commit or unsetting the key.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage

### Next decision surface

Maintainer triage on this issue. I will open a PR against it with the change, its tests and the docs update.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [X] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [X] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.title: [Bug]: Email channel does not store inbound attachments as the docs say
issues.body:
### Affected component

channel

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

The email channel page (`docs/book/src/channels/email.md`, "Attachment handling") says:

> Inbound attachments are stored under `<workspace>/attachments/<conversation>/`. The agent gets file paths in its context and can read them via the `file_read` tool.

The code does not do this. `EmailChannel` has no workspace directory, and nothing in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/email_channel.rs` writes to disk:

- `extract_attachments` turns each non-text MIME part into an in-memory `MediaAttachment { marker: None, .. }`. The bytes live for one turn and no path reaches the agent, so a PDF or spreadsheet cannot be opened later with `file_read`, forwarded, or archived.
- `extract_attachments` skips every `text/*` part ("already handled by extract_text"), but `extract_text` only falls back to a text attachment when the email has no body. A CSV or `.txt` attached to an email that also has a body is dropped without a trace.
- `collect_configured_channels` builds `EmailChannel` without a workspace, unlike Telegram, Matrix and WhatsApp Web, which all get `Config::channel_workspace_dir("<type>.<alias>")`.

The documented path came in with the docs overhaul in #5788; I found no commit that ever implemented it.

### Expected behavior

Documents that arrive by email are saved under the channel's workspace and the agent gets a path it can reuse, as the page says and as Telegram (`telegram_files/`) and Matrix (`matrix_files/`) already do:

- Only after the sender passes the allowlist.
- Each attachment that is neither image nor audio is written to a fixed directory inside the workspace, with a sanitized file name (no path separators, no leading dots, bounded length), and nothing is written if that directory resolves outside the workspace.
- The message carries a `[Document: <name>] <path>` line per saved file and the attachment's typed `marker` is `MarkerKind::Document` with that path, the contract Matrix uses, so the media pipeline defers to it.
- `text/*` attachments are saved even when the email has a body.
- Images and audio keep going through the media pipeline, and a channel without a workspace behaves as today.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Configure [channels.email.<alias>] bound to an agent, with the sender in the
   channel's peer group.
2. Send the mailbox an email with a body and two attachments: report.pdf and
   rows.csv.
3. Observed: nothing is written under the agent workspace; the agent sees no
   path for report.pdf, and rows.csv is not mentioned at all.
4. Expected (per docs): both files saved under the workspace and their paths in
   the agent's context.
```

### Impact

An email agent cannot work with the documents people send it beyond one look at the bytes, when the provider accepts them at all: it cannot read a spreadsheet with a tool, attach the original to a reply, or archive it. Text attachments on emails that have a body are silently lost, while the docs say the opposite.

### Logs / stack traces

_None: nothing is logged when an attachment is not saved, which is part of the report._

### ZeroClaw version

`master` at `329e66f76`; also v0.8.5.

### Rust version

1.99.0

### Operating system

Not platform-specific; found by reading the source and confirmed with a test on the dispatch path.

### Regression?

No. As far as I can tell the documented behavior was never implemented.

### Pre-flight checks

- [X] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

---

I will open a PR against this issue: give the configured `EmailChannel` its channel workspace, save documents to `<workspace>/email_files/<message-id>_<n>_<name>` after the allowlist check, mark them with `MarkerKind::Document`, and update the page. I propose `email_files/` rather than the documented `attachments/<conversation>/`: it matches `telegram_files/` and `matrix_files/`, and email has no stable conversation key to name a directory after (threading comes from headers the sender controls). Happy to switch to the documented layout if maintainers prefer it.

issues.title: [Feature]: Show the model's reasoning in Telegram and Slack streaming drafts
issues.body:
### Summary

Show the model's reasoning (thinking) in the Telegram and Slack streaming drafts while a reply is
being generated, the way the Matrix `single_message` draft already can.

### Problem statement

Matrix aliases can stream the model's reasoning into their progress draft via
`channels.matrix.<alias>.stream_reasoning` (`off` | `status` | `full`). Telegram
(`stream_mode = "partial"`) and Slack (`stream_drafts = true`) stream an editable draft as well, but
show nothing about why the model is taking a while: the orchestrator only wired reasoning into the
draft updater for Matrix, and the shared draft updater intentionally drops `StreamDelta::Reasoning`
for every other channel.

Operators who run the agent on Telegram or Slack therefore get a silent draft on long reasoning-heavy
turns, with no way to tell "still thinking" from "stuck" beyond the generic "Waiting on model"
lifecycle line.

### Proposed solution

Add a per-alias `stream_reasoning` field to `[channels.telegram.<alias>]` and
`[channels.slack.<alias>]`, reusing the existing `StreamReasoningMode` enum (`off` | `status` |
`full`), default `off`:

```toml
[channels.telegram.home]
stream_mode = "partial"
stream_reasoning = "full"

[channels.slack.work]
stream_drafts = true
stream_reasoning = "status"
```

- `off` (default): unchanged draft behavior.
- `status`: a liveness-only thinking line in the draft, no reasoning text.
- `full`: the model's raw reasoning rendered as a quote (collapsed `<blockquote expandable>` on
  Telegram, `>` quote on Slack) above the in-progress answer.

The setting is only effective while the alias is actually streaming an editable draft
(`stream_mode = "partial"` / `stream_drafts = true`); otherwise it is inert. Reasoning is draft-only
chrome — the finalized message is rewritten from the answer alone and never contains it.

Implementation outline: generalize the orchestrator's Matrix-only gate to a channel-agnostic
resolver, and add a `Channel::update_draft_with_reasoning` method (default: ignore reasoning) that
Telegram and Slack override.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- No reasoning surface for Discord, Lark, Mattermost, or any other channel.
- No change to Matrix's own rendering or to Matrix `partial` / `multi_message`.
- No change to how the agent loop captures or persists reasoning, and no "keep a collapsed reasoning
  block in the final message" mode (Matrix has no equivalent).

### Alternatives considered

- **Reuse the existing lifecycle status line only.** Telegram/Slack already show "Waiting on model".
  It conveys liveness but no reasoning, which is the actual request.
- **Put reasoning in the answer buffer.** Would leak reasoning into the finalized message and break
  MultiMessage offset accounting, so it is rejected.
- **A new shared enum instead of `StreamReasoningMode`.** `StreamReasoningMode` already models exactly
  these three states with the same semantics, so a second enum would be redundant.

### Acceptance criteria

- `channels.telegram.<alias>.stream_reasoning` and `channels.slack.<alias>.stream_reasoning` parse,
  default to `off`, and appear in the generated schema/field lists.
- With `off`, the draft is unchanged (no behavior difference for existing configs).
- With `full`, reasoning appears in the draft and never in the finalized message.
- Telegram/Slack render helpers are unit-tested for escaping and safe truncation at the platform
  limits.

### Architecture impact

`crates/zeroclaw-config` (schema + generated docs/schema), `crates/zeroclaw-api` (one new `Channel`
method with a default impl), `crates/zeroclaw-channels` (telegram, slack, orchestrator).

### Risk and rollback

Risk: reasoning becomes user-visible on a channel where an operator enabled it — which is why the
default is `off`. Rollback: `git revert <sha>`, or set `stream_reasoning = "off"` and restart.

### Expected routing

Needs maintainer design assessment

### Next decision surface

ordinary triage is enough

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

---

## RFC assessment

This is **not** an RFC trigger. `docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md` lists "a configuration field or
default change" as an explicit non-trigger, and the accompanying PR is a bounded, default-preserving
config-field addition plus one channel-local rendering method. It adds no security layer, changes no
governance, does not refactor cross-cutting architecture, and opens no new subsystem-capability
boundary. If a maintainer disagrees, the substantive effect is a new user-visible egress of model
reasoning on two channels, which could be promoted to an RFC on that basis.

issues.title: Custom (OpenAI-compatible) providers default to text-fallback, and DSML tool markup is neither parsed nor stripped
issues.body:
## Summary

Two related issues for maintainer discussion. Both surfaced while documenting `native_tools` on the `custom` provider slot (docs PR: #11740). Filing as a discussion item, not as part of the docs PR.

### (a) `custom` defaults to text-fallback with no warning

`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/factory.rs`, the `CustomModelProviderConfig` factory (around the `OpenAiCompatibleModelProvider::builder(alias).display_name("Custom")` build):

```rust
if opts.native_tools != Some(true) {
    b = b.without_native_tools();
}
```

So for `[providers.models.custom.<alias>]`, native tool calling is OFF unless the operator sets `native_tools = true`. The `custom` slot is the documented catch-all for "any OpenAI-compatible endpoint" (`docs/book/src/providers/custom.md`), and the large majority of such endpoints support the OpenAI `tools` protocol. Defaulting to the text/XML protocol means:

- the request omits `tools` (`build_iteration_tool_specs` gates on `capabilities_for_model(...).native_tool_calling`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/tool_specs.rs`), and
- the runtime injects the text tool protocol into the system prompt and selects `XmlToolDispatcher` (`tool_dispatcher_for_provider`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs`, with the `"auto"` arm).

Question for maintainers: should the `custom` slot default to **native** tool calling (with `native_tools = false` as the opt-out), or stay text-fallback but emit a startup/config warning when a `custom` alias is used without an explicit `native_tools`? The current default is surprising given the slot's stated purpose, and the only in-repo signal was the schema doc comment, which (before the docs PR) named only Groq.

### (b) DSML tool markup emitted in text-fallback mode is passed through verbatim

Observed on v0.8.5: a DeepSeek-backed model reached over a `custom` gateway (text-fallback, native tool calling off) emitted its own DSML tool markup in the assistant text, e.g.:

```
<｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>
...
</｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>
```

ZeroClaw did not parse it and delivered it verbatim to the chat channel. Setting `native_tools = true` on the alias fixed the behavior (requests then carried `tools`, and tool results were appended to history), but the failure mode is bad when it happens: the user sees raw tool markup instead of either a tool call or an ordinary answer.

The text-fallback parsers that would need to recognize (or at least strip) this markup:

- `crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/src/lib.rs` — `parse_tool_calls` (the standalone parser crate; handles `<tool_call>` XML and JSON/GLM-style bodies). No DSML handling exists anywhere in the repo (`grep -ri dsml` returns nothing).
- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/dispatcher.rs` — `XmlToolDispatcher::parse_response` / `parse_xml_tool_calls` (the dispatcher path used by the turn loop), which scans for `<tool_call>` only.
- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/tool_call_format.rs` — `TOOL_CALL_PROTOCOL_INSTRUCTIONS`, the prompt protocol the model is told to use.

Question for maintainers: should ZeroClaw (i) parse DSML as a fallback tool-call format, (ii) strip unrecognized tool-protocol markup from channel-visible text so it is not delivered raw, or (iii) leave it to the operator to set `native_tools = true`? Note that (iii) is the current workaround, and the `tool_dispatcher = "native"` variant of the workaround is worse: forcing `"native"` without `native_tools = true` selects a dispatcher that expects native tool calls while the provider never sends `tools`, so no tool call is ever parsed and no tool result is appended to history.

## Scope

This is a discussion/design issue. No implementation is proposed here; the docs PR only corrects the `native_tools` / `tool_dispatcher` documentation to match the current code.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose holding-crate exceptions for cost limits, message times, prompt snapshot and delegate activity
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** adds six rows to the holding-crate exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, and widens one existing row, so these changes to `zeroclaw-runtime` can merge under ADR-016:
  - **Operator override of an exceeded shared cost limit** (#11589, for #11585): the budget gate, the approval-adapter timeout plumbing and its localized text, plus releasing a waiting prompt when another session approves (`approval_withdrawn`). The override itself is persisted by `CostTracker` in `zeroclaw-config` so a restart keeps it until rollover; the row's review trigger no longer lists persistence, and adds an override that applies while `cost.allow_override` is off.
  - **Cost warning-threshold notice** (#11692, for #10950): one non-blocking `BudgetWarning` turn event per turn and its RPC `session/update` forwarding.
  - **Stored message times on `session/messages`** (#11622): an optional `created_at` on `MessageEntry`, read from existing ACP session-store or Chat `SessionBackend::load_with_timestamps` records. Both storage owners stay in `zeroclaw-infra`.
  - **Per-session personality-file snapshot** (#11698, for #11696): the `Agent` renders its personality files once per session and reuses that text, so editing `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`/... no longer invalidates the provider prompt cache for every live session; plus the owner-checked `session/reload_context` RPC method that re-reads them on request. First proposed separately in #11702, now folded here.
  - **Delegate child activity forwarding** (#11730, for #10531): a foreground agentic delegate's tool calls reach the parent turn as one live `DelegateActivity` event and `session/update` notification (tool name, secret-redacted argument summary, bounded result preview), so ZeroCode can show what a running child is doing. The event type lives in `zeroclaw-api`; the runtime part is the wiring. Not persisted, not forwarded for background delegates, and no new config key.
  - **Conditional-schema root-argument recovery** (#11720, amending #11371/#11479): decode only an explicitly typed outer object or array before stopping conditional-child traversal, with focused native/fallback routing-persistence tests. The existing reference, composition, ambiguous-type, tuple-array, malformed-input, shape and nesting safeguards remain unchanged.
  - **#11456's existing row** named only `locales/en/cli.ftl`. That PR also adds its key to the es, fr, ja and zh-CN files, so the row now lists `locales/{en,es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`.

  Greptile raised the missing exception on #11692. #11589 changes the same files, and #11622 adds an RPC field, so both need the same record, and so does #11698, and so does the #10531 forwarding work. The six new rows have [Core Team approval](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11697#pullrequestreview-5513413785) on dc792941054ff6b492d876c587040a5035b0c8a0. The timestamp authority cell still needs that current approval link in place of its older ACP-only decision. The record must land before a dependent feature uses the grant. This PR changes no code.
- **Scope boundary:** this does not approve the code of #11589, #11692, #11622, #11698 or the #10531 forwarding change or #11720, and it does not generalise to other cost, budget, history, prompt or delegation work. The #11456 edit adds only the four locale paths. Each row lists the files, behavior and exclusions it covers.
- **Blast radius:** six added placement grants and one widened path list. The diff changes documentation only; the grants affect where future runtime changes may land.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `domain:architecture`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:high`, `risk:manual`, `size:XS`, `type:docs`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11589, #11692, #11622, #11698, #11456, #11585, #10950, #11696, #10531, #11720, #11708. Replaces my own draft #11702 (same row, now closed).

### What this does, simply

New features in `zeroclaw-runtime` need a recorded Core Team exception before they merge. This PR records six bounded exceptions: cost-limit overrides, cost warnings, stored message times, personality-file snapshots, delegate activity, and conditional-schema argument recovery. Each row names the allowed files, destination owner, and review condition. It also adds four translation paths to an existing exception. Each feature still needs its own implementation review.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: documentation-only change to one table.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38515111756/job/115694362723) passed on dc792941054ff6b492d876c587040a5035b0c8a0. This establishes the required-check result. The docs gates select `docs/book/src`; they do not validate this table. The targeted checks below cover its Markdown structure.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not establish the authority or scope of an exception. [The recorded approval](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11697#pullrequestreview-5513220955) includes the #11720 amendment. The later current-head confirmation includes the Chat timestamp projection. Update that timestamp authority cell, then recheck the final head and required checks before merge.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Author-reported checks: the added #11720 row passes `git diff --check` and explicit Markdown lint with `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, reporting 0 errors. The link collector tests pass and every table row has four cells.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The file lists against each PR's diff: #11589 at 225c52bb636f changes exactly the seven `zeroclaw-runtime` paths its row names, #11692 at 0bd22cf74fc4 changes exactly its four, and #11622 at dc8df7f2a25c90eb2ad0616c58a115975adac3c8 changes exactly `rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs` in runtime. The timestamp changes cover ACP history and Chat backend records. This inventory correction follows the [current-head review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11697#pullrequestreview-5521783767). #11698 at baea2ded64ad changes exactly `src/agent/{agent,prompt}.rs`, `src/tools/delegate.rs` and `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs` in runtime. #11456 adds its key to all five locale files. #11730 at 7262bec589a3 changes exactly `src/agent/tool_execution.rs`, `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`, and `src/tools/{delegate,delegate_activity,mod}.rs` in runtime. The #11720 row matches the one-file conditional-recovery repair at b92d5f20957 and its native/fallback persistence tests; it preserves the original #11436 approval without extending that approval to the amendment. The behavior claims were checked against the code: `try_send` and the turn-local latch in #11692; the period-bound grant on `CostTracker`, the per-agent exclusion and fail-closed handling in #11589.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the author reported none. The description cleanup used source, review, and CI records; it did not rerun the author's commands.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** after merge, run `git revert <landed-squash-commit>` for this PR. This withdraws the six prospective grants and the locale-path expansion. It does not undo feature code already accepted under a valid grant.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an unlisted runtime change is treated as covered, or a dependent feature relies on an authority cell that still says confirmation is required. Check the feature diff against the recorded paths and behavior; this documentation change has no runtime metric or alert.

milestone.title: v0.8.6
milestone.description:

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.8.6 runtime](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v086-runtime), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

prs.title: fix(rpc): restore principal-owned Chat sessions after restart
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **Readiness:** Draft for review, blocked on integration and provider acceptance. GitHub reports conflicts against `master`; only labeling/risk automation has run, with no required code checks reported at publication. The recovery scenario passed in both corrected Keycloak attempts, but each complete Keycloak run still passed 22/23 because a different WebSocket-opening operation timed out. Authentik remains 11/19. No combined 23/23 result or milestone closure is claimed.
- **What changed and why:**
  - A remote owner could authenticate after daemon restart but `session/new` refused their persisted Chat session because its TUI binding existed only in the old process. Recover the exact RPC Chat row only when its durable principal and agent match the authenticated caller and requested agent.
  - Keep the restored candidate unpublished until history preparation succeeds. Recheck admission, live incarnation, durable owner, current permissions, workspace and environment at the relevant effects. Administrator privileges cannot substitute for durable ownership, and recovery cannot take another live TUI binding.
  - Guard restore-time history trimming inside the SQLite transaction, and hold a database-level owner-read boundary through live publication. RPC and gateway can open separate SQLite connections, so a connection-local mutex alone cannot fence another writer.
  - Add seven regression tests covering recovery, refusals, live bindings, administrators, queued/publication changes, guarded trimming and competing SQLite writers. Existing capacity/generation controls also run in the focused validation.
- **Scope boundary:** [Incremental repair](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/compare/7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7...85af504800c9062b18bf6c34e1d4cb33562c025d) on the tested OIDC stack (four files). Chat recovery only; no ACP recovery, token-validation relaxation, provider compatibility change, schema/config migration or milestone closure. Acceptance harness changes remain on a separate fork branch.
- **Blast radius:** RPC Chat restoration and the SessionStore publication helper; additive guarded transcript replacement in SessionBackend/SQLite; SQLite owner-read effects used by restoration and messages disclosure. Owner-read effects now briefly reserve the SQLite writer boundary across their synchronous callback.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11423. Related #8289. Related #10412 for overlapping agent-ownership admission work; its migration/claim contract must be reconciled when the stack converges.

### What this does, simply

After a restart, the daemon has forgotten its live sessions but still has their transcripts and owners on disk. This repair lets an authenticated owner reopen their own Chat history without a privileged local warm-up. Another user, an administrator who does not own the row, or a caller trying to take an existing live connection is still refused. If ownership or permissions change while recovery waits, the pending request cannot publish the session or trim its history under stale authority.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` enrollment and Chat JSON-RPC (`channel=rpc`) over mTLS WebSocket; synthetic identities and disposable providers. Terminal rendering is not exercised.
- **Setup / preconditions:** SQLite session persistence, a configured OIDC provider, two mapped principals allowed to use the same agent, and nonempty Chat transcripts created through RPC. Use the pinned [acceptance harness](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/tree/1916a099b1c064a7ffb4fb938402807d3cab7828/tests/manual).
- **Steps to run:** Create and read each principal's own transcript; retain signed TUI continuity; stop and restart the actual daemon; initialize with the same principal; call `session/new` with the existing ID and agent; read its messages. Attempt foreign messages/append/new/delete from the other principal and re-read both owners afterward. The harness case is `populated-principal-storage-survives-daemon-restart`; the workflow records setup, process identity and cleanup.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Both owners recover their exact nonempty transcripts; cross-principal attempts fail and leave the owners' data unchanged.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The old live-map check refuses the owner before durable restore. The executable red control uses the pre-repair RPC files from the tested stack, rather than claiming a current-master binary run.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Fork validation run](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38602531986) verifies production-source equivalence, formatting, harness self-tests, 20 exact Rust regressions, the old-RPC regression control, four deliberate guard removals, strict Clippy for runtime/infra, and the shipped CLI build before the real-provider jobs. These are focused fork checks, not the upstream required PR gate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-master integration and the eventual landed revision are not validated by this pinned-stack run. This is not the full workspace/all-features suite, cross-platform acceptance or an independent reviewer approval. Full two-provider acceptance failed: the final Keycloak attempt passed 22/23, with `signed-reconnect-and-stale-continuity-refusal` timing out while opening a WebSocket; Authentik passed 11/19 required cases and failed 8/19. Its failed cases are `client-credentials-cli-through-mtls-rpc`, `browser-pkce-cli-through-mtls-rpc`, `device-cli-through-mtls-rpc`, `wrong-audience-denied`, `unmapped-service-denied`, `offline-lifetime-cap-denied`, `introspection-deadline-and-revoked-reconnect`, `oidc-config-removal-and-restore-keeps-remote-closed`. The connection timeouts remain unresolved; no guard or timeout was relaxed, and token-purpose validation was not weakened.
- **Separate stack follow-up:** The [sop_workshop classification report on #11410](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11410#issuecomment-6124198437) remains open. Source review supports the missing constrained-principal classification and shared SOP write path; this recovery patch does not reproduce or repair that tool-authority concern.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0.
  - `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/manual -p test_oidc_acceptance.py -v`: `Ran 23 tests`, `OK`.
  - `python3 tests/manual/oidc_exact_regressions.py`: 20 distinct named Rust tests; each selected exactly once, exit 0, `1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`.
  - `python3 tests/manual/oidc_recovery_controls.py`: old RPC owner-positive assertion fails with `-32003`; removing the final durable-owner guard, current-authority guard, trim authorization, or database transaction each causes a named assertion failure. Each control requires exit 101, one executed test, zero ignored, and an actual test failure. The old control corrects two test-only fixture details while retaining old RPC production code. Exact source bytes are restored afterward.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-infra --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: exit 0 on restored source.
  - `cargo build --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw`: exit 0.
  - Real-provider harness: Keycloak 22/23 required cases passed; Authentik 11/19. Counts include setup and cleanup. Both jobs verify the same binary artifact and SHA256. Required inventories, case order and timeouts are unchanged. The restart assertion now requires the exact expected refusal at each transport/durable-owner state and no success result; the previous assertion wrongly required FORBIDDEN before the foreign session was live. That failed run is retained, and all eight observed refusal codes are recorded.
  - Retry disclosure: the first corrected Keycloak run passed recovery but failed `unmapped-service-denied` on WebSocket opening timeout. One unchanged Keycloak-only retry reran all 23 cases against the same binary artifact: recovery and that unmapped-service case passed, but `signed-reconnect-and-stale-continuity-refusal` timed out at connection opening. Build/regression and Authentik receipts are from attempt 1; the final Keycloak result is attempt 2. Both full Keycloak runs remain failed; their cases are not combined into a green result. The timeout root cause has not been established.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source self re-review traced identity, admission/constructor waits, final publication, history trimming, backend factory wiring, lock order, owner/agent restamping and unchanged live TUI policy. A separate receipt verifier reconciles raw named-test logs, failure reasons, provider inventories, job conclusions, exact heads and binary artifact upload/download digests. This is not an independent human review.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output from CLI enrollment and daemon JSON-RPC receipts in the real-provider harness. No layout or renderer changes; protocol transition evidence is recorded below.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Production `85af504800c9062b18bf6c34e1d4cb33562c025d`, harness `1916a099b1c064a7ffb4fb938402807d3cab7828`. [Build and provider logs](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38602531986) and artifacts `oidc-current-regressions`, `oidc-keycloak-evidence`, `oidc-authentik-evidence`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Old owner recovery: `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` / `-32003`. Repaired Keycloak case: `populated-principal-storage-survives-daemon-restart` passed with two nonempty owner transcripts, unchanged private memory and bidirectional foreign-access refusal. No visual rendering claim.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Actual daemon restart now permits durable Chat owner recovery; ownership/authority changes at tested effects prevent unauthorized publication or history mutation. Competing SQLite writes are blocked until the guarded effect ends, then permitted afterward.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust tests were not used; Linux hosted execution supplies the Rust and real-provider receipts. Full workspace and cross-platform checks remain upstream integration gates. Earlier missing-component, fixture compile and superseded/cancelled runs are retained and do not count as final validation; an early red control that failed before the owner-positive assertion was rejected and corrected.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes — authenticated remote principals can recover their own persisted Chat sessions when no live binding exists. Exact durable ownership, requested agent, current authority and live absence are required; administrator status cannot bypass ownership.
- New external network calls? No in production. Disposable provider calls are validation-only on the separate fork harness.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; test identities and transcripts are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Recovery admits a previously blocked path to private history. Refusal, allowed-control, controlled-race, mutation and real-provider tests cover its ownership boundaries; legacy NULL-owner and unsupported stores fail closed.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for clients depending on the exact denial code from `session/new` for a missing-live foreign/legacy record: the existing `FORBIDDEN` code may now be returned where the live-map check previously returned `SESSION_NOT_OWNED`. Both remain opaque refusals. Persisted formats and successful existing live-session behavior are unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Treat both `FORBIDDEN` (`-32012`) and `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` (`-32003`) as refusals; do not infer record existence from either. No database migration or configuration change is required. Authenticated recovery requires an already owned SQLite Chat row; ownerless histories are not adopted. Custom backends must implement guarded conversation replacement to support over-cap remote recovery; the default refuses that write.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed merge/squash commit with `git revert <landed-commit>`. Do not delete or rewrite durable transcripts. This returns remote restart recovery to the prior refusal and removes the new guards with the repair.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** An owner cannot reopen a known Chat session after restart; restore returns ownership/busy/internal errors; logs report `Failed to authorize session restore` or `Failed to persist Chat restore trim`. Check the supported local recovery path and retained transcripts before retrying; do not weaken ownership to force recovery.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — no PR is superseded.

prs.title: fix(oidc): preserve reserved characters in enrollment credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

Current head: 7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7.

Depends on #11422. Related #8289. Base branch: `master`; the prerequisite stack is retained.

OAuth enrollment sent literal client IDs and secrets through HTTP Basic. For a client ID such as `zc-service: +/%`, a conforming identity provider receives the wrong credentials. Encode each component before Basic serialization, as required by [RFC 6749 section 2.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749.html#section-2.3.1).

Reuse the existing introspection component encoder for device authorization, device polling, and client-credentials enrollment. Keep reqwest's sensitive Authorization header handling. The supplemental diff is limited to that existing helper's visibility, the enrollment caller, and one HTTP-boundary regression. Public clients and browser code exchange keep their existing form authentication paths.

### What this does, simply

Service and device enrollment now preserve punctuation in configured OAuth credentials, so valid credentials arrive at the provider intact. This changes request encoding, not which identities or permissions the daemon accepts.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Register a disposable confidential Keycloak client whose ID includes a colon, space, plus, slash, and percent sign; configure its issuer, client ID, audience, and secret in an OIDC entry.
- **Interface exercised:** `cli`, through `zeroclaw oidc token <alias>` and the provider's real token endpoint.
- **Before:** The CLI fails client authentication although a correctly form-encoded Basic request with the same credentials succeeds.
- **After:** The CLI prints exactly one access-token line. Do not paste that token into review evidence.
- **Automated command:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::auth_provider::enrollment::tests::enrollment_basic_credentials_round_trip_on_every_endpoint -- --exact`

### How I tested

- **Current integration:** Head `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7` retains its previous published head `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231`, pinned master `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293`, and refreshed adjacent prerequisite `4535e321f4d65cf092903522540a4df66754dea7` as ancestors. The six draft refreshes were pushed atomically by ordinary fast-forward; contributor histories are retained. The old-to-new changes are six upstream files, with only independent Fluent additions requiring resolution. The separate #11234 author-adoption candidate is not imported into these drafts.
- **Current focused validation:** The [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on exact source `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`: formatting; `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests`; config 7, storage 209, RPC 878, authority 26, principal 92, and steering 15 tests, all with zero failures/ignored; and Clippy for runtime/infra/config with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`. Fourteen selected RPC regressions each have exactly one passing record. Filters overlap; these are per-command results, not a unique-test total or full-workspace run. The separate superseded canonical-admission job in that workflow failed compilation; its failure is not hidden by this successful combined-stack job.
- **Current upstream CI:** Fresh required checks run on the published head above. Their exact status and the landing decision are recorded in the [coordination handoff](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408#issuecomment-6023921255). A passed fork job is not a substitute for those checks or independent Core review.
- **Adversarial review:** The independent refresh review verified all six old heads and canonical `d5df4214` ancestry, every refreshed stack link, byte identity with master for the five non-Fluent upstream files, and exactly one occurrence of each retained SOP/timeout Fluent key. No actionable finding remained in this bounded refresh review. The broader prior security review remains recorded on its earlier source, not represented as a new full sweep.
- **Historical sensitivity evidence:** [Earlier validation](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) on `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231` passed enrollment 46/46 and demonstrated intended failures when append guarding or steering revocation was removed. These tests were not rerun as mutation tests in the current six-draft refresh; the relevant OIDC implementation is unchanged by this upstream-only refresh.
- **Limits:** Local Rust execution remains blocked by Windows Application Control (OS 4551), without a bypass. No production deployment, provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, or milestone closure occurred. The earlier Keycloak 20/20 and Authentik 10/18 result does not certify this integration. Required CI, Core review, and a safe prerequisite landing decision remain distinct gates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; existing enrollment endpoints and redirect refusal are retained.
- Secrets/tokens/credentials handling changed? Yes. Correctly form-encode the two Basic components before reqwest serializes them; retain its sensitive-header marking. Credentials stay out of the form for confidential Basic clients.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No. Tests use synthetic credentials and disposable providers.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Inherited session compatibility:** The #11408 prerequisite requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.
- Backward compatible? Yes for conforming OAuth providers. Plain credentials retain the same wire bytes. Nonconforming providers that expect unencoded reserved characters may reject the corrected request.
- Config/env/CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Retry enrollment with the existing configured credentials.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** Revert `86eab94be1` and then `be5156721c` after integrating the prerequisite stack. This reintroduces reserved-character enrollment failures.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Device or service enrollment returns a provider client-authentication error for otherwise valid credentials.

## Supersede Attribution

Not a replacement. Prerequisite contributor commits are retained through #11422.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: fix(auth): guard private SOP access and configure commits
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master. Depends on #11410 and #11266. Prerequisite contributor commits are retained. Review this PR's supplemental changes separately from its cumulative stack. Current head: fc96815d43abdf01f877be73f725b60a3d68f1ab.
- **What changed and why:** Enforce the recorded principal, agent, namespace, and tenant at SOP status, count, approval, and advance boundaries, including factory and pipeline captures and audit-disabled registries. Resolve direct completion audit through the original run owner. Retain unowned operator assistance. Restrict global RPC run views to administrators and recheck after engine contention before projecting either success or a missing-run error. Preserve the actual-lock-wait configure regression and integrate the complete prerequisite stack.
- **Additional boundary repairs:** Commit session/configure overrides and Agent/provider state atomically after the final incarnation and live credential/owner checks. Preserve the existing coarse configure permission contract, including authorized controls.
- **Scope boundary:** OIDC security hardening and regression coverage. Two-provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, and milestone closure remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** Private SOP reads and transitions, audit persistence, registry owner routing, global RPC run reads, and atomic configure publication under current credential authority. This PR now includes production privacy repairs as well as inherited private-pipeline and subagent behavior.
- **Linked issues:** Related #11127, #11239, and #8289. No milestone closure is claimed.

### What this does, simply

Owned tools can access only their exact private plane; ownerless legacy runs are not public. Global RPC run views require admin and remote WSS detail remains refused. Unowned operator tools can assist without copying audit data into shared memory.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, review this exact head and the combined #11423 integration; rerun validation after any subsequent dependency or conflict-resolution change.
- **Interface exercised:** Real RPC handlers and factory-built tool registries with synthetic principals, temporary databases, refusal assertions, and successful owner/operator controls. Storage tests use actual SQLite contention.
- **Setup:** A permitted Rust build environment with the repository's pinned toolchain and locked dependencies.
- **Expected:** Unauthorized requests have no new run, provider, mutation, transcript, or cross-owner audit effect; unchanged authorized controls succeed.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib sop_
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
```

### How I tested

- **Current integration:** Head `fc96815d43abdf01f877be73f725b60a3d68f1ab` retains its previous published head `8f7ecfaad29dcf1f6f465831938a31990d648bc3`, pinned master `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293`, and refreshed adjacent prerequisite `c2ad7a8e62d22accbe13387927b8f6869ed46baa` as ancestors. The six draft refreshes were pushed atomically by ordinary fast-forward; contributor histories are retained. The old-to-new changes are six upstream files, with only independent Fluent additions requiring resolution. The separate #11234 author-adoption candidate is not imported into these drafts.
- **Current focused validation:** The [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on exact source `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`: formatting; `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests`; config 7, storage 209, RPC 878, authority 26, principal 92, and steering 15 tests, all with zero failures/ignored; and Clippy for runtime/infra/config with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`. Fourteen selected RPC regressions each have exactly one passing record. Filters overlap; these are per-command results, not a unique-test total or full-workspace run. The separate superseded canonical-admission job in that workflow failed compilation; its failure is not hidden by this successful combined-stack job.
- **Current upstream CI:** Fresh required checks run on the published head above. Their exact status and the landing decision are recorded in the [coordination handoff](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408#issuecomment-6023921255). A passed fork job is not a substitute for those checks or independent Core review.
- **Adversarial review:** The independent refresh review verified all six old heads and canonical `d5df4214` ancestry, every refreshed stack link, byte identity with master for the five non-Fluent upstream files, and exactly one occurrence of each retained SOP/timeout Fluent key. No actionable finding remained in this bounded refresh review. The broader prior security review remains recorded on its earlier source, not represented as a new full sweep.
- **Historical sensitivity evidence:** [Earlier validation](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) on `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231` passed enrollment 46/46 and demonstrated intended failures when append guarding or steering revocation was removed. These tests were not rerun as mutation tests in the current six-draft refresh; the relevant OIDC implementation is unchanged by this upstream-only refresh.
- **Limits:** Local Rust execution remains blocked by Windows Application Control (OS 4551), without a bypass. No production deployment, provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, or milestone closure occurred. The earlier Keycloak 20/20 and Authentik 10/18 result does not certify this integration. Required CI, Core review, and a safe prerequisite landing decision remain distinct gates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem scope? No. The changed boundaries reduce access and retain existing operator controls.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets or credential formats changed? No. Authority is resolved from the existing canonical accepted policy.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No; principals, payloads, and workspaces are synthetic.
- New prompt-injection source? No. Private run output and captured tools are treated as protected data/effects.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Inherited session compatibility:** The #11408 prerequisite requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.
- **Backward compatible?** No for callers relying on the previously unsafe access described above. Owned tools can access only their exact private plane; ownerless legacy runs are not public. Global RPC run views require admin and remote WSS detail remains refused. Unowned operator tools can assist without copying audit data into shared memory.
- **Config/env/CLI surface changed?** No new settings, flags, or schema migration.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade:** Review the restrictions before rollout; keep this stack together and use existing operator workflows for refused administrative operations.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** Revert the new repair commits with `git revert aaa681d085 f455ba115b 758418ba73 c52a1afc7e 662acf5fae` on the integration branch, resolving conflicts against later stack changes. Preserve the canonical authorization dependency. A rollback reopens the corresponding security boundary and requires explicit assessment.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable symptoms:** Unexpected permission refusals, SOP store-busy errors, missing owner audit records, or failed targeted/parallel runtime tests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not a replacement. Depends on the PRs above; original contributor commits are retained. Overlapping session authorization resolves to #11234's implementation.

prs.title: fix(auth): guard cron writes and contain unscoped execution
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master. Depends on #11409 and #11230; canonical effect authorization is retained from #11234. Prerequisite contributor commits are retained. Review this PR's supplemental changes separately from its cumulative stack. Current head: 754cbb2a859efff35371300899e019c789703cc6.
- **What changed and why:** Withhold session-data, cron, and peer execution tools from non-admin sessions and captured aliases; propagate withholding into retained delegates. Patch cron jobs inside an IMMEDIATE SQLite transaction, reload the actual row, then resolve current authority and shell policy and hold the lease through commit. Reject queued demotions, grant revocations, owner changes, and shell-to-agent changes. Reconcile inherited overlapping session code to the canonical #11234 implementation.
- **SOP workshop follow-up:** Address the [reported permission gap](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11410#issuecomment-6124198437) by marking `sop_workshop` as requiring an unrestricted principal. Its `apply` action persists shared SOP definitions whose later execution does not carry the caller's ceilings. Existing factory, alias and delegate filtering now withholds it. This follow-up changes six production lines; the rest is regression coverage.
- **Additional boundary repairs:** Include the latest SOP decision/config-lock repairs and factory ownership binding through the declared stack; no additional cron behavior changes in this follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** OIDC security hardening and regression coverage. Two-provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, and milestone closure remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** Cron persistence, RPC patch authorization, session tool surfaces, shared SOP authoring, and dependency integration.
- **Linked issues:** Related #11127, #11239, and #8289. No milestone closure is claimed.

### What this does, simply

Non-admins lose principal-unaware execution tools. Agent cron modification and triggering require admin. Shell patch authorization is checked again after writer contention; existing scheduled jobs continue. Shared SOP authoring also requires operator reach, including when invoked through a renamed skill alias.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Review the incremental change from `c2ad7a8e62d22accbe13387927b8f6869ed46baa` to `754cbb2a859efff35371300899e019c789703cc6`; rerun after dependency integration or conflict resolution.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** RPC Chat/ACP handlers and real tool dispatch, using synthetic peer-credential principals, temporary SQLite stores and SOP files. These are runtime tests, not browser/TUI presentation tests or a fresh OIDC-provider acceptance run.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Locked dependencies and Rust 1.98.0 for the recorded Linux run. SOP procedural memory is enabled in the regression fixtures; a real builtin skill alias targets `sop_workshop`.
- **Steps to run:** Run the exact tests below. The [fork-only harness](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/3256b766e85c125865e69045f305d0ec1390a97c/tests/manual/oidc_workshop_regressions.py) lists all 11 tests and four required negative controls.
- **Expected on this branch:** Non-admin direct/alias calls are refused without changing proposals, writing SOP files or reloading a new SOP. Administrator/local-operator controls apply successfully. Demotion while a prompt waits removes both entry points. Synchronous, parallel and background delegates omit both while ordinary tools remain usable.
- **Prior behavior:** On this PR's previous head, the direct and queued-demotion controls actually applied shared SOPs and the delegate exposed the workshop. Removing alias flag forwarding also permits an alias to apply. This A/B proof uses the previous PR head with the new tests; current-master integration is still pending and is not represented as an executed A/B run.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::principal_sop_workshop_refuses_direct_and_alias_effects -- --exact
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::principal_sop_workshop_queued_demotion_prevents_persistence -- --exact
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_delegate_children -- --exact
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests -- -D warnings
```

### How I tested

- **Current source and CI evidence:** [Run 38633025640](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38633025640) passed on validation commit `3256b766e85c125865e69045f305d0ec1390a97c`. The job verifies the entire source tree matches production `754cbb2a859efff35371300899e019c789703cc6`, excluding only its two fork-only harness files. No harness file is added to this PR.
- **Commands run and output:** All 11 distinct named runtime tests each report `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`. Three old-code runs and one alias-forwarding mutant each report exactly one executed failure with the intended assertion; compilation errors and empty filters do not qualify. Original source bytes are restored before the passing tests. Formatting and `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests -- -D warnings` passed. Raw logs and JSON records are in the run's `oidc-workshop-regressions` artifact.
- **Coverage:** New direct/alias tests cover Chat and ACP with wildcard selectors, named tool selectors and a restricted agent selector. A real native-tool prompt tests queued demotion and an unchanged administrator. Existing delegate coverage now includes the actual workshop and its alias in captured registries, with an unrestricted positive control. The remaining focused tests cover normal SOP creation/application, factory registration, alias withholding, independent delegates and existing session-data demotion behavior.
- **Preserved failing evidence:** [Run 38630921611](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38630921611) verified all four negative controls but then failed because the new ACP fixture had no session store. The fixture was corrected to use the existing SQLite-backed Chat/ACP helper; the production fix was unchanged. Only the corrected run is claimed as passing.
- **Adversarial pass and re-review:** Rechecked classification through factory construction, RPC narrowing, skill/Arc wrappers, retained delegate registries and final SOP writes/reload. Separately reconciled the raw test inventory, failure markers and source pins after the passing run. No further actionable issue was found in this bounded self-review; this is not independent reviewer approval.
- **Historical stack evidence:** The earlier [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`, including RPC/storage/authority/principal/steering filters and Clippy. Those filters overlap, and they are not current-head or full-workspace results. [Earlier enrollment and mutation evidence](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) remains pinned to `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231`.
- **Known CI/integration gap:** Fresh required upstream checks and Core review remain separate from the fork job. The PR currently conflicts with master; downstream draft heads do not automatically contain this update. Reconcile the stack and rerun the required integration gates before landing.
- **Beyond CI:** Local source/receipt re-review and whitespace checks passed. Windows Rust test execution remains blocked by Application Control (OS 4551); no bypass was used. No full workspace run, fresh real-provider run, deployment or migration/rollback rehearsal is claimed by this follow-up.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation change. The tested revision and exact tool-dispatch results are recorded above. Provider acceptance and OIDC/v0.9 milestone closure remain open.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem scope? No. The changed boundaries reduce access and retain existing operator controls.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets or credential formats changed? No. Authority is resolved from the existing canonical accepted policy.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No; principals, payloads, and workspaces are synthetic.
- New prompt-injection source? No. Private run output and captured tools are treated as protected data/effects.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Inherited session compatibility:** The #11408 prerequisite requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.
- **Backward compatible?** No for callers relying on the previously unsafe access described above. Non-admins lose principal-unaware execution tools. Agent cron modification and triggering require admin. Shell patch authorization is checked again after writer contention; existing scheduled jobs continue.
- **SOP workshop compatibility:** Non-admin sessions lose the entire `sop_workshop` tool and its aliases, including read/proposal-management actions, even with wildcard selectors. Use an existing administrator/local-operator workflow for shared SOP authoring. No action-specific exemption or new grant is introduced.
- **Config/env/CLI surface changed?** No new settings, flags, or schema migration.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade:** Review the restrictions before rollout; keep this stack together and use existing operator workflows for refused administrative operations.

## Rollback

- **SOP follow-up rollback:** `git revert 754cbb2a859efff35371300899e019c789703cc6 d8bbd14ffea9e1c48fc4621a9df9ba1321a1ec1f` reverts the fixture correction and classification repair on an integration branch. Reverting the classification reopens the shared-SOP permission gap.
- **Earlier repair rollback:** Revert the new repair commits with `git revert 44770c946d` on the integration branch, resolving conflicts against later stack changes. Preserve the canonical authorization dependency. A rollback reopens the corresponding security boundary and requires explicit assessment.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable symptoms:** Unexpected permission refusals, SOP store-busy errors, missing owner audit records, or failed targeted/parallel runtime tests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not a replacement. Depends on the PRs above; original contributor commits are retained. Overlapping session authorization resolves to #11234's implementation.
