prs.title: fix(rpc): guard SOP and session effects with current authority
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master. Depends on #11220 and #11234. Prerequisite contributor commits are retained. Review this PR's supplemental changes separately from its cumulative stack. Current head: c9a193ceba32224187e79fbfd8d3ffc16a19d848.
- **What changed and why:** Require administrator authority for SOP RPC start and decisions, including wildcard non-admins. Hold canonical current authority through synchronous effects and use a shared-data store view that immediately refuses connection or SQLite writer contention. Preserve configured operator execution and the existing SOP tool markers.
- **Additional boundary repairs:** Hold current authority before SOP decision lookup, broker outcomes, and final overlay disclosure. Capture the real selection with a recursive read so a queued config writer cannot deadlock an already-held SOP effect lease.
- **Session effect repairs:** Guard append and rename at the durable storage effect, retain live Agent/generation/TUI ownership through publication, and authorize `session/abort` after the real cancellation lock. Revoke queued remote steering when its TUI binding changes, including an A-to-B-to-A transfer. Keep create-only run-once admission distinct from resume and preserve its published generation; preflight the existing close permission and report a late cleanup failure after a completed turn.
- **Scope boundary:** OIDC security hardening and regression coverage. Two-provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, and milestone closure remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** SOP RPC dispatch, run-store contention, session storage and live publication, `session/abort`, remote steering, and transient run-once lifecycle.
- **Linked issues:** Related #11127, #11239, and #8289. No milestone closure is claimed.

### What this does, simply

Non-admin SOP RPC execution is now refused. Retry an administrator request when the SOP store is busy; ordinary background store timeouts are unchanged. Model-visible wildcard containment also depends on #11410. Session writes, `session/abort` and queued steering now refuse stale authority or transport ownership at their final effects. Run-once reports a late close failure instead of silently returning success.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, review this exact head and the combined #11423 integration; rerun validation after any subsequent dependency or conflict-resolution change.
- **Interface exercised:** Real RPC handlers and factory-built tool registries with synthetic principals, temporary databases, refusal assertions, and successful owner/operator controls. Storage tests use actual SQLite contention.
- **Setup:** A permitted Rust build environment with the repository's pinned toolchain and locked dependencies.
- **Expected:** Unauthorized requests have no new run, provider, mutation, transcript, or cross-owner audit effect; unchanged authorized controls succeed.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib session_
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
```

### How I tested

- **Current integration:** Head `c9a193ceba32224187e79fbfd8d3ffc16a19d848` retains its previous published head `2e6c2b7835abe169fb0cbaf6ecceafb0e21faefc`, pinned master `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293`, and refreshed adjacent prerequisite `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293` as ancestors. The six draft refreshes were pushed atomically by ordinary fast-forward; contributor histories are retained. The old-to-new changes are six upstream files, with only independent Fluent additions requiring resolution. The separate #11234 author-adoption candidate is not imported into these drafts.
- **Current focused validation:** The [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on exact source `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`: formatting; `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests`; config 7, storage 209, RPC 878, authority 26, principal 92, and steering 15 tests, all with zero failures/ignored; and Clippy for runtime/infra/config with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`. Fourteen selected RPC regressions each have exactly one passing record. Filters overlap; these are per-command results, not a unique-test total or full-workspace run. The separate superseded canonical-admission job in that workflow failed compilation; its failure is not hidden by this successful combined-stack job.
- **Current upstream CI:** Fresh required checks run on the published head above. Their exact status and the landing decision are recorded in the [coordination handoff](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408#issuecomment-6023921255). A passed fork job is not a substitute for those checks or independent Core review.
- **Adversarial review:** The independent refresh review verified all six old heads and canonical `d5df4214` ancestry, every refreshed stack link, byte identity with master for the five non-Fluent upstream files, and exactly one occurrence of each retained SOP/timeout Fluent key. No actionable finding remained in this bounded refresh review. The broader prior security review remains recorded on its earlier source, not represented as a new full sweep.
- **Historical sensitivity evidence:** [Earlier validation](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) on `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231` passed enrollment 46/46 and demonstrated intended failures when append guarding or steering revocation was removed. These tests were not rerun as mutation tests in the current six-draft refresh; the relevant OIDC implementation is unchanged by this upstream-only refresh.
- **Limits:** Local Rust execution remains blocked by Windows Application Control (OS 4551), without a bypass. No production deployment, provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, or milestone closure occurred. The earlier Keycloak 20/20 and Authentik 10/18 result does not certify this integration. Required CI, Core review, and a safe prerequisite landing decision remain distinct gates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem scope? No. The changed boundaries reduce access and retain existing operator controls.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets or credential formats changed? No. Authority is resolved from the existing canonical accepted policy.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No; principals, payloads, and workspaces are synthetic.
- New prompt-injection source? No. Private run output and captured tools are treated as protected data/effects.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Session compatibility:** This PR requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.
- **Backward compatible?** No for callers relying on the previously unsafe access described above. Non-admin SOP RPC execution is now refused. Retry an administrator request when the SOP store is busy; ordinary background store timeouts are unchanged. Model-visible wildcard containment also depends on #11410.
- **Config/env/CLI surface changed?** No new settings, flags, or schema migration.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade:** Review the restrictions before rollout; keep this stack together and use existing operator workflows for refused administrative operations.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback path:** Revert the supplemental session/SOP repair commits on an integration branch in reverse dependency order, preserving contributor prerequisites and upstream #11576. Re-run the denied/permitted authority tests before any rollback deployment; reverting these repairs reopens the corresponding boundaries. This refresh does not claim a completed rollback rehearsal.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable symptoms:** Unexpected permission refusals, SOP store-busy errors, missing owner audit records, or failed targeted/parallel runtime tests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not a replacement. Depends on the PRs above; original contributor commits are retained. Overlapping session authorization resolves to #11234's implementation.

prs.title: feat(a2a): extract A2A protocol core into a dedicated zeroclaw-a2a crate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extract the A2A protocol core out of `zeroclaw-api` / `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` into a single `zeroclaw-a2a` crate, so the wire model, outbound client, and inbound protocol handling have one ownership home instead of four, and the protocol layer doesn't depend on any host config module.
  - Follow the official `a2a-rs` layering: the crate defines `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource` as host-implemented seams and keeps its own config types, letting hosts adapt + inject.
  - Wire moves from `zeroclaw_api::a2a_wire` to `zeroclaw_a2a::wire`; `api` stops re-exporting it.
  - Hosts adapt through `A2aPeerSourceHost` (implements the protocol-layer `A2aPeerSource` over the host's **live** config handle) and the standalone `a2a_router` defaults closed to task operations.
- **Scope boundary:** Organization-only extraction — no new A2A protocol capability, no config-field change. Streaming and inbound task management are explicitly out of scope. The extraction preserves the pre-existing live/lazy host behavior (see below); it does **not** intentionally change runtime behavior.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` loses its `a2a_wire` module (import sites moved); consumers of `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` / `zeroclaw-runtime` see no tool, route, or behavior change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #3566; Implements (RFC) #11254

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's A2A support previously lived in four crates, split by hosting crate rather than by protocol: the wire model in `zeroclaw-api`, the outbound client in `zeroclaw-tools`, and the inbound surface in `zeroclaw-gateway`. That made every A2A extension thread re-export paths across multiple manifests. This PR consolidates the A2A protocol core into one `zeroclaw-a2a` crate whose layout mirrors the official a2a-rs SDK, and keeps host-coupled glue (the 4 `a2a_*` tools, gateway card building + auth) in the host crates, adapted through `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource`.

### Live configuration ownership (review follow-up)

The first revision of this PR snapshotted peers, decrypted tokens, and proxy policy at client-construction time. That regressed the behavior the pre-extraction client had via its live config handle: removing a peer, rotating a token, tightening private-host policy, or changing the proxy no longer took effect on a retained agent, and one peer with a corrupt credential disabled all four tools.

This revision restores live/lazy semantics through a single host-implemented seam, `A2aPeerSource`, consulted on **every** call:

- `peers()` returns the current peers with **raw** (undecrypted) token fields — no snapshot.
- `resolve_token()` decrypts **lazily**, for the resolved peer only — one broken credential can no longer disable the whole tool set.
- `proxy_policy()` is resolved per call, including the `tool.a2a` service-scope check, so a proxy scoped to another service (or disabled while its URL is configured) does not block A2A.
- `settings()` reads card-cache TTL / response cap / SSRF allowlists live.

The protocol crate depends on none of the host's config modules (it holds an `Arc<dyn A2aPeerSource>`), preserving the RFC's config boundary while keeping resolution host-owned and current-at-use.

## Testing (required)

### How I tested

- `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean, no warnings.
- `cargo +1.98.0 doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` (Rustdoc warnings gate) — clean.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a` → `94 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a` → `34 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client` → `36 passed; 0 failed` (2 ignored = cross-harness external-peer tests)
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib a2a` → passed

The A2A conformance/security tests moved with the code. Tests that had been dropped during the extraction were restored, and new boundary tests were added for the host adapter: lazy token decryption (encrypted / missing-dir / literal), disabled and other-service proxy scopes, live config reload (a removed peer disappears, settings follow), and the standalone catalog's `catalog` interface marker.

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — organization-only extraction; behavior matches the pre-extraction client.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a --lib
  test result: ok. 94 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a
  test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client
  test result: ok. 36 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The host source reads live config per call (verified by a reload test: publishing a config with a peer added/removed is reflected immediately); proxy policy honors the `tool.a2a` service scope; a standalone `a2a_router` rejects task injection without a configured admission check; the standalone catalog emits the `catalog` interface marker so a single published alias is not mistaken for a single agent by `select_interface`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface change)

### CI note

All checks affected by this PR are green (Lint incl. the Rustdoc gate, Format, Clippy incl. Windows-targeted, MSRV, every `Check`, every `Test`). The `Security` job is red on `cargo deny`, reporting newly published rustls advisories — `RUSTSEC-2026-0346/0347/0348/0349` against `rustls 0.23.45`, the version `master` also pins. That is a repository-level dependency finding (an upstream rustls bump or a `deny.toml` ignore), independent of this change and reproducible on `master`; it is not introduced by or fixable within this PR.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No behavior change.** Peer-token decryption stays host-owned (`A2aPeerSourceHost`, via the canonical `SecretStore`) and is now performed lazily per resolved peer; the protocol layer only applies `${VAR}` interpolation to the plaintext it is handed.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>` is the plan. Organization-only extraction with no data/config surface; reverting the merge restores the prior layout.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A (no `Supersedes #` used).

prs.title: test(hardware): pass arduino-cli flags through the Windows fake
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The advisory Windows job always runs `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-hardware --features hardware --lib`, whatever a PR touches. Two `arduino_upload` tests fail there, so every `ci:windows` run has been red since at least 2026-09-26, whatever the PR under test changed.
  - `fake_cli_success_runs_all_stages_and_cleans_workspace`: the Windows fake `arduino-cli` is a PowerShell script whose `param()` block uses `[Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)]`. That attribute makes it an advanced script. Windows PowerShell then reads the upload stage's `-p` as the abbreviated `-PipelineVariable` common parameter and swallows the port value with it, so the logged call never starts with `upload -p`. The fake now reads its arguments from `$args` in a plain script, where `-p` passes through unchanged. The product command line (`upload -p <port> --fqbn <fqbn> <sketch>`) is unchanged and correct.
  - `failed_preflight_does_not_compile_or_upload`: PowerShell's `Add-Content` ends each logged line with CRLF on Windows, and the test compared the log with `"version\n"` byte for byte. It now compares the logged calls line by line, like the neighboring assertions.
- **Scope boundary:** The fixture repair is test-only. Current signed successor adds one temporary PR11364-only Windows evidence workflow; all eight Arduino bodies, the fake/product source and operation deadlines remain unchanged. The workflow uses its own job/pipe lifetime and bounded evidence handling; it changes no production tool behavior. Its CI execution and artifact-export surface require high-risk review.
- **Blast radius:** The original two fixture expectations plus the temporary qualification workflow. Ordinary required CI and the existing Windows advisory continue independently.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11425, #11630 and #7432; the existing coordination trackers and original PR history are retained.

### What this does, simply

The Arduino upload tool is tested against a fake `arduino-cli` that records how it was called. On Windows the fake is a PowerShell script, and PowerShell quietly took the tool's `-p` (port) flag for one of its own options, so the record never showed the upload call the test looks for. The record also ended lines with Windows line endings, which one test did not expect. The fake now passes every flag through untouched, and the test compares lines rather than raw bytes. Nothing about the real tool changes; this only stops two tests from failing on every Windows run.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on Windows only; the Unix fake is a shell script and was never affected.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None user-facing; hardware tool unit tests with a fake CLI.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Windows machine with the MSVC toolchain and Windows PowerShell, or the `ci:windows` label on this PR.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-hardware --features hardware --lib arduino_upload::`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** All `arduino_upload` tests pass.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `fake_cli_success_runs_all_stages_and_cleans_workspace` and `failed_preflight_does_not_compile_or_upload` fail as quoted below.

### How I tested

**Current signed revision:** `d0d57ff3cd19ac55a55f5c52aef005f95e0a172d`, tree `4749125a85b3b4869fbbafe6a53ce1a796cbe56b`, direct parent `de4e14f4ca752b34804911e293d018095969d76f`. The one-workflow change suppresses nextest payload output with `--failure-output never --success-output never` and permits a bounded failure summary only after complete capture, owned-process cleanup and a successful private decision write/flush/close. The separate finalizer checks the current source, selection, executables, command result and private completion marker. Unknown or incomplete transcripts retain the minimum failure receipt. Success still requires all eight named cases to pass. The original Arduino source, operation deadlines, production command and workflow budgets remain unchanged.

On the dedicated Linux dev-box, Python 3.12.3 executed all 56 unique `PR11364_SYNTHETIC_PASS` checks and reported `PR11364_SYNTHETIC_COUNT 56`, using the exact candidate helper. These are in-memory parser, write/close, handoff and validator controls. They do not exercise Windows process ownership, real nextest output or the eight Arduino cases.

The [current exact-eight Windows run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38665274393), attempt 1, is in progress; preparation passed and build/list has started. [Current Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38665274363) and the [broad Windows advisory](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38665274217) remain separate. The Quality Gate Security job has reported the shared Rustls advisories addressed by #11736. No current eight-pass or full Windows acceptance is claimed. This PR remains draft with the outstanding human review unchanged.

**Retained prior test failure:** [run 38627742015](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38627742015), attempt 1, on `de4e14f` completed FAILURE. Setup/list succeeded, then test reported `E_COMMAND_EXIT` and verification reported `E_PREVIOUS_STEP`. Its named results, numeric child exit and underlying cause were not published by the minimum-failure contract and remain unknown. The current diagnostic change is not a demonstrated repair of that failure.

**Retained prior setup failure:** [run 38606615454](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38606615454) on `679dcd5` failed with `E_NEXTEST_VERSION`, before list/build/test: zero named controls judged. Its private banner remains unknown. Pinned nextest source documents `-V` as one line and `--version` as multiline, which supports this query correction without proving the old returned text or fixture startup cause. Prior ordinary QG also failed the shared Rustls Security requirement; #11736 remains a separate repair. No blind retry or historical execution credit is claimed.

**Actions allowlist impact:** Every `uses:` source is pinned and matches existing `actions/*`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@*` and `Swatinem/rust-cache@*` patterns; no expansion or settings change is needed. Logical metadata/build/test deadlines remain, but source review does not guarantee a hard per-kernel-call deadline or actual Windows cleanup.

**Historical author-reported fixture evidence below:** These original local and older-hosted claims retain their revisions; release review did not execute them locally and supplies no transfer to the new workflow/head.


- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required jobs build and run the Unix side of these tests. The advisory Windows job that this PR opts into runs the changed PowerShell fake.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The Windows fake runs only in the opt-in advisory job. This Mac has no PowerShell and cannot build for Windows (`ring`'s build script needs the MSVC and Windows SDK headers).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Before, on Windows: [run 36796530916, job 110161368722](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36796530916/job/110161368722) (head `5b2798892a`, 2026-10-01); identical in [36727402219](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36727402219/job/109928083263) and [36709065808](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36709065808/job/109866477705).

  ```text
  Summary [   4.963s] 179 tests run: 177 passed, 2 failed, 1 skipped

  panicked at crates\zeroclaw-hardware\src\peripherals\arduino_upload.rs:655:9:
  assertion `left == right` failed
    left: "version\r\n"
   right: "version\n"

  panicked at crates\zeroclaw-hardware\src\peripherals\arduino_upload.rs:619:9:
  assertion failed: calls.lines().any(|line| line.starts_with("upload -p "))
  ```

  The same run shows `upload:eof` in the stdin log and `result.success`, so the fake did run the upload stage. Only the `-p <port>` pair was missing from its logged arguments.

  After, on macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64, rustc 1.97.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.140). The focused test run used this branch's head; the clippy and full-suite runs used a local tree combining this PR with its five siblings, which touch disjoint files:

  ```text
  $ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-hardware --features hardware --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 35s
  (exit 0)

  $ cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-hardware --features hardware --lib arduino_upload::
       Summary [   2.118s] 8 tests run: 8 passed, 182 skipped

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed files>
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```

  Historical public `6b98ff7` Windows selection produced 2 PASS and 6 preflight failures; startup cause remains unknown. The `679dcd5` exact-eight run stopped in setup, and the later `de4e14f` run failed without retrieved named results. Those revisions supply no current execution credit. The broad advisory cannot substitute for the exact named controls.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The full `--features hardware` suite on macOS intermittently fails `subprocess::tests::execute_returns_success_before_descendant_closes_output_pipes` at its 4 s PID-readiness deadline. That is unrelated: it fails the same way with `master`'s `arduino_upload.rs` (2 of 3 runs) and passes alone.
  - Not verified locally: the PowerShell fake itself (see the gap above).

prs.title: feat(channels/email): trust an extra CA for IMAP and SMTP
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - IMAP (`EmailChannel::connect_imap` and `zeroclaw_tools::email_imap::imap_connect`, used by the email tools) trusted only `webpki_roots`, and SMTP with `smtp_tls = true` only lettre's defaults. A mail server signed by a private or corporate CA could not be reached, and IMAP has no non-TLS path.
  - New `EmailConfig::tls_ca_cert_path`, named and documented like the MCP (#9405) and provider (#5797) option. Its certificates are added to the IMAP root store on top of the web PKI roots (`imap_root_store`) and to lettre's `TlsParameters` for SMTP (`smtp_tls_parameters`). Chain and hostname verification stay on.
  - The file is read by the MCP loader itself: `mcp_transport::load_tls_ca_pem` now takes an error prefix (`"MCP server `name`"` / `"email channel"`) instead of an `McpServerConfig`, and the absolute-path check moved into it. So the email option gets the same rules (absolute path, no `~`, regular file, 1 MiB cap, `O_NONBLOCK` open so a FIFO cannot hang the caller) and MCP's error messages are unchanged. The PEM bundle is parsed with `rustls-pki-types`; an empty or invalid bundle fails the connection.
  - `create_smtp_transport` now builds every mode on one `builder_dangerous(host).port(..).credentials(..)`, adding `.tls(Tls::Wrapper(..))` for `smtp_tls = true`, which is what `SmtpTransport::relay` did.
  - Docs: schema doc comment (feeds the generated reference) and a short "Mail servers signed by a private CA" section on the email page.
- **Scope boundary:** no client certificates, no verification bypass, no OS trust store, no change for configs without the key. Plain-text SMTP (`smtp_tls = false`) does not use the CA. #11748 (STARTTLS) is open in parallel and touches `create_smtp_transport` too; whichever merges second needs a small rebase to pass `smtp_tls_parameters()` to `Tls::Required` as well. I will do that rebase here if #11748 lands first.
- **Blast radius:** IMAP and SMTP connections of email channels and the email tools that set `tls_ca_cert_path`; MCP remote transports through the shared loader (behavior and messages unchanged, covered by its existing tests).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11751

### What this does, simply

Some companies run their own mail servers with security certificates issued by their own internal authority instead of a public one. ZeroClaw's email channel only trusted the public authorities, so it refused to connect to those servers, and there was no setting to fix it. This adds `tls_ca_cert_path`: point it at the company's certificate file and the channel trusts it in addition to the public ones, both for reading mail and for sending it. It is the same setting, with the same safety rules, that ZeroClaw already offers for model providers and MCP servers. Nothing changes for anyone who does not set it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The tests stand up a local TLS server whose certificate is signed by a fresh private CA and check, through the channel's real connect and send paths, that the handshake fails without the option and succeeds with it.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, which includes the `zeroclaw-channels` email tests (`channel-email` is a default feature) and the `zeroclaw-tools` `email_imap` and `mcp_transport` tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `imap_connect` in `zeroclaw-tools` (email tools) gets the same one-line root-store change as the channel's `connect_imap` but has no handshake test of its own; its root store is covered by `tls_ca_cert_path_adds_its_certificates_to_the_imap_roots`.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email
test email_channel::tests::connect_imap_trusts_tls_ca_cert_path ... ok
test email_channel::tests::send_over_smtp_tls_trusts_tls_ca_cert_path ... ok
test email_channel::tests::invalid_tls_ca_cert_path_fails_the_connection ... ok
test result: ok. 89 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1888 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- email_imap mcp_transport
test result: ok. 94 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2002 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
test result: ok. 1778 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # BASE_SHA = merge-base with upstream/master
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `connect_imap_trusts_tls_ca_cert_path` and `send_over_smtp_tls_trusts_tls_ca_cert_path` run each path twice against a fresh `localhost` server signed by a private CA: without `tls_ca_cert_path` the server sees a failed handshake, with it the handshake completes (the server then refuses the session, which is not under test).
  - Mutation check: with the configured roots dropped from both paths, both tests fail (`2 failed`).
  - `invalid_tls_ca_cert_path_fails_the_connection`: a relative path fails `send` with "must be absolute" instead of falling back.
  - `tls_ca_cert_path_follows_the_mcp_file_rules`: relative and `~` paths, a missing file, a directory, a file over 1 MiB and a file without certificates each fail with the matching message (the directory case accepts the Windows open error, like the MCP test does).
  - All existing MCP custom-CA tests (FIFO, symlink, oversized, relative, redirect, wrong host) pass with the shared loader.

Adding a CA widens trust only for the email connections of that channel alias, the same trade-off operators already make for MCP servers and providers; verification is never disabled.

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. `channels.email.<alias>.tls_ca_cert_path` is a new optional key; existing configs load and behave as before. To use it, set the absolute path to a PEM CA file and reload the daemon.

prs.title: fix(channels/email): do not answer automatic mail
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `dispatch_email` turned every new message from an allowed sender into a turn, including out-of-office replies, bounces and newsletters, and the agent's answer went back by email. Against another autoresponder that can become a mail loop.
  - `build_parsed_email` now records why a message is automatic (RFC 3834): `Auto-Submitted` other than `no` (parameters after `;` ignored, case-insensitive) → `auto_submitted`; `Precedence: bulk|list|junk` → `precedence`; `List-Id` or `List-Unsubscribe` → `mailing_list`. `dispatch_email` drops such a message first, before the allowlist and de-duplication, and logs `Action::Skip` with `channel`, `alias`, `sender`, `subject`, `reason`.
  - The blocked-sender record, the other inbound drop, was `Action::Note` with only `Blocked email from <addr>`. It is now `Action::Reject` with the same attribute set and `reason = "not_allowlisted"`. I kept it in this PR because it is the sibling record of the new one (same function, same attributes, same operator question: why did this email not reach the agent); happy to split it out if preferred.
  - Docs: the Safety section of the email page describes both drops and their `reason` values.
- **Scope boundary:** inbound filtering only. No opt-out setting for agents that should answer list mail (none is needed for any current use I know of; easy to add if someone asks). No change to outbound headers (the channel does not set `Auto-Submitted` on its own replies; that is a separate decision). Gmail Push is not touched.
- **Blast radius:** inbound email turns. Mail carrying these headers no longer reaches the agent; everything else is dispatched as before. Log consumers matching the blocked-sender record by `event.action = note` will see `reject` instead; the message text is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11749. Related #5528 (runaway outbound email, different cause).

### What this does, simply

Some email is written by machines, not people: "I'm out of the office" replies, "your message could not be delivered" notices, newsletters and mailing lists. Those messages carry standard headers that say so, and the email standard asks automatic responders, which the agent is, not to answer them. ZeroClaw ignored those headers, so the agent replied to them, and two automatic responders can keep answering each other. Now the email channel drops those messages before the agent sees them and logs why. The log record for mail from senders who are not allowed is also made structured, so an operator can see which mailbox, sender and subject were involved without reading free text.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The tests drive `dispatch_email`, which the IMAP loop calls for every fetched message, and read the emitted records from the log broadcast hook.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`; `channel-email` is in `zeroclaw-channels`' default features, so these tests run there.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the changed code.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text

(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email
test email_channel::tests::automatic_mail_reason_flags_rfc3834_and_list_headers ... ok
test email_channel::tests::dispatch_email_drops_automatic_mail_from_an_allowed_sender ... ok
test email_channel::tests::dispatch_email_delivers_mail_a_person_sent ... ok
test email_channel::tests::dispatch_email_rejects_blocked_sender_with_structured_attrs ... ok
test result: ok. 90 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1888 filtered out

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # BASE_SHA = merge-base with upstream/master
Summary: 0 error(s)

No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

  - `dispatch_email_drops_automatic_mail_from_an_allowed_sender`: an `Auto-Submitted: auto-replied` message from a `*` allowlist never reaches the channel's receiver, and the captured record has `event.action = "skip"` and `channel`, `alias`, `sender`, `subject`, `reason = "auto_submitted"`.

prs.title: feat(channels/email): send over SMTP with STARTTLS
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `create_smtp_transport` had implicit TLS (`smtp_tls = true`, `SmtpTransport::relay`) or plain text. A server that takes submissions only on 587 with STARTTLS, such as `smtp.office365.com`, could not be used, so an Office 365 mailbox could receive through the channel but not reply.
  - New `EmailConfig::smtp_starttls` (default `false`). When `true`, the transport upgrades with `Tls::Required`, the setup lettre's `starttls_relay` uses: if the server does not offer STARTTLS or the upgrade fails, the send fails before `AUTH` or any mail is sent. It takes precedence over `smtp_tls`.
  - The three modes now share one `builder_dangerous(...).port(...).tls(...)` path; `Tls::Wrapper(TlsParameters::new(host))` is exactly what `relay` built, so implicit TLS is unchanged.
  - Docs: `smtp_tls` and `smtp_starttls` have schema doc comments (the generated config reference is built from them), and the Outlook / Office 365 section, which had no SMTP guidance, gets a working example and the note that SMTP uses password auth (`oauth2` is IMAP-only).
- **Scope boundary:** no SMTP XOAUTH2, no opportunistic STARTTLS, no change to defaults (`smtp_tls = true`, port 465). IMAP is untouched. No migration: the field is additive and `#[serde(default)]`.
- **Blast radius:** outbound email for configs that set `smtp_starttls = true`. Every other config builds the same transport as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11747

### What this does, simply

Mail servers accept outgoing mail in one of two secure ways: encrypted from the first byte (usually port 465), or a plain connection that is switched to encryption before logging in (STARTTLS, usually port 587). ZeroClaw's email channel only knew the first way, and Office 365 only offers the second, so an agent on an Office 365 mailbox could read mail but not answer it. This adds a `smtp_starttls = true` option for the second way. If the server refuses to switch to encryption, nothing is sent, so the password never travels in clear text. Existing setups do not change.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The tests drive `Channel::send` against a local fake SMTP server and assert the exact command sequence the client sends; a live Office 365 check needs a tenant with SMTP AUTH enabled and adds nothing the sequence does not show.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`; `channel-email` is in `zeroclaw-channels`' default features, so both new tests run there. `zeroclaw-config` tests cover the default/serde of `EmailConfig`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the changed code. No test performs a successful TLS upgrade (that needs a TLS-capable fake server); the tests prove the upgrade is requested and enforced.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email
test email_channel::tests::send_without_tls_never_issues_starttls ... ok
test email_channel::tests::send_with_smtp_starttls_upgrades_before_credentials ... ok
test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1888 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
test result: ok. 1778 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # BASE_SHA = merge-base with upstream/master
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `send_with_smtp_starttls_upgrades_before_credentials`: the fake server greets, advertises `STARTTLS` and `AUTH PLAIN LOGIN`, and answers `STARTTLS` with `454`. The client's commands are exactly `["EHLO", "STARTTLS"]` and the send fails: no `AUTH`, no `MAIL FROM`. On `master` the same config cannot be expressed, and `smtp_tls = true` starts a TLS handshake on the plain-text port instead.
  - `send_without_tls_never_issues_starttls`: with both flags off, the client starts with `EHLO` and never sends `STARTTLS` (plain-text behavior unchanged).
  - **Not verified:** a send through a real Office 365 tenant on this head.

The pre-push hook (`cargo test --workspace`) was skipped with `--no-verify` because of local disk limits; required CI runs the same suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: SMTP credentials can now be sent after a STARTTLS upgrade. `Tls::Required` refuses to continue if the upgrade is not offered or fails, so they are never sent in clear text on this path; the test asserts no `AUTH` follows a refused upgrade. Certificate and hostname verification are lettre's defaults, as for implicit TLS.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. `channels.email.<alias>.smtp_starttls` is a new optional key defaulting to `false`; existing configs load and behave as before. To use Office 365, set `smtp_host = "smtp.office365.com"`, `smtp_port = 587`, `smtp_starttls = true`, then reload the daemon.

prs.title: fix(channels/email): save inbound documents to the channel workspace
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The email page says inbound attachments are stored under the workspace and their paths handed to the agent. Nothing was ever written: documents reached the agent only as bytes for one turn, and a `text/*` attachment was dropped whenever the email had a body (`extract_attachments` skips text parts, and `extract_text` only uses one when there is no body).
  - `collect_configured_channels` now gives `EmailChannel` its `Config::channel_workspace_dir("email.<alias>")`, as it already does for Telegram and Matrix.
  - In `dispatch_email`, after the allowlist and de-duplication checks, every attachment that is neither image nor audio is written to `<workspace>/email_files/<message-id>_<n>_<name>`. Its typed `marker` is set to `MarkerKind::Document` with the saved path and the content gets a `[Document: <name>] <path>` line, the same contract Matrix uses (`format_media_marker`), so the media pipeline defers to it. With a workspace, text attachments are saved too, even when there is a body.
  - Hardening: the name is the basename only, with control characters replaced, leading dots stripped and length bounded (extension kept); the message id is reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. `email_files/` is canonicalized and refused if it resolves outside the canonical workspace (e.g. a symlink). Any failure is logged (`Action::Save`, scrubbed error) and the email is delivered as before.
  - Docs: the "Attachment handling" section now describes what the code does. I used `email_files/` instead of the documented `attachments/<conversation>/`: it matches `telegram_files/` and `matrix_files/`, and email has no stable conversation key (threading comes from sender-controlled headers). The old path came in with the docs overhaul (#5788) and was never implemented.
- **Scope boundary:** inbound only. No retention or cleanup of `email_files/` (Telegram and Matrix keep files indefinitely too). Images and audio are not saved and keep going through the media pipeline. No config or schema change. The one-shot send builder (`build_channel_by_id`) is unchanged because it never receives mail. Outbound attachments and #9993's "bytes only" rule are untouched: nothing here reads a file named by a message.
- **Blast radius:** inbound email turns on configured email channels. The agent now sees `[Document: …]` lines and, for text attachments on emails with a body, attachments it did not see before. Disk usage grows with inbound documents, bounded per email by the existing `max_attachment_bytes`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11745

### What this does, simply

When someone emails the agent a PDF or a spreadsheet, the agent used to get the file's bytes for that one reply and nothing else: no copy on disk, no path, and a `.txt` or `.csv` attachment was thrown away if the email also had text in it. The docs said the opposite. Now the email channel saves those documents in the agent's workspace, next to where Telegram and Matrix already save theirs, and tells the agent where each one is, so it can open it again later with its file tools. Only mail from allowed senders is saved, file names are cleaned so they cannot escape the folder, and pictures and voice notes are handled exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new tests drive `dispatch_email`, the function the IMAP loop calls for every fetched message, with a real MIME message and a real temp workspace, and assert the files on disk, the content lines and the typed markers.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`. `channel-email` is in `zeroclaw-channels`' `default-channels`, so the email tests below run there. `Lint` builds them with `--features ci-all`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test asserts the one-line orchestrator wiring (`collect_configured_channels` returns `Arc<dyn Channel>`, which exposes no workspace accessor). It mirrors the Telegram and Matrix lines next to it.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email
test result: ok. 91 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1888 filtered out

$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base upstream/master HEAD) scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)

$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `dispatch_email_saves_documents_to_workspace_with_marker_lines`: a multipart email with a body, a PDF named `../report.pdf`, a CSV and a PNG. The PDF and CSV land byte-identical under `email_files/` as `doc-1exampleinvalid_0_report.pdf` and `_1_rows.csv`, the content carries both `[Document: …] <path>` lines, exactly those two attachments are marked, and the PNG stays unmarked for the pipeline.
  - `dispatch_email_without_workspace_keeps_documents_in_memory`: no workspace means today's behavior (no lines, no markers, CSV left to `extract_text`).
  - `dispatch_email_saves_nothing_for_a_blocked_sender`: with a workspace and a sender outside the allowlist, nothing is delivered and `email_files/` is never created.
  - `dispatch_email_refuses_email_files_outside_workspace` (unix): `email_files` is a symlink to another directory; nothing is written there and the email is delivered without markers.
  - `safe_file_name_strips_paths_and_leading_dots_and_bounds_length`.
  - **Not verified:** delivery from a live IMAP mailbox on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** clippy reports two `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` errors in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs` (untouched by this PR) on my local stable 1.99 toolchain; CI pins 1.98.0. I allowed that lint and `deprecated` for the local run only. The pre-push hook (`cargo test --workspace`) was skipped with `--no-verify` because of local disk limits; required CI runs the same suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the channel now writes sender-supplied bytes under the agent workspace. Only allowlisted senders' mail is written, into one fixed directory whose canonical path must stay inside the canonical workspace, with names reduced to a bounded basename that cannot contain separators or start with a dot. The new model-visible text is the sanitized file name inside a `[Document: …]` line; the attachment content was already model-visible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. Files already saved under `email_files/` are inert and can be deleted.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `failed to save email attachment` or `failed to prepare email_files directory` warnings (`event.action = save`, outcome failure) from `zeroclaw_channels::email_channel`; the email is still delivered.

prs.title: feat(channels/whatsapp-web): save inbound images and mark them like Telegram
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - An inbound WhatsApp Web image was downloaded into a `MediaAttachment { marker: None }`, and the message said `[Image]`. The bytes lived for one turn. With `media_pipeline` on, the model saw them once, inlined as base64; with it off (the default, see #10975), it saw nothing. Either way the agent had no file afterwards, so a tool that archives a receipt or attaches a photo to a report could not reach the original.
  - The channel now does what Telegram does with `telegram_files/`. When it has a workspace, each provider-loadable image of the message is written to `<workspace>/whatsapp_files/<phone>_<message id>_<n>.<ext>`, its attachment's `marker` is set to that absolute path with `MarkerKind::Image`, and the content carries `[IMAGE:<path>]` in place of the `[Image]`/`[Sticker]` placeholder (or ahead of any text). The pipeline already defers to a channel-rendered marker (`channel_rendered_owned_disposition`), so the image reaches the model exactly once, as an image, and does so whether or not the pipeline is enabled.
  - The file-name prefix is the sender's phone number, digits only, never the LID. It is the sender JID when that is a phone-number JID (device suffix dropped), else the alternate JID, else the LID-to-phone mapping the allowlist check already resolves. Files from one person share a stable prefix, and two senders never collide. The message id is reduced to ASCII alphanumerics.
- **Scope boundary:** images and stickers that `provider_loadable_image_mime()` accepts, on the message itself. Quoted attachments stay in memory. No change to video, audio, documents, retention/cleanup of `whatsapp_files/` (Telegram keeps its files too), the Cloud API channel, or config.
- **Blast radius:** the WhatsApp Web inbound path for messages carrying an image, when the channel has a `workspace_dir` (the daemon always sets one). Such messages now write one file per image and render a path marker instead of `[Image]`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11255. Related: #10975.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `channel`, `channel:whatsapp`, `risk:medium`, `size:M`

### What this does, simply

Photos sent to the bot over WhatsApp Web are now kept as files in the agent's workspace, and the agent sees them as images it can open and show to the model, the same way Telegram already works. Before, a photo lived in memory for one turn, and with the media pipeline off the model only saw the word `[Image]`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional, if a spare WhatsApp account is available.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `whatsapp_web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Web-mode `[channels.whatsapp.<alias>]` channel bound to an agent with a vision-capable model.
- **Steps to run:** send the bot a photo from an allowed number, with and without a text message around it.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `<agent workspace>/whatsapp_files/<number>_<id>_0.jpg` exists with the photo's bytes, the inbound content is `[IMAGE:<that path>]`, and the model describes the photo, with `media_pipeline` on or off.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no file; content `[Image]`; the model sees the photo only with `media_pipeline.enabled = true`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Lint job, which runs clippy with `--all-targets --features ci-all` and so compiles this code and its tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the tests are linted in CI but not run there: the required Test job uses default features, and `whatsapp-web` is not one of them. I ran them locally with the feature on (commands below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh
==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean
gate exit=0

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web --lib --tests -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web --lib
test result: ok. 2253 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - New tests: `sender_phone_digits_never_uses_the_lid` (phone JID with a device suffix, LID plus phone alt, LID plus mapping, LID alone gives no name), `inbound_file_stem_keeps_only_safe_message_id_characters`, `save_inbound_images_writes_and_marks_loadable_images` (bytes on disk equal the attachment, absolute marker target, `MarkerKind::Image`, a video in the same list left alone), `save_inbound_images_failure_leaves_the_attachment_in_memory` (a file where the directory should be: no marker, bytes still delivered), and `content_with_image_markers_replaces_only_the_placeholder`.
  - Mutation checks: making `sender_phone_digits` fall back to the sender JID whatever its server, and dropping the `attachment.marker` assignment, each make the matching test fail.
  - The no-double-image behavior rests on the pipeline's existing `image_already_marked_by_channel_is_not_double_described`, which this change relies on rather than reimplements.
  - **Not verified yet:** a live run on a paired number. I will add the result, file hash comparison and token count for the turn to this PR.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the pre-push hook was skipped with `--no-verify`. It runs `cargo test --workspace`, and on this machine it failed in `zeroclaw-hardware` on `subprocess::tests::execute_returns_success_before_descendant_closes_output_pipes` ("fixture must record a positive PID before the readiness deadline"), a timing-sensitive test in a crate this PR does not touch. Run alone, it passes 3 of 3 times. Every crate the hook reached before it, `zeroclaw-channels` included, passed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (tests use `1555…` numbers)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The channel now writes bytes received from chat participants to disk, as Telegram already does. The directory is fixed (`<workspace>/whatsapp_files/`), and the file name is built only from digits, ASCII alphanumerics of the message id, an index and an extension from `mime_extension` (which already rejects path characters), so a crafted message id or MIME type cannot leave that directory. Only images the provider loader accepts are written.
  - The file name carries the sender's phone number, which the channel already treats as the sender identity. Write failures are logged without the path, so the number does not reach the log sink.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Content for image messages changes from `[Image]` to `[IMAGE:<path>]`, the form Telegram and Discord already deliver.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. Files already written are inert.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. A channel built without a workspace keeps the old behavior.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** warnings `failed to create whatsapp_files directory`, `failed to resolve whatsapp_files directory` or `failed to save WhatsApp image attachment`; the message is still delivered with the in-memory image, as before.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Stage the declared `sign_manifest` example and genuine `vendor/` path-patch inputs before dependency prefetch in the default, Debian and Alpine Dockerfiles. The original seven image jobs lacked the example; after that correction, the next run exposed the missing crossterm path patch. Both inputs are now present before Cargo parses the temporary tree.
- **Regression protection:** Four named architecture methods check signer target declaration/staging/replacement and canonical vendor path-patch staging. Internal refusal variants cover missing, late, wrong-stage, wrong-path, comment-only and removed inputs, including LF/CRLF forms.
- **Scope boundary:** Four files only. Existing build commands, features, profiles, cache policy, base images, generated zones, runtime images and size checks retain their bytes. This does not change the real signer example, Containerfile, ignore policy or dependencies.
- **Blast radius:** Source-image dependency staging and architecture tests. No product API, credential, permission or configuration change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7432; Related #11310; Related #11221. The shared Rustls repair in #11736 remains a separate change.

### What this does, simply

The plugin manifest names a signing example, so Cargo requires its file to exist even when building another target. These Dockerfiles first copy only manifests and create temporary targets to cache dependencies. The new example was missing from that temporary tree. The primer now seeds that minimal target and copies the genuine vendor tree required by the root manifest. prs.title: feat(channels): stream model reasoning in Telegram and Slack drafts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Matrix already streams the model's reasoning into its `single_message` progress draft
    (`stream_reasoning = "off" | "status" | "full"`). Telegram (`stream_mode = "partial"`) and
    Slack (`stream_drafts = true`) stream an editable draft too, but had no way to show reasoning:
    the orchestrator only fed reasoning to the draft updater for Matrix, and the generic draft
    updater dropped `StreamDelta::Reasoning` outright.
  - Adds a per-alias `stream_reasoning` field to `[channels.telegram.<alias>]` and
    `[channels.slack.<alias>]`, reusing the existing `StreamReasoningMode` enum. The default is
    `off`, so existing configurations behave exactly as before.
  - Replaces the Matrix-only orchestrator gate with a channel-agnostic
    `stream_reasoning_for_config` resolver. Matrix keeps its own `single_message` gate, so its
    behavior is unchanged.
  - Adds `Channel::update_draft_with_reasoning` (default: drop the reasoning and edit the plain
    answer) and overrides it in Telegram (collapsed HTML blockquote) and Slack (mrkdwn quote).
  - Reasoning is draft-only chrome: `finalize_draft` rewrites the message from the answer alone,
    so the delivered reply never contains it.
- **Scope boundary:** No reasoning surface is added for Discord, Lark, Mattermost, or Matrix
  `partial`/`multi_message`; Matrix's own rendering is untouched. No model-provider, agent-loop, or
  tool-surface change.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (two typed fields, so the generated config field lists and JSON
  schema grow two entries), `zeroclaw-api` (one new `Channel` method **with a default impl**, so no
  existing implementor breaks), `zeroclaw-channels` (`telegram.rs`, `slack.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs`).
  Every channel that leaves `stream_reasoning` unset takes the pre-existing code path.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11743.

### What this does, simply

When you talk to the agent on Telegram or Slack, the bot already posts a "draft" message and edits
it while the answer is being written. The Matrix channel can additionally show *why* the model is
taking a while, because it can display the model's reasoning. Telegram and Slack could not: the
plumbing that carries reasoning from the agent loop to the draft existed, but it was switched on
only for Matrix, and the shared draft updater deliberately ignored reasoning for everyone else.

This PR gives those two channels the same switch, spelled the same way Matrix spells it:

```toml
[channels.telegram.home]
stream_mode = "partial"       # an editable draft must exist
stream_reasoning = "full"     # off (default) | status | full

[channels.slack.work]
stream_drafts = true
stream_reasoning = "status"
```

- `off` (default): the draft is byte-for-byte what it is today.
- `status`: the draft shows a liveness-only thinking line ("🤔 Thinking..."), with no reasoning text.
- `full`: the draft shows the model's raw reasoning as a quote above the in-progress answer —
  a collapsed `<blockquote expandable>` on Telegram, a `>` quote block on Slack.

The reasoning is *draft* chrome only. When the answer is complete the draft is rewritten from the
answer alone, so the message the user keeps never contains the model's private thinking. If the
channel is not streaming an editable draft (`stream_mode = "off"` / `"multi_message"` on Telegram,
`stream_drafts = false` on Slack) the setting is inert — there is no draft to put it in.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` — `telegram`, `slack`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Telegram alias with `stream_mode = "partial"` (or a Slack alias with
  `stream_drafts = true`) and a model provider that emits reasoning/thinking deltas. Start the
  channel (`zeroclaw channel run` or the service).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On `master`, ask the bot a question that takes a while to answer. Watch the draft message.
  2. On this branch, set `stream_reasoning = "full"` on the same alias, restart the channel, and
     ask the same question.
  3. Let the answer finish and read the final message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The draft shows the reasoning in a quote/blockquote above the
  in-progress answer; the final message is the answer alone, with no reasoning.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The draft shows only the answer text (and, on Slack, the
  generic "Waiting on model" lifecycle line); a `stream_reasoning` key on the alias is simply not
  recognised, so the draft never shows reasoning.

### How I tested

```sh
# formatting
cargo fmt --all -- --check

# compiles the changed crates with the two channel features enabled
cargo check -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-slack,channel-telegram

# new unit tests: config surface, per-channel resolver, render helpers, draft updater
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib stream_reasoning
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-slack,channel-telegram --lib reasoning

# clippy over the changed crates, warnings denied (the workspace-wide
# ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh is the same clippy invocation plus fmt,
# scoped here to the three touched crates)
```

the only other reasoning-path tests; they are unchanged and still pass.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Rust` (fmt + clippy + workspace tests)
  covers the changed crates; the docs gates cover the Telegram/Slack prose.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live Telegram/Slack transport is exercised in CI — the new

  Telegram/Slack render helpers (escaping, truncation, entity safety) and the draft updater's
  reasoning accumulation. I did **not** run against live Telegram or Slack workspaces.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no existing rendered output changes at the default

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)

  these two channels when an operator opts in. That is the point of the feature, and it is why the
  default is `off`. Reasoning text is passed through the same `zeroclaw_runtime::security::scrub` +

  generated channel field lists with their `off` default. To opt in, set the field on the alias and
  restart the channel.

  on the affected alias and restart the channel.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** the `stream_reasoning` field itself is the toggle; `off` is

- **Observable failure symptoms:** none expected. If a Telegram draft edit fails after the HTML
  blockquote is rejected, the code logs
  `editMessageText (reasoning draft) failed; falling back to plain text` at `DEBUG` and retries the
  plain-text edit.

prs.title: test(ci): capture affected Quickstart CLI states
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; receiving base `329e66f76394b00af9d00b767e00ad298133961e`.
- **What changed and why:** Adds an auxiliary workflow, capture helper and 60 authored controls (47 retained and 13 added) to prepare real CLI Quickstart evidence for the affected plugin list and completion states. The product is pinned separately to immutable public revision `a441e0cb755ebb3e1656eeee04e694c070d79214` / tree `5c4290c8ba4b62309f8311fa38cf628f120720c0`.
- **Scope boundary:** Exactly three new auxiliary files. No production, dependency, config schema, guest authority, existing required gate, release recipe or owner-policy change. Capture is manual-only; this PR provides no actual capture or acceptance result.
- **Blast radius:** Maintainer-invoked Linux evidence collection, owned child process cleanup and short-lived artifact export. The path-selected PR job runs only the authored harness controls.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7432; Related #11309.

### What this does, simply

This prepares a way to observe the changed Quickstart list and completion through the real CLI and terminal window. It preserves genuine selected empty values, separate no-row and cancellation cases, source/window/run bindings and raw terminal bytes. Owned process cleanup uses an unreaped direct-child anchor, and rich output stays private until the complete bundle validates. A successful capture and finalizer must both authorize rich upload; failure has a separate minimum receipt.

The helper assumes a single-threaded Linux process, default SIGCHLD and no other direct waiter/reaper. Its refusal rules are conservative. It does not provide isolation from an independently malicious same-UID host, escaped descendants or host death. Synthetic-token checks and PNG envelope validation are not universal privacy or pixel proof.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, after source review/publication, using hosted authored controls first. Actual manual capture requires a separately selected run after default-branch enrollment.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; real terminal-backed Quickstart. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** For authored controls, Python 3.11 on the workflow's Linux runner. For capture, the reviewed hosted workflow and isolated synthetic data; product source remains pinned to a441e0c.
- **Steps to run:** On the published branch, the five-minute job runs `python scripts/ci/quickstart_cli_evidence_test.py -v`. After normal review/enrollment, a maintainer may select the manual workflow; capture follows only a successful unit job. No capture was run for this draft.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The job should select all 47 authored controls. An actual approved capture should bind the supported CLI/window states and cleanup/export receipts to the exact source/run/attempt; rich upload must refuse incomplete or unsafe evidence. These are expectations, not observed outcomes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same auxiliary files/command/workflow are absent; master supplies no result from this harness. The pinned product behavior is unchanged by this auxiliary PR.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Harness run 38573063425](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38573063425), attempt 1, passed all 47 individually named controls after explicitly checking out signed head `1be4efd77b929b0ff047aae8033c1e34542eee85`. These exercise the authored helper contracts with mocked kernel/GUI boundaries. The manual evidence job was intentionally skipped on this PR event. [Quality Gate 38573063706](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38573063706) is a separate, still-unqualified requirement; old branch CI and source review supply no execution credit.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** All 47 authored controls passed, but real Linux wait/PTY/window/CLI cleanup, actual export refusal and artifact delivery remain unexecuted. The mocked controls do not establish actual capture, real process-group cleanup, universal secret detection or human pixel/privacy acceptance. Required CI, non-author Core reviews and normal default-branch enrollment remain separate.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Static Python AST parsing (no import), safe YAML parsing, extracted `bash -n`, Git/text/hash checks only: `47 methods; exact approved bytes; AST/YAML/Bash-n PASS`. Hosted `python scripts/ci/quickstart_cli_evidence_test.py -v`: `Ran 47 tests in 0.301s`, `OK`; all 47 named rows are present in the actual job log. Published signed revision `1be4efd77b929b0ff047aae8033c1e34542eee85`, tree `04eeb9a4977702cec8331256a8e233e73b45a4cc`; full-index patch SHA256 `9ca523d7c7c66cd5d4d2cf008d84259e8996f9427bd7d942453babfa58bf0783`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source-only preservation: all three reviewed blobs/modes match; existing master entries and workfiles are unchanged; the rich upload uses actual AND gates. No helper/test import or process/CLI/PTY/GUI/socket/native/compiler execution occurred.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for this auxiliary addition: it does not change the product UI. Real CLI/window screenshots and human acceptance for #11309 remain pending; no image or final-interface result is claimed here.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Harness controls ran on exact signed `1be4efd` / tree `04eeb9a4977702cec8331256a8e233e73b45a4cc`, in the linked run. Product CLI/terminal capture is NOTRUN; future capture stays pinned to a441e0c with source/run/attempt/frame/context bindings.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** NOTRUN; no old screenshots or source assertions are represented as new visual proof.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The historical47controls belong to `1be4efd`; all60named current methods passed on `6c91836`. No actual CLI/window action or affected-state capture has run.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local helper/tests/CLI/GUI/PTY/socket/Rust/Cargo/native execution was excluded. Hosted unit controls ran; actual capture is manual-only and requires reviewed default-branch enrollment before a selected run.

### Current review follow-through

**Current signed helper head:** `6c918363fed928119c8395a8891c55cb08ac40d1`, tree `54d46f0bd53e4559b2afebb5b6c7a0715a66000e`, normal forward parent `14d442d2538fe8807b59e2610c9a1ccb37b1c4cf`. Root SourceOwnerReview and independent source review approved a two-file correction; the workflow and all production/build inputs are unchanged.

The helper now copies only the two fixed, stable compiler outputs into fresh strict private single-link files, checks both original and copy before publication, latches cancellation through ownership cleanup and receipt commits, and preserves only a verified current minimum-failure cause. Two legacy Git object-ID SHA1 calls explicitly declare nonsecurity compatibility use; independent SHA256 checks remain. Private export and rich upload guards are unchanged.

Thirteen new regression methods cover these boundaries. [Current control run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38629392066), attempt 1, completed SUCCESS. Actual job116076805897 checks out this head and prints all60unique named method PASS rows, including the corrected Bridge cancellation control, followed by `Ran 60 tests in 0.361s` and `OK`. Internal variants are not separate named executions. [Current Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38629392227) completed FAILURE:32 successful jobs,10 declared skips and Security plus the required gate failed. This is the shared Rustls block, not a full-QG success. The 47 named passes linked above belong only to `1be4efd` and provide no execution credit to this successor. Shared Rustls Security remains separately blocked until #11736 lands and receiving qualification passes.

**Retained test-only failure and correction:** On `14d442d`, run38628225846 executed 60 methods and failed with five subtest TypeErrors: the new private-write wrapper accepted two positional arguments while real write_json passed the optional third replace argument. The successor adds that optional parameter and forwards it unchanged in two test lines. Root and independent reviews verified all stages, assertions, helper/workflow and other59 bodies unchanged. Historical failed observations stay failed; this is not a production-helper repair.

No actual build/materialization, CLI capture, cleanup, screenshot or privacy acceptance is claimed. The design assumes single-thread Linux with the existing direct-child wait owner and quiescent compiler output. It cannot guarantee cleanup under kernel faults, host death or SIGKILL, prevent privileged races, or make cancellation/ready observation an OS transaction. All three findings remain investigating until actual proof. Default-branch enrollment and any manual capture remain separate decisions.

**Actions allowlist impact:** All added `uses:` references are pinned and match the existing `actions/*` and `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@*` patterns. This workflow requires no allowlist expansion or repository-policy change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** The auxiliary manual runner uses isolated temporary directories, bounded Linux proc observation, owned child groups and terminal-window capture. Repository permission is `contents: read`; no production permission or guest grant is added. Actual cleanup ownership still requires hosted proof.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** A future manual run obtains public source/build/window prerequisites and uses a bounded synthetic fixture server. It does not invoke an agent/model/guest tool turn. No such calls were executed in this preparation.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Synthetic secret-bearing capture files stay private; full bundle validation and a current decision gate rich export. Failure exports only a fixed-field minimum receipt. Known-byte/field rejection does not prove universal privacy or protection against an independent malicious same-UID writer.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No;** fixtures use synthetic project-scoped values. Real screenshots and artifact contents still require explicit review.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** This auxiliary path makes no agent/model request.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Process identity, wait/reap order and interrupted export are substantive risks. The source retains unreaped ownership until signal retirement, conservative refusal, private staging, complete byte/context validation, separately gated safe failure receipts and one-day artifact retention. These source safeguards remain unexecuted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes;** auxiliary-only addition.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes, auxiliary CI helper/workflow only.** Existing product config/env/CLI interfaces are untouched.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The manual recipe retains the reviewed pinned toolchain; no workspace floor/dependency change.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. Normal default-branch workflow enrollment is a maintainer operation, not a product migration. [GitHub requires the dispatch workflow on the default branch](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/manually-run-a-workflow).

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual auxiliary commit through the normal PR workflow, removing only these three files. No production migration is required.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Actual capture remains gated by explicit manual dispatch and unit-job success.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed capture/finalizer, missing safe decision, conservative ownership/cleanup refusal, incomplete/unsafe export or missing minimum receipt. These must not be treated as capture success or retried blindly.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A; no superseding relationship. Related #7432 and #11309 remain the coordination homes.

---

Labels belong in the GitHub UI. The owned-process and private-export boundary warrants `risk:high`; two independent non-author Core approvals and protected integration are required. Source review supplies no capture, privacy, pixel, platform or release acceptance.
