prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Make `model_routing_config upsert_agent` preserve omitted agent fields and existing risk/runtime profile references instead of rebuilding them on every call.
  - Persist only the requested agent, provider, and profile paths so unrelated configuration, comments, and unknown fields survive the update.
  - Isolate explicit profile changes, reject ambiguous shared or colliding profile mutations, and require older config files to be migrated before this targeted writer changes them.
  - Format missing, shared, and colliding risk/runtime profile errors through the existing tool Fluent catalog, using translated entries when installed and English fallback otherwise.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR does not add live config publication, config-commit admission, concurrent-writer coordination, or provider probe/rollback behavior. PR #10034 independently owns provider probing and rollback.
- **Blast radius:** The built-in `model_routing_config` tool's `upsert_agent` action and the persisted agent/provider/profile entries it intentionally updates. Other actions keep their existing save behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11606

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets an agent choose which AI model a helper agent uses. Previously, changing only that choice could also reset the helper's permissions and limits and rewrite unrelated configuration.

This PR leaves settings alone when the call does not mention them. If a call explicitly changes permissions or runtime limits, the helper gets its own copied settings rather than changing settings another agent might use. Current-schema configurations keep their comments and unrelated values; older schemas must first use the supported migration command.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This is the smallest coherent repair because provider-only preservation, explicit profile isolation, and targeted persistence share one `upsert_agent` transaction. Fixing only the provider assignment would leave explicit profile updates able to overwrite shared state or lose default-sensitive values. The implementation reuses the existing typed config and dirty-path writer; the added branching keeps risk-profile and runtime-profile rules explicit at the cost of more code in this cold administrative path.

Because this is an author-owned `risk:high` change to the security-policy boundary, it still requires the repository's independent Core Team approvals before merge.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — focused regressions exercise the production tool action against temporary config files without asking a reviewer to risk a real operator config.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 38341340687](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38341340687) is running on current head `e89a136d046f7965483ee3eeef22c9869d78fff0`. It covers workspace tests, lint, security, supported build/check targets, channels, plugins, MSRV, and Windows. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live operator-config smoke was run. The preceding implementation's disposable harness invoked `ModelRoutingConfigTool::execute` against temporary config files; it does not establish live runtime publication, config-commit admission, or concurrent-writer behavior.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The current localization repair passed formatting, the 20 focused tests, comment hygiene, and diff integrity. The earlier implementation also passed affected-crate Clippy, docs checks, and the disposable tool-action smoke at `28a47dde2e7d397023b42acf29b7ef94f3aef104`.

prs.title: fix(providers): send configured extra_headers on Anthropic requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The `anthropic` family accepted `extra_headers` in config (the schema documents it for every family) but never forwarded it: `AnthropicModelProviderConfig::create_provider` dropped `opts.extra_headers`, and the provider had nowhere to put them. Only the compatible, openai, hailo-ollama and opencode providers read the field. A gateway that authenticates with its own header and rejects `x-api-key` therefore answered every request with 401, with no warning that the configured header was ignored.
  - `AnthropicBuilder::extra_headers` validates the map once (invalid names or values are skipped with a warning, the same handling as the compatible provider) and marks values sensitive. The provider sends them as client default headers on both the buffered and the streaming client, so every request path picks them up without touching the five request sites. Clients that carry extra headers stop at a cross-host redirect (`opencode_session::redirect_policy`), and a failure to build such a client is returned as an error rather than replaced by a client without the headers.
  - Headers the provider sets on the request itself (`x-api-key`, `Authorization`, `anthropic-version`, `anthropic-beta`, `content-type`) keep the provider's value, because reqwest lets request headers replace client defaults. A configured `x-api-key` cannot override the real credential.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to auth selection, beta headers, request bodies or any other provider. No new config key: `extra_headers` already exists on `AnthropicModelProviderConfig`.
- **Blast radius:** Only anthropic-family entries that set `extra_headers`. With the map empty (every existing config that works today) the provider still uses the shared cached runtime client, so requests are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed; found while pointing an anthropic entry at a gateway that authenticates with its own header.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets you add your own headers to requests sent to a model provider, for example a key that a company gateway asks for. For Claude models talking the Anthropic protocol, that setting was quietly ignored: the headers never left the machine, so a gateway that needed them refused every request.

Now those headers are sent on every request, streaming or not. ZeroClaw's own key and protocol headers still win if a configured header has the same name, and setups that do not use the setting behave exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: the wire behaviour is covered by capture-server tests on both request paths and through the factory.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- extra_header apply_auth
# test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1941 filtered out
```

- Buffered and streaming requests carry the configured header, and a configured `x-api-key` does not replace the provider credential (exactly one `x-api-key` value on the wire).
- Invalid header names and values are skipped, valid ones kept, values marked sensitive.
- Redirects, buffered and streaming, through loopback servers: a same-host 307 is followed and the final hop gets the header; a 307 to another port stops and the other server receives no request; a 307 from `localhost:<port>` to `127.0.0.1:<same port>` stops and the origin records no request on the target path. The localhost cases run a same-host redirect first, so the stop cannot come from a failed `localhost` lookup.
- Client build failure (an invalid runtime proxy): the buffered call and the thinking-stream request both return an error, and no request reaches the server.
- Factory path: `AnthropicModelProviderConfig::create_provider` delivers `opts.extra_headers` to the wire.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate (fmt, clippy, workspace tests) covers the touched crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None in CI.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each new test fails with its fix taken out (local edits, not committed): without the redirect rule the redirect tests fail because the cross-host server gets a request; with the hostname comparison removed from the rule, the two same-port tests fail and the cross-port tests still pass; with a fallback to the shared client on build failure, the build-failure test fails because the request reaches the server. Before the fix, a live anthropic entry pointed at a header-authenticated gateway logged a 401 naming the missing header on every request and fell through to its fallback. A local build carrying this change (the same header, client and redirect code; it also carries #11544's stream idle bound) has run that entry since 2026-10-07. Streaming requests complete through the gateway with no 401, and a buffered request reached the gateway's per-model authorization (a 403 for a model the account may not use), which the gateway checks only after the configured header authenticates the caller.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 745f0add (on master e654b4b7), focused `--lib` tests above and `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test`: CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: configured header values, which can be credentials, now leave the machine on anthropic requests, as they already do on the other families. Values are marked sensitive so they are redacted from debug output, the warning for an invalid entry names the header and never the value, the provider's own credential headers cannot be overridden, and configured headers are not forwarded across a cross-host redirect.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merged commit (`git revert <squash-commit>`). Before merge, drop this patch to restore the existing behavior in which native Anthropic requests ignore configured extra headers.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Removing `extra_headers` restores the old request behavior for that entry but may prevent a header-authenticated gateway from accepting requests.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Header-authenticated gateways reject requests, or client initialization reports a transport setup failure. Credential-boundary concerns remain under review; rollback does not revoke or rotate any credentials already transmitted.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): make scrollbar seeking continuous across loaded history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Use the same absolute pointer mapping for scrollbar clicks and drags, so dragging no longer jumps back toward the pre-click position.
- Make the scrollbar cover the complete loaded transcript while retaining the 1,000-entry render window. Intermediate seeks skip entries that produce no visible rows.
- Paint the scrollbar inside the same track used for pointer hit testing. Reuse indexed viewport lookup for thumb position and preserve transcript selections until cached content changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Loaded transcript navigation. Keyboard bindings, clipboard transport and history pagination remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** Chat and Code transcript rendering, scrollbar pointer handling and selection during seeking.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10301.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `risk:medium`, `zerocode`, `topic:zerocode`.

### What this does, simply

The scrollbar currently moves on a click, then calculates the following drag from the position before that click. This makes the transcript jump. In long sessions, its range also describes only the current render window, so it cannot seek directly to older loaded messages.

This repair makes pointer position choose the transcript position consistently. The track can reach the oldest and newest loaded messages and positions between them without rendering the entire history. A character selection stays valid while the viewport moves within the same cached content and clears when seeking replaces that content.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, terminal mouse forwarding is useful additional evidence for the original SSH report.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui`, Chat and Code panes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run this branch's `zerocode` against your normal daemon and open an existing session with enough loaded history to scroll. Use the same session on `master` for comparison; no provider turn is needed.
- **Steps to run:** Click the middle of the right-edge scrollbar, hold the button and move one row. Drag to its top and bottom. For a long loaded transcript, seek between older and newer messages, resize the terminal, and repeat. Select transcript text and move the scrollbar within the same render window. Repeat over SSH in Windows Terminal or WezTerm when available.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The viewport stays at the clicked position before the pointer moves, then follows the drag. The track reaches the loaded-history endpoints. Selection survives movement within one cached geometry and clears when that geometry changes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The first drag uses the old scroll anchor, and long-history seeking stays within the current render window.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** After publication, the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, including ZeroCode's mouse-dispatch and render tests. `Fmt` and `Lint` cover formatting and Rust linting. Current-branch CI is pending publication.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Real terminal/SSH mouse forwarding and a direct capture of scrollbar presentation.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

git diff --check
exit 0

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

On `c9ce4f68288b` (rebased onto current master, ported to the `transcript_layout` cache from #11459), through the remote cargo wrapper:

```text
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode scrollbar
```

prs.title: fix(zerocode): keep composer and completion keys and clicks out of the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** the chat pane handles any non-character chat chord before the composer sees it (`chat_action_bypasses_text_input`). Up, Down and Esc are chat browse chords, so the composer's own handling of them was unreachable, and the completion popup ignored the mouse entirely.
  - `a2c38b7526`: Up/Down go to the composer whenever it holds text, through `InputBarState::claims_edit_key`. The cursor moves through multi-line input, and the popup highlight moves (the popup only opens on `/…` input, so it's covered). Before this, the transcript scrolled.
  - `15c247bedc`: Tab and Esc go to the composer while the popup is open, so Esc closes the popup instead of reaching the chat. The popup records its rect when rendered: a left click on a row fills that entry (same as Tab), the wheel moves the highlight, and other events inside it are swallowed so they don't reach the transcript underneath. Before this, `handle_mouse` only hit-tested the input box, and the popup draws above it.
  - `4a1089532a`: a short terminal clips the popup to fewer rows than matches. It now scrolls to keep the highlighted entry visible and maps clicks through the scroll offset (Greptile finding).
- **Scope boundary:** no change to which completions are offered, the popup's look or position, or Up/Down in an empty composer (still transcript/browse navigation).
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode composer only. With text in the input, Up/Down no longer scroll the transcript; PageUp/PageDown and browse mode still do.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. Found while dogfooding #10905, whose two new commands (`/restart-session`, `/restore-context`) share a prefix.

### What this does, simply

When you type in ZeroCode's input box, the arrow keys scrolled the chat instead of moving the cursor, so you couldn't move between lines of a long message. When you type `/`, a list of matching commands pops up above the input; you couldn't move through it with the arrows, Esc didn't close it, and clicking an entry did nothing. Now the arrows move the cursor (or the highlight, when the list is open), Esc closes the list, the mouse wheel moves the highlight, and clicking an entry picks it. With an empty input the arrows still scroll the chat.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode chat and ACP panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** any ZeroCode session with some transcript above the input.
- **Steps to run:** (1) Type two lines (Shift+Enter between them), press Up. (2) Type `/re`, press Down, then Up, then Esc. (3) Type `/` and click the third entry.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** (1) the cursor moves to the first line. (2) the highlight moves with Down/Up; Esc closes the list. (3) the input fills with that command and the list closes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** (1) and (2) scroll the transcript; the highlight stays on the first entry and Esc does not close the list. (3) nothing happens to the list.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the key routing and hit-testing. Terminal mouse reporting itself is not exercised.
- **Commands run and tail output** (on a Mac mini through our cargo wrapper, at 4a1089532a):
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- autocomplete arrow_keys_move composer_vertical_navigation composer_claims_completion` → `test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed`. `clipped_autocomplete_scrolls_to_keep_the_highlight_visible` fails with the popup scroll removed.
  - With all three rules removed (Up/Down claim, Tab/Esc claim, popup hit-test), 6 of the 7 new tests fail: `composer_vertical_navigation_precedes_transcript_in_chat_and_code`, `arrow_keys_move_the_slash_command_highlight_in_chat_and_code`, `composer_claims_completion_keys_only_while_the_popup_is_open`, `clicking_an_autocomplete_row_fills_that_command`, `clicking_the_autocomplete_border_keeps_the_popup_open`, `scrolling_over_autocomplete_moves_the_highlight`. The seventh (`closed_autocomplete_does_not_capture_clicks`) guards the other direction. With only the Esc rule removed, `composer_claims_completion_keys_only_while_the_popup_is_open` and the Esc step of `arrow_keys_move_…` fail.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode` → `1452 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on this machine.
  - `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings
  - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both files is clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Both chat-level tests drive `Chat::handle_key` in Chat and ACP panes, so they cover the routing that was broken, not just the input bar. The same behavior (the Up/Down commit has been in our dogfood stack since 2026-10-06) is in the experiment build [`experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984) (dogfood base [0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d)).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No rendering changed: the popup's layout and styles are untouched; only which keys and clicks reach it.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 4a1089532a, `input_bar::tests`, `chat::tests::composer_vertical_navigation_precedes_transcript_in_chat_and_code`, `chat::tests::arrow_keys_move_the_slash_command_highlight_in_chat_and_code`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (see above).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Dan verified on 2026-10-13 in [`experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984) (dogfood base [0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d)): Up/Down move the popup highlight, Esc closes the popup, and clicking a row fills that command. That build carries a port of this change onto the experiment line with the same behavior, not head 15c247bedc itself.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full workspace test was skipped; the change is confined to `zerocode`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Rebinding the input-bar `history prev/next`, `accept completion` or `cancel completion` keys still applies, because the claim resolves through the same keymap.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 4a1089532a 15c247bedc a2c38b7526`

prs.title: feat(runtime): surface cost warn_at_percent warnings in ZeroCode
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions) - **What changed and why:** - `CostTracker::check_budget` returns `BudgetCheck::Warning` once recorded spend reaches `cost.warn_at_percent` of the daily or monthly limit, but `enforce_tool_loop_budget` only handled `Exceeded`. The warning was dropped, so the first sign of a limit was a failed turn. - The main tool loop now calls `announce_budget_warning` before the hard-limit gate. It sends a new `TurnEvent::BudgetWarning { current_usd, limit_usd, period }` at most once per turn. It never blocks the turn: an exceeded limit is still `enforce_tool_loop_budget`'s stop, and a full or closed event channel just drops the notice. - The RPC surface forwards the event as a `budget_warning` `session/update` (`SessionUpdateEvent::BudgetWarning`, `period` is `"day"` or `"month"`). - ZeroCode parses it and shows a system notice: "Cost warning: $8.25 of the $10.00 daily limit spent (82%). Turns stop at the limit." The daemon repeats the event on every turn while spend stays over the line. The client shows it once per period and limit per session, so it reappears only when the limit changes or the other period crosses its own threshold. - **Scope boundary:** no notice for a turn that stops at the hard limit (that is still the failed-turn message, and #11589 covers the override prompt). ACP (`acp_server.rs`) and the web gateway (`ws.rs`) ignore the new event; their `_ =>` arms already drop unknown variants. Only the English locale gets the new strings; the other locales fall back to English. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. - **Blast radius:** a new `#[non_exhaustive]` `TurnEvent` variant. Every existing match has a wildcard arm (workspace `check --all-targets` passes). One extra `check_budget(0.0)` per provider call, which is the same ledger read `enforce_tool_loop_budget` already does. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10950. Related #11585, #11589. ### What this does, simply ZeroClaw can be told to warn you when you have spent, say, 80% of your daily AI budget. The code that works out "you are at 80%" already existed, but nothing passed the result on, so you never saw a warning. You only found out when a turn failed at 100%. This PR passes the warning through to ZeroCode, which shows it once as a line in the chat. Nothing is blocked and no setting changes. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode) - **Setup / preconditions:** an isolated config with `[cost] enabled = true`, a small `daily_limit_usd` (for example `0.50`) and the default `warn_at_percent = 80`, on a priced model. - **Steps to run:** chat until recorded spend passes 80% of the limit, then send one more message. - **Expected on this branch (after):** a "Cost warning: $… of the $0.50 daily limit spent (…%)" system line appears once, before the reply. Later turns don't repeat it. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no warning. The first visible sign is "Budget exceeded: … Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets." when the limit is hit. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover all three crates touched. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the logic. The live crossing in ZeroCode is being dogfooded (below). - **Commands run and tail output** (run on a Mac mini through our cargo wrapper, at 5f66713d5a9d): - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_warning spend_past_the_warning spend_below_the_threshold` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- budget_warning` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - Each test fails with its fix removed: with `announce_budget_warning` made a no-op and the dispatch arm returning `None`, 2 of the 3 runtime tests fail; with the client dedupe disabled, `budget_warning_shows_one_notice_per_period_and_limit` fails. - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → `Finished` - Wider runs: `zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::turn rpc::dispatch agent::cost` gives 938 passed, 1 failed; `zerocode --bin zerocode` gives 1447 passed, 1 failed. The two failures (`new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`) also fail on master on this machine. - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files is clean. - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tested with $40 budget. Warning appeared at $33.73. - **Visual interface evidence:** - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5f66713d5a9d, ZeroCode chat state (`chat::tests::budget_warning_*`). - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** above - **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full `cargo test --workspace` was skipped; CI runs it. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The notice is client-side chat state and never enters model history. - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Yes. Older clients ignore an unknown `session/update` type. Older daemons never send it. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `warn_at_percent` now does what its docs say. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 5f66713d5a9d` - **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.warn_at_percent = 100` makes a warning coincide with the limit, which in effect turns it off. - **Observable failure symptoms:** repeated cost-warning lines in ZeroCode, or none at all. Grep the runtime trace for `cost warning threshold reached`.

prs.title: fix(tools): expose scenario routing requirements
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Advertise `hint`, `model_provider`, and `model` as required nonblank strings when `model_routing_config` selects `upsert_scenario`. Put the guarded `if` and `then` directly on the object schema, without a top-level composition wrapper. Require an explicit action in the condition so an omitted action still defaults to `get`.
  - Share that field list with validation and report all missing, non-string, or blank required fields in one localized error, before reading or changing configuration.
  - Preserve whole-object argument recovery for schemas with `if`, `then`, or `else`. Decode one JSON-stringified value matching an explicit object/array type, then stop before conditional child traversal. Keep the existing reference, composition, tuple-array, ambiguous-type, malformed-input, shape and depth safeguards.
- **Scope boundary:** Other action contracts, optional-field parsing, persistence, permissions, provider implementations, and repetitive-tool recovery are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Consumers of this tool's parameter schema and scenario-validation feedback, plus native and text-fallback argument recovery for explicitly typed conditional schemas. The flat argument object and tool registration remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11708.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded #11371/#11479 scope amendment is proposed separately in the existing exception batch #11697. It covers only explicit outer object/array decoding for conditional schemas and its focused regressions. Explicit Core Team approval must be recorded before merge; the existing #11436 approval covers only the original scope. This implementation PR does not change ADR-016 or the exception table.

### What this does, simply

Agents use this tool to choose which model handles a kind of request. Previously, its published instructions did not say which fields a scenario update required. If a model left several fields out, the tool reported only the first problem, leaving the model to discover the others over successive retries.

This change publishes the complete required set for scenario updates and returns every invalid required field together. The model receives enough information to correct the call in one retry. This does not guarantee that a model follows the instructions or chooses the right tool, and it does not turn model routing into a network-permission control.

Some models return the entire argument object as a JSON string. The new conditional schema initially prevented ZeroClaw from decoding it, so a requested scenario update could become a successful read without saving anything. The response parser now restores the declared outer object before dispatch. It leaves conditional child values to the tool's normal validation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The focused suite exercises the actual tool dispatch, configuration bytes, schema cleaner, and prompt serializer deterministically; interactive model tool choice is nondeterministic.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# Passed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib model_routing_config
# test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 2071 filtered out; finished in 0.27s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib argument_preservation_tests
# test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 5718 filtered out; finished in 0.08s

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
# Passed.

```

- **Coverage:** Tests check complete correction feedback for missing, wrong-type, and blank strings, byte-identical configuration after invalid calls, argument errors before config-read errors, preserved read-only admission, implicit `get`, partial `set_default`, valid scenario persistence, and dotted-provider agent calls without `model`. They also check that raw, OpenAI-cleaned, and Anthropic-cleaned schemas preserve the guarded requirements without root composition keywords, and that the complete schema reaches the text-tool prompt.
- **Recovery coverage:** The real routing tool's schema enters `interpret_chat_response` through native and extra-encoded text-fallback calls. Both retain `upsert_scenario` and save the expected route to a temporary configuration file. A separate control proves that conditional object/array schemas decode only their outer type and leave child strings untouched. Existing controls cover free text, references, composition, ambiguous types, tuple arrays, invalid input, type mismatches and depth limits.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace Test job covers the tool and runtime library tests; Lint and Format cover the changed Rust code. [Required CI passes](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38505495932) at recovery commit `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, including Test, Lint, Format and CI Required Gate. Head `d42af917707b76cd8dd1610529b1e83529f5193b` restores the original exception documentation after relocating the proposal to #11697; its complete tree matches the tested recovery commit. Fresh CI is pending.
- **Known coverage gap:** A live local-model conversation and vendor endpoint acceptance have not been tested. The tests establish contract visibility and validation behavior, not universal backend acceptance or a measured reduction in model retries.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The generated English catalogue matches the canonical catalogue plus the renderer's provenance header. No provider server or agent configuration was changed for testing.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or rendering behavior changes; the changed error is a tool result returned to the model.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tool tests ran at `48253684a5cb589a3ff158a9c4747011f06ec6f9`. The runtime argument-preservation suite ran on the patch committed as `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, with source identity checked afterward. Evidence is in the owning module tests and the output above. The macOS linker warned that the test harness's unwind section exceeds the compact-unwind table limit; compilation and all selected tests completed successfully.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** An incomplete `upsert_scenario` call returns one error naming all invalid required strings and leaves saved configuration unchanged. JSON-stringified valid calls preserve their selected action and save the route rather than silently reading configuration.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and Clippy were not repeated; the focused suite covers this bounded repair, with broader coverage left to hosted CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. The tool's schema descriptions and validation feedback change. The new error contains fixed field names, never argument values, and existing write admission remains in place.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing valid calls retain their behavior. Invalid scenario calls receive complete feedback instead of the first-field error.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Tool argument metadata, invalid-call feedback and conditional-schema argument recovery change; there are no new operator settings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Omitted-action reads, partial default updates, and dotted-provider agent updates keep their existing contracts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits and rebuild or reinstall the previous binary. No configuration migration is needed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Valid routing calls unexpectedly fail or become reads without saving a route, omitted-action reads require scenario fields, or invalid calls return a missing-localization-key error instead of the complete correction.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This PR does not supersede another contribution.

prs.title: fix(web): keep the chat input focused through a turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The chat message box was `disabled` for the whole turn (the input lock from #6220). Disabling a focused element drops its focus, so every follow-up message needed a click first, and Tab had to cycle through the rest of the page to reach the box.
  - It is now `readOnly` during a turn instead. Typing is still blocked and the "Running…" placeholder and dimming still show (`read-only:opacity-40` alongside `disabled:opacity-40`), but focus stays in the box.
  - `handleSend` now refuses while a turn runs. A read-only field still fires Enter, and an image upload or drag-and-drop can still change the draft mid-turn; the disabled box used to hide that.
  - Stop hands focus to the box as it is clicked, because the Stop button unmounts when the turn ends and would otherwise take focus with it. It does this before the abort request, so the request settling never moves focus: a control the user moves to while it is pending keeps focus.
- **Scope boundary:** nothing can be sent mid-turn, as before. The disconnected and loading states still use `disabled`. The send, upload, and model-picker controls are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** the chat composer in `web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx` only. During a turn the dimmed box now keeps its focus ring, stays in the Tab order, and is announced as read-only rather than unavailable. On touch devices the on-screen keyboard would likewise stay open through a reply, as before #6220 (not tested).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11658. Related #6220.

### What this does, simply

While the agent is replying, the chat box is locked so you can't send another message on top of the running one. It was locked in a way that also took the cursor out of the box, so after every reply you had to click back into it before typing. Now the box is locked as read-only, which keeps the cursor where it was: the moment the reply finishes, you can type the next message. You still can't type or send during the reply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a running gateway with the dashboard and any agent.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the agent chat, type a message, press Enter. When the reply finishes, start typing without clicking.
  2. Send another message and press Stop during the reply. Start typing without clicking.
  3. Send another message and, during the reply, open the conversation picker (or click another control).
  4. Delayed Stop: with browser network throttling on (for example Firefox DevTools → Network → Regular 2G), send a message, press Stop, then immediately open the conversation picker.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** 1 and 2: the text goes straight into the message box. 3 and 4: focus stays where you moved it when the reply or the abort finishes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** 1 and 2: nothing is typed until you click the box, and Tab reaches it only after cycling through the page's other controls.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Web Permission Tests` runs `cargo web check` (API client generation plus `tsc -b`) and `npm run test:contexts`, whose `pretest:contexts` step runs `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` with both new component tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The component regression runs in Web Permission Tests through `pretest:contexts`; CI does not exercise real browser focus. Firefox on Linux was checked manually as described below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a throwaway container (the project's Rust build image, Node v24.20.0), on this branch:
  ```text
  $ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin web -- check     # gen-api + tsc -b
  ==> npx tsc -b
  exit 0
  $ cd web && npm run test:contexts
  > zeroclaw-web@0.1.0 pretest:contexts
  ✔ the composer stays focusable and read-only during a turn and sends nothing until it ends
  ✔ Stop hands focus to the composer at once and not again when the abort settles
  exit 0   (every suite reports "ℹ fail 0")
  $ npm test
  exit 0   (every suite reports "ℹ fail 0")
  $ npm run build
  exit 0   (only the existing chunk-size warning)
  ```
  Against `master`'s `AgentChat.tsx`, both new tests fail:
  ```text
  ✖ the composer stays focusable and read-only during a turn and sends nothing until it ends
    AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
    + actual - expected

    + undefined
  ✖ Stop hands focus to the composer at once and not again when the abort settles
    AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Stop focuses the composer before the abort request settles

    0 !== 1
  ```
  The Stop test fails the same way against this PR's first commit (`c2b063c2a`), which focused only after the abort settled.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** In Firefox on Linux, against a daemon built from master `d03325172` with this branch at `d9fe717bd` (plus two of my other open PR branches, neither touching `web/`) and `embedded-web`, I ran the four steps above: focus came back after a completed reply and after Stop. Opening the conversation picker during a reply moved focus to it, and focus stayed there when the reply finished. With Firefox network throttling, opening the conversation picker right after Stop kept focus in the picker when the abort settled, whether I clicked it quickly or a little later. Not verified: Chrome, Safari, touch devices.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `d9fe717bd` merged into master `d03325172`; `web` dashboard; Firefox on Linux.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** in the first comment below: the message box focused, with the caret in it, right after a reply finished, without a click (taken on `c2b063c2a`; the second commit changes only the Stop path).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** send and wait for the reply → the box keeps focus. Send, then Stop → focus returns to the box. Send, then open the conversation picker during the reply → focus stays on the picker. Throttled send, Stop, then the conversation picker straight away → focus stays on the picker after the abort settles.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no Rust code changed, so `cargo fmt`, `clippy`, and `cargo test` weren't run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose recall, docs and status placement exceptions
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Add three bounded placement proposals to `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` for #10567, #9579 and #11513. Each extends an existing runtime subsystem and lacks a covering recorded exception.
- **Memory recall dates:** Cover the existing memory-injection renderer, forwarding of the public opt-out, date-shaped prefix handling, existing character-budget accounting, and focused renderer/pipeline tests. Memory storage and the public setting retain their current owners.
- **Built-in docs skill:** Cover this one embedded guide, its lowest-precedence resolution, read-on-demand versus inline prompt behavior, tool registration/read support, and the runtime origin adapter. Existing channel, gateway and dashboard consumers retain their owners.
- **Configured profile status:** Cover only the optional configured-profile alias in the existing `agents/status` response, its canonical config lookup and focused valid/missing-profile test. Profile resolution stays in config, and presentation stays in ZeroCode. This does not report a running session's retained profile generation or limits.
- **Scope boundary:** All three rows explicitly await Core Team approval. Each names permitted paths, its extraction destination and a review condition. This PR does not grant itself approval or change the implementations. #9579's separate localization feedback still needs reconciliation in that implementation.
- **Blast radius:** Three new rows in one placement table. The 36 existing records and the standing exception rules are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10567, #9579 and #11513.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw is splitting its large runtime into smaller owners. New work in the transitional runtime needs a recorded exception before it merges. These changes show stored dates beside recalled facts, ship a small guide that helps agents consult the installed version's tools and documentation, and report an agent's configured runtime profile to the existing status client.

These are additions to the existing prompt, skills and RPC machinery. Extracting that machinery first would turn each feature into a larger ownership refactor. This PR proposes limited permission to finish them where their callers already live, while naming where the code should move and when to reconsider the placement. The Core Team can approve or refuse the proposals independently of the feature reviews.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. This changes the placement record; compare each proposed scope with the linked implementation's runtime diff.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh CI has started at `f6e7c89a0f1c56a315ad2f85a0da5b0e57bd83ed`. [Docs Style](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38516993198/job/115698045317) and [Format](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38516993198/job/115697919849) pass; aggregate required CI remains incomplete. The changed `AGENTS.md` is outside the docs gate's default `docs/book/src` selection, so I also ran the Markdown check with the file selected explicitly.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Lint and integrity checks validate the record's structure, not the placement decision. Core Team review must assess the proposed scopes and destinations.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The prepared three-row patch passes `git apply --check`. Explicit-file Markdown lint reports zero errors. `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` passes its six helper tests and reports no added links. Table inspection confirms four cells per row and all 36 existing records preserved. Diff integrity checks report no whitespace errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Compared #10567 at `58bf2cee547405177616dc5f4e3b0fc4d384a3bc`, #9579 at `455457b0264b3dc04dabfdfdecd5b9d0250a8cb3` and #11513 at `196500bf9d7684dba4071059975e9863c5f5f643` with their production callers and runtime paths. Checked master's table and the open exception-record PRs for covering or duplicate proposals. The memory row assigns rendering to the agent loop, not the memory backend. The skills row is limited to `zeroclaw-docs` and preserves operator overrides and existing tool policy. The status row projects only the current configured alias and preserves config ownership and missing-profile omission.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No displayed interface changes.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Cargo and live application smoke add no evidence for this documentation-only patch. Feature validation remains in the separate implementation PRs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No runtime permissions change. The proposed development-placement permission takes effect only through Core Team approval and the recorded scope.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The embedded instructions are part of #9579, not this record-only change.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed commit adding these three rows, then reconcile any covered feature that has not yet merged. Removing the permission record does not undo an implementation already accepted under a valid grant.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None for the placement record.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A row covers paths or behavior beyond its named feature, omits a receiving caller or extraction owner, or misstates approval. Correct the record before relying on it for implementation merge.

prs.title: fix(security): apply configured firejail_args to the Firejail wrapper
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `FirejailSandbox` used to be a unit struct, and `wrap_invocation` built a fixed argument list. Configured `firejail_args` never reached the firejail command line, even though the risk-profile schema accepts them and `security status` feeds them into the sandbox config. The struct now holds validated extra arguments. `create_selected_sandbox` builds it through `FirejailSandbox::with_args(&sandbox.firejail_args)` on both the explicit-backend path and the auto-detect path. The arguments go after the wrapper's own flags and hardening flags, and before the wrapped invocation, so firejail reads them as its own options and not as arguments to the target command.
  - Validation follows the maintainer decision on #11594. An entry is rejected if it is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, is `--`, isn't a single `--option` / `--option=value` (for example `none` or `-q`), or names an option that would undo the wrapper. The rejected options are `--profile` (the wrapper sets `--noprofile`), `--include`, `--ignore` (it can drop the wrapper's flags), `--private` / `--private=…` (the wrapper sets `--private=home`; `--private-tmp`, `--private-etc=…` and similar are still allowed), `--allow-debuggers`, `--join`, `--join-or-start`, `--join-network`, `--join-filesystem`, `--chroot` / `--chroot=…` (chroot mode clears Firejail's `--noroot` and skips the private home setup, undoing the wrapper's `--noroot` and `--private=home`), `--seccomp-error-action=log` (logging executes the syscall instead of preserving seccomp denial), and every `--keep-dev-*` option (`--keep-dev-shm`, `--keep-dev-ntsync`, `--keep-dev-tpm`), which Firejail documents as re-exposing host devices or the host `/dev/shm` even with the `--private-dev` the wrapper requires. Option names may contain dots (`--seccomp.block-secondary`, `--caps.drop=…`): each dot-separated segment must start with a letter or digit, so `--seccomp.`, `--.x` and `--a..b` are still rejected. The name grammar and the conflict check are separate steps.
  - If Firejail is selected but its arguments are rejected, the sandbox becomes `RejectedFirejailArgsSandbox`. It refuses every command (`wrap_command` / `check_initialization` return `InvalidInput` with the reason), the same way `FailedSeatbeltSandbox` does. It does not fall back to running without the arguments or to `NoopSandbox`, since either would present the configured hardening as active when it isn't.
  - `sandbox_posture`, which feeds `security status`, now describes the active Firejail backend as "Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (…reason…)". Before, it described a configuration that wouldn't be applied.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR doesn't touch #11538 / #11539 (the hard-coded `--private=home` / `--nowheel` launch failures) or the docs change in #11591. It doesn't edit the schema doc comment or the generated `config.md`. `firejail_args` still has no effect when another backend is active (Landlock, Bubblewrap, and so on), which matches its documented meaning ("when sandbox_backend resolves to firejail").
- **Blast radius:** Linux, and only when Firejail is the selected sandbox backend. With empty `firejail_args` (the default and all presets) the firejail command line is byte-for-byte the same as before; a test covers this. A profile that has non-empty `firejail_args` gets them applied now. If they're invalid, its shell commands are refused with the reason and no longer run without them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11594

### What this does, simply

A risk profile can list extra Firejail options in `firejail_args` (for example `--net=none`), but ZeroClaw silently ignored them while still reporting them back. Now they're actually passed to firejail. Options that would break or weaken ZeroClaw's own Firejail setup, or that aren't Firejail options at all, are rejected with a clear message. In that case commands are blocked, not run as if the hardening applied, and the sandbox status says so.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new behavior is in command construction and backend selection, which the unit tests cover without needing firejail installed. A live Firejail smoke test would add signal, but I couldn't run one here (see below).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust test and lint jobs run the `zeroclaw-runtime` unit tests, which include the new `security::firejail` and `security::detect` tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Nothing exercises a real firejail binary. The non-Linux `cfg` branches (where firejail isn't compiled) were only checked by reading them: I don't have a macOS/Windows target installed, so CI's cross-platform jobs are the check for those.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::firejail security::detect`
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_passes_configured_args_before_the_wrapped_command ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_without_configured_args_is_unchanged ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_single_options_with_and_without_values ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_are_not_options_or_undo_the_wrapper ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_with_args_reports_rejected_args_before_probing ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::selected_firejail_with_rejected_args_blocks_commands_instead_of_dropping_them ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::firejail_posture_reports_rejected_args ... ok
    test result: ok. 43 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5663 filtered out; finished in 0.03s
    ```
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/firejail.rs` or `security/detect.rs`. The crate still fails clippy on lints that already exist on master with this box's newer toolchain: deprecated `fetch_update` in `rpc/upload.rs` and `rpc/dispatch.rs`, and `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`. This PR doesn't touch those files.
  - Follow-up commit 806fc4b (review fixes: option-name validation, Fluent text, comment hygiene): `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security:: i18n::` → `test result: ok. 405 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → passed; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → no findings in `security/`.
  - Follow-up commit aca1e8ad (review fixes: reject `--keep-dev-*`, accept dotted option names). With only the validator change reverted, the two new tests fail:
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_reexpose_host_devices_despite_private_dev ... FAILED
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_dotted_options_and_passes_them_before_the_wrapped_command ... FAILED
    test result: FAILED. 19 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5688 filtered out
    ```
    With it: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::firejail` → `test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed` (including `firejail_rejects_malformed_dotted_option_names`), and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::` → `test result: ok. 365 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/`; it still stops on the same pre-existing toolchain lints listed above.
  - Final-command output at aca1e8ad (`cargo build --bin zeroclaw`, Debian 13 x86_64, `firejail` 0.9.74 installed so Firejail is the selected backend, `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`, temporary `HOME` and `--config-dir`, an agent whose risk profile sets `sandbox_enabled = true`, `sandbox_backend = "firejail"`). Only the `Sandbox:` line differs between the two runs; the full output is in the PR comment.
    ```
    # firejail_args = ["--keep-dev-shm"]
    $ zeroclaw security status --agent local
    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (firejail_args rejected: --keep-dev-shm conflicts with the options ZeroClaw's Firejail wrapper sets))

    # firejail_args = ["--seccomp.block-secondary", "--net=none"]
    $ zeroclaw security status --agent local
    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Linux user-space sandbox (requires firejail to be installed))
    ```
  - Follow-up commit f4af67eb (review fix: reject `--chroot`). With `--chroot` removed from the conflict list, the new test fails:
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_chroot_because_it_disables_noroot_and_private_home ... FAILED
    --chroot: ["--net=none", "--chroot"]
    test result: FAILED. 21 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5688 filtered out
    ```
    With it: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::firejail` → `test result: ok. 22 passed; 0 failed`. Final-command output at f4af67eb (same setup as above, `zeroclaw 0.8.5 (f4af67eb7)`):
    ```
    # firejail_args = ["--chroot=/srv/firejail-root"]
    $ zeroclaw security status --agent local
    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (firejail_args rejected: --chroot conflicts with the options ZeroClaw's Firejail wrapper sets))

    # firejail_args = ["--seccomp.block-secondary", "--net=none"]
    $ zeroclaw security status --agent local
    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Linux user-space sandbox (requires firejail to be installed))
    ```
  - Follow-up commit 4cb5845d (review fix: reject `--seccomp-error-action=log`): the validator rejects the logging action through the existing conflict/InvalidInput path. `firejail_rejects_seccomp_log_action_that_allows_blocked_syscalls` covers the override alone and alongside independent restrictions; `firejail_accepts_seccomp_deny_actions_with_independent_restrictions` retains `kill` and `EPERM`, `--net=none`, dotted hardening options and configured order. Current [Quality Gate run 38342067128](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38342067128) completed successfully. Current PR checks report 45 successes and 8 skipped checks, with no failed or pending checks. This update relies on CI for this head; it does not claim a fresh local test or new final-command capture.
  - On `master` the new tests don't compile, because there's no way to give `FirejailSandbox` arguments. That is the bug: the configured value has nowhere to go.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read every `FirejailSandbox` construction site: `detect.rs` was the only production one. `runtime_shell_assembly` and `security status` both reach it through `create_sandbox` / `sandbox_posture` with `risk_profile.sandbox_config()` / `sandbox_config_from_policy`, and both carry `firejail_args`. I did **not** run a command inside a real Firejail sandbox, so I haven't observed `--net=none` actually cutting the network. For the `security status` capture above I installed the firejail package so backend selection picks Firejail; that command only probes `firejail --version` and does not start a sandbox.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The only user-visible text change is the posture description string, shown above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run the full workspace `cargo test` / `cargo clippy --all-targets`, because only `zeroclaw-runtime/src/security` (two files) and the English CLI Fluent catalogue changed. The crate's `security::` tests and lib/test clippy cover them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Configured Firejail options are now applied, and options that would loosen the wrapper's baseline (`--profile`, `--include`, `--ignore`, `--private`, `--allow-debuggers`, `--join*`, `--chroot`, `--keep-dev-*`, `--seccomp-error-action=log`) are rejected. A rejected configuration blocks commands and doesn't fall back to an unsandboxed run.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the default (empty) `firejail_args` and every preset. A profile that already sets `firejail_args` changes behavior: valid options now take effect, and invalid ones now block that profile's shell commands with a reason.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The existing `firejail_args` key starts doing what its docs say.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: if `security status` or a refused command reports "firejail_args rejected", write each option as one `--option` / `--option=value` entry, or remove the option the message names.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Emptying `firejail_args` in the risk profile restores the previous firejail command line exactly.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** shell commands failing with `firejail_args rejected: …`, or `security status` showing "Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked".

Phase 2: The Runtime. Complete the remaining runtime-composition and installable-plugin outcomes from RFC #5574 alongside compatible rolling fixes.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.8.6 runtime](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v086-runtime), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: a clean runtime composition API; the accepted Wasmtime/WIT execution bridge in supported artifacts; registry lifecycle including updates; plugin installation during onboarding without Cargo; and the agreed minimal core-tool set with measured binary size.

Completion requires release-binary proof of tool execution, Discord plugin install/use, and onboarding without a Rust toolchain. This replaces the previous fixes-only scope. Feature acceptance, normal review/CI, and explicit release holds for breaking changes still apply.

prs.title: fix(runtime): reject tool-call envelopes leaked into prose instead of rendering them
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (head `87432f7ae2`; merges cleanly with current master `0f8fb9d372`)
- **What changed and why:**
  - **Symptom.** On `gpt-5.6` via the codex provider (intermittent, about three occurrences in one evening on a production instance), a turn's tool calls arrived glued **into** the visible reply as raw JSON instead of the structured channel: prose, then `{"content":null,"tool_calls":[…]}` followed by a Gemini-style `{"content":…,"tool_code":…,"tool_name":…}` stub, then more prose and a hallucinated success claim. The user saw envelope bytes as garbage text, the tool never executed, and the model then claimed the work was done.
  - **Why every existing layer missed it.** The response starts with prose, so the whole-response JSON pass and every envelope classifier — all gated on the text *starting* with `{`/`[`/tag/fence — never fire. The field payload was additionally malformed by a python-style `\'` escape inside the `arguments` string: invalid JSON, plausibly why the provider delivered the calls as text in the first place.
  - **Fix: detect and retry, never execute.** A complete tool protocol object naming an active tool — after prose, inside other JSON, or inside malformed outer text — now trips the parse-issue path in `detect_tool_call_parse_issue_for_known_tools`, so the turn is rejected and retried with model feedback instead of rendered. Detection scans for JSON values, walks each parsed value's whole tree, and covers canonical, alias- and Responses-shaped envelopes, malformed protocol members of a complete envelope, and python tool stubs. A `\'`-repaired copy is scanned (removed only at odd backslash-run parity, so the legal `\\'` is untouched), so the observed malformed payload is still seen. Every leak-detection site that decides whether a name in model output refers to an active tool applies the parser's alias normalization, so a leak naming `bash` is treated like one naming `shell`. The detector is deliberately bounded to these shapes; what it does not cover is listed under Security.
  - **Why not execute the leaked call.** An earlier revision of this PR salvaged calls from prose. Review showed, and three further review passes on progressively stricter scanners confirmed, that whether an embedded object is a genuine leak or data the model is quoting (a JSON array, a truncated transcript tail, a YAML-style mapping) cannot be decided from text. Executing it therefore lets model-echoed business data smuggle a tool invocation. Rejection with retry fixes the user-visible defect — no protocol bytes rendered, no false completion — while the model re-issues the call through the structured channel.
  - **Streaming parity.** Final rejection cannot retract text already streamed, so the stream guard reaches the completed-response verdict from the same inputs. It holds an unfinished JSON-like value from its own opener, so a leak split across deltas is not forwarded before an identifying key arrives, while ordinary inline JSON in prose keeps streaming; brackets inside strings do not count, and the per-chunk scan is bounded by bytes examined so a run of closed values cannot crowd out a later unfinished candidate. It receives the active tool names from the turn's own tool specs, independently of whether the provider request carries native tool specs, so the text-tool route is covered. It checks the whole buffer on every release, because a release emits everything ahead of the candidate anchor too.
  - **Documentation guard.** A reply that quotes the protocol while explaining it is not rejected, on the completed and the streaming path. Two questions are answered separately. `looks_like_tool_protocol_example` decides whether the reply is documentation; for tag- and fence-delimited calls that is judged for the reply as a whole by any example or sample wording in its visible text ("Sample tool call:", "Example tool call:", "示例如下:", or an explicit framing phrase), because tags are an executable format and a tag that is not documentation is parsed as a real call. `unframed_embedded_protocol_mentions_known_tool` then rejects a reply that is documentation as a whole but carries a bare protocol object naming an active tool without its own framing clause, so one illustrated example exempts only itself. Framing is explicit illustrative phrasing in the clause that ends at the object: only prose counts, so quoted data cannot frame the leak after it; a sentence terminator or a line break closes the clause, with a fence opener excepted and the periods of "e.g." not counted; and a stray tag marker without its own closer is not a span that can hide a leak. Ordinary narration words ("creating the sample page", `examples/`, documentation-domain links) never qualify.
- **Scope boundary:** No text-embedded envelope is ever parsed into a call. No change to the structured tool-call channel, to any provider's request/response mapping, to the whole-response parse passes, to retry policy, or to tool approval. Only the observed `\'` defect is repaired; other malformations are not. The provider-side root cause is not addressed.
- **Blast radius:** The runtime's known-tool parse-issue detection (every provider's text path), the streaming protocol hold-back, and the channel orchestrator's stripping of isolated tool-call artifacts, which now recognizes aliased tool names as its envelope branch already did. A false positive rejects and retries a reply that quotes a complete protocol object naming an active tool without framing it (see Security). A shape outside the detector's scope is rendered as text.
- **Linked issue(s):** No tracking issue was filed; the defect was diagnosed directly from production payloads. Related #10445 (landed; this branch was rebased onto it at the reviewer's request).
- **Labels:** `bug`, `agent`, `channel`, `runtime`, `experienced contributor`, `channel:core`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `topic:provider-transport`

### What this does, simply

Sometimes a model answers in words but also pastes a tool call into the text, as raw JSON, instead of sending it through the proper channel. Before this change, that pasted text was shown to the user as if it were part of the answer, and in one version of this fix it was even run. Now the runtime notices a complete tool call hiding in the text, refuses the whole reply, and asks the model again, so the user never sees protocol bytes and nothing pasted into prose is ever executed. The streaming path holds back the same text before it reaches the screen, since a rejection cannot take back what was already shown. A reply that merely explains or quotes the format as an example ("for example, a call looks like this: …", in English, Spanish, French, Japanese or Chinese) is left alone.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the leak is intermittent and provider-side, so a live A/B cannot be reproduced on demand; the byte-exact field payloads are replayed deterministically in the regression suite instead.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required workspace build/clippy/test matrix covers the three changed crates; the change is Rust-only with no visual surface. At head `87432f7ae2` (run 38075876268) the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38075876268/job/114284927332) passes, with [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38075876268/job/114282600299), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38075876268/job/114282600273) including the rustdoc gate, [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38075876268/job/114282600005) and [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38075876268/job/114282696530) green; 48 jobs succeeded and none failed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for the detection boundary — every placement and guard rule is pinned by a deterministic regression. Documented detection gaps are listed under Security.
- **Commands run and tail output (at head `87432f7ae2`; exit codes captured from cargo itself):**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                        # clean
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   # clean
$ RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels   # clean
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 224 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored      (zeroclaw-tool-call-parser)
test result: ok. 5644 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored     (zeroclaw-runtime)
$ bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh    # defaults, 3 runs x 16 threads: runtime 5644 and channels 1972 on every run
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh          # passed
```
The same gates pass on the merge result with current `master` (`0f8fb9d372`).

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Both byte-exact field payloads are detected and produce no call; the first is left untouched as visible text for the runtime to reject. At the stream boundary: a python-stub leak split at every byte boundary is never forwarded; the text-tool route suppresses it with no native tool specs; an example framed in an earlier delta streams unchanged, and a framed stub split at every byte still streams whole, while an unrelated earlier phrase exempts nothing; a framed illustration followed by an unframed leak, in one delta or several, suppresses the leak, as does a tag example followed by a bare leak; a unicode-escaped key or a named tool-result envelope ahead of the candidate anchor is not released; and inline JSON in prose keeps streaming. Parser regressions cover every placement surfaced across the reviews — the reviewer's prose-prefixed business array, array-wrapped leaks, complete envelopes inside valid, truncated or malformed outer arrays and objects, closers hidden in double- and single-quoted strings, apostrophes and inch marks, repaired `\'` escapes, tag-adjacent and `<think>`-wrapped structure, a quoted transcript tail, a tuple, and plain narration — each asserting no call, detection, and that the documentation guard stays off; alias names on the stub, tag and malformed-text arms; quoted data that tries to frame a following leak; a line break closing the framing clause; "e.g." framing only its own clause, while "i.e." and a snake_case `page_g_2` frame nothing; stray and plural tag markers that must not hide a leak; a tag or fenced example beside a separate unframed leak; and genuine documentation, including a second framed example, that stays exempt. At the runtime boundary: leaked envelopes and stubs are rejected with no tool call; a tag example beside a bare leak is rejected without its tag executing; five ordinary tag-documentation replies (period-ended lead-in, a dotted file name, a transcript, a numbered list, a trailing explanation after a fence) render with no call; and five ordinary replies (an API explanation quoting a tool result, a Python code sample, an elided example, markdown-link prose, a framed envelope) render without a retry. Every mechanism was mutation-checked: reverting it fails a dedicated regression. Two named exceptions: the stream guard applies the unframed check at both the candidate and the release site, and each alone is backstopped by the other, so only removing both fails the streaming regression; and the candidate-level framing check is backstopped by the whole-buffer release check. NOT verified: a live provider reproduction (intermittent).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no interface presentation changed; leaked protocol bytes are no longer rendered.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `87432f7ae2`; no interface surface. Evidence is the exact-head CI above and the deterministic stream-guard, parser and runtime-boundary regressions.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A reply embedding an unframed complete protocol object for an active tool is suppressed from the stream and rejected for retry; a reply that frames it as an explicit example is streamed and rendered unchanged, and a documented tag call is rendered, not executed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace clippy/test left to CI; the scoped runs and CI's parallel runtime gate above cover the three changed crates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No — fixtures reproduce the leak's structure with illustrative command strings and no personal data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: this changes how untrusted model output that embeds tool protocol JSON is handled — it is rejected and retried instead of rendered. Nothing embedded in text is ever executed, so model-echoed data cannot trigger a tool. Residual risks: (1) a reply that quotes a complete protocol object naming an active tool without an explicit example phrase in its own clause is rejected, and if the model keeps quoting it the retries end in the existing fallback error; (2) the detector is bounded, and these are not detected, so such replies are rendered as text: an object that is itself cut off and never closes, replies longer than the 64 KiB scan bound, a tool result that names no tool, a bare call object with no container key (the channel orchestrator strips it only when it stands alone on a line outside a code fence), a duplicate or whitespace-padded protocol key, and a tag leak in a reply whose visible text uses example or sample wording, which is rendered as text rather than executed.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of the branch commit. The change is stateless — no schema, config, or persisted data — so a revert fully restores prior behavior on the next build.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** false-positive rejections appear as turns retried with the "response resembled an internal tool protocol envelope but no valid tool call could be parsed" feedback on replies that only quoted protocol data, and in the worst case the fallback error after retries; a detection regression shows known-tool protocol JSON rendered to users again.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.8.6 runtime](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v086-runtime), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.
